## Summary

Fixes multiple instances of naive `\n` escaping/unescaping across `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli` that corrupted valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals, regular expressions, and inline/fenced code spans during file edits and UI/tool text normalization.

## Details

1. **Model family detection for `aggressiveUnescape` in `write_file` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/write-file.ts`)**:
   - When `experimentalDynamicModelConfiguration` is enabled, `isGemini3Model` previously only checked `modelConfigService.getModelDefinition(resolved)?.family === "gemini-3"`. For Gemini 3 models without an explicit entry in `modelDefinitions` (such as `gemini-3-flash` or `gemini-3.0-pro`), it returned `false`, causing `aggressiveUnescape` to become `true` in `write_file` and stripping valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals via `unescapeStringForGeminiBug`. `isGemini3Model` now falls back to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/` when no model definition family is present.
   - Updated `isGemini2Model` to accept `config?: ModelCapabilityContext`, resolve model aliases (such as `auto-gemini-2.5`), and match hyphenated Gemini 2 model names (`/^gemini-2(\.|-|$)/`).
2. **File content correction & LLM escaping prompt (`packages/core/src/utils/editCorrector.ts`)**:
   - Short-circuit `ensureCorrectFileContent` before running `unescapeStringForGeminiBug` when `disableLLMCorrection && !aggressiveUnescape`.
   - Fixed template literal escaping in `correctStringEscaping` where `\\n` vs `\n` was unescaped in the prompt template, which previously instructed the LLM to replace `"bar\nbaz"` with a multi-line string containing a literal newline and referenced `corrected_new_string_escaping` instead of `corrected_string_escaping`.
3. **Context-aware newline normalization (`packages/core/src/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/ask-user.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/Banner.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useBanner.ts`)**:
   - Replaced naive `.replace(/\\r\\n/g, "\n").replace(/\\n/g, "\n")` calls with `normalizeEscapedNewlines`, which converts unescaped `\n` and `\r\n` sequences to actual newlines while preserving double-escaped backslashes (`\\n`), inline/fenced markdown code spans (e.g. `` `\n` ``), and standalone quoted escape tokens (`"\n"`, `'\n'`).

## Related Issues

Fixes #22466

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests for `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli`:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/models.test.ts src/utils/editCorrector.test.ts src/tools/write-file.test.ts src/utils/textUtils.test.ts src/tools/ask-user.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts src/ui/components/messages/ThinkingMessage.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run lint and typecheck across the monorepo:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```

prs.title: fix(vscode-ide-companion): register all extension disposables in context.subscriptions
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->

In `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`, two pairs of adjacent `vscode.Disposable` registrations inside `activate(context)` were enclosed in redundant outer parentheses (`(reg1, reg2)`), causing them to be evaluated as comma expressions (`SequenceExpression`) where only the second `Disposable` in each pair was appended to `context.subscriptions`. This PR removes the redundant parentheses so all registered `Disposable` instances—including the `gemini.diff.accept` command and `vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` listener—are tracked in `context.subscriptions` and deterministically disposed upon extension deactivation.

Additionally, this PR enables the ESLint `no-sequences` rule (`{ allowInParentheses: false }`) across the monorepo to prevent unintended comma operator expressions in argument lists and statements.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

1. **Extension subscription registration
   (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`)**:
   - Removed the redundant outer parentheses around the `gemini.diff.accept` and `gemini.diff.cancel` command registrations in the first `context.subscriptions.push(...)` call so both `Disposable` objects are passed as separate arguments.
   - Removed the redundant outer parentheses around the `vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` and      `vscode.workspace.onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust` listener registrations in the second `context.subscriptions.push(...)` call so both `Disposable` objects are passed as separate arguments.
2. **Unit test coverage and mock fidelity (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/utils/vscode-mock.ts`,    `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.test.ts`)**:
   - Updated `vscodeMock.workspace.registerTextDocumentContentProvider` and      `vscodeMock.commands.registerCommand` to return `{ dispose: vi.fn() }` objects matching the `vscode.Disposable` interface.
   - Added a unit test in `extension.test.ts` verifying that all 16 disposables registered during `activate(context)` (specifically including `gemini.diff.accept` and `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`) are added to `context.subscriptions` and disposed when `context.subscriptions` is cleaned up.
3. **ESLint `no-sequences` enforcement (`eslint.config.js`, `packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.test.ts`)**:
   - Enabled `'no-sequences': ['error', { allowInParentheses: false }]` in `eslint.config.js` to catch parenthesized comma expressions inside function call arguments.
   - Replaced the single comma expression in `oauth2.test.ts` with a standard block body in the `setTimeout` mock.

prs.title: fix(core): normalize leading slashes in file search query for @ autocomplete
prs.body:
## Summary

Normalize leading slashes and dot-slashes (`/`, `./`, `\`, `.\`) in `@` file search patterns to enable path autocompletion when typing `@/` or root-relative paths in the CLI input prompt.

## Details

- **Problem:** When users type `@/`, `@/src`, or `@./package.json` to mention files/directories from the project root, the extracted query previously included the leading slashes (e.g. `'/'`, `'/src'`). Because file search indexes workspace files as relative paths without leading slashes (e.g. `package.json`, `src/`), the fuzzy search engine (`AsyncFzf` / picomatch) treated the leading slash as a literal match requirement. This caused 0 matches to be returned for root-level files and top-level directories, which suppressed the autocomplete dropdown and disabled Tab completion.
- **Solution:** In `RecursiveFileSearch.search` and `DirectoryFileSearch.search` (`packages/core/src/utils/filesearch/fileSearch.ts`), normalize the incoming search query by stripping leading `./`, `.\`, `/`, or `\` path prefixes before querying `fzf` or picomatch.
- **Completion Replacement:** In `useCommandCompletion`, accepting a suggestion replaces the range immediately after `@`, cleanly replacing `@/` or `@/src` with `@<completed_path>` without duplicating slashes.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `fileSearch.test.ts`, `useAtCompletion.test.ts`, and `useCommandCompletion.test.tsx` verifying recursive, non-recursive, async initialization, and text buffer replacement behaviors.

## Related Issues

Closes #29453

## How to Validate

1. Run unit test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/filesearch/fileSearch.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useAtCompletion.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useCommandCompletion.test.tsx
   ```
2. Interactive test:
   - Start the CLI: `npm start`
   - In the prompt, type `@/`. Verify the dropdown opens displaying root-level files (`package.json`, `README.md`) and top-level folders (`src/`).
   - Type `@/pack` and press Tab. Verify it autocompletes to `@package.json `.
   - Type `@/src` and press Tab. Verify it autocompletes to `@src/`.

prs.title: fix(ui): handle surrogate pairs when truncating in sanitizeForDisplay
prs.body:
## Summary

`sanitizeForDisplay` truncated strings by UTF-16 code units
(`sanitized.length` and `sanitized.substring()`). When the truncation boundary
fell between the high and low surrogate of an astral character such as an emoji,
the result contained an unpaired surrogate, and the character was dropped when
the text was rendered in the terminal UI.

The function now measures and truncates by code points using the existing
`cpLen` and `cpSlice` helpers, so surrogate pairs are kept intact ahead of the
`...` marker. This applies to every call site that passes a `maxLength`:
suggestion descriptions (`SuggestionsDisplay`), help text (`Help`), file command
descriptions (`FileCommandLoader`), and terminal notification
title/subtitle/body (`terminalNotifications`).

## Details

- **Truncation** (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts`):

  ```ts
  if (maxLength && cpLen(sanitized) > maxLength) {
    sanitized = cpSlice(sanitized, 0, Math.max(0, maxLength - 3)) + '...';
  }
  ```

- **Boundary clamp**: `substring()` treats a negative end index as `0`, whereas
  `cpSlice()` follows `slice()` semantics and counts a negative end back from
  the end of the string. `Math.max(0, maxLength - 3)` keeps the existing `'...'`
  result when `maxLength` is smaller than 3; without it,
  `sanitizeForDisplay('abcdef', 2)` would return `'abcde...'`. No current caller
  passes a value below 3 (they use 48, 64, 100 and 180).
- **Behavior**: `maxLength` now counts code points. Output is unchanged for
  strings without astral characters. For strings that contain them, the UTF-16
  `length` of the result can exceed `maxLength` (e.g. 101 code units / 100 code
  points for the first test case below).
- **Tests** (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts`), three new cases:
  1. `'a'.repeat(96) + '😀' + 'b'.repeat(50)` truncated at 100 returns
     `'a'.repeat(96) + '😀' + '...'` with no unpaired surrogates.
  2. `'😀'.repeat(50)` truncated at 20 returns `'😀'.repeat(17) + '...'`
     (code-point counting).
  3. `maxLength` values below the ellipsis length return `'...'` for both ASCII
     and non-ASCII input (lower-bound clamp; covers both `cpSlice` code paths).

  The unpaired-surrogate assertion uses `/[\uD800-\uDFFF]/u`. The `u` flag is
  required: without it, the character class also matches both halves of a
  correctly paired emoji.

- **Not in this PR**: grapheme clusters made of several code points (ZWJ
  sequences, flags, skin-tone modifiers) can still be cut between code points.
  The output remains well-formed UTF-16, but a partial sequence may be shown;
  grapheme-aware truncation would require `Intl.Segmenter`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29301

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests for the changed module:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all 88 tests pass.

2. All `packages/cli` test suites (7537 tests) pass locally, along with lint and
   typecheck.

3. Full workspace validation runs through the upstream GitHub Actions CI
   workflows.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore approval focus after cancelling editor selection
prs.body:
## Summary

Make Escape close external-editor selection and return to usable pending tool approval. The user can then Allow or Reject the edit without cancelling the request or changing the editor preference.

## Details

Suspend the underlying approval controls while a dialog is visible, and prioritize the editor dialog's Escape handler over stream cancellation. Closing editor selection emits an undefined selection without persisting a preference. The scheduler returns to approval; cancelling the selector never executes the edit.

The integration regression includes a competing stream-style Escape handler and verifies both Allow and Reject, the build-file security warning, unchanged settings, and listener cleanup. No authentication, public settings-schema, model-catalog, or package-version changes.

## Related Issues

User-reported regression; no linked issue.

## How to Validate

Validated final head `67fc04dfc424c1f2bf760886a2cda9d75634992d`, based on upstream `ed96faedfd5571f055c44f2c9509d62321d1138d`.

- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --root packages/cli src/ui/components/ToolConfirmationQueue.editor.test.tsx src/ui/components/ToolConfirmationQueue.test.tsx src/ui/components/messages/ToolConfirmationMessage.test.tsx src/ui/components/EditorSettingsDialog.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useEditorSettings.test.tsx --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1`: 77/77 pass on Linux Node 24.21.0 and native Windows Node 24.14.1. The competing-handler integration fails both cases before the dialog-priority correction and passes afterward.
- A real terminal fixture launches the compiled CLI with an isolated project/home and localhost Code Assist server. It requests a `write_file` edit to `package.json`, opens editor selection, sends one Escape, checks that the file is unchanged and the security warning/approval return, then separately verifies Allow changes the file and Reject leaves it unchanged. Both cases pass with CLI exit 0 on Linux and native Windows source launches, isolated actual packed-npx launches, and the built Linux Docker artifact. Fixture updates and update notifications are explicitly disabled.
- Native Windows runs use an isolated NTFS checkout with native dependencies. Source blobs match this head; core/devtools resolution from the actual CLI entry points to its own workspace builds. Actual npx launches use a verified isolated prefix through `npm exec --offline --no-install --call`, preserving the fixture project directory and preventing global binary shadowing. Native cold launches needed a 120-second fixture allowance; an extra captured-process wrapper was removed after a direct-launch comparison. Native PTY helpers retained handles after recording the CLI exit-0 assertion and were cleaned up separately; helper teardown is not reported as a successful product command.
- Linux `npm run build`, affected `npm run typecheck`, `npm run bundle`, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, and `git diff --check` pass. Native affected CLI build/typecheck and bundle generation pass. Locally packed artifacts are installed into isolated consumers before the npx feature probes.
- Docker Allow/Reject probes pass on the built candidate artifact under Linux Node 20.20.2. Native Windows also launches both Docker probes through WSL; those are Linux containers, not native Windows-container coverage.
- Full `npm run preflight` completed on this exact head in a disposable Linux checkout under Node 20.19.0 with two Vitest workers. Install/format/build/full lint/all typechecks pass and tracked source remains clean. CLI reports 10 failed, 7,401 passed, 4 skipped; core reports 76 failed, 8,296 passed, 57 skipped. All 86 failing records, including duplicate parameterized identities, reproduce on the matching upstream base with the same runtime, dependencies, isolated home, and worker bounds. There are no candidate-only failures. They concern mocked home/workspace paths, keychain mocks, and unavailable `bwrap`. Separately, `npm run test:scripts` passes 202/202 and `npm run test:sea-launch` passes 17/17.

GitHub [Testing: CI for this head](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/actions/runs/39123363790) reports `action_required`. A maintainer must approve the external-contributor workflow run; local results do not imply CI passed. Links and E2E runs have the same approval gate. macOS/Seatbelt are unavailable; Podman fixtures remain pending because host sudo authentication is unavailable.

prs.title: fix(core): recognize dotted Gemini 3 models in supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse
prs.body:
When Gemini CLI runs without dynamic model configuration (`experimental.dynamicModelConfiguration` unset or `false`), `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse()` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`) determined Gemini 3 support via `model.startsWith('gemini-3-')`. Because modern dotted Gemini 3 model names (such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) do not match the prefix `gemini-3-`, `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` returned `false`. As a consequence, binary image data returned from tools like `read_file` was emitted as a separate sibling `inlineData` part adjacent to `functionResponse` instead of being nested within `functionResponse.parts`.

This change updates `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse()` to use the regex `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/` (matching the pattern used by `isGemini3Model`), correctly enabling multimodal function responses for all Gemini 3 model variants. In addition, tests verify that `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` preserves nested `parts` within `functionResponse`.

## Details

- **`supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`)**:
  - Updates the fallback check from `model.startsWith('gemini-3-')` to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/.test(model)` so that dotted Gemini 3 models (e.g. `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash`) are recognized as supporting multimodal function responses.
- **Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/config/models.test.ts`: verifies `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` returns `true` for dotted Gemini 3 models (`gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`).
  - `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts`: verifies that `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` preserves nested `parts` on `functionResponse` objects when normalizing tool call identifiers.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29589

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/models.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
   ```
2. **Full Preflight**:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Place a sample image (e.g. `pic.png`) in the workspace.
   2. Build and run the interactive CLI with a Gemini 3 model (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash` or `gemini-3.5-flash`):
      ```bash
      npm run build
      node packages/cli/dist/index.js -m gemini-3.8-flash
      ```
   3. Instruct the model to inspect the image:
      ```text
      Use read_file on pic.png and tell me what is depicted in the image.
      ```
   4. **Expected**:
      - The tool execution embeds the image in `functionResponse.parts`.
      - The model describes the actual image content accurately rather than hallucinating an image description from an empty placeholder.

prs.title: fix(cli): bound inline history re-render after terminal width changes
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Bounds the work performed by the inline renderer (`ui.useAlternateBuffer: false`, `ui.terminalBuffer: false`) when the terminal width changes, and reduces the repeated output that resize refreshes leave in the terminal scrollback. 

The change is split into two commits so each concern can be reviewed on its own:

1. **`fix(cli): bound inline history re-render after terminal width changes`** (the change requested in #21924). Each debounced static refresh remounted Ink `<Static>` with the entire chat history, so the cost of a width change (React reconciliation, Yoga layout, and the stdout payload) grew linearly with session length. A remount that follows a width change now re-prints the newest history until it exceeds 1,000 characters and covers at least one screen, always including the newest item. Message content is never altered, and the items that are not re-printed are those that had already scrolled into the terminal's native scrollback.
2. **`fix(cli): reduce repeated inline output after terminal resizes`** (additional fixes found while validating the first commit manually). Three sources of repeated output were independent of how much history is re-printed: the viewport erase sequence, refreshes triggered by pauses during a drag, and Ink's full-terminal redraw. Static refreshes now erase the viewport in place, width changes are debounced by 300 ms, and the inline layout stays one row shorter than the terminal while output height is  constrained.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
### Commit 1: bounded resize refresh (issue goal)

- **Resize refresh window (`useStaticHistoryStartIndex.ts`, new)**:
  - `countHistoryItemChars` counts the content characters an item prints (text, tool descriptions, and string, diff, or ANSI tool output), uses a fixed size for non-text content, and stops counting at a limit so large tool output is not scanned in full.
  - `countHistoryItemMinRows` returns a conservative estimate of the rows an item occupies at a given width (wrapped non-empty text lines and one row per tool call, without blank lines, margins, borders, or tool output), so the window errs toward covering more than one screen.
  - `getResizeRefreshHistoryStartIndex` accumulates items from the newest backwards and keeps including older items while they fit in `RESIZE_REFRESH_MAX_HISTORY_CHARS = 1000` or while the window is shorter than the terminal height. The newest item is always included and no item is truncated, including within a long single response.
  - `useStaticHistoryStartIndex` keeps the start index fixed for each `historyRemountKey`, preserving the append-only `items.slice(index)` contract of `<Static>`, and computes it during render so the remounted `<Static>` never prints an intermediate full-history frame. The window is applied only when the remount follows a terminal width change and the history is an append-only continuation of the items already printed; any other remount (theme or Markdown toggles, Ctrl+O, `/clear`, session resume, `/chat` load, rewind) prints the full history as before.
- **Inline static list (`MainContent.tsx`)**:
  - Passes `historyItems.slice(startIndex)` to `<Static>` and includes `AppHeader` only when the full history is printed.
  - Provides the terminal height and main area width used to size the window.
  - Removes the `staticHistoryItems` and `lastResponseHistoryItems` memos, whose concatenation was identical to `historyItems`.
  - The alternate buffer and terminal buffer renderers are unchanged.
- **Design notes**:
  - The 1,000-character figure from the #21924 discussion is used as a budget for how much older history is re-printed, not as a truncation limit, so no message content is dropped.
  - The one-screen minimum guarantees that everything visible before the refresh is drawn again; without it, older items still on screen but outside the character budget would be erased and not re-printed.

### Commit 2: repeated output after resizes (additional fixes)

With the bounded refresh in place, manual runs still showed earlier output repeated in the scrollback. Each of the following causes produced copies regardless of how much history a refresh re-prints, so they are fixed together in a separate commit:

- **Viewport erase (`AppContainer.tsx`)**:
  - Change: `CLEAR_VIEWPORT` moves the cursor home and erases down (`CSI H`, `CSI J`) instead of using `CSI 2 J`.
  - Reason: VTE-based terminals implement `CSI 2 J` by moving the visible screen into scrollback, so every refresh left the previous screen, including the composer and footer, above the re-printed history. `CSI 3 J` is still never emitted, so the scrollback preserved since #29792 is kept.
- **Resize debounce (`AppContainer.tsx`)**:
  - Change: `RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS` is raised from 100 ms to 300 ms.
  - Reason: terminal emulators re-wrap previously printed rows while the window is resized and can push them into scrollback. With 100 ms, every pause in a quick back-and-forth drag triggered a refresh whose output was re-wrapped by     the next movement (seven partial copies of a short history after one drag). A delay that spans those pauses produces a single refresh once resizing settles.
- **Inline layout height (`DefaultAppLayout.tsx`)**:
  - Change: in inline mode, while output height is constrained, an always-rendered wrapper caps the dynamic UI at one row shorter than the terminal, hides overflow, and anchors content to the bottom so the input stays visible.
  - Reason: Ink's legacy renderer appends every `<Static>` print to an internal buffer that is never reset, and when the previous dynamic output was at least as tall as the terminal it switches to a full-terminal redraw that writes `CSI 3 J` and replays that whole buffer, including one copy per `refreshStatic()` remount (eleven copies of the header in one run, with the earlier scrollback erased). Pending output is budgeted against the composer height measured on the previous render, so the dynamic UI could reach the terminal height for a frame.
  - Scope: the cap is not applied while Ctrl+O expands output or in the alternate buffer and terminal buffer renderers. The inner root keeps its natural height for `useFlickerDetector`, and the wrapper is always rendered so toggling the cap never remounts `<Static>`.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

fixes: [#21924](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21924)

## How to Validate

<!-- List exact steps for reviewers to validate the change. Include commands,
expected results, and edge cases. -->

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:

   ```bash
   # Commit 1: bounded resize refresh
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useStaticHistoryStartIndex.test.ts src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx
   # Commit 2: viewport erase, resize debounce, and inline layout height
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx src/ui/layouts/DefaultAppLayout.test.tsx
   ```

   - Verify all tests pass, including:
     - Re-rendering only the newest history (and never the oldest item) when `<Static>` remounts after a terminal width change.
     - Re-rendering only the newest part of a long single response, without the prompt or the start of the response.
     - Re-rendering the full history when `<Static>` remounts without a width change, and printing items appended after a bounded refresh.
     - Erasing the viewport in place without `CSI 2 J` or `CSI 3 J`, and refreshing once 300 ms after the last width change.
     - Keeping the inline layout shorter than the terminal unless output is expanded with Ctrl+O.

<!-- Check all that apply before requesting review or merging. -->

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent duplicate history and double telemetry in confirm_action flow
prs.body:
## Summary

Prevents duplicate user history entries and double-fired `gemini_cli.slash_command` telemetry events when confirming a `confirm_action` (or `confirm_shell_commands`) slash-command flow.

## Details

- **`confirm_action` history re-addition:** Passes `false` for `addToHistory` when recursively calling `handleSlashCommand` on confirmation, aligning `confirm_action` with `confirm_shell_commands`. Previously, confirming an action (such as overwriting an existing `/chat save <tag>` checkpoint) re-added the user slash command to chat history whenever an intermediate message arrived while the confirmation prompt was open.
- **Double-fired slash-command telemetry:** Adds a `shouldLogCompletion` guard in `handleSlashCommand` and sets `shouldLogCompletion = false` right before recursive re-execution in both `confirm_action` and `confirm_shell_commands`. This ensures only the inner re-execution logs the final `SlashCommandStatus` (`SUCCESS` or `ERROR`) instead of firing a second `SUCCESS` event from the outer `finally` block.
- **Unit tests:** Adds unit tests under `Action Result Handling` in `slashCommandProcessor.test.tsx` covering confirmed, cancelled/declined, and error re-execution flows for both `confirm_action` and `confirm_shell_commands`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29032

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/slashCommandProcessor.test.tsx src/ui/commands/chatCommand.test.ts
   ```
2. Manual CLI & telemetry verification:
   ```bash
   rm -f /tmp/gemini-telemetry.log
   GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1 GEMINI_TELEMETRY_TARGET=local GEMINI_TELEMETRY_OUTFILE=/tmp/gemini-telemetry.log npm start
   ```
   - Send a prompt so conversation history is non-empty, run `/chat save testfix`, then run `/chat save testfix` again and confirm `Yes` on the overwrite dialog, then `/quit`.
   - Verify `/tmp/gemini-telemetry.log` records only **1** `"subcommand": "save"` event per `/chat save` invocation (instead of double-firing on confirmation) and the user command is not duplicated in chat history.

prs.title: fix(cli): handle terminals that render ambiguous-width characters as wide
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #24181. On terminals that render **East Asian Ambiguous-width** characters as two cells — macOS Terminal.app with *"Unicode East Asian Ambiguous characters are wide"*, the iTerm2 / GNOME Terminal (VTE) / WezTerm equivalents, GNU screen `cjkwidth on`, CJK-locale `wcwidth` terminals — every Ink border glyph (`─ │ ╭ ╮ ╯ ╰`) occupies 2 cells while the CLI measures it as 1. Every bordered row is wider than the terminal and soft-wraps, and the inline renderer erases the previous frame by its *logical* line count, so a ghost copy of the UI is left in scrollback on **every render** — the "a new line appears for every character I type" in the report (the spinner alone does it too). Affected users cannot get past the first trust/auth dialog.

With this change the CLI measures what the terminal actually does, so layout and terminal agree and the UI redraws in place. Terminals that render these glyphs in one cell (the vast majority) get **no behaviour change**.

## Details

- **Detection** (`terminalCapabilityManager`): the existing one-shot, hidden startup query burst additionally prints `─` at column 1 and asks for the cursor position (`CSI 6n`, VT100 DSR). Column 3 ⇒ ambiguous glyphs are wide; column 2 ⇒ narrow; no reply / timeout / implausible column ⇒ unchanged default. Parsed from the same stdin buffer before the DA1 sentinel; the probe line is cleared like the rest of the burst. Exposed as `areAmbiguousCharactersWide()`.
- **Measurement** (`textUtils`): `setAmbiguousCharactersWide()` flips `string-width`'s `ambiguousIsNarrow` inside `getCachedStringWidth` (cache cleared). Since #29883 Ink measures through `getCachedStringWidth` as well (`setStringWidthFunction` in `interactiveCli`), so this is the single source of truth for layout, text wrapping and the output buffer; the setter re-registers the function with Ink to drop Ink's own per-character width cache. Applied in `setupTerminalAndTheme()` right after detection, next to the background-colour result.
- **Auto-wrap**: new pure helper `shouldDisableLineWrapping(useAlternateBuffer, ambiguousWide)` in core. DECAWM is now also turned off — and restored on exit through the same cleanup path the alternate buffer already uses — when the terminal is ambiguous-wide: Ink's border renderer writes the right `│` in the last column, and a two-cell glyph there would still wrap even with correct measurement. The same check replaces the alternate-buffer-only re-disabling in `useSuspend` (Ctrl-Z / `fg`) and `AppContainer` (after external editors and the manual OAuth flow), which restore auto-wrap for the shell and turn it off again afterwards.
- **Why existing tests never caught it**: the test renderer's xterm.js and `string-width` both default to "ambiguous = narrow", so emulator and layout agree by construction. The new regression test registers an ambiguous-wide Unicode provider in xterm.js and asserts the user-visible contract (one copy of the dialog, every row fits).
- **Not in this PR** (needs `@jrichman/ink`): the fork's `render-border.js` repeats `─` by cell count and Yoga reserves 1-cell borders, so in ambiguous-wide terminals the top/bottom borders lose their right corner to clipping and the left `│` uses one padding cell. Harmless (nothing wraps, nothing ghosts), but a fork follow-up would make it exact.

## Related Issues

Fixes #24181
Related to #15585, #6988 (same symptom class), #29883 (routes Ink's measurements through `getCachedStringWidth`, which this builds on)

## How to Validate

1. `npm run build && npm run bundle`
2. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/ambiguousWidthRendering.test.tsx src/ui/utils/terminalCapabilityManager.test.ts src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts src/utils/terminalTheme.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useSuspend.test.ts src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx src/gemini.test.tsx
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/terminal.test.ts
   ```
3. Real terminal (reporter's setup): Terminal.app ▸ Settings ▸ Profiles ▸ *Advanced* ▸ International ▸ enable **"Unicode East Asian Ambiguous characters are wide"**, open a new window and confirm `printf '%s\n' '──────────' '----------'` prints the first line twice as long as the second. From an **empty** directory run `GEMINI_CLI_HOME=$(mktemp -d) node /path/to/bundle/gemini.js` and press ↓ a few times on the trust dialog.
   - Before: borders look dashed and wrap; a new partial copy of the dialog is pushed into scrollback on every keypress / spinner tick.
   - After: the dialog redraws in place and scrollback stays clean. `--debug` logs `Detected ambiguous-width characters as wide (cursor column 3)`.
   - Linux equivalents: GNOME Terminal ▸ Preferences ▸ Compatibility ▸ *Ambiguous-width characters: Wide*, or `screen` with `cjkwidth on`.
4. Control: with the option off (or any standard terminal) rendering is unchanged; `--debug` logs `... as narrow (cursor column 2)`.
5. Edge cases: Ctrl-Z then `fg` (auto-wrap is given back to the shell while suspended and turned off again on resume); open and close the external editor (Ctrl-X); `ui.useAlternateBuffer: true`; inside tmux (tmux answers the probe with its own width model); non-TTY / `-p` prompt mode (no probe, no change).

## Pre-Merge Checklist

<!-- Check all that apply before requesting review or merging. -->

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not needed, no user-facing settings or docs change
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS

    - [ ] npx

    - [ ] Podman

  - [ ] Windows

prs.title: fix(core): normalize CRLF line endings before diffing in getDiffContextSnippet
prs.body:
When `EditToolInvocation.execute` (`packages/core/src/tools/edit.ts`) edits a file that uses CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings (or when running on Windows), `editData.currentContent` is normalized to LF (`\n`) during `calculateEdit`, whereas `finalContent` is converted back to CRLF (`\r\n`) before calling `getDiffContextSnippet(editData.currentContent ?? '', finalContent, 5)`. Because `getDiffContextSnippet` (`packages/core/src/tools/diff-utils.ts`) passed `originalContent` and `newContent` directly to `Diff.diffLines` without normalizing line endings, every line differed in its newline representation (`\n` vs `\r\n`), causing `getDiffContextSnippet` to return the entire file instead of a compact 5-line contextual snippet around the modified lines.

This change normalizes `\r\n` to `\n` on both `originalContent` and `newContent` before calling `Diff.diffLines` in `getDiffContextSnippet`.

## Details

- **`getDiffContextSnippet` (`packages/core/src/tools/diff-utils.ts`)**:
  - Normalizes `originalContent` and `newContent` by replacing `\r\n` with `\n` prior to calling `Diff.diffLines(normalizedOriginal, normalizedNew)`, ensuring unchanged lines match regardless of LF vs CRLF line endings while still slicing output lines via `newContent.split(/\r?\n/)`.
- **Unit Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/tools/diff-utils.test.ts`: verifies that `getDiffContextSnippet` returns only the changed line and surrounding context when comparing LF against CRLF strings in either direction.
  - `packages/core/src/tools/edit.test.ts`: verifies that `EditToolInvocation.execute` on a 25-line CRLF file returns a compact contextual snippet in `llmContent` rather than the entire file content.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29130

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/diff-utils.test.ts src/tools/edit.test.ts
   ```
2. **Full Preflight**:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Create a multi-line file with CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings in a temporary workspace:
      ```bash
      python3 -c 'open("/tmp/crlf-sample.txt", "wb").write(b"\r\n".join(f"line {i}".encode() for i in range(1, 31)) + b"\r\n")'
      ```
   2. Build and launch the interactive CLI:
      ```bash
      npm run build
      DEBUG=1 node packages/cli/dist/index.js
      ```
   3. In interactive mode, ask Gemini CLI to update a single line in the middle of the file:
      ```text
      Use the edit tool to change "line 15" to "line 15 updated" in /tmp/crlf-sample.txt
      ```
   4. **Expected**:
      - The `replace` / `edit` tool execution succeeds, preserves CRLF line endings on disk (`file /tmp/crlf-sample.txt`), and returns a compact 5-line context snippet (`...\nline 10\n...\nline 15 updated\n...\nline 20\n...`) in the tool response (`llmContent`) rather than echoing all 30 lines of the file.

prs.title: fix(core): allow trusted system paths on Android (Termux) for ripgrep resolution (#21836)
prs.body:
## Summary

Allow trusted system directory prefixes on Android/Termux environments in `isTrustedSystemPath()` so that native ripgrep binaries (e.g. installed via `pkg install ripgrep`) can be resolved and executed by `grep_search`.

## Details

In Termux on Android, ripgrep installed via package managers resides in `$PREFIX/bin` (`/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/rg`). Previously, `isTrustedSystemPath()` only permitted standard FHS paths (`/usr/bin`, `/bin`, etc.) and Windows paths, causing system ripgrep on Termux to be rejected as untrusted and falling back to JavaScript file searching or failing.

This change:
1. Adds trusted prefix checks for Android (`platform === 'android'`), checking `$PREFIX/bin` (when valid), `/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin`, `/system/bin`, `/system/xbin`, `/bin`, and `/usr/bin`.
2. Strictly validates and normalizes `$PREFIX` to ensure it is an absolute POSIX path under Termux's dedicated system package hierarchy (`/data/(data|user/<id>)/com.termux/files/usr`), preventing path traversal, malicious package prefixes, or trusting user-writable directories (such as `files/home`).
3. Preserves the security guardrail that rejects paths inside the current working directory to prevent search path interruption / RCE.
4. Adds comprehensive unit tests in `paths.test.ts` and `ripGrep.test.ts` covering trusted and untrusted paths on Android, including malicious/invalid `PREFIX` variations.

## Related Issues

Fixes https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21836

## How to Validate

Run unit tests for path validation and ripgrep resolution:
```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/paths.test.ts
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts
```
Expected result: All tests pass, including Android/Termux resolution and untrusted path rejections.

prs.title: docs(extensions): add research-mode example extension
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a complete, ready-to-install **example extension** under `docs/examples/research-mode/` that turns Gemini CLI into a Perplexity-style research assistant.

### Commands added by the extension

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/research <topic>` | Deep research brief: TL;DR, cited key findings, causal analysis, perspectives/contradictions, provenance + confidence table, open questions |
| `/research:quick <question>` | Fast cited answer (<300 words) with a confidence label |
| `/research:compare <A> vs <B>` | Evidence-based comparison matrix with a verdict |
| `/research:bharat <topic>` | India-first research: .gov.in/RBI/SEBI sources, INR pricing, Hinglish output |

### Why it is a good docs example

- Demonstrates the full extension layout: `gemini-extension.json` manifest, `GEMINI.md` context file, and namespaced TOML commands (`commands/research.toml` + `commands/research/*.toml`).
- Follows the authoring best practices documented in `docs/extensions/writing-extensions.md`.
- Shows honest-uncertainty patterns: explicit citation numbering, `[offline knowledge - verify]` fallback when `google_web_search` is unavailable, and a per-claim confidence table.
- Includes a causal-analysis (cause -> mechanism -> effect + counterfactual) section, teaching prompt-design for analytical reasoning.

## Checklist

- [x] Documentation-only change (no runtime code touched)
- [x] All files follow the documented extension format
- [x] Extension installs and loads via `~/.gemini/extensions/` and `/commands reload`

Note: I have read the contribution guidelines; CLA signing in progress.

prs.title: fix(core): skip file writes after cancellation
prs.body:
## Summary

Cancelling `replace` or `write_file` during a file read can still overwrite the
target or create a new file. Recheck cancellation after content preparation
and immediately before writing.

## Details

Keep cancellation errors out of the file-write error handler. This does not
undo writes that have already started.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29971

## How to Validate

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --root packages/core src/tools/edit.test.ts src/tools/write-file.test.ts src/utils/pathMutex.test.ts src/scheduler/tool-executor.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1
```

152 tests pass on Windows with Node 20.19.0. The eight new cases use real files
and cancel during reads or directory access, covering existing and missing
targets. All eight fail against unchanged upstream production code.

Build, typecheck, and ESLint pass. On Windows, `npm run preflight` stops at
the YAML lint command's shell quoting. That check passes through Git sh with
`PYTHONUTF8=1`. Formatting and configuration checks pass. ShellCheck reports
two existing SC2292 notes in `tools/caretaker-agent/scripts/deploy.sh`.

Full tests: 16,443 passed, 51 failed, and 98 skipped. The same 51 failed cases
reproduce on upstream `363a13119a57354f469732577518b9d6b319d1d6` with the same
environment: 27 CLI, 23 Core, and one SEA launcher test. CLI also reports five

prs.title: fix: support rootless Podman with keep-id
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes sandbox startup for rootless Podman by correctly preserving the host user’s UID/GID inside the sandbox. Previously, Podman rootless sessions could fail when the sandbox tried to create or drop to a mapped user, because the container did not have a matching user entry in `/etc/passwd` or required a different identity model than Docker.

This change makes the Linux sandbox path compatible with rootless Podman by creating a user matching the host UID/GID when needed, then running Gemini as that user instead of leaving the process running as root. This preserves file ownership and avoids permission problems when the workspace is bind-mounted from the host.

## Details

- Updates the container startup flow to detect when the sandbox is running under rootless Podman.
- Uses a defensive entrypoint that checks for user creation tooling (`useradd` / `groupadd`) before attempting UID/GID mapping.
- Creates a matching container user for the host UID/GID, then launches Gemini CLI under that mapped identity.
- Keeps the existing root-based bootstrap behavior for cases where the container must first create the user before dropping privileges.
- Preserves the existing Docker/Podman behavior for standard sandboxing while avoiding rootless Podman breakage on Linux.

This is especially important for host-to-container file ownership consistency, where files created inside the sandbox should remain owned by the user on the host rather than by root.

## Related Issues

None.

## How to Validate

1. Ensure rootless Podman is installed and working:
   ```bash
   podman info
   ```

2. Start Gemini CLI in rootless Podman mode from the repo:
   ```bash
   GEMINI_SANDBOX=podman npm start
   ```

3. Inside the sandbox, confirm the effective user matches the host:
   ```bash
   id
   pwd
   ls -ld .
   ```

4. Create a temporary file in the repo and confirm it is owned by your host user, not root:
   ```bash
   touch /tmp/podman-check
   ls -l /tmp/podman-check
   ```

5. Repeat with a project file inside the workspace to verify the sandbox can write without permission errors.

Expected result: the sandbox runs successfully under rootless Podman, and file ownership/permission behavior matches the host user instead of root.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

<!-- Check all that apply before requesting review or merging. -->

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)

prs.title: fix(core): keep oversized and boundary lines in read_background_output
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_background_output` reads the last 64KB of a log and always dropped the first line of that window when it didn't start at byte 0. A log that is one line longer than 64KB came back as `Full Log Output:` with nothing after it, a complete first line was lost when the window started right after a newline, and truncated output was still labelled "Full Log Output".

## Details

- read one extra byte before the window to tell whether it starts mid line
- drop the partial first line only when other lines follow; when it's the only line, keep it as a fragment
- skip the continuation bytes of a UTF-8 character cut by the cap, so the fragment doesn't start with U+FFFD
- the header says when earlier output was truncated
- the read stays bounded at 64KB plus one byte, and the session ownership check is unchanged

## Related Issues

Fixes #29944

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
```

New tests cover a 70,000 character single line, a window that starts right after a newline, a partial first line followed by a full one, and an "é" split by the cap. Against main's source all 4 fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

prs.title: fix(cli): use isWithinRoot for theme file home directory check
prs.body:
### Description
Replaces the naive string `startsWith` home directory check in `ThemeManager.loadThemeFromFile` with `isWithinRoot` from `@google/gemini-cli-core`.

This addresses two issues:
1. Prevents sibling directories sharing a prefix (e.g. `/home/user-sibling` when home is `/home/user`) from bypassing the home directory boundary check.
2. Normalizes path comparison on Windows (`process.platform === 'win32'`) so that valid themes inside the user's home directory are not rejected due to drive letter or path casing differences.

Fixes #29955

issues.title: [High severity] 1.0.60 WSL2 regression: CLI MainThread spins at ~215% CPU while idle, TUI output frozen until restart (regression of #2208)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
## Severity / Impact

- **Severity: High** — the TUI becomes effectively unusable; live output (assistant reasoning and streamed text) never paints until the CLI is restarted.
- **Impact: High** — reproduces on every fresh session, immediately after a clean machine reboot, with default usage. Workflow-blocking.
- **Regression of previously-fixed [#2208](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/2208)** ("copilot cli in wsl spinning on the cpu with an unresponsive tui", reported on 1.0.10, closed as completed 2026-04-07). The same class of bug is back in 1.0.60.

### Describe the bug

On **1.0.60** under **WSL2 (Ubuntu-22.04)**, the CLI process spins at ~**215–220% CPU continuously, even while idle** (between turns, with no prompt running). The render/event loop is CPU-starved, so after I submit a prompt the assistant's reasoning and streamed output **do not appear on screen** — the UI looks frozen. The work is actually completing in the background (events are written to `events.jsonl`); **only restarting the CLI makes the result appear**.

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.60` (latest; `dist-tags.latest = 1.0.60`).

### Environment

- WSL2, Ubuntu-22.04, x86_64
- TERM=xterm-256color, not inside tmux/screen (WSL relay PTY)
- 31 GiB RAM (not memory-constrained), load average ~2–4

### CPU / thread profile (the signature)

Measured on a **freshly rebooted** machine, fresh process, **idle** (no active turn):

```
PID 73114  total %CPU = 215–221  (cumulative since start, i.e. continuous spin)
  MainThread   ~98%   (full core)
  V8Worker     ~30%   x4   (GC/JIT helper threads thrashing)
  tokio-rt-worker ~0%
/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/wchan = 0   (RUNNING, not blocked on I/O — confirmed busy-spin)
```

On **1.0.59** (same machine, same session, launched via `--prefer-version 1.0.59`) the identical session is healthy: MainThread idle at ~0%, no V8Worker spinning, cumulative %CPU actually *decreases* over time (proving near-idle). **Downgrading to 1.0.59 fully resolves it.**

### Steps to reproduce

1. On WSL2 (Ubuntu-22.04), run `copilot` on 1.0.60 (interactive TUI).
2. Submit any prompt that streams reasoning/output.
3. Observe: output does not render live; `top` shows the CLI MainThread pegged at ~98% (≈215% total) even when idle between turns.
4. Restart the CLI — the previously "missing" output now appears.

### Expected behavior

Idle CPU near 0%. Streamed reasoning and assistant output render live in the timeline without requiring a restart.

### What was ruled out (so it's clearly a CLI regression, not user config)

All of the following were tested and did **not** fix it on 1.0.60; the spin persisted on a cold-booted machine with a fresh process:

- `/compact` (timeline reduced to ~120 KB)
- Trimming MCP servers (74 → 30 child processes)
- Removing a large custom-agent data folder from `~/.copilot/agents/` (stopped a 1,139-file scan, but unrelated to the spin)
- Lowering reasoning effort `high → medium`
- Lowering `logLevel` `all → info`
- No background subagents/sidekicks active (`GITHUB_CONTEXT_SIDEKICK_AGENT=false`)
- Bundled Node runtime (not the system/nvm Node)

The only change that resolves it is **version 1.0.60 → 1.0.59**, which strongly implicates a render/event-loop regression introduced in 1.0.60.

### Additional context

- Prior fixed issue (same symptom class): #2208.
- The 1.0.60 changelog adds a new max reasoning-effort tier and several render-related changes; a busy-loop in the streaming render/poll path is the most likely area.
- Happy to capture a CPU/devtools trace if useful (as was attached to #2208).

issues.title: macOS: keychain prompts on every launch when GitHub-signed and Microsoft-signed copilot binaries share login-keychain items (XARA partition mismatch)

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, `copilot` stores credentials in legacy login-keychain items (`copilot-cli`, `copilot-mcp-oauth`). macOS XARA protection scopes each item's ACL to a *partition list* containing the Team ID of whoever last wrote it.

The same CLI ships under two different Developer ID Team IDs:

| Path | `Identifier` | Team ID |
|---|---|---|
| `~/Library/Caches/github-copilot-sdk/cli/<ver>/copilot` | `copilot` | `VEKTX9H2N7` (GitHub, Inc.) |
| `/Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot.app` | `com.microsoft.clawpilot.copilot` | `UBF8T346G9` (Microsoft) |

Both read and write the same items, so each one invalidates the other's approval. "Always Allow" never sticks and the user is prompted forever.

From `log show --predicate 'process == "securityd"'`:

```
09:08:23  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:VEKTX9H2N7  ACL ("teamid:UBF8T346G9")
09:08:23  asking user about XARA partition for 'teamid:VEKTX9H2N7'
09:08:23  displaying keychain prompt for .../github-copilot-sdk/cli/1.0.73/copilot
09:08:30  user approved 'always allow' -> adding XARA partition 'teamid:VEKTX9H2N7'
09:08:41  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:UBF8T346G9  ACL ("teamid:VEKTX9H2N7")
09:08:41  displaying keychain prompt for /Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/.../copilot.app
09:47:18  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:UBF8T346G9  ACL ("teamid:VEKTX9H2N7")
10:03:28  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:VEKTX9H2N7  ACL ("teamid:UBF8T346G9")
```

Signature confirmation:

```
$ codesign -dv --verbose=2 ~/Library/Caches/github-copilot-sdk/cli/1.0.73/copilot
Identifier=copilot
Authority=Developer ID Application: GitHub (VEKTX9H2N7)
TeamIdentifier=VEKTX9H2N7

$ codesign -dv --verbose=2 "/Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot.app"
Identifier=com.microsoft.clawpilot.copilot
Authority=Developer ID Application: Microsoft Corporation (UBF8T346G9)
TeamIdentifier=UBF8T346G9
```

**Amplified by an orphaned-item leak.** My login keychain held **765** `copilot-mcp-oauth` items against **8** files in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`, so **757 were orphans**. Creation timestamps show a new batch on every launch:

| Month | Items created |
|---|---|
| Feb-Apr 2026 | 10 |
| May 2026 | 138 |
| Jun 2026 | 364 |
| Jul 2026 (27 days) | 253 |

Three launches on 2026-07-27 produced 10 new items (6 at `15:47:43Z`, 3 at `16:08:35Z`, 1 at `17:03:34Z`), none of which matched a config file -- orphaned on creation. Each orphan is born with a single-Team-ID partition list, so each is a latent prompt.

This overlaps #2112, which diagnoses the stale-entry half on Windows/keytar. The macOS partition-list collision looks separate and unfiled.

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.75` (Scout-embedded) and `1.0.73` (SDK cache).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, use a host that embeds the GitHub-signed CLI (e.g. the Copilot app, via `github-copilot-sdk`).
2. Also use a host that embeds a Microsoft-signed copy (Microsoft Scout).
3. Sign in and configure at least one OAuth-based MCP server.
4. Launch each app in turn. Approve "Always Allow" when prompted.
5. Prompts return on the next launch of the other app, indefinitely.

### Expected behavior

Approving "Always Allow" once should be durable. Concretely:

1. When creating keychain items, set a partition list trusting every Team ID the CLI ships under (`teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9`) rather than letting macOS default to the writing binary's own Team ID.
2. Reuse the existing `copilot-mcp-oauth` item for a given server instead of writing a freshly-hashed one per launch, and delete the entry it supersedes.
3. Consider the data-protection keychain (`kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain` plus a shared access group) instead of the legacy file keychain, which sidesteps XARA partition lists entirely.

### Additional context

- **OS:** macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
- **CPU:** arm64 (Apple silicon)
- **Shell:** zsh

Manual workaround -- trust both Team IDs. This is one-time and resets whenever an item is recreated:

```bash
security set-generic-password-partition-list \
  -S teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9,apple-tool:,apple: \
  -s copilot-cli ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

security set-generic-password-partition-list \
  -S teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9,apple-tool:,apple: \
  -s copilot-mcp-oauth ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
```

Orphans can be identified by diffing keychain account names against `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/*.json` basenames:

```bash
security dump-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db | awk '
  /^keychain:/ { acct="" }
  /"acct"<blob>=/ { l=$0; sub(/^.*"acct"<blob>="/,"",l); sub(/".*$/,"",l); acct=l }
  /"svce"<blob>="copilot-mcp-oauth"/ { print acct }' | sort -u
```

Deleting the 757 orphans is safe and requires no keychain authorization (deletion does not decrypt the item, so it produces no prompt).

issues.title: WSL: clipboard write via clip.exe fails (quoted path in cmd /c), mouse selection copies nothing
issues.body:
**Version:** 1.0.105 (also seen on 1.0.104)
**Environment:** WSL2 (Ubuntu 26.04) + WSLg, GNOME Console (VTE, no OSC 52 support)

**Problem**
Selecting text with the mouse and copying leaves the clipboard empty. `/copy` works.

**Logs**
`writeToClipboard: clip.exe failed; relied on OSC 52: Error: clip.exe exited with code 1`

**Root cause**
On WSL the CLI spawns `cmd.exe /d /c 'chcp 65001 >nul & "<path>\clip.exe"'`. The quotes around the path get escaped when launched from WSL, and cmd reports:
`'\"C:\Windows\System32\clip.exe\"' is not recognized as an internal or external command`
so it exits with code 1. The CLI then falls back to OSC 52, which VTE terminals ignore, so nothing reaches the clipboard.

**Verification**
Running the same command without the quotes around the clip.exe path exits 0 and the text lands on the Windows clipboard.

**Workaround**
Remove the quotes around `${n}` in the `chcp 65001 >nul & "${n}"` template in `cli-main.js`.

**Suggested fix**
Don't quote the path (or escape it correctly for WSL interop), or invoke `clip.exe` directly instead of via `cmd /c`.

issues.title: Images returned from MCP tool results are silently dropped when using a BYOK provider

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug When a session uses a **bring-your-own-key (BYOK) provider**, image content returned from an **MCP tool result** is silently dropped before it reaches the model. The tool executes and its result is returned, but the pixels never arrive. The failure is silent: there is no error, no warning, and no empty response. The model simply answers as if it had seen an image, confabulating a plausible description. This makes the bug easy to ship without noticing — a test that returns a predictable image (a red square, colours in a canonical order) will *appear* to pass. Isolation, from the reproducer below — identical script, server, tool, question and machine, with only the provider changing: | Provider | Image via blob attachment on a user turn | Image via MCP tool result | |---|---|---| | Default Copilot provider | ✅ correct | ✅ correct | | BYOK (`provider={"type": "azure", ...}`) | ✅ correct | ❌ **wrong — confabulated** | The attachment control passes under BYOK, so the deployment is multimodal and reading images fine. Only the tool-result path is affected. Both `wire_api` values (`responses` and `completions`) fail identically. The Python SDK side looks correct: proxying the same MCP call through a custom tool and converting it with `convert_mcp_call_tool_result` produces a well-formed `binary_results_for_llm[0]` with `type="image"`, `mime_type="image/png"` and intact base64 — and the model still doesn't see it. So the content appears to be lost below the Python SDK, in the request assembly for BYOK providers. ### Affected version ``` GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-9. ``` `github-copilot-sdk` 1.0.9, `fastmcp` 3.4.2, `mcp` 1.28.1. ### Steps to reproduce the behavior The script below is self-contained. It starts a small MCP server exposing one tool that returns a PNG, then asks the model a question that can only be answered by looking at the pixels. The image is four solid-colour quadrants in a **random** arrangement drawn from a six-colour palette — 360 possibilities. This matters: a model that never receives the image cannot guess correctly, so confabulation is distinguishable from success. (In every failing run here, the answer came back as the canonical `red green blue yellow`.) 1. `pip install github-copilot-sdk fastmcp uvicorn` 2. Run `python repro_mcp_image.py` with no extra environment — **both variants pass.** 3. Set a BYOK provider and run again — the control still passes, the MCP variant **fails**: ```bash export REPRO_AZURE_BASE_URL=https://.openai.azure.com/openai/v1 export REPRO_AZURE_MODEL= export REPRO_AZURE_TOKEN= export REPRO_WIRE_API=responses # also fails with: completions python repro_mcp_image.py ``` Observed output under BYOK: ``` Random arrangement (1 of 360): yellow orange blue green PNG: 3,301 bytes control -- PNG as a blob attachment on the user turn -> 'yellow orange blue green' CORRECT mcp -- PNG returned from an MCP tool result -> 'red green blue yellow' tool_called=True WRONG ```
repro_mcp_image.py ```python """Minimal reproducer: images returned from an MCP tool result never reach the model.""" from __future__ import annotations import asyncio import base64 import os import random import struct import sys import zlib import copilot import uvicorn from copilot.generated import rpc from fastmcp import FastMCP from fastmcp.utilities.types import Image PORT = int(os.environ.get("REPRO_PORT", "8899")) PALETTE = { "red": (220, 30, 30), "green": (30, 180, 60), "blue": (40, 70, 220), "yellow": (240, 220, 40), "purple": (140, 40, 180), "orange": (245, 140, 20), } def make_quadrant_png(colors: list[tuple[int, int, int]], size: int = 512) -> bytes: """A PNG split into four solid quadrants: TL, TR, BL, BR. No image library needed.""" def chunk(tag: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes: return ( struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF) ) half = size // 2 raw = bytearray() for y in range(size): raw.append(0) top = y < half for x in range(size): left = x < half idx = 0 if (top and left) else 1 if top else 2 if left else 3 raw += bytes(colors[idx]) return ( b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", size, size, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(bytes(raw), 6)) + chunk(b"IEND", b"") ) IMAGE: bytes = b"" TOOL_CALLED = False mcp = FastMCP("repro") @mcp.tool async def get_test_image() -> Image: """Return a test image for visual analysis.""" global TOOL_CALLED TOOL_CALLED = True return Image(data=IMAGE, format="png") app = mcp.http_app(transport="streamable-http", path="/mcp/") SYSTEM = ( "You are a visual analysis assistant. When asked about an image, you MUST " "look at the actual image. Never guess. Answer exactly as instructed." ) INSTRUCTION = ( "The image is divided into four solid-colour quadrants. Report the colour of " "each quadrant, choosing from: red, green, blue, yellow, purple, orange.\n\n" "Reply with EXACTLY four lowercase words separated by single spaces, in this " "order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. No punctuation, no " "explanation, no other text." ) MCP_QUESTION = "Call the get_test_image tool, then look at the image it returns. " + INSTRUCTION def session_kwargs() -> dict: """Default Copilot provider, or BYOK if REPRO_AZURE_* are set.""" base_url = os.environ.get("REPRO_AZURE_BASE_URL") if not base_url: return {} model = os.environ["REPRO_AZURE_MODEL"] token = os.environ["REPRO_AZURE_TOKEN"] return { "model": model, "provider": { "type": "azure", "wire_api": os.environ.get("REPRO_WIRE_API", "responses"), "base_url": base_url, "bearer_token_provider": lambda _a: token, "model_id": model, }, } async def ask(*, mcp_servers=None, attachments=None, question: str) -> str: client = copilot.CopilotClient(log_level="error") await client.start() try: extra = {} if mcp_servers: extra["mcp_servers"] = mcp_servers extra["available_tools"] = copilot.ToolSet().add_mcp("*") session = await client.create_session( system_message={"mode": "replace", "content": SYSTEM}, on_permission_request=lambda *_a: rpc.PermissionDecisionApproveOnce(), streaming=False, **session_kwargs(), **extra, ) if mcp_servers: await asyncio.sleep(2.0) # allow MCP negotiation to finish send = session.send_and_wait(question, attachments=attachments) if attachments \ else session.send_and_wait(question) response = await asyncio.wait_for(send, timeout=180) finally: await client.stop() data = getattr(response, "data", None) return (getattr(data, "content", "") or "").strip().lower() async def main() -> None: global IMAGE names = random.sample(list(PALETTE), 4) IMAGE = make_quadrant_png([PALETTE[n] for n in names]) print(f"\nRandom arrangement (1 of 360): {' '.join(names)}") print(f"PNG: {len(IMAGE):,} bytes\n") server = uvicorn.Server( uvicorn.Config(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=PORT, log_level="warning") ) server_task = asyncio.create_task(server.serve()) for _ in range(100): if getattr(server, "started", False): break await asyncio.sleep(0.1) results = {} try: print("control -- PNG as a blob attachment on the user turn") answer = await ask( question=INSTRUCTION, attachments=[ { "type": "blob", "data": base64.b64encode(IMAGE).decode("ascii"), "mimeType": "image/png", "displayName": "test.png", } ], ) ok = answer.split()[:4] == names results["control (attachment)"] = (ok, answer) print(f" -> {answer[:60]!r} {'CORRECT' if ok else 'WRONG'}\n") print("mcp -- PNG returned from an MCP tool result") answer = await ask( question=MCP_QUESTION, mcp_servers={ "repro": { "type": "http", "url": f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/mcp/", "tools": ["*"], } }, ) ok = answer.split()[:4] == names results["mcp (tool result)"] = (ok, answer) print(f" -> {answer[:60]!r} tool_called={TOOL_CALLED} " f"{'CORRECT' if ok else 'WRONG'}\n") finally: server.should_exit = True await asyncio.sleep(0.3) server_task.cancel() print(f"expected: {' '.join(names)}") for name, (ok, answer) in results.items(): print(f" {name}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} -- {answer[:60]!r}") sys.exit(0 if all(ok for ok, _ in results.values()) else 1) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ```
### Expected behavior An image returned from an MCP tool result should reach the model under a BYOK provider, exactly as it does under the default provider — or, if that is not supported, the CLI should surface a clear error or warning rather than silently discarding the content and letting the model answer from priors. ### Additional context - OS: Linux x86_64 (WSL2), bash. - Both `wire_api: "responses"` and `wire_api: "completions"` reproduce. - Reproduces both with native `mcp_servers=` configuration and with a custom tool that proxies the MCP call and converts it via `convert_mcp_call_tool_result` — which suggests the loss is in BYOK request assembly rather than in MCP handling. - The silent-confabulation failure mode is the most costly part of this: without a randomised image, the bug looks like success.

issues.title: GPT-6.1 Sol Locks up plan implementation
allowedMcpServers entries using serverName never match

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`allowedMcpServers` entries using `serverName` never match — named servers are blocked as "not permitted by enterprise managed allow list"

`serverName` matchers in a server-managed `allowedMcpServers` policy don't match anything. A server whose label exactly matches a `serverName` entry is blocked the same way as a server that isn't on the list. In the same session, `serverUrl` and `serverCommand` entries in the same policy work as expected.

The docs say `serverName` "matches the user-assigned server label exactly" and applies to "any server":
https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings#allowedmcpservers

The docs don't describe any condition that disables `serverName` matching. For example, they don't say it applies only when the list has no `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` entries. If that is the intended behavior, it isn't documented.

This is Copilot CLI 1.0.89, GitHub Copilot app 1.1.23, Windows 11 (build 26200). 

This is a server-managed team policy file (`.github-private`), applied through `overridable` at the enterprise level. Here is a shortened version. The client cache shows the full list was received (`keys=[allowedMcpServers,...]`, all entries present):

```json
{
  "allowedMcpServers": [
    {"serverUrl": "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp"},
    {"serverName": "workiq"},
    {"serverName": "azure-devops"},
    {"serverName": "miro-mcp"},
    {"serverUrl": "https://mcp.miro.com"},
    {"serverCommand": ["npx", "-y", "next-devtools-mcp@latest"]}
  ]
}
```

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.89.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Apply a server-managed policy like the one above.
2. Add these servers with `--additional-mcp-config`. Use a minimal stdio MCP server for `node mini.js`.
   ```json
   {"mcpServers":{
     "workiq":           {"type":"local","command":"node","args":["mini.js"]},
     "zz-not-listed":    {"type":"local","command":"node","args":["mini.js"]},
     "appian-dev-tools": {"type":"http","url":"https://mcp-probe.invalid/mcp"}
   }}
   ```
3. Run:
   `copilot -p "Reply OK" --additional-mcp-config @extra.json --log-level all --log-dir ./logs`


### Expected behavior

`workiq` and `appian-dev-tools` **should start**, because they match `serverName` entries. `zz-not-listed` should be blocked.

*Instead*, all three are blocked with identical messages. The remote probe URL is never contacted.

```
[DEBUG] Skipping MCP server "zz-not-listed": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
[DEBUG] Skipping MCP server "appian-dev-tools": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
[DEBUG] Skipping MCP server "workiq": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
```

In the same run, servers that match a `serverUrl` entry (for example Microsoft Learn and Miro) or a `serverCommand` entry (for example `next-devtools-mcp`) connect normally.

Before we added `serverUrl`/`serverCommand` entries, 8 of our 10 configured servers were blocked even though every one of them had an exact `serverName` entry. Only the 2 servers with `serverUrl` entries loaded. Adding `serverUrl`/`serverCommand` duplicates is our workaround.


### Additional context

- **The block isn't visible to users.** The skip is logged only at DEBUG. In the Copilot app's MCP settings, the blocked servers show a spinner that stops after about 20 seconds with no status icon, error, or policy message. Users see a blank row. Other servers in the same list show a green check or an error badge, as expected.
- **Related, but a different cause:** #4419 and #4957 cover servers dropped by an interim or early fail-closed policy. In our case the policy resolves normally (`source=server`, `serverFetchFailed=false`) and the named servers are still blocked on every run.
- I can share full DEBUG logs on request.
