issues.title: perf(v2): every LLM call re-reads and re-decodes the full session history (O(n) per step, O(n^2) per session)
issues.body:
### Description

Every LLM call re-reads, re-decodes, and re-converts the **entire** persisted history from SQLite:

1. Full-table SELECT (`session_id = X AND seq >= boundary`, no upper bound) — `SessionHistory.messageEntries`
2. Per-row `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(SessionMessage.Info)` — `decodeMessageRow`
3. Full `toLLMMessages` conversion of every message
4. `JSON.stringify` of the whole message array for the request

All four stages are O(history length) on every call, and the step loop issues at least one such load per step (more with retries/steering). Per-step cost grows linearly with history; cumulative CPU per session is quadratic. Stages 1+2 also allocate roughly 2x the history size in transient objects per call, which sets the floor for the JavaScriptCore heap high-water mark under Bun.

This problem class was reported against the v1 architecture and those issues were closed with the v2 rewrite (#18136, #20285, #29730 — see "Related issues"). The v2 subsystem is a new implementation (Effect + drizzle + Bun/JSC) and the pattern is present there as well; this issue reports it on current v2 code with per-row measurements and a measured reference fix (#51499).

### Plugins

None (benchmark scenario, no plugins loaded).

### OpenCode version

v2.0.10 (self-compiled from the `v2.0.10` tag; `bun build --compile --single --skip-web-ui`). Measurements taken on v2.0.10; code paths and the reference fix re-verified against the current `v2` branch tip.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let a session accumulate multi-MB history (the 2-5 MB pre-compaction window is the realistic range; 100+ steps with sizeable tool results gets there).
2. Run the tiered microbenchmark from the reference PR (`packages/core/bench-history.ts`) against a copy of the session DB — it times SELECT, Schema decode, conversion, and stringify separately through the real `Database.layer` stack.
3. For heap behavior: send SIGUSR1 to `opencode serve` at the same point in matched baseline/patched runs and diff the heap snapshots.

Measured per-row cost (v2.0.10, 103-row / 348 KB real session DB):

| Stage | Per row |
|---|---|
| drizzle SELECT + row parse | 10.0 µs |
| Effect Schema decode | 16.0 µs |
| `toLLMMessages` conversion | 8.3 µs |
| `JSON.stringify` | 4.4 µs |

SQL read + Schema decode (what a history cache eliminates) is ~70% of opencode's own chain, before the provider SDK's own conversion/serialization. Chain cost per LLM call by history size: ~4.4 ms at 400 KB, ~23 ms at 2 MB, ~56 ms at 5 MB.

End-to-end (mock provider, 100 scripted steps, self-compiled baseline vs patched with identical build flags, per-run sandbox wipe, request-sequence equality gates; harness: [konghayao/harness-perf-benchmark](https://github.com/konghayao/harness-perf-benchmark)):

| Scenario | Serve CPU | Tree RSS mean | Tree RSS peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 KB history | 6.3 ± 0.5 core·s | 409 ± 8 MB | 683 ± 53 MB |
| 4 MB history | 27.7 ± 1.5 core·s | 775 ± 62 MB | 1105 ± 65 MB |

Paired SIGUSR1 heap snapshots at the same point in matched runs differ by only ~4 MB of live heap — the high-water differences are garbage-accumulation timing (JSC's GC is allocation-triggered), not retained data.

A reference implementation — incremental per-session cache keyed by `(sessionID, compaction boundary)`, seq watermark, invalidation on non-append writes (projector UPDATE/DELETE incl. revert, transfer import), plus an opt-in `OPENCODE_GC_ON_STEP=N` knob — is in draft PR #51499 with full dose/response data: CPU -2.7% to -8.5% on the 4 MB scenario across two batches, RSS flat to +2% (the tradeoff is explained and evidenced in the PR), and deterministic memory behavior when the knob is enabled.

### Screenshot and/or share link

N/A (data tables above; scripts and raw data described in #51499).

### Operating System

Linux 5.15.0-94-generic x86_64.

### Terminal

N/A (headless `opencode serve` under the benchmark harness).

### Benchmark environment

CPU: AMD EPYC 9K65, 16 vCPUs. RAM: 30 GB. Runtime: Bun 1.4.2 (JavaScriptCore + mimalloc). All numbers are pairwise interleaved A/B runs on the same machine with the sandbox wiped between runs.

### Related issues (checked — not duplicates)

- #18136 (closed): same problem class in the v1 architecture (`prompt.ts` / `filterCompacted` / V8 paths).
- #20285 (closed): v1 session-loop performance proposal including an incremental message cache — direction aligned, but it targeted the v1 codebase that the v2 rewrite replaced.
- #29730 (closed): v1 OOM report with a 4-copy analysis of the v1 pipeline (`session.ts` / `message-v2.ts` / UIMessage).

All three predate the v2 architecture and are closed. This issue is the v2 continuation with per-row measurements on current code; the reference implementation is #51499.

issues.title: Mini follow-up stays stuck after a prompt fails before admission
issues.body:
### Description

Mini can display a prompt request error and then leave a queued follow-up stuck. Closing the footer also fails to finish the interactive runtime in this state.

This occurs when a follow-up is submitted while the first prompt request is in flight, and the first request fails before its admission callback runs. The runtime displays the error and returns, but the queue waits for follow-up admissions that are themselves waiting for the first prompt's admission promise. That promise is only resolved in the later cleanup block.

I reproduced this locally through `runInteractiveDeferredMode` with the existing footer fixture and a deferred transport failure. Settling the active admission before waiting for dependent admissions releases the follow-up and lets close finish.

### Plugins

None.

### OpenCode version

2.1.4, V2 local source reproduction.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start an ordinary prompt in Mini and keep its initial request pending.
2. Submit a follow-up before the initial prompt is admitted.
3. Let the initial request fail before invoking its admission callback.

Expected: after displaying the error, Mini admits the follow-up or reports its failure, and closing the footer completes.
Actual: the error is displayed, but the follow-up admission is never called and runtime completion remains pending after close.

The deterministic local test drives this sequence through the real interactive runtime with deferred promises; it does not call a provider or live server.

### Screenshot

Not applicable; runtime liveness regression tested with the footer fixture.

### Operating System

Linux.

### Terminal

Local Bun runtime test harness.

issues.title: tui: session tab list renders opaque separator/underline colors on transparent themes
issues.body:
## Summary

On a theme with `"transparent"` backgrounds, the TUI session tab list paints its separator lines, tab underlines, and several dimmed label colors as **fully opaque** blocks, so the tab strip does not match the rest of the interface. The root cause is that the shared color-mix helper discards the alpha channel, so any mix involving a transparent theme color returns an opaque color.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18
- OS: Linux cachyos 7.2.8-1-cachyos (linux x64)
- Terminal: `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: release (`opencode` 2.0.18)
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Create a custom theme in `~/.config/opencode/themes/` that sets the background tokens to `"transparent"` (see config below).
2. Set `theme.name` to that theme and `theme.mode` to `dark` in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`.
3. Run `opencode` and open two or more sessions so the tab strip is visible (`tabs.mode` is `auto` by default).
4. Compare the tab strip against the rest of the UI.

## Expected Behavior

Every color in the tab strip should be derived from the theme with its alpha channel preserved, so a transparent theme produces a fully see-through tab strip, consistent with the rest of the interface.

## Actual Behavior

The tab strip renders opaque separator/underline bars and fully-opaque dimmed labels, while the surrounding UI remains transparent.

## Additional Context

### Root cause

The color-mix helper used throughout the TUI drops alpha:

```ts
function cH(e, a, r) {
  const d = e.r + (a.r - e.r) * r
  const n = e.g + (a.g - e.g) * r
  const g = e.b + (a.b - e.b) * r
  return He.fromInts(Math.round(d * 255), Math.round(n * 255), Math.round(g * 255))
}
```

`He.fromInts(r, g, b, a = 255)` defaults alpha to `255`, and `cH` never passes a fourth argument, so **every** mixed color is fully opaque regardless of its inputs. This is invisible with ordinary themes, where all inputs are already opaque, but it breaks any theme that uses `"transparent"`.

### Affected call sites in the session tab component

`packages/tui/src/component/session-tabs.tsx` derives most of its colors through `cH`:

```ts
const h = () => theme.background.raised.base
const m = () => theme.background.action.primary.$selected
const y = () => theme.background.raised.high

const N = () => cH(theme.text.formfield.base, h(), 0.55)
const R = memo(() => cH(h(), theme.text.base, 0.04))
const U = memo(() => cH(h(), theme.text.base, 0.05))
const Oe = memo(() => cH(h(), y(), y().a))
const t = memo(() => cH(h(), wr(), wr().a))
```

Consequences with a transparent theme:

- `Oe` and `t` are the **colors and backgrounds of the separator lines** drawn above and below the tab list. `cH(h(), y(), y().a)` is called with a mix weight of `y().a`, which is `0` for a transparent `raised.high`, so the call is *intended* to return `h()` including `h`'s alpha — but `cH` forces alpha to `255` and returns an opaque fill instead.
- `U` and `R` are the **top border and outer border** colors of each tab in horizontal layout. These are meant to be a 4–5% tint of the text color over the background; with a transparent background they come out as solid bars.
- `flashColor` / `outerFlashColor` / `glowColor` / `completionColor` on the pulse and underline widgets use the same pattern (`cH(h(), theme.text.base, 0.22)`, `cH(h(), theme.text.base, 0.006)`, etc.), so the busy/attention animation paints opaque bars over a transparent background.
- `N`, `Sa`, `go`, `Wr`, `vt`, `bs`, `ds` are dimmed label colors computed as mixes against `$t`. Because the mix ignores alpha, the dimming is computed as though the background were opaque, so dimmed labels also render at full opacity.

Note that the tab **row** backgrounds themselves (`wr()` returning `h()`, `y()`, or `m()`) read theme tokens directly and do respect transparency — which is why the tab rows look correct while the separators and underlines around them do not.

### Suggested fix

Interpolate alpha in the mix helper rather than discarding it:

```ts
function cH(e, a, r) {
  const d = e.r + (a.r - e.r) * r
  const n = e.g + (a.g - e.g) * r
  const g = e.b + (a.b - e.b) * r
  const alpha = e.a + (a.a - e.a) * r
  return He.fromInts(
    Math.round(d * 255),
    Math.round(n * 255),
    Math.round(g * 255),
    Math.round(alpha * 255),
  )
}
```

This is a no-op for fully opaque themes, so it should be low risk, but it will change the appearance of every component that mixes colors, so it may be worth checking the diff view and dialogs as well.

### Related

- #28350 — `fix(tui): code block left border background still opaque when theme background is transparent` (closed): same pattern in a different component.
- #30056 — `Badge text invisible when theme background is transparent or none` (open).
- #51134 — `tui: collapsed reasoning title ignores thinkingOpacity (hardcoded 0.6 alpha)` (open).
- #42704 — `refactor(tui): finish theme compatibility cleanup` (open).

### Secondary observation: V1-format themes are regenerated, not honored

The theme in this report uses the legacy V1 `defs` + flat `theme` format. When the TUI detects that shape it does not use the authored values; it regenerates an entire token tree from hue scales derived from the accent colors. `backgroundPanel` and `backgroundElement` are never referenced directly — the equivalents become `$hue.neutral.700` / `$hue.neutral.600`, and `background.base` / `background.raised.*` are rebuilt rather than taken from the file. So the transparency of the raised surfaces the tab list reads is incidental rather than controlled. Authoring the theme in the v2 `base` / `dark` format makes those tokens explicit, but it does not fix the alpha bug above.

### Config used

`~/.config/opencode/cli.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json",
  "theme": { "name": "transparent", "mode": "dark" }
}
```

Relevant part of `~/.config/opencode/themes/transparent.json` (V1 format, Catppuccin Mocha text colors):

```json
{
  "defs": {
    "text": "#cdd6f4",
    "textMuted": "#9399b2",
    "surface": "#585b70",
    "surfaceHigh": "#45475a",
    "surfaceMax": "#313244"
  },
  "theme": {
    "background": "transparent",
    "backgroundPanel": "transparent",
    "backgroundElement": "transparent",
    "backgroundMenu": "transparent",
    "borderSubtle": "surface"
  }
}
```

Frequency: 100% reproducible on 2.0.18. No workaround found from theme configuration alone.

issues.title: Windows: every spawned console process flashes a black window (git.exe ~1/sec on v2.0.20) — re-report of #22414, #31629
issues.body:
### Description

On Windows, every console-subsystem process opencode spawns allocates a visible console window, because the spawn does not pass `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. The windows open and close instantly — roughly 1 per second.

`git.exe` is the most visible case. From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`:

```
message="spawning process" command="C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.EXE"
  args="[\"--git-dir\",\"C:\Users\herna\.config\opencode\.git\",\"--work-tree\",...]"
```

Rate: 417 `git.exe` spawns in the last 20 000 log lines, 60-68 per minute, in bursts of ~6 within 350 ms. They come from the project repo and from the snapshot repo (`~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<id>/.git`).

Same for any local MCP whose `command` is a console binary (`node.exe`, `python.exe`): one window per MCP start.

Mechanism: a console-subsystem child of a GUI-subsystem parent calls `AllocConsole()`. Only the spawner can suppress it, via `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` or `DETACHED_PROCESS`.

Previously reported and closed administratively rather than fixed: #22414 and #31629 (60-day inactivity), #38715 (auto-closed), #42440 (`COMPLETED`, but last comment is "I will screen record it later today if you still cant replicate it"). Still reproduces on v2.0.20.

### Plugins

```
@herjarsa/omo-meta-governor@latest
opencode-omniroute-plugin@latest
superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
```

### OpenCode version

```
v2.0.20
```

### Steps to reproduce

```
1. Windows 11, open the desktop app with a few projects open.
2. Work normally (or open a session in an active project).
3. Watch for black console windows opening and closing ~1 per second.
```

Confirmed by log count rather than by eye: count `spawning process` lines mentioning `git.EXE` in `opencode.log`.

### Screenshot and/or share link

No screenshot: the windows close in under a second, so a capture is not practical. Log excerpt above is the reproducible evidence.

### Operating System

```
Microsoft Windows 11 Pro Insider Preview  build 28120.10.0.28120
```

### Terminal

```
Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0  (also affects the desktop app, which spawns without a terminal host)
```

### Notes

Workarounds tried, all of which failed:

- Delegated console host via `HKCU\Console\%%Startup` — **made it worse**, any console app started an endless window loop.
- Windows Terminal `windowingBehavior: "useExisting"` — no effect.
- A GUI-subsystem launcher wrapping each MCP with `CreateNoWindow` + stdio relay — works with file-redirected stdio, but under opencode live pipes every MCP fails with `mcp connect failed ... "Request timed out"`.
- Removing `cmd.exe`/`npx` shims from MCP definitions — fewer processes, but `node.exe` is still a console app, so the window remains.

`"snapshots": false` reduces the churn (it removes the snapshot-repo git calls) but costs file undo/revert, and does not affect project-repo git calls.

issues.title: Prompt POSTed to session HTTP endpoint during config-reload window is persisted but excluded from assembled context; assistant re-emits previous reply byte-identically
issues.body:
### Description

Headless deployment (`opencode serve`, prompts delivered by HTTP POST to the session prompt endpoint from a local automation relay). A prompt POSTed while a configuration-reload wave was in progress was persisted to session storage (sequence number and timestamp assigned) but was not included in the context assembled for the model call. The assistant "reply" to it was a byte-identical duplicate of the reply given to the previous turn 40 minutes earlier. The caller received HTTP success with the wrong answer; nothing in the response or the log marked it as stale.

**Timeline (UTC; server log + session database)**

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 23:12:26 | Last normal turn completes (assistant reply A, seq 2241) |
| 23:12:49 | Session idle |
| 23:51:59–23:53:23 | Config-reload wave: burst of `configuration normalization diagnostic` WARN entries (80 log lines in this window) |
| 23:52:03.509 | Relay POSTs a new prompt to the session endpoint (logged) |
| 23:52:03.5xx | User message persisted (seq 2252); assistant message created same second (seq 2254) |
| — | seq 2254 text part: length 888, SHA-256 `99d2738f39eb9edb6042936b…` — identical to reply A |

**Evidence**

- Session database (`session_message`): user row seq 2252 and assistant row seq 2254, both at 23:52:03. No other turn between 23:12:49 and 23:52:03 — the session was idle, so a concurrent running turn cannot explain a reused response.
- SHA-256 of the seq 2254 text part equals the SHA-256 of the seq 2241 text part (the 23:12:26 reply): byte-identical duplicate, not a paraphrase.
- The POST timestamp falls inside the config-diagnostic burst. POSTs to the same endpoint outside reload windows, before and after, produced correct replies.
- Interpretation (the only one consistent with the above): the persisted prompt was not part of the context assembled for that model call, so the model re-answered the previous turn.

**Expected:** the POSTed prompt is included in the context assembled for the next model call, and the assistant answers the new prompt.

**Actual:** the prompt is persisted but skipped during context assembly. The assistant regenerates the previous reply byte-for-byte. The caller sees success carrying the wrong answer — a silent failure for headless/automated deployments; no error is surfaced anywhere, so callers must detect it themselves (e.g. by hashing consecutive replies).

### Plugins

None configured (no plugin entries in user config, no local plugin files) — the reload wave was pure config-file normalization.

### OpenCode version

v2.0.16 (npm `@opencode/cli`; upstream git tag `v2.0.16`, object sha `3a103fe0`)

### Steps to reproduce

Not yet reduced to a minimal script. Observed sequence:

1. `opencode serve` with a session that has at least one completed turn; let it go idle.
2. Trigger a config reload (rewrite the user config file).
3. Inside the reload window, POST a new prompt to the session prompt endpoint.
4. Observe: the user message is persisted with a sequence number; the assistant reply is identical to the previous turn's reply.

### Screenshot and/or share link

None — headless server deployment; the evidence above is taken from the server log and the session database.

### Operating System

Linux 7.2.5-3 x86_64 (Arch-based)

### Terminal

Not applicable — headless `opencode serve` bound to loopback; client is curl over loopback (shell: bash)

issues.title: provider: OpenCode Go Anthropic route masks upstream errors as "Provider request failed with HTTP 400"
issues.body:
## Summary

With OpenCode Go, models served over the Anthropic Messages route (for example `opencode-go/qwen3.8-flash`) surface every upstream rejection as the opaque message `Provider request failed with HTTP 400`. The route returns an empty error payload, so the real upstream reason (for example a content-filter rejection) is lost and the user cannot tell what failed.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18
- OS: Darwin 27.0.0 (darwin arm64)
- Terminal: Kaku (`TERM_PROGRAM=Kaku`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: Homebrew (`opencode-v2` 2.0.18), channel latest
- Active plugins: local `rtk` plugin (shell command rewrite only; unrelated to provider requests)

## Reproduction

1. Connect OpenCode Go and select a model whose catalog entry uses the Anthropic runtime, e.g. `opencode-go/qwen3.8-flash` (`package: "@opencode/ai/providers/anthropic"`, `settings.baseURL: "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1"`).
2. Build a session whose context the upstream rejects. In my case a long assistant text (a NetBird/DNS investigation, ~11.5k chars) trips Alibaba's Qwen content filter.
3. Send any next prompt in that session (or call `POST /api/session/:sessionID/generate`).
4. The step fails with `Provider request failed with HTTP 400` and no further detail.

Network-level, the request is `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` and the response is HTTP 400 with body:

```
event: error
data: {}
```

An SSE error event whose payload is an empty object. With `stream: false` the same request returns:

```json
{"model":"qwen3.8-flash"}
```

Neither body carries `error.message` or `code`.

## Expected Behavior

The upstream rejection should be surfaced with its real message so the user can act on it. In this case the underlying reason is knowable: the same content sent over the OpenAI-compatible runtime (`POST /chat/completions`) returns

```json
{"error":{"param":null,"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: [data_inspection_failed] <400> InternalError.Algo.DataInspectionFailed: Input text data may contain inappropriate content."}}
```

## Actual Behavior

opencode can only report `Provider request failed with HTTP 400`. In opencode 2.0.18 the error mapping for provider HTTP errors falls back to `Provider request failed with HTTP <status>` whenever the response body has no `message`/`code` (see `XC()` near `Provider request failed with HTTP ${e.statusCode}` in the server bundle). Because the Anthropic route returns `data: {}`, there is nothing to surface.

## Additional Context

- The failure is deterministic for a given context, so retrying the same prompt keeps failing with the same opaque 400.
- Workaround that restores the real message: override the model's runtime so requests use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which preserves the upstream error body:

```jsonc
{
  "providers": {
    "opencode-go": {
      "models": {
        "qwen3.8-flash": {
          "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After this override the same step reports `Upstream request failed: [data_inspection_failed] <400> InternalError.Algo.DataInspectionFailed: Input text data may contain inappropriate content.`

- Two possible fixes on the OpenCode side:
  1. When the Anthropic route receives an error event with an empty payload, fall back to the raw HTTP response body/status text so the message is not silently dropped.
  2. Have the Go gateway include the upstream `error.message` in the Anthropic error event instead of `{}`.

issues.title: npm 12 upgrade leaves the Windows executable stub
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode upgrade` can report success with npm 12 while leaving the published text stub in `bin/opencode.exe`. The next invocation fails on Windows because the file is not a valid executable.

The updater runs `npm install --global --force` without allowing the target package's lifecycle scripts. npm 12 can block postinstall and still exit 0, even with `ignore-scripts=false`. Adding `--allow-scripts=@opencode/cli` lets postinstall replace the stub.

I reproduced that policy behavior with a synthetic package in an isolated Windows install prefix using npm 12.0.2 and Node 24.21.0. The flag also preserved explicit `ignore-scripts=true`. This report covers the updater command; #48884 covers the broader packaging behavior when scripts are disabled.

### OpenCode version

Reported on the upgrade from 2.0.16 to 2.0.18.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a working npm installation of OpenCode 2.0.16 and npm 12.0.2, with `ignore-scripts=false` and no script approval for `@opencode/cli`.
2. Run `opencode upgrade 2.0.18` using the npm method.
3. Run `opencode --version`.

The upgrade reports success, but Windows rejects `bin/opencode.exe`. Running the installed package's `postinstall.mjs` manually repairs it.

### Operating System

Windows

issues.title: desktop: file links send literal ellipsis (U+2026) to /api/fs/read and 404
issues.body:
## Summary

In the desktop app, clicking a file link whose displayed path is abbreviated with a
home-directory ellipsis (`…`) sends that abbreviated string **verbatim** to
`GET /api/fs/read/…`, so the request 404s. The real file exists and opens fine by its
full path. The ellipsis is `U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS` (`%E2%80%A6`), not `~`, and the
server does not expand it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.15 (desktop app, `opencode-cli.version`); update to 2.0.18 staged
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64), Windows 11
- Terminal: Unavailable — OpenCode desktop app (Electron); `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: latest — desktop installer (`@opencodedesktop`)
- Active plugins: none found in config (only an MCP `playwright` server configured)

## Reproduction

1. In a desktop session, have the assistant reference a file that lives **under the home
   directory but outside the project**, for example
   `C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\commands\grill-me.md`.
2. Click the file link in the chat.
3. The UI shows `Failed to load file` / `File not found`.
4. The server log shows the abridged path requested literally.

## Expected Behavior

The link opens the real file. Any home-prefix abbreviation or middle-truncation used for
display should be expanded back to the real absolute path before the `fs/read` request.

## Actual Behavior

The request path still contains the display ellipsis:

```text
GET /api/fs/read/%E2%80%A6/config/opencode/commands/grill-me.md   -> 404   (x2)
```

`%E2%80%A6` decodes to `…` (U+2026). The real path
`C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\commands\grill-me.md` exists (2041 bytes) and reads
successfully by full path, so only the link expansion is broken.

The same happens when the chat text itself used a shorthand ellipsis:

```text
GET /api/fs/read/%E2%80%A6/skills/engineering/prototype   -> 404   (x3)
```

## Additional Context

- The abbreviation seen in the UI is the home prefix (`C:\Users\<user>\.`) collapsed to
  `…/`; the click handler appears to use the *rendered* text as the path.
- Related but distinct: #50876 and #50881 cover **relative / basename** links resolving
  against `$HOME`; #50913 covers a URL-style path resolving to `C:\static`. This issue is
  specifically the literal `…` surviving into the request URL.
- Secondary symptom: the `skill` tool's supporting-file sample lists bare relative names
  (e.g. `SKILL.md`); clicking one requests `GET /api/fs/read/SKILL.md` -> 404, because the
  client has no base directory for the skill and does not resolve it against the skill
  root.
- Frequency: 100% reproducible on 2.0.15 across several clicks.
- Workaround: open the file from a terminal or editor instead of clicking the chat link.

issues.title: desktop: "needs permission" system notification never fires although setting is enabled (completion notifications work)
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode Desktop 2.0.18 (Windows): Preferences → Notifications → "Show system notification when permission is needed" (系统通知→权限) is **enabled**, and Windows itself allows OpenCode notifications (banner + sound, Do-Not-Disturb off) — yet when a permission request is pending, **no system notification ever fires**: no toast, no sound, no notification-center entry. Agent-completion notifications ("回复已就绪") from the same app are delivered fine, so the notification pipeline works; only the permission trigger is dead.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18 (desktop app, Electron)
- OS: Windows 11, 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: n/a (desktop app)
- Shell: PowerShell 7 (portable)
- Install/channel: latest release
- Active plugins: @prevalentware/opencode-goal-plugin, local handoff-on-compact (irrelevant — the notification is desktop-client behavior)

## Reproduction

1. In OpenCode Desktop: Preferences → Notifications → enable 系统通知→权限 ("Show system notification when permission is needed"); optionally enable 音效→权限.
2. In Windows Settings → System → Notifications: global ON, 勿扰 OFF, OpenCode allowed with banner + sound.
3. Configure an `ask` permission rule for any tool (e.g. `{ "action": "wincontrol_Clipboard", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`) and trigger it so a permission request goes pending. The in-app approval card ("需要权限", resource `*`, buttons 拒绝 / 始终允许 / 允许一次) appears and the tool call blocks.
4. Switch focus to a different application and wait.

## Expected Behavior

A Windows toast using the app's own locale string `{{sessionTitle}}（{{projectName}}）需要权限` (this template exists in the shipped zh locale bundle, so the feature is implemented at the UI level), plus the configured permission sound.

## Actual Behavior

Nothing fires: no banner, no sound, and no entry in the notification center (verified via Win+N). The pending request exists only inside the unfocused OpenCode window, so the call blocks indefinitely with zero external signal.

## Timeline of today's observations (2026-09-26, local UTC+8)

| ~Time | Event | System notification? |
|---|---|---|
| 21:07 / 21:10 | Two permission dialogs appeared (earlier session), user clicked Allow once | none recorded |
| 22:29 | Added `ask` rules for wincontrol tools, config hot-reloaded | — |
| ~22:31 | Test A, window focused: `wincontrol.Wait` blocked 4.96 s total (~3 s human click latency), in-app dialog shown | n/a (focused) |
| ~22:35 | Test B, deliberately Alt+Tabbed away: `wincontrol.Wait` blocked **43 s** awaiting decision | **none — no banner, no sound** (user report) |
| ~22:40 | Opened Windows notification center: four "回复已就绪" completion notifications present (21:03/21:57/22:13/22:41), **zero "需要权限"** | — |
| ~23:05 | Test C, user defocused: `wincontrol.Clipboard(get)` blocked **59 s**; in-app "需要权限" card visible in screenshot | **none** (user report) |

Frequency: 100% — every pending permission request today (at least 4) produced no system notification; two of them had the user explicitly defocused and watching for one.

## Additional Context

- Completion notifications prove the Windows notification path works for this app; only the permission event never emits.
- The zh locale bundle contains both the setting description ("当需要权限时显示系统通知") and the notification title template ("{{sessionTitle}}（{{projectName}}）需要权限"), so the trigger appears simply not wired (or gated on a condition that never holds, e.g. a different event type than what the server emits for MCP-tool asks).
- Impact: users relying on `ask` to gate risky tools get no signal that a call is stuck while working in another window. Combined with the in-app prompt not stealing focus, the ask gate becomes a silent indefinite wait.
- Related: #51504 follow-up comment (retested there: `ask` itself works for MCP tools, including while unfocused — the request genuinely blocks; this issue covers the missing notification that is supposed to surface exactly that state).

issues.title: v2: no credential path for custom provider IDs breaks adding custom providers from GUI clients
issues.body:
### Description

Custom providers seem to have no working credential path on the v2 integration API, which breaks adding them from GUI clients:

- `Integration.connection.key` (packages/core/src/integration.ts) dies with `Key method not found: <id>` unless an integration with that exact ID is registered.
- Key methods are only registered for providers present in the models.dev catalog (packages/core/src/plugin/models-dev.ts) plus plugin-defined ones — so a *custom* provider ID can never get a key through `integration.connect.key`.

Concretely: OpenChamber's custom-provider form routes the API key through this endpoint and always fails with "Integration not found: <id>" for any custom ID (filed as openchamber/openchamber#4038). The official desktop dialog works around this by using the legacy `auth.set` (packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts) + config write instead.

Separately: a user on the stable OpenCode Desktop reports being unable to add custom providers/models from the UI — can you confirm which desktop release ships the custom-provider dialog (packages/app/src/components/dialog-custom-provider.tsx), and whether it is expected to work against the bundled server?

**Question:** is `auth.set` the intended long-term path for custom-provider credentials, or should `integration.connect.key` also accept arbitrary provider IDs? Right now any third-party GUI following the integration API cannot add custom providers.

### OpenCode version

Source analysis of dev branch (2026-09-27); stable desktop 1.2.x

issues.body:
## Summary

In the OpenCode desktop app, the effort (variant) selector chip in the composer disappears when the mouse passes over it — but only when the effort is set to `Default`. With any explicit effort (`Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Xhigh`, `Max`) the chip stays visible on screen at all times.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18 (desktop)
- OS: Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition), kernel `7.2.7-200.fc44.x86_64`, Wayland session
- Terminal: N/A (GUI app launched from the desktop entry; parent shell has `TERM=xterm-256color`)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: Fedora RPM `opencode-2.0.18-1.x86_64` (vendor `OpenCode <hello@opencode.ai>`), `latest` channel, binary at `/opt/OpenCode/ai.opencode.desktop`. Desktop shell is Electron 44.4.3 / Chromium 152.0.7977.130.

## Reproduction

1. Open the OpenCode desktop app.
2. Leave the effort selector at its initial value, `Default`.
3. Move the mouse pointer across the effort chip in the composer's bottom toolbar (to the right of the model selector).
4. Observe the chip vanish and reappear as the pointer moves over and away from it.
5. Open the effort dropdown and select an explicit value, such as `Max` or `Xhigh`.
6. Move the mouse pointer across the chip again — it now stays visible the entire time.

## Expected Behavior

The effort chip should stay rendered and visible regardless of the selected effort value. Hovering it should only add a hover highlight, never remove the control from view.

## Actual Behavior

When the effort is `Default`, the chip's visibility is bound to hover state: it disappears while the pointer is over it and reappears when the pointer leaves, so it is difficult to see and difficult to click. When an explicit effort is selected, the same chip is always visible and behaves normally.

## Additional Context

issues.title: reasoning_options=[toggle] yields zero variants for @ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers (485 models, e.g. all Xiaomi MiMo)
issues.body:
## Description

Models whose models.dev entry declares `reasoning_options = [{ type = "toggle" }]` get **no variants at all** when their provider package is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Since `variants` is what clients render a reasoning control from, those models look like they have no reasoning support — even though `reasoning: true` is set and the API does support toggling.

`reasoningToggle()` in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` only maps two packages and returns an empty object for everything else:

```ts
function reasoningToggle(model: Provider.Model) {
  if (model.api.npm === "@ai-sdk/alibaba")
    return { none: { enableThinking: false }, high: { enableThinking: true } }
  if (model.api.npm === "@ai-sdk/cohere")
    return { none: { thinking: { type: "disabled" } }, high: { thinking: { type: "enabled" } } }
  return {}
}
```

`reasoningVariants()` then calls `nonEmptyVariants(reasoningToggle(target))`, and `nonEmptyVariants({})` returns `undefined` → `variants` is empty. `nvidia` escapes via a dedicated branch in `reasoningEffort`'s sibling path, and `openrouter` has its own transform that implements `case "toggle"`.

Count from the current models.dev catalog: **499 models across 83 providers** declare a toggle on `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`; 14 of those are nvidia, so **485 get no reasoning control**. Affected providers include all four Xiaomi token-plan providers (`xiaomi`, `xiaomi-token-plan-cn`, `xiaomi-token-plan-ams`, `xiaomi-token-plan-sgp` — every `mimo-v2*`, `mimo-v2.5*`, `mimo-v2.6*` model), plus zenmux, llmgateway-providers, novita-ai, qiniu-ai, ofox, wandb, zhipuai, empiriolabs, 302ai, opencode, and ~70 more.

## Concrete case: MiMo-V2.6-Pro on Xiaomi Token Plan (Europe)

models.dev is correct here and documents its source:

```toml
# providers/xiaomi-token-plan-ams/models/mimo-v2.6-pro.toml
# Toggle: thinking.type = enabled|disabled
# Source: https://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/tokenplan/Token Plan/quick-access
reasoning_options = [{ type = "toggle" }]
```

Measured against the live endpoint (`token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com`, `mimo-v2.6-pro`, identical prompt):

| request | `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` | `reasoning_content` in reply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` | 0 | absent |
| `thinking: {type: "enabled"}` | 12 | present |
| `reasoning_effort: "low"` | 12 | present |
| `reasoning_effort: "high"` | 12 | present |

So the toggle is the only control the API honours, `reasoning_effort` is ignored, and opencode v2 cannot express the toggle on this package.

For contrast, an effort model on the *same* package does get variants: `deepseek-v4.1-flash` → `low`/`high`/`max`.

## No config-level workaround

Model-level `options` are filtered through opencode's own option schema before reaching the provider, not passed through verbatim. Against a local echo server on the OpenAI-compatible path:

- `options: { reasoningEffort: "high" }` → body contains `reasoning_effort: "high"`
- `options: { thinking: { type: "disabled" } }` → body contains `thinking: null`
- `options: { user: "probe-marker" }` → dropped

So there is no way to hand-write the `thinking` body field from config for an openai-compatible provider.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider, e.g. `xiaomi-token-plan-ams` with `npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`.
2. Request the model info for a toggle model, e.g. `GET /provider` (v2.0.12) and read `variants` for `mimo-v2.6-pro` → `[]`.
3. Repeat with an effort model on the same provider, e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` → `["low", "high", "max"]`.
4. `reasoningVariants()` in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` shows the toggle branch resolving to `undefined` for this package.

## Question about the fix shape

Adding a `reasoningToggle()` case is a small code change, but the wire field is provider-specific: MiMo wants `thinking.type`, Alibaba `enableThinking`, nvidia `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, OpenRouter `reasoning.enabled`. A generic default for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` would be wrong for most of the 485. Options I see:

1. models.dev gains a field describing the toggle body shape (e.g. `reasoning_options: [{ type = "toggle", body = { thinking = { type = ... } } }]`), and `reasoningToggle()` honours it.
2. dedicated provider packages for the big ones (`@opencode/ai/providers/xiaomi`), as exists for deepseek/zai/anthropic/etc.
3. at minimum, keep the capability visible to clients even when no variant can be built, so the model isn't presented as non-reasoning.

Happy to go with whatever direction you prefer — I can also test a candidate mapping against the providers' documented APIs.

## Environment

- OpenCode version: 2.0.12
- Operating System: macOS (darwin-arm64)
- Terminal: OpenChamber desktop (managed `opencode serve`)
- Plugins: none

prs.title: fix(mcp): request offline access so OAuth servers issue refresh tokens
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59820

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The MCP OAuth authorization URL never asked for offline access, so Google's authorization server returned only a ~1-hour access token and no refresh token — an hour after each sign-in every request 401s and the server reports "requires user authorization" (log shows `mcp oauth authorization completed ... hasRefreshToken=false expiresIn=3599`). This sets `access_type=offline` on the authorization URL at the single point where OpenCode hands it to the browser (`redirectToAuthorization` in `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth.ts`), covering initial login and re-authorization. RFC 6749 §3.1 requires authorization servers to ignore unrecognized request parameters, so servers that already issue refresh tokens (Linear, Sentry, etc.) are unaffected. `prompt=consent` is deliberately not sent, so consent prompting behavior is unchanged; if Google does not re-issue a refresh token on a silently re-approved existing grant, the user can revoke the grant once and re-authorize.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `cd packages/core && bun run test test/mcp-oauth.test.ts` — 23 pass, 0 fail (new test included).
- `cd packages/core && bun typecheck` — no type errors; root `bun run lint` — 0 errors.
- Full `cd packages/core && bun run test` — 6903 pass, 8 fail; those 8 (shell-syntax and git-utility tests) fail identically on unmodified `dev` and are unrelated to this change.
- The new test fails with the change reverted and passes with it. The existing `requests offline_access without forcing a consent prompt` test guards that no `prompt` parameter is added.

To verify by hand: sign in to a Google OAuth-backed MCP server (e.g. the Gmail MCP server), check the authorization URL in the browser contains `access_type=offline`, then that the log shows `hasRefreshToken=true` and later `operation=refresh` instead of hourly 401s.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): schedule prompts from agents, /schedule and the experimental API
prs.body:
**Agents, people and apps can now schedule a prompt for later: ask "check CI every hour for the next 8 hours" and the session wakes itself.**
Stacked on #59401, which added the storage and timer. Everything here stays off unless `experimental.schedules` is on where the session lives.

💡 **Why**
#59401 can fire schedules, but nothing could create one yet. This PR gives the agent, the user and apps a way in.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Let the agent schedule work itself. It gets `schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_pause`, `schedule_resume` and `schedule_delete` in the `opencode` tool namespace. It can only see and change its own session's schedules.
- Type `/schedule every morning at 9 check CI` (or just `/schedule` to list them). The agent turns that into a schedule.
- Manage schedules from apps through `client.experimental.schedule.{create,list,get,pause,resume,delete}` (`/api/experimental/schedule`).
- Write `when` the short way: `{ in: "20 minutes" }`, `{ at: "2026-10-27T09:00" }`, `{ every: "1 hour" }` or `{ cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" }`, with an optional `tz`, plus `ends` and `prompt`.

🚦 **How it ships**
Off by default. With `experimental.schedules` off, the tools and `/schedule` aren't registered, and the API returns 403. They appear or disappear when config changes, without a restart. Conditional checks (`if` / `until` shell commands that need approval) come in the next PR.

```diff
+ agent / /schedule / app -> schedule({ when, ends?, prompt })
+   -> flag off where the session lives? -> 403, or the tools are hidden
+   -> another session's schedule?       -> not found
+   -> the timer from #59401 fires it later as a prompt
```

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round">
  <style>
    .hand{transform-origin:36px 36px;animation:spin 4s linear infinite}
    .msg{animation:fly 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .dot{animation:pulse 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes spin{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
    @keyframes fly{0%,20%{transform:translateX(0);opacity:0}30%{opacity:1}60%,100%{transform:translateX(96px);opacity:1}}
    @keyframes pulse{0%,55%{opacity:.25}65%,85%{opacity:1}100%{opacity:.25}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.hand,.msg,.dot{animation:none}.msg{transform:translateX(96px)}}
  </style>
  <circle cx="36" cy="36" r="20" opacity=".6"/>
  <line class="hand" x1="36" y1="36" x2="36" y2="22"/>
  <line x1="36" y1="36" x2="46" y2="36" opacity=".6"/>
  <g class="msg">
    <rect x="66" y="27" width="34" height="18" rx="6" opacity=".9"/>
    <line x1="73" y1="36" x2="93" y2="36" opacity=".5"/>
  </g>
  <rect x="160" y="14" width="66" height="44" rx="8" opacity=".5"/>
  <line x1="170" y1="28" x2="208" y2="28" opacity=".35"/>
  <line x1="170" y1="44" x2="196" y2="44" opacity=".35"/>
  <circle class="dot" cx="216" cy="44" r="3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>
</svg>
```

📊 **Proof:** new tool tests cover the flag gate, the full create → list → pause → resume → delete flow, `/schedule`, and another session's schedule reading as missing. A server test drives the real HTTP API through the generated client, including 400 for a bad duration or two triggers in one `when`, and 403 where the flag is off. Tools recheck the flag on every call, so a config change takes effect mid-session. 30 core, 1 server and 44 client tests pass.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/schedule.ts`, the `owned` check. Schedule ids aren't secret, so every tool call checks that the schedule belongs to the calling session. prs.title: feat(core): scheduled tasks storage and time triggers (experimental)
prs.body:
**A schedule can now wake a session with a prompt: once, at a set time, every N minutes, or on a cron, behind an experimental flag.**
This PR adds only the storage and the timer. Agents and apps can't create schedules yet; that comes in the next PR.

💡 **Why**
Long-running work like "check error rates every 10 minutes for the next 8 hours" needs the session to wake on its own, not wait for someone to type.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Create a schedule for a session with `when` (in, at, every, cron, with an optional time zone), `ends` (after, at, times) and a prompt to send.
- List, get, pause, resume and remove schedules from server code.
- Trust that each firing reaches the session exactly once, even if the server crashes mid-firing or was down when it came due (one catch-up firing, marked late).

🚦 **How it ships**
Off by default. Turn on `experimental.schedules` in config. With it off, creating a schedule fails and the timer never fires. An optional top-level `timezone` setting picks the zone when a schedule doesn't name one; otherwise the server's own zone is used.

```diff
+ server start -> one timer loop: sleep until the next due schedule (at most 30s)
+ due -> skip if the last prompt is still unread
+      -> send prompt with id "msg_<schedule>_<run>" (a repeat id is a no-op)
+      -> then advance the schedule to its next time, or mark it done
+ prompt fails -> mark it "failed" and try again in 5 minutes
+ paused while firing -> the run still counts, so resuming sends the next run, not a repeat id
```

🕐 **Clocks falling back:** a cron slot never fires twice in the repeated hour. `Cron.next` picks the first pass of a repeated time; if that's already behind us, we step forward an hour until a slot is ahead. So `*/10` runs through the first 1:00–1:59 and resumes at 2:00, rather than firing through both.

↩️ **Undo:** revert isn't enough, because the migration has already created the `schedule` table in every database that ran this build. The table is harmless and empty unless the flag was turned on, but removing it needs a follow-up migration.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/schedule.ts`, the `fire` and `step` functions. The schedule row is updated only after the prompt is admitted, and the prompt id comes from the run number, so a crash in between re-sends the same id instead of a duplicate. The rest is routine.

<sub>Planned feature · no user reports · not measured</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun run script/test.ts test/schedule.test.ts` (core): 24 pass, covering a pause during firing, `at` times with a space before the offset, one-shot `in` and `at`, `every` with `ends.times` and `ends.at`, cron across the Nov 1 DST change and inside the repeated hour, one late catch-up, the 5-minute backoff after a failed prompt, rejecting a zero duration and `ends.times` below 1, overlap skip, crash between admit and update, session delete cascade, flag off, pause/resume, and the loop waking on its timer
- `bun typecheck` in core, schema and server: pass

prs.title: fix(tui): navigate the transcript with keypad Home and End
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55533. The same bug was reported separately as #57113, already closed as a duplicate of #55533.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Under the kitty keyboard protocol a terminal reports NumPad navigation keys as their own functional key codes. `@opentui/core` 0.6.8 decodes them as `kppageup` (`CSI 57421 u`), `kppagedown` (`CSI 57422 u`), `kphome` (`CSI 57423 u`) and `kpend` (`CSI 57424 u`), and `@opentui/keymap` accepts all four as named single-stroke keys — but no default binding claimed any of them. So the keypad key next to a working key was silently dropped: in a session, plain `End` jumps to the last message and NumPad `End` does nothing.

This PR lists each keypad key beside the key it mirrors, in `packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts`:

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.first` | `ctrl+g,home,alt+home` | `ctrl+g,home,alt+home,kphome` |
| `session.last` | `ctrl+alt+g,end` | `ctrl+alt+g,end,kpend` |
| `session.page.up` | `pageup,ctrl+alt+b` | `pageup,ctrl+alt+b,kppageup` |
| `session.page.down` | `pagedown,ctrl+alt+f` | `pagedown,ctrl+alt+f,kppagedown` |

**Why the session navigation commands and not the prompt.** These are the navigation keys whose plain counterpart already has exactly one meaning in the session view, and that meaning is transcript navigation. Plain `Home` and `End` are deliberately reserved for the transcript: `input.buffer.home` and `input.buffer.end` default to `none`, and `config-v2.test.tsx` pins that with `reserves home and end for navigation`. Binding the keypad keys to the buffer commands instead would give NumPad Home a different meaning from the plain Home key beside it, which is the split #55533 asks to be rid of. Users who want the prompt behaviour still get it from the `keybinds` override the issue itself shows.

**Scope.** The NumPad arrow keys are not included: `up` and `down` are shared by the prompt, history, dialogs and the session, so mirroring them changes far more than the reported End/Home/PageUp/PageDown case. `alt+end` (`session.messages_last_user`) is not mirrored either, since there is no natural keypad chord for it.

An earlier PR of mine, #55870, proposed the same keypad mirrors; I closed it when the prompt half looked like the target. This PR is that direction, aimed at the transcript half #55533 actually reports.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `mirrors plain navigation keys on the keypad` in `config-v2.test.tsx` asserts, for each of the four commands, that the resolved bindings contain both the plain key and the keypad key. It runs against `resolve()` from `src/config`, the table the TUI loads (`src/app.tsx`). `config.test.tsx` pins the legacy `src/config/v1` table, which only config migration still reads (`packages/cli/src/config/migrate.ts`), so it is unchanged by design.
- Red before green: with the four default values reverted to their previous strings, the new test fails (`1 fail`, 35 pass); with the change, `config`, `config-v2` and `keybind` pass (37 pass, 0 fail).
- The key names and codepoints above are read from the installed `@opentui/core` 0.6.8 (functional-key table) and `@opentui/keymap` 0.6.8 (named single-stroke key set), not from memory. The branch installs the versions the workspace catalog pins.
- `tsc -b` clean for `packages/tui`; `oxlint` and `prettier --check` clean on both changed files.
- I could not press a physical NumPad key while testing: this machine has no numeric keypad. The link from key to command therefore rests on the core's codepoint table and the keymap's named-key set cited above, plus #55533's reproduction, which shows the terminal sending `^[[57424u` while the binding never fires.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(ai): make provider model() settings optional and rename configure inputs to Config
prs.body:
### Problem

Every provider's top-level `model` export required a settings object, even when all settings are optional, and providers named their `configure()` input type differently (`Config`, `LanguageModelOptions` or `Options`).

### Change

```ts
// before
OpenAI.model("gpt-5", {})
type C = Groq.LanguageModelOptions

// after
OpenAI.model("gpt-5") // same as OpenAI.configure().responses("gpt-5"), auth from env
type C = Groq.Config
```

- I added `ProviderPackage.Model<Settings, Options, Compact>`. Settings are optional when every key in the provider's settings is optional. Providers that need a value (Alibaba region or baseURL, Azure, Cloudflare AI Gateway and Workers AI, OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI-compatible Responses, Anthropic-compatible) still require settings.
- Provider `model` exports and their sibling loaders (`chatModel`, `messagesModel`, `responsesModel`, `imageModel`, `decisionModel`) default missing settings to `{}`. Return types are unchanged.
- `ProviderPackage.Definition` is unchanged, so package authors still get a required `settings` parameter and core keeps passing it.
- Every provider's `configure()` input type is now called `Config`. I renamed the old types rather than aliasing them:
  - `LanguageModelOptions` → `Config`: Azure, Baseten, Cerebras, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Cloudflare Workers AI, Cohere, DeepInfra, DeepSeek, DigitalOcean, Fireworks, Groq, Meta, Mistral, OpenRouter, Together AI, xAI
  - `Options` → `Config`: OpenCode, TypeSafe AI, Vercel AI Gateway
  - OpenAI-compatible's private `GenericModelOptions` is now the exported `Config`

### Breaking

Code that imports `X.LanguageModelOptions` or `X.Options` from `@opencode/ai` for the providers above must switch to `X.Config`. Nothing else in the monorepo used the old names. Runtime behavior and calls that pass settings are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(core): add subagent concurrency limit
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #27110

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds `experimental.subagent_concurrency`, a cap on how many subagents execute at the same time; unset keeps today's no limit.

This is a port of the v1 attempt (Jieiku@101be29). v1 wrapped the task tool's inline run effect; v2 subagents do not run inline. The child executes from prompt admission to job settlement, so a call that starts a run takes the permit before admitting the child's prompt, and a forked fiber releases it at settlement. The permit therefore spans foreground and background calls alike: a background subagent holds it past the tool's return, and a foreground call that gets backgrounded keeps it until the child settles. A `catchCause` gives it back when admission fails before the job exists, so a failed call cannot erode the limit.

Two calls take no permit, and the reason is the same in both: a permit marks a run, and neither call starts one.

- **A nested call runs under its ancestor's permit.** The ancestor holds its own until it settles, and it cannot settle while the tool call it is waiting on is this one, so a second permit is a deadlock at any limit rather than a slow path.
- **Continuing a running child joins its job.** The steer reaches a child that is already executing, so that child counts once instead of twice.

The limit therefore counts top-level subagents; `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx` says so where it describes the option.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/tool-subagent.test.ts`, against the gated fake execution: two background calls keep peak execution at one and the second prompt out of the inbox until the first settles; a nested call from a running child gets through at `subagent_depth: 2` with `subagent_concurrency: 1`; a steer reaches a running child while that child still holds its permit. The nested and steer cases both hang (30s test timeout) on the previous head and pass on this one.
- Config tests cover a valid value and a rejected zero.
- `bun run check` passes (lint + typecheck), and `typecheck:tsc` passes in `packages/schema`, `packages/core` and `packages/client` on the merged head.

The branch is `dev` merged in and the four conflicts resolved: two keys landing at the same spot in `experimental.ts`, `config/normalize.ts` and the generated promise `ConfigEntry`, plus the test file's import block, which upstream moved to `@opencode/ai/effect`. `packages/client` is regenerated, not hand-edited.

Long code blocks in assistant messages now keep their copy button in view while you scroll through them, so you can copy without scrolling back to the top. - It sticks below `--sticky-accordion-top`, so in the timeline it stays under the session header, the same offset the sticky tool group headers use.
- Hover/focus visibility and the always-visible touch behavior are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(core): price Copilot long-context tiers and cache writes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52089
Closes #59671 

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

GitHub Copilot costs were undercounted badly on long sessions. In my case (#59671): a 3h session on Copilot / Claude Haiku 5.5, 348 requests, ~344K average context, OpenCode showed $1.56 when the real bill is roughly $9.34 (between $2.03 and $10.15, since Copilot picks the price tier per request by prompt size).

Two causes, both in the Copilot provider code:

1. Copilot's `/models` payload ships two price tiers (`default` and `long_context`, the latter starting above `default.max_prompt_tokens`). The builder only read the default tier.
2. The builder hardcoded cache writes to $0 (`cache_write_price` is in the payload, unread), and both usage adapters dropped `cache_write_tokens`, so cache writes weren't counted at all.

Pricing that session's totals at the ≤100K rates with free writes gives $1.5557 — cent-exact with the displayed $1.56, which is how I know exactly which rates the old code applied.

The builder now emits the write price and a context-tier cost entry, which `SessionUsage.calculateCost` already applies per request, so no calculator change was needed. The adapters map `cache_write_tokens` into `cacheWrite`. While there I replaced their hand-rolled `noCache` arithmetic with `ProviderShared.subtractTokens`/`sumTokens` like the shared protocols use: three of the four paths left `noCache` undefined on responses without cache details, which downstream prices the entire prompt at $0, and none of them clamped against broken breakdowns.

Deliberately not addressed: Copilot's own reported billed amount (#35765) and the richer `pricing` shape from #59460.

### How did you verify your code works?

New unit tests against the Copilot rate card for Claude Haiku 5.5: long-context tier applies above 100K prompt tokens, default tier at exactly 100K, cache writes priced, reasoning billed as output, a malformed `long_context` object no longer drops the model from the catalog, cache-write mapping in all four adapter paths, plus regressions for the $0-prompt and negative-`noCache` cases. The adapter regressions fail on the parent commit and pass with this change. `bun run check` passes, and the `packages/core` suite has the same 4 failures as a clean `dev` checkout (all environment-related).

prs.body:
`generate.yml` and `nix-hashes.yml` on v1 fail with `appId option is required` because `OPENCODE_APP_ID` and `OPENCODE_APP_SECRET` were removed. This switches v1 to the same mechanism dev uses, which needs only `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

### Nix hashes: same as dev #59464
- `nix-hashes.yml` becomes `bot-nix-hashes.yml`, copied from dev. The `hash` and `compute` jobs use a read-only token and no secrets. `publish` (`contents`, `pull-requests` and `actions` write) runs only `.github/nix-hashes/publish.sh` from the triggering commit. It commits only a validated `nix/hashes.json` to `bot/v1-nix-hashes`, opens or updates the PR into `v1`, dispatches `typecheck.yml`, `test.yml`, `nix-eval.yml` and `check-bot-scope.yml` on the branch, and runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash`.
- `check-bot-scope.yml` and `.github/nix-hashes/validate.sh` are copied from dev. The check fails `bot/v1-nix-hashes` unless it changes only a valid `nix/hashes.json`.
- Differences from dev: the branch is `v1`, the bot branch is `bot/v1-nix-hashes`, the path filters match v1 (no `services/*`), and the concurrency group is v1-specific.

### Generate: same as dev
Dev removed its generate bot (15f0fc9e00) and checks generated files in pull requests instead. `generate.yml` is removed here, and `typecheck.yml` gets a `generated` job. It runs `./script/generate.ts` (SDK build, OpenAPI and prettier) and fails if that changes anything. v1 is currently clean under it.

### Removed
- `generate.yml`.
- `docs-locale-sync.yml`: it only triggers on pushes to `dev`, and dev doesn't have this file, so it never runs.
- `models-snapshot.yml`: it is scheduled, so it runs from dev, where the file doesn't exist. It also targets `v2`.
- `.github/actions/setup-git-committer`.

No v1 workflow references `OPENCODE_APP_ID`, `OPENCODE_APP_SECRET` or `actions/create-github-app-token` anymore.

### Before the bot can merge on v1 (ruleset 25933885, not changed here)
The `update` rule only lets bypass actors change `v1`, and `github-actions` isn't one. Until that changes, `publish` opens or updates the PR, then fails at `gh pr merge`. The PR stays open for someone to merge.

v1 also has no required status checks, so `check-bot-scope` wouldn't gate auto-merge. Both changes are needed together:
1. Require the `bot-scope` check (GitHub Actions app, integration 15368) on `refs/heads/v1` in a **separate** ruleset that has no `github-actions` bypass. A bypass on 25933885 would also skip its own rules.
2. Add the GitHub Actions app (Integration, actor_id 15368) to 25933885's bypass list with `bypass_mode: "pull_request"`, so it can only merge through a pull request.

Auto-merge is already enabled for the repository.

### Checks
- actionlint before: 27 unknown `blacksmith-*` labels plus 2 findings, both in the deleted `docs-locale-sync.yml` and `generate.yml`. After: 24 unknown labels and nothing else.
- `bash -n` passes on `publish.sh` and `validate.sh`, and `validate.sh` accepts v1's `nix/hashes.json`.
- `./script/generate.ts` leaves v1 unchanged.

prs.title: fix(core): call an RPC method that declares only one schema
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59755

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The RPC docs allow a method to leave out whichever side it does not use, but the call path passed the missing schema straight to the validator: `isStandardSchema` ran `"~standard" in schema` on `undefined` and the whole call became `rpc.internal`. A method declaring only an `output` schema could not be called at all, and the mirror case — only an `input`, nothing to return — failed the same way on the way out.

`parse()` now returns the value untouched when there is no schema to validate against, and `isStandardSchema` only looks for the marker on an object, which is how `tool/runtime.ts` already guards the same check. Nothing else changes: a declared schema still validates, and bad input still comes back as `rpc.invalid_input`.

One thing I did not do: make `input` / `output` optional in `Rpc.Method`. I tried it, and it breaks the generic constraints in `client/src/effect/rpc.ts` and `plugin/src/effect/rpc.ts` in five places, so it is a separate design question about how a client should type a method with no schema. The test therefore builds its definition the way a JavaScript plugin would, one cast at that boundary.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/rpc-one-sided-schema.test.ts` calls an output-only method, an input-only method, and a third case that sends `{ text: 42 }` to the input-only method to show validation still rejects it.

On `dev` (`f669c46`) the first two fail with exactly the error from the report — `TypeError: schema is not an Object. (evaluating '"~standard" in schema')` — and pass on this branch.

- `bun test test/rpc-one-sided-schema.test.ts test/rpc-handler-errors.test.ts` in `packages/core` — 8 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core` — clean

prs.title: feat(ext): add Code Coach - AI coach that watches prompts, diffs, and terminal output
prs.body:
## What this is

**Code Coach** — an AI coach that watches what you ask your coding agent and what the agent produces, teaches the first principle underneath the bug, and remembers what you have already learned. It observes; it never writes code.

Two packages:

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| `packages/extensions/code-coach-mcp` | The model half: MCP server over stdio, triage → coach, learner profile |
| `packages/extensions/code-coach-vscode` | The client: observers, persistent card, commands, settings |

## The loop

```
you type a prompt ──► observer captures it
                          │
                          ▼
                   cheap triage model
                   "is this worth interrupting for?"
                          │
             ┌────────────┴────────────┐
             │ no                      │ yes
             ▼                         ▼
          silence                 coach model
      (the default)           nudge + explanation
                              + better prompt + tags
                                       │
                                       ▼
                              persistent card
                     Explain · Fix my prompt · Snooze · Ignore
                                       │
                                       ▼
                              learner profile
                     counts, mastered at 3, depth per concept
```

The card has **no timer**. It stays until you click Ignore or Snooze, or a new nudge replaces it. A later silent triage does not overwrite a nudge you are still reading.

## Observers — what watches what

| Where you work | Prompt | Diff | Terminal |
|---|---|---|---|
| VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf | clipboard, CDP (browser), UIA (desktop), or `Coach this prompt` | save diff (LCS) | terminal API when available |
| Claude Desktop | UIA (Windows, best effort), clipboard | — | — |
| Chrome / Edge chat (claude.ai, chatgpt.com, gemini, …) | CDP composer reader | — | — |
| A terminal outside VS Code | clipboard | — | — |
| Any MCP client | `coach` tool | `coach` tool | `coach` tool |

**1. Save diff** — on save, a line-based LCS diff between the last saved baseline and the current content.

**2. Terminal** — `onDidWriteTerminalData` (proposed API) error lines are sent as `context`. Absent when the API is unavailable; the observer is simply not there.

**3. Clipboard** — polls every two seconds, keeps the last prose-looking text. The universal fallback.

**4. Browser CDP** — attaches to a browser launched with `--remote-debugging-port`, lists chat tabs via `/json/list`, and evaluates a small expression that finds the visible composer. It remembers the last non-empty text and emits it **when the composer clears** (what every chat UI does on send). No keystrokes, no network interception. Opt-in, local port.

**5. Windows UI Automation** — a long-lived PowerShell helper reads `AutomationElement.FocusedElement` every 700 ms. It only reports `ControlType.Edit` (never `Document`, which would dump a whole page) and only emits when the field is cleared or loses focus. Opt-in, read-only, Windows only.

All five funnel through `ObserverHub`, which drops short text, huge pastes, and the same prompt from the same source inside a 30 s window.

## Why not a keyboard hook

InterviewCoder and Cluely use OS-level capture because they are stealth desktop apps. Copying that mechanism into an open-source developer tool would be the wrong trade:

- A global keyboard hook sees **every** keystroke in **every** app: passwords, 2FA codes, private messages, other people's data.
- One bug or one compromised dependency turns the coach into a keylogger.
- The thing the coach needs is "the prompt the developer just sent", not "every key".

So the observation layer reads the **composer** instead. Same goal, far smaller blast radius, opt-in.

What this borrows from the references: Clicky's teacher loop, Cluely's screen-awareness, InterviewCoder's multi-provider desktop shape. What it does not borrow: the stealth capture model.

## Honest gaps

- **Embedded webviews are still opaque.** Cursor's and Claude's in-app chat panels expose no public API. CDP cannot attach to them; UIA is best effort. Clipboard and the explicit command remain the fallback.
- **CDP needs a debug port.** Deliberate opt-in, not a default. Chrome 136+ refuses remote debugging on the default profile, so the README documents a separate `--user-data-dir`.
- **UIA is best effort.** Only Edit controls, only known apps, only on Windows.
- **The coach is a model.** `uncertain` and the "don't invent vulnerabilities" instruction reduce false positives; they do not eliminate them.
- **Free-tier OpenRouter accounts are tight.** `CODE_COACH_MOCK=1` makes the pipeline testable without credits and is never the default.

## Verification

```
code-coach-vscode   60 pass / 0 fail / 108 expects across 10 files
code-coach-mcp      10 pass / 0 fail /  31 expects across  2 files
tsc -p .            clean in both packages
oxlint src          clean
```

- Real stdio end-to-end test: spawns the server, initializes MCP, calls `coach`, asserts the profile was updated, asserts `source` and `uncertain` round-trip.
- Fake CDP server tests cover the handshake, target filtering, `Runtime.evaluate`, and the **composer-clears → prompt emitted** transition.
- The CDP DOM expression was also run against a real headless Chrome: it read the typed composer text, then read empty after clearing.
- UIA parsing tests reject `Document` controls, short/huge text, and unrelated apps.
- Live OpenRouter tests **skip** (not fail) on 402/429; the free-tier key is drained.

## Packaging fix

The extension previously compiled to ESM (`module: esnext`). VS Code 1.90 loads extensions as CommonJS, so it would not have loaded at all. It now emits CJS via `module: node16` / `moduleResolution: node16` / `rootDir: src`, verified by inspecting `dist/extension.js`.

## Setup

```bash
cd packages/extensions/code-coach-mcp && npm install && npm run build
cd ../code-coach-vscode && npm install && npm run compile
```

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the environment the extension host inherits, or point `codeCoach.mcpServerPath` at the built server. Browser and UIA observation are off by default and enabled in settings.

Full architecture and per-observer documentation: `packages/extensions/code-coach-vscode/README.md`.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #59789

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

`select` in `acp/sessions.ts` wrote the new model or agent into the local selection before calling the server, so the server's event for that switch would be a no-op. If the switch failed, nothing put the old value back, and later requests used a model or agent the server never switched to.

Now the selection only changes once the switch succeeds. While a switch is in flight it's kept in a pending set, and the server event for it still doesn't send an extra `config_option_update`. Server events also bump a counter per field, and a switch only writes its value if no server event touched that field while it was running, so a slower switch can't overwrite a newer server choice.

prs.body:
Ported from anomalyco/opencode-pty#31. Part of the stack for anomalyco/opencode-pty#25; builds directly on `dev` (#59700 has merged), no prerequisite.

### Issue for this PR

Fixes anomalyco/opencode-pty#25 (this PR completes it)

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

- The Unix daemon loop now sleeps in `poll(2)` on the listener plus a private wake channel (`UnixStream::pair`, non-blocking, `CLOEXEC`) instead of a 10 ms sleep. The timeout is the minimum of the next ownership deadline, a 2 s safety net, and the accept back-off.
- `Control` notifies under the ownership mutex for every stop/ownership mutation. `Control::tick` drains the wake channel, observes, detects missed wakes, and ticks under the same lock, so a missed wake is detected deterministically (a warning in release builds; an error in debug builds, with cleanup still running).
- Handler completion wakes the loop, so finished connections close promptly.
- EMFILE-class errors (`EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, `ENOBUFS`, `ENOMEM`) from accept or cancellation now pause accept for 100 ms instead of killing the daemon.
- Windows keeps its 10 ms poll via stubs. Follow-up: `WaitForMultipleObjects` on the connect event plus a stop event, and replacing the per-terminal 10 ms root-exit poll.
- Enables the `poll` feature of `nix` in `packages/process-daemon/Cargo.toml` (no new crates; `Cargo.lock` is unchanged).

Ported from the opencode-pty commit; the only difference is that connection handlers are spawned with plain `thread::spawn`, as on `dev`.

prs.title: fix(ci): sign v1 with release environment credentials and publish only from v1
prs.body:
v1 publish run 40565869462 failed in `sign-cli-macos` and both macOS `build-electron` jobs. `apple-actions/import-codesign-certs` rejects the empty password of the new passwordless certificate.

### Signing (ported from #59768)
- Replace `apple-actions/import-codesign-certs` with a run step. It decodes `APPLE_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE` to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, creates `build.keychain` with a random password, imports with `-P ""`, sets the partition list and adds the keychain to the search list. An `if: always()` step deletes the keychain, the .p12 and the .p8. The keychain name is still `build.keychain`, which `CSC_KEYCHAIN` and the CLI signing step expect.
- Use only the new credentials. Notarization goes through electron-builder with `APPLE_API_KEY` (the path to the .p8 written from `secrets.APPLE_NOTARY_KEY`), `APPLE_API_KEY_ID` (`vars.APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID`) and `APPLE_API_ISSUER` (`vars.APPLE_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`). Fallbacks to `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY`, `APPLE_API_KEY_PATH` and `APPLE_API_ISSUER` are removed.
- `sign-cli-macos`, `sign-cli-windows`, `build-electron` (all matrix entries) and `publish` now run in `environment: release` unconditionally. Azure login already works in the release environment on dev's `release.yml`.

### Publish only from v1
- `publish.yml`: the push trigger is now `v1` only. Removed `ci`, `beta`, `fix/npm-native-binary-install` and `snapshot-*`. `version` requires `github.ref == 'refs/heads/v1'`, and `publish` requires `needs.version.result == 'success'`, so a dispatch on any other ref publishes nothing.
- Removed beta-only logic: the `opencode-beta` `GH_REPO`, `--sourcemaps`, the beta `OPENCODE_CHANNEL` and the beta Sentry environment from `publish.yml`, plus the beta draft-release branch in `script/version.ts`.
- `nix-hashes.yml`: dropped the `beta` push trigger. The commit job only runs on v1.
- `containers.yml` and `unlock.yml` (dispatch): the job only runs on v1.
- `publish-vscode.yml` and `publish-github-action.yml`: a dispatch only runs on v1, and a tag must point at a commit that is an ancestor of `origin/v1`.

### Checks
- actionlint reports the same findings before and after: 27 unknown `blacksmith-*` runner labels plus 2 existing issues in `docs-locale-sync.yml` and `generate.yml`.
- `bash -n` passes on every run step in the touched workflows. oxlint passes on `script/version.ts`.

### Merging
Merging is a push to `v1`. It starts `publish.yml` with no approval, because the `release` environment only has a branch policy (dev and v1) and no required reviewers. That run publishes a `0.0.0-dev-<timestamp>` preview to npm under the `dev` dist-tag. It does not create a GitHub release, Docker image, AUR package or Homebrew update. `deploy.yml`, `generate.yml`, `test.yml`, `typecheck.yml` and `nix-eval.yml` also run on that push.

prs.title: fix(stats): ignore requests rejected before routing
prs.body:
## Problem

The stats sync counted every Go/Free `generation.completed` event, including requests rejected before routing (`attempts = 0`). Those requests have no route, no endpoint and no usage, but their `model_requested` string still became a model dimension and got a page on `/data`.

One rejected request on 2026-09-19 for the nonexistent `glm-5.5-flash` (HTTP 400, 0 attempts, no workspace) produced `/data/zhipuai/glm-5.5-flash`. That page is now being shared as evidence of an upcoming model.

## Change

- Add `attempts > 0` to the source filter of the usage/geo and retention queries, so only requests that reached an upstream route are counted.

R2 check: across all `generation.completed` rows since 2026-05-28, every `attempts = 0` row has no route, failed, and has null usage, and `attempts` is never null. The filter therefore drops no tokens or cost.

## Effects

- The lake contains no `attempts = 0` events after 2026-09-20 13:44 UTC. For current traffic, this is a guard rather than a behavior change.
- Inside the display window (2026-09-02 to 2026-09-20), the daily history pass will stop counting pre-routing rejections, mostly Free-tier 429/403s and Go 400s. Request, session, unique-user and error counts for those days drop accordingly. Token and cost totals stay the same.
- The sync only upserts, so rows that already exist for a dimension no fresh query returns are not deleted. The existing `glm-5.5-flash` row stays until it leaves the 56-day window (about 2026-11-14) unless it is added to the `StatsHiddenModels` secret.

## Verification

- `bun test src/domain` in `packages/stats/core`: 34 pass, including the new query test
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/stats/core`
- oxlint on the changed files: clean

Requested by: @adamdotdevin (Adam via Slack)
