prs.title: fix(core): honor compaction retained-text budget
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #43250. Enforces the reported retained-text budget invariant; when no complete exchange fits, retaining no recent tail is permitted by the issue. Coordination: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/43250#issuecomment-5984568666

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Compaction currently walks backward from the retention budget to a user boundary, which can retain an entire oversized exchange. Select the next complete user exchange within the allowance instead; if none fits, summarize everything. Include separator and rounding overhead, and honor `keep.tokens: 0`.

The regression retains 76,099 characters with a 15k allowance before this change, then fails to continue after switching to a smaller model. With the fix, it summarizes the exchange and continues. Original messages remain stored.

Keeping whole exchanges can leave no verbatim tail even when individual assistant messages would fit. This change does not guarantee that the summary plus retained text and reply reserve fit every model, or repair an existing oversized checkpoint.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Both oversized-exchange regressions fail on current `v2` and pass with the patch.
- 259 tests pass across compaction, configuration, runner, provider-context, native-compaction, and compaction-transport suites. Covers zero retention, separator rounding, assistant-only history after a checkpoint, and continuation. Uses offline deterministic model responses, not live provider validation.
- Core `bun run typecheck`, changed-file oxlint, and Prettier checks pass.

prs.title: feat(ui): add gallery navigation to image preview
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related feature request: #58295. This PR is a draft while the design direction is reviewed.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The web image preview could only show one image, so a message with several images (for example a render set) required closing and reopening the preview for each one.

This passes the images from the markdown block into the preview, keeps the clicked image as the starting point, and adds previous/next buttons, a position counter, and left/right arrow keys to the preview's control strip. Single-image previews are unchanged. Moving between images moves the origin state, so closing restores the thumbnail for the image currently shown rather than leaving the first one hidden.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/ui` and `packages/session-ui`
- oxlint on the changed files
- Component tests in `packages/session-ui/component-tests/image-preview-gallery.spec.ts` for gallery navigation, thumbnail restoration on close, and arrow-key passthrough for single images
- The new full-bleed preview screenshots below are from the component story; the narrow layout was checked for control-strip fit

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(tui): navigate the transcript with keypad Home and End
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55533. The same bug was reported separately as #57113, already closed as a duplicate of #55533.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Under the kitty keyboard protocol a terminal reports NumPad navigation keys as their own functional key codes. `@opentui/core` 0.6.8 decodes them as `kppageup` (`CSI 57421 u`), `kppagedown` (`CSI 57422 u`), `kphome` (`CSI 57423 u`) and `kpend` (`CSI 57424 u`), and `@opentui/keymap` accepts all four as named single-stroke keys — but no default binding claimed any of them. So the keypad key next to a working key was silently dropped: in a session, plain `End` jumps to the last message and NumPad `End` does nothing.

This PR lists each keypad key beside the key it mirrors, in `packages/tui/src/config/keybind.ts`:

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.first` | `ctrl+g,home,alt+home` | `ctrl+g,home,alt+home,kphome` |
| `session.last` | `ctrl+alt+g,end` | `ctrl+alt+g,end,kpend` |
| `session.page.up` | `pageup,ctrl+alt+b` | `pageup,ctrl+alt+b,kppageup` |
| `session.page.down` | `pagedown,ctrl+alt+f` | `pagedown,ctrl+alt+f,kppagedown` |

**Why the session navigation commands and not the prompt.** These are the navigation keys whose plain counterpart already has exactly one meaning in the session view, and that meaning is transcript navigation. Plain `Home` and `End` are deliberately reserved for the transcript: `input.buffer.home` and `input.buffer.end` default to `none`, and `config-v2.test.tsx` pins that with `reserves home and end for navigation`. Binding the keypad keys to the buffer commands instead would give NumPad Home a different meaning from the plain Home key beside it, which is the split #55533 asks to be rid of. Users who want the prompt behaviour still get it from the `keybinds` override the issue itself shows.

**Scope.** The NumPad arrow keys are not included: `up` and `down` are shared by the prompt, history, dialogs and the session, so mirroring them changes far more than the reported End/Home/PageUp/PageDown case. `alt+end` (`session.messages_last_user`) is not mirrored either, since there is no natural keypad chord for it.

An earlier PR of mine, #55870, proposed the same keypad mirrors; I closed it when the prompt half looked like the target. This PR is that direction, aimed at the transcript half #55533 actually reports.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `mirrors plain navigation keys on the keypad` in `config-v2.test.tsx` asserts, for each of the four commands, that the resolved bindings contain both the plain key and the keypad key. It runs against `resolve()` from `src/config`, the table the TUI loads (`src/app.tsx`). `config.test.tsx` pins the legacy `src/config/v1` table, which only config migration still reads (`packages/cli/src/config/migrate.ts`), so it is unchanged by design.
- Red before green: with the four default values reverted to their previous strings, the new test fails (`1 fail`, 35 pass); with the change, `config`, `config-v2` and `keybind` pass (37 pass, 0 fail).
- The key names and codepoints above are read from the installed `@opentui/core` 0.6.8 (functional-key table) and `@opentui/keymap` 0.6.8 (named single-stroke key set), not from memory. The branch installs the versions the workspace catalog pins.
- `tsc -b` clean for `packages/tui`; `oxlint` and `prettier --check` clean on both changed files.
- I could not press a physical NumPad key while testing: this machine has no numeric keypad. The link from key to command therefore rests on the core's codepoint table and the keymap's named-key set cited above, plus #55533's reproduction, which shows the terminal sending `^[[57424u` while the binding never fires.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---

prs.title: fix(ci): import passwordless macOS signing certificate
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Follow-up to #59760. The `sign-macos` job failed at "Import certificate" (run 40599245269) with `p12Password must not be empty`.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The `release`-environment `APPLE_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE` is a .p12 with no password. `apple-actions/import-codesign-certs` v2.0.0 refuses an empty `p12-password` before it imports anything.

This PR replaces that action with a `run` step that:
- decodes the certificate into `$RUNNER_TEMP`
- creates `build.keychain` with a random password
- imports the certificate with `-P ""`
- sets the key partition list
- adds the keychain to the user search list
- deletes the temporary .p12

The secret is passed through `env:`. I kept the keychain name `build.keychain` because `sign-cli-macos.sh` and `sign-desktop-macos.sh` look up the identity with `security find-identity ... build.keychain`, and `codesign` finds the key through the search list. A new `if: always()` step deletes the keychain and any leftover .p12.

`release-dry-run.yml` gets the same change. Both steps still skip when `dry_run == 'true'`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- actionlint: the same 33 findings as on `origin/dev` (unknown Blacksmith runner labels), and no new ones.
- `bash -n` passes on the new step scripts and on `.github/release/*.sh`.
- `bun run check` passes.
- Not tested on a macOS runner. No release workflow was dispatched.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): add /goal with a client-side done check
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR Refs #27167 **Alternative to #58508.** It has the same idle hook, `/goal` and TUI, with these differences: - **No new server event.** #58508 adds `session.settled`. Here clients work out "done" from data they already sync (part 2). - **No `native` flag on the `compaction` hook.** The goal doesn't add a note to compaction summaries. It relies on the unsaved reminder and on continuations restating the objective, so the plugin API change is just the `idle` hook. - **The desktop goal pill is a built-in GUI plugin** (`packages/gui-plugins/src/goal`), using the SDK's `ComposerPill` registry, instead of a custom capsule in the app. - **Leaner.** There are no storybook stories, no component test for the desktop capsule, and fewer tests. Only one of the two should be merged. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds `/goal `: the Session keeps working, turn after turn, until a reviewer decides the objective is met. Building it needed a reliable notion of "the Session is really idle", so the PR has five parts: 1. **Session `idle` plugin hook.** Lets a plugin continue a Session at the point it would go idle, inside the same execution. 2. **"Done" notifications.** Clients hold the "done" sound while a direct subagent is still running, with no new server event. 3. **`/goal` plugin.** Built-in, and it uses only public plugin APIs. 4. **TUI.** Shows the goal state under the prompt, with a dialog. 5. **Desktop.** A built-in GUI plugin shows the goal as a composer pill, with a menu. #### 1. Session `idle` hook The runner fires `idle` with `{ sessionID, background }` where a Session would otherwise go idle: work is finished and no input is pending. To keep going, a plugin admits input the normal way, for example `ctx.session.synthetic(...)`. The runner then re-checks the inbox and runs another step in the same execution. If nothing was admitted, the Session goes idle as before. Today a plugin can only react to `session.execution.succeeded` by queueing a new prompt. That has three problems: - Every round is a new busy period, with its own idle notification. - A user prompt can race the continuation. - A crash between rounds leaves nothing to resume. Deciding inside the drain avoids all three. - **`background`** lists the background shells and subagents still running for the Session or any descendant. It comes from `SessionBackground.outstanding`, which walks the in-memory job registry up the parent chain and makes no queries when nothing runs. When the Session's own shell or subagent finishes, its notice wakes the Session and the hook runs again, so a plugin that waits for it can simply return. Work a descendant owns, such as a shell a subagent left running, wakes that descendant instead, so it is listed for information only. - **When it runs.** Only when nothing is pending and the runner isn't mid-continuation. Never after an interruption or failure, or when a steer-scoped drain leaves queued input parked. It runs through `restore(...)`, so a slow hook stays interruptible. - **Moves and reloads.** A move or Location reload landing at the idle boundary no longer skips the hook: `stepped` is carried through `Moved` / `Reloaded`. - **Restarts and loop limits.** Continuations reuse durable inbox admission, so restart recovery resumes a loop that was still going. The step allowance resets at each idle boundary, so a plugin that always admits input must bound its own loop. The README says so. - **Types** are added to both the Effect and Promise plugin `SessionHooks`. #### 2. "Done" notifications Desktop and the TUI play the "done" sound on every `session.execution.succeeded`. A Session waiting on background subagents ends an execution when its turn ends, and again each time a subagent's result wakes it. So it beeps while the subagents are still working, and again for each one. The clients now work it out from data they already sync. On `session.execution.succeeded` for X, they play "done" only if none of X's direct children is `running`: ```ts data.session.family(id).some( (c) => c !== id && data.session.get(c)?.parentID === id && data.session.status(c) === "running", ) ``` `status` comes from `store.session.active`, which is set from `execution.started` and `succeeded`/`failed`/`interrupted`. - Only direct children count. A grandchild reports to its own parent, so waiting on it could mean no sound at all. - Running shells don't count, or a Session with a dev server running would never play "done". - Failed and interrupted executions still notify right away. In the TUI the check sits in the `succeeded` handler only, and `subagent_done` sounds are unchanged. - Desktop: `shell/notifications/notification.tsx`. TUI: `feature-plugins/system/notifications.ts`. Known gap: if a child Session hasn't reached the client's store yet, the check misses it and "done" plays early. That's no worse than today. A server-side event like #58508's `session.settled` is the fallback if this turns out to be too fragile. #### 3. `/goal` `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts`. The design draws on the harness notes in `specs/goal/`. The whole goal runs as **one execution**: each continuation is admitted from the `idle` hook, so the user gets one notification at the end. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Goal as Goal plugin participant Runner as Session runner participant Model participant Reviewer as Reviewer (session.generate) User->>Goal: /goal Goal->>Goal: save goal in Session metadata Goal->>Runner: kickoff (notice "Goal: ") loop until done, paused or stalled Runner->>Model: steps (tools, edits, …) Runner->>Goal: idle hook { sessionID, background } alt background subagent still running Goal-->>Runner: return (its result wakes the Session later) else Goal->>Reviewer: has the objective been met? Reviewer-->>Goal: {"verdict": …, "reason": …} Goal->>Runner: hidden continuation (on "continue") end end Runner-->>User: one execution, one "done" notification ``` ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Active: /goal Active --> Active: reviewer "continue" → hidden continuation Active --> Active: subagent running / reviewer "wait" → no-op Active --> Complete: reviewer "done" Active --> Paused: reviewer "blocked" or "paused" Active --> Paused: user stops · execution fails · 3 stalled rounds · 50 rounds Active --> Paused: no usable verdict twice · hook error · server restarted Active --> Paused: idle 30 min waiting on background work · reviewer request too large after compacting Paused --> Active: /goal resume (fresh round budget) Active --> [*]: /goal clear Paused --> [*]: /goal clear Complete --> Active: /goal ``` | | | | --- | --- | | **Reviewer** | `ctx.session.generate` runs the Session's own model on the full history, tool results included, and shares the cached prefix. It answers with one JSON line: `done`, `continue`, `blocked`, `paused` (the user asked to stop) or `wait` (offered only while the Session's own background shells run, and never for long-running servers). An unusable answer, including `wait` when it wasn't offered, is retried once. On a context overflow the plugin compacts and asks again. A second overflow in the same round pauses. | | **Continuation** | A steered synthetic message that restates the objective, wrapped in ``, plus the reviewer's reason and next step. It has no description, so timelines don't show it. User input admitted at the same boundary still goes first. | | **Progress** | A round stalls when the model made no tool calls since the last kickoff or continuation, or when the reviewer gives the same reason as the round before. Three stalled rounds in a row pause the goal with "Not making progress: ". A hidden backstop of 50 rounds catches anything stall detection misses. Neither number is shown in the UI. | | **Kickoff** | A synthetic message described as "Goal: ", so timelines show one notice row instead of the whole template. A `/goal` with attachments sends the kickoff as the user's message instead, because only a prompt carries attachments. An untitled Session is named after the objective. | | **State** | Session metadata, key `opencode.goal`, shaped by `SessionGoal.State` in `@opencode/schema/session-goal`: `{ id, sessionID, objective, status, reason, rounds, maxRounds, boot, updatedAt }`. Clients decode it with `SessionGoal.fromMetadata`. Children and forks copy metadata, so a goal only acts for the `sessionID` that set it. | | **Background work** | While one of the Session's own background subagents runs, the reviewer isn't asked. The Session's own background shells are listed for the reviewer instead of blocking, so a dev server can't stall the goal. Work owned by descendants is ignored, because it never wakes this Session. | | **Compaction** | The goal lives in metadata and every continuation restates it. After a compaction, the `context` hook adds a short reminder of the objective, which isn't saved, until a kickoff or continuation is in view again. Native compactions included. | | **Restart** | Each process has a boot ID. At startup the plugin pauses active goals from an earlier process among the 100 most recent Sessions. Any other is paused at its next idle point instead of being resumed by restart recovery. | | **Waiting** | If nothing has run for 30 minutes after an execution ended (a hung subagent, a shell that never exits), the goal pauses instead of looking active forever. A new execution cancels the wait. | | **Races** | The goal is re-read after the reviewer returns, so a `/goal pause` or `clear` sent mid-review wins. Every write the loop makes re-reads first and applies only if the goal is unchanged, so a user's command is never overwritten. User commands write unguarded. A failing hook pauses the goal instead of failing the execution. | | **Commands** | `/goal ` or `/goal ""` (replaces any earlier goal, max 4,000 characters), `pause`, `resume` and `clear`. They run immediately, even mid-turn. A bare `/goal` returns the status and usage as the command error. `opencode run` has no slash commands, so `/goal` isn't available there yet. | #### 4. TUI ```mermaid flowchart LR Plugin["goal plugin
writes metadata"] -->|session.metadata.updated| Store["client store
(now handled)"] Store --> Status["prompt footer
◎ goal · ◎ goal paused · ◎ goal met"] Status -->|click| Dialog["goal dialog
objective · pause · resume · clear"] Dialog -->|/goal pause| Plugin ``` - **Client store.** `packages/client/src/solid/data.ts` ignored `session.metadata.updated`, so metadata changed only on a full re-read. It now replaces the Session's metadata from the event. It uses `reconcile`, so dropped keys go away. - **Goal status** (`GoalStatus` in `feature-plugins/prompt/goal.tsx`, rendered by `prompt/footer.tsx`). A short item under the prompt beside the subagent/shell counts: `◎ goal`, `◎ goal paused` or `◎ goal met`. - It shows only the state; the objective is in the dialog. - Active is muted, paused uses the warning colour and met the success colour. - There's no round counter. - **Dialog.** Clicking the status opens the objective, the status and the last reason, with `p` pause, `r` resume and `x` clear depending on the status. - **Timeline.** The kickoff notice uses `◎`. #### 5. Desktop A built-in GUI plugin, `packages/gui-plugins/src/goal`, listed in `src/renderer.ts` and `src/main.ts` like the other built-ins. It contributes one `ComposerPill`, so the host renders it in the composer lane next to the activity and todo pills. The app itself has no goal code. - **Pill.** `Goal`, `Goal paused` (warning tone) or `Goal met` (success tone). - **Menu.** The objective as its heading, then the actions that apply in one row: Pause, Resume and Clear. They call `session.command` with `/goal …`, and a failure shows an error toast. Like Codex's footer and Claude Code's `◎ /goal active`, the reviewer's reason isn't shown; a bare `/goal` returns it. - **SDK and host.** `ComposerPillView` gains `actions` (`ComposerPillAction`): buttons the host draws in one row at the bottom of the pill's menu, as menu items so the keyboard still reaches them. A long `title` made the menu heading run past the window, so the host now wraps it to three lines and truncates. Both are documented in the SDK, and `plugin-host.spec.ts` covers actions. - **State.** Read from the session's metadata in the client store with `SessionGoal.fromMetadata`, so a goal copied from a parent isn't shown. The host shows no pills in a subagent's session. - **Strings.** The plugin's own `i18n/en.ts`. #### Not in this PR - A configurable reviewer model. It currently uses the Session's model. - A token budget. - Check-ins during long waits. - `toolChoice: "none"` for `session.generate`. The reviewer request still carries the Session's tools; the prompt says not to call them. ### How did you verify your code works? **Idle hook** (`packages/core/test/session-runner.test.ts`): - Input admitted from the hook runs a second request in the same execution, for both `resume: false` and `resume: true`. - The hook fires only once the Session would go idle, not between tool steps. - `background` holds the Session's own and its descendants' background work, and not another Session's. - A background notice re-runs the hook. - A move at the idle boundary still fires the hook once at the destination. **Done notifications** (the TUI's `notifications.test.ts`): - A parent succeeds while a child runs: no sound. - The last child goes idle, then the parent succeeds: one sound. - A running grandchild doesn't hold the parent back. **`/goal`** (`packages/core/test/plugin/goal.test.ts`, 14 full-stack scenarios against TestLLM, plus `goal-watchdog.test.ts`): | Scenario | Expectation | | --- | --- | | continue, then done | One execution. Kickoff is a "Goal: …" notice. The continuation is hidden and carries the reason and next step. Complete after 1 round. | | same reason repeated / rounds without tool calls | Paused: "Not making progress: …" | | tool calls and a new reason each round | Keeps going | | two unusable verdicts | Paused | | background subagent running | Reviewer not asked until the subagent's notice wakes the Session | | grandchild subagent or a subagent's shell running | Reviewer still asked; `wait` isn't offered and counts as unusable | | user stops the Session | Paused, "Stopped by the user" | | goal from an earlier process (at idle and at startup) | Paused, not continued | | child created while the goal is active | Copied goal ignored | | `/goal pause` during review / after the loop decided | The user's pause wins | | compaction while active | The next request carries the unsaved reminder, placed before the user's prompt | | reviewer overflows once / twice | Compacts and completes / pauses | | idle past 30 minutes (TestClock) | Paused; a new execution cancels it | | `pause` / `resume` / `clear` | Fresh budget on resume; `clear` keeps other metadata keys | Each guard fails its test when removed. **Clients:** - `solid-data.test.ts`: a metadata update that drops a key removes it. - `prompt-footer.test.tsx`: - the footer shows `◎ goal` muted, with no objective or round counter; - it opens the dialog on click and turns warning when paused; - it ignores a goal copied from a parent. - I drove the real TUI against this branch with `opencode-drive`: `/goal`, a hidden continuation, met, the dialog, then a second goal stopped with Esc and paused. **Checks** after rebasing onto `dev`: - `bun run check` passes. - `lint:changed` is clean. - The affected core, client, TUI and app suites pass. ### Visual A looping animation for the desktop app's "What's new" dialog. GitHub only shows its source.
SVG source ```svg ```
### Screenshots / recordings **TUI.** Real TUI and server from this branch, driven with `opencode-drive`; only the model and reviewer replies are scripted. The recording shows `/goal`, a continuation, met, the dialog, then a second goal stopped with Esc. | | | | --- | --- | | **Start:** `◎ goal` under the prompt, at the right.
| **Long output:** the status stays and the continuation adds no row.
| | **Met.**
| **Click the status:** objective, status, reason and actions.
| | **Stopped with Esc:** the goal pauses.
| | **Desktop.** The built-in GUI plugin's composer pill, rendered by the real window host. | | | | --- | --- | | **Active**
| **Paused**
| | **Met**
| **Long objective** wraps to three lines
| | **Light theme**
| | ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(plugin): let composer pills render their own popover content
prs.body:
Stacked on #59437, targeting `client-done-check`.

Lets a composer pill render its own popover content instead of adding more declarative fields to the view. The host keeps the pill and the overlay; the plugin owns only what's inside, like every other slot.

### SDK (`packages/plugin/src/gui/registries.ts`)
- Remove `ComposerPillAction` and `ComposerPillView.actions` (added in #59437, never shipped).
- Add `ComposerPill.menu?(input: ComposerPillMenuProps): JSX.Element`, where `ComposerPillMenuProps` is `ComposerPillProps` plus `close()`.
- `menu` lives on the pill rather than the view: `show` re-runs whenever its inputs change, so a render function on the view would remount the content on every goal update. On the item it renders once per open and updates through its own reactivity, like `Slot.render` and `Panel.render`.
- When a pill has `menu`, clicking it opens the popover and the view's `rows` / `run` are unused. The capsule stays locked to `label`, `icon`, `tone` and `title`.

### Host (`packages/app/src/session/composer/plugin-pills.tsx`)
- A pill with `menu` opens a Kobalte `Popover` (as the todo pill does), not `Menu`, because arbitrary content does not belong in a menu's keyboard model. The host renders the heading (`title ?? label`, three lines max) and the panel chrome, then the plugin's content, untracked and inside the plugin's existing `Contribution` error boundary.
- The rows path goes back to dev's behavior, except for the three-line heading from #59437.

### Goal plugin
- Pause/resume/clear are now `@opencode/ui` `Button`s in the goal's `menu`. Each one closes the popover and then sends the command.

### Tests
- Restored the existing composer pill story to dev's version and added a story covering `menu`: the host heading, the plugin content, `menu` winning over `rows`, `close()`, and a fresh render on reopen. Making `close` a no-op makes the new story fail.

### Checks
- Typecheck for `plugin`, `gui-plugins` and `app`
- `bun run lint:changed`
- `script/sdk-docs.ts`
- `plugin-host.spec.ts -g "composer pill"`: 2 passed

I haven't checked the goal popover visually against a real session.

Requested by: @neriousy (Filip via Slack)

prs.title: chore(deps): bump zod to 4.6.7
prs.body:
Bumps zod from 4.1.8 to 4.6.7 in the root workspace catalog (used by `packages/core` and `packages/console/app`). The lockfile only updates the top-level zod entry; the nested 4.6.7 copies under astro, `@astrojs/sitemap` and `@modelcontextprotocol/*` now dedupe to it. zod 3.x users are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(app): keep the inbox Working shelf in a stable order
prs.body:
The Working shelf in the Inbox sidebar reordered on almost every streamed message. It inherited the inbox's newest-`time.updated`-first sort, and the server bumps a session's `time_updated` on every message event, so running sessions kept trading places.

The shelf now keeps arrival order. On first paint, sessions that are already working keep the current order. A session that starts working is added at the bottom. Once a row is on the shelf, it stays in place until its run ends or it moves to Needs attention. If it starts working again later, it goes back in at the bottom.

- `arrivalOrder` (new, `inbox-order.ts`) keeps the previous keys that are still present, then appends new keys.
- `SidebarInbox` stores the Working key order in a memo that receives its previous value, and builds the section from that order. The other sections are unchanged.

Testing:
- `bun test … src/shell/titlebar/inbox-order.test.ts` (4 pass)

- `bun run lint:changed`: clean. CI's lint runs on every touched file, so this also clears two older findings in `inbox.tsx`: a missing blank line before `return` in `DeleteDialog`, and the `status() as Exclude<…>` assertion. That assertion is now a narrowed `statusLabel` helper.

prs.title: fix(codemode): fail fast instead of hanging when a script awaits a promise that can never settle
prs.body:
**Code Mode no longer hangs forever when a script awaits a promise nothing can resolve.**
Code Mode has no timers, so a model that wants to sleep writes `await new Promise(r => r)`. That promise can never settle, and the session sat stuck until someone interrupted it. Long tool and browser calls are not affected: anything still running keeps the program alive.

❌ **Before**
1. The script awaits a hand-made promise whose resolver is never called.
2. No tool call or other work is running, so nothing can ever settle it.
3. ❌ `execute` waits forever: no error, no timeout (core sets none).

✅ **After**
1. The script awaits a hand-made promise whose resolver is never called.
2. The interpreter sees that every part of the program is waiting on another part and no tool call or host work is running.
3. ✅ `execute` fails right away: "The program awaited a promise that can never settle: nothing else is running. Timers aren't available, so don't sleep or wait on a hand-made Promise." with the line of the `await`.

The Code Mode prompt also gains one line: no `setTimeout` or sleep, and never await a hand-made Promise to wait.

```diff
  await promise:
-   wait until it settles
+   mark this job as waiting on the promise
+   if every live job is waiting on something unsettled and no tool call or host work is running:
+     fail the program with the deadlock error (program code can't catch it)
+   wait until it settles
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `await new Promise(r => r)` after a tool call | ❌ hangs | ✅ fails at once, line 2 |
| Same inside an async function, a returned promise, `Promise.all`/`race`/`any`, `.then` | ❌ hangs | ✅ fails at once |
| `return f()` where `f` awaits a never-settling promise | ❌ hangs | ✅ fails at once, points at the `await` inside `f` |
| `try { await new Promise(() => {}) } catch {}` | ❌ hangs | ✅ fails, not swallowed |
| Hand-made promise resolved later by a tool call | ✅ works | ✅ works |
| `Promise.race([never, toolCall])` | ✅ works | ✅ works |
| Async generators and chained `.then` over tool calls | ✅ works | ✅ works |

The deadlock tests hang (time out) without the change; the 3 no-false-positive tests pass both ways. Code Mode: 1424 pass, 0 fail.

👀 **Read:** `Pending.block` and `Pending.check` in `promises.ts`. Every job that runs program code or a tool call is tracked while it lives; waits on a promise, resolver or generator register a "still blocked?" check that reads the target's state directly, so a job that was just woken never counts as blocked. Tool calls and host work never register, so anything in flight keeps the program alive. `Promise.all`/`race`/`any` register one check for all members on the combinator's job. The rest is routine.

Follow-up, not in this PR: a default wall-clock timeout for `execute`. It's left out on purpose because long browser and tool calls are legitimate; a CPU-spinning loop (`while (true) {}`) still has no limit unless `limits.timeoutMs` is set.

<sub>🔍 Seen in real use: a Code Mode script that awaited a never-resolved Promise after `browser.tabs.open` hung the session · no public issue · reviewed by openai/gpt-6.1-sol before push (one finding, a lost location for nested awaits under `return f()`, fixed with a test)</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test` in `packages/codemode`: 1424 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test test/promise.test.ts -t "deadlock detection"` with the source change stashed: 5 fail (5 s timeouts), 3 pass
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/codemode`: no type errors
- `bun test test/codemode/catalog.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 18 pass

</details>

prs.title: fix(changelog): keep line breaks in code blocks
prs.body:
Fenced code blocks on `/changelog` rendered on a single line. The `main code` rule sets `white-space: nowrap` for inline code, and it also applied to `<pre><code>`, so the lines in the v2.2.0 `diff` block were joined and the line widened the page.

This change adds two rules:

- `main pre code { white-space: pre; }` keeps the line breaks.
- `main pre { overflow-x: auto; margin: 0 0 12px; }` scrolls long lines inside the block instead of the page and matches paragraph spacing.

No syntax highlighting is added.

Verification: I rendered the current `CHANGELOG.md` through the worker's `handle()` at 1280px and 390px in dark mode. The diff block shows four lines, and the `<pre>` scroll width equals its client width at both sizes. `bun test` and `bun typecheck` pass in `services/changelog`.

prs.title: fix(update): only apply minimum versions on stable channels
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue; follows today's dev update loop.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`selectArtifacts` honored a `minimum = 1` row on any channel. Dev (and beta) build numbers reset, so a legacy dev minimum such as `0.0.0-dev-20000` compared as newer than current builds like `0.0.0-dev-18952`. Clients were served the minimum on every check and kept "upgrading" to a build they had already passed.

Minimums now only apply on `latest`, the only stable channel (`allowedChannels` publishes to `dev`, `beta` and `latest`; `next` is an alias for `beta`):

- Lookups ignore minimum rows outside `latest`, so a stray row can't cause a loop.
- `POST /admin/minimum` returns 400 when setting a minimum outside `latest`. Clearing still works, so stray rows can be removed.
- The admin page only shows "Set minimum" for `latest` rows, and still shows "Clear minimum" on any row that has one.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `services/update/test/index.test.ts`: a dev minimum above the active build is ignored, and the admin endpoint rejects a dev minimum. Both fail without the fix. The existing minimum-selection test now runs on `latest`.
- `bun test` and `bun typecheck` in `services/update`, and `bun run check` from the repo root.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally

### Issue for this PR

N/A. Moves macOS signing to the new credentials in the `release` environment.

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The `sign-macos` job now reads the Apple credentials stored in the `release` environment instead of the old repo-level secrets. It already runs with `environment: release` whenever it isn't a dry run.

- Certificate import: `secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE` with `p12-password: ""`. The new .p12 has no password, and `apple-actions/import-codesign-certs` v2.0.0 passes the value straight to `security import -P`, so `-P ""` works.
- Notarization: `secrets.APPLE_NOTARY_KEY`, `vars.APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID` and `vars.APPLE_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`. `.github/release/sign-desktop-macos.sh` still writes the .p8 to a temp file for `xcrun notarytool --key`; I only renamed its env vars to match.

These old secrets are no longer read on `dev`: `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY`, `APPLE_API_KEY_PATH` and `APPLE_API_ISSUER`. The desktop electron-builder config doesn't sign or notarize, so it needed no change. `v1`'s `publish.yml` is untouched; it already prefers the new names and falls back to the old ones.

- Create, install and share [Desktop plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui) (experimental) ([#55246](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55246), [#59469](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59469), [#59489](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59489))

- Plugins can now attach and update keyed session instructions with ctx.session.instructions.entry.put/list/remove. Instead of editing the system prompt and busting the prompt cache, each change is added as a small update at the next step. The entries also survive compaction and reverts, and they don't start an extra model turn. ([#56550](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56550))
- Restored the Todo tool in desktop via opt-in ([#59092](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59092))
- Add configurable prompt cache TTLs per provider/model ([#59157](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59157))

### Breaking changes

#### `@opencode/ai` root is now the Promise API

`@opencode/ai` now works like `@opencode/sdk` and `@opencode/client`: the package root exports the Promise API, and the Effect API moved to `@opencode/ai/effect`. `@opencode/ai/promise` is removed, and the wildcard subpath export is replaced with an explicit list of provider and protocol entry points. ([#58847](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58847), [#59183](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59183))

```diff
-import { AI } from "@opencode/ai/promise"
-import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { AI } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai/effect"
```

#### The OpenCode GitHub Action is removed

The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published. Remove it from your workflows. ([#59032](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59032))

#### TUI plugins require OpenTUI 0.7

`@opencode/plugin` now requires `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.7.0, up from 0.6.8 or later. Plugins that depend on OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install until they upgrade. In OpenTUI 0.7, custom renderables read their hooks from their class at construction: assign `renderBefore`, `renderAfter`, and `onLifecyclePass` in the constructor instead of as class fields, call `refreshHooks()` after adding a hook by reflection, and replace `defineNativeIntegration()` with a `static nativeIntegration` declaration. See the [OpenTUI 0.7.0 release notes](https://opentui.com/docs/releases/0.7.0). ([#59295](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59295))

issues.title: Gemini strict tool schemas: optional parameters fail with "didn't specify the schema type field"

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
AI-assistance note: the issue body was drafted with an AI agent on my machine, then reviewed and verified by me. All experiments and data above come from my own testing.

## What happened

With any Gemini 3+ model on the `google-generative-ai` api, a request with tools that have optional parameters fails before the first token:

```
Unable to submit request because `read` functionDeclaration `***.limit` schema didn't specify the schema type field.
```

`read` (offset, limit) and `bash` (timeout) are enough to trigger it. Reproduces on 1.4.0 with `pi -ne` (no extensions), custom provider with `api: "google-generative-ai"`, model id `gemini-4-argon`.

The id matches `^gemini-(\d+)` with 4 >= 3, so `supportsGoogleStrictToolSampling` is true and `makeStrictJsonSchema` emits this for every optional property, adding it to `required`:

```json
{ "anyOf": [ { "type": "number" }, { "type": "null" } ] }
```

Gemini rejects a node whose only type sits in an `anyOf` branch named `null`, and nothing retries with non-strict tools.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a provider with `"api": "google-generative-ai"` and a model whose id starts with `gemini-4` (or `gemini-3`).
2. `pi -ne --model provider/model --tools read "read the first line of README.md"`
3. 400 before any output.

Same endpoint, raw request, tool with one optional number property:

| property schema sent | result |
| --- | --- |
| `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"null"}]}` | 400, didn't specify the schema type field |
| same plus top-level `"type":"number"` | 400 |
| same through legacy `parameters` instead of `parametersJsonSchema` | 400 |
| `{"type":"null"}` | 400 |
| `{"anyOf":[{"type":"number"},{"type":"string"}]}` | 200 |
| `{"type":["number","null"]}` | 200 |
| `{"type":"number","nullable":true}` | 200 |

The endpoint is real Gemini: an invalid type value returns `Invalid value at '...type' (google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.Type)`.

## Expected behavior

Optional parameters should reach Gemini in a form it accepts (`type: ["number","null"]`, or `nullable: true`), or the request should retry once with preferred tools non-strict, the way the Anthropic provider does after a strict-schema rejection. #11325 already rewrites `const` to `enum` on this same `parametersJsonSchema` path.

I can test a patch on this setup if that helps.

issues.title: durable bash tool reports grep/rg/diff exit 1 (no match) as an error

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

In `packages/durable`, the bash tool reports exit status 1 from search/diff tools as a hard error:

```ts
// src/tools/bash.ts
const exited = { severity: "error", code: "exit_code", message: `Command exited with code ${exitCode}` };
return { structuredOutput, isError: true, diagnostics: [exited] };
```

`grep`/`rg` exit 1 means "no match"; `diff`/`cmp` exit 1 means "differences found". Both are normal results, not failures.

### Why?

It's not cosmetic in a harness. The model sees this for a successful search:

```
[error] Command exited with code 1
```

and reacts as if the command broke — retries, changes approach, or tells the user the command failed. We hit this repeatedly in real sessions, e.g. `grep -n "function line(" file` (pattern genuinely absent) shown as an error, and `ls | grep -i bash` (no such test file) likewise. Anything that greps for an optional pattern does it.

### How? (optional)

Capture the command that actually ran (the `for (const command of commands)` binding is out of scope after the loop), and classify exit 1 as a result **only** for a single simple command:

- reject anything the shell could compose: `; | & `` ` `` `$(` `)` `<` `>` newline — in a compound command the status belongs to the last word, so the head name proves nothing;
- skip leading `VAR=value` assignments, take the command head (basename);
- if head ∈ {grep, egrep, fgrep, rg, ag, diff, cmp} and status is 1 → `severity: "notice"`, message `Command exited with code 1 (no matches or differences)`, `isError: false`.

Everything else keeps today's behaviour, including exit 2+ from those tools.

Patch and a regression test are ready locally; `test/tools.test.ts` passes (36 passed, 1 skipped). Happy to open a PR if you'd like it. Say the word and I'll also relax `isError` to stay `true` if you'd rather not change failure semantics — the message hint alone already fixes the confusion.

Version: `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.4.0, macOS, Node 26.

issues.title: codemode: `describeOutput` prints the full type for union output schemas, so one tool adds about 8k characters to every request

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

With `codemode.mode: "on"`, each declared tool's description gets a line saying what a script call resolves to. For an object output schema, `describeOutput` shortens this to field names via `describeFields(schema, 1)`. For a union (`anyOf`) output schema, `describeFields` returns `undefined`, and `describeOutput` falls back to the entire `renderToolOutputType(schema)` string, flattened onto one line.

A tool with a union output schema therefore puts its whole output type into the prompt. That text is sent with every request, in every session that declares the tool.

## Observed

- Pi 1.4.0, with `@aliou/pi-processes` 0.13.2 installed and `codemode.mode` left at the default `on`.
- The `process` tool's `outputSchema` is `Type.Union([...])` with 7 action variants (start, list, stop, write, update, clear, output), defined in `extensions/processes/tools/schema.ts:322`.
- In the system message recorded in the session file, `process`'s description is **8,112 characters, and 8,004 of them are the `Codemode: \`tools.process(args)\` resolves to ...` suffix.** The suffix includes nested `@integer` and `@maxLength` annotations and the comment text from the schema.
- That one suffix is about 11% of the entire startup prompt in my setup (about 71.6k characters across the system sections and tool declarations).
- By comparison, `bash`, which has an object output schema, gets a 114-character suffix: `` `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }` ``.

## Where

`packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/tool.ts`, unchanged on `main` as of 24382bed:

```ts
function describeOutput(schema) {
	const type = renderToolOutputType(schema);
	if (type === "string") return "a string";
	const fields = describeFields(schema, 1);           // undefined for anyOf/oneOf
	return `\`${fields ?? type.replace(/\s+/g, " ")}\``; // full rendered type
}
```

## Suggested fix

Give unions the same field-name summary objects already get. For `anyOf`/`oneOf` where every variant is an object, list each variant with `describeFields(variant, 0)` joined by ` | `. If the variants share a `const` field, such as `action`, it could lead each entry:

```
`{ action: "start", notify, process } | { action: "list", counts, filters, processes } | ...`
```

That would be about 300–400 characters instead of 8,000. For any other schema that `describeFields` can't summarize, a short fallback, such as "`an object; see describeTool(\"process\")`", would keep this from recurring, since `describeTool()` already returns the full declaration when a script needs it.

There's no per-tool setting to turn the suffix off. The only workaround is `codemode.mode: "only"`, which changes how every tool is presented.

issues.title: Compaction/summarization requests share no prefix with live turns — every compaction pays a full prefill

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make compaction/summarization requests share the token prefix of the live conversation instead of starting from scratch: pass the session's system prompt and tool declarations to the summarizer and replay the conversation messages as-is, appending one user instruction ("summarize the conversation above"). Today every summarization call serializes the conversation into a fresh `<conversation>` prompt with a fresh system prompt and no tool declarations, so it shares zero prefix with the turns that produced it. Legacy path stays for callers that want it.

### Why?

On any provider with prefix caching (Anthropic, local vLLM APC, ...) the summarizer call pays a full prefill of the whole history on every compaction — minutes at 100k+ context. Measured on a local vLLM endpoint (Qwen3.8-27B, APC on): a forced compaction issued a summarizer request with **0 cached tokens**; replaying messages + session system prompt + tools turned that into **+2048 cached tokens** with behavior unchanged (summary quality same, the tool-call guard still applies). Tool declarations matter because provider chat templates render them into the system block — omitting them breaks prefix sharing even with identical messages.

Same root cause as #9411 (branch summaries). #9773 means this can't be worked around from an extension today, since `before_provider_request` never fires for summarization.

### How?

Optional trailing `systemPrompt` / `tools` parameters on `compact()` / `generateSummaryWithUsage()` / `generateTurnPrefixSummary()` (+ the branch-summary call, which would fix #9411 in the same stroke); `AgentSession._runDefaultCompaction()` passes `this.systemPrompt` and `this._getCallableTools()`. Legacy behavior is byte-identical when the params are omitted.

Implementation is written and tested on my fork (branch `prefix-preserving-compaction`, PR #11499 — auto-closed before I understood the gate, sorry): unit tests for both paths, all 46 existing compaction tests pass, cache-hit metrics verified live. I'll extend it to branch summaries and reopen the PR if you approve.

issues.title: pi-durable: make extension start a task on each turn without a tool call

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I'm not sure if I'm missing an existing pattern, so this is partly a question.

I'd like an extension to start its own task on every turn, with the same lifecycle as manual compaction: conversation-owned, cancelled by `abort()`, included in idle waits. As far as I can tell, extension code can only create tasks from a tool's `execute` or from another task. Hooks can't commit, and `conversationCreated` is host-only.

### Why?

Example: run the project's tests after each turn that edited files. The conversation should stay busy until they finish, Stop should cancel them, a restart mid-run should resume, and the result should be saved for the UI and the next turn. A task fits all of that, but:

- A tool only runs if the model calls it.
- `onYield` runs before the answer is committed, so a long test run delays it, and a hook can't save the result.

Today the host has to create the task itself, but this does not give the users of such hosts the power to create similar extensions themselves.

In `packages/durable/src/codemode/codemode.ts`, import `toCodemodeIdentifier` from `@earendil-works/pi-codemode/declarations` instead of `@earendil-works/pi-codemode/portable`. The other names imported from `/portable` in that file are types and can stay as an `import type`.

The extension receives its sandbox through `CodemodeToolOptions.sandbox`, so it never needs the VM itself. A host that supplies its own `CodemodeSandboxBase` still gets the WASM runtime in its module graph. We run Code Mode scripts in a native QuickJS engine inside a React Native app and currently patch this import.

[describe.ts](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/58c0b02ce552adab76014e7ed712ab7981359aa8/packages/durable/src/codemode/describe.ts#L9) in the same directory already imports `toCodemodeIdentifier` from `/declarations`, which re-exports the same function from `identifier.ts`.

issues.title: pi-durable: let durable tasks keep the conversation busy
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Kinda related to my previous #11141. I'd like a way for a task to keep the conversation busy (no new input while it runs).

My use case: at the end of a turn, I want to create a task that captures a git checkpoint snapshot of the whole repo. This task has two requirements:

1. It can't be cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, otherwise it could produce corrupted snapshots
2. It has to keep the conversation busy: users shouldn't be able to prompt while it runs, because a new turn could write files mid-snapshot.

I can't find a way to do this in the current durable. The naive way to check whether a session is busy is to look at `live.run`: if it's defined, the session is busy (no more messages allowed); if it's undefined, it's idle.

This works fine, but tasks don't change `live.run`; only generation tasks do. So one could think: "I'll make my host's busy check look at both `live.run` and foreground (`background: false`) tasks". Only foreground, because background tasks should in fact stay in the background and not block. Then I'll create my checkpoint task as foreground.

This could work, but it raises two issues:

1. Foreground tasks are always cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, with no way to opt out. I could live with that and make the checkpoint task handle its own abort.
2. It breaks manual compaction. Manual compaction should run in the background, yet it should be cancellable. How should it be classified? If it's `background: false`, then to keep conversing while it compacts, the busy check must NOT look at foreground tasks, otherwise the session is marked busy and you can't continue. If it's `background: true`, it's no longer cancelled by `abort()`, and idle waits stop including it.


### Why?

Without this, a host has to enforce busy itself while such a task runs, and other clients or extensions on the same session don't see it.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

issues.title: fix(ai): recognize LiteLLM ContextWindowExceededError in isContextOverflow
issues.body:
### What happened?

When routing requests through a LiteLLM proxy, context window overflow errors return HTTP 400 with the following message format:

```text
400: {"message":"litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: litellm.BadRequestError: litellm._pre_call_checks: Context Window exceeded for given call. No models have context window large enough for this call.
Model=Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Max Input Tokens=262144, Got=265262
model=Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. context_window_fallbacks=None. fallbacks=[]."}
```

In `@earendil-works/pi-ai` (`src/utils/overflow.ts` / `dist/utils/overflow.js`), `isContextOverflow()` checks `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`.
The current patterns match Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, etc., but do not match LiteLLM's `Context Window exceeded for given call` or `litellm.ContextWindowExceededError`.

Because `isContextOverflow()` returns `false`, `AgentSession` treats this as a fatal 400 Bad Request error instead of context overflow. As a result, the automatic compaction and retry recovery (`_runAutoCompaction("overflow", willRetry)`) never triggers, causing the session / subagent to crash immediately.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an LLM provider via LiteLLM proxy (where LiteLLM enforces `max_input_tokens`).
2. Run a turn or continuous tool-use loop until input tokens exceed LiteLLM's `max_input_tokens`.
3. LiteLLM returns HTTP 400 with `litellm.ContextWindowExceededError`.
4. Observe that `isContextOverflow()` returns `false` and the run crashes with an unhandled 400 error instead of automatically compacting and retrying.

### Expected behavior

`isContextOverflow()` should identify `Context Window exceeded for given call` / `ContextWindowExceededError` as a context overflow, allowing `AgentSession` to perform automatic overflow compaction and retry the request transparently.

Suggested regex patterns in `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`:
```ts
/Context Window exceeded for given call/i,
/ContextWindowExceededError/i,
/Max Input Tokens=\d+, Got=\d+/i,
```

### Version

0.112.0 / @earendil-works/pi-ai 1.4.0

issues.title: Preserve hard line breaks and soft-wrap semantics for accurate TUI selection copy

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I would like pi-tui to preserve line-boundary semantics through rendering and copying, so mouse selection can join soft wraps introduced by viewport width while retaining hard line breaks from the source content.
#506 describes this symptom, and #7721 attempted to track soft wraps with invisible markers. I understand the compatibility and risk concern raised when that PR was closed: custom components would also need to understand and propagate those markers.
I would therefore like to suggest a different direction: optional semantic selection metadata kept separate from display strings. Built-in components such as `Text` and `Markdown` could provide it, while components without it would naturally retain the current copy behavior. This could solve the hard-break/soft-wrap problem without requiring existing custom components to understand hidden markers.

### Why?

I can reproduce this in Kitty, Alacritty, and Ghostty: copying a response wrapped because of viewport width inserts extra newlines into the clipboard. This does not appear to be specific to one terminal.
The distinction still exists inside `wrapTextWithAnsi()`: it first separates source newlines, then creates visual wraps with `wrapSingleLine()`. However, it ultimately returns only `string[]`, so that boundary information is lost. Fullscreen selection copy later reconstructs the result with:
```ts
const text = lines.join("\n");
```
Every visual row therefore becomes a hard line break. `/copy` preserves the original full assistant message, but cannot copy an arbitrary mouse selection. The public extension API also has no access to transcript selection coordinates or the built-in copy reconstruction path.

### How?

One possible design is optional selection information associated with each visual line, for example:
```ts
interface SelectionLineProjection {
  text: string;
  joinerToPrevious?: string;
  selectableColumns?: { start: number; end: number };
}
```
The joiner could preserve a real `"\n"`, omitted whitespace, or `""` for a continuous soft wrap such as a long token or CJK text. Layout, clipping, and scrolling would propagate this sidecar without interpreting it, and fullscreen selection copy would use it to reconstruct selected text. Lines without a projection would fall back to the existing visual-row behavior.

issues.title: Allow `watchEvents` in pi-durable resume from the last seen entry
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide the ability for `watchEvents` to resume from a previously seen point by passing an entry id as a "last seen" argument .

When provided the returned `snapshot.entries` holds only the active entries with a higher ID, and includes `snapshot.after` to confirm this is a resumed stream. The rest of the snapshot (including partial message, tools, inbox, agent, usage) are still sent in full.

The client drops its entries before the marker's `head`. If the "last seen" is an unknown value the snapshot is returned in full without the `after` key.

### Why?

If a client disconnects or goes offline, on reconnection it would be ideal to only have to stream the events that happened since the reconnection rather than retransmitting the full stream.

This can be implemented in user land by discarding the earlier events but ideally it'd be built in.

### How? (optional)

Something like:

```ts
const stream = await watchEvents(harness, id, context, { after: lastSeenId });
```

Entries are already stored with increasing IDs. So ideally we'd check the `after` value then filter `snapshotOf(view).entries`.

An example of an expected stream including compaction.

 Fresh stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx)`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 180, "kind": "pi.user", "model": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Fix the flaky login test" }] },
       { "id": 181, "kind": "pi.assistant", "model": [{ "role": "assistant", "content": [ … ] }] },
       // … 30 more entries, 182–211 …

       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],
     "run": { "inputs": [41] },
     "generation": { "attempt": 1, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The test fails because" }] } },
     "tools": [], "nestedTools": [], "compactions": [], "inbox": [],
     "agent": { … }, "usage": { … }
   }
 ```

Resumed stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx, { after: 212 })`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "after": 212,
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],

   [{ "type": "message_update", "usage": { … }, "changes": [{ "type": "text_delta", "contentIndex": 0, "delta": " expires mid-test." }] }]

    { "type": "turn_end" }, { "type": "run_end", "inputs": [41] }, …]
 ```

issues.title: `pi update` misdetects vite+ installs as npm and creates a second global install

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

When pi is installed via [vite+](https://viteplus.dev) (VoidZero's toolchain package manager), `pi update` detects the install method as `npm` and runs an npm global install — producing a second, divergent `pi` installation instead of updating the existing one.

## Reproduction

1. Install pi via vite+, which places it at:
   `~/.vite-plus/packages/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/<id>/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/`
2. Run `pi update`.

**Expected:** pi detects that the install is not managed by npm and either updates via vite+ or prints the manual-update instructions.

**Actual:** `pi update` runs an npm global install, creating a second `pi` in npm's global prefix. The vite+ copy (the one on PATH) is untouched.

## Cause

`detectInstallMethod()` infers the install method purely from path substrings:

```ts
resolvedPath.includes("/npm/") || resolvedPath.includes("/node_modules/") ? "npm" : ...
```

Any package manager that keeps an npm-compatible layout (`lib/node_modules/...` under its own root) matches the `/node_modules/` branch — vite+, and likely others. The subsequent npm-prefix inference then targets npm's global prefix, not the actual install root.

(Related: #7756 covers the same bug class for pnpm.)

## Suggested fix

Check for a manager-specific path segment (e.g. `/.vite-plus/`) or marker file before the generic `/node_modules/` fallback, and treat unrecognized managers as `"unknown"` (manual update message) rather than assuming npm. A conservative variant: only classify as `npm` when the resolved path sits under npm's actual global root (`npm root -g` / prefix), not merely any `node_modules` directory.

## Environment

- pi: latest (installed via vite+)
- OS: Linux

In `codemode`, spend `inlineBudget` on tool names and descriptions instead of inlining full TypeScript declarations, and degrade tools past the budget to name-only (`- \`name\``) instead of dropping them.

### Why?

A single extension with ~13 `codemode` tools already exhausts the 3000-token `inlineBudget` on every turn because each entry inlines its full TypeScript input/output schema. Any tool that does not fit the budget is dropped without even its name, so the model cannot tell it exists.

For reference, OpenAI's [Tool Search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) keeps a deferred function's `name` and `description` visible upfront and only defers `parameters`:

> For an individual deferred function, the model still sees the function name and description, so in practice tool search is mostly deferring the parameter schema.

And Claude Code's `ToolSearch` lists all deferred tool names upfront (one per line, no schemas) and loads schemas on demand:

```text
The following deferred tools are now available via ToolSearch. Their schemas are NOT loaded — calling them directly will fail with InputValidationError. Use ToolSearch with query "select:<name>[,<name>...]" to load tool schemas before calling them:
mcp__slack__list_channels
mcp__slack__post_message
```

### How? (optional)

PoC in https://github.com/astrosheep-zero/pi/pull/2 — the diff is tiny (~12 lines in `packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/tool.ts`, net -1 line).

issues.title: Preserve system updates in the retained context after compaction

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Keep system messages in their original positions within the retained range: from `firstKeptEntryId` up to, but excluding, the compaction entry.

### Why?

I understand that [#9548](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9548) intentionally folds pre-compaction system updates into the checkpoint. I propose revisiting this specifically for updates within the retained range, where their order relative to retained messages can matter.

For example, an extension switches a session from read-only to editing. Within the retained range, the assistant first refuses to edit a config file, then edits it after a system update changes the rules and enables the `edit` tool. The current compacted context becomes:

```text
Current implementation:
  system: editing allowed; tools = read, edit [checkpoint]
  summary
  user: update the config                    [first kept]
  assistant: I cannot edit the config
  user: try again
  assistant: edits the config
```

The original session entries remain intact, and the final state is correct. What is lost in the model-visible context is the timing of the system update relative to the retained messages. Editing appears to have been allowed throughout the retained history, making the change in behavior harder to interpret.

### How? (optional)

Move the checkpoint's reference point from the time of compaction to immediately before `firstKeptEntryId`. Store the complete prompt and tool state there, then retain the subsequent system updates in order:

```text
Proposed change:
  system: read-only; tools = read             [checkpoint]
  summary
  user: update the config                     [first kept]
  assistant: I cannot edit the config
  system: editing allowed; add edit tool      [retained update]
  user: try again
  assistant: edits the config
```

The final replayed prompt and tool state should match the current implementation. Models that support mid-conversation system messages should see the updates in order; other models should continue to receive the collapsed current state.

I would like to implement this change if the maintainers agree with the direction.

issues.title: tui(latex): display math wider than the content width is wrapped line-by-line, destroying the 2D layout
issues.body:
### What happened?

Display math is laid out as several 2D rows. When that layout is wider than the Markdown content width, `render()` word-wraps each row independently, so fractions/matrices split and the equation stops lining up. Same for `$$…$$` and `\[…\]` blocks.

### Steps to reproduce

No extensions (`pi -ne`); reproduced by rendering the Markdown component directly at content width 30 (the layout below needs 31 columns):

```latex
\[
\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{i^2} + \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx
\]
```

Actual — bottom row torn off, `dx` pushed between rows:

```text
 ∂² u   ∂² u   n   1   1
 ──── + ──── = ∑   ── +∫ f(x)
 dx
 ∂ x²   ∂ y²  i=1  i²  0
```

### Expected behavior

Keep the block intact, or fall back to the raw LaTeX when it does not fit — never split one layout row from its siblings. In `packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts` the `latexBlock` branch emits the rows and `render()` wraps every non-image line with `wrapTextWithAnsi`; passing the content width into `renderLatex` (returning `undefined` when the layout overflows) would reuse the existing raw fallback.

### Version

1.4.0 (macOS arm64, Arch Linux x86_64)

issues.title: Startup notification storm: one 'No models match pattern' notification per stale enabledModels entry

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

At startup, Pi fires **one standalone warning notification per stale `enabledModels` entry** that does not match any registered model. With 100+ accumulated entries this produces a 300+ notification storm that makes the desktop unusable until the cycle finishes. The storm repeats on every restart.

## Environment

- Pi 1.4.0 (Linux, x86-64, `pi` ELF binary)
- Model provided by an **extension-registered provider** (`venice` provider via a custom extension that registers a runtime catalog from the Venice `/models` API)
- `settings.json` (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`) with `enabledModels` containing 104 entries

## Repro

1. Use an extension that registers a provider + virtual model with a **live model catalog** (models change over time).
2. Over time, `settings.json`'s `enabledModels` accumulates entries from every catalog enumeration (104 entries on my machine: `venice/*` ids that no longer exist in the current catalog, plus leftover `radius/*` and `opencode/*` entries from other providers that aren't even loaded).
3. Restart Pi.

**Actual**: 300+ notifications, one per non-matching pattern, each reading `Warning: No models match pattern "[model]"`. There is no way to quell the cycle; it delays/denies useful startup until it drains. The agent (OpenBot on `pi --mode rpc`) is rendered unusable during the storm.

**Expected**: entries with no matching model are skipped silently, or at most produce **one aggregated warning** listing the unmatched patterns. A settings list should not generate one OS notification per entry.

## Root cause observation

The binary emits a distinct `warning` diagnostic per pattern:

```js
const noMatch = (pattern) => diagnostics.push({
  type: "warning",
  code: "no-match",
  message: `No models match pattern "${pattern}"`,
  pattern
});
```

Each diagnostic is surfaced as its own notification at startup, with no coalescing or cap.

## Suggested fix

- When resolving `enabledModels` / `--models` scopes, treat unmatched patterns as a single warning (e.g. "No models match patterns: a, b, c (N total)"), or skip them quietly — a scope is a preference, not an error.
- Consider capping or rate-limiting startup warnings per session.
- Optionally: do not persist every catalog model into `enabledModels` as a saved pattern; store only user-selected models.

## Workaround

Prune `settings.json` → `enabledModels` to only the actively used model:

```json
{ "enabledModels": ["venice/jev"] }
```

Also related: `--models` scope patterns resolve per provider and warn on ambiguity ([#10160]), but that path at least emits a single warning — the startup enabledModels path does not coalesce at all.

## Impact

Any user of an extension-registered provider with a changing catalog (Venice API is an example) hits this. It is a quality-of-life regression that turns every restart into a notification denial-of-service.

issues.title: Resume drops all built-in tools when the session branch is truncated (orphan parentId after ENOSPC)
issues.body:
**Version:** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0 (latest release at the time of writing), Windows. Anthropic provider, several extensions (pi-hashline-edit-pro, @ff-labs/pi-fff, @tintinweb/pi-subagents, pi-mcp-adapter). `defaultTools`: `read, bash, powershell, edit, write, grep, find, ls, codemode, tool_search`.

### What happened

1. In a long session the disk filled up. `appendFileSync` in the session persist path (`dist/core/session-manager.js:812`) threw ENOSPC for one entry. `_appendEntry` (`session-manager.js:815-819`) had already put that entry into `byId` and `leafId`, so the process kept running, and the next persisted entry references a parent id that is not in the file. In my file entry `49231a1f` has `parentId: "29d71f0c"`, which does not exist, and carries `errorMessage: "ENOSPC: no space left on device, write"`.
2. After later restarts, `getBranch()` (`session-manager.js:1062-1072`) walks from the leaf and stops at that orphan. The branch no longer contains the initial system message with the full tool loadout, only three later system patch messages.
3. `_restoreToolsFromTranscript` (`dist/core/agent-session.js:1389-1412`) rebuilds the loadout only from the system messages on the branch (`getCurrentTools(systemMessages)`), and excludes built-in tools from the "new tools" (`!this._baseToolDefinitions.has(name)`, line 1405). The comment on line 1404 says "Built-in tools follow `defaultTools` instead", but `defaultTools` is not applied on this path. The `compaction.systemMessage` checkpoints on the branch, which still declared `read`/`bash`, are not consulted (comment, lines 1391-1392).
4. Result: on the first prompt after the restart, Pi persisted a system message whose `toolsRemoved` lists `read, bash, powershell, write, grep, find, ls, codemode, tool_search`. Only extension tools stayed active. The next compaction checkpointed the reduced set. Because the removal is now recorded, a plain restart and `/reload` keep these tools inactive ("Removed tools stay inactive", line 1399). The model silently lost its shell and file reading in the middle of a long session.

### Expected

Any of:
- seed the restore from the latest `compaction.systemMessage` on the branch, which holds the full loadout;
- when the branch has no initial/full declaration, fall back to `defaultTools` for built-ins, as the comment on line 1404 says;
- surface and retry persist failures, or detect an orphaned `parentId` on load instead of silently truncating the branch.

### Workaround

From reading the code, not verified yet: `pi --session <id> --tools +read,+bash,+powershell,+write,+grep,+find,+ls,+codemode,+tool_search`. `applyToolModifiers` runs after the replay (`agent-session.js:1407`), and a list of only `+name` entries modifies the default selection (`docs/cli.md`, `--tools`).

### Related

#11376 (removing an initial tool mid-session), #10785 (tool restore on resume).

issues.title: Nested executeTool calls can survive parent cancellation with an explicit signal

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Clarify whether parent cancellation should always propagate through `ctx.executeTool()`, even when the caller supplies an explicit `AbortSignal`. In Pi 1.4.0, `options.signal ?? signal` replaces the parent's signal; current main does the same.

### Why?

A permission extension can revoke approval and abort the owning operation, yet a pending nested action can still start afterward.

Reproduction: invoke a nested builtin write or harmless custom tool with an independent signal; pause a downstream `tool_call` handler; cancel the parent via `ctx.abort()`; release the handler. The nested action executes. Without the explicit signal, it is cancelled.

### How? (optional)

If detaching cancellation is not intentional, combine parent and explicit signals with `AbortSignal.any`, preserving the nested call's own cancellation/timeout. Otherwise, what is the supported way for a permission extension to revoke a pending nested call?

An isolated SDK-copy experiment changed only this signal expression: four failing cancellation cases became green; 24 synthetic native-dispatch cases and eight signal-contract checks passed. This is not a full upstream-suite or CLI-bundle validation. I can provide a focused fix and regression test once the intended contract is agreed.

issues.title: Bedrock: request fails when tools have more than 16 optional parameters
Built-in OpenCode model catalogue ships retired models as free-model baseline

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Pi ships a built-in OpenCode model catalogue that is used as the baseline for
free OpenCode models (e.g. `pi-opencode-direct` registers its free models from
"Pi's built-in OpenCode catalogue"). That catalogue contains model ids that
OpenCode's backend no longer serves, so the models appear selectable but fail at
request time with `Model is unavailable` / `deprecated`.

## Evidence

As of 2026-10-27, the live endpoint `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/models`
returns only a subset of the ids present in Pi's built-in OpenCode catalogue.
Examples that ship in the built-in catalogue but are rejected by the backend:

- `exo-free` → `Model exo-free has been deprecated.`
- `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free` → `Upstream request failed: Model is unavailable.`
- `cat-jam-free`, `space-bunny-free`, `step-5-preview-free`,
  `longcat-2.5-preview-free`, `minimax-m3.1-flash-free`,
  `nemotron-3-ultra-free` → same family of errors.

Verified with `opencode run --model opencode/<id> "Reply with exactly: OK"`.

The live endpoint is the availability truth; the built-in catalogue behaves as
a stale snapshot. Consumers (gentle-shell, pi-opencode-direct, etc.) keep
offering these dead models in `/model`.

## Suggested fix

Prune the built-in OpenCode catalogue against the live `/models` endpoint at
generation time, or mark entries as unavailable/retired so downstream consumers
can filter them out.

## Impact

Low severity (requests fail fast), but it makes the model picker misleading and
breaks automation that iterates the catalogue. Workaround used locally: gate the
picker on an explicit live-derived allowlist.

issues.title: openai-responses: other models' function_call items are replayed without namespace, OpenAI 400s
issues.body:
> Written by an AI agent (Claude Code) working for me. It reproduced this live against api.openai.com.

### What happened?

When tools are declared through `additional_tools` (the `"changes"` tool-support mode), OpenAI puts each tool in a namespace named after the tool. Its own `function_call` items come back with `"namespace": "<tool name>"`.

`convertResponsesMessages` keeps `namespace` only when `isSameModel` is true (`packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts:387` and `:396`). So a history where another provider called a tool (DeepSeek, Anthropic, ...) replays that call without one. OpenAI then rejects the whole request:

```
400 Missing namespace for function_call 'read'. It does not exist in the default namespace.
Round-trip the model's function_call item with its namespace field included. (param: input[8].namespace)
```

The effect is that any switch to a Responses model that supports `additional_tools` (seen with `gpt-5.4-mini`) fails once the conversation holds another model's tool call.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a conversation on a non-OpenAI model that calls a tool.
2. Switch it to `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` with the same tools and send the next turn.
3. The request carries an `additional_tools` item plus a `function_call` with no `namespace`, and gets a 400.

### Expected behavior

A replayed call from another model whose tool was declared via `additional_tools` gets `namespace: <tool name>`. I tried this on the exact failing request body, setting `namespace = name` on the foreign `function_call` items: OpenAI accepted it and the model went on to call `read`.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-ai 1.4.0, also present on main at d5b3de2.

Happy to send a PR if this direction looks right.
