issues.title: A lightweight entry point for defining extensions for pi-durable
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a subpath export, such as `@earendil-works/pi-durable/extension`, that exports the extension-authoring helpers (`defineDoc`, `defineExtension`, `hook`, `ToolTask`) and their types. It should not load the session runtime, storage or model code.

### Why?

These helpers are only on the root export, and importing the root loads the whole runtime. In 1.4.0, a module that only defines an extension pays about 180 ms and 742 modules for that one import. On Cloudflare Workers this cost hits every cold start. The package already has narrow subpaths (`./codemode`, `./env`, `./tools`, `./storage/*`, ...), so this fits the existing pattern.

Repro (Node 24, pi-durable 1.4.0):

```sh
npm i @earendil-works/pi-durable@1.4.0
node --input-type=module -e "const t=performance.now(); await import('@earendil-works/pi-durable'); console.log(performance.now()-t)"

# 513.1185280000001 (no disk cache)
# 165.471654
# 214.493499
# 185.04169
```

### How? (optional)

A new entry module that re-exports only the authoring helpers, plus an exports entry for it. Type-only imports stay as they are.

I’d be happy to implement this myself and open a PR if the subpath name and export set work for you.

issues.title: OpenCode Go: send x-opencode-session from a conversation lineage id

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`StreamOptions.sessionId` is currently the only value pi-ai sends as `x-opencode-session`. OpenCode's own client sends something different there: an id that groups one conversation's requests for cache routing (its "affinity"), which for a child session is the *parent's* id, while the child's raw id travels in a second header, `x-opencode-session-id`.

Reference, from OpenCode's client:

- `SessionAffinity.get()` — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/session/affinity.ts#L5-L8 — "children share the parent's, forks the fork source's"
- the per-request header set — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts#L276-L293
- the Go docs that spell out the requirement — https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/console/go.mdx (see "Where can I use it?" and "Validated Clients")

Proposal: add `StreamOptions.sessionAffinity?: string`, defaulting to `sessionId`, and send it as `x-opencode-session` on the OpenCode providers (plus `x-opencode-session-id` from the raw `sessionId`).

### Why?

A child conversation inherits its parent's message history: a subagent starts from a prefix of the parent, and a forked branch is a copy of it. If the child reports its own id as the session header, that identical prefix lands in a different cache bucket and gets served cold again, which is exactly the cost the header exists to avoid. OpenCode solves this by reporting the tree root as the affinity and keeping the raw id in a separate header.

OpenCode is the reference client for the Go subscription, so matching its header semantics is the correct thing for pi-ai to do — a Go gateway cannot tell a child from an unrelated conversation otherwise.

This is also not specific to one host: any client whose sessions form a tree needs an id that groups the tree, while still identifying the individual session. pi-ai already has the affinity vocabulary (`sessionAffinityFormat`, `sendSessionAffinityHeaders`); the only missing piece is a way to supply the affinity value instead of deriving it from `sessionId`.

### How? (optional)

- `packages/ai/src/types.ts`: `sessionAffinity?: string` on `StreamOptions`, next to `sessionId`. Absent means today's behavior, so nothing changes for existing callers.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/opencode-headers.ts`: `const affinity = options.sessionAffinity ?? options.sessionId`, send `x-opencode-session: affinity` and `x-opencode-session-id: options.sessionId`; caller-supplied headers keep winning, as they do now.
- Optional follow-up: use the same value for the `openai` / `openrouter` affinity formats and for `src/utils/identity.ts` custom endpoints pointing at opencode.ai.
- Tests: extend `packages/ai/test/opencode-provider-headers.test.ts` with the override, the fallback, and the preserved caller header.

I have this change working against 1.3.0 locally and can open a PR if the direction is acceptable.

---

Drafted with an agent from my notes; I reviewed it and stand behind the technical claim.

prs.title: feat(compaction): prefix-preserving summarization calls
prs.body:
## Problem

Every compaction/summarization call today serializes the conversation into a fresh prompt (`<conversation>…</conversation>` + `SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT`) and sends it **without tool declarations**. The resulting request shares no token prefix with the regular turns that produced the conversation, so on any provider with prefix caching the summarizer call pays a full prefill of the entire history (at a 100k-token context that is minutes of prefill at typical prefill rates). Tool declarations are also rendered into the system block by most provider chat templates, so omitting `tools` alone would break prefix sharing even with an identical message list — this was caught by measuring `prefix_cache_hits` deltas against a local vLLM endpoint with APC enabled.

## Change

Add optional trailing `systemPrompt?: string` and `tools?: Tool[]` parameters to `compact()`, `generateSummaryWithUsage()` and `generateTurnPrefixSummary()`. When provided, the summarization request:

- replays the conversation messages **as-is** (no re-serialization),
- uses the **session's own system prompt and tool declarations**, so the rendered system block is byte-identical to regular turns,
- appends exactly **one** user instruction (the existing summarization prompt + previous summary, if any).

When the parameters are omitted (all existing callers), the legacy path runs unchanged — the diff is fully backward compatible.

`AgentSession._runDefaultCompaction()` now passes `this.systemPrompt` and `this._getCallableTools()`.

## Verification

- New unit tests (`test/compaction-prefix-preserving.test.ts`): legacy path keeps the fresh serialized prompt; prefix-preserving path carries the session system prompt, tools and conversation messages with the instruction appended as the last user message; previous-summary merging lands in the instruction.
- Existing compaction suites: 46 passed, 0 failed.
- Measured end-to-end against a local vLLM endpoint with prefix caching enabled (Qwen3.8-27B, MTP, `--prefix-match-unit 512`): the summarizer call during a forced compaction went from **0 cached tokens (legacy)** to **+2048 cached tokens (prefix-preserving)**, while the post-compaction turn remains the expected single cold start (the history is replaced by the summary).

## Notes

- The instruction is appended as a plain user message; the existing "Summarization attempted to call a tool" guard still applies, and the model is instructed not to continue the conversation.
- A follow-up worth considering: a replay-based invariant checker (session log → outgoing requests) — during verification of this change it confirmed the projection is byte-reproducible and caught a tools-declaration mismatch that message-only comparison missed.

## Summary

The docs refresh (#9898) cut `docs/extensions.md` from about 3,100 lines to 130, dropping API reference and tool guidance. #11039 restored part of it. This PR restores the full guide and corrects it against current source.

- **Structure:** the original sections, with the ASCII lifecycle diagram replaced by three Mermaid diagrams (run, turn, session) and ordered hook lists, plus a handler composition table.
- **Merged:** content added after the cut: tool exposure, calling other tools, structured output, MCP servers, `registerToolRenderer`, virtual models, `provider_stream_event`, `before_agent_start` `messageType`.
- **Corrected:** removed or renamed APIs (`modelRegistry.stream()`, prompt sections are `<tools>`/`<rules>`, `builtin:read` paths, `highlightCode`), wrong behavior claims (errors only by throwing, `model_select` on restore, `sendUserMessage` always triggering a turn, override warning, `truncateLine` bytes), examples that did not type-check, links to removed `tui.md` patterns and `rpc.md` anchors, and wrong API lists in the examples table.
- **Kept:** anchors that other docs and changelogs link to, as `<a id>` tags.
- **Fixed example:** `reload-runtime.ts` tool queued `/reload-runtime` with `deliverAs: "followUp"`. Queued text reaches the model as a plain user message, so the command never ran and Pi never reloaded. prs.title: fix(ai): detect LiteLLM ContextWindowExceededError as context overflow
prs.body:
LiteLLM's pre-call context check rejects requests that are too large with HTTP 400 and a message like:

```
litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: litellm.BadRequestError: litellm._pre_call_checks: Context Window exceeded for given call. ... Max Input Tokens=262144, Got=265262 ...
```

None of the `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` matched this wording, so `isContextOverflow()` returned false. As a result, the agent session never ran overflow compaction and retry, and the turn failed with the 400 error.

This change adds `/context window exceeded/i` to `OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` and documents the error in the doc comment that lists providers.

Testing:
- Added a regression test in `packages/ai/test/overflow.test.ts` with the exact error message from the issue. It fails without the pattern and passes with it.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/overflow.test.ts` in `packages/ai`: 32 passed.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Running `isContextOverflow()` directly on the reported message returned `false` before this change and returns `true` after it.

Fixes #11492

prs.title: fix(env): include stderr in pi-env startup errors
prs.body:
When the daemon exits before `hello`, the error has only the exit code. For example, with `loginShell: true` and a profile that aborts on a missing file:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
```

`sshConnection`'s probe and deploy steps already report ssh's stderr, so this is about the launch itself: a login profile, a daemon that can't execute, or a `Connection` created with its own command, which has no probe or deploy step, so auth and network errors also end up here.

This keeps a short stderr tail until `hello` and adds it to startup errors:

```
pi-env exited with code 3 before it was ready
remote stderr:
profile: /opt/toolchain/env.sh: No such file or directory
```

The tail is capped at 20 lines / 2000 chars, with terminal escapes and control characters stripped. Ready sessions are unchanged.

I hit it while testing `loginShell` against an sshd in Docker. Tests are in `test/connection.test.ts`, and `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass.

prs.title: fix(tui,coding-agent): handle selection page keys in all scrolling lists
prs.body:
Fixes #7629. Supersedes #7680 by @muyiyr (co-author): same approach, rebased on current `main`, narrowed in scope, with a generic fullscreen capture flag instead of a page-key-specific one.

## Problem

`tui.select.pageUp` / `tui.select.pageDown` are configurable, but most lists ignore them:

- `SelectList` (slash commands, file autocomplete, theme/thinking pickers) and `SettingsList` (`/settings`) do not handle them.
- Editor autocomplete forwards only up/down to its list.
- Model, scoped models, auth, user message, llama search, and `/mcp` selectors have their own navigation without page keys.

In fullscreen mode there is a second problem: `tui.altScreen.pageUp/pageDown` default to the same keys and always scroll the transcript, so even a list that handles the keys never receives them.

With the remapping from the issue (`"tui.select.pageDown": "ctrl+v"`), Ctrl+V in an open autocomplete menu also pastes an image, because `app.clipboard.pasteImage` runs first.

## Changes

- `getSelectPageIndex()` (pi-tui): returns the index one page up/down, clamped to the list bounds. Used by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, and the coding-agent selectors. Page keys clamp at the ends; up/down keep their existing wrap behavior.
- `Component.capturesViewportInput?: boolean`: while a component that sets it has focus, fullscreen viewport keys go to it instead of the transcript, the same rule focused overlays already follow on `main`. Transcript search and mouse wheel are unchanged. Set by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, `Editor` (only while autocomplete is open), and the scrolling coding-agent selectors (session/tree selectors not while renaming or editing a label).
- `CustomEditor`: while autocomplete is open, page keys reach the menu before app actions, following the existing precedence exception for history keys.

Not set on `ctx.ui.select`, trust, first-time setup, and thinking selectors: they show every option, so there is nothing to page, and the transcript stays scrollable while answering an extension prompt (see #10769).

## Behavior change

In fullscreen mode, PageUp/PageDown (and the other viewport keys) move an open list or autocomplete menu instead of scrolling the transcript. Outside fullscreen mode, default bindings behave as before.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Other selection keys vs app actions while autocomplete is open, e.g. `tui.select.up` remapped to Ctrl+P still cycles the model (#2133, #10408).
- `/resume` checks `app.session.*` before selection keys.
- Remaining hardcoded keys and key hints (scoped models Escape/Ctrl+C, `pi config` Ctrl+C, synthetic Enter in searchable submenus).
- #4748: extensions using their own pi-tui copy see default keybindings.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- pi-tui: `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, editor autocomplete, and `TuiAltScreen` capture tests (all `node --test` pi-tui tests pass)
- coding-agent: model selector with remapped Ctrl+V/Alt+V, `CustomEditor` Ctrl+V paging vs image paste, `/mcp` menu capture

prs.title: fix(tui): fall back to raw LaTeX when display math is wider than the content width
prs.body:
Display math (`$$…$$`, `\[…\]`) renders as several 2D rows: numerator, fraction bar and denominator are separate lines. When the layout was wider than the Markdown content width, `render()` wrapped each row with `wrapTextWithAnsi` on its own. Only the overflowing row broke, so the rows below moved down and the equation no longer lined up. For example, `dx` landed between the fraction bar and the denominators.

The `latexBlock` case in `Markdown.renderToken()` now checks the rendered layout against the available width. If any row is too wide, it uses the raw LaTeX source, the same fallback already used when parsing fails. The raw source then wraps like normal text. Layouts that fit render exactly as before.

**Testing**
- Added a regression test in `packages/tui/test/markdown.test.ts` using the equation from the issue. At width 40 it renders the 2D layout unchanged. At width 30 it falls back to the raw `\[ … \]` source, with no fraction bars and no line wider than 30. The test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `node --test test/markdown.test.ts`: 93 pass. `node --test test/latex.test.ts`: 111 pass.
- `npm run check` reports no errors in the touched files. The only errors are 6 type errors in `packages/ai/test`, caused by stale generated model data, and they are the same on `main` without this change.
- Reproduction at width 30, before the fix:
  ```
  ∂² u   ∂² u   n   1   1
  ──── + ──── = ∑   ── +∫ f(x)
  dx
  ∂ x²   ∂ y²  i=1  i²  0
  ```
  After the fix, the raw source, wrapped:
  ```
  \[
  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial
  x^2} + \frac{\partial^2
  ...
  \]
  ```

Fixes #11483

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep session memory in line with the file when a write fails
prs.body:
When writing a session entry failed (ENOSPC, EBUSY, ETIMEDOUT on network drives), `SessionManager._appendEntry` had already added the entry to memory and made it the current leaf. The process kept running, and the next entry written to disk pointed to a parent that was not in the file. On resume, pi follows the history only back to that gap: everything before it disappears. In #11460 that also dropped the first system message, which declares the tools, so resume turned off every built-in tool.

`_appendEntry` now undoes the in-memory append if writing fails, then rethrows. The error reaches the caller as before; later entries chain to the last entry actually on disk.

Reports of this problem:
- #11460: ENOSPC; resume dropped all built-in tools.
- #10166: failure injected with EBUSY; the next entry on disk points to a missing parent.
- #10661: ETIMEDOUT on Windows + NFS; resumed sessions showed only the last few messages. That report also describes NUL holes in the file, which this change does not address.

**Testing**
- Two tests in `test/session-manager/file-operations.test.ts` make writes fail with real file permissions: a read-only session file (failed append) and a read-only session directory (failed first file creation). They check that the entry is not kept, the leaf is unchanged, the next entry chains to the last written one, and the reopened session's branch contains both entries. Both fail without the change and pass with it.
- `test/session-manager/` and `test/default-tools-setting.test.ts` pass (140 tests).
- `npm run check` passes.

Fixes #11460

Requested by @davidbrai

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): pass thinking level to branch summarization
prs.body:
The `/tree` "Summarize" option ignored the session's thinking level. `AgentSession` already passes `thinkingLevel` into the `generateBranchSummary` options, but `generateBranchSummary` never read it, so the request was built without `reasoning`.

For reasoning models on OpenAI Responses and Azure Responses, a missing `reasoning` becomes `effort: thinkingLevelMap.off ?? "none"`. Models that don't accept `"none"` then reject the branch summary with a 400 error:

```
Unsupported value: 'none' is not supported with the 'gpt-6-astra-…' model.
```

This change adds `thinkingLevel` to `GenerateBranchSummaryOptions`. It sets `reasoning` on the request when the model supports reasoning and the level is not `off`, the same rule compaction uses in `createSummarizationOptions`.

**Testing**
- Added a test to `packages/coding-agent/test/branch-summarization.test.ts` that records the stream options for three cases: a reasoning model at `xhigh`, a reasoning model at `off`, and a non-reasoning model. The expected `reasoning` values are `["xhigh", undefined, undefined]`. Without the fix, the test fails and every case gets `undefined`. With the fix, it passes.
- Ran `branch-summarization`, `agent-session-branching`, `branch-summary-extensions` and `compaction-summary-reasoning`: all pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Not tested against a real provider endpoint.

prs.title: perf(tui): skip grapheme segmentation when painting the scrollbar
prs.body:
Issue: #11461

`replaceScrollbarCell()` asked for the grapheme at the bar column with `getGraphemeCellRange()`, which runs `Intl.Segmenter` over the whole row, then sliced the row twice more. That runs once per row and per frame while the scrollbar is visible.

Measured with the shipped `renderLayoutFrame`, 300 messages in a 110x55 viewport, one line scrolled per frame, scrollbar in `auto`:

- bar visible: 3.98 ms per layout frame
- bar hidden: 0.07 ms per layout frame

A terminal row is almost always printable ASCII that ends exactly on the bar column: cell N is the N-th printable character, the replaced cell is one character, and there is no tail to keep. `plainAsciiWidth()` recognises that case and one pass builds the row, carrying the codes seen before the cell so the row background stays under the bar. Every other row keeps the general path unchanged.

After: 0.13 ms per layout frame, with byte-identical frames over 600 compared frames (plain text, CJK/emoji/tabs/hyperlinks, widths 37/60/110, plus rows with backgrounds, hyperlinks, and rows longer or shorter than the viewport).

A test covers the background-under-the-bar case in `packages/tui/test/layout.test.ts`. `node --test test/layout.test.ts` passes and `npm run check` exits 0.

Inline `ctx.ui.custom()` components never report pi as blocked through OSC 7501 program status. This is on purpose, because the same API hosts loaders. As a result, a custom dialog that waits for the user (an approval prompt, the `question.ts` example) shows up as `working`, and the terminal cannot tell that pi needs input.

The extension dialog stack already stores a blocked status for each dialog and reports the visible one. This change adds an optional `blocked` option to `ctx.ui.custom()`:

ctx.ui.custom(factory, { blocked: { kind: "question", message: "Pick a color" } });

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): hidden thinking with an empty label renders no rows
prs.body:
When thinking was hidden and the hidden-thinking label was set to `""` (for example with `ctx.ui.setHiddenThinkingLabel("")`), every assistant message that contained thinking still drew blank rows:
- thinking followed by a tool call drew 2 blank rows;
- thinking followed by text drew 3 blank rows before the text.

`AssistantMessageComponent.updateContent()` had three causes:
- It counted hidden thinking as visible content when deciding on the leading and trailing spacers.
- It always added the label component. With an empty label the theme's escape codes are still there, so the component rendered one blank row.

**What changed**
- A hidden thinking run with an empty label is now skipped entirely. Its run index is still advanced, so click overrides on other runs keep their indices.
- Spacers are now added lazily, just before the next visible block. The result is the same as before: one spacer before the first visible block, and one after a visible thinking run that is followed by more visible content. But spacing now follows what actually renders.
- Default behaviour (the "Thinking..." label, or expanded thinking) is unchanged.

- Added two tests to `test/assistant-message.test.ts`:
  - a hidden thinking run with an empty label renders nothing, both before a tool call (`[]`) and before text (`["", "answer"]`);

- `npm run check` passes. The `test/assistant-message.test.ts` and `test/interactive-mode*` tests pass.
- Rendering the component directly, with hidden thinking and an empty label:
  - thinking + tool call: before, 2 blank rows; after, `[]`;
  - thinking + text: before, 3 blank rows then the text; after, `["", " hi"]`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): skip npm audit and fund output when installing pi packages
prs.body:
`pi install`, `pi remove` and `pi update --extensions` run npm without `--no-audit`, so npm prints its "N vulnerabilities … run `npm audit fix`" advice after every install. pi gives users no way to clear that warning, and following it causes harm. In `~/.pi/agent/npm`, `npm audit fix` runs without `--legacy-peer-deps`, so npm installs the host-provided `@earendil-works/pi-*` peers there: a second copy of pi. The comment above `getNpmInstallArgs` warns against exactly that.

The change adds `--no-audit --no-fund` wherever pi already passes `--legacy-peer-deps` to npm:
- `getNpmInstallArgs` (npm package installs and updates)
- `getGitDependencyInstallArgs` (dependency installs for git packages)
- npm uninstall

pi's managed self-update (`runManagedNpmCi`) already passes both flags. bun and pnpm arguments are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(tui): recognize kitty F1-F12 sequences and ignore F13+ keys
prs.body:
With the kitty keyboard protocol active, these function keys were not recognized:
- F1, F2 and F4 arrive as `CSI P`/`Q`/`S`, or as `CSI 1;<mod> P/Q/S`.
- Any F-key pressed with a modifier, e.g. `CSI 15;5~` for Ctrl+F5.

`matchesKey` returned false whenever a modifier was set and only compared against the legacy sequences. `parseKittySequence` did not know any F-key forms. So shortcuts bound to keys like `f1` or `ctrl+f5` never fired.

Separately, F13–F35 (and other kitty functional keys) arrive as CSI-u codepoints in the Private Use Area. `decodeKittyPrintable` returned them as text, so the editor inserted invisible U+E020+ characters into the prompt.

Changes in `packages/tui/src/keys.ts`:
- Add F1–F12 internal codepoints. Map `~` numbers 11–15, 17–21, 23 and 24 to them.
- Parse the `CSI [1;mod[:event]] P/Q/S` form. F3 is left out because `CSI 1;<n>R` collides with cursor position reports, so kitty sends F3 as `CSI 13~`.
- Let the `f1`…`f12` cases in `matchesKey` fall back to `matchesKittySequence` so modifiers work. Name the keys in `parseKey` output.
- Make `isKeyRelease` and `isKeyRepeat` recognize `:3`/`:2` events on P/Q/S, so F1/F2/F4 releases don't trigger shortcuts a second time.
- `decodeKittyPrintable` now rejects the kitty functional-key PUA range (57344–63743). Keypad keys are normalized to ASCII first, so they still decode.

Testing:
- Added tests in `packages/tui/test/keys.test.ts`. They cover kitty F1–F12 with and without modifiers, F3 not being confused with a cursor position report, release and repeat detection, and F13+ not decoding as text. Two of the new tests fail without the change; all pass with it.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep open extension dialog visible when the editor component is replaced
prs.body:
`ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()` always cleared the editor slot and put the new editor there with focus. If an extension dialog (`confirm`/`select`/`input`/`editor`, or an inline `custom()` component) was open at that moment, the editor replaced it on screen. The dialog was still on the dialog stack and its promise still pending, but nobody could see or answer it. It hung until its timeout, or forever without one.

Now `setCustomEditorComponent` leaves the editor slot and focus alone while a dialog is open. The new editor is still created and wired up, and `showTopExtensionDialog` shows it when the last dialog closes. Without an open dialog nothing changes.

Testing:
- Added a regression test to `test/interactive-mode-extension-dialogs.test.ts`. It opens a confirm, replaces the editor, then checks that the confirm stays visible and answerable and that the new editor is focused afterwards. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Ran the reproduction from the issue in tmux (`pi -e ./a.ts -e ./b.ts`, where a.ts opens a non-blocking `confirm` in `session_start` and b.ts calls `setEditorComponent`).
  - Before: only the editor shows, and the confirm times out.
  - After: the confirm shows, and Enter gives `answer: true`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep grep context lines aligned with ripgrep when a file has a lone CR
prs.body:
When `context` is set, the grep tool reads the file again to print the lines around each match. It turned CRLF into LF and also turned every lone CR into LF before splitting the text into lines. ripgrep, which supplies the match line numbers, counts lines only at LF. A lone CR therefore added an extra line on pi's side, so every later line was off by one.

For example, in a file containing `before\rprogress\nneedle\nafter`, a search for `needle` with `context: 1` showed `progress` as the line-2 match and left out `after`.

The fix keeps the CRLF normalization and splits only on LF, so pi numbers lines the same way ripgrep does. Displayed lines already have `\r` removed, so the line before the match now shows as `beforeprogress`.

**Testing**
- Added a test in `packages/coding-agent/test/tools.test.ts` for a file with a lone CR searched with `context: 1`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `test/tools.test.ts`: all 87 tests pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Reproduction from the issue. Before the fix:
  ```
  f.txt-1- before
  f.txt:2: progress
  f.txt-3- needle
  ```
  After the fix:
  ```
  f.txt-1- beforeprogress
  f.txt:2: needle
  f.txt-3- after
  ```

Fixes #11398

Requested by @badlogic

issues.body:
**Context**

A widely reported third-party test this week (Cohere, on the open-weights Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with Microsoft's CTI-REALM benchmark; VentureBeat and other outlets, Oct 27–28) described a session where the model's reasoning trace stated it would not use external tools, while the runtime concurrently attempted an outbound network transfer that the test sandbox blocked. We have not independently reproduced this, and we cite it only as a public example of a general failure class: **divergence between the model's stated plan and its actual tool-call behavior**. The report is not evidence for or against any particular mitigation — the class itself is what a harness can, in principle, partially catch with deterministic rules; actual coverage is an empirical question.

**Proposal: a plan–execution delta hook**

qwen-code already ships a Hooks system and a sandbox. A small deterministic hook package could compare, per turn:

1. tools the reasoning/plan text *claims* to use vs. tools actually invoked (`function_call` events);
2. outbound network destinations attempted vs. the tool allowlist implied by the plan;
3. repeated denied/retried calls with the same tool+args signature (a persistence signature — useful as a pre-escalation signal).

Design notes: rules operate purely on the event stream (no model internals), so the approach is model-agnostic by construction. Extracting the *claimed* plan from free-form reasoning text is the hard part — we would start with conservative exact-match rules and treat ambiguous cases as no-violation (false-negative-biased by design). Verdicts are deterministic (same input → same verdict) and audit-logged; determinism is a property of the rules, not a correctness claim.

**Reference implementation**

We maintain an independent open deterministic verifier for agent action streams: github.com/PHM-Audit/phm-agent-verifier-tests — rules plus test artifacts. Across a 100k-scenario adversarial suite (per-scenario verdicts), no missed violations and no false blocks were observed, with hash-chain-verified audit logs (the chain attests log integrity, not rule correctness). That suite is not qwen-code production traffic, so we treat it as a design reference, not a benchmark claim. The delta rules above are a small subset; we would be glad to contribute them as a qwen-code hook (Apache-2.0, matching this repo's license) if maintainers find the direction useful.

*Note: harness-hardening suggestion for a model-agnostic failure class — not a claim about any specific model's intent; the cited report is third-party and unverified by us.*

### Architecture and ownership

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[WebShell / product client] -->|Product REST and SSE| J[Java control plane]
    J -->|Session / Prompt / Resume| Q[qwen serve]
    Q --> L[Legacy engine / ACP]
    Q --> H[Managed TS Harness]
    H --> M[Model service]
    H -->|Tool requests and results| B[Embedded Runtime Broker]
    B -->|Java-initiated HTTP and SSE| R[On-demand Tool Runtime]
```

The Broker is embedded in the Java service in the hosted reference deployment. `qwen serve` keeps the common Session protocol and hosts the Legacy/Managed engines; the Harness owns the single model loop, context, compaction, and tool orchestration. The Runtime owns files, Shell, and admitted tool-side effects. It receives neither the user Prompt nor model credentials. Local Managed uses a local Runtime provider and does not require Java.

Hosted deployment starts with one Java instance plus a `qwen serve` sidecar and a default Session-exclusive Runtime process/Pod; #14435 adds separately gated Workspace residency. Model inference uses a pre-published immutable AgentBundle while Runtime provisioning proceeds in parallel; only tool execution waits for readiness. Multiple Sessions may share the Harness process without sharing their model context or permission view.

### Initial release boundary

The first hosted validation slice uses a single Java/sidecar deployment, immutable published configuration, a Session-exclusive Runtime, and Read/Write/Edit/foreground Shell. Member collaboration is not a release prerequisite for this slice. Board #13928, peer messaging #13955 and plan approval #13974 have landed upstream; plan enablement and collaboration deployment promotion remain optional and behind their own acceptance gates. Approval, durable results/file history, cancellation cleanup, and safe continuation after clean Runtime reclamation remain required. Existing product SSE/history can serve this slice; the full public API, multi-instance takeover, and extension migration have separate gates.

W0 adds Workspace selection and fixed cwd. W1 restore/backfill/verified mount relocation and W2 controlled same-Workspace cwd changes have landed within their recorded boundaries. Later authorized directory creation/registration is implemented by the Workspace/SSH slices above. Arbitrary server-path registration, clone/worktree creation, and changing existing Sessions' directories are outside W0. Sessions using the same Workspace share files, so their tool turns need the existing Workspace lease/settlement discipline.

Accepted recovery/support policy for the first release is one Java control plane on one trusted Linux host, with sequential compatible Hosted Harness replacement only for supported and accepted states. Public CSI/Pod qualification, two surviving control planes and cross-host takeover retain independent gates. The experimental server/embedded-Broker archive is implemented in #14176, while publication and formal support remain separate. Parent-close active child cancellation is implemented by #14218. Stream liveness is completed by #14512 (`46bf492d05`); deployment wait/retention/capacity values still need measured acceptance.

### Acceptance criteria

- The adopted staged path-independence matrix is a release gate: Hosted proves its bounded scope with ordinary local-only state unreachable; local now requires its M6 exit acceptance under the opt-in; shared dependencies are inventoried before the run. No existing component or recovery report substitutes for this gate.
- With Runtime startup delayed by 15 seconds, published-configuration model output starts first; a no-tool Turn can finish, and a tool Turn waits and continues in the same model context.
- Sessions retain their engines after restore; a Managed failure causes no Legacy replay. Ordinary-host Legacy/Managed coexistence is an acceptance gate for local support promotion, not the first Hosted slice.
- Lost create/Prompt/execute/ACK responses resolve through original identities without duplicating side effects. Unknown outcomes remain explicitly blocked.
- Two Workspaces and different child directories execute Read/Write/Shell in the intended locations. A retry after changing defaults keeps the original binding; missing mounts or revoked access never fall back to another directory.
- Java restart and clean Runtime reclamation retain the Session binding; physical identity is verified before reuse, and old writers cannot mutate a newer binding.
- Committed SSE replay and Snapshot-plus-tail recovery preserve order without duplicate content. MQ delay cannot block local post-commit SSE; SQL unavailability is surfaced with bounded backpressure.
- Large output can be read/downloaded after Runtime cleanup. WebShell distinguishes tool outcome, partial/missing capture, delivery failure, and truncated preview; storage failure never causes tool re-execution.
- Cancellation settles admitted tools and descendant processes. Production enablement additionally requires actor/tenant isolation, capacity limits, and the fault gates for the selected deployment profile.

## Why is this needed?

Hosted execution should not make the first model response wait for a tool container. Splitting the model loop from tools, however, creates ownership and recovery boundaries: a selected directory must survive process changes, an ambiguous tool call must not run twice, and a browser reconnect must recover committed progress. Permanent per-fragment storage also grows without a retention/materialization plan, while Runtime-local output disappears when the environment is reclaimed.

This proposal joins those boundaries into one implementable contract while preserving Qwen's existing agent semantics and local deployment. It gives reviewers a scoped rollout and observable exit gates instead of treating an experimental branch or a passing component test as the finished product.

### 架构与职责

链路为：产品前端 → Java 控制面 → qwen serve → Legacy 或 Managed Harness；Managed Harness 调用模型，并通过 Java 内嵌 Runtime Broker 调用按需 Tool Runtime。Java 主动发起到 Runtime 的 HTTP/SSE。上方架构图展示同一链路。

Java 内嵌 Broker；qwen serve 保留统一会话协议与双引擎；Harness 负责唯一模型循环、上下文、压缩及工具编排；Runtime 负责文件、Shell 和已准入的工具副作用，不接收用户 Prompt 或模型凭据。本地 Managed 使用本地 Runtime provider，不依赖 Java。

托管首版采用单 Java + qwen serve Sidecar + 默认 Session 独占 Runtime 进程/Pod；#14435 增加独立门禁下的 Workspace 常驻。模型使用预发布不可变 AgentBundle，与环境启动并行；只有工具执行等待环境就绪。多个 Session 可共享 Harness 进程，但不共享模型上下文或权限视图。

### 首版范围

首版采用单实例、预发布不可变配置、Session 独占 Runtime，验收 Read/Write/Edit/前台 Shell。成员协作不作为该首版交付前置；board #13928、成员消息 #13955 与计划审批 #13974 均已在上游合入，计划启用与协作部署开放继续可选并遵循各自验收门禁；审批、结果/文件历史持久保存、取消清理、干净回收后的续轮仍是必需项。可复用既有产品 SSE/历史；完整公共 API、多实例接管和扩展迁移各有独立门槛。

W0 支持创建时选择 Workspace 并固定 cwd；W1 恢复、存量回填、可验证挂载迁移，以及 W2 同 Workspace 内受控切换目录已按各自边界合入。后续授权目录创建/注册已由上方 Workspace/SSH 切片实现。W0 不提供任意服务器路径注册、clone/worktree 创建或已有 Session 目录编辑。同 Workspace 的会话共享文件，工具轮次需要遵守 Workspace 租约与结算规则。

首版已接受的恢复/支持策略为单 Java 控制面、同一可信 Linux 主机，仅在已支持且验收的状态下顺序替换兼容 Hosted Harness。公开 CSI/Pod 资格、两个存活控制面与跨主机接管保留独立门禁。实验 Server/嵌入式 Broker 归档已在 #14176 实现，公开发布与正式支持独立。父关闭主动取消 child 已由 #14218 实现；流存活检测已由 #14512（`46bf492d05`）收尾，部署等待/留存/容量数值仍需实测验收。

### 实施顺序

A～H 是能力阶段，不是一个大改动的串行列表。A/C/E、B 中共用的 owner 与禁止回退保障，加上必要 F 验收构成首个 Hosted 闭环，不等待完整 D 或可选普通宿主 Managed 引擎的支持提升。

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| 阶段 | 交付与门槛 |
| --- | --- |
| A | 冻结身份、接口、owner 与延迟基线。 |
| B | 持久化引擎 owner，禁止运行中 fallback。双引擎宿主 B2 与 M1–M6 已实现，#14483 在 `--experimental-paired-engines` 后完成 M6 注册；#12737 已关闭，默认开放和完整本地验收仍独立。 |
| C | Broker 绑定/执行 Repository、租约、Runtime 通信及原执行查询。 |
| D | 公共 Agent API、持久准入、投影、续传与兼容客户端契约。 |
| E | Hosted Sidecar，模型与环境并行，禁止本地工具 fallback。 |
| F | 对已开放能力完成 ACK 丢失、SSE 缺口、进程崩溃、取消、输出交付及存储故障验收。 |
| G | 外置权威 Session 历史/checkpoint，先证明 fencing 和接管再取消 owner 粘性。 |
| H | H0 共用记录 → H1 MCP → H2 Hooks → H3 Shell/Monitor → H4 子 Agent/workflow/team → H5 Channels → H6 自动化。 |

Workspace 拆为 **W0a 契约/Registry → W0b 持久创建 → W0c 执行目录 → W0d WebShell → W0e 重启/回收验收**；完整输出拆为 **O1 捕获/引用契约 → O2 Hosted 持久交付和回执恢复 → O3 API/工具卡 → O4 保留清理及已准入扩展**。它们细化 A～H，不形成另一套路线图。

### 验收标准

- 已采纳的分阶段路径独立性矩阵是交付门禁：Hosted 在普通本地专属状态不可达时证明限定范围，本地路径现在需在 opt-in 下完成 M6 退出验收，运行前列出共享依赖；既有组件或恢复报告不能替代该门禁。
- Runtime 延迟 15 秒时，使用预发布配置的模型输出先返回；无工具轮次可完成，有工具轮次等待后继续同一模型上下文。
- 会话恢复后引擎不变，Managed 失败不经 Legacy 重放。普通宿主的 Legacy/Managed 共存属于本地支持提升的验收门槛，不是首个 Hosted 闭环的前置条件。
- 创建、Prompt、执行或 ACK 响应丢失时按原身份查询，不重复副作用；未知结果明确 blocked。
- 两个工作区和不同子目录的 Read/Write/Shell 位置正确；改变默认值后的重试仍保持原绑定，目录失效/撤权不回退其他目录。
- Java 重启与 Runtime 干净回收后保持 Session 绑定，复用前验证物理身份，旧 writer 不能修改新绑定。
- 已提交 SSE 与 Snapshot+tail 恢复保持顺序且不重复内容；MQ 延迟不阻塞本机提交后推送；SQL 不可用时有界背压并呈现失败。
- Runtime 清理后大输出仍可读取/下载；工具结果、部分/缺失捕获、交付失败及预览裁剪分别展示，存储失败不触发工具重跑。
- 取消能结算已准入工具并清理后代进程；生产开放前另验收 actor/tenant 隔离、容量限制及所选部署的故障门槛。

## 为什么需要

托管工具容器的启动不应阻塞模型首输出，但分离模型与工具后，目录归属、执行恢复和客户端续传必须有清晰边界：所选目录要跨进程保留，不确定的工具不能重复执行，断线客户端要找回已提交进度。永久逐片段保存会持续膨胀，Runtime 本地输出也会随回收丢失。

本提案在保留现有 Agent 语义和本地部署的基础上，把这些边界整理为可实施契约，并提供分阶段开放及可观察的验收门槛，避免把实验分支或单项测试当作完整产品。

## 补充信息

### 与现有议题的关系及仓库范围

- #11695 及 #11696/#11697/#11698 分别覆盖执行分离、凭据边界、环境资源化；本提案补 Managed Session 的集成与发布契约，保留这些独立范围。它不预设上游 core 接受托管 Java 控制面；上游协议/runtime 改动与 hosted reference 的代码归属需要分别评审。
- #11868 的 event/journal 外置对应 G 的权威存储，区别于 Java 公共事件/Item 投影及可选 MQ。
- #3803 继续跟踪 daemon 总体演进，本提案保留统一 Session 协议和渐进迁移路径。

2. **首版与生命周期：** 保留普通工具、W0 固定绑定和各能力门禁；单 Java 控制面/同一可信 Linux 主机仍为首版支持边界。父 CLOSE/DELETE 方案 B 已由 #14218 实现，#13875 已关闭；G3 首版恢复已实现，#12952 的双存活 owner/跨主机阶段和 #14481 剩余矩阵仍开放。D7 input/cancel 已由 #14470 提供 opt-in `java_durable`，默认仍是 Harness-confirmed。

4. **路径独立性，验收仍欠：** 固定 engine owner、不运行时 fallback，不要求跨引擎迁移 Session。M6 已实现，本地一行转为可以开展自身验收，不再因缺少注册而阻塞。

issues.title: CI: Integration Tests (no-AK, No Sandbox) fails at Checkout with "fatal: pack has 1 unresolved delta"

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/development
labels.description: Development experience

labels.name: scope/ci-cd
labels.description: Continuous integration/deployment

issues.body:
## What happened?

During the CI run for PR #13815 (head `d80f16c277`, run [38198248458](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38198248458)), the `Integration Tests (no-AK, No Sandbox)` lane (job key `integration_no_ak` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job [114645716645](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38198248458/job/114645716645)) failed at step 4, `Checkout`. The pinned `actions/checkout@v6.0.3` call (`fetch-depth: 1`, ref `refs/pull/13815/head`) retried the fetch three times within roughly 30 seconds; every attempt failed identically:

```text
fatal: pack has 1 unresolved delta
fatal: fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output
The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128
```

Timestamps: 2026-10-12 03:04:01Z, 03:04:14Z, 03:04:30Z (UTC). All subsequent steps (Node setup, dependency install, and the actual `test:integration:no-ak:sandbox:none` gate) were skipped — zero test code executed.

The same run's `Test (ubuntu-latest, Node 22.x)` job checked out the same ref successfully and got all the way to its test step, so the repository and the ref were readable at that moment; the failure was lane-local and transient. A later push re-ran the lane without any workflow change.

## What did you expect to happen?

The checkout step fetches the PR head successfully, or the job retries at a level that can absorb a transient fetch failure, so the integration gate actually executes its deterministic test set.

## Client information

Not applicable — this is a GitHub Actions infrastructure failure on the repo's own CI (`integration_no_ak`), not an authoring-CLI issue.

## Anything else we need to know?

- **Candidate mechanism (unverified):** three immediate retries hitting the identical `unresolved delta` signature points at a server-side pack that was momentarily unhealthy (renegotiation during repack/GC) or an interrupted transfer stuck in the runner's fetch cache, rather than a one-off network drop. The ref being fetched is the pull-request head at `fetch-depth: 1`.
- **Why the existing resilience does not absorb it:** the job's pre-checkout recovery steps handle leftover worktrees and workspace ownership, but the failure is inside `actions/checkout` itself, after which the job has no job-level retry.
- **Suggestions:** (a) add a job-level retry or a small git-fetch fallback loop for checkout-phase failures on this job; (b) if it recurs on the self-hosted pool, capture the runner's git version — `unresolved delta` during depth-1 negotiation has historically correlated with old git clients against a partially repacked repo; (c) use this issue to track recurrences — only one observation so far.
- This lane was classified as an infra flake during PR #13815's CI diagnosis (failed at step 4 of 13 with no code involvement); filing here so the signature has a tracker if it repeats.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 发生了什么?

PR #13815(head `d80f16c277`,run [38198248458](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38198248458))的 CI 中,`Integration Tests (no-AK, No Sandbox)` 车道(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 中 job key 为 `integration_no_ak`,job [114645716645](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38198248458/job/114645716645))在第 4 步 `Checkout` 失败。pin 在 v6.0.3 的 `actions/checkout`(`fetch-depth: 1`,ref 为 `refs/pull/13815/head`)在约 30 秒内三次重试 fetch,每次都以同样的错误收场:

```text
fatal: pack has 1 unresolved delta
fatal: fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output
The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128
```

时间戳：2026-10-12 03:04:01Z、03:04:14Z、03:04:30Z(UTC)。后续所有步骤(Node 安装、依赖安装、真正的 `test:integration:no-ak:sandbox:none` 门禁)全部 skipped——一行测试代码都没执行。

同一 run 的 `Test (ubuntu-latest, Node 22.x)` job 用同一个 ref 成功完成了 checkout,并一路跑到了测试步骤,说明当时仓库与 ref 本身可读;这次失败是车道局部且瞬时的。之后一次推送在未改动 workflow 的情况下重新跑过了该车道。

## 期望行为

checkout 步骤成功拉取 PR head;或者 job 在某个能吸收瞬时 fetch 失败的层级上自动重试,使集成门禁真正执行其确定性测试集。

## 客户端信息

不适用——这是仓库自身 CI(`integration_no_ak`)的 GitHub Actions 基础设施故障,与 CLI 使用无关。

## 其他背景

- **候选机制(未证实)**:连续三次重试命中完全相同的 `unresolved delta` 签名,更像是服务端 pack 短暂不健康(repack/GC 窗口内的重协商)或 runner 侧 fetch 缓存里的中断传输,而不是单次网络抖动。被拉取的 ref 是 pull-request head,`fetch-depth: 1`。
- **现有韧性为何包不住**:该 job 的 checkout 前恢复步骤只处理遗留 worktree 与 workspace 属主问题;失败发生在 `actions/checkout` 内部,而 job 级没有任何重试。
- **建议**:(a) 为该 job 的 checkout 阶段加 job 级重试或小规模 git-fetch 兜底循环;(b) 若在自托管池上复现,顺手抓 runner 的 git 版本——depth-1 协商下的 `unresolved delta` 历史上与旧 git 客户端面对部分重打包的仓库相关;(c) 用本 issue 记录复现,目前仅观察到一次。
- 该车道在 PR #13815 的 CI 归因中被定性为 infra flake(13 步中的第 4 步失败,零代码参与);在此建档以便签名复现时有追踪点。

</details>

## What would you like to be added?

<!-- managed-agent-fg-status:en:start -->
### Final delivery status — closed 2026-10-28

Verified against [`main` = `9acb3a5a1d`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/9acb3a5a1d68aad0705ad4d420830affb59cc95a), the actual integration-test methods, the merge commit GitHub records for each PR, and the scheduled SDK Java run [40572268860](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40572268860) (2026-10-28 03:47 Beijing). The Java sources are byte-identical between that run's `127c2ab9048` and current `main` — the commits between them touch only `.github/` and `scripts/` — so the run's Hosted results carry to this head. This closeout ran no new build or runtime acceptance.

**Delivery: a–f are implemented and green on main. The tracker is closed as completed; the cells it never gated are carried in #15750.**

| Letter | Merged PR (commit) | Gate on main | Packaged cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | #12873 (`df9374d435`) | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.lostBrokerRepliesNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` | acquire, prepare, prepare-twice, start, status, cancel, release, release-before-forward |
| b | #12888 (`3124af5bcc`) | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.sessionStoreFailuresNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` | arguments, intent, await-runtime, result-message, result-checkpoint, result-reply, turn-reply |
| c | #12896 (`d63a5ed61c`) | `HostedProcessCrashIT.processCrashesNeverReplayHostedToolsOnMySql` | harness-prepare, harness-start, harness-unknown, harness-result, spring-kill, worker-kill, worker-stop, recovery-settlement |
| d | #12924 (`92f4d4f645`) | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.cancellationRequiresPhysicalSettlementOnMySql` | prepared, running, status-unavailable, cancel-reply |
| e | #12942 (`cd0b35c153`) | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.disconnectedObserversResumeWithoutReplayingTheToolOnMySql` | sse-gap, on both the public `Last-Event-ID` and the WebShell `afterSequence` surface |
| f | #12954 (`a0559f1807`), #13061 (`0a8eb8724f`) | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.shellOutputFailuresNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` and `providerRetriesKeepContractsAndCloseAdmissionOnMySql` | publisher-kill, worker-kill, receipt-failure, receipt-reply; start-retry, raw-contract, release-reply |

In that run's `Hosted process fault gates / MySQL 8.4 / Java 21` job, `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT` ran 12 tests with 0 failures and 1 skipped (455.9 s) and `HostedProcessCrashIT` ran 2 with 0 failures (207.4 s), on real MySQL 8.4. The lane's single error is FG10b in `HostedWorkflowRelayFaultGatesIT`, owned by #15744 — not an FG6 cell. Both classes sit in the pinned Hosted lane list in `scripts/tests/hosted-process-ci.test.js`, and the round's contract is `docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md` with its `.zh-CN.md` counterpart.

One planning note below is superseded in both places it appears. The `--inflight-failover` and `--continuation-failover` E2E modes are no longer gated: G1 (#13083) enabled them and they run in the `Hosted failover E2E / Java 21` job, which passed in the same run (Linux only).

The cells this round never gated are recorded with their source in #15750: FG6e still replays through the test-only `HostedSseGapProbe` relay rather than public Workspace Turn admission; the M4 provider-media cell is skipped in every CI lane because no workflow sets `qwen.provider.media.bundle-ready`; and letters c–f assert a non-Windows host while a and b carry no platform assertion, so the POSIX FIFO and signal choreography has no Windows witness. Automatic continuation after process loss, orphan adoption and W0e reclamation stay with #12766 and #12670, not with Stage F. The original planning and acceptance scope below is retained as a historical baseline.
<!-- managed-agent-fg-status:en:end -->


**FG6**, the next Stage F slice in #12380: multi-process fault gates for the **Hosted tool turn**. #12831 connected the private Hosted model loop to Workspace Read/Write/Edit through the Runtime Broker, and #12848 is adding foreground Shell. Stage F asks every enabled capability to pass ACK-loss, SSE-gap, process-crash, cancellation, output-delivery and storage-failure tests. This path has only part of that coverage today.

FG1–FG5 (#12748, #12752, #12804) cover the Broker ↔ Runtime tool path and W0c context installation. FG6 adds the Harness side of the loop: the packaged Hosted Harness, the Session Store and the Broker's two-phase dispatch, on a real database.

### Where main is today

- **Contract under test.** The Hosted tool-turn design (`docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md`) fixes the order:
  1. Acquire one Runtime Session and its storage owner.
  2. Commit the model response, argument resources, `tool.intent` events and an `await_runtime` checkpoint, then reserve (`executions:prepare`) and start each call.
  3. Persist every outcome before the model continues.
  4. Release only after result and history settle.

  The failure rules:
  - A definite `workspace_busy`/`workspace_unavailable` refusal before storage is claimed is an ordinary turn error.
  - A lost start reply queries only the original execution.
  - An unknown outcome, a failed result commit, unverified cancellation or a failed release blocks the Session at its durable wait.
  - Cold load keeps refusing unsettled input.
- **Existing coverage.** `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT` runs in the Hosted MySQL job with real Spring, MySQL, the packaged Harness and a fake model. Its driver (`integration-tests/helpers/hosted-workspace-tool-turn-driver.ts`) proxies the Harness → Broker edge and covers:
  - one dropped start reply, recovered through the original execution;
  - a lost status that ends with the Session blocked;
  - Shell refusal, multi-round replay, and a text-only answer before the Runtime is ready.

  Unit tests cover the rest with fixtures.
- **Not covered by a multi-process gate.**
  - Lost acquire, prepare and release replies.
  - Session Store failures: a failed commit before start, a failed result commit, a lost reply to a commit that applied.
  - A killed Harness, Spring server or worker at each boundary.
  - The cancellation variants.
  - An SSE disconnect during a tool turn.
  - Any of the above for Shell output (#12848) or the provider controls (#12868).
- **Failover modes.** The E2E runner's `--inflight-failover` and `--continuation-failover` modes are still gated (#12801). They expect a replacement Harness to continue the original Prompt. Automatic continuation after process loss is W0e/Stage G work, which the tool-turn design leaves open.

### Proposed gates

| Slice | Gates | Exit check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FG6a — lost replies (Harness → Broker)** | Drop or delay the reply to acquire, prepare, start, status, cancel and release, one at a time. | Prepare retries resolve the same reservation. Start and status recover only through the original execution identity. A lost acquire or release leaves the Session blocked with ownership retained. Each call has at most one physical effect, checked against the Workspace files and the Broker's start ledger. |
| **FG6b — Session Store failures (Harness → Store)** | Fail the argument, intent or `await_runtime` commit; fail the result commit after the tool ran; drop the reply to a commit that applied. | A failure before start leaves zero filesystem effects. A failed result commit blocks the Session without re-execution. A dropped reply resolves to the committed state on reload, with no duplicate records. |
| **FG6c — process crashes** | SIGKILL the Harness after prepare, after start and before the result commit. SIGKILL the Spring server during an execution. SIGKILL or SIGSTOP the worker mid-tool. Then restart and reload. | No replay and at most one effect. An unknown outcome stays blocked, with no terminal event. Cold load refuses the unsettled input. The storage owner is retained until W0e reclaims it. |
| **FG6d — cancellation** | Cancel before start, during an operation, with status unavailable, and with the cancel reply dropped. | A prepared cancellation settles without invoking the Runtime. Only a physically settled execution produces a terminal Turn. Otherwise the Session blocks. |
| **FG6e — SSE gap** | Disconnect the public and WebShell event streams during a tool turn, then resume with `Last-Event-ID` (D3). | The Turn keeps running, and the replayed sequence has no duplicates and no gaps. |
| **FG6f — Shell output and provider controls** (after #12848 and #12868) | Kill the publisher or worker mid-stream; drop the receipt commit; retry a start under the seven-field reference; drop the reply to a release that closes admission. | Incomplete capture blocks continuation. Retries cannot switch execution contracts. Admission is closed before Workspace ownership is released. |

Every gate must fail when the guard it covers is removed, following the FG1–FG5 mutation practice. The gates run against MySQL or MariaDB, not only H2. FG6a–FG6e can start now, because #12831 is merged. FG6f follows #12848 and #12868.

### Out of scope

- **Automatic continuation after process loss**, orphan-worker adoption and reclamation (W0e, #12766, #12670, Stage G). FG6 gates today's block-and-never-replay contract instead. The two gated failover modes stay gated until that work lands.
- **Real-model runs.** A deterministic fake model keeps the gates reproducible.
- **Public Workspace message admission and UI.**

### Questions before implementation

1. **Where the gates live.** Should they extend the Hosted `*IT` family and its TypeScript driver in `managed-agent-server`, which already spawns the packaged Harness against MySQL, or should the Runtime Broker `fault-gate` rig spawn the Harness itself? I lean toward the Hosted driver, adding a Store proxy and process-kill hooks.
2. **CI budget.** The Hosted MySQL step has a 5-minute limit and the fault-gate step 10 minutes. Should FG6 get its own step or job?
3. **Failover modes.** Should `--inflight-failover` and `--continuation-failover` stay gated until W0e/Stage G? Or should they be re-targeted now to assert the current contract: a blocked Session, the original `executionCallId`, and no second effect?

## Why is this needed?

The Hosted tool turn is the first path where a model's tool call crosses three processes, the Harness, the Spring server and the worker, with durable state in both the Session Store and the Broker. #12380's acceptance criteria require lost responses to resolve through original identities without duplicate side effects, unknown outcomes to stay blocked, and cancellation to settle only with physical stop evidence. Today those rules are gated only for a dropped start and a lost status. The other failure points in the design's turn sequence are covered only by unit tests with fixtures.

Part of #12380. Follows #12748 (FG1–FG4) and #12804 (FG5).

## 希望增加什么?

<!-- managed-agent-fg-status:zh:start -->
### 最终交付状态 — 2026-10-28 关闭

对照 [`main` = `9acb3a5a1d`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/9acb3a5a1d68aad0705ad4d420830affb59cc95a)、实际集成测试方法、GitHub 为各 PR 记录的合并提交，以及定时 SDK Java 运行 [40572268860](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40572268860)（2026-10-28 03:47 北京时间）核实。该运行的 `127c2ab9048` 与当前 `main` 之间 Java 源码逐字节相同——两者之间的提交只动 `.github/` 与 `scripts/`——因此该运行的 Hosted 结果可沿用到本 head。本次收尾没有新跑 build 或运行时验收。

**交付：a–f 均已在主干实现且为绿。本 tracker 按 completed 关闭；始终未上门禁的格子记入 #15750。**

| 字母 | 已合入 PR（提交） | 主干上的门禁 | 打包用例 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | #12873（`df9374d435`） | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.lostBrokerRepliesNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` | acquire、prepare、prepare-twice、start、status、cancel、release、release-before-forward |
| b | #12888（`3124af5bcc`） | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.sessionStoreFailuresNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` | arguments、intent、await-runtime、result-message、result-checkpoint、result-reply、turn-reply |
| c | #12896（`d63a5ed61c`） | `HostedProcessCrashIT.processCrashesNeverReplayHostedToolsOnMySql` | harness-prepare、harness-start、harness-unknown、harness-result、spring-kill、worker-kill、worker-stop、recovery-settlement |

| f | #12954（`a0559f1807`）、#13061（`0a8eb8724f`） | `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT.shellOutputFailuresNeverReplayEffectsOnMySql` 与 `providerRetriesKeepContractsAndCloseAdmissionOnMySql` | publisher-kill、worker-kill、receipt-failure、receipt-reply；start-retry、raw-contract、release-reply |

在该运行的 `Hosted process fault gates / MySQL 8.4 / Java 21` job 中，`HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT` 跑 12 个用例、0 失败、1 跳过（455.9 s），`HostedProcessCrashIT` 跑 2 个、0 失败（207.4 s），数据库为真实 MySQL 8.4。该车道唯一的错误是 `HostedWorkflowRelayFaultGatesIT` 的 FG10b，归属 #15744，不是 FG6 的格子。两个类都在 `scripts/tests/hosted-process-ci.test.js` 钉住的 Hosted 车道清单中；本轮契约为 `docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md` 及其 `.zh-CN.md` 对应版本。

下方有一条计划说明在它出现的两处均已被取代。`--inflight-failover` 与 `--continuation-failover` 两个 E2E 模式不再关闭：G1（#13083）已启用它们，并在 `Hosted failover E2E / Java 21` job 中运行，该 job 在同一次运行中通过（仅限 Linux）。

本轮始终未上门禁的格子连同依据记入 #15750：FG6e 仍通过 test-only 的 `HostedSseGapProbe` 中继重放，而非公共 Workspace Turn admission；M4 provider-media 用例在所有 CI 车道都被跳过，因为没有 workflow 设置 `qwen.provider.media.bundle-ready`；c–f 各字母断言非 Windows 主机，而 a、b 没有平台断言，因此 POSIX FIFO 与信号编排没有 Windows 见证。进程丢失后的自动续跑、孤儿收养与 W0e 回收归属 #12766 与 #12670，不属于 Stage F。下方原始计划与验收范围作为历史基线保留。
<!-- managed-agent-fg-status:zh:end -->


**FG6** 是 #12380 中 F 阶段的下一片:为 **Hosted 工具回合**补多进程故障门禁。#12831 已把私有 Hosted 模型循环经 Runtime Broker 接到 Workspace 的 Read/Write/Edit,#12848 正在加入前台 Shell。F 阶段要求每项已开启的能力都通过 ACK 丢失、SSE 断流、进程崩溃、取消、输出投递和存储故障测试,这条路径目前只覆盖了其中一部分。

FG1–FG5(#12748、#12752、#12804)覆盖了 Broker ↔ Runtime 的工具路径和 W0c 上下文安装。FG6 补上回路中 Harness 这一侧:打包后的 Hosted Harness、Session Store 以及 Broker 的两阶段派发,并在真实数据库上运行。

### main 上的现状

- **被测契约。** Hosted 工具回合设计(`docs/design/2026-09-27-hosted-workspace-tool-turn.md`)规定了顺序:
  1. 获取一个 Runtime 会话及其存储所有权。
  2. 提交模型回复、参数资源、`tool.intent` 事件与 `await_runtime` 检查点,然后逐个预留(`executions:prepare`)并启动调用。
  3. 模型继续之前持久化每个结果。
  4. 结果与历史都结算后才释放。

  失败规则:
  - 占用存储之前收到明确的 `workspace_busy`/`workspace_unavailable` 拒绝,按普通回合错误处理。
  - 启动应答丢失时只查询原执行。
  - 结果未知、结果提交失败、取消无法确认或释放失败,会让会话停在持久等待处。
  - 冷加载继续拒绝未结算的输入。
- **现有覆盖。** `HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT` 在 Hosted MySQL 任务中运行,使用真实 Spring、MySQL、打包后的 Harness 和假模型。它的驱动(`integration-tests/helpers/hosted-workspace-tool-turn-driver.ts`)代理 Harness → Broker 这条边,覆盖了:
  - 丢一次启动应答,并通过原执行恢复;
  - 状态查询丢失后会话被阻塞;
  - Shell 拒绝、多轮重放,以及 Runtime 就绪前的纯文本回答。

  其余部分由使用 fixture 的单元测试覆盖。
- **尚无多进程门禁覆盖的。**
  - acquire、prepare、release 的应答丢失。
  - Session Store 故障:启动前提交失败、结果提交失败、已生效提交的应答丢失。
  - 在各个边界上杀掉 Harness、Spring 服务端或 worker。
  - 各种取消情形。
  - 工具回合期间 SSE 断开。
  - 以上各项在 Shell 输出(#12848)与 provider 控制(#12868)上的对应情形。
- **失败切换模式。** E2E 运行器的 `--inflight-failover` 与 `--continuation-failover` 模式仍处于关闭状态(#12801)。它们期望替代的 Harness 能续跑原 Prompt,而进程丢失后的自动续跑属于 W0e/G 阶段的工作,工具回合设计将其留作开放问题。

### 门禁拆分

| 切片 | 门禁 | 验收 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **FG6a — 应答丢失(Harness → Broker)** | 逐一丢弃或延迟 acquire、prepare、start、status、cancel、release 的应答。 | prepare 重试得到同一个预留。start 与 status 只能通过原执行身份恢复。acquire 或 release 应答丢失时,会话保持阻塞并保留所有权。每个调用最多一次物理副作用,以 Workspace 文件和 Broker 的启动记录核对。 |
| **FG6b — Session Store 故障(Harness → Store)** | 让参数、意图或 `await_runtime` 的提交失败;让工具执行之后的结果提交失败;丢弃已生效提交的应答。 | 启动前的失败不产生任何文件系统副作用。结果提交失败会阻塞会话,且不会重新执行。应答丢失的提交在重新加载时得到已提交的状态,不会出现重复记录。 |
| **FG6c — 进程崩溃** | 在 prepare 之后、start 之后、结果提交之前 SIGKILL Harness;执行期间 SIGKILL Spring 服务端;工具执行中途 SIGKILL 或 SIGSTOP worker。然后重启并重新加载。 | 不重放,最多一次副作用。结果未知时保持阻塞,且没有终态事件。冷加载拒绝未结算的输入。存储所有权保留到 W0e 回收为止。 |
| **FG6d — 取消** | 分别在启动前、操作进行中、status 不可用时取消,以及丢弃取消的应答。 | 已预留但未启动的取消不调用 Runtime 即可结算。只有物理上已结算的执行才产生终态 Turn,否则会话阻塞。 |
| **FG6e — SSE 断流** | 工具回合期间断开公开与 WebShell 的事件流,再用 `Last-Event-ID`(D3)续传。 | Turn 继续运行,重放的序列不重复、不缺失。 |
| **FG6f — Shell 输出与 provider 控制**(#12848、#12868 合入后) | 在输出流中途杀掉发布端或 worker;丢弃回执提交;用七字段引用重试启动;丢弃"关闭准入"的那次 release 的应答。 | 捕获不完整时阻止继续。重试不能切换执行契约。在释放 Workspace 所有权之前先关闭准入。 |

每个门禁都必须在去掉它所覆盖的防护后失败,沿用 FG1–FG5 的变异做法。门禁在 MySQL 或 MariaDB 上运行,而不仅是 H2。#12831 已合入,FG6a–FG6e 现在即可开始;FG6f 在 #12848、#12868 之后进行。

### 不在范围内

- **进程丢失后的自动续跑**,以及孤儿 worker 接管与回收(W0e、#12766、#12670、G 阶段)。FG6 钉住的是当前"阻塞、绝不重放"的契约。两个已关闭的失败切换模式,在这部分工作落地前继续保持关闭。
- **真实模型运行。** 使用确定性的假模型,以保证门禁可复现。
- **公开的 Workspace 消息准入与 UI。**

### 实现前需要确认的问题

1. **门禁放在哪里。** 是扩展 `managed-agent-server` 中的 Hosted `*IT` 系列及其 TypeScript 驱动(它已经会针对 MySQL 启动打包后的 Harness),还是让 Runtime Broker 的 `fault-gate` 装置自己启动 Harness?我倾向于 Hosted 驱动,在其中加入 Store 代理和杀进程的钩子。
2. **CI 时间预算。** Hosted MySQL 步骤限时 5 分钟,fault-gate 步骤限时 10 分钟。FG6 是否单独设一个步骤或任务?
3. **失败切换模式。** `--inflight-failover` 与 `--continuation-failover` 是否继续关闭到 W0e/G 阶段完成?还是现在就改为验证当前契约:会话被阻塞、沿用原 `executionCallId`、不产生第二次副作用?

## 为什么需要?

Hosted 工具回合是第一条让模型工具调用跨越三个进程的路径:Harness、Spring 服务端与 worker,持久状态同时存在于 Session Store 和 Broker 中。#12380 的验收标准要求:丢失的响应通过原始身份解决,不重复产生副作用;结果未知时保持阻塞;取消只能凭物理停止的证据结算。目前这些规则只在"启动应答丢失"和"状态查询丢失"两处有门禁,设计中回合序列的其他故障点只有使用 fixture 的单元测试覆盖。

属于 #12380,接续 #12748(FG1–FG4)与 #12804(FG5)。

issues.body:
## What happened?

The web-shell smoke job on `ecs-qwen-hz4-6` failed before dependency installation because the host's default sans-serif font did not match the CI baseline.

[Run 40548570065, job 122345968679](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40548570065/job/122345968679), 2026-10-27 17:14:32 UTC (2026-10-28 01:14:32 Asia/Shanghai):

```text
##[error]default sans-serif is 'WenQuanYi Zen Hei,文泉驛正黑,文泉驿正黑', expected 'DejaVu Sans'. Install fonts-dejavu-core on this host; see .github/scripts/ecs-runner/README.md.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The job metadata confirms that `Check host font baseline (self-hosted)` failed; checkout and Node setup succeeded, and browser tests were skipped.

#15410 already provides the installer and checker. Its description records successful provisioning on hz1/hz2, but does not establish deployment on hz3–hz6. The confirmed mismatch is on hz4; the other hosts need verification. This historical job does not establish whether the host has since been repaired.

## What did you expect to happen?

Every host serving the web-shell smoke lane should satisfy the same font baseline. Keep the existing fail-fast check enabled.

@yiliang114 — could we check deployment coverage across hz1–hz6 using the existing scripts?

- [ ] Run the font checker on each host as the runner service account; record host, time and result.
- [ ] On failing hosts, apply the existing [font baseline installer](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/.github/scripts/ecs-runner/install-qwen-font-baseline.sh), then rerun the [checker](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/.github/scripts/ecs-runner/check-font-baseline.sh).
- [ ] Verify web-shell smoke on each repaired host and attach job links.
- [ ] Include this baseline in new-host provisioning.

## Client information

Not applicable to the local Qwen CLI: this is a Linux self-hosted CI environment issue. The affected runner is `ecs-qwen-hz4-6`; the exact job and failed step are linked above. No host changes or CI reruns were performed for this report.

## Related issue

Git checkout failures are tracked separately in #13951. This report does not attribute them to network quality or ARM64 compatibility, and does not claim that all hz job failures have the same cause.

### What would you like to be added?
