- Release automation limits release-note summary requests to three concurrent waves, keeps result order, and refreshes release PRs from main before automated approvals. ([#15500](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15500)) by @yiliang114
- Managed Web Shell prevents duplicate message composers and keeps drafts stable during Session polling or permission-rule rerenders. ([#15496](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15496)) by @doudouOUC
- On Linux, Web Shell no longer shows the native directory Browse button when the X11 display is unreachable. ([#15434](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15434)) by @yiliang114
- Raises timeout budgets for the standalone Node/Bun regression suite on the release pool and cleans up outdated exemptions. ([#15102](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15102)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Refuses to start pull-request autofix watch from a checkout that cannot run it and reports the required working directory. ([#15506](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15506)) by @wenshao
- Simplifies Web Shell status display when loading phrases are hidden and improves status text contrast. ([#15423](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15423)) by @deggs7
- Keeps incremental lint history fetching lightweight and surfaces fallback as a CI warning and step summary. ([#15511](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15511)) by @yiliang114
- Gives eligible main push SHAs separate CI concurrency groups so independent main validations are not displaced by newer pending runs. ([#15508](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15508)) by @yiliang114
- Authenticates managed-runtime OSS preflight checks so release publishing can verify existing artifacts and avoid failed uploads. ([#15504](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15504)) by @yiliang114
- Runs the self-hosted SDK Java test suite before taking the host lock to reduce timeouts and lock contention in CI. ([#15254](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15254)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Prevents the main CI failure tracker from filing issues for post-merge PR reruns that do not reflect the merged tree. ([#15250](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15250)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Hides unavailable Managed background tools so Background Shell and Monitor appear only when the session can run them. ([#15497](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15497)) by @doudouOUC
- Fixes a managed-agent shutdown error caused by lifecycle renewal scheduling. ([#15231](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15231)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Unblocks independent same-tenant resident workspaces blocked by an unreclaimed binding and fixes hosted file tool admission. ([#15457](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15457)) by @doudouOUC
- In Web Shell standalone sessions, Language: UI is now a user setting, so changing it no longer fails with workspace-scope errors. ([#15521](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15521)) by @wenshao
- Failed queued automatic memory extraction now logs a debug warning instead of causing an unhandled rejection. ([#15338](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15338)) by @wenshao
- Credential-free release preparation jobs now run on shared ECS runners in the official repository, with existing fallbacks preserved. ([#15517](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15517)) by @yiliang114
- Headless CLI retries now show a retry classification on stderr, making transport failures and restart reasons easier to diagnose. ([#15515](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15515)) by @yiliang114
- In Web Shell, /autofix-pr watches now persist as durable tasks, so they survive idle session reclamation and appear in Scheduled tasks. ([#15523](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15523)) by @wenshao
- Deletes a turn's memory catalog snapshot record when the turn is removed, preventing orphaned snapshots while preserving catalog continuity. ([#15540](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15540)) by @yiliang114
- Fixes ARM64 CI lane pricing so self-hosted lanes get correct ceilings: lint 45 to 90 minutes and no-AK integration 30 to 60 minutes. ([#15529](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15529)) by @yiliang114
- Hosted sessions now persist Todo and project committed task lists, showing them in Managed WebShell so later turns use the latest state. ([#15155](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15155)) by @yiliang114
- Incremental lint CI now deepens history until the merge base is provable, reducing unnecessary full-repository scans on long-lived pull requests. ([#15525](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15525)) by @yiliang114
- Incremental Prettier checks now group files by the nearest configuration directory, so formatting rules and ignores apply correctly across touched paths. ([#15531](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15531)) by @yiliang114
- Kubernetes Harness pool now passes qwen serve the managed runtime broker URL and token environment pair, with clearer errors for missing, invalid, or non-HTTPS Broker URLs. ([#15394](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15394)) by @wenshao
- The tui-parity Check TUI impact gate now runs on the persistent ECS pool for trusted PRs, while untrusted fork PRs stay on GitHub-hosted runners. ([#15561](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15561)) by @yiliang114
- UserPromptSubmit hook context is no longer duplicated on the next turn after automatic compaction, and compression checkpoints are protected from later rescue mutations. ([#15575](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15575)) by @yiliang114
- The Mod runtime now targets Claude Code 2.1.310, accepts tool.check answers with setting fields, and reports that version from $.session.version(). ([#15560](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15560)) by @qqqys
- UserPromptSubmit hook context remains deduplicated after memory catalog snapshots or added message parts, preventing repeated hook context copies in CLI requests. ([#15556](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15556)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): resolve the pool's Maven dependencies through a domestic mirror ([#15610](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15610)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): stop failing the Maven bootstrap on a rate-limited pool egress ([#15539](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15539)) by @yiliang114
- fix(managed-agent): retry read-only attestation after EOF ([#15608](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15608)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(ci): resolve libfaketime for the host architecture ([#15609](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15609)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): bound setup-java on the pool and fall back to the tool cache ([#15605](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15605)) by @yiliang114
- fix(web-shell): match cancellation duration to turn summary ([#15615](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15615)) by @ytahdn
- fix(web-shell): hide turn navigation without sufficient gutters ([#15604](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15604)) by @ytahdn
- fix(core): stop warning about a placeholder in the attribution header ([#15636](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15636)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): resolve the pool's Maven dependencies from the intranet mirror ([#15641](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15641)) by @yiliang114
- fix: preserve interleaved reasoning in TUI and Chat replay ([#15621](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15621)) by @DragonnZhang
- fix(cli): preserve previews and verify installed OpenTUI distribution ([#15655](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15655)) by @chiga0
- fix(ci): Isolate Managed runtime release test classes ([#15676](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15676)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(ci): deepen until the lint scope's own acceptance holds ([#15644](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15644)) by @yiliang114
- fix(release): extend standalone runtime download retries ([#15673](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15673)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- fix(ci): preserve setup-java JDKs during pool fallback ([#15623](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15623)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): keep the sdk-java cache write-back on a failed suite ([#15555](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15555)) by @wenshao
- fix(serve): Fix Hosted local state and foreground Shell validation ([#15670](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15670)) by @doudouOUC
- fix(release): close the failure issue once a re-run passes ([#15711](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15711)) by @yiliang114
- fix(ci): refresh the stale ci.yml workflow-size baseline ([#15717](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15717)) by @wenshao
- fix(web-shell): keep session rename responsive ([#15688](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15688)) by @wenshao
- fix(cli): preserve OpenTUI extension update state ([#15716](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15716)) by @chiga0
- fix(ci): Preserve canonical artifacts across job retries ([#15713](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15713)) by @doudouOUC

### Performance

- Runs web-shell and standalone tests concurrently with the main CLI test suite to shorten required Linux CI time. ([#15438](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15438)) by @wenshao
- Keeps unchanged legacy memory catalog snapshots stable in history to improve DashScope cache reuse, resume, and retry behavior. ([#15246](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15246)) by @yiliang114

### Documentation

- Updates scheduled-task gate examples so copied first-run commands include required repository and PR options. ([#15452](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15452)) by @sxl-lucky7
- docs(design): external Hosted Workspace profile (phase 2) ([#15520](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15520)) by @yiliang114
- docs(managed): describe gate scanner capacity under the row pool ([#15571](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15571)) by @wenshao
- docs: clarify usage statistics across authentication methods ([#15554](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15554)) by @sxl-lucky7
- docs(qwencloud): document the forced attribution header and pin the admission split ([#15633](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15633)) by @yiliang114

### Internal Changes

- test(cli): cover remaining Managed Workspace activation refusals ([#15460](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15460)) by @doudouOUC
- Corrects the managed-agent CSI inventory column count so test suites pass after permission-rule columns were added. ([#15469](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15469)) by @yiliang114
- test(ci): pin the disk-pressure collector revision and FULL_PAYLOAD run bodies ([#15475](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15475)) by @yiliang114
- Adds an integration test verifying the removeScratchDir retry budget removes busy scratch directories without logging cleanup warnings. ([#15488](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15488)) by @yiliang114
- Tests now capture expected disk-full log output so real CI disk-full failures are easier to distinguish from deliberate test errors. ([#8549](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/8549)) by @EthDing
- Managed Agent tests now wait for a dead worker to become unusable before checking lease identity reuse or reconciling its loss. ([#15503](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15503)) by @yiliang114
- SDK Java CI retains Surefire and Failsafe failure reports and preserves original SQL causes in channel ownership race tests. ([#14910](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14910)) by @Aling33
- Adds CI regression coverage to keep JUnit report paths where CI collects them. ([#15502](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15502)) by @barry166
- Applies the slow-host policy to hosted approval test waits so slow runners get longer approval-test timeouts. ([#15183](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15183)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adjusts hosted approval test waits based on runner load policies to improve CI reliability on slower hosts. ([#15101](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15101)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adds automated checks for memory recovery and hard-rescue catalog accounting to prevent regressions. ([#15535](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15535)) by @yiliang114
- Adds automated checks for managed-agent row pool fan-out and corrects design documentation on shutdown and task limits. ([#15528](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15528)) by @yiliang114
- Adds a repeatable Harness Kubernetes qualification workflow for deploying, verifying, and exercising shared pools. ([#15519](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15519)) by @doudouOUC
- test(cli): pin the lifecycle-protocol refusal on the load route ([#15536](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15536)) by @yiliang114
- Adds tests verifying the lint --setup guard installs only required linters and installs nothing when no lane is selected. ([#15533](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15533)) by @yiliang114
- Consolidates catalog visibility rules so curated history reads consistently hide catalog snapshots when legacy memory is suppressed. ([#15534](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15534)) by @yiliang114
- Centralizes QwenCloud MaaS host list usage for telemetry classification and DashScope admission to keep host handling consistent. ([#15532](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15532)) by @yiliang114
- Hosted harness tests now use longer adaptive wait budgets for interrupted-model checks, reducing flaky timeouts without changing asserted behavior. ([#15551](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15551)) by @yiliang114
- test(managed-agent): align S1 acceptance fixtures with runtime contracts ([#15585](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15585)) by @doudouOUC
- Managed Agent workspace upload admission tests now use valid binary upload parameters and upload-status queries, and expect precise not-found errors for unknown uploads. ([#15588](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15588)) by @doudouOUC
- test(runtime-broker): build the extension-profile fixture paths portably ([#15598](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15598)) by @yiliang114
- test(cli): budget the skill-recovery poll through the settle policy ([#15589](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15589)) by @yiliang114
- test(lint): pin the .gitignore grouping arm and the batch stride ([#15640](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15640)) by @yiliang114
- Pin unknown sed long options ([#15223](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15223)) by @waybarrios
- ci: run every suite but CLI and core in the side test lane ([#15570](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15570)) by @wenshao
- test(cli): read xn-- hosts by the running URL parser in the Broker URL fixture ([#15544](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15544)) by @wenshao
- test(integration): widen the ready-prompt budget on GitHub-hosted macOS x64 ([#15692](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15692)) by @yiliang114
- chore(goal): remove an unused evidence helper and stale /goal hook comments ([#15693](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15693)) by @qqqys
- test(web-shell): raise the 200-record history-viewport smoke budget to 300s ([#15656](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15656)) by @yiliang114
- refactor(managed-agent): close the scanner row-pool residues (#15527) ([#15632](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15632)) by @yiliang114
- test(managed-agent): initialize the snapshot pool connection synchronously ([#15715](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15715)) by @doudouOUC
- test(cli): close the deferred review Suggestions from #15625 ([#15710](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15710)) by @wenshao

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Engine 0.10.3 implementation and release qualification. Includes the planned runtime, context, review, localization, terminal and installation/uninstall work, plus the full crate decomposition: no crate above 50,000 production lines, aiming for about 10,000.

Track concrete remaining acceptance on each issue; a landed slice or local check does not mean the complete issue or release has shipped. Contributor PRs retain their authorship. issues.title: Fleet workers spawn `codewhale` from PATH, not the running binary: all fail from the desktop Engine or a full-path install
issues.body:
## What happens

Every Fleet worker fails to start when `codewhale` isn't on `PATH`, even though a Codewhale binary is running the fleet:

```
$ codewhale fleet run tasks.json --max-workers 2      # run by full path, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
Fleet run: fleet-b2dab371 tasks=2 leased=2 queued=0
$ codewhale fleet status
fleet: runs=1 ... completed=0 partial=2 failed=2 ...
$ codewhale fleet inspect fleet-b2dab371-local-1
latest_event: seq=6 failed recoverable=false reason=starting worker fleet-b2dab371-local-1: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The local mock model received zero requests.

## Cause (source)

`configured_codewhale_binary()` (`crates/tui/src/fleet/executor.rs:57`) returns `$CODEWHALE_FLEET_CODEWHALE_BINARY` or the bare name `"codewhale"`, which is resolved on `PATH`. The CLI (`lib.rs:3894`, `:3956`) and the Runtime API (`runtime_api.rs:2065`) both use it.

## Why it matters for launch

- **Desktop:** the app starts its bundled Engine (`Codewhale.app/Contents/MacOS/codewhale app-server`) with the app's environment. Launched from Finder, `PATH` is `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, and codewhale-app never sets `CODEWHALE_FLEET_CODEWHALE_BINARY`. So `/v1/fleet/runs` workers either fail like this, or run whatever older `codewhale` happens to be on `PATH`, giving silent version skew against the Engine that owns the run.
- **CLI:** a full-path install not on `PATH` fails the same way. A machine with several installs (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew) runs workers with a different version from the one the user started.

## Suggested fix

Fall back to `std::env::current_exe()` before the bare name. The Runtime API test harness passes its own `fleet_codewhale_binary` override, but `tests.rs:1410` defaults to `configured_codewhale_binary`, so check that tests relying on the old default still pass.

Repro: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/fleet/` (tasks.json, old-run.txt; mock model on 127.0.0.1:18930). Binary: main release build from 2026-10-27 13:54. The resolver is unchanged on origin/main (`478b29eae5`).

## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The first localization slice landed on main in [a129eb544a](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/a129eb544aa2c11f534971b92c619ea390f122d0): question/approval/handoff/waiting chrome and the portable /color feedback use the locale catalog across all 15 packs. Those observations used a synthetic loopback fixture, not a real provider. Remaining surfaces, including /undo and /diff prose, keep this issue open. This is unreleased candidate source.

<!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `settings.toml`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

With the UI in Simplified Chinese, the main flow is translated: the composer placeholder 输入消息…, approval options 仅允许本次 / 不允许, the pet status 思考 / 回复 / 完成, the plan-handoff question 你想如何继续？, and the footer. But several messages you see in an ordinary session stay in English. None of these strings are in `crates/localization/locales/*.json`; they're hardcoded at the call site:

| What you see | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `/undo` note: `Undid your request "…". 1 file is back as it was before it: … The request and its reply were removed from the conversation.` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:323` (`format!("Undid {request}. {count} before it:…")`) |
| `/diff` pager title `Changes since session start` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:174` |
| `/color` note `Composer color for this chat: red` / `…reset to the theme default` | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/color.rs:73-74` |
| Tool card status `… · waiting for approval` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1411` |
| Plan handoff / question chrome: `Action required`, `Question 1 of 1`, `Other`, `Type a custom response`, `1-4 quick pick ↑/↓ move Enter confirm ←/h back Esc cancel` | `crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs` (e.g. `:459`) |
| Approval card `Save:   always ask first` | `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/ask_rules.rs` |
| Grouped activity `Explored 3 files: explore +3 ›`, `patch done · Updated tides.py · +1 -1` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs` |

## Repro
1. Put `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `$CODEWHALE_HOME/settings.toml`, or choose 简体中文 in `/settings`.
2. In a Git repo, ask for a fix that runs a shell command and edits a file, approve the card, then run `/diff`, `/undo` and `/color`.

## Expected
These go through `tr(locale, MessageId::…)` like their neighbours, and appear in `en.json` and every locale pack. `scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` only checks keys that exist, so it can't catch strings that never became keys.

## Notes
- The CHANGELOG for 0.10.2 also says the pet's activity words and the update note follow the UI language, and both do. These strings are the visible gap next to them.
- Fix direction: move each string to a `MessageId`, add the en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja values (the other locales can fall back), and consider a small lint that flags new user-facing `format!`/string literals in `crates/tui/src/tui/` and `crates/commands/src/` outside the localization crate.

Found while recording a Chinese-language 0.10.2 demo.

issues.title: /rc failure reason vanishes after a 12 s toast; /rc status then says 'off' (main) or a bare '/rc failed' (0.10.2)
issues.body:
## What a user sees

When `/rc` (or `codewhale rc`) can't start remote control, the reason appears only in a 12-second status toast. After that:

- **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf):** the footer shows a bare `/rc failed`. The reason survives only under `/rc status`: `Remote control: failed before connecting · Codewhale rejected remote-control enrollment (503 Service Unavailable): RunnerEnrollmentError. · /rc to retry`.
- **main candidate 091c3e59c0:** the toast reads `This build or session does not have an enrollable identity.`, then `/rc status` says just `Remote control: off`, with no failure and no reason.

Nothing reaches `$CODEWHALE_HOME/logs/tui-*.log` in either case.

## Repro

Local stack (`npm run web:local`, fixture sign-in), then `CODEWHALE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:18787 codewhale login --no-open` (approve in the browser), then `codewhale rc`, and wait 15 s. Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/webrc/rc-after-login.txt`, `rc-cand.txt`.

## Expected

The last start failure persists: `/rc status` reports it, and the footer says what to do. A refusal before connecting (unstamped build, missing journal dir, enrollment 4xx/5xx) is not "off". Write it to the TUI log as well.

Note: the candidate refusal is expected for an unstamped local build; this issue is only about the vanishing reason.

issues.body:
People must be able to remove Codewhale reliably, whichever supported route installed it. This is a required 0.10.3 acceptance item requested by the founder.

Current source already contains removal instructions and a Windows NSIS uninstaller, so this ticket is about completing and proving the whole uninstall journey. It does not assume that every existing uninstall path is broken.

Source baseline: main `916d3227e8`.
- [Install guide: uninstalling](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/916d3227e8/docs/INSTALL.md#L864) currently relies on manual binary deletion/package-manager commands and separate data removal.
- [Windows NSIS uninstaller](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/916d3227e8/scripts/installer/codewhale.nsi#L142) removes owned binaries, launcher, shortcut, registry entries and its PATH entry; this is existing implementation, not proof that every distribution is qualified.

## Acceptance for 0.10.3

- [ ] Give users a discoverable, supported uninstall path for direct shell/manual installs, npm, Cargo, Homebrew, Windows PowerShell/direct installs, NSIS, WinGet and Scoop. Package-managed copies use their package manager's removal mechanism.
- [ ] Remove the installation's owned executables and aliases (`codewhale`/`codew`), bundled extension-host artifacts, launchers, shortcuts, completion files and exact product-owned PATH/shell integration. Respect custom install directories and ownership/symlink boundaries; preserve shared runtimes and unrelated files.
- [ ] Preserve user configuration, credentials, sessions and workspace content by default. Any optional data purge must clearly list its scope and require an explicit choice; normal uninstall must not search broadly and delete matching directories.
- [ ] Inventory any product-installed background/startup integration and handle it by verified ownership. Report running-process, permission and partial-removal failures rather than saying uninstall succeeded.
- [ ] Handle multiple installation methods/copies: if another `codewhale` or `codew` remains on PATH, identify it and explain the remaining removal step. Repeated uninstall is safe, and reinstall works afterward.
- [ ] Record isolated install → use/help/version → uninstall → absence/leftover check → reinstall receipts for each supported route/platform, using existing checks where applicable. Validate retained data and unrelated sentinel files. Mark unavailable platform evidence explicitly; documentation alone does not qualify the flow.
- [ ] Update the install guide, package/installer guidance, help/discoverability and CHANGELOG. If a new command/flag is introduced, update its feature registry row in the same slice.

Target release: **0.10.3**, before the candidate freeze. Track execution with the existing 0.10.3 scope packet (CW-7525).

Verification must use disposable prefixes/environments; do not uninstall the founder's active installation or remove their data. This issue authorizes no release, publication, paid VM/provider use or destructive host cleanup.

---

Part of the runtime/TUI crate split. Read first: `docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md` and the mover `scripts/split/move-modules.py` (it `git mv`s a top-level module, edits the `mod` lines, adds the name to the TUI's single path-alias block in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:143-152`, and sweeps stale path strings). A lowercase reading of this task is "move small files"; the point is that these are **runtime-side subsystems with already-clean boundaries** — process supervision, shell dispatch, credentials exchange, runtime policy/logging, feature registry — that belong in the headless crate and will grow there.

Run slices one at a time — do not stack two `RS-n` slices in one working tree.

## Goal

Move ten modules from `crates/tui/src/` into `crates/runtime/src/`. Each one has **zero upward references** today (verified by `scripts/split/module_graph.py --report`), so no ratchet entry changes; their only dependencies are modules already resident in `crates/runtime` (or each other):

- `child_env` (1,423 lines) — no deps
- `logging` (134) — no deps
- `external_credentials` (938) — no deps
- `dsh_credentials` (148) — depends on `external_credentials` (moves in this batch)
- `shell_dispatcher` (994) — depends on `host_terminal` (already in runtime)
- `runtime_policy` (167) — no deps
- `process_tree` (935) — no deps
- `features` (375) — no deps
- `runtime_log` (588) — no deps
- `working_set` (2,505) — depends on `workspace_discovery` (already in runtime)

## Plan

1. Dry-run first: `python3 scripts/split/move-modules.py --dry-run child_env logging external_credentials dsh_credentials shell_dispatcher runtime_policy process_tree features runtime_log working_set` — read the printed path sweep. `--dry-run` writes nothing.
2. Run it for real, one module list in one change.
3. `crates/tui/tests/feature_registry.rs:10` carries `#[path = "../src/features.rs"] mod features;`. Update the include to the new location (`../../runtime/src/features.rs`) or switch the test to the runtime export if `features` is made `pub` there. Keep `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` green — it is the `docs/features.toml` drift guard and must keep failing on flag drift.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-status-20261025 -->
## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The ambient-index loss footer is on main in [423dff6af5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/423dff6af5). The requested description-length control and remaining documentation/localization work are still scheduled; the existing 400-character cap is not being represented as configurable yet.

<!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed issues for "skill description", "skills index", "skill catalogue", "truncat", "MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS", "skills budget", "prompt budget". Related but distinct: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only policy), #6526 (same failure class on standing instructions: hard-coded ceilings, no knobs, invisible trim), #4698 (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed). This issue is about the ambient skills index: what the model is allowed to see, and what nobody is told when text is cut.

## What problem does this solve?

Codewhale puts a bounded index of skills into every system prompt. Each row is a name, a slice of the skill's `description`, and the `SKILL.md` path. The slice is capped by a compile-time constant; the block is capped by a share of the route window. When either limit bites, the model gets a shortened description — and the only disclosure anywhere is a per-skill note behind `/skills inspect`, a diagnostic subcommand.

**The mechanics, verified at `f19aa7772` (0.10.2):**

- Per-row cap: `MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 400` — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`.
- Block budget: `window_tokens × 4 chars × 5%`, floor 2 400, ceiling 40 000 chars — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:56-68`, `:84-97`. Neither value is configurable.
- Three tiers — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1948-1954`:
  1. full rows, each capped at 400;
  2. proportional shortening when the total does not fit, with a 40-char floor (`:71`);
  3. names only, plus an omission line (`:2167`).
- A row is split into summary + trigger at an English marker, and the trigger is promised at least half the cap when both exist (`:1903-1946`). Only four markers are recognized: `use when:`, `use when `, `use this when `, `use this skill when `.
- Cut text ends in `…`, added by `truncate_for_prompt` (`:2177-2188`).

**What is surfaced today — and credit where it is due.** `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note when a description exceeds the cap, added in `ba386a0cf` (2026-09-02):

```
note: description is N chars; the model index shows at most 400 — trim it,
or end it with `Use when: <trigger>` so the trigger survives shortening
```

`crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:486-501`, inside `inspect_skills` (`:445`). Reachability matters: bare `/skills` opens the Extensions UI (`:313-315`), and `/skills <prefix>` prints descriptions without this note (`:376-441`). The comment above the note states the intent exactly: "say so here instead of cutting an imported skill mid-sentence with nobody told."

That note is useful, and the authoring advice in it is correct. It is also the whole of the disclosure:

- **It is user-facing only, and behind a diagnostic subcommand.** Bare `/skills` opens Extensions; the note is in `/skills inspect`. The model's prompt does not carry the count, a footer, or a marker beyond `…`; the Usage paragraph tells the model to use `load_skill` "if the index was truncated" (`mod.rs:1971-1976`), a condition the model cannot reliably detect.
- **It fires only for the tier-1 cap** (`description > 400`). When the pack overflows the block budget, tier 2 shortens descriptions proportionally — including descriptions well under 400 — with no note anywhere, and tier 3 drops names with an in-prompt omission line only.
- **It is not a startup or discovery signal.** Nothing is written to the log, and `/context` reports the rendered block with no note that rows were shortened (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`). A user who never runs `/skills inspect` never sees it; a session that loads a new pack never sees it.
- **It is not a count.** With 50+ skills the note appears in a long list, per skill, with no aggregate ("23 of 47 descriptions shortened").

**Measured on a real 52-skill pack under `~/.agents/skills` (identifiers redacted):**

- 32 099 chars of `description` in total; 20 091 (~63%) can reach the model.
- 47 of the 52 carry a "Not for" clause; in 23 of them the clause is absent from the rendered row. Checked by re-implementing `split_trigger` + `description_split` from the code and comparing the rendered string, not by raw offsets.
- 18 of the 52 have no recognized trigger marker, so their row is cut mid-sentence before the triggers.
- Fixed scaffolding (names + paths) is ~3 300 chars. At a 400 cap this pack renders ~23.8k chars.

The budget is not the binding constraint on large routes; the constant is. On a 1M-token route the index budget is ~36 000 chars after the fixed header/usage cost and the warning reservation; the pack's untruncated rows would need ~35.8k (the four bundled skills add ~0.75k), so the budget would force only a small trim — yet the 400 cap removes ~12.0k chars. The warning reservation is easy to miss: when discovery produced any warning, the renderer withholds up to 20% of the block budget for warnings, capped at 3 232 chars (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:2026-2032`). On a 150k route the index then gets ~26 000 chars, and the cap could rise to ~450 before tier 2 begins; on 128k the index gets ~21 600, which this pack at 400 already exceeds, so it is already in tier 2 with no note anywhere.

**Why this matters beyond one pack.** Most users install published skills rather than writing them. Sampled `description` lengths in `anthropics/skills` are 204, 277, 319, 437, 837 and 952 chars, while the Agent Skills spec allows 1024. A large share of published skills therefore arrives truncated, and the authoring fix ("keep it short, end with `Use when:`") is advice the author only meets if they happen to run `/skills inspect` on the machine where the skill is installed.

**The recovery path exists but is unbudgeted.** `load_skill name="list"` returns full descriptions (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`) — ~32k chars for this pack, i.e. a large unbudgeted read the model has no reliable reason to take.

**Prior art inside the repo.** `/skills inspect` already names the cap; #6526 proposes the same pattern for standing instructions — config-optional ceilings plus a bounded first-turn notice when content is trimmed. The skills index has the ceiling and the human note, but not the config, the aggregate, the log line, or the first-turn notice.

## What should Codewhale do?

Four separable pieces, smallest first.

**1. Extend the existing notice beyond `/skills inspect`.**

- Add one aggregate line to the block when any row is shortened at any tier: `- ... descriptions shortened for N of M skills; load_skill name="list" returns full text.` Cost ~90 chars.
- Emit a discovery-time warning when `description` exceeds the cap and no `when_to_use` is present, through the channel that already exists: the `### Skill load warnings` section (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1976`, `:2153-2165`) and `logging::warn` — the same path that already reports shadowed skills and unknown frontmatter keys. The `/skills inspect` note and this warning should come from one computation, not two.
- Record the same fact in the context report entry for `SourceKind::SkillsBlock` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:613-622`), so `/context` shows a degradation, not only a size.

**2. Tell the model that something was lost — open question below.**

A footer is the cheapest honest signal. A per-row marker costs chars on every row, and `…` is ambiguous because authors use it. Keep `…` as the visual cue; make the count explicit once per block.

**3. Make the limits configurable, mirroring the ecosystem.**

- `[skills] listing_max_description_chars` — per-entry cap. Default today is 400; the spec allows 1024, Claude Code defaults to 1 536 for `description + when_to_use`.
- `[skills] listing_budget_fraction` — share of the route window. Default 0.05 today; Claude Code uses 0.01.
- Precedence: explicit config > window-derived default, resolved in one place and used by both prompt build (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`) and `/context` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595`).

**4. Add a per-skill "name-only" state.**

Today the only per-skill lever is `disable-model-invocation: true`, which removes the skill from the model catalogue entirely (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:866-877`, `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`). A middle state would keep the name in the index and spend zero description budget — the same idea as Claude Code's `skillOverrides: "name-only"`. It is also a better fallback than the current 40-char floor: a 40-char fragment costs almost as much as a name and routes worse than no description at all. This overlaps with #7066's proposed `explicit_only` list; the two could share one policy surface.

**Sequencing options** (maintainers decide; effort/risk are estimates):

- **Option A — report only.** Footer + discovery warning + context-report note, sharing one computation with the existing `/skills inspect` note. Small diff, no config, no behaviour change. Risk: ~90 chars per request.
- **Option B — A + two config keys.** Adds docs and, if the flag is user-visible, a `docs/features.toml` row (`AGENTS.md:114-116`). Medium diff. Risk: two knobs that interact with the window-derived default; needs one resolver.
- **Option C — B + name-only state.** Larger; touches prompt rendering and the skills manager; coordinate with #7066. Risk: policy surface grows; must stay distinct from `explicit-only` (which hides the skill from the catalogue entirely).
- **Option D — raise the default cap to 1024 without knobs.** Small diff, large prompt-cost change on small windows: at a 128k window the index budget is ~21.6k after the warning reservation and this pack already exceeds it, so a higher cap deepens tier 2 instead of revealing more text.

Recommendation: A first, then B; C with #7066. Do not raise the default before the total budget is configurable.

## Where?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- Docs

## Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today: keep `description` short by hand and end it with `Use when: …` (the advice `/skills inspect` already prints); set `disable-model-invocation: true` per skill; restrict discovery with `[skills] scan_codewhale_only = true` (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`); move skill directories out of the scanned roots. None of these makes a shortened row visible to the model or at startup, and none covers tier 2.

Claude Code, for comparison:

- Listing budget is 1% of the context window by default (`skillListingBudgetFraction`), or a fixed character count via `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET`. Ours is 5% of the window — more generous in total, not configurable.
- Per-entry text (`description` + `when_to_use`) is capped at 1 536 chars by default (`skillListingMaxDescChars`), configurable. Ours is 400, below the spec's 1024.
- On overflow Claude Code keeps every skill name and drops descriptions starting with the least-used skills. Codewhale shortens every row proportionally to a 40-char floor, so every skill degrades a little instead of a few degrading to a name.
- It warns in the debug log, reports the applied listing size in `/context`, and estimates cost per skill in `/doctor`. Codewhale reports the block size, and only a per-skill note in `/skills inspect` for the 400 cap.
- `skillOverrides` has four per-skill states written from the `/skills` menu: `on`, `name-only`, `user-invocable-only`, `off`. Codewhale has on / fully off.
- `when_to_use` is a first-class Claude Code field appended to the description and counted toward the same cap; Codewhale implements the same field (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`) — good — but spec-only distribution paths reject it, so it is not a portable substitute for a well-formed description.

The Agent Skills specification: `description` is required, 1–1024 characters, and must say both what the skill does and when to use it; `name` is ≤64 chars; `compatibility` ≤500; progressive disclosure is metadata (name + description) always, body on activation, `scripts/`/`references/`/`assets/` on demand.

## Open questions

1. **Should the model be told that rows were shortened?** Arguments for: the model is the only consumer of the routing surface, and today it can only suspect a cut from `…`; a footer lets it decide to call `load_skill name="list"`. Arguments against: ~90 chars on every request, and the model rarely needs the full text; a per-row marker is noisier still. Precedent: #6526 proposes a bounded first-turn notice for trimmed instructions, and `AGENTS.md` says "Model-visible means logged".
2. Should truncation be a session event? The rendered prompt is logged, but the decision to shorten is not.
3. Usage-based dropping vs proportional shortening: Claude Code drops descriptions of the least-used skills first. Does Codewhale have or want usage data? Is a uniform 40-char fragment the right fallback?
4. Default cap: 400 (today), 1024 (spec), or 1 536 combined (Claude Code)? What happens to prompt-cache stability when the cap depends on the route window?
5. `when_to_use` is appended unconditionally (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`). When the description already contains `Use when:`, this produces a second marker; `split_trigger` resolves by marker priority and then first occurrence, so the appended sentence ends up in the trigger tail and can be cut when the combined text exceeds the cap. Should the append be skipped when a marker is already present?
6. Companion files: `collect_companion_files` lists only files directly beside `SKILL.md` (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:321-346`); `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` are never enumerated, so the spec's resource layer is invisible unless the body names the files. Intended (body must reference them) or a gap?

## References

- Agent Skills specification — https://agentskills.io/specification
- Optimizing skill descriptions — https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions ("the description carries the entire burden of triggering")
- Claude Code skills documentation (frontmatter reference; "Skill descriptions are cut short"; `skillOverrides`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- Claude Code settings reference (`skillListingBudgetFraction`, `skillListingMaxDescChars`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference
- Public skill samples — https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- Related issues: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only), #6526 (config knobs + visible notice for trimmed standing instructions), #4698 (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed)
- Code at `f19aa7772`: `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`, `:56-71`, `:84-97`, `:855`, `:866-877`, `:1903-1946`, `:1948-1954`, `:1971-1978`, `:2153-2170`, `:2177`; `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:313-315`, `:376-441`, `:445`, `:486-501`; `crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`, `:273`, `:321-346`; `crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`; `crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`; `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`, `:264-265`; `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`

## Reproduction

1. Put ~50 skills with 600–1000-char descriptions under `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, or install a published pack.
2. Start a session with `CODEWHALE_DUMP_SYSTEM_PROMPT=1` (`crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1949`) and read the `## Skills` block from the dump.
3. Rows end in `…`. The block carries no count; `/context` reports only the block size; the log has no line. `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note, but only for descriptions over 400 chars and only when the user runs that subcommand.
4. Force the block over budget (e.g. a small route window) to see tier 2 shorten descriptions below 400 with no note anywhere.
5. `load_skill name="list"` returns the full descriptions, i.e. the text exists and was silently cut from the routing surface.

Environment: codewhale 0.10.2 (dev), commit `f19aa7772`, Linux; reproduced on a 1M-token route and a 150k-token route.

## Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Runtime/render performance

milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
Every user message in the agent currently wakes the large model to decide the routine things: what the intent is, whether a tool is needed, and what to do next. For a simple message that costs one to three seconds and real money, even when no big thinking is required at all.

The idea is a Decision Gate at the front door. A small, fast decision model answers those routine questions in one quick pass without generating any text, and returns typed answers with confidence scores, such as whether the turn needs a tool, whether it can be answered from what is already known, and what the primary intent is. A simple routing layer then sends each message to the cheapest correct path, and whenever the small model is unsure it falls back to the full model exactly as today. The agent is never worse, only faster when the decision is obvious. It can run on home hardware, a CPU or a small GPU, because the decision models are small and open.

The change is safe to adopt. It is off by default, so a user who does nothing sees the exact current behavior. When it is turned on it runs in shadow mode at first, which means it only classifies the turn and logs its recommendation through the existing tracing logger. It does not change routing, it does not skip the model call, and it does not alter any user-visible behavior. It fails open on any error, timeout, non-2xx response, or malformed reply, so the agent always continues as if the gate were never there. It adds no heavy dependency, because it talks to the decision backend with a plain HTTP POST using the reqwest client the project already uses. The decision model itself is installed out of band and is never bundled.

We would like to contribute this as an optional feature. The concept and the reference implementation are by Andrea Bruno and are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. If the project adopts the idea or the code, we kindly ask to keep a short credit to Andrea Bruno and a link to the harness-superfast repository in the docs. The decision models themselves (Von, OpenJev, Laya) are third-party open models; only the integration architecture and the routing method are ours. The white paper is called harness-superfast.

A pull request with a first, off-by-default shadow-mode increment is ready and linked from this issue.

issues.body:
Hey! o/

Quick intro — I use Claude Code backed by DeepSeek and I've been eyeing DeepSeek-TUI for a bit. I'm on FreeBSD and I finally gave `npm install -g deepseek-tui` a shot today. Here's what I got:

```
root@worker:/home/user # npm install -g deepseek-tui
npm error deepseek-tui install failed: Unsupported platform: freebsd.
Supported platforms: 'linux', 'darwin', 'win32'.
npm error No prebuilt binary is available for this platform/architecture combo.
```

Fair enough — I knew it was a long shot :]

So here's my humble request: would you consider adding FreeBSD to the supported platforms? Two possible paths (not mutually exclusive, one can come way later than the other):

- **Ship a FreeBSD prebuilt binary on GitHub Releases** — The npm package already does the heavy lifting (downloads + installs binaries). It just needs a `freebsd` binary to pick up. This would unblock `npm install -g deepseek-tui` for us BSD folks right away.
- **`pkg install deepseek-tui`** — A proper FreeBSD port/package down the line. That's the long game, and I'm not expecting anyone to drop everything for it. But if it could land on the roadmap somewhere, that'd be amazing.

I know maintaining packages and build matrices isn't free. If you have no time for it right now, no worries — could you maybe plan it and add it to the roadmap? That way I know it's on the radar and I can keep an eye out. Totally fair if it's a "someday maybe" thing.

And hey, if you ever want someone to test the BSD side of things, I'm around and happy to help. Break my system, I don't mind :]

Cheers for the work you put into this — looking forward to trying it one way or another!

<!-- cw-0103-status-20261025 -->
## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The current source receipt fix is [2c4f090a9f](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2c4f090a9f): when preserving an existing CRLF file, the write result says so. This does not add explicit LF/CRLF selection. That requested behavior remains an enhancement; this issue is not being represented as fully fixed.

<!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

Leave these confirmations unchecked until you have personally verified them before submission. This draft does not claim a fresh duplicate search or reproduction on the latest release.


### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Codewhale's write tool converts CR-free content to CRLF when the overwritten file used CRLF (first newline decides) and reports plain success, so a user's explicit request to save with LF endings is silently not honored and the agent tells the user the file is LF.

Observed behavior:
write with LF-only content -> 'Successfully wrote 215 bytes'; the file on disk keeps CRLF on every line (next read and final workspace file); the agent claimed LF endings in 9/10 runs (grep_files for \r returned 0 matches).

write 'Creates the file if it does not exist, overwrites it if it does' with the given content; the user explicitly required LF line endings only. Caveat: CRLF preservation is an intentional upstream fix (#5909/#5911) for unintended conversions.

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Prepare notes.txt with CRLF endings and the words verison, shure, and Anounce. The recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines. Inspect the raw bytes after write; a rendered text preview alone cannot establish LF conversion.

Please save a corrected version: fix those three words and store the file with Unix LF line endings only (no carriage returns). Rewrite the whole file with your file write tool rather than with shell commands. Then tell me what the file now looks like.

Track concrete remaining acceptance on each issue; a landed slice or local check does not mean the complete issue or release has shipped. Contributor PRs retain their authorship. Complete planned implementation and product review before freezing one candidate for final local and hosted validation. Publication is a separate authorized release step. No calendar due date is promised.

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

After I set the multiline input mode, I can no longer send messages with Shift+Enter.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Set to multiline input mode.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 1.10.2

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Linux

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Deepin 25 Terminal + bash

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

My operating system is Deepin 25.2.2, and the Linux kernel version is 6.18.48-amd64-desktop-rolling.

### 0.10.3 admission — founder, 2026-10-26

The founder explicitly admitted this report to the full 0.10.3 program. Original GitHub issue #7093 is assigned to milestone v0.10.3 (73); preserve the reporter's body and attribution to @luestr. Reuse this existing codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7093 issue rather than filing a duplicate.

Reported environment: Deepin 25 Terminal + bash, Deepin 25.2.2, Linux 6.18.48-amd64-desktop-rolling, GitHub release install. Reported version is literally `codewhale 1.10.2`; do not silently treat that spelling as independently verified 0.10.2 evidence.

Root owns triage and integration. Inspect negotiated terminal key encoding and multiline submit dispatch, preserve newline/paste safety and existing user bindings, and distinguish terminal inability to encode Shift+Enter from a Codewhale dispatch regression. Acceptance requires a working, truthful submit path in multiline mode for legacy and enhanced keyboard input, existing focused checks, and direct terminal-sequence observations. No new permanent tests/comments requested. Source scope will be narrowed after discovery; do not edit the frozen shared native batch.

### Source triage — 2026-10-26

The requested headless Codewhale helper completed using OrcaRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; root independently checked the owning handler. An explicitly reported Shift+Enter in multiline mode reaches `submit_decided_composer_input` and then `App::handle_composer_enter`, which reapplies the paste-burst newline guard. Ctrl+Enter instead calls `submit_input` directly. This is a concrete dispatch defect; a fix must bypass the guard only for deliberate modified submission while preserving bare-Enter paste protection, slash-menu selection and launch/session behavior.

A separate compatibility path remains under investigation: legacy terminals can encode Enter and Shift+Enter identically. The current capability check is cached but can block for up to two seconds on its first call, so any capability-based handling must initialize before the input pump and keep rendering nonblocking. The reporter's actual Deepin key bytes have not been captured; do not claim their exact cause or a Linux reproduction yet.

Readonly helper report: `/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/artifacts/headless-helpers-20261026/linux-multiline-7093/REPORT.md`. Root integration owner remains unchanged; next patch stays outside the frozen native batch until that check completes. No correction is yet compiled, landed or shipped.

### Local candidate evidence — 2026-10-26

The candidate now bypasses paste-burst newline handling only for deliberate modified submission, keeps Ctrl+Enter steering behavior, provides Alt+Enter as the portable multiline submit path, and initializes keyboard capability negotiation before the input reader starts. Help reflects the available capability.

The selected existing multiline/key-routing/paste checks passed within a TUI run of 914 passed and four unrelated failures, whose repairs are in progress. Eight scoped PTY observations passed for the frozen vendored event-read example: supported replies, flags-only timeout, delayed/fragmented replies, incomplete replies, unsupported terminal, silence, and source closure. Normal cases preserved ordinary input exactly once and in order; source closure surfaced an error promptly.

This is macOS PTY/source evidence. An actual Deepin terminal run and a fresh full Codewhale TUI observation remain open. The candidate is uncommitted and unshipped; keep this issue In Progress.

issues.body:
CodeWhale 是个大项目，有海量的文档。虽然后期借助了 LLM 来翻译，但翻译那些文档进中文已经耗费了我太多的心神。后期英文文档更新，中文文档应当一起同步。然而，AI翻译的技术文档质量，大家懂得都懂——只停留在“能读”，至于看着费不费劲，那是另一码事。

不只是我们 CodeWhale，其他许多开源项目也面临着这样的困境。我希望能够牵头成立一个小型的汉化组，用爱发电，去汉化、跟进开源的英文项目或日文项目，让更多的简中网友能了解到这些它们。不仅让这些优秀的项目免于雪藏，也降低了许多项目的使用门槛。

如果有意愿加入此组的，请在此 Issue 下留言。如果人齐，到时候我会建立一个 QQ 群，把大家都拉进去。到时候我们一起合作，打通语言壁垒。

肯定会有人觉得这没必要。但我觉得千里之行始于足下，或者说不积小流无以成江海。

现在，大部分文本都是AIGC——我这不是在怪罪 Hmbown 兄弟，他已经很尽力了，换作我，我肯定连i18n都没想到，但他竟然同时维护这么多语言。我觉得我们这样做，也是为 Hmbown 和像他一样的人减轻一部分负担。

语言的壁垒是真实存在的，我听说很多外国人看中国汉字都看得头昏，可能 Hmbown 老兄也觉得我们汉语的方块字有点难懂。既然如此，我们就成立一个志愿的汉化组吧！就让我们来帮他点忙，也相当于是分工协作了；同时也帮 CodeWhale 这条大鲸鱼游得更远！

欢迎所有想要给 Codewhale 贡献、但是却觉得无从下手的人——路就在这里！

开源万岁，协作万岁，共享万岁，知识万岁！

> 如有意愿，请添加我的QQ号：2163018547（彁）并注明来意。

---

CodeWhale is a large project with a huge amount of documentation. Although we later used LLMs to help translate it, translating those documents into Chinese still cost me far too much time and energy. Going forward, when the English docs are updated, the Chinese docs should be synced as well. However, everyone knows the quality of AI-translated technical documentation—it only reaches the level of “readable.” Whether it’s actually easy to read is another matter entirely.

It’s not just CodeWhale. Many other open-source projects face the same predicament. I hope to take the lead in forming a small Chinese localization group, powered by love rather than money, to translate and keep up with open-source English or Japanese projects, so that more Simplified Chinese-speaking users can learn about them. This would not only keep these excellent projects from being buried and forgotten, but also lower the barrier to entry for many of them.

If you’re interested in joining this group, please leave a comment under this issue. I’ll then create a QQ group and invite everyone in. Together, we can work to break down language barriers.

Some people will definitely think this is unnecessary. But I believe that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step—or, as the saying goes, without accumulating small streams, one cannot form rivers and seas.

Right now, most of the text is AIGC—I’m not blaming our friend Hmbown for this. He’s already trying his best. If it were me, I definitely wouldn’t have even thought of i18n, yet he’s actually maintaining so many languages at the same time. I think by doing this, we’re also easing some of the burden for Hmbown and people like him.

Language barriers are real. I've heard that many foreigners get dizzy just looking at Chinese characters, and maybe our friend Hmbown also finds our Chinese square characters a bit hard to understand. In that case, let's form a volunteer Chinese localization group! Let's give him a hand—it would essentially be division of labor and collaboration—and at the same time help CodeWhale the big whale swim even further!

Everyone who wants to contribute to CodeWhale but feels at a loss about where to start is welcome—the path is right here!

Long live open-source! Long live collaboration! Long live sharing! Long live knowledge!

> If you're interested, please add my QQ: 2163018547 (彁) and mention your purpose.

milestone.title: Help wanted
milestone.description: Good places to contribute: scoped issues a contributor can pick up without maintainer-only access. Comment on the issue to claim it, and see CONTRIBUTING.md. Release blockers live in the version milestones.

issues.body:
## Problem

While a foreground shell command runs and is not waiting for interaction, the tool card shows the detach hint instead of the command. In `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1031-1039` the header is chosen as:

```rust
let command_summary = command_header_summary(&self.command);
let compact_foreground_wait = self.is_foreground_shell_wait();
let header_summary = if compact_foreground_wait {
    Some(FOREGROUND_SHELL_WAIT_HINT)          // "Ctrl+B → /jobs"
} else {
    self.interaction.as_deref().or(Some(command_summary.as_str()))
};
```

`is_foreground_shell_wait()` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1006-1011`) is true for exactly the state the user watches while work happens — `Running`, assistant-issued, no interaction. So the command is invisible precisely while it runs, and the row reads `run running (81s) · Ctrl+B → /jobs`.

With the default `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"` this is total for the live view: a collapsed cell is the header line alone ("the tool-name + arg/command summary as the single intent line", `crates/tui/src/tui/app/types.rs:140-146`), and the hint has taken that line. The command still exists one level down — the card body renders it through `render_command_mode` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1140`, `:2160-2176`: capped at `TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT` = 6 wrapped lines with a details affordance in live mode, unwrapped in the transcript) — but that means expanding the card or leaving the transcript for `/jobs`.

A second, related truncation applies in every other state: `command_header_summary` (`crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:2187-2195`) keeps only the **first line** of the command, so a multi-line invocation (heredoc, `&&` chain, `for` loop) shows one line and hides the rest.

Nothing here is configurable: no key for either behaviour exists in `settings.toml`, `crates/tui/src/settings.rs`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs` or `crates/config/src/lib.rs`. The full command is available in `/jobs` — `cmd: <full command>` with cwd and output tail (`crates/tui/src/tui/shell_job_routing.rs:21-56`) — but answering "what is it running?" then means leaving the transcript.

## Proposed solution

One display setting whose absent/off value is exactly today's behaviour:

```toml
# settings.toml, alongside the other display knobs and editable from /config
running_shell_command = "off"        # off | first_line | full   (default: off)
```

- **`off` (default, and what an absent key means)** — no change at all: the header stays the detach hint. Existing installs and every user who never sets the key see precisely what they see today.
- `first_line` — the hint stays and the command's first line is appended: `cmd: cargo test -p codewhale-tui · Ctrl+B → /jobs`.
- `full` — the whole command is rendered, wrapped to the card width and bounded by the existing line budget (`TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT = 6`, `crates/tui/src/tui/history/constants.rs:27`), with the detach hint kept on the last line so the affordance is never lost.

Why this shape is cheap and safe:

- It is pure presentation: the command is already in the transcript and in the job snapshot, so nothing new has to be captured.
- The default preserves the reason the current design exists — the row must advertise `Ctrl+B` → `/jobs` — so the change is strictly opt-in and reversible by config.
- `full` must wrap, not overflow, and must respect narrow card widths, the same bounded-line discipline the body already uses.
- If an enum is unwanted, the equivalent is a boolean `show_running_command` (default `false`) plus `running_shell_command_detail = "first_line" | "full"`.

## Use case

Long builds, test suites and installs in a multi-repository workspace: the operator glances at the screen and needs to know which command is running, in which of several concurrent lanes, without expanding a card or looking an id up in `/jobs`. It matters most for multi-line commands, where today even a non-running card shows only the first line — a `for` loop or heredoc is indistinguishable from its first statement.

## Alternatives considered

- `/jobs` — prints the full command with cwd, status, exit code and output tail, but it is a separate view while the question is asked *inside* the transcript.
- Expanding the tool card — the body does render the command (live: up to 6 wrapped lines; transcript: full), so this is the closest workaround today; it costs an interaction per glance, and in the default `compact` collapse mode the live cell shows nothing but the header anyway.
- Putting the command in the footer or status strip — crowded; it already carries mode, model, context and tokens.
- Unconditionally showing the command — rejected: it would remove the detach affordance from the one row that carries it.

## Impact

Every session with a long-running shell call, and every multi-line command in every session (the first-line truncation). The cost is one settings key and a rendering branch; with the default unchanged, the risk is confined to users who opt in.

## Additional context

- Live reproduction on 0.10.0 (dev) @ `384439634` with `show_tool_details = true`, `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"`, `calm_mode = true`: the cell read `run running (81s) · Ctrl+B → /jobs` while the command ran.
- Relevant code: `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1006-1011` (`is_foreground_shell_wait`), `:1031-1039` (header choice), `:1140` and `:2160-2176` (body command rendering), `:2187-2195` (`command_header_summary`); `crates/tui/src/tui/history/constants.rs:27` (`TOOL_COMMAND_LINE_LIMIT`) and `:112` (`FOREGROUND_SHELL_WAIT_HINT`); `crates/tui/src/tui/app/types.rs:140-151` (`ToolCollapseMode`).
- `/jobs` output shape: `crates/tui/src/tui/shell_job_routing.rs:21-56`.

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux
- codewhale: 0.10.0 (dev), built from `Hmbown/CodeWhale@384439634`
- Settings: `show_tool_details = true`, `tool_collapse_mode = "compact"`, `calm_mode = true`, `show_thinking = true`
- Shell/terminal: bash tool shell, tmux

issues.title: feat(compaction): optional model-invoked self-compact (with note-to-self) as a complement to engine-owned auto-compact

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Extra attention is needed

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

labels.name: compaction
labels.description: Context management / compaction

labels.name: tools
labels.description: Tool execution, tool schemas, tool UX, and built-in tool behavior

milestone.title: Help wanted
milestone.description: Good places to contribute: scoped issues a contributor can pick up without maintainer-only access. Comment on the issue to claim it, and see CONTRIBUTING.md. Release blockers live in the version milestones.

issues.body:
## Problem

Auto-compaction in Codewhale is entirely harness-owned: when
`auto_compact_threshold_percent` is reached, the engine cuts at the request
boundary. There is **no tool the model can call** to compact (or to request a
compact) at a boundary the model chooses.

Closest existing surface:

- `memory_checkpoint_put` / `memory_checkpoint_get` — save/resume working state
  *if* the model knows a compact is coming (no model-facing pressure under auto
  ON today — see companion proposal for soft notice);
- `/compact <focus>` and Ctrl+L — **operator-only** (`Op::CompactContext` is
  host-sent from TUI / runtime, not in the model tool catalog);
- `[compaction] summary_instructions` / `retained_user_message_tokens` —
  operator knobs for *how* summarization runs, not *when*.

So the model cannot:

- compact when it just finished a coherent milestone and before the next noisy
  tool burst;
- attach a short note-to-self / handoff intent at the moment it decides to cut;
- recover mid-session when it *knows* history is degraded, without waiting for
  the 80% line (or asking the operator to type `/compact`).

For contrast: **Claude Code** prompts the model to *ask the user* to compact
(model-facing reminder, still human-gated); **opencode** auto-compacts from the
harness without a model-invoked compact tool. Neither exposes "model decides to
cut now" as a tool either — but Codewhale also has no conversational fallback
under default auto ON, so the gap is larger here.

Harness-only compaction is fine for interactive TUI use. It is weak for
off-loop / fleet style sessions where the model is the only party that knows
the task shape (headless `exec` has no `/compact` at all today).

## Proposed solution

Add an **optional, model-invoked compaction path** that sits *beside* engine
auto-compact, not instead of it. **Default: OFF** (opt-in via capability /
config until the companion soft-notice UX exists).

### Design constraints

1. **Engine keeps force.** Auto threshold, emergency path, and survival
   contract remain the backstop. Self-compact is best-effort, not a second
   authority that can race the guard (#5620 lesson: no competing ceremony —
   but a *single explicit model action* is a different contract than a prose
   "please compact now" line in every turn).
2. **Single turn-loop / single compact owner:** reuse the existing manual
   compaction op path (`handle_manual_compaction_op` / `Op::CompactContext`)
   rather than a parallel implementation. One summarizer, one survival
   contract, one artifact save.
3. **Note-to-self:** optional short `note` (or `focus`) argument on the tool,
   passed into the same channel as `/compact <focus>`
   (`CompactionConfig.focus`) / operator `summary_instructions` so a deliberate
   note can influence the summary or be re-stated after it — without inventing
   a second memory store.
4. **Gate: default OFF.** Tool catalog entry behind capability/scope (same
   pattern as `Capability::Checkpoint`); opt-in only (config flag or posture).
   Do not ship default-on before the companion notice issue lands.
5. **Idempotence / concurrency:** one compact per tool call. While a pass is
   running, further requests are rejected or dropped as redundant — today a
   concurrent manual `/compact` gets "already in progress", and a deferred
   manual is dropped when an auto pass starts/settles
   (`compaction_flow.rs`). A model tool should follow the same rules, not
   invent a merge.
6. **KV-cache:** tool schema is session-pinned prefix — state the effect
   (catalog change only if gated; no volatile thresholds in the tool
   description that churn every turn).

### Shape options (maintainers decide)

| Option | Shape | Effort | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. `self_compact` tool → existing manual compact op (+ optional note) | Thin wrapper over today's path | Low–Med | Need clear tool description so models do not spam it |
| B. Allow model to emit the same steer/op the UI sends on Ctrl+L | Minimal new surface | Med | Authorization / who may compact mid-turn |
| C. No tool; only soft notice (companion) so the model asks the user | Smallest | Low | Still needs a human in the loop — weak for off-loop |

Recommended framing: **A**, **default OFF**, after or with soft notice so the
model actually knows when the action is useful.

### Open questions for maintainers

- Opt-in mechanism: capability bit, settings flag, or posture-only?
- Should a model-initiated compact skip the "ask user" step entirely when
  posture is full auto, or always confirm?
- Does `note` merge with operator `summary_instructions` or only affect a
  one-off pass?
- Interaction with #6217: should the tool description embed the same remaining
  budget numbers (careful: churn)?

## Use case

- Long refactor: model finishes module N, context is 70–75%, next step will
  explode tool output — self-compact now with a note "module N done, start N+1
  from tests/".
- Off-loop worker with no human watching `/settings`: cannot run `/compact`
  itself today (and headless `exec` has no manual compact path).
- Recovery after a noisy tool: model decides history is past usefulness and
  cuts before the engine's 80% line (optional, if allowed).

## Alternatives considered

- **Status quo:** operator types `/compact` or waits for 80% — works for
  interactive, not for autonomous boundaries.
- **Only `memory_checkpoint_put`:** preserves state across *engine* compact,
  but does not let the model choose the cut or attach note-to-self for the
  summary pass.
- **Re-enable prose "run /compact" in turn_meta under auto ON:** rejected by
  #5620 (competing ceremony) — a real tool is an explicit action, not ambient
  instruction spam.
- **Full three-threshold notice/warning/force stack in the model:** larger UX
  surface; soft notice (companion) + optional tool is the smaller coherent
  slice.
- **Claude Code-style "ask the user" only:** needs a human; does not cover
  off-loop workers.

## Impact

Unlocks off-loop / fleet patterns already present in the product (sub-agents,
headless runs) without removing engine-owned defaults. Interactive TUI users
can ignore the tool while default stays OFF. Pairs with soft notice (companion
issue) and meter (#6217).

## Additional context

- Tool catalog precedent (model decides when to spend an action): closed
  **#4196** (agent-callable verify/critique).
- Checkpoint tools already gated by capability:
  `crates/memory/src/protocol.rs` (`Capability::Checkpoint`).
- Manual compact path already exists and is operator-only today
  (`Op::CompactContext`, `handle_manual_compaction_op`, `/compact <focus>`).
- Engine-owned force under auto ON is intentional (#5620 close rationale:
  sixteen tool reads / three automatic compactions, no ESCALATED ceremony).
- Reference design outside this repo (not a dependency): self-compact Pi agent
  (disler/self-compact-pi-agent, video 3b0U4_02bAE) — staged thresholds, a
  model-called compact tool, note-to-self around the ~270k mark (from the
  talk transcript; design contrast only).
- Companion proposal: soft model-facing notice while auto ON — **#6425**.

_No secrets or session logs in this issue. Static analysis of local fork +
public docs; not yet validated on a live release build._

issues.body:
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.13 (body: '0.9.13 ships /pet'; filed 2026-09-14).
>
> **What remains**
>
> * Human with a Kitty-protocol terminal: run the pet/QA.md real-terminal procedure (docked/full, resize, Escape image cleanup, braille fallback, tmux/SSH, reduced motion) and record measured frame timing, CPU, RSS and input latency
> * Run shared-owner acceptance with the TUI habitat and the desktop view on one live session (one producer, one audio lease, owner restart, competing owner, storage failure) and record it in pet/QA.md
> * Forward accepted Engine metadata to the pet from crates/app-server, not only the TUI producer
> * Record the default-appearance decision against crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/appearance.rs Default, and tick off item 5 after confirming owner.rs:931-946 covers the failed case as well
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
>
> * Item 5 (typed completion outcome) appears done: crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/owner.rs:931-946 at v0.10.1 feeds turn_outcome completed vs interrupted through the projection and asserts an interrupted turn gets no Done presence and no done_effect_id
> * Item 3 (Engine metadata beyond the TUI) not done: git grep -i pet in crates/app-server/src at v0.10.1 returns only an unrelated 'competing' test name (daemon_windows.rs:327); no pet metadata forwarding
> * Item 4 (default appearance) cannot be confirmed as decided: crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/appearance.rs:15-27 has a single hard-coded Default with no record of the 'Codewhale by default' decision
> * Item 1 (real-terminal qualification) has no receipt: pet/QA.md:28 still describes the Kitty-probe plus fallback-terminal check as a procedure, and pet/QA.md:253-254 says native active-session delivery and device transport remain open
> * Item 2 (shared-owner acceptance across TUI and desktop) has no receipt in pet/QA.md or pet/SHARED.md at v0.10.1; could not verify it was ever run
> * Issue comment from the 0.10.0 readiness pass ([#6370](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6370>)) states nothing on the list was executed; no commit in v0.10.0..v0.10.1 and no CHANGELOG line references #6155

---

0.9.13 ships `/pet` ([#6154](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6154>), from [#6110](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6110>) plus the prepared shared-owner/Kitty patch). What it ships on is test evidence and the prepared-archive receipts; these acceptance items were explicitly not done and stay open here (split out of #6109 so the umbrella can track the cross-surface owner work):

1. **Real-terminal visual qualification** of the Kitty pixel habitat: docked→full transitions, continuous motion, resize, Escape image cleanup, a fallback (braille) terminal, tmux/SSH behaviour, reduced motion. Measure delivered frame timing, CPU, RSS, bandwidth and input latency in the terminal; the only numbers today are the raster microbenchmark (17.09 ms mean / 19.55 ms p95, \~150 KB/frame, excludes transport) and a 30 Hz simulation. 60 fps is a target, not a measured result. Computer Use access to Ghostty/Terminal was denied in the preparing session; do not relabel browser or native screenshots as terminal proof.
2. **Shared-owner acceptance**: open the TUI habitat and the desktop/browser view on one live session, compare identity/tick/digest at a retained frame, interact from either side, close and reopen the TUI, confirm continued ownership, one producer, one audio lease, durable appearance. Exercise owner restart, a competing owner, source change, storage failure.
