prs.title: fix(setup): keep the setup checkpoint when a second instance is running
prs.body:
## Summary

Four defects, from two user reports of the same class.

The first: "Setup provider/model state was not saved: failed to persist setup
state to `C:\Users\asus.codewhale\setup_state.json`". The path is wrong, the
write failed for a reason, and `doctor` was independently reporting a
half-applied setup that did not exist. Each had its own cause.

The second: "宠物模式未能保存：无法删除要被替换的文件。(os error 1175)" from
`/config pet_mode --save`. Same class, one API further along: the earlier fix
covered `atomic_write`'s `MoveFileExW`, and `settings.toml` goes through
`ReplaceFileW`, which reports its own fourth contention code.

## Changes

- **A setup checkpoint survives a held destination.** Two running Codewhale
  windows share one home and both rewrite `setup_state.json` when the provider
  or model changes. `atomic_write` staged the write correctly and then lost the
  replacing rename: the loser of that race finds the destination held open for a
  read, and Windows refuses the rename outright while that handle lives (no
  `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`). Only that condition is retried — six attempts,
  `n * 50ms`, 750ms in total.
- **A settings write survives the same thing.** `settings.toml` is replaced with
  `ReplaceFileW` rather than `MoveFileExW`, so the retry lives at that call too.
  Both now share one allow-list:

  - 5 `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`
  - 32 `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`
  - 33 `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`
  - 1175 `ERROR_UNABLE_TO_REMOVE_REPLACED`

  Why 1175 belongs there and `ReplaceFileW`'s other two failure codes do not:
  1175 is documented as "the destination file is not modified, and the
  replacement file still exists under its original name", so a retry starts from
  the state it just read. 1176 and 1177 can leave the replacement renamed away,
  or holding the old file's streams with its contents no longer guaranteed, so
  those surface at once.

  `SetFileAttributesW` failing is about the *source*, not a held destination, so
  it is never retried; and the failure path still restores
  `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY` before each retry, so `TempPath` keeps its cleanup
  behavior if the last attempt loses too.

- **The message stops eating its own cause.** It used `{err}`, which prints only
  the outermost `context` and drops the source chain, so the path was the only
  thing left to look at. It now uses `{err:#}`.
- **`doctor` stops flagging a user's own temp-named logs.** The
  `stale_setup_temp_files` check matched any file whose name starts with
  `.tmp`, so scratch files such as `.tmp-build-release.log` made a clean home
  report as half-applied. It now matches what a staged write leaves behind when
  it never lands: `.tmpXXXXXX` with no extension, which is the shape
  `tempfile` creates for a sibling.
- **A note keeps the backslashes in a path.** This is where the wrong path in
  the first report came from: the note is correct, the renderer is correct, and
  the note was the one that did not escape. A transcript note is machine-generated
  and names paths, but it goes through the markdown renderer, which honours
  CommonMark §2.4 — a backslash before ASCII punctuation is an escape, so `\.`
  yields `.`. `escape_note_backslashes` now doubles a bare backslash in note
  prose, at the one place every note passes through.

  Three regions are passed through exactly as written, because the renderer
  already copies them verbatim and doubling a backslash inside one would
  *print* the extra backslash:

  - a fenced block, closed only by a run at least as long as its opener;
  - a line carrying a delimiter the renderer treats as a passthrough (backtick,
    `*`, `~~`) — inline code, bold, italic and strikethrough are the shapes a
    note's third-party text (MCP guidance, extension prompts) brings with it;
  - a table row.

  `_`-delimited emphasis is deliberately not a passthrough trigger: `_` is
  everywhere in identifiers (`setup_state.json`), and a false positive would
  leave the paths this pass exists to protect untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Run locally on Windows:

- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime --lib -- only_a_held_destination` →
  **1 passed**: the allow-list retries 5/32/33/1175 and refuses 2/3/112/87.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- only_a_contended` → **1 passed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- persistence` → **29 passed; 0
  failed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- a_system_note` → **3 passed**;
  `a_fence_of_four_backticks_is_not_closed_by_three` → **1 passed**. A plain
  Windows path survives intact, a fenced path is not doubled, a fence shorter
  than its opener does not close it, and inline code / bold / strikethrough / a
  table row are passed through.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- doctor_setup_consistency` → **4 passed**,
  the two existing cases included, so the narrower match did not stop the check
  from firing on a real orphan.
- `codewhale doctor` on the authoring machine no longer prints the
  `half-applied setup detected (stale_setup_temp_files_in_codewhale_home)` line
  it printed before this change.

**What I could reproduce of the 1175 mechanism, and what I could not:** a
destination held by an ordinary reader makes `ReplaceFileW` fail with 32, and
the same call succeeds once the handle is closed — that is what the retry buys.
A handle opened *with* `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` plus a read-only mapped view did not
reproduce 1175; the replace simply succeeded. So 1175's presence on the list
rests on its documented post-failure state rather than on a local repro. If a
maintainer can reproduce it deterministically, that would be worth adding as a
test.

Not run locally: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`. CI is the
first full run; treat this section as what was actually observed, not a claim
about the whole gate.

### A note about Windows on `main`

When this branch was written, `main` did not build its test target on Windows,
for reasons this branch does not touch:

- `crates/tui/src/extension_host/supervisor.rs:1553` — `native_snapshot_roots`
  is read only under `cfg(not(windows))`, so `dead_code` denies the build;
- `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:1902` — `load_global_context_file` is
  `#[cfg(test)]` and has no caller in the test target;
- `crates/util/Cargo.toml` does not enable reqwest's `stream` feature, so
  `utils/response_body.rs` cannot call `bytes_stream()`.

Those were from the `[skip ci]` crate-split commits, and the Linux jobs were
unaffected. They are left out of this branch.

## Checklist

- [x] Updated docs or comments as needed (root CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`, packed
      slice regenerated with `scripts/sync-changelog.sh`)
- [x] Added or updated tests where relevant
- [ ] Verified TUI behavior manually if UI changes (the note path is covered by
      unit tests on the rendered spans)
- [x] Harvested/co-authored credit uses a GitHub numeric noreply address (no
  external contribution in this change)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: two user-visible failures of the same class — a write refused because
another handle held the destination — whose parts turned out to be independent
defects.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

prs.title: style(tui): apply rustfmt to mcp
prs.body:
## What and why

The CI lint job first reported two existing rustfmt differences in `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs`. After those were corrected, Clippy reached existing `large_enum_variant` errors in the serializable protocol and TUI request enums, followed by runtime and utility lint findings.

This PR restores the lint gate with focused changes:

- applies the formatter output in `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs`;
- boxes large enum payloads while preserving their existing JSON representations;
- uses idiomatic `Default`, `Option::replace`, helper ordering and lock-lifetime fixes for the runtime, utility and TUI lint findings;
- keeps Clap parsing behavior unchanged by boxing only the MCP add command's argument payload;
- gates test-target-only probe paths precisely so production dead-code checks stay strict.

The runtime changes are layout and lint fixes; they do not change production behavior.

The PR also fixes two deterministic CI data issues exposed while validating the branch:

- pins the receipt-covered DSH compatibility adapter to LF so a Windows checkout cannot change its source hash;
- records the shipped first-party marketplace revision in both changelog copies so the release consistency check matches the asset.

## Issue

No-Issue: restore the repository CI gates for existing formatting, Clippy, cross-platform receipt and release-consistency drift.

## How I tested it

- `git diff --check`
- `./scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check`
- `python3 scripts/check-provider-registry.py`
- `python3 scripts/check-bundled-plugin-claims.py`
- CI run [40596056980](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/40596056980): Version drift, formatting, Clippy, MSRV, Windows workspace tests, extension-host runtime checks, safety gate, mobile smoke and npm wrapper smoke passed.

The Ubuntu workspace test still reports a group of existing baseline failures in untouched CLI/TUI integration and PTY tests (configuration migration, provider detection, outbox and terminal timing). The failure is not in files changed by this PR; it needs a separate mainline investigation. Cargo is not installed in this environment, so Rust compilation and tests are supplied by CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused lint and CI repairs, started from current `main`
- [x] Wire JSON shapes preserved
- [x] Cross-platform receipt bytes are pinned
- [x] Changelog copies are synchronized

prs.title: fix(tui): only say "Model set to" when the model changes
prs.body:
## What and why

Hosts send `Op::SetModel` whenever they resync the engine's model, not only when it changes: `/effort high` resends the current model, and so does `/clear`. The engine answered every one with `Model set to: <model>`, which lands in the footer after the host's own receipt. `/effort high` at 100×24, before:

```
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])                     Model set to: mock
 mock · thinking: high   context 0%   cost: unknown (billing basis unknown)
```

After:

```
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])                 Reasoning effort: high
 mock · thinking: high   context 0%   cost: unknown (billing basis unknown)
```

The `SetModel` handler now notes whether the model differs from the one already set and only sends the status then, the way `SetCompaction` has reported only a real switch since 04de8eb67. Everything else the handler does still runs on every resync (route limits, capabilities, prompt refresh, `SessionUpdated`). Switching models still says `Model set to: <model>`: `/model mock-two` ends with `Model set to: mock-two` in both builds.

## Issue

No-Issue: an unchanged model resync replaces the footer receipt with "Model set to"; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock, with this change and with a build of `main` from before it: `/effort high`, then `/model mock-two`. The footers above are from those runs.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15362 passed, none failed, with the engine tests among them.
- Merged into `main` at 7fe0cc2b4: fmt and `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags are clean, and the 1710 engine, model and effort tests pass.

prs.title: fix(commands): don't total unreported cache tokens as 0 in /cache
prs.body:
## What and why

`format_cache_history` renders a turn with no cache telemetry as `—` in its hit, miss and write cells and keeps it out of the totals, so a route that never reports cache tokens doesn't read as one that never hits. The totals line still printed those empty sums as numbers. One tool turn against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that reports no cache fields, then `/cache` at 120×50, before:

```
    1  openai/mock                  20     70      —      —      —       —        —           —   7s
    ...
    sum_write: 0  sum_reasoning: 0 (already inside out)
    Σ in: 20   Σ hit: 0   Σ miss: 0   avg hit ratio: —
```

After:

```
    1  openai/mock                  20     70      —      —      —       —        —           —   8s
    ...
    sum_write: —  sum_reasoning: 0 (already inside out)
    Σ in: 20   Σ hit: —   Σ miss: —   avg hit ratio: —
```

The function now notes whether any listed turn reported cache telemetry and prints `—` for `sum_write`, `Σ hit` and `Σ miss` when none did, the same mark the rows and `avg hit ratio` already use. Once one turn has reported, the totals read as before, so the `cache_history` fixtures don't change. `Σ in` and `sum_reasoning` aren't cache telemetry and keep their numbers.

## Issue

No-Issue: /cache totals unreported cache tokens as 0; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME against a local OpenAI-compatible mock, one tool turn and then `/cache`, with this change and with a build from before it. Apart from the age and ttft readouts, the two totals lines above are the only lines that changed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean. CI's clippy is clean for `codewhale-commands` and `codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands`: 28 passed. `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15277 passed, none failed, with the `/cache` tests and the `cache_history` baselines among them.
- Merged into `main` at 17ebeb5f6, fmt is clean, and the 28 `codewhale-commands` tests and the 425 cache and diagnostics tests in `codewhale-tui` pass. CI's clippy (1.99) stops on `main` itself there, at `crates/protocol/src/op.rs:209`; with `--no-deps`, `codewhale-commands` is clean.

prs.title: fix(catalog): read the token limits a live model listing states
prs.body:
## Summary

A route that is not OrcaRouter, OpenRouter or Concentrate builds its live
catalog rows through the generic branch of `catalog_delta_from_models_body`,
and that branch gave every row `limit: None`. A provider that publishes
per-model context and output ceilings in its own `/v1/models` body therefore
lost them, and a custom route with no bundled catalog row fell back to
`LEGACY_DEEPSEEK_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS` (128K). Operators saw 128K for a model
whose listing states 1M, carrying an `unverified ctx` chip that correctly
admitted the number was a guess.

The same body is now read a second time, best-effort, to attach the limits each
row states. Nothing here can fail a refresh that used to succeed.

## Changes

- **Recognised shapes**: the OpenAI `limit` block (`context`, `output`), flat
  `context_length` / `context_window` / `max_model_len` / `max_context_length`,
  `max_output_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`, and a relay `metadata` block
  carrying `context_limit`, `context_budget` and `output_budget`.
- **Precedence**: `metadata.context_limit` outranks `metadata.context_budget`,
  because the first states the model capability and the second the share one
  deployment will accept. `limit.context` stays ahead of every flat field.
- **Per-field parsing**: candidates are parsed in priority order and the first
  one that reads as a positive whole token count wins. The first draft selected
  a field by presence and then parsed whatever it had selected, so
  `{"context_length": 200000, "metadata": {"context_limit": "1M"}}` produced no
  context at all and the route fell back to 128K — the exact symptom this pass
  exists to remove. A malformed field now costs its own candidate, nothing else.
- **`input` stays empty**, so no route is clamped on an inference.
- **OpenCode Go**: the per-model limit map is keyed through the same
  canonicalization the cutline applies, so a rewritten roster id still matches
  the row the provider stated.
- **Isolation**: the roster still comes from the provider's typed parser, and
  this pass drops only that row's limits when a row is unreadable.
- **One existing test updated**: `custom_catalog_schema_ignores_table_name`
  pinned the generic branch's whole verdict, `limit.is_none()` included. Its
  point is that the Baseten enrichment (pricing, `supported_features`) never
  reaches a non-Baseten endpoint, and that still holds; a flat `context_length`
  is a field any OpenAI-shaped listing may carry. It now asserts the ceiling
  that survives and the enrichment that does not, so it keeps guarding #6289
  instead of the 128K fallback.

## Evidence

Measured against a local stub listing, unchanged input, pre-fix binary versus
this one:

```
row-a  metadata.context_limit "1M" + context_length 200000
       before: ctx absent (route fell back to 128000), out 32000
       after:  ctx 200000, out 32000
row-b  limit {context 1048000, output 64000}   both: unchanged
row-c  no limit stated                          both: absent
```

Against the relay that reported the defect, `model resolve` now answers
`context_tokens: 1000000, output_tokens: 32000` for `claude-haiku-5.5` and
`context_tokens: 1048000` for `deepseek-v4-pro`, both `used_fallback: false`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Six new cases in `crates/tui/src/client/test_cases_09.rs`; synthetic ids, no
network. All six pass on `Test (ubuntu-latest)`:

```
PASS limits_a_live_listing_states_context_and_output_ceilings
PASS limits_a_relay_metadata_block_states_capability_ahead_of_budget
PASS limits_one_unreadable_field_costs_only_its_own_candidate
PASS limits_a_row_stating_no_readable_ceiling_is_left_out
PASS limits_a_body_without_a_data_array_yields_no_limits
PASS limits_a_generic_route_keeps_the_limits_its_listing_states
```

### First CI round: what was this branch and what was the tree

`Test (ubuntu-latest)` reported 18 failures on the previous revision. One was
this branch, and it is fixed in `b427867e8`:

- `client::tests::custom_catalog_schema_ignores_table_name` — see the last
  bullet under Changes.

The other 17 are PTY and environment tests whose failure points do not touch
`client.rs` or the `/models` parser, and they fail for terminal-shaped reasons.
Two examples from the same log:

- `automations_editor_pty::…_across_terminal_sizes` — `missing "second /
  private-second"`, with a 12x40 frame that rendered only the first row; the
  case took 87.8s.
- the three `diagnostic_read_only` cases — sealed-home helpers.

The full list: `automations_editor_pty`, `contextual_tips_pty` (×2),
`diagnostic_read_only` (×3), `exec_stream_drop_acceptance`,
`extension_host::tests::auto_uses_node_…`, `launch_card_pty`,
`lifecycle_outbox_exec` (×3), `plugin_e2e_acceptance`,
`screen_mode_inline_pty`, and two `codewhale-cli` `config_bundles` /
`config_set` cases. I have not run those on a clean `main`, so I am stating
where they fail rather than claiming they are pre-existing.

### Three jobs red for reasons outside this diff

- **Lint**: `cargo fmt --check` diffs only `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs:1442` and
  `:4498`, two hunks from `e1acc381a`. This branch does not touch that file;
  `client.rs` is clean under `rustfmt 1.9.0`.
- **Version drift**: `Feature commit 4cf2d2cff references #7093 / #7097, but no
  release-note receipt exists`. `4cf2d2cff` is already on `main`; the job's own
  text calls this advisory for `v0.10.1..HEAD`.
- **Test (windows-latest)** and **Extension host runtimes (windows-latest)**:
  - `crates/tui/src/extension_host/supervisor.rs:1554` — `native_snapshot_roots`
    is read only under `cfg(not(windows))`, so `dead_code` denies the build;
  - `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:1906` — `load_global_context_file` is
    never used on Windows;
  - `src/dsh/dsh-message-compat.js` no longer names
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand@0.2.1-rc.2`.

  All of it arrived before this branch. `MSRV check (1.89)` and `Safety gate`
  pass. I can send the Windows lint fixes as a separate PR if that helps.

## Checklist

- [x] Updated docs or comments as needed (root CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`, packed
      slice regenerated with `scripts/sync-changelog.sh`)
- [x] Added or updated tests where relevant
- [ ] Verified TUI behavior manually if UI changes (no UI change)
- [x] Harvested/co-authored credit uses a GitHub numeric noreply address (no
  external contribution in this change)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: found while diagnosing a relay whose `/v1/models` states 1M for a
model the route reported as 128K. It shares the symptom in #7096 (a 1M window
reported as 128K) but not its cause: that report's rows do carry the limit and
it is dropped by the endpoint-identity guard in `complete_from`, while here the
row's limit was never read at all.

## Attribution

prs.title: fix(commands): localize diff feedback
prs.body:
## What and why

`/diff` returns English feedback and a pager title even when another UI language is selected. Route its nine user-facing messages through the existing presentation facet and typed diagnostics mapping, with translations in all 15 complete locale packs.

For example, with Simplified Chinese selected, `No changes since session start` becomes `会话开始以来没有变更`. English output, error/action behavior, filenames and raw Git payloads stay unchanged.

## Issue

Refs #7071 (partial)

This PR addresses `/diff`. `/undo` and the other remaining surfaces are still tracked in #7071.

## How I tested it

On Linux, using the installed toolchain and linker:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check HEAD^
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=/usr/bin/cc scripts/dev-cargo.sh test -p codewhale-commands --lib --locked
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=/usr/bin/cc scripts/dev-cargo.sh test -p codewhale-localization --lib --locked
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=/usr/bin/cc scripts/dev-cargo.sh clippy -p codewhale-commands --lib --locked --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=/usr/bin/cc scripts/dev-cargo.sh clippy -p codewhale-localization --lib --locked --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or
```

Formatting, whitespace checks, 28 commands tests, 54 localization tests, and the focused Clippy checks passed. The existing command fixture now supplies English presentation, and its capability expectation includes `PRESENTATION`.

A committed regression case also runs the actual diff handler against the Simplified Chinese catalog and verifies translated interpolation, the stat header, pager title and unchanged raw patch. It fails against the original English-only handler and passes with this fix. The changed command/localization crates additionally pass Clippy with `--all-targets --all-features --no-deps`.

A separate local reproduction harness (not included in this commit) invokes the actual registered handlers and real catalog/mapping/interpolation. It reproduces the Chinese failure against the original handler, then checks the updated handler across all complete locale packs. Its output is:

```text
BASELINE: 8/8 Chinese expectations fail as reproduced; sample "No changes since session start"
FIXED Chinese sample: 会话开始以来没有变更
PASS: 120 localized outcomes (8 × 15), 8 English parity comparisons, 135 catalog/mapping contracts, 30 opaque-payload cases; action/error/patch preserved
```

Clippy including dependencies encountered the existing `clippy::large_enum_variant` warning in unchanged `crates/protocol/src/op.rs:209`. The focused checks above exclude dependencies and use the project's documented allowances.

The full TUI/workspace build, real host Git collection and interactive terminal/pager rendering were not exercised locally. No UI screenshot or recording was captured; the reproduction verifies returned messages and pager metadata, not visual rendering.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

The docs/feature-registry item is not applicable: this fixes translation of the existing `/diff` feature.

AI disclosure: AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, translation, testing and review on behalf of @laozidabo. The account owner has not personally written or technically reviewed it.

prs.title: fix(tui): shed to the folder name before clipping the launch card's path
prs.body:
## What and why

The launch card's context row keeps the last two components of the workspace path and then clips the result from the right, so when those two are wider than the row, the clip lands on the folder you are in. A workspace `ws` under a parent folder called `customer-portal-redesign`, at 50×24, before:

```
      ⣀⣴⣶⣾⣶⣆        codewhale      v0.10.2 (dev)
    ⢀⣼⣿⠛⠉⠉⠙⠻⠟⠃      …/customer-portal-redesign/…
```

After:

```
      ⣀⣴⣶⣾⣶⣆        codewhale      v0.10.2 (dev)
    ⢀⣼⣿⠛⠉⠉⠙⠻⠟⠃      …/ws · main
```

At 40×12 the row went from `…/customer-portal-redesign…` to `…/ws · main`, and at 38×20 from `…/customer-portal-rede…`. It now drops to the folder alone when two components don't fit, and still clamps after that. That is the order `empty_state_caption` in the same file already follows ("Better a bare name than a path clipped mid-component."), and it is the caption this screen shows once the card dissolves: at 50 columns, after the first keystroke, it reads `…/customer-portal-redesign/ws · main`. With the shorter path the branch fits again, so ` · main` comes back at these widths, as it shows whenever the full row fits.

#7103 fixes the same kind of clip in `/context` by cutting from the left. This one sheds components instead, because this file already has a rule for it.

## Issue

No-Issue: the launch card clips the workspace folder off a long path; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, with this change and with a build of `main` at eaff21a8b, and captured the launch card at 140×40, 100×32, 80×24, 60×16, 50×24, 40×12 and 38×20 under that long parent folder. Only 50×24, 40×12 and 38×20 changed, each in that one row. With the workspace directly under HOME, 40×12 and 30×12 read `~/ws · main` in both builds.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 14401 passed, none failed, with the 299 `underwater`, launch, `workspace_context` and truncation tests among them. `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.
- On `main` itself, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails in `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs` and the blocking-calls budget fails in files this doesn't touch. CI's clippy (1.99) stops at `crates/protocol/src/op.rs:209`; with `--no-deps` it flags 13 places in `codewhale-tui`, none of them in `underwater.rs`.

prs.title: fix(fleet): enable rename_exclusive on Android to prevent SELinux EACCES linkat fallback
prs.body:
Refs #6983

## Summary
This PR enables exclusive rename (`renameat2` with `RENAME_NOREPLACE`) on Android target platforms across `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`, `crates/tui/src/plugins/builtin.rs`, and `crates/config/src/private_directory.rs`.

## Problem & Root Cause
Context compaction and snapshot publishing on Android (Termux) fail with `Permission denied (os error 13)`.

In PR #6983, Android support was added to `WorkspaceFile::open_confined` by including `target_os = "android"`. However, the conditional compilation attribute in `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs` for `rename_exclusive` remained:
```rust
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
fn rename_exclusive(...) -> io::Result<bool> { ... }

#[cfg(all(unix, not(any(target_os = "linux", target_vendor = "apple"))))]
fn rename_exclusive(...) -> io::Result<bool> {
    Ok(false)
}
```
In Rust's target architecture, `target_os = "android"` and `target_os = "linux"` are mutually exclusive (`#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` evaluates to `false` for `aarch64-linux-android`).
Because `rename_exclusive` returned `Ok(false)` on Android, callers such as `atomic_write_retained` (invoked during compaction / write_session_relative_immutable) fell back to creating hard links via `libc::linkat`.

On Android devices, SELinux policy enforces that applications in the `untrusted_app` domain (such as Termux and other applications running within app private directories like `/data/data/...`) are explicitly denied permission to create hard links (`linkat`), consistently returning:
```
os error 13: Permission denied (os error 13)
```

## Solution
1. In `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`:
   - Updated `rename_exclusive` and `exclusive_rename_outcome` target cfgs to `#[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]`.
   - Updated fallback cfg to `#[cfg(all(unix, not(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android", target_vendor = "apple"))))]`.
2. In `crates/tui/src/plugins/builtin.rs`:
   - Updated `publish_snapshot` target cfgs to include `target_os = "android"`.
3. In `crates/config/src/private_directory.rs`:
   - Updated `move_no_replace`, `linux_boot_id`, `linux_process_start_predates_boot`, and process status validation to support `target_os = "android"`.

Android uses the Linux kernel (kernel >= 3.15, including all modern Android kernels), where `SYS_renameat2` (syscall 276 on aarch64) with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (flag 1) is fully supported and allowed under Android SELinux `untrusted_app` domain. This completely avoids the restricted `linkat` fallback.

## Verification
- Verified on Android device (`aarch64-linux-android`, Android kernel 6.6) under the `u:r:untrusted_app_27` SELinux domain:
  - `linkat` reproduces `errno=13 (Permission denied)`.
  - `SYS_renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` succeeds with return code `0`, preserving atomicity without overwriting existing files.
- `node web/scripts/check-facts.mjs` passed cleanly (`committed facts.generated.ts matches workspace`).
- `cargo check --offline -p codewhale-cli` compiles cleanly without warnings or errors.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the workspace folder in view when /context shortens its path
prs.body:
## What and why

The `/context` inspector shortens the workspace path with `semantic_truncate`, which cuts from the right, so a narrow pane keeps the root and drops the folder that says which workspace this is. With a workspace path a few columns wider than the pane, at 50×16, before:

```
  …/cw-tools/ru…
```

After:

```
  …cw-tools/run/ws
```

(Both lines are shortened here; the real ones start at the root and the volume name.) This switches that one line to `workspace_context::truncate_left`, the helper the status line's workspace chip already uses for the same reason, so the tail stays and the `…` moves to the front. A path that fits renders as before: at 72×20 and 120×30 the inspector is identical with and without the change.

## Issue

prs.title: fix(ci): preserve DSH receipt bytes on Windows

## What and why

The Windows extension-host job checks the exact SHA-256 receipt for `src/dsh/dsh-message-compat.js`. The repository currently leaves that file under the default `text=auto` rule, so a Windows checkout can rewrite it to CRLF and make the pinned source receipt fail even though Unix checkouts remain unchanged.

This adds an explicit `eol=lf` attribute for the receipt-pinned source file. It keeps the bytes identical across platforms without changing runtime behavior.

## Issue

No-Issue: repair cross-platform checkout normalization for the existing Windows CI failure.

## How I tested it

- `git check-attr -a -- crates/tui/extension-host/src/dsh/dsh-message-compat.js` reports `eol: lf`
- `git ls-files --eol` reports the file as LF with the explicit attribute
- `git diff --check`

prs.title: fix(catalog): inherit model facts across a provider's host move (#7096)
prs.body:
## What and why

OpenCode Go's live roster is still fetched from `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, while models.dev now publishes the provider's `api` as `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1`. `CatalogOffering::complete_from` required those two base URLs to fingerprint-match before inheriting *any* fact, so the models.dev limit for `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (1,000,000) was dropped and the window fell back to `LEGACY_DEEPSEEK_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS` (128K).

Thanks @ImBearChild for the precise diagnosis. It pinned the exact guard, both fingerprints and the fallback path.

A context window belongs to the model, not to the host serving it. For a live row completed from a model-describing layer (bundled, models.dev, cloud facts, Codewhale corrections):

- the configured base must still match the live roster (unchanged)
- the published-base match now gates only **endpoint-scoped** facts: `transport`, `provider_api`, `provider_npm`, `status`, `cost`
- **model-scoped** facts (limits, modalities, reasoning, family, etc.) are inherited regardless of host

Live-to-live and config/user-override arms are unchanged. `complete_facts_from` (the signed cloud patch path) still copies everything.

**Not in this PR:** moving the `opencode-go` descriptor to the `inference/` host. The current docs split chat (`/inference/go/openai/v1`), Anthropic messages (`/inference/go/anthropic/v1`) and models (`/inference/go/v1`), which the single model-aware `base_url` can't express. `zen/go/v1/models` still returns 200 (checked 2026-10-26), so the route itself is healthy.

## Issue

Closes #7096

## How I tested it

- `scripts/dev-test.sh config`: 806 run, 806 passed, 1 skipped
- `scripts/dev-test.sh tui provider_lake catalog context_window opencode`: 365 run, 365 passed
- Throwaway reproduction, not committed per repo policy: a live `opencode-go` row at `zen/go/v1` plus a models.dev row with `api = inference/go/openai/v1` and `limit.context = 1_000_000`.
  - Without the fix: **FAILED** (context stays `None`).
  - With the fix: passes. Context is 1,000,000, `provider_api` and `cost` are not inherited, and a mismatched configured base still returns `false`.
- `cargo fmt -p codewhale-config -- --check` clean

Not run: full workspace suite, or a live `/setup` session against OpenCode Go.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior (existing suites; reproduction above was not committed)
- [x] No user-facing feature added or changed

prs.title: feat(context): per-scope instruction budgets with visible truncation (#6526)
prs.body:
## What this is

Standing instructions (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.codewhale/instructions.md`, the
global `~/.codewhale|.agents|.deepseek` layer, the configured
`instructions = [...]` array, and `.codewhale/rules`) are budgeted **per scope,
in estimated tokens**, and every trim or skip is visible to the user, the model,
and `/context`.

Today all of it goes through one 48 KiB byte pool. This branch replaces that with
two independent scopes and a structured notice contract. It is the design in
`docs/design/INSTRUCTION_BUDGET_6526.md` (committed here, §1–§10), which is the
plan discussed on #6526.

## Status

Merged `main` into the branch, so the PR is mergeable. That merge resolves the
overlap with `10ce9cde` in `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs` in favour of this
branch's loader — see the next section for what that costs and what the
alternative looks like. `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` on the merged tree
exits 0.

## Relationship to `10ce9cde` (`Refs #6526`, "part 1")

`10ce9cde` already landed part 1 on `main`: an instruction file over the 100 KiB
per-file cap is now **truncated** (head + sized marker) instead of skipped, with a
sized warning. This branch was written before that commit and does not contain it;
the two overlap in `project_context.rs` (`read_context_file`,
`load_dir_instructions`, the global loader, the source listing) and `prompts.rs`
(`read_prompt_file_bounded` / `cap_prompt_text`).

Where they disagree, and this is the decision I need from you:

| | `10ce9cde` (on `main`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| file over the per-file cap | truncate to 100 KiB, warn | skip at 8 MiB (memory-safety ceiling), notice |
| aggregate ceiling | 48 KiB bytes | `min(100k tokens, 25% of usable window)` per scope |
| trim direction for one oversized file | keep the tail | keep the head |

The obvious reconciliation — and what I would do if you want it — is to keep
`10ce9cde`'s truncation as the *content* policy (100 KiB, sized marker, sized
warning, reusing `read_prompt_text_bounded`) and keep the 8 MiB ceiling only as
the memory guard that skips, with the per-scope token budgets applied on top.
Tell me which column wins and I will rebase onto `main` and adjust.

## What the branch does

**Selection** (OpenCode's model, codewhale's own sources preserved): `AGENTS.md`
wins; a directory without one falls back to `CLAUDE.md` (`claude_fallback = false`
opts out); an explicit `project_instruction_imports = ["claude"]` co-reads. A
candidate skipped for size or emptiness counts as absent and the next one is
tried; a file already loaded from a wider scope is reported as a duplicate and
does not trigger the fallback. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is the last resort after the
six global candidates.

**Budgets**: usable window = route window − output ceiling − max(10%, 2,048
tokens). Each scope is `min(absolute_tokens, percent × usable)`; defaults 100k /
25%. A scope over budget drops whole files from the broadest end first (root-most
ancestor, then the workspace last); a single file above the remaining budget keeps
its head with a marker carrying bytes and estimated tokens. Rules are charged to
the project scope after the chain and keep a head-first trim. The configured
`instructions` entries are global authority and are charged there.

**Skips are not trims**: `file_max_bytes` (8 MiB), an empty file, the 50-file
rules cap, and a symlinked duplicate are reported with the limit that produced
them. `policy = "refuse"` stops the session on a trim (TUI and `exec`); skips
never stop it.

**Static-prefix guard**: base prompt + instructions + skills index + tool schemas
must stay under `static_prefix_guard_percent` (80%) of the usable window. On a
breach the largest scope is trimmed by the overage, the header is recomposed and
re-pinned once under a declared reason, and the result is reported.

**Notice contract**: path, scope, source, action (`kept`/`trimmed`/`skipped`/
`refused`), bytes kept/dropped, estimated tokens kept/dropped, limit kind, and
`fallback_selected`. Channels: a `HistoryCell::System` cell at TUI start, stderr
for `exec` text output, one runtime-provenance message on the first turn (so it is
in the logged transcript — the plan's `announce_active_skill` reference no longer
exists in this tree; LSP diagnostics use the same mechanism), and per-source rows
in `/context report`.

**Config**: new `[instruction_budget]` table with `deny_unknown_fields`, user
config only — the project overlay ignores it and warns, like `instructions` — and
validated at load, so a broken table fails the launch.

**Cache**: still keyed on files. Raw `instruction_segments` are cached and trimmed
per request, so a window change never invalidates the cache and a content change
never reuses trimmed text.

## Measured

From the design doc (§1.7), on a real setup: global `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` 71,522 B
plus a project `AGENTS.md` 37,571 B assembled to 109,093 B. Under the 48 KiB pool
the project file plus ~16% of the global survived and ~58.5 KiB were dropped with
no operator-visible notice. Under this branch both fit (global ≈ 24k tokens,
project ≈ 12k), and any future loss is named per source.

Effective budgets (raw windows, before the output/safety reserve):

| window | usable ≈ | per scope | both scopes | guard 80% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32k | 26.8k | 6,700 | 13,400 | 21,400 |
| 128k | 113.1k | 28,275 | 56,550 | 90,500 |
| 1M | 897.9k | 100,000 (10%) | 200,000 (20%) | 718,300 |

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` (after the merge with `main`): exit 0.
  That is the **library** target, so it does not compile `cfg(test)` code; the
  hosted `Test (ubuntu-latest)` job is the gate that does.
- `scripts/release/check-feature-release-notes.sh <base> HEAD`: this PR's own
  feature commit carries its `#6526` release-note receipt.
- The shipped trim core (`keep_head_within_tokens` + its marker and accounting,
  extracted verbatim from `budget.rs`) was compiled standalone with `rustc` and
  executed over Cyrillic, CJK, emoji, ASCII and mixed inputs at five budgets
  (1, 12, 200, len/7, len-1): it terminates, always cuts on a UTF-8 boundary,
  keeps at most the budget, and byte accounting is exact. This is the path that
  an earlier draft could hang on, so it is worth executing rather than arguing.
- **Hosted CI:** `Change detection`, `Check formatting`, `MSRV check (1.89)`,
  `DCO`, `Contributor gate`, `Plugin conversion`, `VS Code extension` and the
  extension-host runtime jobs pass. Two checks are red on `main` itself and are
  inherited here — see the comment on this PR for the reproduction on a pristine
  `main` checkout:
  - `Version drift` → `node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js` fails on `main`.
  - `Lint` → `cargo clippy` fails on `main` (`crates/agent-contract/src/role.rs:148`,
    plus five version-dependent lints in `crates/tui` files this PR does not touch).
- **Local test execution is still not claimed.** The shared cargo registry and
  target dir are read-only on the machine I built this on, so the build runs
  against an isolated `/tmp` target where `codewhale-tui` needs roughly an hour of
  codegen and then hit a tmpfs quota on the incremental query cache. The hosted
  `Test (ubuntu-latest)` job is the gate for the suite.

## Known limits (also in `docs/design/INSTRUCTION_BUDGET_6526.md` §10)

- Foreign *fragments* (`.cursorrules`, `.clinerules`, …) keep their own bounded
  cap and are not charged to the project scope; they are reported in `/context`.
- `policy = "refuse"` is enforced at TUI/`exec` start; the ACP/app-server
  surfaces trim and report.
- The TUI `/context` rows do not include the configured `instructions` entries
  (the `App` holds no config); headless `/context` and the startup notice do.
- The startup line resolves budgets for an unknown window (128k default); the
  model notice and `/context` use the route's real window.
- Hard links are not deduped (symlinks are).

## New tests

Covering the branches in §5.9: selection truth table (8), per-scope trims (5),
skips and caps (4), configured entries and cache (3), `refuse` (1), guard
arithmetic (4), stable-prefix measurement (2), the report rows (1), the project
overlay (1), plus unit tests for the budget resolution. If the project would
rather not grow the suite, say so and I will drop them into a separate commit —
the design doc asks for them, `AGENTS.md` asks for the opposite.

Refs #6526 — not `fix`/`close`.

prs.title: fix(tui): resolve the state root before opening session-side state
prs.body:
A relocated state root (a Windows junction, or a symlink on Unix) makes every
session save fail before it writes anything. The user gets the red
"cannot save session" notice and the log records one line per attempt:

```text
WARN persistence: persistence write failed what=session:<id>
  error_kind=InvalidInput error=Fleet artifact path must stay within the workspace
```

No `sessions/<id>.json` appears. Relocating `~/.codewhale` to another volume is
a documented setup, so this leaves those users unable to keep any session.

## Root cause

`SessionManager::save_session_inner` hydrates the approval receipts before it
serializes the document, and `ApprovalReceiptStore::log_file` opened
`<sessions>/<id>/approval_receipts.jsonl` through the strict
`WorkspaceFile::open`. On Windows that opener walks the path component by
component and refuses any reparse point — including the junction that *is* the
state root. The save therefore dies in the hydration step on a directory the
user deliberately relocated, while the session document itself (a plain
`write_atomic`) was never reached.

Routing session receipt data through the confined opener was the right
direction; the missing piece is that the state root is a root the user owns and
may relocate. `open_resolved_root` (added in #6947 for the artifacts path) is
the opener for exactly that: it resolves the root once, then runs the same
link-refusing walk below it. #6949 made the same distinction for sub-agent
state.

This is not a regression from an unreleased branch: the strict opener was
already in the 0.10.2 release, and 0.10.2 reproduces the failure unchanged.

## Changes

- **`approval_log.rs`** — the receipt log takes `open_resolved_root`. This is
  the change that unsticks saving, and it fixes session *load* by the same
  call (`replay`, `compact`, `load_if_present` share `log_file`).
- **`session_export.rs`** — the artifact reads and the two directory checks in
  a session archive take the same opener, so `sessions export` no longer fails
  on the layout where saving already failed.
- **`tui/clipboard.rs`, `tui/file_mention.rs`** — the clipboard image sink and
  the screencapture attachment sink sit under the state root too. Both can fall
  back to a workspace directory when no home resolves, so each picks its opener
  from the root it actually holds: the resolved opener only for
  `<home>/.codewhale`, the strict opener for the caller-supplied fallback.
- **`tui/pet_watch/owner.rs`, `tui/pet_watch/persistence.rs`** — the pet
  habitat store, the descriptor read and the lifetime lock.

No boundary moves. `open_resolved_root` resolves the root and then applies the
same per-component refusal, so a link *below* the state root is still an error;
`WorkspaceFile::open` remains the opener for caller-supplied workspace roots
(`runtime_api/workspace.rs`, `fs_confined.rs`, `fleet/artifacts.rs`, `fleet/store.rs`).

## Reproduction

1. Make `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` a junction to another volume:
   `mklink /J %USERPROFILE%\.codewhale D:\CodeWhaleData`
2. Start a session with tools (`codewhale exec --auto "..."`) or run `/save`.
3. Before: exit path reports the save failed, `logs/tui-*.log` records
   `persistence write failed what=session:... error=Fleet artifact path must
   stay within the workspace`, and no `sessions/<id>.json` is written.
4. After: the document lands in the junction target and the notice is gone.

## Testing

Run from this branch:

- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui` — exit 0, no warnings.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo build --release --locked -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui` — builds
  the shipped binaries.
- Clippy: none of the six changed files gains a lint. Worth knowing that a
  local clippy runs newer than CI's stable on this machine (1.98) and reports 32
  existing `-D warnings` failures across `crates/tui` and `crates/runtime` on
  untouched code — `chunks_exact` in `runtime/src/child_env.rs` (a
  `#[cfg(windows)]` function CI's ubuntu lane never compiles),
  `too_many_arguments` in `tui/src/client.rs`, `compaction.rs` and
  `pet_watch/owner.rs::run_world` (whose signature this PR does not change), and
  others. `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked` therefore cannot be
  made green on this machine; CI's own clippy run is the reference.
- **End to end on the reported layout.** With `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` left
  as a junction to `D:\CodeWhaleData`, the built binary ran
  `codewhale exec --auto "Run the shell command: echo CWJUNCTION_OK"`, exited 0,
  and wrote `sessions/cf02b940-8436-4289-b16b-756d7a516228.json` (58,986 bytes)
  through the junction. The same state root produced the failure above on the
  previous binary.

**Not verified here:** the `codewhale-tui` unit-test target does not compile on
this machine — `rustc` exhausts memory linking the lib test binary — so I could
not run `linked_state_root_resolves_once_and_keeps_the_inner_rule`
(`crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`) locally. That test already pins the property
this change relies on (a root junction is accepted after one resolve, a link
below it stays refused), and this PR does not change the opener itself. CI is
the first place it will actually run.

## Related Issues

Closes #7098

Same class of failure as #6947 (session artifacts) and #6949 (sub-agent
state): a user-owned relocated root treated as if it were an untrusted
workspace root.

## Checklist

- No behavior change for an unlinked state root: on Unix `open_resolved_root`
  is the same call as `open`; on Windows it canonicalizes once and then runs the
  identical walk.

### Steps to reproduce

With the `oc-path` plugin enabled, create `tsconfig.json` in an otherwise empty temporary workspace:

```json
{"compilerOptions":{"paths":{"*":["types/*"],"@app/*":["src/*"]}}}
```

Run from that workspace:

```sh
openclaw path find 'oc://tsconfig.json/compilerOptions/paths/*' --json
```

### Expected behavior

Return two concrete paths, including `oc://tsconfig.json/compilerOptions/paths/"*"`, which can be reused with `path resolve` or `path set`.

### Actual behavior

The registered CLI handler rejects with:

```text
OcPathError: resolveOcPath received a wildcard pattern; use findOcPaths instead: oc://tsconfig.json/compilerOptions/paths/*
code: OC_PATH_WILDCARD_IN_RESOLVE
```

The traversal emits the literal key as an unquoted wildcard, then its own final resolution rejects that generated path.

- No running Gateway, live account, or private configuration is involved. This is a local file-addressing failure.

Merged #130499 fixes quoting of positional dotted keys; the shared quoting helper still does not quote a literal `*`. Open #168375 changes recursive wildcard traversal and does not address literal key quoting.

issues.title: [macOS] update repair remount settlement fails with "Package settlement inode or device mapping changed" on a publication-complete journal (launcher bound to staged inode, not recorded publication)
issues.body:
## Summary

After a reboot changed the APFS Data volume device number, `openclaw update` was blocked by a retained `publication-complete` journal, and `openclaw update repair` could not settle it. The remount-settlement path binds the live launcher to the staged copy's inode instead of the inode recorded in `publications_json`, so it fails with `Package settlement inode or device mapping changed.` even though every recorded object keeps its inode and only the device number changed.

Related (device-number drift, other phases/platforms): #169050, #166135.

## Environment

- macOS 26.3.1, Apple Silicon, npm global install (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), managed LaunchAgent Gateway
- 2026.10.7 installed on Oct 25; macOS rebooted later the same day; update to 2026.10.8 attempted Oct 28
- `st_dev` of the data volume changed 16777231 -> 16777234

## Symptoms

- `openclaw update`: `update-recovery-pending: Package publication journal does not match its installation: parent (recorded 16777231:283702; current 16777234:283702; device number changed only); control dir (...); journal (...)`
- `openclaw update repair`: `Package settlement inode or device mapping changed.`
- Gateway keeps serving 2026.10.7 throughout; installed package tree verified intact (12,249 inventoried dist files, all sha256 match)

## Journal state (read-only copy of `package_activation`)

- `phase=publication-complete`, `intent=null`
- Recorded inodes for parent, control dir, journal, anchor, helper, previous, launcher roots, candidate, bin dir all match current inodes; device number differs uniformly (one-to-one old->new mapping)
- `publications_json = [{"name":"openclaw","identity":"<dev>:423828446"}]`, which equals the live `/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw` symlink inode
- Launcher entry: `previousIdentity` ...:407628097, `candidateIdentity` ...:423420916 (the staged copy under `<anchor>/launchers/openclaw`). The live launcher is a published copy with a different inode

## Cause (source read in 2026.10.7, 2026.10.8, 2026.10.10-beta.4 and main)

In `inspectRemountedPackagePublication` (`src/infra/package-update-activation-settlement.ts`) the launcher loop does:

```ts
const historical = previous && previous.split(":")[1] === current.split(":")[1]
  ? previous
  : entry.candidateIdentity;
...
bind(historical, () => packageActivationIdentity(launcher, "launcher"));
```

For a completed publication the live launcher's inode is only recorded in `record.publications`, and it differs from both `previousIdentity` and `candidateIdentity`, so `bind` throws the inode mismatch. `assertPackageActivationSelectedLaunchers` already resolves the expected identity via `record.publications.find((p) => p.name === entry.name)?.identity`; the settlement path does not.

## Verified workaround

Copied the helper (`<anchor>.control/recovery.mjs`) and replaced the single `historical` line with:

```js
const published = record.publications.find((item) => item.name === entry.name)?.identity;
const historical = published ?? (previous && previous.split(":")[1] === current.split(":")[1] ? previous : entry.candidateIdentity);
```

Ran the documented separate-helper path (`<node> recovery-patched.mjs --anchor <anchor> --operation <id> repair`). It verified the full candidate tree, launchers and device mapping, archived the journal to `.superseded-<id>` and reported `No package was republished and no service was restarted`. A normal `openclaw update` to 2026.10.8 then succeeded.

## Suggested fix

- In the settlement launcher bind, prefer the `publications` identity for the launcher when the phase is `publication-complete` (or generally when a publication entry exists), falling back to the current logic.
- Add a regression test: `publication-complete` journal, all recorded inodes unchanged, uniform device-number change, launcher published as a copy with a distinct inode.

## Side note

The Gateway's automatic update campaign holds the executor lease for about a minute every two hours; a manual helper run during that window returns `Another update executor owns this installation`. Retrying outside the window works.

issues.body:
# Feishu streaming smoothness regression: card-update strategy changed between `larksuite/openclaw-lark` 2026.7.16 and `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.9.9

## Summary
On this host, Feishu reply streaming felt smooth ('typewriter') on the 2026.7.x plugin (`larksuite/openclaw-lark`, last release 2026.7.16). After moving to `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.9.9 the output looks stepped (users report ~1s pauses between visible steps). The two plugins use materially different card-update strategies.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (bcfc888), node v24.21.0, Linux.
- Channel: Feishu (Lark) via websocket, 5 accounts.
- `channels.feishu.streaming = { block: { enabled: false, coalesce: { minChars: 8, maxChars: 400, idleMs: 100 } }, mode: 'partial' }`
- `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault` unset; `agents.defaults.blockStreamingChunk` unset.

## Evidence A — implementation comparison
| | old `larksuite/openclaw-lark` 2026.7.16 | current `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.9.9 |
|---|---|---|
| card update impl | `flush-controller` + `THROTTLE_CONSTANTS` | rewritten `FeishuStreamingSession` |
| card throttle | `CARDKIT_MS: 100` (PATCH_MS 1500) | `STREAMING_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS = 160` |
| content gate | none (`cardkit.js`: 'full cumulative text, not a delta') | `shouldPushStreamingUpdate`: immediate push only if text ends with `[\n。！？!?；;：:]` or grew >= `STREAMING_SIGNIFICANT_DELTA_CHARS = 18` |
| client-side pacing | no `streaming_config` | `streaming_config { print_frequency_ms: {default:50}, print_step: {default:1} }` |

## Evidence B — measured cadence with 2026.9.9
Instrumented the plugin (temporary probe, removed afterwards):
- host feed (`update(text)`): 88 calls / 26.7 s — min 225 / p50 293 / p90 376 / max 708 ms; gaps >900 ms: 0
- actual push (`writeCardContent`): 87 / 26.4 s — min 225 / p50 294 / p90 375 / max 707 ms; gaps >900 ms: 0
- effective text rate ~9.6 chars/s
So the OpenClaw pipeline itself is NOT producing 1 s gaps; the visible stepping correlates with the changed update strategy + client rendering.

## Hypothesis
The rewrite replaced frequent ungated CardKit content flushes (100 ms) with a 160 ms throttle plus a content gate, and added `streaming_config` client-side pacing. Combined, the card updates land less predictably than before, which reads as pauses.

## Suggested direction
1. Make the card-update throttle and `shouldPushStreamingUpdate` gate configurable (or restore the old flush behavior), and/or
2. Make the card `streaming_config` (`print_frequency_ms`, `print_step`) configurable.

## Repro
1. Send a Feishu message that produces a multi-line reply.
2. Observe the card fill in visible steps (vs smooth typewriter on 2026.7.16).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.5, a legitimate Telegram album send failed with OutboundDeliveryError: Network request for sendMediaGroup failed. The retained caller result did not establish a lower-level transport cause or whether Telegram had accepted the album. This reports the observed failure and diagnostic gap, not a proven OpenClaw transport root cause.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

A normal album operation failed after approximately 62 seconds with:

~~~text
OutboundDeliveryError: Network request for sendMediaGroup failed
~~~

The application did not retain a complete final receipt set. Earlier messages in the surrounding ordered delivery may already have been accepted. The album outcome remains **ambiguous**, not definitely unsent. No resend, claim reset or forced production reproduction was performed.

A deterministic isolated reproduction, recursive underlying cause, transport phase, bytes transmitted, and remote acceptance evidence are not available. We cannot attribute the failure to DNS, TLS, a proxy, an upload timeout, Telegram, or an OpenClaw defect from this wrapper alone.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), observed during the incident.

### Operating system

Linux x64; Node.js 24.

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

~~~text
OutboundDeliveryError: Network request for sendMediaGroup failed
~~~

Only the sanitized observed error is supplied; no private payloads, destinations, paths, tokens or raw logs are attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Installed-source inspection found the documented telegram.http path in extensions/telegram/src/send-context.ts: createTelegramHttpLogger accepts Grammy HttpError and emits a warning under telegram/diagnostic with operation plus redactSensitiveText(formatUncaughtError(err.error ?? err)). The request diagnostic wrapper is used by the album-send path. src/infra/errors.ts selects an Error stack/message; this is not a guarantee of recursively preserved cause codes or transport-phase evidence.

We have no retained telegram.http warning for the historical failure. This report does not establish that an enabled flag failed to log the request. We seek supported collection guidance for a future ordinary occurrence.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed scheduled Telegram album-delivery attempt on the stated installation. Consequence: delivery could not be confirmed, so the application's dependent workflow remained blocked rather than risk a duplicate send. General frequency, remote acceptance and broader prevalence are unknown.

### Additional information

**Application-wrapper limitation, not attributed to OpenClaw core:** the existing delivery bridge retains selected scalar CLI evidence but not stderr/nested exceptions, and stores its final receipt aggregate only after the complete ordered result sequence. This contributes to the retained evidence gap. Missing application final state does not prove the native request was never dispatched or that the entire delivery was lost.

The smallest documented next collection appears to be a separately approved, preserve-and-merge addition of **only telegram.http**, with the file-log threshold allowing warnings, at planned maintenance. Documentation requires a Gateway restart. No logging change or restart has been made, and no send will be forced for diagnosis. A future legitimate-send interval can be retained alongside unchanged canonical receipt evidence and sanitized before sharing.

**Maintainer request:** please confirm whether this supported flag is the correct bounded collection path and whether existing native evidence can expose the same-attempt underlying error name/code/nested-cause codes, elapsed time, and actually observed connect/TLS/upload/response stage/status. If no supported producer exposes these, preserving available redacted cause information would help distinguish failure classes. Those fields are requested, not asserted to exist. Added diagnostics should avoid message/media contents, private endpoints, credentials and destination identifiers.

No automatic retry is requested. A generic network error or absence of a final application receipt must not be treated as proof of non-dispatch. Historical ambiguity remains unless matching complete canonical receipts can be recovered; a later successful send would not explain this earlier failure.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The desktop Review menu offers an enabled **Edit file** action to a guest whose workspace file is read-only. Selecting it opens the normal rendered file preview without an editor, Save control, or explanation. The same guest's direct Files menu correctly omits Edit.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a guest connection with `operator.sessions.read` and `operator.sessions.write` in a session with a Git worktree.
2. Have the agent make a change to a small Markdown file, then wait for its work to finish.
3. Open **Review**, select **All Changes**, and open the changed file's Actions menu.
4. Select the enabled **Edit file** item.
5. Inspect the selected file view and its **More file actions** menu.

### Expected behavior

Review should represent the operation the existing file owner can perform. A read-only file should retain its opening, rendered/source viewing, and download actions without offering an enabled editing operation. The direct Files menu already derives Edit from the actual file capability.

### Actual behavior

On the tested guest connection, Review showed Edit as enabled. One click opened the rendered Markdown report, with no editable CodeMirror control, no Save button, and no visible explanation. Independent file readback before and after the click returned the same SHA-256. The file's own actions menu did not contain Edit.

This is a misleading affordance. The read-only boundary itself remained intact; no file write or privilege bypass occurred.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8, source commit `58b88a8b0a80edd769c1335d971809ab9ff24a38`.

### Operating system

macOS; Chromium 156.0.8078.4.

### Install method

Isolated source-backed native Gateway and Control UI, with fresh guest identity and a disposable repository.

### Model

The affected operation is a manual file action after the agent turn has finished; it does not invoke a model.

### Provider / routing chain

Browser → same-origin Gateway proxy → OpenClaw.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The current-source native scenario reproduced the guest action once. The report was 390 bytes, and its SHA-256 stayed `79d86c8d73456c6ca74dcfb71c7d871715f1cc7bfce6408de1fa60a30d032466` across the click. The rendered preview and enabled menu were also captured.

At this revision, [Review's menu predicate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/58b88a8b0a80edd769c1335d971809ab9ff24a38/ui/src/pages/chat/components/session-diff-file-view.tsx#L350-L365) treats the general `openFileView` callback as edit capability. The [workspace file owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/58b88a8b0a80edd769c1335d971809ab9ff24a38/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace-content.runtime.ts#L161-L170) additionally requires the actual file hash, uniform line endings, the advertised write method, and admin scope. The reader correctly declines editing when that capability is absent.

### Impact and severity

Affected users are read-only workspace viewers using desktop Review. The demonstrated impact is a dead-end Edit action and confusion about whether the file can be changed. There was no data loss or unauthorized write. This report covers one current-source native guest reproduction; mobile behavior and a historical regression range were not established.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.
