labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the existing Discord message tool issue a single-use, expiring invite for an explicitly selected guild text channel using the configured Discord account.

### Problem to solve

A community organizer may ask their assistant for a fresh invitation to share with a new member. Discord supports creating this object, but OpenClaw's native Discord actions currently cannot issue it. Posting an existing URL does not create a fresh, limited-use invitation.

There is concrete demand for the underlying task: a [bot developer asks how to generate an invite in a guild their bot has joined](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57677178/how-to-make-a-discord-bot-to-create-a-invite-in-other-guild), and the [fo40-bridge author describes a community join flow using one-use invites](https://developers.reddit.com/apps/fo40-bridge). These are external Discord workflows. Applying the task to OpenClaw's native message tool is an inference, not a claim that those authors use OpenClaw.

The proposed benefit is access through the existing selected-account, message-action, and requester-permission boundary. Users can already perform the task through Discord's UI or another integration.

### Proposed solution

Add one Discord-owned creation action, with `invite-create` as a suggested name. The first scope is an ordinary guild text channel, one use, a positive lifetime up to Discord's seven-day limit, and unique issuance. For example: “Create a single-use invite to this channel that expires in one hour.” A 24-hour default lifetime would match Discord's ordinary expiry default; the lifetime field name is a maintainer choice.

Use the existing Discord `channels` action gate and configured account. Fetch the target's actual channel type and guild from Discord and verify the eligible target and any supplied guild; do not trust model-provided guild metadata. Carry the host's trusted requester identity into the existing guild-action permission path and check `CREATE_INSTANT_INVITE` for that target channel. Let Discord enforce the bot's own permission independently. A bot's credentials or membership must not substitute for requester authority. Preserve the existing direct-owner origin rules and message action/target policies.

Issue `POST /channels/{channel.id}/invites` with a JSON body requesting the chosen `max_age`, `max_uses: 1`, `unique: true`, and ordinary membership (`temporary: false`). Return the created code/link and channel/guild identity, distinguishing provider-returned metadata from requested values. This action returns a tool result; it does not independently post the link elsewhere.

This requires the smallest addition to the shared closed action vocabulary and targeted-mutation facts, plus the Discord adapter, schema, guild-action dispatch, and existing REST owner. It does not require a new core tool or generic SDK.

### Alternatives considered

- Create the invite in Discord's UI. This works and is the simplest option for manual use.
- Use an existing Discord MCP server. [This implementation](https://github.com/ExilProductions/discord-mcp/blob/337d5c8dbb3ff208fc613f5797ef7e9de427b763/src/discord_mcp/tools/invites.py) already supports invite creation; a separately configured integration is a valid solution. A native action would keep the operation in the existing Discord account and message-tool policy surface.
- Use a script, skill, or custom plugin calling Discord's official API. This is feasible with current extension contracts. It requires maintaining that separate integration; a missing generic extension contract is not the justification here.
- Post a previously created invite. Useful when that link's lifetime and usage policy are appropriate, but it does not issue a new single-use object.

### Impact

- Affected: operators who manage Discord communities through the native message tool and want to issue fresh joining links.
- Severity/urgency: a native capability gap with working alternatives; no measured urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Public sources establish the task, not an OpenClaw usage rate.
- Consequence: the invitation step requires Discord's UI or another integration even when the assistant can already manage the target channel. No user counts or time savings have been measured.

### Evidence/examples

At OpenClaw main `341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa`, [the shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [Discord's action discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.ts) expose no invite creation action. Existing [guild-action permission handling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.guild.ts) and [REST operations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/send.guild.ts) provide an implementation home. The same relevant action gap was checked separately in latest stable v2026.10.7 (`157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e`).

[Discord's official contract](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel#create-channel-invite) defines the creation operation, lifetime, usage limit, and uniqueness. The demand links above establish external tasks; source inspection establishes the native entry-point gap. No live Discord or installed-plugin experiment was performed for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The first scope excludes invite listing/revocation, permanent or unlimited-use links, guest/stream/application invites, recipient binding, role assignment, member auto-add, Reddit integration, and a persistent invite manager. An invite allows guild entry subject to Discord's ordinary rules; it does not grant otherwise denied channel access. A one-use link remains shareable and is not restricted to a named person.

Suggested implementation: extend the existing Discord channel actions and guild-admin dispatcher, add a channel-scoped `CREATE_INSTANT_INVITE` guard using existing permission helpers, and call the existing account-bound REST client. Classify creation as a targeted mutation, without conversation-read/read-only or message-delivery semantics. Keep current host request assertions and account ownership checks through awaited permission work, gateway handoff, queueing, rate-limit handling, and result consumption. Reuse the Discord request owner's live assertion at dispatch and retries; the current effect-authority compatibility helper alone is not an authorization check. Do not mark the source conversation delivered merely because an invite was issued.

Use the current rate-limit machinery for a rejected 429. A timeout or lost response after dispatch can leave issuance unknown: do not automatically replay a unique create. Cancellation cannot revoke a link already accepted by Discord. No new credential store, config mechanism, dependency, or durable job is needed. The exact action/lifetime-field names and whether the existing `channels` gate is the preferred product grouping remain maintainer decisions; no implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- Through a real installed official Discord plugin and its native message tool, a permitted requester selects an eligible text channel and requests a one-hour invite. The result identifies that channel/guild and a real issued code; wire inspection shows one use, a 3600-second lifetime, and unique issuance. A consenting test account can join with it, and another attempted use fails under Discord's policy. Separately verify expiry of an unused short-lived invite.
- A requester with the necessary channel permission can create an invite without `MANAGE_CHANNELS`; lack of requester permission or bot permission fails without silently changing the target or privileges. Do not add invite listing as a prerequisite.
- Disabled account/gate, disallowed action/target, mismatched account or guild, and forged requester fields cannot issue an invite. Reject DMs, categories, and thread targets for this first scope. Existing caller/registration/account closure while queued prevents a new effect or unauthorized result exposure.
- Normal chat actions remain usable, two explicit create requests ask for distinct unique invitations, and a lost create acknowledgment produces an honest unknown outcome without a second automatic create or a fabricated chat receipt.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Docker, updating an existing 2026.7.2 install to v2026.10.3 fails at the startup doctor with "Failing check state-schema (step-refused): Failed migrating shared state database schema at [redacted-path]", with no cause shown, and the gateway does not start.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a Docker install running 2026.7.2 with its state in a named volume (data written by 2026.7.2).
2. Build the image from tag v2026.10.3 and start the gateway with the same volume at /home/node/.openclaw (plus a new empty volume at /home/node/.config/openclaw).
3. Read the gateway log: the doctor stops at state-schema and the container restarts about every 15 seconds.
4. Stop the gateway and run `openclaw doctor --fix` once with the same mounts: same failure.

### Expected behavior

The docs (docs/install/docker.md, "Upgrading container images") say replacing the image while keeping the same mounted state is supported, and the new gateway runs startup-safe migrations before reporting ready. The same volume restored from backup starts normally on 2026.7.2.

### Actual behavior

The doctor saves pre-migration SQLite backups, then stops with "Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue" and "Failing check state-schema (step-refused)". The path is shown as [redacted-path] and no cause is printed. `openclaw doctor --fix` fails the same way.

### OpenClaw version

v2026.10.3 (commit 59cb44796b0)

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

docker (Docker Desktop 4.86.0, WSL2, image built locally from tag v2026.10.3 with OPENCLAW_IMAGE_APT_PACKAGES=poppler-utils)

### Model

Not applicable: the failure happens at startup, before any model is used. (Configured on 2026.7.2: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable to this failure. On 2026.7.2: openclaw -> api.deepseek.com (direct).

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue. Resolve the reported migration failure before retrying. Later repairs were not run.
Failing check state-schema (step-refused): Failed migrating shared state database schema at [redacted-path]
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: /home/node/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: /home/node/.openclaw/agents/openclaw/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: /home/node/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-<id>.bak
(7 identical failures logged in /tmp/openclaw between 14:19:19Z and 14:20:47Z; searching that log for "cause", "SqliteError", "constraint" and "locked" found nothing.)

`openclaw doctor --json` output:
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":0,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/final-config-validation","severity":"error","message":"Legacy agents.entries default markers need explicit surface owners. Run \"openclaw doctor --fix\".","path":"agents.entries"}]}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Checked on a read-only copy of state/openclaw.sqlite: PRAGMA user_version = 6, PRAGMA integrity_check = ok. Host disk had 396 GB free.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one Docker install on Windows 11, updating from 2026.7.2.
Severity: blocks the update; the gateway does not start on v2026.10.3.
Frequency: every attempt (7 automatic startup attempts and 1 manual `doctor --fix`, same result).
Consequence: could not update; restored the pre-update backup into a new volume and returned to 2026.7.2. No data lost.

### Additional information

Last known good: 2026.7.2. Only bad version tested: v2026.10.3. Not tested: 2026.10.4 or later, or any intermediate version.
Possibly related to #180705 (state migration failing during update). Differences: that report is a native Ubuntu/systemd install on 2026.10.4 -> 10.5 with a "state database is busy" message. Mine is Docker on Windows from 2026.7.2 -> 10.3, with no lock or "busy" message. The gateway container was stopped when I ran `doctor --fix`, and it failed the same way.
Workaround: restored the pre-update backup into a new volume and ran the old image.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Browsing from an open file preview to its Root folder can halt Control UI rendering, leaving the conversation and file controls frozen while the native task continues and completes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In the desktop Control UI, start a coding task in a project worktree and let it produce a README and implementation files.
2. Open Files, then open README.md. In the observed journey, attach that README to a substantive follow-up coding request and submit it.
3. While the follow-up is working, click **Root** in the file preview's breadcrumb.
4. Observe the browser console and let the task finish without reloading the page.

The attachment and active task describe the tested journey; they have not been established as prerequisites for the file-header exception.

### Expected behavior

Root should show the folder and leave chat and file navigation usable. An accepted task completion should remove Stop and show the completed answer. The preceding run in the same browser context completed with that behavior.

### Actual behavior

The Root click raises `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path')`, followed by `REACTIVITY_HALTED`. File navigation no longer updates the page. The native follow-up completed successfully with 73 passing tests, and the active pane's synchronous run state became idle, but the visible conversation retained Stop and its old 13-second activity frame.

An ordinary same-page reload restored the completed answer and removed Stop. The session and worktree stayed the same, and no new model request was submitted.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe; build `2026.10.8-f76e79be6a8f-2026-10-28T02-16-59.438Z`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1; Playwright Chromium desktop viewport, 1440 × 1000.

### Install method

Isolated source-backed Gateway and Vite Control UI.

### Model

Existing configured coding model. This report concerns the browser file-header exception; no model change was used to reproduce or recover it.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway → configured OpenAI coding route.

### Logs

```text
[REACTIVITY_HALTED] An uncaught error halted the reactive system.
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path')
  at get name (chat-sidebar-file-chrome.tsx, copy-path action icon)
[REACTIVITY_HALTED] Update ignored: the reactive system was halted by an earlier uncaught error.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The current Gateway socket was identified independently from the Vite socket and matched the visible pane's client instance and connection generation. The final event arrived on that connection. The pane remained visible, presented, and non-inert throughout; this was not a hidden parked pane or a new request started during recovery.

The served failing getter maps to [the copy-path action icon](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-file-chrome.tsx#L194). Its caller uses [one conditional value for visibility and the controls object](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-file-view.tsx#L144). Root navigation can make that value false while retained descendants still read the required controls shape. This is the source-backed cause of the newly reproduced case; a correction is not yet validated.

### Impact and severity

The observed desktop guest workflow loses usable conversation and Files updates until reload, although native work continues. One fresh end-to-end reproduction captured the exception and the idle-owner/stale-DOM mismatch. No saved-work loss was observed, and no general frequency or other-platform claim is made.

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
### Summary

The gateway's own WAL auto-checkpoint on `state/openclaw.sqlite` is reported as blocked on every attempt since boot, and has **never completed**:

```
openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader
  state=blocked  checkpointedFrames=866  logFrames=17091
  consecutiveBlocked=14  lastCompletedAtMs=null  never_completed=true
```

The WAL therefore keeps growing (unbackfilled 41.5 MB at 15:33 → 65.7 MB at 19:09) instead of being checkpointed.

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.7 (c074824)**
- Windows 10.0.26200 (x64), Node v24.18.0
- State DB `state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 405 MB, `-wal` 47–73 MB

### What was ruled out

A Sysinternals **handle.exe** scan of all processes for `openclaw.sqlite`:

```
node.exe  pid: 33900  .sqlite  x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -wal     x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -shm     x1
```

**No other process holds any handle on the DB** — every handle belongs to the gateway process itself. This is not an external contender; the pin is **in-process**.

The gateway's own telemetry cannot name the holder either:

```json
"candidate_connection": {
  "connectionId": 2, "operation": "sqlite connection", "ownerKind": "worker",
  "threadId": 2, "ageMs": ~25200000, "transactionOpen": false,
  "trackedReaders": 0, "blockingOwner": "unknown",
  "readerCount": 0, "scope": "current-thread", "nativeStatements": "unobserved"
}
```

Note the internal inconsistency: it reports "blocked by a reader" while also reporting `readerCount: 0` and `blockingOwner: unknown`.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Maintenance stops the gateway, checkpoints cleanly, restarts:
   `[checkpoint] PASS | [('openclaw-agent.sqlite',(0,0,0)), ('openclaw.sqlite',(0,0,0))]` (12:00:01)
2. After restart (~12:03) the block immediately re-forms and **never** clears for the rest of the uptime (observed 12:03 → 19:05, 71 blocked records, `never_completed=true`).
3. Only another full gateway restart clears it.

### Correlated (NOT proven) impact

- `Agent run failed: the Gateway state database was busy (SQLite: database is locked)`
- repeated `cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`

Same DB, same subsystem. Timing supports a link; no controlled reproduction was done, so causation is **unproven**.

### Suggested directions (guesses)

- Likely a long-lived connection or unclosed read snapshot inside the worker pool (threadId=2, `ownerKind=worker`) — a single un-reset statement pins the WAL.
- `blockingOwner=unknown` + `readerCount=0` + "blocked by a reader" suggests the reader-tracking path does not cover all connection kinds.

---
*Reported from a self-hosted single-user deployment. Paths sanitized.*

issues.body:
### Issue type
Feature / localization request (with supporting evidence from a real QQ bot session)

### Summary
The restart-recovery / pending-final delivery notice is a **hardcoded English string with no i18n and no config toggle**. On a Chinese-language deployment it surfaces as a raw English paragraph in the user's chat, where it reads like the model "leaked an English thought." It is actually emitted by the core runtime, not by the agent.

The string is:

> I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat, so I won't resend it automatically. Please ask for any missing remainder.

### Where it lives
- Constant `PENDING_DELIVERY_NOTICE` in `src/channels/turn/pending-delivery-notice.ts` (observed compiled in `dist/execution-*.mjs`), used by `deliverPendingDeliveryNotice()` via `runtime.sendRecoveryNotice(...)`.
- The transcript records these as `model: "delivery-mirror"` / `api: "openclaw-transcript"` with `idempotencyKey: main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:<intentId>`, confirming they bypass the model entirely — so prompt-level language instructions cannot affect them.
- I could not find any config key or schema field to disable, redirect, or translate this notice; it is not wrapped in an i18n layer.

### Observed behavior (sanitized)
Channel: QQ official bot (`qqbot`), agent personas configured to reply only in Simplified Chinese, OpenClaw 2026.9.9.

1. A long final reply (an accounts/billing answer produced via several `exec` tool calls) was generated while the gateway restarted; two `[System] previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart` markers were recorded and the delivery outcome settled as `unknown`.
2. Roughly 40 hours later, when the user sent the next message ("测试"), session recovery drained the owed notice and posted the **English** paragraph into the Chinese DM ~3 s later, immediately before the model's normal Chinese reply.
3. Result: the user believed the Chinese-speaking agent had suddenly emitted an internal English "thinking" message. The actual reply was delivered correctly; the only problem is the unexplained, unlocalized runtime notice.

This channel runs long tool-heavy turns frequently, so restart/interruption-window `unknown` deliveries are disproportionately common here, making the English notice recur specifically on this agent.

### Why existing issues don't cover this
The spurious/replacement behavior is tracked separately (#154416, #162554, #149325), and an operational-notice suppression/redirect policy is proposed in #113501. This request is narrower and independent: even when the notice is **correctly** sent (genuinely unknown delivery after a restart), it should not be unconditionally English with no way to localize or disable it.

### Requested
Any one or combination of:
1. **Localize** runtime recovery/operational notices (at minimum this one), selecting language from a config/locale (e.g. `messages.locale: "zh-CN"`) rather than a hardcoded literal.
2. Allow **custom notice text** per channel/account (templates), so operators can write it in their users' language.
3. Allow the notice to be **suppressed or redirected** (which may be subsumed by #113501 — happy to close in favor of that if the policy covers `pending-delivery-notice`).

Happy to provide sanitized logs or a Chinese suggested translation if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

The Ask OpenClaw greeting turn loads the persona files of the system agent owner (usually `main`). The prompt holds that agent's `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `name=<agent name>`. The model then sometimes greets as that agent ("Hey 🎀 — <name> here") and not as OpenClaw. Ask OpenClaw chat turns do not load these files.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9a1b4f`).
2. Use a config with `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, a second agent, and a model behind an OpenAI-compatible provider. Config:

```json5
{
  models: { providers: { litellm: { baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:4000", apiKey: "sk-mock", api: "openai-completions", models: [{ id: "chat", name: "chat" }] } } },
  agents: {
    ownership: "explicit",
    defaults: { model: { primary: "litellm/chat" }, systemAgent: { agentId: "main" } },
    entries: {
      main: { workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace", identity: { name: "Nova", emoji: "🎀" } },
      mark: { workspace: "~/work/mark" },
    },
  },
}
```
3. Put a `SOUL.md` and an `IDENTITY.md` with a persona name in the `main` workspace.
4. Run `openclaw gateway run` and open `/custodian` in the Control UI.
5. Record the prompts at the model endpoint.

### Expected behavior

The greeting prompt holds only the OpenClaw identity. `SYSTEM_AGENT_GREETING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` says "You are OpenClaw, the system itself". `docs/concepts/main-session.md` describes Ask OpenClaw as "a separate system-care conversation".

### Actual behavior

The greeting request holds the `main` persona. The working directory is the temp planner folder, but Project Context comes from the `main` workspace:

```text
Runtime: name=Nova | agent=main | session=agent:main:in-memory:openclaw-greeting-<id> | ...
### Workspace
Working directory: /tmp/openclaw-planner-f85un4
# Project Context
SOUL.md: persona/tone. Follow it unless higher-priority instructions override.
### <home>/.openclaw/workspace/SOUL.md
You are Nova. Always open with "Hey 🎀 — Nova here." PERSONA-MARKER-7731
### <home>/.openclaw/workspace/IDENTITY.md
- Name: Nova
- Emoji: 🎀
...
### Conversation Context
You are OpenClaw, the system itself — caretaker of this machine's gateway, config, channels, and agents.
```

The prompt gives the model two identities. On a real install with `litellm/chat`, Ask OpenClaw showed this greeting after a config change (agent names replaced):

```text
Hey 🎀 — <main name> here. Config's valid, gateway's up, both agents (`main` and `<second agent>`) are on `litellm/chat`, and no channels are degraded. No update waiting.
Channel health is available and clean. What do you need?
Heads up: the config was edited outside OpenClaw while I was away — open History to review it.
```

Earlier greetings in the same conversation said "I'm OpenClaw, the system agent". So the visible fault is intermittent. The prompt content is not intermittent.

### Evidence

Isolated `HOME`, published `openclaw@2026.10.5`, a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that records each request. Persona marker `PERSONA-MARKER-7731` is in `main`'s `SOUL.md` only.

| Request | `agent=` in Runtime | Working directory | `SOUL.md` / `IDENTITY.md` of `main` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ask OpenClaw greeting (`openclaw-greeting-*`) | `main` (`name=Nova`) | `/tmp/openclaw-planner-*` | ❌ loaded |
| Ask OpenClaw chat turn ("who are you?") | `openclaw` | `<home>/.openclaw/openclaw/workspace` | ✅ not loaded |

The same result shows on all three builds that I tested:

| Build | Greeting loads `main` persona | Chat turn loads `main` persona |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9a1b4f`) | ❌ yes | ✅ no |
| `openclaw@2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`) | ❌ yes | ✅ no |
| main `ad55c5ec39`, local build | ❌ yes | ✅ no |

### Likely cause

`runConfiguredSystemAgentText` in `src/system-agent/assistant.ts` runs greeting and planner turns with `agentId: route.agentId` and a temp `workspaceDir`. The temp folder does not isolate bootstrap files. `run-orchestrator.ts` sets `canonicalWorkspace = resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(config, preparedAgentId)` and passes it as `bootstrapWorkspaceDir`. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.ts` loads bootstrap files from `bootstrapWorkspaceDir`. `resolveRuntimeAgentName` adds the owner name to the Runtime line. These lines are unchanged on main `ad55c5ec39`.

`runSystemAgentTurn` uses `agentId: "openclaw"`, so chat turns are not affected.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9a1b4f`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu, Gateway in a Docker container (report). Linux (repro).

### Install method

Docker (report). npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`, `openclaw@2026.10.8` and a local build of main (repro).

### Model

`litellm/chat`

### Provider / routing chain

`models.providers.litellm` (`api: "openai-completions"`), embedded runner. Repro used a local mock server at the same provider config.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Ask OpenClaw users whose system agent owner has a workspace persona.
Severity: Annoying. Users think that the main agent answers in the setup chat.
Frequency: The persona loads on every greeting turn. The model follows it on some of them.
Consequence: Users do not know which agent they talk to.

### Additional information

Related: #161146 (open PR that passes the owner workspace to planner turns). Related: #160777. Related: #165112.

issues.title: [Bug]: reply with MEDIA posted twice (2nd copy text-only) when a message is steered into the run

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:message-loss
labels.description: Channel message delivery can be lost, duplicated, or misrouted.

issues.body:
### Summary

When a user message is steered into an active run, and the assistant message *before* the steer carried media (`MEDIA:` directive), the reply is posted twice on Slack: once with the attachment (the message_end media block reply), then again **text-only** when the run's final payloads are delivered.

Seen on `2026.8.33`, Slack channel thread, `claude-code-cli` provider over `openai-completions`, block streaming off. The same index-equality check is still on `main` (`isDirectBlockRetryBlocked` / `isDirectTextRetryBlocked` in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-payloads.ts` as of ee5c5ae4e3), so I expect it reproduces there too.

### Sequence (from gateway log, one run)

1. Run starts for message A. While it is working, the user sends B and C; both get `steerTargetRunId` = the active run (`reply hot path timings ... reason=active_run_injected`).
2. Assistant message #0 ends with text + `MEDIA:/path/doc.pdf`. At message_end the media path emits a block reply; with block streaming off, `createBlockReplyDeliveryHandler` sends it via `sendDirectBlockReply` (non-text content). Slack gets **text + PDF**. `directlySentBlockPayloads[0]` is tagged `assistantMessageIndex: 0`.
3. The run continues for the steered messages B and C → assistant message #1 (`NO_REPLY`). `state.assistantMessageIndex` becomes 1 and `lastAssistantTextMessageIndex` is reset.
4. Run ends. `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` tags **every** payload with a single `assistantMessageIndex: attempt.lastAssistantTextMessageIndex`, so the final payload for message #0's text gets an index ≠ 0.
5. `buildReplyPayloads` → `isDirectlySentBlockPayload`: the content key matches, but the index doesn't → not deduped. `preserveDirectlyUnsentPayload` → `hasDirectlySentText` looks up text fragments by the (wrong) index → no match → payload kept. Then `filterMessagingToolMediaDuplicates` strips the already-sent PDF → Slack gets the **same text again, without the attachment**, ~9s after the first post.

Without a steer (single assistant message) the indexes match and dedupe works. We checked 7 other steered runs the same day with no media in the answer; none doubled.

### Repro (unit level)

Calling `buildReplyPayloads` (2026.8.33 dist) with block streaming off:

- `directlySentBlockPayloads = [{ text: T, mediaUrls: [P] } @ assistantMessageIndex 0]`, `directlySentBlockKeys` = its content key
- final `payloads = [{ text: T + "\nMEDIA:" + P } @ assistantMessageIndex 1]`

returns `[{ text: T }]` (the duplicate). With the final tagged index 0, it returns `[]`.

### Suggested fix

Root cause is that the final payload's `assistantMessageIndex` is the run's last text index, not the index of the message that produced that text. Proper fix: carry a per-text message index through `assistantTexts` → `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads`.

Minimal fix we are running locally: in `isDirectlySentBlockPayload`, once the content key matched a directly sent block, treat a payload that has media as already sent regardless of index (same text + same media URLs is the same reply). Text-only repeats in a later message still go through the index check, and a later message with a *different* file still posts.

```js
if (!params.directlySentBlockKeys?.has(contentKey)) return false;
if (resolveSendableOutboundReplyParts(payload).hasMedia) return true;
```

Unit cases (steer idx0→1, idx0→-1, no-steer control, different file in later message, text-only repeat) pass with the patch; the first two fail without it.

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
## Summary

Cron-scheduled automations bound to a Telegram account start failing with \`Scheduled account "<name>" is unavailable\` after gateway restarts, even though the account remains present in \`openclaw.json\` and live messaging on that account keeps working. Deleting and recreating the automation from a live session fixes it — until the next restart.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2)
- Linux aarch64 (kernel 5.15.199-tegra, Jetson), node v24.22.1
- Gateway runs as systemd user service \`openclaw-gateway.service\`
- Telegram channel with ~10 accounts in \`channels.telegram.accounts\` (bot tokens via secret store), \`defaultAccount: main\`

## Automation setup

- \`agentTurn\` cron job, \`schedule: 0 13 * * 2-6 Asia/Shanghai\`, \`sessionTarget: isolated\`, \`wakeMode: now\`
- \`delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "telegram", to: "<chat-id>", accountId: "mitegong" }\`
- Job state shows \`scheduledToolPolicy: { version: 1, mode: "account", ownerSessionKey: "agent:mitegong:telegram:mitegong:direct:***", ownerAccountId: "mitegong" }\`

## What happens

The job ran successfully for days, then began failing every scheduled run with:

\`\`\`
Scheduled account "mitegong" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account.
\`\`\`

Job state at time of failure: \`consecutiveErrors: 4\`, \`lastRunStatus: "error"\`, \`lastDeliveryStatus: "unknown"\`, \`lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus: "not-requested"\`.

## Evidence that this is a runtime binding issue, not configuration

1. The \`mitegong\` account is present in \`channels.telegram.accounts\` in the current \`openclaw.json\` **and in every config backup** going back weeks (7 snapshots checked). Nothing is missing from config.
2. Live Telegram messaging on the \`mitegong\` account works fine at the same time the scheduled run fails (user conversations on that account are unaffected).
3. Failures correlate with gateway restarts (CLI \`systemctl --user restart\`):
   - Restart at 2026-10-26T20:54Z → next cron run 2026-10-27T05:00Z failed with this error.
   - After the automation was deleted and recreated from a live session (~2026-10-27T06:45Z, which fixed the same failure mode once before), another restart occurred at 2026-10-27T14:24Z.
4. This is the **second occurrence** of this failure mode on the same job; both times recreation fixed it.

## Expected behavior

A gateway restart should not permanently break scheduled automations whose accounts are configured and healthy. The scheduler should re-resolve the account binding from config on startup (or retry resolution at run time) instead of erroring until the automation is manually recreated.

## Workaround

Delete the automation and re-add it from a live session on the target account (refreshes the owner binding). Works until the next gateway restart.

## Possible fix direction

On \`Scheduled account unavailable\`, attempt to re-resolve the account from \`channels.telegram.accounts\` / current account registry before failing the run; or make \`scheduledToolPolicy\` account bindings restart-safe.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), npm global install, Linux x86_64, systemd unit `openclaw-gateway`
**Setup:** Docker sandbox per agent; ~13 stdio MCP servers bundled per session (azure-devops, sharepoint, github-* via docker, word-document-server, pdf-text, ado-attachment, bc-code-intelligence, ...); several cron automations (command payloads) on the same host.

## Summary

With `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs` **unset** (the docs say the runtime default is 600000 ms, "one-shot embedded runs request cleanup at run-end"), the session-scoped bundled MCP runtime of every sandboxed agent session stays alive after the run ended: **13 `service-child-relay.js` children of the spawn broker per session**, never evicted (observed up to 13 h old). Each relay → `service-child-group-anchor.js` → the real stdio MCP server (e.g. `npm exec bc-code-intelligence-mcp` → `sh -c` → node).

`src/process/spawn-broker/worker.ts` (lines 121-122 at tag 2026.9.6 / commit `eb377ac`) has a hard cap:

```ts
async function launch(
  message: Extract<BrokerRequest, { type: "spawn" | "spawn-execa" }>,
): Promise<void> {
  if (stopping || owned.size + starting.size >= 256) {
    const error = new SpawnBrokerError("Spawn broker request capacity exceeded");
```

(The npm-bundled `dist/` build this report was originally filed against strips the TypeScript types, so it reads as `async function launch(message) {` there, but the guard condition and error message are identical.)

~19 sessions fill it. From then on **every** new spawn through the broker fails (`exec`, the sandbox `read`/`ls` tools, MCP starts of new sessions: `[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "…": stdio startup cleanup did not confirm closure | Spawn broker request capacity exceeded`), the gateway then reports `Spawn broker is unavailable` for every tool call, and it does not recover without restarting the gateway. All agents and cron automations share the same 256 slots, so production agents and cron jobs fail as well.

## Measurements

Gateway up 13 h 13 min, broker child count (`pgrep -P <broker pid> | wc -l`) = **256**, i.e. exactly the cap. Age distribution of the children: 0h: 15, 7h: 26, 9h: 26, 10h: 13, 12h: 127, 13h: 49 (mostly multiples of 13 = one set per session start). Broker itself healthy (0 % CPU, 67 MB RSS); ulimits not the cause (gateway: 524288 open files, 442174 processes). Cron automations failed at the same minutes ("Automation … failed 2 times"); agents reported a BLOCKER because `read`/`ls`/`exec` were unavailable.

After a clean gateway restart, with the key still unset (broker children after each step):

| moment | children |
|---|---|
| fresh gateway, idle | 0 |
| 1 min into one agent run | 13 |
| 3 min after that run ended | 13 |
| after 3 sequential runs | 39 |
| first of these sets, 48 min after its run ended | still alive |
| one config hot-reload later (see below), 2 min after the reload | 0 |

**Setting the key explicitly fixes it.** I set `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs = 600000` (exactly the documented default) via config. The hot-reload (`[reload] config hot reload applied (mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs)`) disposed the 39 leaked sets within about two minutes (not within 60 s). Then one fresh agent run:

| moment | children |
|---|---|
| before the run | 0 |
| run ended (09:36:57) | 13 |
| +3 / +6 / +9 min | 13 / 13 / 13 |
| +12 min | **0** |

So with the key authored, idle eviction works and happens about 10 min after the run ended. Two things remain unclear and might be part of the bug:

1. With the key unset, the documented default of 600000 evidently is not applied (children of 13 h survived), and "one-shot embedded runs request cleanup at run-end" did not happen either (the set survives until the idle TTL fires).
2. I cannot tell whether the explicit value works after a *fresh gateway start* or only after a hot reload (I have not restarted since). I will report back.

## Expected

- Session-scoped MCP runtimes disposed at run end for one-shot runs and after `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs` otherwise, with the documented default when the key is unset.
- A broker that is full should recover: capacity reclaimed, no permanent `unavailable`; the 256 cap configurable and surfaced in `openclaw status`/diagnostics.

## Workaround

Set `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs` explicitly (e.g. 600000). A change under `mcp.*` also disposes the cached runtimes of existing sessions (useful to purge a full broker without restarting the gateway, although it takes ~2 min).

## Notes

- `openclaw diagnostics` does not exist in 2026.9.6, so no diagnostics export is attached. I have the full gateway journal and a `ps` snapshot from the incident and can attach them.
- The file path/line reference above (`src/process/spawn-broker/worker.ts`, lines 121-122) was corrected against the `openclaw/openclaw` source at commit `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b` (tag 2026.9.6) when filing this; the original draft cited the bundled `dist/` path (`spawn-broker/worker.js`), which doesn't exist in this repo's source tree.

## Possibly related

Found while searching for duplicates — none of these match the specific symptom (spawn-broker process-count cap + sessionIdleTtlMs default not applying when unset), but they may share root cause in the MCP runtime/session lifecycle area:
- #144527 (closed as duplicate of #157062) — isolated cron runs leak a session MCP runtime until the *in-memory* `liveRuntimeSlots` accounting cap (also 256, but a different counter, not OS child processes) is hit.
- #157062 — root-caused `liveRuntimeSlots` leak when `joinCleanup()` throws on "uncertain" cleanup (streamable-http DELETE 404).

issues.body:
### Summary

Please decide whether Slack should support an opt-in that makes an already-admitted, explicitly mentioned **bot-authored informational group turn** reply-optional when group silence is allowed. This asks for a product-policy decision; it does not claim the documented current requiredness is a regression.

### Problem to solve

In cooperating-bot rooms, a completion/FYI notification may explicitly mention a peer only to deliver context. The receiving agent may have nothing useful to add. A genuinely empty completed answer is still a missing required reply and can trigger recovery/error output, keeping otherwise finished exchanges alive.

Exact completed `NO_REPLY` is a different case: merged #170534 already honors deliberate token-based silence on main. This request concerns the remaining optional-completion policy, including a genuinely empty final; it does not seek to reimplement that merged fix.

### Proposed solution

Ask the Slack/runtime owners to accept or reject a backward-compatible, operator-controlled policy at the existing reply-expectation owner:

- Applies only to authorized bot senders, an admitted group/channel turn with an explicit bot mention, and resolved group silence `allow`.
- When opted in, the turn may complete silently without a forced visible-answer recovery, while ordinary useful replies still work.
- Preserve the current default. Human explicit mentions, DMs, authorized commands, `disallow`, sender access, and bot-ingress protections keep their existing contracts.
- Do not prescribe a new configuration key or implement a new public surface before the owners choose the scope. If the supported answer is to require exact `NO_REPLY` and leave truly empty explicit mentions required, please record that decision here.

### Evidence and scope

On official `openclaw@2026.10.8` (build `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; verified tarball SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`), an isolated synthetic fixture with Slack group context, `SenderIsBot: true`, `WasMentioned: true`, explicit mention provenance and group silence `allow` returns `required` from the distributed owner. The current-main owner likewise has no bot-sender exception for explicit mentions. This is source/distributed-function evidence, not a fresh live Slack incident or end-to-end model run.

Historical motivation and the original policy request: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164946#issuecomment-6266529788 . That issue is closed for its original Discord/exact-`NO_REPLY` defect. #169927 is also closed for the existing intentional-silence solution; neither closure approves this distinct truly-empty opt-in policy.

### Alternatives and related work

- Use the existing exact-`NO_REPLY` contract: already supported on main, and a valid alternative if owners reject this policy.
- #166380 changes the delivery hint only for turns that are **already optional**. It leaves explicit-mention admission required, so its merge alone does not answer this request.
- #177555 / #160750 / #160752 govern whether **untagged** bots are admitted. This request starts after explicit bot admission and does not expand sender authority.
- #164877 handles implicit-thread requiredness, not explicit bot mentions.

No private runtime patch, modified employee package or configuration change is proposed or distributed. No customer content, workspace identities or credentials are included.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Only after maintainer direction on the public contract. The behavior should stay in the existing owning path; no independent workaround is proposed.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
M4V video bytes are correctly detected as `video/x-m4v`, but the playback owner returns an unsupported-format fallback instead of classifying portable codecs or preparing the existing MP4 rendition.

### Steps to reproduce
1. From a source checkout with FFmpeg/ffprobe available, generate a tiny MPEG-4 Part 2 clip:
   ```sh
   ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i 'color=c=blue:s=16x16:r=4:d=0.5' -an -c:v mpeg4 -threads 1 -brand 'M4V ' -f mp4 clip.m4v
   ```
2. Read the file through `detectMime({ buffer, filePath })`; it returns `video/x-m4v`.
3. Pass that detected MIME, the real file path and current file stat/identity to `resolvePlaybackMetadataForSource` and `resolvePlaybackTranscode` with `kind: "video"`.
4. Compare with the same file passed as `video/mp4`. Repeat using `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for a portable H.264 control.

### Expected behavior
The M4V spelling should use the existing MP4/MOV codec policy: H.264 with a portable profile and pixel format passes through; MPEG-4 Part 2 enters the bounded H.264 MP4 rendition path. This is the observed behavior for the identical bytes classified as `video/mp4`. OpenClaw already recognizes and preserves M4V type/extension metadata (#116928).

### Actual behavior
Both real M4V fixtures return metadata without a `playback` field and `{ kind: "fallback" }` from the playback resolver. Their duration and dimensions are correctly probed. The same bytes labeled `video/mp4` return `playback: "native"` for H.264 and `playback: "transcode"` for MPEG-4 Part 2.

### OpenClaw version
Source main `c0ca702a75806d7d87d676ba43c9b3349e7d2860` (package version 2026.10.3).

### Operating system
Debian GNU/Linux 13, Linux x64, Node 24.19.0, FFmpeg 7.1.5.

### Install method
Source checkout with its own frozen-lockfile pnpm installation.

### Model
Not applicable; reproduction calls the actual media source/playback owner without a model.

### Provider / routing chain
Local synthetic M4V -> media MIME detector -> playback source resolver. No live provider or channel.

### Logs
```text
MPEG-4 Part 2 M4V (931 bytes):
  detected MIME: video/x-m4v
  metadata: { durationMs: 500, width: 16, height: 16 }
  playback: { kind: "fallback" }
  identical bytes with video/mp4: playback "transcode"

H.264 High/yuv420p M4V (1590 bytes):
  detected MIME: video/x-m4v
  metadata: { durationMs: 500, width: 16, height: 16 }
  playback: { kind: "fallback" }
  identical bytes with video/mp4: playback "native"
```

### Impact and severity
Affected path: assistant video attachment playback. Nonportable M4V codecs never receive the playable MP4 rendition, even when FFmpeg is available. The failure reproduced for both synthetic M4V files. Native browser/device playback was not tested; this report establishes the source resolver failure, not every client's response to the original bytes.

### Additional information
`PLAYBACK_TRANSCODE_POLICY.video` lists `video/mp4` but omits the detector-produced `video/x-m4v` spelling from native and codec-probe maps. The existing `mov` demuxer already handles these bytes. No new codec, demuxer, upload allowlist, or dependency is needed.

issues.body:
### Summary

`memory-lancedb` should register a memory search `runtime`, so the Control UI Memory page works when it owns `plugins.slots.memory`.

### Problem to solve

With the official `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` as the memory slot owner, the Control UI Memory page can't show or search anything. The plugin only registers `publicArtifacts`:

```js
// extensions/memory-lancedb/dist/index.js (2026.9.4 installed; 2026.9.6 from npm is identical)
api.registerMemoryCapability?.({ publicArtifacts: { async listArtifacts(params) { /* … */ } } });
```

Without a `runtime`, `ensureMemoryRuntime` returns `{ searchRuntimeRegistered: false }` and every host-side memory search call fails:

```
$ openclaw gateway call doctor.memory.status --params '{"agentId":"main"}'
{ "agentId": "main", "searchRuntimeRegistered": false,
  "embedding": { "ok": false, "error": "memory plugin unavailable" } }

$ openclaw gateway call memory.search --params '{"query":"test","agentId":"main"}'
Gateway call failed: memory plugin unavailable
```

Since #155117 the Overview shows a neutral "Host memory search is unavailable — memory-lancedb does not provide a host memory search runtime" hero instead of a failure. That is accurate, but the page is still empty and the Memories tab search still fails.

Meanwhile the memory system itself is healthy, so this is purely an operator-visibility gap:

- `openclaw ltm stats` / `ltm search`: LanceDB store OK, vector recall OK.
- `openclaw memory search "…" --agent main` and the agent's `memory_search` / `memory_get` return hits from the memory-core file index. memory-core's tool opens its manager through `getBuiltinMemorySearchManager` directly, not through the slot owner.
- `memory_recall` / `memory_store` / `memory_forget` and auto-recall work.

The agent can search its memory, but the operator can't see it from the UI. The only config-level "fix" is setting the slot back to `memory-core`, which drops the LanceDB tools and auto-recall and cuts off the stored memories. So users of the featured first-party memory plugin are left with a Memory page that never works.

### Proposed solution

Have `memory-lancedb` pass a `runtime` in `registerMemoryCapability`, like memory-core does (`createLazyMemoryRuntime`):

- `getMemorySearchManager(params)` returns a manager backed by the plugin's LanceDB store. It embeds the query with the configured embedding provider, runs the agent-scoped vector search it already uses for `memory_recall`, and maps rows to the result shape the Memories tab renders (text, score, source, id).
- `closeMemorySearchManager` / `closeAllMemorySearchManagers` release the table handles.
- Optional hooks (`authorizeSearchHits`, `classifyWorkspaceMemoryPaths`, `supportsWorkspaceMemoryReadSources`) can stay unset at first.

Plugin authors have already pointed out that a third-party slot owner which registers a `runtime` gets a working Overview and search (see #138366). The first-party plugin would then be the reference implementation of that seam.

### Alternatives considered

- **Fallback in core**: when the slot owner registers no runtime, `memory.search` and the Memories tab fall back to the builtin file-index manager, labelled as such. That mirrors what the agent's `memory_search` tool already does, and it would also help third-party slot owners without a runtime. But it would still show nothing of the LanceDB store itself, which is where `memory-lancedb` keeps its memories. It works as a complement, not a replacement.
- **Slot back to `memory-core`**: the UI works (file index only), but the LanceDB tools and auto-recall are lost. Not viable.

### Impact

- Affected: every install using `memory-lancedb` (featured in the plugin catalog) as the memory slot owner.
- Severity: annoying to workflow-blocking for operators. Nothing in the Memory page can be inspected, and the only way to audit memories is the CLI (`ltm list` / `ltm search`) or asking the agent.
- Frequency: always, by design of the current registration.
- Consequence: memories can't be reviewed from the UI, which makes it hard to spot bad or stale auto-captured entries.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Docker on Linux, `plugins.slots.memory = "memory-lancedb"`, Ollama embeddings; memory-core loaded as the dreaming sidecar. Startup log: `memory plugin not selected for the memory slot; skipping its indexing runtime and recall registration (consolidation lifecycle preserved) (plugin=memory-core)`.
- Discussed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138366#issuecomment-5844801270. The issue author agreed it is a separate gap from the Dreams provider and preferred a `runtime` in `memory-lancedb` over a core fallback.
- Related: #153016 (same symptom with a third-party slot owner, closed by the neutral hero in #155117).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Should stay backward-compatible: `memory-core` as slot owner is unchanged, and the runtime only exists when `memory-lancedb` holds the slot.

issues.body:
## Summary

With OpenClaw.app running, the gateway service restarts continuously at irregular intervals (measured: 32s to 727s, degrading to ~60s). Sessions die mid-task with WebSocket 1005/1006 closures. Quitting the app stops it completely — 14h44m of uninterrupted uptime with the app closed, versus restarts every few minutes with it open.

## Environment

- **Version:** 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), macOS
- **LaunchAgent:** `gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`
- **Two installs of the same version coexist:**
  - `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw` (what `which openclaw` resolves to; `doctor` runs from here)
  - `~/.openclaw/tools/node-v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/openclaw` (app-managed runtime)
- Both `package.json` files report `2026.7.1-2` — this is **not** a version skew.

## Mechanism (verified)

1. `openclaw doctor` reports *"Gateway service entrypoint does not match the current install"* and offers to repair it.
2. Accepting the repair writes a plist that still contains the **old entrypoint** — it fixes `PATH` only. The stale-entrypoint warning therefore recurs.
3. Editing the plist manually to the homebrew path **does work**: the gateway starts clean from it, health `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`, no module errors.
4. **On launch, the app rewrites the LaunchAgent back to its own path and boots the service to apply it:**

```
09:29:44  app launched
09:30:10  plist rewritten (manual edit reverted)
09:30:11  [gateway] signal SIGTERM received
```

Manual fix survived **26 seconds**.

## Process chain (captured by 1s process sampling)

The invocations are too short-lived for a plain `ps` snapshot:

```
launchctl bootout gui/501 .../ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
  ← openclaw-gateway
    ← openclaw
      ← /Applications/OpenClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/OpenClaw
        ← launchd
```

## Excluded with evidence

- **No `StartInterval`** in the plist; `RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive` only
- **ProcessType Interactive** — not macOS resource throttling
- **No crashes** — every stop is a clean `"[gateway] signal SIGTERM received"`
- **No health-monitor failure** logged; it only ever logs at startup
- **Cron:** 6 enabled jobs, 0 overdue, none on a matching interval
- **Not a version skew:** both `package.json` report `2026.7.1-2`

## Additional observations

- `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-restart.log` stopped recording on 2026-07-22; none of these restarts appear there. The live log is `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`.
- `openclaw doctor` reports cron at `~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json`, which was migrated away on 2026-06-05 and no longer exists; live cron is in `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` (`cron_jobs`, `cron_run_logs`).

## Expected behavior

Either the app tolerates a separately-installed CLI without rewriting the service definition, or `doctor` recognises the app-managed entrypoint as legitimate instead of flagging it and offering a repair that cannot hold.

## Practical impact

Sessions are interrupted mid-task, subagents can be pruned during recovery, and long-running orchestration is unreliable while the app is open. The browser UI at `http://127.0.0.1:18789/` works normally — everything gateway-side is unaffected by quitting the app, which is the stable workaround.

issues.body:
### What happens

`openclaw backup create` archives every configured agent workspace in full. When an agent builds a project in its workspace (here, an agent that set up a Remotion video project and ran `npm install`), the workspace gains a dependency tree. That tree can be rebuilt from its lockfile, yet it goes into every archive and takes up most of the backup's time.

Measured on one Windows 11 install (runtime 2026.9.6, Node 24.21.0, Defender on, no exclusions):

- Archives of this install taken before the tree existed, timed from the output folder's creation to the archive's write: 2 min 05 s (412 MB archive), 1 min 50 s (712 MB) and 3 min 47 s (3.4 GB, mostly two large model files).
- One agent then created `agents/<agent>/workspace/<project>/node_modules`: 15,144 files, 794 MB. That is about three quarters of the files in the archived roots (about 19,900).
- The next archive took 18 min 46 s for 1.05 GB.

So file count, not size, drives the time: a 3.4 GB archive of two large files took under 4 minutes, while 15,000 small files added about 17 minutes.

docs/cli/backup.md already treats this kind of tree as rebuildable for plugins: "nested `node_modules/` dependency trees are skipped as rebuildable install artifacts" under `extensions/`. For agent workspaces there is nothing between the whole workspace and `--no-include-workspace`, which drops the agents' own files too. Plugins cannot help either. `backupResources` takes a fixed `relativePath` under `scope: "state"` or `"agent"`, with no workspace scope and no globs (docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md, "backupResources reference"), and explicit workspace paths override exclusions (docs/cli/backup.md).

### What we would like

A documented way to leave regenerable folders inside workspaces out of an archive, reported in `skipped` with reason `regenerable` as the existing rules are. Any of these would work:

1. A config key with workspace-relative patterns, for example `backup.workspace.regenerable: ["**/node_modules"]`, honoured by `backup create` and listed in the result.
2. `backupResources` entries with `scope: "workspace"` that accept a glob segment (`**/node_modules`), so that a plugin that knows its agents build projects can declare them.
3. The same default the `extensions/` tree gets: workspace `node_modules/` trees are skipped as rebuildable, with an opt-out.

In each case restore would stay as it is: the operator rebuilds the dependencies (`npm ci`), as the docs already say for plugin dependencies.

### Why it matters

Hosts that take a backup before an update, or on a schedule, cannot let it run for 20 minutes, and agents that write code or build media projects will keep making these trees. #136318 (closed) was the same kind of tree stalling an archive outright. Earlier pull requests for general exclude patterns (#40804, #40810, #44288) were closed for inactivity rather than declined. This request is narrower: regenerable trees inside workspaces only, reported in the result.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (the same rules are in the 2026.9.9 docs and on main), Windows 11, Node 24.21.0. Every archive above, the fast ones included, also held a browser profile (447 MB, 308 files) and voice models (148 MB). At a few hundred files, they do not explain the change from 2 to 19 minutes.

Explain how the owner is selected, how `--agent <id>` pins it, and that creation fails when no owner can be resolved. Cover script-job warnings as well as agent-turn warnings.

## Actual docs behavior/content
The docs say omission falls back to the default agent (`main`) and mention only agent-turn warnings.

## Impact
Operators may expect an automation to stay on `main` when their configured owner is another agent, or expect successful creation without a resolvable owner.

## Evidence
- [CLI warning and request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e0f1692a6e19f8383c00c0693531dc9a84c47bea/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts#L345)

issues.body:
### Summary
On the **Portals** page the preview frame does not use the available window height. On any viewport taller than ~910px the layout is capped at 720px, leaving empty space below the embedded app.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a portal (e.g. "show me in a portal" for any dev server).
2. Open **Control UI → Portals** in a desktop browser window taller than ~1000px (e.g. 1440p, maximised).
3. Select the portal.

**Expected:** the preview (rail + frame) fills the viewport down to the bottom edge, like the chat pane.
**Actual:** the layout ends at 720px; the rest of the page is blank. The embedded app has to scroll inside a short frame.

### Cause
The Portals page stylesheet sets
```css
.portals-layout { min-height: min(720px, 100vh - 190px); display: grid; ... }
.portals-preview__frame { flex: 1; height: 100%; min-height: 480px; }
```
`min(720px, …)` caps the height at 720px, and the layout has no `height`/`flex: 1`, so it never grows to the viewport.

### Proposed fix
Let the layout fill the remaining height of the page container instead of a fixed cap, e.g. make the page body a flex column and give `.portals-layout` `flex: 1; min-height: 480px;` (or `height: calc(100dvh - <header offset>)`), keeping the current behaviour on narrow/mobile widths (≤768px). Minimal diff: one CSS rule in the Portals page stylesheet; no behaviour change for the rail or the new-tab fallback.

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.10.8, Control UI on desktop Chrome/Safari (macOS). Workaround today is an injected script that sets the height from `window.innerHeight`, which has to be re-applied after every update.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A pending `BOOTSTRAP.md` causes the embedded runtime to add a system instruction to commit edits, which conflicts with an explicit request to leave changes uncommitted for review. A live CLI reproduction completed the requested code change and tests but created a local commit anyway.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a clean disposable Git workspace containing a small JavaScript project, ordinary coding guidance in `AGENTS.md`, and the current `BOOTSTRAP.md` template. Record HEAD. The project guidance must not itself require committing.
2. Run a fresh built-in OpenClaw agent through `openclaw agent exec --isolated --auth-env-only --cwd <workspace>` with an authenticated OpenAI model.
3. Ask for a real code correction, focused tests, and a README example, ending with: “Leave all changes uncommitted so I can review the diff before deciding the commit boundary. Do not push or open a pull request.”
4. Inspect HEAD, the working-tree diff, and the tests independently after completion.

The tested project calculated basket subtotals. The requested correction accounted for item quantities, treated a missing quantity as one, and covered zero quantity and an empty basket.

### Expected behavior

The requested changes and tests are completed while HEAD remains unchanged and the diff stays available for review. Git backup is documented as optional, and the bootstrap template says the user's request comes first.

### Actual behavior

The live run advanced HEAD from `39ffab6` to `6d4bda5` and left a clean working tree. The new commit used the fixture's ordinary Git identity and the subject “Fix basket subtotal to account for item quantities.” Tests and independent subtotal assertions passed. Session metadata verified the OpenClaw harness and full BOOTSTRAP injection.

Two fresh controls passed: an explicit request to create a local commit produced one; the same no-commit request without BOOTSTRAP left HEAD unchanged and the three edited files uncommitted. These observations support the instruction conflict but do not establish a deterministic model failure rate.

### OpenClaw version

Source build at d83e466e42c3238a952c52835a559ba875fbbf94.

### Operating system

Linux x64 remote Testbox, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0.

### Install method

Source checkout with locked dependencies; native `pnpm openclaw agent exec` entry point.

### Model

Live OpenAI model through the built-in OpenClaw harness; model identifier retained privately.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw embedded runtime → OpenAI, with existing environment-based authentication.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The [bootstrap preparation owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d83e466e42c3238a952c52835a559ba875fbbf94/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bootstrap-prepare.ts#L165-L172) adds the commit reminder whenever loaded BOOTSTRAP is non-missing. This is independent of the [document-injection filter](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d83e466e42c3238a952c52835a559ba875fbbf94/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bootstrap-prepare.ts#L138-L140). A real-file owner-path probe also confirmed that limited project mode receives the reminder while BOOTSTRAP has zero injected characters.

### Impact and severity

Users who want to review or group edits before committing can receive an already-committed result during pending workspace setup. This changes the requested Git workflow. The observed failure was a normal local commit, not a permission bypass; no push or PR publication was requested or observed. Original guest-session attribution and broader failure frequency remain unverified.
