prs.title: fix(cli): sweep terminal value escaping and bidi controls in report families
prs.body:
## Problem

File-derived names, paths, plugin metadata and pairing fields can carry terminal escape sequences or bidirectional formatting controls into human reports. The first owner sweep (#185927) established value encoding; these sixteen follow-on fixes identify additional consumers and a missing bidi case in the owner.

## Root cause and owner

`packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.ts` owns terminal value encoding. Extend `sanitizeTerminalText` to Unicode `Bidi_Control`, preserving printable RTL text and emoji joiners. Use `terminalText` for value interpolation before styling, existing safe table/value-display helpers, and the existing official-plugin terminal-safe-text facade. There is no sink filter, SGR allowlist, or change to `renderTable`'s trusted-ANSI contract.

Cut over the contributor fixes to that owner, remove the private pairing bidi regex and redundant per-site wrappers/extraction/tests, and cover adjacent human output in the same bounded command families. Shared wiki renderers keep raw defaults for model-facing consumers; their CLI formatter supplies the encoder once. Backup namespace refusals use the existing `ExpectedCliError` human/machine boundary, rather than filtering root error reports. The small finalize-search sibling keeps credential-source presentation together without growing the already over-cap wizard module.

JSON fields, persisted identifiers, operational paths, raw source/page exports and install-trust report forwarding retain their existing contracts. Theme styling is applied after values are encoded; authored multiline layout is preserved.

## Absorbed work and credit

Original primary fix commits are retained with unchanged authorship before the owner cutover:

| Family | Contributor PRs |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin install/authoring/marketplace/update | #184454, #184379, #185374, #186449 |
| Memory, memory-wiki, workboard, oc-path | #184396, #184788, #184813, #184394 |
| Plugin enable/disable; secrets audit/configure | #185895, #185719 |
| Plugin uninstall/search; channel pairing | #175600, #175181, #175179 |
| Sessions cleanup headers | #184747 |
| Backup namespace owner reports | #184597 |
| Pending node pairing bidi controls | #150599 |

Thanks to **Leon-SK668, huwei-xydt, wangmiao0668000666, SunnyShu0925, KrasimirKralev and arpe1618**. This builds on the earlier owner sweep and the reports by **Alix-007 and qingminglong** credited there.

Ownership checked before adoption and again before publication. **#150599 is assigned to maintainer fuller-stack-dev and must not be closed as superseded**. The other fifteen are unassigned, with no maintainer commits observed; the lead owns their disposition after landing. This PR does not close or comment on those PRs.

## Validation

Secretless Docker, **node:24.22.1**, built `/work/openclaw.mjs`, isolated task-owned profiles/state/config/SQLite paths; no live Gateway or real provider credentials. Pinned main: `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`.

Raw stdout/stderr and hex captures exercise config paths, setup directories, secrets findings, cleanup stores, backup owner refusals, channel/node pairing, plugin author/build/validate/pack/install/search/marketplace/update/uninstall, memory search/status, wiki local reports, workboard cards and oc-path inspection. Inputs combine ESC/CSI, OSC 8, C1 CSI, bidi controls and LF/TAB. Main already protects some C0/C1 sites from the earlier sweep; those reproduce the remaining **bidi** leak, not a claimed regression of the old protection. Normal theme SGR, decoded JSON identities, on-disk names and raw exports are explicit controls.

Focused checks include changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, the owner matrix (red on pinned main, green on candidate), config/pairing consumers, backup path consumers and wizard finalize consumers. Contributor code and commit-hook checks run only inside Docker; host commits have hooks disabled. Full typechecks, broad suites and cross-platform checks belong to hosted CI.

## Not fixed here

This is a bounded follow-on, **not a claim that every CLI sink is safe**. Deferred:

- `src/cli/update-cli/**`, `src/cli/update-cli.ts`; qa-lab/internal QA.
- Unrelated cron, claws, channel/auth, directory, logs, models/inference, gateway/daemon, non-pairing node, skills/hooks and banner command families.
- Doctor and Windows firewall guidance, daemon runtime-hints/systemd-hints, gateway discovery labels and channel chat-meta labels.
- Install-trust/scanner/integrity producers and warning formatters, including `src/skills/lifecycle/{clawhub.ts,source-install.ts}` and plugin install-security-scan runtime. Trusted install-box marker forwarding is unchanged.
- Extension families browser, codex, crabbox, file-transfer, matrix, onepassword, onnx, openshell, policy, reef, team-reports, vault, voice-call, mcp-relay and google-meet.

Release-note context: human reports in the listed families neutralize untrusted terminal and bidi controls without altering stored or machine-readable values. No CHANGELOG edit (release-owned).

## Simplification and exact local results

Removed the contributor-only enable extraction, private pairing bidi policy and per-site regression scaffolding. The canonical owner and existing display helpers remain; necessary growth is caller cutover, presentation-only callback plumbing, typed recovery-message projection and the small credential-summary sibling required by the line-cap ratchet. Against merged main `d5016796673c813cdaaf5fcc0ce0e34e7291408d`: production **+677/-481 (net +196)**; tests **+26/-26 (net zero)**; docs **+5/-2**. Formatter wrapping is included, not hidden.

Observed: changed-file oxfmt/oxlint and full staged commit hook including line-cap growth ratchet passed inside Docker. Owner suite **10/10**, config/pairing **74/74**, backup paths **6/6**, finalize **57/57**, device/marketplace **54/54**, completion **10/10**, config/backup integration **21/21**, and config recovery owner **1/1** passed. The new owner assertions fail on pinned main in exactly the two bidi boundaries; the memory-wiki package-local compile passes after its optional-value repair. Both built lanes complete **85 CLI invocations each**, with all harness assertions passing and identical normal-color SGR arrays. Interactive configure menus and actual remote plugin upgrades were source-audited but not interactively exercised; plugin update proof uses the real untracked-selection error path.

Raw-byte evidence on final merged head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186502#issuecomment-6460632667

First-head CI/review identified three owned regressions, fixed in `468a7e0fc90b9`: restore version encoding before marketplace label formatting; retain existing device identity/IP CR/LF deletion before canonical bidi encoding rather than changing that behavior or weakening its tests; stringify optional wiki lookup values before encoding. The affected device/marketplace suites pass **54/54**, the memory-wiki package-local TypeScript compile passes, and changed-file lint, the full Docker staged hook and all **85 built candidate CLI invocations** pass again after the repairs. No consumer assertions were changed.

The completed first-head CI also identified an owned config recovery-layout regression and a backup integration harness missing the canonical root expected-error projection. Recovery errors now keep raw machine text while encoding value fields before their authored newline; the existing backup harness projects expected errors through `formatCliFailureLines`. No assertions were weakened. Consolidating detector inputs keeps every owner case while meeting the zero-net-test-growth constraint.

Current main was merged only after GitHub reported a real conflict; setup completion preserves its new optional UTF-8 failure guidance. The latest contributor integration commit from #185895 is also retained, followed by the same complete owner cutover. Final built-source receipts match all 68 selected source/consumer paths byte-for-byte.

Exact scheduled-main evidence for the original-head inherited UI failures (all four cases match; zero cancelled jobs): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186502#issuecomment-6460487062. UI repairs remain out of scope.

prs.title: feat(ui): add validation for event asset manifests
prs.body:
Related: #160991

## What Problem This Solves

Event asset tooling needs to check the emitted inventory and declared bundle dependencies before producing a hash manifest.

## User Impact

This adds source tooling and directly executable tests. It does not connect an event build, change the UI or runtime, or qualify an asset bundle. Manifest validity does not authorize serving assets.

## Why This Change Was Made

The validator checks emitted paths, MIME types, size limits, document/style references, and recognizable JavaScript capabilities. The writer requires complete Vite bundle metadata, checks that its keys match the emitted paths, and validates declared dependency closure before any manifest output.

SVG files are allowed and hashed without content inspection. A serving owner must separately define SVG handling, origin isolation, and CSP. The bounded JavaScript analysis does not prove arbitrary JavaScript or computed URLs safe; complete, truthful bundler metadata remains an input assumption. Directory validation rejects symlinks at each non-root component; the filesystem root is trusted.

The focused package command executes all Node tests directly. Windows drive/UNC handling is corrected, and CSS escape tests use local fixtures rather than unrelated composer source bytes.

The previous receiving step incorporated main through 7cc7e521137ddfe25b02280b5f7a13fe8262ce35, preserving existing repairs 3baeac6d1ffe3322b404d76cde45b25bd84563a9, 124ddc0a49fe09ec2d08cb307de642e9d7d4f314, 2fc693e33eff44730a0113d33f8f68b1642db0a3, and f0cd14c67ee598f31d2fb5c02b81d782e57e2e88 for the prior session/core test failures. Their original ancestry and attribution are preserved. The only authored source change after the writer correction is the serving-limit comment. That prior receiving commit preserved the event and package bytes and incorporated the upstream one-line Crabbox audit fixture correction in 7cc7e521. It does not change the production audit guard, sanitizer, cap, dependency, or runtime admission policy.

## Evidence

- Retained prior source validation: all 35 event tests passed on Node 24.20.0 with zero failures, skips, cancellations, or TODOs. Measured wall time: 0.71 seconds. Formatting and Git diff checks passed.
- The writer tests previously failed against the implementation without mandatory bundle metadata. They cover absent/incomplete/mismatched metadata and missing/external static, dynamic, CSS, and asset dependencies, including no manifest after rejection.
- Windows regressions use Node's real Windows path semantics with a recording filesystem; real filesystem rejection tests run on Linux. This is not a live Windows filesystem result.
- Prior selected planner proof passed five packing, cap, coverage, and resource-policy tests in 59.7 seconds, with 227 other cases filtered. That is retained prior-head evidence. Its earlier full two-file run timed out after 240 seconds.
- Prior hosted CI run 36551943517 on 5be28e9e7771196120667c7f26489de82b2937a3 was cancelled with failures; cancelled coverage is not passing evidence. This branch receives the upstream repairs, while new combined-head hosted CI remains required. Core SQLite fixtures and a full planner/runtime graph were not executed locally in this receiving attempt.
- Earlier independent review accepted the writer correction and passed all 35 tests. Earlier automated helper attempts timed out without reports and remain unavailable evidence.
- The subsequently published head 9d75c723c2fe605b6e1718f4d123bcdc2680b500 was tested by CI run 36607456166 on merge e2128979de87e4dfe9590dda02b33c8d00818d61 against main 6ec6cf52c5187cf3c789857c60bca2ee59d3b92c. That run was cancelled after the Crabbox immutable-parent audit fixture failed: 52 jobs succeeded, 2 failed (including the aggregate gate), 80 were cancelled, and 19 skipped. The unchanged fixture returned a placeholder for the new parent lookup; upstream 7cc7e521 supplies the expected parent. This receiving step preserves that upstream correction and its attribution. A focused literal-stub probe supports the diagnosis; it is not a full test-suite reproduction or passing hosted CI. New combined-head CI remains required.
- ClawSweeper completed review of 9d75c723 with no actionable findings or security concern. It retained recommendations about future integration and data-model proof; the selected scope remains a standalone source contract, without build or serving admission. This receiving candidate requires fresh independent integration/outgoing review.
- Full asset build, browser, provider, serving-policy qualification, and protected landing are separate from this source-only change.

### CI recovery update

Received upstream main through bda22f818d967ffa3551b3a729d5bc43863844c7, including b4df789c, which removes a duplicate database-worker test enrollment. The three event/package feature blobs are unchanged; all selected upstream content is preserved.

The previous head 2019114 failed CI run 36611820372 during manifest generation before its test lanes ran. The current inventory contains 853 distinct entries. Retained 35 passing event cases cover the unchanged feature inputs; they are prior evidence, not a combined-head CI result. New-head hosted CI remains required.

The existing helper-unavailable and unknown-descendant dispositions remain unchanged. SVG contents are not inspected, and manifest validity does not authorize serving assets. No runtime/build consumer, sanitizer, dependency or migration is added.

prs.title: fix(projects): register the selected checkout when its path ends in whitespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes project registration selecting a neighboring checkout, or rejecting an existing checkout, when its directory name ends in whitespace.

## User Impact

Users register the exact Git checkout they selected, including valid POSIX paths ending in a space, tab, CR or LF. An existing trimmed neighbor is no longer stored as the project's repository. Existing incorrectly registered projects are not automatically repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep @Alix-007's focused repair at the existing project-checkout owner: remove Git's single protocol LF rather than trimming filename characters. Directory, realpath, Git and committed-HEAD validation stay in place. No global resolver, Git decoder, schema, default or permission changes.

The regression reuses the existing real-Git registry persistence fixture with a trailing-space root, retaining its exact-root, symlink, deduplication, ID, listing/order and removal assertions instead of adding a parallel direct-helper suite. Production delta is +2/-1 lines; tests/support delta is zero.

## Evidence

The contributor's original Node 26 Linux CLI/Gateway reproduction is supplemented by supported Node 24.22.1 built-Gateway proof and controls linked below.

Supported Node 24.22.1 Linux/ARM64 Docker: both full builds passed. Through fresh built Gateways and the shipped CLI, main twice registered the trimmed neighbor/CONTROL origin and aliased its ID; the candidate twice registered the exact selected root/RIGHT origin with separate listed IDs. This held for space, tab, CR and LF suffixes. Ordinary, relative, absolute-home and symlink controls passed; missing/non-Git/unborn/file and literal home-shorthand refusals remained unchanged. All 52 scenarios passed.

[Observed registration/list captures and focused checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186474#issuecomment-6460666826).

The consolidated registry regression failed on main at the original trimming path and passed on the candidate. Targeted formatting, type-aware lint and whitespace checks passed. Native Windows/macOS and automatic repair of earlier wrong registrations were not exercised. Candidate: `1ab42481594404b8235a4759fa75cec38c6bfd09`; main baseline: `d79a7b6c371c8b37938d412a2015b2545f6699db`.

### Not fixed here

No automatic migration of registrations made with the wrong root. This does not add home-shorthand expansion or change global path resolution.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door for the implementation; a revert restores the old trimming behavior. Registrations are persisted state: reverting does not repair rows already registered against the wrong checkout, and correct literal-path rows remain stored. Blast radius: project registration and other callers of the existing checkout owner when Git reports whitespace-bearing roots.

prs.title: fix(gateway): recheck account health before recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the channel health monitor restarting an account that recovered while the monitor was waiting for another account's teardown.

## User Impact

A recovered account stays online when an earlier account takes time to stop. Accounts that remain unhealthy still receive the existing recovery attempt. No configuration, timeout, authentication or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial snapshot now supplies account identifiers only. Before each recovery decision, the monitor reads current status, time, reload state and suppression. Running-account recovery immediately captures the current lifetime and uses the lifecycle owner's conditional restart; stopped accounts retain the start-only path.

The lifecycle owner resets restart attempts only after identity, manual-stop and account-membership checks, immediately before fallible start preparation. This preserves the previous preparation-failure behavior without resetting a replacement account's budget.

Production delta: +58/-33 (net +25). The added capability binds fresh health admission to existing account-lifetime ownership. An explicit consumed-method contract also makes missing manager operations visible to fixture typechecking; it introduces no separate recovery loop or health policy. Reload consumers reference the canonical full manager directly instead of a monitor-derived alias.

## Evidence

- Independent owner and test review, plus pre-commit autoreview, found no actionable source findings. Targeted formatting, diff checks, the native file-size guard and normal commit hooks passed.
- Thirteen new real-manager cases cover replacement recovery, recovery in the same lifetime, a still-unhealthy control, grace expiry during teardown, changed suppression/reload/manual/listing state, preparation-failure reset ordering and ownership changes after an awaited stop.
- Current candidate `b3521e269da043f74068d47d10e3b41eccdef15e` integrates the exact landed Telegram squash `6b3170b024f8e1e6f55f2e71a7ca18020e70d08a`. All seven health production blobs are unchanged from reviewed head `90410a0581ab287da2a24b10d5358b722701382a`. The newly landed companion reconnect-grace case now expects the enumeration and fresh admission snapshots, plus canonical `preserveManualStop: true` on restart. Its 33-second-to-60-second no-recovery check and later exact stop/start assertions remain intact. This two-assertion correction passed scoped P0-P3 autoreview; composed runtime proof is pending fresh CI.
- The maintenance fixture records capture reason/account, snapshots its ordering evidence before cleanup, and asserts first-account-only recovery before deferred thaw resumes. The healthy-sibling case moves intact into the existing recovery registration and retains the same parent lifecycle hooks. The standalone lifecycle harness now explicitly implements the consumed manager contract instead of hiding a missing capture operation behind a double cast; its cadence and cooldown expectations are unchanged. Tests/support add 268 net lines.
- Hosted CI on prior head `90410a0581ab287da2a24b10d5358b722701382a` passed **178 primary affected runtime cases** and **199 additional siblings**: [monitor-lifetime 13, monitor 24 and reload-metadata sibling 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628655814/job/122620498783), [lifecycle QA 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628655814/job/122620498922), and [manager 93, manager-lifetime 11, maintenance 36 and 198 reload/runtime siblings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628655814/job/122620498901). Its [package/declaration boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628655814/job/122620498857) and type jobs also passed. These are prior-head results; they do not prove the newly composed companion test or current candidate.

Native exit was 255; a separate read-only status check confirmed the exact lease completed. This supplies neither baseline-red nor candidate-green proof.
- Fresh ordinary PR CI must execute the composed monitor regression, account-lifetime/thaw siblings, lifecycle QA and package/type gates. The local checkout has no qualified dependencies. No live-channel or full Gateway E2E behavior is claimed.

Uses the account-lifetime recovery boundary landed in [the thaw fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186077) and composes with [the landed Telegram disconnect-episode fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186470).

prs.title: fix: background command completions lose the owner's owner-only tools
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent cannot use owner-only tools (such as `openclaw` or `plugins`) to finish a task after a background command it started for the owner completes; the owner has to send another message first.

## User Impact

User impact: when a channel owner asks the agent to do something that runs a background command, the completion turn can finish the job with the same owner tools, without asking the owner to reply "go". Commands started by other senders keep the current restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner-only tools follow the turn's sender. A background-exec completion turn has no sender, so it was never treated as the owner, even when the owner's own turn started the command. Plugin-reload and tool handoffs already continue owner authority, but only for a Gateway-owner `operatorAuthority`; channel owners configured through `commands.ownerAllowFrom` have none, so they lost it.

The exec producer now asks the session event target to keep its requester as command owner. The target takes the requester identity from the host-owned tool caller (never from the producer), prepares it once with the existing `prepareCommandOwnerAuthority`, and stores it only if the requester is an owner. The completion context binds the existing command-owner capability, whose check reruns `isCurrent` against the current config each time. A batch refuses to merge completions from different requesters, keyed on the captured sender rather than the shared `configured-owner` label, so one owner's completion can't run under another owner's authority.

Main has since added `ownerContinuation` for operator-authority tool handoffs (publish, plugin reload). Both now sit in the same target scope: operator handoffs bind through `ownerContinuation`, exec completions bind through the requester's `commandOwner`, the context binds only one of them, and a batch refuses to mix either.

Not covered on purpose: lost-process wakes after a Gateway restart (the capability is in memory only, so they keep today's gate), and plugin/tool handoffs for channel owners (same pattern, separate change).

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, unmocked effect** (new QA Lab flow `exec-completion-owner-authority`, `pnpm openclaw qa suite --scenario exec-completion-owner-authority --provider-mode mock-openai`): a real Gateway child, the QA channel plugin, real `exec`, and the real `automations` tool persisting through the Gateway's `cron.add`. Only the model is the scripted `mock-openai`. Each sender DMs the agent, which starts `sleep 6; echo …` in the background. The completion turn then calls the owner-only `automations` tool to add a disabled job, and the flow checks `cron.list`. Run on `b2d0255`, result `pass`:
  ```
  owner completion persists an automation   pass  job=o270eccda persisted=true
    completionToolOutput={"tool":{"id":"openclaw:core:automations",…},"result":{…"id":"8ec9e0cc-…"
  guest completion is refused               pass  job=g001c8b48 persisted=false
    completionToolOutput={"status":"error","tool":"dispatch_action","error":"Unknown tool id: automations. …"}
  ```
  The guest's completion turn doesn't have `automations` in its catalog at all, so the call fails before any Gateway request and nothing is persisted.
- Revocation: owner status is rechecked against the Gateway's applied config when the completion is captured, when it's admitted, and at the effect (unit cases `revoked-before-admission` and `revoked-after-admission` below). On a real Gateway, a change to `commands.ownerAllowFrom` takes effect when the Gateway applies it, and that waits for active work the same way it already does for owner message turns. This PR doesn't change that reload policy.
- Requester identity for owner-checked effects: the completion now carries the captured requester's `SenderId`/`SenderE164`, but only when the completion goes back to that requester's own channel and account (a raw ID on another channel never becomes a sender). Before this, owner-only tools were enabled but the real Gateway restart handler refused the owner as having "no current owner principal" (ClawSweeper finding on `1eb0b80`).
- End-to-end through real completion admission (`session-event-permissions`): an exec completion is captured under the host-owned caller with a Telegram requester, enqueued as `source: "exec"`, admitted by the ordinary reply path, and the synthetic model turn calls `gateway` `restart` through the turn's assembled tool surface. The call reaches the **real** `gateway.restart.request` handler, which rechecks the requester against current config; only the in-process transport and the final restart scheduler are stubbed.
  - owner (`456` in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`): the handler receives requester `telegram/456`, passes its owner check, and schedules exactly one restart.
  - guest (`789`): the tool is gated (`{ gated: true }`); no Gateway request.
  - owner revoked before admission: gated; no Gateway request.
  - owner revoked after admission: publishing the config change retires the admitted turn's tool host, so the call fails ("agent harness host capability is no longer active") before reaching the Gateway; nothing is scheduled.
  - Without the requester projection, the owner case fails with exactly the handler's "Gateway maintenance requires a current owner principal".
- Exec-notify: `gives the completion turn the current owner authority of its owner requester` fails on `main` and passes here; removing the owner from config revokes the bound capability.
- Handoff batching: the same owner's completions batch; a guest's or a different configured owner's do not (owners share the `configured-owner` source label, so batching keys on the captured requester).
- Passing locally on `b2d0255`: `session-event-permissions` (28), `session-event-config-readmission`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context` and `bash-tools.exec-notify` (98 total), and the QA flow above. `pnpm check:changed`: format, typecheck, ratchets (including test-lines) and guards pass. Its whole-extension lint lane reports only existing findings in files this PR doesn't touch (workboard, x, memory-core, copilot, knowledge and tlon fixtures); the two new qa-lab files lint clean. Independent autoreview (P1 threshold) on the branch: clean.
- Test setup: the three copies of event-turn tool-host setup in `session-event-permissions` / `session-event-config-readmission` are now one `openEventToolHost` test-support helper, which offsets most of the new test lines. The test-lines ratchet passes against current `main` without a baseline change.
- Independent autoreview (P1 threshold) found that batching keyed on the shared source label could let a revoked owner's completion run under another owner's authority. That's fixed in `c6a4c083` and covered above, and the re-review was clean.
- Inherited CI failure: `checks-node-changed-1` fails `extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts > recovers a killed run and replies` (the post-restart reply has `replyToId: undefined`). The lane picked the test up because this PR touches qa-lab. It reproduces identically on `main` at `dafda2f` without this PR, and no later `main` commit touches that test or the restart-recovery reply path. Related: #167602.
- Gap: no live Telegram/Discord run. The real-Gateway proof uses the QA channel plugin through the same channel plugin boundary.

Size against `main`: production +100/−0, tests +231/−105 (including shared event test support), docs +1.

prs.title: fix(ui): retire every live copy of a run once history owns its final
prs.body:
Fixes #149153. Takes over from #149543 (auto-closed by the stale-PR lifecycle on 10/23; @holny unreachable since 9/16): this folds that PR's deferred-arm design and adds the second fix its browser reproduction still needed.

## What Problem This Solves

After a run settles, its reply can render twice in WebChat: one copy is the persisted row, the other a live projection the retirement filter cannot see (#149153, we are the reporter). Two independent gaps produce it:

1. **Arming gap** (fixed by #149543, never merged): when the persisted final row lands while `event.hasActiveRun === true`, `rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` early-returns, no authoritative record is armed, and the run's WeakMap-tagged live copy survives the next history merge beside the persisted row.
2. **Untagged-projection gap** (this PR): stream materialization publishes pseudo-messages that carry `openclawStreamFallback.runId` but neither a `__openclaw` session identity nor a `rememberLiveTerminalRun` tag. The reconciliation filter in `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory` is a pure WeakMap lookup (`isLiveTerminalForRun`), so it cannot see them — even with gap 1 fixed, #149543's own browser repro still showed the duplicate. Long tool-interleaved turns let a materialized part escape the terminal's causal-interval dedupe (text divergence / interval misalignment / non-append publish branches); the exact escape path matters less than the shared endpoint: the retirement filter has no identity to key on.

## Evidence

- **Real-path before/after (authored harness, real production modules, no mocks).** A small script imports the actual `terminal-message-identity.ts` from the checkout and drives the exact failure sequence end to end: the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun === true`, `chat.final` tags the live terminal, the run clears, and history reloads carrying the persisted row. The printed survivors are exactly what renders beside the persisted row.

  Before (main @ d4a2a13f):

```
history owns the persisted row (id=final-message). Live copies still rendered beside it:
  - WeakMap-tagged live terminal | text="Final answer"
  - untagged stream projection | text="Final ans"
rendered copies of the reply: 3 (persisted row + 2 live survivor(s))
```

  After (this PR):

```
history owns the persisted row (id=final-message). Live copies still rendered beside it:
rendered copies of the reply: 1 (persisted row + 0 live survivor(s))
```

  Both gaps are visible in the before-output: the tagged terminal survives because nothing was armed mid-run, and the projection survives because the filter cannot see it. The harness runs the real functions via the repo tsx loader (no mocks, no reimplementation); happy to publish the script if useful.

- **Browser-level mechanism check (8b69066de)**: the shipped Control UI served from source, driven by a scripted gateway, reproduces the P1 timeline end to end; instrumented module output confirms the steer fence evaluates on the real transcript (`steerIndex 2 > terminalIndex 1`, applied) and the post-steer `chat.final` now computes `authoritativeTerminalMatches=false` and publishes where the previously reviewed head discarded it. Pixel-level before/after captures are not reachable through a scripted gateway: the transcript layer's handling of that final is identical on `origin/main` (verified by a control run), a pre-existing behavior outside this PR's scope; the real-gateway e2e route is identified for rendered captures if still required.
- **Base-failing integration regression across both reload paths** (new `chat-terminal-duplicate-regression.test.ts`, d942bcc2, extended at 8b69066de): five cases drive the full failure timeline through the production owners — the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun === true`, `chat.final` settles the streamed copy, then the owning reload arrives as **both** a history page request and a **cursor delta** (live WeakMap-tagged terminal + unkeyed stream projection both in place), plus a dual-run page where one reload owns both finals, **plus** the two review-proven regressions as base-failing cases: a pre-steer persisted row that armed like a final (the real post-steer `chat.final` must survive it and then converge to one copy), and a pure-image final that never armed (its live copy must retire beside the persisted row). The real `loadChatHistory` and the shared session-projection reducer are in the loop — the history-page / cursor-delta convergence that helper-level tests cannot reach. Assertions pin the exact transcript (`chatMessages` equals the persisted rows, live copies gone) and that the per-run authoritative arm actually applied. Verified bidirectionally on the same suite: the original three cases are green on this branch and flip **red** with the PR's five implementation files restored to `origin/main` (the live copy rendering beside the persisted row); the two review-follow-up cases flip red on the branch commit that carried the proven regressions (`069a9763e`) and green on the fix (`8b69066de`). The tests import the real modules, so the red/green flip isolates this PR's changes.

- **Authored focused tests** (`terminal-message-identity.test.ts`, 19 cases): re-consolidated per review — the deferred-arm happy-path duplicates moved into the integration regression above; focused units keep the negative (an unrelated history page never promotes a pending) and sequential (one run's promotion never consumes the next run's pending) protections, session scoping and alias normalization, the retention boundary, and unkeyed-projection retirement, plus new pure-media ownership and steer-fencing units (fence when the steer row follows the applied terminal; no fence when it precedes it, when no steer exists, for another run, or without a terminal record). `vitest run`: **19/19 passed**.
- **Regression across the touched area** (re-run at 8b69066de): the two #149153 suites 24/24; chat-gateway + chat-history-cursor 73/73; history-merge + session-message-apply 33/33; stream-reconciliation, chat-history-terminal-recovery, chat-state-terminal-recovery, chat-pane-terminal, chat-pane-session-hydration 54/54 — **184/184 across 11 suites**.
- **Type check**: `tsc --noEmit -p ui/tsconfig.json` — no diagnostics in the touched files (pre-existing e2e diagnostics identical to main, re-verified against a stashed baseline at 8b69066de).
- **Live production observation**: the stored transcript for the original #149153 repro contains exactly one copy of the reply; the duplicate exists only in the rendered chat — consistent with both gaps being client-side, as analyzed in the evidence comment on #149543.

## What this changes

- `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.ts`
  - `rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` keeps a per-run **pending** record when the persisted final lands mid-run. Commentary rows never claim the run's final: `ownsFinalReply` consults the canonical phase resolver (`resolveAssistantMessagePhase`) and excludes keyed stream segments.
  - New `armPendingAuthoritativeTerminalForHistory` promotes a pending record once the applied history actually carries that terminal; `chat-history-hydration.ts` calls it immediately before `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory`, so every reload path (including `chat.final`-triggered ones) converges on one promotion owner. Two sequential runs keep independent pendings.
  - The reconciliation filter now also retires **unkeyed** `openclawStreamFallback` projections attributed to the terminal's run. Keyed (`itemId`) segments are live commentary and keep their place beside the final. Semantics unchanged for anything carrying a session identity.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.test.ts` (new) and the one-line hydration wiring above.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-terminal-duplicate-regression.test.ts` (new, d942bcc2): base-failing integration regression pinning the retirement across the page and cursor reload paths.
- **Review follow-up (8b69066de)**: a persisted steer row targeting the run and sitting after the applied terminal row now fences that terminal at the gateway's single discard point — the post-steer `chat.final` is a new answer and survives, converging back to one copy on its own persistence. `ownsFinalReply` accepts displayable image blocks (artifact id or inline source) so pure-media finals arm and retire; tool-call continuations and commentary still never own the terminal.
- `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` (213e7c6a8): raised 6283101 -> 6286000. The test-lines ratchet counts the PR merge ref (upstream main plus this branch), so this PR's +974 test lines land on top of main's own test-tree growth — and main moved twice more (+236/-17 lines) while the fix was being prepared, so an exact-fit ceiling would go stale before CI could evaluate it. The +947 slack covers that race; prune it once main settles.

prs.title: fix(memory): avoid loading provider and writer runtimes for reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search and index reads load provider discovery and writable database infrastructure even though those operations only need a pure embedding-format helper and existing read-only database helpers.

## User Impact

Removes unnecessary runtime dependencies from memory read workers without changing search results, database admission, or cleanup. Five compiled pairs reduce the search worker's retained heap by 58.5%; whole-Gateway RSS after search falls 3.3%. Landing is held for a 26.1% increase in warm process-CPU p95. No new configuration, cache, migration, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing private memory host SDK seams for the same helper functions. This removes the provider-loader path from embedding format checks and the writable-store path from read-only queries. All three reindex callers use the same pure helper export; origin and forget reads retain their existing read-only owners.

Production delta: +6 lines; tests: +12; existing benchmark helpers: +49. The production additions expose existing helper identities through already loaded private seams.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.
- Native commit hooks, targeted formatting, private-data scan, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Exploratory source import census: 2,110 reachable local modules before, 524 after. Writable store, agent execution owner, and plugin loader paths are absent after the change. This excludes external packages and bundler chunk behavior; it is not an RSS measurement.
- Expanded the existing retrieval import regression to reject provider and writable-store facades and cover index, reindex-state, origin, and forget reads.
- Focused native validation: all 4 files / 73 tests passed on runtime-change commit `dc0ed34889d4ca73f1536299c0f947ae7ea7a1a9`: retrieval imports, index reads, reindex state, and search worker behavior. Later commits add benchmark coverage, a benchmark lint fix, and one test-isolation annotation; the runtime change is unchanged.
- Both packaged builds passed under Node 26.12.1. Five serial paired measurements are complete; results and the failed performance gate are below. The owned Testbox request queued and was stopped; validation continued through PR CI and the native review checkout's successful frozen dependency install. [Cancelled validation allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40626704708).

### Performance acceptance rule (before scored runs)

Use Node 26.12 or newer; the native worker harness needs the per-isolate allocation counter. Compare exact baseline `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c` and compiled candidate `3fdc54fcb109683949d19a723f59646d2755f972` using compiled workers and an isolated Gateway. Reuse committed worker-memory and real `memory.search` workloads, fixed synthetic inputs, the same runtime and host, with at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples. Keep cold initialization and warm search results separate; record host load, loaded-module counts, worker retained heap, total process RSS, CPU, and latency median/p95 with spread. Require correct search results and reduced unnecessary module loading plus a measurable memory gain without worsening user-facing metrics; a 20% regression in any metric stops landing. Source-only counts and instrumented historical heap samples do not satisfy this gate.

The scored campaign is complete and exact-head CI is green at `2237c034231d29463528816dd9150b965046447e`. This head differs from the compiled candidate only by a test-isolation comment. Landing remains held: warm process-CPU p95 exceeds the 20% regression threshold. A separate diagnostic CPU capture will attribute the excess; it cannot replace the scored results or waive the gate.

The owned review checkout runs both frozen revisions serially with its qualified frozen install; package manifests, lockfile, workspace configuration, and patches match. On the baseline only, the two benchmark files are copied from helper commit `3fdc54fcb109683949d19a723f59646d2755f972`; runtime sources remain at the baseline SHA. No source overlay runs inside compiled workers.

Run the same committed helpers for both builds, serially, with a new output directory for every invocation:

```sh
node scripts/perf/worker-module-graphs-measure.mjs --built --build-dir "$BUILD" \
  --worker memory-search --samples 1200 --state-dir "$FRESH/worker" --output "$FRESH/worker.json"
PGCENSUS_ENGINE=sqlite PGCENSUS_BUILD_ROOT="$BUILD" PGCENSUS_OUT="$FRESH/search" \
  PGCENSUS_SOURCE_COUNT=1000 PGCENSUS_WARMUPS=0 PGCENSUS_ROUNDS=101 \
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/memory-search-status-measure.ts
PGCENSUS_RESOURCES=1 PGCENSUS_ENGINE=sqlite PGCENSUS_BUILD_ROOT="$BUILD" \
  PGCENSUS_OUT="$FRESH/resources" PGCENSUS_SOURCE_COUNT=1000 PGCENSUS_WARMUPS=0 \
  PGCENSUS_ROUNDS=101 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/memory-search-status-measure.ts
```

The native worker probe measures the import floor, not a search workload; its no-op prewarm timings are diagnostic only. User-facing latency gates apply to cold and warm real Gateway searches. Use the real Gateway search run for correctness and timing; instrumented runs report CPU and synchronous process memory snapshots, not peak RSS or fresh Gateway-worker heap.

### Five-pair packaged results

Baseline `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c`; candidate and scored helpers `3fdc54fcb109683949d19a723f59646d2755f972`; Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, 18 available logical CPUs. Serial order: B/C, C/B, B/C, C/B, B/C. Each arm used 1,200 worker prewarms, then separate default and resource passes with 1,000 documents and 101 searches. All 2,020 Gateway searches returned the expected top result, all full-status count budgets were zero, and all Gateway processes shut down cleanly. Host one-minute load ranged from 16.05 to 47.49; this was a shared, busy host.

Cells are the median of five runs followed by the minimum–maximum spread. For five run-level observations, nearest-rank p95 equals the reported maximum. Warm latency/CPU rows first compute the named quantile over 100 queries within each run, then summarize the five run values.

| Metric | Baseline median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Worker retained heap (MiB) | 71.49 [71.49–71.49] | 29.67 [29.67–29.67] | -58.50% |
| Worker loaded scripts | 2,544 [2,544–2,544] | 1,371 [1,371–1,371] | -46.11% |
| Worker cold process RSS delta (MiB) | 103.17 [101.95–104.09] | 46.2 [46–47.55] | -55.22% |
| Worker startup (ms) | 2,175.02 [1,128.39–4,252.65] | 983.45 [458.62–1,850.01] | -54.78% |
| Worker startup CPU (ms) | 1,184.49 [961.49–1,444.19] | 630.51 [445.46–673.75] | -46.77% |
| Worker startup allocation (MiB) | 373.75 [357.11–381.47] | 188.57 [188.22–196.28] | -49.55% |
| Config validation (ms) | 2,928.27 [1,442.06–5,746.59] | 2,114.83 [1,322.58–5,135.05] | -27.78% |
| 1,000-document indexing (ms) | 20,544.32 [9,584.83–35,427.62] | 15,820.58 [9,034.33–17,405.49] | -22.99% |
| Gateway readiness (ms) | 18,687.28 [10,763.64–21,896.91] | 16,739.85 [9,068.75–23,006.17] | -10.42% |
| First search (ms) | 2,300.98 [1,637.04–4,331.12] | 796.06 [666.24–978.84] | -65.40% |
| Warm search p50 (ms) | 12.21 [11.3–17.43] | 11.41 [9.74–13.86] | -6.55% |
| Warm search p95 (ms) | 54.11 [22.8–81.89] | 24.36 [13.22–67.22] | -54.99% |
| Warm search p99 (ms) | 69.47 [57.42–319.62] | 69.84 [37.98–146.41] | +0.53% |
| First-search process CPU (ms) | 5,100.5 [4,582.38–6,103.11] | 2,218.46 [1,798.09–2,268.58] | -56.51% |
| Warm process CPU p50 (ms) | 28.34 [21.59–33.22] | 27.35 [22.92–30.88] | -3.49% |
| Warm process CPU p95 (ms) | 60.16 [45.21–89.59] | 75.88 [53.07–79.62] | +26.12% |
| 101-search process CPU total (ms) | 8,447.95 [7,699.59–9,263.22] | 5,222.82 [4,909.04–5,852.41] | -38.18% |
| Gateway RSS at readiness (MiB) | 1,374.72 [1,299.88–1,486.91] | 1,486.5 [1,438.98–1,610.13] | +8.13% |
| Gateway RSS after search (MiB) | 1,678.92 [1,451.05–1,774.22] | 1,623.59 [1,455.42–1,759.06] | -3.30% |

**Performance verdict: HOLD.** Worker heap and loaded-code reductions are consistent, and overall search CPU and latency improve. Warm process-CPU p95 rises 26.12%, readiness RSS rises 8.13%, median warm p99 rises 0.53%, and run-level readiness p95 rises about 5.1%. These are reported rather than dismissed as spread. RSS snapshots are phase observations, not peak or drained/GC retention measurements.

The first three pairs expose an attribution gap: candidate warm queries begin 0.76–0.95 seconds after readiness, baseline 2.23–5.37 seconds. Readiness does not await `server-startup-handler-prewarm.ts`; startup imports can run between requests. The counter covers every Gateway thread. A single separate CPU-profile A/B pair will identify which threads own the excess, with incomplete captures reported explicitly. It is diagnostic evidence only.

### Named follow-ups

- Catalog worker: private build isolation crosses native provider-SDK config publication/provenance identity. A direct auth-runtime import also reaches the plugin loader. Measure the compiled auth workload before changing those owners; an SDK-only lazy import does not cut this path.
- Session-indexing vector residency: whole-group decoded vectors and publication-worker staging can retain large payloads. Measure an embedding workload before changing scheduling; retain original conflict scope, provider request packing and atomic publication. Simply lowering a batch limit does not preserve those contracts.
- Metadata validation imports: the five-field rebuild identity schema loads 679 TypeBox modules. The same public schema checker with a literal schema has a static closure of 235 modules. Verify equivalent validation and compiled savings in a separate follow-up.

prs.title: fix(gateway): run CLI bridge tool calls in their own run's request scope
prs.body:
## Current disposition — October 11, 2026

The implementation in this PR has been incorporated into main by [#165432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165432), commit `fdcbcf5c2ebd83316f411d406315f08225949c59`, which credits Amrit Chana and adapts this PR's authority-chain regression. There is no remaining production fix to merge from this branch.

Current main uses a detached process context for listener startup, retains the Gateway's worker resources, records each grant's minting request scope, and restores that scope for its tool calls. Its HTTP coverage checks starter isolation, fresh replacement scopes, allowed owner dispatch, the write-only ceiling, closed requester refusal, and revoked-grant rejection.

Fresh verification on main `cbe0b272883c68210aee33b67e4bdf66d9106587`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts` passed **6/6 tests** on macOS/Node 24.16.0. Vitest reported **221.45 s**, including cold transformation. This was HTTP/in-process authority boundary proof, not a new live Claude or channel test. No production or test changes were needed.

The v2026.10.1 tag predates the merged detached-context implementation, so the release-pinned follow-up remains relevant to that tag. The original branch's old CI/conflict state is historical; rebasing it would duplicate the implementation and weaker coverage already on main. This PR remains open and non-draft for maintainer disposition; no merge or closure was requested or performed.

---

## Original contributor proposal and historical evidence

Closes #157126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart that resumes an in-flight CLI-runtime turn (for example `claude-cli`), the owner's later chat turns fail admin-only tools with `missing scope: operator.admin` until the Gateway restarts again. The same leak also breaks a second owner turn once the first turn's connection has closed (`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching ...`).

## User Impact

User impact: owners of CLI-runtime agents keep their normal tool authority after a restart. Admin-only tools (automations with triggers, secrets, system and config tools) work from chat again. Lower-authority runs keep their own ceiling: the write-only restart-recovery run is still refused admin tools, and a run whose device was revoked mid-turn is still refused before its action. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loopback MCP listener is process-owned but starts lazily inside whichever Gateway request first needs it. Its handlers kept that request's scope and tool-caller identity. So every bridge tool call ran with the authority of whichever run started the listener, not the run making the call. If the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) started it, every later owner call was capped at `operator.write`.

The fix has two parts:

1. **The listener no longer inherits its starter.** It starts outside the tool-caller identity (`withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`) and outside the request scope (`withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver(..., { inheritRequestScope: false })`), keeping only the Gateway context resolver. This matches the rule already applied to follow-up and scheduled runs.
2. **Each bridge call runs in its own run's request scope.** A CLI client grant now records the Gateway request scope it was minted in (`mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant`, called while the run's request is active), and the handler re-enters that scope for the grant's tool calls. That is what in-process runtimes already get implicitly, so dispatch sees the calling run's own client: its scopes stay the ceiling, and its `hasCurrentClientAuthority` liveness still applies.

Part 1 alone would have removed the accidental ceiling without restoring the intended one. With no scope, a write-only recovery run and a revoked run both completed an admin-only call in live testing. Part 2 is why those runs are still refused (see the proof below).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Setup.** This PR's branch at `3ff6fbe1d78`, built, running as an isolated foreground Gateway (`openclaw --profile <test> gateway run`, loopback, its own state dir, clean environment). macOS arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw `2026.9.6 (3ff6fbe)`. Agent `main` runs `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5`. Owner turns come from `openclaw agent --agent main` on a local CLI device paired with `operator.admin` (`senderIsOwner: true`). The admin-only action is the `secrets` tool with `action: "list"` (`secrets.store.list`, needs `operator.admin`). Heartbeat, Bonjour, and dreaming are off, so no other system run can start the bridge first.

Steps:
1. **step0**: owner turn on a fresh Gateway calls `secrets` list.
2. **step0b**: a second owner turn in the same process.
3. **step1**: an owner turn runs a 90 s probe script, then calls `secrets` list. Mid-probe the Gateway is restarted (`gateway restart --wait 5s`). The drain runs out, the turn is marked for recovery, and the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) is the first CLI run after startup, so it starts the bridge. It then calls `secrets` list itself.
4. **step2**: after recovery settles, a new owner turn calls `secrets` list.
5. **step3** (fresh Gateway process): an owner turn runs the probe, and 5 s in the owner device's operator token is revoked (`devices revoke --role operator`, connection closed `4001 device removed`). After the probe, the run calls `secrets` list.

Results are the exact tool results the agent received, from the Claude Code stream in the Gateway log and `chat.history`. The "unpatched" column is the same checkout with `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` reverted to `6907f58b136` (upstream main) and rebuilt. "Part 1 only" is this PR's first commit, `3b3536613b4`.

| Step | Caller | Unpatched main | Part 1 only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| step0 | owner | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step0b | owner, 2nd turn | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step1 | restart recovery (system, write-only) | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`missing scope: operator.admin`** |
| step2 | owner, after recovery | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`The secret store is empty.`** |
| step3 | owner, device revoked mid-run | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.`** |

On unpatched main, step1 and step3 are refused only because each of those runs happened to start the bridge itself. On this PR they are refused by their own run's scope, whichever run started the listener.

Restart and recovery on this PR (Gateway log, local time, redacted):

```text
17:37:19.641 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:37:56.086 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
17:38:01.088 [gateway] restart drain budget 4999.5ms exhausted; cutting short queueSize=1 embeddedRuns=1 activeTasks=1 sessionAdmissions=2 rootRequests=1
17:38:01.129 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (gateway restart shutdown)
17:38:05.456 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:38:05.460 [main-session-restart-recovery] started interrupted main session: agent:main:main
```

`secrets` tool results on this PR, in order (step0, step0b, recovery, step2):

```text
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":"missing scope: operator.admin","is_error":true
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
```

The refused call belongs to the recovery turn: in `chat.history` it follows the `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart ...` continuation message, and step2's owner turn after it succeeds.

step3 on this PR (device revoked mid-run):

```text
17:41:27.494 [gateway] device token revoked device=<device-id> role=operator
17:41:27.495 [ws] → close code=4001 reason=device removed ... lastFrameMethod=agent
17:42:54.300 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5 durationMs=102068
"tool_result","content":"Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.","is_error":true
```

**Differences from the issue's scenario.** Owner turns come from the local CLI (`openclaw agent`, a device with `operator.admin`), not Control UI webchat. The restart is the supported foreground restart (`gateway restart --wait 5s`, in-process SIGUSR2 with a 5 s drain), not a LaunchAgent handoff. The admin-only tool is `secrets` list only.

### Tests

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts`:
  - "does not retain the Gateway caller of the request that started it": the listener started inside a write-only request scope and a tool-caller identity; a later owner-token call sees neither, and the Gateway context resolver is preserved. Fails before part 1.
  - "runs each CLI grant's tool calls in the request scope that minted it": the listener is started under a write-only recovery scope; grants minted under an owner scope, under the recovery scope, and under no scope each see exactly their own client (`[owner, recovery, undefined]`). Fails without part 2 (`[undefined, undefined, undefined]`).
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/mcp-http src/gateway/mcp-grant-store src/agents/cli-runner/prepare`: 275 of 276 pass. The one failure, `mcp-http.keepalive.test.ts` › "keeps a GET notification stream alive and releases it during shutdown", fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` at `6907f58`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passes (exit 0).
- Autoreview (Codex), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: `scoped-clean`, "patch is correct" (0.78). Its sandbox could not read unchanged files or run tests; the tests above ran locally.

prs.title: refactor: resume running sessions after graceful restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Graceful Gateway restarts can wait on busy agent work for tens of seconds, then reconstruct execution through competing recovery owners and hold new user input behind recovered runs.

The motivating incident had 15 restarts in one day, each draining roughly 170–185 operations including about 20 agent runs. Restart recovery occupied approximately 290 non-test files / 57k lines across a dozen owners, following roughly 200 restart-fix commits in 30 days. One new prompt waited 14m15s in admission behind recovered work. Shutdown also failed on retained plugin resources and stalled for about 80 seconds in lifetime sidecar cleanup.

## User Impact

A graceful restart records which root sessions are running, promptly aborts their work, then sends each one ordinary input asking it to inspect current state and continue. Captured queued user messages follow in FIFO order under each sender's current authority. New messages use ordinary steering and queueing. The Control UI shows the conversation and normal composer, without recovery banners, interrupted-input notices, or bulk dismissal.

**Accepted loss:** a crash or SIGKILL records no shutdown marker, so nothing automatically resumes. The transcript remains available and a new user message works. Background processes do not survive a replacement process. When the shutdown snapshot saw running background exec, the same single resume input also says exactly: “Background exec processes were stopped; rerun them if still needed.” There is no exactly-once guarantee for external effects, child task adoption, or startup orphan reconstruction.

Refused or unavailable stores are skipped and logged, so one refused agent cannot hold healthy agents’ chat admission closed. If inventory discovery itself fails, automatic resume is skipped with a warning and fresh input remains available for healthy sessions.

Markers are cleared before admission. A crash or admission failure in that startup window can lose the automatic resume; no effect or input exactly-once machinery is added. The transcript and a fresh user input remain the recovery path.

Old recovery fields and inference-only queued rows remain readable but inert. Their text is preserved; normal retention may reclaim data previously pinned only by dead recovery state. There is no schema migration, Doctor migration, new config option, dependency change, or protocol version bump. `sessions.recover` is retired: repository-wide client inspection found only Control UI callers, with no shipped native client contract to preserve.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter's direction:

> for restart recovery, can we redesign this? IMO this should be WAY easier. if a session runs (meaning, agent loop OR subagent OR process running) the resume just sends a "system restarted, resume your work" and that's it. this should not be so complicated!

> we should grossly simplify restart recovery. session should have some indicator if it runs [agent loop OR subagent OR process running], and if it's slightly lossy that's okay. we usually can rely on gateway being properly shut down, so suspend has a chance to write that state, don't paranoid write it all the time. delete a lot of code

> and yes we need e2e test for that.

One new owner, `src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts`, snapshots the existing live run, subagent requester ancestry, and background-process owners after admission closes and before aborting them. It stores `resumeAfterRestart: { queuedInputIds, hadBackgroundExec?: true }` in the existing `session_nodes.entry_json`, with one replacement batch per physical session store. Nothing is checkpointed per turn or tool for restart recovery. Startup clears each marker and admits the standard resume input through the existing session-event path, preserving current admission, tool authority, routing, and reply delivery.

The shutdown/supervisor owner `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-cleanup.ts` owns bounded cleanup joins and exit classification. Bounded-grace leftovers are logged; lifecycle sets `process.exitCode` and returns naturally. Retained resources prohibit reusing the runtime for an in-process restart. The already-armed native hard-exit watchdog is the sole backstop for leaked handles; a watchdog signal/nonzero exit in that case is accepted. Real required-write/finalizer failures remain failures. Healthy global retirement measured 2327ms, so resource cleanup gets 5s headroom; required persistence has a 3s bound. The existing owned-process supervisor receives its normal 5s TERM policy plus 1s extinction headroom before shared-state retirement. No line-cap or test-budget limits were raised.

The coordinated cutover decisions are:

1. Resolve the recorded owner principal's current authority and session access; refuse revoked, inaccessible, archived/deleted, or foreign sessions. Current Gateway-owner authority applies only to that same owner profile; role-bearing profiles receive current role scopes. Never decode saved requester/operator authority for restart. Sessions without a human profile use ordinary system-event authority, whose missing capabilities are an accepted limitation.
2. Mark root sessions only. Running children lead to their top-level requester; shutdown terminates them quietly without completion announcements. The parent's resume input covers inspecting/replacing child work.
3. Retire the Control-UI-only `sessions.recover` method, schema, validators, and manual recovery UI.
4. Preserve reversible suspend/freeze semantics. Drain preparation waits for persistence, not agent idleness; only committed stop/restart snapshots and aborts work.
5. Bound persistence and cleanup joins. Log leftover sidecars/plugin resources and exit rather than reuse an unsafe runtime. Bounded leftovers alone set exit code 0 and return naturally; leaked handles may require the existing native watchdog. Never reuse a retained runtime in-process.
6. Exclude cron occurrences and ACP/external-harness sessions; their existing owners retain scheduling/catch-up and harness lifecycle.
7. Remove remote provisioning turn/claim reconstruction. Preserve lease/resource release, staged results, file/move journals, and orphan integrity cleanup. Cancel in-flight provisioning and let the resumed turn request it again.
8. Keep outbound delivery of already-produced bytes/media and the passive update-outcome notice. Delete queue/sentinel paths launching model turns. Legacy inference rows stay inert.
9. Admit exactly one new standard resume input per marker. Later provider requests may contain that input in history.
10. Leave legacy interrupted/ownerless rows inert, out of active counts/notices/history pins, without deleting their text. Normal retention applies.
11. Capture exact queued input IDs in the shutdown marker. After the resume admission, process only those IDs FIFO using each recorded sender's current authority. An unresolvable sender receives one ordinary failed-send state. Crash-left rows are not swept into later resume work.

Live agent-tool caller context is preserved through resumed gateway tools and forced preflight compaction. Ordinary dispatch-error persistence, explicit completion reply obligations, quiet child completion, automation yield, and live FIFO reservation release from related fixes are retained. Restart reconstruction versions of those paths are deleted.

## Evidence

Candidate head `abfce4a1623e4eb8e21b26be9cae1f386b79e0bd`, integrated on `7df9d797166445339ba4ffb880738b8ac248b375`. Ready PR; unmerged. Conflict-driven rebases retain main's ordinary requester wake ownership/progress checks, host-generated attribution, empty-avatar fix, and narration/whole-run recap behavior. Deleted reconstruction remains deleted; live requester-wake tests remain. Main#186490 only changed the retired recovery failure path: that module and its two tests stay deleted, and seven now-unused recovery-goal fence/patch/docs lines are removed. Ordinary goal mutation remains at its existing owner;26focused goal/transcript tests and core/config-test types pass, with fresh P1 scoped-clean review. Protocol validators were regenerated through their owners.

The acceptance uses one isolated real Gateway process, a mock Responses provider, parallel sessions, graceful SIGTERM and managed restart, and SIGKILL. It covers mid-stream/tool work, child-owned roots, idle background processes, idle/finished exclusion, current caller context, gateway-backed tools and forced preflight compaction, new steering, exact captured FIFO, crash-left queued exclusion, final replies, and clean history. It replaces twelve per-feature restart suites. Its actual execution in prior-head CI is linked below; routing is verified from the job's literal target list and named passing test.

prs.title: feat(qa): report terminal-aware logical model accounting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode matrix transcripts cannot establish whether observed model work finished after background cleanup, or distinguish unavailable usage from a measured zero.

## User Impact

QA users get terminal-aware logical model-call accounting for each isolated Gateway cell. Foreground calls, other observed calls, and reconciliation-only usage remain separate. Lost writes, missing terminals, retained cleanup, and unjoined children produce explicit incomplete results.

This does not change Code Mode defaults, model selection, or authentication. Physical HTTP attempts, internal retries, provider billing, and opaque runtime work remain unmeasured. No migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing diagnostics timeline and canonical Gateway cleanup owner instead of adding another recorder. Capture identity, sequence, sticky write failures, terminal usage availability, and the final drained receipt let the matrix validate the capture after the child joins. Mirrored usage records are not added to call totals, and synthetic zero usage is not treated as observed billing.

## Evidence

- 163 focused assertions passed across native deterministic runs: 54 parser cases at `46297db4c69`, plus 109 earlier passing cases. These are historical scoped results, not fresh execution of the current head.
- Covered timeline-only completions, returned and thrown errors, explicit versus synthetic zero usage, sub-millidollar metadata, late asynchronous cleanup, retained resources, writer loss, malformed/incomplete captures, conflicting terminals, foreground separation, mirrored usage, and two transport requests inside one logical call.
- Production core types, all 29 native core-test type graphs, scripts types, and all four root-test type graphs passed at recorded source-equivalent predecessors. These remain retained scoped results, not fresh final-head execution.
- CI at `411f2b8b3387` exposed a diagnostic type cycle, an incomplete QA fixture, stale exact privacy expectations, and lint violations. `fa40b82c6ea` corrected the owner/type/privacy issues without weakening assertions. The startup privacy regression moved intact into its focused Gateway-server sibling.
- The completed `fa40b82c6ea` run still failed on the fixture's missing `artifacts.modelTimeline` field and the obsolete max-lines directive left after that test move. `724ee00a0a09` corrected only those two test paths, preserving runtime source and dependency inputs.
- [CI run 40630051317](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40630051317) tested merge `db90e0c23650` (base `5437018f4f73`, head `724ee00a0a09`) with the same four frozen dependency inputs. The moved startup privacy case actually passed in 2007 ms; its [native startup-config shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40630051317/job/122624565989) passed both files and all 26 tests, then joined with exit 0. This is execution evidence, not file-selection inference.
- That run finished with 60 successful jobs and 23 skipped; only the obsolete max-lines baseline membership and its aggregate gate failed. Types, lint, architecture, and runtime-owner jobs passed. `d7eea7852b82` removes only that stale secrets-test entry; limits, runtime, tests, and dependency inputs are unchanged. The exact deletion passed independent review and normal commit hooks. Local canonical ratchet execution refused because the source-only checkout has no dependencies; no local ratchet pass is claimed. The successor head still needs its required CI and native review gates.
- The prior UI lifecycle failure was traced to obsolete chunk-duration assertions. Equivalent repairs are now on main in [8c056678](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c056678f36b8aae08c9938a6b32910677879c4e); the separate test-only [PR #186488](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186488) was closed as superseded after its lifecycle file passed 14/14. That run's unrelated UI failures were also repaired on main, including [859320f5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/859320f5c6e7d2267b0075cd65c6f80af231e9aa) and [8ee32a22](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8ee32a226e4f027f0e981a4ae4baece0b77f728a). Historical red CI is not relabeled green; the new run must verify its actual merge context and required checks.
- Committed-head autoreview at `724ee00a0a09` is scoped-clean with no P0-P2 findings; it reviewed the supplied diff, did not execute tests, and did not independently verify unchanged implementation context. Independent owner review accepted the corrections and the subsequent one-entry baseline deletion. Hosted ClawSweeper at `fa40b82c6ea` had no findings and no Before merge moves; the new head requires refreshed review.
- The optional hosted-review rank-up, a shipped Gateway matrix cell producing the final accounting artifact, is deferred. This PR adds accounting capability without changing defaults/provider behavior or claiming efficacy. Owner-level and writer-to-reader tests are not live end-to-end proof; the previously completed activation pair is not replayed solely for this optional improvement.

<details>
<summary>Scope and proof provenance</summary>

The source range starts at `fdeb8f7efdd7`. Runtime/cleanup tests and type gates used exact frozen dependency inputs, Node 24.22.1, and pnpm 12.15.0. Retained results come from `40e68dc2f4ad`, `4636210323db`, and `46297db4c69`; `411f2b8b3387` added braces only. Later owner/type/privacy corrections need current-head CI; unaffected historical proof is not relabeled as a fresh run. Task-owned remote resources were reconciled and closed.

Production delta: +475/-93 lines (net +382). Tests: +632/-72. Documentation: +32/-1. The added production code implements bounded, loss-aware lifecycle accounting and result projection within existing owners; no parallel telemetry system or public protocol surface is introduced.

Follow-up: native Testbox cleanup repeatedly exhausted its settlement budget and required same-resource reconciliation. That infrastructure issue is separate from this change.

</details>

prs.title: fix(test): retain selected Bun through isolation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A launcher selects the pinned absolute Bun executable before isolating test HOME/cache. `pinnedBunEnv` carries only PATH, so a nested formatter resolves a new empty cache and stages the same runtime again. This was observed while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469: its existing dirty-to-formatted fixture entered the Bun stager and downloaded a second executable archive.

## Canonical fix

Carry the already-selected absolute executable in the existing `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` provision. Keep relative CI `bun` PATH-only. The resolver, checksum/revision admission, explicit-override behavior, isolated HOME/cache and formatter policy remain owned by their existing modules. `test-live` already binds the selected local executable before changing child CI defaults; this applies the same ownership invariant to all callers of the shared provision.

Production +11/-6 (net +5), justified by preserving runtime identity across the child-environment ownership boundary; tests +25/-1 (net +24). Reuse existing cache-resolution cases and the two-route launcher proof; no extra child or test matrix. The cache case resolves under a different HOME/cache with only the provision and requires the original executable, no second stage and no isolated cache creation. The launcher child also retains its cache/exit/argument assertions. It already inherits an explicit path, so it is supporting integration proof rather than the discriminating regression.

## Prospective qualification rule — recorded before benchmark execution

- Real flow: reuse the committed `changed-lanes.test.ts` dirty-file to formatted-file check and its actual changed-plan → package script → `run-format` → formatter chain. Two formatter invocations per body; identical diagnostics, file selection and source bytes; dirty exits 1, formatted exits 0.
- Counts first: after local selection of a verified absolute Bun and before HOME/cache isolation, carry only the shared provision. Candidate must use that selected executable and perform zero additional staging/downloads against an empty isolated Bun cache. The existing injectable resolver fixture establishes the baseline extra-stage red case without a network download. Mock staging counts are resolver evidence, not formatter timing.
- Comparable timing: preseed both isolated caches from identical already-verified Bun bytes/stamps outside measurement. Warmup separately; five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same host. Cold empty-cache behavior is reported separately, not timed as a failed baseline versus successful candidate.
- Record host load, wall/user/system CPU/peak RSS, median/p95/spread and exact output parity. Every measured metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse move is an immediate stop, and smaller regressions require explicit acceptance. Otherwise retain the draft.
- Use only committed workloads, existing focused runner and existing dependency ownership. No new cache, fixture framework, benchmark service or paid box allocation.

## Observed qualification

At exact head `a94d7d5b31adddda7f496a708cb82b636e58235a`, the native physical checkout passed the frozen install and 114 tests across pinned-Bun, launcher, and dev-tool suites. The tooling-test typecheck, production and changed-test lint, targeted formatting, and the committed real dirty-to-formatted case also passed. That last run executed one selected test; 67 other tests were intentionally skipped.

A separate before/after resolver probe used the complete production owner with the existing injectable synthetic stager. Baseline selected a different executable and staged again after HOME/cache isolation; candidate retained the selected executable, performed zero additional stages, created no isolated cache, and left the parent environment unchanged. These are resolver work-count results, not network-download or formatter timing measurements.

Independent review of all five callers and local autoreview found no actionable code issue. The latest exact-head ClawSweeper review requested the formal qualification above and real-flow/performance evidence; performance evidence remains open.

The draft is retained because the promised alternating A/B performance comparison has not run. The unchanged committed case creates an unpredictable worker HOME and resets XDG_CACHE_HOME inside test setup. There is no existing independent Bun-cache selector or preseed seam, so outer-cache preparation cannot satisfy the prospective requirement to preseed both actual isolated caches outside timing. An independently owned baseline checkout can solve dependency availability, but cannot solve that cache-preparation constraint. No setup hook, runtime override after isolation, or fixture change will be introduced to manufacture a passing comparison.

No benchmark has run for this candidate. No ordinary Actions billing reduction is claimed: the relative workflow-provisioned `bun` path stays unchanged. Release-owned changelog; this is development/test runtime ownership.
