prs.title: fix(update): avoid recopying admitted rollback images
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native update rollback capture prepares a private SQLite image to establish the source generation, disposes it, then prepares the same database again for the recovery snapshot. Large database families pay for the extra acquisition and byte comparison while activation is stopped.

## User Impact

This draft carries that exact admitted image into the recovery snapshot within the same capture operation. No schema, configuration, persistent cache, or operator action changes.

**Blocked draft: the predeclared paired performance gate failed.** The repair reduces logical reads, but six timing, CPU, or peak-memory metrics across four cells exceed the 1.05 limit. No metric reaches the 1.20 hard-stop threshold. These results do not qualify promotion; no sample was discarded, no threshold changed, and no unchanged rerun is planned.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generation owner retains one cleanup-owned image per admitted SQLite family. The snapshot owner consumes it after checking its exact identity. The existing inventory/engine admission, final integrity and foreign-key checks, normalized/publication hashes, post-capture generation, and later rollback refusal remain in place.

Retention covers the whole inventory admission interval. Rejected images, failed transfers, and cancellation join cleanup; a failed transfer does not reacquire another image. Ordinary generation readers still dispose their private image.

Production change: +408/-244 (net +164), justified by the explicit image ownership and cleanup transfer. Tests and the committed measurement workload are counted separately. Release-note context: avoid repeated large-database acquisition during native update rollback capture; measured end-to-end benefit is still pending.

## Evidence

Base: `d3184ac52b6a2df26a5dc6e856581f42178f3978`. Draft head: `fdfbe06dfcdf73fc6163373be7edbee23397e2ee`.

- Original regression fails on Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned Bun fork with native copying both auto/off: 6,316,032 observed private-image JavaScript read bytes exceed the 4,211,200 bound for the 2,105,344-byte fixture.
- First candidate passes that unchanged bound and all 18 fresh/retained integrity cases on both engines. Two newly added fixture assertions failed and were corrected. A separate independent source review identified a cleanup-classification gap, corrected with pre-classification and PostgreSQL cleanup-refusal cases. The final committed head now passes all 77 tests in the three changed test files on both Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun (154 passing cases); the native command joined with exit 0 and settled cleanup.
- The counter observes JavaScript comparison/hash reads. It does not measure every native SQLite/copy read or physical device I/O. Auto mode is not evidence that reflink succeeded.
- Fresh autoreview of the complete local candidate at diff `a1448e454cf6b832713c4ae8890c6b59ec6fbcfea0e60143412df800dd3ff21a` completed with no P0–P2 findings (gpt-6.1-sol, medium; execution unavailable in reviewer isolation). Local ClawSweeper was not used because its available runner checkout had unrelated local state; the selected autoreview route remains explicit.
- The final three-file run covers committed WAL, original/stopped/maintenance capture siblings, integrity/foreign-key/catalog corruption, FULL-auto-vacuum normalization, later-write rollback refusal, and cleanup failure. Broader restore/transfer/cancellation and measured staging-resource proof, type/build/CI, and published-driver update acceptance remain pending. The completed paired performance result below is unqualified.
- No live database was copied or changed for this proof, and no service restart or deployment is part of this PR.

### Paired result: unqualified

Exact head/base/harness above; 80 timing processes and 16 separate count processes completed. All 192 sample rows and their source/resource witnesses were retained. The native command exited 0 with settled cleanup; the disposable baseline checkout was removed. The native stdout capture was preserved before successful-run cleanup (102,648 bytes; SHA-256 `063b89d82b2a85bac21e04f864ec1bc8396d0eedb58249a44cb6d22668c66f8c`).

prs.title: fix(extensions): let commands finish when their timeout exceeds the timer limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes extension commands being killed almost immediately when `api.exec` receives a timeout longer than Node's signed 32-bit timer limit.

## User Impact

An extension can give a command a valid long timeout without accidentally turning it into a 1 ms timeout. Ordinary deadlines, explicit cancellation and process-tree cleanup retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The extension execution owner now uses the existing absolute-deadline scheduler with a monotonic clock. The scheduler rearms bounded native timers until the requested deadline, and its cancellation handle is released at both existing completion boundaries. No new timeout policy or timer helper is introduced.

## Evidence

Product head: `17602160cea1d5d95038d855727abeb320e95d35`. RED base: `fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e`. Normal `cliStartup` build; Node 26.12.1, Linux, 2026-10-28.

Real production entry: the built public `plugin-sdk/agent-sessions.js` registers an extension factory; that extension calls its real `api.exec`. The child writes an actual completion file after 150 ms. The SDK host separately checks that file's existence; the collector captures the host's stdout, stderr and exit status. This is a public SDK integration with a real subprocess and filesystem, rather than a claim of running a model or a live external provider.

Collector invocation, identical for base and head:

```sh
node numeric-extension-proof.mjs "$CHECKOUT" "$PHASE"
```

The exercised extension operation is:

```js
await loadExtensionFromFactory(async (api) => {
  const result = await api.exec(process.execPath, [
    "-e",
    'setTimeout(()=>{require("node:fs").writeFileSync(process.argv[1],"completed");process.stdout.write("completed")},150)',
    markerPath,
  ], { timeout: timeoutMs });
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ observed: result, markerExists: fs.existsSync(markerPath) }) + "\n");
}, fixtureDirectory, createEventBus(), createExtensionRuntime());
```

The collector starts a fresh SDK host for each timeout, with a private HOME/state and no production config, and captures the host's separate filesystem check of its child's marker. Actual captured results:

```json
{"version":"RED","timeout":2147488648,"observed":{"stdout":"","stderr":"","code":1,"killed":true},"markerExists":false}
{"version":"GREEN","timeout":2147488648,"observed":{"stdout":"completed","stderr":"","code":0,"killed":false},"markerExists":true}
```

The base also emits `TimeoutOverflowWarning`; head emits no warning. Legal controls on both versions: 3000 ms allows the same child to finish with one marker; 30 ms kills it with zero markers. All three SDK host processes complete normally. Only task-owned children and temporary files are used, with evidence outside the product branch.

Validation: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts src/agents/sessions/exec.real.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20 passed, measured wrapper wall 155.702 s including cold worker compilation. Added real-child cases take 77 ms and 62 ms; existing resistant-descendant cleanup takes 6.046 s. Targeted format, type-aware core lint, core typecheck, normal build and `git diff --check` pass. Direct independent review of this base/head (P0–P2): no actionable findings. The official local autoreview helper was unavailable (401), so the explicitly authorized independent review route was used. Upstream CI has not yet run at initial publication.

Scope: production +9/-4 lines; tests +11/-0. The smallest complete fix reuses `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`; existing signal listeners, cancellation settlement, output limits and process termination remain with their owners. No public SDK shape, config/default, protocol, schema, security-policy or migration change.

Not tested: physically waiting multiple weeks, native Windows/macOS, a model-driven extension workflow or released-package upgrades. This proof demonstrates removal of immediate overflow and retained short-deadline termination; existing scheduler tests cover rearming across the native timer limit.

prs.title: fix(doctor): schema upgrades back up every database twice
prs.body:
Related: #178177
Related: #178346

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` copies every agent database twice during a schema upgrade, even when the upgrade only bumps version metadata.

## User Impact

User impact: schema upgrades in Doctor finish minutes sooner on hosts with large agent databases and write gigabytes fewer backup bytes. Stores the upgrade did not migrate keep the full rollback backup as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor decided whether to take the full heartbeat rollback backup from the schema check made *before* the declared version phase ran. After that phase had already migrated every pending store and kept its own scoped backups, Doctor still treated them as outdated and made a second full, integrity-checked copy of every agent database plus the shared state database.

The decision now counts only stores the version phase did not commit. Refused or unreadable stores, unmigrated stores, and runs where the version phase returned nothing (for example full-image backups) still take the full backup. Heartbeat-specific pending work still forces it as before.

## Evidence

Isolated reproduction (no network, isolated HOME, never live state): a copy of a real install with 15 agent databases (6.8 GB, largest 6.2 GB) rolled back from schema 32 to 31, timed with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `doctor.heartbeat-migration-backups` | 119.3 s | 0.3 s |
| Backup files written | 32 (7.38 GB) | 16 (141 MB) |

prs.title: fix(agents): prevent unknown models after creating secondary agents
prs.body:
Closes #58289

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a secondary agent created through `agents.create` can fail with `Unknown model` when its selected custom model exists only in the configured system agent's `models.json`.

## User Impact

User impact: secondary agents without a local catalog can use the system agent's custom model inventory while retaining their own authentication; existing secondary catalogs remain authoritative, and no secondary `models.json` is created, copied, or overwritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared model runtimes now use the configured system agent's catalog as a read-only fallback only when the secondary agent has no local `models.json`. The fallback participates in runtime identity and worker serialization so startup and on-demand discovery agree.

The inherited catalog is inventory, not credential authority. It is parsed with the same JSONC-compatible parser as `ModelRegistry`; provider API keys plus authorization, cookie, and token-like provider/model headers are removed. Safe route headers are preserved only for the matching provider/model/transport route, and current runtime configuration still wins. Embedded transport now forwards the sanitized headers returned by model resolution, while authentication remains request-scoped to the secondary agent.

## Evidence (October 28 update)

Merge commit `7a0c2366de1fa6cf4bd7924d6158a4a4077c3bd2` integrated upstream main `228596060e33dfcddbb6740416f381daac6f84fe` without rewriting the PR branch. Follow-up commit `b37ba82e91e6fbbc380df339185f905aeeca4bf1` fixes compatibility failures from that merge. Commit `98c5af5729e5839e99a0ecc68289294b9e12cedb` updates the E2E Gateway test harness to supply a recovery owner; the test throws if a real recovery restart is requested. The missing-secondary-catalog issue remained present in upstream source before this merge: prepared runtime capture and scoped catalog loading still read only the secondary agent directory.

The PR preserves a read-only catalog fallback only when the secondary catalog is absent. The secondary agent keeps its own credential authority; inherited provider/model authorization, cookie, token-like headers and API keys remain filtered. The ClawSweeper P2 finding is addressed: request-scoped headers reach the generic custom API stream fallback, while nullable header deletion sentinels are preserved.

Local verification on Node 24.20.0:
- Core production typecheck passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`.
- `embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts`: 27/27 passed.
- `attempt-native-provider-authority.test.ts`: 3/3 passed.
- `prepared-model-catalog-worker.test.ts`: 3/3 passed.
- `stream-resolution.request-headers.test.ts`: 2/2 passed, including custom API fallback.
- Three targeted fallback, local precedence, and credential/header isolation tests in `prepared-model-runtime.sources.test.ts` passed.
- `oxlint` on the six follow-up files, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passed without increasing the baseline.
- The SQLite offline-maintenance lock failure was reproduced on both the PR candidate and clean upstream main `228596060` under the same Node and test command.
- Full Gateway E2E passed locally on the final candidate: 1/1 using `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1` with loopback access. It verifies successful `agents.create`, two secondary-credential requests, and zero further provider requests after both credential stores are cleared. The in-process test Gateway now has a recovery owner that throws if an actual recovery restart is requested. The exact CI base `5437018` has the same relevant Gateway reload and test-helper code; this was a test harness compatibility issue. Root test typecheck was blocked locally by missing Discord workspace dependencies, while hosted checks on the previous head passed.

## Remaining gates

- Evaluate hosted checks on the current head `98c5af5729e5839e99a0ecc68289294b9e12cedb`; previous-head failures are not current-head results.
- Maintainer design and security approval remain required. This contributor update does not supply that approval.

prs.title: fix(macos): iMessage replies stop after app updates until Automation is re-granted
prs.body:
Closes #178719

Related: #186117 reports Automation failures on the iMessage account; this PR keeps the grant across app updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: outbound iMessage stops after an OpenClaw.app update when the Gateway runs as the app-managed background service. Every send fails with AppleScript -1712 until Messages Automation is granted again by hand, while `channels status` stays green.

## User Impact

Automation and Full Disk Access grants given to the background Gateway carry over to later app updates. The first move onto the new path (including Node to Bun) still needs one approval, and when Automation is missing the send error now says which grant and which process to check instead of a bare AppleScript code.

## Why This Change Was Made

`BundledRuntime` keeps owning the runtime layout. App-managed services now pin `<state>/runtime/service/bun`, a clone of the selected build's Bun; the package and SQLite library still load from the concrete build. `matchesBundledRuntime` accepts the stable path only when it is byte-identical to that build's Bun, so the "one matching build" rule from #161709 holds.

- Installs stage the clone with an atomic rename. After a failed install the staged Bun follows the installed service: it stays when the service now runs this build, the previous clone comes back otherwise, and a first clone is never deleted.
- Runtime collection also checks the arguments of a process running the stable Bun, so it never removes a build that process still loads.
- Restoration keeps the retained executable: hosting-change recovery resolves the build from its package entrypoint, and installed-service custody binds the expected command and runtime pin to the executable the service actually runs.
- A paused service updated by the app keeps the stable Bun in its resume command, and Resume stages the new build there first. Operator-pinned runtimes keep their own path.
- iMessage: AppleScript -1712 and -1743 send failures now append guidance naming the Automation grant, the local Gateway runtime path (or the SSH host for remote Messages), and the one-time re-grant after a runtime move. Other errors and `bridge_v2` failures are unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause</summary>

`installArguments` passed `--runtime-path runtime.bun.path` (`<state>/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun`), and each app update reinstalled the service onto the new build's path. tccd attributes the Gateway's Apple events to that path (`responsible_path=…/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun` in the report), so each update created a new TCC client. A `runtime/current` symlink does not help: the kernel records the resolved path (see Evidence).

</details>

## Evidence

### macOS keeps the Automation grant on the path

A self-signed check on macOS 27.0.1 (hardened runtime, production Bun entitlements, test certificate removed afterwards). A LaunchAgent runs `<profile>/runtime/service/bun probe.js`; the probe asks Messages for `count of accounts`, an Apple event that needs Automation and sends nothing.

- Step 1: Bun A on the stable path prompts once; allowed.
- Step 2: Bun B (different bytes, same signing requirement) renamed over the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 3: Bun B re-signed ad hoc (new identifier and cdhash) at the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 4: the step 2 binary, unchanged, at a second profile's path: tccd prompts again and creates a new grant with `identifier_type=Path`.

So the grant is keyed by the executable path: moving the same signed binary to a new path costs a new approval, which is what every update did before this PR. Replacing the binary at a fixed path, signed or ad hoc, keeps it.

<details><summary>Probe output and tccd log</summary>

```

# LaunchAgent ai.openclaw.tcc178719a runs /bin/sh -c 'exec <profile>/runtime/service/bun probe.js', probe asks Messages for 'count of accounts' (Apple event, nothing sent)

## step 1: build A on the stable path, user clicked Allow
## step 2: build B (different bytes, same signing requirement) renamed over the same path, no prompt
{"at":"2026-10-27T22:02:31.275Z","executable":"~/.openclaw-tcc178719a/runtime/service/bun","bunRevision":"807211511f81e0a6639bc9eb41d67120f6b85316","sha256":"d3e4344360be1fa9","osascriptExit":0,"result":"6","error":""}
{"at":"2026-10-27T22:03:32.837Z","executable":"~/.openclaw-tcc178719a/runtime/service/bun","bunRevision":"191755ec115ece3dd642eba3cb0143cecb5e5d7a","sha256":"7407fb87d376ea39","osascriptExit":0,"result":"6","error":""}

## step 3: ad-hoc re-sign of build B (identifier bun-5555..., cdhash 722b8337...) renamed over the same granted path, no prompt, grant still applies
{"at":"2026-10-28T03:24:07.685Z","executable":"~/.openclaw-tcc178719a/runtime/service/bun","bunRevision":"191755ec115ece3dd642eba3cb0143cecb5e5d7a","sha256":"bf323a1e678e8fc8","osascriptExit":0,"result":"6","error":""}
2026-10-28 08:54:07.661 Df tccd[635:12bd08] [com.apple.TCC:access] REQUEST: tccd_uid=501, sender_pid=64614, sender_uid=501, sender_auid=501, function=TCCAccessRequestIndirect, msgID=64614.13
2026-10-28 08:54:07.680 Df tccd[635:12bd08] [com.apple.TCC:access] Platform binary prompting is 'Deny' because: is Platform Binary
2026-10-28 08:54:07.680 Df tccd[635:12bd08] [com.apple.TCC:access] target_executable_path_URL: file://~/.openclaw-tcc178719a/runtime/service/bun

## result: the Automation grant follows the executable path (identifier_type=Path). Moving the same signed binary to a new path re-prompts; replacing the bytes or signature at the same path does not.
```

</details>

### Automation diagnostic through a configured Gateway

Ran this branch's Gateway on an isolated profile and port with the iMessage channel on `imsg` 0.20.0, `sendTransport: "applescript"`, and Messages Automation denied for the launching process. `channels status` stays green, and one send to the reserved, undeliverable `test@example.invalid` fails before dispatch with the new guidance (`disposition: not_started`, nothing sent):

```
# Isolated Gateway from this PR (profile imsgtest, port 29872), iMessage sendTransport=applescript, Messages Automation denied
# Captured output of the two commands below, run once each against that Gateway

$ openclaw channels status
- iMessage default: enabled, configured, running, connected

$ openclaw message send --channel imessage --target test@example.invalid --message "OpenClaw Automation diagnostic test (undeliverable address)"
❌ Delivery failed before dispatch: code=-32603 {
  "transport": "applescript",
  "operation": "send",
  "detail": "Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1743.",
  "retry_safe": true,
  "disposition": "not_started"
} Messages Automation was denied. Check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation for the Gateway/launcher on the Messages Mac. Local Gateway 
runtime: "<isolated-home>/.cache/openclaw/bun/openclaw-v1.4.4-20261024-807211511f-webkit-a2976f02e6/darwin-arm64/bin/bun". An app update that 
switches Node to Bun or moves the Gateway to a new runtime path needs this grant once; review the process macOS identifies, not just Terminal or 
OpenClaw.app. Channel probes do not verify sending. | -32603 | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED | -32603
```

### Upgrade from the latest stable release

Ran the official notarized OpenClaw.app 2026.10.7 (latest stable macOS release in `appcast.xml`) as a background service on an isolated named profile (port 29871). Its service runs Bun from the per-build path. That Bun's designated requirement is `identifier bun … certificate leaf[subject.OU] = FWJYW4S8P8`, with nothing build-specific, so between signed builds only the path changes:

prs.title: fix: preserve native exec failure diagnostics in Code Mode
prs.body:
Fixes #186509

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode can hide the reason a native exec call failed. For example, an unavailable working directory is correctly refused before command launch, and native exec explains how to use an existing directory or the default cwd. The agent receives only the structured failure fields when the whole result is returned through Code Mode, so it cannot see that recovery guidance.

## User Impact

Agents receive the existing diagnostic text as `message` when a returned failure has no nonempty structured `message` or `error`. They can use that information to choose a supported recovery. Existing structured diagnostics retain precedence, and ordinary completed commands retain their current exit codes and output without added presentation text.

The cwd refusal and sandbox boundaries are unchanged. Returned failures remain values, including when the outer Code Mode cell completes successfully; thrown errors remain catchable. This change does not grant permission to retry a command or change the existing side-effect and cancellation rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guest-value projection previously preserved text only when the result carried an explicit `isError: true` marker. Native exec reports failure through its structured status and keeps its explanatory reason separately from aggregated process output. The projection now also uses the existing shared tool-result failure classifier, so it recognizes that established failure representation without introducing another classification rule or changing native result envelopes.

Raw output-schema validation still runs before the guest value is enriched. The existing text fallback, structured-message precedence and downstream output handling remain in place. The guest API documentation now describes status-based failure diagnostics alongside explicit error markers.

## Evidence

On base `01a33a2b399eec12746d550164bc4bd4214e3986`, a regression using registered native exec through the real Code Mode bridge and Agent loop first confirms the native refusal text, then fails specifically because the agent-visible value lacks `message`. Its recovery sequence uses the default cwd to process a disposable input file, with a recorded file effect to detect duplicate execution. It also checks successful output and an ordinary completed exit code of 7.

The existing integration coverage is extended to exercise structured-message precedence, strict raw output-schema validation, catchable thrown errors, and network-content protection for returned status failures. Changed-file formatting and lint passed remotely, as did the selected production and test type graphs and 394 related cases across 22 files. After a fixture-only portability correction, the two edited test files passed all 42 cases with one worker. Their wall durations were 11.28s and 9.05s (including test loading); hosted CI seconds are pending. Independent review is complete and CI passed all 38 selected jobs on this head, including the selected Node, type, static, boundary, documentation and UI end-to-end checks. Per-file CI timing was not exposed in the run artifacts. Natural real-model recovery in the isolated guest environment remains pending: the deterministic Agent test scripts model responses and is not autonomous-model proof.

prs.body:
Closes #186436

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Ask OpenClaw greeting as the main agent when its configured owner has workspace persona files.

## User Impact

Greetings and command planning keep OpenClaw's caretaker identity. The configured owner still supplies model, authentication, and runtime policy. Normal caretaker chat keeps its existing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

A temporary execution directory did not isolate bootstrap context: the runners resolve the owner's canonical workspace. The shared greeting/planner runner now selects the existing lightweight bootstrap mode. The regression passes actual dispatch parameters into the production bootstrap resolver with synthetic SOUL.md and IDENTITY.md files, and checks that no file content is injected.

Original fix and report by @jondihaynes; their commit is preserved. Main was merged without rebasing or force-pushing. Duplicate planner setup was consolidated while retaining JSON-plan and transport coverage. Production **+1/−1 (net 0)**, tests **+41/−49 (net −8)**, docs **+2/−0** against main `228596060e33`.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI → Gateway → Ollama proof**, macOS, Node 26.12.1, `qwen2.5:7b`, isolated state and browser profiles, recording loopback relay. Both screenshots are fresh model responses, not replayed fixtures. Only synthetic persona data is shown.

| Observation | Main `228596060e33` | Candidate `31c51f3e3820` |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `ollama/qwen2.5:7b` | same |
| Greeting runtime owner | `main`, name `Nova` | same |
| `PERSONA-MARKER-7731` / `IDENTITY-MARKER-7731` in greeting request | both present | both absent |
| Visible greeting | “I'm Nova, your personal assistant.” | “Hello! Today is October 27, 2026. How can I assist you today?” |
| Native provider prompt tokens | 2,194 | 2,001 (−193) |
| Provider generation wall time | 1.84 s | 1.51 s |

The token/time numbers are single observed calls, not a benchmark; greeting facts and timestamps also differed. Regenerated common prompt snapshots are unchanged (template token delta 0). The owner name intentionally remains runtime metadata; its persona instructions are excluded.

**Before — actual main:**

![Ask OpenClaw on main introducing itself as synthetic owner Nova](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7757e455-b6e6-4dab-9f6c-7d727c04ad1c)

**After — greeting and normal caretaker chat:**

![Fixed greeting and normal caretaker chat identifying as OpenClaw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fef86194-5671-4fae-9cf8-7de244fba06e)

The normal chat sibling used `agent=openclaw`, excluded both markers, and answered “I am OpenClaw, your system agent.” Browser proof: 11.77 s before; 14.66 s after including the sibling chat; no page errors.

Planner sibling: the production `runSystemAgentWithInference` command entry, after canonical async runtime-config preparation, completed a real `qwen2.5:7b` probe and planner turn. Its request retained OpenClaw identity, allowed commands, `Default agent: main`, the selected model, and `Gateway reachable: true`, while excluding both persona markers. It returned valid JSON with a status reply and no command/configuration write (2.697 s provider time; 57.10 s including cold source-tooling setup).

**Existing CLI limitation:** cold `openclaw setup --message` failed before inference with “Runtime config is not prepared.” The affected startup/preparation files are unchanged from the pinned base. The prepared production-entry proof above does not claim that the ordinary cold CLI invocation succeeds; that separate startup issue is not changed here.

Validation: **58/58 tests passed** (`assistant.configured.test.ts`: 12; `bootstrap-files.test.ts`: 33; `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`: 13), 149.99 s including 35.0 s cold worker preparation. The new regression took 11 ms and fails on the original defect with both persona contents visible (393 ms test, 65.18 s command including cold preparation). Services test typecheck, core typecheck, focused lint/format, full build (7m41s), and all ten baseline ratchets passed. No ceiling or baseline exception was added.

CI [run 40630023998](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40630023998) passed on `31c51f3e3820aef0e9c45df90b75070195a5cd37`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Independent Codex review of this committed range at P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Validation is local macOS; CI supplies broader platform coverage.

~~~~json
The active runtime provides the available OpenClaw tools directly. Use only exposed tools; names are case-sensitive.
The AGENTS.md Tools section guides usage; it never grants availability.
Single global file workspace unless explicitly told otherwise.
## Tool Call Style
Routine low-risk: call silently.
Narrate only complex, sensitive/destructive, or requested steps.
First-class tool exists: use it; never ask user for equivalent CLI/slash.
/approve is user command; never execute via shell/tool.
allow-once covers only that exact command; later commands need their own exec policy decision.
Approval preview: exact full command/script, including chains/multiline. Keep preview separate from /approve; never use script as approval id/slug.
## Care
Before config/scheduler edits (crontab/systemd/nginx/shell rc/timers): inspect; preserve/merge. Whole-file replacement only explicit.
Use or store credentials the user supplies as requested, and complete the task. In the final reply, briefly acknowledge how the supplied credential was used or stored, without repeating its value. Keep the acknowledgment factual and non-alarming.
For user-requested login or pairing in a group, deliver short-lived codes and verification URLs only to the requesting user in private, then acknowledge in the group without them.
Channel, provider, and credential setup: terminal `openclaw channels add <channel>` or `openclaw configure` masks secrets.
## OpenClaw Control
Do not invent commands.
For the Gateway hosting this session: In a connected chat, the owner can send `/update` with commands.restart enabled (the default), regardless of the agent's tool profile. For a chat update request, direct the user to `/update`. Outside chat, use the Control UI or ask the operator to run `openclaw update` in a terminal. Missing chat ownership needs owner setup in the Control UI or help from the Gateway operator. Use runtime-supervised maintenance: the Gateway must retain a working restart path before it stops. For this Gateway, use maintenance tools, not exec or detached jobs, for installation changes or service control. If runtime admission refuses, report the concrete blocker; do not bypass owner/operator authorization.
## Documentation
Docs: <source>/docs
Mirror: https://docs.openclaw.ai
Source: <source>
For official OpenClaw support, visit https://community.openclaw.ai/. Keep self-service docs, Discord social chat, reproducible GitHub bug reports, and private security reporting separate.
OpenClaw behavior questions: docs first using available tools. AGENTS/project/workspace/profile/memory = instructions/user memory, not product design truth.
Configuration docs: `docs/gateway/configuration.md`, `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`.
If docs are silent/stale, say so and inspect local source.
Can't-do claims: a missing tool or failed call shows this session's limits, not OpenClaw's; check the local docs before saying OpenClaw can't.
Diagnosis: run `openclaw status` when possible; ask only if blocked.
## Assistant Output Directives
- Media attachment: own line `MEDIA:<path-or-url>` per item; path is not prose.
- Directive starts line, plain text, outside fences/Markdown; never inline or wrapped.
- Attached voice note: `[[audio_as_voice]]`.
- Native reply starts with `[[reply_to_current]]`; explicit id only: `[[reply_to:<id>]]`.
- Directives stripped before render; channel config controls delivery.
## Messaging
- Current-session final text normally routes to source.
- Completion event requesting update: rewrite in normal voice; send. Never forward raw metadata or silent placeholder.
- OpenClaw messaging: use available messaging tools, never shell commands, the CLI, curl, or direct RPC. Missing messaging tools are not permission to use another route.
- Subagents return results through their accepted completion path; parents relay required coordination. Do not send acknowledgments or duplicate completion reports.
- Other services (e.g. email): user-authorized CLI/API use is allowed; normal tool permissions and approvals still apply.
## Conversation Context
You are OpenClaw, the system itself — caretaker of this machine's gateway, config, channels, and agents.
Speak in first person, brief and warm, no corporate filler. Report status honestly; nominal systems get one calm line.
Return only the greeting as markdown: 2-5 short lines, no heading, no JSON, and no inline command suggestions.
If an update is available, mention the version and offer an upgrade. If channelHealthAvailable is false, say channel health is unavailable. If channels are degraded, name them.
Do not invent causes, activity, fixes, or state beyond the supplied facts.
~~~~

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(auth): configured primary account blocks CLI fallback
prs.body:
Closes #158421. Thanks to @HerbertHuerto for the corrected report and @aoclaw-glitch for the per-agent reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A configured primary account can be mistaken for an explicit conversation pin when fallback changes CLI provider, rejecting a usable destination account. Genuine user/user-link intent can also change while placement or execution preparation awaits. Native Claude login needs its selected identity preserved even though it has no forwarded credential ID.

## User Impact

Configured Chat and event fallbacks can select the destination runtime's account. An unchanged native login pin remains usable; a changed or removed explicit pin stops execution. Scheduled inference retains recorded-account and current-credential checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth owner carries configured-account provenance as a runtime-only fact and distinguishes native execution identity from forwarded credentials. Credential consumers keep a forwarding-only ID projection. Chat and event-Cron admission compare current explicit intent with the identity actually selected, retaining current-row, lifecycle and awaited-effect guards.

Public V1 declarations remain source-compatible; additive V2 supplies awaited admission and current-owner assertions, and bundled/internal consumers use V2. This does not certify legacy V1 deferred-I/O behavior. There is no authored config option, SDK subpath, dependency, schema or protocol-version bump against main.

This revision integrates official main `58b88a8b0a80edd769c1335d971809ab9ff24a38`. The integration retains main's per-input origin and private prompt context, forwards them through the existing Claude input owner, and preserves V2 admission before native writes. The existing-session test retains both V2 and main's private-context observations.

## Evidence

Head: `a30e7603b14cc8d198817aea4e1e46ef94760e89`; tree: `b48e6921b87fe98212127c0b76fadd3ec2c5901a`. Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 match the branch requirements. The official lock and dependency definitions are unchanged from the previously qualified installation; no dependency reconciliation was needed.

- **Current-tree behavior:** 206 tests in 10 complete files passed on tree `0e6ce739f587ea016b17dd24061666dc5bfa6b08`. The subsequent conflict repair changed only the budget within the 79 recorded PR/test/owner/dependency inputs; all 10 test-file hashes are identical. That run is reused as unchanged-input behavioral evidence, not described as a new-head execution. The complete public account file retains all 16 account scenarios through `getReplyFromConfig` and `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn`, real SQLite pin mutation/readback, actual admission owners and an owned Node CLI protocol child. Positives launch once; changed intent prevents launch; an unrecorded scheduled account is rejected before backend preparation. Chat's public error marker and the settled lifecycle reason are checked separately. Claude runtime, private/resume context, existing-session and steering consumers are included in this run.
- **Current checks:** The six-root production/test consumer typecheck passed again after the final main integration. Seven-file core typed lint, whole-PR formatting, line caps and maximum-line checks passed on the preceding source-identical PR revision; line caps and whitespace passed again after the final integration. Anthropic typed lint stopped before analysis because plugin-SDK declaration preparation exceeded its existing 300-second timeout; it is **not** recorded as passing. The timeout was not increased
- **Budget:** The contributor explicitly approved a bounded main-relative allocation for this PR, including conflict synchronizations: official main ceiling 6,300,000 + measured net 1,298 = **6,301,298**. The native ratchet passes at **6,296,663**, retaining main's **4,635-line** slack. The original 6,286,325 ceiling failed at 6,287,574 before the first approved adjustment This scoped allocation is limited to this PR's measured net test growth, at most 1,298 lines, and preserves main's existing slack when main is synchronized. It retains independent account, compatibility and lifecycle proof rather than dropping assertions or increasing timeouts. Earlier fixture consolidation removed 319 counted lines of manual setup; that reduction compares repair revisions and is not the complete PR's net delta against main.
- **Independent review:** The complete 68-file P0–P2 source review was scoped-clean on the recorded same-tree review snapshot, including eight full owning-module contexts. A separate budget-only review was also scoped-clean. The final mechanical budget conflict repair preserves those reviewed source inputs Static review did not independently execute tests or certify vendor/package behavior.

Historical admission evidence remains bounded: on `46f34c8f`, three selected actual fallback/session-admission cases rejected unchanged native pins before the pre-execution barrier. The mutation case supplied no before-fix post-mutation result, and the final corrected fixture was not replayed on that old head. Earlier 48/83-case local runs and other historical executions retain their original trees and are not added to the current totals.

The earlier [CI run 40573714129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40573714129) belongs to `a122e58c`, not this head: 57 jobs succeeded, 27 were skipped, and the test-line ratchet plus aggregate gate failed. Current-head [CI 40632043305](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40632043305) has now attached and is in progress, alongside current-head artifact and contract checks; these are pending evidence.

## Remaining Proof and Review

Current-revision maintainer security/dependency and SDK codeowner review remain required. The earlier [a122 CI artifact build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40573713800/job/122434413082) emitted declarations and verified 160 public SDK subpaths on merge `d0fbe106`/base `451ec41c`; that is prior-merge artifact evidence. Current-head package emission/exports and isolated native consumer/runtime proof remain unverified. The local declaration-preparation timeout is preserved as an environment/proof gap.

Real shipped Gateway/vendor cold and warm execution, persisted-account edits through a vendor runtime, retained-settings installation/upgrade, and isolated legacy V1 deferred-I/O behavior remain unverified. The owned protocol child is not a vendor binary. Source compatibility and local source-backed typechecking do not establish those runtime or installation claims. The budget decision does not waive these proof gaps or maintainer approvals.

prs.title: fix(scripts): preserve PR tooling across process handoffs
prs.body:
## Problem

PR tooling can retire an installation while a surviving process still reads its projected packages. A wrapper can also lose the selected physical Git executable across PATH and process handoffs. The issue is grounded in the repository's source and Linux fixtures; no shipped-release incident is claimed.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185962

Related upstream work and credit: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185493.

## User impact

Keep live dependency projections usable across creator exit and overlapping installs. Preserve the selected Git context, including native GitHub CLI execution on Windows. Refuse uncertain ownership with a visible diagnostic and retain the installation rather than infer deletion authority.

## Why this change

- One dependency-free SQLite owner records readiness, holds and settlement before package selection or installation. Builtin SQLite avoids a Kysely bootstrap cycle. The existing physical metadata mutex remains separate from synchronous database transactions.
- Holds bind the entry, canonical anchor path and physical identity. A committed hold precedes projection; creator FD9, exact identity and full process drain precede release. Missing, corrupt, replaced or incompatible authority is retained/refused. Collection grants deletion only after committed eligibility and final physical checks.
- Fresh v3 storage has one authority. No schema-version bump, migration, old-v2 deletion, parallel file ledger or runtime fallback is introduced. The initial unshipped layout rejects the older PR-only three-column hold key without changing that database.
- Git admission captures a physical executable and preserves its execution environment. Native Windows GitHub CLI gets matching explicit Git policy or capability refusal before execution.
- Bootstrap authority is qualified independently of the selected historical workflow and caller helpers. Runtime import closure keeps declaration files as artifacts while excluding them from executable graph traversal; source-import mode remains intact.
- Regression fixtures use genuine creator/FD9/materializer authority and historical workflow-admission records. Concurrent fixture observations use the metadata mutex. The test-line ceiling equals the actual integrated count, without spare headroom.
- Preserve the required bigint-to-number metadata-wait conversion with one documented typed-lint exception and matching exact allowance. Register maintained standalone Knip commands as exact entry roots, without ignoring files or changing zero-unused enforcement.

Production changes: 1,303 added / 208 removed, net **+1,095**, including the Darwin workflow, declarations and explicit Knip configuration. This growth owns durable predependency lifetime state, authenticated bootstrap and physical Git handoffs. Tests: 3,153 added / 509 removed, net **+2,644**; the canonical LF ratchet counts +2,643 because the Python file is outside its pathspec. Scalar counter metadata is neutral.

## Evidence

Current candidate: **361570dc23768601b58af43c7485919e4ee8c8b5**, tree **aba981479e99e9c0197d31888ca70ae61906716d**, with signed ordered parents **09b724a68ae399b9b14c1e645c886bafa324dff6** (B) and the fixed product baseline **228596060e33dfcddbb6740416f381daac6f84fe** (Y). Native source-preserving integration and independent whole-tree postguards verified all **61,023 tracked entries**: the other 25 PR paths retain B's exact modes and blobs; every non-PR entry is exact Y. The 27-path diff against Y is 269,887 bytes, SHA256 `d7c790ef9daaf1c75679e7523e5cfa5ecf63ce72360652e73d7c263ad7bfeeb1`.

The two genuine merge conflicts were resolved through the native baseline owner. Knip preserves all 14 approved standalone-command roots, the separate live-test launcher, main's new Code Mode and session-selection roots, and its plugin benchmark entry. No new duplicate, missing entry, ignore or wildcard is introduced. The counter is **6,297,082**, exactly the planned integrated tree with zero headroom: independently verified prior baseline 6,293,484 plus 955 lines across 93 changed main test paths gives Y's actual 6,294,439, then the unchanged PR adds 2,643. Y's committed ceiling was 6,295,000; the resolution uses actual counted blobs, not ceiling addition.

**Current C is source-qualified; exact-C installation, normal hosted CI, Darwin and final-head ClawSweeper clearance remain pending.** The previous B proof is carried only across demonstrated unchanged implementation inputs. Y changes seven audited install inputs: the human-mentions schema, conversation validator, their generated predicate/validator outputs, and the gateway event inventory. All 608 frontier members are accounted for; manifests, lock/patches, all 31 PR/markdown package pins and Bun191 remain unchanged, but the changed digest selects the normal full-tree dependency identity. A fresh target installation is required. The older 205-workspace installation is not an exact-C install receipt. The changed shared database-worker analysis also requires the final canonical checks/CI; its prior result is not silently carried.

Source review is composed. The a242dfbf full 11-pass review completed non-clean with one distinct eager-bootstrap diagnostic P2 repeated across partitions. Signed 7993175 changed only that expected diagnostic while preserving exit status, nonexecution, marker and exact-binding assertions; its fresh COMMIT review reported no findings. Signed 01fb8b0 then applied the independently checked five-path lint/Knip/count correction and received a clean narrow COMMIT review. Native integrations preserve those implementation bytes. C's two metadata resolutions have independent source/count/tree review. The original non-clean full-branch report is not relabeled as a clean C review.

Historical exact-442 Linux [run 40612772493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40612772493) completed all 28 stages: **25 passed; the aggregate exited 1**. Each actual Node24.22.1 and pinned Bun191 focused group passed **271 tests / 15 intentional platform skips**. Separate actual Node and Bun ledger workloads each passed all **19 workers**, covering shared holds, five pressure entries, committed settlement and collection. Source-before/after passed; ordinary settlement verified the lease claim and both keys absent. Those are 442 execution facts, not exact-C execution.

The three historical RED surfaces were handled without weakening the gates:

- **03, production lint:** Node and Bun return bigint nanoseconds and the wait API requires numeric milliseconds. The correction keeps the required conversion and adds one documented exact checker allowance plus its matching explicit allowlist entry. Production lint passed later on B with zero warnings or errors. The inference cause remains unproved; follow-up: **oxlint-tsgolint7.0.2004 hrtime.bigint inference false positive**.
- **07, Knip:** the correction registers 14 maintained standalone commands and the one live-test launcher as exact roots. B's production and full-tree zero-unused scans, targeted config lint and formatting passed. No ignore, wildcard, scanner or assertion change was used. No unrelated baseline aggregate PASS is invented.
- **28, matched reader:** the original admission stopped before either arm because its candidate package row was copied from A3. All nine candidate rows were regenerated from committed B, while the six original-source provider files and all 31 genuine donor packages remained exact. The first admitted fixture then failed without an arm outcome. Independent inspection found a missing closing reader-loop brace and unowned child/stream failures; the original failing Socket's identity remains unknown. The proof-only repair fixes syntax and failure ownership without changing product code, pressure, deadlines or domain assertions.

B's reduced **14-stage** follow-up [run 40620327582](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40620327582) produced **13 PASS and one fixture failure**, aggregate exit1. Line/count, production/test lint and type lanes, both Knip scans and targeted config lint/format passed. Actual Node24.22.1 and Bun191 each passed **14 suppression tests and three source-closure tests**. Receiver and final source guards verified B's exact tree, baseline carrier, all 27 paths and tracked cleanliness. Ordinary stop settled that lease; claim and both keys were absent.

The separate repaired matched-only [run 40622793829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40622793829) passed its sole stage: **baseline `RED_LIVE_READER_ENOENT`; B candidate `GREEN_RETAINED_SAME_PHYSICAL_PACKAGE`; both joined**. Each arm registered a real reader, observed creator exit0 before five distinct pressure installations, checked a fresh read, then joined the reader and inherited streams. Candidate identity matched its own original physical package; the arms do not share an inode. Both read identical payload bytes, SHA256 `3a03c47fcb20ceb65d5a938816b1e3ef047fc2e43e9991dbc9638e44d010811d`. Strict six-file original-source, nine-file candidate and 31 genuine package admissions passed. Stage and aggregate exited0; the outer native controller exited1 solely on a GitHub cleanup-reconciliation deadline. Ordinary exact stop then exited0 with claim and both keys absent. Independent full-output/custody review passed. This is **13 earlier B stages plus one separate matched PASS**, not a clean one-shot 14-stage run or outer exit0.

Both B executions used their own normal frozen installation across 205 workspace projects. Actual Node24.22.1 and Bun191 identity were checked before proof. Bun was version1.4.4, CLI revision `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, runtime commit `191755ec115ece3dd642eba3cb0143cecb5e5d7a`, executable SHA256 `0cef667e2f3fd465b6429904ed074381a679be379ec44fa42b5f460ed118b2b8`. Primary runtime/SQLite source and official metadata were separately inspected; actual explicit ledger execution supplies behavior evidence. These receipts do not replace the new exact-C installation.

Fresh exact-442 Windows [run 40612735050](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40612735050), job122567956298, passed **15 tests / three intentional POSIX skips**, including three source-closure cases. It used its own target installation, Node24.22.1, pnpm12.15 and Vitest5.0.5. Non-skipped actual GH2.103.0 offline sync/async behavior passed in two working directories, including denied selected-Git status78 and configuration preservation. Source/dependency inputs were unchanged, process exit0 and hosted teardown succeeded; teardown does not attest descendant settlement. This remains historical Windows evidence.

The later isolated Mac attempt synchronized a separate exact-B checkout but stopped during the native macOS functional preflight: native provider-error exit7, commandMs0, cleanup unconfirmed/SSH255. **The external proof controller, private Node24 installation and all five Darwin suites were UNRUN.** The native claim and workspace are retained; remote preflight worker/drain state is UNKNOWN. No stop, deletion, retry or replacement is asserted. Named upstream follow-up: persist preflight identity before dispatch and provide exact completion reconciliation. This retained Mac recovery state is separate from local source reconciliation and hosted CI.

Earlier a3d07 Darwin evidence (30 Python passed / one optional-profile skip; 209 TypeScript passed / six skips) is historical and does not qualify the current collector. The inherited system-Bash supervisor repair remains preserved. Ordinary hosted CI and required Darwin checks still need exact-C results. Native source READY and `github_pending` are publication records, not successful runtime, full-gate or merge stamps. Custom B proof cannot substitute a native full stamp or GitHub required checks.

The source conflict resolution and counter accounting are now recorded on C; live mergeability still needs verification after publication. Final-head ClawSweeper re-review remains pending. No auto-merge, release or deployment action is requested.

prs.title: fix(logging): redact hostnames and nicknames from support bundles
prs.body:
Closes #127419

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: diagnostics exports retain standalone IRC hostnames and nicknames despite the documented support-bundle privacy contract.

## User Impact

User impact: standalone host/hostname, bind-host, and nick/nickname fields are masked in exported config and snapshots. Hosts embedded in URL strings remain available for diagnostics.

**Maintainer decision remains required before merge:** the existing whole-field policy also masks the object-valued `desktop.host` settings and enum-valued `tools.exec.host` routing mode. Please confirm this conservative privacy/usefulness tradeoff; the implementation does not claim that approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing shared identifier-field expression with anchored hostname/nickname alternatives. Adjacent names such as hostCount and nicknameEnabled remain untouched. The final production delta is one line replaced, with no additional redaction path or dependency. Folding the equivalent expression into the existing classifier also keeps the file within the repository's 700-line lint limit.

The issue's full discussion and related #172285 discussion were checked. #172285 remains open and covers payment credentials, a separate vocabulary in the same classifier. This PR preserves the issue review's request for a maintainer decision on the shared field taxonomy.

## Evidence

Current head: `336bad7fcd6202f8b31b5fa70cc4c525472025f4`. Validated in an isolated checkout with Node 24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0.

- Two committed regressions (+74 lines in existing test files) exercise both sanitizers' exact field-name boundary and every generated ZIP entry with IRC-shaped config/health plus daemon status.
- **100/100 repository tests passed** on the final candidate (75.21s including wrapper preparation). Restoring only the production classifier from base `6b72c79119382fc4ae82d547db6efbcb888d0f50` makes both new cases fail: **2 expected failures / 98 passes**.
- Targeted oxlint: 0 warnings/errors on the three changed files. Oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.state-logging.json` typechecking passed.
- Independent P0–P3 `autoreview` found no actionable findings in its reviewed scope. The subsequent regex union was independently checked for identical pattern/flag semantics and against 108 key variants, followed by the final 100-test and lint rerun. This does not resolve the maintainer policy decision.

Committed-test command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts \
  src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### Real CLI / Gateway export

The normal repository `pnpm openclaw` entry completed its required `qaRuntime` build and CLI bootstrap guard on the clean published head. A fresh HOME, config and state directory were used with a loopback-only test Gateway and disabled discovery. Synthetic `IRC_HOST`/`IRC_NICK` environment values were supplied alongside the same config fields. Real Gateway health returned the nonempty synthetic identities before export.

```sh
pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port "$TEST_PORT" --auth none
pnpm openclaw gateway call health --json --timeout 10000
pnpm openclaw gateway diagnostics export --output "$PROOF_DIR/support-fixed.zip" \
  --json --timeout 10000 --no-stability-bundle
```

The export exited 0. Its JSON receipt's path and byte count matched the newly written ZIP; its modification time was after this command started. Every entry name and file body was scanned. Both health and status snapshots completed successfully. The following is the sanitized verification output, including the built head and the input/output values:


prs.title: fix(memory): sanitize file-derived terminal search reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory search` prints file-derived result paths and Markdown snippets directly into human terminal output. A normally indexed Markdown file can therefore introduce terminal-control sequences into a successful search report. Existing CLI tests strip VT characters before comparing ordinary output, which can conceal this boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing SDK `sanitizeTerminalText` in the one search renderer shared by local and attached-Gateway result owners. Sanitize the shortened display path before applying trusted theme styling. prs.title: fix(workboard): restore Add to Workboard in session menus and open the card from the chip
prs.body:
Closes #183966

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.9.2 (PR #138618) the Control UI has no **Add to Workboard** entry, so turning an existing session into a Workboard card takes 11 clicks/inputs through the New-card dialog (or an undocumented `openclaw gateway call`), and the session-header chip only opens the card's board — on a busy board that costs extra clicks to find the card.

> **Recommendation:** **Restore menu capture and direct card opening:** Restore the operator workflow in sidebar and Sessions menus, reuse the existing capture owner, and make the chip select the linked card details.

## User Impact

Users can again add a session to Workboard in one click from the session menus (sidebar, Sessions-page row menu, chat session menu), with the card titled from the session and notes seeded from the recent conversation, landing directly on the new card's details; once a card exists the same entry reads **Open Workboard card**, and clicking the session-header chip opens the linked card's details on its board instead of only the board.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a **behavior-restoring** fix: PR #138618 (merged 2026-09-04) deleted `extensions/workboard/browser/session-action.ts` and the registration, while the capability owner — RPC `workboard.cards.captureSession` (`extensions/workboard/src/gateway.ts:449` under `operator.write`, implemented in `extensions/workboard/src/store-core.ts:387` with deterministic per-session card id, existing-card reuse, and archived-card restore) — was never removed and stays the single capture owner. The plugin now registers one session-placement action through the existing SDK contract (`registerAction`, `src/plugin-sdk/control-ui.ts:320`), consumed by the shared session-menu plumbing (`ui/src/plugins/control-ui-actions.ts:7` → sidebar/Sessions/chat menus), calls that same RPC, and the chip seeds the shared card state then opens `openCardDetails` (`extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-card-details.tsx:58`). No core UI files, no new owner, no new surface. `docs/plugins/workboard.md` (:631, :711) still describes this workflow, so restoring the code makes the docs true again without a docs edit.

**Product-decision risk (disclosed):** the issue reporter asked @Patrick-Erichsen whether #138618's removal was deliberate (that PR gave no reason; the 2026.9.2 notes only say no replacement workflow was added), and #183966 carries `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`. Maintainers may still choose the docs-only route (issue point 4). If that decision lands against UI restoration, close this PR and take the docs-only alternative instead — the change is self-contained on this branch, so stopping costs nothing.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): sanitize file-derived human inspection reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`path resolve --human` and `path find --human` can copy C1 terminal-control characters from a JSONC key/value into an inspection summary. JSON quoting already escapes C0 characters, but it leaves C1 characters intact. A successful inspection should display readable text while preserving the underlying file and address identities.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing public SDK `sanitizeTerminalText` at the shared human leaf formatter and at find's concrete-path display. Quote leaf values first to preserve the existing visible quoting. No new sanitizer, dependency, parser rule, configuration, or API is needed. `registerPathCli` owns these summaries; the existing find/resolve adapters and JSONC scanner supply the original data.

The actual installed `jsonc-parser` scanner accepts these C1 characters in ordinary JSON strings. Rejecting them or rewriting canonical paths would change the data contract. Explicit `emit --human`, dry-run source and diff output are byte-oriented artifacts, so their existing behavior is retained. This follows the accepted file-derived reporting boundary, rather than changing operator-argument echoes.

All-state symptom, symbol and owner-path searches found no equivalent implementation. Open #172164 covers wildcard array tests and #180918 covers frontmatter comments; their overlap with the old test module does not implement this rendering fix. All original 70 tests remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Human inspection keeps ordinary Unicode readable and strips control sequences from file-derived summaries. Structured JSON retains the exact original key/value/address. Explicit raw exports and source files retain their original bytes. There are no permission, configuration, default, storage, protocol, migration or dependency changes.

## Evidence

Compiled-CLI RED: clean `18d2633de8abd677ae1852b48950701bce8ff302`; GREEN: clean `e230c34d3e215152d0d05ed418bcb6cf33ccd7ba`, parent main `f0d422a7cb485eb19ff9671aa3a588cb4cf3a46a`. The CLI/find/resolve/SDK sanitizer owners match between executed RED and parent. Fresh main `95dff1e02bc59bc86dd6e75ff93d7ab2714daac9` retains these owners and the publication contracts; native merge-tree verification is clean. Each run checks `dist/build-info.json.commit == HEAD`.

The same frozen recorder uses ordinary synthetic JSONC files and the real built CLI/plugin registration in fresh isolated HOME/config/state. Its four actual commands are:

```sh
node dist/entry.js path find 'oc://report.jsonc/*' --file <fixture>/report.jsonc --human
node dist/entry.js path find 'oc://report.jsonc/*' --file <fixture>/report.jsonc --json
node dist/entry.js path find 'oc://positive.jsonc/*' --file <fixture>/positive.jsonc --human
node dist/entry.js path emit <fixture>/report.jsonc --human
```

The controlled key is `café` followed by CSI/OSC/ST sequences (code points U+009B, U+009D and U+009C); the value starts `中文🍵` and contains the same kinds of controls. Both are accepted as normal file contents. All four commands exit 0 with empty stderr on both builds. RED human find contains six C1 characters; GREEN contains zero and produces this captured stdout:

```text
1 match for oc://report.jsonc/*:
  oc://report.jsonc/café  →  leaf @ L1: "中文🍵" (string)
```

The Unicode-only positive remains identical. JSON parses to the original controlled path/value on both builds, and explicit `emit --human` remains byte-identical to the controlled input, including all six C1 characters. A separate reader reopens the actual two source files/config, checks their hashes, reparses JSON and all eight captured stdout/stderr streams, and checks exact human/raw output. It invokes zero new OpenClaw commands. There is no internal result injection, Gateway, model, external API or production state.

RED takes 19.87 s; GREEN takes 20.12 s. prs.title: fix(agents): don't stop CLI-backed replies as stalled while the model is still thinking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI-backed replies could be stopped as stalled even though the model was still producing new thinking. That thinking did not count as semantic progress.

## User Impact

Long reasoning turns on CLI backends now keep running instead of being cut off by stall recovery. Fuller reasoning output still displays. Configured limits stay unchanged. No extra configuration or migration is required; nothing has been deployed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser marks fresh thinking text and positive per-message thinking-token deltas as progress. The handler credits the current attempt only after the output-suppression guard allows the output. Replays, prefixes, heartbeats, stale output, tool-owned output and yielded output never count. An optional SDK hook makes one private, read-only assessment before semantic stall recovery. It is limited to 10 seconds or the remaining hard budget, whichever is shorter. Unavailable, obsolete or failed captures resolve once as unknown, so capture cannot loop. Without a hook, the existing recovery path runs with no added delay. The stop, hard-deadline and attempt/backend registration fences are unchanged. The change does not swap models or threads or send a new Claude health ping. The adapter reports only current local facts or unknown. This change does not cover the separate CLI no-output timer or general node and supervisor health.

Tradeoff: the public test line ceiling rises from 6,288,829 to 6,290,224 (+1,395: 747 inherited, 648 from this PR) and leaves no slack. That covers 46 new cases (156 → 202 expanded). I consolidated 37 lines without losing coverage. This ceiling is the test-size ratchet, not a watchdog budget.

## Evidence

- AutoReview (Codex through the configured ClawRouter, P0–P2), base c8b7c4c4 → head 9e7808f7: **incomplete, not clean**. It ran 7 passes with 0 accepted findings. 4 batches had gaps in determining context, and a full intact pass would not fit the fixed 512k prompt capacity. Published head 93178e78 has the same tree.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186446#issuecomment-6459136186) reviewed 93178e78 against main dafda2f7. It found no code issues but says the merge conflicts must be fixed before merge.
- Two independent local source reviews passed, and the code-comment contract audit reported no open questions. I deferred one non-blocking nit from an earlier review.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 81 passed. Across all 8 affected files, 225 passed with 1 existing Linux skip. That result comes from 9e7808f7 and is reused because the inputs did not change.
- Real parser/handler/watchdog tests failed 2 cases before the fix and pass after it. Obsolete-capture tests went from 3 failed and 24 passed on the old code to all 27 passing.
- Local core lint, format, diff check, SDK import/export and ratchets pass. The canonical store declaration guard blocks the core SDK compiler and extension typed lint, so I don't claim a static compiler pass. The full build is unproven, and CI is pending.
- No shipped CLI or Gateway turn has run past the semantic stall window. The proof comes from a harness with real modules and a synthetic native process, not live vendor behavior.
- Three merge conflicts with main remain. This PR is not merge-ready and has not been merged or deployed.
