prs.title: fix(control-ui): release old transcript memory after switching chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching away from long chats can leave obsolete transcript bodies and scheduled layout work retained after their presentation ends.

## User Impact

Obsolete message bodies can be collected through the layout owner, and disconnected footprint writes stop immediately. Reconnecting still preserves scroll-restoration geometry and measured row floors. No settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The layout owner now stores actual key/revision records, rather than retaining full rendered rows behind a narrower TypeScript type. It owns one cancellable animation-frame/idle task; identity checks prevent retired callbacks from writing or clearing replacement work. Terminal host disposal also releases the layout's cache access.

This replaces the uncancelled scheduling flag with lifecycle ownership. Production/tooling: +69/-37 (net +32); tests: +261/-8 (net +253). Existing weak memoization avoids copying unchanged row geometry on every render.

## Evidence

- Regression-first proof: the unchanged eight-case lifetime suite failed at the intended retention/reconnect assertions before the fix, then all eight passed. Independent unowned GC controls passed. The final candidate repeated only this affected suite after the terminal-reset consolidation: 8/8 passed in 5.67s.
- Existing geometry tests: 13/13 passed. Runtime-routing inventory: 7/7 passed. Scoped formatting and final host lint passed without warnings.
- A verified Testbox source capsule ran UI production/test type checks, the UI build (22.88s), and Chromium geometry tests (16/16 passed). The initial runner exited 1 during GitHub cleanup settlement; the same completed lease subsequently reconciled through the native owner with exit 0. [Remote run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40616181429).
- The first [candidate CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40618304470) exposed a GC-fixture control failure before the payload assertion. The control now allocates inside the existing synchronous setup helper, so only WeakRefs cross the suspended test frame. With the same corrected assertions and Node 24.22.1, the actual UI unit-test entry point fails all eight cases on the original production and passes all eight on the repaired production. No extra collection, retry, or timeout was added; the engine's retaining cause remains unproven.
- That CI run also failed three collapsed-reply E2E cases at their initial disclosure selector, before search/reply/reveal. Fresh bundled builds from the pinned `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe` main production and the repaired production reproduce the same three failures with Node 24.22.1 and Chromium. Both fail at initial disclosure, before search/reply/reveal actions; the deep case has the same six-summary strict-selector error at line 79. The upstream chat-folding change `e7f0546192744a786b60b607401e030b0f83940d` and unchanged test/fixture inputs establish scoped pre-existing attribution. The paired wrapper remains exit 1, including an obsolete final-diff postcondition; complete immutable tree parity independently verified restoration afterward. This does not claim those E2E cases pass.
- The failing test-line guard required one deliberate integration with main at `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`, preserving upstream changes. The resolved-tree counter measured 6,293,961 lines. This PR adds 253 meaningful test lines without deleting unrelated coverage. The later shared allowance in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186456 already covers them: exact canonical-pattern deltas give 6,294,320 combined lines against its 6,295,000 ceiling. This PR now makes no ceiling change; the redundant prerequisite https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186465 was closed.
- Independent and fresh source reviews cover the complete owner/test changes against that pinned integration base, with no actionable findings. Removing only the ceiling edit preserves all six reviewed source/test blobs exactly. The virtual-core 3.19.2 cleanup/reconnect contract was inspected directly. Exact-head CI is complete: 40 jobs succeeded, 25 were skipped, and only the three attributed collapsed-reply failures plus their aggregate CI gate failed. The eight lifetime cases and the ratchet passed. Exact-head ClawSweeper review has no findings; native preparation retains the failed-CI attribution rather than calling the run green.

The tests prove collection and cancellation at these owner boundaries. They do not measure Firefox peak heap/RSS or claim that every DOM reference held by a retained host is released. Live application/embedded-view custody remains separate.

The optional ClawSweeper rank-up request for built Control UI heap/navigation proof is deferred to the queued mounted-window and aggregate-presentation measurements. The owner-boundary proof here does not claim whole-application or deployed Firefox collection.

prs.title: fix(ui): streamed chat replies lose the agent avatar
prs.body:
Related: #183267, #186044, #186290

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a streamed assistant reply in Control UI chat renders without the agent avatar while it streams, and `checks-ui-e2e` on `main` fails in four files whenever the UI e2e lane is selected (scheduled runs since `fdeb8f7efd`).

## User Impact

User impact: streamed replies show the agent avatar again, as #186044 intended. The Control UI e2e lane is green on main again for these files (the prompt height-cap failure was already fixed by #186409).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Product fix (avatar).** #186044 guarded `isTurnBlock` so a run frame that only holds a live stream (empty `messages`) keeps its identity. #183267 merged right after it and added `group.messages.every(presentationOwnsFooter === false)`, which is `true` for an empty list, so the live frame became a turn block again and lost its avatar. The non-empty guard now covers both `every()` checks. `chat-flow.streaming` "keeps the pending telemetry row stable through acknowledgement and streaming" is the regression test (unchanged; red on main, green here).
- **Stale tests after #183267** (in-place, untimed **Worked** chunks; narration stays visible; the turn recap owns the run's duration, per the updated `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md`):
  - `chat-run-lifecycle`: the 13 s duration that excludes the failed turn's idle time is now asserted on the recap ("Done in 13 seconds"), including after a later run's lifecycle row and after reload; the work label is "Worked".
  - `chat-cold-load-anchor`: the cached first frames must show the recap's "Done in 3 minutes" instead of "Worked for 3 minutes".
  - `chat-collapsed-reply-reveal`: earlier narration is no longer folded, so the test asserts it stays visible and that every tool chunk stays collapsed (several chunks in the deep case) before and after replying through search. The reply-reveal, highlight, scroll and request assertions are unchanged.
- **Stale test after #186290:** `browser-dictation-status` now expects Dictation **Configure** to open `/settings/talk`, not model setup.

## Evidence

On a remote Ubuntu test VM (Node 24.22.1, Chromium headless shell 1248, `--maxWorkers 2`, private network namespace), running
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner` on the five affected files plus `new-session-page.cloud-startup`:

| Tree | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main `228596060e3` | 7 failed / 30 passed: the same assertions as main CI (`'Worked' to be 'Worked for 13 seconds'`, `null not to be null` avatar, strict-mode 6 `.chat-work-group button`, `Worked for 3 minutes` timeout, `/settings/talk` vs `/settings/model-providers`) |
| this branch | 6 files / 42 tests passed, 3 of 3 repeats |

Failures were collected from main scheduled runs 40615065526 (`fdeb8f7efd`) and 40621333872 (`dafda2f722`); `b1844ddb1d` (run 40611224841) had only the dictation and prompt-height failures, which bounds the chunk breakage to #183267 / #186323, and #186323 has no UI rendering changes.

Also: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on touched files, `tsgo -p tsconfig.ui.json`, and the related unit files (`chat-message-group.solid`, `chat-transcript-duration`, `chat-thread`; 118 tests) pass.

Gap: no new screenshots. The avatar change restores #186044's reviewed output rather than introducing a new visual, and the streaming e2e asserts the avatar element.

prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

## Evidence

Candidate: `d7b47f3a7b33d16786c766b2768df0e0f92505d4`; ordinary merge parents are the previous accepted head `41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6` and fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa`.

prs.title: fix(cli): load Unicode PowerShell completion files on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PowerShell completion installation failing to load when the Windows state directory contains non-ASCII characters, and cached completion corrupting Unicode command choices in Windows PowerShell.

## User Impact

Windows PowerShell users can reload installed completion from Unicode paths and receive the original Unicode choices. Re-run the existing completion installation command to repair a previous profile. No configuration or migration is required. Existing UTF-16 profiles keep their encoding; ASCII and non-Windows output remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows PowerShell reads BOM-less script files as ANSI. Declare UTF-8 only when the existing profile/cache writer emits non-ASCII text. Keep profile preservation, atomic publication, and stdout generation with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Native Windows, Node 24.22.1, actual `powershell.exe` 5. The command-entry reproduction used `registerCompletionCli` with `completion --shell powershell --install --yes`, a real cache under a task-only `state ü 空` directory, and then dot-sourced the resulting profile. Paths below are redacted; no platform or filesystem mocks.

```text
BEFORE
profilePrefix: 23204f (no BOM)
powershell.exe: exit 1
CommandNotFoundException: the cache path is decoded incorrectly

AFTER
profilePrefix: efbbbf
powershell.exe: exit 0
{"major":5,"loaded":true}
stderr: ""
```

The committed regressions exercise actual PS5 file decoding for new/existing profiles and the real CLI cache writer with a bounded fixture command registry, then request completion through `CommandCompletion.CompleteInput`. Existing tests evaluated script strings directly and therefore missed file decoding.

- Unmodified owner: **3 failed, 16 passed, 3 existing POSIX-only skips**; the two Unicode-path cases fail on profile reload, and the cached choice is decoded incorrectly.
- Repaired owner: **19 passed, 3 unchanged skips** across both files; 12.10 s wall time, about 7.6 s native profile test time. Native PS5 processes are necessary to test its file decoder. GitHub’s incremental CI matrix skipped the Windows job; the native Windows/PowerShell results above are local.
- Targeted maintained production/test types, typed lint (four files), formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent manual review and canonical complete five-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, zero findings; all six file/context hashes unchanged. The compatibility consumer suite had 19 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped: its untouched Windows Bash/MSYS fixture fails identically on the clean base, with no added skip or weakened assertion. Full exact-head CI passed on `4088c2c3d5cc8c2ee08cf025999f14811cf30181` (run 40628894530). Native Windows timings above are local; GitHub CI timing is not presented as a measured before/after test-cost comparison.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The two existing file producers remain the owners. No new API, setting, dependency, shell invocation in production, or wrapper is introduced. One existing profile table gains two concrete filesystem-decoding cases; one CLI-writer regression protects Unicode cache contents. Distinct open completion PRs #173223 (quote escaping) and #162918 (option terminators) were inspected and do not repair file encoding.

</details>

prs.title: feat(openai): accept Codex v3 GPT-Live voices
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: choosing one of the newer Codex GPT-Live voices (for example `himari`) for `gpt-live-1-codex` silently falls back to `cove`.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk, Discord voice, and Voice Call on the Codex route can use the 16 voices Codex added to its realtime v3 list. The public `gpt-live-1` route and its voice list are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex expanded the realtime v3 (`gpt-live-1-codex`) voice list in openai/codex#52363 (`RealtimeVoicesList::builtin().v3` in `codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`, checked at openai/codex@6ae8b8aa7c60). It adds `aube`, `bubbie`, `haetsal`, `hanul`, `himari`, `leher`, `miko`, `neer`, `porto`, `rindo`, `rio`, `rivage`, `selva`, `sonna`, `tinta`, and `viola`. `OPENAI_GPT_LIVE_VOICES` still listed only the original nine, so `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoice` replaced the new names with the default.

GPT-Live-1.1 (announced 2026-10-15) does not introduce a new Codex model id: Codex main still sets `DEFAULT_FRAMELESS_REALTIME_MODEL = "gpt-live-1-codex"` in `codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs`. So this PR changes no model ids. The public API `gpt-live-1` 1.1 is not out yet, so nothing is added for it.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-wire-profile.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver.test.ts` (rebased on main after #179894 moved the catalog voice-profile case into `realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts`): 3 files, 37 tests passed. The new case checks that `himari` is kept on `gpt-live-1-codex` and still falls back to `marin` on `gpt-live-1`.
- Applied the same list change to a local 2026.10.2 install: `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoiceCapabilities("gpt-live-1-codex")` now returns all 25 voices, and `resolveOpenAIQuicksilverVoice("gpt-live-1-codex", "himari")` returns `himari`.
- Base-fail / head-pass: with the same tests and the pre-PR `realtime-quicksilver.ts`, 2 of 37 fail (`keeps Codex v3 voices on the Codex route only`: expected `himari`, received `cove`; `publishes gpt-live-1-codex with its own catalog voice profile`). With this PR: 3 files, 37 tests pass.
- Live Discord call, 2026-10-22, on a 2026.10.2 install with the same 16 voices added to its dist (`gpt-live-1-codex`, ChatGPT sign-in route, `agent-proxy`). The speaker asked to switch to `himari` mid-call; on the second request (the first was cancelled when a new utterance superseded the delegating turn, which ends its voice-control authority as documented), the realtime session reconnected with `voice=himari` and replied in that voice. The speaker confirmed the voice changed. Gateway log, IDs redacted:

      17:53:08.138 [discord] voice: realtime bridge starting mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1-codex voice=himari ...
      17:53:10.608 [discord] voice: realtime bridge ready mode=agent-proxy provider=openai model=gpt-live-1-codex voice=himari
      17:53:10.613 [discord] voice: voice changed guild=<G> voice=himari
      17:53:10.614 [ws] res ✓ talk.voice.set 2488ms
      17:53:10.858 [discord] voice: realtime lifecycle server:session.started
      17:53:19.487 [discord] voice: realtime assistant transcript (14 chars): <"switched to himari" in Japanese>
      17:53:28.396 [discord] voice: realtime assistant transcript (13 chars): <reply to a greeting>
      17:53:30.598 [discord] voice: participant left event queued ...

  No provider error or relay failure in that session. A recorder bot in the same channel captured about 5 s of bot speech after the switch (`silencedetect` at -45 dB: 55.3–57.3 s, 60.5–60.8 s, 64.8–66.5 s, 68.2–69.3 s of an 80 s recording; the switch completed at 50.1 s).
- Separately, `OpenAI GPT-Live gateway relay failed` occurred on this host on 2026-10-20/21 with the original `arbor` voice as well as `himari`, so it does not appear specific to the new voices. It is being investigated separately and is not addressed here.

prs.title: fix: ClawRouter primaries get no utility model when utilityModel is unset
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: composer predictions, generated titles, progress narration, Activity recaps and Side chat have no utility model when the primary model runs through ClawRouter (for example `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol`) and `utilityModel` is unset. Composer predictions on the Utility choice fail with "Composer predictions are unavailable for the selected model".

## User Impact

User impact: with `utilityModel` unset, a ClawRouter primary now uses a small model from the same vendor when the key's catalog lists it:

- `clawrouter/openai/...` uses `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna`
- `clawrouter/anthropic/...` uses `clawrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`

Other vendors, and keys that do not grant that model, behave as before (no automatic utility model). An explicit `utilityModel`, or `""` to disable it, still wins. GPT-6 Luna is text-only through ClawRouter, so Side chat questions with images need an image-capable `utilityModel`. Other utility tasks are text-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic utility selection reads one `defaultUtilityModel` per provider from the plugin manifest. One value cannot serve a router that fronts several vendors, and ClawRouter declares none. Reusing the vendor plugin's own default would also be wrong: the OpenAI plugin keeps `gpt-5.6-luna` because direct OpenAI accounts may not expose GPT-6 Luna, while ClawRouter serves `openai/gpt-6-luna`.

So a provider catalog can now declare `defaultUtilityModels`, keyed by the vendor prefix of the primary model id (`<vendor>/<model>`). ClawRouter declares `openai` and `anthropic`. Router grants differ per key, so the declared model is selected only when the router's current catalog lists it as chat-capable. That catalog is the caller's, otherwise the agent's published Gateway catalog. Without a known catalog, nothing is derived. A provider with a `defaultUtilityModel` keeps exactly its current behavior. Other routed providers (OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode Go) declare nothing and are unchanged. The trailing `@profile` auth owner is preserved, and callers that pass a session's model derive from that session's vendor.

The hosted model-catalog publisher omits `defaultUtilityModels`, like `family`: the resolver reads installed manifests only, and older clients validate hosted bundles strictly.

`models status` now resolves the automatic utility model against the Gateway catalog it already reads, and `system.info` and the models preview use the catalog they already hold. The status helper moved to a sibling file to stay within the line cap.

## Evidence

- New `utility-model` cases fail on the base (2 positive routed cases) and pass with the fix. They cover the router's declared model for the primary vendor, the preserved `@work` profile and a session-specific vendor. They also cover the unchanged cases: a vendor without a declaration, a declaration the credential does not offer, a decision-only (`chat: false`) row, and no known catalog.
- Isolated real Gateway (built `dist`, test-instance helper, fake ClawRouter `/v1/catalog` and `/v1/responses`, primary `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no `utilityModel`):
  - **Catalog lists `openai/gpt-6-luna`:** `models status --json` reported `{ ref: "clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna", source: "provider-default" }`, and `system.info` reported `status: "auto"` with that model. `sessions.title.prepare` (utility-only) returned the title produced by a `POST /v1/responses` with `model: "openai/gpt-6-luna"`.
  - **Catalog without Luna:** status `source: "none"`, `system.info` `unavailable`, title `null`, and no Luna request.
  - This was a scratch proof and is not committed.
- Affected suites pass (15 files): `utility-model`, `model-catalog-normalize`, `models-list-result.*` (configured-static, openai-routes), `list.status`, `simple-completion-runtime.*`, `utility-completion.*` (including `clawrouter`), `dashboard-session-title`, `conversation-label-generator`, clawrouter `index` and `native-model-facts`. Also passing: `system-info`, `session-row-projection`, `progress-narrator`, `composer-prediction-completion` and `chat-prediction-handler`.
- Also passing: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint on the changed files, oxfmt, `check:docs`, `check:bundled-channel-config-metadata`, both import-cycle checks, `check:line-cap-ratchet` and `git diff --check`.
- Local autoreview (`odin-autoreview`, branch mode, P0–P2): scoped-clean.
- `test/scripts/publish-model-catalog*.test.ts` (3 files) pass. Without the omission, the new manifest key fails strict hosted-bundle validation.
- No config, state, Doctor or migration change, so there is no upgrade-specific path. Explicit and disabled utility settings are covered by the unit cases above.
- Rebased onto main `d79a7b6`, which includes the fixes for the previously inherited failures (#186460 for `setup-apply.test.ts`, #186409 for the new-session prompt e2e, and `8c05667`/`8ee32a2` for the chat e2e regressions after #183267). The rebase was clean; production commits are patch-identical to the reviewed ones. `setup-apply.test.ts` passes locally on this head.
- Gap: no live hosted ClawRouter call. The routing proof used a local fake router.





### Test lines

There's no baseline change. This PR's net test-line delta is −3 against main. The routed cases are new rows in the existing resolver table, and over-expanded fixture literals in the two touched test files are collapsed; no assertion is removed.

prs.title: feat(memory-lancedb): report health and serve search through the memory provider runtime
prs.body:
Related: #158822

## What Problem This Solves

With `memory-lancedb` selected, its tools can store and recall memories while Gateway memory status and provider-neutral reads report that the memory plugin is unavailable.

## User Impact

Operators get real LanceDB health through `memory.status`, and authorized Gateway `memory.search` v2 / `memory.get` calls can read the same agent-scoped store. Provider-runtime reads enforce owner-private access: other conversation audiences receive no hits and perform no embedding request. The Control UI Memories tab still needs provider-record support; that work remains in #158822, as agreed in the [maintainer scope decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165756#issuecomment-6459895626).

No configuration, dependency, stored-data, schema, or migration change. Existing memory tools and automatic recall keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This connects the existing store, embeddings client, and read-only statistics reader to the existing public provider-runtime contract. It preserves current main's service-owned database lifecycle and rechecks live caller authority after embedding and table preparation, immediately before a native read. Health also revalidates after awaited statistics, and retained readers stop when memory is disabled for their agent. Health never embeds and never exposes provider error text or private records.

Merged current main into the contributor's branch, preserving all contributor commits. Thanks @ScientificProgrammer for the adapter and original authorization proof.

## Evidence

The isolated current-main Gateway stored a synthetic memory using Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, but status, search v2, and get all returned `UNAVAILABLE: memory plugin unavailable`.

Focused checks: 22 provider/store tests and 85 related fixture tests pass; the refactored five-case store staleness suite also passes. Three new regressions fail on the pre-repair adapter and pass after the fix: health after revoked authority on both success/error, and a retained reader after memory is disabled. Extension production/test typechecks, type-aware lint, format, and required baseline ratchets pass.

Test command wall times include cold worker compilation: provider/store 25.61s; related fixtures 126.51s; final staleness rerun 7.18s. Test execution itself is under five seconds per file. Production: +342/-7 (net +335); tests: +735/-740 (net -5). The production growth supplies the new adapter; existing public tool paths are retained intentionally. Test growth is offset by shared fixtures and parameterized cases without removing behavioral coverage.

Live proof on commit `a08126ca4e1349c55a890e29cb1a4cd355110001` (macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1), using an isolated Gateway, three synthetic records, Memory Wiki as the session consumer, and real Ollama `nomic-embed-text` through a recording relay:

| Path | Embedding calls | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Owner `memory.status` | 0 | `ready`, 3 memories |
| Owner `memory.search` v2 | 1 | 3 records, expected record ranked first |
| Owner `memory.get` | 0 | Expected stored text |
| Owner-private agent search | 1 | 3 records |
| Conversation-audience agent search | 0 | No records and no native table calls |
| Session reset while `checkoutLatest()` is held | 1 | Turn aborted; no native query dispatched after release |
| New owner turn after reset | 1 | 3 records again |

The held refresh lasted about 360ms, well within the 15-second search budget. A real Qwen2.5 7B turn retrieved the record through the same Gateway path and answered “rooibos tea” (8.94s including client startup). Its initial generic request searched the tool directory; the successful control used an explicit `dispatch_action` instruction. Deterministic session turns supplied the authorization/race proof. Platform limit: local runtime proof is macOS; CI covers the broader matrix. No live operator state was used.

`pnpm build` passed (240.98s); the affected entrypoint import profile is qualified. Independent Codex review of this head is clean: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

prs.title: fix: slow Markdown previews with unmatched emphasis
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session headlines and Markdown previews can spend substantial CPU time processing long messages with repeated unmatched emphasis markers.

## User Impact

These messages now use linear emphasis scanning while preserving the existing plain-text output, Unicode boundaries, and flatten-before-truncation behavior. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared normalizer's three backtracking expressions repeatedly searched the same remaining text after unmatched openers. One forward-only delimiter scanner replaces them, retaining delimiter-width preference, earliest valid closing markers, and the existing pass order. Link and code handling are unchanged.

The scanner trades a small constant cost on densely matched text for bounded work on unmatched input. On 8,192 matched spans, median elapsed time increased by 0.6–4.5 ms; plain-text controls were approximately unchanged. This is not a universal speedup claim.

## Evidence

- Exact old/new exported functions matched on 105,768 short and Unicode cases under Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`.
- Isolated Linux proof used Node 24.22.1 and that same pinned Bun fork, with 2 available CPUs and 7.65 GiB RAM. Each cell alternated five baseline/fixed samples; input preparation and process startup were excluded from call timings. All output assertions passed.
- At 8,192 unmatched openers, median elapsed milliseconds were:

  | Runtime | Underscores | Asterisks | Strikethrough |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Node | 380.55 → 2.09 | 364.49 → 2.53 | 78.41 → 2.26 |
  | Pinned Bun | 188.90 → 1.83 | 177.17 → 1.70 | 113.39 → 2.19 |

- Standalone normalization-core package build, published-export smoke, package typecheck, and focused lint/format passed. All 92 tests passed across the four normalizer/headline/preview/ClawHub files on Node 24.22.1.
- Fresh autoreview through P3 was scoped-clean on the final two-file candidate against `d3184ac52b6a2df26a5dc6e856581f42178f3978`; independent source review also found no blocking defect. Production delta: +59/−7 lines; tests: +22.

Exact-head [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40627871082) completed with 113 successful jobs, 24 skipped jobs, and one failed Talk test shard plus its downstream aggregate gate. `security-fast` passed. The [failed shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40627871082/job/122617561168) contains three `talk.client.create` cases that dereference `agentRuntime.session.prepareSessionEntryPatch` on an empty mocked runtime. The CI report classifies these as unknown because no matching scheduled-main job exists. Independent source attribution confirms the fixture and failing owner are unchanged between the actual CI parent and tested merge; the dereference was introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186197, while the test still supplies `agentRuntime: {}`. No baseline test execution or green-CI claim is made.

Named follow-up: update the Talk test runtime fixture to provide the real session preparation contract introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186197. That unrelated fixture repair is kept separate from this performance change.

These synthetic results establish the normalizer improvement, not the cause or size of any particular production request delay. No production deployment or service restart is part of this change.

prs.title: fix(state): serve session reads during startup integrity inspection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session lists, conversation metadata, and boards failing or waiting for the full database integrity scan after an unclean Gateway restart.

## User Impact

Existing current-schema agent databases can serve committed read-only snapshots while writable admission waits for integrity inspection. Writes retain their existing deferred admission. Databases requiring schema/index repair remain unavailable until preparation completes; no schema, storage format, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup owner previously used one readiness decision for reads and writes. A synthetic 3.21 GB agent database with 10,000 sessions and a 94 MB unclean WAL spent 12.5 seconds in full integrity inspection, while schema inspection took 14 ms. The existing clean-shutdown receipt already avoids unnecessary scans; this change preserves the scan after unclean shutdown.

Read readiness is bound to the current inspection, physical database paths, and Gateway configuration. Readers retain schema, ownership, canonical-row, file-identity, and quarantine checks. They observe committed SQLite snapshots, including committed WAL, without certifying unchecked pages elsewhere. Failed preparation or a retired owner revokes read readiness. Early secrets/model publication runs under a read-only preparation scope, so notification callbacks cannot inherit writable startup authority.

Read operations that themselves require a mutation, including cold-transcript restoration and abandoned queued-input reconciliation, still wait for writable admission. Board display snapshots can read during inspection; callbacks that authorize actions retain their existing ordering.

## Evidence

A real local dev Gateway was killed during five mock-provider streams, given an unclean WAL, and restarted from built dist. The fixture has 10,000 sessions, 1 GiB transcript payload (3,214,258,176-byte database), five agents, five reconnecting clients, and 40 synthetic plugins. First-reconnect RPC timings:

| Method | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| sessions.list | 14,369 ms | 223 ms |
| sessions.resolve | 14,325 ms | 141 ms |
| sessions.describe | 14,327 ms | 143 ms |
| board.get | UNAVAILABLE | 157 ms |
| sessions.messages.subscribe | UNAVAILABLE | 74 ms |
| models.list | 13,454 ms | 156 ms |
| chat.metadata | UNAVAILABLE | 264 ms |
| chat.history | not separately baselined | 261 ms |

Candidate probes verify persisted session identity and transcript input. All finish more than ten seconds before integrity completes. All five interrupted turns recover exactly once in both arms.

Owner read readiness moves from full preparation at 18,900 ms to 3,922 ms. Full writable preparation remains 18,091 ms. Native open phases (base → candidate): integrity 12,506 → 11,952 ms; total validation 12,548 → 11,962 ms; schema 14 → 12 ms; SQLite open 1 → 1 ms; configuration 7 → 7 ms; registration 8 → 6 ms. Background migration is 950 → 1,228 ms. A smaller baseline with 256 MiB transcript payload scanned in 3,278 ms, showing the size-dependent cost is full integrity, not schema inspection.

These are startup-availability observations, not throughput claims: one request per method, no steady-state load/CPU/allocation/GC claim. The 1-minute host load was 13.52 → 12.25 during base and 15.11 → 14.57 during candidate. Unclean main WAL sizes were 94,006,072 and 106,543,232 bytes. The existing integrity scan is retained. A second restart with the bundled workboard plugin (41 plugins total) returned all nine read probes in 70–233 ms, including `workboard.cards.list` in 155 ms, while integrity took 11,745 ms. All five turns again recovered exactly once; 1-minute host load was 10.99 → 10.64.

- The real native regression fails against base source while integrity is held (resolver returns refusal instead of the expected session). Candidate uses the Gateway reader, returns stored data before releasing the scan, and keeps the write waiter pending. Missing indexes, invalid canonical rows, failure, cancellation, supersession, and escaped publication callbacks remain covered.
- Focused owner/Gateway/board checks: 122 passed, one Linux-only skip. After the final read-dispatch change: native integrity plus reader-lane and import-closure checks passed; the earlier auth/metadata checks passed all 22 tests. Core typecheck, changed-file lint, export-collision guard, and diff checks pass.
- Test-line delta is −1, including shared test support; no ceiling or baseline changed. Runtime source grows by 340 lines because the existing owner needs separate revocable read/write admission and the callers need a complete read cutover. The publication/retry path remains shared; full inspection machinery is preserved by the write-safety contract. Production plus proof-script/type delta is +450 lines. The test count remains neutral through shared fixtures and scenario consolidation.

Reproduction usage is in `scripts/perf/startup-recovery-admission-measure.ts`; no shared performance README changes.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable). The configured autoreview provider did not match the operator route; the explicitly authorized independent review found missed metadata/history callers, which were fixed and rereviewed cleanly.

The focused and live proof used the pre-rebase source on `beb12fafdee6`; the branch then rebased cleanly onto `b61ab6deb40c`. The native integrity file was rerun after rebasing: 38 passed and one Linux-only skip, including the held-integrity Gateway read regression. PR CI is the exact-head broad gate.

Initial CI run `40625489816` exposed a test typing error in this change (`it.for` timeout options), now repaired. It also exposed stale startup lifecycle fixtures: a writable-admission assertion awaited read readiness, and two publication gates assumed publication always followed writable opening. Those fixtures now exercise the explicit read/write phases. The recovered-config test retains its original assertions; its blocked RPC probe runs before injecting config because the test RPC helper republishes fixture config. The runtime implementation is unchanged by these CI repairs.

Baseline attribution used the exact CI main parent `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c`, the pinned Bun runtime, and one test file at a time. The unchanged parent reproduces both `setup-apply.test.ts` failures (25 other tests pass), both `run.shared-integration.test.ts` retry-count failures (154 pass), and all three `talk/handlers/index.test.ts` missing `prepareSessionEntryPatch` failures (98 pass), with the same assertions/stacks as CI. Candidate source was restored byte-for-byte after each baseline run. No CI rerun was used to chase green.

The test-only CI repairs passed focused validation: all three affected startup recovery/supersession cases pass (83.68 s), the other ten startup cases passed in the preceding full-file run, and the native integrity timeout cases plus the exact failing test-type leaf pass. Changed-file lint/format and test-line ratchet pass. Fresh independent review is clean. The repaired branch rebased cleanly onto `a488a29bd4ae`; this also incorporates the main-owned setup and retry-fixture repairs. Current head: `bf8d8eda6ec10e69eaba87a91c132477abe6a3d1`.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): owners can grant group chats access to private knowledge
prs.body:
Related: #186050, #186066, #186067, #98542

## What Problem This Solves

Group and channel conversations can only use their own conversation partition of an agent's Knowledge store, so an owner has no way to let a team chat read from, or save to, the agent's private knowledge.

## User Impact

An operator admin can grant a group or channel conversation **read**, **save-only**, or **read and save** access to its agent's private knowledge from **Knowledge → Settings → Stores & sharing → Conversation access**. Threads and other key-denoted child sessions of that conversation inherit the grant. Read grants also get the Knowledge index and automatic recall; grants that allow saving can also approve automatic recall (`knowledge_recall`); read-only grants refuse saves with a clear error and drop save guidance from the prompt. Removing access returns the conversation to its own partition and fails in-flight work at its next authority check. Ungranted conversations behave exactly as before.

No new config: grants are Knowledge state stored in its existing `registry.sqlite` (the `meta` table, no schema change), so they persist across restarts and apply immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Knowledge already resolves every call from the host-minted memory audience; a conversation audience carries its stable session key. Knowledge now looks that key (or its nearest `:`-delimited ancestor) up in owner grants and, when granted, resolves the call to the private partition for the granted operation. It never reads session rows. Because the grant is part of the pinned principal, a revoked or narrowed grant fails the existing live checks for work already in flight. A grant change is one compare-and-set in the registry worker and takes effect when it returns, and the settings page lists the viewed agent's group and channel conversations to pick from, marking grants that match no known conversation.

The core memory audience and owner-private paths are unchanged. Recall approval made under a grant is recorded as `approved_by: owner-private`, the existing value, so the record format does not change; history still records which agent and session wrote it.

Accepted edges, named rather than coded around:
- Write tools stay registered in read-only conversations: the feature-plugin tool contract has no per-session availability hook, so hiding them would need a core SDK change. Saves fail with an explicit read-only error, and the prompt builder drops save guidance for read-only grant keys. The pre-compaction flush plan has no session key, so in a read-only conversation its saves fail the same way.
- Granting or revoking read access changes that conversation's system prompt (index and save guidance) on its next turn; the owner's change is the invalidation.
- A revoke racing a save that already passed its last authority check can still publish that one save; unlike assignment cutovers, grant edits don't drain store lanes.

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `access.ts`: `audiencePrincipal` maps a conversation audience to the private partition for granted reads/writes, refuses writes under a read-only grant, and otherwise keeps the conversation partition. Feature and provider principals take the live grant lookup; provider principals report `sessionPrivate` (owner audience or read grant) for automatic recall.
- `store-registry.ts`: grants in the registry snapshot and a compare-and-set `grant` operation; `stores.ts` reads them from the published snapshot.
- `store-assignments.ts`: `stores_grant` operator action (operator.admin, role agent ceiling, revision check, caller-currency check before the write, 500-grant cap matching the settings list) and grants in the settings snapshot.
- `service.ts`: `knowledge_recall` accepts conversations whose grant allows saving.
- `memory-index-hook.ts`: index for any session whose principal reads the private partition.
- `conversation-access-view.ts` + `settings-view.ts`: Conversation access section; sessions are listed with the operator's own `sessions.list` access for labels and the picker only.
- Docs: stores-and-access caller-authority table and Conversation access section, memory-provider index/recall/flush notes, plugin overview and Control UI table.

</details>

## Evidence

**Isolated Gateway, real agent and model** (registry-backed grants; later commits only reorder the recall check and cap grants at 500, both covered by tests). A disposable QA Gateway built from this branch (qa-channel transport, live `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, Knowledge as memory slot, empty provider config so no host credentials or state were used) ran the full flow through real agent turns and the real `stores_grant` operator action:

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Owner DM saves "Zephyr launch plan" | lands in `private/` |
| Ungranted `#kg-room`: grep / save / index | `NOT-FOUND`; save lands in `conversations/<id>/`; `INDEX-ABSENT` |
| Grant **read**: grep / index | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON`; `INDEX-PRESENT: Zephyr launch plan` |
| Grant **read**: save | `FAILED: Knowledge is read-only in this conversation…`; private unchanged |
| Grant **read**: thread `…:kg-room:thread:kg-thread-1` grep | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON` (inherits) |
| Ungranted `#kg-other` grep | `NOT-FOUND` |
| Gateway restart, then read grep | `CODENAME=BLUE-HERON` (grant persisted in `registry.sqlite`) |
| Grant **read-write**: save | lands in `private/` |
| Ungranted → read → read-write: `knowledge_recall` | not found → `FAILED: …read-only…` → `APPROVED`; record gains `recall.summary` with `approved_by: owner-private` |
| Grant **write**: grep / save | `NOT-FOUND` (own partition); save lands in `private/` |
| Revoke: grep / index | `NOT-FOUND`; `INDEX-ABSENT` |

**Settings → Stores & sharing** (same isolated Gateway; before uses main's Knowledge UI bundle):

Before:

![Stores & sharing before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a46717d-9591-41e8-84a2-15291003d7f4)

After (one granted room, one grant whose conversation no longer exists, picker offering the remaining group):

![Stores & sharing after, with Conversation access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f4473be-7258-4d26-8e9a-bec4e34563b0)

**Tests.** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge` on the registry change: 55/56 files pass; the one failure (`publication.test` cross-process timing, under concurrent load) and `live-state` (watcher; this host is at its inotify instance limit) pass when rerun alone. New `conversation-grants.test.ts` covers per-mode reads/writes through the service, thread inheritance and the `:` key boundary, read-only prompt guidance, revocation/narrowing fencing an already-opened principal via the registry, admin/revision conflicts, grants surviving a service restart, and recall approval per grant mode including as the first call after a restart (red without the fix); `memory-index-hook.test.ts` covers index injection per grant mode for a thread; `stores-config.test.ts` covers most-specific grant lookup. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on changed files, and format pass.

Simplification: no config key, schema migration, journal or core contract; grants are one registry `meta` value and reuse the existing principal pinning and settings page.

Fresh review: local autoreview (Codex engine, P0–P2). The first revision's config-lag P1 went away with config storage. On the registry version it found one P2: `knowledge_recall` as the first call after a restart checked grants before the registry loaded; fixed with a regression. A later pass flagged that grants beyond the settings list's 500-entry bound would be saved but hidden; grants are now capped at 500. The rerun on the final head is clean.

Requested by @jalehman, with @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2429e543-7982-4d97-98a9-e1cd884488e2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/01a776c7-92f7-4399-a321-68962af05358)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman
- @Patrick-Erichsen

prs.title: fix(gateway): query fork-remote head owners for session PR lookup
prs.body:
Related: #183747

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session PR lookup shows no open PR when the working branch was pushed to a fork remote instead of origin.

## User Impact

When a checkout has a non-origin GitHub remote that holds the current branch (for example origin=openclaw and a fork remote for the contributor), the Control UI session PR row now finds and shows the open PR whose head lives on that fork, instead of always querying the origin owner and rendering nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readCheckoutGitContext` only exposed the origin owner, and `fetchBranchPullRequests` built the PR `head=` query as `originOwner:branch` alone. When the branch exists only on a fork remote, GitHub returns an empty list for that head and the session shows no PR — even though the PR is open against the parent repo.

The fix adds an optional `alternateHeadOwners` list to `GitCheckoutContext`: non-origin GitHub remotes whose remote-tracking ref actually holds the checked-out branch. `fetchBranchPullRequests` tries each head owner against the base repo first, then repeats the same owner list against the fork parent, preserving the previous single-owner behavior when the field is absent.

### ClawSweeper review follow-ups (this head `f425d0b8333`)

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| Real behavior proof through running Gateway/Control UI | **Isolated running Gateway + WS client** (loopback token auth, free port): empty lookup → fork remote-tracking ref appears → `refreshSessionKeys` resubscribe delivers PR #182621 with both `head=openclaw%3A…` and `head=huwei-xydt%3A…` through `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe`. Terminal transcript below. |
| P2: Select matching packed refs without splitting the full inventory | `listContextBranchRefs` now matches only this branch's non-origin remote-tracking records via a selective `matchAll` regex (same approach as `readGitRefs`) instead of `split("\n")` over every packed line. Covered by a packed-refs unit test (`pack-refs --all`, no loose ref). |
| Low-value loader alternate-owner happy-path test | Removed; the Control UI subscription proof already exercises the same loader queries and returned PR at a stronger boundary. |
| P1: retain bounded replacement-ref directory walker | Current tree uses `listDirectoryTreeStrictSync` for both `refs/replace` and the new remote-ref inventory. No recursive name-only readdir. |
| P2: invalidate checkout context when matching fork refs change | Context revision now includes non-origin remote-tracking ref existence for the selected branch (`listContextBranchRefs`). Covered by red-on-base unit test and the Control UI proof (empty → push → PR). |
| P2: check branch refs before deduplicating remote owners | Owners are collected first, filtered by held `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`, then deduplicated. Covered by `a-old`/`z-fork` unit test. |
| P2: restrict candidate remotes to the checkout’s effective GitHub host | Alternate remotes parse only against the checkout’s effective host (`github.com` for public origin, configured host otherwise). Covered by public↔enterprise mismatch unit tests. |
| P2: insert proof test in canonical lexical order | `gatewayDatabaseWorkerTestFiles` keeps the proof path sorted. |

Branch cache key includes the sorted lowercase alternate owners so entries cannot leak across owner sets.

## Evidence

**Reproduction (API level, before fix):**
- `GET /repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls?head=openclaw:fix/nodes-camera-list-cameras-key` → `[]` (origin owner holds no PR for the branch)
- `GET /repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls?head=huwei-xydt:fix/nodes-camera-list-cameras-key` → PR #182621 (the PR actually lives on the fork head)

**Live running Gateway + WS Control UI proof (shipped entry point + real GitHub API):**

One-off local run (not committed: hard-codes a personal fork/PR and needs a token). Starts an **isolated loopback Gateway** (`startGatewayWithClient`, token auth, free port — never the operator's live 18789 service), connects a real WS `GatewayClient` with `operator.read`, and drives `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe` / `refreshSessionKeys` against a seeded session whose `spawnedCwd`/`worktree` point at a real git checkout (origin=openclaw, fork=huwei-xydt):

1. Before the fork push: the running Gateway delivers `pullRequests: []`; no fork remote-tracking ref exists.
2. `git update-ref refs/remotes/fork/fix/nodes-camera-list-cameras-key` (simulates first `git push fork`).
3. Resubscribe with `refreshSessionKeys` → Gateway delivers PR #182621. Observed GitHub requests include both head owners.

```text
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 OPENCLAW_TEST_PRS_TOKEN=<redacted> \
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<empty-dir> OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST_QUIET=0 \
  pnpm test:live -- src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-fork-remote.live.test.ts

[live-gateway-proof] PR delivery after fork ref: number=182621 headOwners=openclaw,huwei-xydt branch=fix/nodes-camera-list-cameras-key headQueries=3 gateway=loopback-token ws=controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe refreshSessionKeys=1
✓ src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-fork-remote.live.test.ts > Control UI session PR lookup with a running Gateway (#183747) > delivers the fork PR over a real Gateway WS subscription after the remote-tracking ref appears 109237ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Committed Control UI real behavior proof (stubbed GitHub, real checkout + subscription):**

`src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-fork-remote.proof.test.ts` — real git checkout (origin=openclaw, fork=huwei-xydt), default session PR loader through `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe` / `pollNow`:

1. Before the fork push: subscription delivers `[]`; no fork remote-tracking ref exists.
2. `git update-ref refs/remotes/fork/<branch>` (simulates first `git push fork`).
3. Next poll delivers PR #182621; observed GitHub requests include both `head=openclaw%3A…` and `head=huwei-xydt%3A…`.

```text
✓ |gateway-database-workers| src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-fork-remote.proof.test.ts > delivers the branch's PR only after the fork remote-tracking ref exists (#183747)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Packed-refs selective match (committed with this head):**

```text
✓ |gateway-core| … discovers the fork owner from packed remote-tracking refs without a loose ref (#183747)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```

**Red → green unit tests (committed with the fix):**
- `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-git.runtime.test.ts`: real git fixtures prove `alternateHeadOwners` population/omission, host restriction, dedup-after-ref filter, context re-read after first fork push, and packed-refs discovery via `runGitReadOperation`. Red on base (field absent), green with the fix. 8/8 green.
- `src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs-fork-remote.proof.test.ts`: Control UI subscription boundary (empty → push → PR).

**Related suites green on this head:**
- `control-ui-session-prs-git.runtime.test.ts` (gateway-core): 8/8
- `control-ui-session-prs.test.ts` + proof (gateway-database-workers): 26/26 across the three files run together
- `vitest-cli-ownership.test.ts`: 10/10

**Validation:** oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files. `git diff --check` clean.

## Notes

- Enterprise/public host mismatch is rejected for alternate remotes so a foreign-host owner cannot be queried on the wrong host.
- Context revision stays a pure filesystem read (no extra Git subprocess on every poll); only the presence/absence of matching non-origin remote-tracking refs invalidates it. Packed inventories are scanned with a selective regex so large tag/snapshot inventories are not materialized as a full line array on every poll.

prs.title: fix: pause goals when restart recovery cannot continue
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session goal remains labeled as actively pursuing work after restart recovery definitively stops because its interrupted turn cannot resume.

## User Impact

Stopped goals now show Paused with the recovery failure reason instead of misleadingly appearing active. The objective, accounting, and history are preserved; repair the underlying interruption and explicitly resume the goal to continue.

This change does **not** fix successful automatic continuation after a recovery turn. It does not add a goal scanner or change permissions, schemas, or recovery retry policy. The coordinated restart simplification in [#185730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185730) deletes this recovery owner; this narrow repair targets the current main implementation rather than introducing an alternative redesign.

## Why This Change Was Made

The definitive interruption and tombstone paths bypass ordinary run-failure goal handling. They now use the existing goal transition and commit the pause atomically with the recovery notice. A captured-goal comparison rejects a stale notice rather than overwriting a newer goal action; inactive goals remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Six existing fixture variants were red on base `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c`: terminal recovery left the goal active instead of paused.
- Focused production recovery/SQLite tests: **18/18 passed**, including repeated recovery and a goal completed during notice preparation. Command: `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-peer-source.test.ts src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-terminal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Wall time **53.49s**; Vitest duration **51.56s**. CI seconds are pending.
- Core and affected agent/session test TypeScript configurations passed; scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Author simplification pass completed.
- Proof uses production recovery/persistence owners with controlled external dispatch, not a real-model Gateway restart. No live sessions were changed.

Reported by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2a248a5b-43ba-45b6-b683-8571fe4a20cd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/56b74b98-2dc7-4a47-a978-b3a6b8e12ba7)

## Worked on by

prs.title: refactor(cli): reuse TTY fixture in container target tests
prs.body:
Related: #171994

## What Problem This Solves

The container CLI tests maintain a second copy of the shared stdin/stdout TTY fixture lifecycle.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Container routing, error handling, proxy safeguards, update rejection, and all existing test coverage remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix: resolve native Windows Git plugin paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local Git plugin installs rejecting native Windows relative, parent-relative, and absolute paths. Also preserves an explicit `release.git` ref when a relative path is normalized and parsed again.

## User Impact

Windows users can install local Git plugins using normal native path syntax. Paths containing spaces, Unicode, and `@` ancestors are retained. No settings or migration are required. Existing absolute `.git` repository names retain their interpretation; use the already-supported `#ref` form when a literal absolute path and a ref would otherwise be ambiguous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one existing local-path classification owner for ref admission and local resolution. Normalized Windows local refs use the unambiguous `#` selector, so a ref ending in `.git` cannot turn into part of the repository path. This addresses the review’s normalized-spec round-trip finding without changing remote Git transport, consent, policy, or publication transactions.

## Evidence

Native Windows / Node 24.22.1, real `runPluginInstallCommand`, Git, filesystem and safe npm install; activation disabled and all state/config task-isolated. The local fixture contains distinct `main` and `release.git` commits. Exact terminal result fields:

```text
requestedRef: release.git
mainCommit: 96d550607741acd090566d89e7cba75e2cae36b5
requestedCommit: 81a4fbe1eaa66524688a31cbad7d197e75f4e0ff
exit: 0
errors: []
installedArtifacts: 1
```

The proof asserts that the installed repository HEAD equals the requested commit, differs from main, and the installed JavaScript exactly equals the ref-specific bytes. The command wrote its isolated config. Native proof does not independently assert durable install-record serialization or update replay; those consumers were reviewed from source. No live Gateway or personal configuration changed.

- Original native-path cases reproduced the unsupported-spec failure before repair.
- Review finding reproduced before correction: parsing a relative `@release.git` succeeds, but parsing its normalized spec loses the ref and appends it to the repository path.
- Final complete installer owner suite: **34 passed** (29.77 s wall time; about 3 s test time). A new real CLI reproduction also exposed literal `@` path data being mistaken for a ref after file-URL transport; encoding that path data in the existing source planner fixes the full user flow. Two existing staging-path assertions now use the native separator instead of a hard-coded POSIX separator, resolving their five Windows failures without weakening the expected staging basename. Native timings are local; no CI before/after test-cost comparison is claimed.
- Complete CLI preflight suite: **22 passed**, including red/green native-path → encoded file-URL → Git parser round-trip. Actual CLI fixtures additionally install `@acme/plugin`, `team@acme/plugin.git`, and a literal `repo@release.git` repository, asserting exact installed commit and JavaScript bytes.
- Earlier broad update-consumer suite: **82 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped**; all three Windows EPERM cleanup failures reproduced on its exact base. That suite mocks the Git installer; no unrelated cleanup change is included.
- Final targeted production/test types, typed lint (four files), format and whitespace: passed. Independent manual review plus canonical full four-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, both passes zero findings, all five source/context SHA-256 hashes unchanged. Full exact-head CI passed on `ca46f803ad1817d5a79913e3e806c34ae64cd721` (run 40625843299); both required ci-gates passed.

<details>
<summary>Scope and ownership</summary>

The Git parser, its existing owner test, the existing local-source transport adapter and its existing preflight test change. One private classifier replaces two duplicated path predicates; a ref guard retains legacy ancestor interpretation, and canonical Windows local refs remain unambiguous. No new API, dependency, platform mock, fallback, or additional feature. Distinct from #185333’s file-URL decoder. Inspected competing Git-install diffs do not implement this parser repair.

</details>

prs.title: fix: respect uncommitted edits during workspace setup
prs.body:
Fixes #186489

## What Problem This Solves

During pending workspace setup, the embedded runtime adds a system instruction to commit changes after edits. That instruction can conflict with a user's request to keep a diff uncommitted for review. In a live reproduction, the requested code correction and tests succeeded, but the agent created a local commit despite the explicit no-commit boundary.

The reminder is derived from loaded agent-home bootstrap files. It can also reach a selected project when limited bootstrap routing withholds the BOOTSTRAP document itself.

## User Impact

Pending setup no longer introduces a separate application-level commit requirement. Commit timing remains governed by the user's request and workspace conventions. Explicitly requested commits, Git initialization, and internal durable workspace saving retain their existing owners and behavior.

This changes no permission, configuration, schema, tool availability, or user-authored workspace instruction. Existing private Git backup guidance remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair removes the reminder at the bootstrap preparation owner. Restricting it to full bootstrap mode would leave the reproduced canonical-workspace conflict intact, while adding a command guard or intent parser would introduce unnecessary policy and complexity.

The existing bootstrap-mode integration table now asserts that loading pending setup does not add a commit policy. The workspace guide makes the optional nature of commit timing explicit. The production change removes seven lines; the regression extends existing coverage by two lines without another fixture or test process.

## Evidence

On the baseline, a fresh natural request to fix quantity-aware basket subtotals, add tests, and update the README advanced HEAD despite asking to leave changes uncommitted. Independent Git inspection confirmed an ordinary task commit. The built-in OpenClaw harness and BOOTSTRAP injection were verified from session metadata. The same no-commit request without BOOTSTRAP left the edits uncommitted; an explicit-commit control produced a commit. All three completed the requested calculation behavior and passed independent assertions.

The strengthened owner regression failed on the baseline in precisely the full and limited pending-bootstrap cases, with the unwanted reminder in `workspaceNotes`; the other 13 cases passed. Candidate checks and prompt-prefix stability passed. Fresh live after-controls on this head kept the constrained edits uncommitted with unchanged HEAD despite full BOOTSTRAP injection, and still created a normal local commit when requested. Both completed the code task and passed the tests and independent semantic assertions. The owner-path probe also confirms that full and limited modes no longer add the reminder while preserving their document-routing behavior. Live model observations are bounded behavioral evidence, not a deterministic compliance guarantee.

Candidate validation passed remotely: changed-file formatting/lint, the native selected consumer type checks, all 15 bootstrap-preparation cases, all 13 prompt-prefix stability cases, and `git diff --check`. The changed test file took 6.45 seconds wall time (about 1.44 seconds in test bodies); the native shard including worker preparation took 31.72 seconds. The hosted CI file took 12.13 seconds wall time (14.22 seconds for its shard), and CI completed successfully on this exact head.

Independent engineering review and canonical Auto Review are clean. The additional system-prompt cache-prefix suite passed all seven cases; all required hosted CI completed successfully on this exact head. ClawSweeper accepted the queued review but did not expose a completed verdict during bounded observation, and its documented public observer endpoint returned HTTP 403; no ClawSweeper rating is claimed.

## What problem this solves

Three repository validators compare the lexical command path to the resolved module URL. Running one through a directory symlink can therefore exit successfully without checking anything, even when the fixture contains a conflict marker, non-erasable TypeScript, or forbidden changelog attribution.

## Fix

Let the runtime own entrypoint identity through `import.meta.main` in `check-no-conflict-markers.mjs`, `check-script-erasability.mjs`, and `check-changelog-attributions.mts`. Remove unused imports. Keep the existing diagnostic, exit, import, and Bun-to-Node parser ownership paths.

This repairs the sibling validators identified while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186367. No shared direct-run helper, environment policy, parser, or validation rule changes.

Production +3/-6 (net -3); tests +50/-17 (net +33). Existing conflict-marker and erasability assertions are parameterized for ordinary and directory-symlink entrypoints. The changelog CLI test exercises its actual invalid-input diagnostic in both modes. Fixture roots are canonicalized before the deliberate alias is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real Node 26.12.1 probes against all three complete production owners: original direct invalid-input execution exits 1; original symlink execution silently exits 0. Candidate direct and symlink execution both exit 1. Imported helpers remain quiet and exit 0.
- The erasability control initially also encountered the platform temporary-directory alias. Canonicalizing the fixture root isolated the intended explicit symlink reproduction; no production fallback was added.
- Fresh full-owner independent review and local autoreview: clean, no P0-P3 findings. Final reviewed binary diff SHA256 `6c789e24ae3089231652bebdeafa485364d12871344c5ecae251491b01487c5c`.
- Qualified pinned formatter hook and `git diff --check` pass. No dependencies were installed or linked into the source worktree.
- [Node entrypoint contract](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#importmetamain) and [Bun entrypoint contract](https://bun.sh/guides/util/entrypoint) support `import.meta.main`. Formal focused Vitest passed: 3 files / 19 tests, bound to exact head. Targeted pinned format and focused boundary lint pass. Real pinned Bun 1.4.4 → Node 26.12.1 handoff passed 12 baseline/candidate cases covering invalid/valid syntax, direct/symlink entrypoints and quiet imports. The complete fixture has three scanned implementation files, including two required support modules. Candidate rejects enum syntax through Node's strip-only parser and reports valid-input success through both entrypoints; original symlink entrypoints silently skip. Ordinary exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628540299) completed successfully (30 passing jobs, 29 intentionally skipped). Native preparation completed against the unchanged reviewed head. No full local gate or paid test box was allocated.

No measured runtime or billing savings claim. These checks must actually execute before any optimization can be trusted. Release-owned changelog: no product behavior or public API change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI CI can report a missing collapsed tool preview while its lazy summary renderer is still loading.

## User Impact

No runtime or visual change. This repairs test readiness without changing lazy loading, preview behavior, assertions, timeouts, or worker policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

After mounting the real tool-message shell, await its actual summary module before starting the existing DOM assertion window. Use the mount helper's returned container and disposer instead of creating a second fixture handle. All 23 cases and 44 lexical expectations remain; the file shrinks from 502 to 498 lines.

## Evidence

- Scheduled main [run 40621333872, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40621333872/job/122596016679), head `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`: the exact collapsed-preview case fails with `expected undefined to be 'tool'`. The relevant test, loader, renderer, and wait helper have no source delta to this repair's base.
- A controlled hold of the real `chat-tool-card-row.solid.tsx` import reproduces that same assertion through the unchanged native one-second wait (1,043 ms). With the repair, the DOM wait is confirmed not started while the import is held; releasing the gate loads the real exports and the original assertions pass. No fabricated renderer, new timer, sleep, or polling loop. All temporary controls are removed.
- Final complete file: **23/23 passed** using the repository wrapper with **Node 24.22.1 / pinned Bun 191755ec1**. Wrapper wall time **3.68 s**; the encompassing format-plus-test command took **4.75 s**. The first exact-head CI run is complete; no rerun, dispatch, or proof-only push was used.
- UI-chat test type graph, typed lint, formatting, whitespace, and unchanged test-line ratchet pass. Independent frozen P0–P2 review reports no actionable finding.
- Limits: the original hosted import latency was not measured, and the entire 727-file UI shard was not replayed locally. The controlled boundary proof demonstrates the readiness race rather than claiming an original-run timing trace. The unrelated stdout/SQLite and other owned CI failures remain outside this patch.

### Exact-head CI and remaining failures

[CI 40627907544, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40627907544), head 6699b97ae31a431f44deb6a828bfad89aab048b1, finished **red: 22 passed, 5 failed, 29 skipped** (56 jobs). All three UI unit shards passed. The failures are four E2E jobs plus their aggregate gate. Executed job durations sum to **7,344 observed job-seconds**, not billing, CPU time, or incremental cost.

- E2E 1: dictation settings destination and reply-less-turn duration match exact main 40621333872 case/assertion failures.
- E2E 3: cold-load anchor locator timeout matches that same main run.
- E2E 4: streaming telemetry matches main 40621333872 and exact-base main 40627045980. Appearance columns is separately qualified as unrelated by complete source isolation: production, responsive CSS, settings, E2E tests and fixture owners are unchanged between the actual protected CI parent and this PR. The sole changed unit test is not a production or E2E entry. Its case passes on the untouched exact base with a fresh production build; **the CI Appearance cause remains unexplained, not repaired or claimed reproduced**.
- E2E 6: all three collapsed-reply reveal cases and selector failures match **main shard 2**. The gate's job-name-only new label compared main shard 6, which ran a different selected scope; it does not establish a newly introduced case failure.

Actual CI checkout 568c0d7a806465101c4c3a9182b77282f38264a5 has ordered parents 228596060e33dfcddbb6740416f381daac6f84fe and the reviewed head. Its complete delta is only this unit-test file. Native inherited/unrelated-failure admission must retain the red run and independently enforce writer authority, security and required reviews; ordinary passing-CI admission is not claimed.

After restoring missing pinned dependencies in this task-owned install, local follow-up passes 23/23 tests, matching types, typed lint and formatting. A filtered install initially left mixed TypeBox links; the normal complete frozen install resolved that setup failure without source/lockfile changes. No shared install was modified.

Co-authored with @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix(ui): fill the portals preview to the viewport height
prs.body:
Fixes #186396

## What it changes

The Portals page layout tracked the viewport only up to 720px: `.portals-layout` used `min-height: min(720px, calc(100vh - 190px))`, so on any window taller than ~910px the preview (rail + frame) stopped at 720px and the rest of the page stayed blank, forcing the embedded app to scroll inside a short frame.

The rule now sizes the grid from the available viewport height on every window size (`min-height: calc(100vh - 190px)`), matching the fill-height behavior of the chat pane. The rail, the embedded-mode sizing, and the mobile fallback are untouched.

## Verification

- New regression test `ui/src/pages/portals/portals-layout.node.test.ts` asserts the layout rule grows with the viewport instead of capping via `min()`. It fails on the pre-fix stylesheet (capped rule present) and passes after the change.
- The existing Portals suites (`portals-page.test.ts`, `portal-reachability.test.ts`) pass unchanged (31/31).
- `oxlint` clean on the touched test file.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #186396.

Standalone Portals stopped growing at their 720 px minimum on tall windows, leaving unused space beneath the preview. The route was missing the shell's bounded flex-height chain.

- Let the Portal page, layout and preview grow through that bounded flex chain, without a viewport-offset calculation.
- Preserve the iframe's short-window height floor and narrow one-column layout. Embedded Portals bypass the standalone boundary; permissions and protocol behavior are unchanged.

## Tests

Add tall, short and narrow browser regression cases using the default suite server. Consolidate the direct Portal page/reachability fixtures, preserving all 27 page cases and all distinct geometry assertions. The total test-line delta against the merge base is **0** (+98 layout browser, −60 page, −38 reachability). The existing **6293776** test-line ceiling is unchanged; the previous +79 increase is removed.

Focused checks on the final test changes:
- 42/42 Portal page, reachability and shell-trait unit cases pass.
- Candidate layout browser cases: 3/3 pass. The identical test against main fails the tall-height assertion, with both short/narrow controls passing.
- Changed-test lint and format, changed-CSS stylelint, and diff whitespace checks pass.

## Evidence

[Real built-Gateway Chromium comparison and rendered before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186433#issuecomment-6459946222).

Main `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3` and the candidate were built in isolated Node 24.22.1 containers. The real `portal.open` RPC registered a local HTTP application, which the UI loaded through the real Portal proxy. Two fresh tall-window browser runs per version reproduce main's 720 px layout and the candidate's 873.421875 px layout, reaching the available content bottom at 968 px. Short/narrow and ordinary-route controls are recorded in the linked comment. The runtime is unchanged from contributor head `90e711855b0ee66569bafc30d61160c4669d0617`; the subsequent consolidation changes tests only.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous layout; no state, config, schema or published contract changes. The blast radius is standalone Control UI Portals sizing and scrolling. Embedded Portal identity, permission restrictions, stale/pending results and recovery remain protected by the existing focused cases.
