prs.title: fix: continue imported PRs after destination changes
prs.body: Fixes #186442. ## What Problem This Solves A guest continuing an imported PR cannot refresh it after the author changes its destination branch: preparation tells the author to restore the old base. The existing refusal prevents a stale successful result, but leaves ordinary contribution work blocked even when the PR and head branch are unchanged and the guest remains authorized. ## User Impact Explicit preparation reconciles the PR's current destination and exact review comparison. A destination-only refresh preserves the guest's staged and unstaged edits, files, commits and branch history; it does not merge the destination into the PR head or change the destination on GitHub. Publication continues to use the same PR and head branch under the existing identity and write-access checks. If remote source work must also be integrated, the existing conflict-resolution path remains responsible for it. An interrupted refresh keeps its accepted source head while updating the destination used for review. The tool guidance directs the agent to reconcile recoverable changes from the user's intent and ask a focused question for a material ambiguity. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing PR binding already owns the destination consumed by publication and metadata actions. Preparation now updates that binding together with its review comparison instead of requiring a reversal on GitHub. The unchanged-head path selects only a review base, avoiding file synchronization and staging. Review installation completes before a finished source adopts the new destination, so a failed review remains retryable. Publication's strict live-target checks remain in place. No schema, permission, public tool argument or external retarget operation is added. The source integration and review owners retain their existing responsibilities. ## Evidence The new registered-action regression fails on unchanged production at `8f2190bb63cc8ff1cafceffbf1bb429232c1ad5d` with the restore-old-base error. It imports real Git source, saves guest commit history and distinct staged/working bytes, changes the destination, and checks the comparison and preserved state. Existing same-repository, fork and interrupted-conflict cases cover continuation with the new destination. Changed-file formatting/lint and all ten selected type-check aggregates passed. There are 158 qualified focused tests across ten files: 111 Gateway cases, eight prompt-prefix checks, and 39 tool/handoff checks. The Gateway batch took 201.54 seconds; the affected prompt/tool retry took 84.86 seconds. The first description check caught refresh guidance being offered before managed adoption; that guidance is now scoped to the existing capability. All selected hosted CI jobs passed on `1b6532ba471c3e86304c89f9dfbbc379a81f816f`. ### Live guest continuation An ordinary guest continued an owned test PR with a meaningful README documentation task, saved a local commit, and made an uncommitted follow-up edit. The actual PR author then changed only its destination. On the baseline, the agent preserved the work but could not publish without restoring the old base. After updating only the isolated preview to the exact fixed head, a natural retry in the same saved conversation reconciled the destination and review comparison, passed all 30 repository tests, and published to the same PR and original head branch. A normal read-only status follow-up confirmed completion. Native publication receipts and GitHub readback verified that the appended commit has the original head as its single parent, the chosen destination remains selected, and the title, body, author and draft state are unchanged. Published README bytes match the saved local content. The guest's HEAD, branch, index, staged files and uncommitted edit remained intact; the intended review ref changed. Current guest scopes remained limited to session read/write, and a harmless privileged read-only inspection was denied. The live case uses one private same-repository fixture with synthetic post-login ingress and the existing trusted-host Code Mode boundary. It does not claim production sign-in or hostile-code isolation. No conflict arose from the base-only retarget; newer-head conflicts, interruption, forks and revocation are covered by the registered-action tests. Independent engineering review and canonical Auto Review are clean. The matched captures and 69-second recording below show the actual natural conversation; private UI details are redacted. The clip joins the initial continuation to a later read-only confirmation; the intervening wait and status-check work are omitted, and the transition is labelled. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Baseline preserves saved work but refuses continuation until the old destination is restored\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78f3038b-6f80-4f07-8e39-252e82b6555d) | ![Fixed build confirms publication to the same PR with its new destination and saved local work intact\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54b388d6-8c01-4fa8-b5d7-a44ad9b87731) | ### Natural continuation and read\-only completion confirmation; idle interval omitted and labelled https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d575b295-72fd-4edc-9b30-5612c82e6841 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 8f2190bb63cc8ff1cafceffbf1bb429232c1ad5d - Exact head: `1b6532ba471c3e86304c89f9dfbbc379a81f816f` - Scenario: An ordinary guest continues a README contribution, preserves local work after the author changes the destination, and updates the same PR\. A read\-only follow\-up confirms publication\. - Runtime/build: Before: 2026\.10\.8\-8f2190bb63cc\-2026\-10\-28T02\-06\-13\.760Z\. After: 2026\.10\.8\-1b6532ba471c\-2026\-10\-28T02\-57\-45\.316Z\. Same saved guest conversation, native OpenClaw runtime\. - Destination and target: Same PR and head branch; author\-selected destination retained\. - Published history: New published commit has the original PR head as its single parent\. - Saved work: Guest HEAD, branch, index and file hashes preserved; only the intended review ref changed\. - Authority: Guest session read/write scopes retained; privileged read\-only inspection returned FORBIDDEN\. - Exact before/after runtime build identities verified through native hello and owner records\. - Ordinary human prompts; internal actions and assertions stayed in the harness\. - Native published receipt and GitHub parent/destination/file readback independently confirmed completion\. - Private model/footer fields and a private repository notification are redacted; primary result text is unchanged\. - The same conversation has extra normal continuation/status turns after update; no layout or latency claim\. - Original recordings are retained through assessment; the 69\-second clip labels its omitted idle interval\.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep unfinished progress visible after delegation
prs.body:
Related: #137188

## What Problem This Solves

Successful parent completion could falsely mark unfinished saved checklist steps as completed, even while delegated work was running.

## User Impact

Checklist counts, markers, and accessible labels retain the agent-authored state. A separate activity line reports delegated running, queued, waiting, failed, and stopped work across chat, progress details, hovercards, and board widgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep durable checklist state separate from session outcomes. Reuse the child roster and common card renderer, and observe board targets directly so sessions outside a bounded roster still receive current status. Failed reads expose retry; stale observations cannot replace a successor session. The owning progress-card documentation describes the distinction.

Thanks @johan-eilertsen for the original fix; contributor commits and authorship are preserved.

## Evidence

- Regression on main `364c0d4ebcd4`: the mounted card incorrectly showed completion and the browser scenario lacked delegated counts. Both pass with the fix.
- Existing focused proof: 154 tests across eight affected UI suites, UI typechecking, targeted typed lint and formatting. Mock-Gateway Chromium proof covers two running/three queued children, child failure, collapse, reload and mobile; the saved checklist stays one completed, one in progress and one pending. No real provider/channel round-trip was attempted; synthetic Gateway state exercises this UI-owned behavior.
- Exact original UI3 replay: original pre-shard manifest, native `3/3`, three workers, `bun-all`; all 728 file paths match CI on both its main parent and merge commit. The hosted reconnect failure passes on both (47ms base, 65ms merge). Merge: 8,096 pass/1 fail, 221.35s; base: 8,092 pass/2 fail, 191.06s; nine Node-only tests pass on each. Both fail the native-undo browser assertion; only base also fails Escape-focus. These are local macOS results, not Linux CI success or a claimed repair.
- Exact original E2E1 replay: original include manifest, Node 24.22.1, four workers, native `1/6`. All 134 executed file paths match hosted job 122524471573. Its route-mismatch case passes in 2.826s; 558 tests pass. The only local failure sends Control+f on macOS despite the unchanged platform shortcut requiring Command+f; that case passes in the original Linux run. Baseline weighted sharding selects a different 133-file set without the route case (542 pass/2 skip; missing local WebKit causes one setup failure). The earlier isolated ten-case route suite passes on both base and head; that narrower run is not the same packed baseline proof.
- Removed screenshot file-writing after the sanitized captures were published and reused identical fixtures without removing assertions: 37 fewer test lines than contributor head `79c379bebebe`.

Integrated current main by an ordinary merge, preserving contributor commits. The prompt-attachment E2E now uses main’s deterministic scrollbar expectation from #186409. Both that file and the test-line baseline are unchanged from main. `git diff --check` passes. Existing code review and regression/browser proof are reused for this mechanical refresh; no local suites, typecheck or autoreview were repeated.

prs.title: refactor: rename Claws to Templates throughout OpenClaw
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Use Templates consistently for reusable agent definitions instead of exposing the same feature as Claws across the product, CLI, settings, and registry integration.

## User Impact

The canonical UI is **Templates**, with **Create Template**, **Review your Template**, **Settings → Labs → Templates**, and `/templates` routes. Authors use `openclaw templates create|validate|dev|build|inspect|add` and `package.json.openclaw.template: "CLAW.md"`.

This maintainer-directed change intentionally breaks the experimental naming contract: no old user-facing command or route aliases are retained. Historical immutable archive selectors remain a bounded read contract; current package writers use the new selector. `CLAW.md`, its format semantics, ordinary-agent one-way Add, consent, and dependency ownership remain unchanged. OpenClaw/ClawHub branding, ClawPack, ClawSweeper, and mascot/theme names are unrelated and unchanged. No manual deployment or package release is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rename the feature at its owners and bundled callers together: CLI, Labs/config, catalog/creator UI, Gateway protocol, package metadata, registry-family consumption, provenance, drafts/cache paths, docs and tests. ClawHub and the official catalog are coordinated companions; this is not a second manifest format or a new template lifecycle.

Specification companion: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/79.

## Evidence

- Real isolated CLI proof completed all six new commands, including a successful Add followed by ordinary `agents list`. The generated package keeps `CLAW.md` and selects it through `openclaw.template`; the retired `claws` command rejects.
- Inspected before/after browser captures cover catalog and detail; candidate captures cover Labs and creator review. These run the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures, not a live-provider interaction. Screenshots were delivered in the originating chat before the branch push and are attached in the proof comment below.
- Feature sweep: 256 unit, 40 Gateway, 4 protocol and 83 infrastructure tests passed (three platform/filesystem skips). One warned-skill CLI failure was repaired; the final affected rerun passed 17 CLI and 7 provenance tests. The whole original sweep was not replayed.
- UI: 136 component/route tests and 23 sidebar/navigation tests passed. Catalog/detail, Labs and creator browser proofs passed.
- Full build, core/UI typechecks, scoped lint (120 core-owner and 17 UI files), feature stylelint, protocol/native generation, i18n verification and safety ratchets passed. Docs checked 16,219 links with zero broken; canonical changelog mirrors passed.
- Cross-repository schema check: the companion catalog's 150 manifests and 58 OpenClaw profiles parse with the actual new core implementation. The registry/feed bridge is being checked against the committed consumer before companion landing.
- Tested code revision: `71f1c0942ecbdc3acb5cdee311bde4c0baec75e9`; final `c0d0c2893ada9922b64c43ebd5c53868d13ce31e` adds only the checked documentation-link/mirror followup.

Broad PR CI remains the broad integration gate. Earlier local all-feature testing caught one warned-skill CLI failure; the affected final CLI tests passed after repair. Whole-repository lint was not clean and includes untouched paths; scoped checks above are the local claim, not a claim that all repository-wide checks pass. No live model/provider or deployed-product proof is claimed.


Inspected screenshot comparisons: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186457#issuecomment-6459144244. All six attached images were verified decoded and displayed in the actual GitHub PR page (1440×900 originals, nonzero displayed widths).

Current head `66d424e61a1da81d8b6e275a0e2e1b2aa78bc496` resolves the actual conflict by integrating main `97a5eb7189f07d598f256c00dce5dc680c6b62ab`. Upstream MCP rollback correctness and generated mentions fields are preserved under the new namespace. Remaining feature-only shared deletion/recovery/policy keys and CSS selectors are renamed coherently. Affected verification passed: 23 infrastructure and11 protocol cases,17 registry cases,8 browser cases, scoped types/lint/style/protocol/i18n. Initial stale provenance fixture failures were repaired and the full affected registry file passed; no assertions or lease guards were weakened.



Known inherited limitation: a real Executive Assistant BOOTSTRAP Add attempt returns `partial` / `add_failed` / `State lease worker ownership was refused`. The identical complete response was reproduced on an independently built pre-rename baseline `2e72690d0acbde9c1d8e274a0531938807102c65` with controlled naming-only input changes. Data Analyst and Incident Response real Gateway Add/readback/deletion succeeded. This change does not claim to fix the inherited bootstrap refusal or provide live-model proof.

Selected automated review route: hosted read-only ClawSweeper, with local repair ownership. Current service documentation retires autofix/repair commands, so no obsolete opt-in command or competing bot writer is used. Required CI and native maintainer checks still apply.


Final conflict-resolved catalog capture and exact-delta verification: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186457#issuecomment-6459820962. Registry/catalog companions: https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4104 and https://github.com/openclaw/awesome-claws/pull/8.


## Existing published-data boundary

A live pre-cutover check returned the existing Official Claws feed with150 published packages (versions0.1.1/0.1.2). A bounded download of `@openclaw/access-entitlement-review-coordinator@0.1.1` verified its published SHA-256 and historical `openclaw.claw: "CLAW.md"` selector without extracting or executing code. Existing shared Gateway tables also predate Labs activation. The cutover therefore cannot assume empty persisted state merely because the feature is experimental.

Canonical product, CLI and public API names remain Templates; old user-facing command/route aliases are not required. New package writers use `openclaw.template`. Historical immutable archives must stay readable without byte/digest changes, and shared storage must be preserved through its established owner or safe physical-storage projection. The corresponding reader/storage/upgrade repairs are required before coordinated landing; no production migration, package republish or data deletion is performed by this PR workflow.

prs.title: fix(slack): honor configured silence for implicit thread follow-ups
prs.body:
Related: #141556. Complements #141957; bot admission is separate (#160750 / #160752).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unwanted missing-reply notices when an unmentioned Slack thread follow-up returns `NO_REPLY` despite `surfaces.slack.silentReply.group: "allow"`.

## User Impact

Implicit reply-to-bot and participated-thread follow-ups can honor configured group silence. Explicit mentions, native slash commands, direct chats, unknown mention provenance, and default/disallowed group silence retain required replies. No configuration or stored-data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack records implicit thread admission as `WasMentioned: true` with `MentionSource: "implicit_thread"`. The existing requiredness owner now distinguishes that from an explicit request before applying the existing silence policy.

#141957 preserves authored silence in the output collector; it does not change this input classification and cannot make a required implicit-thread turn optional. This PR does not alter its scope.

Thanks to @shannon0430 for the fix and @zabealbe for the report. Sarah's #164848 changes another paragraph in the shared documentation; its tool-history and startup-context behavior is unchanged. No overlap with Pash/Sarah behavior changes.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and bundled Slack plugin in a secretless Node 24 Docker container, using a mock Slack Web API/Socket Mode boundary and a scripted Responses model returning `NO_REPLY`. Baseline rebuilt with the unchanged expectation owner at `344b71032447521feaff383f619667801dff6d83`; all other production sources in that comparison were identical. After integrating current main, the candidate was rebuilt and the same three cases rerun at `d07875a25badfee5d5a0878e27605ceb3caa9b04`.

| Input, with group silence allowed | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unmentioned reply to bot-authored thread root | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice | 1 model request; 0 replies; completed/idle |
| Explicit bot mention in thread | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice | 2 model requests; 1 failure notice |
| Native `/openclaw` invocation | 2 model requests; 1 failure response | 2 model requests; 1 failure response |

Captured boundary output (synthetic identifiers omitted):

```text
baseline: implicit modelCalls=2
baseline: reply="Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again."
candidate: implicit modelCalls=1 replies=[]
candidate: message dispatch completed ... outcome=completed
candidate: session state ... new=idle reason="run_completed" queueDepth=0
candidate: explicit mention modelCalls=2 failureNotices=1
candidate: native slash modelCalls=2 failureResponses=1
```

The implicit completion was observed in the Gateway lifecycle log, not inferred only from a quiet interval. Explicit mention failure was posted to the original thread; the native slash failure used its response URL. Both are expected negative controls, not successful-answer evidence. This is isolated channel-boundary proof, not live Slack or real-provider proof.

Focused checks: 24 tests passed across the reply expectation and existing failure-reply suites (9.31 seconds Vitest duration). Reverting only the owner made the implicit-allow regression fail (`expected required to be optional`), while the six boundary cases passed. Changed TypeScript passed Oxlint; the regression file was formatted with Oxfmt.

Simplified contributor coverage from 86 to 32 lines: removed the synthetic admission pipeline and duplicated downstream completion assertions, retaining the actual policy regression and distinct safeguards. Against the merge base: production +3/-1, tests +32/-0, documentation +1/-1. The two net production lines carry and consume existing provenance in the existing owner; no new mechanism is needed.

### Telegram Test Server proof

Also ran the built Gateway and Telegram plugin at this exact head through the checkout's Telegram E2E runner, with a Convex-leased QA user and SUT bot, actual TDLib Test Server delivery, `surfaces.telegram.silentReply.group: "allow"`, and a scripted Responses provider. A proof-only recorder extension replied to the observed bot-authored root (its TDLib message identity was checked), rather than replying to the user's seed. The baseline rebuilt only the unchanged main expectation owner.

Captured, redacted native timeline:

```text
HEAD:
  4.396s  SUT: P164877_TG_ROOT
  4.613s  user: unmentioned reply to that SUT root
          primary model requests=1; terminal outcome=completed; no SUT message
 50.505s  user: explicit @SUT mention
 52.068s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error

BASE:
  4.581s  SUT: P164877_TG_ROOT
  4.785s  user: unmentioned reply to that SUT root
  6.580s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error
 50.309s  user: explicit @SUT mention
 51.978s  SUT: Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.
          primary model requests=2; terminal outcome=error
```

Both 105-second recordings completed. Request counts above are the primary agent's `gpt-5.5` Responses requests, correlated with its three inbound turns; auxiliary memory requests are excluded. The implicit head turn reached the model and completed, so its silence was not a dropped input. The successful proof lease was released, private credential and TDLib state removed, and both Gateways stopped. Raw identities remain only in private proof; no live production Telegram or real model-provider claim.

CI on this head is blocked by an inherited failure in [checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38485509739/job/115598538462): `tombstones a redelivered source whose recovery claim is already terminal` receives `UNAVAILABLE: Session facts are unavailable; retry the request` at the session-authorization assertion. The same focused case fails identically on clean main `c8111aba15e` and this head, before the reply runner is invoked. No CI rerun or replacement push was requested.

**Merge danger:** two-way door; reverting fully restores prior behavior. Blast radius is group/channel requests with implicit-thread provenance and an explicitly allowed silence policy; explicit requests and other channels' ordinary mention classifications remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop plugin updates from starving behind a renewing lifecycle lease
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin updates and forced installs losing admission repeatedly to shorter plugin lifecycle operations, with wait messages identifying only an opaque lease token.

Fixes #167050. Thanks @itanyplus for the incident timeline and follow-up.

## User Impact

An already waiting command gets admission before later acquisitions once the active operation releases or expires. Wait messages include the recorded purpose, PID, and host. Active installers retain exclusion through npm work and settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The state lease store now records expiring FIFO intents in the existing lease table. Admission and grant remain in the existing transaction; polling refreshes intent expiry without changing arrival order. Cancellation cleans up the exact owner's intent, and crashed or stalled waiters expire after 30 seconds. Diagnostic holder metadata is separate from process-bound reclaim authority, so recording an installer PID cannot permit takeover while its npm children survive.

There is no SQLite schema, dependency, CLI option, or config change. Current main's retained-artifact cleanup checks for candidates before acquiring and repeats hourly; its 30-second startup/retry delay is not an unconditional reacquisition loop. The 30-second heartbeat keeps its owner token. The reporter's actual rotating process remains unidentified. The npm install owner already repairs and verifies the `openclaw` peer link before and after npm, so that path is preserved and checked by the live fixture.

The consumer run also exposed a pre-existing worktree capacity race under a controlled schedule: completed checkouts retained old pending-byte debt when a postcheck refused, so concurrent creates could reject each other. The bounded owner correction settles only decreases of its own existing debt on refusal. Peer debt, safety reserves, refused increases, and live commit authority are preserved.

## Evidence

- Base CLI reproduction: isolated state, no Gateway running, periodic fixture acquisition every 50 ms. `pnpm dev plugins update --all` logged rotating holders/advancing expiry and finished only after competition stopped: 250 rotations, zero yields.
- Regression is red on the base: the waiting update exhausts its acquisition budget behind `periodic-5`; the recorded holder description is absent from warnings. Native and worker success/cancellation, FIFO ordering, abandoned-intent expiry, active renewal, and diagnostic/reclaim separation are covered.
- Focused owner suite: 25 passing tests, 21.06 s reported duration; the new contention cases take about 0.4 s each. Three consumer suites caught an owner-construction ordering assumption; the constructor was factored without changing their authority assertions, then all 27 tests passed.
- Live CLI/npm proof: a loopback registry served a synthetic plugin at 1.0.0 and 1.0.1. `pnpm dev plugins install npm:openclaw-lease-fixture@1.0.0 --force --accept-capabilities --acknowledge-install-policy-warning`, then `pnpm dev plugins update openclaw-lease-fixture@latest --accept-capabilities --acknowledge-install-policy-warning` while a separate process repeatedly acquired the lifecycle lease. Isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and profile were used. Result: `{"code":0,"observedWait":true,"completedWhileCompeting":true,"rotations":294,"yielded":134,"elapsedMs":15193}`. The selected install record points to version 1.0.1, and its `node_modules/openclaw` is a symlink. The warning names the fixture purpose/PID/host.
- Selected all 86 consumer test files found through the changed lease owner. Across completed groups and focused repairs, 1,086 tests passed, six cases were skipped in PostgreSQL-tagged suites, and three destination-authority E2E cases were blocked during setup by the host volume's existing group-writable ancestor. No permissions were changed and no guard was bypassed. The two product failures found by the broad run (heartbeat retention and capacity debt settlement) were repaired; final affected replay: six files, 81 passing tests.
- Capacity proof: controlled concurrent hydration reproduces both disk-space refusals on the unchanged base. The new owner regression is red on the original capacity worker and green with the fix, including refusal of a debt increase; the same controlled service case now passes in 1.319 s. Completed-worker retention is green in 1.186 s. No timeout, retry, assertion, or baseline was weakened.
- Final checks: core typecheck, state-test typecheck, focused capacity-test typecheck, lint on touched source/tests, oxfmt, madge (zero cycles), and `git diff --check` pass.
- Slow-suite observation: the unchanged archive/worktree lifecycle file spent about 200.2 s across 20 cases. Its fixture constructs isolated Git/SQLite state and performs real archive/restore work; no base performance comparison is claimed. E2E build preparation took 3m27.8s, including 2m45.9s compilation. PR CI remains broad proof.
- Isolated Codex autoreview at P0/P1 against `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`, including unchanged cleanup/storage/worker-owner context: no actionable findings. The final complete diff, including retention and capacity repairs, passed the same isolated review with no actionable P0/P1 findings.

Production delta: +156 lines (+228/-72); tests: +177 lines (+178/-1); docs: +7 lines. Existing tests were preserved; the added cases cover distinct admission, cancellation, expiry, and diagnostic safety contracts. The full SQLite inventory check is omitted under the local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad checks.

prs.title: fix(slack): hand transport authority to route-discovery lookups
prs.body:
Related: #185972

## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. Remote consequence: a workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired; the request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

**Precedent: #185972** — `fix(googlechat): stop metadata lookups after sender authority expires` (merged 2026-10-27). Its body states verbatim:

> "Separate follow-up: audit Slack's analogous route-discovery callback handoff."

This PR is that follow-up. Same shape, same mechanism: forward the **existing** `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the route-discovery network owner; zero new validators/options/config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`):

```ts
/** Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests. */
assertDirectAdapterHandoff?: () => void;
```

Slack already implements the guard everywhere except the route path:

| Path | State before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Action path (`action-runtime.ts:276-282`, `312-319`, `actions.ts:229`) | already forwards the callback into `createSlackLookupClient` / write clients |
| Send path (`client-delivery.ts:390`) | already fences delivery via `beforeRequest` |
| Conversation metadata (`channel-type.ts:60-67` → `client-options.ts:176-190`) | `resolveSlackConversationInfo` already accepts the callback and `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts it before every fetch |
| **Route path (`channel.ts` `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`)** | **dropped it — the only remaining gap** |

This change forwards the already-supplied callback at the three route call sites, widens `resolveSlackChannelType`'s parameter type to pass it through, and hands it to `createSlackLookupClient` in `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` (that factory already accepts and fences it). The fence implementation itself is untouched; action and send paths are untouched; no other channel is touched.

Production LOC: +15/−13 (net +2 across three files: `channel.ts` +12/−12 — the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects consolidate into one shared lookup scope, which both forwards the callback and keeps this over-cap file from growing, as the line-cap ratchet requires; `channel-type.ts` +1; `enterprise-user-route.ts` +2/−1). Test LOC: +154/−5 (net +149).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — completes #185972's transport-authority handoff coverage for Slack's analogous route-discovery path.

## User Impact

An accepted message keeps its successful receipt and local history. With **current** authority, route discovery is byte-for-byte unchanged: the same requests go out and the same routes resolve (proven live below). With **invalid** authority, Slack no longer receives new route-discovery metadata requests; the route resolution fails with the authority error instead of silently completing a lookup the operator's admission no longer covers. Callers without handoff context (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`, cron delivery targets) pass no callback and behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Heads

- Base (RED): `d45ff6de6c486eb7d68931492e84af4842e02e44` (`docs: point logo work to the brand-kit README (#186198)`, current `main` at pickup)
- Candidate (GREEN): `c9dd1c0a42` (branch `fix/slack-route-discovery-handoff`, rebased onto main `dafda2f722`; production diff identical to the originally reviewed head. Red/green and dist proofs below were recorded at pre-rebase head `45b95e3f9650d22d847d1d81bcd74a1b8f31f35e`; the rebases left the production diff byte-identical. History: `45b95e3f` → rebased to `08e8c0e99c` (baseline bump dropped) → `fe08c2f4c3` (contributor-side rebase onto newer main) → `c9dd1c0a42` adds the `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` assertion alignment, see Maintainer edits.)

### Trigger reachability (producer-chain)

The stale-authority input is produced by production code, not by a test-only seam:

1. **Producer** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-transcript.ts:64`: `assertDirectAdapterHandoff: () => stateContext.workerContext.admission.assertCurrent()`. The worker admission assertion is the owner-held liveness check; it fails after Gateway restart or when the delivery is superseded by a newer admission.
2. **Forwarder** — `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:228-236`: the **only** caller that forwards the handoff into `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` (`:235`).
3. **Drop point (base)** — `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts` route implementation discards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` for all three remote lookups.
4. **Fence (already shipped)** — `extensions/slack/src/client-options.ts:176-190` `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts the callback before every fetch once it is attached.

### Red → Green assertions

- **RED (base)**: with a handoff callback that throws, route resolution still completes and the remote lookups still fire — `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` (Enterprise), `conversations.info` (D/G) — and the callback is never invoked. Exactly the 3 new stale tests fail at their `.rejects.toThrow("transport authority expired")` assertion; all other 53 tests pass.
- **GREEN (candidate)**: the same stale callback is invoked before any request and the route rejects with the authority error with **zero** network requests (stub request-log delta `[]`).
- **Legal control (no false positives)**: with a current callback, both base and candidate resolve the same routes (`to: team:T11111111:user:U12345678`, `to: user:U09G2DJ0275`) and the lookups run normally — the fence only rejects genuinely invalid authority.

### Commands × exit

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Head | Exit | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `d45ff6de6` | 1 | 3 failed / 53 passed (56) — fails exactly at the 3 stale-authority assertions | 1m19.6s |

prs.title: fix(codex): reselect first-reply binding ownership after app preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #184339. A fresh Codex conversation can reject its first reply when concurrent MCP App preparation publishes a preliminary binding after the reply snapshots an absent binding but before it acquires the binding lease.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withCodexThreadLifecycleBinding` owns snapshot → native queue → binding lease ordering. It now releases an obsolete empty selection and reselects the published binding once, acquiring its native queue before the binding lease. This applies across physical clients: actual Gateway discovery and reply startup can use different clients. Preparation still decides replacement eligibility; this retry does not authorize replacing active work.

A changed nonempty snapshot, second conflict, expired authority, and runtime ownership mismatch retain their existing failure paths. Another client's protected runtime still rejects without submitting a turn. The repair remains in the existing owner; no config, schema, protocol, SDK, or dependency change.

## User Impact

The first reply proceeds after concurrent discovery publishes and releases its preliminary runtime, including when discovery used another physical client. The regression also preserves retained same-client discovery, cancellation before native turn submission, and protected foreign-client refusal.

## Evidence

Head: `f77fbc3958896781fbd1cb286343106d0a331685`.
Named base: `80ed71747c783a099fa14fc175a8d30c5123cb4d`.

### Regression and checks

- Formal `ocpr prove --phase pre` on the named base records the exact `CodexThreadBindingConflictError` during publication, before `turn/start`; original discovery controls pass.
- The initial implementation `f249d5b` passed same-client tests but **failed** formal built Gateway proof. Diagnostic booleans confirmed a different physical client. That failed result was recorded and blocked SHIP until corrected.
- The expanded regression replayed against `f249d5b` fails with that exact conflict for released cross-client publication. The final head passes six first-reply cases, including persisted assistant output, cancellation/no turn, and protected cross-client refusal/no turn.
- Formal exact-head post proof runs the six related files below, followed by the full supported build and built CLI/Gateway scenario. All complete successfully. The native lifecycle control uses the real pinned Codex binary with a local synthetic provider.
- Plugin production/test TypeScript graphs, targeted type-aware lint, pinned formatter, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Canonical independent AutoReview P0–P2 of the final staged candidate, including complete unchanged caller/callee context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The earlier INDEX-only finding is corrected in this head.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/mcp-app-first-reply.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.adoption.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-connection.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/mcp-app-session-preparation.lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build
node openclaw.mjs --version
# Isolated built CLI: sessions.create → concurrent mcp.app.discover + chat.send → chat.history
```

### Redacted shipped-entry output

The same isolated Gateway scenario holds native App preparation while the first reply starts, then releases preparation. It observes native method calls and the persisted response through the built CLI, rather than inferring success from `chat.send` acceptance.

```text

sessions.create          success             success
chat.send                accepted            accepted
mcp.app.discover          exit 0              exit 0
binding conflict         observed            absent
native turn/start        0                   1
completed reply          false               true
reply in chat.history    absent              present
Gateway shutdown         clean               clean
formal post command                          exit 0
```

The final visible assistant response is `First reply accepted during concurrent app preparation.` Build metadata is checked against the exact Git head before running the Gateway. Processes, state, config, workspace, and credentials are synthetic/task-owned; the test does not use production Gateway/state or contact OpenAI.

Physical native contract inspected in sibling Codex `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:526–590` and `:1315–1395`. This proves shipped OpenClaw entry/ordering/output against a local native protocol simulator, plus the separate pinned-native control. It does **not** establish real OpenAI-account, deployed-service, or reporter-installation acceptance.

## Main Reconciliation and Review Status

ClawSweeper Revision 2 accepted the prior `f9e00b4` behavior proof as sufficient (`live_output`), found no actionable findings, and assessed the fix scope Complete. Its one remaining author request was to reconcile the overlapping test cleanup on main while preserving all six cases.

This head normally merges named main `fa1b6bc4c633030475345aceb4298d46822145b8`, preserving published history. The only conflict was main's `c833796fa6d` direct Promise assertion cleanup in the existing test. The resolved test uses direct rejection assertions for cancellation/protected foreign work and a direct successful-terminal assertion for replies; native turn and persisted-output observations remain. All six scenarios pass. The production adoption implementation is byte-identical to `f9e00b4`. The PR diff against integrated main remains two files.

Fresh canonical P0–P2 AutoReview of the reconciled candidate is scoped-clean, with no actionable findings. Plugin production/test types and targeted lint pass. New exact-head formal post proof repeats the related tests, full build, and shipped-entry overlap scenario; prior-head evidence is retained separately.

The reconciliation and current-head evidence are ready for review. No merge is requested or performed by the author.

prs.title: fix(plugins): sanitize file-derived IDs in authoring reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful `plugins validate` and `plugins pack` reports print the plugin ID read from the project's entry/manifest directly into human terminal output. A normally accepted ID containing control characters can therefore introduce terminal escapes or an extra apparent report line, even though the validation or archive creation succeeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing terminal-text sanitizer at those two human ID interpolations. Both JSON branches return before display formatting, and the packer's raw receipt remains unchanged. The owner is the existing CLI reporting boundary in `src/cli/plugins-authoring-command.ts` and `src/cli/plugins-feature-artifact.ts`, reached through `plugins-cli.ts`.

The current SDK `defineToolPlugin`/`definePluginEntry` and normal manifest loader accept these string IDs; normal validation compares exact generated metadata. Tightening that input contract would be a different change. An existing sanitizer already handles the presentation operation, so no new helper, dependency, SDK export, parser, validation rule, or configuration is needed.

This deliberately excludes init/build and explicit output-path confirmations, which echo the operator's arguments. It follows the file-derived-report boundary retained by the maintainer in #176007. Open #173178 fixes JSON5 manifest parsing in the adjacent authoring module and does not implement this output repair.

## User Impact

Human validation and pack reports display the ID as readable terminal text, retaining ordinary Unicode while escaping CR/LF/TAB and removing terminal sequences. JSON plugin identity, exact project metadata, archive contents, digest, activation receipt, and output path remain unchanged. No plugin is installed or activated by this change; no permissions, defaults, protocol, storage, or migration behavior changes.

## Evidence

Actual compiled-CLI RED: `18d2633de8abd677ae1852b48950701bce8ff302`. Exact candidate GREEN: `7e9b0c5af4e4e591877f8b43a9ea3ba1265321ad`, based on main `f0d422a7cb485eb19ff9671aa3a588cb4cf3a46a`. The authoring entry, metadata generator, validation, packer, SDK definition, loader, and package-entry admission owners are identical between the executed baseline and parent. A fresh check against main `f5eb9570aac03eccd09bf38d8a155d4039fc768f` finds those owners and the five publication contracts unchanged; native merge-tree verification is clean.

The same frozen driver creates two isolated projects using normal built `plugins init`, replaces each synthetic entry with an ordinary SDK-authored JavaScript plugin, and runs normal `plugins build`, `validate`, `validate --json`, `pack`, and `pack --json`. It supplies each project's own installed compiler from the checkout's existing dependency package, without downloading or changing the OpenClaw installation. Fixture paths are ordinary; the controlled ID exists only in the plugin file, never as a validate/pack argv value.

Representative public commands:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs plugins validate --root <synthetic-project>
node openclaw.mjs plugins pack --root <synthetic-project> --out <ordinary-output>.tgz
```

The two project IDs are plain `café-🦀` and a controlled string described here with explicit notation: `café<ESC>[31m<LF>forged<TAB>row<CR>🦀`, where the bracketed names mean code points U+001B, U+000A, U+0009 and U+000D. All 12 actual CLI invocations on each build exit 0 with empty stderr. On RED, validate/pack human output contains the control sequences and forged line; on GREEN it contains visible escape text on the original report line. Init/build output and the Unicode-only fixture remain unchanged.

Captured GREEN human output, with only the fixture directory redacted; `\n`, `\t`, and `\r` below are visible text:

```text
Plugin café\nforged\trow\r🦀 is valid.
Packed café\nforged\trow\r🦀: <fixture>/metadata-café-🦀.tgz
SHA256: 436f045b741ba72134b3e186cca7ff821ad997d60e077b88a85e2fd30d7ed460
Use plugin_activate_artifact with this path and digest to request activation approval.
```

Captured GREEN validation JSON parses to `valid: true`, `errors: []` and the original controlled ID. Independent readback compares that parsed ID with the source manifest's exact string, including all four control code points above. This paragraph uses explicit code-point notation because the GitHub body transport rewrites the ESC escape representation; the saved raw subprocess output and receipt hashes remain unchanged.

The real controlled archive is 685 bytes with the digest above. Both human and JSON pack commands produce byte-identical archives; a separate reader extracts the actual `package/openclaw.plugin.json` and compares it byte-for-byte with the source manifest. Its original controlled ID remains intact. The reader also checks actual package/entry files, archive digests, JSON activation path/digest, and all 24 saved process streams. It issues zero new OpenClaw CLI calls. These are real pack/readback operations, without installation, activation, Gateway, model, external API, or production state.

RED takes 41.453 s and exact-head GREEN 37.520 s. The clean source revision and `dist/build-info.json.commit` match on both runs. Frozen driver SHA256: `4a245f808345d577a57aef54ccc0698073ddf8ae28b1673b21d3cd7ebba7965a`; source/build-guard wrapper: `ad01d6e60fb9dd52ec8b6bf07ed73f2fab91d7cdc25f8cbe8e521f9daf830192`. RED receipt: `6eb5333f81c3126b7a5bac28202234323b9a5b302a4fce73506f024baef762c6`; GREEN receipt: `623336bec0f13df85ea5ef2fab5f0c70792dc77c44645b7e45d234f27acb5b8d`; independent GREEN readback: `dfcccad79c9274e3b9b4010f0d3374725c66f454fa237c05d7eb4ae6992a84f4`.

Validation:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-authoring-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-feature-artifact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm build sourcePerformance
git diff --check
```

- Both new display regressions fail before production changes. Final full authoring suite: 27/27 PASS, 138.30 s wall, including 97.605 s normal worker preparation. Artifact wrapper: all 18 native internal cases PASS, 17.35 s wall. The first cold RED run also hit an existing install test's 120 s timeout; the final single full rerun passes without changing the timeout or test semantics.
- Source-backed scoped tsgo PASS, 94.70 s; canonical typed-lint JSON PASS, zero diagnostics, four files, 293 rules, 62.90 s wall. Scoped format/diff checks PASS. Exact-head `sourcePerformance` build PASS, 303.09 s. Local verification time is not a product performance benchmark.
- Four files: production +4/-2 (two existing sanitizer calls and imports), tests +98/-8. Existing JSON-only validation coverage is consolidated with the Unicode/control cases; the native pack regression retains actual archive and receipt verification. Author simplify/test audit completed; independent review was waived by the user. The contributor identity hook stayed enabled.

Not tested: plugin installation/activation, every authoring error diagnostic, sanitization of argv/output paths, GUI terminal rendering, cross-OS, packaged upgrades, broad suites, or hosted PR CI. This is a bounded successful-report repair, without a claim that all plugin diagnostics or all terminals have been exercised.

## Agent Transcript

Implemented with Codex assistance. Actual task-scoped visible excerpt; unrelated turns, raw tools, credentials, private paths, and reasoning omitted.

<summary>Authorized sanitized agent transcript</summary>

Assistant: “另一个终端输出候选已缩小范围，排除了仅回显用户输入、维护者曾不接受的改动。”

</details>

prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve disconnect episodes during recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram accounts being prematurely restarted by the health monitor while their transport is already retrying, and accounts remaining marked connected after polling stops.

## User Impact

Polling and webhook recovery now expose one continuous disconnect episode. The existing 120-second reconnect grace can protect an active retry, then let the health monitor take over if the outage continues. No configuration, timeout, authentication, or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram status publisher owns the outage: both recovery and error updates mark the account disconnected and publish its first disconnect time. Later retries keep that time and publish fresh diagnostic objects; readiness or a new account start resets it. This preserves blocked authentication errors and the polling worker's own retry handling.

Production changes are confined to the publisher: +15/-2 lines (net +13), recording the lifecycle fact where it occurs. Existing large test files move the affected watchdog and startup cases into their existing fixture owners to respect the file-size guard.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and pre-commit autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Targeted formatting, staged diff checks, and the HEAD-relative file-size guard pass.
- Added regression coverage for polling exits/setup failures before retry backoff; watchdog recovery across transport replacement; webhook startup/registration retries; immutable timestamps and recovery resets; fatal 401/404 handling; and the existing 119,999/120,000 ms health-policy boundary.
- Polling fixtures hold retry backoff. Webhook fixtures hold retry API calls after a zero-duration backoff, verifying status before readiness and stable outage timestamps.
- Focused Blacksmith Testbox execution passed **161 tests** on the pre-integration candidate `61fdf8653f39f9b0d1e20fc75b0ebad42fe0c404`: health monitor 25, health policy 22, polling session 30, webhook 82, transport publisher 2. [Proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40541250226) verified all eight changed file hashes before execution; one worker and a 4 GiB Node heap ran three Vitest shards in 218.69 seconds. The requested four-CPU tier supplied two CPUs and approximately 7.65 GiB RAM.
- The payload passed, but the wrapper returned exit 1 when its final cleanup-status verification exhausted the command deadline. A separate read-only native status check confirmed the exact lease completed. This is preserved as a cleanup-verification failure, not reported as a clean wrapper exit; no test rerun was performed.
- **Current head `73f6c3485e8190f4e773c6917b622f1f255b6764` passed ordinary CI:** [run40628018731](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40628018731), 39 successful jobs, 27 skipped, zero failures, including the aggregate gate. prs.title: fix(msteams): preserve non-bot mention names in inbound text
prs.body:
Related: #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Teams inbound preparation removes every `<at>...</at>` span, including non-bot display names. In the reported group message, `@Bot so @Other User and Third Person can use you` reaches agent text as `so  and Third Person can use you`.

## User Impact

Non-bot mentions remain readable as `@Display Name`. Bot mentions are removed only when the matching mention entity identifies `activity.recipient.id`. Missing or ambiguous identity evidence preserves the name. This addresses mention loss only; the issue's entity-quote and forwarded-message requests remain open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize at the existing Teams inbound preparation owner, before batching, for raw activity text and HTML attachment fallback. Match entities by their text spans rather than array order; identical spans with conflicting identities remain visible. Keep the existing mention-admission decision. HTML decoding happens once, and removing an HTML bot span preserves the text boundary.

This is a narrow follow-up to @galiniliev's #102379 and the later user comment requesting a bot-ID-based mention fix. The issue's two comments and all 30 discussion/review comments on that PR were read. Its actual state is closed, unmerged since October 17; the issue's older bot comment still calls it open. The final old review reported no remaining code findings. Related quote-preview #101856 and outbound-quote #126169 are merged; thread routing #150416 and emoji-attachment #177373 concern distinct behavior. Their discussions and current states were checked. Fresh issue-number and semantic PR searches found no open equivalent mention repair.

## Evidence

The two changed source files and three production probe dependencies match base `1e89f5b3fe894352579ea7b62ed958687ef62520` by Git blob hash. A temporary source-module probe exercised the real normalizer, `prepareMSTeamsDebounceEntry`, `assembleMSTeamsInboundFacts`, and `prepareMSTeamsInboundContent`, with the actual HTML decoder and attachment extractor.

Before: the reported input lost `Other User`. After: it produced `so @Other User and Third Person can use you.`. All 25 scenarios passed, including reordered entities, recipient mismatch or absence, missing entity data, same-name distinct spans, ambiguous identical spans, tag case, multiline labels, one-time entity decoding, literal encoded tags, raw-text precedence, HTML text boundaries, empty labels, bot-only input, and ordinary text. The mention-admission result matched baseline in every scenario. Independent review and a second execution passed; the final boundary additions were reviewed and rerun as well. Changed-file formatting and whitespace checks passed. Source delta: +42/-7 across two files.

**Draft / remaining validation:** The probe substitutes media, Graph, persistence, and other surrounding dependencies. It does not exercise a Gateway, a live Teams tenant, real debouncer flushing, or final model delivery. No test files were added or changed, and no build, full test suite, or project typecheck was run. The local `oxlint` executable was unavailable. These validation gaps remain before marking ready.


**Review follow-up:** The subsequent review identified three existing `inbound-facts.test.ts` fixtures that expect `<at>Bot</at>` to disappear without recipient/mention identity data. Those fixtures need explicit matching bot identity to exercise the new intended contract; missing identity deliberately preserves `@Bot`. This is a source-inspection finding, not a locally observed test run. Test files remain unchanged under the task constraints, so this compatibility work and the integration-proof gaps above remain open.

prs.title: fix(cron): trigger conditions time out forever when runtime preparation exceeds the trigger budget
prs.body:
Closes #184358

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cron `trigger.script` condition times out on every tick, and stalls the Gateway for ~30 s each time, when preparing its runtime takes longer than the 30 s trigger budget.

## User Impact

User impact: on slower hosts, trigger conditions start evaluating after one warm-up timeout instead of failing forever, and the Gateway no longer blocks its event loop on the same cold plugin load every interval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trigger runtime preparation was tied to the deadline of the evaluation that started it. When the deadline passed, the preparation was aborted and evicted, so the next tick started the same cold load again and could never finish inside 30 s.

Preparation now follows only the caller's cancellation, plus its own limit of `max(120 s, script budget)`. A missed deadline keeps the preparation cached so the next tick reuses it. Cancellation still starts cold, and a preparation that outlives its limit is evicted even if it ignores its signal (a late result is disposed through the existing runtime lifetime). A later caller's cancellation does not discard shared preparation, matching the existing cache-hit path.

This does not make plugin loading itself asynchronous; plugins that cannot be borrowed from the Gateway registry still load synchronously once.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway proof (after fix vs. `main`).** Isolated Gateway from this source checkout (separate `--profile`, loopback port, no channels) on Jetson AGX Xavier, Node 24.22.1. One job: `every 1m`, command payload, condition `return { fire: false, state: { at: Date.now() } }`. To get a preparation slower than the 30 s budget on demand, I added a local, uncommitted 35 s `await` right after the plugin registry load in `prepareTriggerRuntime` (it logs `[proof] simulating a slow trigger preparation`). Fresh job state for each run; timestamps are KST.

| Build | Preparations | Scheduled ticks |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (92f5a947) | every tick: 18:29:04, 18:30:05, 18:31:35 | all `error` / `timeout` (32768, 30058, 30087 ms); `consecutiveErrors: 3`, after which error backoff stops evaluating |
| this PR (548d052a) | once: 19:04:29 | first tick `timeout`; then evaluated every minute with no further preparation: `triggerEvalCount: 7`, `consecutiveErrors: 0`, trigger state updated through 19:10:30 |

<details>
<summary>Redacted Gateway output</summary>

```
# main
18:29:04.957 [proof] simulating a slow trigger preparation (async): 35000ms
18:30:05.047 [proof] simulating a slow trigger preparation (async): 35000ms
18:31:35.232 [proof] simulating a slow trigger preparation (async): 35000ms
runs: 18:29:01 error timeout 32768 | 18:30:04 error timeout 30058 | 18:31:35 error timeout 30087
state: {"triggerEvalCount": 22, "consecutiveErrors": 3}

# this PR (fresh job)
19:04:29.875 [proof] simulating a slow trigger preparation (async): 35000ms
(no further [proof] lines)
state at 19:10:34: {"triggerEvalCount": 7, "consecutiveErrors": 0, "triggerState": {"at": "19:10:30"}}
```

With a synchronous 35 s block in the same place (closer to the original 31 s plugin load), `main` repeated the blocking preparation on two consecutive ticks before a microtask ordering let one finish ahead of its abort; this PR blocked once.

</details>

**Tests and checks**

- Focused tests in `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`:
  - `reuses a preparation that outlives its first evaluation's deadline`: fails on `main` (preparation runs twice), passes with this change.
  - `keeps preparation past the trigger deadline and evicts it at its own limit`: fails on `main` (signal aborted at 30 s), passes with this change.
  - `keeps shared preparation when a later waiter is cancelled`, `lets a script payload prepare for its whole budget`: cover the remaining paths.
  - Existing `starts cold after cancellation without waiting for the old preparation to settle` still passes.
- `pnpm test src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.22.1, aarch64): 25/26 pass with this change; on `main` the three new deadline tests fail. `src/cron/trigger-script.plugin-reload.test.ts`: 3/3 pass.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean. `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host (the `tsrs` binary needs glibc 2.33+); `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no errors in the touched files. Relying on PR CI for the full typecheck.
- Live observation that motivated the change (OpenClaw 2026.10.7, Jetson AGX Xavier, 1-minute trigger job): every tick logged `loaded 17 plugin(s) (2 attempted) in ~31000ms`, `liveness heartbeat delayed`, then `cron trigger evaluation failed (timeout)`. Details and redacted logs are in the linked issue.

<details>
<summary>Local test environment note</summary>

On this aarch64 host, `honors current host auto for a canonically captured pinned exec cap` fails with `service child cleanup identity lost` both with and without this change; it exercises native exec process supervision, not trigger preparation.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Kubernetes-hosted Gateways log a warning that "another supervisor may be managing this Gateway" after routine Pod deletes, and log `failed to handle SIGTERM: Error: OpenClaw state process owner is no longer current` at error level when a Pod is deleted during a config-triggered in-process restart, even though the Gateway stops cleanly.

## User Impact

User impact: operators running the Gateway under Kubernetes (or with `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external`) no longer get pointed at a competing supervisor that does not exist, and a stop that lands during an in-process restart no longer looks like a failure. Shutdown and restart behavior is unchanged; other SIGTERM handler failures still log at error, and native/unmanaged installs keep the existing hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The cross-lifetime stop count lives in the shared state database, so on a persistent volume every Pod replacement counts. Under a declared platform supervisor (Kubernetes, or `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external`; the same check Doctor already uses to skip service management) the count is logged at info without the competing-supervisor hint. The check moves into `resolveGatewayPlatformSupervisor` and Doctor reuses it.
- During an in-process restart the closing iteration releases Gateway state before the next one acquires it. A SIGTERM in that window cannot read a durable restart intent, and the handler already falls back to stop. That exact case (SIGTERM accepted during shutdown and the state owner reported as retired) now logs at info. The owner-retired error gets a shared constructor/predicate; its message is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source-built Gateway on a remote test VM, `gateway run` on loopback, before (current main) vs after (this branch):
  - Three plain SIGTERM stops on one state dir: without Kubernetes env, both builds log `stopped after SIGTERM 3 times in 5 min: another supervisor may be managing this Gateway` (hint kept). With `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST/PORT` set, main logs the same warning; this branch logs `[lifecycle] stopped after SIGTERM 3 times in 5 min (Kubernetes manages this Gateway)` at info.
  - `config set gateway.controlUi.basePath` (restart-requiring), SIGTERM as soon as `restart mode: in-process restart` is logged (2 runs per build): main logs `failed to handle SIGTERM: Error: OpenClaw state process owner is no longer current`; this branch logs `received SIGTERM after shutdown released Gateway state; stopping without a restart intent`. Both then log `received SIGTERM during shutdown; finishing shutdown without restart` and exit.
- New tests fail on main and pass here: `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.test.ts` (Kubernetes and external supervisor cases), `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` (`stops quietly when SIGTERM finds state released by an in-place restart`; plus a guard that the same error outside shutdown stays at error level).
- Passing: `pnpm test` on `gateway-boot-lifecycle`, `run-loop` (168 tests), `doctor-service-repair-policy`, `gateway-state-owner`; `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`; format and oxlint on touched files.

prs.title: fix(slack): record explicit top-level sends in source sessions
prs.body:
Related: #142037

## What Problem This Solves

An explicit top-level Slack send can succeed in the current channel yet fail to record source delivery because the inbound context also contains an automatic reply anchor.

## User Impact

Standalone channel replies are recorded as delivered. Real thread sessions, bound threads, and callers without an admitted scope remain conservative; ordinary replies to the automatic anchor still match.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep conversation scope separate from the transport reply anchor. Derive scope once from the admitted message-action capability, with recovery fallback only when a private source-turn identity exists, and carry it through the current renamed terminal hook and subscription completion. Root receipts use conversation scope; nonempty thread receipts still compare against the actual transport anchor.

## Evidence

### Current validation — October 28

Merged main `01a33a2b399eec12746d550164bc4bd4214e3986` in `edd503f564fc4f57c994f8b8e7d334c5a9bdb6dc` to resolve the session-preparation import conflict. This preserves main's model-window initial-context reader and the direct `SessionManager` import used by this patch. Main independently absorbed the exact prior `ClientToolPreparation` erased type inline. All other authored added/deleted edit sequences across the 21 files are unchanged; no source-reply behavior was added during this refresh.

- Fresh isolated Linux CPU, Node 24.22.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0: **99 tests across three affected files pass** (session preparation, stream preparation and source-reply classification), through the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`, in **44.78 seconds wall**. These exercise the current preparation/steering consumers and fixed-adapter source-reply boundaries; they are not live Slack E2E.
- All 21 authored files pass formatting, and `git diff --check` passes. Combined type-aware lint/type checking reports the **same 5 declaration portability diagnostics as complete pinned-main source in the same environment**, with no candidate-only diagnostics. This check remains **not fully green**. All overlaid source hashes are verified against the staged candidate; the control uses complete pinned-main source.
- The October 25 canonical scoped P0–P2 review is reused under the mechanical-refresh policy. The authored runtime/test edit sequences remain identical, with only the exact upstream-absorbed erased type inline dropping out of the PR diff. This is review reuse, not a fresh review claim.
- Prior head `58852975897e1785c37b5745449aca34bdfb00c6` completed hosted CI with **72 successful checks, 53 skipped and one neutral**, including successful CI/security/dependency gates ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40464731408)). **New-head CI is separate and is not claimed complete here.** The October 27 98-test result and older results below remain prior-head evidence. The existing live-Slack limitation remains: no qualified Convex login/leased QA driver–SUT route for this task.

### October 26 validation (historical)

Merged main `b22db9cddd288692cf0278a29b717e3e6c137942` in `f96245805e19e6d65933e9f0b043881b5399b6a8` to resolve the new Gateway fixture conflict. Main narrowed the catalog-executor test interface to `activeSession`; the resolved Gateway test is byte-for-byte main, so its obsolete PR-only fixture field disappears from this diff. The other **20 files retain identical authored added/deleted edit sequences** relative to their respective main bases. This refresh adds no delivery or thread-policy changes.

- Isolated Linux CPU, Node 24.22.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0: **69 tests pass across three affected files** (Gateway direct-command steering, source-reply classification and stream preparation), using the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`, in **65.72 seconds wall**. The Gateway lane took 26.63 seconds and the two agent/infra files 14.00 seconds; per-file hosted CI cost has not been measured. The Gateway tests exercise actual isolated RPC steering/queue ownership, rather than only the fixture helper.
- Formatting passes for the 20 authored files and the unchanged Gateway test; the introduced diff passes `git diff --check`. Combined type-aware lint/type checking reports **the same five Vitest declaration portability diagnostics on candidate and complete pinned-main source**, with no candidate-only errors. That check remains **not fully green**. Every overlaid source hash and the unchanged Gateway test hash were verified after the control source was restored.
- Reuse the October 25 canonical P0–P2 review for this mechanical refresh: its authored edit sequences are unchanged and the superseded Gateway fixture change is removed. The 291-test result and independent review in the next section are explicitly prior-head evidence, not a new 291-test run.
- Current head `f96245805e19e6d65933e9f0b043881b5399b6a8` has completed hosted CI: **72 successful checks, 53 skipped and one neutral**, with successful `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive and dependency-review statuses ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40226117303)). All current-head checks are terminal. Local validation remains the 69-test run described above; the broader 291-test run below is prior-head evidence. Fresh live Slack/Gateway E2E retains the limitation described below.

### October 25 validation (historical)

Merged main `3672bd28a26f8fa7bd3bafcb253ec585c9cf020e` in `4c40135df6b3fed5b4105051be2d5abfd265131e` to resolve four conflicts. Kept main's session/projection recovery and stream changes, its removal of the old large execution-phase test, and its shared Slack fixture. The existing forwarding assertion now lives in the retained watchdog-recovery test; the fixture still returns the send mock needed by the delivery regression. No thread-isolation or delivery policy was relaxed.

The merged preparation owner exceeded its existing 700-line limit. The same source-thread selector now lives in the existing message-terminal owner and is invoked at the same point, after session preparation awaits and immediately before hook installation. Capability binding, explicit false, recovery fallback and the original input object's private source-turn facts are unchanged. Inlining a single-use erased type alias keeps preparation within the unchanged limit.

- Isolated Linux CPU, Node 24.22.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0: **291 tests pass across nine files**, through the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`, in 83.49 seconds wall. Combined type-aware lint/type checking still reports **five diagnostics** in main's two test-support owners: four TS2883 declaration portability errors involving Vitest's Procedure and one TS4058 involving Constructable.
