- Fresh canonical autoreview, using same-host Claude Opus 4.8 after both configured Codex models were unavailable, completed both passes with **no P0–P2 findings**. The final single-use type alias inline is an equivalent erased-type cleanup after that review. Source inspection also confirms the unchanged session-thread parser accepts a missing session key.

Current-head hosted CI is separate from these local results. **Fresh live Slack/Gateway E2E has not been run**: the existing Convex login and leased driver/SUT route remain unavailable. The older live transport proof and October 19 review below remain historical.

### October 19 validation (historical)


Merge repair `72f5cc876e3c51d1c8a3428536970c3747d2ddce` incorporates main `ecb279c9b54a335803b4bda5f8753403790bfd4d` to resolve the new conflicts. Retained its physical-store stream-owner test, sandbox separation, and shared billing fixture. Restored the existing Slack fixture's send-spy return after upstream's helper refactor, preserving the dispatch and source-route assertions. A namespace import of the existing source-turn owner and an inlined one-use capability read keep the file within its existing size gate, without adding a wrapper or changing the admitted-scope fallback.

- Isolated Linux, Node 24.16.0, frozen pnpm 12.11.1: **284 tests pass across nine files**, using the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1` (70.84 seconds wall). After the mechanical capability-read/import cleanup, the final preparation owner passes its 27-case replay (25.50 seconds wall); other tested production inputs are unchanged. This covers the real `runMessageAction` boundary, route classification, admitted-scope preparation, terminal hooks, subscription completion, CLI tracking, and both conflicted test owners.
- Replacing only the classifier with the pinned main implementation reproduces the standalone-channel failure: **1 failed, 13 passed**. Bound/unknown controls stay passing; candidate bytes were restored and verified.
- Final formatting and type-aware lint with type checking pass for all 20 changed files (0 warnings/errors); `git diff --check` passes. Fresh independent canonical autoreview on the final frozen source returned `scoped-clean` for P0–P2, with no actionable findings (same-host configured Claude Opus route). Its patch-bearing pass reviewed the full diff; the other partition contained Git-status metadata. Unchanged helper contracts and fresh live Slack E2E remain the stated limits.

This is current channel-boundary proof with fixed test adapters. **Fresh live Slack/Gateway E2E has not been run**: this task has no qualified Convex login/leased QA driver–SUT route. The September live controls below remain historical. Current-head hosted CI and its job seconds still need to complete; this update does not claim those gates passed or that earlier unrelated-looking failures were attributed.

Simplification keeps the existing route-classification owner and one admitted scope; it adds no manager, schema, or parallel delivery path. The obsolete inline billing fixture propagation disappears into main's shared fixture. Against the pinned merge base: production +38/-4, tests/fixtures +391/-2 across 20 files.

<details>
<summary>Historical verification on earlier revisions (not current-head proof)</summary>

### October 17 validation (historical)
### Current Validation — October 17

Merged main `b46ec6167975f57fa33cc298e78c8338ae59746e`, preserving its renamed terminal hook and test reorganizations. The delta is 21 files, +427/-6 (including existing fixture propagation).

- Isolated Linux, Node 24.16.0, frozen pnpm 12.11.1: 251 tests pass across seven source-reply, action-execution, admission, stream, terminal-hook, subscription, and CLI tracking files through the repository wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1` (69.73 seconds wall). After formatter-only cleanup, both affected files pass a further focused 61-test run (16.44 seconds wall).
- The real `runMessageAction` boundary covers standalone, bound, and unknown scopes. Replacing only the route classifier with unchanged main reproduces the standalone-channel failure (1 failed, 13 passed), while bound/unknown controls remain passing. Candidate bytes were restored and verified.
- Pinned formatting, type-aware lint with type checking, and scoped diff checks pass. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

This is channel-boundary proof with test adapters, not a fresh live Slack session or full hosted CI pass. Earlier live/CI investigations and measurements below belong to their named revisions; current-head CI still needs to complete.



Related: #142037

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicit top-level Slack send can be treated as a different conversation when the inbound context also carries a synthesized reply anchor.

## User Impact

User impact: `message_tool_only` replies sent explicitly to the current Slack channel are recorded as delivered instead of being left as a mute terminal turn, while real thread-root sessions remain isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

For `topLevel: true`, delivery placement now compares the receipt with the thread identity parsed from the admitted session key. This avoids treating `currentThreadTs`, which may be an auto-reply anchor, as proof that the admitted conversation itself is threaded. Bound Slack thread sessions can intentionally use an unsuffixed session key, so the classifier also preserves `sameChannelThreadRequired` as the authoritative fallback. Session preparation resolves that fact once from the admitted message-action capability (or host recovery context); both the installed terminal hook and subscription completion consume it. Callers without an admitted fact remain conservative: only an explicit `false` allows clearing a transport reply anchor, so older CLI callers cannot acquire new false source-completion evidence.

## Evidence

The original reviewed PR head fails the new unsuffixed bound-thread classifier regression (`expected false`, `received true`; 1 failed and 14 passed). A classifier-only correction also fails the bound-thread installed-hook regression (1 failed and 27 passed). The final installed-hook behavior proof checks that a standalone channel final send records delivery exactly once and returns `terminate: true`, while suffixed and unsuffixed bound thread sessions record no source delivery and do not terminate.

Revision 3's reviewed head `facfc9b6d24ba5fec7940770f6016a23fd644efb` also fails the new subscription completion regression (1 failed, 2 passed, 195 unrelated cases skipped): a settled parent-channel send from an unsuffixed bound thread incorrectly records `sourceReplyFinal: true`. The corrected completion handler preserves the send evidence without setting that final marker, the message-tool-only source-delivery state, normalized source-reply suppression text, or the shared delivered callback. A CLI lifecycle regression independently fails before the conservative unknown-fact correction and passes afterward. Session, execution-phase, and stream tests cover the admitted-fact propagation seams, including distinct policy/transcript session keys and admitted `false` overriding a recovery `true`.

The corrected candidate passes:

```text
source-reply-mirror.test.ts + message-tool-terminal.test.ts + tool-media-payloads.test.ts
message-action-execution.source-reply.test.ts + embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts
message-action-turn-capability.test.ts + attempt-session.test.ts
attempt-execution-phase.test.ts + attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts
embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts + cli-runner/execute-tool-tracking.test.ts
embedded-agent-subscribe.lifecycle-billing-error.test.ts + cron/isolated-agent/run.terminal-lifecycle.test.ts
428 passed across 13 files

oxfmt --check: passed
oxlint --deny-warnings: 0 warnings, 0 errors (230 rules)
pnpm tsgo:prod: passed
pnpm tsgo:test:root: passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test --stripe 1/1 --concurrency 2: passed (all 19 core-test graphs)
```

Validated candidate `7ac1347296fd5699a9bc9e227e512577ee26057a` on Linux with Node 24.16.0 and pnpm 12.3.4 against base `8cdb0d6df06bffcc4f407ad1dbf3598792814a8d`. The full 428-test replay, changed-file formatting/lint and all 19 core-test graphs pass on this candidate. Production and root-test typechecks passed on the preceding `a6b73145fa1b03f7fdbe1a43c506b25f12eafc20`; this follow-up changes only three test fixtures, with no production changes.

The two hosted core-test stripes exposed obsolete `sandboxSessionKey` arguments in the billing and cron lifecycle fixtures. Both are now removed; the admitted-fact session fixture also avoids spreading an existing `never`-typed fixture. No assertions were weakened. Revision 6 reviewed this exact candidate with no actionable code findings, while retaining the unexplained recursive-spawn CI failure and live Slack proof as merge risks.

Hosted CI is not green: the latest observed checks include 174 successes and two failures, consisting of [one recursive-spawn boundary test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34929273844/job/104254086366?pr=148721) and the aggregate gate. The complete job log identifies Node 24.20.0 and synthetic merge `0bcd0f580a2d6d168374f20bf4bfc4e1eedd538b`, with then-main parent `fe8d383796f73e3b983198f19581af1273631e7e`; the previous Node 24.16 PR-head/base focused runs are not an equivalent CI comparison.

The repository CI wrapper replayed the complete 10-case production-boundary file in original file order on those frozen merge/main inputs. As root, merge passed 10/10 and main failed the original line-449 assertion (1 failed, 9 passed). In a separate task-owned copy as existing nonroot uid/gid 65534, merge failed that same assertion (1 failed, 9 passed) and main passed 10/10. Node 24.20, max workers 3 and an 8192 MiB heap budget were pinned; nonroot runs set both CI/GHA flags. These sequential single-run pairs reverse outcome, so the cause remains unresolved: neither an unrelated-CI claim nor a PR-introduced-defect claim is established. Scoped Git blob verification covered all merge-overlay and PR-control paths plus runner/runtime manifests (83 blobs), and candidate source was restored after each main comparison.

Exact original ordered-prefix attempts stopped in the preceding Gateway group before reaching spawn, on both inputs. Even after task-local Git/rsync extraction, both attempts reported 7 failed / 217 passed / 1 skipped files and 18 failed / 3559 passed / 2 skipped cases; this is matching aggregate statistics, not proof that every failure has the same cause. Remaining local issues include native-tool compatibility/library resolution and root-owned worker rejection. The replay host differs from GitHub's runner. No timeout, retry policy, assertion, runtime guard or unrelated source was changed; no successful complete-prefix replay or hosted CI rerun is claimed.

The earlier frozen-lockfile dependency install encountered a Matrix native-library download reset; linking was completed with lifecycle scripts disabled for those pure-logic tests. This installation limitation is separate from the hosted spawn failure.

### Real Slack transport validation — September 15

The exact candidate `7ac1347296fd5699a9bc9e227e512577ee26057a` was subsequently started through the supported CLI in task-owned Linux state, with a dedicated, explicitly authorized Slack app and test channel. A deterministic loopback Responses provider selected normal advertised tool calls; the unmodified embedded runtime and Slack transport executed them. This uses real Slack receipts, not fabricated transport results or paid inference, and is transport/lifecycle proof rather than model-quality proof.

- **Ordinary channel positive control:** a real standalone ingress with `requireMention:false` and `replyToMode:off` entered an unsuffixed channel session. A `message` send with `topLevel:true`, `final:true` visibly reached the parent channel; its real receipt matched the UI platform identity and reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. Supported history and a bounded read-only query of the existing native run-outcome table paired that exact run/session/model with `tool_delivered/completed`, no active run and no pending input.
- **Genuine-thread paired control:** a real Slack thread reply entered the actual suffixed source session under per-channel `replyToMode:all`. Its first `topLevel:true`, `final:true` send visibly reached the parent channel with a receipt containing no thread identity and no current-source route marker. That successful result did **not** end the run: the same source run issued a second tool call, omitting `topLevel` and `threadId`. Normal routing inherited the original Slack thread; its real receipt and thread UI identity matched and the result reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. The exact thread run/session/model subsequently recorded `tool_delivered/completed`, with no active run or pending input.

The first ordinary-input attempt uncovered only a fixture bug: the Responses adapter appends a protected internal-context user carrier after the actual user. It produced probe text without a tool send and is not counted as a pass. The live fixture now skips only that complete carrier envelope on verified version-4 sessions; its 14 secretless protocol regressions pass. The successful ordinary case and the single genuine-thread case were independently reviewed. No production source, tool schema, admission check, timeout or assertion was changed to produce the live results. Credential values, private Slack identifiers and raw platform timestamps are intentionally omitted.

**Remaining limits:** the unsuffixed runtime-bound-thread case still has deterministic classifier, installed-hook and subscription regressions, but no live transport proof. Missing current-source route markers are observed result markers, not direct captures of subscription booleans or hook exactly-once internals. Ordinary message-tool display mirrors are not asserted to be durable final delivery mirrors. The unexplained hosted spawn failure remains unresolved; these live Slack controls do not make CI green or establish an unrelated-failure diagnosis.

### Current-main update — September 24

The preceding CI and live-transport notes are historical evidence for head `7ac1347`. This branch now merges current `main` at `6c513528` in non-force commit `0b405858`. The nine merge conflicts were resolved against the refactored `agentSession` flow while preserving propagation of `sameChannelThreadRequired`. GitHub reports the current head as mergeable.

On Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.4.2, focused execution-phase (23/23), source/session/stream (98/98), terminal (28/28), CLI (8/8), and new Slack completion (3/3) checks pass. Core and root-test typechecks, changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, and diff whitespace check pass. The broader subscription-handler file had 215 passes and three `ask_user` start-path failures (two missed callbacks, one timeout); without a same-main control replay, their cause is not attributed. The scoped independent review found no actionable P0/P1 issue. The first hosted run on `0b405858` found a missing `sameChannelThreadRequired` field in the merged billing test fixture. Follow-up `8dd2ab04` adds `false` to that fixture; the direct agents-root typecheck and `git diff --check` pass. The same hosted run also had a canceled architecture job and a failing subagent admission test outside the changed paths; neither is attributed yet without a same-main comparison. Local Vitest and oxfmt are blocked by Windows Application Control on the native Node binding. Hosted CI on `8dd2ab04` has finished and is not green. Typechecking passed, but three test shards failed in subagent completion admission, gateway send/resume, and outbound reconnect-drain; the aggregate gate also failed. These failures are outside this PR's changed paths, but without a same-main control run I am not attributing them to infrastructure or to this PR. No unrelated assertions or production code were changed to mask them.

### Current-main maintenance — October 1

Merged current main (00f3a206302), preserving the recipient/account/physical-part checks and the extracted test fixtures. Replaced the retired thread-info wrapper with its existing loaded-plugin owner. Independent scoped review found no remaining material issue. Linux / Node 24.16 / pinned pnpm 12.5.1: 309 tests pass across six affected files; formatting and type-aware lint pass for all 19 changed files. Five-file run: 113.6s wall; handlers file: 45.7s wall (about 4s test work, most time is compiler/import setup). Windows tooling was blocked before tests, so these are Linux boundary tests, not a live Slack claim.

### CI follow-up — October 1

Fixed the two missing sameChannelThreadRequired fields in the Gateway/cron test fixtures. Both affected tsgo projects, formatting and type-aware lint pass; Linux Node 24.16 runs pass 2 Gateway + 23 cron tests (100.99s / 53.20s including setup). The hosted worker reclaim/force-abandon failures are in unchanged tests and owners; no Slack causal path was found, but a failing main reproduction has not been established. Those failures remain unexplained; no timeout relaxation or CI rerun was requested.


</details>

prs.title: test(mcp-events): await state database teardown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, the MCP Events service test fixture can delete its temporary SQLite directory while worker-owned WAL/SHM handles are still closing, producing EBUSY cleanup failures.

## Change

Await the existing asynchronous state database teardown before removing the temporary directory.

## Evidence

- Environment: Windows 11 Home, Node v24.22.1.
- Baseline control with the former synchronous close restored: the focused MCP Events test failed during fixture cleanup with EBUSY unlinking openclaw.sqlite-shm (1 failed, 19 skipped).
- Fixed revision, same focused test: 1 passed, 19 skipped.
- Fixed revision, full suite: pnpm vitest run extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 passed 20/20.
- pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts passed.
- pnpm exec oxlint extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts passed.
- git diff --check passed.

Fixes #184812


## Additional proof

- Head: `cea68caba`
- Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts`
- Result: **1 test file passed; all 9/9 MCP Events lifecycle tests passed**, including the awaited state-database teardown path.
- Command: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts`
- Result: **passed**.
- The test exercises the real extension service hooks and database lifecycle cleanup; no external provider or service is required.


## Additional base/head behavior proof

- Base revision `e990b80e`: running `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts --reporter=dot` on Windows reproduced the original cleanup failure: **15 failed, 1 passed**, with repeated `EBUSY` errors unlinking `openclaw.sqlite`, `openclaw.sqlite-wal`, and `openclaw.sqlite-shm` during fixture cleanup.
- PR head `cea68caba`: the same command passed **1 test file, 20/20 tests**; the same state-database teardown now awaits worker retirement before removing the temporary directory.
- The run used the repository's real MCP Events service fixture and real SQLite worker lifecycle on Windows, with no external provider or service.



<details><summary>Raw Windows terminal output</summary>

```text
BASE e990b80e
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts --reporter=dot
15 failed | 1 passed
Error: EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink '...\\openclaw.sqlite-wal'
Error: EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink '...\\openclaw.sqlite-shm'

HEAD cea68caba
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts --reporter=dot
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 20 passed (20)
```

The paths above are intentionally shortened to omit user and machine details.
</details>



## Reproducible Windows proof

prs.title: fix(secrets): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting config and env files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw secrets apply` (and `secrets configure --apply`) migrates plaintext secrets to SecretRefs and then rewrites the operator-managed files it touched. Two of its read paths decode with replacement semantics and later persist the decoded text back to the same path, so a single undecodable byte is silently rewritten as U+FFFD:

1. The env scrub loop in `projectPlanState` (`src/secrets/apply.ts`) reads each `.env` with `readFileSync(envPath, "utf8")`, scrubs migrated plaintext, and `runSecretsApply` writes the scrubbed string back to the same path via `writeTextFileAtomic`. Undecodable bytes anywhere in the file — including lines the scrub never touches — become U+FFFD on disk.
2. `captureFileSnapshot` / `restoreFileSnapshot` take rollback snapshots of the config and env files through the same lossy decode; when a later write fails, the rollback itself persists U+FFFD over the original bytes. The config case is reachable: a config whose undecodable byte lands inside a string value still passes config validation (`valid: true`), so apply proceeds to the write phase.

Both paths permanently destroy original bytes in files the operator owns.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode strictly with the existing `decodeUtf8File` helper (`src/agents/utf8-file.ts`) — the same rule the edit/apply_patch tools already enforce (precedent: #114895, "reject the operation before writing and leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged"), and the same strict-admission pattern as the merged oc-path (#168491) and memory-wiki (#168583) fixes.

Strict admission is conditional on an actual rewrite, mirroring #168491's editing-verb-only rule:

- A dotenv file is rejected only when the scrub would change its contents (`scrubbed !== current`); a malformed dotenv file the plan has nothing to remove from is left alone and never blocks the migration.
- Rollback snapshots reject malformed bytes at capture time, before any write; both rejection points run ahead of the write phase, so a rejected apply leaves every file byte-for-byte unchanged with a clear error naming the path.

Valid UTF-8 files are unaffected, including multi-byte content and a literal U+FFFD stored as proper UTF-8 bytes (locked by a regression test).

## User Impact

- `secrets apply` / `secrets configure --apply` can no longer silently corrupt `.env` or `openclaw.json` bytes outside the migrated values.
- Migrations that never needed to touch a malformed dotenv file still proceed.
- Operators see an actionable fatal error (`File <path> is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be edited safely.`) instead of discovering U+FFFD damage later.

## Evidence
Current head: `d08be805a328ff06b62d06968e5e15c8fe432cd8`, rebased onto `aa5d060d0ab` (base `main`).
`main` inlined the env scrub loop out of `scrubEnvFiles` into `projectPlanState`, so the hunk moved; the
behavior, the four tests and the conditional admission are unchanged. Every number below was produced on
this head.

### Regression tests — `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`

Four new tests:

- `refuses to rewrite a malformed UTF-8 env file during scrub` — `.env` with `0xFF` on a line the scrub never touches, plus a migrated plaintext line; apply rejects with the path in the message, and both the `.env` and the config remain byte-for-byte equal to their pre-apply contents.
- `still applies when a malformed UTF-8 env file has nothing to scrub` — `.env` with `0xFF` but no migrated assignment; the migration succeeds and the file is byte-for-byte intact (conditional admission).
- `refuses to snapshot a malformed UTF-8 config for rollback` — config with `0xFF` inside a string value (still passes config validation); apply rejects before any write and the config bytes are unchanged.
- `still scrubs a valid UTF-8 env file with non-ASCII content` — valid multi-byte content plus a literal U+FFFD round-trips byte-exact while the migrated plaintext is scrubbed (strict admission does not over-reject).

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/secrets/apply.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)          (371.77s wall, cold transform cache)
```

With only `src/secrets/apply.ts` reverted to `aa5d060d0ab` (same tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/secrets/apply.test.ts -t "UTF-8"
 × refuses to rewrite a malformed UTF-8 env file during scrub
 × refuses to snapshot a malformed UTF-8 config for rollback
 ✓ still applies when a malformed UTF-8 env file has nothing to scrub
 ✓ still scrubs a valid UTF-8 env file with non-ASCII content
 FAIL  refuses to rewrite a malformed UTF-8 env file during scrub
 AssertionError: promise resolved "{ mode: 'write', changed: true, …(6) }" instead of rejecting
 FAIL  refuses to snapshot a malformed UTF-8 config for rollback
 AssertionError: promise resolved "{ mode: 'write', changed: true, …(6) }" instead of rejecting
      Tests  2 failed | 2 passed | 26 skipped (30)
```

The two failures are the rejection assertions; the two conditional-admission controls pass on both sides,
so the test targets the persisted bytes, not the mere presence of an invalid byte.

### Real behavior proof — shipped CLI entry point

Same production entry point for every run (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts secrets apply --from plan.json`),
fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real `openclaw.json` + `.env`, plan built by hand against the shipped
plan schema (`models.providers.apiKey` → `env:default:OPENAI_API_KEY`). Red is the same tree with only
`src/secrets/apply.ts` reverted.

**env scrub path — `.env` holds the migrated plaintext plus a `0xFF` byte on a line the scrub never touches**

| run | exit | `.env` bytes | `0xFF` | replaces with `EF BF BD` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `aa5d060d0ab` | 0 | `... 4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 ff 62 0a ...` → `... 4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 ef bf bd 62 0a ...` | gone | yes |
| head `d08be805a32` | 1 | `4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 ff 62 0a ...` (sha-identical to before) | kept | no |

```
head: exit=1
  Secrets apply failed: File /tmp/.../state/.env is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be edited safely. | ERR_ENCODING_INVALID_ENCODED_DATA
before-hex: 4f50454e41495f4150495f4b45593d…0a4e4f54453d61ff620a554e52454c415445443d76616c75650a
after-hex : 4f50454e41495f4150495f4b45593d…0a4e4f54453d61ff620a554e52454c415445443d76616c75650a
```

**rollback-snapshot path — `openclaw.json` carries `0xFF` inside the `apiKey` string value (still valid config), `.env` holds the same lossy-decoded value**

| run | exit | `openclaw.json` sha256 | `.env` sha256 | `0xFF` in config |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `aa5d060d0ab` | 0 | changed | changed | gone |
| head `d08be805a32` | 1 | identical | identical | `73 6b 2d 70 72 6f 6f 66 2d 70 6c 61 69 6e ff` kept |

```
head: exit=1
  Secrets apply failed: File /tmp/.../state/openclaw.json is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be edited safely.
config-sha: identical
env-sha   : identical
```

**control — malformed `.env` the plan never rewrites (must not block the migration)**

```
head: exit=0
  Secrets applied. Updated 1 file(s).          (config only)
ENV-BYTES: unchanged
after-contains-0xff: true   after-contains-efbfbd: false
```

<details>
<summary>Previous head (`b191c67a`) evidence — packaged CLI builds, upgrade compatibility, lint</summary>

### Real behavior proof — packaged CLI, shipped entry point

Built the packaged CLI twice in an isolated container (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`): once from this branch and once from `main` with only `src/secrets/apply.ts` reverted (the baseline). Each run used a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` whose `openclaw.json` holds a plaintext `apiKey`, then ran the shipped entry point `node dist/index.js secrets apply --from plan.json`.

**RED — `main` baseline, `.env` contains the migrated plaintext plus a `0xFF` byte on an unrelated line:**

```
exit=0
  Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
-- env before (hex) --  ... 4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 ff 62 0a ...   ("NOTE=a", 0xff, "b")
-- env after (hex)  --  ... 4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 ef bf bd 62 0a ...  ("NOTE=a", U+FFFD, "b")
ENV-BYTES: CHANGED
after-contains-0xff: false
after-contains-efbfbd: true
```

Apply "succeeded" and the `0xff` byte came back as `ef bf bd` (U+FFFD) — the original byte is permanently lost.

**GREEN — this branch, same input:**

```
exit=1
  Secrets apply failed: File /tmp/.../state/.env is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be edited safely. | The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8 | ERR_ENCODING_INVALID_ENCODED_DATA. ...
ENV-BYTES: unchanged
after-contains-0xff: true
after-contains-efbfbd: false
```

Apply refuses before any write; the `.env` is byte-for-byte identical and the config is untouched.

**GREEN — this branch, `.env` malformed but containing no migrated plaintext (conditional admission):**

```
exit=0
  Secrets applied. Updated 1 file(s).    (config only — the .env is not rewritten)
ENV-BYTES: unchanged
after-contains-0xff: true
```

The migration proceeds and the malformed dotenv file keeps its exact bytes.

**Control — this branch, valid UTF-8 `.env` (`NOTE=a合法 😀 b`):**

```
exit=0
  Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
-- env after (hex) --  4e 4f 54 45 3d 61 e5 90 88 e6 b3 95 20 f0 9f 98 80 20 62 0a ...
after-contains-plaintext: false
```

Migration succeeds: the plaintext line is scrubbed and the multi-byte note line is preserved byte-exact.

### Shipped-CLI proof — malformed config rejected before any write (rollback snapshot path)

Same packaged build (`node dist/index.js`), isolated state dir: `openclaw.json` carries a `0xFF` byte inside the `apiKey` string value (valid JSON5 after lossy decode, so config validation passes and the plan reaches the write phase), and a valid `.env` holding the same lossy-decoded value (so the `.env` is also a pending rewrite target):

```
exit=1
  Secrets apply failed: File /tmp/.../state/openclaw.json is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be edited safely. | ERR_ENCODING_INVALID_ENCODED_DATA ...
-- state dir file inventory diff (before vs after) --
  ./.env           sha256 identical
  ./openclaw.json  sha256 identical
  (+ only ./state/openclaw.sqlite* bootstrap files — created by any CLI startup;
   a bare `secrets audit` on a fresh state dir creates the same four files)
-- config after (hex) --  ... 73 6b 2d 70 72 6f 6f 66 2d 70 6c 61 69 6e ff 74 65 78 74 ...  ("sk-proof-plain", 0xff, "text")
```

Apply refuses at rollback-snapshot capture: no plan-target file is created or modified.

### Upgrade compatibility — published stable × this head

State written by the published stable package (`openclaw@2026.10.4` from npm, reports `OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)`), then loaded and migrated further by this head's packaged build:

prs.title: fix(cli): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting shell profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw completion --install` reads the existing shell profile with replacement-mode UTF-8 decoding, then rewrites it. A single invalid byte such as `0xff` becomes U+FFFD and is persisted into `.zshrc` / `.bashrc` / `config.fish`. The original profile bytes are lost.

A shared strict reader also broke two optional callers: onboarding/`doctor --fix` rethrew encoding failures after durable setup succeeded, and read-only hook inspection treated any Latin-1 comment as "not installed", suppressing Doctor's missing-cache repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Own admission at `readCompletionProfile` with an explicit mode:

- `mutate` (install/rewrite): `isUtf8` throws a typed encoding error, leaves bytes untouched, and returns the session `source <cache>` recovery command
- `inspect` (status/Doctor/onboarding): lossy UTF-8 decode so ASCII OpenClaw source lines beside Latin-1 comments stay recognizable

Optional callers share `findOptionalCompletionInstallFailure` (write permission **or** encoding) and warn with session recovery instead of aborting finalize/`doctor --fix`. Direct `completion --install` still fails closed.

## User Impact

**Before:** `completion --install` can silently rewrite a Latin-1/truncated profile; the same encoding failure can abort onboarding finalize; a Latin-1 comment beside a valid ASCII hook makes Doctor think completion is absent.

**After:** malformed UTF-8 exits non-zero on direct install with `The file was left untouched` plus session recovery. Setup and Doctor warn and continue. Latin-1 comments do not hide an installed ASCII hook, so missing-cache regeneration still runs. Legal Unicode profiles still receive the completion block.

## Evidence

- Owner: `src/cli/completion-runtime.ts` `readCompletionProfile(mode)` → `installCompletion` / `isCompletionInstalled` / `usesSlowDynamicCompletion`
- Optional callers: `findOptionalCompletionInstallFailure` → `src/wizard/setup.completion.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-completion.ts`
- Registered CLI: `registerCompletionCli` → `completion --shell zsh --install`
- Tests: runtime inspect/mutate + Latin-1 hook; doctor status + encoding recovery; setup encoding nonfatal

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Silent UTF-8 replacement on rewrite; onboarding/Doctor abort on encoding; lost installed-hook recognition beside Latin-1 comments
- **Canonical reachability path:** `src/entry.ts` → `registerCompletionCli` → `installCompletion` → `readCompletionProfile(..., "mutate")`; Doctor/onboarding → `checkShellCompletionStatus` → `readCompletionProfile(..., "inspect")`; optional install → `findOptionalCompletionInstallFailure`
- **Boundary crossed:** Write-only UTF-8 admission; read-only inspection stays permissive for ASCII hooks
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** `node:buffer` `isUtf8`; no new config/schema
- **Real environment tested:** Isolated `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `ZDOTDIR` on Node 22.23.1; production `src/entry.ts` CLI for the write path; Vitest caller-path coverage for P1/P2
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ export HOME=/tmp/oc-completion-cli-proof/home
$ export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-completion-cli-proof/state
$ export ZDOTDIR=$HOME SHELL=/bin/zsh
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts completion --write-state --yes --shell zsh
$ python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path.home()/".zshrc"; p.write_bytes(b"export KEEP=\xe5\x90\x88\xe6\xb3\x95-"+bytes([0xff])+b"-before\n")'
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts completion --shell zsh --install --yes
$ python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import hashlib; b=(Path.home()/".zshrc").read_bytes(); print(hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest(), b.hex())'
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
write_state_exit:0
malformed_sha256 00e5328dec4514f204af8faf0b90bc4ea4b326a1f44fa97520421f01a6ac7325
[openclaw] Reason: Failed to install completion: Shell profile must be valid UTF-8: ... The file was left untouched. For this session, load the prepared cache with: source .../openclaw.zsh.
install_malformed_exit:1
after_malformed_sha256 00e5328dec4514f204af8faf0b90bc4ea4b326a1f44fa97520421f01a6ac7325
unchanged True
install_valid_exit:0
keeps_unicode True
has_completion True
```

Caller-path regressions for ClawSweeper P1/P2:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/completion-runtime.test.ts -t 'Latin-1|malformed-profile'
✓ keeps malformed-profile status inspection nonfatal
✓ still recognizes an installed ASCII hook beside a Latin-1 comment

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts -t 'Latin-1|UTF-8'
✓ does not abort status checks when the shell profile is not valid UTF-8
✓ still reports a missing cache when a Latin-1 comment surrounds an installed hook

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/wizard/setup.completion.test.ts -t 'encoding|permission'
✓ offers session recovery after a profile permission error
✓ keeps quickstart finalization alive when profile encoding blocks install
```

Head: `ec5be148fee968b4b9ca20abe78c2d2819a47e33` (rebased onto current main).

- **Observed result after fix:** Direct install still refuses malformed UTF-8 without rewrite; inspect mode keeps ASCII hooks visible beside Latin-1; setup/Doctor treat encoding like permission failures with session recovery.
- **What was not tested:** Packaged `dist/entry` build. Native Windows PowerShell UTF-16 profiles were not re-run here. Full install suites need CI's current `@openclaw/fs-safe` (local checkout nm is older than main).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: malformed UTF-8 from a value file, piped value, or dotenv import can silently overwrite stored secrets/environment values with altered text.

## User Impact

User impact: malformed byte input fails before storage changes, including partial dotenv imports; valid UTF-8 and existing BOM/newline behavior remain supported.

No config defaults, storage schema, protocol, permissions, migrations, or upgrade behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete bounded input buffer before converting it to text, using the existing input-validation error and CLI exit-2 path. Both set/import and file/stdin use the same reader.

## Evidence

### Current-head maintenance

- Product head: `83700dd69ce3bccff09e1c484a4af38af9fa19b8`; integrated main: `5dce97b1362ff634333c32940aba4f9a1bb477b2`; clean reviewed tree: `694a4cb1dcbba080ee7b3229d94d1e3a3968c46b`. Original contributor commits are retained; ordinary merge/push, no force-push.
- Repair: Integrated main after the named hosted onboarding E2E failed. Main supplies its missing openclaw.chat.history mock. The bounded UTF-8 reader and atomic storage validation remain unchanged. After preparing the missing plugin browser assets using their repository-owned builders, the originally failing onboarding E2E passes locally.
- Production entry / exact collector command: `node "$HARNESS" "$CHECKOUT" store green` (Node 26.12.1, Linux, isolated HOME/config/state; no production service).
- Canonical owner: Shared bounded secrets-store file/stdin input readers -> existing validation classifier -> canonical SQLite secret-store persistence owner.
- Recorder/readback boundary: Normally built real secrets store CLI -> separate read-only SQLite SELECT after each child exits. Four malformed set/import file/stdin routes exit 2 and preserve every row and metadata column; four legal BOM/newline/Unicode controls persist their expected values.
- Acceptance-red: retain the original baseline executions and SHAs in the historical evidence below. This maintenance reruns GREEN plus controls and does not claim a new baseline run.
- Validation: 36/36 related secrets-store tests pass; originally failing custodian-onboarding-locale E2E 1/1 passes (177.73 seconds including normal UI build). Changed-file type-aware lint, format and independent source/test review PASS. Normal cliStartup build has a clean exact-head stamp; required hosted exact-head checks remain separate.
- Acceptance-green / controls: current-head receipt below. Tests/review are separate from runtime proof.
- Cleanup / limitations: collector children exited and owned listeners closed. Synthetic state is retained with its receipt. No external provider authentication, live production Gateway/channel, interactive TTY, other OS or installed-release upgrade. Repository-owned security/area-owner approval is not waived by runtime proof.

prs.title: fix: malformed UTF-8 input silently corrupts rewritten text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent replacement of malformed UTF-8 when importing secret-store values, installing shell completion, or applying a secrets migration that rewrites config or environment files.

Related: #167250, #168460, #175125.

## User Impact

Malformed byte input is refused before mutation instead of being saved with replacement characters. Existing store values and operator-managed files remain unchanged. Valid UTF-8, including literal replacement characters, continues to work. Completion inspection remains tolerant of legacy comments, and optional Doctor/setup installation explains how to load the completion cache for the current session without modifying the profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing strict UTF-8 input owner for these mutation boundaries and existing agent edit/apply_patch consumers; remove the duplicate agent decoder and per-site validators. Preserve bounded reads, regular-file checks, UTF-16 PowerShell profiles, secret disclosure policy, and no-op environment-file inspection.

This integrates the original fix commits by @Alix-007 (#167250), @hugenshen (#168460), and @wangmiao0668000666 (#175125), with their authorship retained. The regression cases are consolidated into existing fixtures: test and test-support line delta is zero against the integration base. Production delta is +88 lines, primarily strict profile admission and optional-install recovery.

### Not fixed here

Update-handoff output (#186033) is excluded. This does not convert legacy encodings or make every read-only text reader strict. Secret input files are never rewritten: the secret-store defect is corruption of the persisted value, not mutation of the source file.

## Evidence

Focused affected-consumer checks passed 222 cases across ten files, including the registered CLI/default failure renderer and streaming archive decoder. Type-aware lint: zero warnings/errors across all 19 changed TypeScript files. Container formatting and whitespace checks passed. The config/env regression table fails on baseline production in all three malformed-byte cases and passes its valid-byte control.

Both refs completed full Node 24.22.1 Docker builds. Through the shipped CLI, main silently saved replacement characters for malformed profile/config/env bytes and secret set/import file/stdin input; the candidate refused every malformed mutation with a clear normal-output error and preserved prior files/store values. Valid CJK/emoji/literal U+FFFD and no-op malformed `.env` controls passed on both refs (22 scenarios). The secret-store check used synthetic readable env-kind values without changing secret-kind disclosure policy; input files stayed unchanged on both refs.

[Observed CLI captures and regression results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186476#issuecomment-6459852608).

[Latest-stable v2026.10.8 compatibility proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186476#issuecomment-6460102730): the same state opened successfully on the candidate with existing config/SecretRefs/env bytes/readable store values preserved, the write-only stored secret resolving through public dry-run preflight, and UTF-8 BOM completion remaining byte-preserving and idempotent. Native Windows UTF-16 was not executed.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: no schema or permission changes, and a revert restores permissive decoding. A revert cannot recover bytes already corrupted by an earlier version. Blast radius: secret-store file/stdin ingestion, secrets-apply config/env rewrites, completion installation and optional Doctor/setup recovery, and existing agent edit/apply_patch UTF-8 refusal.

prs.title: fix #169718: memory search sync warnings hide the underlying cause
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw memory search` prints `memory sync failed (search): <wrapper>` warnings built with `String(err)`, which discards `Error.cause`; the real exception (e.g. an `ERR_INVALID_STATE`/`database is not open` use-after-close underneath a wrapper) never reaches the operator, so diagnosis dead-ends at a generic wrapper message (issue #169718).
- Solution: format both background-sync warnings with a policy-free formatter that keeps the nested cause chain and error codes. The plugin-sdk's `formatErrorMessage` redacts internally, but the repo log policy is "write raw; redact only at egress", so `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` gains a `formatErrorMessageRaw` re-export of the shared policy-free formatter and the two log-bound warnings use it without any redaction wrapper.
- What changed: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.ts`, `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/error-runtime.ts`
- What did NOT change: warning cadence, log level, and sync behavior are unchanged — only the rendered text gains the nested cause chain; masking still happens at the egress sinks (verified: the console transport renders `password=<redacted>` while the raw record keeps the full text); the neighbouring `search-bootstrap-fallback` warning keeps its `tools`-mode redaction because that text is model-bound; the `watch`-path warnings and the retired short-term-lock wrapper are out of scope.
- Data-model compatibility: logging-only change; no schema, stored-data, or index-format changes.

Fixes #169718

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Background memory sync failures during `memory search` surface as a bare wrapper string; the nested cause that explains the failure is dropped, so operators cannot tell what actually failed.
- **Real environment tested:** feat/issue-169718 worktree on current main (cc4315e0def), Node v24.20.0: (1) the shipped CLI flow — isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + workspace, FTS-only config (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), real `memory index` + `memory search` via the built `openclaw.mjs` launcher; (2) a render probe feeding a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (`ERR_INVALID_STATE database is not open`, the exact error class from the issue) through the old and new warning construction.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Shipped CLI flow: index real notes, then search (background sync warning path is live)
  export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated>/state OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=<isolated>/workspace
  node openclaw.mjs memory index
  node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  # Render probe: real node:sqlite use-after-close error through old vs new formatting
  node --import tsx render-probe.mts
  # Regression tests
  npx vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  Render probe with a real `node:sqlite` use-after-close error (the issue's `ERR_INVALID_STATE` class) wrapped the way the sync path wraps failures:
  ```text
  real cause: ERR_INVALID_STATE | database is not open
  before: memory sync failed (search): Error: memory index maintenance failed
  after:  memory sync failed (search): memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE
  ```
  The same wrapper on the before code drops the cause entirely (`String(err)` renders only `Error: <wrapper message>`); after the fix the nested message and code are appended.
  Shipped CLI runs (real index + real search; the background sync warning path fires when the sync owner loses write admission during teardown) — before code vs this head:
  ```text
  $ node openclaw.mjs memory search "release checklist" --min-score 0
  No matches.
  # before: [memory] sync failed (search): Error: Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  # after:  [memory] sync failed (search): Memory database owner closed or changed before write admission
  ```
  (For single-level errors without a `cause`, only the redundant `Error: ` prefix disappears; the fix's value is the nested cause chain when one exists, as shown above.)
  Regression tests: `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` — the two new cases fail on the before code (`AssertionError: expected ... to contain 'database is not open'`) and pass on this head; the full suite passes (19 tests).
- **Observed result after fix:** Warnings from the search sync path now include the nested cause message and code (`memory index maintenance failed | database is not open | ERR_INVALID_STATE`), so the underlying failure is visible instead of dead-ending at a wrapper message; search results, exit code, and sync behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** the issue's original 2026.9.9 short-term-lock wrapper no longer exists on main, so that exact `storage-error` line cannot be reproduced today; natural single-level failures (e.g. `database is locked`) render identically before and after. No live gateway or embedding provider was involved — the proof exercises the real search/sync code path in the memory-core extension, which is where the warnings are emitted.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-orchestration.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: a background search sync that fails with a cause-carrying error renders the wrapper message plus the nested cause message and code in both the `search` and `search-bootstrap` warnings.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the defect is the choice of string conversion at two adjacent log sites; driving the real manager search path with a failing sync pins the rendered warning text end to end.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the two search-path sync warnings interpolate `String(err)`, and `String()` on an Error yields only `Name: message` — `cause` and nested codes are silently discarded.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test pinned the rendered warning text for a cause-carrying sync failure; neighbouring warnings had already migrated to `formatErrorMessage`, leaving these two sites behind.

prs.title: fix(browser): omit unparsable gateway hint from extension pairing
prs.body:
Closes #186454

## What Problem This Solves

A browser node whose relay is local but whose Gateway is remote receives a pairing string the shipped Chrome extension always rejects, so setup ends at "Manual setup required (malformed_response)".
- Problem: for `gateway.mode: "remote"` over plaintext `ws://`, the pairing builder copied the remote Gateway URL into the optional `gateway` hint even though the extension accepts only `wss://` or loopback `ws://` hints. `parseGatewayHint` returned null, so `validatePairingFields` rejected a pairing whose relay URL and token were valid.
- Solution: publish the optional hint only when the extension can parse it. The relay URL, token, and relay validation are unchanged.
- What changed: one shared URL predicate in `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.ts` now drives both relay-URL validation and hint emission; a regression test covers the plaintext remote case in `extension-pairing.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the extension's URL policy, relay transport validation, `wss://` hint behavior, and `--gateway-url` validation errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer emitted optional metadata its only consumer is guaranteed to reject; fixing the producer keeps the plaintext-connection restriction intact.
- Best fix: omit unusable optional hints at the producer instead of relaxing the extension's URL policy (a plaintext non-loopback Gateway is still refused).
- Alternative: make the extension tolerate the hint — rejected because the hint carries no authority and widening that check increases risk for every pairing.
- Risk / non-goals: only the unusable-hint case changes; local loopback hints and `wss://` remote hints keep their current bytes.

## User Impact

`openclaw browser extension pair` and the native macOS bootstrap now hand the installed extension a pairing it accepts when the browser node uses a local relay in front of a plaintext remote Gateway, instead of requiring manual setup.

## Evidence

After the fix, the same browser-node configuration produces a relay-only pairing that the shipped extension parser accepts:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node --import tsx proof.mts
[1] browser-node plaintext ws:// remote gateway
    topology        : browser-node
    pairingString   : ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension#<64-hex token>
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<64-hex token>"}
[2] browser-node wss:// remote gateway (control)
    topology        : browser-node
    pairingString   : ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension?gateway=wss%3A%2F%2Fgateway.example.com%3A9444#<64-hex token>
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<64-hex token>","gatewayUrl":"wss://gateway.example.com:9444"}
```

Before the fix, on `origin/main`, case 1 emitted the unusable hint and the shipped parser returned null:

```text
[1] browser-node plaintext ws:// remote gateway
    pairingString   : ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension?gateway=ws%3A%2F%2F192.168.1.20%3A8080#<64-hex token>
    extension parse : null -> malformed_response
[2] browser-node wss:// remote gateway (control)
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<64-hex token>","gatewayUrl":"wss://gateway.example.com:9444"}
```

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| browser-node + plaintext `ws://192.168.1.20:8080` | hint emitted, parser returns null | hint omitted, parser accepts |
| browser-node + `wss://gateway.example.com:9444` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |
| direct-remote `wss://…:9443` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |

The new regression test is red on `origin/main` and green with the fix; the existing relay integration test that builds and parses the pairing still passes:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.test.ts --run
 ✓ omits a plaintext non-loopback gateway hint that the extension cannot parse
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/gateway-relay-route.integration.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

On base, the same regression test fails with `expected 'ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension?gatewa…' to be 'ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension#…'` (1 failed, 4 passed).

What was not tested: no Chrome extension or native host was launched; the shipped parser (`extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/relay-core.js`) was exercised directly against the producer output.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source reading plus `node --import tsx` to trace the pairing builder into the shipped extension parser, then added the producer guard and its regression test. The implementer understands the code: the extension rejects any pairing whose `gateway` hint fails its own `isAllowedWebSocketUrl` check, so the producer must not emit a hint that check rejects. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

## What Problem This Solves

The repository test-line budget limits changes that add net regression coverage once the tracked total exceeds its ceiling. This PR sets the ceiling to **6,300,000**, giving the existing ratchet a fixed amount of additional headroom while retaining its enforcement rules.

The credential regression coverage discussed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181597 supplied the original motivation. That earlier failure is historical context; this policy change does not establish whether another PR passes against its current base.

## User Impact

Contributors can add distinct regression coverage while the tracked total remains within the new ceiling. Over-ceiling changes that increase test lines still fail, and the existing allowance for non-growing changes remains in place. No test assertions or runtime behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing checker already supports deliberate manual increases and reports them for review. Updating its single canonical scalar implements the selected fixed ceiling without adding an exception, changing counting rules, or removing coverage. The pruning command continues to lower the ceiling only; it does not raise it automatically.

## Evidence

Head 5fe382cac2c39edefbdd0789696920ff9319bb65 integrates main b4cc6fe87a18220ac11a0a3377b0a3ef43cf2093 and retains the existing contributor commits. Its complete main-relative change is the single scalar from 6,295,000 to 6,300,000. Exact-tree comparison confirms that all other tracked files, including every test assertion, remain unchanged.

The canonical `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base b4cc6fe87a18220ac11a0a3377b0a3ef43cf2093 --no-merge-base` passed on an isolated Linux runner using Node 24.22.1 and the locked pnpm 12.15.0 dependencies: **6,294,095** test lines, ceiling **6,300,000**, and **5,905** lines of headroom. It emitted the expected manual-increase warning. Exact scalar bytes, whitespace, a clean tested worktree, and the complete non-scalar comparison also passed.

The pure base also passed at 6,294,095 lines under 6,295,000, leaving 905 lines. Earlier executed over-ceiling, zero-growth controls remain applicable because the checker, comparison helper, and regression assertions are unchanged. No claim is made that another PR's current composition fails its budget.

Vincent's takeover preserved this exact head and all maintainer commits. A fresh canonical Node 26.12.1 check on macOS independently passed with the same 6,294,095 total and 5,905 slack; this is separate from the Linux proof above. Production and test LOC are unchanged; metadata is +1/-1.

[Exact-head CI 40625044020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40625044020) completed successfully: all 58 jobs terminal, 28 successful and 30 skipped. Its actual tested merge was `7dacc766204154c0b390c64eb552c9ff87fac179`, combining this head with main `b61ab6deb40cc640aec077b6e6a7b93a44b5422c`. Security review and required gate contexts pass. [ClawSweeper revision 10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185911#issuecomment-6442745758) covers this exact head with no findings or before-merge items. No checks were restarted by the takeover.

Native completed-hosted preparation and live ordinary squash admission remain required. No application build, runtime, or model replay is required for this single policy value.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local changed checks silently omit a tracked path when it changes between a regular file and a symlink. Git reports status `T`, which the worktree and index allowlists excluded.

## User Impact

Local checks, staged remote delegation, changed-test planning, and changed package-lock selection retain those paths instead of treating the change as an empty scope. No product configuration or CI admission policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three restrictive status filters from the canonical changed-path producer. Committed comparisons already retain every status; worktree and staged comparisons now follow that contract. Exact NUL-delimited names and both rename endpoints stay intact.

The existing real-Git lifecycle regression also covers both file-to-symlink and symlink-to-file transitions through worktree, staged, combined, and committed comparisons. It reuses the same repository and Git commands.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126198

## Evidence

- Native Node 26.12.1 reproduction on the base: Git reports `T src/source.ts`, but worktree, staged, and combined discovery return `[]` and do not select the core lane. The committed comparison retains the path.
- The same production-owner probe after repair retains the path and core lane in all four modes. A second probe verifies both type-change directions.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Autoreview P0–P3: scoped-clean, no findings (confidence 0.93), base `f4ae2740789dc8e45706abc128e592c3f99732ff` through the exact changes committed as `aae752d5025f6dad03cd321d62757ee8eeb241fd`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its runner checkout is dirty; the automatic exact-head hosted review is recorded below. Independent owner/caller review also found no actionable defect.
- Focused native tests, pinned formatting and focused boundary lint pass, as detailed below. Broader type-aware lint and typecheck are delegated to ordinary PR CI; they are not claimed as local passes.
- Production delta: +1 explanatory comment, no added executable logic. Test delta: +8 lines in the existing lifecycle fixture; no new test case or subprocess.

No CI runtime or billing savings are claimed.

## Focused native qualification

At exact signed head `aae752d5025f6dad03cd321d62757ee8eeb241fd`, five focused cases pass using the native qualified dependency installation: renamed/type-changed paths in both directions, explicit staged package-script base, pending merge index, inert/active edits, and regular-file lifecycle comparison. Targeted pinned formatting, focused boundary lint and diff checks pass.

The initial full-file native `review-tests` run was interrupted with exit 130 after an existing formatter fixture began staging the pinned Bun executable again inside its isolated HOME/cache. No source assertion failed; this is not a full-file pass. Task-owned children were joined/stopped and the retained operation lock was recovered through the native wrapper. The selected-executable identity loss is a separate producer-level follow-up. Broad ordinary PR CI remains required before landing.

## Hosted review follow-through

[The automatic exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469#issuecomment-6459804042) found no introduced correctness or security defect and requested completion of the pending qualification. Five focused native cases, pinned formatting and focused boundary lint are now recorded above. The selected staged-base cases invoke the real `changed-lanes.mjs` CLI in a disposable Git repository; the type-change lifecycle case and separate original/candidate owner probes cover both status-T directions. Broader type-aware lint and typecheck remain assigned to ordinary PR CI and must pass before merge. The head has not changed, so no rating-only re-review request is being sent.


## Completed pre-merge qualification

The unchanged exact-head ClawSweeper review's single Before-merge qualification item is satisfied by the five actual selected Vitest cases, targeted pinned format check, focused boundary lint, and completed ordinary CI. CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40626894476 passed on head aae752d5025f6dad03cd321d62757ee8eeb241fd: 42 successful jobs, 29 skipped, no failures; tooling test types, lint, baseline ratchets and openclaw/ci-gate passed. prs.title: feature(sessions): add processes list|stop CLI for existing Gateway RPCs
prs.body:
Implements #182642

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI already observes and stops session exec children via `sessions.processes.list` / `sessions.processes.stop`, but the sessions CLI has no processes verbs. Headless operators must open Control UI or ask the agent to kill a runaway process. Distinct from cold-storage inventory (#181294) and from bulk kill-all (#12554).

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw sessions processes list <key> --json` returns `{ sessionId, processes, truncated }`. `openclaw sessions processes stop <key> <processId> --session-id <id> --instance <id> --json` requests a stop using ids from the matching list response. Stale `--session-id` fails closed. Unreachable Gateway fails like sibling Gateway-backed sessions commands. Registered CLI also accepts `--port` for local Gateway targeting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapter only: register `sessions processes list|stop`, forward validated params (including Gateway `--port`) to existing Gateway methods, print Gateway JSON, and document next to other sessions ops. No new Gateway methods, schema, or permissions.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/sessions-processes.ts`, `src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.ts`, colocated failure-envelope test, `docs/cli/sessions.md`
- Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/sessions-processes.test.ts` — **1 passed** (failure envelope only; dropped low-value mock mapping tests)
- Packaged CLI e2e below: real running exec child → list → stop with returned identities → child exits

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw sessions processes list|stop` that call existing `sessions.processes.*` RPCs; listing must surface a real running exec child; stop must use returned identities and cause the child to exit; stale session / unreachable Gateway must fail closed.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw sessions processes list|stop` → `sessionsProcessesListCommand` / `sessionsProcessesStopCommand` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("sessions.processes.list"|"sessions.processes.stop", …)` → existing handlers in `src/gateway/server-methods/session-processes.ts` → `bash-process-registry` observation.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` and existing process observation owners. No new process registry or permissions.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run --port 18797` with token auth; agent turn with a local mock OpenAI-compatible model that issued `exec` `{ command: "sleep 180", yieldMs: 0 }` so a Gateway-owned background child entered the session process registry.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Gateway already running with coding profile + mock model that calls exec(sleep 180, yieldMs:0)
KEY=agent:main:proc-proof-3
node openclaw.mjs sessions processes list "$KEY" --url ws://127.0.0.1:18797 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# → processId=lucky-ocean instanceId=792a7d5e-… status=running name="sleep 180"
# host: sleep 180 PID alive
node openclaw.mjs sessions processes stop "$KEY" lucky-ocean \
  --session-id 0a0f1e12-7d0b-4308-9187-b57d1d05b694 \
  --instance 792a7d5e-00a6-474b-8223-c05175be20c3 \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:18797 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# → { "requested": true }; host sleep child gone
node openclaw.mjs sessions processes list "$KEY" --url ws://127.0.0.1:18797 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# → status=killed exitSignal=SIGTERM exitReason=manual-cancel
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# list — REAL running exec child (exit 0)
{
  "sessionId": "0a0f1e12-7d0b-4308-9187-b57d1d05b694",
  "processes": [
    {
      "processId": "lucky-ocean",
      "instanceId": "792a7d5e-00a6-474b-8223-c05175be20c3",
      "name": "sleep 180",
      "status": "running",
      "startedAt": 1792864835790,
      "tail": "",
      "truncated": false,
      "canStop": false
    }
  ],
  "truncated": false
}

# host before stop: sleep 180 PID present
# stop with returned identities (exit 0)
{ "requested": true }

# host after stop: CHILD EXITED (no sleep 180)

# list after stop (exit 0)
{
  "sessionId": "0a0f1e12-7d0b-4308-9187-b57d1d05b694",
  "processes": [
    {
      "processId": "lucky-ocean",
      "instanceId": "792a7d5e-00a6-474b-8223-c05175be20c3",
      "name": "sleep 180",
      "status": "killed",
      "startedAt": 1792864835790,
      "endedAt": 1792864845197,
      "tail": "",
      "truncated": false,
      "canStop": false,
      "exitCode": null,
      "exitSignal": "SIGTERM",
      "exitReason": "manual-cancel"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": false
}

# agent turn receipt proving Gateway-owned exec spawned the child
"successfulToolNames": ["exec"]
```

## Notes for reviewers

- Maintainer product decision remains open (expose vs keep Control-UI-only); this PR is the thin CLI adapter only.
- Low-value happy-path mock mapping tests removed; failure-envelope unit coverage kept.
- AI-assisted. Maintainers can edit.

prs.title: docs: clarify session run status before replacing work
prs.body:
Related: #64103

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reading session inventories lack an explanation of terminal-looking run statuses and can mistake them for permanent session or task completion.

## User Impact

The existing tool description and session guide now explain last-run outcomes and suggest considering a same-session follow-up before spawning replacement work, subject to current access and lifecycle admission checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the [narrow clarification proposed in the current issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64103#issuecomment-4323766467). `done`, `failed`, `timeout`, and `killed` retain their existing meanings. A run outcome neither establishes overall task completion nor guarantees that another run will be accepted.

No wire values, output fields, schemas, runtime behavior, or admission checks change. In particular, this does not infer a `resumable` flag from status or promise that all terminal-looking sessions can continue. The reported duplicate-spawn cascade has not been deterministically reproduced on current main; this PR addresses the evidenced guidance gap and does not claim to fix that runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh on main `f76e79be6a8`; current head `dabc114bb05dd2efaa529314c2cb111a7bef8d3b` retains the clarification and updates generated prompt snapshots using [remote generation](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40625874783). [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40626164721) passed on this head. Earlier runtime evidence below refers to its stated earlier head.

- Running-Gateway proof on exact head `71f5e43e823366b069e440036711e82ffb2536a5` passed: an authenticated agent turn used the normal deferred-tool `tool_describe` control, and the next HTTP request to the loopback mock OpenAI Responses endpoint contained the complete updated `sessions_list` description. The captured description exactly matches the committed snapshot; `agent.wait` returned `ok`, shutdown was clean, and the process tree was joined. No task tool was executed.
- Inspected the canonically assembled model-facing tool description. The generated dynamic-tool JSON changes only `sessions_list.description`; input schemas and all other tools remain unchanged. The other three regenerated artifacts contain derived prompt counts and SHA-bound deltas.
- Existing description tests fail against the old text for both the default and Control UI-linked descriptions, then pass 10/10 with this clarification. Vitest duration: 0.681 s; total local wall time: 2.711 s. Per-test hosted CI time is not yet measured.
- Canonical prompt-snapshot regeneration and fresh check passed: all seven snapshot artifacts current.
- All `check:docs` constituent checks passed: docs formatting, docs/template lint, MDX, i18n glossary, internal links, config examples, and changelog mirrors. Internal-link audit: 14,930 links, zero broken; docs lint: 1,316 files, zero issues.
- Focused TypeScript lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the final seven-file diff also received a clean read-only scope and semantics review.

Validation used direct repository Node entrypoints with a read-only borrowed dependency installation whose manifest and lockfile match the candidate, plus isolated `markdownlint-cli2` 0.23.3. No dependency reconciliation or full installation was performed. Full build, full runtime suite, and full typecheck/`check:changed` aggregate were not run for this guidance-only change.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and assembled guidance</summary>

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-description-presets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --check
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/tool-description-presets.test.ts src/agents/tool-description-presets.ts
git diff --check
```

New text in the assembled `sessions_list` description:

> Run outcomes: `done` means success, `failed` error, `timeout` time limit, and `killed` cancellation. These describe the last run, not task completion or whether the session can continue. Before spawning replacement work, consider a same-session follow-up; it still requires current access and lifecycle checks to admit new work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Running Gateway: sanitized model-request capture</summary>

The fixture used the production `startGatewayServer`, `GatewayClient`, `agent`/`agent.wait` RPCs, built-in OpenClaw runtime, normal Tool Search catalog, and OpenAI Responses transport. Its synthetic model provider configuration followed `src/gateway/test-openai-responses-model.ts`. HOME, state, config, and workspace were isolated; token authentication and ordinary `operator.read`/`operator.write` admission were retained. Only `sessions_list` was allowlisted, and the mock model requested metadata through `tool_describe`, not execution of the inventory or any task tool.

The default tool surface defers `sessions_list`. The initial direct-descriptor probe correctly failed that fixture assumption after a successful agent turn; the corrected capture follows the advertised discovery control and observes its description in the next real provider HTTP request. No product behavior was changed to obtain the proof. The model service itself is a deterministic local mock, not paid/live-model inference.

```text
GATEWAY_READY {"sourceHead":"71f5e43e823366b069e440036711e82ffb2536a5","sourceTree":"e417d6eeca95c67872990fd80fa6eeb4e75215e1","auth":"token","scopes":["operator.read","operator.write"],"provider":"loopback mock OpenAI Responses"}
MODEL_REQUEST {"path":"/v1/responses","model":"guidance-proof","advertised":["tool_call","tool_describe","tool_search"],"toolResultCount":0}
MODEL_REQUEST {"path":"/v1/responses","model":"guidance-proof","advertised":["tool_call","tool_describe","tool_search"],"toolResultCount":1}
PROOF_PASSED {"sourceHead":"71f5e43e823366b069e440036711e82ffb2536a5","capturedRequests":1,"runStatus":"ok","tool":"sessions_list","descriptionSha256":"14a7cf93216d198becec0519cdb00394bc535e713f628a769dbcb77e65b1cac4"}
FIXTURE_CLOSED
MODEL_DESCRIPTION {"name": "sessions_list", "description": "List visible session metadata and groups; filter ownerId/creatorId, projectId/workspaceDir, group/pinned, kind/agent/activity/archive. relationship=owned|created|involving selects the authenticated requesting user's sessions, not the agent's owner. Metadata-only by default. limit defaults to 100; larger requests stay valid but limitApplied never exceeds 200. count is this page, not an inventory total. Continue with nextOffset and identical filters while hasMore; truncationReason names a scan/byte budget. Pages are live: deduplicate by agentId/key/sessionId or restart for a fresh inventory. archived=all includes active and archived rows. Preview recent messages inline via includeLastMessage/messageLimit; includeDerivedTitles adds derived titles. enrichmentOmitted means previews exceeded the byte budget; read history separately. Run outcomes: `done` means success, `failed` error, `timeout` time limit, and `killed` cancellation. These describe the last run, not task completion or whether the session can continue. Before spawning replacement work, consider a same-session follow-up; it still requires current access and lifecycle checks to admit new work. Use before history/send target selection."}
```

Fixture command: exit 0; total wall time 118.684 s; owned process tree joined. Worktree remained clean at the published head throughout.

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): session stops accepting messages after a deeply nested tool result
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A tool result with `details` nested deeper than 1000 levels is stored without error. After that, every append to the same session fails with `Error [ERR_SQLITE_ERROR]: malformed JSON`. The session stays stuck after a Gateway restart.

SQLite JSON functions reject documents nested deeper than 1000 levels. The latest-event query in `readActiveTranscriptAppendParentId` runs `json_each` on the stored event, so one deep row blocks every later append.

Closes #186480

## User Impact

One tool result can make a session unusable. For example, an MCP tool that returns `structuredContent` nested 1001 to about 2400 levels has this effect. The user must start a new session to continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeTranscriptJsonValue` in `src/config/sessions/transcript-json.ts` is the last step before both transcript write paths store a value. The fix caps it at 256 levels. A deeper subtree becomes the string `"[Truncated: nested too deeply]"`, so stored JSON always stays below the SQLite limit. `requiresNativeJson` also stops at the cap, so the native `JSON.stringify` path never walks the deep part.

A cap of 256 levels is far above normal tool output and far below 1000. The change does not repair sessions that are already stuck.

## Evidence

Regression test: `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-deep-values.test.ts`. It appends a tool result with `details` nested 1100 levels through `guardSessionManager`, then appends a user message.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main `beb12faf` | ❌ `Error [ERR_SQLITE_ERROR]: malformed JSON` on the next append |
| this branch | ✅ next append stored, 1 passed |

`pnpm test src/config/sessions/transcript-json.test.ts`: 11 passed on this branch.

Real Gateway run. I built main `beb12faf` and this branch `c3452cae` in separate worktrees. Each run used an isolated state dir, a loopback Gateway, and no API keys. A local OpenAI-compatible mock acts as the model. A stdio MCP server returns `structuredContent` nested 1100 levels. The same script drives both builds with `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:proof --json`.

| Step | main `beb12faf` | this branch `c3452cae` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Model calls the MCP tool | ✅ `TOOL-DONE` | ✅ `TOOL-DONE` |
| 2. Ordinary message, same session | ❌ exit 1, `malformed JSON \| ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` | ✅ `PONG` |
| 3. Restart the Gateway, ordinary message | ❌ same error | ✅ `PONG` |

Gateway log on main, turn 2 and turn 3 (after restart):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=211 error="malformed JSON" errorName=Error taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:proof
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=malformed JSON | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
-- Gateway restarted on the same state dir --
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=2001 error="malformed JSON" ... sessionKey=agent:main:proof
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=malformed JSON | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
```

The branch Gateway log has no `malformed JSON` line.

Stored tool-result row in `transcript_events`, read back from the agent SQLite file:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Max JSON depth of `details` | 1102 | 256 |
| Max JSON depth of the event | 1208 | 362 |

Checks on this branch: `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the changed files. Node 24.22.1, Ubuntu 24.04.
