prs.title: fix(secrets): avoid false plaintext findings for config-owned env markers
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Generated `models.json` intentionally stores an env SecretRef's variable name as its API-key marker. A custom variable such as `FACTCHAT_API_KEY` is currently reported as `PLAINTEXT_FOUND` even when the same configured provider owns that exact reference.

Fixes #121543. Related to #87723.

## Why this change was made

The audit now selects the source provider through the writer's existing `normalizeSourceProviderLookup`, then uses `resolveConfigSecretRef(..., includeResolved: true)` to recover the winning provider's reference, including shorthand already materialized by config loading. Only an API-key value equal to that provider's env-reference ID receives the exemption. Canonical-key precedence is preserved before inspecting the credential source. Headers, unrelated providers, losing aliases, literal uppercase credentials, and unresolved objects retain their existing findings.

This continues the narrow audit-side work in #121578, #121594, #121633, and #87873. Those PRs are closed without merging; #121578's closing comment invites a fresh current-main repair. The replacement addresses the review gaps around include-backed references, populated environment variables, mixed-source alias collisions, and the marker/merge import cycle. Merged #97622 only covered known markers on the config audit surface.

## User impact

Source-owned custom env markers stop producing misleading plaintext warnings. Serialization, credential resolution, and persisted data formats are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source-level before/after probe: **27 scenarios passed** using the production `collectModelsJsonSecrets` function extracted verbatim from each revision, with real provider-lookup, reference-resolution, include, config-env-substitution, marker, and bounded JSON-reader modules. Plugin metadata readers used a fixed fixture inventory.
- Changed positive cases reproduce the finding on the base and clear it on the patch: object refs, pending/populated shorthand, include-backed populated shorthand, later-alias ownership, dotted provider names, and the production source-managed writer's output.
- Negative controls preserve findings for cross-provider and mismatched IDs, talk-only ownership, literal/escaped/mixed templates, canonical env/file/store/literal/absent winners in either insertion order, losing aliases, sensitive headers, and unresolved objects. Malformed JSON remains a sanitized unresolved finding.
- Inspected the production snapshot path: include resolution precedes `resolveConfigForRead`; `createConfigFileSnapshot` attaches its resolution facts to `sourceConfig`. The probe directly executes include and env-read helpers, but does not execute the complete snapshot orchestration.
- `oxfmt --check src/secrets/audit.ts` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review and pr-simplify completed. Production delta: **+18/-0 in one file**; tests: **+0/-0**. Reuses existing lookup/provenance owners without new state or a parallel parser.

### Validation limits — kept as draft

This is source-boundary evidence, **not a completed production CLI run**. Full audit import remains blocked by missing runtime dependencies (`kysely`); the existing audit Vitest command stopped before tests because its subprocess preparation lacked `typescript`. No completed build, full test-suite result, live provider request, or Windows-specific reproduction is claimed. The workspace instruction prohibited adding/changing tests and running builds, so no repository tests were changed and no further compilation was attempted. Maintainers should run the existing focused audit/writer suites and the normal type/import-cycle gates before merge.

AI-assisted implementation and review.

prs.title: fix(cli): directory lookups rewrite openclaw.json and enable unrelated plugins such as codex
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw directory self|peers|groups` rewrites `openclaw.json` and enables plugins the user never chose (for example `plugins.entries.codex.enabled: true` from an `openai/*` default model) when a lookup runs.

## User Impact

User impact: directory lookups leave `openclaw.json` unchanged unless they install a missing channel plugin, and then they write only that install. Plugin loading still applies auto-enable at runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The directory setup step applied global plugin auto-enable to the authored config and committed the result whenever auto-enable reported a change. This write and the matching channel-auth write were added together in March. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131235 later moved this step to the authored source config and kept the auto-enable write as an intentional enable branch. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145575 then chose install-only persistence for channel auth (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144972); this PR applies the same choice to directory. Gateway startup already applies auto-enable for its runtime without writing config.

- Explicit-channel resolution now receives the authored source config, as channel auth does since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145575, and only its install-on-demand change is committed.
- Directory execution already reads the refreshed runtime config after any write, and plugin loading applies auto-enable at runtime.
- The existing test that asserted the write is rewritten as the regression, and the docs line that described "auto-enable writes" now says a lookup does not write plugin auto-enable to config.

## Evidence

Tested at `e4dffa42d3e` (base `upstream/main` `11d0c854192`). The CLI proof was captured at `25c2b9481d6`; the head differs from it only in the regression test and one docs line, so the production code that ran is the same.

Built CLI on Ubuntu 22.04 with Node 24, an isolated home and state directory, no network and no provider keys. Starting config: `{"agents":{"defaults":{"model":"openai/gpt-5.5"}},"channels":{"whatsapp":{}}}`. Command: `openclaw directory self --channel whatsapp --json`.

Before (base `11d0c854192`):

```text
{
  "status": "unavailable",
  "channel": "whatsapp",
  "accountId": "default",
  "reason": "plugin-returned-no-self-identity"
}
exit 0
sha256 before: acc33b000ebe36ea5ce0daa0c95853364d4a9225e6486ded2d0f9605bc9f5b32
sha256 after:  c439973140defb66151b810397b5a98414152503c52cb572c8c68c17918e0f97
$ diff -u openclaw.before.json openclaw.json   (excerpt; hunk header, reformatted lines and meta omitted)
+  "plugins": {
+    "entries": {
+      "openai": {
+        "enabled": true
+      },
+      "codex": {
+        "enabled": true
+      }
+    }
+  },
```

After (this PR):

```text
{
  "status": "unavailable",
  "channel": "whatsapp",
  "accountId": "default",
  "reason": "plugin-returned-no-self-identity"
}
exit 0
sha256 before: acc33b000ebe36ea5ce0daa0c95853364d4a9225e6486ded2d0f9605bc9f5b32
sha256 after:  acc33b000ebe36ea5ce0daa0c95853364d4a9225e6486ded2d0f9605bc9f5b32
$ diff -u openclaw.before.json openclaw.json
(no change)
```

Observed result: the same lookup output on both sides; on the base the config gains `plugins.entries.openai` and `plugins.entries.codex` (plus the `meta` stamp every write adds), with this PR the file is byte-identical.

Upgrade from the latest stable (`openclaw@2026.10.5` from npm) to this PR, same isolation, two state directories written by the stable CLI and then used by this PR's built CLI (`config validate`, `directory self --channel <ch> --json`, `directory self --json`):

- A, stored auto-enable entry: stable `config set agents.defaults.model openai/gpt-5.5` and `directory self --channel telegram` left `plugins.entries.openai.enabled: true` in the config (the bug in the shipped release). After the upgrade the config validates, both lookups return the same result as stable, and the file keeps the entry byte for byte (SHA-256 `b90ae0bf…` before and after).
- B, no stored entries: stable `config set agents.defaults.model openai/gpt-5.5` on a WhatsApp config, no `plugins` section. After the upgrade the config validates, both lookups reach the WhatsApp plugin, and the file stays byte-identical (`8a070d3d…`), so directory operation does not rely on persisted auto-enable entries.

<details>
<summary>Upgrade run output</summary>

```text
$ [stable] openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
$ [head] openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (e4dffa4)

== scenario A

exit 0

$ [head] openclaw config validate
Config valid: <tmp>/A/state/openclaw.json
$ [head] openclaw directory self --channel telegram --json
{ "status": "unavailable", "channel": "telegram", "accountId": "default", "reason": "plugin-returned-no-self-identity" }
exit 0
$ [head] openclaw directory self --json
{ "status": "unavailable", "channel": "telegram", "accountId": "default", "reason": "plugin-returned-no-self-identity" }
exit 0
sha256 after head:   b90ae0bf27af3b4c8069d6eded5b15334c695bda30822618de5ac0b4f609c8dc
config unchanged by this branch

== scenario B
$ [stable] openclaw config set agents.defaults.model openai/gpt-5.5
Updated agents.defaults.model. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
plugins.entries after stable: null
sha256 after stable: 8a070d3d4a86006581317dbc7f5b995e47d5f9cfa6cfb88de7134dc795c3c250
$ [head] openclaw config validate
Config valid: <tmp>/B/state/openclaw.json
$ [head] openclaw directory self --channel whatsapp --json
{ "status": "unavailable", "channel": "whatsapp", "accountId": "default", "reason": "plugin-returned-no-self-identity" }
exit 0
$ [head] openclaw directory self --json

```

JSON results are shown on one line; the head runs also printed an unrelated Telegram plugin SDK deprecation warning, omitted here.

</details>

Regression test: "does not persist plugin auto-enable during an omitted-channel lookup" and "… an explicit-channel lookup" in `src/cli/directory-cli.test.ts` both fail on the base (`replaceConfigFile` called once) and pass here; the other 17 tests in the file pass on both.

Checks: the touched test file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, time below), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `git diff --check`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI. The one red CI job, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and `openclaw/ci-gate`, which reports it), fails its mock-exports step on `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.missing-command.test.ts`, a file this PR does not touch. The CI merge base `7cb1ea1f8e8` already contains https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b78b230a1c, which added that file, but not https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cc942bc04e1, where main fixed its mock; `pnpm test:ci-failed` lists it as pre-existing.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds (vitest duration of its own shard) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cli/directory-cli.test.ts` | 6.50 s | 46.18 s in `checks-node-changed-1` (96% transform) |

Simplify pass: the auto-enable call, its import and the auto-enable commit condition are gone, leaving one writer (install-on-demand); the rewritten test keeps only the no-write regression for the omitted and explicit channel paths, since selection from the runtime config is already covered by the implicit-channel test. Behavior still protected: install-on-demand writes for an explicit channel and runtime-config selection for an omitted one. Delta against the merge base: production +4/−10 in 1 file, tests +16/−25 in 1 file, docs +1/−1.

Not covered: only `directory self` with an explicit channel ran through the built CLI; the omitted-channel path is covered by the regression test, and `peers`, `groups list` and `groups members` share the same setup step. No run used a channel whose own plugin is enabled only by auto-enable; that path relies on plugin loading applying auto-enable at runtime. No live channel account was used, so the lookup itself returned no identity on both sides.

prs.title: fix(cli): compare gateway state dirs case-insensitively on Windows
prs.body:
Closes #185913

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Windows, `openclaw configure` (and `openclaw doctor`) falsely report that the CLI and the installed Gateway service use different state directories when the two spellings of the same physical path differ only by letter case, so `configure` refuses to run.

## User Impact

User impact: on Windows, when the CLI's resolved state/config paths and the installed Gateway service's recorded paths point to the same NTFS directory but differ only in case (and the trailing state directory does not exist yet), setup and doctor now work instead of failing with a false "different state directories" error. Paths that genuinely differ are still detected and reported.

## Why This Change Was Made

`compareCliGatewayStateDirs` (src/cli/state-dir-gateway-check.ts) compares the CLI and Gateway paths byte-for-byte with `!==`. Windows path identity is case-insensitive, and `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` preserves the input's case for not-yet-created trailing components (it only realpaths the deepest existing ancestor). So `.openclaw` vs `.OPENCLAW` for the same physical directory resolves to two strings that differ only by case and is misreported as a divergence, which the `configure` state-store guard (`stateStoreGuard: "run"`) turns into a hard refusal.

The fix compares Windows paths case-insensitively (matching the repo's established Windows path-identity idiom) while keeping case-sensitive comparison on POSIX, where paths are genuinely case-sensitive.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11 (win32). The shipped CLI was built from this branch and run under Node 26.12.1 (the CLI requires Node >=24.22.1 / >=26.12.1); the real commands below reproduce the issue scenario end to end.

**Exact reproduction before the patch** (calls the actual `compareCliGatewayStateDirs` through the real `realpathExistingAncestorSync` with a non-existent `.openclaw` / `.OPENCLAW` trailing component under an existing parent):

```
A resolved: C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\...\existing-dir\.openclaw
B resolved: C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\...\existing-dir\.OPENCLAW
case-sensitive comparison  => true   (falsely reported as different)
case-insensitive comparison => false (physically the same directory on NTFS)

outcome (before fix): {"kind":"refuse","message":"No credentials or configuration were written.
CLI and installed Gateway service use different state directories (CLI: ...\\.openclaw;
Gateway: ...\\.OPENCLAW) and config paths (...) ..."}
```

**Observed result after the fix:** the same call returns `{"kind":"allow"}`.

**Regression test:** added `state-dir-gateway-check.test.ts > treats state and config paths that differ only by case as the same directory`. It is `skipIf(process.platform !== "win32")` and:
- red on base: `1 failed | 6 passed` (guard returns `refuse`, expected `allow`)
- green with the fix: `7 passed`

**Focused tests after the fix (all passing on Windows):**
- `src/cli/state-dir-gateway-check.test.ts` — 7 passed
- `src/cli/program/preaction.test.ts` — 20 passed
- `src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts` — 22 passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — exit 0 (typecheck)

## Shipped CLI behavior proof (real commands, Windows 11)

The real CLI was built from this branch (`OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (22dc684)`). A Windows scheduled task records the installed Gateway service environment with `.OPENCLAW` (uppercase) while the CLI is invoked with `.openclaw` (lowercase) — the same physical directory, with the trailing component not yet created.

### 1. Setup — `openclaw gateway status --deep`

```
Service: Scheduled Task (registered) (diagnostic only, not the check target)
Service file: ~\.openclaw\gateway.cmd
Service env: OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OPENCLAW OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OPENCLAW\openclaw.json
Config (cli): ~\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.openclaw\openclaw.json (missing)
```

The installed service records `.OPENCLAW`; the CLI config resolves `.openclaw` (missing).

### 2. `openclaw configure` with the case-only alias — opens, no refusal

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.openclaw
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.openclaw\openclaw.json
openclaw configure

Interactive configuration requires an interactive terminal (TTY).
For non-interactive setup, use these subcommands instead:
  openclaw config set <path> <value>  write a config entry
  ...
```

With the fix the state-store guard returns `allow`, so `configure` proceeds (in a TTY it opens the Configure UI).

### 3. `openclaw configure` with a genuinely different path — still refuses (guard active)

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OTHER
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OTHER\openclaw.json
openclaw configure

[openclaw] Reason: No credentials or configuration were written. CLI and installed Gateway service use different state directories (CLI: C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OTHER; Gateway: C:\Users\10211007.WIN-Q55IS7UUBKD\AppData\Local\Temp\ocproof\.OPENCLAW) and config paths (CLI: ...\.OTHER\openclaw.json; Gateway: ...\.OPENCLAW\openclaw.json). Fix: run OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR='...\.OPENCLAW' OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH='...' openclaw configure.
```

Before the fix, the case-only scenario in (2) produced exactly this refusal; after the fix only genuinely divergent paths do.

### 4. `openclaw doctor` uses the identical comparison

Doctor's state-directory note (`noteGatewayStateDirectory` / `noteInstalledGatewayStateDirectory` in `src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.ts`) calls the same `compareCliGatewayStateDirs` + `inspectInstalledGatewayStatePaths` that the `configure` guard above uses, rendering the same outcome as a warning instead of a refusal. The case-only alias therefore produces no "Gateway state directory mismatch" warning — the allow result demonstrated in (2) applies. (The note is rendered by the interactive Doctor TUI, which requires a TTY; the shipped-command evidence above exercises the identical comparison through the `configure` guard.)

## Root Cause

Windows paths are case-insensitive at the filesystem level, but `compareCliGatewayStateDirs` compared them with a byte-for-byte `!==`. Because `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` realpaths only the deepest existing ancestor and re-appends unresolved trailing components using the input's original case, two spellings of the same not-yet-created directory (e.g. `.openclaw` vs `.OPENCLAW`) survive resolution as case-different strings and are misreported as divergent state trees.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage layer: unit (pure function, no I/O required to reproduce; the `realpathExistingAncestorSync` behavior it depends on is itself covered by `src/infra/path-existence` tests).
- Target file: `src/cli/state-dir-gateway-check.test.ts`, the new `treats state and config paths that differ only by case as the same directory` case.
- Why it is the minimal reliable guardrail: it directly exercises the two changed `!==` comparisons in `compareCliGatewayStateDirs` on the platform where they are wrong (`skipIf(process.platform !== "win32")`), is red on the base and green with the fix, and existing tests in the same file still cover genuinely divergent paths (the "refuses an offline home mismatch" case) and canonical symlink identity.

## Scope Boundary

Only the state-store guard comparison in `src/cli/state-dir-gateway-check.ts` was changed, plus its regression test. The same case-sensitivity class of issue in `src/cli/profile.ts` (profile-isolation path comparisons) is intentionally out of scope for this PR and is a separate follow-up. No CLI behavior changes on POSIX.

## AI-Assisted Work

This change was developed with AI assistance (code analysis, reproduction, and test authored with an AI coding agent) and verified locally on Windows per the evidence above.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

Related: #178058

## What Problem This Solves

Browser actions repeat a DNS policy check while preparing the response URL, even when that same address was admitted earlier in the request.

## User Impact

Unchanged-tab actions avoid one redundant lookup and return the same result and URL. This draft addresses the response-only duplicate; it does not claim to eliminate all per-action DNS checks or prove meeting audio recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action route opts in to reuse its admitted address only for response URL projection, with an exact URL and complete navigation-policy match. Changed URLs, changed policies, missing admission and cancellation retain validation. Execution and navigation guards remain authoritative. There is no cross-request cache, new setting or protocol change.

## Evidence

Actual Browser Bridge HTTP actions against an isolated Chrome 155 tab on macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0, with the default browser policy and real system DNS. Five serial baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes; all 30 actions per revision returned identical page data and response URLs. All ten `about:blank` controls performed zero hostname lookups.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DNS lookups per unchanged action | 4 | 3 |
| Warm action median (25 samples) | 270.30 ms | 270.70 ms |
| Warm action p95 | 289.54 ms | 287.59 ms |
| Cold completion median (5 samples) | 4770.63 ms | 4827.54 ms |
| Cold completion p95 | 5633.91 ms | 5371.78 ms |

The committed opt-in workload is rerunnable with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs extensions/browser/scripts/bench-act-dns.ts --chromium <chromium-executable> --output <result.json>
```

Cold completion includes isolated browser/page/bridge startup and the observer positive control. Action timing excludes observer flushing. No delayed DNS or simulated browser/provider results were used; slow-resolver stalls and meeting audio loss were not reproduced.

prs.title: feat(claws): add local packages through the gateway and preserve setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Integrations cannot add a converted local Claw package through a running gateway: the gateway Add API only accepts ClawHub coordinates, while an offline writer cannot mutate live gateway state.

## User Impact

An admin-authorized client can plan and add an absolute local package path on the gateway host. Installation uses the existing Claw checks, lifecycle, plugin consent, integrity validation, and rollback. Retrying an installation that rolled back before agent creation preserves its first-run instructions. Imported memory and skills no longer cause the first turn to discard custom setup instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source adapter feeds the existing Add owner:

```text
local package or ClawHub coordinate
  → resolve and inspect
  → plan + integrity check
  → native Add lifecycle
```

Local planning and application require `operator.admin`. Remote clients must transfer their package to the gateway host first. Rollback retires the existing workspace setup state along with a workspace it created and removed.

## Evidence

- Before: local source payload rejected by the gateway schema. After: an actual handler test installs instructions, the exact avatar bytes, and `BOOTSTRAP.md` as an ordinary agent.
- Before: failed Add → rollback → retry reports complete but omits `BOOTSTRAP.md`. After: the same actual-handler regression preserves the setup file.
- Regression coverage follows native Add through first-turn workspace preparation: imported memory and skills preserve a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md`; stock-template cleanup and explicit completion retain their existing behavior.
- Focused plan/apply, authorization, stale-source, schema, plugin handoff, and stateless rollback tests pass. Core type graphs, boundary checks, targeted lint and formatting pass.
- The full build passes, including CLI startup and plugin SDK export checks.
- Live isolated gateway proof at combined stack head `e33e4d5ca2b`: a fresh Stalk Bot installation completed a real agent turn with all 236 characters of custom setup instructions and 3,459 characters of memory injected without truncation. The setup file remains after the turn.
- Real WebSocket authorization regression passes for local packages: admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and real device-token revocation at the pre-effect gate prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The catalog positive control remains covered. No authority predicate is mocked; assertions cover agent configuration, installed-plugin records, and extension directories.
- Final setup regression and existing workspace sibling cases: 53 tests passed. Final runtime build passed; private workspace-logic changes do not alter the declaration/SDK export surface checked by the preceding full build.

**Merge risk:** reversible code change; affects the Claw Add source boundary and cleanup of newly created workspaces. Existing ClawHub behavior remains covered.

Prior-head CI blocker: the unchanged updater mock check also fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710); the [native classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992603758/job/117280609263) marks it pre-existing. That aggregate remains red; no exception or unrelated fix is included. The conflict-only stack restack onto `acd27635` preserves all three core patches exactly; current-head CI must run separately.

Additional private-QA full-build check: SDK declarations exceed the private testing budget. An isolated captured-main build produces the same 456 public-reachable declaration files byte-for-byte (5,440,829 bytes versus the 5,340,536-byte cap). No budget change or unrelated repair is included. Runtime/UI artifacts were generated; the full command is recorded as failed.

Compatibility evidence is scoped to the existing state contract and production boundaries. Compared directly with `v2026.10.4`, setup state remains version 1, `WorkspaceSetupState` fields are identical, and the complete `workspace_setup_state` SQL definition is byte-identical. The PR changes no persisted schema or config format. Existing completed state skips reconciliation; rollback cleanup only retires a newly created, uncommitted workspace. The 48 passing workspace cases plus 5 native Add cases cover retained completed timestamps/content, stock cleanup, concurrent completion, custom pending setup, and explicit completion. This is not a claim that a full product upgrade was executed.

Paired saved runtime proof: before the setup fix (`5ffb1320fcc`), `bootstrapExists=false` and `bootstrapInjected=false`; after (`e33e4d5ca2b`), `BOOTSTRAP.md` injected 236/236 characters without truncation and remained present after the turn. The baseline predates the fix; it is not an exact current-merge-base replay.

## Main refresh (2026-10-27)

Merged current `main` (`cfccaef15a4`) into this branch instead of rebasing, so the stacked #174960 keeps its history. Conflicts were resolved against main's publisher package names, Claw drafts, workspace attestation hashes, and rollback effect leases; the gateway validators were regenerated.

Main's Gateway Add now holds plural state leases (#184784), but its bootstrap setup-state write still requested generic worker admission, so lease admission refused every Claw that ships `BOOTSTRAP.md` ("State lease worker ownership was refused"). `8d64690136b` passes the held lease identities to the worker and asserts them inside the transaction, as worktree capacity does. The existing local Add handler test fails on the unfixed code and passes with the fix; it now confirms the Gateway config-write application, which main's Add requires.

Local proof on `ed5ea8ff143`: 14 focused test files pass (Claw Add plan/apply/stateless/manifest, local handler, Gateway method scopes, workspace and bootstrap, agent creation, state-lease transactions; 2m17s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`); `tsgo:core`, core src test types, oxlint, oxfmt, `protocol:check`, and `gateway:validators:check` pass. The real-Gateway e2e was not rerun locally; PR CI covers it.

Upgrade compatibility after the refresh (ClawSweeper's data-model request): the PR's diff against `main` touches no persisted schema, migration, config, or Doctor file. Its only schema change is the Gateway wire protocol (Add request params and the plan-response manifest disclosure), which is not stored. Lease identities travel only in the in-process worker command. The `workspace_setup_state` table and `WorkspaceSetupState` shape belong to `main` and this PR leaves them unchanged. Existing completed setup still skips reconciliation; a never-completed workspace with a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` now stays pending until setup completes, which is the intended fix.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Fixes #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate`, the only insert path. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error, and hosts without ranged listing stand down the same way instead of scanning inline.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (17 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; and a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current validation: both overflow files passed 18/18 tests in 9.05s warm; the boundary suite passed 12/12 in 4.05s; oxlint, oxfmt, and production extension typecheck passed. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload can paint cached transcript rows and then change their link labels, image presentation, notices and avatars. The proposed display-only snapshot facts keep prior complete rows visible while live authority reconnects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transcript IndexedDB owner retains bounded row facts and previously displayed authorized inline thumbnails. Its projection reset, cached-window pruning and existing scope/sign-out invalidations own their lifecycle. Cached pixels authorize neither reads nor actions. The runtime compression removed parallel image, snapshot-validation and facts modules; handwritten runtime growth fell from +1,018 to +760 lines (25.3% reduction).

## User Impact

The accepted complete-row visual result is preserved. This experiment is closing without a ready PR because the required net-zero test/support line gate remains unmet. No merge or new runtime optimization was performed in this round.

## Evidence

Runtime candidate: `76115e6bd389b8f528cf058436492c89d6302bce`; matched main control: `842dfae24ad1b73a9599f6c57fdc5d581b49cc80`. The current main rebase and header-hydration integration remain pending. Archived-state change #185788 is already an ancestor; #186056 is not.

The existing 11-pair signed-in native comparison has zero late visible row facts and zero thread-height changes in all 11 reloads on both routes. That native viewport qualifies the titled session link and managed image; the broader links/images/notices/avatars fixture was qualified separately in the previously accepted experiment. These claims are not pooled.

### Accepted tradeoff

The maintainer accepted the remaining chat paint/blocking cost. Existing unprofiled chat paint medians with animation sampling disabled are 419.36 → 442.10 ms (+22.74 ms); formal animation-enabled LoAF blocking is 171.90 → 196.60 ms (+24.70 ms). The corresponding paired median deltas are +28.54 ms and +16.80 ms. No profiled timing replaces these results, and no observer cost is subtracted.

The earlier extended-fixture dashboard FCP tradeoff, 184 → 192 ms (+8 ms), remains explicitly accepted: baseline A/A paired 0 ms, reversed-order B/A paired +8 ms, repeated A/B +4 ms. It is separate from the later native-rig comparison.

### Single CPU-profile pair

AWS Crabbox `cbx_2b7af9ff6eb7`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, run `run_ed69fd547fe14a3ab4016867ad9522c6`; observed 93.7% CPU idle. Exactly one baseline/candidate chat warm pair was profiled. Cold and seed reloads were unprofiled qualification only. Both exact sourcemaps, raw CPU profiles and timeline traces were retained locally.

Sampled candidate work in the largest mount microtask:

| Suspect | Approximate sampled ms |
| --- | ---: |
| Object-URL creation | 0.165 |
| Title owner, inclusive | 0.164 |
| Snapshot-record owner, inclusive | 0.817 |
| Image presentation owner, inclusive | 1.750 |
| Avatar owners, inclusive | 2.121 |

Inclusive samples overlap and must not be added. The largest native layout read maps to the same existing transcript layout owner in both arms (22.17 → 21.15 ms sampled self time). Largest mount microtasks were 143.06 / 151.12 ms under profiling; these are attribution, not performance results. The pair did not identify a cheap cache-owner fix or causally account for the entire unprofiled paint delta. Asynchronous decoding and object URLs scoped to mounted images already exist. No runtime change was made, so the conditional five-pair follow-up was not triggered.

### Geometry and focused proof

The prompt-attachments e2e file has 10 passes / 1 failure on both pinned main and candidate. Both fail the same first-prompt geometry assertion: expected overflow `auto`, received `scroll`. This is inherited from the matched main control. File wall times: 54.210 / 51.097 seconds, one worker.

The audited native reconnect file passes 2/2, one worker, 24.526 seconds. Thirteen focused unit files pass 283 tests, individually with one worker; wall times range 2.46–6.26 seconds. Remote and local audit patches match after normalizing Git index-hash abbreviation. No full-suite or fresh-ready-head CI claim is made.

### Test-line stop

The published head has +909 test/support lines against its merge base. The reviewed, tested audit patch removes 118 lines across eight test files and remains staged locally, leaving a proposed +791 (1,093 added / 302 deleted). The baseline file is untouched. This is our unmet gate, not an inherited test-line failure. The scoped audit retained distinct display/admission, storage, privacy, cancellation and lifecycle proof; no additional quota-only deletion was made.

Handwritten runtime delta remains +760 (1,676 added / 916 deleted). The campaign's literal production-stat filter reports +1,616 (2,698 / 1,082); that filter also includes fixtures, generated files and TSX tests.

Prior exact-head branch autoreview was clean through P2. The test-audit review raised three P2 concerns; source-based adjudication rejected them because retained tests cover managed-avatar no-decode presentation, direct/prewarmed projection reset, and timer-only persistence without lifecycle flush. The raw review verdict and adjudication remain preserved; this is not a new full-candidate clean-review claim.

Current draft checks have broad jobs skipped. The current PR-context check succeeds; the older same-SHA context failure was superseded by the corrected evidence heading and successful checks. The unpublished audit patch has no GitHub CI result. The current-main rebase, final review and ready-head CI are pending the test-budget decision.

The AWS lease is released, has no host, and cleanup is complete. No local Gateway was started. Previous inspected synthetic before/after media remains in the [prior experiment evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186172#issuecomment-6458701107).

prs.body:
Related: #161885

## What Problem This Solves

This draft currently conflicts with main. The candidate below predates the current Talk admission and CLI authority lifecycle; it needs to be adapted and revalidated before the behavior can be claimed on current main.

Browser Talk consultations fail with an Anthropic API-key error when the selected model uses `claude-cli`, without trying the configured fallback. This revision also closes the terminal-event gap found in the submitted adapter when session-read or model-lock preflight rejects.

## User Impact

Browser Talk honors model-scoped CLI routing and the configured fallback chain, including CLI-only setups without a direct provider API key. Caller permissions, generated-prompt visibility and cancellation stay with the existing owners. No configuration or public SDK changes are required.

This covers the Control UI/native GPT-Live consultation path. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime plugin consultation paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser consultation enters the canonical admitted turn/fallback owner and selects the runtime for each candidate. It retains one admission, transcript recorder and terminal result across attempts. Non-steerable CLI turns use GPT-Live's existing joined replacement path; revoked or foreign authority remains a hard failure. The existing completion-claim block moves to a focused sibling module because its original file is over the line cap.

The correction requested in the [landing review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164229#issuecomment-5969946723) now puts fallible session-read/model-lock preflight and selection inside the existing terminal backstop's try/catch/finally. Regressions cover both rejections and cancellation while the read is pending. The refreshed candidate preserves upstream fixture changes, removes two obsolete internal CLI call properties, and prunes exactly four retired Talk mock-baseline entries using the repository guard.

## Evidence

- Current-main rework is pending: preserve candidate-specific runtime selection, source and tool authority, cancellation, session lifecycle, and terminal write ownership. The evidence below applies to the earlier candidate identified in this PR, not a refreshed head.

- **Current candidate:** 180 tests across nine owning files passed in 231.497 seconds, using eight canonical Vitest shards and a fresh frozen installation. This covers routing/preflight, whole-turn CLI timing, termination classification, fallback, async auth discovery, Talk storage/lineage and parent-session forking. Canonical mock-baseline shrink, conflict-marker and both line-cap guards passed.
- **Fresh repository autoreview:** scoped-clean through P2, zero findings, on tree `cee305578f2ee173f1136930713f86a9e20fdfb8`. The interrupted first attempt produced no validated report; its single recovery completed successfully. Independent source assessment found no incompatible upstream owner contract.
- **Product validation before this necessary rebase:** 697 tests across 39 files passed in 522.763 seconds on tree `61d9f1df2cc6b2d313609d49564c897bdc5e977e`. The three preflight regressions fail on the uncorrected adapter for missing terminals, then pass after the repair. All five candidate production blobs remain byte-identical after the rebase.
- On that prior tree, the **full canonical build passed** in 1696.478 seconds, with every step retained. Core/UI production types, script types, the canonical OpenAI package graph, affected agent/Gateway test-type graphs, changed-core typed lint, full formatting, preflight/tail guards and all three unused-export scans passed.
- The prior-tree **real-Gateway replay passed** CLI primary, CLI429-to-loopback fallback, direct embedded and ordinary agent controls. Reduced `operator.read` + `operator.talk` CLI launches disable native tools and retain the five-tool readonly MCP allowlist. Repeated calls, single-use claims, CLI cancel/replacement, zero successor HTTP requests after fallback-boundary cancellation, and direct upstream cancellation pass. All 15 recorded runs have exactly one terminal.

[Scripts, sanitized observations, review receipts and exact source hashes](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/d530ab2f733aaf74a1e4dc1585e546b4c9f7943d/proof/issue-161885-terminal-repair)

The rebase onto `8dbf0538e72f7ca09504640dcf80ef089f4550f9` resolves the mock-baseline conflict by preserving main and removing exactly the same four retired Talk entries. It also retains upstream fixture and Gateway inventory changes. Current publication is `e7cfae3f6cb0aabe4633e82bac09c967ce8ec284`, tree `cee305578f2ee173f1136930713f86a9e20fdfb8`. Earlier build/Gateway proof was executed as an exact staged delta on base `3c0f7e4c5cdade301b896970c9afbf4ab253de5e`, tree `61d9f1df`; production-blob equivalence does not make that proof a rerun of current upstream composition.

prs.title: fix(discord): native slash commands fail in a plugin-bound thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native slash commands fail with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` in a Discord thread that a plugin has bound with `/codex bind`. The Gateway logs `Session key does not contain an agent id; resolve it with the configured default agent.` I saw `/status` and `/codex binding` fail this way on main at da60d41, and `/codex detach` fail the same way on an earlier main commit, 572cb278b243. A plain message in the same thread works. Native commands in a DM or a top level guild channel do not hit this, and neither do threads bound to an ACP or subagent session.

## User Impact

Native slash commands in a plugin-bound thread now run against the same session as in an unbound thread, with the agent that thread's route selects. A plugin command such as `/codex binding` reaches its handler with the thread id and parent id it uses to find its binding. No configuration change is needed.

In an in-process run at an earlier head, 59a4746d, `/codex binding` in a plugin-bound thread failed with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` and never reached the plugin, while `/status` worked, when the channel routed to a non-default agent and the binding record named a different agent.

One base refusal is not kept, on purpose. With a `match: { channel: "discord", accountId: "*" }` route binding and no narrower scope, `/new` and `/reset` in a plugin-bound thread under a disabled parent failed on main with the session key error. They now reach the existing `binding.channel` recovery exception, as in an unbound thread with that route binding. The failure was the crash and not a rule about disabled parents, so I did not add code to keep it. Without that route binding a disabled parent still blocks `/new`, as a test pins.

The source at v2026.8.1-beta.1, the stable tags I sampled through v2026.10.5 and main has this failure, and I did not run those releases. v2026.7.35 resolved the key to the default agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native route passes the thread binding record's session key to `resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute` as the bound session. That function calls `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey`, which throws when a key has no agent id, and a plugin binding key such as `plugin-binding:codex:...` has none. The inbound message path has skipped plugin-owned records since #45318, at `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts:57-59`. It treats them as unbound, and the plugin command finds its own binding from the conversation. This change adds the same guard in `native-command-route.ts`.

The guard returns `undefined` where the message path returns an empty string, because the native dispatcher does not treat an empty string as unbound. `src/channels/native-command-session-targets.ts:13` would take it as the command's session key, and `native-command.ts:304` tests `boundSessionKey != null` to bypass the ACP guild guards for `/new` and `/reset`. An empty string would let those commands skip a disabled-parent denial.

An unbound thread takes its agent from the channel route, and plugin binding metadata has no agent id, so the record's agent can differ from the route's. For a plugin-owned record, `native-command.ts` now takes the agent for the session lookup, the plugin command call and the reply recording from `effectiveRoute.agentId`. Other thread records and configured bindings keep their previous agent. Before this, the shared plugin runtime at `src/plugins/plugin-command-execution.ts:58` rejected the mismatched agent and session pair before any handler ran.

Telegram and Slack thread commands use the core runtime binding route, which classifies plugin-owned records, so this change is Discord only. #146898 overlaps on the call chain only. It edits `route-resolution.ts` for free ACP keys, which this change does not touch.

## Evidence

Focused tests fail on main and pass with this change. A local Gateway run on da60d41 and 915f97d shows the session key failure and its fix end to end against a stand-in for Discord, but not the non-default-agent path, which only the focused tests cover. No real Discord client, server or model was used in either, and that is the live gap.

The tests are in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.interaction-boundary.test.ts`, in a `plugin-bound thread` describe. The change adds five cases to the 16 on main at eb8fa7d, 21 in all. The cases drive the real internal Discord client. REST, session lookup, the status reply builder, the agent turn, the reply recorder and the `codex` handler are stubs. Parsing, access policy, route resolution and plugin command dispatch are real.

- Three cases use agent `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>`. `/codex binding` must reach the handler with that session key, `args: "binding"` and the thread and parent ids. `/new` under a disabled parent must get `This channel is disabled.` with no context build and no agent turn.
- The work-route case routes the channel to `work` and gives the plugin-owned record `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread id>`. The session lookup, the handler call and the recorded reply must all use agent `work` and that session.
- The refusal case has an agent-owned subagent record that names `main` with bound session `agent:work:subagent:bound`. The handler must not run, and the reply must be `⚠️ Command failed. Please try again later.` Before #180173 the shared plugin runtime threw on this mismatch. It now catches the error and drops its text.
- At 8ffec518 all 17 pass. With only `native-command-route.ts` reverted to da60d41, 13 pass and the work-route case and the three `main` cases fail with `Session key does not contain an agent id`. prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` once media streaming is active, and Voice Call starts the stream inside the answer command. So noise suppression could never be started per call on inbound realtime Telnyx calls, and the engine could never be chosen. Telnyx's number level setting only runs its default engine.

## User impact

Operators can set `telnyx.noiseSuppression` (`direction`, optional `engine`, optional `engineConfig`) to denoise caller audio on inbound realtime Telnyx calls before it reaches the realtime model, including Krisp's telephony voice isolation model for callers in rooms with other people talking. It is off by default. When it is unset, when a call has no media stream, and for every outbound dial, the Telnyx requests are byte for byte unchanged. The plugin config surface budget rises by ten keys.

## How it works

- When the setting is on and the call streams, Voice Call answers without stream params, calls `suppression_start`, then `streaming_start` with the same stream fields. Telnyx support confirmed this order.
- If `suppression_start` fails or exceeds a 5s timeout, Voice Call logs a warning and streams anyway, so the 30s stream token is still valid for `streaming_start`.
- If `streaming_start` fails after the answer, the call is hung up instead of being left silent.
- `engineConfig` is passed as `noise_suppression_engine_config` with Telnyx's field names (Krisp `model` and `suppression_level`, DeepFilterNet `attenuation_limit` and `mode`, AiCoustics `enhancement_level` and `voice_gain`). It requires `engine`.
- Docs state the prerequisite Telnyx support confirmed: a number level suppression setting engages the default engine at answer and collides with `suppression_start`, returning a 500, so it must be set to `disabled` first.
- Known limitation, only with the setting on: if Telnyx processes the stream less answer but its HTTP response is lost, the call stays answered without media until it ends.

## Evidence

- Unset path: the streaming answer and dial tests compare exact request bytes and pass unchanged.
- New tests cover request order, the wait for suppression to settle, the 5s timeout, fail open on 422 and on network errors, answers without a stream, hangup when streaming fails including when the hangup itself fails, unchanged outbound dials, runtime wiring, config schema, and the engine config mapping for Krisp and AiCoustics.
- `extensions/voice-call`: 58 files, 734 tests pass on v2026.10.7. Format, lint, extension type check, `config:docs:check`, and `config:schema:check` pass.
- Live Telnyx verification of the per call path is pending the number level setting being disabled on our test number; the request order itself was confirmed by Telnyx support.

Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): keep flood guard correct across backward clock steps
prs.body:
Replacement for closed-unmerged #156693, addressing the proof gaps from its ClawSweeper review.

## Problem

The flood buffer is insertion-ordered, but the guard reverse-scans it as though timestamps are sorted and stops at the first out-of-window value. A backward wall-clock step can place a stale timestamp between newer in-window starts, causing the guard to under-count a real burst.

## Fix

Count every in-window start, sort those timestamps newest-first, and derive the same threshold-oldest retry instant from the filtered set.

## Proof

This revision replaces the unreachable direct fixture from #156693 with scheduler-reachable state:

- the unit regression builds the buffer exclusively through `recordRunStart`, with `lastRunStartedAtMs` equal to the final recorded start;
- the scheduler regression drives six manual wakes through the registered handler/bookkeeping path across a backward clock step, then verifies a scheduled wake is skipped as `flood` with `retryAtMs: 1005001`;
- `runOnce` remains at six calls, proving the seventh wake was actually blocked.

The prior downstream proof run measured the focused cooldown test at ~0.3s single-worker and the scheduler harness at ~2.3s; fresh CI on this rebased head should provide the current-main result.

No stored-data or scheduling-contract changes outside the flood-counting assumption.

prs.title: improve(android): build only bundles for store releases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Store and Internal releases spend time building a third-party APK that neither Google Play nor Firebase consumes.

## User Impact

Both release operations build only the signed phone and Wear AABs. Third-party APK publication and local `pnpm android:release:archive` retain their existing artifacts. No configuration or secret changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release lane selects the existing build helper's new `store` artifact group. Both AABs still share one Gradle invocation, and the helper retains its source, metadata, signing-certificate, and checksum checks. Version planning, screenshots, notes, atomic upload, and recovery are unchanged.

This removes an unused build variant through the existing owner. The test diff is two lines smaller overall, with no baseline or ceiling change.

## Evidence

- The release-owner regression failed on the base because Store and Internal selected `third-party apk`; it passes with only the phone and Wear AABs. The same fixture verifies that the default archive still includes the APK.
- Focused release CLI, artifact/signing, and Fastlane gate tests: 25 passed, 23.16s wall time. After consolidating redundant printed-metadata assertions, the changed file passed again: 14 tests, 16.16s wall time / 14.45s test time.
- Targeted scripts/tooling test type checks, lint, format, Ruby syntax, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Simplification retained the existing build owner and archive default, without adding runtime state, a wrapper, or a cache.

### Build comparison results

The [five-pair hosted comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40613213394) passed all ten builds and the acceptance rule below. Median helper time improved **36.95%**, from **814.15s to 513.33s**; complete sample median improved **34.29%**, from **875s to 575s**. Every paired helper and complete sample improved. The diagnostic jobs all used GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners.

In every pair:

- Selected Gradle targets: **3 → 2** in the single artifact-build invocation.
- Executed Gradle task log entries: **208 → 151**. Exactly **57 `ThirdPartyRelease` tasks** disappeared, with no common task executions removed or added. The shared license check remains.
- Two signed AABs and their checksum sidecars passed verification in each sample. Both AAB SHA-256 hashes were **identical between baseline and candidate**. Baselines also built and verified the APK; candidates produced no APK.

All timings below are seconds. p95 is nearest-rank, hence the maximum for five samples. Spread is max minus min.

| Metric | Median, all → store | p95, all → store | Min–max, all → store | Spread, all → store |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build helper | 814.15 → 513.33 | 906.94 → 586.80 | 568.66–906.94 → 404.47–586.80 | 338.28 → 182.33 |
| Complete sample step | 875.00 → 575.00 | 982.00 → 651.00 | 621.00–982.00 → 458.00–651.00 | 361.00 → 193.00 |
| Signing preflight | 58.65 → 58.71 | 72.42 → 60.77 | 49.83–72.42 → 49.00–60.77 | 22.59 → 11.77 |

The unchanged signing-preflight command's median moved by +0.06s (+0.09%); its p95 decreased. No paired helper or complete-sample regression occurred. The complete sample uses Actions step timestamps, including reset, preflight, build, verification, and all daemon cleanup; it does not omit the Kotlin cleanup wait.

The [committed workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f225a2ce2854e41bb3826128655223d053e59f96) runs `scripts/android-store-bundles-comparison.py` for `all`, then `store`, with the environment defined in the reusable sample workflow. Download its five `android-build-comparison-pair-N` artifacts for proof JSON, logs, and Gradle profiles. It pins implementation `6df59b5d5fe4576551ae271c7a1316830467219b`; final PR head `56667f8d1c54ce00f5aeecd2ece9a732738cb08b` differs only by seven deleted test lines. The diagnostic helper is checked against production source with only one `--profile` argument added. The workload uses a synthetic certificate and publishes no builds.

<details>
<summary>Individual samples, setup, and resource observations</summary>

Each pair had four observed vCPUs. All paired values are baseline → candidate; setup and job times are shared by the whole pair.

| Pair / CPU | Helper | Change | Complete sample | Preflight | Shared setup | Pair job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 / Intel Xeon 6973P-C | 568.66 → 404.47 | -28.87% | 621 → 458 | 49.83 → 49.00 | 134 | 1227 |
| 2 / AMD EPYC 9V74 | 814.15 → 513.33 | -36.95% | 875 → 575 | 58.65 → 58.71 | 129 | 1588 |
| 3 / Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C | 632.03 → 417.70 | -33.91% | 691 → 471 | 55.70 → 50.37 | 135 | 1307 |
| 4 / AMD EPYC 7763 | 906.94 → 586.80 | -35.30% | 982 → 651 | 72.42 → 60.77 | 125 | 1766 |
| 5 / AMD EPYC 7763 | 823.35 → 552.32 | -32.92% | 895 → 616 | 67.91 → 60.39 | 131 | 1652 |

Build-stage host samples were recorded every five seconds. Minimum sampled available memory improved in all five pairs. Host CPU utilization was 90.7–94.9%, with zero observed CPU steal. Maximum observed swap use was 76 KiB; these observations show no material swap pressure. Load averages are kernel measurements, including runnable/waiting work, rather than process CPU percentages.

| Pair | CPU busy %, all → store | Minimum available GiB | Mean 1-minute load | Peak 1-minute load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 92.05 → 91.63 | 6.38 → 7.56 | 6.58 → 6.79 | 8.55 → 8.21 |
| 2 | 93.88 → 92.10 | 6.66 → 7.50 | 7.53 → 7.47 | 9.91 → 9.76 |

Available memory is a sampled VM-wide observation, not exact peak process RSS. GNU time CPU/RSS excludes detached Gradle/Kotlin daemons; the VM-wide samples cover their resource use. Pair 1's mean load rose slightly (6.58 → 6.79), and pair 5's peak load rose (10.00 → 10.63); CPU utilization, available memory, and complete sample time improved in both pairs. This comparison measures the build stage under the conditions below, not the entire screenshot/upload pipeline.

The baseline's Gradle profile identifies the removed work, including third-party lint analysis, R8, and Kotlin compilation. These task durations overlap and are not summed as wall-time savings.

</details>

### Build-only comparison: acceptance rule declared before execution

Compare the real helper's `--artifact all` baseline with `--artifact store` on the same committed candidate source and synthetic signing fixture. Use five serial interleaved pairs (ABABABABAB), each pair on a fresh GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner. Baseline and candidate share that runner's CPU, OS, SDK, and frozen Node dependencies; each gets a separate empty Gradle home and clean generated/build outputs, followed by the unchanged signing preflight. Stop the task-owned build daemons between samples. This measures same-host paired builds with cold Gradle/project outputs and post-preflight build timing; no full fresh-runner setup or warm-cache speedup is claimed.

Required counts: two signed AABs and two verified checksum sidecars in every sample; selected Gradle tasks fall from three to two; executed third-party tasks and produced APKs fall to zero. Source/signature/checksum checks must all pass. No Play, Firebase, OpenAI, release-ref recording, promotion, or production credentials are used.

Timing rule: candidate helper median improves by at least 5%, candidate p95 does not exceed baseline p95, and no paired helper or complete-sample regression reaches 20%. Report individual samples, median, nearest-rank p95, min/max, preflight/setup and complete-sample times (reset, preflight, build, and daemon shutdown), shared pair setup/job times, CPU/memory observations, and host load. Any material regression stops acceptance; no measured improvement means withdrawing the optimization. The committed diagnostic harness lives on a separate branch and is excluded from this PR.

<details>
<summary>Earlier diagnostic attempt, excluded from results</summary>

The [first diagnostic campaign](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40609971800) stopped after two successful builds because the diagnostic counter incorrectly treated the shared `validateThirdPartyLicenseAssets` check as APK-variant work. Its AMD baseline and Intel candidate also exposed CPU-model variance. Those incomplete samples are excluded. Before the qualifying run, the workload was corrected to count only actual third-party variant tasks and pair both modes on the same CPU with independently cold Gradle state. The gain/regression thresholds were unchanged, and the revised conditions were recorded before that run.

</details>

### CI and review

[Exact-head GitHub-hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611121982) settled: **42 passed, 24 skipped, two red jobs**. All seven Android jobs passed: phone, Wear, third-party tests, ktlint, screenshots, and both native page-size jobs. The test-line ratchet passed.

`check-dependencies` reports Knip unused files/exports across 18 paths, all verified byte-for-byte unchanged from the branch base. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` fails because of that job. There are no remaining failures attributable to this diff; CI is not fully green. Automatic CI was superseded. Automatic OpenGrep was force-canceled after GitHub assigned its Blacksmith runner; it has no hosted override and is not counted as passing proof.

Independent P0/P1 local autoreview of the implementation against `ca305f7d942550ea5aea5a218193fb506e55208a` and a fresh pass of the assertion consolidation against `6df59b5d5fe4576551ae271c7a1316830467219b` found no actionable issues. The hosted ClawSweeper review of the final head likewise reported no source findings; its missing build-comparison evidence is supplied above. The local ClawSweeper CLI attempt failed structured-output validation (`unexpected nextStep`) and is not claimed as a clean review.

Current head: `9d5d58e2ed2afa0a5e8a0bb8fe82422d66428192`. Both sets of SQLite regressions remain intact. The PR still changes six files, preserves original commits and human credit, and adds no attribution footer.

**Current-head focused validation:**
- All 40 tests pass: SQLite transcript (3), Telegram prompt context (15), shared transcript context (9), and tool-prefix stability (13).

**Live Telegram Test Server proof passed on prior head `09618b32c5e141cd74e35b91d88b9388ac0727dc`.** Five actual Gateway processes shared isolated SQLite state across four orderly replacements. A Convex-leased, independently authorized TDLib user observed the dedicated Test Server bot's replies.
