prs.title: fix(browser): preserve native CORS preflights
prs.body:
## Summary

Browser navigation guards used Playwright catch-all page routing, which made Chromium treat intercepted CORS preflights as permissive and could send a cross-origin request the destination rejected. This change moves guard handling into document-only CDP interception, preserves native CORS, and explicitly settles both a committed timed-out page opening and a committed streaming action document without cutting off subframe authority checks. It preserves the invocation-scoped navigation policy introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 and does not depend on the unmerged policy-removal proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703.

## What Problem This Solves

1. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation.ts`, guarded actions and guarded `goto` used catch-all Playwright routing. Playwright could synthesize a successful CORS preflight, so a rejecting destination received the non-simple `PUT`.
2. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-fence.ts`, the existing operation-owned fence tracked document redirects and out-of-process frames but did not own the route handler or limit Fetch interception to documents.
3. The first document-only implementation waited for a terminal Network event after a committed streamed document timed out. Chromium does not consistently emit that event after `Page.stopLoading`, so cleanup could replace the original Playwright `TimeoutError` and close a usable committed tab.
4. A successful action could also return before delayed response headers committed streaming main-frame HTML. Cleanup sampled commitment once, then waited 20 seconds even after the later commit, failed, and retained interception until page close, so later navigation on the otherwise usable tab was aborted.

The net effect was excess page-script network authority before this fix plus committed-page recovery regressions in its first revisions.

## Why this design

- Intercept only `Document` resources through the operation-owned CDP session; leave preflights and subresources on Chromium's native network path.
- Keep top-level/subframe checks, redirect/OOPIF ownership, and live invocation authority in one fence.
- Establish a same-target protocol barrier before cleanup so a queued document cannot escape interception.
- On navigation failure, acknowledge `Page.stopLoading`, settle the fence's owned document state, and preserve the original navigation error.
- Observe main-frame commits through the owning CDP session and re-evaluate settlement throughout cleanup, without stopping unchanged-main-frame subframe/OOPIF chains.
- Disable Fetch before detaching and retain interception when cancellation cannot be confirmed.
- Add no setting, dependency, public API, or migration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related browser-navigation work

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 | Invocation-scoped document policy for browser actions | The base includes it. This PR preserves its policy and changes only the interception mechanism and cleanup. |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703 | Unmerged proposal to retire native navigation-policy enforcement | This PR keeps the current contract and does not depend on that proposal. |

The shared navigation files compose with the existing policy: this branch narrows interception and repairs cleanup without redefining the allowed destinations.

## Evidence

| Path × mode | Final-effect observation | Reproducible command and result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original catch-all route mechanism | With no route, rejected CORS sent `OPTIONS` only; with the base catch-all `page.route("**", route.fallback)` mechanism, the same rejecting destination received `PUT` and no `OPTIONS`. | `node /tmp/openclaw-1129-probe/probe.mjs` against pinned `playwright-core` 1.64.1 reproduced the before/without-route differential shown below. |
| Guarded action; destination rejects CORS | Destination recorded `OPTIONS` and zero `PUT` requests. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-cors.live.test.ts` — rejected action case passed. |
| Guarded `goto`; destination rejects CORS | Destination recorded `OPTIONS` and zero `PUT` requests. | Same command — rejected `goto` case passed. |
| Guarded action; destination consents | Destination recorded `OPTIONS`, then exactly one `PUT`. | Same command — consenting case passed. |
| Denied document | The attempted `127.0.0.2` fixture destination recorded zero document requests under a policy allowing only `127.0.0.1`; source URL and title remained unchanged. | Same command — denied-document/source-preservation case passed. |
| Allowed redirects across main frame and OOPIF | Each allowed goto/action/early-return/existing/new/nested-frame case recorded exactly one destination request. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-authority.live.test.ts` — allowed cases 6/6. |
| Revoked redirects across main frame and OOPIF | Each revoked case rejected with the authority error and recorded zero destination requests; a subsequent new owner navigated successfully. | Same command — revoked cases 6/6. |
| Shipped create-page streamed timeout | `createPageViaPlaywright` returned the committed tab after the 1-second timeout; URL, title `Committed stream`, and body `ready` remained usable. | `pnpm test:live -- extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-create-page-timeout.live.test.ts` — 1/1 passed. |
| Committed action stream | The guarded action returned before the fixture's one-second-delayed response headers, cleanup observed the later main-frame commit, completed without response EOF, retained URL/title/body, and a subsequent navigation succeeded. The earlier reviewed implementation failed the immediate-header variant after 20.1 seconds. | CORS live suite delayed-commit streamed-action case passed in 1.176 seconds. |
| Unit and repository gates | Fence lifecycle/create-page tests passed 45/45; the connection-owner acceptance set passed 75/75 after migrating its CDP fixture; format, production/test types, scoped type-aware lint, structural guards, and import-cycle checks passed. | `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts ...` and `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`. |

The sink observations come from fixture HTTP-server request counters and the real Chromium page's committed URL/title/body; fixtures use loopback only and contain no credentials or private endpoints. The redacted current-head terminal trace below comes directly from opt-in output after each sink assertion.

<details>
<summary>Original base-mechanism differential (real Chromium)</summary>

```text
Chromium 153.0.8010.12
{"guarded":false,"allow":false,"result":"rejected TypeError","targetReceived":["OPTIONS /deny-false"]}
{"guarded":false,"allow":true,"result":"resolved 200","targetReceived":["OPTIONS /allow-false","PUT /allow-false"]}
{"guarded":true,"allow":false,"result":"rejected TypeError","targetReceived":["PUT /deny-true"]}
{"guarded":true,"allow":true,"result":"resolved 200","targetReceived":["PUT /allow-true"]}
```

Here `guarded=true` installs the original base's exact catch-all Playwright route/fallback mechanism; the rejecting destination receiving `PUT` is the regression this PR removes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Real-Chromium terminal proof (current head)</summary>

```text
[browser-proof] cors owner=action methods=OPTIONS put=0
[browser-proof] cors owner=goto methods=OPTIONS put=0
[browser-proof] cors consenting=OPTIONS,PUT deniedDocuments=0 sourcePreserved=true
[browser-proof] redirects owner=goto revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=goto revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] redirects owner=selected-page action revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=selected-page action revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] redirects owner=early-returning action revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=early-returning action revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] redirects owner=existing iframe revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=existing iframe revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] redirects owner=new iframe revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=new iframe revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] redirects owner=nested iframe revoke=false sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=1 subsequentOwner=not-needed
[browser-proof] redirects owner=nested iframe revoke=true sourceRequests=1 guardedDestinationRequests=0 subsequentOwner=succeeded
[browser-proof] stream committed=true subsequentNavigation=true

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       17 passed (17)
```

</details>

## Boundary decisions requested from browser owners

1. Confirm that document-only interception remains the intended owner for top-level and OOPIF navigation policy while Chromium owns CORS and subresources.
2. Confirm that an acknowledged top-level `Page.stopLoading` is the correct terminal boundary for retaining a usable committed tab after a navigation timeout or a successful action commits an unfinished main-frame response.

## Testing

- Added `pw-session-navigation-cors.live.test.ts` for rejected/consenting CORS and denied-document source preservation.
- Extended it with a one-second delayed-header committed-action regression and subsequent-navigation proof, plus opt-in redacted sink traces.
- Added `pw-session-create-page-timeout.live.test.ts` through the shipped `createPageViaPlaywright` entry point.
- Re-ran `pw-session-navigation-authority.live.test.ts` for allowed and revoked redirects across main-frame and OOPIF paths (12/12).
- Updated the fence lifecycle suite and removed two mock cases that no longer exercised their named failures.
- Migrated `pw-session.connections.test.ts` from the removed route rendezvous to an EventEmitter-backed CDP session and `Fetch.enable` interception rendezvous; Clawsweeper's exact four-file acceptance command passed 75/75.
- Focused unit suites passed 45/45; all 17 live Chromium cases passed.
- Scoped changed-file gate passed against `upstream/main`; the documented dead-code skip applies only to an unrelated full-tree finding.

prs.title: fix(gateway): mark failed restart-safe browser chats unread
prs.body:
Closes #160003

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed browser chat turns staying read when workspace preparation fails after restart-safe admission, before the agent takes over.

## User Impact

Users see unread activity for a browser turn that fails after they mark the admitted message as read. Internal CLI Goal work and progress refreshes stay quiet. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart-safe terminal writer omitted the visibility fact required to advance session activity. Carry that fact through the existing chat work admission to the terminal event. Keep the unread predicate and durable claim rules unchanged.

Retry preparation retains its original conditional await from #164682 (`00daeebaf390ac9144c567ca399dd8a3707dc1ee`). Fresh sends reserve synchronously when preparation needs no worker read. The correction removes the unrelated unconditional await introduced in the first revision.

prs.body:
Related: #105976. Replaces the stale, unmerged implementation in #105994 for the message API rejection diagnostic.

## What Problem This Solves

A Feishu message API rejection with business code `230028` currently reaches the generic “reply completed without visible content” recovery message. The user is told the turn may have been interrupted even though Feishu rejected delivery under its content policy.

## User Impact

The delivery error handler sends one neutral content-policy notice after cleanup, including after an earlier chunk was accepted. The notice retains the same account, reply/thread target and required mentions. If sending the notice fails, the existing no-visible-reply fallback remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the business code when `assertFeishuApiSuccess` rejects a fulfilled SDK response, and recognize structured codes through Axios errors, cause wrappers and aggregate delivery errors. Queue the notice on the current idle chain so fallback evaluation cannot race it. This keeps the current partial-delivery, suppression and deferred-finalization owners instead of restoring the older extracted fallback controller.

This follows the neutral-notice decision in [the Feishu owner’s comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92445#issuecomment-4954237744) and credits @sliverp’s earlier #105994 implementation. That PR was closed as stale on October 24 with an invitation to submit a fresh implementation on current main; its complete discussion and the earlier redaction discussion were reviewed.

Scope: this changes the diagnostic for structured message API `230028` failures reaching the delivery-error handler. It adds no redaction, altered-content retry, or file fallback. It does not change CardKit error translation or the existing generic streaming-final recovery path from #152086, and does not claim that broader path has been validated against tenant policy rejection. The issue is related rather than automatically closed.

## Evidence

- Complete source modules transformed and executed in a standalone Node probe with synthetic dependencies and send functions: 10 dispatcher scenarios passed. The same HTTP 400 / `230028` input produces the generic fallback on the base and the policy notice on this change. Controls covered fulfilled business errors, aggregate causes, partial delivery, concurrent error/fallback handling, notice failure, cleanup failure, ordinary errors and intentional silence.
- Two additional interleaving probes held the notice send pending while another error, idle cleanup and fallback ran: one notice on success; one notice attempt followed by generic recovery on notice failure. No duplicate notice or deadlock.
- Six classifier/assertion controls passed, including cyclic causes, unrelated codes, a code appearing only in error text, and successful responses.
- Repository-configured `oxfmt` and diff whitespace checks passed. Both current-main file blobs still matched the pinned base immediately before publication.
- Draft validation limit: dependencies and message sends were substituted in the probes. No native Feishu SDK, live tenant, shipped Gateway, Vitest suite, full typecheck or build was run. No tests were added or modified.

Simplification: two existing files, source +53/-1, no new controller or dependency. Existing lifecycle ownership is preserved; the added state only prevents repeated notices within the dispatcher’s turn.

AI-assisted: yes.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep note frontmatter out of durable memory
prs.body:
Related: #148186

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes note bookkeeping such as `status: active` entering memory recall and durable-memory promotion when it appears inside complete leading YAML frontmatter.

## User Impact

Note bodies retain their original citation lines; metadata is excluded from indexing and rejected during promotion rehydration. YAML-looking session content remains eligible. The chunking revision advances from 6 to 7 so the existing index owner can rebuild unchanged files after upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Markdown Core's existing delimiter and normalization grammar, with a source-line range, through the private SDK boundary. The extractor moves into a dependency-free module so indexing does not import the YAML parser. Indexing, citation readback, and rehydration agree on LF, CRLF, and bare CR; incomplete frontmatter remains ordinary content.

This follows @gisk0's #148190, which was closed unmerged by the inactivity bot on October 22. I read its full discussion, including the outstanding index-invalidation and CR-line findings, and checked that no open or merged replacement covers #148186. This patch addresses those code findings against current source; the runtime evidence gaps below remain.

Simplification: one shared extractor replaces the previous in-file implementation; no parallel parser or persisted schema is added. Production delta: +87/-46 lines across 7 files; no test-file changes.

## Evidence

At base `b703c84a84c947e198b6a683408a3ddaba9179c4`, directly invoking production `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` on:

```text
---
status: active
---
Durable body content.
```

returned one chunk containing all four lines. With this patch, the same call returns only `Durable body content.` at source line 4.

On Node 24.22.1:

- Actual production preparation function: 13 checks passed covering LF/CRLF/CR with and without frontmatter, metadata-only notes, BOM, incomplete blocks, session preservation, and curated-entry line offsets.
- Isolated actual rehydration module logic: 13 checks passed covering stale metadata rejection after relocation, body acceptance across all three line endings, session-corpus preservation, and incomplete blocks. Workspace reads/path resolution and unrelated helpers were injected; this is **not** a complete runtime proof.
- `oxfmt --check` for the original 6 changed files and the additional read helper and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent code review caught the bare-CR fallback inconsistency; the fix and production checks above include that correction.
- Review follow-up: the production `buildMemoryReadResult` reproduced the bare-CR mismatch (`from: 4, lines: 1` returned zero lines). It now recognizes LF, CRLF, and bare CR consistently with indexing. With the actual shared extractor and read-result module loaded through the repository source loader, 35 assertions passed across citation line 4, all three line endings and mixed endings, continuation offsets, character caps, intentional trailing blanks, and empty files. This is a source-module check, not an installed `memory_get` run. Full `readMemoryFile` import is still blocked by the missing `p-map` dependency.

**Draft / remaining validation:** The existing Vitest suite did not execute: dependencies were initially missing, and the repository runner then attempted an unavailable pinned Bun setup. A direct full rehydration import was also blocked by missing transitive dependencies. No build or test-file edits were performed, following the task constraints. The review-requested committed regressions and full suites remain outstanding under those constraints. An installed search-to-`memory_get`/promotion run and an upgrade from genuinely contaminated pre-fix index rows still need verification; no claim is made that those paths or full CI have passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channels being restarted twice when host-thaw recovery waits for active work and health monitoring recovers them first.

## User Impact

Accounts recovered by another owner stay online. Accounts still affected by the original timing gap continue through the existing bounded recovery window. No configuration or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture each affected account lifetime when the timing gap is detected, before active-work deferral. The account lifecycle owner conditionally stops and replaces only that captured lifetime, checking ownership again after awaited teardown. Maintenance owns the pending targets and deadline; the separate core-runtime target list and retry-selection mode are removed.

Manual stops, account removal, incomplete cleanup retries, and account-specific failure diagnostics remain intact. Shared lifecycle contracts stay separate from the manager's private runtime store, avoiding an import cycle.

Production delta: +240/-165 (net +75). The growth supplies the conditional lifetime-replacement boundary and its connected contracts; tests add 292 net lines.

## Evidence

- Independent source review covered the lifecycle owner, scheduler ordering, health monitoring, callers, and sibling recovery paths.
- Targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and the native line-cap ratchet passed for the authored fix.
- Regressions exercise the reported deferral order, identical start timestamps, health-first scheduler wake, failed-stop recovery by another owner, later timing gaps, interrupted admission, late timeout cleanup, and retry diagnostics.
- **150 changed-suite tests passed at current head `8793a69450f42e58b04440fe31004d9e506a473d`.** [The runtime shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40619916638/job/122591696163) passed channel-manager 93, account-lifetime 11, work-scope 1, maintenance 36, and telemetry 9. [Ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40619916638) completed successfully: 42 checks passed, 27 skipped, none failed. The exact-head hosted review at 02:22 UTC on October 28 found no actionable finding or remaining rank-up move.
- The current candidate integrates pinned main `2262f3d2d82c8743dcda1087032e57e60db890a2`. Only the test-budget conflict was resolved, retaining the same ceiling; all 15 authored Gateway blobs and the production/test diff remain identical to the prior tested candidate. Current-head CI covers the integrated candidate; this does not claim unchanged dependency context.

Local dependency qualification refused reuse. Focused remote thaw attempts queued and were stopped before payload execution. Baseline-red/head-green, isolated full-Gateway, and live Telegram recovery proof remain unverified; the regressions use real maintenance, scheduler and account-lifecycle owners. No live-channel success is claimed.

## Test-Budget Justification

Pinned main `2262f3d2d82c8743dcda1087032e57e60db890a2` contains **6,293,974** counted test lines, independently verified from the ratchet's exact filename patterns and literal newline counts: 58 changed matching blobs add 737 lines to the previously verified 6,293,237. Its existing ceiling is 6,293,776.

The reviewed recovery fixes add this PR's **292** lines, the separate Telegram disconnect-episode fix's **241**, and the separate health-admission fix's **235**: **6,294,742** combined. The ceiling is **6,295,000**, with **258** disclosed lines of slack. This follows the documented ratchet policy and [merged rounded-allowance precedent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185857). Both follow-ups reuse this allowance.

[The separate test-budget allocation PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186456) is pending landing. It sets this same ceiling on main to resolve the shared-file conflict while preserving this PR's reviewed head.

## Separate Follow-ups

Telegram transport retry status owns its disconnect episode. Health monitoring must refresh each account's status after awaiting an earlier account. Those are separate narrow fixes; this PR repairs deferred outer account replacement.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the Claw agent reload wait on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after adding a Claw agent, the CLI's wait for the Gateway to apply it keeps polling far past the 15-second reload window when the system wall clock steps backward — the deadline is seeded and compared on the wall clock while the polls sleep on the monotonic clock.

## User Impact

User impact: running `openclaw claws add` on a machine whose clock steps backward (NTP correction, VM or laptop resume) now always reports the bounded `Gateway did not apply the Claw agent configuration in time` outcome after the real 15-second window, instead of hanging the add command on a wall-clock-inflated polling loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inline `waitUntilAgentAvailable` closure seeded `deadline = Date.now() + CLAW_AGENT_RELOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` and looped `while (Date.now() < deadline)`, while the poll sleeps run on the monotonic clock. A backward wall-clock step stretches the budget by the step, so the loop keeps issuing real `config.get` requests for `15s + step`.

The wait is extracted into `waitUntilClawAgentAvailable` in a new `src/cli/claws-agent-wait.ts` (so the regression test can import it without the heavy claws-cli.runtime import chain) and the deadline now lives on `performance.now()` — seed, loop condition, and remaining computation. This continues the cross-clock-domain series (#174151, #181335, and the merged fleet: #155846, #182180, #182778, #182859, #183742, #184525, #184576); the Claw agent reload wait is an unclaimed CLI site in the same family.

The committed regression uses injected clocks (the mocked transport reports a persistently unapplied roster; the mocked sleep advances a monotonic reading while the wall clock stays frozen at a rewound instant), and a real-time race caps the OLD behavior.

No add-command flow, gateway RPC, or recovery semantics change; behavior on a clock that never steps is identical.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — stock main behavior via the reverted module, regression test: config.get keeps reporting an unapplied roster, wall clock frozen 10 minutes behind. Stock main keeps polling past the whole budget:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/claws-cli.monotonic.test.ts
 × ends the reload wait at its monotonic deadline when the wall clock rewinds
   → expected 'still-running' to contain 'did not apply'
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — the same scenario fails with the bounded error, and the module suites pass:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/claws-cli.monotonic.test.ts
      Tests  1 passed
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/claws-cli.inspect.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.project.test.ts
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

### Real runtime proof (real Gateway WebSocket transport, in-process wall-clock rewind)

A real local WebSocket gateway fixture speaks the real Gateway wire protocol. The production `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` runs its full client stack (event-loop readiness, device identity bootstrap, challenge connect — ~21s, absorbed by a warm-up call before the budget is seeded). The fixture answers every `config.get` with a persistently unapplied agent roster. Only `Date.now` is rewound in-process on the first poll of the actual wait; `performance.now()` reports all real elapsed times.

```console
TRACE[claws] t=28ms    real gateway WebSocket fixture on ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
TRACE[claws] t=21344ms gateway client warmed up (bootstrap absorbed)
TRACE[claws] t=21356ms wall clock rewound by -600000ms (in-process Date.now injection)
TRACE[claws] t=21356ms RPC config.get -> {configRevisionHash:"saved", appliedConfigHash:"older"} (poll #1)
PROOF[claws] variant=fixed budget=15000ms wall_rewind=-600000ms -> state=error:Gateway did not apply the Claw agent configuration in time config_get_polls=134 settled_by_cap=true cap_elapsed_real_ms=36401

TRACE[claws] t=20231ms wall clock rewound by -600000ms (in-process Date.now injection)
TRACE[claws] t=20231ms RPC config.get -> ... (poll #1)
PROOF[claws] variant=old budget=15000ms wall_rewind=-600000ms -> state=still-waiting-at-cap config_get_polls=222 settled_by_cap=false cap_elapsed_real_ms=45322
```

Stock main is still issuing real `config.get` polls at the 25-second cap (222 polls, past the whole 15-second budget — it would continue for the length of the rewind); with this PR the wait fails with the bounded error after the real 15-second budget (134 polls).

**Behavior matrix** (config.get always unapplied, wall clock rewound 10min at poll #1):

```text
clock during wait           => add command resolves       => result
normal (no step)            => after 15s window           => bounded report
wall rewind 10min (pre-fix) => still polling at 25s cap   => unbounded by the step
wall rewind 10min (post-fix) => after 15s window           => bounded report
```

Also verified on the changed tree: `pnpm format:check` and the changed-file lint/typecheck lanes from `pnpm check:changed` (pnpm/corepack-shelling lanes fail on this Windows contributor box for the environmental reasons documented on #182778/#182859/#183742, unrelated to this diff). CI runs those lanes authoritatively.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing disk-code permission in AOT standalone builds when an installed plugin starts a disk worker or dynamically imports a sibling module.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared standalone option resolver owns the AOT policy used by the desktop artifact. It now sets `compile.allowCodeFromDisk` and records `--aot-allow-code-from-disk` in build identity for both emitted-JavaScript and source AOT builds. Desktop callers consume that policy without duplicating it.

## Evidence

- The generated compiler-request regression failed before the fix because the permission was absent. Both focused suites now pass: 86 tests, including both AOT input modes and permission omission from the JIT support companion.

Coverage includes disk workers, dynamic imports, CJS/ESM/published-TypeScript activation, and fetched Teams installation/loading. No `allow-jit` entitlement was used; string code generation remained blocked and ShadowRealm absent.

The signed runtime proof used OpenClaw `364c0d4ebcd400ee4285eb989ed60d2a8b000b93`, Bun `8361397097ff663952d55f8fcde0cd6928783406`, and the linked WebKit fix. This PR adds focused recipe coverage; it does not claim a fresh full runtime qualification on its own head.

prs.title: fix(agents): recover gateway-reported invalid tool input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic-compatible relay gateways (observed with a OneAPI-style relay in front of Claude) validate `tool_use` input themselves. When upstream emits malformed tool arguments, the relay fails the response with:

```
Upstream returned invalid tool input for 'exec'.
```

No tool call reaches OpenClaw, so nothing was dispatched. But this text is not in `PRE_DISPATCH_TOOL_CALL_REJECTION_MESSAGES`, so the existing rejected-tool-call recovery (#142176, #164274) never applies. Earlier tools in the same attempt usually had side effects, so the generic silent-error retry is vetoed too. The run ends with "The agent run failed before producing a reply."

## User Impact

User impact: when a relay rejects a malformed tool call before it runs, the agent continues the turn once instead of ending with no reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `isPreDispatchToolCallRejectionMessage` also accepts an anchored match for `Upstream returned invalid tool input for '<tool>'.` (tool name 1–128 chars, no newlines, optional trailing period, whitespace trimmed).
- The message then flows through the existing recovery owner with every guard intact: settled-tool checks, reply-delivery veto, and a single continuation using the "rejected before it ran" instruction.

No new retry policy, budget, or config.

## Evidence

**Live failures (redacted, Gateway log on OpenClaw 2026.10.5).** One day produced 5 terminal failures, all from the same relay provider, across Claude Sonnet and Opus, on `exec` (4) and `edit` (1):

```json
{"event":"embedded_run_agent_end","tags":["error_handling","lifecycle","agent_end","assistant_error"],
 "isError":true,"failoverReason":null,"model":"Opus 5.5","provider":"<relay>",
 "rawErrorPreview":"Upstream returned invalid tool input for 'edit'.",
 "providerRuntimeFailureKind":"unclassified"}
```

```
message processed: channel=webchat ... outcome=error duration=205203ms
```

In the session transcript, the last turn before the failure had completed `exec` calls (backup and copy) plus an `edit` whose arguments the relay rejected. The final assistant message is `stopReason: "error"` with no visible reply.

**Focused tests.** The `gateway diagnostic` shape was added to the existing "continues once after settled tools" matrix in `terminal-resolution.rejected-tool-call.test.ts`:
- Without the matcher change, this case fails: the run resolves terminal instead of `{ action: "retry" }`.
- With the change, it passes: 17/17. The test checks a single continuation, the "rejected before it ran" instruction, and terminal completion on the second rejection, so completed tools are not replayed.
- The test-line delta is net 0.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.

**Not yet shown.** I don't have a run where the relay error is followed by a successful live continuation. I'll add redacted logs from a patched Gateway once the relay reproduces it again.

prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Single-image edits through the bundled LiteLLM provider always send multipart `n=1`. LiteLLM's Gemini edit backend rejects that explicit unsupported parameter with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`, even though omitting `n` already means one output image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the LiteLLM **edit** request builder changes: include `n` when `count > 1`, otherwise use the endpoint's existing single-image default. Multi-image edits retain their requested count and normal error handling. No global `drop_params`, new retry, model-name special case, or transport change.

The contributor's commit is preserved. A follow-up narrowing commit restores the original generation builder and its default-count assertion. **Image generation is unchanged**, including JSON `n: 1` for a single generated image. The issue reports that generation already works; changing that behavior is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Single-image Gemini edits no longer fail solely because OpenClaw supplies redundant `n=1`. Explicit multi-image requests still send their count rather than silently dropping an unsupported parameter. Other providers and generation requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Current integrated head `401c2aad24c67e9c53aa098d47821341dadba1b2` merges current main `a7fe06b17a966`. The reported conflict was only in the provider test file: upstream’s consolidated layout is retained, with default-edit omission, explicit multi-image count, and generation count=1/count=2 assertions preserved. The production provider is byte-identical to proven `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`, so the linked Gateway A/B evidence carries; this integration does not add a real-provider claim. Fresh isolated frozen install, changed-file format check, and provider suite pass **20/20**. Current delta: production **+5/-1**, tests **+13/-5**.

[Built-Gateway A/B multipart captures and output receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6432278843), comparing pinned main `ce503a58dad3b06cfba1cc357bab3e5a0435f024` with narrowed candidate `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`:

- Fresh isolated Linux `node:24.22.1` containers installed frozen dependencies and passed supported `pnpm build:runtime`. The runtime artifact contains the final production change; the final amendment only consolidated tests.
- The shipped agent command dispatches to the built Gateway, whose real `image_generate` tool runs the LiteLLM provider against a local LiteLLM-compatible HTTP fixture. It receives a real PNG file part. The fixture models the reported Gemini contract: reject explicit edit `n` with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`; accept omission and return a known valid PNG.
- **Main twice:** default count and explicit count=1 each send multipart `n=1`, receive HTTP 400, and persist no output PNG.
- **Candidate twice:** the same default/explicit-one operations omit `n`, receive HTTP 200, and persist one PNG each. Shipped image metadata decoding reads both as 1×1 PNGs, 68 bytes each.
- **Controls on both refs:** shipped `infer image edit` with non-Gemini `gpt-image-2`, count=2 sends `n=2` and writes two PNGs. `infer image generate` with the Gemini route, count=1 still sends JSON `n: 1` and writes one PNG. Generation behavior is unchanged.
- Gateway image work is asynchronous: the first agent turn acknowledges task admission. The recorded failure/success is the actual provider operation and persisted artifact, not a claim that this initial acknowledgement failed.
- Before integration, candidate provider tests passed **10/10** and changed-file format checks pass. The strengthened existing default-edit multipart regression fails on main exactly at `form.has("n")` (true versus expected false) and passes with the fix. Default omission is consolidated into the existing multipart test; explicit multi-image count remains a distinct regression.
- Simplification retains one request builder and adds no helper/state owner. That pre-integration delta was production **+5/-1**, tests **+20/-0**; current integrated totals are listed above.

Earlier contributor evidence exercised the public CLI and a real LiteLLM 1.105.0 proxy with stubbed Vertex AI. That remains earlier-head evidence, not a real Gemini API run. This new run proves the narrowed production path through a built Gateway but also uses local model/provider fixtures.

**Outstanding proof prerequisite:** the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6109716373) explicitly requests an actual Gemini image returned through LiteLLM because the dependency's AGENTS.md requires real provider APIs. No Gemini credentials are available to this proof lane. The known PNG above is fixture output, not real Gemini output, and does not satisfy that requirement if it remains applicable.

## Not fixed here

Generation is intentionally unchanged. This does not enable Gemini multi-image counts, globally discard unsupported parameters, prove semantic image-edit quality, or establish real Gemini deployment behavior. Unsupported explicit multi-image parameters still surface their normal errors.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores explicit `n=1` on single-image LiteLLM edits; no schema/config migration or durable-state change. Blast radius is LiteLLM multipart image edits. Generation and other providers are untouched.

prs.title: perf(ci): avoid redundant database graph queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite worker ratchet repeats compiler queries that cannot change graph classification: receiver queries before forwarding policy applies, and the same AST call location during factory/member closure expansion.

## User Impact

Internal CI work only. Classification policy, credential validation, inventories and public APIs stay unchanged. Focused correctness and performance qualification pass. Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review remain pending; no end-to-end ratchet or billing saving is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate receiver resolution behind the existing call shape, tier, file, caller, member and argument identity. Preserve function/same-file/receiver checks and multiple-policy-row `.some` semantics.

Track first-seen call/new-expression locations at the closure producer within one immutable checker snapshot. Keep first-occurrence order, type/reviewed exclusions, member/family expansion and the separate Symbol guard for distinct locations. No result cache, changed exemption or source reuse across inspections.

Production +29/-19 (net +10); tests 0. The production growth owns bounded closure worklist membership and keeps compiler queries behind the policy boundary that consumes them. Relative to prior head6a3: +29/-22 (net +7), including formatter-only receiver-block reflow.

Tracing spent 426.095 of 569.295 seconds in current/baseline graph classification. This locates the expensive phase; it does not attribute that duration to these sites. [Tracing CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40608889317).

## Evidence

- New exact signed head: e8892a03b418f7772033642671e2af62742a7acb.
- Independent owner/dependency analysis plus full-owner autoreview: no actionable P0-P3 findings (confidence 0.94). The checker snapshot and forwarding mappings remain fixed throughout closure discovery; failed queries still abort without partial output.
- Direct pinned TypeScript inspection: batch symbol lookup sends every supplied location; canonical AST identities persist within the supplied snapshot. Native compiler CPU effects remain unproven.
- New-head native Node compatibility and ratchet/cache tests: 112 passed. Focused scripts type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Source checkout is code-only. The required tooling test typecheck and broad gates remain for exact-head hosted CI; older proof is not substituted.

### New-head measured result: prospective rule passed

The complete 93-case compatibility file passes under Node 26.12.1 and the pinned Bun fork. All 110 complete ordered inspections, including the empty snapshot with zero requests, match exactly. Actual Bun executable hash and revision match the committed Darwin arm64 pin.

Actual excluded counter runs: compiler requests2337 to2220; scalar symbol requests513 to422; batch symbol requests498 to472; all encoded symbol-location slots1095 to973; closure slots236 to205. The existing mixed-receiver case observes7 slots/3 requests to4 slots/2 requests. Node and Bun agree on those counts.

One excluded counted warm-up per variant; five serial interleaved A/B pairs with raw committed bytes; one additional counted Bun parity run. All13 commands succeeded. Timed one-minute host load7.001-7.477. The driver restored the clean exact candidate after normal completion.

| Metric | Baseline median / p95 / min-max | Candidate median / p95 / min-max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wall_s | 2.730000 / 2.760000 / 2.720000-2.760000 | 2.670000 / 2.750000 / 2.650000-2.750000 |
| body_ms | 880.639669 / 928.802797 / 860.856209-928.802797 | 848.059628 / 893.641990 / 809.364836-893.641990 |
| file_ms | 882.385498 / 931.185059 / 862.497803-931.185059 | 849.928955 / 895.504639 / 810.249023-895.504639 |
| user_s | 2.680000 / 2.730000 / 2.650000-2.730000 | 2.660000 / 2.730000 / 2.650000-2.730000 |
| sys_s | 0.830000 / 0.860000 / 0.820000-0.860000 | 0.820000 / 0.860000 / 0.780000-0.860000 |
| rss_bytes | 459440128.000000 / 471941120.000000 / 458358784.000000-471941120.000000 | 459276288.000000 / 470188032.000000 / 450560000.000000-470188032.000000 |

Wall median improves2.198%; body median improves3.700%. Every recorded median/p95 wall, body/file, CPU and RSS metric holds or improves, meeting the unchanged prospective rule. This focused result does not establish full-repository ratchet speed, Windows execution or billed-minute savings.

The initial harness preflight rejected a non-unique lookup marker before launching any workload; it was narrowed to the closure lookup and independently reviewed before the13 successful commands. No timing sample was discarded or rerun.
### New prospective performance acceptance rule (published before first execution)

- Baseline: 4456a96af6ca5b809e58391a92fc4b58190bb13b. Candidate: e8892a03b418f7772033642671e2af62742a7acb. Same qualified native checkout, dependencies, Darwin arm64 host and Node 26.12.1. Use the complete committed compatibility test file in original order: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/database-worker-compat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=json --outputFile=<temporary-report>`.
- One excluded instrumented warm-up per variant, then five serial interleaved A/B pairs in fresh processes. Timed runs use raw committed module/test bytes, without the counter shim. Report load, median, nearest-rank p95 and min/max for wall, body/file duration, user/system CPU and peak RSS.
- Count real compiler wire requests and encoded symbol-location slots in excluded runs. Require fewer total requests and symbol slots, identical complete ordered inspection results, and unchanged ordered full-file case results. The existing mixed-receiver case must observe closure work falling from 7 slots/3 requests to 4 slots/2 requests; these are source-derived expectations until observed.
- Run the full compatibility file under the pinned Bun fork too; check actual runner executable hash/revision and ordered result parity. Preserve aliases/reexports, typed receivers, escaped/live members, callbacks, worker entries and cycles. Run related ratchet/cache proof and required static gates separately at the exact new head.
- Win: required count/parity proof passes and every measured median/p95 wall, body/file, CPU and RSS metric holds or improves. A worse metric keeps the draft on hold. No unchanged rerun, waived metric, Windows inference or billing claim. Focused tests do not prove end-to-end ratchet speed.

prs.title: fix(ui): reaction picker opens above scrolled messages in WebKit
prs.body:
Closes #184937

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the reaction picker opens far above its message in supported WebKit when a long conversation has scrolled to a nonzero virtualized row offset.

## User Impact

Reaction choices stay beside the clicked message instead of appearing over earlier messages or outside the viewport. No settings, data, or API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Position the existing absolute row window with `top` instead of a transform. WebKit 26.4 omits the ancestor transform when resolving the native popover's CSS anchor. The existing scroll extent, row containment, and native overlay/focus owners remain unchanged; no browser sniffing, extra observers, or JavaScript positioning fallback is added.

## Evidence

- **Supported WebKit 26.4, bundled Control UI:** 100 synthetic messages, real chat route, wheel scrolling and Add reaction. The original renderer opens the picker offscreen with a **10,560 px positioning error**; the fix opens it **6 px below its trigger**, with zero positioning error, and selecting 🎉 produces the expected reaction write. Captures were recorded at `96523d62be1c`; both production files remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

- **Corrected E2Es:** all **26/26** cases pass on the refreshed base plus this complete candidate through a fresh production bundle. Reply search/send/reveal, deep viewport positioning, keyboard admission, 13-second timing, successor-run isolation, output tokens and reload checks remain covered. No cases were deleted or skipped.

- **Menus and reactions:** **20/20 Chromium** checks and **20/20 supported WebKit 26.4** checks pass on the refreshed candidate using Node 26.12.1, with the matching Playwright protocol client for the supported engine. This includes every menu-surface and changed reaction-picker case. Repository dependency pins are unchanged. The default current-WebKit launcher could not start because of missing host libraries; the already-qualified supported-version executable was used instead, without disabling the dependency validator.

- UI production and relevant test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent Auto Review of the **complete seven-file candidate** against `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean, no findings**; source-only review, not independent execution of the supplied proof; unchanged implementations were unavailable to that reviewer and were inspected by the implementer.

### Current exact-head CI and review

Current head: `9a27c536d0080c2dac4f1ae93554ac2ccb8ff204` on the existing `openclaw/ember-prawn` branch. [Exact-head CI run 40621766865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40621766865) **passed**: all three UI browser shards, all six scheduled E2E shards, baseline ratchets, lint, production/test types and selected guards passed. Preflight binds head `9a27c536d008` to tested merge `f241ec3732596c844e4aafc621aceaf7daf8e9c7` on base `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`. Both [canonical ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40621766865/job/122600703580) and [generic ci-gate, dependency review and security-sensitive review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40622855580) **passed**. Full final-readiness inventory was read through both public REST pages: **104 check runs (43 successful, 61 skipped) plus three successful required status contexts; zero failed or pending**. This resolves the managed reader’s 100-item truncation. Skipped lanes are not claimed executed. No merge or gate waiver is requested.

The prior exact-head run at `97048c395102` passed all three browser shards and all six scheduled bundled-UI E2E shards, lint and typechecks; its sole failing leaf was [the test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40618574194/job/122587247320). The 626-line overage and net PR delta +124 were reproduced on exact merge `ce15f37b9a130825ba1f45a4547cbafd0f0ffe98` against base `542a03d30c953964f7d4176954d09a20423c147f`. The current candidate replaces duplicate regression wiring with the production session owner (37 fewer test lines) and incorporates upstream budget maintenance. **No ceiling/baseline/configuration change, test deletion, weakened assertion, retry or waiver is included.** On refreshed base `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`, the unchanged ratchet passes: **6,293,887 lines / 6,294,048 ceiling, 161 lines of slack**.

[Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186295#issuecomment-6453429076) completed for `9a27c536d0080c2dac4f1ae93554ac2ccb8ff204`: **overall readiness 5/6, proof confidence 5/6, patch quality 5/6 — diamond lobster**. Proof is **sufficient (screenshot)** with directly inspected bundled-UI captures; **Findings: None; Before merge: None**. Actual labels include `proof: sufficient`, `rating: 🦞 diamond lobster`, and `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`. This is readiness for human maintainer review, not merge approval or a claim that native macOS/Safari execution occurred. The PR remains open and unmerged.

<details>
<summary>CI attribution, correction scope and cost</summary>

Historical [run 40580767857](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40580767857) failed on inherited main issues: five curly errors repaired by [8b2b0997a578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b2b0997a5780c074f0f7cdf766e274509b72771), and the background-draft toast button/link selector repaired by [bb9b2fd4fcbb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bb9b2fd4fcbb732371de08a71da8bf317f3965c1). Both repairs were incorporated by the managed main-base refresh; the corrected desktop/mobile toast E2Es pass 2/2 locally.

[Run 40614550577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40614550577) at `d96533df83a2` then found five E2E failures and one menu-color failure. Its actual tested base is `fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e`, with synthetic merge `92cc41ed872d4421fc94305223556f13c06f1b8b`. The two old ci-gate failures are downstream aggregates, not additional test defects.

**Five E2E failures are executed-base inherited:** clean detached checkouts with private frozen dependencies and the same normal bundled-UI entrypoint yield **5 failed / 21 passed** on both the exact main base (120.25 s) and CI merge (116.46 s). The corrected three files pass **26/26 in 43.97 s** on the merge. These are controlled Linux sandbox comparisons using Node 26.12.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0, not a claim to reproduce hosted concurrency or clear hosted CI.

- Dictation Configure now intentionally opens Talk settings ([340b8a77 / #186290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/340b8a77ecd102419698313f0347345ba1e5d55b)); the E2E now checks that destination rather than reverting the production owner.
- Landed inline narration and untimed work chunks ([e7f05461 / #183267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e7f0546192744a786b60b607401e030b0f83940d)) supersede the single folded-narration assumption. Reply tests retain the complete user journey while checking that narration stays inline and every visible work disclosure stays collapsed.
- Whole-run timing belongs to the final recap, not individual work stretches. The lifecycle test checks **Done in 13 seconds**, 42 output tokens, no borrowing of the later 27-second run, and timing restoration after reload.

**Menu timing remains attribution-qualified:** CI sampled alpha 0.06 where the exact selected-color assertion requires 0.08 after one animation snapshot. The color mismatch did not reproduce in the isolated pre-fix 20/20 local run. A targeted probe did show all three keyboard variants reaching the assertion while the submenu was still `opening`, despite child focus and parent expansion; pointer variants were already `open`. The correction waits for that submenu’s existing `overlay-after-show` event, then retains the parent-animation wait and the **same exact color, focus, collapse and navigation assertions**. No timeout increase, retry, skip or CSS/production-menu change was introduced. The exact CI triggering event and base-versus-added-test scheduling attribution are not claimed proven.

Simplification: the production repair remains the original offset-property substitution plus explanatory comment; no fallback positioning owner, browser sniffing, observers or new API. Four test-only CI corrections were added to preserve real assertions against landed contracts. Total diff: **7 files, +109/−21; production net +1, tests net +87**. Relative to `97048c395102`, the regression is 37 lines shorter: the existing production `ChatSessionVirtualizerHost` now owns real measurement, initial restoration, virtualizer/renderer lifetime and cleanup instead of reassembling those owners by hand. It still checks a nonzero first rendered row, placement before and after scrolling, reaction selection and cleanup; every prior case and assertion remains. The separate lifecycle consolidation audit found no sound large deletion without obscuring distinct sequencing, so no such refactor was made.

Refreshed candidate: all **26/26** corrected E2Es pass through a fresh production bundle (**75.12 s** wall time; lifecycle **21.125 s**, dictation **18.324 s**, reply reveal **8.990 s** test time). They exercise actual bundled UI interaction and cannot be replaced by wording-only unit checks. Combined menu/reaction invocations: Chromium **20/20, 8.65 s** wall (menu **5.920 s**, reactions **1.371 s** test time); supported WebKit **20/20, 21.77 s** wall (menu **16.789 s**, reactions **2.551 s** test time). Relevant typechecks, lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Initial unrestricted test-compiler invocations exhausted available threads; the same repository checker completed with four-CPU affinity, without source changes or suppressions. Exact-head hosted CI is now green, including the formerly failing ratchet. Earlier 22-check WebKit 27.2 and Chromium sibling runs, reaction E2Es and the focused first-wheel/row-admission E2E remain prior-head supporting evidence, not fresh-head CI.

</details>

**Limitations:** browser execution was in an isolated Linux sandbox, not Safari or the packaged macOS app. No Mac runner or user machine was used. Gateway traffic uses the repository’s canonical mock-Gateway helper, not a live model/provider. WebKit 27.2 already handles the original transform correctly; supported 26.4 establishes the need for the repair. Existing Solid strict-read diagnostics occur on base and fix and are not suppressed.

### Visual evidence — bundled Control UI, WebKit 26.4

Same synthetic conversation and interaction, 1280 × 900 viewport; inspected 1280 × 780 crops exclude the composer without changing message/picker pixels. Wheel settling differs (scrollTop 10806 before / 10933 after), so compare relative picker placement, not identical scroll coordinates.

**Before** — Add reaction is open but the palette is offscreen at y=-10060, 10,560 px from its intended position.

![Before: scrolled reaction palette opens offscreen in bundled Control UI on WebKit 26.4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73d4900e-e7b6-4edd-b3b7-1794603faee7)

**After** — the palette opens 6 px below its trigger, and reaction selection writes successfully.

![After: scrolled reaction palette stays beside its message in bundled Control UI on WebKit 26.4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08e96164-c188-4690-891e-58040b59ff5e)

<details>
<summary>Replay method and supplementary renderer proof</summary>

The bundled replay used the production Vite build, `startBundledControlUiE2eServer` and `installMockGateway`. Only `chat-transcript-layout-solid.tsx` was restored from `451ec41c26c67cca7d8a61b7da6b0188cf52249e` for red, then restored to the fixed bytes in a finally block; this is not a whole historical-base replay. prs.title: fix(telegram): compact consecutive progress tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Telegram's Working preview has a bounded height. Repeated Bash/Exec rows can fill most of it, pushing useful steps and progress updates out of view. Counted rows leave room for more distinct activity without enlarging the preview.

## Summary
- Compact consecutive identical status-only tool calls into one row, such as `Exec ×12` or `Automations ×4`, with no fixed count cap.
- Preserve identical safe details: `Sessions: 30 ×2` and `Skill Read: github ×2`. Different limits, skills or tools start separate rows.
- Keep failures, approvals, other detailed rows and authored progress boundaries separate.
- Count actual invocations, not lifecycle callbacks. Tool execution, full history, raw command mode and other streaming modes are unchanged.
- Opt-in through one optional compositor input, `compactToolRuns`, set only by Telegram.

## Before
User-provided examples: repeated tool rows crowd out other activity.

![Before: repeated Bash, Exec, Skill Read and Sessions rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/master/184712-before-collage.jpg)

## After
Real tool calls on an isolated QA Gateway: **Exec ×12 → Automations ×4 → Sessions 30 ×2 → Sessions 10 → Sessions 30 ×2 → Skill Read github ×2**, followed by a different skill, a fresh Exec series and a separately visible failure.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7aeeafa-9eb5-43e7-af1b-d5ef5ef26e65

Cropped user recording; audio and private chat sidebar removed.

## Evidence
