prs.title: fix: reject native Talk consults after session store changes
prs.body:
Fixes #186186

## What Problem This Solves

An open native Talk call retains its selected session store. After a supported hot change to `session.store`, a newly requested provider consultation could still update metadata in the old store and enter model dispatch, even though the same call's voice lookup rejected that storage target.

The callback missed the routing assertion already owned by its prepared session target. Checking only the physical voice record, caller, or session incarnation did not detect the logical store change.

## User Impact

A new native consultation now rejects an invalidated storage target before committing consultation metadata or starting model work. Start a new call to use the current route. Valid calls continue normally, existing calls retain their selected agent when only Talk defaults change, and accepted work keeps its existing lifetime when audio detaches.

This uses the existing storage configuration and session representation. It adds no configuration option, schema, provider API, or new cancellation policy. Ordinary voice transcript persistence remains under its existing owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native consult admission now invokes the retained target's existing routing predicate against current configuration. The configuration used to start the consultation is read after readiness completes. The same live assertion is composed into the existing host authority for the consultation's metadata patch, so a route change during awaited preparation cannot pass an earlier check and then write the old session.

The regression extends the existing native callback and SQLite fixture with two store-change timings: before admission and after real workspace preparation. It shares native-call setup and successful-consult assertions with the existing browser and relay custom-main controls. All four scenarios remain, including completion-claim handling and the no-write/no-dispatch checks. Existing routing and lifetime fixtures cover the unchanged behaviors.

## Evidence

On base `d1cda17dde7fbd744d812cf7da80ee5aa20b03eb`, the valid call succeeded, then a store-only transition made the fresh target current and the old target/voice lookup reject. The stale callback nevertheless succeeded, changed the old SQLite row's timestamp, preserved its session identity, and reached the embedded-execution stub a second time; the new store had no corresponding session. The preparation-timing regression also failed on that unchanged base.

The candidate passes remote changed-file formatting/lint, all 38 selected type graphs (reusing unaffected passes after a fixture type correction), and 127 tests across 11 Talk owner/consumer files. The behavioral batch took 208.39 seconds in Vitest, including fixture startup; native test execution took 214.48 seconds. Both new rejection cases pass alongside ordinary routes, selected-agent affinity, permission/identity guards, accepted detach, requester-final ownership, and terminal persistence coverage.

The focused tests exercise real native callback admission and SQLite persistence while stubbing the final model executor. A separate isolated Linux Gateway on the same candidate tree passed real OpenAI audio delegation through the existing Gateway-relay transport: the configured backend model read an unseen workspace marker, then `config.set` and the configuration watcher changed the session store while preserving the Gateway process, connection, and voice call. The retained voice lookup rejected the target, and a second spoken file request produced the native delegation routing rejection with zero subsequent model starts and no diagnostic drops. The created call and client closed successfully. This proves the real provider/model/reload boundary. The isolated realtime configuration used an explicit delegation policy, so this is controlled technical proof rather than natural guest-task usability. Browser media and deployed guest behavior are not claimed, and ordinary finalized voice transcript persistence is outside the consultation-metadata assertion.

The original patch passed the full build. Canonical Auto Review and the same independent engineering reviewer are clean for the consolidated patch; all 38 tests in the revised native fixture pass, while both invalidation cases fail against the original production code and both unchanged-target controls pass. The consolidation removes 18 lines from the first revision without dropping a scenario or moving tests outside the counter.

The patch was replayed unchanged onto ae9b009123ec83ad999400dc48bac05c9fd5b317 to consume its already-landed test-line policy. The integrated native target and permission fixtures also pass all 42 tests, with the affected type graph passing. The exact combined tree passes the canonical counter: 6,285,927 lines against the accepted 6,287,068 ceiling, leaving 1,141 lines of room. No ceiling edit, unrelated-test deletion, or waiver is part of this PR. The earlier [test-line failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40558880765/job/122383125797) belongs to the superseded head. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40594728016) on the replay passed all selected jobs.

The target reproduction on fff56630338adf921d6eb30fbd411452cdf4adf1 confirms both stale consultations still change the old row and reach a second model dispatch, while both ordinary controls pass. Applying the unchanged patch passes all four cases. Those results remain applicable after inspection of the later target changes. The final composition with b46d011db972a982bf8b8b94331505473dd07851 passes the canonical counter: 6,293,862 test lines against its accepted 6,294,048 ceiling, leaving 186 lines of room. This PR contributes 72 test lines and includes no ceiling change, unrelated deletion, or waiver.

prs.title: fix: avoid false queued recovery Stop test failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent Gateway CI failures when Stop cancels a queued restart-recovery run while its recorded-input read is still waiting on real worker I/O.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This test-only repair keeps the existing cancellation and restart-recovery checks without treating fake-clock progress as completion of a real worker read. No production, permission, storage, timeout, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the source's abort signal before starting cancellation, then wait for that signal or the cancellation operation to finish before checking it and releasing the held dispatch gate. All existing abort, no-dispatch, retirement, explicit-cancellation, and retryable-recovery assertions remain.

Contributor credit: @jalehman and @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0c2aaa61-d7c9-4c74-b24e-d1c501b07a43)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f3f06927-e415-4d2f-bd3b-fdd0b79c7569)

## Evidence

- Original failure: [CI run 40619461616, job 122590201264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40619461616/job/122590201264), queued restart-recovery Stop case, expected the abort signal to be true.
- Reproduced on main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`: the cold five-case recovery subset fails only Stop before this change (4 pass, 1 fail); the same subset passes all five after this change. Pinned Bun fork, one worker, repository Vitest wrapper. Wall time: 8.28 s before / 8.33 s after.
- Diagnostic observation: at fake-clock budget exhaustion, `readSessionSubmittedInput` had started but had not settled. Waiting for Vite imports did not settle that worker I/O. The failed fixture then released dispatch before Stop reached the queued source. Diagnostic instrumentation was removed.
- Main's original eight-file shard also passed both as a combined replay (455 tests) and in CI's two-config sequence (41 + 414 tests), demonstrating cold-path sensitivity rather than a consistent cancellation failure.
- Repaired original eight-file shard, in CI's config sequence: 6 files / 41 tests pass (25.38 s), then 2 files / 414 tests pass (90.55 s). The full agent file protects multiple cancellation/dispatch contracts and takes longer than 30 s; the cold focused regression is 8.33 s.
- Targeted Gateway-methods TypeScript check, changed-file oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) of the complete local diff against the main SHA above found no actionable findings; unchanged-harness context was not available to that tool. A separate independent GPT-6.1 Sol review read the complete changed helper, harness setup/reset, clock helpers, real Stop/worker-read chain, and RPC/interruption/timeout paths: no actionable P0–P2 findings, no missing changed scope. Read-only review; tests are the implementation owner's evidence.
- Simplification: no production changes; test delta +5/-4 lines. Existing completion signals replace polling; no extra mocks, retries, sleeps, or larger timeouts.
- Hosted exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review remain required before merge; CI seconds are not yet available.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @jalehman

prs.title: fix(policy): sanitize human CLI reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Policy's terminal reports interpolate file-derived names and findings directly. A valid policy filename containing terminal controls can ring the bell or forge report lines during an ordinary conformance comparison; command-owned error diagnostics likewise print raw identifiers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the SDK's existing `sanitizeTerminalText` at one human line writer shared by policy check/compare/watch reports, and sanitize command-owned stderr diagnostics. Preserve the exact explicit/piped JSON result values and existing conformance, attestation, severity and exit decisions. This continues the machine/human separation accepted in merged #181758; no enforcement or policy rule changes.

Existing-solutions preflight: the maintained terminal-core/SDK sanitizer already owns this contract, so this reuses it. No new library, wrapper sanitizer, plugin or service is required. The selected complete owner is `extensions/policy/src/cli.ts`; its registration, callers, sibling reports, tests, source handling and sanitizer were read. All-state title/symptom/symbol/path searches and complete Leon/Alix public open-footprint/changed-file checks found no viable same-invariant competitor. Latest checked main `8cebac4847362f4d5b9f94656551789e9f3756c7` leaves the report owners and exercised update/policy call paths unchanged. Terminal-core now also exports `terminalText`; the existing `sanitizeTerminalText` behavior is unchanged. Updated root/contribution, review-flow and test-authoring guidance was read; the recorded Node 24.22.1 meets the new minimum. This head merges cleanly with that main without changing its recorded source/build proof.

## User Impact

Operators can compare and inspect policy reports safely while retaining Unicode and report layout. Scripts keep raw source filenames and findings, and still receive exit1 for a genuinely weaker policy.

No new or changed config/default, protocol/schema, dependency, migration, permission or storage contract. Existing trusted report layout and severity styling are retained. Release-note context: safely render human policy CLI reports without rewriting machine/raw values.

## Evidence

- Actual native RED source/build: `173c8537d5ae4ea1da4200ba59da584b76bb5600`. Exact GREEN source/build: `aa467098453b911af0fc02f2b42c61724e32f3fa`, tree `b4898184060afe9390aacfd6673db6f648243761`; clean independent worktree, Node v24.22.1, Linux, task-owned isolated HOME/state/config/files. No production instance, external service, model call or real channel was used.

A real PTY exercises ordinary and control-containing conformant files plus a genuinely weaker candidate; plain/explicit JSON pipes cover automatic machine-output selection and raw field readback. RED owned report text contains BEL/C1 and a forged line; GREEN removes those data controls and displays data LF literally. Conformant comparisons still exit0, weaker comparisons exit1, and all eight original policy/config files remain byte-identical. The original complete PTY captures include the normal CLI banner/progress controls; only the policy report is claimed safe.
- Same proof command before/after: `node openclaw.mjs policy compare --baseline <baseline.jsonc> --policy <candidate.jsonc>`; full setup, companion calls, original lengths/hashes and complete stdout/stderr are below.

Both RED/GREEN readbacks PASS and launch zero additional product calls. These are saved real subprocess/PTY streams and actual file/SQLite readbacks, not merely test outcomes or script assertions.

| Tests-only baseline | 34 PASS / 3 intended FAIL; 47.02 s |
| Focused GREEN | 37/37 PASS; 45.27 s |

Commands (one worker; wrapper/preparation time included above):

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.source.json --format json extensions/policy/src/cli.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts
```

The local ignored typecheck project only scopes the repository's existing strict test config to the two touched files plus ambient declarations; no compiler/lint setting is weakened. Full Vitest test timing includes startup/compilation; no hosted CI duration is claimed. Diff numstat is additions/deletions:

```text

```

The existing report calls share one terminal-safe line writer; JSON and policy evaluation stay on their original paths. No new rule, state, API or enforcement behavior. Required CI and the first durable bot/human review can only occur after publication; neither is preclaimed here.

prs.title: fix: refresh mobile Fastlane certificate roots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android and iOS Fastlane bundles still include Excon 1.7.3's eMudhra root certificates after the CA compromise.

## User Impact

Both frozen mobile build-tool bundles consume Excon 1.8.0's updated CA data. Existing legitimate private CA configuration continues to work. This is a root-bundle refresh: explicit/custom trust stores can still restore affected chain acceptance, so this update alone does **not** completely reject compromised keys.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regenerate both locks with the required Ruby 4.0.7 and Bundler 4.0.23. The only changes are Excon's version and verified RubyGems checksum; Fastlane 2.241.1 and every other dependency remain unchanged. Excon is build tooling and is not redistributed in the mobile application payload.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `1647682843c3043d047dec830ebd415cbdf6acfc`; base: `5f71bbf09e6aa91884a5d0389838cef33d6e87ab`.

- Both frozen installs and bundle checks pass, as do the actual repository Android/iOS Fastlane helper `--version` calls. Official Excon 1.8.0 gem SHA256: `56d414519bff28bf95dd800ad4690a2fc0b8a49caf00367b70ecdbac71f91c93`; installed 34-file manifest: `5b63ad6c529ea5ff8a5e0ae69cdc7c2d23e67ac49308a221920d8b296a25a8d0`.
- Controlled actual installed Excon/Fastlane HTTPS comparison on native Linux ARM64, Ruby 4.0.7/OpenSSL 3.0.13: all 14 incident endpoints have matching verified certificate identities and successful independent chain/hostname controls. Default acceptance changes from 7/14 to 0/14 after the root refresh; those failures are **UnknownIssuer**, not key revocation. Supplying the authenticated older roots via environment file, explicit file, properly rehashed directory, or explicit OpenSSL store still accepts all 14. The actual Fastlane `github_api` action confirms the same default/additional-trust distinction on representative direct/cross-sign endpoints.
- Public GitHub/RubyGems HTTPS, legitimate private CA HTTPS (including the actual Fastlane action), untrusted-private rejection and hostname-negative controls pass. No verification is disabled. Initial fixture failures and their corrections remain preserved; only missing controls were replayed.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 review is scoped-clean. `git diff --check` passes. Evidence export SHA256: `543ba63a75bfdb225c00572ddfbda12b2cc132787cc2ec17e3c6c3846bbb2a76`.

Native macOS/mobile build, signing/upload, all eight incident keys, independent Fastlane transports and installed fleet delivery remain unproven. Existing Android global-Fastlane fallback remains operator-owned. No release or store upload was run. PR #179108 also changes these locks but still selects Excon 1.7.3; reconcile its overlapping lock edits if it lands later.
## Current gates

CI run [40281061184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40281061184) has a failed [android-test-third-party job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40281061184/job/121434603764): one of 3,764 tests, `NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest.coldStartUsesAnAllowedAgentBeforePatchingTheGatewayDefault`, reports “Chat must wait for the allowed roster.” This Gradle path does not invoke Ruby/Bundler/Excon, but that source separation is not matched attribution. The current-base run skipped Android; failure attribution remains unproven pending equivalent base/candidate evidence. No unrelated Android repair or gate waiver is included. The `openclaw/ci-gate` and legacy aggregate also fail by propagation of this Android result. Its informational classifier cites a passing named test on older scheduled main (`db92acff277255f64e14866d29ebcb00592822b1`), with “selected scope not compared”; the retained JUnit confirms that pass, but it does not close controlled attribution. The actual exact-head ClawSweeper review found no source defect, and requested accessible TLS evidence and disposition of the Android gate. The [inspectable existing exact-head TLS proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184302#issuecomment-6410523722) now includes legitimate success, all fourteen matched incident results, pre-request TLS failure stack/source ordering, direct chain/hostname controls, exact artifact identities and the explicit old-trust acceptance caveat. This is handshake/call-stack evidence, not a packet capture. Android attribution and its failed gate remain unresolved. The [actual subsequent final-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184302#issuecomment-6410412850), completed October 26 at 07:29 UTC, reports no actionable source findings and sufficient shipped-entry-point proof; its only remaining before-merge item is Android failure attribution and required-gate disposition.

prs.title: fix(plugins): sanitize human update reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins update` writes returned plugin/hook outcome messages directly to stdout or stderr. Plugin IDs accepted by normal local installation can contain terminal controls, so even an ordinary dry-run skip can ring the bell or forge a report line. Direct selection/ownership diagnostics and integrity-drift prompts share this missing human-text boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sanitize each outcome message once before its existing severity styling, preserving success/skipped/error routing and exit decisions. Use the same existing sanitizer on command-owned dynamic diagnostics and integrity prompt fields, retaining the prompt's deliberate three-line layout. Raw updater outcomes, install IDs, package/config persistence and source-selection policy are unchanged. Both plugin and hook outcomes use this renderer.

Existing-solutions preflight: the maintained terminal-core/SDK sanitizer already owns this contract, so this reuses it. No new library, wrapper sanitizer, plugin or service is required. The selected complete owner is `src/cli/plugins-update-command.ts`; its registration, callers, sibling reports, tests, source handling and sanitizer were read. All-state title/symptom/symbol/path searches and complete Leon/Alix public open-footprint/changed-file checks found no viable same-invariant competitor. Latest checked main `8cebac4847362f4d5b9f94656551789e9f3756c7` leaves the report owners and exercised update/policy call paths unchanged. Terminal-core now also exports `terminalText`; the existing `sanitizeTerminalText` behavior is unchanged. Updated root/contribution, review-flow and test-authoring guidance was read; the recorded Node 24.22.1 meets the new minimum. This head merges cleanly with that main without changing its recorded source/build proof.

## User Impact

Operators can read update results without package-derived control sequences reaching the report. Café, 中文 and emoji survive. JSON/storage identities and exit meanings do not change; this adds no update source or automatic action.

No new or changed config/default, protocol/schema, dependency, migration, permission or storage contract. Existing trusted report layout and severity styling are retained. Release-note context: safely render human plugin CLI reports without rewriting machine/raw values.

## Evidence

- Actual native RED source/build: `173c8537d5ae4ea1da4200ba59da584b76bb5600`. Exact GREEN source/build: `52d6150dc3e59ed981670e173070661e9bc8d3e0`, tree `55d6fa1f64e779c9c23b7fdfb077aa2aef9a17d4`; clean independent worktree, Node v24.22.1, Linux, task-owned isolated HOME/state/config/files. No production instance, external service, model call or real channel was used.
- Six public CLI calls per revision: install two task-owned local plugins with the plugin system disabled, then run selected and bulk `--dry-run` updates for each. Both supported path-source installs succeed; both update selections correctly skip path sources with exit0. RED report bytes contain BEL/C1/data-newline controls; GREEN renders them safely. An independent reader reopens both authoritative SQLite installed-index rows, both configs and all twelve original/installed source files, verifying unchanged raw IDs/bytes and absent register() markers. Four status classes and both plugin/hook output channels are additionally covered by focused regressions.
- Same proof command before/after: `node openclaw.mjs plugins update --all --dry-run`; full setup, companion calls, original lengths/hashes and complete stdout/stderr are below.
- Frozen recorder SHA256 `5059d75346efe1b42885420e04cd5608999b08d95833eacbb152947679ad7e92`; separate disk/SQLite reader SHA256 `3cde35321991104e90ea6cee5d04f9b16fe3f39e00c902a86014755e67d13e8f`. Both RED/GREEN readbacks PASS and launch zero additional product calls. These are saved real subprocess/PTY streams and actual file/SQLite readbacks, not merely test outcomes or script assertions.
- Author simplification and test audit completed. The user explicitly waived independent autoreview; no independent review pass is claimed. Production/test LOC below are separate; no generated/lock/proof asset files are committed.

| Gate | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Tests-only baseline | 27 PASS / 5 intended FAIL; 213.61 s |
| Focused GREEN | 32/32 PASS; 210.32 s |
| Strict source/test types | PASS; 25.47 s |
| Canonical typed lint | 293 rules, 2 files, zero diagnostics; 79.36 s |
| Format / whitespace | PASS |
| Exact source build | PASS; 282.79 s |
| Native RED / GREEN | 6/6 actual calls; child wall totals 47.918 s / 49.682 s |

Commands (one worker; wrapper/preparation time included above):

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.source.json --format json src/cli/plugins-update-command.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/tsconfig.plugin-update-report.json --incremental
OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/cli/plugins-update-command.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.update.test.ts
git diff --check
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance
```

The local ignored typecheck project only scopes the repository's existing strict test config to the two touched files plus ambient declarations; no compiler/lint setting is weakened. Full Vitest test timing includes startup/compilation; no hosted CI duration is claimed. Diff numstat is additions/deletions:


Eleven net production lines cover the shared outcome renderer, all command-owned direct dynamic diagnostics and the existing integrity prompt's layout; no new helper, API, state or update path. Required CI and the first durable bot/human review can only occur after publication; neither is preclaimed here.

The following subprocess captures are complete. Within each JSON string, decode `[U+hhhh]` to that control code point, and `[JSON-ESCAPE-U+hhhh]` to a literal backslash, lowercase u and the shown four hex digits. The collision-checked codec round-trips every original string and survives the publication transport. Only task-root/checkout/executable paths are normalized. prs.title: fix(plugins): tool hooks cannot tell the memory flush from a non-owner turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `before_tool_call` hooks receiving the originating requester without the run trigger, making a host memory flush indistinguishable from its source turn.

## User Impact

Plugins can read optional `ctx.trigger` metadata, such as `"user"`, `"cron"`, or `"memory"`, when the run producer supplies it. Requester identity is unchanged. The trigger does not grant authorization, and existing hooks remain compatible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the trigger at the existing tool-context builder. Move the tool-context types into their own module while preserving existing reexports, so the already oversized hook-type module does not grow. Document availability and the authorization boundary in the tool-hook guide.

Original contribution by @TheDoshus (Doshus <122617686+TheDoshus@users.noreply.github.com>), preserved in the branch history.

## Evidence

- Regression on current main: the real `runBeforeToolCallHook` path omits `trigger: "memory"`. The same test with the fix observes the trigger and unchanged requester, and confirms that an absent trigger remains absent.
- Focused approval-policy and before-tool-call suites: 81 tests passed, including the regression (3 ms), existing approval ownership, cancellation, parameter rewriting, and hook behavior. The policy suite took 9.2 seconds of test time; the E2E suite took 21 seconds including compilation. Runtime preparation took 8m46s on this host.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, core source typecheck, agent-tools test typecheck, and diff checks passed. Current-main integration preserved the tested source bytes.
- Independent Codex review through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Production +57/-42 (net +15), tests +24, docs +5. The original production delta was +19; the shorter metadata comment removes four lines. Remaining growth preserves public reexports while extracting the oversized type module.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40583393224 (completed; inherited lint failure only).
- No fresh live model or channel test was run: the memory-flush producer needs a separate agent scenario, and external channel credentials are unavailable. Contributor-provided isolated CLI evidence on the previous head covered ordinary and memory-flush runs; it is historical evidence.

CI note: [check-lint-core-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40583393224/job/122494333130) reports the same five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx` as scheduled main run [40578163761, check-lint-core-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40578163761/job/122450734896). Only that job and the resulting CI gate failed; no jobs remain unfinished. Exact error signatures match, and this PR changes neither UI file. The automatic report leaves attribution unknown because selected scopes differ. No unrelated UI repair or CI rerun was made.

prs.title: fix: avoid retaining reply contexts through dispatcher registry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-lived Gateway may keep abandoned reply contexts alive when a reply producer never calls `markComplete()`. The process-wide registry previously held a pending-count callback that strongly retained the dispatcher closure and turn data.

## User Impact

Gateway reply-context memory can be reclaimed even when an unfinished dispatcher leaves its pending reservation behind. Shutdown/restart pending counts remain reserved until the owning completion path runs; this is a partial memory mitigation, **not** a fix for the underlying missing-completion producer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store dispatcher-owned mutable numeric pending state in the registry instead of registering a callback that captures the reply context. Preserve enqueue, in-flight delivery, completion, settlement, and restart reservation semantics.

## Evidence

An isolated, built CLI Gateway experiment on Node 24.22.1 measured the original parent commit and corrected code with the same synthetic missing-completion workload. After GC, **16/16** synthetic contexts remained on baseline and **0/16** remained on the candidate; all **16** abandoned pending reservations remained, and an additional final reply was delivered successfully. Heap snapshots independently showed 16 synthetic marker objects on baseline versus 0 on candidate. The exact commands, caveats, and hash identities follow below. **These do not constitute a clean full test-suite pass**: affected Gateway Vitest, lint/typecheck, and current-head CI still require completion.

Related: #184140

## Problem and change

An unfinished reply dispatcher leaves a pending-count callback in the global registry. That callback can retain the dispatcher's V8 closure context, including delivery options and turn data. Replace that callback with dispatcher-owned mutable numeric state, preserving enqueue, completion, settlement, and restart reservations.

This is a **partial memory mitigation**. It does not identify or repair a producer that misses `markComplete()`; abandoned reservations deliberately remain pending. No TTL, configuration, permissions, persistence, or public SDK change.

The two redundant helper/count tests requested for removal have been removed. Existing restart coverage remains. The latest commit adds rerunnable measurement tools and formats the migrated close-test call; production logic is unchanged from tested head `91fcb5bb65a2029afa5c12a1a77dd7f95c98f139`.

## Actual built-Gateway proof — 2026-10-27

Node **24.22.1** (supported by this revision), Linux x86_64. Installed the frozen lockfile with the available pnpm 11.25.0; the repository pins 12.15.0, so this is not pinned-package-manager qualification.

Baseline: `db92acff277255f64e14866d29ebcb00592822b1` (parent of the production fix). Candidate production: `91fcb5bb65a2029afa5c12a1a77dd7f95c98f139`. Proof tools are committed at `6e21e8cc942bca17f779c8ff043cc83d256c1584`.

Both real compiled CLI Gateways reached **`/readyz` with `ready: true`**, using separate empty state/config directories, fresh loopback ports, disabled plugins/channels, and a scrubbed child environment. No model calls or real messages. The parent verified the measured PID equals the launched Gateway PID, main thread is 0, CLI entry is `dist/entry.js`, and the factory is imported through `dist/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime.js`. Worker preloads are explicitly excluded.

Workload: abandon 16 real dispatchers without completion, each capturing a synthetic 65,536-element array; yield and force GC 12 times; then enqueue a real final reply behind a delivery barrier, mark completion, release delivery, and inspect settlement.

| Observable | Callback baseline | Numeric-state candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Abandoned contexts still alive after GC | 16/16 | **0/16** |
| Abandoned dispatcher objects still alive | 16/16 | **0/16** |
| Synthetic context instances in V8 snapshot | 16 | **0** |
| Synthetic payload backing-store self bytes | 8,388,864 | **0** |
| Pending reservations after GC | 16 | **16** |
| Pending with extra delivery blocked | 18 | **18** |
| Pending after markComplete, delivery still blocked | 18 | **18** |
| Pending after extra delivery settles | 16 | **16** |
| Additional final replies actually delivered | 1 | **1** |

The **identical default regression expectation** (`alive == 0`) failed on the baseline with `AssertionError: (16, 0)` (exit 1) and passed on the candidate (exit 0). Both Gateways' actual shutdown consumer subsequently logged `pendingReplies=16`, confirming orphaned reservations were not silently discarded. The harness terminates its own Gateway after measurement; clean shutdown is not claimed.

The baseline snapshot contains this representative **strong path**, excluding weak edges:

```text
global activeReplyDispatchers Set -> table -> tracked object
  -> pending closure -> V8 Context.options -> options.deliver
  -> delivery closure context -> DispatcherRetentionProbeContext
```

The candidate snapshot has zero such marker objects. Backing-store bytes above are the synthetic arrays' self sizes, **not** whole-heap savings or dominator retained sizes. This is synthetic missing-completion fault injection through the real production bundle, not a reproduction of the incident's unknown natural producer.

### Reproduce

Install dependencies and build separate baseline/candidate checkouts. Use the same committed proof scripts for both:

```bash
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-gateway.py /path/to/base baseline /path/to/proof
# Expected: exit 1, alive=16 against the default zero expectation.
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-gateway.py /path/to/candidate candidate /path/to/proof
# Expected: exit 0, alive=0.
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-snapshot.py /path/to/proof/baseline-gateway.heapsnapshot 16
python3 scripts/perf/dispatcher-retention-snapshot.py /path/to/proof/candidate-gateway.heapsnapshot 0
```

Raw snapshots/logs remain private because they can contain process data. The table and graph above contain only inspected synthetic evidence; credentials, actual endpoint addresses, and private paths are omitted.

Compiled factory identities verified from the SDK imports:
- Baseline `reply-dispatcher-loglChz_.mjs`, SHA256 `ea7a2d34a2357d2063f500b108abd1a243a7a4356f21312296223c6cfdc59bff`: callback registration.
- Candidate `reply-dispatcher-ClcrVgn2.mjs`, SHA256 `84683942aa0675de57cd951107f0031dfc32653cc416cfc8c2f00d52434dfc3e`: numeric-state registration.

## Checks and remaining gates

- Candidate `pnpm build:runtime`: **exit 0**, all build phases completed. It retained an artifact lock after an unverified child-cleanup warning; no lock was bypassed.
- Baseline runtime rebuild emitted the callback bundle and the actual Gateway reached ready. **Overall build exit 1** at runtime-postbuild: ambiguous `findSystemGatewayServices` bridge exports after seeding unchanged built artifacts. This is **not clean baseline packaging qualification**; the selected factory chunk was independently checked as above.
- Repository Gateway Vitest run: **20 passed, 36 failed, 13 unhandled errors** across 56 cases. All three existing restart-reservation cases passed. The close suite's first failure was a supervised-process cleanup deadline, followed by supervisor-shutdown/global-singleton-reset errors. Baseline inheritance of those failures is **not established**. A narrower rerun was interrupted during resource contention and is not a pass.
- Changed TypeScript/JS files: oxfmt **passes**, including correcting the migrated close-test formatting. Python tools: Ruff **passes**; Python compilation and Node syntax checks **pass**. Independent source review found and corrected preload callback, worker attribution, and missing zero-count assertion issues.
- Repository oxlint and core tsgo attempts: **blocked before checking** by retained `file_lock_stale` artifact ownership. Typecheck/lint are **not claimed passing**.
- One earlier concurrent build was OOM-killed; the serial candidate build above succeeded. No throughput/latency or live-agent claim.
- Broad GitHub CI was skipped on the prior Draft head; current-head CI and maintainer review remain required.

**Keep Draft pending review of this evidence and unresolved checks.** The memory mitigation now has before/after runtime and heap-retainer evidence; missing-completion lifecycle repair remains separate.

prs.title: fix: replayed exec commands fail with bash syntax error when secret-file reads are redacted
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
(no tracking issue yet — happy to file one if preferred; this is a small, focused fix)

Required PR title:
fix: replayed exec commands fail with bash syntax error when secret-file reads are redacted

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: exec tool commands that read secrets at call time — the common
`TOKEN=$(cat ~/.openclaw/secrets/API_KEY)` idiom — fail in bash with
`syntax error near unexpected token ')'` whenever the redaction pipeline touches
the command text and something replays it (a follow-up turn copying a command from
an error message, progress/approval rendering, or transcript replay).

The redaction of `KEY=$(cat …)` replaces only the captured chunk `$(cat` with `***`
and leaves the closing `)` verbatim:

```
before: TOKEN=$(cat ~/.openclaw/secrets/svc-panel-token); curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" …
after:  TOKEN=*** ~/.openclaw/secrets/svc-panel-token); curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" …
bash:   /bin/bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `)'
```

The orphaned `)` is not valid shell. Any surface that echoes a redacted command back
into `exec` therefore dies at parse time, before the secret substitution ever runs.

## User Impact

User impact: agents and users can keep the "read a secret from a file at call time"
pattern without the redaction pipeline corrupting the command; redacted command text
stays syntactically valid and replayable for the env/assignment capture shapes this change
scopes to, while opaque-credential captures keep masking as they do today.

## Why This Change Was Made

`redactSensitiveText` / `redactToolPayloadText` mask assignment-shaped values
(`TOKEN=…`, `secret=…`, `--password=…`) via patterns whose unquoted value class stops
at the first whitespace. For a command substitution the captured value is just the
opener `$(cat`, so masking it deletes the opening `$( ` but keeps the expansion's
closing `)` from the untouched remainder — broken shell syntax.

This PR skips masking only for **unquoted partial expansion openers captured by the shell/env
assignment rules** (`shellReferencePreservingPatterns`: `ENV_ASSIGNMENT`,
`ESCAPED_ENV_ASSIGNMENT`, `STANDALONE_ASSIGNMENT(_QUOTED)`) — a captured chunk that starts with
`$(` or `${` and does not contain the matching `)`/`}`. Outside those rules it skips masking only
for an **unbalanced `${NAME` variable reference**: that is an identifier rather than credential
material, and masking it deletes the opener while keeping the closing `}` — the
`Authorization: Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}` case, which hits this because
`HTTP_AUTH_OPAQUE_CREDENTIAL_PATTERN` excludes `}` from its value class. Captures owned by
opaque-credential rules (URL userinfo, connection strings, structured auth headers,
operator-configured patterns) keep masking `$(`-shaped values exactly as before, because in those
rules the captured chunk *is* the credential, even when it happens to begin with `$(`.
Security properties are preserved:

- Partial openers carry **no literal secret by definition** — the value is resolved by
  the shell at run time from a file/variable/subprocess, and everything after the
  first space was never masked by these chunk patterns anyway. Redacted output leaks
  exactly what the old output already showed.
- Quoted captures (`TOKEN="$(cat …` captured whole) hold the whole expansion and still mask to a
  balanced placeholder — byte-identical to before (fixture-guarded).
- Known secret **values** remain masked independently by the registered-value exact
  pass and the vendor-token grammars (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, URL userinfo, bearer literals),
  which are untouched — fixture-guarded.
- The existing shell-reference preservation mechanism (`shellReferencePreservingPatterns`,
  `MY_TOKEN=$MY_TOKEN`) already encodes the intent that assignment patterns should not
  corrupt shell structure; this extends it to command substitutions, which reference a
  secret *location* rather than containing the secret.

## Evidence

Reproduced on current `main` (`90c8780d`, v2026.10.7) with Node 24.22.1, Linux:

```
$ node --import tsx repro.mts   # imports src/logging/redact.ts directly
BEFORE (git stash of the fix):
  OPENAI_API_KEY=*** ~/.openclaw/secrets/key)          <-- orphan ')'
  export TOKEN=*** ~/.secrets/x) && curl -s https://example.test
AFTER (with fix):
  OPENAI_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.openclaw/secrets/key)          <-- unchanged
  export TOKEN=$(cat ~/.secrets/x) && curl -s https://example.test
```

Observed mutation on the shipped release (2026.6.8 npm, Oct 26 2026): a `write` tool call
whose content contained the literal example
`TOKEN=` + `$(cat ~/.openclaw/secrets/svc-panel-token); …` arrived on disk as
`TOKEN=*** ~/.openclaw/secrets/…` — the tool-argument redaction path
(`embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.sanitizeToolArgs`, removed from `main` on 2026-10-10 per
`src/plugins/compat/agent-harness-records.ts`: *"pass tool arguments unchanged. Secret
masking belongs in diagnostics"*) mutates the exact string before execution/persistence on
the shipped release. This PR fixes the redaction **engine** itself (`src/logging/redact.ts`),
which is shared by the release's argument path and every remaining display/persistence
surface on `main`.

Session logs from a non-upstream OpenClaw 2026.6.8 deployment: a scan of
`~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl` (deduplicated) found **94 corrupted exec-command
occurrences across 16 session transcripts**
spanning Sep–Oct 2026, signature `(TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|...)=<mask> ~/...` — an assignment
whose expansion opener was masked while the tail survived inside stored tool calls.

Concrete example (cron session, Oct 16 2026):
the transcript stores the emitted argument verbatim as `TOKEN=*** ~/.openclaw/secrets/svc-panel-token); code=$(curl …` (the corruption happened before the tool call was recorded),
bash rejected it with `syntax error near unexpected token ')'` (exit code 2), and the
agent had to rewrite the task as an out-of-band script — the standard community
workaround for this class of failure. Same signature recurs across months of sessions
when a follow-up turn replays a redacted command through exec.

Focused tests (all pass with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`):

- `src/logging/redact.test.ts` — new regression test
  `keeps shell command substitutions syntactically valid when masking` (unquoted
  `$(cat …` / `${VAR` forms preserved; quoted and literal-value masking unchanged):
  `51 passed (51)`, `Test Files 1 passed`.
- `src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts` — recorded pre-fix outputs over a 250-sample
  corpus stay byte-identical (proves no masking regression, no new exposure):
  `3 passed (3)`.
- Companion redaction suites `redact-performance.test.ts`,
  `redact-pattern-allocation.test.ts`, `redacting-stream.test.ts`,
  `redact-large-text-security.test.ts`: `14 passed (14)`.
- `bash -c` replay proof: the production command shape, passed through
  `redactSensitiveText()` of the **base commit** and of the **fixed** tree, then executed:
  base → `exit=2`, `/bin/bash: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token `)'`
  (byte-identical to the production log); fixed → `exit=0`.

<details>
<summary>Test outputs</summary>

```
✓  logging  src/logging/redact.test.ts (51 tests) 1436ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  51 passed (51)

✓  logging  src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts (3 tests) 1814ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

</details>

## Implementation notes

Two-file change, 92 insertions, no API/config changes:

- `src/logging/redact.ts`: add `isPartialShellExpansion(token)` and
  `isPartialShellVariableReference(token)`, then use a two-width guard in `prepareRedactionCapture`
  (before masking is computed): `isShellReferencePattern ? isPartialShellExpansion(token) :
  isPartialShellVariableReference(token)`, where `isShellReferencePattern` is the existing
  `shellReferencePreservingPatterns` membership test in the same closure. Assignment rules keep the
  full partial-expansion exemption; every other rule only exempts an unbalanced `${NAME` reference,
  which cannot carry literal credential material and would otherwise leave an orphan `}` (this is
  what `Authorization: Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}` hits, because `HTTP_AUTH_OPAQUE_CREDENTIAL_PATTERN`
  excludes `}` from its value class). Comments record why `$(`-shaped captures are not exempted
  outside the assignment rules.
- `src/logging/redact.test.ts`: regression test using `String.fromCharCode(36, 40)` so the corpus
  itself survives redaction of this file in logs and transcripts (dogfooding the bug). It asserts
  the env-assignment command shapes and the bearer `${MY_TOKEN` reference come back unchanged, and
  that opaque-credential captures stay masked — both an `$(...)`-shaped URL-userinfo password and a
  balanced `${PASS}` one, so the exemption cannot be read as loosening credential rules.

prs.title: feat: add a Settings toggle to disable the direct Archive shortcut
prs.body:
Closes #163739

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Pressing the direct archive chord (`Ctrl+Shift+A` on Windows/Linux, `⌘⇧A` on macOS) unconditionally archived the active session. Users whose browser or extensions already claim this chord (such as Chrome's native Tab Search or Firefox add-ons) had no way to opt out of the intercept.

## User Impact

Users can now toggle **Archive keyboard shortcut** on or off under **Settings → Appearance**. 
- **When Disabled:** The browser retains control over the `Ctrl+Shift+A` / `⌘⇧A` chord. The Archive action remains fully accessible via the chat header `...` menu and the bare `A` key.
- **Persistence & Scope:** Stored locally in browser settings (`Stored in this browser only`). Default behavior remains enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change provides a lightweight, local opt-out so browser shortcuts are released cleanly without disrupting primary session workflows or menu-driven interactions.

## Verification & Testing

- **Local Targeted Checks:**
  - `pnpm lint:ui:i18n` → Passed (exit 0)
  - `pnpm format:check` → Passed (46,601 files clean)
  - `oxlint` on modified UI files → 0 warnings, 0 errors
  - `npx tsc --noEmit -p ui/tsconfig.json` → 0 errors
- **Note on Full Monorepo Lint:** Full `pnpm lint` hit a Windows worker timeout during `plugin-sdk boundary dts` compilation (`ETIMEDOUT`), deferring monorepo pipeline verification to GitHub Actions CI.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: avoid reporting recovered model attempts as failed runs
prs.body:
Related: #185496

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading terminal-failure diagnostics when a model candidate fails and the outer fallback chain continues successfully. Production monitoring counted these inner `lane task error ... errorName=FailoverError` records as failed runs, even though the runs handed off to their configured fallback.

## User Impact

No change to responses, retry budgets, fallback selection, or persisted state. Operators retain the fallback owner's existing candidate/reason/next-model decision log, without a duplicate terminal-looking queue error. Direct terminal failures and unrelated cleanup errors retain their error logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runner already knows whether it is executing an outer-chain candidate. Carry that fact in the queue's existing diagnostic metadata and suppress only candidate `FailoverError` logging there. The outer fallback owner already records handoff and exhaustion, so this adds no logger, recovery abstraction, or new state.

The regression now uses the real command queue: the old fixture bypassed it. Its redundant routing-callback echo and unused fixture hook were removed; final execution trace and routing-decision receipt assertions remain. Production delta: +6 lines; test delta: -10 lines. No baseline changes.

## Evidence

- Red on base `7c0f75ece787e7be7248ea712b9c1df3aacfa814`: the existing successful-fallback test fails its new no-lane-error assertion after removing the fixture's queue bypass. The captured call is `lane task error` with `errorName=FailoverError`; the fallback itself succeeds. Body 4.766s, wrapper 36.38s.
- Green: `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.timeout-cooldown.e2e.test.ts src/process/command-queue.failure-logging.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 45 tests passed. The 36-case embedded suite took 42.607s and the four-case cooldown suite 8.024s; complete wrapper 93.22s. The existing integration scenarios exercise real run entry, fallback, queue, session and cleanup owners with scripted model attempts; no added provider requests or live Gateway. Their cost covers existing distinct timeout/replay/profile contracts, rather than new diagnostic test boots.
- The queue's existing error table also proves a direct terminal `FailoverError` remains error-level; cancellation and independent cleanup failures retain their existing assertions.
- Passed targeted typechecking: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <config> --incremental` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json`.
- Passed targeted lint via `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on all six changed files; targeted format check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview: complete final local snapshot against the base above, P1, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. Unchanged fallback-owner and terminal-settlement modules were supplied as context.
- Initial PR CI found two stale exact-metadata expectations in `lane-controller.test.ts`. `pnpm test:ci-failed 186444 --run` reproduced both failures; updating the existing expectation for the new diagnostic flag yields 32 passing tests (13.38s wrapper). Targeted typecheck/lint/format and a fresh P1 review cover that one-line repair; production is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(xai): keep Talk connected after interrupted response replacement
prs.body:
Closes #184207

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes xAI Talk disconnecting with “Realtime provider output has no live response owner” when server VAD interrupts a response and its successor arrives without the interrupted response’s terminal event.

## User Impact

The conversation can continue with the new answer instead of closing. Late output from the interrupted answer remains discarded. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI adapter now settles the interrupted response as canceled before admitting a distinct identified successor. This is restricted to an observed server-VAD interruption; ordinary overlapping responses still hit the existing relay guard. Pending user transcription survives the handover.

The change uses the existing response owner and completion callback rather than relaxing shared ownership rules. Production delta: +25/-1 lines; one integration regression exercises the real adapter, relay ownership, and session harness.

## Evidence

On upstream base `e83186f4e8343a4b37001d0e726ef34e02d10a2a` with this patch:

- **Red/green regression:** the new test fails on the unpatched bridge with the exact ownership error, then passes with the fix. It covers the missing A terminal, canceled A turn, distinct B turn, preserved user transcript, discarded late A audio/text/tools/terminal, successful B completion, and rejection of arbitrary overlap.
- **46 tests passed** across the xAI provider suite and new relay-ownership regression. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts src/gateway/talk/relay/xai-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint (including package-boundary declaration preparation), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Two independent reviews found no actionable defects.
- **Separate live Gateway smoke:** two real xAI runs received generated PCM through `talk.session.appendAudio`, interrupted a counting response with a sky-color question, then asked an ordinary arithmetic question. Each returned three distinct turns; 608 and 527 audio frames, zero errors. Replies included “A clear daytime sky is blue” and “Two plus two is four.”

**Proof limits:** live smoke used the candidate xAI plugin with previously built core/UI at a different, carried base—not this upstream head. Both live runs received the predecessor’s normal terminal, so those earlier runs did not exercise the missing-terminal branch. The October 27 fault-injection proof below now exercises it through real transport. The earlier synthetic smoke did not test physical microphone/remote playback. A full upstream runtime build was not tested. The earlier carried-base full-runtime build attempt stopped on a missing dependency; it is not claimed as passing. The fix was subsequently deployed to production; the manual microphone test below is additional evidence, not a reproduction of the rare branch.

### Production microphone interruption test — October 26, 2026

The patched production Gateway completed a manual Web Talk session using the real xAI provider and physical microphone. The user rapidly changed requests while answers were being generated. Gateway diagnostics recorded eight response lifecycles: five completed and three canceled, with no session warning/error or ownership failure. The conversation continued after all three cancellations, and the user confirmed normal playback.

Redacted lifecycle excerpt (HKT; response IDs replaced with A–F):

```text
20:33:24.840 response.created A
20:33:30.058 client response.cancel A
20:33:30.283 response.outcome A cancelled; response.done A
20:33:30.516 response.created B
20:33:31.119 response.done B
20:33:33.034 response.created C
20:33:37.374 client response.cancel C
20:33:37.605 response.outcome C cancelled; response.done C
20:33:39.639 response.created D
20:33:43.350 client response.cancel D
20:33:43.587 response.outcome D cancelled; response.done D
20:33:45.655 response.created E
20:33:49.650 response.outcome E completed; response.done E
20:34:27.011 session.closed
```

This establishes production cancellation/recovery behavior with real microphone input. All three cancellations were client-triggered, and each predecessor terminal arrived before its successor. It does **not** establish that the server-VAD missing-terminal branch ran. The October 27 controlled real-transport fault injection below supplies the missing-terminal branch proof.

### Review fixes — `77127e9b`

Moved the ownership composition regression to the core relay test suite, obtaining the xAI provider through its public plugin registration entry and the harness through the plugin SDK. The socket mock preserves real-module exports. No production code changed in this follow-up.

The relocated regression fails on the original unpatched bridge and passes with the repair. Another 71 affected tests pass. Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, plugin boundary checks, and the mock-export ratchet pass locally. Fresh PR CI and review remain pending. The production microphone evidence above remains smoke coverage, not a claim of live missing-terminal reproduction.

### Real-transport missing-terminal fault injection — October 27, 2026

**Passed through a real xAI WebSocket and an isolated Gateway running the production build** (`b891b0f0ba0312a8f3aabb627d0b4e0a4554aaaa`, carrying this adapter fix). A single-connection transport filter withheld A's real `response.done`, forwarded the next real speech/VAD event and response B, then replayed five captured A frames after B started. The Gateway settled A as canceled, admitted B, rejected late A output, completed B, and completed a third ordinary turn. The client received **932 audio frames, zero Talk errors, and no late A audio after B began**. Test processes were stopped afterward; production was not changed.

This is controlled production-boundary fault injection, not a claim that xAI naturally omitted a terminal during this run. A had completed upstream; its terminal was withheld before reaching the adapter. Real provider events and audio drove the Gateway's missing-terminal handover. The test used generated PCM, not a physical microphone. The runtime was a carried production build, not a fresh build of the PR head.

<details>
<summary>Redacted filter and Gateway trace (UTC filter timestamps; +08:00 Gateway timestamps)</summary>


```json
  "successorAndFollowupCompleted": true,

  "audioFrames": 932,

  "naturalMissingTerminalObserved": false

```
</details>

### Final fixture and CI-boundary repair

Socket construction now resolves a fixture-owned promise instead of timer polling. The core regression loads the xAI public entry through the existing bundled-plugin facade loader, avoiding a static extension dependency in the core typecheck graph. Production behavior is unchanged by these fixture repairs.

Validation for the final fixture: regression passes (639 ms test time; 5.23 s total Vitest duration) and fails on the unpatched bridge at the ownership assertion. Scoped typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Compiler file-membership inspection of the changed test includes zero bundled extension source files. The broad local boundary checker was obstructed by preserved dependency-backup directories; fresh PR CI remains the full-graph gate. CI timing for this revision is pending.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop background exec completions from replaying full history into a fresh thread
prs.body:
Related: #183286, #179363, #172026, #178982

## What Problem This Solves

When a background `exec` finishes in a Codex-backed WebChat session, the completion wake does not continue the session's bound native thread. It starts a fresh transient thread, replays the full session history into it uncached, and does it again for the follow-up turn. On a long session every completion wake costs a full uncached history read. In one observed session, four completion wakes each sent about 190k uncached input tokens.

This finishes, for event wakes, what #183286 started: tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. #183286 kept seven native Codex thread, plugin, and supervision declarations stable across owner and completion turns. A completion wake still differed from the user turn in three other ways, and each one alone forces a new thread:

1. **Tool-policy scope.** The default session-event source policy caps every follow-up at the producer's tool list. A wake with a cap runs as a turn-scoped restricted turn, which the Codex harness serves on a transient thread with native code mode off (48 eager dynamic tools instead of 10).
2. **`skill_workshop` schema.** The personal-library schema is published only on human turns that carry an authoring grant. A wake publishes a narrower schema, the dynamic tool catalog fingerprint changes, and the bound thread rotates. The Claude CLI runner already fixed this in #172026 (`resolveStableCliSkillAuthoring`); the embedded/harness path never used it.
3. **Conversation context.** An internal (WebChat) session stores no delivery route, so `buildSessionEventContext` never matched the wake's own WebChat route and dropped the session chat type. The wake's developer instructions then lacked the "You are in a WebChat direct conversation" line, the live thread config fingerprint changed, and Codex had to cold-resume the thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each layer is fixed where the difference starts, without widening authority:

- **Scope (A).** A cap from a conversation-scoped producer turn is the session's own policy, and the follow-up re-derives that policy itself. `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` marks the caller identity session-scoped when the policy scope is `conversation` and no caller-supplied source policy exists, and `session-event-target` skips it only when the follow-up's destination is the same session. The mark is not set when group, per-DM, or sender policy narrowed the producer (`groupPolicy`/`senderPolicy`). Those come from the inbound request, the wake cannot rebuild them, and the cap keeps carrying them. The caller-inheritance merge keeps the mark only for an inherited owner of the same agent and session that has no narrower cap of its own. Cross-session follow-ups, sender-narrowed producers, and turn-scoped producers keep the cap exactly as before.
- **Policy lifetime stays host-owned.** No public SDK option is added. The host already computes the attempt's policy lifetime for Codex (`pluginHarnessToolPolicyScope`, `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies`). Host policy preparation now records that value in the attempt's host capability, and the host's tool construction (`createToolSurfaceAsync`, which is how Codex builds every dynamic tool) passes it to the internal tool options. A plugin cannot set it through tool options: a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope` is overwritten by the host value, and when the host has none the cap stays in place (fail-closed).
- **`skill_workshop` (B).** The #172026 helper moves from `cli-runner/` to `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` as a per-runtime factory and is also applied at the embedded attempt dispatch. Internal turns publish the session's last human shape with an expired grant: the declaration matches, personal-library calls fail with `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`, and workspace calls keep the ordinary no-grant rule (unsandboxed runs only). Grants that are already expired (transcript follow-ups, stranded-reply recovery) now carry `expired: true` and no longer replace the remembered human shape.
- **Context (C).** For a session that stores no delivery route, an event on that session's own WebChat route (`channel: "webchat"`, `to: <sessionKey>`, the shape `chat.send` and subagent announce already use) keeps the session chat type. Events routed to any other session still get none.

Out of scope, noted for follow-up: when a thread's config does change (for example a model switch), Codex can take longer than OpenClaw's 2-second unload budget to close a code-mode thread after `thread/unsubscribe` (measured 0.7 s, 2.9 s, and 10.6 s in this harness). The cold resume then fails with "Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration". With this change, completion wakes no longer take that path.

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. Every claim below was checked by running it.

## User Impact

- Background `exec` completion wakes in Codex-backed sessions continue the bound thread with native code mode on. The wake reads the session prefix from cache instead of replaying the full history uncached, and the next user turn stays on the same thread.
- No tool, personal-library, or workspace access is widened. Sessions narrowed by group, per-DM, or sender policy keep today's behavior, including the fresh-thread wake.
- On internal turns with a remembered personal default target, `skill_workshop` calls that rely on that default now return `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED` instead of running against the workspace. Explicit `target=workspace` calls keep the no-grant rule.

## Evidence

Regression tests, each shown failing without its fix and passing with it:

| Test | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `host-capability.tool-policy-scope.test.ts` (new): host-prepared scope reaches tool construction; a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"` does not | 2 failed, 1 passed (host value not injected) | 3 passed |
| `session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects: same-session" | fails: `writeOffered: false`, expected `true` (the producer cap is kept) | passes |
| `agent-tools.session-event-cap.test.ts` "a sender narrowed by toolsBySender" (real `createOpenClawCodingTools`, real caller identity, no mock) | fails: `expected true to be undefined` when the sender check is removed | 3 passed |
| `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` "keeps the human shape when a follow-up passes an expired grant" | 1 failed, 3 passed | 4 passed |
| `session-event-context.test.ts` "keeps the session chat type only for $route" | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` "offers the human turn's skill_workshop definition on an internal turn" | asserts the surfaces differ without the helper | equal with it |

### Authority controls around the same-session exemption

`session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects" runs the production path: a real `captureSessionEventTargetForHost` under a caller identity, the real `enqueueSessionEventForHost` admission, the real harness host capabilities and managed tool surface, and a real file write. Each row captures a producer whose ceiling lists only `read`:

| Row | Producer identity | Follow-up tool surface | File after the follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| `same-session` | same session, marked session-scoped | `write` offered | written |
| `restricted-sender` | same session, not marked (the caller leaves the mark off when `senderPolicy` or `groupPolicy` narrowed the turn; see the caller test above) | no `write` | unchanged |
| `cross-session` | other session, marked | no `write` | unchanged |
| `revoked-before-write` | same session, marked; the session permission mode is set to `read-only` after the tool surface is built | `write` offered, call refused (authority/permission error) | unchanged |

Result: 4 passed. With `session-event-target.ts` restored to its base version, the `same-session` row fails (`writeOffered: false`).

Expired personal-library calls: `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` builds the real coding tools for an internal turn and shows `skill_workshop` with `target: "personal"` rejected with "fresh message" (`AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`). `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` shows an expired grant refuses personal-library calls and never replaces the remembered human shape; the sandboxed-run refusal for workspace calls is unchanged code from #172026 and is not re-tested here.

What this does not show: the embedded dispatch wiring (`resolveStableEmbeddedSkillAuthoring` at `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`) is a single call covered by the two tests above through the same factory, not by a dispatch-level test.

Touched suites: the files above plus `gateway-caller-context.test.ts` and `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` pass. The new production-boundary rows pass 4 of 4. `tsgo` core and the `src` test shards: clean. `oxfmt` on the repository: clean. `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against the base commit: OK (the PR adds no mock factory and no line to `agent-tools.ts` or `cli-runner/prepare.ts`).

### Required test lanes that fail on this PR's CI

Three required lanes failed on the earlier heads. Each was checked against `main`:

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.exec-completion.test.ts` "an empty CLI final": fails the same way with every file this PR touches restored to `origin/main` (`1e89f5b3fe8`), and fails in CI on unrelated PRs (for example https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40290743775 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292785214). It is inherited.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` "drains a restored interrupted predecessor before later cohorts": fails the same way with the PR's files restored to `origin/main`, and fails in CI on an unrelated PR (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292474849). It is inherited.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.operator-continuation.test.ts`: all 20 tests pass locally on this branch merged with `origin/main`. I could not reproduce the CI failure. By construction this PR cannot reach that path: the new session-scoped marking requires `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"`, which that test never sets, so its follow-up ceiling is unchanged. I did not find this failure on another PR, so I cannot call it inherited.

Live run against a real Codex app-server (codex 0.162.1, the version pinned on `main`), an isolated gateway, and `chat.send`. Script: user turn, a turn that starts `exec` with `background=true`, the completion wake, then a user turn. Wire capture of the app-server JSON-RPC, base `4fa442e3327`:

prs.title: fix(plugins): authenticate native MCP servers with environment-backed headers
prs.body:
Closes #184192
Related: #160244

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes PostHog and other enabled native MCP plugins sending literal environment placeholders as authentication headers, resulting in failed tool discovery.

## User Impact
Native plugin header credentials resolve from the Gateway environment using the existing config grammar. Missing or empty required variables skip the affected server with a generic diagnostic; healthy siblings remain available. Enable only plugins whose declared endpoints you trust.

## Why This Change Was Made
Resolve at the native-manifest boundary, not the shared HTTP transport: already-resolved operator config must not be interpolated twice. Reuse the config parser for escaping and defaults; leave URLs, process fields, third-party bundle formats, and operator override precedence unchanged. Manifest metadata is not mutated.

The open stacked PR #160244 already identifies this fix direction. This is a small standalone fix against current main for the independently observed released PostHog failure, with fresh regression proof. It does not replace or close that work. No inspection-only option is added because current callers do not require it.

Simplification: no new parser, state, cache, public option, or per-provider code. Necessary growth is 44 production additions/1 deletion, 91 test additions/2 deletions, and two documentation lines.

## Evidence
- Base: `b17d07fc01e0ce6efdc569d890140f1a11488239`. Two added regressions fail on unmodified production source (literal headers; missing servers retained), while nine existing tests pass.
- `corepack pnpm test src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **11 passed**. Fixed run: 26.38s wall time, 23.48s runner duration; individual new tests 2ms each. Cold compilation dominates.
- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-config.cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **14 passed**, 10.13s wall time.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json src/plugins/bundle-mcp.ts src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts`: passed, no problems in two files.
- Targeted oxfmt check, plugin-extension import boundary, one-file docs MDX check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent isolated autoreview at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Regression coverage includes expansion, escaping, fallback, unsupported syntax, one-pass substitution, unchanged URL/manifest, undefined/empty variables, sibling retention, ownership metadata, and credential-free diagnostics.

Limits: these are production-loader boundary and consumer tests, not a live PostHog test of the patched package or a full Gateway end-to-end run. Original reported live evidence is 401 through the released plugin versus 200 with direct credential initialization. No real credentials were used in the checkout. Hosted CI timing/results are pending. A first consumer command named a nonexistent auth-status test and ran no tests; the corrected existing suites above passed. The contribution guide names a retired source-boundary script; the current plugin-boundary checker passed instead.
