prs.title: fix(infra): keep Windows process start deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync` derives its deadline and per-attempt remaining budget from the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but hands those budgets to `spawnSync` timeouts, which are consumed by the monotonic clock. When the wall clock is shifted, the two clocks disagree and Windows process-start detection either stalls (clock rolled back → inflated remaining budget) or kills a healthy probe (clock jumped forward → negative remaining).

**Problem**: cross-clock-domain deadline — wall-clock seed/remaining read, monotonic timeout consumption.

**Solution**: derive the deadline and both remaining-budget reads from `performance.now()` so all three sit on the monotonic clock, and round both positive budgets up with `Math.ceil` to preserve Node's `spawnSync` integer-timeout contract (fractional timeouts throw `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`). The exhausted-budget checks (`<= 0`) are retained.

**What changed**: `src/infra/windows-process-start.ts` — three `Date.now()` → `performance.now()`, plus `Math.ceil` on both positive budgets. Nothing else changed: return contract, timeout values, `timeoutMs` parameter, and all callers are untouched. The deadline is a process-local closure variable — never serialized, persisted, reported, or compared against a wall-clock value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The same cross-clock-domain bug family has been fixed across the codebase (prior monotonic-clock PRs), and the sibling Darwin reader (`src/shared/pid-alive.ts`) already rounds its monotonic remaining budget with `Math.ceil` before spawning.

## User Impact

On Windows, system time adjustments (manual changes, NTP corrections) no longer make process-start identity checks return `null` or stall. Concretely, `openclaw gateway stop` keeps terminating its own Gateway after a clock jump instead of reporting success while the Gateway keeps serving. Rounding fractional budgets also prevents Node's `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` rejection when `performance.now()` subtraction yields a fractional timeout.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI proof — complete Windows Gateway workflow** (`windows-latest`, `SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof` workflow `windows-cli-proof-184162.yml`, run 40443823765). The job runs the shipped `openclaw gateway install --allow-unconfigured --force` (real Scheduled Task Gateway), waits until it listens, then runs the shipped `openclaw gateway stop --force --json`, which resolves the Scheduled Task owner and re-verifies the live Gateway PID with `readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync()` before terminating it. `NODE_OPTIONS=--import cli-clock-shift.mjs` steps `Date.now()` forward +10s on the deadline read inside that reader; `performance.now()` is untouched, so the skew is a pure NTP-style wall-clock jump. The only build difference between the two halves is the three-line revert.

```text
=== post-fix (performance.now + Math.ceil) :: openclaw gateway stop ===
stop exit=0
  "action": "stop",
  "ok": true,
  "result": "stopped",
VERDICT[post-fix]: STOPPED gateway identity verified and terminated
CONTROL[post-fix]: CONTROL_STOPPED plain stop released 19123
```

prs.title: fix(cron): restore automation run history for administrator chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes administrator chats being able to inspect an existing automation while reading its run history fails with `Automation not found`, including managed dreaming jobs.

## User Impact

Administrators can read an existing automation's run history using their admitted management authority, including selecting a specific run. No permission changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing management grant to `cron.runs`, as already happens for `cron.get`. Keep the management and recovery tool schemas and descriptions consistent with that capability. Existing caller restrictions, grant validation, and current-job restrictions still apply.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real authenticated administrator chat: `get` succeeded while `runs` failed. After deploying the fix, both succeeded and the native tool returned all eight retained dreaming runs.
- Added a regression using the real automation tool, grant binding, Gateway handlers, and persisted SQLite history. It fails before the fix, passes afterward, and verifies that a call without the management grant is still denied.
- All 89 focused tests passed, covering run visibility, grant/context handling, management and recovery schemas, requester authority, and tool-prefix stability.
- Production typecheck, targeted lint/format, documentation validation, and runtime build passed.
- Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The isolated PR checkout matches the tested and deployed source byte for byte.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and timing</summary>

Focused suites: `cron.runs.test.ts`, `cron-tool.management.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`, `requester-cron-authority.integration.test.ts`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, with `--maxWorkers=1`.

The new regression took 2.165 seconds. The run-history suite took about 26 seconds of test execution and 159.34 seconds wall time; the remaining focused suites took 327.82 seconds wall time, largely compilation. The integration test crosses the grant-forwarding boundary that isolated handler tests missed. CI timing is pending.

Additional checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:check`, `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm build:runtime` (2 minutes 45.6 seconds).

</details>

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): simplify complete cached rows [do not merge]
prs.body:
## Outcome: stopped before landing

The compression is complete, but the signed-in native confirmation does not clear the performance gate. This experiment must not merge. The final head is `76115e6bd389b8f528cf058436492c89d6302bce`, compared with pinned main `842dfae24ad1b73a9599f6c57fdc5d581b49cc80` after integrating the connect-first and boot-ordering changes.

The visible cached-row result survives: all 11 warm pairs on each route have the resolved session link and decoded inline thumbnail at first transcript paint, zero later changes to those displayed facts, and zero thread-height change. The formal chat LoAF secondary is adverse: 171.9 [169.1–182.95] → 196.6 [186.95–207.25] ms, paired median +16.8 ms, 9/11 worse. It meets both predeclared adverse rules. The controls demonstrate observer sensitivity but do not clear this result. No costs are subtracted and no groups or old-head results are pooled.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link could paint cached transcript text and then change its link labels, image boxes/pixels, notice rows, and avatars. Campaign evidence recorded title-chip restyling around 1.05 s, image completion around 1.28–1.64 s, and later notice/avatar changes. The branch retains previously displayed row facts with the cached row.

## Why This Change Was Made

The disposable transcript snapshot owns the display projection. It retains resolved inline link display, intrinsic image dimensions and previously authorized inline thumbnail Blobs, canonical archive facts, and bounded avatar source identities consumed through the existing avatar URL cache. Message-derived reset/compaction/system notices derive from cached messages.

| Fact | Previous wait/cache | Branch behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session label | Document-memory titler, then live lookup | Apply retained label with Markdown; refresh differing live labels |
| PR metadata | Document-memory preview cache and best-effort prefetch | Apply retained inline badge/label facts with the row |
| Image geometry | Supplied dimensions survive; learned intrinsic dimensions did not | Retain learned dimensions with source/rendition identity |
| Thumbnail pixels | Document-memory bytes or HTTP cache; ticketed artifacts are not HTTP-cacheable | Restore previously displayed inline bytes through a Blob URL with the row |
| Archive divider | Canonical facts existed in live history but not persisted metadata | Retain canonical facts and use the existing notice builder |
| Assistant portrait | Known-good URL cache existed, but transcript source identity/pre-live consumption was missing | Retain source identity and use the existing cached-only avatar read |

Limits remain 8 links and 8 images per retained message entry, facts for at most 80 retained entries, bounded strings, and 32 thumbnails / 8 MiB total / 256 KiB per image. Keys include gateway/account/session scope, artifact/source identity and rendition. Facts/bytes are pruned with the cached window and cleared by existing scope/reset/sign-out invalidations. Tickets, tokens and credential-bearing transport URLs are excluded; animated/full-size originals remain outside the byte budget.

## User Impact

A completed visit can restore retained display facts without live read authority. Cached bytes grant no network or action authority. Interactions keep their live admission; missing/evicted bytes use the existing loader. Disposable projection version 7 resets incompatible caches. No Gateway protocol or durable server shape changes.

## Runtime compression

The requested compression removes 258 handwritten runtime TypeScript/TSX lines: growth falls from +1,018 to **+760**, a **25.34% reduction** against the same rebased base. Native image presentation/gallery share one owner. Snapshot records own validation/serialization; the store retains IndexedDB lifecycle. Eager link binding owns registration/stamping, and the lazy titler owns live lookup admission. Row display facts share one module. Five superseded modules from the pre-compression implementation are deleted, one-use wrappers/duplicate field lists removed, and all consumers migrate. Bounds, object-URL cleanup, privacy projection, scope invalidation and single-writer lifecycle remain. The compressed bundle fits main's existing chat asset limits; earlier budget increases are removed.

Handwritten UI runtime is 1,676 insertions / 916 deletions, net +760. The specifically requested production filter reports **55 files, 2,698 insertions / 1,082 deletions, net +1,616**. Its literal exclusions also retain generated validators, benchmark/fixture code and TSX browser tests. Growth implements the explicitly approved bounded byte retention, privacy/eviction lifecycle, initial display and live catch-up contract.

Touched areas: transcript message/snapshot cache and record/store; shared row facts; native image owner and image frame/actions/opening; Markdown/link title owner and consumers; transcript notice metadata; avatar cache consumers; Team-scale fixture/bench/probes; owning regression/native tests and Control UI documentation. `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is unchanged.

## Evidence: final-head measurement and attribution

One AWS lease `cbx_44744dc49171`, actual `c7a.4xlarge` (16 CPUs, about 31 GiB RAM), run `run_c1040ca1544dd9932e9648d779ac42be` ([run portal](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c1040ca1544dd9932e9648d779ac42be)). Both builds use the same instance, repository Playwright Chromium, synthetic signed-in trusted-proxy state, 3,000-session fixture, 80 ms RTT / 10 MiB/s profile, 1720×1180 dark viewport, 8-second observation window, no CPU profiling, and 11 interleaved AB/BA pairs per route. Pre-measurement host idle was 94.86%. Every pair remains in its original group. Cold loads and a separately archived extra untimed seed are excluded from warm statistics.

Each selected seed has 21 messages and 69 nonempty history commands in both slots. All 12 captured non-lane top-level fields have equal UTF-8 byte lengths between slots; equal lengths do not prove content identity. The same Gateway fixture/profile is used. Positive candidate title/thumbnail qualification precedes measurement. The fixture's native visible window has one ticketed/managed image and a session title; the literal PR anchor does not exercise decorated PR metadata, assistant portraits are offscreen, and no notice divider or second separately cacheable image is visible. Earlier accepted extended-fixture results and the current extended smoke test remain separate coverage; the native confirmation does not claim all four branches are visually requalified.

All 48 formal and all 48 sampler-off app/main boundaries were inspected from original compositor PNGs, adjacent predecessors and complete captured state sequences, then imported through the canonical offline audit path. Negative-time old-page frame zero is excluded. These establish captured boundaries, not every display vsync. ElementTiming and actual inspected PNG times are reported separately. LCP belongs to the code block in this fixture, not the attached image. Later highlighting, reactions, sidebar, Details/widget and reconnect changes remain outside the four-fact census. Thread height is already stable on pinned main after the geometry work.

| Chat LoAF group | First slot median [Q1–Q3] | Second slot median [Q1–Q3] | Paired median Δ | Lower / higher pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Formal baseline/candidate, sampler ON/ON | 171.9 [169.1–182.95] | 196.6 [186.95–207.25] | +16.8 ms | 2 / 9 |
| Identical baseline, sampler OFF/OFF | 173.0 [154.25–185.4] | 171.4 [162.8–173.0] | −1.6 ms | 6 / 5 |
| Identical candidate, sampler ON/OFF | 201.0 [192.9–209.05] | 193.7 [179.5–200.85] | −14.2 ms | 9 / 2 |
| Baseline/candidate, sampler OFF/OFF | 175.5 [160.4–180.35] | 192.4 [176.8–198.35] | +28.2 ms | 4 / 7 |

The identical-candidate factor control demonstrates an observer effect, but no identical-baseline ON/OFF factor group isolates the full interaction. The OFF/OFF application comparison overlaps and has mixed pair signs, so it does not establish a LoAF regression under the latest rule; its adverse-direction estimate also does not prove absence of application cost. Actual inspected first-main paint in OFF/chat is additionally adverse by separated IQRs: 419.36 [402.78–433.77] → 442.10 [436.11–453.72] ms, paired +28.54 ms, 7/11 higher. This remains separate from the formal comparison and ElementTiming.

All 132 warm LoAF scalar totals equal the sum of exported raw frame blocking within floating precision; no observed frame/script begins after exact stop. Early IDB-attributed work maps in both exact served-bundle source maps to `ui/src/lib/chat/control-ui-database.runtime.ts:25`, the transaction-completion promise listener. Its formal chat paired duration rises +15.9 ms in 11/11 pairs; attribution includes promise continuations, so this does not identify storage itself as the cost. Unknown-source animation callbacks also grow (paired duration +24.6 ms, including +21.3 ms forced style/layout); their blank source URL prevents exact function attribution. These are script durations, not exclusive LoAF costs, and cannot be subtracted from blocking. The remaining fact observer stays active even with the animation sampler OFF. The application-versus-observer cost is unresolved, so the declared formal adverse result is retained.

## Snapshot growth and separate byte footprint

| Selected session | Snapshot JSON before → after | JSON growth | Separate retained thumbnail bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat | 53,482 → 54,006 B | +524 B / +0.980% | 1 / 204 B |
| Dashboard | 55,863 → 56,399 B | +536 B / +0.959% | 1 / 204 B |

Both JSON increases meet the 5% cap. JSON plus the separately counted Blob payload grows by 728 B / 1.355% on chat and 740 B / 1.319% on dashboard. This is logical record/payload size, not physical IndexedDB allocation, avatar cache size or browser HTTP cache. Global byte footprint equals the selected session in this isolated fixture. The earlier extended fixture had two retained thumbnails totaling 177,520 B; that is a different fixture/head and is not substituted for this native seed.

## Validation

Final-head focused and native proof passed: 30 focused unit files; five Chromium files / 57 tests; six native files / 25 tests; extended-fixture smoke; both full/chat UI-e2e type configurations; UI/scripts/core-test types; controller, formatting, parity, targeted lint; both production UI builds and asset comparison. The real session-link regression uses the actual unadvertised resolver catalog: five assertions fail on the pre-fix production path and all 27 pass after repair, with live client/phase/scope/permission checks retained.

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times on this lease: cached-image 4.588 s; snapshot-write 4.352 s; session-link titling 4.597 s; native media-files 29.513 s; uploaded-image recovery 25.260 s; session-link reconnect 25.677 s; Team-scale 28.770 s; warm boot 47.028 s; optional requests 25.358 s. The 30-file focused invocation took 64.732 s.

The aggregate changed gate remains red: three unused-export findings reproduce on pinned main, and core lint exits 137 on both candidate and pinned main (main control wall 393.797 s). The same export names are `formatRestartRecoveryAdmission` in `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-presentation.ts` and `classifySqliteWorkerExecute` / `sqliteWorkerRequestClasses` in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-request-class.ts`. There is no OOM diagnostic; no cause is invented. No baseline/expected-failure exceptions are added. Earlier pasted-text/theme full-UI failures pass on both current pinned main and candidate; the QA automation file still has baseline failures. The final full UI suite was deliberately interrupted after the performance stop decision (36m32s in that phase; 299 file-result lines at the cancellation checkpoint). It is incomplete and supplies no full-suite pass. The observed failure was `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.prompt-attachments.e2e.test.ts`: the first-prompt growth/identity geometry case. Its planned pinned-main classification did not run before cancellation, so it remains unclassified; it is not labeled inherited. Partial logs and the earlier completed focused/native/main-control receipts are preserved.

Detached canonical autoreview of the exact final head is clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. This static review does not override runtime/performance gates. Exact-head CI recorded 13 successful, 79 skipped and one failed PR-context check after the report edit. The context check required a literal authored Evidence heading; that report heading has been corrected. The broad ready-PR gate has not run, and skipped checks are not called a pass. The closed experiment is not reopened or rerun to chase green. The inherited test-lines ratchet must be reported if encountered; its baseline is never edited.

## Prior accepted qualification

Before compression, head `54ce4726e255cc8dd6eb1e8b8f9bbc67b812df33` against main `200f33bdb28712f25994b4134267515834903d81` on AWS `cbx_f42a46dd2a88` measured complete cached links/images/notices/avatars with first rows, zero later fact changes and zero height change in 11/11 warm reloads on both routes. Chat first rows were 572 → 504 ms (−68 ms); dashboard 512 → 452 ms (−60 ms). The extended fixture included ticketed plus cacheable images, decorated PR metadata, a notice divider and visible avatars. Those accepted results are retained as prior-head evidence, not final-head proof.

## Accepted tradeoff

The maintainer explicitly accepts dashboard FCP rising from 184 to 192 ms (+8 ms) as a sub-perceptual tradeoff for complete cached rows and earlier first rows. The original result had non-overlapping IQRs: 184 [182–184] → 192 [188–192], with a paired median of +4 ms.

Same-code A/A had a paired median of 0 ms, overlapping IQRs, and mixed signs. Reversed candidate-first B/A retained 184 [184–184] → 192 [188–192], with a paired median of +8 ms and separated IQRs. Repeated A/B measured 184 [184–188] → 188 [188–192], with a paired median of +4 ms (9 worse / 1 better / 1 tied). Results remain separate, without pooling or A/A subtraction. Complete first-row facts and zero subsequent fact/height changes remained 11/11 in both candidate control groups.

This is an accepted measured tradeoff; the FCP increase is not classified as noise. No function-level cause or inherent Blob-decoding cost is claimed.

### Dashboard FCP controls on the same instance

All groups use 11 interleaved pairs on the original AWS c7a.4xlarge lease, with unchanged candidate and baseline heads. A/A uses baseline in both physical slots. B/A places the candidate first; its reported deltas are still candidate minus baseline. A/B repeats the original physical order. A/A shares the first native app-written, live-DOM-qualified baseline snapshot between both identical-code slots; B/A remaps the existing strict candidate snapshot qualifier to physical slot zero. The qualifier body is unchanged. A/A controls reload-slot/order effects for the same build ID and asset URLs; it does not independently isolate distinct-build switching overhead. B/A and canonical A/B cover that distinction. The copies were removed before focused native replays. Controls are reported separately, without subtraction or pooling.

prs.title: fix(discord): cancelled deliveries keep sending text, media and voice
prs.body:
Closes #184060

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord text, media and voice sends keep going after a delivery is cancelled, because the abort signal never reaches the Discord client.

## User Impact

User impact: a cancelled or timed-out outbound delivery now stops sending further Discord requests, instead of continuing in the background.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord client and retry path already honor an abort signal. The adapter dropped `ctx.signal` when it built send options, and `DiscordSendOpts` omitted `signal` by type. The signal now goes through the shared send context (text, media, voice) into that existing path. No new abort logic.

Not covered: polls. `ChannelPollContext` has no signal, so a fix needs a core contract change. Left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

- New test in `outbound-adapter.test.ts`: red on base, green with the fix.
- `outbound-adapter.test.ts`: 29 passed. `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` clean.
- `check:changed`: lint and format pass. Two checks did not run locally: the SQLite worker ratchet (needs `rg`, not installed) and the dead-export scan. This change does not touch either area.
- Gap: no live Discord e2e run.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Current author head: `b61e37141b7760e0933aedd671d9ee9f73a78b55`. The latest ordinary merge consumes official main `6f04e7abd6c645c3c030663e7fd369834998d8ac`, including the adopted native-touch timing repair #178645. The earlier ordinary merge at `230fee6b` consumed the official cached-title repairs #178510 and #178474 from `79262d05`. The existing feature patch is preserved. Validation below attributed to `688e9537` or `230fee6b` remains prior-head evidence; current integration checks and CI are recorded at the end.

- Removed the vacuous channel-route test and duplicated mocked direct-Wiki allow/deny cases requested by review. The real-owner Wiki suite and owner-backed retrieval/denial proof remain.
- Fixed the actual `no-shadow` lint failure by reusing the existing anchor constant.
- Kept main's current session-send input parsing, target checks and authorization owner; removed two unnecessary extracted helpers. The proposal's send delta is now the propagation of existing scoped access into `runWithScopedSessionAccess`.
- Local focused authority validation: 43 tests passed. A follow-up covering Wiki and session-send siblings passed 94 tests; it resolves the temporary test-spy import failure from removing the duplicate cases.
- Core typecheck, touched-file type-aware core/extension-test lint, format, config baseline generation/check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the complete candidate found no actionable P0-P2 defect. Product acceptance remains pending.
- [Exact-head CI run 39419691631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39419691631), candidate `688e953733d74df955d692de1892f4711c76ebcc`: the previous UI boot-budget and all five core-lint lanes pass. The remaining failed [mocked-Gateway cold-load case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39419691631/job/118617967183) is the same intermittent failure already recorded on official main `6a2e9a1f9ea002b14e2847e8ca89e2b90c37f59d`, [run 39401671859 / job 118557975798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39401671859/job/118557975798): `expected 'New session' to be 'Synthetic cold-load conversation'` in `chat-cold-load-anchor.e2e.test.ts`.
- The green CI on the integrated base `d53309cd8ea4d0761fec3ac81ae73290b81e569a` ([39417964143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39417964143)) **skipped UI E2E**, so it is not a passing control for this case. A later full main run [39415536071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39415536071) passed the mocked UI shards, consistent with an intermittent failure; the branch is not being rerun or changed merely to chase green.
- This candidate changes no UI files. Between the earlier main failure and the integrated base, the inspected chat-pane changes belong to informed persistent-stream approval #177941, not cached-title ownership; the cold-load test and transcript snapshot owner are unchanged. A local pinned-main replay reached a different, earlier `Worked for 3 minutes` wait timeout; that local result is **not** presented as reproduction of the CI cached-title assertion.
- The known main CI failure follows CONTRIBUTING's existing-main-failure policy: no unrelated test-only repair, assertion weakening, budget increase, or duplicate CI-fix PR is added here. The remaining CI acceptance is a maintainer decision, not a claim of green CI. Final exact-head readback: run 39419691631 completed. All three PostgreSQL shards and the other product/static/test jobs succeeded; the only failed leaf is the known-main cached-title case above, plus its dependent aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. No new or unclassified failed leaf remains. This is contributor-complete with an inherited intermittent CI failure, not all-green CI.

## Real behavior proof

The existing isolated published-stable upgrade proof remains valid for the unchanged native-memory path: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 persisted SQLite -> candidate offline Doctor/source Gateway with the real native memory worker. It proves same-channel retrieval, exclusion of other channels/accounts/workspaces/providers/agents, denied sibling mutations, and route reassignment denial without external APIs or live Slack.

The newly added direct Wiki proof covers the previously missing consumer boundary through the production query adapter and real Gateway disclosure owner. It uses synthetic search input; it is not a live external-provider or customer-data proof.

## Evidence boundaries and remaining work

Not claimed: the public packaged updater/install path as a whole, live Slack/customer traffic, external model calls, cross-OS behavior, or broad benchmarks. The prior reviewed head has successful hosted CI; current-head CI is tracked below. Current 47-file canonical autoreview and focused integration checks are complete. Maintainer acceptance of the retrieval-only channel config/SDK contract remains a separate product decision. No production runtime or account configuration was changed.

### Adopted official cached-title repair and current integration

The title repair is adopted upstream through #178510 (`58c3f35e0e1894bc837871e5ca58b47be78031f2`) and #178474 (`fe739f62fcfa1f91dfaa25f7a710292da190822c`). Duplicate #178478 is closed and #178470 is resolved. This branch consumes those official main commits; it adds no separate UI patch.

The feature patch-id is unchanged across this merge. All 46 non-baseline feature files retain their exact contents; the baseline keeps the same one-row deletion against main. 43 focused integration tests passed; applicable prior canonical review and real-owner proof are retained. On the same official UI sources, the original synthetic cached-tail Chromium case passed with en-US/CPU4 (6.831 s case, 21.85 s wrapper), retaining the official pending-hydration/first-title assertions and the original title/scroll checks. Local diagnostic setup was restored exactly after testing. No assertions, timeout, CI routing or runtime configuration were changed by this contribution.

**Previous integration CI (`230fee6b`):** [39469559363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39469559363) completed **FAILURE** on `230fee6b17bc5fa24706b349f02268237feec8c9`: all 111 jobs terminal, 85 successful / 24 skipped / one failed UI leaf and its dependent `openclaw/ci-gate`. The remaining [UI 2/8 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39469559363/job/118790829856) is `chat-widget-scroll.e2e.test.ts`, “keeps touch flings continuous through widgets and preserves the reader during streaming”: 257 px total travel did not exceed the existing 260 px assertion. This mock-Gateway scenario has no demonstrated changed feature path. That source equivalence does not establish an exact matching main-CI failure or prove a timing root cause.

Two bounded, unchanged official-base replays used the canonical UI E2E wrapper, Node 24.19.0, and normal Chromium mobile touch emulation, without CPU throttling. Neither reproduced 257 > 260: both passed the preceding fling assertions and failed later at the “Scroll to latest” button wait (line 264, 10 s). ### Native touch-fling CI diagnosis

The uncontrolled input-velocity defect is now established by a measured paired experiment and has an existing maintainer-owned repair in #178645. The same 120 ms pause immediately before widget release makes the original fixture produce 235 px total travel / zero inertia and fail its unchanged 260 px assertion. With that PR's explicit input timestamps, the same actual pause produces 475 px total / 240 px inertia. Both begin with 1,430 px of available scroll, ruling out a range clamp for this paired failure. A complete canonical en-US replay also passed, including upward fling and reader preservation during streaming. Measurements, clock distinctions, full-case limitations, and cleanup are [published on the existing repair PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178645#issuecomment-6298363342).

This proves the failure mechanism and the repair, not the unrecoverable input timing of the historical 257 px sample. #178645 completed full [CI 39474657403](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39474657403): 28 successful / 28 skipped / 0 failed; all nine mocked UI shards, both real-Gateway shards, and the final CI gate passed. The current integration retains all 47 feature files, with 44 exact prior feature blobs. The other three changes are official mock-baseline shrinkage, canonical generated configuration hashes, and the official test-only normalization-helper migration. The generated hash conflict was resolved by the canonical generator and its check. prs.title: fix(team-reports): bound API response bodies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Team Reports can buffer an unbounded GitHub or Discord API response during collection, causing a memory spike even though request timeouts already exist.

## User Impact

Responses above the existing SDK's 16 MiB ceiling now stop with an explicit compatibility warning; Discord does not retry an oversized response. Ordinary parsing, pagination, rate-limit waits, and transient retry behavior are preserved.

**Unresolved compatibility decision:** a legitimate API page above 16 MiB that previously succeeded will now fail collection or produce an incomplete report. The Team Reports owner still needs to accept that tradeoff or settle the ceiling using representative large-collection measurements, as requested in the [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145765#issuecomment-5644488969). No owner acceptance or representative production measurements are claimed here. Synthetic large responses, the earlier small public responses, and documented item-count pagination limits do not establish that 16 MiB is safe for large organizations or GitHub Enterprise Server.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both source clients use the existing Plugin SDK bounded response reader through one plugin-local helper. The reader owns byte/idle bounds and overflow cancellation; client finally blocks still release guarded responses. GitHub preserves an actionable source warning, and Discord immediately returns deterministic oversized-response errors.

This update resolves the current-main import conflict in sources/http.ts while retaining main's abortable sleep and long-timer changes. The original six-file response-bound delta is unchanged (+123/-8 overall, +38 production lines). There are no new configuration options, schema changes, or pagination changes.

## Evidence

Candidate: `4054a59df7ea4b82f437bcab51655d3f28e6646a`, based on canonical main `b006608299d8adcbf09b383a283e3fba90a60c7d`.

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test:extension team-reports`: 272 tests passed across 19 files; 95.8 s command wall time (93.21 s Vitest duration).
- Focused GitHub/Discord source and transport selection: 56 tests passed across four files in 11.49 s wall time. The changed GitHub transport test file used 64 ms test time; the Discord file used 49 ms. Stream tests verify cancellation and guarded release.
- Native HTTPS transport proof used the actual production clients with `globalThis.fetch`, an isolated localhost peer, an ephemeral certificate, and synthetic data only. No fetch or Response mock, external API, or user credential was used. Eight cases passed on the candidate (4.31 s command wall time) and on the main control (3.66 s).
  - The peer sent valid JSON padded to 18 MiB. Main consumed all 18,874,368 bytes and returned successfully through both clients. The candidate rejected with the source-specific 16 MiB error; both peer connections closed after 16,908,288 bytes written, before the complete body, with exactly one request per client. Peer-written bytes include transport buffering and are not a claim about retained memory.
  - Ordinary `[]` and exactly 16,777,216-byte valid JSON controls succeeded through both clients on both revisions.
  - Caller-abort controls cancelled both native-fetch requests and closed the peer; no extra request was made.
  - This proves bounded transport behavior and the changed compatibility boundary, not representative collection-size safety. The temporary proof file and certificate are not in the patch.
- Focused formatter, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Repository-native autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects and preserved the unresolved owner decision.
- Scoped TypeScript check of the six touched files and their transitive imports passed with the repository compiler (54.49 s wall time). This is not the broad extension typecheck.
- Previous-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680788685) passed for `594dd2e8f0ce3adc6f291405c6aed87db9a96ef5`; that is historical evidence only. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37100959323) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed for `4054a59df7ea4b82f437bcab51655d3f28e6646a`. All 65 CI jobs completed successfully or were intentionally skipped. The `checks-node-changed` job took 123 s and `checks-node-changed-extensions-config` took 108 s including setup; these are job wall times, not per-file test timings.

Authenticated large-source collection, full local build, full aggregate check, and the unfiltered repository test suite were not run. Owner acceptance of the fixed ceiling remains required before merge.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

## Evidence

Current head: `95d83ad28f203ee6ec15ad60f69c06060a7235a5`. Exact-head [CI39994486818](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39994486818) **passed**: 75 jobs (47 success, 28 skipped), no failures or pending jobs.

- **160 distinct relevant tests passed cumulatively**: 128 PDF/provider/sibling/config tests, 26 official subagent-fixture tests and 6 new authority controls. The final-effect follow-up's affected suite is 48/48 (6 authority, 13 opt-in, 29 existing PDF), a subset of that total. Full/runtime builds, affected production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, SDK exports, schema/docs and formal extension/core graph boundaries pass. Independent full-candidate, credential-handoff and final-effect reviews found no actionable P0/P1 defect.
- **Authority red/green:** before the fence, each of four retired-owner cases sent one synthetic HTTP request. After it, operator and physical-credential retirement after provider or DNS awaits each require reached-injection, the correct owner failure, HTTP0 and no completion fallback. Allowed and nearest-forbidden controls also pass. Provider cases use the real bundled callback; DNS cases use the real guarded-fetch lookup seam. These are authority-owner tests, not live credential rotation.
- **Published stable 2026.10.6 saved-config upgrade:** verified official artifact integrity, authored ordered settings with the published CLI, then validated and edited the same isolated saved state with the built candidate CLI. Ordering and limits are preserved, absent remains absent and explicit false remains false. This is configuration compatibility proof.
- **Earlier real OpenAI API proof:** the actual PDF tool/prepared provider/extractor, using synthetic documents only, returned HTTP200 and expected results for native input and four extraction cases (unset, selected page, password/encrypted, configured text-only). An initial HTTP401 exposed the scoped sentinel-handoff error; the corrected native request returned HTTP200, native=true and expected values. Its successful result was reconciled without replay after a harness-only model-label assertion correction. This proof is bound to preceding implementation head `ac5c3699`; the relevant native transport/payload owners remain unchanged. It is separate from the real Gateway proof below.

### Real isolated Gateway, normal agent route

The built official CLI and GatewayClient used real pinned WSS admission, `health` RPC, one durable synthetic profile, normal `agent`/same-run `agent.wait`, `deliver: false`, and actual `users.setRole` plus effective-role readback. The planner model remained allowed while the nearest negative excluded only the PDF model. PDF model/fallback selection was fixed explicitly.

The Gateway ran the actual run-owned PDF tool. Its planner/PDF HTTP used a synthetic loopback sink through the existing runtime-dependency seam, retaining real DNS/Agent/pinned dispatcher and the final synchronous HTTP authority check. Body/auth inspection was in memory only.

| Condition | Planner HTTP | Native PDF HTTP | Extraction PDF HTTP | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Allowed | 2 | 1 | 0 | Expected actual PDF tool result; pinned dispatcher observed |
| Same-profile/scopes, PDF model denied | 2 | 0 | 0 | Actual model refusal while planner remained usable |
| Role retired while PDF input held | 1 | 0 | 0 | Official owner change; original run ended/error and active root work returned 1 → 0 after release before HTTP0 was recorded |
| `pages: "2"` | 2 | 0 | 1 | Selected-page BETA present; excluded-page ALPHA absent |

All four submissions occurred once, and the original runs reached terminal state with backend work settled. The held-input Gateway retirement proves actual operator wiring; precise provider/DNS timing is covered separately by the focused red/green tests above.

The seven planner requests and seven other intercepted requests are counted separately. The latter remain unclassified and are not treated as PDF/fallback proof; there is no all-process external-egress claim. Gateway runtime build `4b0f4c12` was exercised from test-only source head `7c7816f3`, with explicit runtime-owner bindings to this head. The build is not relabeled as a build of the later merge commit. No production service, employee role, customer document or real channel delivery was used. All task-owned Gateway/driver processes and temporary credential/config/profile/TLS/log state, including failed attempts, have been removed.

## CI and Review Follow-through

Earlier CI found the generated config baseline and an inherited subagent fixture problem. Later official main changed that fixture's completion contract, so the borrowed adjustment was retired in favor of the exact official fixture files and its negative assertion. An authority test's private-extension import was also replaced with the existing public bundled-provider facade; both formal boundaries pass. These repairs add no PDF production behavior.

Previous implementation CI [39968310938](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39968310938) and authority CI [39986691358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39986691358) passed at their respective heads. A final true conflict against official main `53fb615a` was limited to the generated configuration hash. This branch normally merges that fixed main and resolves the hash with the official generator. Independent blob review preserves the feature/authority/Gateway owners; the only tracked help-file change comes from official main. Current-head CI is reported above separately from preceding evidence.

prs.title: fix(codex): duplicate final reply after a resumed parent waits for a native child
prs.body:
## Status: blocked on correctness, not ready to merge

[Follow-up investigation and failing owner-boundary regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186128#issuecomment-6458850513). The current head can falsely settle an unconsumed result. Neither turn completion nor proxy-observed provider completion proves native sampling completion. The new local regression reports 28 passed / 1 failed; it simulates the native schedule, not an end-to-end native reproduction. No production repair has been pushed, and the hosted test-line ratchet remains red.

The proposed direction is to expose native sampling completion after resume and consume that signal in the existing receipt owner. The original implementation description and historical evidence below are preserved for review, not a recommendation to merge. In particular, the earlier turn-completion composition advice is superseded by this finding.

---

Related: #156070

## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, a Codex parent can receive a native child's result through `wait_agent` and answer it. A separate automatic `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run then gives the same answer again.

## User Impact

On providers that native Codex treats as OpenAI (OpenAI API key and Codex/ChatGPT login), a resumed conversation that waits for a native child and answers it in a turn that completes normally no longer gets a second automatic answer for that result. In the tested yield/unconsumed scenarios, results the parent did not sample are still delivered automatically. No configuration change or migration is needed.

**Known correctness limitation:** a native compaction-setup failure after a preempted or mailbox-failed request can cause a result to be marked consumed without a completed sampling. The detailed condition is below; this edge has not been reproduced end to end.

Not changed, so an extra reply can still happen (nothing is dropped in these cases):

- **Other provider names.** Native removes the per-item metadata this fix reads unless the provider is named exactly `OpenAI`. That covers OpenClaw's subscription-sharing route and custom Responses providers. Routes that do not use the inference proxy are not covered either.
- **WebSocket incremental requests.** On the covered routes native can use WebSocket `response.create`, which sends only new input. If the parent makes another model request in the same turn after the one that carried the result, that later request no longer carries it and the result stays pending. The end-to-end runs below used HTTP.
- **Uncertain samplings.** The result stays pending if the parent's turn fails or is interrupted, or if a later model request in the turn no longer carries the result. It also stays pending if context compaction or a hook other than `Stop` runs after the request that carried it, or if the foreground owner is released or yields before native reports the turn completed.

"Consumed" here means native completed a parent sampling that carried the result. That is neither a durable native acknowledgement nor channel delivery. Recovering a pending child result across Gateway replacement is not tested.

The native contract below was checked against the managed Codex 0.164.0. Older or newer external app-server overrides were not validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex streams raw item events only to threads started with `experimentalRawEvents`, and `thread/resume` has no such option. V2 `wait` items carry no receiver status, and after resume the alternative raw envelope events are also absent, so OpenClaw records no receipt and the completion owner delivers the already-consumed result again.

#130503 tried to fix this on the native side by renewing the raw-event opt-in on resume. It was withdrawn to keep completion handling in OpenClaw without a Codex protocol change, and Codex 0.164.0 still has no resume opt-in. This change stays in OpenClaw. #166349 tracks the broader parent-wake and restart semantics; this PR fixes only the duplicate.

The receipt still reaches OpenClaw: native sends the child's `FINAL_ANSWER` envelope as current-turn input in the parent's next model request, which the plugin already authorizes. The parent's receipt tracker holds the receipts carried by the turn's latest ordinary model request, and hands them to the existing tracker when native reports that turn `completed`, unless compaction or a non-`Stop` hook ran in between.

<details><summary>Settlement rules and native contract</summary>

Resumed threads get no per-sampling completion notification (`rawResponse/completed` is a raw event). `thread/tokenUsage/updated` is also emitted after a context-window error, on rate-limit headers and around compaction, so it does not prove that a sampling succeeded. The change therefore uses this evidence:

1. The parent's receipt tracker holds only the receipts carried by the parent turn's **latest** model request. Each later request replaces them. A request that is not an ordinary sampling, such as compaction or review, carries none.
2. Native `contextCompaction` items, and `hook/started` for any hook other than `Stop`, discard what is held for that turn. These are how native can complete a turn without another sampling after a preempted or interrupted stream: a hook that blocks steered input, or a session-start hook after compaction. `Stop` hooks run only after a final sampling completed.
3. When native reports that same turn `completed`, the held receipts go to the existing tracker. This happens behind the existing owner gate (bound, not yielded, not settled) and before the turn observer marks the owner's model execution settled.

Native's contract, as checked in source: a turn is `completed` when no turn-affecting error was recorded. Retries rebuild the prompt from the current recorded history. Same-turn preemption can drop a streaming request and continue the turn. Compaction or a token-budget rollover can then remove `FINAL_ANSWER` items before the next sampling. A blocking input hook can also end the loop without another sampling. Capture always precedes forwarding, so it is ordered before the turn's completion.

One native path is not covered: if setting up a mid-turn compaction fails before the compaction task starts, native reports the turn `completed` with neither a `contextCompaction` item nor an error. A result could be marked consumed only if, in the same step, the request carrying it was also preempted or hit a mailbox stream error and a compaction was due. The underlying `completed` status there looks like a native status issue. This remains an unresolved correctness limitation for maintainer consideration, not a demonstrated no-drop guarantee.

Held receipts are foreground-only. They are discarded when an owner releases its turn, when the last owner releases, and when a parent retires or the monitor is disposed. Matching, alias, predecessor/successor and custody state stay in the existing tracker. Fresh threads keep their raw-event receipts unchanged.

Checked in openai/codex rust-v0.164.0:

- `ThreadResumeParams` has no raw-event option. The resumed listener is attached with raw events disabled (`app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`). `rawResponseItem/completed` and `rawResponse/completed` are dropped for listeners without the opt-in (`app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs`).
- `handle_turn_complete` reports `Failed` only when a turn-affecting error was recorded, otherwise `Completed`; aborts report `Interrupted` (`app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs`).
- Sampling retries rebuild from recorded history. Preemption and mailbox stream errors return a follow-up without `response.completed`. Mid-turn compaction or rollover can run before the next sampling, and a blocking input hook can end the loop (`core/src/session/turn.rs`). Remote compaction excludes `FINAL_ANSWER` items (`core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs`). Compaction tasks emit a `contextCompaction` item (`compact.rs`, `compact_remote_v2*.rs`, `compact_token_budget.rs`).
- Token-count notifications are also emitted after `ContextWindowExceeded`, on rate-limit events and during compaction (`core/src/session/turn.rs`, `compact*.rs`).
- Non-OpenAI providers have `internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough` cleared before the request is sent (`core/src/client.rs`, `model-provider-info/src/lib.rs`).
- Hook notifications are emitted for synchronous, non-built-in hooks (`core/src/hook_runtime.rs`).
</details>

**Composition with #149490** (open; rewrites the same tracker): #149490 holds raw receipts until a later non-compaction `rawResponse/completed`. That is a raw event, so it does not fire on resumed threads. If both land, the input receipts held here should keep settling on `turn/completed` and should not be routed through #149490's "wait for a later response" gate, which never fires after the turn ends. The two changes touch overlapping lines in `native-subagent-delivery-receipts.ts` and the monitor wiring, so whichever lands second needs a manual merge.

## Evidence

[Inspectable original-head terminal results and test boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186128#issuecomment-6448741684), including the restart/wait case, unconsumed-result control and failing baseline. These are retained runs, not proof of a later repair.

The reproduction and test results below come from the prepared source-build investigation. The publication review inspected the retained logs and exact patch, but did not rerun those tests.

Base `ba1828c8fb5554b752e11cdba0306fa2d1d4c634` (`main`), head `d7ca03a8938a66809aa7334a67daa2c273b7c7d7`; native Codex 0.164.0 from the lockfile. The change was first developed on `89bc6de`; none of its nine files changed between the two bases, and the commit is patch-identical.

**Freshness check (2026-10-27).** Upstream main had advanced to `5cf6a7fd4ebaebb9f1fee12a1d33f2ab291e3f86`; all nine patch-target files have identical Git blob IDs to the tested base `ba1828c8`. This is a source-drift check, not a rerun of tests on that newer main. #156070 remains open; #149490 remains open and unmerged at `9d4bc16a`.

**Real Gateway scenarios** (isolated state, real native app-server with V2 multi-agent, scripted loopback Responses provider over HTTP, synthetic credentials, provider named `OpenAI`). The steps follow the issue: an ordinary turn, then a real Gateway restart. The parent spawns a child, calls `wait_agent` and answers. After an ordinary turn, a fresh request re-tasks the same child and waits again.

| Scenario | Base | This change |
|---|---|---|
| Restart, parent consumes the result via `wait_agent` | **Fails**: the parent answers, then a separate `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run answers again (every base run) | Passes: one answer per result, no automatic run, same child reused, session idle |
| Restart, parent yields instead (result never sampled) | — | Result delivered automatically exactly once |
| Restart, terminal provider error on the request carrying the result (turn fails) | — | Result stays pending and is delivered once; one answer |
| Restart, one-shot provider 503 on that request (native retries) | — | One answer, no automatic run |
| Restart, one-shot OpenClaw request-preparation failure on that request | — | One answer, no automatic run |
| No restart (fresh thread) | — | One answer per result, no automatic run |

The first row was rerun on both the base and head above; the second row was rerun on the head only. The other rows ran with the same patch on the earlier base `89bc6de`.

The preemption, compaction and hook-stop paths could not be driven by a scripted provider alone; they are covered by the owner-boundary tests below.

**Tests**

- `native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts` (owning monitor boundary, real tracker and delivery owner):
  - With the production change reverted, 5 cases fail: the duplicate (with and without a following `Stop` hook), both reused-child cases, and the release-lifetime case.
  - Against the previous revision of this change, 4 cases fail: a later request without the result, compaction after it, a non-`Stop` hook after it, and held evidence surviving release.
  - With this change, all 28 pass. The remaining new cases keep failed, interrupted and earlier-turn results pending.
- `inference-routing.test.ts`: only ordinary `/responses` turn input is offered for receipt capture. All 49 pass; with the production change reverted, that case fails.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 12 s and 11 s wall when warm (46 s and 23 s on a cold transform cache, over 80% transform). Each file runs under 2 s of test time. The 11 new monitor cases total 18 ms, and the 2 routing cases 2 ms.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` (438 files): 5,319 passed, 17 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `transport-startup.test.ts` (`ProcessInspectionError`, from the local sandbox's process-inspection permission) and fail identically on base.
- `pnpm check:changed` against the base: 31 of 32 lanes pass, including extension and extension-test typecheck, changed-file lint and format, and the line-cap and other ratchets. The dead-export scan is red with 20 entries that are identical on base, none in the changed files. `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` reports 14 entries, also identical on base and none in the changed files. The monitor shrinks by 2 lines.
- The change does not alter provider request bytes; `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes.
- Local review: canonical autoreview was not run in the preparation lane because model-service access was outside that lane's authorization; only its P0–P2 dry run succeeded. No completed canonical-autoreview result is claimed for this submission.
- Actual review evidence: independent Astra and Opus AI source reviews examined the r2 patch/tree on base `89bc6de4583cb2b3fd70a6bb52dd1a5e1db202c9`, supplied head `42a1336656637c2df8829ce3d69ac1af8af665b6`. Both returned **approve-with-changes**, with no P0/P1 findings; required P2 scope disclosures (native version and WebSocket efficacy) are included above. The reviewed patch and final submission have the same stable patch ID, `4a7dea7442e030a81a3aaf94f634c156c9c7b1d6`. A separate native Codex handoff review inspected the exact final patch (`ba1828c8` → `d7ca03a8`) for correctness, ownership and loss paths and found no new actionable P0–P2 production-code finding; a separate evidence review checked retained logs and corrected count/scope wording. Those publishing-lane reviews did not rerun tests. The compaction-setup loss edge remains explicitly unresolved, not waived by these reviews.

Not covered: a real-native run of the preemption, compaction or hook-stop paths; WebSocket transport; external app-server versions other than 0.164.0; a pending child result surviving Gateway replacement; channel delivery. The reporter's `queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming` warning did not appear on the tested `main` snapshots, although the duplicate `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run did.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): reject altered local session cursors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local Claude session and transcript pagination accepts altered spellings of an OpenClaw-issued cursor, including appended junk, padding, and extra JSON fields.

## User Impact

Valid local continuation cursors still advance to the next page. Altered or non-emitted local cursors are rejected with the existing Anthropic error labels. Paired-node cursors remain bounded opaque strings and are forwarded unchanged across version-skewed nodes. No stored-data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic local offset codec delegates to the existing shared session-catalog paging owner, removing the permissive decoder instead of maintaining a second canonicalization policy.

The current conflict refresh keeps the shared cursor implementation and preserves main’s existing catalog and transcript tests. A focused parser regression covers both error labels and canonical cursor validation.

## Evidence

- Current head `a160b4d70285bb0cf116c7517bdfb5fbe574f453` is based on main `4420648c404`; CI is pending. Results below are historical proof for earlier heads, not runs on this revision.

Previously tested head: `34ee2b4e21fbe87e1ab63a453bfde21b18dafa72`.

### October 20 conflict-repair checks

- Catalog, transcript, and discovery-budget suites: **41/41 passed**, one worker, 95.4 seconds wall time; approximately 4.1 seconds of test execution. The split transcript file's two cases took 38 ms.
- Shared session-catalog SDK suite: **11/11 passed**, one worker.
- Negative control: restoring only the base decoder under the repaired tests makes exactly the catalog and transcript cursor-rejection cases fail because their promises resolve. The repaired source was then restored byte-for-byte.
- Targeted typecheck, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, all three plugin import-boundary checks, changed-file line cap, and `git diff --check` passed. Canonical lint also completed its package-boundary declaration preparation.
- The canonical assertion-safety shrink-only command was run; the only baseline change is the Anthropic parser row, 5 → 3.
- Fresh isolated repository autoreview was **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no findings. The published Git tree matches the reviewed candidate.
- The global max-lines guard failed identically on this candidate and the exact base, reporting existing suppressions in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`. These files are untouched; this is not reported as a passing gate.

### Retained real Gateway and CLI proof

The previously accepted shipped-entry-point proof ran at `d3ec47248aad31eec285e205fd22fbfae9681f66`, against an isolated on-disk two-session Claude catalog, using the built Gateway and `pnpm openclaw gateway call`:

- `sessions.catalog.list`: the first page returned the newer fixture session; its issued cursor returned the older session.
- `sessions.catalog.read`: the first page returned the two newest transcript items; its issued cursor returned the two older items without overlap.
- Appending `!`, appending `=`, and adding an extra JSON field were each rejected in both flows. Catalog responses contained host error `LOCAL_READ_FAILED`; transcript calls exited 1 with Gateway `INVALID_REQUEST` and `transcript cursor is invalid`.

That run exercised plugin registration, file discovery, Gateway handlers, authenticated WebSocket transport, and the CLI. Only synthetic data was used. Update checks, telemetry, and hosted model-catalog refresh were disabled; state and processes were cleaned up. Its supported memory-bounded `qaRuntime` build passed, including the bootstrap guard and 53 built-module/doctor-closure checks.

The proof parser was byte-identical to previous head `dd9577292229490d61f65a27c77f3790e062a94f`, whose [October 16 review accepted the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111252#issuecomment-5014746361). The current local codec functions and introduced production patch remain identical, but other main changes mean the entire parser blob is no longer identical. This is retained historical proof, not a claimed new Gateway run.

Prior validation also included 442 passing Anthropic tests across 31 files; the separate CLI-runtime Unix-socket fixture hit `listen EPERM`, leaving 35 tests skipped and a secondary teardown failure. That historical sweep was not a complete passing extension lane.

The full repository build/check/test aggregate and global extension typechecks were not rerun locally. Current-head CI is authoritative for the broader gates; the previous green run does not stand in for this head.

prs.title: fix(sessions): recover transcript rewrites from concurrent appends
prs.body:
Related to #184909

## What Problem This Solves

A transcript maintenance rewrite is planned from one transcript revision. When an accepted in-flight input (or another writer) appends while the rewrite prepares or publishes, the version check rejected the whole rewrite, so the retry that asked for it ended the turn with a local conflict (`Session transcript changed while preparing rewrite …`) instead of answering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteTranscriptEntriesInSessionManager` is the single owner for maintenance rewrites. On a rewrite revision conflict it now reloads the persisted revision and re-plans exactly once when the branch only gained entries (a concurrent append). Reset/compaction boundaries still reject, and in-memory session views keep the existing rejection because they cannot reread storage. Nothing is written when recovery is refused, so an older plan can never overwrite a newer user turn. The conflict classifier stays private to this owner so the architecture graph keeps no new edge.

## User Impact

A message accepted while a turn is running no longer turns into "Unable to finish this reply" when recovery rewrites the transcript. Both the accepted input and the repaired history survive; a real reset or compaction during a rewrite still fails closed. No schema, storage format, or configuration changes, so existing stores load unchanged.

## Evidence

Real runtime, shipped `SessionManager` (SQLite/WAL) + shipped rewrite owner, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Node 26.12.1.

**Concurrent accepted input.** Base `d43865a98` vs head `685f298ab`, same script (second manager appends "in-flight input" during preparation):

```
# base
REWRITE_OUTCOME: {"rejected":true,"message":"Session transcript changed before rewrite publication"}
BRANCH_CONTENTS: ["user:first","assistant:tail","user:in-flight input"]

# head
[session-recovery] transcript gained 1 appends during rewrite; re-planning once sessionKey=agent:main:evidence-184909
REWRITE_OUTCOME: {"changed":true,"rewrittenEntries":1}
BRANCH_CONTENTS: ["user:rewritten first","assistant:tail","user:in-flight input"]
IN_FLIGHT_INPUT_COPIES: 1
```

**Existing-data compatibility.** A populated 42-entry transcript created by the base build is reopened by the head build, rewritten, and recovered with the concurrent append:

```
CREATED_BY_BASE_ENTRIES: 42
# head, same store
LOADED_LEGACY_ENTRIES: 42
REWRITE_OUTCOME: {"changed":true,"rewrittenEntries":1}
FIRST_AND_LAST: ["user:rewritten legacy first","user:in-flight input"]
IN_FLIGHT_INPUT_COPIES: 1
TOTAL_AFTER: 43
```

**Regression matrix** (vitest, Node 26.12.1):

| Case | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| append before the rewrite prepares | conflict rejected | re-planned, both inputs kept |
| append before the rewrite publishes | conflict rejected | re-planned, both inputs kept |
| concurrent reset boundary | rejected | rejected (guard intact) |
| in-memory intervening write | rejected | rejected |
| stale suffix bytes / navigation change | rejected | rejected |

Suites run: `transcript-rewrite*.test.ts` (4 files, 26 tests), plus `thinking-replay-repair`, `server-endpoint-compaction`, `tool-result-truncation`, `session-actor-memory-metadata`, `session-manager-maintenance-async`, `session-manager-mutation-boundaries` — 128 tests green. `check-madge-import-cycles` 0 cycles, `check-test-lines-ratchet` 6,279,972 / 6,280,000, oxlint and oxfmt clean.

**Gateway turn (L4).** Isolated Gateway started from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts gateway`), real WS `chat.send`, scripted Anthropic-Messages endpoint that rejects the replayed thinking signature on the first request:

```
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=local api=anthropic-messages status=400 ... runId="t3-1" requestNumber=1
[agent/embedded] [session-recovery] Anthropic thinking stream error; retrying once without thinking blocks: sessionId=gateway-184909-trace3
[agent/embedded] [session-recovery] stripped thinking blocks after provider rejected replay: repaired=1 sessionKey=agent:main:trace3
```

That is the maintenance rewrite under test running inside a live Gateway turn (23:51:02.405 → 23:51:04.998, a 2.6 s window over an 802-entry transcript, on the same code path the PR recovers).

**Boundary:** the linked incident itself needs a slow or interrupted provider response plus a mid-turn accepted input, which this machine cannot hold stable long enough for a Gateway replay; the traces above are real runtime of the rewrite owner at the conflict boundary, not a Gateway turn replay.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep/git to trace the rewrite owner and its four callers, vitest to reproduce the conflict against a real SQLite transcript, and real Node scripts for the before/after and existing-data traces. The implementer understands the code: a rewrite may only publish against the revision it planned from, so recovery must reload that revision and re-plan before writing, and it must never rewrite across a reset or compaction boundary.

prs.title: feat(android): add Android Auto support with voice talk, navigation, media, and camera controls
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds native Android Auto support to the official OpenClaw Android companion app (`apps/android`).

### Key Features
- **CarAppService Integration**: Implemented `OpenClawCarAppService` and `OpenClawCarSession` using `androidx.car.app:app:1.7.0` (`IOT` category).
- **In-Car Screen (`OpenClawCarScreen`)**: Live gateway connection state and Push-to-Talk (PTT) action.
- **Audio Focus Management (`CarAudioController`)**: Uses `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_EXCLUSIVE` to pause car radio/music during voice interactions.
- **Vehicle Controls (`CarVehicleActionController` & `CarCommandHandler`)**:
