prs.title: fix(claude-cli): preserve completion context when queued inputs arrive
prs.body:
Related: #185746, #184098

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude-backed sessions can lose a child's completion context while the parent is busy, or record OpenClaw-supplied context as if the user typed it.

## User Impact

User impact: queued inputs retain their own origin and completion context, while inbound metadata and resume notes stay separate from human-authored text.

Forwarded inputs are marked synthetic in Claude's native history. Their canonical messages remain visible, but their prompt rows are omitted from Claude's fallback-history seed. Private context retains full producer fragments and can use more input tokens than the compact inline form. No configuration change or migration is required.

This does not repair historical transcripts, the remaining static-prompt/bootstrap resume drift, or the separate legacy display sanitizer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #185746 rather than repeating its absorbed fixes. The host forwards per-input provenance and private context through the existing injection contract; Claude associates that context with the queued input UUID, including hook reruns. Initial prompts and same-session completion catch-up use the same private-context boundary. Raw-process transports retain their existing inline path.

A shared provenance predicate replaces separate initial/queued classification, and caller-surface-only tool differences no longer change the native binding fingerprint. Existing canonical transcript and admission owners remain authoritative. #184098's assistant-answer ownership work is complementary and untouched.

## Evidence

**Current conflict repair, head `3b540c04491533e6fac5effbf0adceea05c91930`:** GitHub reported another scalar-baseline conflict while the previous candidate completed CI. Reconciled with main `50d56a527f344490e85173213a52db608f5aa2f6`; all 24 non-baseline PR patches remain identical.

The exact integrated test count and ceiling are **6,291,977**, with zero slack. Main contributes 6,291,653 lines against its 6,291,318 ceiling; this PR still contributes 324. The 659-line adjustment is 335 inherited lines plus 324 PR lines, with no extra allowance or removed coverage. Working-tree/staged ratchet checks and whitespace validation pass.

At **2026-10-28 00:31 UTC**, the full paginated inventory for prior head `f1f0b0f28453a54a9e71ff93376b58bb7f5b2a30` showed **137/137 completed check runs, no failures or pending checks**, and successful [CI gate, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40609202889). The [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40607669417/job/122551638219) also passed. The only subsequent conflict was the baseline scalar; no runtime or test behavior changed. **Current-head verification, 2026-10-28 00:51 UTC:** the complete paginated inventory contains **135/135 completed check runs, with no failures or pending checks**. The [CI gate, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611218665) are all successful. GitHub reports this exact head mergeable with a clean merge state; the PR remains open and unmerged.

The admission and worker-preparation suites passed after the initial integration: **211 tests across two files in 39.79 seconds**, one worker, using the current pinned Bun fork. Later integrations did not touch any non-baseline PR file. Earlier review and real-Claude evidence apply to the unchanged patch, not a claimed new live-model run. The initial conflict-repair head `43f2326` had passed the functional tests, build, lint, and type checks but its [test-line job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40605896214/job/122545848903) saw 229 lines of newer-main drift; that was corrected in the green `f1f0b0f` candidate.

**CI baseline reconciliation, head `30f978f216420381384a10d4b0e263aa8eb69909`:** all 134 check runs completed on prior head `01adeb5b5e1e61c363791e538b21f72f8a5fb31b`. Functional tests, build, lint, and type checks passed; only the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40539941713/job/122316965497) and its aggregate gate failed after CI merged a newer main. It counted 6,286,548 lines against the then-published 6,285,064 ceiling.

At that head, the branch was reconciled with main `0e38bda9526bdde3c4287a5163ddbb6b47c7fe98`. The only conflict was the scalar baseline. The exact integrated count is **6,286,283**, now the ceiling with **zero slack**; main itself has 6,285,959 test lines against its 6,285,587 ceiling, and this PR adds 324. Thus the 696-line adjustment comprises 372 inherited lines and 324 PR lines, not spare allowance. Both working-tree and staged ratchet checks pass. The admission and worker-preparation suites were rerun after integration: **211 tests across two files passed in 46.16 seconds**, using CI-pinned Bun and one worker. The existing PR source changes are preserved; no assertion, deadline, selection, or ratchet implementation changed. **Final hosted CI verification, 2026-10-27 17:14 UTC:** the complete paginated inventory contains **133/133 completed check runs, with no failures or pending checks** on this exact head. The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40548225201), dependency review, and security-sensitive review statuses are all successful. The [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40545566110/job/122336250065) passes, as do the functional, build, lint, and type checks. The PR remains open and unmerged.

**CI fixture follow-up, head `01adeb5b5e1e61c363791e538b21f72f8a5fb31b`:** the [startup shard now passes on hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537167966/job/122306442757) at the prior head `e4e34e8238e32df394b3de4dd409d5dc420f116d`: worker compilation completed in 39.6 seconds before test launch, then all 65 tests passed in 28.40 seconds (72.29-second wrapper invocation). The watchdog is unchanged.

That run also exposed a [CLI admission fixture failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537167966/job/122306442657): the negative runtime-build test replaced every subprocess with empty success, including the newly eager worker compiler. Artifact verification correctly rejected the missing output. The fixture now reuses the existing controlled worker compiler and only stubs the Vitest reader; the exact selection, runtime-build failure sentinel, and exit assertions remain intact. No production code changes in this follow-up.

- The exact Node reproduction failed before and passed after the fixture repair. The entire modified file passes **168 tests on CI-pinned Bun**, one worker, 16.09 seconds in Vitest / 17.07 seconds including the wrapper. The failing hosted group previously ran for 301.76 seconds; that is prior-head evidence, not the new fixture cost.
- Tooling TypeScript checking, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the exact-count ratchet pass. Independent Auto Review of this two-file follow-up against snapshot `5fb5ff7e31c964a9264773fc83d91aa04864add1` is **scoped-clean at P0**; it is not a P1/P2 review or independent test rerun.
- All 134 check runs for this head have now completed; the functional repair is green. The remaining baseline-only failure and its reconciliation are recorded above. No unchanged re-push, CI rerun, or merge was requested.

**CI startup follow-up, head `e4e34e8238e32df394b3de4dd409d5dc420f116d`:** the existing eager-worker preparation selector now includes `server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts`. Its required compiled workers are prepared before Vitest starts, rather than consuming the startup shard's 60-second no-output window. Test selection, the full compiler preset, artifact verification, cancellation, and the watchdog deadline remain unchanged. Excluded and unrelated Gateway selections stay lazy.

- Both direct-runner and project-runner regressions failed before the fix (workers absent at test launch) and pass afterward. **66 focused tests across three files passed**, including the existing watchdog, tamper-rejection, cancellation, and cleanup coverage; measured together in 30.80 seconds with one worker.
- A forced-cold run of the actual failing file through the project runner, using CI's pinned Bun fork and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`, passed **all 65 tests**. Compilation took 37.8 seconds **before** test launch; Vitest took 19.53 seconds and the invocation 59.81 seconds. This proves the ordering repair locally, not an exact replay of the hosted runner's cache/CPU conditions.
- Tooling TypeScript checking, focused lint, formatting, diff whitespace, and the exact test-line ratchet pass. Auto Review assessed the three-file follow-up against local published-candidate snapshot `3a31774ca7fbe610927a5e0b56515b54b1c5a455`: **scoped-clean at P0**, not a P1/P2 review or independent test rerun. The earlier runtime review is retained separately below.
- The hosted result and subsequent fixture repair are recorded above; these local startup results remain tied to `e4e34e8238e32df394b3de4dd409d5dc420f116d`.

The original [compact-small-20 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40520328291/job/122246271787) on `dc659641854df29e4a282e9984cd3ac45b3f6c31` occurred before tests: a cache miss caused 58.6 seconds of compilation, then verification crossed the watchdog deadline. The earlier 65-test passing replay did not reproduce that failure. This follow-up fixes the preparation ordering instead of increasing the timeout or counting compiler chatter as progress. Prior baseline, boundary, build, lint, and type-check successes remain evidence for that prior head only.

**Real before/after proof:** [@Marvinthebored's exact-head report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185915#issuecomment-6442857090) compares main `ed0eb799279` (including #185746) with unmodified PR head `d8334a83487`, using two isolated Gateways with identical config and fresh state:

- A child completing during a 70-second foreground exec: before, the parent received a generic event without the result; after, private hook context carried the result and the parent answered “42.”
- Four human turns: before, five rendered user bubbles; after, four. Ordinary native user text is exactly what was typed, with metadata in hook context.
- Literal internal-looking human text remains human; session-gap notes stay out of user text; forwarded session input becomes synthetic and is still acted on. Exec/automation wakes remain synthetic.

These are the contributor's reported live observations, not a new live-model run by this CI repair. The CI repairs change test ownership, the exact count baseline, and worker-preparation selection, not this PR's Claude/session runtime logic. Its base has advanced to `50d56a527f344490e85173213a52db608f5aa2f6`; live qualification still belongs to the exact head above.

Prior repair verification on base `a6be2f6aee7fd9782563d54e33e4b60995853008` (before the baseline-only follow-up):

- **405 tests passed across 19 files in one invocation**, eight project shards, 346.65 seconds. Coverage includes native steering/completion, prompt-prefix stability, session reuse, history merging, plugin parsing, and real durable import.
- The previously failing extension-boundary suite now passes all 11 tests; the full core compiler-graph boundary check also passes.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, lint of both revised test files, formatting, diff whitespace, and the test-line ratchet pass.
- Independent static review found one index-only type annotation omission, already present in the verified working tree; that correction is included in the published repair. It found no additional actionable P0–P2 runtime or security defects. This review is not a new live-model qualification.
- The original busy-parent regression failed against base `ed0eb799279` because the private completion result was missing, and passed with the runtime repair. The CI follow-up does not alter that runtime fix.

<details>
<summary>CI repair and measured test-budget exception</summary>

The failed core compiler graph and boundary check came from a Gateway test importing Anthropic's private implementation. Plugin parsing and repeated literal-message coverage now live in the existing plugin-owned suite. The existing Gateway integration case retains real durable import, display projection, and idempotent re-import assertions without crossing the plugin boundary.

Test consolidation reduced the patch's net test growth from 324 to **297 lines**. The retained cases protect distinct failures: per-input provenance and busy-parent completion through the native protocol; private prompt fragments and resume/gap context; native-tool versus caller-surface binding continuity; and native/canonical history plus durable import. Deleting them solely to meet the count would remove distinct regression coverage.

The previous exact-count adjustment passed locally but failed on CI’s newer merge base: [run 40514361208](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40514361208/job/122225150041) measured **6,284,291**, 134 above its 6,284,157 ceiling. The branch was reconciled with main `491ce01c486b62c3ec7017bdb7faf81aeb246e4b`, which already raises the upstream ceiling to **6,285,000**. Its measured test count is **6,284,740**; the boundary repair added 297, totaling **6,285,037**.

The startup-ordering follow-up adds **18 test lines** by extending the existing runner fixture and selection table, bringing the full PR delta to **315** and the measured total to **6,285,055**. These cover the two real runner entry points plus excluded/unrelated selection without new fixture infrastructure. The admission-fixture correction adds another **9 test lines**, bringing the full PR delta to **324**. It replaces a blanket child-process stub with the existing controlled compiler and a narrower reader stub, preserving the negative runtime-build case. Following the documented narrow exception path, the ceiling at that stage was exactly **6,285,064**: **64 lines** above its then-current upstream base, with no spare allowance. The later CI merge-base drift and then-exact **6,286,283** ceiling are explained at the top of Evidence. The Claude/session runtime and boundary-repair tests remain unchanged; their prior focused tests and review are retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as a new live or CI pass. The startup-ordering follow-up has its own proof above. No behavioral expectation, assertion, test selection, or other ratchet is relaxed.

The reported `prepare.ts` growth was an advisory line-cap warning; that CI check passed. Runtime wiring was not changed merely to silence the warning.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): send inbound context privately instead of in the user's message
prs.body:
Related: #185915, #185945

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Claude CLI sessions, OpenClaw put its own context into the text of the user's message: inbound conversation context, the Git co-author note, queued `System:` events, and the session drift and gap notes. Claude saved that text as the user's prompt. Chat history then imported it as a second user bubble, because the importer's text stripping did not recognize every fragment (the co-author note, for example).

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin transport already has a private channel for host context: the `UserPromptSubmit` hook's `additionalContext`, which #185945 also uses for steered inputs.

- `buildCliCurrentPrompt` returns the inbound context fragments and the drift/gap notes as `prependContext` when the session runs on the plugin transport. The rendered prompt holds only the sender's text. Other transports keep the old inline rendering.
- Native Claude prompts now hold only what the person typed, and forwarded inputs are synthetic meta rows (#185945). So the importer's prompt-decoration matching has no new input to clean. This PR removes it:
  - `cli-session-history.prompt-text.ts` (system-event, gap-note, requester-hint and routed-envelope stripping)
  - the `routed_key` / `undecorated_text` views and the matchers that used them
  - the display cleanup for unmatched imported rows
- History import goes back to the two keys that v2026.10.7 shipped: the text, plus a copy without the drift note. The removed views shipped only on `main` and beta. The history index is an in-memory SQLite table rebuilt on each read, so no stored schema changes.

## User Impact

A Claude CLI message shows once in chat history, as the person wrote it. Claude still gets the same context, through the prompt hook. On sessions that ran before this change, rows written by beta builds can show their old context prefix again, as they did on v2026.10.7.

## Evidence

**Live, real Claude CLI, Control UI.** Same turns on `main` and on this branch (stacked on #185945):

| `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![main: OpenClaw context shown as the user's message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40df4e35-a1a4-46d4-96f5-5812d5de426f) | ![this PR: only the typed message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/929d9f9d-a3fd-44dd-868e-ab2fdcb1dda9) |

- `main`: the user bubble holds the Git co-author note and the queued `System:` session-creation events above "Reply with exactly the word DONE."
- This PR: `chat.history` has one user row per turn, holding only the typed text. Claude's transcript records the same context as `hook_additional_context` on `UserPromptSubmit`.
- The busy-parent scenario from #185945 still passes on this branch: the subagent result steered into the running turn reaches the parent, and history shows no extra user rows.

**Tests and checks**
- `prompt-context.test.ts`, `prepare.durable-context.test.ts`, `prepare.existing-session.test.ts` and `execute.native-history-owner.test.ts` cover the plugin-transport split and the unchanged inline rendering.
- All `cli-session-history*`, `session-history*`, `chat-history*cli*`, `strip-inbound-meta` and `cli-runner` suites pass (93 files).
- `check:changed` lanes: typecheck, lint and boundaries pass. The dead-export scan flags three exports in files this PR does not touch; `main` has the same failures.

Size: +250/−698. Test lines: −240.

Credit: @Marvinthebored found this and wrote the private-context change in #185915. This PR is its second part.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. A revert restores inline context and the old matchers; nothing persisted changes. Blast radius: Claude CLI prompt rendering on the plugin transport and imported Claude CLI history display.

prs.title: fix: Claw Add leaves MCP servers behind when it fails after adding one
prs.body:
Fixes #185276
Related: #185275; follow-up to #185854

## What problem this solves

A failed Claw Add can still leave earlier MCP requirements in global configuration when a later lifecycle-lease or forward-current check fails before entering that action's write wrapper. The caller receives cleanup refs only if the whole awaited install succeeds or an error carries them. A plain later failure loses the refs accumulated by earlier successful writes.

This is **not superseded by #185854**, which closed #185275. Current-main shipped-entry proof below confirms that its committed-write recovery works, while the separate later-action path in #185276 remains broken.

## Fix and user impact

Keep the operation's in-flight MCP ref list caller-owned and record each intended entry before its write. Any rejection leaves that same list available to compensation. The existing rollback still reacquires the lifecycle lease, skips pre-existing requirements, compares current configuration digests and supplies the expected server/current-authority checks before removal. Absent failed-write entries are dropped harmlessly; concurrent changed entries are preserved.

This removes the exception-carried inventory and redundant post-failure commit probe without weakening committed-then-rejected rollback. Successful Add behavior, stored config formats, permissions, authority propagation and lease policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

[Current-main supersession check, shipped Add receipts, committed-write proof and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185866#issuecomment-6458655872).

- Main: `fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e`, including #185854 (`1a7afa7a5bd7ed0d59fdbcf655319c0f4efee045`).
- Candidate: `22e6d405c5fdbb895fca6eaaf42dc1dbfcf6ab81`.
- Full `pnpm build` succeeded for both refs in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Each run has isolated profile/state/config/workspace/ports and an integrity-checked local ClawPack registry fixture.
- Target: built **public `claws.add.apply`**, called through `openclaw gateway call`; readback: actual **`openclaw mcp list --json`**, checked against persisted configuration. No installer helper is used as the mutation target, and no result refs or database state are fabricated.

### Later-action failure: main twice vs candidate twice

The normal canonical lease API holds `second` while public Add commits `first`. Public inventory confirms `first` is present. A supported `config patch --file` turns Claws off; after the policy write commits, the coordinator releases `second` and the configuration application finishes successfully without restarting the Gateway. Add naturally fails the forward-current check before that later write wrapper; no exception is injected in these runs.

| Run | Inventory while Add waits | Inventory after partial Add |
|---|---|---|
| Main 1 | `preexisting`, `first` | `preexisting`, **`first` left behind** |
| Main 2 | `preexisting`, `first` | `preexisting`, **`first` left behind** |
| Candidate 1 | `preexisting`, `first` | `preexisting` only |
| Candidate 2 | `preexisting`, `first` | `preexisting` only |

All four return the normal partial result with the Claws-disabled error. This establishes the current-main defect separately from #185854.

### Committed-then-rejected configuration replacement

Reused the prior #185854 syscall fault probe against the newly built current implementation. The real atomic config rename completes, a snapshot captures `first` plus `preexisting`, then acknowledgement rejects with `EIO`. Public Add returns partial and normal compensation runs.

**Main twice and candidate twice** both remove `first` and retain `preexisting`. The replacement path is reachable through the shipped Add entry, and the candidate retains the merged fix's rollback contract after deleting its probe. The earlier proven harness remains retained separately; no production guard was relaxed to obtain the result.

### Controls on both refs

- Pre-existing requirement remains byte-identical in every run.
- A supported concurrent patch changes `first` while Add waits: the changed entry remains intact after failure on both refs.
- Failure before the first replacement leaves only the pre-existing entry; the tentative absent ref is harmless.
- Successful three-requirement Add returns complete and keeps all requirements.

All **14 shipped-entry runs** pass. The concurrent-change control uses the later-action failure; it is not presented as a simultaneous replacement/second-writer fault. The committed-write/changed-writer owner regression also passes.

Focused checks: **23/23 tests** across the two changed owner suites; type-aware Oxlint **0 warnings / 0 errors**; Oxfmt clean on all four changed files. Whole PR: production **+34/-67 (net −33)**; tests **+40/-66 (net −26)**. No source repair, test-ceiling refresh, schema or configuration change was needed on top of the contributor head.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior in-memory bookkeeping without migrations or stored-data rewrites. Blast radius is failed Claw Add compensation for shared MCP requirements. A wrong ref could remove another writer's server or leave one behind; unchanged digest, expected-server, lease and authority safeguards remain in place and are covered by preservation controls.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): gateway stalls after every model call when content capture is on
prs.body:
Closes #158116

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `diagnostics.otel.captureContent: true`, the gateway blocks its event loop for minutes after each model call once a session's prompts carry a lot of text, tool output or image data.

## User Impact

User impact: a gateway with content capture enabled stays responsive on large sessions, and it still exports redacted, size-bounded content attributes.

On one gateway running a busy Telegram group session (prompts well over 1M characters), the main thread blocked for ~150 s after every model call. All three bots on that gateway stopped answering for 40 minutes: Telegram polling stalls, `/readyz` timeouts, liveness heartbeats overdue by ~150,000 ms. Setting `captureContent: false` cleared it immediately.

Gateways that set `logging.redactPatterns` still redact every captured string whole, as main does, and export the same attributes as main. They get a smaller speedup: 32.2 s -> 3.5 s for the slowest model call measured below.

Content small enough to export untruncated is now also redacted string by string before serialization. Before, it was only redacted as serialized JSON, where escaping turns a line break into `\n` and hides a line-start `password=...` from the text rules, so the value was exported unmasked.

A value whose JSON is over the 128 KiB attribute budget but fits once its secrets are masked is exported whole, as on main, for JSON up to 4x the budget (`a98c2d54130`), and past that when what made it large is a secret the export window cut open, such as a JWT with a 600,000-character payload (`3425a53b077`). The price is one whole-value redaction pass for every captured value between 1x and 4x the budget, including those that then still have to be truncated: up to 8x the budget, measured below.

## Why This Change Was Made

`safeJsonString` redacted the whole serialized value only to find it was over the 128 KiB attribute budget. It then tried up to 63 truncation budgets, and every attempt redacted each string in full before cutting it. That ran once each for `gen_ai.input.messages`, `input.value` and `openclaw.content.input_messages` (and again for outputs and tool definitions), so redaction work grew with prompt size x attempts x attributes, all on the main thread.

With this change:

- The truncation budget is chosen from unredacted sizes; only the candidate that gets exported goes through the redactor.
- A clipped string is redacted over its kept prefix plus a lookahead: 4,096 characters, or the longest registered secret when that is longer. A secret that starts before the cut and ends inside the lookahead is masked as it would be in the full text. Registered secrets only match whole, so the longest one always fits; core reports its length through a new `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`, counting the URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms it registers with each value.
- Some secrets need a part the lookahead can cut off: a private key block without its END line, a quoted secret without its closing quote, a JWT without its signature, a URL password without the `@` after it, an Atlassian `ATATT` or `ATCTT3xFfG` token without its `=` suffix, and a form first pair's value without the `&key=` after it. When the window ends inside one of these, the string is redacted whole by the shared redactor instead, while its export can afford it: 8x the export's size, so 1,048,576 characters for a content attribute and 32,768 for a log body. For a JSON value past 4x the attribute, the strings redacted whole are then substituted, and the value is exported whole if it fits. Past the budget, the window masks the secret from its start, after masking registered values whole the way the shared redactor does first.
- Core tells whether the window ends inside such a secret, through a new `findTruncatedSecret(text)` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core` (`src/logging/redact-open-secret.ts`). For the rules that run as linear matchers (the Atlassian tokens, JWTs, both URL password rules, form first pairs and private keys) it runs the shared matcher itself over the window's last run of non-whitespace characters (the whole window for private keys) with a closing appended: `=AAAAAAAA`, a JWT payload and signature, `@`, the rest of a form pair's `&key=` (`&a=`, or `a=` after a bare `&`, or `=` after the start of a key), an END line. A match that runs into the closing, or that the window alone does not hold, is open, and is masked from where the redactor would start its mask. So the check follows each rule's prefixes, letter case, boundaries and `;base64,` exemption. For quotes, it asks the redactor whether the key before the last quote of each kind, a stand-in value and the closing quote would be masked; the probe skips whitespace between the key and the quote, starts its key context on a non-word character, looks only at its own stand-in, and stays under 512 characters. A quoted value that a form rule also reads (`api_key="...`) keeps its closing quote.
- Configured `logging.redactPatterns` replace the default string rules, and a configured rule can need any amount of text after the start of its match. When they are set, every string is redacted whole and the 8x cap below is off, as on main. Core reports this through a new `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`, which reads the same logging config the redactor does.
- Masks shorten a redacted window, so the export could reach the window end and show part of a fixed-length secret the cut split. A window its masks shorten is redacted once more, wider.
- Clipped text sent to the redactor is capped at 8x the attribute budget per JSON candidate; a candidate over the cap falls through to the next, smaller budget. When the cap rules out every candidate that would fit the attribute, the export keeps 16, then 4, then 1 object fields, so fewer strings are clipped and each keeps more text. Only when that also fails is the export `{"truncated":true,"reason":"max_redaction_work",...}` instead of `max_attribute_size`.
- `normalizeOtelLogString` (log bodies, log attributes, string content) uses the same bounded prefix.
- `input.value` and `output.value` reuse the `gen_ai.*` serialization instead of producing it a second time.
- JSON up to 4x the attribute budget is redacted whole first (each string, then the serialized JSON) and exported whole if the result fits. A credentials dump shrinks by about half when masked, so main exported such values complete and this branch used to truncate them. The pass sends at most 8x the budget to the redactor, the cap a truncated candidate already has; past 4x, and when the result still does not fit, truncation runs as before. Since #161480 the redactor's built-in rules scan the whole text, so the pass masks a token wherever it falls in a long string.

Without configured `logging.redactPatterns`, redaction work per content attribute is now bounded by the attribute budget plus the longest registered secret, instead of the prompt size. Masks and quote probes can make a clipped string cost up to about five windows, so a JSON attribute's work can exceed the 8x budget it is chosen by: 6.3M characters for a model call with 200 tool results full of masked secrets, against 248.6M on main's code for the same input (Evidence). A value between 1x and 4x the budget adds its whole-value pass on top: at most 17x the budget per attribute when it does not fit. Strings redacted whole because their window ended inside a secret add at most 8x more, and the substituted pass for a value past 4x at most 8x again. With configured rules, work still grows with the prompt, but only the exported candidate is redacted.

## Evidence

[CI run 39795491565](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39795491565) executed merge `0173c137fdeb87a73f8c99bc6e794d3616d82906` against base `3cd9bddb36d93d43b50595dfd0d5b18a4478a0c9`: 67 jobs passed, 26 skipped, 3 failed plus the aggregate gate. The failures are:

All three files have identical Git blobs at that exact base and executed merge. The PR's 17-file delta includes none of them. This establishes file equality; it does not establish that the two runtime failures reproduce on the base. No matched frozen-dependency runtime control was available for this update. [Upstream 271329fd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/271329fd32df15f9347099872d1c35e756597cad) already repairs the missing Twitch helpers; I have not duplicated that change.

Maintainers still need to accept reduced large-value capture completeness and the three public logging SDK methods. The older [CI 39320561097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320561097) is terminal: **101 jobs, 72 success, 25 skipped and 4 failures**, including the aggregate. The inspected repair/doctor path supports that possibility, without identifying the creating process.

Before/after checks match all 57,927 base and 57,933 merge source blobs, types/modes and index trees, with no nonignored untracked files. The exact base therefore exhibits the same signature without this PR's delta in these recorded conditions. The earlier four-CPU arms passed, but the artifact histories, missing original package/plugin baselines, Intel/AMD difference, approximately 66 GB/8.2 GB RAM and measured load prevent a CPU-only causal claim or an explanation of the original hosted failure. The requester-settlement owner remains unchanged. These historical results do not validate the later runtime-budget assertions, and they remain separate from the October 20 CI result recorded above.

- A token that starts before the export cut is still masked, on all five export paths (message part, tool result, log body, and the two 128K tool call paths).
- A private key cut off before its END line is not exported.
- A line-start `password=...` in content that fits untruncated is masked in `gen_ai.input.messages` and `openclaw.content.input_messages`.
- A quoted secret whose closing quote lies past the lookahead is masked, for each quoted rule, on the message part, tool result (including the 128K string paths) and log body exports; also behind a run of zeros, with 260-300 spaces between key and quote, and wherever the probe's key context starts (a sweep over the cut offset).
- A fixed-length secret the cut splits after earlier masks shorten the window is masked.
- Cost rows for a long escape run, a long separator run, and secret-dense quoted text keep the probes bounded.
- A JWT that starts 200 characters before the cut, with its signature past the lookahead, is masked on all five export paths, for a 6,364-character token with compact claims, a 6,780-character one with indented claims (payload `ewog...`), and the compact one with an `EYJ` prefix. Base64url JSON with no dot that crosses the window end is kept.
- An `ATATT`, `ATCTT3xFfG` or lower-case `atatt` token, and a `code=` form value, that start 200 characters before the cut with their `=` suffix or `&state=x` 5,120 characters later are masked on all five export paths.
- A `code=` form value whose redaction window ends at the `&` of its next pair, or inside its key (`&st`), is masked on all five export paths.
- `findTruncatedSecret` reports the secret's start for each covered rule cut before its closing part, the closing quote for a JSON secret and a quoted form value, and the value's start for a form value before its next pair's `&` or a clipped next key. It reports nothing for a complete URL password, a web URL's port, a dot-free `eyJ` run, a token prefix inside a word or in a `;base64,` data URL, a form key no rule masks, a form value before its whole next pair or before `&` and a digit, or a closed private key.
- A registered secret longer than the lookahead (4,608 characters, registered through `generateSecureToken({ redact: true })`) that starts 10 characters before the cut is masked on the same five paths.
- With `logging.redactPatterns: ["SECRETSTART[q]{5000}END"]`, a match that starts 200 characters before the cut and ends past the lookahead is masked on the message part, tool result and log body exports. The two 128K tool call paths are left out of this one case: configured patterns run in 16,384-character chunks (`src/logging/redact.ts`, `replacePatternBounded`) and that cut is a chunk boundary, so a whole-value pass cannot match across it on main or here. That is read from the code, not measured at this head.
- A URL password of 5,000 or 10,000 characters that starts 200 characters before the cut, with its `@` past the lookahead, is masked on all five export paths, for `https://` and `postgres://` URLs, and so is a `postgres://` password holding a `/`, past the budget and within it. A port and path that cross the cut are kept for `https://`, and for `postgres://` within the whole-string budget; past it a `postgres://` port and path are dropped.
- With a 65,536-character secret registered, a model call with 200 tool results of 100,000 characters stays under the model-call work bound.
- An object of 512 strings of 5,000 characters, whose smallest truncation fits the attribute but not the redaction cap, exports 16 of its 64 keys with 512 characters a string and no token body. With a 1,048,576-character secret registered, a 2,000,000-character tool input exports the `max_redaction_work` summary.
- A message past 4x the attribute holding a JWT with a 600,039-character payload is exported whole and masked, with 320 or 22,400 characters of text after the JWT; a registered value holding `password="` at the start of a log body is masked whole, within and past the whole-string budget.
- JSON over the budget that fits once masked is exported whole, including one long string with tokens across the 16,384, 32,768 and 65,536 offsets; a value under 4x that does not shrink is truncated within its work bound; one just over 4x gets no whole-value pass; and a token at the cut is still masked after a whole-value pass that does not fit.
- The existing cut cases now put 1,100,000 characters after the cut, past 4x and past the whole-string budget, so they keep exercising the windows.

Branch history, each measured at the time: the two cut-boundary tests fail on this branch if the lookahead is set to 0 or the private-key guard is removed, and removing the 8x cap fails the 200 x 5 case. 13 open-quote tests fail on `87eb422f779`, the first version of this branch, and the later ones fail on the commit before their fix. The 5 registered-secret tests fail on `e3bfb598ff6` with the secret's first 10 characters in the export. The 5 JWT tests fail on `a6477692e1d` with the JWT header in the export, and the indented-claims token fails on `a395b25f21d` on both 128K tool call paths. The base64url case fails if any `eyJ` run is masked. The 3 configured-pattern tests fail on `b6a7955897d` with `SECRETSTART` in the export. The 5 URL-password tests fail on `4ab95960e9d` with the password in the export. The 65,536-character cost test fails at 26,667,962 characters if the cap counts only the 4,096-character minimum lookahead, and the summary test gets `max_attribute_size` on `3c9a420fc33`.

`getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` is covered in core by `src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.test.ts` (1 test): the length follows registration, drops when the longest value is evicted at 512 registrations, and returns to 0 on reset. Keeping the cached length across membership changes fails the first after the eviction (`expected 32 to be 24`). `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()` is covered in `src/logging/config.test.ts`: true for a configured list, false for an empty one, which keeps the default rules. Treating an empty list as configured fails it (`expected true to be false`).

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/diagnostics-otel
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/logging/config.test.ts src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.test.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts src/logging/redact-open-secret.test.ts
```

**Test cost.** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on an M4 Pro, Node 26.10.0 (the first two at `3425a53b077` merged with main, the other two at `40e00389277`):

| file | wall | Vitest duration | tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service-content-normalization.test.ts` | 15.0 s | 12.8 s, 29% of it in tests | 82 |
| `test/diagnostics-otel-registered-secret.test.ts` | 8.9 s | 6.7 s | 2 (new) |
| `secret-redaction-registry.test.ts` | 1.6 s | 0.53 s | 2 (1 new on this head) |
| `config.test.ts` | 1.6 s | 0.52 s | 10 (1 new in this PR) |

Summed test time for the normalization file is 3.6 s for 82 tests, against 2.5 s for 72 at `a98c2d54130`. The 13 cases for ClawSweeper's latest review take 0.59 s together; the slowest, the capped 512-string object, takes 0.23 s. The cut fixtures carry 1,100,000 characters after the cut so they stay on the window path; within the whole-string budget each would redact its whole string. At `70e38024d0b`, on the shared M4 Pro at load 12 to 19, the 92-test normalization file took 10 to 22 s wall across three runs and `redact-open-secret.test.ts` 1 to 2 s.

**CI.** Run 37976075567 on `a98c2d54130` (merged into main `164210c355e`) is red on five jobs, none in this diff. Four trace to main commits that main has since repaired; the fifth did not reproduce:

- `checks-node-changed-3`: `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive.gateway.test.ts` > "migrates local onboard plugin install records in the setup write", `TypeError: lease.assertCurrent is not a function`. Main's #167702 (`f4cb17e8408`) added the `lease.assertCurrent()` call and the onboarding fixture still fabricated the older lease shape. Main fixed the fixture in `e69931d6e6a`, after that base.
- `checks-ui-e2e` 1/9, 7/9 and 8/9: `chat-session-prefetch-gating`, `chat-flow.history-recovery` and `session-prefetch` (`expected +0 to be 1`, `Timed out waiting for 1 chat.history requests`). Main's #167906 (`b0fb3ac3321`) made history prefetch intent-only, 23 minutes before the run; main updated the three tests in `8cc90d08c0a`.
- `checks-ui-e2e` 2/9: `chat-widget-sandbox.e2e.test.ts`, `elementHandle.hover: Timeout 22ms exceeded` at the end of a 41.7 s run. Not reproduced: 3 of 3 passes at about 17 s on main alone and 3 of 3 with this branch.

Controls on the M4 Pro. Main alone at that base `164210c355e`, with none of this PR's code: the onboarding file 1 failed, 17 passed with the same error and stack, and the three UI files 3 failed, 5 passed with the same messages. This head merged with main `f8239ea9470`, which has both fixes: onboarding 18/18, the three UI files 8/8, the widget file 3 of 3. This PR changes no file under `ui/`, `src/commands` or `src/plugins`. The earlier red on `452a23f4716` (run 36369333378, `session-accessor.sqlite-cleanup-race.test.ts`) is not among this run's failures.

**Risks.**

- The whole-value pass covers JSON up to 4x the budget, and past it a value whose size comes from strings the window cut open inside a secret, up to 8x the budget of such strings per attribute. Any other value past 4x whose redacted JSON would still fit, which needs masking to remove more than three quarters of it, is exported truncated where main exports it whole: knowing its masked size means redacting all of it, which is the work this PR removes.
- That pass is extra main-thread work for every captured value between 1x and 4x the budget, whether or not it ends up fitting: at most 8x the budget per JSON attribute, about 2.1M characters for a model call's two input serializations. Measured above on an M4 Pro: +15 ms for prose and +172 ms for unbroken alphanumeric runs. Not measured on slower hardware. Main redacts the same values whole and then again for each truncation attempt.
- With configured `logging.redactPatterns`, a value between 1x and 4x that fits once redacted now exports whole, as on main, where before it was clipped. Configured patterns run in 16,384-character chunks on long strings (see the chunking bullet below), so a configured match split by a chunk boundary deep in such a string is exported, as it is on main.
- A clipped string is no longer redacted past its lookahead, unless `logging.redactPatterns` is set. Quoted values, private keys, JWTs, URL passwords, Atlassian tokens, form first-pair values and registered secrets that run past the lookahead are masked from their start. The check is each core rule's own matcher, so whatever that rule could still match is dropped: base64url data with an `eyJ` prefix in any letter case and a dot, a run starting with `ATATT` or `ATCTT3xFfG` at a token boundary, and the value of a form key the core rule masks, when they cross the window end. Not covered: `SG.` keys, Slack webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and `FlyV1 fm<digits>_` also need text after an unbounded run, but that run is an identifier (key id, team and bot ids, bot id, version) and would have to pass 4,096 characters before the secret part reaches the export. Within the whole-string budget such a string is redacted whole instead, as on main. Not covered: a JWT whose header alone runs past the lookahead exports its header up to the cut (the header carries JOSE parameters, not claims or the signature).
- Past the whole-string budget, a database URL's port and path that run to the window end without whitespace or `@` are dropped from the port, and a web URL's port followed by a run without `/`, whitespace or `@` to the window end is dropped from the port. Main keeps both.
- Gateways with configured `logging.redactPatterns` keep main's whole-value redaction and main's attributes, so a large model call still blocks the main thread for seconds there: 3.5 s for 200 tool results of 100,000 characters, against 32.2 s on main, measured on 09-27.
- Configured patterns still run in 16,384-character chunks with no overlap on text over 32,768 characters (`src/logging/redact-bounded.ts`), so a configured match crossing a chunk boundary is missed. The 128K attributes' cut at 131,072 is one of those boundaries. Main behaves the same; built-in rules scan the whole text since #161480.
- Without configured rules, the 8x cap keeps less content than main when a transcript clips hundreds of strings. With the test file's 200 tool results x 5 parts, `openclaw.content.input_messages` is 25,379 characters against 101,491 on main (`gen_ai.input.messages` is the same 119,491 on both), for 2.1M characters of redaction against 338M. An object of 512 strings of 5,000 characters exports 66,715 characters (16 of 64 keys, 512 characters a string), where main redacts 27.2M characters and exports 70,135 (all 64 keys, 128 characters a string). The 138-message transcripts above are unaffected.
- A long registered secret widens every clipped string's window by its length, so redaction work grows with it and JSON attributes keep fewer items to stay under the cap. Measured before the merge, without configured rules, with the longest registered surface form at each length:

  | Longest registered secret | Log body of 5M: redacted | Tool output of 5M: redacted | 200 tool results of 100,000: redacted / results kept in `gen_ai.input.messages` | 6 tool results of 3M: redacted / export |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 4,096 or less | 8,192 | 135,168 | 2,091,962 / 200 | 247,046 / all 6 |
  | 6,144 | 10,240 | 137,216 | 1,660,238 / 100 | 271,622 / all 6 |
  | 20,000 | 24,096 | 151,072 | 2,113,338 / 50 | 437,894 / all 6 |
  | 65,536 | 69,632 | 196,608 | 1,640,618 / 10 | 984,326 / all 6 |
  | 1,048,576 | 1,052,672 | 1,179,648 | 2,166,058 / 10 | 126 / `max_redaction_work` summary |

  1,048,576 is the default file-provider `maxBytes` (`src/secrets/resolve.ts`). Log bodies and tool outputs keep their full budget in every row. The last cell predates `3425a53b077`, which tries fewer object fields before the summary; I have not measured that row again.
- This adds three public plugin SDK functions in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`, `findTruncatedSecret()`, `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` and `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()`, and raises the public export and callable budgets by three each (3,742 and 2,195 after merging main `4a05c7c5d59`). The first returns a position and a closing quote for text the caller already holds; the second returns a length and no values; the third returns whether `logging.redactPatterns` is set. Plugins run in-process as trusted code (SECURITY.md, "Plugin Trust Boundary"). I didn't have core mask a partial registered value at the cut instead, because that matcher would tell a caller whether some text is the start of a registered secret. `src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.ts` is in the credentials tier of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`, so the new head needs a maintainer's `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.
- `max_redaction_work` is a new `reason` value in the truncation summary. Main has no redaction cap. It is now reached only when even one string's window is over the cap, as with a 1,048,576-character secret registered.
- Bounded masking lives in the plugin, which asks the shared redactor about whole strings and probe text; the alternative is one bounded operation on the shared redactor, which would be a different public SDK function than the three this PR adds. That is a maintainer decision this PR does not take.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Direct-engine timings cannot show the production owner's catalog preparation, required-reply scheduling or worker continuation costs.

## User Impact

Maintainers can run a deterministic opt-in workload through the public execution owner and compare both executors with correctness checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing production test harness and warm resource host. Measure independent process arms, keep warmups separate, assert values and exact mock bridge effects, and report worker phases, process CPU and sampled RSS with their limits.

Stack step 5 of 7; depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185904. Kept draft until the parent lands and the branch is integrated onto main.

## Evidence

- The unchanged probe SHA-256 aa5013a745c9fca6d780ffb5b36cd333fdb1a255a3e756a6bc625f4d4dbcb8a6 was used for the completed five-pair runtime comparison: 1,760 timed cells, 660 warmups and 28,320 timed mock bridge calls. A separate Node follow-up ran 1,600 timed cells. Historical measured source identities are retained in the final investigation PR; they are not relabeled to this split head. This is not ShellBench, packaged startup or peak Gateway RSS proof.
- Local autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3), 443b2e3ebe0f5255dca6bd531d88641aec99ab4a → 05c474f67d5fd79331ce1e55eda1d0750c2240a2: complete, no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute project code.
- Opt-in test/measurement source: +208/-0. Production logic: +0/-0. No new config/default surfaces.

## Integration

Rebased onto main snapshot 4f78407ee8fcd8391cbea3eb1105141c89ea5915 with upstream store-error behavior preserved. No PR in this stack changes the test-line ceiling. Main's existing ceiling covers the full 594-line corpus; the assembled canonical check passes at 6,284,262 / 6,285,000. Historical focused proof and measurements remain separate from current-head CI.

## Test-line budget

The immutable owner probe adds 208 test lines. Integration is pinned to main beb12fafdee64721e2598148b13527f0b9386ad3: 6,293,568 test lines against a 6,293,290 ceiling, already 278 over. Main plus this probe is 6,293,776, so adjust the ceiling by 486 lines to that observed total, with zero spare allowance. Both a direct literal-newline Git-tree count and the canonical check-test-lines-ratchet.mts command agree. No tests are renamed, excluded or deleted.

Historical CI 40540211648 at 7624 passed 30 jobs;40543704004 at 1fcf failed only the ratchet by 5 lines added on main during push. CI 40615291967 at 9ee8ed35 passed 30 jobs with 29 planned skips and 0 failures, with clean independent review. Native submission then stopped before a successor intent when GitHub mergeability changed, and a bounded investigated retry found a concurrent main ceiling conflict. Those statuses remain historical; fresh CI/review qualify this head separately. Benchmark SHA256 aa5013a745c9fca6d780ffb5b36cd333fdb1a255a3e756a6bc625f4d4dbcb8a6 is unchanged.

## Current publication

Head `78f000f3fb938a0b1e784dfd6a8f81219eebfa36` is integrated onto pinned main beb12fafdee64721e2598148b13527f0b9386ad3. The owner benchmark is unchanged; this integration repairs only its shared test-line budget/source binding. The child probe and documentation patches remain identical through the signed restack. Historical measurements retain their original runtime identities; newer Node retention and shared-worker diagnostics are outside those timing inputs. Fresh exact-head CI and review qualify this publication separately.

## Current-head qualification

Head `78f000f3fb938a0b1e784dfd6a8f81219eebfa36`: [CI 40617708978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40617708978) passed 30 jobs with 29 intentional skips and zero failures, including the test-line ratchet. Fresh independent review found no actionable finding or pre-merge action and independently confirmed the exact 6,293,776-line count. Historical performance measurements remain distinct from current-head CI.

prs.title: fix(macos): New Thread exhausts memory during session creation
prs.body:
Closes #186215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac transport now routes ordinary creation through its existing captured new-session lease. This replaces the recursive default-dispatch path without introducing another request builder or changing generic transports and iOS.

## Evidence

This is a draft proof head, not a readiness claim.

- Finite native base-red: [fork run 40568043055](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40568043055), Intel macOS 26, proof commit `cd45388962cfa007d6bf3052dbee8ada9d3e8c3b` on upstream base `1b50ce5a6835798634c4d98ac87891f4e5290120`. The exact explicit-options regression ran once and failed with the expected unsupported-options error after its captured-lease control. The test is unchanged in this fix.
- Added sibling coverage for plain and legacy existential creation, disconnected and retired/replaced sockets, recovery, and a mismatched window Gateway pin.
- Normal staged Git hook and native localization inventory passed; private-key scan and whitespace check passed. No lockfile or generated-source changes.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2) reviewed the complete two-file candidate against `c4c345af4e8842219a880c13a1788a560878dc84`: scoped clean. Static review is not native test proof.
- Native Mac evidence on public head `2b916adf3896eb18fb11d7702c9dd203fa1aaecf`: [fork run 40574165243](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40574165243) compiled the native test bundle and OpenClaw product; all 35 transport mapping tests passed, including `explicitSessionCreationUsesCapturedGateway`. [Complete artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40574165243/artifacts/12768336365). The workflow failed afterward because its proof wrapper requested a missing coverage output from a noncoverage build; this was not a failed test assertion, and the overall run is not claimed green.
- Completed native GREEN on the unchanged public head: [fork run 40577761227](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40577761227) succeeded on Intel macOS 26. All 35 `MacGatewayChatTransportMappingTests` passed, including `explicitSessionCreationUsesCapturedGateway`; pinned SwiftFormat and SwiftLint passed, with zero lint violations. The corrected wrapper retained the exact-SHA build cache and removed only the mismatched coverage flag. [Complete native evidence artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40577761227/artifacts/12770192447).
- Real-app attempt [fork run 40582646027](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40582646027), workflow SHA `ff7f800e3ecde940fa11ecd4c5a080b09b09c3b3`, finished **setup-incomplete, not real-app proof**. The exact base app/package built, but its isolated Gateway exited 78 before readiness. No native New Thread UI verdict was reached, no provider POST occurred, and the PR-green arm never started. [Diagnostic artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40582646027/artifacts/12772811768). The artifact lacks the Gateway error text, so the complete startup cause is not established.
- The fork fixture independently fails the full strict config schema on retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat`. A proof-only correction removes that field, requires exact-source/exact-config CLI validation before Gateway startup, and explicitly preserves sanitized Gateway stdout/stderr. The complete corrected fixture passes root/core schema checks and strict validation with source plugin manifests; the combined correction received independent P0–P2 review and 42 local diagnostic/oracle controls passed. Those checks do not prove hosted startup or native UI behavior, and the correction is not part of this PR.
- Corrected serial real-app attempt: [fork run 40598236532](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40598236532), exact workflow `e9030d57da25d6fcfdfbd44a4a7bb14240abd1a5`, driver SHA-256 `c42d3b9af08bff92d54c1a1c1ca6279e547d71e2ede93a7aad00813b9aa6ee55`, targets the unchanged public PR head. The retired heartbeat field is removed, exact-environment config validation and fixed sanitized Gateway diagnostics are present. This run finished **failure / base-red incomplete**, not a qualifying red reproduction. The exact base app/Gateway package built successfully; the red-control driver then returned `status: "incomplete"` with `cleanup: "owned-process-groups-retired"`. The PR build, green control, and exact-head verdict gate did not run. [Diagnostic artifact 12779383222](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40598236532/artifacts/12779383222) uploaded successfully (43 files). Authenticated artifact inspection by @harjothkhara identifies the first failure as `ax-snapshot failed/timed out` at fork driver `proof/new-thread.mjs:288`. Gateway config validation passed, the isolated Gateway started, and native app status reached primary `connected`. The first AX snapshot returned only `{ "ready": false }`; the next produced no output before timing out. No New Thread action or PR-green arm ran. The existing helper does not distinguish missing-process/no-window readiness and has no in-flight AX-stage diagnostics, so the specific cause of the blocked AX call remains unestablished. The contributor also inspected `capture-preflight.png`: Finder/Dock around an otherwise black desktop, with no OpenClaw window. The exact driver takes that image before launching the app, so it supplies no post-launch window-visibility proof. The fork-only diagnostic proposal is being extended to require an independent owned-PID/executable, frontmost/unhidden, onscreen-window gate and window-ID capture before AX traversal. Native compilation/runtime validation of that extension is still pending; no real-app red/green or successful GUI proof is claimed.
- Pending before readiness: remaining shared consumer checks, guarded real-app New Thread proof, and required CI. Proof-driver code remains fork-only and is not part of this PR.

Contributor: @harjothkhara.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dad4e96a-6b6b-4377-b233-13a0c609eb71)

## Worked on by

- @harjothkhara

prs.title: refactor(test): flatten backup singleton cases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four backup tests still use singleton case tables, including a temp-directory branch that no remaining case can reach. This follows the maintainer-requested test simplification campaign.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. All four cases and their assertions remain; production backup behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `withState` fixture directly, spell out each retained input, and remove the unreachable nested-tempdir setup. Test names remain unchanged. Production delta: 0 lines; test delta: -9 lines.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): prevent missing workspace baselines after cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sandboxed managed sessions becoming stuck when manifest cleanup collects a stalled preparation before its baseline or checkpoint is published.

## User Impact

A stale preparation now fails before publishing references to missing content, and retrying the session prepares the preserved live files again. Older missing baselines can recover from an intact pending-checkpoint result without discarding either workspace's edits. Unverifiable divergence still refuses recovery and reports both preserved paths with an inspection command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Immutable pack preparation and root publication use separate worker transactions. Packs prepared at sweep epoch E are collectible at E+2, but publication previously accepted their digest without checking that window. Preparation now returns its epoch, and the writer checks the oldest preparation epoch before any mutation. Ordinary manifest reads omit the potentially large checkpoint payload; only repair requests load it. The existing schema, retention window, lease checks, and commit settlement remain unchanged.

Recovery can reverse an authenticated checkpoint delta in memory when a live workspace matches its resulting tree. It publishes repaired CAS metadata only if the reconstructed tree matches the saved baseline digest. Comparing or recreating workspaces cannot recover an unknown three-way merge base; no automatic selection between divergent edits is introduced.

## Evidence

- Deterministic red-on-base store regression: run two sweeps after preparation and before publication. Base incorrectly resolves the publication after its packs were collected.
- Red-on-base recovery regression: neither workspace equals the old baseline, but one exactly matches the saved checkpoint result. Base refuses; the repair reconstructs and verifies the old baseline without modifying either live file.
- Five focused suites: `local-workspace-{store,manifest-scan,cas,conversion,projection}.test.ts` through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1`: **82 passed, 2 preexisting environment skips**; 393.36s suite time / 423.38s wrapper wall time. The skipped cases require real Podman or raw non-UTF-8 filenames unsupported by this filesystem.
- Final touched-file run after fixture cleanup: store, manifest-scan, and CAS: **31 passed**; 157.60s suite time / 187.91s wrapper wall time. Worker/runtime preparation accounts for most overhead; the new manifest-scan recovery test itself took under 0.2s.
- Targeted typecheck extends `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json` with only the nine touched TypeScript files: passed. Focused `run-oxlint.mjs`, `run-format.mts --check` for all 11 changed files, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex autoreview, P1, complete working-tree change against base `451ec41c26c67cca7d8a61b7da6b0188cf52249e`, with complete publication/GC/recovery context: no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Follow-up limiting checkpoint reads to repair: affected store and manifest-scan suites **26 passed**, 169.78s suite / 193.46s wrapper wall time; targeted typecheck/lint/format passed. P1 autoreview of that delta against `e242a31b008570e7938a8d946ee44f79d7cbdff0` found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Accepted edge case: a reconciliation spanning two sweeps may need another session attempt even if some earlier prepared content has since become reachable. Keeping the oldest preparation epoch covers unpinned scan output across observation commits.
- Existing known-tree insertion proof is consolidated into the rollback/lost-reply test. All assertions and CAS sharing/GC contracts are retained; net test lines decrease by 13. Production code grows by 79 lines; documentation grows by 18.
- No live Gateway, user state, deployment, schema migration, dependency, or configuration change.

## CI Classification

Exact-head CI run 40578654178, attempt 1, failed only `check-lint-core-2` (job 122454243417) and its downstream `openclaw/ci-gate`; `security-fast` passed. The root failure is five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` (lines 31–32) and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx` (lines 288–289 and 362). Reactive-use and max-lines diagnostics are warnings.

Core stripe 4/5 was run locally on CI's main parent `5010c3e80f8bb2271bbd347d4639218f84f9fac4` and reproduced exactly those five errors, including identical files, messages, and locations. The UI tree, lint rule/configuration owners, dependency manifests, and warning-source objects are identical between that parent and tested merge `fb4746a70ec39bf378a50ceac661e2a71857c89c`, whose second parent is the reviewed head `f1a6f74fafbce52ff582af01a7ad4815f44549a7`. These failures are unrelated to this worker-environment fix. CI remains failed; the authorized native pre-existing-failure exception is selected. No CI rerun or branch update was used.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): clone admission scope buckets directly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Publishing a full SQLite admission snapshot rebuilt a complete write-scope Map from already prepared immutable buckets before structured cloning. A newly connected receiver could incur that extra allocation after every scope publication.

## User Impact

A modest reduction in allocation and CPU during SQLite worker admission. Scope retirement, live revocation, write settlement, FIFO ordering, schemas, and public SDK APIs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Full snapshots now carry the existing nonempty buckets directly; receivers install their cells into the existing owned Map. Cursor deltas still carry only changed cells. This deletes the lazy full-Map materializer and six net runtime production lines. The benchmark harness grows by 46 lines to make cloning, receiver installation, and work counts reproducible. Snapshot selectors explicitly require only database identity. No cache, fallback representation, configuration, schema, or budget change is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance: remove clone-time Map materialization, preserve scope authority and immutable snapshots, and retain a measured CPU/allocation win without a demonstrated regression.

Synthetic Linux owner workload: 40 databases × 1,000 initial session/context scopes, 100 warmup and 3,000 measured operations per arm. Each operation discovers one scope and clones that database's full snapshot; the second workload also installs the clone into a retained receiver. Two concurrent pairs with swapped interleaved CPU sets, exclusive measurement lock, and the existing host guard. Allocation sampling ran separately from timing. Base: `ad55c5ec3920ee0f84738ea0158fd7686be6e476`.

| Work per operation | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Publish + clone allocation | 1,728,187 B | 1,578,873 B | −8.6% |
| Publish + clone CPU | 3.404 ms | 3.171 ms | −6.8% |
| Publish + clone elapsed | 3.223 ms | 3.090 ms | −4.1% |
| Including receive allocation | 1,903,509 B | 1,750,281 B | −8.0% |
| Including receive CPU | 3.617 ms | 3.352 ms | −7.3% |
| Including receive elapsed | 3.350 ms | 3.186 ms | −4.9% |

Untraced total GC per operation fell from 0.0383 to 0.0122 ms for cloning and 0.0453 to 0.0237 ms including receipt. Clone-pair maximum pauses: 2.039→0.416 and 1.767→0.567 ms; receive-pair maxima: 2.586→0.866 and 2.112→0.740 ms. Clone GC counts: 187→155 and 185→155; receive: 198→163 and 196→162. No separate major-GC or pause-percentile conclusion is claimed. Host load was 3.8–4.8 during these untraced arms. Traced CPU is context only: clone sampling CPU rose 1.2%, while untraced CPU improved in both pairs.

A separate 50-operation count run recorded 56,275→0 clone-time Map-entry insertions. The regression assertion fails on base at the old getter and passes with this change. Existing immutable-snapshot and retirement proofs remain; the worker test now also retires/replaces a scope after dispatch and verifies the write invalidates its replacement.

Validation: 116 focused tests passed across `sqlite-database-write-receipts`, `sqlite-schema-facts.native`, `sqlite-database-admission.retention`, `sqlite-database-admission.worker`, `sqlite-database-write-scopes`, and the session deletion/lifecycle-publication consumers. Focused test commands used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`; file test time ranged from milliseconds to about 16 seconds, wrapper wall time up to 54 seconds including worker compilation. Targeted core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and diff whitespace checks passed. One development rerun was discarded because source changed during compilation, then rerun against stable source. No Testbox lease was used; PR CI supplies broad proof.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), P0–P2: one missed test consumer was fixed and re-reviewed; no remaining actionable findings. Autoreview refused the requested provider mismatch before inference; operator configuration was not changed.

Rerun the committed owner harness with `node --expose-gc scripts/perf/sqlite-admission-release-measure.mjs <source-root> <owner-file> <label> <timing|allocation|counts> 3000 100 1 <install-scope-snapshot|install-scope-receive>`.

Limits: this is the explicitly requested fast-path owner-deletion proof, not a Gateway stress campaign. No production load was generated. Gateway revisions/min, handler/list/event-loop tails, allocation rate, RSS/heap, and whole-Gateway CPU were not measured. The harness models cloning and installation, not worker scheduling.

prs.title: fix #183856: stop writing retired top-level channel to session entry
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When `/status` is the first message after a chat `/new`, the fast reply session initializer wrote a retired top-level `channel` field into the session entry. `openclaw doctor` then reported `Found 1 durable session row(s) with legacy delivery fields` and kept reporting it after every `doctor --fix`.
- Solution: Stop emitting the retired top-level `channel` field from the fast session initializer. Channel identity is already owned by the canonical `delivery` block, so dropping the stray field loses no routing information.
- What changed:
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts`: removed the `channel` variable and its `...(channel ? { channel } : {})` spread in `initFastReplySessionState`.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts`: added a regression that seeds a post-`/new` session owning canonical external `delivery`, bootstraps a native `/status` over it, and asserts the resulting `sessionEntry` has no `channel` property, keeps the reused `delivery` block untouched, and is a no-op for Doctor's legacy-delivery normalizer.
- What did NOT change: The `delivery` block, `chatType`, `subject`, `groupChannel` and all other canonical session fields are untouched. Doctor's legacy-delivery normalizer and its repair behavior are unchanged. No persisted schema or cache format changes.

Fixes #183856

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A native `/status` right after `/new` wrote the retired `channel` key next to the canonical `delivery` block, making doctor repeatedly ask for repair on healthy sessions. After the fix the fast initializer no longer emits the field, the reused canonical delivery survives, and the resulting entry is a no-op for Doctor's legacy-delivery normalizer (so a persisted row is not flagged).
- **Real environment tested:** `issue-183856` worktree on top of latest `main` (`e850f7c5`), running the real `initFastReplySessionState` fast bootstrap flow (native `/status`, `Provider=telegram`) through the existing fast-reply test harness, and the real Doctor delivery-state repair suite against SQLite `session_nodes.entry_json` rows.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Regression: native /status fast bootstrap must not persist a retired channel field,
  # must keep the reused canonical delivery, and must be a no-op for Doctor's normalizer
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 \
    npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts -t "retired top-level channel"
  # Full fast-path suite
  npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts
  # Doctor's delivery-state repair over real SQLite rows (data-model compatibility:
  # a row carrying channel/route/lastAccountId is found, repaired to canonical delivery,
  # and stops being reported)
  npx vitest run src/commands/doctor-session-delivery-state.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ getReplyFromConfig fast test bootstrap > does not persist a retired top-level channel field on a native /status fast bootstrap
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  1 passed | 9 skipped (10)

  // get-reply.fast-path.test.ts: 10/10 passed
  // doctor-session-delivery-state.test.ts: 7/7 passed
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** On the base, the bootstrap's `sessionEntry` carried `channel: "telegram"` (assertion failed with `Received: "telegram"`). After the fix the same bootstrap produces a `sessionEntry` without a `channel` property, with the seeded canonical external `delivery` block intact, and `normalizeLegacySessionEntryDelivery` returns the entry unchanged (a persisted row is not reported by doctor). The Doctor suite proves the end-to-end data model: a durable row carrying `channel`/`route`/`deliveryContext`/`lastAccountId` is found by `repairCanonicalSessionDeliveryStates`, repaired to a canonical `delivery` block, has every `LEGACY_SESSION_DELIVERY_KEYS` key stripped, and is no longer reported on the next scan.
- **What was not tested:** A live Telegram Gateway with an isolated agent DB and an actual `openclaw doctor` run against the persisted `session_nodes.entry_json` was not executed in this environment; the fix is verified at the exact producer (fast session initializer) with the native `/status` path, and the doctor normalizer that flags the field is covered by its own suite against real SQLite rows. The unrelated `get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts` file could not be run locally due to a pre-existing startup hang in this environment (it does not import the changed module); it runs in CI.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: a native `/status` fast bootstrap (Provider `telegram`) over a post-`/new` session that owns canonical external `delivery` must (1) not produce a top-level `channel` property, (2) keep the reused `delivery` block, and (3) be a no-op for `normalizeLegacySessionEntryDelivery` — the exact normalizer Doctor applies when deciding whether a durable row needs repair.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: It exercises the exact producer (`initFastReplySessionState`) on the exact reported trigger (native `/status` after `/new` with a provider present), asserting the retired key is absent and that the persisted row would not be flagged by Doctor; the doctor-delivery suite independently asserts the normalizer's repair of already-affected rows.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `initFastReplySessionState` in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts` computed `const channel = normalizeOptionalString(ctx.Provider)` and spread `...(channel ? { channel } : {})` into the `SessionEntry`. `channel` is a retired `SessionEntry` slot key (`RETIRED_SESSION_SLOT_KEYS` in `src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts`); the core `SessionEntry` type no longer carries it. The canonical `delivery` block already owns channel identity, so the field was pure legacy metadata that doctor flags.
- Missing detection / guardrail: The fast initializer emitted a retired session field that the durable-row normalizer and doctor explicitly classify as legacy, with no consumer reading it back.
