prs.title: fix(perf): discard terminated worker subtrees from native profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native memory profiling can wait for workers that have already terminated. When a worker owns nested workers, Node can tear down the descendants without running their JavaScript exit observers, leaving stale census records.

## User Impact

No Gateway runtime behavior changes. Developers can collect native-memory checkpoints around transcript commits without stale descendant records invalidating the snapshot. A changing live census still rejects the sample.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each observed worker inherits its full ancestor chain. The surviving parent's exit observer removes that terminated subtree while preserving unrelated workers. The transcript benchmark exposes separate forced-GC checkpoints before and after work and cleanup; these diagnostic runs are explicitly excluded from timing comparisons.

## Evidence

- Real Node worker regression fails before the fix for both forced and natural parent exit: two descendant records remain. Both modes pass after the fix, with the unrelated sibling still responsive.
- Covers two nested levels, explicit worker environments, SHARE_ENV, and explicit execArgv.
- Node 26.12.1 standalone fixture, syntax checks, targeted formatting, and diff checks pass. The two regression cases also passed in the Linux CI Bun-hosted Vitest lane: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40568683569/job/122417721783.
- Independent autoreview of the complete branch change: scoped-clean through P2.
- CI found the inherited worker environment value was inferred as Node's broad Serializable union. The follow-up adds the number-array JSDoc contract; runtime behavior is unchanged.
- The first integrated CI tree exceeded the test-line ceiling by 49 (26 new regression lines plus 23 baseline overage). Native main at fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e has 170 lines of headroom, so no ceiling increase or test deletion is needed.
- ClawSweeper's optional rank-up request for the complete Linux allocator scenario is deferred: both corrected Blacksmith Testbox attempts queued and were stopped under the proof-routing policy. The RSS campaign retains that measurement as a follow-up. No memory-savings or complete allocator-integration claim is made.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve check budgets after slow candidate snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native updates aborting healthy candidate checks after a slow state snapshot and Doctor pass exhaust a separate 30-minute validation deadline.

## User Impact

Candidate checks get their existing state-sized allowance independently. An explicit `--timeout` still limits the admitted update overall, and cancellation still drains accepted work before recovery. The installed updater must include this fix; selecting a newer candidate alone does not change the running updater.

The restored default is 300 seconds plus 40 seconds per 32 MiB of copied database and plugin input for each check: lower for small state, higher for large state (2 GiB gives 2,860 seconds). No runtime config or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate wrapper imposed an aggregate deadline before snapshotting and also replaced the canary's automatic per-check budget with 1,800 seconds. The canary already owns snapshot and runtime-check budgets; the admitted update owns an operator-specified overall deadline. This removes the duplicate deadline while preserving inherited cancellation, SQLite admission checks, progress-writer custody, and bounded capability/port probes.

## Evidence

All **78 wrapper/canary tests passed**, including actual child processes and persisted update-ledger writes, on tested candidate `fb356450eb9e7f98c09fa427f8113fa4ffce79be`. Final head `b25c9f4db962860bc40a4e2f0aef5ebf8f86a384` preserves the same ten changed files, package/lock inputs, and relevant update/SQLite/process owner inputs. The long default-path regression uses synthetic elapsed time/capacity; explicit overall deadlines stop silent Doctor and lint children and join settlement. Accepted commit receipts, source replacement, and uncertain cleanup retain their authority checks.

The same long regression fails at the original 1,800-second limit when only the wrapper is replaced with its base version. Three focused help/port cases also passed; the final normalized port fixture passed both cancellation cases and targeted type-aware lint. Formatting, normal commit hooks, and diff checks pass. A queued Testbox allocation was stopped before execution; focused proof used the native PR workspace.

Independent review accepted the production repair, cancellation-test correction, final lint correction, and signed baseline refresh. Autoreview covered the complete working snapshot committed as `7a19e28b8bd2a337401d398fd3665734f84a3507` against `843abed3a886e62c272b9ed11e91ec55b4a73534`; its sole obsolete-index finding was resolved by staging that reviewed snapshot. A fresh P0–P2 autoreview of `7a19e28b8bd2a337401d398fd3665734f84a3507` → `9fec277f0b983826f37c797a1ac351386edaca15` found no issues. Those reviews still cover the byte-identical ten non-baseline PR files and package/lock inputs after the mechanical baseline refresh; the prepared product diff SHA-256 is `6926248f16f531251f25727e086df72cc8eba3f7841c30a121170cfac915c965`.

The final native test-line ratchet passes against the selected main baseline. The PR adds 198 ratchet-counted test lines and leaves the existing ceiling unchanged; there is no config diff.

The reported failure spent 734.465 seconds snapshotting and 1,002.995 seconds in a successful Doctor pass, then killed lint after 63.235 seconds (1,800.695 seconds combined), with no lint findings or output-limit failure.


Exact-head [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40587616730) completed with one unrelated failed workload: [core lint stripe 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40587616730/job/122484871484) reports five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx`. Both failed files and the inspected lint inputs are byte-identical in protected-main parent `5b1482d925dd9742229e3a55396e606a42a2b1ef` and tested merge `06749677e803c34c0a722791fd60baa32b1bd993`; update/infra lint leaves passed. Main already contains the [canonical brace repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b2b0997a5780c074f0f7cdf766e274509b72771). Landing uses the native attributed inherited-failure route, retaining the failed CI result and enforcing independent security, required reviews, exact-head identity, and live writer authority.

<details>
<summary>Scope and remaining limits</summary>

- Reuses existing process, SQLite admission, canary, and update deadline owners; production net +15 lines.
- Preserves source-replacement, uncertain receipt, and revoked-authority handling.
- Existing raw canary termination can report an advisory if close remains unconfirmed after TERM/KILL; this change does not claim process-tree extinction or alter that separate behavior.
- ClawSweeper rank-up follow-up: installed-driver fleet validation follows landing because the current updater must first acquire the fixed wrapper. A latest-stable upgrade matrix is separate follow-up work; the scoped repair is covered here by real child/ledger boundary proof and the old-wrapper red control.
- Release-note context: native updates no longer consume later candidate-check time while copying state or running an earlier check.

</details>

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop seeding new thread sessions from the room transcript
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A new Matrix thread's session was forked from the room session: `handler-context.ts` set `route.parentSessionKey` to the room's `mainSessionKey` for every thread target, so `prepareReplySessionParentFork` copied the room's transcript — including earlier turns, tool calls, and tool results — into the thread's first prompt. The issue's `context-diag` capture shows a thread first turn starting with `messages=4 roleCounts=assistant:2,toolResult:1,user:1` inherited from unrelated room history.

The docs promise only the thread root as extra context, and Discord/Slack gate exactly this behavior behind an opt-in (`thread.inheritParent`, default `false`) that Matrix never got.

Fixes #176224.

## Changes

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-context.ts`: thread targets no longer request a parent transcript fork — `route.parentSessionKey` is always `undefined`. The room session is still carried as `route.modelParentSessionKey` (the restart-recovery / model-parent fact), mirroring Discord's disabled-inheritance shape. Thread sessions keep their scoped keys (`:thread:<id>`) and the thread root still rides along as supplemental context via the untouched `supplemental.thread` path.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` + `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.context.ts`: transcript inheritance and restart-recovery replacement are now separate facts in the shared lifecycle. Recovery admission and canonical tombstone replacement fall back to `ModelParentSessionKey` when the fork request is withheld, and the recovery fork only runs in the tombstone-replacement branch — ordinary first turns never fork. This preserves the recovery path deliberately enabled by aa3fb33ba8a (#130196) for eligible tombstoned thread sessions (unlocked, unbound, no prior fork, authorized human turn).
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.test.ts`: the room-thread assertions now pin both isolation (`ParentSessionKey` absent) and recovery (`ModelParentSessionKey` set) at the existing handler boundary.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.hooks-and-send-policy.test-utils.ts`: core regression proving a human turn into a tombstoned, not-yet-forked thread session is still admitted and replaced via the model parent key.
- `docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md`: states the isolation behavior explicitly.
- The earlier `handler-context.test.ts` call-shape suite was removed per review: coverage lives at the existing handler boundary, which exercises the real core context builder.

## Evidence

Live proof driving the shipped Matrix handler-context assembly with the real core context builder (`src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts`) and the real finalize step, for a room-thread message rooted at "Plan lunch" (`extensions` harness semantics, terminal output):

After this fix:

```
=== Matrix thread message — finalized inbound context (real core builder) ===
thread target            "$lunch1"
SessionKey               "agent:main:matrix:room:room1:thread:$lunch1"
ParentSessionKey         (absent)                                <- no room transcript fork request
ModelParentSessionKey    "agent:main:matrix:room:room1"          <- restart-recovery source retained
ThreadStarterBody        "Plan lunch"                            <- thread root context retained
```

Before this fix (current main `d0e8fc8a103`), the same trace shows the fork request (`ParentSessionKey "agent:main:matrix:room:room1"`) and no `ModelParentSessionKey` — that request is what copies the room transcript into the thread's first prompt.

- Red/green regression: on base, a thread target's `route.parentSessionKey` receives the room session key; with the fix it is absent and `ModelParentSessionKey` carries the room key (asserted in `handler.test.ts` at the existing handler boundary, which runs the real core context builder).
- Full `extensions/matrix` suite: all passing (handler tests now 59/59 on the rebased head, including the new room-thread isolation/recovery assertions). Core `auto-reply-reply`: all passing for the touched area (`dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` + `session-parent-fork-prepare.test.ts`, 298/298, including the tombstone-replacement regression); a full-project run earlier showed 9 failures that reproduce on main or flake under parallel load (media-history x8, module-identity x1) — unrelated to this change.
- Typecheck, lint, and format are clean: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:all`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint` (0/0 on changed files), `oxfmt --check`.


### Effect-level live proof (durable init, transcript, model input, denial at the effect)

An in-process harness drives **shipped code paths only** — the real Matrix handler context assembly (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-context.ts`) with the real core finalize, then the real shared pipeline `dispatchInboundMessage` → `dispatchReplyFromConfig` → `initSessionState` (real agent DB + session lifecycle) → embedded agent run → **real provider I/O** against the repo's e2e mock OpenAI server (`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, which logs every request body, i.e. the captured model input). All data is synthetic; nothing real is exposed.

**A. Ordinary thread isolation (model input, not just context shape).** A room turn seeds `agent:main:matrix:room:room1` with the sentinel `SENTINEL-ROOM-HISTORY-7f3a9c`; a thread turn rooted at "Plan lunch" then runs through the real Matrix producer + pipeline. Captured provider requests:

| req | path | room sentinel in model input | thread marker | ThreadStarterBody |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| room turn | `/v1/responses` | **1** | 0 | 0 |
| thread turn | `/v1/responses` | **0** | **1** | **1** |

The ordinary thread's model input contains no room history while the thread-root context and the thread's own message remain — at the durable effect (session init + transcript + model input), beyond the finalized-context trace above.

**B. Eligible recovery via `RecoveryParentSessionKey`.** Tombstoned thread children are seeded in the pre-upgrade stored shape (the recovery key never lives on disk; it arrives per-message):

- Unauthorized sender presenting the recovery key (`InboundAccessAuthorized: false`): dispatch rejected with `SessionRestartRecoveryTombstoneError`, tombstone preserved, **0 provider requests**.
- Authorized human `user_request` with `RecoveryParentSessionKey`: the real fork commits (`forkedFromParent=true`, `forkSource={"sessionKey":"agent:main:matrix:room:room1",…}`), tombstone cleared, replacement transcript created with explicit parent linkage (`parentSession: "sqlite:main:<room-session-id>:…"`), provider request issued for the recovery turn, reply delivered.

**C. Room-policy-denied sender at the effect.** The shipped ingress matcher `resolveMatrixAllowListMatch` denies a non-allowlisted sender; that sender carrying the recovery-parent handoff (unauthorized `room_event` + `RecoveryParentSessionKey` + tombstoned thread) is rejected before transcript creation, the store stays untouched (tombstone intact), and **0 provider requests** occur. The existing authorization guards are demonstrated at the effect, not only in unit assertions — the recovery-parent handoff cannot be used by a forbidden sender to create a replacement transcript or begin a provider request.

**D. Data-model compatibility — real `openclaw@2026.10.5` upgrade.** Durable state was generated by the real `openclaw@2026.10.5` release (npm) through its own CLI (`openclaw agent --local` with real provider I/O): settings (`openclaw.json`) and an agent DB at `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` holding one live session (`agent:main:main`, no PR-introduced fields) whose multi-event transcript contains the sentinel `LEGACY-ROOM-HISTORY-7f3a9c`. The PR-head core then took over the same state dir, unmodified:

1. **Schema admission + migration.** The new core requires the documented upgrade step; `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates the agent DB schema version 25 → 31 with the session entry, session id, and all transcript events preserved (`schema_meta.app_version` still records `2026.10.5`).
2. **U1 — continuation of the pre-upgrade session.** A post-upgrade turn into the same session runs through the new pipeline; the captured model input contains the legacy sentinel — the pre-upgrade transcript is preserved in context across the upgrade.
3. **U2 — new threads created post-upgrade are isolated.** A new Matrix thread (real producer + shared pipeline) contains **0** occurrences of both the room marker and the legacy v2026.10.5 transcript sentinel in its model input, while the thread's own marker and `ThreadStarterBody` remain present.
4. **U3 — store coherence.** The upgraded entry keeps its `sessionId` unchanged and remains writable/loadable by the new core.

Stored-data fencing additionally holds for pre-upgrade-shaped recovery data: the tombstoned entries in scenario B/C carry legacy `mainRestartRecovery` fields in the stored shape a pre-upgrade release produces (the recovery key never lives on disk; it arrives per-message). They load, are honored, and upgrade semantics apply correctly — eligible recovery replaces (B2); unauthorized/ordinary starts stay fenced (B1/C2).

Full procedure and terminal output: see the upgrade proof section of the run log (`U1`/`U2`/`U3` assertions, exit 0, repeatable).

### Running Gateway/Matrix entry-point proof (wire-level)

A real Gateway process (`startGatewayServer`: WS server, gateway lock, agent DB engine, plugin registry, subsystem logs) with the bundled Matrix channel auto-started, receiving messages over the wire from a homeserver through the real sync-ingress path, dispatching through the real shared pipeline (durable sessions + transcript) into real provider I/O, and delivering replies back over the real Matrix send path. The homeserver is a fake in-process Matrix client-server API (`/sync` long-poll, `/event/{id}`, room state, `/send`) — wire-compatible, loopback-only, all data synthetic; nothing real (IPs, keys, phone numbers, non-public endpoints) is exposed.

Two gateway runs (close → seed → restart):

- **G1–G5 isolation.** The gateway starts and the Matrix monitor syncs against the homeserver; the room's pre-existing history contains the sentinel `SENTINEL-ROOM-HISTORY-7f3a9c`. A thread message rooted at "Plan lunch" is injected over the wire; it reaches the provider as the thread session's main model input with **0 occurrences of the room sentinel** while the thread starter body ("Plan lunch") is retained; the reply is delivered over the Matrix send path.
- **R0–R5 eligible recovery.** Between the two runs, a `mainRestartRecovery` tombstone entry (`entry_valid=1`) is inserted directly into the gateway agent DB for the thread session key. On restart, an authorized sender's thread message recovers: the model input legitimately contains the room-transcript sentinel (explicit fork from the room session), the tombstone is cleared in the store, and the recovery reply is delivered on the wire.

Terminal assertions (exit 0, repeatable; harness `.workbuddy/live-proof/gateway-entry-proof.mjs` against the reviewed head unchanged):

```
[gw-proof] G1 PASS: gateway server started
[gw-proof] G2 PASS: matrix monitor syncing against fake homeserver (sync rounds=20)
[gw-proof] G3 PASS: thread message reached provider as main model input (2 requests with marker, main=1)
[gw-proof] G4 PASS: thread model input contains room sentinel (requests with sentinel=0/1)
[gw-proof] G4b PASS: thread model input retains thread starter body (root context) (1/1)
[gw-proof] G5 PASS: reply over Matrix send wire (2 sends)
[gw-proof] R0 seeded tombstoned thread session: agent:main:matrix:channel:!room1:example.org:thread:$rootR
[gw-proof] R1 PASS: gateway restarted, monitor syncing again (sync rounds=16638)
[gw-proof] R2 PASS: recovery thread message reached provider (2 requests with marker, main=1)
[gw-proof] R3 PASS: recovery forked from room transcript (sentinel present in recovered model input, 1/1)
[gw-proof] R4 PASS: tombstone cleared after eligible recovery
[gw-proof] R5 PASS: recovery reply over Matrix send wire (phase-2 sends=2)
```

Contrast at the same wire boundary: an ordinary new thread → room sentinel **absent** (G4) with the starter body retained (G4b); a tombstoned thread with eligible recovery → room transcript **present** via the explicit fork (R3) and the tombstone cleared (R4).

Boundary: the entry-point proof uses a fake but wire-compatible homeserver rather than a public federated one; the Gateway process, sync ingress, durable session state, shared pipeline, provider I/O, and send path are all real. Matrix ingress is additionally exercised at the shipped handler/ingress layer in the finalized-context trace and effect-level proof above.

### Media proof (recorded terminal run)

A terminal recording of the effect-level proof running live against this PR's head (`03e4d56c081`, shown in-frame via `git log --oneline -1` on the PR branch). The recording executes `.workbuddy/live-proof/run-effect-proof-filtered.sh`, which runs the real effect proof end to end and only filters per-turn diagnostic noise lines for readability — every assertion line below is produced verbatim by the run; the wrapper is quoted in full in the comments.

![Effect-level proof terminal recording (PR #177272)](https://github.com/Linux2010/openclaw/releases/download/proof-artifacts-177272/media-proof-effect.gif)

The recording ends on the full assertion set and `pipeline exit status: 0`:

- **Scenario A** — `thread model input contains room sentinel: 0` while the thread marker and `ThreadStarterBody ("Plan lunch")` remain present (isolation at the model-input effect).
- **Scenario B** — `B1` unauthorized recovery-key dispatch rejected with the tombstone preserved and 0 provider requests; `B2` the eligible recovery fork commits from the room session, clears the tombstone, and delivers the reply.
- **Scenario C** — a room-policy-denied sender is rejected before transcript/provider I/O with the tombstone intact and 0 provider requests.
- **Scenario D** — pre-upgrade-shaped durable state loads and is honored by the new core.

### Compatibility surface of the new route fact

The single channel-facing addition is the optional `RecoveryParentSessionKey` fact, threaded through exactly four internal layers, each additive:

| Layer | Change | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (`MsgContext`) | optional field + reserved-purpose doc comment | additive; unset unless the Matrix restart path emits it |
| `src/channels/turn/types.ts` (`RouteFacts`) | optional field | additive |
| `src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts` (core builder) | passes `route.recoveryParentSessionKey` through | additive passthrough |
| `src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence-scope-key.ts` | one scope-field entry | additive |

- The public plugin contract is unchanged: **zero files under `src/plugin-sdk/` differ from the merge base**, so bundled and external plugins see no new or changed SDK surface.
- `ParentSessionKey` and `ModelParentSessionKey` semantics are untouched; `RecoveryParentSessionKey` is a separate optional dimension consumed only by the restart-recovery replacement (fenced from ordinary session starts by the lifecycle owner).

- No new configuration options and no default changes for existing users.

## Notes

- Model routing is unchanged: stored model overrides resolve through the derived parent of the `:thread:` session key (`resolveParentSessionKeyCandidate`), so a new thread still resolves the room's `/model` override exactly as before. (An earlier revision of this description incorrectly claimed the fallback was removed.)
- Compatibility: eligible tombstoned, not-yet-forked thread sessions remain replaceable after upgrade — recovery now sources from the explicit `RecoveryParentSessionKey` (emitted by the Matrix restart path) instead of the withheld fork request, and `ModelParentSessionKey` is fenced from lifecycle behavior entirely. The v2026.10.5 upgrade path is exercised end to end above: `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates the agent DB (schema 25 → 31) with sessions and transcripts preserved, pre-upgrade transcripts continue to serve context, and no manual data migration is needed.
- Discord and Slack gate transcript inheritance behind an opt-in (`thread.inheritParent`, default `false`) that Matrix never got; this change aligns Matrix with that default without adding a Matrix-specific knob.
- The shared fork machinery in `src/auto-reply/reply/` keeps a single owner for both facts; Discord, Slack, and subagent forks are unaffected (their `ParentSessionKey` keeps precedence, `ModelParentSessionKey` is only a fallback).
- No new configuration options.

Session-only clients lose targeted Inbox invalidations, while session and presence events must respect invitation membership.

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): keep each steered input's own origin and context
prs.body:
Related: #185915, #185746

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a message arrives while a Claude CLI turn is running (for example a subagent's completion while its parent is busy), OpenClaw injects it into that turn. The Claude runtime then dropped that input's private context and never marked it as host input. The parent lost the child's result, and Claude told the model "The user sent a new message".

## Why This Change Was Made

The host already prepares each queued input's provenance and `currentInboundContext`. Only the Claude injection path threw them away:
- the `UserPromptSubmit` hook returned no context for injected inputs
- the native write never set `isSynthetic`

Changes:

- `CliBackendMessageInjection.queueMessage` takes optional per-input `promptOrigin` and `promptContext`. This is the same contract as the initial prompt. An injected input never inherits the running turn's origin: a person can steer a host turn, and a completion can arrive during a person's turn.
- The steering adapter sets them from the input's own transcript provenance and inbound context.
- The Claude runtime returns that context from the prompt hook, including on hook reruns, and sends host inputs with `isSynthetic`.
- `inter_session` provenance (forwarded messages, subagent completions) is now host input as well as `internal_system`. A message from another session was not typed by this session's operator.
- Removed `readClaudeCliInterSessionProvenance`, which read forwarded-message provenance from native prompt text. Forwarded inputs are now synthetic meta rows that the importer never reads.
  - Local Claude runs always use the plugin transport, and node-placed Claude history is not imported by the Gateway.
  - So the parser only served transcripts written before this change: those rows now show as plain user rows.

The canonical transcript is unchanged: forwarded messages keep their provenance, sender and visibility.

## User Impact

A subagent result that arrives while its Claude CLI parent is busy now reaches the parent with its content, and the parent no longer treats it as the user's message. When Claude falls back to another provider, its recent-turns prelude skips forwarded prompts, as it already skips cron and recovery prompts (#185746).

## Evidence

**Live, real Claude CLI (Claude Code 2.1.310).** I ran isolated Gateways on `main` (`53763ed`) and on this branch:
- The parent spawns a subagent that must reply with a secret, then runs `sleep 75`, then reports the subagent's reply.
- It must not poll or use `subagents`/`sessions_history`.
- The subagent finishes during the sleep, so its completion is steered into the running turn.

| | Parent's answer | How Claude presented the steered completion to the model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | `NO-RESULT` | "The user sent a new message while you were working" |
| this PR | the subagent's exact secret | "[MESSAGE FROM NON-USER SOURCE - NOT USER INPUT]", with the completion context |

In an earlier run without the polling ban, the `main` parent had to fetch the result itself with `subagents wait` and `sessions_history`. On this branch it already had the result.

**Tests**
- `execute-plugin.steering.test.ts`: the real Claude stdio transport against a fixture CLI.
  - Steered `internal_system` and `inter_session` inputs are sent as synthetic; human steering is not.
  - A steered subagent completion delivers its result ("The fixture count is 42.") through the prompt hook. This fails on `main`.
  - A recorder failure before native acceptance rejects the input instead of losing it.
- `cli-runtime.test.ts`: an injected input's context is returned on the first hook pass and on reruns.
- `execute-plugin.test.ts`: the origin comes from provenance kind only.
- These suites pass: `cli-session-history.routed-prompts`, `session-history.subagent-visibility`, `chat-history-handler.cli-import`, `cli-session-history*`, `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime`.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean.

Size: +169/−125. Production is +93/−77; the rest is the steering regression tests (net +28 test lines). The test-line ratchet passes against current `main` without a ceiling change.

Credit: @Marvinthebored found this and wrote the original fix and its tests in #185915. This PR is the first part of that change.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. A revert restores the old injection path. Native meta rows already written stay hidden. Blast radius: Claude CLI steered and forwarded inputs, and third-party CLI backends that implement `registerMessageInjection` (the new argument is optional).

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse owner selection facts revisions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated session-row publications rebuild filtered metadata Maps in every retained selection, even when the selection facts did not change.

## User Impact

Reduces allocation and CPU in session-list publication while preserving filtering, ordering, archive visibility, membership, and lifecycle behavior. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row owner now retains one selection snapshot and revision. Recents and list consumers compare that revision and physical identity instead of rebuilding the same metadata comparison. The owner compares changed facts once using own enumerable keys without temporary Maps, including metadata-only and board changes; display-only entries retain the revision while publishing their new values. Raw selections without an owner snapshot retain structural comparison because they have no revision receipt.

The snapshot follows the row lifecycle, excludes materialized display graphs, and is cleared on generation renewal. The ordered partition and ancestor contribution structures from #186353 and #186389 are unchanged.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: 10,800 synthetic sessions, 5,000 updates per shape, unchanged/presentation-only/metadata-only publications, one and twenty selection listeners. Include owner preparation and publication fanout. Compare base/candidate in AB/BA order, separate untraced timing and sampled-allocation passes, identical result digests, lower CPU or allocation without a reproducible adverse metadata-update result. Record CPU/update, B/update, GC, latency sample counts, host load and RSS/heap. Measured on an isolated Linux sandbox with paired concurrent processes on swapped interleaved CPU sets. Timing and allocation run separately; setup and warmup are excluded. All 24 paired case digests match.

- Regression fails on base `ad55c5ec3920`: unchanged update constructs two Maps. Candidate passes with zero; a label-only update at the same timestamp invalidates retained selection.
- Initial focused proof: 3 files / 17 tests passed, 73.35 seconds wrapper wall time. Final fixture and retention proof: 3 files / 14 tests passed, 48.71 seconds. Includes archive, lifecycle, membership, seeded write sequences and collection of superseded rows.
- Eager-import and PR-wrapper closure checks: 32 tests passed, 47.39 seconds wrapper wall time. Export collision check passed.
- Scoped lint/format passed. Test-line ratchet passed with six fewer test lines; no baseline or ceiling changed.
- Refinement proof: both changed selection test files passed all 12 tests (51.70 seconds wrapper wall time); scoped format/lint passed again.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings in both the initial and refinement reviews. The prescribed provider was rejected by the configured-route preflight; configuration was not changed.

This uses the explicitly authorized owner-proof fast path for duplicate recomputation deletion. No whole-Gateway load, RPC/event-loop, or live production performance claim is made. Broad typechecking and suites run in PR CI. The initial run passed production/test types and the focused shards but found a type-import cycle in the new comparison module. Its contract now lives in the leaf module. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40615457502) passed on `267f5b00d1506e41110703ebb06ea9c459a5bf4f`, including types, selected test shards, architecture, baseline ratchets, artifacts and the aggregate gate. No CI rerun was used to chase green.

Two swapped pairs per listener count and instrumentation mode, 5,000 samples per case/arm/pair; 240,000 measured publications in total. prs.title: docs(windows): add .cmd token-recovery workaround for Restricted PowerShell
prs.body:
Fixes #183723

## Problem

On npm-style Windows installations with PowerShell's Restricted execution policy, the bare `openclaw` command resolves to `openclaw.ps1` and is blocked before Doctor even starts: `File ...\openclaw.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system` (`UnauthorizedAccess`). The Gateway token-recovery instructions in the docs tell users to run `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` with no launcher caveat, so a user following the documented recovery route gets stuck even though the shipped `openclaw.cmd` launcher works without touching the execution policy.

## Root cause

- npm global installs ship three launchers: `openclaw.ps1`, `openclaw.cmd`, and a bare `openclaw` shim. PowerShell resolves bare `openclaw` to `openclaw.ps1` and refuses it under the current execution policy; `cmd.exe` resolves bare `openclaw` to `openclaw.cmd` because `.ps1` is not in its search list. Neither OpenClaw nor the token-generation command is affected — only the launcher resolution.
- The `.cmd` spelling is required because the resolution, not the tool, is broken: `openclaw.ps1` is an external script subject to the script policy, while `.cmd` files are handed to `cmd.exe` on Windows, so the PowerShell policy never applies. Invoking the launcher explicitly (`& "$env:APPDATA\npm\openclaw.cmd" ...`) therefore bypasses the block without weakening the execution policy.
- `docs/platforms/windows.md` had no troubleshooting section for this launcher layout, and the token-recovery steps in `docs/cli/gateway/running.md`, `docs/help/faq-first-run/quick-start.md`, and `docs/web/control-ui.md` all recommend the bare command with no Windows pointer.
- Native Windows evidence in the issue confirms both halves: `Get-Command openclaw` resolves `openclaw.ps1` (`ExternalScript`) under Restricted policy and bare `openclaw --version` fails with `UnauthorizedAccess`, while the explicit `.cmd` invocation succeeds, including with a custom npm prefix.

## What changed

- `docs/platforms/windows.md`: new "PowerShell blocks the openclaw command" troubleshooting section explaining why the shim is blocked, how to invoke the `.cmd` launcher explicitly, how to locate a custom npm prefix (`npm config get prefix`), and that recovery commands also run unqualified from a regular Command Prompt. It keeps the execution policy alone during recovery and notes that token/password changes require reconnecting or re-pairing existing clients. Also adds a pointer from the existing Doctor trouble-shooting steps to the new section.
- `docs/cli/gateway/running.md`, `docs/help/faq-first-run/quick-start.md`, `docs/web/control-ui.md`: every `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` recovery mention now links to the new section so a Restricted-Policy Windows user is routed to the working launcher.

## Testing

- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` — pass (docs MDX contract, full docs pass on this head's parent content, unchanged by the rebase).
- `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.ps1 --check` on all four touched files — pass (the full `scripts/format-docs.mts --check` run hits a Windows host cmd.exe "command line is too long" limit here; the touched files were verified individually).
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` at repo scale exceeds this Windows host's practical run window locally; the CI `check:docs` gate runs the same anchor/publishing-route contract on every docs PR and validates it there. Cross-page anchors used (`#powershell-blocks-the-openclaw-command`) were checked against the new heading manually.
- Verified against the native Restricted-Policy reproduction and custom-prefix lookup documented in #183723 comments.

## Risk

Low: docs-only change. No runtime behavior, config, or execution policy is touched. Wording describes existing npm launcher behavior rather than prescribing policy changes.

prs.body:
Related: #185145

## What Problem This Solves

The issue reports that `openclaw update cleanup --yes` refuses to retire recovery originals with a destination-verification error even after the Gateway and other known readers are stopped.

## User Impact

The originals remain protected, but cleanup cannot reclaim their space in the reported environment.

## Why This Change Was Made

This draft investigated whether SQLite sidecar metadata changes could trigger the refusal. **The proposed patch is not safe to merge:** it also stops checking WAL and journal timestamps, which can miss real destination writes before originals are deleted. The production cleanup path has not yet established that its own reads change the baseline after it is captured. The issue's root cause and a safe repair remain unconfirmed.

## Evidence

A real SQLite helper test shows that an intervening read-only connection can alter sidecar state, but does not establish that the actual cleanup flow performs that read after baseline capture. Existing retirement tests cover destination mutation; additional proof is needed for WAL reuse and the reported cleanup sequence. Local targeted typecheck and lint passed; the aggregate changed check reported unrelated pre-existing unused exports. CI has a reported failure in a Doctor health test; local replay passed, but its root cause is not established.

## Next steps

Reproduce the reported refusal through the isolated cleanup CLI on macOS, identify the first metadata change after baseline capture, and retain protection against WAL and journal writes before proposing a corrected patch.

prs.title: fix(update): stop update cleanup from failing its own destination check
prs.body:
Fixes #185145. Supersedes #185219.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update cleanup --yes` can invalidate its destination check when its own SQLite reads change sidecar timestamps. A historical device-number change also needs safe re-verification: inode numbers alone cannot identify a database across filesystems.

## User Impact

Read-only WAL/SHM timestamp churn no longer blocks eligible cleanup. A changed device number is accepted only with independent content evidence; ambiguous or different destinations retain their recovery originals with `destination-verification-failed` and an actionable device-change message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared verifier keeps inode, size, link, and fresh content checks. On a device mismatch it requires a journal-free destination whose complete SHA-256 matches either the producer-verified full original or a fingerprint recorded by an earlier verified restamp. A fresh fingerprint of the current file alone never certifies a remount. Scoped backups, data-bearing WAL/journals, and mismatched or missing evidence fail closed.

Only after that check passes does the current maintenance authority permit restamping the manifest's device identity and recording the destination fingerprint. Fingerprinting uses the existing isolated SQLite worker so raw descriptor closes cannot release the serving process's SQLite locks.

**Manifest contract:** this adds optional `databaseIdentity.sha256` to the existing JSON manifest. Older manifests remain readable and can use their producer-verified full-original digest. There is no SQLite schema or CLI/configuration change. General Doctor validation does not reconstruct an old migration's content proof: `openclaw doctor --fix` checks current state but does not automatically recertify ambiguous old backup identities. The recovery documentation states this limitation.

Thanks @thatsrue and @TameTheGame for reporting the two failure modes, and @kaguranananana for the sidecar repair in #185219. Contributor credit remains in the original commit.

## Evidence

- The P1 regressions failed on `0bb80bb4d59806c159aff9c8837227f1f4bdae45`: a same-inode/different-device candidate with different valid SQLite content was retired, and matching content was not restamped. Both pass after repair. The tests explicitly verify the inode and independently calculate the persisted SHA from the retained original bytes.
- Focused retirement/update run: **56 tests passed across four files**, 123.38 s including preparation (127.38 s wrapper wall time). Existing replacement, alias, in-place edit, WAL-commit, sidecar timestamp, and POSIX lock-preservation checks pass.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/update-automatic-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-mutations.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-disposal.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- Consumer proof: **37 files: 450 passed, 1 failed, 2 existing platform skips**, 718.59 s wrapper wall time. The failure was `doctor-session-sqlite.restore-paths.test.ts` / `refuses unsafe v3 restore paths (archive)`: its fixture import had no `legacy-store` move, before destination verification. Inspected the unchanged fixture/import boundary; the isolated full file then passed all 17 cases (33.73 s wrapper wall time). This replay does not establish a root cause or fix. The fixture failure remains an explicit unresolved proof gap; no timeout, retry, skip, or assertion weakening was added.
- Live macOS CLI proof ran the real registered `registerUpdateCli` Commander parser and cleanup handler, without mocks, under isolated HOME/state/config. `update cleanup --dry-run --json` followed by `update cleanup --yes --json` accepted matching full-original content, restamped its device and SHA, and removed its original. The different-content/same-inode case returned **blocked**, retained the original byte-for-byte, and did not write a destination SHA. Harness: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/cleanup-revision/live-cli.mts matching` and `... different`, each with a separate isolated state directory. The normal source launcher was previously refused at runtime-artifact publication, before cleanup; no services were changed.
- Core tsgo, commands-doctor and commands test typechecks, focused oxlint, oxfmt, Madge (zero cycles), and `git diff --check` passed. `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` passed with **net test lines 0**, despite the untouched base being over its ceiling; no baseline edit.
- Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped for local runtime cost. PR CI supplies broad validation.
- Fresh isolated local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete repair against `0bb80bb4d59806c159aff9c8837227f1f4bdae45`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Source assessment only; tests were run separately above.

Fresh full destination reads per artifact remain an open performance review item from the previous head. This repair addresses the P1 identity flaw and preserves those content safety checks.

Full PR delta against merge base `9813528d3c2026a74ba21dc3416a2eb4885fdb9e`: production **+76 / -19 (net +57)**; tests **+141 / -141 (net 0)**; docs +14 / -3. No changelog edit; this body carries release-note context.

prs.title: fix(update): npm preinstall runs on the shell's older Node after the updater selects the managed Gateway Node
prs.body:
Closes #185792

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` says it is using the managed Gateway's Node, then fails in the target package's `preinstall` script because npm runs it with the older Node from the shell's PATH.

## User Impact

User impact: when the shell's Node is older than the target release needs but the managed Gateway's Node is new enough, the update installs instead of failing with `global-install-failed`.

This happens when a release raises its Node floor: the installed release still runs on the shell's Node, so the updater starts normally, but the target's `preinstall` rejects that Node. In the report, 2026.10.10-beta.3 accepts Node `>=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0` and beta.4 requires `>=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1`, so a shell on 24.16.0 updates beta.3 → beta.4 into this failure. (A shell Node below the installed release's own floor is caught earlier: the launcher reruns the command under the managed Gateway's Node.)

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater picks the Gateway's Node for the update and announces it, but the npm environment for the staged candidate install still had the shell's PATH. The selected Node was put on that PATH only later, after staging, so npm and the target's lifecycle scripts (`node scripts/preinstall-package-manager-warning.mjs`, which checks the target's own `engines.node`) ran on the shell's Node. The fix puts the selected Node first on the install PATH when the install environment is created, using the same helper the later runtime step already uses. The Node version checks are unchanged. When the managed Gateway runs from a different installation, the runner is the updater's own Node; the post-install lifecycle step already puts that same runner first on PATH, so staging now matches it.

## Evidence

### Real update runs on Debian 13 with systemd

Two fresh Debian 13 VMs, one per build, set up like the report: OpenClaw 2026.10.7 installed into the shell's npm prefix with shell `node` v24.22.1 first on PATH; the Gateway installed as a systemd user service (lingering enabled) with Node v26.12.1, which `ExecStart` pins. Each ran `openclaw update --yes --tag <target.tgz>`, where the target is a build of the same tree with version 2099.1.1 and `engines.node` `>=26.12.1`: the same shape as beta.3 → beta.4 (the installed release accepts the shell Node, the target raises the floor), one floor higher.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Updater prints "Using the managed service runtime for this update…" | yes | yes |
| Staged `package-install` | failed: `preinstall` "requires Node >=26.12.1", "detected Node 24.22.1" | passed |
| Candidate checks (doctor, config, plugins, recovery, candidate Gateway startup) | not reached | passed |
| Result | `global-install-failed`; still on 2026.10.7 | "OpenClaw updated to 2099.1.1 (from 2026.10.7)", "Gateway: restarted and verified", exit 0 |
| Gateway afterwards | 2026.10.7, `/readyz` ready | 2099.1.1, `/readyz` ready |

<details>
<summary>main: staged install output</summary>

```text
Current runtime (/opt/node-shell/bin/node) differs from the managed gateway service runtime (/opt/node-service/bin/node).
Using the managed service runtime for this update so the gateway can start after the upgrade.
  ✗ package-install (60.65s)
    npm error command /bin/sh -c node scripts/preinstall-package-manager-warning.mjs
    npm error [openclaw] error: this OpenClaw release requires Node >=26.12.1.
    npm error [openclaw] detected Node 24.22.1 (exec: /opt/node-shell/bin/node).
  ✗ package-install-omit-optional (64.89s)
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: global-install-failed.
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>this PR: same setup</summary>

```text
Current runtime (/opt/node-shell/bin/node) differs from the managed gateway service runtime (/opt/node-service/bin/node).
Using the managed service runtime for this update so the gateway can start after the upgrade.
  ✓ package-install (69.64s)
  ✓ candidate-doctor (35.79s)
  ✓ candidate-config (2.86s)
  ✓ candidate-plugins (2.94s)
  ✓ candidate-recovery (2.95s)
  ✓ candidate-gateway-startup (17.42s)
Gateway: restarted and verified.
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2099.1.1 (from 2026.10.7); 12 warnings need attention.
```

</details>

Unrelated to this change, the successful run also logged one "database is locked" from the post-update Doctor ("Automatic database restoration cannot attribute migration writes"); the update carried on and completed. `main` never reaches that step in this setup.

### Upgrade from the latest stable, existing data kept (upgrade-survivor)

The repository's own upgrade test (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh`, the `published-upgrade-survivor` lane, which was skipped in this PR's CI), run from the latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.8` with the lane's settings (scenario `legacy-operator-state`, `auto-auth` restart). For the upgrade to go forward, this branch and unchanged `main` were each built as 2026.10.9 (root and plugin package versions aligned with `scripts/sync-plugin-versions.ts`, committed, packed); nothing else changed.

The test installs 2026.10.8, seeds existing state on it (config, the state database, exec approvals, operator cron and agent state, a Gateway), updates to the candidate, and then checks that the existing data still loads and works: `assert-candidate-schemas`, `assert-automatic-migration`, `assert-survival` (config, state and approvals unchanged and readable), `verify-backup-rollback`, then Gateway health and readiness.

```text
this PR: Upgrade survivor Docker E2E passed baseline=openclaw@2026.10.8 scenario=legacy-operator-state candidate=2026.10.9 updateRestartMode=auto-auth startup=45s updateRestart=1118s healthz=1s readyz=1s status=3s.
main:    Upgrade survivor Docker E2E passed baseline=openclaw@2026.10.8 scenario=legacy-operator-state candidate=2026.10.9 updateRestartMode=auto-auth startup=45s updateRestart=1113s healthz=1s readyz=1s status=3s.
```

The same test from `openclaw@2026.10.6` (CI's baseline for a 2026.10.7 build) also passed for both.

### Tests

- New regression test in the candidate-admission suite: a managed Gateway whose service command uses a different Node than the shell, `openclaw update --yes` with default admission. It checks that the staged `npm i -g` call gets the service Node's directory first on PATH. On unchanged `main` it fails (PATH starts with the shell's directory); with the fix it passes.
- Update suites pass with the fix: `update-cli.candidate-admission` (16), `update-cli.node-runtime`, `update-command-package` and `update-command-runtime-continuation` (45 tests across the four files).
- `tsgo` (`tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json`): clean. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- The fresh-profile path already put the selected Node on the install PATH before staging (covered by `update-command-runtime-continuation.test.ts`); this change covers the existing-profile path from the report.

prs.title: fix(infra): reject lossy UTF-8 in managed update handoff output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed update handoff process lossy-decodes the updater subprocess stdout with `Buffer.toString()`. When the updater emits bytes that are not valid UTF-8, they are silently replaced with U+FFFD replacement characters. If such corruption lands inside the JSON diagnostic output, the downstream `JSON.parse(updaterOutput)` consumes corrupted data with no signal that bytes were lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Decode updater output with the strict `decodeUtf8Input` helper (the same canonical approach already used across the codebase, e.g. #180861). When invalid UTF-8 is detected, the corruption is surfaced explicitly via a log line ("managed update updater stdout contained invalid UTF-8; retained a lossy copy") while still retaining a lossy copy so the string/JSON contract and the update flow never break. The `createHandoffLineReader` marker decode gets the same strict treatment.

The decoder binding is exposed to the spawned helper process through the sealed runtime module, which the helper already `require`s, so the fix works in the real child process and in the vm-sandboxed termination tests.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change for valid UTF-8 output (including multi-byte CJK and split-across-chunk sequences). Invalid UTF-8 is now detected and explicitly annotated instead of silently corrupted, making managed update diagnostics reliable.

## Evidence

### Committed regression (head passes, base fails)

`update-managed-service-handoff-termination.test.ts` now includes a malformed-stdout regression that drives a split multi-byte CJK sequence ("安装") interleaved with an invalid 0xFF byte through the shipped `runOwnedUpdateCommand` updater-output decode path and asserts the warning + intact CJK + completed settlement. The suite is 8/8 green on head; on the pre-fix base the same test fails because `Buffer.toString("utf8")` emits no warning. Bidirectionally verified (revert → 1 failure; restore → 8/8).

### Real staged-helper process proof (shipped entry, no vm sandbox)

Spawned a **real detached node process** running the real compiled `HANDOFF_SCRIPT`, which `require()`s the real staged **sealed runtime** (`<dir>/runtime/managed-handoff-runtime.mjs`, esbuild bundle exposing `decodeUtf8Input`), prepares a real SQLite lease DB via the shipped `prepareManagedHandoffLeaseStore`, acquires the lease, and drives a real updater child (latest-stable → candidate) that writes split multi-byte UTF-8 + an invalid 0xFF byte to stdout. Credentials/IPs/non-public endpoints redacted.

```
===== REAL-HELPER PROOF RESULTS =====
PASS  lease DB prepared
PASS  helper READY
PASS  helper exit 0
PASS  intact CJK decoded
PASS  invalid byte -> U+FFFD
PASS  retained-lossy warning logged
PASS  helper completed code=0
PASS  latest-stable->candidate transition
ALL PASS
--- handoff.log ---
managed update ownership transferred; validating while the gateway serves
starting managed update command: openclaw update
managed update update command pid=128508
{"status":"ok","after":"candidate","root":".../.openclaw-update-handoff","label":"安装�ok"}
managed update update command exited code=0 signal=null
managed update updater stdout contained invalid UTF-8; retained a lossy copy
managed update helper completed code=0
```

This establishes, through the staged helper's sealed-runtime loader with real subprocess I/O: ① the updater stdout 0xFF byte is rejected by strict `decodeUtf8Input` and produces the shipped warning, ② valid split multi-byte CJK (安装) is reconstructed intact, ③ the lossy copy still `JSON.parse`'s to `status:"ok"` and settlement completes (helper exit 0), ④ the latest-stable → candidate transition is performed (candidate.json written), with existing settings/data untouched.

### Other checks

- Sealed runtime binding chain verified: `decodeUtf8Input`/`Utf8InputError` resolve through the sealed module and the helper destructure.
- `createHandoffLineReader` still detects ASCII markers even when a chunk contains invalid bytes.
- oxlint clean on all changed files; no lockfile changes.

Reproducer: `pr-186033-evidence/proof-real-helper.mjs`.

prs.body:
Closes #183555
Depends on #181339; land the shared inline-narration presentation first.

## What Problem This Solves

Native completed-work headings omit operation counts, so readers must expand a section to learn what ran.

## User Impact

Collapsed headings show operation kinds and failed, blocked, skipped, or unknown outcomes. Expanded headings also show the total tool-call count. The shared disclosure serves both iOS and macOS, and preserves a supplied duration. Inline narration keeps separate work stretches untimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heading uses the same tool interpretation as the visible cards, including recorded outcomes, wrapper display identities, and prepared visibility. Calls are deduplicated within their run; fallback identities stay local to their source message. The existing disclosure owns expansion and wrapping, and all new heading strings use native localization.

Original implementation and regression work by @Marvinthebored; contributor commits are retained. Inline activity is decoded with the message contract; the transcript cache still clears transient activity before saving, so this does not change its storage schema.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI [40596049371](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40596049371), attempt 2, is green, including `ios-screenshots`, its evidence check, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Review follow-up: no actionable code findings remain; the requested new native runtime capture is a proof gap. Final-head validation uses focused sandboxed Swift tests, and no native app was launched on this host.

- The current main heading is duration-only. With the contributor implementation, production transcript projection reproduces a successful split read labeled “unknown” and two separate calls collapsing to one count. Both regressions now pass; all 51 focused summary, activity, completed-work, chunk, transcript-row, and serialization tests pass in the private OS sandbox.
- Targeted Swift lint and formatting pass; native localization inventory regeneration is unchanged. The existing demo transport has a pre-existing function-length violation in the broad lint scan; the five changed production files pass without violations.
- Isolated Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The cleanup removes the second tool-message interpretation path from the bubble renderer and delegates both consumers to the existing activity owner.
- Incremental diff against #181339: production +131, tests +130, generated localization inventory +22, docs +2. The initial contributor diff was production +114, tests +90, generated +22. Remaining production growth is the localized category/outcome heading plus run/source-scoped counting and shared orphan-result handling.
- The prior `ios-screenshots` failure (run 40209238887, job 121217016127) was simulator provisioning: watchOS 27.0 had two registered disk images. The first final-head screenshot attempt also failed, for a different simulator problem: [run 40596049371, job 122512796770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40596049371/job/122512796770) passed all four iPhone and all four iPad tests, then the Watch simulator returned to Shutdown during boot. A single targeted retry after that diagnosis passed the screenshot job and final CI gate on the same head. The collected phone/tablet chat images show the welcome screen, not the new work heading.

The before/after images below are the contributor's inspected, controlled iOS simulator comparison using synthetic command history. They precede the inline-narration stack and its untimed work stretches. prs.body:
Cached header display is preserved through reconnect: inspected signed-in warm reloads improve from **0/11 to 10/11 stable headers on both routes**, sharing displacement is **0 px**, and snapshot growth is **1.64% / 1.57%**. Chat hello remains **+42.49 ms** in the unprofiled comparison; the time-boxed profile below does not fully attribute that difference. This tradeoff is disclosed for maintainer review.

## Latest test-only follow-up: zero test growth

Head `26398e19efe6b944cebbed635e1aece64fe6edbb` rebases the lane onto current main and changes only `ui/src/components/viewer-facepile.test.ts`. The follow-up removes **35 net test lines** (55 added / 90 deleted), bringing the **entire PR to 0 net test lines** under the canonical ratchet patterns. No product code or `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` change. The lane's production delta remains +345 under the requested filter (+210 actual UI runtime); this follow-up adds zero production lines.

The test-audit pass inspected the facepile, presence projection/grouping, Activity-link and mounting owners, overlapping tests and history before editing. The consolidation retains every distinct behavior proof:

| Former case / assertion | Protected behavior | Remaining proof and reason for consolidation |
|---|---|---|
| `gates face links on host opt-in` plus `retains a participant avatar through metadata updates` | Opt-in hrefs, tooltip text/ARIA targeting, stable avatar and initials DOM, updated accessible name, retained focus and navigation using the updated label | One linked/unlinked table now checks the initial two-person facepile and updates one person in place. Both cases mounted the same production composition; duplicate setup is removed, all assertions remain. |
| `keeps collaboration UI dormant for a solo identity` plus the missing-user-ID self-exclusion case | Duplicate self tabs do not count as multiple people; an off-session second person does; the browser's incomplete row and another self tab remain excluded while Alice renders | One shared self-tab fixture drives both true/false predicate assertions and the rendering check. The old "dormant UI" case only called a predicate; its distinct checks remain explicitly exercised. |
| Shared-owner label table plus trusted/untrusted avatar-route table | Session/profile owner labels, permitted image route, rejected foreign origin, fallback initials | One presentation table keeps both owner variants and both original Ada URL inputs with independent expected image/label values. Repeated avatar mount/settlement is removed. |
| Cache-object identity comparison inside the ordered static-participant case | Incidental memo identity of an unrelated payload | Removed: that payload was never supplied to the component, which consumed `staticParticipants`. It could pass without the component exercising presence. Ordered profile/agent rendering, overflow, absence of viewer tagging and empty-list removal remain; projection semantics and namespace behavior retain their owner tests. The labels and hydrated agent-face assertions now share one settlement callback. |

Cached-avatar sharing/revisions/provenance and directory-demand checks remain in this file. Native cached-header stability, partial-presence handoff, live joins/leaves, inert sharing geometry and scope/sign-out retirement tests are unchanged. No production/test-support export or helper becomes orphaned.

Final local commands `pnpm test ui/src/components/viewer-facepile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` and `pnpm test ui/src/lib/presence-users.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` each passed **15 cases**, with wrapper wall times **4.00 s / 4.38 s**. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent local autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**; the reviewed file remains byte-identical after the mandatory final rebase. Linux/native proof and completed exact-head CI are reported below.


Linux proof used AWS `m7a.xlarge`, lease `cbx_4e3d7ec0b7e6`, [run_1fb47135b5aba674f3239781a9f5f1d3](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1fb47135b5aba674f3239781a9f5f1d3). The changed file and presence sibling passed **15/15 each** (command wall 6 s / 5 s), targeted lint passed, the full build passed, and native cached-header e2e passed **2/2 routes** (30 s command wall). The test-line ratchet passed with **net delta 0** despite inherited global debt (remote total 6,291,644; ceiling 6,291,318). All three test-audit deadcode phases were run: they fail on **identical diagnostic lists on candidate and pinned main `a479bc7f2443da646d5c220e6a78df9b3fbd4566`**. These are existing SQLite/agent export findings and 15 existing measurement/helper paths; the consolidation introduced no new orphan.

Exact-head [CI 40611012583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611012583) is **completed / failure: 39 passed, 24 skipped, 4 failed including the aggregate**. **`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passed.** All 15 consolidated facepile cases passed in CI. Remaining reds:

| CI check | Classification / control |
|---|---|
| [UI e2e 5/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611012583/job/122562808992) | Same inherited prompt `scroll` / `auto` failure, already matched on main in 10/10 focused and 2/2 full-shard runs per arm above. Separate lane owns it. Current shard: 509 passed / 1 failed. |
| [UI e2e 1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611012583/job/122562808966) | **Inherited** dictation microphone-picker route assertion: actual `/settings/talk`, expected `/settings/model-providers`. The exact case fails with the identical assertion on pinned main after its clean full build (1 failed / 8 filtered). Current CI shard: 572 passed / 1 failed. |
| [UI 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611012583/job/122562808997) | **Unreproduced; not classified as inherited.** Widget-card `retains video playback through title changes after the player loads` expects an iframe immediately after Play plus `flush()`, but receives null in CI. The unchanged widget file passes **26/26 on both main and head** with CI's pinned Bun/config; the exact case alone also passes **1/1 on each arm**. Main's recorded **593-file unit cohort passes all 6,373 tests**, including that case, at worker cap 3 and two-CPU affinity. This narrower cohort excludes the other projects in CI's Bun phase and runs on a 16-GiB host, so it is not a complete reproduction of the eight-GiB CI environment. The CI failure precedes execution of the changed facepile file. No product/test expectation was changed or CI job retried to hide it. |
| openclaw/ci-gate | Aggregates the three failures above. |

The first main unit-cohort attempt hit the include-file helper's existing non-literal-path guard before running tests; it is retained as a setup failure, not a product verdict. The verified replay used the same 593 recorded paths as explicit CLI filters and checked the final file count. Both candidate and main source checkouts remained clean. The focused main controls ran sequentially on the same lease after candidate proof. The lease is released; all owned fixture servers/browsers were retired. The remaining widget CI failure is disclosed for lead disposition; this lane stops before merge.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload of a chat or dashboard deep link cleared header viewers, then inserted sharing controls and moved the facepile. Campaign evidence described fourteen visible application states on a signed-in dashboard deep-link reload; this change addresses the header portion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scoped pane snapshot now owns at most three viewer display records, the overflow count, owner-viewing fact, and one sharing display mode. First-pane hydration consumes these facts with the transcript through the existing prewarm path. Self-only hello presence remains incomplete until the normalized full roster arrives. A late pane can read that completed roster from the existing client presence owner; no new presence store, subscription, or RPC is introduced.

The inert cached sharing trigger keeps the native control geometry until the admitted live control replaces it in the same commit. Explicit live permission revocation can still remove it. Known avatar URLs skip eager profile-directory resolution and reuse the existing avatar URL/HTTP cache. Display never waits for image loading. Cached facts grant no mutation authority.

This integrates the connect-first fix #185886 and the cached archived-session state from #185788. Both sets of optional facts survive the same cache preservation chain. Disposable projection version 7 resets older pane snapshots once; the existing scope/sign-out invalidation and pruning owners remain in charge. No new operator configuration, Gateway protocol, server schema, or durable server record.

## User Impact

Known viewers and sharing geometry remain on the cached page while the socket catches up, then real presence changes update in place.
