prs.title: fix(hooks): webhook and join-introduction turns no longer run with owner-only tools
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: webhook, mapped-hook, plugin-trigger and channel join-introduction agent turns run with owner-only tools (gateway, plugins, nodes, terminal, conversations_*, full sessions control and more) even though a hook token is ingress access, not an authenticated owner.

## User Impact

User impact: hook agent turns are no longer owners on embedded, Codex and CLI runtimes, so untrusted payload content can no longer drive owner-only tools. **Behavior change on upgrade:** hooks that used an owner-only tool lose it. Operators opt a hook back in with `hooks.mappings[].allowedOwnerTools` (or `hooks.allowedOwnerTools` for direct `/hooks/agent` requests). `openclaw doctor` shows a note for enabled hooks without a grant, and `openclaw security audit` warns on every grant (`hooks.owner_tools_granted`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/gateway/config-hooks.md`, `SECURITY.md` and the prompt-injection docs already say hook tokens grant ingress, not a sender identity. #81065 made CLI hook runs non-owner; a later general refactor (02182d5a303) dropped that without a hook-specific reason, and #91749 made a missing sender bit count as owner, so embedded hook turns kept every owner-only tool except `intent`. #183913 and #183987 pinned that surface deliberately and deferred the decision here.

- **One decision owner.** The execution context decides: `senderBitOf` returns `senderIsOwner: false` for every ingress principal (webhook, plugin hook, channel join), placement included. Embedded, Codex and the CLI loopback all read that bit, so there are no per-runtime checks. The old pins are updated on purpose.
- **Grant shape.** `allowedOwnerTools: string[]` on a mapping, plus top-level `hooks.allowedOwnerTools` for direct `/hooks/agent` (it has no mapping). It follows the existing hooks allowlist naming (`allowedAgentIds`, `allowedSessionKeyPrefixes`) and sits next to the mapping's other opt-in, `allowUnsafeExternalContent`. Unknown names fail config validation with the accepted list. Transforms cannot set or widen it, plugin triggers never carry one, and the context builder keeps only grantable names whatever produced the facts.
- **A grant does not make the turn an owner.** It only exempts the named tools from the owner-only denial. Message actions, MCP, memory provenance and every other owner-identity check stay non-owner. An earlier draft lifted the owner bit, and autoreview showed that leaked into those paths.
- **Grantable tools.** These are gated only by the owner-only refusal, which the grant lifts: `gateway`, `plugins`, `nodes`, `computer`, `screen`, `mobile_ui`, `terminal`, `openclaw`.
- **Non-grantable tools:**
  - `conversations_list`, `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`: they refuse any non-owner turn themselves, so a grant could not make them work.
  - `sessions`: it keeps its non-owner control-only mode; full control needs an owner identity.
  - `portal`: it keeps its non-owner mode, limited to the turn's own session target.
  - `intent`: standing intents always require an explicit owner identity.
  - `automations`: its scope comes from the execution context, so a hook turn may act only on its own automation.
- **Validation.** Any non-grantable or unknown name fails config validation with the accepted list; it is never silently dropped. A test pins the grantable list against the owner-only list, so a new owner-only tool needs its own grant decision.
- Join introductions already run with `toolsAllow: []`; non-owner there is defense in depth.
- **Known limit: plugin triggers.** Plugin triggers such as the IMAP trigger (#130230) are the same ingress principal in code (`gateway.hooks.plugin` → `plugin-hook`). They are non-owner on every runtime and have **no grant path**: the dispatcher drops any grant on a plugin dispatch. Per-tool owner identity for conversation and sessions grants is tracked separately.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- The hooks hardening audit findings moved verbatim from `audit-extra.sync.ts` to `audit-hooks.ts`, because the line-cap ratchet rejects growth in the 859-line file. The Doctor note lives in its own module for the same reason.
- Accepted edge: a grant is read when the hook request is accepted. A hooks config reload already refuses dispatch of accepted work (`isHooksConfigCurrent`), and a grant removed mid-turn applies to the next turn.
- Default mapping ids (`mapping-<n>`) appear only in audit text; grants travel with the accepted action, not with the id.
</details>

## Evidence

- **Crabbox AWS proof:** rerun pending on `95a19761d6f`, which changes only docs and a test. The previous head `9ff1c2db8e744bc39e8a7af2f836dd475f267553` passed: Provider `aws`, c7a.8xlarge, lease `cbx_fb7abac1650e` (released), run [run_3a2d28ed5c2b3f592fa32b8e75af8fda](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3a2d28ed5c2b3f592fa32b8e75af8fda), exit 0. Command: `crabbox run --provider aws --timing-json -- bash proof/4a2-remote.sh`. The proof script, its QA scenario and the mock-model step stay local and are not committed.
  - Phase A, QA suite with a real Gateway child and mock-openai. A direct `/hooks/agent` turn and a mapped hook turn that called the owner-only `plugins` tool got "plugins needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner". The same mapping with `allowedOwnerTools: [plugins]` reached the tool and listed plugins.
  - Phase B, upgrade on one state dir:
    - The `openclaw@2026.10.7` Gateway's hook turn reached `plugins` (`listedPlugins: true`).
    - This head's `doctor --fix` printed "Hook agent turns are not owners …" and how to grant a tool.
    - This head's Gateway ran the same hook with the same config and refused it (`refusedForOwner: true`).
    - After `allowedOwnerTools: ["plugins"]` was added as the note says, the hook reached the tool. `security audit --json` reported `hooks.owner_tools_granted` (warn).
    - `allowedOwnerTools: ["intent"]` failed `config validate` with the accepted list.
- Local QA suite (real Gateway child, mock-openai): a direct `/hooks/agent` turn and a mapped hook turn calling `plugins` were refused with "plugins needs the owner's authority"; the same mapping with `allowedOwnerTools: [plugins]` reached it and listed plugins.
- Local upgrade from `openclaw@2026.10.7` on one state dir: the v2026.10.7 Gateway's hook turn reached `plugins`. This head's `doctor --fix` printed the note. This head's Gateway refused the same hook. After adding `allowedOwnerTools: ["plugins"]` as the note says, the hook reached it and `security audit` reported `hooks.owner_tools_granted`. `allowedOwnerTools: ["intent"]` failed `config validate` with the accepted list.
- Static replay (`scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts`) over the maintainer's 110 stored jobs: rows identical between the merge base and this head (equal 98, loss 55, gain-intended 48, pause 12, retarget 4, all from earlier phases). **No gain-unexpected.** Stored jobs carry no ingress principal. That Gateway has no `hooks` config and no IMAP trigger, so no ingress losses there.
- Tests: `run.event-trigger-automations-scope` (embedded hook and plugin-trigger turns refused, grant exempts only the named tool, join intro non-owner), `execution-context-tool-policy` (embedded and CLI loopback, ungranted and granted), `execution-context`, `execution-context-owner-authority`, `hooks-mapping` (transforms cannot set or widen a grant), `config.hooks-module-paths` (every non-grantable name and unknown names fail validation), `audit-gateway-exposure`, `doctor-hooks-owner-tools-check`, `dangerous-tools`, `server.hooks`, `doctor-health-contributions`. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, and `config:docs:check` passes.
- Autoreview (Claude, because Codex CLI auth is unavailable on this host): the findings were addressed. Granted turns now stay non-owners, plugin dispatch strips grants, and the context keeps only grantable names.

<details><summary>Size</summary>

Against the merge base: production +386/−171, including the ~190-line verbatim audit move; tests +302/−41; docs +50/−3. Nothing is removed beyond the superseded "ingress keeps its surface" branches.
</details>

prs.title: improve(postgres): reuse prepared statements so PostgreSQL stores stop re-planning every query
prs.body:
Closes #183698

## What Problem This Solves

With the PostgreSQL engine, every parameterized store statement is sent as a new unnamed statement and parsed again on each call, so session turn writes spend a large share of each round trip re-preparing the same SQL.

## User Impact

User impact: agent and state stores on PostgreSQL commit session turns about 24% faster (one writer and four concurrent writers), with the same results and no configuration change. SQLite is unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge worker sent parameterized queries through node-postgres as unnamed statements, which repeat Parse on every execution. Each bridge connection now names its parameterized statements by SQL text, so the server parses each one once per session and reuses the prepared statement afterwards. Plan choice stays automatic: PostgreSQL may keep a generic plan or keep building custom plans per execution, as `plan_cache_mode = auto` decides.

- **Bounded:** at most 256 statements per connection (pgjdbc's default), least recently used is `DEALLOCATE`d.
- **Batches unchanged:** parameterless SQL keeps the simple protocol, which multi-statement batches need.
- **Schema identity:** the cache lives on one connection, whose `search_path` is its store namespace. PostgreSQL re-analyzes a prepared statement when `search_path` changes (for example `SET LOCAL search_path` during schema verification); the test covers it.
- **DDL on the same connection** (Doctor migrations) drops every cached statement right after it runs, so later statements in the same migration transaction re-prepare.
- **DDL on another connection** can change a cached statement's result type (`0A000 cached plan must not change result type`). An autocommit statement is re-prepared and run once more (it failed before executing). Inside a transaction it cannot be retried: that transaction fails once with `0A000` and the statement is re-prepared on next use. Base never hits this (it re-parses every time), so this is the one new failure mode; it needs a column change on a table while another connection holds a cached `SELECT *`-style statement on it in an open transaction. I did not find a path that runs schema DDL against a store a live Gateway is using, but I have not proven there is none.

node-postgres has no deallocate API and skips Parse for names in its per-connection `parsedStatements` map, so the worker removes names from that map whenever it deallocates them (`pg` is pinned at 8.23.1; the one type assertion for that map carries a `SAFETY:` note).

### Open design question: generic plans (not in this PR)

Forcing generic plans gave much more for turn writes in my earlier measurements (one writer 727 → 1,757 turns/10 s, see #183698), but forcing them globally made the memory vector search about 10% slower (50 vs 45 ms), because that query benefits from custom plans. If maintainers want that gain, the options are:

1. a role- or database-level `plan_cache_mode` that operators choose (no code; affects every query, including search), or
2. `SET plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan` only for named statements on hot write paths, keeping search on `auto` (needs a per-statement opt-in from the store owners).

I left this out so this PR is a pure statement-reuse change with default planning.

## Evidence

Base `8ad3d6f8922` (origin/main). Benchmarks ran at `cf802649e15`; the current head adds only the typed assertion and comment wording from review (the regression test was re-run on it and passes). The only difference between the two arms is `src/infra/postgres-sync/bridge.worker.ts` (base vs this branch), swapped in the same checkout. PostgreSQL 17.11 on a Mac mini (Unix socket, isolated database, `synchronous_commit=off`).

**Regression test** (`src/infra/postgres-sync/reuse.postgres.test.ts`, "parses each parameterized SQL text once per connection and survives DDL elsewhere"), real PostgreSQL:
- base: fails, `expected +0 to be 1` (no prepared statement on the connection after three identical calls)
- this branch: passes, along with the other 11 tests in the file

It also checks: the right schema's rows under a changed `search_path`, autocommit recovery after `ALTER TABLE` on another connection, one failure then recovery inside a transaction, and that DDL on its own connection drops the statements.

**Turn writes through the public owner** (`persistSessionTranscriptTurn`, two-message turns, gateway database role, agent+state on PostgreSQL), 10 s windows, interleaved base/fix, 6 runs each, 0 errors, load1 3–5:

| writers | base turns/10 s (median, range) | this PR | base p50 / p95 ms | this PR p50 / p95 ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1,159 (1,127–1,181) | **1,440** (1,298–1,594), +24% | 8.66 / 12.82 | 7.09 / 9.92 |
| 4 | 2,839 (2,672–4,016) | **3,525** (3,365–3,809), +24% | 13.75 / 20.98 | 11.21 / 15.70 |

**Memory search, no regression with default planning** (`scripts/bench-memory-search.mjs`, production SQL through the bridge, 20,000 chunks, 100 queries per mode after warmups, 2 runs per arm, interleaved; mean of the per-run p50/p95):

| mode | base p50 / p95 ms | this PR p50 / p95 ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vector | 166.2 / 170.9 | 166.0 / 169.7 |
| keyword | 12.8 / 14.3 | 12.4 / 13.5 |
| hybrid | 180.8 / 184.2 | 178.7 / 182.8 |

All 600 per-query result hashes are identical between base and this PR. (This is the cost that forcing generic plans globally made worse, so it was the regression to check.)

For context, the turn round-trip work in #182810 measured bridge transport at 0.03–0.07 ms per trip on the same base ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182810#issuecomment-6405188150)). That leaves per-statement parse (and planning) as the remaining per-trip cost; this removes the repeated parse.

**Shipped entry point, isolated Gateway, real model** (CLI built from this head, `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (98582b6)`; a fresh state dir with the `state` and `agent` families on PostgreSQL 17.11 over a Unix socket, isolated database and role; `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` created the schemas; `openclaw gateway run` on a loopback port with token auth; every turn sent with `openclaw agent --agent main --session-id named-proof-real --message …` through the Gateway). The model is `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` served through the bundled `anthropic` plugin's Claude Code CLI backend (`agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`), a real hosted model; the Gateway log shows `cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5` for each turn. Timestamps are local, replies are verbatim:

```
06:57:54  gateway ready (6 s); worker startup state: postgresBridgeCount=4
06:58:00  turn 1  status ok  5.3 s  "READY"
06:58:01  turn 2  status ok  1.5 s  "My previous reply was the word READY."
06:58:02  turn 3  status ok  1.4 s  "Red, Yellow, Blue"
06:58:03  ALTER TABLE <agent schema>.transcript_events ADD COLUMN named_probe int   (separate psql connection, Gateway running)
06:58:04  turn 4  status ok  1.5 s  "I just listed red, yellow, and blue."
06:58:04  ALTER TABLE <agent schema>.transcript_events DROP COLUMN named_probe
06:58:05  turn 5  status ok  1.4 s  "1, 2, 3, 4, 5"
06:58:07  turn 6  status ok  1.5 s  "6"
06:58:08  Gateway SIGTERM (exited after 1 s); gateway run again; ready after 6 s
06:58:20  turn 7  status ok  5.6 s  "READY"        (first reply recalled across the restart)
          transcript_events rows in the agent schema: 15
          Gateway log: 0 lines matching error|0A000|26000 (363 lines across both Gateway lives)
07:00:36  Gateway started a third time: `gateway call sessions.list` returns the one session;
          `gateway call chat.history` returns 14 messages, the seven user/assistant pairs above in order
```

The only SQLite files in that state dir are the 8 KB anchors that PostgreSQL-backed stores keep; the transcript exists only in PostgreSQL.

**Other checks:** the `src/infra/postgres-sync`, `src/infra/database-engine` and `src/state` PostgreSQL suites on real PostgreSQL pass, including the Doctor version-migration rollbacks. The only failures were 9 tests that need `CREATE DATABASE`/`CREATE ROLE`, which my test role lacks (they fail in setup). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files pass.

An independent automated review of the branch found no actionable issues; its one open question (anything else deallocating statements behind the cache, such as `DISCARD ALL`) does not apply: nothing in `src/` or `extensions/` issues `DISCARD` or `DEALLOCATE` besides this worker.

**Not measured:** provider transports other than the Claude Code CLI backend, a Gateway running for hours (server memory per backend is bounded by the 256 limit, but I have not watched it over a long run), and PostgreSQL versions other than 17.

**Simplification pass:** an earlier draft had a separate `statement-cache.ts` module plus a unit test against a fake server. I folded the cache into the bridge worker that owns the connection and dropped the fake-server test in favor of the single real-PostgreSQL regression test. Delta vs merge base: +98/-1 production lines in one file, +37 test lines in an existing suite.

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(mattermost): add allowBots mention policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost has no equivalent of Slack's `allowBots` policy. When thread participation is enabled, implicit activation also applies to other bot authors, so an allowlisted bot can trigger a turn in an engaged thread without a new explicit mention.

## Solution

- Add `allowBots: true | false | "mentions"` at account and group scope.
- Identify bot authors through the post's `from_bot` property (both boolean and Mattermost's string form) or the Mattermost user's `is_bot` field.
- In `"mentions"` mode, require explicit activation for bot authors even when thread participation would admit a human follow-up. Authorized control-command behavior is preserved.
- Keep `allowBots: false` for disabling bot-triggered turns and the default `true` for existing behavior.
- Avoid a new sender lookup in the default mode when Mattermost already supplies `sender_name`.
- Document the setting and regenerate channel config metadata.

Human thread participation and existing sender/channel restrictions remain unchanged.

The intentional `+4` channel config-surface entries are the root/account and group variants of the new `allowBots` policy (including account-scoped group overrides). This is required for Slack-compatible policy precedence, not an unrelated budget increase; the generated config docs baseline is refreshed with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19/19 passed on the fixed tree; the same regression test fails on the pre-fix schema (1 failed / 18 passed), then passes after restoration.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent read-only review (xai/grok-4.7) found two P1 issues; both were fixed and covered with regressions for string/boolean `from_bot`, failed sender lookup, and group precedence. No post-fix independent re-review is claimed.
- Live Mattermost API contract check: the tested bot account returns `is_bot: true`; the tested human account omits the flag, which the `=== true` check handles.

## Local environment gaps / CI-required proof

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-posts.bot-threads.test.ts` includes the behavioral regressions, but the local suite did not start: its compiled worker was killed with exit 137 twice on the 8 GiB host, including with a 2 GiB heap cap. No passing behavioral result is claimed locally.
- Targeted `run-oxlint` did not reach linting: plugin-sdk boundary dts preparation timed out after 300 seconds. The source tree was verified clean of interruption artifacts.
- PR CI is required for the behavioral suite, lint/typecheck, and broader compatibility proof.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agent.run can carry a fallback ladder so a pinned model no longer dead-ends on a quota 429
prs.body:
Closes #186418
Related: #151980, #141115, #181981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation caller that pins a model on the WebSocket agent.run request loses the agent's configured model-fallback ladder, so a quota-class 429 ends the run instead of advancing to the next candidate.

The request schema had no way to express a chain, so the only lever an automation caller had was to pin a model - which silently suppresses the configured ladder. Operators who configured a working fallback chain for the agent had no caller-side way to keep it alive.

## User Impact

User impact: automation callers can now send an explicit fallback ladder with their agent.run request, so a provider quota window on the pinned model no longer ends the run - the run advances to the next candidate the caller named.

This is opt-in and additive. A request that pins a model and sends no ladder behaves exactly as before: the pin stays strict and the configured chain stays suppressed, which is the contract #151980 asks to keep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already had the pieces to carry a run-scoped chain, but the wire protocol could not express one. Rather than relax the strict-pin contract, this change adds an explicit field so the caller states the chain it wants:

- agent.run accepts an optional fallbacks array of provider/model refs. Entries are trimmed, de-duplicated, and bounded to 16.
- The ladder is authorized exactly like a model override: a caller without the model-override scope is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and a clear message.
- Every named model is checked against the agent's visible model set and the caller's operator authority before the run starts, so a caller cannot widen model access by naming extra chain entries.
- The chain travels with the run as a request-scoped override, so it is used for this run only and does not become session state.

The request-level pin remains the primary model; the ladder only adds candidates behind it.

## Evidence

Focused test runs, both green on this branch (rebased onto main at d2491817):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 44 passed (44)

Typecheck:

    pnpm tsgo:test:root -> exit 0 (all root shards)
    pnpm tsgo:test:packages -> exit 0

New coverage:

- src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts - a request that carries both a pinned model and a ladder keeps the ladder and reports it as request-scoped; a request with a ladder but no model-override scope is rejected; a request with no ladder leaves the override unset.
- src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts - a request-supplied ladder survives a pinned model during model selection, and a request-supplied chain that names a model the agent cannot use is rejected before the run starts.

Behavior with no fallbacks in the request is unchanged, so existing agent.run callers are unaffected.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep foreign launchd job scan working above 64 candidate labels
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #183805

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where macOS hosts running more than 64 user-defined LaunchAgents with `ai.openclaw.*` labels lost the foreign-launchd-job diagnostic entirely: `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw doctor`, and the Gateway restart-storm attribution all degraded because the scanner threw "Too many OpenClaw launchd jobs to inspect safely" before inspecting anything.
- The same all-or-nothing behavior also discarded already-inspected findings when the 10-second inspection budget ran out mid-scan.
- **Related:** #183805 (reported against v2026.10.7, 157d8c2); clawsweeper review recommended bounded partial findings with an explicit disclosure of skipped jobs while preserving removal safeguards.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `findForeignLaunchdJobs` now degrades to a bounded partial scan instead of aborting: it inspects the first 64 sorted candidate labels and returns those findings plus an explicit skipped-job count; the same applies when the time budget runs out mid-scan. `gateway status` (new partial-inspection warning), `doctor` (disclosure line in the foreign-jobs note), and the restart-storm warning (disclosure appended to the message) all keep working and tell the user the results are partial.
- **Out of scope:** No ownership marker, no new configuration, and no documentation change reserving the `ai.openclaw.*` prefix (the issue's alternative requests); per-job `launchctl print` failures still surface as inspection errors rather than being silently degraded.
- **Highest-risk area:** removal authority. It is unchanged: `repairForeignLaunchdJob` still performs a fresh native inspection before any `disable`/`bootout`, and uninspected (skipped) jobs are never removal candidates.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The existing classifier and repair regression suite is kept intact; new regressions only assert reporting behavior.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** On a host with 65 or more `ai.openclaw.*` candidate labels, `openclaw gateway status` and `openclaw doctor` report the inspected foreign jobs plus an explicit "N candidate OpenClaw launchd jobs were not inspected; these results are partial" line instead of aborting the check; the restart-storm warning keeps its likely-job attribution and appends the same disclosure.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/daemon/launchd-foreign-jobs.ts` (`findForeignLaunchdJobs`, new `formatUninspectedForeignLaunchdJobs`), the consumer disclosures in `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.launchd.ts` / `status.print.ts` (covered by the new `status.launchd.test.ts` and the partial-scan case in `status.print.test.ts`), `src/commands/doctor-foreign-launchd-jobs.ts`, `src/daemon/restart-storm.ts`, and the regressions named "foreign launchd scan bounds" plus the "discloses uninspected jobs" cases across the four affected suites.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux dev worktree; the scanner logic runs unmodified with `process.platform` stubbed to `darwin` and only the `launchctl` process boundary mocked, which is the same harness the existing foreign-job suite uses (launchd itself is macOS-only).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # regression tests (written first; both failed on the unmodified scanner, see below)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/launchd-foreign-jobs.test.ts
  # format + lint + affected test suites + core typecheck (validate.sh)
  pnpm exec oxfmt --write <changed files>
  pnpm exec oxlint <changed files>
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts src/commands/doctor-foreign-launchd-jobs.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-foreign-jobs.process.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-foreign-jobs.test.ts src/daemon/restart-storm.test.ts
  pnpm tsgo:core
  # review follow-up: mock-export ratchet with the merge-base rev from the review
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base 397abd9b15725ce983ea1f36dc1e9bb8244acd18
  # and against the rebased base (origin/main @ 2649110d60a)
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base origin/main
  # failing CI shard reproduced locally and re-run green after the fix
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
   Test Files  2 passed | 1 skipped (3)   # vitest.daemon.config.ts (launchd-foreign-jobs, restart-storm; process test is darwin-only)
        Tests  40 passed | 2 skipped (42)
   Test Files  3 passed (3)              # vitest.cli.config.ts (status.launchd, status.print, status.gather)
        Tests  73 passed | 2 skipped (75)

   ✓ printDaemonStatus > warns when the foreign launchd job inspection was partial

   ✓ Doctor foreign launchd jobs > reports the partial scan even when no inspected job is foreign
   [validate] 全部通过 ✅                # oxfmt + oxlint + affected vitest suites + tsgo:core

- **Observed result after fix:** with 65 candidate labels the scanner returns the 64 lexically-first inspected jobs plus `skippedJobCount: 1` and no longer throws; when the time budget runs out it returns the findings accumulated so far plus the uninspected remainder; status, Doctor, and the restart-storm warning all disclose the partial scan; removal still requires per-job fresh native re-verification.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep guest access guidance in Profile without Inbox warnings
prs.body:
Related: #157182
Related: #182941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: restricted guests see expected permission limits as Inbox warnings, while role-limited members can be offered an admin request that device approval cannot fulfill.

## User Impact

Your access in Settings → Profile explains the current role and device limits. Guest Inbox stays quiet, and Request admin appears only when the assigned role allows it; separate device approval is still required. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway adds optional `hello-ok.auth.roleAllowsAdmin` from the existing role-policy owner. It is presentation metadata, not authorization. Existing clients ignore the additive field, and absent metadata keeps existing upgrade behavior. Profile and Inbox use the same upgrade owner and controls; pending requests retire when the role ceiling becomes guidance. RPC authorization is unchanged.

The conflict with current main was resolved by preserving main's stronger sidebar alignment assertions. Protocol/schema and native models were regenerated through their owners, with no tracked generated delta. Operator-scope and pairing docs describe the behavior.

## Evidence

The role-ceiling runtime regression failed on base: a pending request remained requesting instead of showing role guidance. The Chromium reproduction also failed on base because a role-limited member was offered Request admin. Both pass with the repair.

200 focused tests passed across the upgrade owner, Profile, Inbox, Gateway auth, and protocol consumers. UI typecheck, targeted typed lint, formatting, diff checks, native protocol generation/determinism checks, and the test budget passed. Independent diff-scoped review through P2 found no actionable findings.

All 16 Chromium browser tests passed (223.1s, excluding cold build). The isolated real-Gateway case passed in 88.4s: synthetic guest → quiet Inbox and Profile guidance → real role promotion → separate browser pairing approval → reload with admin access. Mock-Gateway siblings cover role ceilings, dismissal/reload, pending requests, errors, and unadvertised methods. The real Gateway, proxy, browser, and fresh state were cleaned up by the fixture.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep open node skill watches from deferring restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway whose workspace is backed by a node waits the full 300 s restart deferral, then forces the restart, for every config edit that needs a restart.

## User Impact

User impact: config edits that need a Gateway restart apply in a few seconds on node-backed workspaces, as they already do on local workspaces, instead of after a forced restart five minutes later. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remote Skills watcher holds an idle `ws:node.invoke` request open for the life of its watch, and restart deferral counts every open request, so the deferral can never end on its own. Long-lived subscriptions should not hold back a restart; drain still waits for them to close.

## Details

A Gateway with a node-backed workspace (`plugins.entries.file-transfer.config.workspaces`) defers every restart-kind config change for the full restart deferral budget (300 s), then forces the restart. The same edit on a Gateway with a local workspace restarts in about 2 s.

## Root cause

- The remote Skills watcher (`src/skills/runtime/refresh-remote.ts`) keeps a `workspace.skills` watch open through `openNodeDuplex`. Its in-process `node.invoke` dispatch admits a Gateway root (`ws:node.invoke`) that lives as long as the watch.
- Restart deferral, suspension and idle checks count every active root, so this idle subscription always counts as one active Gateway request.
- The watcher stops only when restart drain begins, and drain begins only after the deferral ends. So the deferral always runs until its timeout.

## Reproduction

Released runtime build (2026.10.7), plain `openclaw gateway run`, a paired `openclaw node run` with the file-transfer commands, and `workspaces.main` bound to that node:

- `gateway.restart.preflight` after binding returns `1 active gateway request(s): ws:node.invoke`. It returns no blockers before the binding.
- `config.patch` of `tools.gatewayPolicy.allow` logs `config change requires gateway restart (tools.gatewayPolicy) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete`, then `restart still deferred after 30022ms with 1 gateway request(s) active`. No restart happens within 60 s.
- The deferral ends only when the node disconnects (`remote skills watcher stopped ... node disconnected (workspace.skills)`).

## Change

- `runAsGatewaySubscription(run)` marks the roots opened inside `run` as long-lived subscriptions. The caller must stop the subscription on the restart drain signal.
- Subscription roots do not count as active root work until restart drain begins. After that they count again, so drain still waits for the watch invocation to close. Every root-count consumer gets this rule: restart deferral and preflight, suspension, idle tasks, and the prepared-restart admission check.
- The remote Skills watcher opens its watch inside `runAsGatewaySubscription`. It already stops on the drain signal.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/skills/runtime/refresh.workspace.test.ts`: a remote subscription whose invocation holds a `ws:node.invoke` root leaves `rootRequests` at 0. After `markGatewayRestartDraining` it is aborted and still counted until it closes. The test fails on main (`rootRequests` 1) and passes with the fix.
- Touched suites: `src/skills/runtime/refresh.workspace.test.ts`, `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts`, `src/process/gateway-work-admission.continuation.test.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-active-work.test.ts`, `src/infra/restart-coordinator.test.ts` all pass (3 Vitest shards).
- Source-built Gateway and node, same reproduction: `pnpm build` checkout, `openclaw gateway run` plus a paired `openclaw node run`, same steps as the reproduction:
  - main: after binding, preflight reports `1 active gateway request(s): ws:node.invoke`. The restart-kind patch is still deferred after 60 s (`restart still deferred after 30007ms with 1 gateway request(s) active`).
  - this branch: after binding and after `skills.status`, preflight reports `safe to restart now`. The same patch logs `all operations and replies completed; restarting gateway now` and the Gateway restarts 2.65 s after the patch.

## Risks

- A subscription root no longer blocks suspension. The watch stays open while the host is suspended, as other idle connections do.
- Work started inside the subscription's own async chain shares its root, so that work is also not counted. Change events reach the watcher on the node connection's request chain, not on the subscription chain.
- The Memory workspace watch (`workspace.memory`) opens a node duplex in the same way, but it does not stop on the restart drain signal. This change leaves it unmarked. It needs its own drain retirement first, so it is better done as a follow-up.

prs.title: chore(agents): cover final system prompt hook context
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

**Problem:** The embedded runner has no regression test proving that `before_agent_run` sees system-context mutations made by `before_prompt_build`.

**Why now:** OpenClaw 2026.9.4 passed a stale pre-assembly system prompt to the gate; current `main` fixed the behavior incidentally, but the contract remains unprotected.

**Value:** Plugin policies can rely on the documented final-system-prompt contract without a repeat of the stale-snapshot regression.

**Fix:** Add one production-path embedded-runner test that injects a marker, captures `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt`, and compares it with the model session prompt.

**Scope:** One test file, 26 added lines, no runtime or public API changes.

**Risk:** Test-only; the main risk is coupling to setup details, mitigated by asserting only the public hook contract and final session prompt.

**Proof:** Current-main source inspection, historical stale-path comparison, a shipped `openclaw agent --local` trace through an isolated synthetic plugin/provider, the test-line ratchet, `git diff --check`, and PR CI.

**Non-goals:** No runtime change, no second policy gate, and no worker-placement changes.

**Maintainer ask:** Confirm this is the right embedded-runner boundary for preserving the documented hook contract.

## What Problem This Solves

The embedded runner lacks regression coverage proving that `before_agent_run` receives the final system prompt after `before_prompt_build` system-context mutations.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Plugin authors gain regression coverage for the documented final-system-prompt contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

In OpenClaw 2026.9.4, the runner captured `systemPromptText` before prompt assembly, so `before_prompt_build.prependSystemContext` reached model inference while `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt` still contained the earlier snapshot. Current `main` [refreshes the prompt after assembly](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts#L213), behavior introduced incidentally by [729c6b1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/729c6b1cc3d0f4aecfceb9af36a815acbdc8f799).

The new test exercises the complete embedded-runner path rather than manually piping one hook result into another. It injects a synthetic marker from `before_prompt_build`, captures the next gate event, and verifies that both the gate and final model session receive the same prompt. This would fail against the [2026.9.4 stale snapshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a9d69d/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts#L101-L102) while preserving the current runtime unchanged.

This is separate from [#182142](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182142), which covers final prompt admission for worker-placed sessions.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Current `main` at `fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e` — verified that the post-assembly refresh remains in place and no runtime patch is needed.
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e` — passed with 144 lines of slack after rebasing onto the current shrink-ratchet baseline.
- Shipped-entry-point trace on OpenClaw `2026.10.3` using isolated state, a synthetic local plugin, and a loopback mock OpenAI-compatible provider:
  - `before_prompt_build` prepended `WORKSHOP_GOVERNANCE_CONTEXT_V1`.
  - `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt` contained the marker (`7735` bytes; SHA-256 `9a32eb7aa63841e038daa0a0a394d3c96233bd5cbda0209c8e7cf1eeb8fc1e04`).
  - The actual model-bound `/v1/chat/completions` system/developer payload also contained the marker (`7350` bytes; SHA-256 `8efd329a52925297f727b78c5bf8bd03391861d68453c5686738ffb7d1f8c928`). Transport serialization changes the byte shape; the exact internal gate/session equality is the assertion added by this PR.
  - The embedded runner returned `proof-ok`; no external provider, credential, private conversation, or production Gateway was used.
- Focused command attempted: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
  - Local result: blocked before test collection because the prepared dependency tree has TypeScript `7.1.0-dev.20260922.1`, while current `main` requires `7.1.0-dev.20261016.1`; the runner failed resolving `typescript/fs`.

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...

Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

(no issues)

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.


---

prs.title: fix: cold source builds exceed memory budget during declaration emit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold source builds can exhaust memory during native TypeScript 7 declaration emission. Node's heap setting does not bound the Go compiler child. A per-child Go target must also account for declaration groups admitted concurrently.

## User Impact

Source builders get an availability-sensitive soft Go memory target for declarations. Explicit caller `GOMEMLIMIT` remains authoritative. There is no runtime or configuration migration.

## Implementation

Rebased onto `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`; current candidate is `078fe921e196b2255dfc228d4834fce5f5e58a97`.

- Keep main's async TS7 API, filesystem boundary, publication and compiler cleanup unchanged. The API has no environment option, so the tsdown worker receives the environment inherited by its native API child.
- Resolve 60% of effective available capacity once, including host availability and cgroup constraints. The staged writer divides that Go-managed share between its selected one or two workers; direct CLI builds account for explicit `--concurrency`.
- Preserve caller overrides. Runtime-only and declaration-disabled builds receive no automatic Go limit. Watch mode receives no automatic limit because tsdown ignores its concurrency setting there.
- Include the policy module in declaration cache inputs.

`GOMEMLIMIT` is soft and excludes non-Go memory; the remaining 40% is a sizing allowance, not a guaranteed RSS reserve. This is a declaration-memory fix, not a claim that a full cold build fits 10 GiB. Runtime-bundling concurrency remains separate in #157739, as [obviyus's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157992#issuecomment-5988468065) identified.

## Evidence

- Memory regressions: **5/5 passed**, 2.31 s real wall time including runner startup.
- Build-wrapper regressions: **88/88 passed**, 4.61 s real wall time including runner startup.
- Related compiler boundary, subprocess, declaration-resolution and native-TypeScript suites: **41 passed, 6 platform-specific skips**. The async emitter itself is unchanged.
- Canonical changed-file checks passed: script and root-test typechecks, formatting, scoped lint, declaration/dependency guards and dead-export scans. Final script and root-script typechecks and scoped lint also passed after the last concurrency adjustment. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review of the complete candidate diff against the pinned base found no remaining P2-or-higher issues. The canonical autoreview helper was attempted but returned `reviewer_unavailable` after authentication failed; it did **not** produce a passing review.
### Current-head real behavior proof

Candidate `078fe921e196b2255dfc228d4834fce5f5e58a97`, Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.5.1, TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20260920.1. Each cell used a disposable no-swap cgroup. The detector matched the exact installed compiler path and SHA-256, not a basename assumption. This package's executable is named `tsc`; the actual declaration children used `--api --async`.

[Full proof run 37273712838](https://github.com/Olli0103/openclaw/actions/runs/37273712838), harness `1775a5b280cc88848d70593de3a2d977aededf95`:

| Cell | Result | Command wall time | Cgroup peak | Observed async compiler target |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Full cold `pnpm build`, 13 GiB | Passed | 825.829 s | 9.624 GiB | 24 serial children, 7669–7842 MiB |
| Full cold `pnpm build`, caller `GOMEMLIMIT=6GiB`, 13 GiB | Passed | 835.984 s | 9.112 GiB | All 24 children preserved `6GiB` |
| Two nonempty canonical extension partitions, 13.75 GiB | Passed | 173.423 s | 10.936 GiB | Two overlapping async children, both `3993MiB` |

The parallel cell used the same staged declaration writer and explicitly reduced Node heaps to 5120 MiB, admitting two nonempty canonical extension partitions. It observed both compiler children from 5.416 s until approximately 159 s. It is not proof of default-heap parallel admission on a larger host.

All three cells recorded zero OOM/OOM-kill deltas, zero container swap use, no timeouts and no lingering sampled workers. Compiler RSS is distinct from the soft Go target; the parallel aggregate sampled compiler RSS peaked at approximately 9.324 GiB.

Complete output comparison covered 24,654 entries across 19 roots, including 647 declaration files. File inventories and hashes matched except the two timestamp-bearing build-stamp files. Only `dist/.buildstamp`'s `builtAt` and `dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp`'s `syncedAt` were normalized; all raw hashes and both named differences are retained in `comparison.json`. There were no unexplained differences. This is not a claim of raw byte-for-byte identity of timestamps.

[Focused run 37271810502](https://github.com/Olli0103/openclaw/actions/runs/37271810502) separately passed the base declaration group in a 10 GiB no-swap cgroup, 80.538 s, 7.558 GiB cgroup peak, observed async child `GOMEMLIMIT=6142MiB`, zero OOM/OOM-kill events.

[Runtime-only smoke recovery 37278655660](https://github.com/Olli0103/openclaw/actions/runs/37278655660), same candidate and harness `b184981251648f2e807758f708f46a6be1a58846`, passed built CLI version, built status-runtime tests, isolated loopback Gateway `/readyz` with `ready=true` and `/healthz` with `ok=true`, then graceful shutdown. The earlier smoke asserted the wrong readiness JSON field and is retained as a failed harness attempt. The recovery did not repeat declarations or the memory proof.

### Full-suite limitations

The full proof workflow is **failed**, not an all-green validation claim. Its contained `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` both reached their 2700 s deadline and were terminated. Both recorded zero OOM/OOM-kill deltas. `check` also failed the SQLite-worker guard because `rg` was absent, and the max-lines guard reported a stale baseline entry. Its 104-package lock validation did not complete. `test` recorded assertion failures before termination, including root-user refusal and a GitHub fetch failure in the network-disabled container. These logs do not establish that every failure is environmental or base-side; no passing full suite or exact-base reproduction is claimed.

Full check/test clearance requires a suitably provisioned non-root, network-capable validation route and classification of remaining assertion failures. No full build or memory stress was run on the production Mac mini.

## Historical Evidence and Remaining Limits

[Run 36148840191](https://github.com/Olli0103/openclaw/actions/runs/36148840191) passed a single cold declaration group on old head `726dea10b3e54389935e0c27744d2cfc35763dd5` inside a 10 GiB no-swap cgroup. That predates main's async emitter and is **not current-head or full-build proof**. Earlier contributor measurements and [run 36108835114](https://github.com/Olli0103/openclaw/actions/runs/36108835114) are historical for the same reason.

The standard runner is not a 24 GiB host. A separately labeled lowered-Node-heap parallel cell can demonstrate shared worker environments, but cannot establish default-heap parallel admission on a larger host. Current-head full `pnpm build` has passed. Full `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` have not passed on the disposable proof host; their failed logs and deadlines are described above. No unconditional 6 GiB or 10 GiB full-build claim is made.

Closes #157783

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and local test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-document.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated service capped at 50% CPU and 6 GiB RAM, final command wall times were 558.46 s and 64.49 s respectively (Vitest-reported durations: 492.82s and 45.86s). The persisted-authority scenarios exercise the real persistence/projection/dispatcher boundary with a causal preparation barrier, not sleeps or a mocked authority decision. CI seconds are not yet measured; these resource-capped local times are not CI estimates.

The old-source regression runs failed as expected in 866.35 s (authorization) and 51.30 s (page errors/retry). Production files were restored and their checksums verified afterward.

All verification used a separate checkout and private test state/config under resource limits. The live Gateway was not restarted, reconfigured, deployed to, or used as a test target.

</details>

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

The public `sessionActions` bridge still needs maintainer sponsorship and a long-term owner. This is an updated review candidate, not a merge request or a waiver of exact-head CI, screenshots, or owner review.

prs.title: fix: batch canonical transcript archive migration transactions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's canonical transcript archive migration opened two immediate SQLite transactions per archive, including archives whose blobs did not need a rewrite. On installations with hundreds of historical archives, each transaction repeats maintenance and update-admission checks while Doctor has the Gateway stopped. Closes #161734.

## Change

Archives are planned in bounded batches of 32. A first SQLite transaction validates and commits changed canonical blobs as **unpublished**, recording original publication timestamps in a small recovery journal. File repair then runs outside the SQLite write transaction. A second transaction restores publication timestamps only for verified files, advances the cursor, and removes only settled journal receipts; missing-file receipts persist until the file returns. If file repair or cursor commit fails, the rewritten rows remain unpublished. On a later run, journal recovery is independent of the caller's batch cursor and tolerates deleted, inserted, or independently rewritten archive rows without restoring stale timestamps. Directive and media migrations share the recovery key, so either owner first settles a pending published row before applying its own transform. A completed directive cursor still admits pending journal recovery, and a later transform of a pending blob carries its original timestamp forward only when the receipt matches the prior blob hash. Maintenance authority is checked at each write boundary and before atomic file publication. The two per-owner journal key names existed only on earlier unmerged heads of this PR; neither current main nor a release tag contains them, so the shared key has no deployed-key migration to perform.

## Evidence

### Exact head `81ee4634e87`

- ClawSweeper's in-progress-cursor finding was reproduced on `c94bac23586`: with an unresolved missing-copy receipt before an `archives` cursor and another archive still after it, Doctor returned `warnings: []`. The integration case failed before the fix and now verifies warning-bearing retries, then file repair, publication timestamp restoration, receipt clearance, and no warning.
- Recovery warnings now reach the in-progress migration result. Identical warnings from journal recovery and the later batch scan are deduplicated; the existing media-migration cases caught that overlap. 48/48 focused tests across four affected files passed on this commit. Core and infra-test typechecks, changed-file type-aware lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. No full local suite was run.
- This commit changes warning propagation only. The copied-existing-Zstd production-helper trace below was measured on `70d446db3a2` and remains earlier-head evidence. Hosted CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review are pending. Published-updater → candidate Doctor validation and acceptance of the durable journal remain maintainer-owned under the existing [handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161900#issuecomment-5914768671).

### Earlier-head evidence on `c94bac23586`

- ClawSweeper's completed-cursor missing-copy finding was reproduced on `70d446db3a2`: a pending receipt survived, but Doctor returned `warnings: []` while the archive file was absent. Recovery now returns a bounded missing-copy summary and path example through Doctor on every retry. After the copy returns, Doctor repairs it, restores the original publication timestamp, clears the receipt, and returns no warning.
- The new integration case calls `migrateHistoricalTranscriptDirectives` with a completed cursor and a missing copy. It verifies two warning-bearing retries followed by file repair and warning clearance. The pre-fix case failed as expected. 46/46 focused tests across four affected files passed on this head; Core and infra-test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. No full local suite was run.
- This head changes warning propagation, not the previously proved blob rewrite or journal recovery mechanism. The copied existing-Zstd trace below was measured on `70d446db3a2` and remains earlier-head evidence. Hosted CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review are pending. Published-updater → candidate Doctor validation and acceptance of the durable journal remain maintainer-owned; the existing [handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161900#issuecomment-5914768671) requests both.

### Earlier-head evidence on `70d446db3a2`

- The two ClawSweeper P2 cases were reproduced as failing regressions on `3b3dae004763`: a complete directive cursor skipped pending recovery, and a second transform of a missing-file pending blob lost its original timestamp. Both pass on this head.
- 45/45 focused tests across archive batching/recovery, canonical media archives, historical transcript directives, and the new complete-cursor integration test. Core and infra-test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. No full local suite was run.
- Exact-head production-helper trace on a disposable copy containing eight existing published Zstd archives. One archive file was removed in the copy. Two sequential transforms changed its pending canonical blob while the file stayed absent; SQLite was then closed and reopened, the stale file was repaired, and the original timestamp, blob digest, file bytes, and journal clearance were verified. No live database or serving Gateway was modified:

```json
{"head":"70d446db3a2","copiedExistingZstdArchives":8,"twoTransformsWhileFileMissing":true,"reopenedDatabaseBeforeRecovery":true,"originalPublicationRestored":true,"blobAndFileDigestVerified":true,"journalCleared":true}
```

- On the previous head, `build-artifacts` failed because generated `extensions/workboard/openclaw.plugin.json` differed from committed bytes. Both real-Gateway UI jobs stopped in prebuilt setup on a dirty checkout before running tests; a large Node shard failed a Gateway subscription assertion, while its infra-storage shard passed. These jobs do not exercise the archive migration diff. Hosted CI for this new head remains pending and is not claimed green.
- Published-updater → candidate Doctor validation on copied existing state and explicit maintainer acceptance of the durable `schema_meta` journal remain open. The [maintainer handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161900#issuecomment-5914768671) requests both. This helper trace does not substitute for the upgrade lane.

### Earlier-head evidence on `3b3dae004763`

- 43/43 focused tests passed: archive batching/recovery (15), canonical media archives (13), and historical transcript directives (15). Added regressions for cursor failure, later file-repair failure, failure in batch 2, row deletion/insertion/independent rewrite before retry, and a temporarily missing file across later batches. The missing-file case keeps its receipt until the file returns and restores the original publication timestamp. A cross-migration regression verifies that a sibling transform after a failed batch carries that timestamp forward. The three focused files took 20.22 seconds on this host; the final cross-migration case is included in the 15-test batching file.
- The 35-archive unchanged fixture observed five immediate transactions (two per batch plus completion) and ten ownership assertions. The previous per-row structure would open 71 transactions.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file type-aware `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed. No full local suite was started for this follow-up.
- Redacted terminal trace from the exact-head production `migrateTranscriptDirectiveArchives` implementation on **copies** of eight existing published Zstd archive records. A legacy reaction directive was injected only into each copy. Trials injected a cursor failure, file-repair failure, or a missing file after failure. They verified that rewritten rows remained unpublished with a persisted recovery journal, closed and reopened SQLite, retried, and verified each final blob digest, file byte sequence, and original publication timestamp. The missing-file trial verified that its receipt persisted through an incomplete retry, then recovered after the file returned. No live database or serving Gateway was modified:

```json
{"head":"3b3dae004763","copiedExistingArchives":8,"injectedLegacyDirectiveArchives":8,"productionHistoricalDirectiveTransform":true,"injectedCursorFailure":true,"injectedFileFailure":false,"missingFileReceiptRetainedAndRecovered":false,"failedBatchLeftAllPublicationPending":true,"persistedRecoveryJournal":true,"reopenedDatabaseBeforeRetry":true,"retryRewrittenArchives":0,"finalBlobDigestFileAndPublicationVerified":8,"durationMs":1646}
{"head":"3b3dae004763","copiedExistingArchives":8,"injectedLegacyDirectiveArchives":8,"productionHistoricalDirectiveTransform":true,"injectedCursorFailure":false,"injectedFileFailure":true,"missingFileReceiptRetainedAndRecovered":false,"failedBatchLeftAllPublicationPending":true,"persistedRecoveryJournal":true,"reopenedDatabaseBeforeRetry":true,"retryRewrittenArchives":0,"finalBlobDigestFileAndPublicationVerified":8,"durationMs":1734}
{"head":"3b3dae004763","copiedExistingArchives":8,"injectedLegacyDirectiveArchives":8,"productionHistoricalDirectiveTransform":true,"injectedCursorFailure":false,"injectedFileFailure":false,"missingFileReceiptRetainedAndRecovered":true,"failedBatchLeftAllPublicationPending":true,"persistedRecoveryJournal":true,"reopenedDatabaseBeforeRetry":true,"retryRewrittenArchives":0,"finalBlobDigestFileAndPublicationVerified":8,"durationMs":1864}
```

This proves the changed migration owner and crash/retry boundaries on copied existing archive data. It is **not** a complete published-updater or candidate Doctor run. The upstream `update-migration.yml` lane is restricted to `openclaw/openclaw`, and this host has no Docker; that release-lane proof and acceptance of the durable `schema_meta` recovery contract remain explicit maintainer decisions. The earlier head passed `pnpm build`; on that head, `pnpm check` passed preflight and typechecks but repository-wide lint hit two untouched max-lines violations. The earlier full `pnpm test` was stopped after 4h15m and has no aggregate result. The eight-archive performance comparison from the initial head was not rerun on this one. This PR does not address the separate Codex-plugin maintenance-lease refusal.
