prs.title: fix(doctor): stop reporting models the published catalog serves
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`core/doctor/model-references` classified configured model refs against offline metadata while `models list` reports the catalog published by the selected Gateway. Google's manifest lists fewer model IDs than its runtime catalog, so Doctor could call an active `google/gemini-flash-lite-latest` "not in the local model catalog" even while the Gateway listed it. The diagnostic compared different inventories.

## What Changed

- `inspectModelReference` accepts published provider/model rows and treats a matching runtime row as `published-model`. Unknown IDs still retain the existing advisory.
- When an active ref is unconfirmed offline, Doctor requests `models.list` from the selected local **or remote** Gateway with the published-catalog capability. It uses the active local Gateway lock's port when appropriate, matching `models list` target selection.
- Ordinary Doctor now puts `process.env` on its production health-flow context and forwards it to the check (including `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT`), as the lint path already did. The core repair flow carries the same environment.
- A selected Gateway owns failure as well as success: an RPC failure cannot be replaced with local rows that might be stale. Only an implicit local target with no running owner uses a read-only local catalog fallback. This model-reference read requests no provider discovery or write.
- Removed one redundant test whose inferred mock type caused the `check-test-types` CI failure. Boundary coverage is in the dedicated test file.

No persisted data model changes or migration/backfill are involved.

## Evidence

**Separate-process CLI/Gateway proof (isolated loopback Gateway, no real provider credentials):** a disposable Google provider fixture publishes `gemini-flash-lite-latest` from its runtime-loaded catalog entry while its manifest seed and the separate CLI's local provider metadata omit that ID. The CLI and Gateway use separate processes. The fixture is synthetic; this proves the catalog ownership and transport boundary, not a Google API call.

```text
Gateway stopped, CLI with default google/gemini-flash-lite-latest:
$ openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references --severity-min info --json
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"findings":[{"target":"google/gemini-flash-lite-latest","severity":"info"}]}
exit 1

Gateway started on isolated loopback port with the fixture provider:
$ openclaw models list --all --provider google --json
{"count":2,"models":[{"key":"google/gemini-2.5-flash"},{"key":"google/gemini-flash-lite-latest","tags":["default"]}]}
exit 0

Separate CLI process, same configured model and selected Gateway:
$ openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references --severity-min info --json
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":65,"findings":[]}
exit 0

Negative controls while Gateway was running:
- Configured google/gemini-flash-lite-latest-typo: info finding remains; exit 1.
- Explicitly selected unreachable isolated port: original model's info finding remains; exit 1.
- Remote-mode CLI targeting the same isolated Gateway: no finding; exit 0.
```

The displayed JSON is a redacted projection of actual CLI output (unchanged result values; omitted unrelated fields and local paths). The commands use the source-built `openclaw.mjs` and isolated state; they never addressed or changed the host's production Gateway.

**Ordinary Doctor, explicit-port final-finding proof:** the isolated CLI config has `google/gemini-flash-lite-latest` as its primary model, and all three ordinary Doctor commands set `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18891`. With the fixture Gateway running on that port, `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` emitted **no** “Configured model … not in the local model catalog” advisory for that alias. With the Gateway still running and a `-typo` model ref, it emitted the advisory for the typo. After stopping the Gateway, the original config and explicit port produced the advisory for the original alias. The stopped-Gateway run ended “Doctor complete” (exit 0). The two Gateway-running runs ended exit 1 because an unrelated Ollama plugin-capture import failed; the published-alias run also reported a separate runtime-tool-schema warning because that check could not load the synthetic model locally. These are not clean full-Doctor passes, and they do not change the model-reference finding comparison.

```text
Gateway running, original model:
$ OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18891 openclaw doctor --non-interactive
No "Configured model ... not in the local model catalog" finding for google/gemini-flash-lite-latest.
Doctor finished with plugin load errors. (exit 1)

Gateway running, typo model:
$ OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18891 openclaw doctor --non-interactive
Doctor information: Configured model "google/gemini-flash-lite-latest-typo" ... is not in the local model catalog. (exit 1)

Gateway stopped, original model and same explicit port:
$ OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18891 openclaw doctor --non-interactive
Doctor information: Configured model "google/gemini-flash-lite-latest" ... is not in the local model catalog.
Doctor complete. (exit 0)
```

This is a line-wrapping-normalized excerpt of the captured terminal output; the full runs include unrelated Doctor notes and local paths.

Local gates: four focused suites passed **40/40** tests, including the new production constructor regression; production and affected `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.other.json` type shards passed; changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks passed; full source build passed. The new production-flow case took 1.08s within a 14.01s suite; the two-suite cold runner wall was 88.27s, dominated by worker preparation. The boundary tests cover local and remote Gateway reads, absent IDs, no-owner fallback, selected-Gateway failure, and environment forwarding through the ordinary Doctor entry point. PR CI supplies broader changed-file checks; the release-only upgrade cell is separate.

## Upgrade behavior

This patch changes only a read-only diagnostic and transient flow-context propagation. It changes no persisted schema, data shape, migration, or writer; existing operator state remains the input. The repository's published-driver × candidate Docker upgrade cell is release-tier and is not admitted on PR CI. It has not been run for this PR; maintainer release validation owns that remaining cell.

Fixes #157010

On iOS, a person can sign in through Cloudflare Access and connect native Gateway clients, yet the embedded Dashboard opens without that Access session. This PR carries the admitted session into the Dashboard and prevents the iOS client from silently reusing a stored operator grant under a different Access principal.

prs.title: fix(agents): terminate background CLI tasks on cron timeout
prs.body:
Closes #138499

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where cron jobs running automated agent turns that launch background CLI tasks via the `exec` tool leave orphaned processes running on the host when the cron job times out, causing the Gateway restart drain loop to block and eventually force-shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a cron job hits its execution deadline, `cleanupTimedOutAgentRun` triggers an abort with reason `"cron_timeout"`. We ensure this timeout reason propagates through `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` and `EmbeddedAgentQueueHandle.abort` to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, where the abort is classified as a timeout with `TimeoutError`.

Key design decisions:
1. **Timeout reason ordering & re-entrancy**: In `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, `input.abortRun(true, createTimeoutAbortReason())` and `attempt.onDeferredLifecycleAbort?.(reason)` are invoked before `attempt.onAttemptAbort?.()`, preventing re-entrant generic cancellation callbacks from the lane controller from latching first and discarding the `TimeoutError`.
2. **Selective background process termination**: In `bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, backgrounded execution retains its abort signal listener until process settlement (`settlement.onSettled = detachAbortListener;`), allowing `isSignalTimeoutReason(signal?.reason)` to terminate background processes on `TimeoutError` while preserving them across ordinary turn cancellations and restarts.
3. **Task settlement & restart unblocking**: Process settlement triggers `finalizeBackgroundExecTask`, recording the task's terminal state and clearing the `background-exec` active work restart blocker in `gateway-active-work.ts`.

## User Impact

Scheduled cron jobs that launch background CLI commands will no longer leak orphaned processes when the cron job reaches its execution deadline, preventing host resource exhaustion and enabling graceful Gateway restarts.

## Evidence

### 1. Real Behavior Runtime Verification
Executed an end-to-end integration test against the real process supervisor, real exec tool, real process registry, and real gateway active work monitor (`verify-cron-timeout-real.ts`):

```text

=== STEP 2: Spawning Real Background CLI Task via Exec Tool ===

Background Session ID: plaid-tidepool
Child PID: 321092
Active background exec session count: 1
Gateway restart blocked before timeout? true
Active blocker before: 1 active background exec session(s)
Child process alive in OS before timeout: true

=== STEP 3: Triggering Cron Timeout Abort ===
Simulating cron scheduler: queueHandle.abort('cron_timeout')
[Attempt] External abort marked
Run abort signal aborted? true
Run abort signal reason: TimeoutError
Abort state terminal outcome: {"kind":"timeout","phase":"prompt","source":"runtime","aborted":true}

=== STEP 4: Waiting for Process Settlement & Task Finalization ===
Finished session found: true
Finished session terminal status: failed
Finished session exit signal/code: SIGTERM
Child process alive in OS after timeout: false
Active background exec session count after timeout: 0
Gateway restart blocked after timeout? false

=== VERIFICATION SUMMARY ===
Real cron timeout process cleanup verified: SUCCESS
```

### 2. Targeted Vitest Test Suites
All targeted suites pass cleanly (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file>`):

- **`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.background-abort.test.ts`** (9/9 passed):
  - `background exec is not killed when tool signal aborts`
  - `pty background exec is not killed when tool signal aborts`

  - `background exec without explicit timeout applies default timeout`
  - `background exec with timeout zero bypasses default timeout`
  - `yielded background exec still times out`
  - `yieldMs exec without explicit timeout applies default timeout`
  - `background exec is killed when tool signal aborts with TimeoutError`
  - `yielded background exec is killed when tool signal aborts with TimeoutError`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`** (30/30 passed):
  - `processes cron_timeout abort through external-abort sequence as a timeout`
  - `preserves timeout classification when onAttemptAbort synchronously triggers re-entrant generic abort`
- **`src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts`** (33/33 passed):
  - `removes the abort listener when an exec process is backgrounded and exits`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.lifecycle.test.ts`** (23/23 passed):
  - `forwards cron_timeout reason to abortEmbeddedAgentRun`
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/deferred-lifecycle-owner.test.ts`** (2/2 passed):
  - `publishes CLI cancellation authority before releasing the embedded attempt`
  - `records only the accepted candidate terminal trajectory`

Fixes #160383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a focused Doctor E2E run compiles native-worker bundles inside its first timed test case on a cold worker cache.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Contributors get the required worker preparation before the focused Doctor test starts, without adding that work to unrelated E2E selections or extending test timeouts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner already prepares workers before Vitest for selected infra tests. This extends that existing selection to the Doctor legacy-state-migration E2E case, using the same CLI/include/exclude matcher. Worker compilation and lifecycle remain with their existing owner.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(acp): closed ACP sessions keep their ACP provenance instead of projecting as native codex
prs.body:
Related: #153706 (this PR covers the `/acp close` path; the issue's completed one-shot cleanup path is owned by #107366 and stays open)

## Summary

`/acp close` now keeps the session's `acp_sessions` row as a terminal `closed` record
instead of deleting it. This mirrors acpx's documented soft-close (`close` marks the
record `closed: true` + `closedAt`; only `sessions prune` deletes) and stops a closed ACP
session from being projected as a native `codex`/`implicit` runtime. A discarding close
(one-shot cleanup, session delete, session reset) still deletes the row, matching acpx's
discard/prune semantics. Any turn or `/acp` control against a closed session fails with a
typed "session was closed" error that names `/acp spawn` as the recovery.

## Decision needed

This changes what the shared state database retains after `/acp close`, so per
`docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` it needs maintainer acceptance
before merge:

- **Rollback safety (ClawSweeper P1, addressed):** a closed row rewrites its `session_id` lifecycle fence to `closed:<revision>`. Every reader that predates closed rows matches only `null`, the entry's `lifecycleRevision`, or its `sessionId` (`acpSessionRowMatchesEntry`), so after a rollback an older build sees **no row** for the closed session, exactly its post-close state today: the session projects as native and a send fails with "ACP metadata is missing" before any backend I/O. The new matcher accepts the prefixed fence against the same revision, so a replaced lifecycle still drops the closed row. Proven by a contract test (`session-meta.closed.test.ts`) and by running the unmodified `origin/main` build on a copied state directory after a close on this branch (see Evidence).
- **Storage shape (no DDL, no schema-version bump):** the closed marker is a new
  `acp_sessions.state` value, `"closed"`. The column is `TEXT NOT NULL` with no
  `CHECK`, no Swift reader, and the row-to-metadata reader already coerces unknown
  states, so no migration is needed. The close time is persisted in the existing
  `last_activity_at` column (a close is the row's final activity) and surfaced as
  `closedAt` by the reader. A dedicated `closed_at` column would need a DDL migration and
  a schema bump; this PR deliberately avoids that.
- **Second interpretation of existing data:** readers must now distinguish `closed`
  rows from live ones. Closed rows are hidden from every lifecycle reader by default
  (manager resume/ensure, startup identity reconcile, one-shot cleanup, spawn re-use,
  thread-binding health, `sessions_send` routing, session reset). Only the three
  provenance projections (`sessions list --json` via the CLI, the Gateway session
  projection, and `/status`'s runtime resolver) and the manager's own session
  resolution opt in with `includeClosed: true`. Main's new worker-thread batched reader
  (`readAcpSessionMetaForEntries`, used by the Gateway row projection) gets the same
  opt-in and its caller passes it, so the list projection stays the provenance path.
- **Retention:** closed rows live exactly as long as their owning session entry. Gateway
  `sessions.delete` and `sessions.reset` already run the ACP close helper; with this
  change that helper prunes a closed row (it has no runtime to cancel). Nothing else
  accumulates: an ordinary close writes one row per session, and re-spawning the same
  key overwrites it. If the maintainer would rather closed rows be pruned by a
  time-based sweep, that is a separate retention change and is not in this PR.

What upstream acpx does (re-checked at main `ee6090d`, v0.19.3, on 2026-09-28; unchanged since `9ab6c75`/v0.19.2: `docs/sessions.md`, `src/session/persistence/*`): it persists two additive optional record fields, `closed` and `closed_at`, with no schema version change; its prune filters by `closedAt ?? lastUsedAt`, so falling back to the last-used time as the close time is acpx's own convention. It never auto-prunes: `sessions prune` is explicit, closed-only, with `--older-than`/`--before`. Prune is local file deletion and never contacts the backend; backend `session/close` is a best-effort step of the close itself. Closed records are skipped by auto-resume but reopenable through explicit embedding APIs; OpenClaw's stricter "never executable" rule here is a product choice on top of that.

Alternatives considered: keep deleting the row and derive provenance from key shape
(rejected: `src/commands/sessions.acp-model-display.test.ts` pins ACP-shaped bridge
sessions without metadata to their configured native model, and that test stays green
here); add a `closed_at` column (rejected: needs a state-schema bump for a value the
existing activity column already carries).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `/acp close`, `sessions list` and `/status` report the closed ACP session as
`agentRuntime: {"id":"codex","source":"implicit"}`, a native runtime the session never
used, and a follow-up message fails with "ACP metadata is missing".

## User Impact

User impact: a closed ACP session keeps showing the ACP backend that ran it
(`acpRuntime: true`, `agentRuntime: {"id":"acpx","source":"session-key"}`), and sending
to it fails with "ACP session … was closed at … Start a new ACP session with /acp spawn"
instead of a missing-metadata error. `/acp close` still unbinds thread targets; a closed
session cannot be resumed, steered, cancelled, or reconfigured. `/reset`, `/new`, and
session deletion on a closed key drop the retained record. `/acp sessions` lists live sessions only; the closed session's ACP provenance shows in
`openclaw sessions list` and the Gateway session views, which is what the `/acp close` help
text in `docs/tools/acp-agents/controls.md` now says.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw's close owner takes two independent flags: `discardPersistentState` (forwarded
to acpx) and `clearMeta` (deletes the `acp_sessions` row). `/acp close` sets only
`clearMeta`, so acpx soft-closed while OpenClaw hard-deleted, and every runtime
projection derives `acpRuntime` from whether a row is readable. Keeping a terminal row
restores parity with acpx and gives the projections a truthful source. Non-executability
is enforced at the manager's single session-resolution point: a closed row resolves as
`stale` with the typed closed error, so every turn and control path already gated on that
resolution rejects it, and lifecycle readers never see the row at all.

One-shot cleanup (`src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) is untouched; it passes
`discardPersistentState: true` and keeps deleting rows. #107366 owns that path.

## Evidence

- Focused regressions, each failing on `origin/main` before the fix and passing after:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.test.ts` (new): `/acp close` flags keep a
    closed row with backend/agent/identity retained; discarding close deletes; closed row
    resolves as terminal with `detailCode: "ACP_SESSION_CLOSED"`; a turn to a closed
    session rejects without touching the row or backend; a second close is terminal and
    only a discarding close prunes.
  - `src/acp/runtime/session-meta.test.ts`: closed metadata hidden from
    `readAcpSessionMeta`, `readAcpSessionEntry`, `readAcpSessionMetaBatch`, and
    `listAcpSessionEntries` unless `includeClosed` is set; `closedAt` derived from the row.
  - `src/commands/sessions.acp-model-display.test.ts`: a closed ACP session lists with
    `acpRuntime: true` and `agentRuntime: {id: "copilot", source: "session-key"}`; the
    bridge-session case (no metadata → configured native model) is unchanged and green.
- Live before/after on an isolated Gateway (stub ACP backend, acpx 0.19.0 at the time of the live proof, real
  `chat.send` → `/acp spawn` / `/acp close` chat-command path):
  - Before (origin/main): after `/acp close`, acpx record `closed: true` with
    `closed_at`; OpenClaw `acp_sessions` row gone; `sessions.list` row
    `agentRuntime {"id":"codex","source":"implicit"}`; send-after-close →
    `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: ACP metadata is missing …`.
  - After (this branch, rebuilt from the rebased head): after `/acp close` the `acp_sessions` row stays with `state: "closed"` (backend/agent/mode/identity retained), `sessions.list` keeps `agentRuntime {"id":"acpx","source":"session-key"}`, send-after-close → `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: ACP session … was closed at 2026-09-29T00:39:22.861Z. Start a new ACP session with /acp spawn …` with the row unchanged, `/acp status` on the closed key returns the same closed error through the command guard, and `sessions.delete` on the closed key prunes the row.
- Rollback proof (unmodified `origin/main` build `9a75b9bdf4c` over a state directory copied after a close on this branch): the closed row is present with `session_id = "closed:<revision>"`, `sessions.list` shows the session as native (`codex/implicit`, today's post-close projection), a send fails with `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: ACP metadata is missing …` and `/acp status` fails the same way, both before any backend I/O; the row is unchanged afterwards. Switching back to this branch's build reads the same row as closed with ACP provenance.
- CI on the first push failed prod/test typecheck and the extension package-boundary compile on one site: the Discord thread-binding health probe spelled the old three-value `storedState` union; widened to include `closed` in a follow-up commit.
- ClawSweeper re-review of the rebased head rated proof "sufficient" (copied-state rollback run accepted) and left one actionable item, the `/acp close` help wording, fixed in the last commit; the remaining items are the storage-owner decision above.
- Unrelated CI failure on the latest head: `checks-ui-e2e (8/9)` failed one Control UI Playwright spec, `ui/src/e2e/login-gate.e2e.test.ts` › "counts down and automatically enters a reachable Gateway after refused upgrades", on a 30 s locator timeout waiting for the busy-state retry button. This branch touches no UI or login-gate code; the same spec passes locally in 1.6 s on this head (23/23 in the file). Main skips UI e2e on its own pushes, so there is no main-side comparison. I cannot rerun the check from a fork; a maintainer rerun of that shard should clear it.
- Gates on the current head (rebased onto main `9a75b9bdf4c`): `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>` green (conflict markers, line-cap/max-lines/assertion ratchets, format, config docs baseline, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing, core tsgo boundary, typecheck core + core tests, coercion helpers, deprecated API usage, dead-export scan); `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over `src/acp` control-plane and runtime tests, gateway session-utils/row-projection/reset tests, sessions/status commands: 4 shards, 961 tests, 0 failures; `pnpm build` ok. New test files are registered in the database-worker lane list because they write SQLite through the host broker. Autoreview (Codex, P2): two findings. One rejected as a false positive: the reviewer assumed `AcpSessionManager.resolveSession` is async, but main keeps the synchronous `resolveSession` beside `resolveSessionAsync`, and the test it flagged passes. The other repeats the backend-discard follow-up below.

Follow-up (not in this PR): a discarding close of an already-closed row prunes the OpenClaw row without asking acpx to discard the backend session, because the closed record is never reopened. That matches current main, where the row is already gone by then and delete/reset never reach the backend either; making `sessions.delete` of a closed key issue a backend `session/close` would mean resuming the closed acpx record first and is a separate decision.

Not covered: a real Cursor/Codex/Claude ACP harness (the local backends need
re-authentication or an npm install this run could not do); the proof is stub-backed, and
the mechanism under test is OpenClaw's own row lifecycle, which is backend-independent.

prs.title: fix(plugins): allow registry refresh to recover stale discovery
prs.body:
Related: #124468

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins registry --refresh` being blocked by the stale plugin metadata it is intended to rebuild after a plugin source changes.

## User Impact

Operators can rebuild the registry when stale discovery causes plugin-derived configuration errors, including a false duplicate-plugin error across configured agent workspaces. The refresh action rejects malformed JSON and invalid core configuration. The refresh itself preserves the config file and installation records and does not activate plugin code. Successful refresh means the persisted registry is fresh; genuine plugin configuration errors can still require separate repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact parsed `plugins registry --refresh` action now uses the existing core-only startup validation path, then rereads the current config under the plugin lifecycle lease before calling the existing registry refresh owner. The lease reaches the writer's transactional ownership check, and the command retains its persisted-replacement freshness verification. Before rebuilding, the command uses the existing legacy installation-index migration owner under the same lease. This preserves legacy-only installation records and canonical conflict precedence; unresolved migration warnings stop the rebuild. Plain registry inspection and unrelated commands retain their existing validation behavior.

The registry action moves into a dedicated lazy command module, keeping metadata repair separate from unrelated plugin-management runtime imports. This fixes the recovery bootstrap cycle; it does not change registry invalidation policy or claim to resolve the broader issue linked above.

## Evidence

- **Real registered-action reproduction:** an isolated fixture retains a physically present, old config-selected plugin source in the persisted registry while an authoritative managed installation selects its replacement. With two configured workspaces and empty `plugins.load.paths`, full config validation reports a false duplicate-plugin error. The registered `plugins registry --refresh --json` command fails before replacement on the original code and succeeds after the fix.
- **Persistence and activation checks:** the repaired registry selects the managed package, keeps its install record, and permits normal full config validation afterward. Configuration bytes remain identical. Both synthetic plugin runtimes contain activation sentinels and remain unloaded.
- **Bootstrap regression:** the actual Commander pre-action hook failed on the original refresh path and now requests core-only validation. Plain inspection remains normally guarded. An option value spelling `--refresh`, a flag after `--`, and invalid flag forms do not obtain recovery admission.
- **Refusal and partial-repair controls:** malformed JSON and invalid core schema leave the persisted registry unchanged. Registry repair can finish with a genuinely invalid plugin setting, while subsequent full config validation still rejects that setting.
- **Tests:** The original change passed 235 unique tests across the affected CLI command, pre-action hook, config guard, registry inspection, lazy loading, and neighboring command-output suites. The legacy correction additionally passed all 17 tests in the registry recovery and existing state-directory migration suites, including canonical ownership precedence and byte-preserving legacy archival.
- **Repository gates:** production typecheck, all 25 core-test typecheck groups, all three dead-export scans, changed-file formatting, line/assertion ratchets, plugin boundaries, runtime import-cycle checks, and the remaining selected static owner guards passed. Type-aware lint passed for the eight changed CLI production/test files and the changed test-routing file. `git diff --check` passed.
- **Correction gates:** Production core and affected config/CLI test typechecks, type-aware lint of all three changed TypeScript files, four-file formatting, line/assertion/wrapper guards, runtime import-cycle checks, and `git diff --check` passed after the migration correction.
- **Build:** The final `pnpm build` passed in 5 min 28 s, including CLI bootstrap imports, plugin control-plane loads, declarations, and UI asset checks. The supported package builder passed tarball integrity and import-graph checks; the package embeds commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a`.
- **Validation scope:** the broad `check:changed --timed` aggregate was intentionally stopped during full-core lint and replaced with lint of the exact touched files; its completed checks were retained. This is not a claim that the entire aggregate or full-repository lint completed.
- **Review:** The actionable legacy-migration review finding is addressed. The earlier candidate received P1 autoreview and independent source review. The CI follow-up received fresh P1 review against the updated main and fixed the lease-ownership issue described below. A subsequent finding about interactive Doctor recovery was examined and rejected as an introduced blocker: the unchanged bootstrap requires separate explicit consent before running Doctor; the refresh itself still requires valid core configuration. Generic interactive recovery behavior is preserved.

### Public CLI and installed update proof

The final package embeds commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a` and has SHA-256 `2fe7e6b6ea152e310582363b687b55c66574929c00d540f44e0d101a87414749`. The installed checks ran in a credential-free Linux container with no host mounts, using actual public CLI subprocesses and synthetic plugin packages. Fixture setup used the existing registry owner; the command, updater, Doctor, and runtime checks were unmodified.

| Boundary | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Original parent public CLI, plugin schema error | `pnpm openclaw plugins registry --refresh --json` exited 1 at normal plugin validation, before recovery could run. |
| Original PR head, legacy-only installation records | The same public command exited 1 with a stale persisted replacement; the linked install record was missing. The focused legacy regression also failed before the correction. |
| Final installed CLI, stale old config source versus managed replacement | A config read reproduced the false duplicate-workspace error. `openclaw plugins registry --refresh --json` exited 0, returned `state: fresh`, selected the managed replacement, preserved installation ownership and config bytes, and left both plugin activation sentinels untouched. Subsequent full `config validate --json` exited 0. |
| Final installed CLI, legacy-only linked ownership | Refresh exited 0 and returned `state: fresh`; the canonical registry retained the linked install record and selected its runtime source. The legacy JSON was archived with identical bytes; config bytes and the runtime sentinel were unchanged. |
| Final installed CLI, genuine plugin config error | Refresh exited 0 with a fresh registry. Both `config validate --json` and plain `plugins registry --json` still exited 1 for the invalid plugin setting. |
| Final installed CLI, invalid core config | Refresh exited 1 before replacing the registry; persisted registry bytes and input config bytes remained unchanged. Fresh-state refresh also passed. |
| Published driver × final candidate | Integrity-pinned official npm `2026.9.5` (`ec9c1a13db89`) ran `openclaw update --tag /inputs/registry-candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json`, exited 0 in 65.56 s, and installed the exact commit above. The real migration, Doctor, plugin/config, and canary Gateway checks completed. Linked legacy ownership survived; subsequent installed registry refresh and full config validation both exited 0. |

The false-duplicate **before** failure is proved at the real registered-action/config boundary; the whole-process source-parent fixture could self-repair during startup and is not claimed as a public-process failure. The separate public-process failures above cover plugin-validation admission and the legacy upgrade regression. Installed success is separate from the production incident's operational repair, and no live channel behavior is claimed by these metadata tests.

Initial fixture-only attempts were retained and excluded from the passing results: a retired configuration field was rejected as designed, and disabling bundled discovery made Doctor's own metadata unavailable. The successful updater used configuration supported by the published driver and normal bundled discovery. CI timing is not yet available.

### CI follow-up

Current reviewed head: `d1cea32ce47847de47fcb7640d9f0092ead3e406`; incorporated main: `5a15cf46eba351142e02e73668b87e5a3727d368`. The merge adopts main's equivalent Session Share service-lifecycle fixture repair (`d7b45d7e7`) and removes this branch's superseded registration helper. All five registry-recovery production files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed `108bbce` head. The earlier before/after and updater proof below remains tied to its stated source; this merge does not claim a new provider or installed-runtime replay.

The prior head's exact [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35861753774/job/107184405898) failed one Gateway lifecycle case: `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts:290` timed out polling for a pending install's captured setup. The failing fixture and its pending-install/config-notification owners are unchanged between that CI merge and current main. A bounded local reproduction ran the entire three-case file in original in-file order on the merged candidate: all three passed unchanged, including the reported case (13.735 s). Command wall was 67.62 s / supported runner 66.96 s. This does not establish the CI failure's cause or prove it fixed; no timeout, assertion, production path or retry policy was changed. The original 39-file CI shard was not replayed locally.

Fresh full-PR autoreview against the incorporated main is scoped-clean through P1; whitespace validation passes. New CI is left to normal repository execution, without claiming all checks green. The previous Session Share correction at `108bbce` started the actual registered catalog services through the existing controlled transport and awaited shutdown before isolated state teardown; main now owns that same lifecycle behavior.

The same complete integration file reproduced **3 failures / 10 passes** before this fixture correction and passed **13/13** afterward. The root-test type graph, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, full-PR file-growth ratchet, and whitespace checks passed. Fresh P0/P1 AutoReview was scoped-clean. These checks establish the targeted repair; the new remote CI run remains authoritative for the whole suite. The installed package and updater evidence below remains tied to its explicitly recorded historical revision, not this later test-only head.

The original CI run tested merge `a9261fbe5b52ddbd3854022cbc9d8088fcbd33a4` against main `69977d1a07613d871c1ea26ff3c28a2ae8aa2ade`. It failed an unchanged memory responsiveness assertion and a Gateway lifecycle shard. The failures were investigated rather than treated as flakes.

Newer upstream repairs address the owning tests: [#155745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155745) synchronizes the two memory lookups with their retrieval worker, [#155751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155751) joins archive-placement fixtures before teardown, and [94b9c471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/94b9c471535b4c6b088852ecf353f45e6cf63307) joins archive lifecycle requests and removes the intermediate polling race. The branch first incorporated main `843b9f60186c54de1b7c479936942403b509826e` with these repairs, then merged main `b2727e7663e21dcb612277be2aa529039fcce6d2` on September 23. No assertions or timeouts were relaxed in this PR.

After the initial merge and ownership-fence correction, all 18 registry recovery and state-directory migration tests passed, including the new revocation case. The affected config/CLI graph typecheck, type-aware lint of the two changed files, formatting, and staged diff checks passed. The actionable lease finding was fixed; the existing consent-gated Doctor behavior was retained after examining its owner and baseline. The September 23 merge is commit `a9856681fc9c4b4f8631a98f651602b9a61f5285` against main `b2727e7663e21dcb612277be2aa529039fcce6d2`. Its 18 focused tests, affected config/CLI type graph, type-aware lint of the migration owner and registry command/test, formatting, and staged diff checks all passed. Fresh P1 AutoReview completed scoped-clean with no actionable findings after the conflict resolution. The working tree was clean after committing with the normal repository hook.

The installed CLI and updater results above remain measurements of package commit `3c383fe6894060ce3f59ff43b2d92875ec5bfa8a`. After the main merge, fresh review identified a missing final ownership check: the outer lease cleanup could reject a cancelled operation only after the command had emitted success. The command now calls the existing lease assertion immediately after the asynchronous inspection. A regression using the registered CLI and a real lifecycle lease cancels during the real inspection; before the correction the command rejects but has already emitted `refreshed: true`, while the corrected path rejects without emitting output. prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Fresh review exposed an empty-target regression on channels without a transport resolver. The shared threading owner now distinguishes an absent reply target from `replyToId: ""`; the latter remains an explicit opt-out. Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.

Verification:
- Added regressions failed on the pre-repair candidate: **3 failed, 46 passed**.
- Repaired candidate: **183 passed across 7 suites**, covering queued delivery, channel boundaries, admission/provenance, resolver delegation, shared threading, empty/false opt-outs, inline override, first-reply slot accounting, and deduplication.

prs.title: fix(android): recheck TLS trust on explicit gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #164026. This is a narrow follow-up to #68438 and #83077: changed-certificate confirmation exists on normal connection setup, but explicit Reconnect with a retained endpoint did not re-enter it.

## User Impact

Reconnect can reach the existing certificate review without requiring Disconnect first. A changed saved fingerprint still needs explicit consent; verification is not disabled and changed certificates are not automatically trusted. An unchanged gateway reconnect also keeps the selected Chat session and existing same-gateway state while retiring stale connection-bound read leases.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained-endpoint refresh now calls the existing beginConnect TLS/trust admission owner inside its existing refresh lifecycle operation. It preserves the existing gateway scope rather than running target-switch Chat reset/restoration. Actual gateway changes retain the default reset behavior. There is no new setting, visual UI, competing trust policy or automatic certificate acceptance.

The initial revision c3aa411b reused the entire normal target-switch entry. Full CI exposed seven Chat lifecycle regressions: the connection replacement no longer preserved the selected session and operator handoff contract. This follow-up corrects that at the runtime owner. The Chat tests and their timeouts are unchanged; the separate Kotlin formatting corrections are included.

## Evidence

### Real setup tested

Native Linux x86_64, Temurin JDK 21, Gradle 9.7.1, AGP 9.4.1 and Robolectric 4.17. TLS/Auth fixtures use SDK 34; the Chat ownership/layout fixtures use native graphics and SDK 36. Android source compilation uses SDK 37. The required runtime artifacts were obtained from the pinned consumer coordinates and checksum-verified. No architecture spoofing or emulated x86 JVM was used for the passing runs.

The real TLS case exercises production NodeRuntime with its **default fingerprint probe** and **real OkHttp TLS/WebSocket transport**, against a loopback server with ephemeral certificates and scripted Gateway protocol responses. Certificate selection changes on the same port while old sockets remain live. Probe results and client transport are not injected.

### Exact commands run after this patch

From apps/android, with dependencies already resolved:

    ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --max-workers=2 -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx3g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8" -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatFullMessageOwnershipLayoutTest --stacktrace

    ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --max-workers=2 -Dorg.gradle.jvmargs="-Xmx3g -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8" -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayBootstrapAuthTest --stacktrace

The source bytes consumed by these passing runs are committed in c5ca34e25bd3420aa042fb0d2b5b1581e3859c22. Original production, the initially published revision and the repaired candidate were bound separately; each temporary control restored the candidate afterward.

### Observed results and measured test cost

| Production source / scope | JUnit result | Suite time | Whole Gradle invocation |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Original production, complete unchanged Chat class | 42 passed | 45.439 s | 116 s |
| Initial PR revision, seven failing Chat cases | Same seven CI failures reproduced | 122.217 s | 207 s |
| Repaired candidate, complete unchanged Chat class | **42 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips** | **45.298 s** | **117 s** |
| Repaired candidate, complete TLS/Auth class | **88 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips** | **17.907 s** | **88 s** |

These are measured scopes, not a performance-speedup claim: the failing control includes expected timeouts, and whole-build time includes startup and compilation. The original changed-fingerprint regression also has the previously recorded negative control: both target prompt cases fail on unmodified production and pass after the TLS fix.

The earlier c3aa411b CI run had the seven Chat failures in both Play and ThirdParty; those prior-head results are not counted as current-head validation.

**Current-head hosted CI passed:** [CI run 37117208537](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37117208537), for c5ca34e25bd3420aa042fb0d2b5b1581e3859c22. The checkout log binds the tested merge 7b91c64955c0be471912c01f5f9884ca0cac5d58 to this head. Android Play, ThirdParty, Wear, ktlint/lint, both native-access page-size configurations, and the aggregate CI gate succeeded. The run had 10 successful jobs and 33 scope-skipped jobs; skipped jobs are not reported as passes.

The current hosted Play JUnit artifact reports **GatewayBootstrapAuthTest: 88 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips, 6.782 s** and **ChatFullMessageOwnershipLayoutTest: 42 passed, 0 failures/errors/skips, 23.747 s**. These are suite-only CI timings, not total job durations. No Chat assertion or timeout was weakened to obtain these results.

### What the proof covers

- Initial pin approval and both role connections; same-port certificate replacement; old/new fingerprint review.
- Pending or declined review preserves the saved pin and desired sessions. Acceptance leads to two replacement TLS/WebSocket connections using saved refresh credentials and the new pin.
- Same-gateway refresh retains the selected Chat session and operator-first handoff, including the deliberately held node lifecycle lock case.
- Stale disclosure/read leases cannot dispatch through a replacement connection. All existing Chat assertions and timeouts remain unchanged.

All four canonical KtLint module checks passed, including the previously failing app test source check. Fresh independent P0/P1 review is clear and applicable staged pre-commit checks passed. Test logs, JUnit XML and exact-source records were retained.

### What was not tested

This is production runtime code under Robolectric with genuine TLS sockets and native-rendered Chat tests, **not an installed APK/physical-phone TLS test or a full production Gateway backend test**. No patched-device UI recording is claimed. The current-head hosted Android jobs passed as recorded above; that is not installed-device TLS coverage or maintainer merge approval.

## What Problem This Solves

Completed native chat turns hide assistant narration inside one work disclosure. The reader loses the explanation between tool operations as soon as the final answer arrives.

## User Impact

The iOS and macOS chat surfaces keep narration and media inline in source order. Only contiguous tool and reasoning work folds into separate disclosures. Loading older history preserves expanded sections, including work before a steer message. Active or unanswered work remains expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat presentation projects mixed envelopes without changing stored history or the message identities used by copy, reply, speech, and reactions. Markdown and reasoning-sensitive envelopes retain their parser context; tool outcomes and source previews stay attached to the correct part. Disclosure identity follows the surviving visible boundary rather than the first loaded work row.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep authored agent order when saving config
prs.body:
Closes #165055

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated macOS config save alphabetizes the agent roster and can change which agent the Gateway treats as first.

The first PR revision also refused saves for valid configurations whose Gateway intentionally returns `raw: null` to protect secrets. The prior follow-up restored those saves through the existing `config.patch` contract. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced Unicode scanner defect that rejected existing quoted keys beginning with a literal combining mark.

## User Impact

Existing configurations retain authored object-key order across local-file and Gateway saves. Valid redacted Gateway configurations remain editable, and quoted Unicode keys survive unrelated full-document saves. No config option, migration, or change to secret redaction is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing `.sortedKeys` alone is insufficient because Swift dictionaries do not retain JSON source order. Both full-document save paths use one source-aware writer. Local saves read the existing file under their existing lock; Gateway saves retain the source with the loaded document's route lease and revision hash.

When the Gateway intentionally withholds source text, the app instead sends only the differences from the loaded structured baseline through `config.patch`. Unchanged agent entries and redacted credentials are omitted, so the Gateway-owned source retains their order and values. Explicit `replacePaths` preserves full-array edit intent for reorder, shrink, and subtree deletion instead of invoking ID-keyed upserts. Revision, route, fallback, and local credential-preservation guards remain in place.

The writer scans Unicode scalars so a literal combining mark cannot absorb an opening quote into a Swift grapheme cluster. Foundation still owns JSON5 validation and key decoding.

The full-document writer retains existing keys, omits deleted keys, appends new keys deterministically, and accepts JSON5 comments, quoted/unquoted keys, escapes, and trailing commas. Retained array values keep their object order when moved or when neighbors are inserted/deleted. Arbitrarily moved-and-modified array objects without stable identity receive deterministic order; comments and whitespace are normalized as before.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `ae4cd9bbcab468fbde71ef994386d2a1aa81e0b6`. Unicode follow-up parent: `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Base: `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`. macOS arm64, Swift 6.4.

### Unicode compatibility control and repaired behavior

At the published parent `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, Foundation accepts a strict JSON document whose quoted key and string value begin with literal U+0301 scalars. An unrelated browser edit fails in both production save owners:

```text
BEFORE local save refused; original fixture unchanged
BEFORE raw-present Gateway save throws DecodingError; no config.set request
AFTER three local saves succeeded; combining-mark key/value and authored order retained
AFTER three raw-present config.set saves succeeded; key/value/order and baseHash retained
```

The exact production `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict`, `ConfigStore.load/save`, and `ConfigJSONWriter` sources were compiled with synthetic transport/peripheral adapters and run using `sandbox-exec -f proof.sb unicode-before-proof before` and `unicode-after-proof after`. The sandbox denies operator files, network, preferences/Keychain services, and child processes. Only disposable fixtures were used; this is not installed-app/live-Gateway E2E.

The new parameterized Swift regression fails before for both double-quoted JSON and single-quoted JSON5, then passes with scalar scanning. It creates literal combining marks through Swift scalar escapes rather than JSON escape tokens and checks preservation across repeated unrelated edits, including strings containing delimiter/comment text.

### Valid raw-null compatibility control and repaired behavior

The exact published first revision `21fa0613ea2f389d6d1eeb998d85ccd3c1c03a12` refuses a valid raw-null save with ConfigStore error 4. At prior head `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, the repaired production `ConfigStore.load/save` owner succeeds against the same boundary.

A synthetic configuration deliberately gives its token the same value as an unrelated configuration field. The exact production `redactConfigSnapshot` owner therefore returns `raw: null` while retaining structured configuration. The proof then exercises five edits through the compiled production Swift save owner and applies the captured requests using the exact production `applyMergePatch` owner:

```text
browser off, browser on, browser off, provider-model reorder, provider-model shrink
5/5 saves succeeded through config.patch
Every request retained baseHash=synthetic-revision
Unchanged gateway/auth and agents were absent from every patch
Auth credential retained; agent roster remained zmain,alpha
Model reorder and shrink retained exact replacePaths and final array intent
```

The Swift owner ran in an OS sandbox against disposable fixtures. Gateway transport and peripheral app adapters were synthetic. This is direct save-owner plus production redaction/merge-contract proof, not an installed-app/live-Gateway end-to-end run. No operator configuration, installed app, or live Gateway was changed.

### Original ordering control

At the earlier first PR revision, compiled exact baseline and repaired local/Gateway serialization owners showed:

```text
Baseline: three unrelated local saves and three config.set encodings -> alpha,zmain
First PR revision: all six retained authored zmain,alpha
All three config.set requests retained baseHash
```

The full-document writer was unchanged by the prior raw-null compatibility follow-up; the scalar scanner correction above is new on this candidate. The earlier raw-null refusal is superseded by the repaired behavior above.

### Tests and checks

- Current exact-source pure serializer and merge-patch tests: **10 tests / 13 cases passed in 0.002s** in a separately linked, audited OS-sandboxed Swift Testing executable. This includes the failing-before literal Unicode regression, existing JSON5 comments/escaped keys/trailing commas, array movement/insertion/deletion, minimal patches, and array replacement/subtree deletion.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in **20.72s**.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed in **21.36s**. This is test-bundle compilation, not native suite execution.
- Strict pinned SwiftLint on both follow-up files passed with zero violations. Full macOS SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Touched tests now use required failable UTF-8 conversions.
- Broad macOS lint / `check:changed` still report only the unchanged, previously documented `QuickChatFocusedTextCapture.swift:232` multiple-trailing-closure violation. All other changed-check lanes passed; no unrelated production fix is included.
- Current independent P2 AutoReview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. Reviewed source bytes match this candidate. Scope is this two-file Unicode follow-up versus the published parent. The inherited Codex auth attempt failed with HTTP401 and is not counted as a clean review.
- Earlier raw-null repair retains its five production-owner saves, nine pure tests/eleven cases, and clean compatibility review at `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Those are explicitly earlier-head measurements; the compatibility owner was not changed by this follow-up.

### Remaining checks and limits

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper reassessment are pending. Previous-head green CI is not current-head validation. Full native test execution requires disposable macOS CI/VM and was not run on the operator desktop. The separate generic JavaScript full-suite attempt was interrupted without an aggregate result and is not claimed as passed or as native proof.

prs.title: improve(ui): skip redundant chat snapshot sanitization
prs.body:
Related: #152861

## What Problem This Solves

Avoids repeatedly sanitizing the full growing assistant reply during Control UI chat streaming.

## User Impact

Ordinary streaming replies require less repeated text processing while hidden reasoning, tool syntax, and runtime context stay hidden. Visible output and saved-message reconciliation retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebased the existing work onto main `c19dc239d20b08948d5f18a89b97ef6a1b5a9bac`, preserving connection-owned wire reconstruction and commentary/item reconciliation. The chat page consumes complete connection-projected snapshots and reuses the canonical incremental text-filter pipeline for proven raw extensions. Replacements and changes to the connection, session, run, or visible stream reset reuse; terminal events retire it.

The old punctuation/256-character boundary guard is removed. Canonical filters remain active after their syntax markers appear, covering ClawSweeper's newline-free long command trace and delayed legacy-result object payload, as well as delayed XML payloads and whitespace-tolerant runtime notices. The UI does not duplicate sanitizer grammars.

## Evidence

Final head: `1ae5b53274cb99f0fcc8023ed0c8c17d582c0381`; browser-tested tree: `371eaade5971d8e0bcabcb6c052140bae8a9c523`.

- **Exact-head CI passed:** [run 37701668239](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37701668239), with 46 successful jobs and 24 policy-selected skips. The previous proof-instrumentation lint error is repaired without suppressions. UI checks, UI-e2e checks, type checks, lint, and bundle performance gates pass.
- **ClawSweeper revision 12:** [ready for maintainer review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153214#issuecomment-5745780700) on the final head. Both prior blockers are resolved; no actionable correctness findings remain, and the recorded browser proof is sufficient. Independent full-candidate autoreview through P2 also found no accepted/actionable findings.
- **Actual Chromium / production UI proof:** all four cumulative-snapshot scenarios passed again on the final head through the built Control UI and mock Gateway. Both requested edge cases use append-only wire frames, verify canonical live text before a saved final, and finish with one reply and no live stream.
- **Measured work reduction:** a 240-update reply reconstructs 125,412 characters. Main's largest sanitizer replacement input was 125,412 characters with 240 calls; the final candidate's largest input is 521 characters with one call. The work-bound regression demonstrably fails on main. Event-emission observations were 61.2 ms before and 24.6 ms after; these are individual local observations, not a portable benchmark.
- **224 unique focused/owner tests passed:** chat event ownership, snapshot boundaries, assistant sanitization, runtime-context stripping, incremental text projection, and message extraction. The old guard's two missed activations were also reproduced directly against canonical projection.
- **15 Chromium browser cases passed:** four snapshot cases plus eleven existing streaming cases covering reconnect, tool activity, normalized Markdown, desktop/mobile error retention, and final reconciliation. The broader eleven-case run and independent review use the same production bytes as the final head; the subsequent commits only correct test-helper arguments and the instrumentation receiver declaration.
- **Local static validation:** all 27 test type-check groups, production core/UI types, focused typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The redundant local broad-check run was stopped after exact-head CI completed its remaining gates; it is not reported as a completed local full check.

The proof uses a real Chromium browser and production UI with synthetic Gateway events. It does not establish that the unidentified WebKit stall in #152861 is resolved; no operator Gateway or live provider was used. No stored-data migration, protocol change, or release is involved.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and cost</summary>

prs.title: fix(xai): utility model requests through the Grok OAuth proxy fail with 426
prs.body:
Closes #153366

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every utility completion (conversation labels, dashboard session titles, summaries via `agents.defaults.utilityModel`) fails with HTTP 426 when the utility model is an xai model on the Grok OAuth proxy, while normal agent turns on the same model succeed. Dashboard titles come back empty and each run spends a failed request on the utility call.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who set `utilityModel` to a Grok model through the SuperGrok/OAuth proxy get working labels, titles, and summaries again on that cheaper model; no config change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct `completeSimple` callers dispatch through `prepareModelForSimpleCompletion`, which asks the provider plugin for a `wrapSimpleCompletionStreamFn`. The xai plugin only implemented `wrapStreamFn`, so utility requests reached `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com` without the CLI identity headers the proxy requires (`X-XAI-Token-Auth`, `x-grok-client-version`, `x-grok-model-override`) and without the payload compatibility patches. This registers a simple-completion wrapper that composes exactly those two wire-contract pieces; the tool-call and fast-mode wrappers stay on the agent path, where they apply.

## Evidence

- `extensions/xai/stream.test.ts`: the new wrapper adds the proxy headers and strips unsupported reasoning controls for a non-reasoning model on the proxy base URL, and leaves requests to the public API base URL untouched (47 tests pass in the file; `index.test.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.test.ts`, `provider-policy-api.test.ts` pass, 85 tests).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passes.
- Live, on the affected 2026.9.5 Docker instance: before the fix every post-run utility call logged `[model-fetch] response provider=xai ... model=grok-4.5 status=426` (also with `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`), while `openclaw agent --model xai/<same model>` returned 200 for all six catalog models. With this change cherry-picked onto `v2026.9.5` (`5713d46`), built, and deployed to the same instance with `utilityModel: xai/grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, the same run logged `model=grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning status=200` twice (label and title) and no 426.

prs.title: improve(android): float Jump to latest above the composer
prs.body:
Closes #155916

## What Problem This Solves

The Android chat's **Jump to latest** action sits in the top header, away from where people read and type in a long conversation.

## User Impact

When newer content is below the visible history, Android users get a clearer, thumb-sized floating action above the composer that returns to the live edge. In an unusually short pane, the action stays out of the composer's way until there is room for it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action moves into the chat pane while keeping the existing reader navigation behavior. Its entrance, exit, and reduced-motion timing follow the Control UI; the circular surface has a stronger shadow and exposes a Material 3 button role and accessible label. The Android reading docs now describe its position.

## Evidence

- On the latest head, the full `ChatComposerLayoutTest` class passed on the Play debug variant (116 tests, 39.6 s wall), together with `:app:assemblePlayDebug` and `:app:ktlintCheck`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed for the app and docs lanes; `pnpm docs:check-mdx` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Astra AutoReview of the original change and a fresh Astra AutoReview of the compact-pane repair returned no actionable P0–P3 findings.
- The compact Details regression failed on the prior head and passes on the repair. [ClawSweeper follow-up with inspected compact before/after screenshots and test results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155918#issuecomment-5814817001).
- Installed and inspected both builds in the API 36 Android emulator using the same synthetic chat screenshot fixture. This is emulator UI evidence, not a live Gateway session.
