prs.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets
prs.body:
Related: #70903

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who resolve a provider billing or usage condition before its recorded reset time stay locked out of the saved auth profile until the stored window expires. There is no supported way to clear it, and the `models auth list` / doctor billing hint is a dead end.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New `openclaw models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>`: one owner-routed, locked write that resets the persisted cooldown, block, disable, and failure counters. It does not touch credentials or auth order. After the write it runs the same shared Gateway auth refresh (`models.authRefresh`) as the sibling `models auth` write commands, so no manual Gateway restart is needed.
- The `models auth list` / `models status` / doctor billing hint now names this command, including `--agent <id>` for the store it came from, because the mutation path rejects an ambiguous agent roster.
- Inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` failures have a health record (`inline-api-key:<provider>`) but no profile row. The command accepts that id when the record exists, so the hint shown for inline keys also works.
- The reset follows the health row that was displayed, not only the credential owner. A row in the agent's own database (a child's local override of an inherited credential, or an inline-key failure) wins over the owner's row after reload, so it is reset too; an agent without such a row gets no database created.
- `usage.ts` is a grandfathered oversized file, so the line-cap ratchet rejects any growth there. `updateOwnedAuthProfileUsage` moved unchanged into `usage-owner-write.ts`, next to the new reset. The dropped-bookkeeping log comes from `main`'s `state-observation.ts`. `usage.ts` shrinks by 29 lines (751 → 722). The move adds no test seam: the dropped-write test mocks the `store-runtime.js` module boundary, as `main` does since #164320.

It does not add polling, shorten provider backoffs, change fallback policy, or remove credentials.

## User Impact

Operators can re-evaluate a recovered provider with one command, without editing SQLite or repeating OAuth. If the failure still applies, the next request restores the cooldown normally.

## Evidence

Head `509ead90b58`, rebased onto `main` at `2f620b970a0`. The last commit addresses the two open P2 findings on `ba7b9103fb4`:

- **Local health row (P2):** the reset wrote only the credential owner's store, so a child's own usage row for an inherited credential stayed, won again after reload, and the command still reported success. It now also resets the agent's own row when one exists. A real-store test seeds that row, clears it, and rereads through a fresh runtime; it fails on the previous implementation. A second test shows an agent with no row keeps no database (it fails if the second write is not gated).
- **Shared state-db hint (P2):** with a roster such as `coder`/`reviewer` no agent owns the shared store, so doctor printed the command without `--agent`. The Shared target now falls back to a configured agent; owner routing reaches the shared profile from any of them. A doctor test covers it and fails without the fallback.

Results on this head:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` passed on `usage-owner-write`, `usage.inherited-owner`, `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure`, `usage`, `auth-clear-cooldown`, `auth-unavailability`, `doctor-auth.profile-health`, `doctor-auth.shared-health`, `models-cli`, and `root-command-descriptions`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `tsgo` test configs `core.test.agents-root`, `agents-other`, `agents-tools`, `commands`, and `commands-doctor` passed.
- `check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` and `check:test-mock-exports --base upstream/main` reported OK; `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` were clean.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet` currently fails on `main` itself (`ui/src/pages/agents/agents-page-state.ts` is listed as stale); this PR does not touch it.

## Remaining merge evidence

- No inspectable real-flow proof yet. A shipped-CLI run against an isolated state directory is refused by the CLI's state-store guard while an installed Gateway service uses another state directory, and the command would refresh that Gateway. Needs an environment without that service for: blocked profile -> `models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>` -> Gateway auth refresh -> recovered provider request.
- Maintainer approval of the user-facing CLI contract is still required before merge.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: docs: note that Go before 1.27 ignores the egress proxy CA bundle on macOS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`secrets.egressProxy` exports `SSL_CERT_FILE` and the other CA variables to Gateway-hosted commands so clients behind the loopback proxy trust its local CA. Go changed how it treats those variables on macOS in 1.27. Through Go 1.26, `crypto/x509` verifies only through the platform trust API, and `release-branch.go1.26`'s `root_darwin.go` ends in `func loadSystemRoots() (*CertPool, error) { return &CertPool{systemPool: true}, nil }`, so a Go CLI such as `gog` built with an older toolchain fails a proxied request with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Go 1.27 added the `x509sslcertoverrideplatform` setting (default `1`), which loads roots from `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` on macOS and Windows instead of the platform store; `0` restores platform-only verification, and the setting is planned for removal in Go 1.31. The egress page lists those variables without either half of that story, so the error reads as a broken proxy.

Fixes #183610

## User Impact

Operators running a Go-based CLI behind the secret egress proxy now see where the limitation applies, that current Go honors the injected bundle, and the supported alternative (`bypassHosts`, which keeps TLS end to end for a client that authenticates with its own credentials) right where the CA variables are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The note sits directly after the injected environment list, because that list is what implies every client trusts the bundle. It qualifies by Go version because the platform behavior changed at 1.27: stating the limit unconditionally is wrong for current Go, and dropping it would leave the 1.26-and-earlier failure unexplained.

## Evidence

- `golang/go` `release-branch.go1.26` `src/crypto/x509/root_darwin.go`: `func loadSystemRoots() (*CertPool, error) { return &CertPool{systemPool: true}, nil }`, so that branch reads no CA-file path.
- `golang/go` master `src/crypto/x509/root.go`: `loadSystemRoots()` returns `&CertPool{systemPool: true}` for Darwin and Windows when `x509sslcertoverrideplatform.Value() == "0"`, and otherwise calls `loadOnDiskRoots(certFilePath, certDirPath)` with the two environment variables.
- `golang/go` `doc/godebug.md` (Go 1.27 section): the setting defaults to `1`, `x509sslcertoverrideplatform=0` disables loading roots from disk, and removal is planned in Go 1.31.
- Not reproduced from a macOS shell here; the claim rests on those three Go sources.
- `docs:check-links:anchors`: 17679 internal links checked; the 7 reported breaks are pre-existing in other pages, none in this file (`#traffic-allowlist` resolves).
- `lint:docs` (markdownlint-cli2): 0 issues.
- `oxfmt` on the edited page: no changes.
- Diff: 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-).

Closes #183610

prs.title: fix: keep recovery notifications quiet on October backport
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backports the quieter channel restart recovery behavior from #186302 to `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`: a recovery attempt currently announces itself before the interrupted request has an outcome.

## User Impact

Channel recovery no longer sends a separate start announcement. Normal results and existing terminal failure notices retain their routes; replacement-session instructions now ask the user to describe the unfinished work after `/new` or `/reset`. Typing remains supported.

This does not change deployment handoff, recovery algorithms or deadlines, Control UI behavior, version pins, or deployments.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adapt the upstream change to the release branch's existing delivery guard and terminal-notice constant, without importing newer recovery machinery. Remove the announcement producer and caller; retain typing ownership, settlement cleanup, final delivery and source-run deduplication.

## Evidence

- Merge the latest October backport (`d9575b6729a45f43e5bcb7846dc5b435f4b57bc5`) without rewriting the two existing commits. The six-file PR patch against the new base is byte-for-byte identical to its original patch; the CI repair brings no additional recovery-notice behavior changes. Independent merge review found no actionable issues. On the merged base, all 168 focused recovery/Telegram tests passed (222.66 s), and native changed checks passed (532.75 s), including core/test typechecks, lint, guards and dead exports. [Exact-head CI run 40609136496](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40609136496) passed for merge commit `94bb1154da34d55083838a9990a755823f224555`. At verification, PR checks reported 59 successful and 47 conditional skips, with no failures or pending checks. The PR remains unmerged pending maintainer confirmation.

- Follow-up `b179b8ebb7c0a8b8cd8f1402a0660b2d87b6d1ff` adapts the Telegram integration-test repair from upstream `004b519f4b18a158b493405243708cd3d9aacb10`. The test uses this branch's existing synchronous delivery guard and real Gateway/Telegram queue, retaining allowed delivery and post-queue permission revocation. No production behavior is changed by this follow-up.
- The Telegram file reproduces 4 failures before this repair and passes all 13 cases afterward. The root-other test typecheck, focused typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent read-only review found no P0-P2 findings. The existing 205-test evidence below remains applicable to unchanged production code.
- Historical CI before the base refresh stopped at `security-fast`: production dependency audit reported inherited critical/high advisories (including DOMPurify, MCP SDK and undici), then fail-fast cancelled selected jobs and `ci-gate` failed ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40588594038)). This PR changes no dependency manifests or lockfile; the cancelled checks are not counted as passed.

Base: `d9575b6729a45f43e5bcb7846dc5b435f4b57bc5` (includes #186371 CI repairs). Upstream source: `badd984eaf61b2da55813725b5f62368bc855c1d` (#186302, still pending at backport preparation).

- Base-red regression: the new running-recovery silence test fails against the base because one start announcement is sent (30.15 s wrapper time); the candidate restores the original account/topic route assertions.
- 205 tests pass across restart recovery (150), outbound recovery (41), Gateway runtime (9), and dispatch startup (5), including the silence regression, original reply routing, terminal failure once across repeated scans, and database reopen. Native wrapper: 267.03 seconds.
- Core and affected agent-session test typechecks, focused typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent read-only source review found no actionable P0-P2 issue. Simplification retained existing owners and added no state, timer, queue, or schema. The repository autoreview CLI was attempted but unavailable with the installed external CLI; its isolation controls were retained. This is not a successful autoreview claim.
- Tests use isolated fixtures and the existing delivery harness; no live deployment/channel end-to-end claim is made. Dependency manifests and lockfile are unchanged.

Merge and deployment are separate steps.

prs.title: fix: previous chat answer stays hidden when a late exec completion arrives
prs.body:
Fixes #186255

## What Problem This Solves

A previous completed chat answer can disappear into the next turn's **Worked** disclosure when a late background exec completion is recorded after that answer with an earlier timestamp. An unmatched CLI import exposes the timestamp reordering, and hiding the exec input previously lost its display-turn boundary.

## User Impact

The completed answer stays separately visible before and after reloading a dashboard conversation. The follow-up's work disclosure no longer takes ownership of that answer. Raw internal exec notices remain hidden; ordinary same-turn narration still folds normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local canonical rows must retain transcript sequence, even when their timestamps go backwards. Unmatched imports are placed after the latest local whose timestamp is no later than the import, using the shared one-pass placement owner in both existing history indexes.

The existing hidden-input boundary now covers exec completions as well as heartbeats and travels through history pages and SSE state. A visible user consumes the boundary without taking the flag. Tool-shaped user rows retain it because they do not start a user turn in the Control UI. The fix changes derived ordering/display projection, not canonical transcript bytes, schema, or public protocol.

## Evidence

[Matching current-main and repaired screenshots, repeated Chromium observations, controls, and regression results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186323#issuecomment-6457781734).

Production-built Control UI served by real isolated Gateways: main `a055ff33bbe74d95357f5d77bedc2cebdbd89c48` twice folds the previous answer; the repaired production code twice keeps it visible, both before and after reload. Expanding main's disclosure reveals the answer. The hidden exec notice remains absent. Normal same-turn and intervening-real-user controls agree on both builds. Candidate canonical transcript bytes remain unchanged across reads/reloads.

This is a deterministic synthetic-transcript replay through real history import, Gateway RPCs and browser rendering, not a native background-process execution claim. A local provider fixture avoids real-provider credentials. No Gateway responses or browser DOM were rewritten.

## Regression Coverage

Consolidated repeated transcript/index setup and inline-SSE fixtures, and reused the existing UI history/reload assertion helper. All distinct assertions remain: memory/worker indexes, backdated local sequence, unmatched import anchoring, plain-user consumption, tool-shaped user rows, hidden exec/heartbeat boundaries, SSE continuity and legacy commentary folding.

- Identical consolidated Gateway regressions: main has **7 intended failures**; candidate **153/153 passing across 8 files**.
- UI grouping/history-reload tests: **21/21 passing**.
- Changed-test Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passing.
- Test/support growth is **0**, reduced from +174; no ratchet ceiling change.
- Production remains the contributor's shared-owner repair: **+152/−23 (net +129)**. The linear import-placement pass replaces the earlier repeated per-import local scan.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: a revert restores the prior derived ordering and display behavior without undoing writes or migrating state. No canonical transcript rewrite, new persistent format, SDK change, or permission change. Blast radius is imported chat-history ordering and hidden-input turn presentation, including paged and SSE history consumers.

prs.title: fix: reach the configured owner on project-parent sessions_spawn preflight
prs.body:
Closes #182467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: project-attached `sessions_spawn` rejects a plugin-resolved child model (`deepseek/*`, native `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) as `Unknown model` or `selected account or native runtime is unavailable`, even though the agent's configured owner knows the model and a normal session on the same installation accepts it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Child spawned from a project-parent session resolves provider-plugin and native-runtime models the agent's configured owner already knows, without the operator having to detach the project or `/reset` the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A project-parent read supplies the project workspace to `withPreparedModelCatalogOwner({ readOnly: true })`. `resolveReadOnlyPublishedModelCatalogOwner` builds two candidates (`full`, `activationFull`); both carry the explicit project workspace, so the resolver's exact-key lookup misses the single configured owner published at the agent's workspace. The configured-workspace fallback inside `resolvePublishedOwner` is also gated on strict workspace equality, so it misses too. The code then falls through to `acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime`, which builds a runtime-free ephemeral catalog without the provider plugin registry — the plugin's `resolveDynamicModel` hook is never invoked and the model is reported as unknown.

This change narrows the preflight to a third read-only candidate that probes at the agent's **known configured workspace** (resolved via `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir`, not any arbitrary workspace) with every other identity dimension carried from the caller and `env` bound to the effective process environment so the resolver's env match stays exact instead of degrading to the wildcard branch. If the configured workspace is not resolvable, the fallback is suppressed and the existing ephemeral read-only path takes over, preserving the prior behavior for that shape.

Agent, agent-directory, inherited-auth, environment, and generation isolation are preserved exactly. Writable publications and non-read-only paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage in `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:
  - Positive: project-parent read falls back to the configured workspace with agent, agent-dir, env, and workspace identity verified in the fallback input; the fallback carries a plugin-provider model that is absent from the ephemeral read-only snapshot.
  - Negative: when a competing publication matches by workspace but diverges on agent / agent-dir / env, the fallback rejects it and the ephemeral read-only path takes over.
  - Suppression: a workspace-less caller does not synthesize a second workspace-less probe.
  - Guard: when the agent's configured workspace is unknown, the preflight skips the project-parent fallback and lands on the ephemeral read-only build.
- Full targeted test suite (6 files, 119 tests) passes locally:
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.workspace.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.plan.test.ts`

<details>
<summary>Review notes</summary>

Marked draft pending maintainer sign-off on scope. ATX reviews surfaced a residual architectural suggestion to gate configured-workspace reuse behind an explicit, validated project-parent predicate; introducing such a predicate expands scope beyond the acceptance criteria recorded in the issue's Codex review ("preserve agent, account, environment, and generation isolation"; "a focused inventory-owner correction"), so it is deferred.

</details>

prs.body:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor stays silent when cross-conversation recall defaults on for a personal install but the required bundled Active Memory plugin is disabled by default.

## User Impact

Doctor and Doctor lint now warn about the missing prerequisite and name both existing choices: set `plugins.entries.active-memory.enabled=true`, or opt out with `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations=false`. The plugin is not enabled automatically; recall defaults, privacy/session eligibility, UI/RPC behavior, and memory status are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing effective plugin-activation owner once per Doctor operation instead of a separate availability policy that treated an absent entry as enabled. Keep the plugin's internal disable switch and the existing warning severity. prs.title: fix: hear Google Meet participants using WebAudio playback
prs.body:
Closes #178681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Google Meet participants being inaudible when Meet renders their speech through WebAudio without `<audio>` or `<video>` elements. The browser bridge can otherwise stay connected while sending silent PCM.

## User Impact

Managed Chrome capture receives Meet's worklet-based participant playback while excluding microphone and assistant audio. A restored pre-join tab reloads once to initialize observation. An active call is never automatically reloaded; capture explains when leaving and rejoining is required. Custom input commands keep their existing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Meet owns early playback-graph observation; the existing shared capture owner connects eligible playback to provider input and restores the original speaker sink on cleanup. Observation alone does not collect audio. The optional `webAudioPlaybackGlobal` parameter and registry contract are documented in the SDK reference. Existing DOM capture remains necessary for other meeting plugins.

Integrated main at `105d109ce594`. Whole-change delta: production +248/-4 (net +244), tests +242/-1 (net +241), documentation +10/-1. This growth provides graph discovery, source revocation, sink restoration, and pre-join lifecycle handling; there is no separate capture transport. The simplification pass found no removable duplicate owner or obsolete DOM path. This capture fix remains separate from consultation-admission repairs.

Thanks to @shannon0430 for the implementation and live investigation. Contributor commits and authorship are preserved.

## Evidence

- **Base red:** real isolated Chromium, synthetic worklet-only Meet page, and production page selection/capture entry points on `364c0d4ebcd4`. With no media elements, PCM peak remained zero and the regression failed (`expected 0 to be greater than 100`; one failure, four cases skipped).
- **Integrated head green:** 116/116 tests in seven files passed in 90.27 seconds including compilation. All five real Chromium cases passed: nonzero worklet PCM, early/late microphone exclusion, disconnected-source retirement, ownership loss, sink restoration, and non-Meet isolation. Shared DOM capture, realtime transport, Meet routing, and Teams/Zoom adapters also passed.
- Commands: `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_E2E=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-meet-playback.chromium.test.ts extensions/google-meet/src/transports/google-meet-audio-routing.test.ts extensions/google-meet/src/transports/google-meet-playback-observation.test.ts src/meeting-bot/browser-audio-capture-source.test.ts src/meeting-bot/realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts extensions/teams-meetings/src/transports/teams-meetings-platform-adapter.test.ts extensions/zoom-meetings/src/transports/zoom-meetings-platform-adapter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

prs.title: fix: preserve durable notes before context overflow recovery
prs.body:
Closes #114081.
Related: #118681. Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the earlier investigation and checkpoint proposal.

## What Problem This Solves

Provider-reported context overflow can compact a conversation without giving the memory provider a chance to save durable notes.

## User Impact

Gateway reply recovery now attempts the existing private memory flush before overflow compaction, using the active session model and its normal fallbacks. A flush already attempted during preflight is not repeated. Completed, skipped, and failed checkpoints are recorded in Gateway logs. No new configuration or persisted schema changes.

This is best-effort preservation: a local provider can reject the checkpoint too when its input does not fit. The checkpoint disables automatic SDK, provider-native, and overflow-recovery compaction; ordinary compaction can continue and report its own failure. Direct lower-level agent calls without a reply owner explicitly log that the checkpoint was skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The proactive and reactive paths had separate admission boundaries. Recovery now calls the reply-owned memory flush instead of adding another implementation. It temporarily releases execution capacity so concurrency one works, checks source authority after the awaited flush, and keeps a per-turn attempt fact across fallback candidates.

## Evidence

- Matched Gateway chat fixture, concurrency one: original production sources make zero flush requests and write no canary; fixed head receives the same provider overflow, runs one flush with a successful write, then compacts and retries successfully. The synthetic `BLUE-OTTER-20340 ships on Friday` decision exists in the daily memory file afterward. Baseline turns took 5.01/3.75 s; final-head turns took 6.13/5.41 s. Two checkpoint model requests are one tool-call/result turn, not two flush attempts.
- Native Ollama `qwen3:8b` through Gateway `chat.send`, observed with `agent.wait` and `chat.history`: real HTTP 400 overflows trigger the checkpoint. With an undersized 6,144-token context, the checkpoint is also rejected and its failure is logged; compaction subsequently fails at the summary output limit, with a visible user error. A separate proactive control writes the canary and later overflow logs `skipped: already attempted this turn`. These native controls prove admission, failure visibility, persistence, and deduplication; they do not prove successful native reactive preservation. No retained source transcript deletion is claimed.
- Three new regression expectations fail against the original production sources (three failures, two controls passed; 156.35 s including compiler preparation). Final component results cover 222 passing tests across nine files. Initial batch: 308.79 s with one fixture-seeding failure; repaired fixture: 129.16 s; final six-file rerun: 353.82 s, all 133 tests passed.
- Final-head full build passed (3m 27s), as did core and targeted test typechecks, required baseline ratchets, line-cap, and formatting. Scoped lint passed in 14.72 s after installing its missing pinned workspace dependency.
- The follow-up native-compaction regression failed on the prior head (one failure, one control passed; 89.21 s). All 115 follow-up tests pass across six files (118.98 s), covering session preparation, native compaction, memory-session custody, and revoked write authority. Core/types, scoped lint, all baseline ratchets, line cap, and format checks pass.
- Final-head independent Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the native compaction owner supplied as source context.
- Final-head source-retirement proof: pause the provider before returning the checkpoint tool call, reset that exact source session, then release the response. The detached run aborts and the daily memory file contains no canary. This exercises Gateway admission through the final write boundary. Proof platform: local macOS only.

Production: +143/-46 lines (net +97); tests: +250/-251 (net -1); docs: +7. The production growth connects existing owners and carries private recovery/cycle controls through their existing entry points; it adds no alternate flush implementation. Nearby pressure calculation and test fixtures were consolidated without weakening assertions.

prs.title: fix(ui): chat hides narration after a run finishes
prs.body:
Related: #180490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed Control UI dashboard chats hiding assistant narration inside one work disclosure, while bubble mode leaves completed tool activity outside that grouping.

## User Impact

Assistant narration and visual results stay inline in source order. Only contiguous tool and reasoning work collapses, in both flat and bubble mode. Opening one work section does not open another, and loading older history preserves expanded sections.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presentation layer now separates mixed assistant envelopes without changing stored history or the source identities used by copy, reply, reactions, and full-message loading. Capped envelopes and envelopes whose Markdown or visibility depends on surrounding blocks remain intact, so full-message recovery replaces one rendering unit. Envelopes carrying saved media also stay intact so their attachments render exactly once. Work disclosures anchor to the following visible boundary so history prepends do not replace their identity. Whole-run timing stays in the final recap and is not assigned to individual work stretches. A fresh pane restores saved timing from admitted cache metadata or the live session row only when it matches the visible completed reply; changing agent or Gateway invalidates the prior recap.

The refresh retains current main's distinct-message identities and ordered transcript indexes. Redundant portable fixture cases, repeated viewport checks, and verbose duration-test setup were removed. Unused session timing inputs were removed from work grouping and its memo keys. The pure projection tests run once; flat and bubble rendering retain separate browser coverage. The preview-order test uses a compact widget so it does not assume offscreen virtual rows stay mounted; the separate geometry regression remains.

Original implementation and regression work by @Marvinthebored; contributor commits are retained.

## Evidence

The prior CI runs [40596392967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40596392967) and [40599346638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40599346638) exposed the test-line ceiling and a first-load video-widget test flake. The existing ratchet stays enabled; assertions, snapshots, and test inclusion are unchanged.

The retained tests cover distinct ordering, source actions, privacy, Markdown, result pairing, recovery, status, and timing boundaries. Earlier consolidation reduced test/fixture growth from 1,823 to 1,424 lines; the final lazy-import wait adds one line.

The video-widget test now waits for its actual lazy import before checking the play button. Its playback and retained-frame assertions are unchanged. All 92 selected widget, duration, progress, and transcript tests pass after integrating main. The production implementation did not change in this CI follow-up. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. A fresh full-candidate review after integration found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The bounded budget follow-up also passed independent review. A later review identified persisted media being copied into every split fragment; the renderer regression reproduced three image tiles from one saved attachment. The repair keeps media-bearing envelopes whole through the existing media reader. All 65 tests in the affected projection, message-group, and video-gallery suites pass after the final integration (17.65 seconds wall time; 12.86 seconds Vitest duration). Independent review of the media repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings. A concurrent main edit then conflicted only in the test-budget scalar. ClawSweeper reviewed that same head with no findings and marked it ready for maintainer review.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only sessions never get the daily session reset
prs.body:
Closes #185942

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `session.reset` set to `daily` (or `idle`), a session used only by voice never resets, so every voice consult re-sends days of old history to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: after the configured reset boundary, voice consults (browser Talk, meetings, voice calls) and new Talk calls start the new conversation, the same as a typed message. Sessions without an automatic reset policy are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Voice consults reused whatever session existed and never ran the reset-freshness check that typed turns run. Before a consult claims its session, it now checks freshness with the shared check (`resolveSessionEntryResetFreshnessAsync`). If the session is stale, the consult rolls it over in place through the same reset lifecycle the agent command uses (`resetSessionEntryLifecycle`): the session id stays the same, the transcript gets a `preserve-tail` reset boundary with reason `daily` or `idle`, and old run metadata and runtime state are cleared.

The rollover runs before the consult's session admission, because rollover cleanup interrupts work bound to the old incarnation. It first applies the existing work-start policy (`resolveSessionWorkStartError`), on the read entry and again on the row it replaces, so archived, restart-tombstoned or provider-paused sessions keep their state and admission still rejects them with the specific reason. Sessions with a locked model selection are skipped, as in the agent command.

All four consult callers (browser Talk, meeting bot, voice-call, FaceTime) share this runtime, so they all get the reset. The reset clears the old incarnation's queued system events and prompt state but keeps queued controller inputs: browser Talk reserves its input before calling the consult runtime and passes that input's signal to the consult, so clearing the mailbox would cancel the very request that triggered the reset (`clearCommittedSessionResetRuntimeState` gains an optional `preserveControllerInputs`; other callers are unchanged). Accepted edge case: any other input already queued when a consult resets the session also continues, into the new conversation. After a day or an idle period without use such a queue is rare, and it holds the user's own requests.

A Talk call also quotes the session's history to the realtime provider and to every consult when it starts, before any consult runs, so a stale session would still replay old context that way. When the reset is due, `readTalkRealtimeInitialItems` now quotes no history; the call's first consult then resets the session in place. The call start itself writes nothing: the Gateway pins the call's session target before the handler reads history, and changing the session there fails `talk.client.create` with "session changed". One read-only check, `resolveDueVoiceSessionReset` (`src/talk/voice-session-reset.ts`), decides for both the call start and the consult. Accepted difference from a typed reset: such a call starts with no quoted history rather than the 6-message continuity tail.

A call that starts before the boundary and keeps running past it holds the history it quoted at start and passes it as every consult's transcript. Consults now take an optional `onSessionReset` callback: when a consult resets the session, the browser Talk and Gateway-relay call owner (`createTalkClientAgentConsultRunner`) clears that snapshot, so the resetting consult and every later one quote none of it. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime transcripts are live call content and do not use the callback.

Because idle expiry now applies to them too, each consult that reuses a session also records `lastInteractionAt`; before, only browser Talk recorded voice activity, so continuous meeting or call use would otherwise have idled out.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts`, with a real session store and the clock pinned to midday:
  - Daily: a voice session started two days ago with one earlier answer in its transcript, `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, then a consult. On `main` the consult's model history still contains the earlier answer (fails). With the fix the history starts fresh, the session id is unchanged and the lifecycle revision is new; a second consult continues that session without resetting again. Control: a session started one minute earlier keeps its history and revision.
  - Blocked: the same stale session, archived. The consult is rejected with "is archived", no run starts and the session is not reset. Fails if the work-start check is removed.
  - Browser reservation: a controller input reserved the way `client-gateway-control.ts` reserves a Talk tool call, its signal passed as the consult's. The consult answers, the input is not aborted and the session is reset. Without `preserveControllerInputs` it rejects with "Session mailbox cleared".
  - Cancelled: the caller aborts while the consult is still preparing. No run starts and the session is not reset; the reset commit checks the caller's signal through `resetSessionEntryLifecycle`'s `commitGuard`. Fails without that guard.
  - Call start (`session-transcript-preview.hydration.test.ts`): a stale session whose first of ten messages holds a code word; a Talk call's starting history is empty and the session's lifecycle revision is unchanged. Control: a same-day session quotes all ten. Fails on `main`.
  - Call crossing the boundary: a caller-supplied transcript of pre-reset history is replaced through `onSessionReset` in the prompt of the consult that resets (`agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts`), and the call owner drops it for the triggering and following consults (`client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts`). Each fails if its half is removed; the owner test fails on `main`.
  - Idle: `idleMinutes: 5`, a consult every four minutes for twelve minutes keeps the session; the next consult after ten quiet minutes resets it. Fails if consults stop recording `lastInteractionAt`.
- On a Linux bench, on this head: all of `src/gateway/talk`, the Talk consult, session-reset cleanup, session fork, config override, session actor memory, call-start history and prompt-prefix stability suites pass (718 tests); on unchanged `main` the new daily, browser-reservation, idle, call-start and call-snapshot regressions fail.
- Changed-file core test typecheck and `tsconfig.core.json` typecheck clean; oxfmt and oxlint clean on the changed files.
- `pnpm check:changed` on the bench: everything passes except the dead-export scan, which reports three unused exports already present on `main` (`extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts`; this branch does not touch them). The wider `src/talk`, `src/gateway/talk` and auto-reply session suites pass (1,094 tests).
- Docs: `docs/concepts/session.md` now names voice consults for both idle activity and automatic reset.
- Stored data: no new fields or migrations; the rollover writes the existing session row fields and the existing transcript reset boundary.

## Real Gateway runs (upgrade from 2026.10.8, real models)

Bench container per run, `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, agent model `gpt-4.1-mini` through a local forwarder that records request bodies (never headers or keys).

1. Day one on the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm: a real Gateway and a Control UI dashboard session, five typed turns. The first says "Please remember this code word for later: PELICAN-DAY1"; the other four are fillers, so the session holds more than the 6-message tail a reset keeps.
2. A copy of that state per run, then the tree's `openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` (the upgrade step), and a Gateway from the tree with the clock two days ahead.
3. Browser Talk: a real Gateway-controlled call (`talk.client.create` with `gateway-control-v1`, `gpt-realtime-2.1`). Headless Chrome posts the WebRTC offer the way the Control UI does, and its microphone plays a recorded question: "Please ask the OpenClaw agent: what code word did I ask you to remember earlier in this conversation? If there is none, the answer is none." The realtime model calls the agent tool, and the Gateway runs the consult through its reservation path.
4. A call crossing the boundary: same call, but the Gateway clock starts at 03:58 the day after day one (session still fresh, so the call quotes the old history at start) and moves to 04:01 once the WebRTC answer is applied, before the question is spoken (it begins after 6 s of silence).
5. Plugin route: one consult through a small proof plugin that calls the plugin SDK's `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, the same call voice-call and FaceTime make.

```text
browser Talk call            agent request   code word in request   daily reset   spoken answer
main (5b1482d925d)           15 messages     yes                    0             "The code word is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 4df25a8)      7 messages     no                     1             "none"

call started 03:58, asked 04:01   agent request   code word in request   daily reset   spoken answer
main (5b1482d925d)                15 messages     yes                    0             "The codeword is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 4df25a8)           7 messages     no                     1             "None. There wasn't a codeword set earlier in this conversation."

plugin-route consult         agent request   code word in request                 reply
main (5b1482d925d)           13 messages     yes                                  "... is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 4df25a8)      9 messages     no                                   "NONE"

Doctor on the 2026.10.8 state: ok on all four runs; talk.client.create succeeds on the stale session
```

The 6 kept day-one messages in the consult are the same continuity tail a typed message gets after a daily reset (`DEFAULT_REPLAY_MAX_MESSAGES`); the realtime call itself quotes none of them. In the crossing run the agent prompt is stamped 04:01 on both trees, so the consult ran after the boundary; on this PR it resets the session and its prompt no longer carries the history the call quoted at 03:58. The consult after that is covered by the call-owner regression above, not by a live run.

Follow-up worth considering: the in-place rollover sequence (clear rotated metadata, new lifecycle revision, reset boundary, runtime cleanup) now appears in both the agent command and the consult runtime; a shared helper could serve both.

prs.title: perf(cron): avoid repeated definition hashing during publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a cron store recreates job objects, causing definition publication to normalize, serialize, and hash both copies of every job even when no definition changed.

## User Impact

Cron publication does less work on the Gateway main thread. Definition notifications and authorization checks retain their existing behavior; no configuration, schema, or migration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Full-store load and CRUD replies carry per-job configuration revisions from the worker when an observer needs them. The service retains the last published revisions and compares tokens; targeted runtime publications derive only the returned rows. Source changes reset the revision map. This removes the duplicate derivation of each previous definition, rather than merely moving both hashes to a worker.

Preparation retains errors as values until a comparison actually needs them. This preserves the existing initial-load and quarantine behavior for malformed stored rows. The strict revision resolver used for authority checks is unchanged.

Production LOC: **+79** (100 added, 21 removed; tests and tooling excluded). This growth is needed to carry the worker fact, maintain its publication lifetime, and preserve lazy errors across the worker boundary. The map holds the current publication's facts and resets with the service's source; validation policy stays with its existing owners.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: 200 unchanged synthetic jobs must emit zero changes and perform zero main-thread definition hashes; changed and removed jobs must emit once. Five alternating base/candidate owner samples measure CPU and wall time at 1,000 publications per arm, with separate allocation sampling at 100 publications per arm. Candidate preparation is included separately so relocated work is not counted as deleted work. Cloning, IPC, and database work are outside this owner benchmark.

Baseline: `4b27ee88cec9` (includes #186245). The measured production files are byte-identical to the final PR head. On a local Mac, the five-pair medians per 200-job publication were:

| Metric | Base | Candidate publication | Candidate preparation | Candidate total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CPU, µs | 5,783.3 | 15.7 | 2,829.8 | 2,844.7 |
| Wall time, µs | 5,805.7 | 15.8 | 2,862.6 | 2,878.3 |
| Sampled allocation, bytes | 9,973,630 | 44,176 | 4,978,455 | 5,022,308 |

Mean paired total deltas: **CPU −50.5%, allocation −49.6%**. Main-thread publication CPU fell about 99.7% and allocation about 99.6%. CPU ranges were 5,649–5,806 µs base versus 2,766–2,908 µs candidate total; allocation ranges were 9,949,517–9,974,164 bytes base versus 5,011,161–5,023,563 bytes candidate total. prs.title: feat(ui): clear failed session alerts from the Subagents panel and session hovercard
prs.body:
Related: #185192, #185054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several child sessions fail or time out, the parent's sidebar row stays red ("Child session X failed: reason") and each failure can only be cleared by opening that child, one at a time; the Subagents panel lists the failures but cannot acknowledge them.

## User Impact

User impact: failure alerts can be cleared in place. In the Subagents panel each unread failure has a **Mark {name} as read** control and the Failed heading has **Mark all as read** (two or more), on desktop and mobile. The session hovercard shows **Dismiss** under a failure, including a child failure folded into its parent row. Acknowledging clears the sidebar alert and hovercard notice on every surface and device, survives reload, and a later failure of the same session alerts again. Panel grouping does not change: failed runs stay listed under Failed, exactly as on main after you open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already decides whether a failure is still an alert: a failed session alerts until its read time passes its failure time, and opening the session writes that read time. These controls send the same conditional `sessions.patch { unread: false }` (fenced by `expectedSessionId` and `expectedMarkedUnreadAt`), so there is one acknowledgement shared by every surface, tab and device, and no new state, option or API.

- Controls appear only where the viewer can patch the failed session. For a child failure folded into a parent row, the hovercard uses that child's own sharing role and manual-unread marker, so a session-scoped owner gets Dismiss and a manually unread child is acknowledged instead of rejected as stale.
- The alert stays until the Gateway row reports the read. If the Gateway rejects the write, an error toast says so with the Gateway's reason ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. ..."), and the alert and its control stay, so the same click retries; the next successful acknowledgement replaces that toast with "Marked as read". It is a toast rather than an inline line because the hovercard can close before the reply arrives (session deletion reports its failures the same way).
- Focus: on desktop it moves to the next failure's control, then to the acknowledged row; on mobile it stays on the row. The hovercard keeps its existing focus restoration.
- Known limits: the acknowledgement is fenced to the session, not a run, so a newer failure that lands between render and click is acknowledged too (opening the session behaves the same today). While the parent conversation is open, main's existing hidden-run read for subagents can acknowledge a child whose retry fails immediately; this PR does not change that path.

## Decision for the area owner

The open question is only whether the Subagents panel and the session hovercard should offer these acknowledgement controls (per row, Mark all as read for two or more, Dismiss in the hovercard). They add no state, option, setting or API: each control sends the same conditional read receipt the Control UI already sends when you open a failed session, so the Gateway stays the single owner of "is this failure still an alert", grouping stays by run outcome exactly as on main, and declining the direction means simply not merging. Approving it on this PR is enough; nothing else depends on it.

#185054 (open, another contributor) makes the same choice for the composer failure cards that #185192 has since removed from main; this PR covers the surfaces that remain.

<details><summary>Surface inventory</summary>

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel, desktop Failed group | Lists failures, no acknowledgement | Per-row Mark as read, Mark all as read (2+); rows stay in Failed |
| Subagents panel, mobile Finished list | Failed rows with red indicator, no acknowledgement | Same controls; rows keep their Failed indicator |
| Sidebar row failure indicator (own or folded child) | Own failure via row menu Mark as read; folded child only by opening it | Cleared by any acknowledgement of the failed session |
| Session hovercard failure section | No action | Dismiss, acknowledging the failing child when folded |
| Background session toast, sidebar issues inbox, chat details tally, native roster | Unchanged | Unchanged (transient, no session failures, or counts only) |

</details>

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `isUnacknowledgedSessionFailure` (`ui/src/lib/session-attention.ts`) is the single failure-alert rule; `sessionRowAttention` and the chat pane's read acknowledgement use it instead of two copies.
- Error attention carries the failed session's `sourceSessionId`, `sourceMarkedUnreadAt` and `sourceSharingRole`, so the hovercard targets the failed session with its own fence and role.
- `canDismissSessionFailure` / `dismissSessionFailures` (`ui/src/lib/sessions/session-failure-dismissal.ts`) own the access check, the conditional write and its rejection feedback (the shared `showToast` owner with `severity: "error"`).
- The hovercard error section moved to `session-hovercard-error.tsx` to keep `session-hovercard-solid.tsx` under the file line cap.
- New copy: `chat.subagentsPanel.markFailureRead` ("Mark {name} as read") and `chat.subagentsPanel.markAllFailuresRead` ("Mark all as read"). `sessionsView.markFailureReadFailed` ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. {error}") and `sessionsView.markFailureReadDone` ("Marked as read"). The hovercard reuses `common.dismiss`.

</details>

## Evidence

### Real Gateway, real failed subagents (Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2)

An isolated Gateway built from this branch (`dist/` plus `dist/control-ui`, served bundle hash checked against the build) on loopback with a synthetic config. A parent turn spawns four real subagents through `sessions_spawn`; only the loopback model provider is scripted, and it rejects every child request with HTTP 400, so each child run fails through the real runtime (`status: "failed"`, `lastRunError: "LLM request rejected: Synthetic provider rejected the request | synthetic_rejection"`). No WebSocket interception; frames are observed passively. Two browser contexts are paired as two devices.

| | Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel with four real failures | ![main: Failed 4, no controls, parent row red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-panel.png) | ![branch: Mark as read per row and Mark all as read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-controls.png) |
| Parent row hovercard (child failure folded) | ![main: failure notice, no action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-hovercard.png) | ![branch: Dismiss under the child failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-hovercard-dismiss.png) |
| After acknowledging | | ![one row read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-one-read.png) ![all read: rows stay in Failed, parent row no longer red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-all-read.png) |
| Second device after reload | | ![device B: no controls, no red row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-device-b-after-reload.png) |
| Same child fails again | | ![device B sidebar alert returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-sidebar-device-b.png) ![device B panel offers Mark as read again (WebKit)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-panel-device-b-webkit.png) |

Sequence asserted in both browsers (all pass):

1. Main build: Failed 4, zero acknowledgement controls in the panel and hovercard, still 4 after reload.
2. Branch build: the hovercard on the parent row names one failed child. That child is also marked unread by hand (`sessions.patch { unread: true }`); Dismiss then sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` equal to its marker and the Gateway advances `lastReadAt`.
3. Mark as read on one row, then Mark all as read on the remaining two: controls go, all four rows stay in Failed, the parent row's red indicator clears.
4. Reload: still acknowledged. A second paired device: no controls, no red row.
5. The operator asks the parent to retry one child; the parent's real `sessions_send` runs it again and it fails again. Both devices show the red parent row with "Child session ... failed" and that one row's Mark as read control.

Captured `sessions.patch` request/response pairs for the four acknowledgements (Chromium; WebKit identical in shape):

| Child | Sent | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| folded child, manually unread | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: <its marker> }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| row control | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| Mark all as read (2) | same shape, one per child | ok, `lastReadAt` set |

Real-seam red for the hovercard fence: the same harness against the previous head of this PR sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null` for the manually unread child; the Gateway answers ok with the entry unchanged (no `lastReadAt`) and the alert stays.

### Rejected acknowledgement and retry (mocked Gateway, Playwright Chromium and WebKit 27.2)

The mock Gateway holds the first `sessions.patch` and answers it with `UNAVAILABLE: Session store unavailable`; the second click goes through. Asserted in both engines: the error toast text, the alert and control still present and enabled, a second `sessions.patch` on the same control, the alert cleared, and the error toast replaced by "Marked as read".

| | Rejected | Retried |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel (WebKit) | ![error toast, Mark as read control still on the failed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, control gone, row still in Failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-retried.png) |
| Session hovercard (Chromium) | ![error toast, sidebar row still red, Dismiss still offered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, sidebar alert cleared](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/chromium-hovercard-dismiss-retried.png) |

A rejection was not forced on the real Gateway: the session store would have to be broken under a running Gateway, or the row changed between render and click, which races the live row update. The retry sends the same request as the real-Gateway acknowledgements above.

### Mobile (mocked Gateway, 390px)

![mobile before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-before.png) ![mobile after marking one read: control gone, Failed indicator kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-after-one-read.png)

### Tests (macOS arm64)

Red = the new tests on the previous head's production code; green = this branch.

- `ui/src/components/session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts`, new: Dismiss on a folded child failure under `operator.sessions.write` sends that child's `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` and `expectedSessionId`. Red: Dismiss is absent (child role dropped); with broad `operator.write` it sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null`. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/lib/session-attention.test.ts`: failure stays an alert until read and alerts again later; error attention carries the source session id, marker and role. Red: source facts missing. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagents-panel.test.ts`, 2 cases: desktop controls only on unread failures the viewer can patch, exact conditional params, rows stay in Failed, focus to the next control then to the row; mobile acknowledged in place with its Failed indicator and focus on the row. Red: fail. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/components/session-hovercard.test.ts`: Dismiss renders and calls its owner only when supplied.
- Rejected write, new: `chat-subagents-panel.test.ts` (desktop and mobile) and `session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts` reject the first `sessions.patch`, then expect the error toast with the Gateway reason, the control still present and enabled, a successful second click, and "Marked as read" replacing the error. Red on the previous head: 3 fail (no toast; the rejection was swallowed). Green: pass.
- Playwright (mocked Gateway) `subagents-panel.e2e.test.ts` and `session-progress-hovercard.e2e.test.ts`, including the two new rejection cases: 19/19 pass in Chromium and 19/19 in WebKit.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, oxlint, oxfmt and stylelint on the changed files: pass.
- Full `pnpm lint`: exits 1 on 11 errors, all in files this PR does not touch (`extensions/copilot`, `extensions/knowledge`, `extensions/oc-path`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/tlon`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, `src/agents/code-mode-execution.ts`); no changed file appears in its output.

prs.title: fix(exec): macOS app node exec with timeoutSeconds 0 ends after 20 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #185429 #139706 #163978 #162789 #135272 #166652 #142874

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` on a macOS app node with `timeoutSeconds: 0` ("0 disables" the process lifetime) ends after about
20 seconds with `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown`, and the result is
lost.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands on a macOS app node return their result instead of an unknown outcome after 20 s.
The node host ships inside OpenClaw.app, so users get this with the next macOS app build. Runs stay bounded by the
Gateway invoke deadline (default 1805 s for `timeoutSeconds: 0`), which cancels the node invocation, the same bound an
explicit `0` already has.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway forwards an exec timeout of `0` to the node as `timeoutMs: null`, documented as "no expiry". The macOS app
runs a null timeout without a timer. The node host's socket client exempted only `0` from its response deadline, so
`null` got the 20 s default. #172117 fixed every finite timeout; this is the one input it left out. The change treats
`null` like `0`.

Reach: the node host collapses an absent nested timeout into `null` before calling the app, so every `system.run`
without a nested timeout loses the node-side 20 s deadline, not only `timeoutSeconds: 0`. Those calls stay bounded
by their Gateway invoke deadline plus `node.invoke.cancel`. Example: the remote-skills bin probe uses a shorter Gateway
deadline, so nothing changes for it in practice. One accepted edge case: if the Gateway link drops mid-run, the node
host waits as long as the companion runs, as it already does for `0`.

Overlap: draft #163978 (last updated 2026-10-15) reworked the same deadline before #172117 landed and targets the
code from before it. This is the minimal residual on current main. The 20 s default for direct callers that omit
`timeoutMs`, pinned in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts`, is unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause path (origin/main 2bf23407639)</summary>

- `src/agents/exec-tool-timeout.ts:24-27`: `timeoutSeconds: 0` gives `runTimeoutMs: 0`, sent as nested `timeoutMs`.
- `src/gateway/node-registry.system-run.ts:71-81`: `timeoutMs <= 0` becomes `null` ("preserving null for no expiry").
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:328`, `:747`: the exec host request carries `timeoutMs: null`.
- `src/infra/exec-host.ts:59-65`: only `=== 0` disables the deadline; `addTimerTimeoutGraceMs(null)` is `undefined`, so the `?? 20_000` fallback applies.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ExecHostExecutor.swift:139`, `ShellExecutor.swift:212-219`: a nil timeout runs with no timer.

The test imports the Gateway normalizer on purpose, so the wire value in the test is the one the Gateway really
sends.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused test `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` "waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run". It runs a
real Unix-domain-socket peer with fake timers: it derives `timeoutMs` from `normalizeSystemRunInvokeParams`, advances a
fake day, then replies.

- Base (`src/infra/exec-host.ts` from origin/main), `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` (excerpt, lines in log order):
  ```text
  FAIL   infra  src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts > exec host real UDS boundary > waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
          "code": "TIMEOUT",
          "message": "TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown",
  Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
  ```
- Branch, `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`:
  ```text
  Test Files  4 passed (4)
       Tests  26 passed (26)
  ```
- Neighboring node-host suites on the head, `pnpm test src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.environment.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 59 passed (59)`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: 33 phases ok, including format, lint, typecheck core and core tests, and import cycles. The dead export scan fails on `extensions/browser/src/browser/client.types.ts: BrowserGraphicsDevice`, a file this diff does not touch (not re-run at base).

### Real behavior proof (macOS app node)

After (app built from this head, `81b290c95b4`):
- Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/40554854403 (mac/proof-3, macos-26-intel, Xcode 26.6)
- App: OpenClaw.app 2026.10.7 debug (adhoc); bundled private runtime build `2026.10.7-81b290c95b4b-2026-10-27T17-58-06.000Z`
- Node: `clientId openclaw-macos`, packaged app, node `8f10b9bf3873…`
- Request: `node.invoke system.run`, `sh -c 'sleep 45; echo done'`, `timeoutMs: 0`
- Result: `ok: true`, `exitCode: 0`, `timedOut: false`, `stdout: "done\n"`; gateway logged `node.invoke 55802 ms`; scenario `PASS 3 head: done after 59s`

Before (same command on a real installed app node, pre-patch):
- App 2026.10.6, commit `41c5d94f722c`, built `2026-10-22T19:35:02Z`; bundled runtime `Contents/Resources/runtime` contains `request.timeoutMs === 0 ? 0 : …` only.
- Gateway `exec` tool, `host=node`, `timeoutSeconds: 0` → `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown` after ~20 s; no stdout.

Gaps: the after case ran through `node.invoke system.run` (the same Gateway → node host → exec-host route, including the patched `exec-host.ts`), not the agent `exec` tool, because the hosted runner exposes no `exec` tool on `/tools/invoke`. The `exec` tool on a patched app node was not run. The test peer proves the TypeScript transport, not Swift policy or native execution. The Swift side needs no change because it already runs a nil timeout without a timer, but its behavior on the cancel path (whether the child dies when the socket closes) was not observed natively.
