prs.title: fix(gateway): store auth token fails CLI Gateway calls on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Related: #151944

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw memory search`, `openclaw memory session-backfill`, and `openclaw gateway call` fail with "gateway.auth.token is configured as a secret reference but is unavailable in this command path" when `gateway.auth.token` is a `store` SecretRef and the state database runs on PostgreSQL. Exporting `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` doesn't help.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who keep the Gateway token in the shared secret store on a PostgreSQL-backed install can run Gateway-routed CLI commands again without putting the token in plaintext or in the environment. Installs whose state stays on SQLite behave exactly as before, including when another database family uses PostgreSQL.

## Why This Change Was Made

These CLI commands route to the running Gateway and deliberately skip storage selection at startup, so the store-backed token was read from the default SQLite state file, which has no entry. Config-first precedence then kept the environment token from replacing the configured ref, as documented. Gateway credential resolution now reads store refs from PostgreSQL only when the effective state family is PostgreSQL and the process hasn't selected an engine. SQLite state takes the unchanged direct path, so an unrelated family's DSN is never resolved. The reduced Gateway dispatch config keeps the `database` section so the state engine is known. Processes that already own a selection are unchanged. No new flags, env readers, or precedence changes.

This doesn't change the generic "Fix:" advice in the shared error text, and it doesn't add `--token` to memory commands; once the ref resolves, neither is needed for this trigger. #151944 is related (same error family, `agent exec`), but in a PostgreSQL reproduction `agent exec` already reached the model call before this change, so this PR doesn't claim to close it.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateways on macOS (own state dirs, port 28789, throwaway PostgreSQL 17). Tokens and DSNs are redacted.

- **Original trigger** (PostgreSQL state, `store`-backed token):
  - Before (main): `memory search`, `memory session-backfill --json`, and `gateway call health` failed with the error above, with and without `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`.
  - After (this head): `memory search test` returns `No matches.` with and without the env var, the backfill preview returns, and `gateway call health` returns `ok: true`. `--token` still works on `gateway call`, and a wrong token is rejected with `gateway token mismatch`.
- **Mixed engines** (SQLite state, PostgreSQL workboard, DSN env ref exported only into the Gateway process):
  - Previous PR head e21ca3b: `gateway call health` failed with `gateway_credentials_required`.
  - This head: `ok: true`, and the SQLite token is read directly.
- **Upgrade from latest stable** (npm `openclaw@2026.10.7`, 157d8c2). Stable rejects the `database` key, so this run uses stable's supported SQLite state with a `store`-backed token.
  - Stable stored the token and an env canary and served `gateway call health` / `memory search`.
  - After `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` with this head (the normal agent DB schema 25 to 37 step, backups saved), the patched Gateway started.
  - Every pre-upgrade config key and value was preserved, the `gateway` section is identical, and Doctor only added defaults.
  - `secrets store list` still shows `GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN` and `UPGRADE_CANARY`.
  - `gateway call health` returns `ok: true`, `memory search test` returns `No matches.` with and without the env var, and `--token` works.
- **Regression tests**, red before and green after:
  - `credentials-secret-inputs.test.ts`: store ref read from PostgreSQL state, existing selection kept, unselectable PostgreSQL engine reports the ref unavailable, and SQLite state with a PostgreSQL-only workboard never resolves the engine.
  - `gateway-dispatch-config.test.ts`: dispatch config keeps `database`.
- **Test runs:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/credentials-secret-inputs.test.ts src/config/gateway-dispatch-config.test.ts src/gateway/credentials.test.ts`: 45 passed.
- **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base HEAD~1` (lanes core, coreTests, docs) passes except two whole-tree scans that flag files outside this diff (`deprecated API usage` in `extensions/codex/harness.ts`, `dead export scan` in `extensions/codex/*` and `src/agents/*`). `git diff --check` is clean.

**Unrelated red shard.** `src/gateway/server.sessions-send.test.ts` fails the same 4 tests (`status: "no_reply"`) on main. The test uses a plain-string token, so the changed `store` path never runs there.

prs.title: feat(backup): create PostgreSQL archives while the Gateway runs
prs.body:
Related: #183094


## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup create` refuses to run while the Gateway is up once any store is on PostgreSQL, so every routine backup on a PostgreSQL install means taking the Gateway down for the whole archive.

## User Impact

User impact: operators on PostgreSQL can take a verified whole-installation archive without stopping the Gateway; it keeps serving requests during the capture.

On one production install with state, agents, and Workboard on PostgreSQL, the nightly offline archive on 2026-10-26 stopped the Gateway at 05:00:04 and it was healthy again at 05:23:35 (15 GB archive, verified). The same morning's update stopped the Gateway at 07:42:39 and the archive step alone ran until 08:08:48. With this change, that nightly backup no longer needs downtime.

Unchanged and still offline-only: `backup restore`, Git backups, generic local snapshots that select PostgreSQL, update capture, and Doctor database ports. With the Gateway stopped, `backup create` keeps taking offline custody exactly as before.

Consistency note for review (per the [storage review checkpoint](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes), this touches reader consistency): with the Gateway running, each PostgreSQL store is exported from its own `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot, and stores are captured one after another, not at one shared instant. That is the same per-store consistency the archive already gives live SQLite stores. Rows committed after a store's snapshot belong to the next backup. Operators who need one quiescent point across all stores can still stop the Gateway first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The PostgreSQL export already reads each store inside one repeatable-read, read-only transaction, so it is safe to run beside a live writer. The archive was refused only because it borrowed the offline-custody gate built for restore and update capture (#170828 added that gate together with the PostgreSQL backup path; its history records no separate reason to exclude online archive capture). This change lets only the archive caller run its read-only capture when a running Gateway or embedded agent owns the state, through the existing `onForeignOwner` hook that read-only commands such as `worktrees list` already use.

Running online exposed one real bug: the export read sequence allocation facts before its snapshot opened. A row committed in between was captured with an ID above the recorded allocation, so a matched restore would reissue that ID and the next insert would hit a duplicate key. Allocations are now read inside the export snapshot, and the manifest's PostgreSQL facts are read after the export; sequences only advance, so this can leave gaps but never reuse a captured ID. Offline behavior is unchanged because nothing writes between the reads.

<details>
<summary>Technical inventory</summary>

- `src/snapshot/database-backup.ts`: `runOfflineDatabaseBackup` takes `{ online: true }`. When set and the caller supplied its config and engine selection, a foreign owner runs the capture in the same database-backup scope instead of refusing. Nested store captures inside the archive join that scope. All other callers still pass `onForeignOwner: "refuse"`. The in-process `hasActiveGatewayStateOwner` refusal (backup inside the Gateway process) is unchanged.
- `src/infra/backup-create.ts`: the archive path opts in with `{ online: true }`.
- `src/snapshot/database-backup-core.worker.ts`: `exportPostgresBackup` no longer pre-reads allocations; `materializeDatabasePort` reads them inside its repeatable-read transaction, and the manifest records a post-export read.
- Docs: `docs/cli/backup.md`, `docs/gateway/postgresql.md`, `docs/install/backups.md`, `docs/reference/database-engines.md` describe online archive capture, its per-store consistency, and which commands stay offline-only.
- Other `createBackupArchive` callers inherit the behavior: `backup create --to <location>` and `migrate apply`'s pre-migration backup now run beside a running Gateway; Doctor's schema-guard archive runs under its own maintenance custody and is unaffected.
- Accepted edge case: a Gateway that stops or restarts mid-capture is not fenced beyond the existing per-store identity and catalog checks; the capture only reads, and restore re-verifies every capsule.
- No config option, schema, retention, or archive format change.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live run, isolated test Gateway on PostgreSQL 17.11** (scratch cluster and state dir, all three families on PostgreSQL):

- BEFORE (main `3b3efe9539c`, Gateway up): `openclaw backup create --verify` refused: "This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership ... This command is offline-only." No archive.
- AFTER (this branch, Gateway up, six Workboard writes through the Gateway during the run, 1 s `/readyz` probe): archive created in 6 s, `Archive verification: passed`, exit 0; 19/19 readyz probes returned 200; standalone `openclaw backup verify` passed; archive contains state, agent, and Workboard PostgreSQL capsules. The Workboard capsule holds the 5 cards committed before its snapshot. After stopping the Gateway, `openclaw backup restore` imported that capsule into a fresh namespace with the same 5 cards.

**Regression tests, red on main and green with the fix:**

- `src/snapshot/database-backup.online.test.ts`: archive capture runs beside a running owner and nested store captures join it; a non-archive capture still refuses. On main: `LocalStateOwnerError ... This command is offline-only`.
- `src/infra/database-engine/logbook-port.postgres.test.ts` (PostgreSQL conformance): a row committed just before the export snapshot opens is covered by the recorded allocation, and a restored store issues the next ID. On main: `expected { value: '70', called: true } to deeply equal { value: '71', called: true }`.

**Consumer tests:** 10 backup unit test files (192 passed, 1 skipped) and 8 PostgreSQL conformance files (27 passed) covering archive create, verify, restore, mixed engines, update capture, Git backup secrets, and agent/state/logbook ports.

**Lanes:** `changed-lanes` selected core, coreTests, docs. `check:changed --staged` passed format, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on changed files, and the database ratchets and guards. Two steps failed, `deprecated API usage` (`extensions/codex/harness.ts:261`) and `dead export scan` (codex, agents, plugins exports). Both fail identically on the unmodified base and name no touched file. `git diff --check` is clean.

Not covered: a full production-sized (15 GB) online run, and a Gateway restart racing a running capture.

<details>
<summary>Command transcripts</summary>

```text
$ openclaw backup create --verify --no-include-workspace --output <scratch>/after.tar.gz
Backup archive: <scratch>/after.tar.gz
Included 1 path:
- state: <scratch>/state
Created <scratch>/after.tar.gz
Archive verification: passed

$ openclaw backup verify <scratch>/after.tar.gz
Assets verified: 1
Archive entries scanned: 29
SQLite database inventory verified.

readyz probe 16:37:08 -> 16:37:28: 19 samples, all 200
created during-1 16:37:10 ... during-6 16:37:28
```

</details>

prs.title: feat(backup): recover local Gateway state with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
Related: #178971

## What Problem This Solves

Recover a replacement Gateway's local identity and PostgreSQL store pointers while its agent history remains in the existing central stores.

## User Impact

Proposes `openclaw backup local create --output <archive> --json` and `openclaw backup local restore <archive> --json`. The private archive contains the SQLite global database, its matched device/client credentials and configured PostgreSQL anchors. It excludes PostgreSQL records, configuration, workspaces and provider secrets managed through external SecretRefs.

Restore requires a stopped Gateway, original configured paths and fresh database targets. This remains a **draft awaiting maintainer acceptance of the storage/public CLI design in #178971**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing full backups export PostgreSQL history and restore fresh namespaces. Replacing a Gateway that will reconnect to the same central stores needs its native global/client pair and original UUID/schema pointers instead. A global-only snapshot cannot restore that pair.

This reuses native updater capture/restore, custody and matched-client receipt owners. The local profile applies the existing global snapshot sanitizer, including removal of pending outbound delivery intent: an older checkpoint must not resend messages acknowledged after capture. Ordinary full-backup rollback behavior is unchanged.

Restore reads configuration without observing or initializing database targets. Under native custody, it validates images, the global/client pair and anchor identities, creates missing private parent directories durably, then prepares and publishes images. A genuinely empty replacement state root is covered.

The archive is a per-database recovery point, not a distributed atomic snapshot. Anchors created after capture require a newer checkpoint; this does not discover namespaces after every local pointer is lost.

## Evidence

A real replacement Gateway then exposed a second portability refusal in the existing SQLite copy owner: its clone-only attempt rejected fs-safe's typed `rename-noreplace` capability error before reaching byte-copy admission. The owner now admits the byte copy and reuses fs-safe's existing guarded, non-overwriting fallback. It preserves source-identity checks, destination exclusivity, post-publication refusal and cleanup-failure handling; no filesystem policy or protection is disabled.

The new copy regression failed before the fix and passes afterward. All 15 copy-owner cases, two prepared-volume cases and 19 restore consumer cases passed across bounded runs (one process-visibility case required host process access). Core types, targeted lint and formatting passed. Fresh independent P0/P1 review reported no actionable findings in the two-file scope. The identical change is in common runtime `127953fd7dacfbfb6438dce323dedad6b05a9f20`; its full build and installed/live recovery qualification are still running.

An installed downstream checkpoint exposed a gVisor portability error: a prepared file and its containing directory report different device numbers even though atomic hard-link publication works. Restore now retains exact prepared-path and file identity checks and lets required hard linking enforce the actual filesystem boundary. It still refuses cross-volume publication without copying. The original installed CLI reproduced the failure in isolated gVisor; the rebuilt installed public CLI restored all five images and the original PostgreSQL anchor in the same isolated gVisor setup, with networking denied and no PostgreSQL connections. The file/directory device numbers were 34/36, confirming the original failure condition.

Current upstream head: `17cd7be8c41a4a2fd0be148bda13cf4ae94a5368`.

- The portability fix passed two red/green regressions (overlay device metadata and EXDEV refusal), all 46 focused snapshot/restore/checkpoint consumer cases, targeted lint and core types. A fresh independent P0/P1 review found no findings. The source and regression are identical between this upstream head and common runtime `122c7e657937e756c643b7f941afae5dde8ac0e7`.
- The native cold-root checkpoint proof and core types passed on prior upstream-only head `f5a9bdaa504000cc35bf0594597785d973300644`. It moves the whole prior state directory, recreates an empty root at the original path, and verifies device identity, global history, PostgreSQL anchor UUID/schema continuity and no acknowledged-delivery replay.
- The identical six corrected files in the common runtime passed **21/21** checkpoint, ordinary backup and updater rollback cases, including foreign-process custody; types, focused lint/declaration preparation, formatting and changed-source line caps passed.
- Fresh independent P0/P1 review confirmed the configuration/sanitizer corrections; a further scoped review of the cold-parent fix found no actionable findings. Reviews were static; executable proofs were run separately.
- The initial upstream head `9058a784` passed **90/90** tests across eight native suites. Those broad suites were not all rerun on this follow-up.
- The prior assembled common runtime `ceb00e7f866e90b8d86637de135fc4d4bffa9f6a` passed its full guarded build, maintained packaging, package integrity and actual Linux full-plugin installation.
- Its **installed public CLI**, offline as UID1000, passed capture → empty same-path root restore → recapture → refusal to overwrite existing targets. This installed pair proof initializes no PostgreSQL anchors; the separate native cold proof covers an anchor.
- Three existing native schema-admission cases passed against real PostgreSQL16: equivalent DDL reopening, changed DDL refusal, and atomic migration rollback/commit with older-binary refusal. They do not establish universal cross-version compatibility.

A restored live Gateway reconnecting to PostgreSQL history and completing a real model-provider turn is still pending downstream rollout qualification. Broad final-head upstream CI remains separate. No duplicate full UI/package build was run on this upstream-only branch.

Maintainer edits, including GitHub's workflow/secrets permission for fork branches, are enabled with the contributor's approval.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid startup restart loops while Tailscale needs login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A supervised Gateway can repeatedly fail startup while Tailscale needs login or machine approval. Restarting the Gateway cannot satisfy that operator prerequisite.

Related: #167072

## User Impact

After a supervised Tailscale Serve startup fails, the Gateway finishes cleanup and waits without listeners. It tells the operator to sign in or approve the node. Once Tailscale reports Running, it attempts normal startup once. The Serve claim and Gateway readiness checks must still pass before service starts.

Foreground startup, Funnel, unknown failures and route conflicts retain their existing failure behavior. The change does not sign in to Tailscale, modify routes, or change Gateway authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway run loop owns recovery. A typed error identifies the missing Tailscale prerequisite. Status checks use increasing intervals capped at 30 seconds. Shutdown cancels the wait and waits for its cleanup. A completed authentication-prerequisite failure does not count toward the crash-loop breaker. Other startup failures and unfinished boots still count.

Recovery restores transport availability. Gateway authentication and personal-identity rules continue to govern access.

## Evidence

### Current main integration — October 26, `67217df40f6`

Published a normal merge of official main `cfb41dddac89dcf40325273b98ffb1c7a9d209a2` into the existing branch. The merge is `67217df40f6d1d2cfbed09d166e4dcf3dc8eafcf`, tree `6c13fb21b1723bc6221147f89aac9cb5c90a16e8`; all prior PR ancestry is retained. This supersedes the earlier preparation-only status below, while preserving its revision-specific evidence.

The two conflict resolutions retain main's genuinely clobbered recovery fixture and its startup operations contract, including `acknowledgeHandledFailure`. The PR's failure tracking still retains independent cleanup failures. Main already contains adjacent Serve-denied handling; it does not contain this PR's supervised login/machine-approval waiting path.

Before integration, the two concrete CI fixture failures were repaired in `0e44dbd647e8edfb61c3c7df1426d75d8ff86c6b`: the publication-history fixture reuses Peter's canonical correction from #184046 (`adc3b39381d0a8bc7e1956b52c42a85841dbdbdc`, cherry-picked with original credit), and the recovery fixture now actually triggers the clobber guard while retaining the token-removal, proxy-preservation and filesystem assertions. Those repairs do not change production behavior.

The exact integrated tree received a fresh scoped-clean Codex P0–P3 source review against the pinned main, with no actionable findings. Diff whitespace and conflict-marker checks passed. The comment audit found no introduced comments or suppressions in the two conflict resolutions. [Canonical CI 40389694351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40389694351) completed successfully for this head. Its actual tested source was GitHub merge `b80700ab98559e2b9f96e100cd50bb2568c149bf`, with main `add78aed91026f6206515c804374cdd2b377f42c` and PR head `67217df40f6d1d2cfbed09d166e4dcf3dc8eafcf` as parents. All scheduled jobs completed with no failures. This supersedes the pending CI statement; it does not establish the separate authenticated Tailscale restoration or installed stable-upgrade scenarios below.

The earlier packaged parking/cancellation proof remains credited to its tested revision. Authenticated recovery through Serve claim and Gateway readiness, and stable-upgrade qualification, remain separate outstanding proofs. The maintainer's supervised-wait-versus-supervisor-retry policy decision is still open. No Gateway, personal app, authentication, Tailscale route or live service was changed by this integration.


### Whole-tree integration preparation, October 25

Current published head remains [`daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41); its completed deletion-only proof is immediately below. No additional source commit or push was made. The existing broad merge-ref CI path remains blocked by conflicts and the unavailable supported imported-PR base integration. Security/context checks are not substituted for broad test CI.

A new scratch-only preparation pins this current head, public main [`4a9db48eae3226b269a49cd7482af30268034960`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a9db48eae3226b269a49cd7482af30268034960), and GitHub-reported real merge base `2ad4d4c019939b43340e632d04da9225acb5dc11`. A single normal public Git batch fetch hydrated all three complete source snapshots. The whole-tree rename-aware merge then completed, identifying exactly two content-conflicted paths: the startup test owner and boot-lifecycle tests. This supersedes the earlier incomplete whole-tree preparation, not its historical evidence boundaries.

The scratch resolutions migrate main’s evolved settlement/classification table into the PR’s extracted owner, retain its event-owned waits and stronger recovery cases, preserve current main’s consolidated lifecycle fixtures while adding the two prerequisite regressions, and use the current no-argument supervisor-identity API in the textually clean caller. The already-removed duplicate test is not restored. Main’s post-start route reclamation and tests plus all paths outside the PR delta are exact pinned main. The resolved scratch index has no unmerged paths. The original preparation tree and four-file patch are retained as historical inputs; the validated final scratch tree and updated patch are recorded below. No already-applied helper-removal hunk remains.

Merged-target scratch validation is now complete for the focused local scope. A separate physical frozen install was prepared inside the task-owned scratch checkout using checksum-verified official Node 26.12.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. The initial Node 24.20.0 install was correctly refused by current main’s version guard; no guard bypass, system runtime change or borrowed dependency reconciliation was used. The scratch checkout has ordinary task-owned Git metadata; no GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE was inherited by test fixtures.

The repository test wrapper ran the owning run-loop, option-collision, Tailscale, boot-lifecycle, current main post-start server-tailscale, supervisor-marker and startup-triage files with one worker: **333 passed, 1 skipped**, seven files across four serial shards in **97.04 seconds**. The skip is the existing macOS-only real immutable-database/chflags case on Linux. The wrapper staged its checksum-verified pinned Bun fork `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`, with Node 26 orchestration and no fallback reported. This is source-bound scratch regression proof, not authenticated tailnet restoration, stable-upgrade proof or current published-head CI.

Production, CLI-test and infra-test typechecks passed. Focused lint passed on 18 changed source files with zero warnings/errors. Formatting initially identified one wrapped call in `tailscale-backend-ready.ts`; only that layout was corrected, and all 18 affected-source format checks now pass. The final line-cap ratchet passed on 18 changed sources; the actual package timeout and assertion ratchets passed (114 files/210 grandfathered sites and 2425 files/5520 grandfathered assertions). Two initial preload-only ratchet commands did not invoke checks and are explicitly excluded from proof; corrected package-script invocations produced the stated results. The final frozen scratch tree is `ec97a2efc7c08acd6a87a4354974db80f13aa2fe`; its sole later source difference is the formatter-only call layout, so no passing suite was repeated. The exact command/outcome/artifact receipt has SHA-256 `645b6cb5b01444f5e42f56febe47d418f436bd15ebc0b43282c3cf5880c7cf20`. Historical preparation artifacts remain preserved.

All paths outside the original 20-path PR delta remain exact pinned main. Local Git history is shallow; immutable commit/tree identities are authentic and the merge-base pin came from GitHub, with no synthetic or replacement ancestry. No native integration review is claimed: the bound review tool cannot target the scratch checkout, and prior published-head reviews were not relabeled. The scratch candidate is **not** published integration, current-head broad CI or a merge-ready verdict. The bound projection and published tree remain unchanged; the live publisher schema supplies no new imported-PR integration contract, so the unchanged refusal was not retried.

Smallest intervention: enable a supported ancestry-preserving main integration for the original PR branch, then validate/review/publish the integrated candidate and run fresh broad CI. Core acceptance of indefinite listener-free first-start parking, an authorized disposable tailnet/systemd environment and second HTTPS peer for authenticated restoration, and latest-stable upgrade/settings-preservation proof remain separate required gates. No test access, credentials, live services or policy acceptance were provisioned by this preparation, and no Diamond or merge-ready claim is made.

### Current revision: duplicate-test cleanup, October 24

Head [`daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41) appends one test-only commit to `943f572bf15eb8c9125f9c23cac5be0c6530b995`. It removes exactly 26 lines: the helper-only second-failure preservation test and its now-unused local setup, as requested by the completed ClawSweeper review. Both immediately following production `runGatewayLoop` distinct-failure drain-path cases remain, along with additional-error, undefined-rejection, cancellation and cleanup coverage. No production source, assertion in a retained case, timeout or baseline changed.

The owning run-loop suite passed all 176 cases (91.77 seconds including compiler preparation; wrapper wall time 94.03 seconds). Targeted lint, CLI test types, formatting, line-cap and timeout-race ratchets, and whitespace checks passed. prs.title: feat(web-fetch): assess unusable pages with opt-in Decision model
prs.body:
Related: #166688

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` can return a successful-looking login, access-denied, bot-check, or navigation shell that provides no source material for the user's question.

## User Impact

Default behavior is unchanged. Operators who enable Decision assistance, select a Decision model, and set `tools.web.fetch.decisionQuality: "shadow"` get a page-quality judgment while retaining content. `"apply"` can withhold text at an unusable-page probability of at least 0.90, only when both the fetched result and evaluated excerpt are complete. Unavailable or uncertain judgments retain the page.

A hosted Decision provider may receive a bounded page excerpt and charge for each evaluation. The five-second evaluation deadline is unchanged. The threshold is experimental, not calibrated for production false-drop rates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing Decision runtime after direct/fallback extraction and outside the shared fetch cache. Evaluation includes at most 6,000 characters of wrapped extracted text plus bounded metadata, not request URL/headers or generated private spill locators. The original result remains cached. The owning agent's consent, selected model, mode and invocation authority are checked around inference; cancellation/source loss remains terminal, and accepted usage is completed only for retained judgments. This does not promise cancellation of already-admitted work or exactly-once final tool delivery.

Real opt-in apply and shadow are both preserved. The one additional core config path is intentional; core placement, page-data transfer/cost and experimental withholding policy remain upstream maintainer decisions. `web_search`, page-change monitoring, provider/dependency changes and production activation are out of scope.

## Evidence

### October 26 integration refresh — `a85c0ff8907832ff0138f007f03560130e5f8c63`

Rebased onto `09104d524ce1a89968716367b8691c4081f7397b` for demonstrated conflicts. Preserves upstream #183797's execution-owned fetch/cache/spill closures rather than restoring the retired request parameter bags. Regenerated config baseline is current-main core +1; channel/plugin counts are unchanged. Fourteen other feature files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. Pre-publication main `31c6d5440b24b91929e9d472d17f652901e7c133` advanced 163 paths with no overlap in the 17 PR paths; merge preview is clean.

- **83 selected tests passed; one unchanged macOS sandbox fixture failed** because it invokes GNU `stat -c` on BSD/macOS. This includes quality/accepted-usage, config, assembly, fallback and prompt-prefix checks. No skip, command shim or weaker assertion; Linux CI remains the platform gate.
- Production and agents-tools test types, scoped type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, generated-config, line-cap and whitespace checks passed.
- **Independent clean-context native integration review: PASS**, no actionable P0–P2 findings; previous full 17-file review remains applicable to unchanged feature bytes. Local AutoReview CLI is unavailable and is not counted as completed review.
- **Exact clean-head runtime build passed** (runtime profile, 1m28.8s), including bundles, built plugin closures and UI. Both runtime stamps identify this clean head.
- **Built Gateway + built CLI agent proof passed all four strict cases**, using actual registered local TypeSafe/Clef inference. A credential-free scripted local agent transport selected the real registered `web_fetch`; this was not `--local` or a helper-only call. Each CLI turn exited 0 and took 4.3–4.7 seconds after Gateway startup.

| Scenario | Unusable probability | Result | CLI exit |
|---|---:|---|---:|

prs.title: feat: let image-capable decision plugins evaluate supplied screenshots
prs.body:
Related: #166113

## What Problem This Solves

Agents cannot submit an already available screenshot to their selected Decision model through `decision_evaluate`, even when that provider can evaluate images.

## User Impact

An agent with an image-capable selected Decision model can explicitly supply local PNG, JPEG, or WebP screenshots and receive typed, advisory answers. Existing text-only models remain text-only. No screenshot is captured automatically, and a Decision result does not authorize a UI action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core tool loads explicit local paths under the active filesystem/sandbox policy, bounds the image bytes and dimensions, and passes bytes—not paths or URLs—through the provider-neutral Decision contract. Plugins declare image support per model; absent declarations fail closed before dispatch. The TypeSafe plugin is the first adapter, using a loopback Clef Flash System One endpoint. Core has no Clef/Ollama dependency. This does not add task-per-model routing, remote image input, automatic interception, or model downloads.

## Evidence

Current repair/proof head: `bda6bfc5d5ae1212ae4a76674fe7cb1679e4acf8`, based on `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0`. The maintenance repair changes only the sanitized invalid-input guidance and its regressions; feature behavior and image bounds are preserved.

- The corrected diagnostic explains required state, nonempty typed questions and one-to-four local image paths without echoing private evidence, paths or exception text. The follow-up preserves the established lowercase `no evidence was sent` substring expected by the unchanged main tool consumer. Its core consumer and guidance-integration suites passed **6/6**, with a matching red-before assertion and an exact-main-target passing control; changed-file lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Broader 48/48 Decision/TypeSafe tests and production types passed at preceding head `4eb21b45b32dac0000e7472c466a9b43af71767b`; the later image/guidance 5/5 result was at `392897116cb643654cbe3d15770f2182e2f50c49`. Those are prior-head results, not broader new-head rerun claims.
- A fresh isolated build of the committed repair passed through `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`; both runtime stamps name this exact head with `inputsClean:true`. The initial pnpm-wrapper attempt failed its input-signature guard after normalizing the lockfile; the clean direct build is the accepted result. No lockfile normalization is in the PR.
- **Shipped entry-point proof:** built `dist/entry.js gateway run`, then built `dist/entry.js agent --agent main --message <synthetic-tool-request> --json` (without `--local`) completed a real Gateway → registered tool → filesystem/image admission → Decision runtime → TypeSafe chain. A scripted OpenAI Responses agent transport emitted the tool call; the positive Decision inference used the pre-existing real local Clef service. A text-only Jev selection rejected the screenshot with zero requests to the separately instrumented selected-provider endpoint. Both CLI turns completed successfully. Sanitized exact-head output is below.
- This proves the shipped agent/tool/provider boundary, not autonomous model tool selection, classifier accuracy or a production Gateway benchmark. Positive wire-image bytes were not separately captured; existing admission/transport tests and prior registered-provider proof cover byte handling. The synthetic JPEG is 44,368 bytes and retains SHA-256 `ee370c24a1805ff56868fc550c4590075919cbb2d1e5800f62178f05d4f6a47e`.
- Independent Astra acceptance covers the guidance repair, one-line compatibility follow-up, and refreshed clean-head shipped proof. New-head hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper review remain separate post-push gates. No production config, credential, service or model download was used; disposable proof state and listeners were removed.
- Build exit was zero with a report-only Control UI startup-JS gzip advisory; no UI source/budget files changed and no passing exact-base size measurement exists, so causal attribution is not claimed.

## Review focus

Please review the local-path and sandbox admission, count/byte/pixel bounds, selected-model pinning, per-model plugin opt-in, cancellation, and exclusion of image bytes from diagnostics/results. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unreadable generated runtime files and missing bundled dependency targets when containers run as arbitrary users, which can prevent the Control UI, plugin assets and runtime modules from loading.

## User Impact

Container users can read shipped application assets and execute declared launchers without widening access to private configuration or operator state. Local image builds accept ordinary group-writable or restrictive source modes, and the mandatory image check uses an unrelated identity within normal rootless UID/GID mappings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one generated-artifact permission owner across builds, staging, and packaging; verify finished packages and images without repairing them during acceptance. Plugin assets precede staging, required workspace targets stay in the image, and partial development profiles and authenticated historical receipts retain their contracts.

The maintainer correction normalizes only the selected final public image payload, honors executable declarations, and safely separates mode-changing hardlinks only when every alias belongs to that payload. prs.title: fix(openai): name the direct image route on 401/403 scope errors
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90074

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenAI image generation fails with a bare `HTTP 401` / `Missing scopes` error that does not say which route or credential OpenClaw used when explicit `models.providers.openai` settings select the direct Images API.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who hit a 401/403 on OpenAI image generation now see the selected route, endpoint, credential class and credential source in the error (or `configured-header` when configured auth headers replaced the resolved credential). When explicit `models.providers.openai` settings pin the direct route, the message also names the `baseUrl`/`api` settings that switch to a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile instead. The original error keeps its class, status and detail; 429 and other statuses are unchanged. Routing precedence is unchanged; no config migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The clawsweeper review on the issue recommends keeping explicit provider settings authoritative and making image failures identify the effective transport and credential class. This PR does only that: on a 401/403 from the direct Images API route, the existing `ProviderHttpError` keeps its class and status (failover classification is unaffected) and gets a short route suffix appended. Query strings are dropped from the shown endpoint, header values are never shown. Credential attribution compares the final request auth header with the resolved credential, so `headers.Authorization` / `request.auth` overrides are reported as `configured-header`. Other status codes and the Codex Responses route are unchanged. The helpers live in a new sibling module `image-generation-diagnostics.ts` (the existing sanitizer moved there unchanged), so the provider file shrinks and the large test file is untouched.

Changed since the review of `33833df6d19`: the suffix is built only from facts resolved before the request (route, resolved credential, explicit direct config), and the OAuth advice depends on the explicit config instead of a profile lookup. Nothing reads the auth store after the request fails, so another provider's pending migration (`AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError`) can no longer replace the HTTP 401/403/429. The annotation runs only for the Images API response itself, not for later image URL downloads. Current `main` is merged in; the conflict in `image-generation-provider.ts` was resolved onto the async auth preparation from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169111 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169714

## Evidence

Real `openclaw infer image generate` runs from built checkouts (`pnpm build`) of the previous head `33833df6d19` and this head `214e40e5f8d`, with real HTTP transport against a loopback Images API stub that answers 401, 403, 429 or 200. Every run uses a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` whose agent still holds a legacy Anthropic profile awaiting migration (the CLI logs `requires legacy credential migration; affected providers: anthropic`), explicit `models.providers.openai` (`baseUrl` = stub, `apiKey` synthetic), and runs inside a network namespace that only has `lo` (`api.openai.com` does not resolve). Each case made exactly one `POST …/v1/images/generations` with `Bearer synthetic-openai-key`; the auth profile file was unchanged afterwards.

The standalone CLI activates a secrets runtime snapshot for the agent before provider auth (`prepareLocalCapabilityAccountSecrets`). To exercise the reviewed case (no prepared `authStore`, no runtime snapshot), these runs skip that one step in the built output of both heads (one added `return;`; diff, restore and checksum check are in the logs):

| CLI run, no runtime auth snapshot | 401 | 403 | 429 | 200 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| previous head `33833df6d19` | Anthropic migration error replaces the HTTP error | same | same | image written |
| this head `214e40e5f8d` | HTTP 401 error + route suffix | HTTP 403 error + route suffix | HTTP 429 error, unchanged | image written |

With the CLI unchanged (snapshot active), both heads kept the HTTP error for 401/403/429; this head adds the explicit-route advice to the 401/403 suffix.

<details>
<summary>CLI output, 2026-10-15 (UTC)</summary>

```text
# previous head 33833df6d19, no runtime snapshot, stub answers 401 (POST 00:58:01Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: Auth profile store …/state/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite requires legacy credential migration; affected providers: anthropic; run openclaw doctor --fix.
# same message for 403 (POST 00:58:08Z) and 429 (POST 00:58:15Z)

# this head 214e40e5f8d, no runtime snapshot, stub answers 401 (POST 00:58:24Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Missing scopes: api.model.images.request [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:35789/s401/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json; explicit models.providers.openai settings select the direct Images API. To use a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile instead, set baseUrl "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex" and api "openai-chatgpt-responses", without apiKey, auth "api-key", or auth headers)
# 403 (POST 00:58:28Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 403): Project does not have access to model gpt-image-2 [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:35789/s403/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json; explicit models.providers.openai settings select the direct Images API. …)
# 429 (POST 00:58:33Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 429): Rate limit reached for images per minute [type=stub]

# CLI unchanged (snapshot active), previous head 33833df6d19, 401 (POST 00:56:03Z)
[image-generation] candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Missing scopes: api.model.images.request [type=stub] (route=images-api url=http://127.0.0.1:34331/s401/v1/images/generations credential=*** source=models.json)
```

</details>

Provider-module counter-check with the seven cases from the review (401/403/429 with and without a prepared store, plus 200; real auth-profile owner, real loopback HTTP): previous head 4/7 (the three no-store cases end in `AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError`), `main` 7/7, this head 7/7. Re-adding an eager post-failure store read to this head makes the new no-store tests in `image-generation-provider.direct-errors.test.ts` fail 3/3.

<details>
<summary>Earlier live run against api.openai.com (2026-10-06, previous head; the advice wording has changed since)</summary>

Setup as in the issue: `models.providers.openai = { baseUrl: "https://api.openai.com/v1", api: "openai-completions" }`, an `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment, a ChatGPT OAuth profile in the auth store (synthetic token), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Before (`origin/main`) | `OpenAI image generation failed (HTTP 401): Incorrect API key provided: syntheti****cess. … [request_id=req_b37ec54f…]`, no route or credential |
| After, resolved credential | same text plus `(route=images-api url=https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations credential=oauth source=profile:openai:chatgpt; … set baseUrl "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex" and api "openai-chatgpt-responses" …)` |
| After, plus `headers.Authorization` in provider config | OpenAI echoes the header key (`sk-proj-****…roof`), message reports `credential=configured-header source=models.providers.openai` instead of the profile |
| Hint followed (`baseUrl` + `api` as suggested, `OPENAI_API_KEY` still set) | `image auth selected: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses …`; request goes to the ChatGPT backend (its 401 comes from the synthetic token) |

The runs also showed what the bare message hid: with the issue's config the OAuth profile token, not `OPENAI_API_KEY`, was sent to the Platform Images API, which is consistent with the `Missing scopes: api.model.images.request` from the original report. Whether that credential choice should change is the open precedence decision on the issue; this PR does not change it.

</details>

Tests (this head):

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/openai --maxWorkers=1` (Linux, 2 shards): 96 files, 1152 passed, 1 skipped, 416 s wall.
- `pnpm test` on `image-generation-provider.direct-errors.test.ts`, `image-generation-diagnostics.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.auth.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.url.test.ts`, `image-generation-provider.tls.test.ts` (`--maxWorkers=1`, macOS): 84 passed, 38.6 s wall.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `npx oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean.
- Baseline ratchets: line-cap, assertion-safety, database-dialect, test-timeout-race and test-mock-exports OK locally against the merge base; CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` green on this head. Its `OPENCLAW_* count 455 exceeds budget 454` warning comes from `main`; this diff adds no `OPENCLAW_*` name.
- `codex review` against the merge base: no findings.

Gaps: the stub stands in for the OpenAI service, so no authenticated OpenAI call was made. The no-snapshot runs change one line in the built CLI to reach the reviewed provider path. CLI output masks the credential class (`credential=***`) because the log redactor treats `credential=` as a secret assignment; the error itself carries `credential=api-key` (asserted in the tests) and `source=` stays visible. Not tested through a running Gateway.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report stt-tts readiness and transports in talk.catalog
prs.body:
Related: #165363 ## What Problem This Solves Android can reject a working native Talk setup because setup readiness is taken from an unrelated realtime provider, while `talk.catalog` does not expose selected-speech readiness and transport metadata. ## User Impact Configured native Talk can use device speech recognition and the selected speech provider without requiring a realtime provider. Existing device-TTS fallback is preserved for missing or unsupported speech providers; a selected, known provider without credentials still requires setup. Realtime Talk continues to use realtime readiness. No configuration migration, schema change, or new dependency is introduced. Physical-device/live-provider and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade validation remain outstanding; the evidence below does not claim those flows have been tested. ## Why This Change Was Made - Derive `speech.ready` from the active speech row's asynchronous configured result and expose `managed-room` transport metadata. - Reuse Android's existing Talk route parser to select native-speech or realtime readiness. Native recognition does not depend on Gateway transcription readiness. - Invalidate setup readiness after configuration changes and reject stale refresh results. Label the shared setup row “Talk,” not “Realtime Talk.” - Regenerate the source-owned native localization inventory for the changed labels and configuration-error text. Translated catalogs and locale metadata remain owned by the localization workflow. Original implementation by @holny; Android route-readiness follow-up and CI correction contributed with @IWhatsskill. ## Work sessions - [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/af8d6636-39eb-4922-8f37-2d4ba8a42bb8) ## Evidence ### Current localization follow-up Commit `7784d02a30ab425bfb75aef40a155ba778c3245a` changes only `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (4 additions, 2 deletions), generated by `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`. - Reproduced the exact `native app i18n inventory drift detected` failure on `63959e26026939388010d16ca2b133d0b7a4891b` using `pnpm native:i18n:verify`. - After regeneration, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes, including Android and Apple source-localization checks; 4,483 inventory entries. - Repeated generation is byte-identical. Verification passes again after the commit; `git diff --check` passes. Local runtime: Node 26.8.2, repository-pinned pnpm 12.9.0, frozen-lockfile dependencies. ### Android behavior and review — retained evidence for 63959e260269393 The localization-only follow-up does not change these runtime/test sources. These are prior-commit results, not a new execution of the whole suite: - The new Android admission regression failed on unchanged pre-fix Android source, then passed with the route-aware fix. - **43 focused Android tests passed:** readiness 13; NodeRuntime admission/stale-result/publication 3; Settings 1; composer 8; config parsing 10; mode manager 3; speech client 5. The selected Gradle tests and Kotlin lint completed in 48 seconds. The new 11-case admission regression took 2.137 seconds; the stale-result regression took 0.058 seconds. These are measured local times, not estimated CI seconds. - Kotlin lint, scoped formatting, documentation-content checks, and whitespace checks passed. - Two independent Codex autoreview passes over the complete implementation candidate and relevant route/fallback/lifecycle context found no actionable P0–P2 issues. ClawSweeper's October 14 review of the same head also reports no code findings, with behavior proof still outstanding. - The earlier exact-parent Gateway handler [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38561600537/job/115844560368) passed 107 tests. This is parent-head evidence, not a current-head Gateway rerun. ### Settings screenshots Actual production Compose Settings rendering in a test harness, using French, a narrow viewport, and large text. These images demonstrate the shared label change only; they do **not** demonstrate successful Talk startup or audio. “Non vérifié” means “Unverified”: the fixture is deliberately disconnected. “Parler” is the translated “Talk” label.
BeforeAfter
### Live `talk.catalog` runtime proof Both scenarios run against an isolated loopback Gateway (`gateway.mode=local`, `bind=loopback`, port 18899) on the candidate build, invoked as `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --params '{}'`. Scenario A - active provider present, no credentials (`talk.provider=elevenlabs`, `talk.providers.elevenlabs={}`): ```json { "speech.ready": false, "speech.activeProvider": "elevenlabs", "elevenlabs.configured": false, "elevenlabs.transports": ["managed-room"], "elevenlabs.modes": ["stt-tts"] } ``` Scenario B - same active provider after adding credentials: ```json { "speech.ready": true, "speech.activeProvider": "elevenlabs", "elevenlabs.configured": true, "elevenlabs.transports": ["managed-room"], "elevenlabs.modes": ["stt-tts"] } ``` This is the readiness the fix derives from the active speech row: the selected, known provider reports `ready:false` (`configured:false`) without credentials, and `ready:true` once configured. A synthetic key was used and does not appear in the catalog output. ### CI failure disposition and remaining proof The [CI attempt for 63959e260269393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38570885471) failed in two independent jobs: - `native-i18n`: missing source-inventory regeneration, corrected by the localization follow-up above. - `android-test-third-party`: downloading `gradle-9.7.1-bin.zip` returned HTTP 500 before tests started. This is not a passing test result or evidence of a code failure. Its downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. New-head hosted CI remains separate from the local passing check; no manual CI rerun or merge is claimed here. The live `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog` evidence above closes the earlier runtime-proof gap; physical-device native Talk startup/audio, device fallback and unchanged realtime admission, and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade runs with settings preserved remain outstanding. No full repository suite was run locally.
Implementation history - The initial test-only commit `ca0f5eeaa0e` did not contain the production change; `2404bf77d27` supplied it. - `33df65b6c59a` preserved main's asynchronous provider-catalog structure and corrected selected-provider readiness for missing credentials. - `63959e260269393` added Android route-aware admission, fallback preservation, configuration-refresh protection, focused regressions, and the shared Talk label. The Android admission blocker is therefore no longer excluded from this PR's scope; live proof remains open as stated above.

prs.title: fix: failed Dashboard updates retain a report after the modal closes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a synchronous Dashboard/Gateway update failure can finish without a persistent report file after the modal closes. The restart audit and completion log also implied changed-path knowledge the Gateway did not have.

## User Impact

Failed admitted updates now retain a sanitized report in the existing `update-reports/<runId>.md` store, and the run ledger marks failed `skipped` outcomes as failed. Unknown changed paths are omitted instead of fabricated. There is no migration or required user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now calls the canonical report-artifact refresher only when it owns a terminal failed run. A started handoff remains the updater/successor Gateway's responsibility. This PR does not repeat the warning-level failure logging already merged in #160091 and does not change updater installation or rollback behavior.

## Evidence

- **Reconstructed red/green negative control (2026-10-02):** A disposable worktree at the single-commit parent `2a390ec087731f6251ad55362a3603138b58e8b6` received only the current versions of `update.test.ts`, `update-unexpected-error.test.ts`, and `update.test-harness.ts` via `git diff | git apply --index`. Its staged test/harness patch SHA-256 (`git diff --cached | shasum -a 256`) was `a419fd75497844f742d5161d7e6abc74d9ed67fe76dbeaa1670dcba1d39491a7`, identical to the corresponding three-file patch in head `ff1b3dafd682c97bae9475ec7e209fc5575c2aae`. Neither `update.ts` nor `update-outcome-observation.ts` was applied to the parent. Workspace dependency links were supplied in the disposable worktree; no other tracked file changed.

  The identical focused command was run from each worktree:

  ```sh
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/update.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/update-unexpected-error.test.ts
  ```

  - **Parent (red): exit 1.** `Test Files 2 failed (2); Tests 4 failed | 52 passed (56)`. Redacted failure excerpt: `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<isolated-state>/update-reports/<runId>.md'` at `update-unexpected-error.test.ts:53`; ledger assertions expected `status: failed` but received `skipped` for `restart-disabled` and `restart-unavailable`; restart audit unexpectedly contained `changedPaths: []`.
  - **Published head (green): exit 0.** `Test Files 2 passed (2); Tests 56 passed (56); [test] passed 1 Vitest shard`.
  - The initial parent attempts failed before meaningful test collection because a fresh linked worktree lacked workspace dependency links; those setup failures are excluded from the red result above. The final red run reached all 56 tests.

  Exact worktree and patch commands (source and proof paths are local checkout paths):

  ```sh
  git -C /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-current worktree add --detach /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054-red 2a390ec087731f6251ad55362a3603138b58e8b6
  git -C /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054 diff 2a390ec087731f6251ad55362a3603138b58e8b6 ff1b3dafd682c97bae9475ec7e209fc5575c2aae -- src/gateway/server-methods/update.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/update-unexpected-error.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/update.test-harness.ts | git -C /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054-red apply --index
  ```

  The focused tests cover the retained report for an unexpected handoff error and for `restart-unavailable`, plus the `failed` ledger classification.
- **Real Gateway behavior on the published head (2026-10-02):** Started `node /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054/openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 64458 --bind loopback --auth none` from `ff1b3dafd682c97bae9475ec7e209fc5575c2aae` with a new disposable `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`, and config `{"gateway":{"mode":"local","bind":"loopback","port":64458,"auth":{"mode":"none"}},"commands":{"restart":false}}`. This is an actual foreground Gateway and local WebSocket RPC exchange, not the test harness; restart was disabled to force a synchronous refusal before any updater or installation mutation. The port was loopback-only, and the Gateway exited cleanly after the read-back.

  ```text
  $ node /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054/openclaw.mjs gateway call update.run --port 64458 --timeout 90000 --json --params '{}'
  RPC exit 0; runId=9fc6be2e-2dda-4ea3-8ee8-aa9f373415d9; ok=false
  result.status=skipped; result.reason=restart-disabled
  $ node /Volumes/Extern/openclaw-160054/openclaw.mjs gateway call update.runs.get --port 64458 --timeout 30000 --json --params '{"runId":"9fc6be2e-2dda-4ea3-8ee8-aa9f373415d9"}'
  RPC exit 0; run.status=failed; run.phase=finished; run.reason=restart-disabled
  $ inspect <isolated-state>/update-reports/9fc6be2e-2dda-4ea3-8ee8-aa9f373415d9.md
  regular file exists (336 bytes):
  ⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: restart-disabled.
  Update mode: git
  Phases: requested (421ms)
  Failed: requested
  ```

  The shown commands use the same isolated environment selectors as the Gateway process; the excerpt is copied from the actual RPC responses and saved report with the temporary state path redacted. The raw updater result remains `skipped` for the refusal, while the durable ledger correctly classifies it as `failed`. This proof covers real Gateway admission, installation inspection, RPC, ledger persistence, and report writing; it does not claim an updater handoff or successful installation.
- **Changed-path provenance:** The same RPC run verifies the scheduled restart audit has no `changedPaths` property and that the failure log omits the old `changedPaths=<n/a>` text. After a type-narrowing-only test correction, the affected restart test passed again: 1 passed, 47 filtered/skipped (exit 0).
- **Static/build checks:** Gateway-methods test typecheck passed (exit 0); core production typecheck passed in the changed-code runner. Changed TypeScript lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Formatting: 7 files passed. `git diff --check`: exit 0. Full `pnpm build`: exit 0 (11m 26.8s).
- The changed-code runner's broad test-type pass was stopped after it selected 26 graphs; the directly affected Gateway-methods graph passed separately. The foreground loopback Gateway exchange above is real RPC proof on the earlier `ff1b3dafd682c97bae9475ec7e209fc5575c2aae` head. No platform-specific managed-helper run is claimed; focused tests exercise the Gateway handler, run ledger, and artifact writer with isolated state and mocked handoff boundaries.


## Current-Head Integration (2026-10-02)

After ClawSweeper identified a conflict with newer `main`, the single repair commit was rebased onto `1ce46edd0db2b28abada9834e934ab06d3e971de`, preserving current campaign-fencing behavior. The report-save closure was then extracted without behavior change into the existing update outcome module to keep `update.ts` within the repository's lint limit. Current head: `816ad3786dce8ca941285e9f1e56fb2cf02fb3df`. A merge-tree check against `f1be74485a89e8bf36055cf7cffd6ff2439da50d` (newer, disjoint `main`) succeeded.

On this exact source: the three affected Gateway test files passed **81/81** (exit 0), the Gateway-methods test typecheck passed (exit 0), changed-file lint reported 0 errors/warnings, formatting passed for all 7 changed files, `git diff --check` passed, and the full build completed with exit 0 (14m 26s, including UI and plugin-SDK output). The separate independent probe passed **4/4** after the helper extraction, including admitted owner-required and restart-disabled refusals. The earlier real foreground Gateway RPC proof remains historical evidence from its named head; it was not rerun on this rebased commit.

Closes #160054

prs.title: fix(ios): Talk turns stop after 30 seconds despite longer timeout
prs.body:
Closes #162784

## What Problem This Solves

Native iOS Talk sent `runTimeoutMs: 30000` with `chat.send`, terminating slower agent runs after 30 seconds even when the Gateway allowed more time. The user could then receive no spoken reply.

## Change

The native Talk caller now omits **only** that run-time override, inheriting the Gateway's configured agent timeout. The separate 30,000 ms request/transport timeout, 120-second completion wait, cancellation, and matching-run-ID checks remain unchanged. Native tests cover both the wire request and the production transcript → chat request → correlated final event → speech-synthesis/audio-player path with a fast synthetic Gateway.

## Evidence by Symptom

- **30-second run override despite 120-second Gateway setting:** A source-anchored `python3` negative control isolated `sendChat` through `waitForChatCompletion` from pre-fix base `2a390ec087731f6251ad55362a3603138b58e8b6` and the changed file, asserting absence of `runTimeoutMs: 30000`. Pre-fix assertion failed (exit 1); post-fix passed (exit 0); the two-case harness passed 2/2 (exit 0). At the real Gateway timeout resolver, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module -e 'import { resolveAgentTimeoutMs } from "./src/agents/timeout.ts"; const cfg={agents:{defaults:{timeoutSeconds:120}}}; const before=resolveAgentTimeoutMs({cfg,overrideMs:30000}); const after=resolveAgentTimeoutMs({cfg}); if(before!==30000||after!==120000) process.exit(1); console.log({before,after});'` passed 2/2 (exit 0): **30,000 ms before, 120,000 ms after**.
- **Keep the 30-second transport deadline:** `native Talk chat request inherits Gateway run timeout and thinking policy` asserts no RPC `params.timeoutMs` and transport `request.timeoutMs == 30000`; it passed on superseded-head CI run [37000275819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37000275819) (0.001 s). The new current-head `native Talk speaks a correlated reply without overriding the run deadline` also asserts no RPC run override, and that the exact final assistant text reaches the injected speech synthesizer and one audio payload reaches the player. The synthetic event uses the request's run ID; this is an orchestration regression, **not** live delayed behavior proof. Its prior 31-second fake delay was removed from ordinary CI after review.
- **No premature local completion or lost correlation:** The production completion wait remains 120 seconds, cancellation checks remain, and the final event still must match the acknowledged run ID. The committed simulator regression exercises that path with an immediate event. The separate disposable live Simulator run below exercises the exact-head production Talk owner against a real Gateway for 101.1 seconds; the microphone input is a disclosed test-only synthetic transcript.

## Validation and Limits

- Current source commit: `8cfe13562e2140be4f028ec50db17b2cf0606563`; PR and fork branch both report that SHA. Current-head CI run [37005793978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37005793978) failed after `** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **` (1,410.5 seconds): simulator preparation's SimSlim download hit repeated `curl (28)` DNS/SSL timeouts, so its focused voice step was skipped. This is CI infrastructure failure, not a passing test. A queued fork-only package job was cancelled with zero steps when local Xcode 27.0 became available; no upstream custom runner was dispatched.
- `swiftc -frontend -parse apps/ios/Tests/TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift apps/ios/Tests/TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests.swift`: exit 0. `PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH" scripts/format-swift.sh ios`: exit 0, 0/462 files need formatting. `git diff --check`: exit 0. Original `pnpm build`: exit 0 (13m 11s); `pnpm test:changed`: exit 0, but selected 0 Vitest targets for Swift files.
- Local Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), iOS 27.0 simulator (24A434): `xcodebuild ... CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build-for-testing` **exit 0** on this exact SHA. `xcodebuild ... -only-testing:<two canonical TalkModeManagerTests IDs> CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test-without-building` **exit 0**; [xcresult local] reports **2 passed, 0 failed**, including the request-boundary and production-entrypoint correlated-speech tests (test run 0.535 s; speech case 0.505 s). Xcode's post-test `simctl diagnose` stalled after test completion and was stopped; xcodebuild then finalized successfully. The unsigned arm64 Simulator app was zipped, integrity-checked, installed, and launched; ZIP SHA-256 `c8d9b51d7b15bac70534b3630f3adf04997d045245e27d720ab6e7d1424c5791`. On exact-head Simulator recheck, native Talk recognition remains compile-time blocked (`startRecognition` throws unless the test-only `allowSimulatorCapture` initializer is true); see the route analysis below. This package cannot serve as live native spoken-turn proof. A strict SwiftLint build first exited 65 with three unrelated upstream violations (two shared-kit cyclomatic-complexity lines, one pre-existing TalkModeManager line); a local-only edit to the ignored generated Xcode project skipped that phase for packaging, leaving the tracked PR worktree clean. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` previously passed 11 selected guards before CLT SourceKit failure; broad `pnpm check` was blocked by missing `rg` and npm-registry 403s during package-lock validation. None is reported as a passing gate.
- AutoReview of the implementation, the first native regression, and the fast follow-up each returned `scoped-clean` at P0/P1 (exit 0). Codex AutoReview was unavailable after connection errors; Claude fallback supplied those results. The fast-test review noted that elapsed-time behavior remains outside automated coverage.
- **Exact-head Simulator feasibility recheck (2026-10-02):** Production `NodeAppModel` constructs `TalkModeManager()` with `allowSimulatorCapture: false` (`NodeAppModel.swift:1053`, `TalkModeManager.swift:467-474`). Both continuous native Talk (`TalkModeManager.swift:727-731`) and native PTT (`:1018`) call `startRecognition`; its `#if targetEnvironment(simulator)` branch at `:1422-1430` throws `Talk mode is not supported on the iOS simulator` before an audio tap, recognized transcript, or native `chat.send`. A host microphone route and `simctl privacy grant microphone` cannot override that compiled branch. Existing test cases explicitly pass `allowSimulatorCapture: true`; their synthetic sockets/speech players remain boundary tests, not a live turn. The exact-head app launched on iOS 27.0 Simulator with microphone granted and `-talk.enabled YES`; its app diagnostic at 14:02:08Z recorded `enabled=true ... gatewayConnected=false` and `start blocked gateway offline`. The installed app showed its unpaired onboarding screen. This runtime attempt did **not** reach the guard, and no `chat.send` or spoken output is claimed. A configured realtime WebRTC/relay route may start before native recognition, but uses a different transport and does not exercise this PR's native correlated `chat.send` timeout owner. The supported `openclaw-debug` URL parser handles agent/dashboard/gateway routes, not Talk transcript injection; ordinary typed chat and an agent deep link are likewise not Talk proof. `simctl io recordVideo` exposes display-video options only, so it cannot by itself prove an audible audio track. That earlier production-app feasibility check produced no delayed turn. The later isolated test-host run below used the existing Simulator capture seam without changing tracked PR source.

## Live iPhone Simulator Talk proof (exact head)

On 2026-10-02, an iPhone 18 Pro Simulator running iOS 27.0 and Xcode 27.0 executed a disposable XCTest test host with the PR-head `TalkModeManager.swift` byte-identical to `8cfe13562e2140be4f028ec50db17b2cf0606563` (SHA-256 `eee5d4c8e3209771abc81bbe9120515ea5a395c6caca9b30d34c4862be852a64`). The host used the existing `allowSimulatorCapture: true` seam and injected one **synthetic transcript** because production Simulator microphone recognition is compiled out. It did **not** mock the Gateway socket, agent, speech synthesizer, or audio player: native Talk connected to a fresh isolated loopback Gateway, sent `chat.send`, waited for the correlated run while the agent executed `sleep 40`, and passed the final reply to the production `TalkSystemSpeechSynthesizer` / `AVSpeechSynthesizer` delegate path.

- Native transcript submission **18:29:26 UTC**; the real Gateway tool completed after 40 seconds; native Speaking began **18:30:53 UTC**; speech completion returned **18:31:07 UTC**, **101.073 seconds** after submission. The test asserted Speaking was observed, completion stayed within 30–120 seconds, and no failure status remained. `xcodebuild test` ended `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` (1 test, 0 failures). The successful call awaited the system synthesizer's `didFinish` continuation; no synthetic TTS completion was injected.
- This proves the native `chat.send` → correlated Gateway final event → system-speech path can survive beyond 30 seconds on the exact source head. It does **not** prove production microphone recognition on Simulator or a physical-device microphone turn. The screenshots show the actual test-host states, not the normal app UI; no audio waveform was recorded, so they do not independently prove speaker audibility.

![Connected and listening in the iPhone Simulator test host at 20:29 CEST](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3d1ccdb-37ed-4c75-b398-0414867bb48a)

![Thinking after the synthetic Talk transcript was submitted at 18:29:26 UTC](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/526d9c4f-a25c-44b5-95f8-dba81f84f741)

![Native system speech active after the delayed Gateway reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f66041c3-8088-4e1d-9359-56c8e12a6aae)

![Speech completed in 101.1 seconds at 18:31:07 UTC](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28f0ac58-02d8-45f9-a9e2-dede1f3f611d)

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

## Evidence

### October 10 maintenance rebase

Current head `ec7b620198aefa13063d23ce3f42d8b8824c47fe`, tested main `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0`. Existing contribution behavior is preserved; no dependency, configuration or migration change is added by this refresh.

Focused Decision evaluator, confidence-report and Markdown suites: 88/88 passed; changed-source formatting/lint and whitespace checks passed. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent. The earlier actual offline CLI replay evidence is retained for unchanged contribution behavior; this is not a new CLI execution. QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains a maintainer decision.

Fresh independent Astra source/integration review found no actionable source defect. Current-head hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper review are pending after publication; older-head CI/review below are historical, not certification of this head. Main advanced to `dd036a4b1d855c366c7b3148a1814c83da765e50`; none of this PR’s changed paths intersects that base drift. Rollback is the prior head `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66`.

<details>
<summary>Retained pre-rebase evidence and review history (not current-head CI)</summary>


### October 8 rebase — current local evidence

Rebased onto main `05161b949bcded143f477df59834b831054f555e` at `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66` to incorporate upstream MCP advisory fix #166217. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent and all six contribution files are byte-identical to the previous head; there is no new dependency or behavior change in this PR.

- Focused evaluator/report/Markdown suites: 88 tests passed across 3 files (Vitest 32.32s; wrapper 35.29s). Extension-test types, scoped typed lint, format/whitespace and line-cap/max-lines checks passed. Independent native Astra rebase/integration review passed with no actionable findings.
- Strict production audit returned no high-or-higher npm bulk advisories and exited 0; upstream repository advisories were not checked. This confirms the previously failing MCP advisory no longer applies to the inherited lockfile.
- Earlier actual CLI replay proof is retained for unchanged contribution behavior. No new local full-suite/build/CLI run is claimed.
