prs.title: feat(stepfun): default to Step 5 Preview with USD usage pricing
prs.body:
Related: #153525 (overlapping Step 5 Preview proposal). This is an independent implementation with official USD pricing and newly captured OpenClaw Web proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Step 5 Preview needs a default catalog entry with USD usage pricing; China endpoints also lost catalog capabilities and prices because their native URLs were not declared by the provider.

## User Impact

New Standard and Step Plan setups select Step 5 Preview by default. Repeating onboarding preserves an existing primary model, fallbacks, and ownership of the `StepFun` / `StepFun Plan` aliases; existing installations can explicitly select `stepfun/step-5-preview` or `stepfun-plan/step-5-preview`.

Standard usage estimates use the official USD rates per million tokens: **$1.00 input, $0.05 cached input, $2.70 output**. Step Plan remains zero in the token-cost catalog because it uses subscription credits. China accounts still receive their separate CNY bill; OpenClaw displays the documented USD estimate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-owned manifest is the canonical catalog and price source. Add Step 5 Preview to both provider surfaces with 1,048,576 context, 65,536 maximum output, text/image input, and low/medium/high reasoning. Switch the shared default model identifier; reuse existing request shaping and cached-token accounting. Live validation caught a second owning-boundary gap: the implicit-catalog endpoint gate rejected `.com` URLs, suppressing both discovery and pricing. Declare all four native Standard/Plan endpoints in the plugin and mirror that metadata in the external-provider catalog. Custom proxies remain excluded. No new configuration option, migration, or core transport path is introduced.

The docs use the plugin catalog in merge-mode examples, keeping model capabilities and prices in one place. Runtime TypeScript is +9/-2 (seven net lines protect existing normalized alias ownership); catalog metadata is +102/-0 for model rows and endpoint ownership; tests are +222/-108; docs are +46/-68.

Sources: [model guide](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/models/step-5-preview), [official USD price table](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/pricing/details), [Step Plan](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/step-plan/overview).

## Evidence

**Live OpenClaw Web validation — candidate `ee6842c1f8dae16a98391115f4adf1b7ba9e0dfc`, isolated local Gateway, real China Standard API, no mocked provider.**

Computer Use drove the real Control UI, submitted a file-reading task, and captured these unedited browser screenshots. The final candidate called `step-5-preview` successfully (HTTP 200 streaming), read the workspace file, and returned marker `STEP5-WEB-20260923` and `137 + 256 + 89 = 482`. The new turn made two file reads and completed with 333 output tokens. The configured primary model is `stepfun/step-5-preview`; no custom model/cost rows were supplied (`models: []`).

![Step 5 Preview real OpenClaw Web conversation and tool execution](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a798a4d5-e312-41ea-ac8a-d8506688cb33)

The Usage page now attributes 86,830 tokens and about **$0.04** to Step 5 Preview, with 50.7K cached tokens, three total tool calls, and zero errors across both turns. The Control UI JSON export reports 35,455 uncached input, 687 output, and 50,688 cache-read tokens: **$0.0398443**, verified against `(input × 1 + output × 2.7 + cacheRead × 0.05) / 1e6`, with zero missing-cost entries.

![Step 5 Preview USD usage after real calls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3ec796d-4c51-4a3b-8cf5-f81e9e78aaac)

![Step 5 Preview model costs and cache accounting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3147a6bf-0502-4239-8f87-5a88330449c3)

<details>
<summary>Controlled before/after: the same original real conversation</summary>

Before declaring native endpoint ownership, the first candidate produced a correct response but the Usage page showed $0.00 and two missing-cost entries. After the fix, without another model call, the same 32,929 tokens were repriced to **$0.0184524** and **zero missing-cost entries**. The `sessions.usage` Gateway receipt reports 16,703 uncached input, 354 output, and 15,872 cache-read tokens:

`(16703 × 1 + 354 × 2.7 + 15872 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0184524`

Before:

![Before endpoint repair: real usage incorrectly unpriced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19c2686-eef0-4c20-bb42-8c8fba4819d1)

After (same original conversation):

![After endpoint repair: the same usage priced in USD](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fc4d92a-82b2-4b20-9b27-b233100062c0)

</details>

### Review follow-up

The default change is intentional and explicitly requested for this PR. Fresh Standard and Step Plan setups use Step 5 Preview; existing explicit selections and aliases must retain their previous meaning. The maintainer can still decide whether to accept that default policy before merging.

The P1 alias finding is addressed at the StepFun onboarding owner: add the default alias only when no existing entry owns its trimmed, case-insensitive name. Twelve region/surface/normalization cases failed before the repair by resolving the old alias to Step 5, then passed after the repair through the actual SDK alias resolver. The new-model default tests remain green. The requested after-repair Web/price evidence is now included above, and all five inline images were confirmed to load anonymously in a browser.

Real CLI validation on final head `eb8beb5bbae`: fresh China Standard onboarding saved primary `stepfun/step-5-preview` and alias `StepFun`. Re-running both China Standard and Step Plan onboarding against a previous-setup configuration retained primary `StepFun`, fallback `StepFun Plan`, and the old whitespace/case-varied Step 3.5 aliases. `openclaw models status --json` then reported `resolvedDefault: stepfun/step-3.5-flash`. These runs used isolated state/workspace directories and skipped service installation. The follow-up changes onboarding alias ownership only; model/request/price code is unchanged from the live Web proof commit above.

### Automated checks

- 54 focused tests passed across provider catalog/request shaping and four onboarding auth choices, including new default selection and preservation of existing primary/fallbacks. The manifest → endpoint owner gate → effective catalog regression failed for both CN endpoints before the fix and passes for all four native URLs, while custom proxies remain excluded. Before implementation, the new-model expectations failed; before changing the default, 18 of 23 default-selection checks failed.
- The live-proof commit runtime, all external plugins, SDK declarations and Control UI build: `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed. The final follow-up head `eb8beb5bbae91ea95fe5719da8ef15d359458264` passed the same build again. A full `pnpm build` also passed before the endpoint-metadata follow-up.
- Changed-scope checks: formatting, guards, all 25 core/UI typecheck shards, plugin production/test typechecks and the dead-export scans passed before the alias follow-up. The broad run was stopped during full-core lint after a separate plugin-boundary declaration preparation timed out at 300 seconds; it is **not** reported as a full gate pass. Final alias-focused syntax lint passed; the final alias-follow-up plugin production typecheck (`tsconfig.extensions.json`) also passed. Hosted CI is separate.
- Independent Claude diff-scope review through the repository autoreview helper: no accepted P0–P2 findings; live validation is reported separately above. A fresh alias-follow-up review was also scoped-clean. Codex reviewer exited before producing a report; its result is not counted as approval.

### Hosted CI follow-up

The ready-for-review run on head `eb8beb5` is still running. [`check-dependencies`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35849554342/job/107144324148) failed in Knip with `scripts/run-swiftlint.mts: swiftlint` (unlisted binary). That script and `config/knip.config.ts` have identical blob SHAs in the tested main parent `760dc1498db8` and CI merge `5510839fe613`; neither file is changed by this PR. This is recorded as a main-side tooling follow-up, not a green CI claim.

### Direct API contract checks

- Real `step-5-preview` streaming requests succeeded both with and without `stream_options`. The default stream delivered final usage.
- A repeated prompt reported 2,843 prompt tokens, 86 output tokens, and 2,560 cached prompt tokens in `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. At the published USD prices, the expected cost is `(283 × 1 + 86 × 2.7 + 2560 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0006432`.
- The provided credential is China-region: China Standard inference was tested; the international endpoint rejected it with 401. Authenticated international and Step Plan inference are **not** claimed as live-tested; their catalog/default behavior is covered by the four-region/plan setup matrix. The maximum context/output limits and image capability follow official documentation, not a maximum-size live stress test.

Keys and browser authentication material are excluded from this PR and all captures.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): stop bot-to-bot reply loops and add allowBots
prs.body:
Closes #183237
Related: #99279, #183887

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost bot accounts can repeatedly wake each other because their posts are treated as human input and never reach the shared bot-pair loop guard.

## User Impact

Mattermost preserves default bot admission while bounding rapid bot-to-bot exchanges with the shared guard. Operators can set `allowBots: false` to ignore bot posts or `"mentions"` to require explicit activation in channels. Human messages and human thread follow-ups keep their existing behavior.

The guard defaults to 20 events per pair in 60 seconds followed by a 60-second cooldown. Slower exchanges can remain under that budget. Channel, account, wildcard, and individual-channel overrides are documented. Both settings are optional; existing configuration shapes need no Doctor migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin identifies Mattermost's server-provided `from_bot` marker, applies admission policy, and supplies bot-pair facts to the existing core guard. Thread participation does not count as explicit bot activation in `"mentions"` mode. There is no Mattermost-specific counter or state store.

Thanks to @hannnnn-l (Han Liu) for the implementation and live investigation. Contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

- Base regression: five intended failures and 17 passing controls in the consolidated suite on `364c0d4ebcd4`; the admission owner was byte-identical on fetched main. The failures cover bot rejection, explicit-mention admission, thread participation, and missing shared-guard facts. Consolidated-suite base run: 213.91 seconds including compilation; assertions took milliseconds.
- Current-head focused tests: 50/50 passed across bot admission, thread mention policy, accounts, and configuration schema after integrating main `14081a8c8b31`; 344.02 seconds including compilation (324.65 seconds Vitest). The same contracts remain covered, with the formerly grouped schema rejection cases reported individually.
- Formatting, syntax lint, and `git diff --check`: pass. Local type-aware lint/typecheck refuse this linked shared install because declaration inputs resolve outside the PR checkout; exact-head CI supplies broad type and integration proof.
- Generated channel schema metadata and configuration baseline regenerated after merging main. Whole-change delta: production +98/-1 (net +97), tests +162/-164 (net -2). The added production code is the admission/configuration surface and shared-guard wiring; no independent guard machinery was added.
- Independent Codex reviews at P0–P2: scoped-clean on the complete integrated diff against `14081a8c8b31` and on the preceding test/ledger consolidation. The final main integration does not change Mattermost or the shared guard.

No fresh Mattermost server/Gateway round-trip was run on this head: recreating the disposable server setup would require a new harness. Prior-head contributor proof used Mattermost 11.7.12, two bot accounts, a human account, and a mock model: stable produced 30 replies in 45 seconds and kept going; upgraded defaults stopped after 65 replies with shared-guard drop logs; `"mentions"` admitted a direct bot mention and rejected unmentioned bot replies; `false` rejected bot posts while retaining human replies. These are prior-head observations, not a claim of a new live run.

prs.title: fix(system-agent): use configured fallbacks when primary admission fails
prs.body:
Closes #151605

## What Problem This Solves

A maintenance conversation can be rejected even when its explicitly configured model fallback works. Reuse that exact successful fallback under the original agent; never substitute a different model, credential, runtime or plugin owner on later turns or approved writes.

## User Impact

A failed primary no longer unnecessarily blocks maintenance. Existing requester checks, explicit approval, tool permissions and native writers remain mandatory. An unconfigured fallback or changed owner cannot authorize persistence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the configured fallback order and profile pins, retain the successful execution binding, and revalidate it on reuse and at persistent-effect boundaries. Secret creation is itself a persistent effect: the binding is checked again at native SQLite commit admission, before the existing synchronous requester check grants the commit. Read-only binding validation does not enqueue config-health writes behind the transaction it is validating.

Current revision: `6cec235d9a72849cd21ff18c9498e0a7f1bef437`. Integration base: `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200`. Contributor history is retained. Current-main CLI text handling, Gateway fixtures and database-worker registration are preserved. The contribution adds no schema, migration, permission mechanism, resource-limit change or secret overwrite/delete; upstream agent schema 38 is retained.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Configured fallback selection and profile order; exact-owner reuse; approved physical config/secret writes; refusal after requester, fallback or credential ownership changes, including a change after the caller's initial check but before native secret commit. Store-backed CLI credentials are also exercised while creating a separate secret.

### Real setup tested

Source integration uses isolated synthetic state, the real chat approval engine, native SQLite workers, team secret store and physical config writer. Only external HTTP model responses and the external CLI backend are synthetic; the CLI process really executes. No production model, account, data or deployment is used.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/inference-fallback.configured-chain.test.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-fallback.configured-chain.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-route.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts src/secrets/store/secret-store-config-ref.worker.test.ts src/secrets/store/secret-store.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-store.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.timeout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

The late secret-write regression first reproduced before the repair: both late fallback removal and credential reassignment left one physical secret behind while config publication was refused. The six unchanged earlier controls passed. This was an actual store read-back failure, not a mocked write result.

After native commit-admission validation and the passive config read (sanitized output summary):

```text
Late fallback removal: rejected; new secrets 0; config reference absent.
Late credential reassignment: rejected; new secrets 0; config reference absent.
Unchanged authority: one new secret and its config reference saved.
Opaque CLI owner unchanged: 6 real CLI probes; one new secret/reference saved.
Opaque CLI owner revoked: 3 real CLI probes; no new secret/reference saved.
Store-backed CLI profile unchanged: original credential preserved; one new secret/reference saved.
Store-backed CLI profile revoked: original credential preserved; no new secret/reference saved.
Complete fallback suites: 2 files, 31 tests passed.
Native secret/SQLite sibling suites: 5 additional files, 112 tests passed.
Existing configured-route suite after identity-owner relocation: 13 tests passed.
```

The 156 cases above are unique across 8 files; filtered/repeated runs are not added. The sibling command includes the earlier two opaque cases; those overlapping cases are excluded from the total. The unchanged route-identity projection was moved into its existing route owner to satisfy the native line-growth ratchet; the complete fallback and existing route suites passed again afterward. A self-wait in the first repair was diagnosed rather than hidden by longer timeouts: config-health observation tried to write shared state while the secret transaction awaited validation. The supported passive snapshot read removes that incidental write without skipping credential, plugin, runtime or requester validation.

### Observed result after fix

A verified configured fallback remains reusable under its original owner. Approved unchanged authority writes; revoked authority cannot create the new secret or publish its reference. A materialized store-backed CLI credential can be checked while another secret awaits commit without the observed self-wait, and the existing credential is untouched.

### What was not tested

Historical compiled Gateway and official `2026.10.4` upgrade-state controls were recorded on the earlier `fac94fb1833b8b7d5b2cde6165ae2fe14eabfadb` lineage. They are not current-revision execution or latest-stable compatibility proof. The later frozen-source runtime build also predates this commit-admission repair.

Fresh compiled Gateway, real-provider traffic and current latest-stable migration were not rerun here: namespace isolation was refused before application startup. No isolation policy was relaxed. In an admitted isolated environment, the remaining product check is the canonical runtime build followed by compiled CLI/Gateway/SDK: failed primary, two retained conversation turns, actual config proposal and separate approval, physical config read-back; then repeat on state created by the current official stable release using its supported native migration. An independently installed candidate release archive remains unqualified. Arbitrary third-party harness callbacks are not exhaustively certified by these fixtures.

## Current CI, review and proposed authority contract

The original 19 contribution source/test files remain byte-identical to the functionally validated predecessor `497ff3ed880f6bb5dba829b403b177cfc7700e55`. The worker registry retains new main entries plus the two fallback suites. Two existing consumer fixtures now follow native snapshot/close contracts: persisted setup reads materialize defaults through the real config validator; device cleanup awaits the existing asynchronous state-database close before its test-latch reset. Production guards, business assertions and timeouts are unchanged.

At tested revision `e3c9e7bfacdfdff41be10937da942e678ef63407` (tree `8e462f23239c5fd3eee3e29212a27538fc1172eb`, main `8828adca7e5877faac3bea151b98c438368a4e3d`), after integrating upstream agent schema 38, the two real fallback/CLI files passed 31 cases, setup passed 27 and device passed 18. These 76 current integration cases include 31 already counted in the earlier 156; they are not added as 76 new cases or called a full-tree test. Core types, the services and gateway-methods consumer type graphs, 293-rule lint and formatting also passed on that integrated candidate. Hosted CI and a new durable review for this publication are pending; no earlier-head status is reused as a fresh full-tree execution.

The setup regression was independently reproduced on the exact CI main parent `c8b7c4c435b1eb037445f637eb808211bdbaecc5` without the contribution: the same two cases failed (25/27 passed). The fixture correction passed 27/27 without relaxing route comparison. The hosted device failure was an active-borrower exception at synchronous cleanup. Its original Node/ARM file passed 18/18 on both main and candidate; this does not reproduce or attribute that Bun/x64 failure. The cleanup now obeys the documented async worker-drain contract; the new hosted run must confirm that boundary. No sleep, catch-and-ignore, runtime substitution in CI or enlarged timeout was added.

Publication head additionally integrates `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200` while preserving the 19 contribution files and two consumer fixtures byte-for-byte. That later full tree has not received another local 76-case execution. Its exact-tree budget counter and native pre-commit passed; hosted CI is the full published-tree acceptance, not a reused local PASS.

**Proposed behavior for review:** an explicitly configured fallback may satisfy maintenance inference only as its exact verified binding under the original agent. Existing tool permissions, explicit user approval and requester authority are unchanged. Removing that fallback or changing its credential/runtime/plugin owner refuses reuse and persistence. This is a proposal for review, not a security waiver or a claimed maintainer decision.

**Before merge:** obtain normal enforced security approval for the final revision and maintainer review of the proposed binding contract. Earlier-head CI and durable reviews are not attributed to this new head. No merge or deployment is requested.

## Related public context

[PR #156755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156755) addresses implicit Bedrock SDK credential proof, not configured fallback admission; that independent change is not included here. [PR #181669](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181669) preserves explicitly pinned session models for automation events; this change does not relax ordinary session pins or introduce another fallback-selection policy.

## Test-line budget and cost

The untouched `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200` main control contains 6,291,362 test lines against its 6,289,827 ceiling. Its canonical zero-delta control passes; the inherited debt is 1,535, not a claimed main functional failure. This contribution adds 1,064 lines, including 17 lines of consumer-fixture compatibility fixes. The supported ceiling adjustment is exactly 2,599 lines over that main ceiling; the actual merged total is 6,292,426. The canonical counter passes with zero additional author-created slack. Earlier 400/1,778-line figures belonged to different main trees and are superseded by this source-bound measurement.

No tests or assertions were removed, and no runtime/resource cap, counter implementation or failure classification was changed. Native ownership and approved persistence tests remain because the before-fix controls exposed an actually saved secret; a mocked write would lose the distinguishing regression.

Prior measured wall times: route 13 cases 29.23s; the two fallback files 31 cases 146.28s in a shared shard. Individual case-time sums were 83.96s for configured-chain and 37.90s for CLI, not per-file wall times. These tests exercise real worker custody, physical writes and CLI processes with isolated authority state; only model responses are synthetic. No live model charges or artificial sleeps were added.

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent stale native dashboard builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native macOS Control UI can retain an older build in persistent WebKit service-worker and HTTP caches. After the gateway updates, the page sends an old `clientBuild` and the healthy gateway rejects the handshake with `control-ui-build-mismatch`, leaving the desktop app disconnected.

## User Impact

macOS dashboard recovery preserves normal desktop navigation and unrelated service workers; this follow-up changes only the regression-test setup, with no new user-visible behavior or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persistent native caches can keep the dashboard disconnected after a Gateway update. The dedicated cache-policy capability repairs that path without enabling embed layout. The integrated-head test repair follows the current asset-helper contract rather than restoring a removed production API.

## Summary

- advertise a dedicated document-start macOS Control UI cache-policy capability without enabling native-embed layout
- unregister only an owned Control UI worker, preserving unrelated same-origin registrations
- report worker lookup, unregister rejection, and unsuccessful retirement diagnostics
- make macOS dashboard loads bypass WebKit local HTTP cache
- preserve service-worker-backed Web Push behavior for non-macOS native hosts

## Evidence

### Current-head test repair — 2026-10-22

Tested/published head: `6b70c22f1a00d3998068c5814e2d002c0eb633e6` (parent: `2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5`). Addresses [the current-head custom-base finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148435#issuecomment-5668643704).

The only source change in this follow-up is the existing custom-base worker test. It establishes `/apps/openclaw/chat` through browser history, temporarily removes both window and document base-path fixtures so the real helper infers the mount, and restores the original URL, history state, property descriptor, and document attribute in `finally`. It calls the current one-argument API and retains the `true` ownership assertion for `/apps/openclaw/sw.js?v=old-build`. No production API, cache behavior, assertion baseline, or mocks were changed.

Validation used Node `24.22.1`, pinned pnpm `12.15.0` through Corepack, and an isolated worktree with its own `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; the lockfile passed all supply-chain policies. Global runtime defaults and shared dependency installs were not changed.

- **Before editing**, the unchanged parent reproduced the reported failure: `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts src/app/public-assets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **23 passed, 1 failed**, with `expected false to be true` in the custom-base ownership test.
- The test-inclusive UI-app typecheck also reproduced **TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2** at the parent. The production UI typecheck passed at that parent because it excludes test files.
- **After the fix**, the same two-suite command — **24 passed, 0 failed** across 2 files; Vitest duration **1.43 seconds**. Hosted CI timing is not yet available for this head.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui.tsbuildinfo` — **passed** (production UI scope, equivalent to `pnpm tsgo:ui`).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-app.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui-app-tests.tsbuildinfo` — **passed**, including the affected test callers.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check ui/src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base 2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5` — **passed** (2,470 files, 5,652 grandfathered assertions; no baseline change).
- `git diff --check 2be78e6fc5214edc1d51f3c5b334b9e6db19fcd5..HEAD` — **passed**.

**Review / proof gaps:** Fresh local AutoReview was attempted through its restricted OpenClaw engine because Codex CLI is unavailable. It returned `reviewer_unavailable`, `engine_failed`, reviewer exit `1`, with no report or verdict. This is not a clean independent-review result. Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper re-review remain pending; this repair does not claim green hosted UI/macOS CI. No new native-app build, retained-profile recovery run, screenshot, production-bundle E2E, or dead-export scan was performed for this test-only follow-up.

### Historical validation — fdd88b27 (not current-head proof)

The results below are retained from the earlier candidate and have not been rerun or relabeled as proof of the integrated/repaired head.

Reviewed head: `fdd88b27e4c9be692a36bcb791e1238c58c92901`

- `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/native-web-chrome.test.ts src/app/public-assets.test.ts src/app/app-host-refresh-control-ui.test.ts src/app/service-worker-refresh.runtime.test.ts` — 44 passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/native-nav-sidebar-toggle.e2e.test.ts -t 'preserves the desktop shell|retires an owned worker'` — 2 passed, 19 skipped by filter; a fresh production Control UI bundle was built from the reviewed head.
  - The shell scenario confirms the document-start macOS capabilities preserve `.shell-nav`, `openclaw-app-topbar`, and `openclaw-macos-titlebar-controls`.
  - The persisted-worker scenario serves the production bundle's real `sw.js?v=stale-profile`, retains that registration across the initial document, injects the native capability at document start for the reloaded document, confirms the capability survived reload, and observes zero owned Control UI registrations afterward.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` — passed.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` — passed; all three Knip export scans reported zero entries.

The reviewed `fdd88b27e4c9be692a36bcb791e1238c58c92901` checkout was compiled into the `OpenClaw` SwiftPM product (`Build complete! (83.97 sec)`) and assembled with the same exact-head Control UI assets into an ad-hoc-signed proof app. `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed. The same persistent WebKit profile was first loaded with the pre-fix production Control UI from `e0b182236cd4dc394c5f3b77152fa94b29e7c809`. Immediately before launching the candidate app, WebKit's service-worker registration database reported:

```text
scopeURL = /
scriptURL = http://127.0.0.1:19943/sw.js?v=2026.9.4-e0b182236cd4-2026-09-14T21-25-13.000Z
```

```text
gatewayBuild=2026.9.4-fdd88b27e4c9-2026-09-16T05-02-45.000Z
reason=protocol mismatch: Control UI updated; reload this page to continue
```

Without deleting or moving any WebKit profile data, the candidate app then opened the dashboard through `DashboardWindowController`. Unified WebKit logging recorded the changed cleanup path executing:

```text
ServiceWorkerContainer::unregisterRegistration: Unregistering service worker.
```

The isolated Gateway then accepted the recovered page from the same native window:

```text
client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.4

```

- The native WebKit profile contained persisted `CacheStorage` and `ServiceWorkers` data for the local gateway origin.
- Moving only the app's Control UI/network cache directories to timestamped backups and restarting recovered the desktop UI; the gateway then served normal requests and the UI showed the connected Local Gateway state.

## Review follow-up

- The macOS document-start script sets `__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_CONTROL_UI_CACHE_POLICY__ = 'reload'` and leaves `__OPENCLAW_NATIVE_EMBED__` unset, preserving the normal desktop shell.
- Worker cleanup is restricted to the inferred Control UI base path and reports registration lookup failures, unregister rejections, and `unregister() === false` results.
- The retirement E2E skips null worker slots before parsing `scriptURL`.
- Native capabilities are installed with `addInitScript`, survive the tested reload boundary, and are asserted before worker-retirement success is accepted.
- The cache-policy helper is internal rather than an unused production export; underscored host globals use lint-safe typed bracket access; the reduced assertion baseline is recorded.

prs.body:
Closes #80664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dreaming admits assistant scratch notes such as `Need commit PR.` and `Now inspect.` as durable session-corpus candidates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared session scanner rejects whole-body assistant chatter before candidate construction, leaving generic transcript export and existing admission/provenance controls unchanged.

This preserves the focused approach from #80666 and #111922 by @ArthurNie, including @vincentkoc's durable-signal boundary refinement. The October 13 update merges current main and resolves the scanner conflict without expanding the three-file contribution.

## User Impact

User impact: Dreaming and session backfill exclude narrowly defined assistant process notes while retaining user text and assistant evidence containing PR numbers, commit SHAs, or results. Previously ingested memory is not rewritten.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `dc71f9a026c25135b26e068ad3fd78af4d3f15c2` (merged main `983f4a3bdbf7`). Fresh main `7c1b789ca5b` has no intervening changes to memory-core or the applicable contribution policy; the candidate merges cleanly. Local timings/results below apply to the candidate, not a synthetic merge with newer main.

- Current-main production baseline: both new regressions fail because all three reported scratch notes enter candidates.
- With the filter: both complete touched test files pass, **34/34**. This includes actual canonical SQLite-backed backfill, user lookalikes, durable assistant results, scan progress, provenance and recovery coverage.
- Independent Claude review on this exact head: clean, no findings. A final one-file autoreview of the test typing correction also returned clean; earlier merge-snapshot autoreviews did not certify attribution.
- Production and test extension typechecks, targeted type-aware lint on all three changed files, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. The conflict update preserves both current-main scanner helpers; the backfill fixture now obtains its type from the canonical transcript helper instead of a removed alias.
- Broader memory-core run: **1,600 passed, four skipped, one failed** in the first 171-file batch; the wrapper did not proceed to the two remaining files. The failure is `manager-provider-probe.test.ts`, which observed one leftover fake timer after a successful embedding probe. The test, fixture and production probe owner are byte-identical to the checked base. One isolation rerun reproduced it, the base-scanner control passed, and the restored final candidate passed **4/4**. This establishes intermittency, not a proven repair; the broad run is not claimed green and no timer assertion was weakened.
- Aggregate changed checks also found pre-existing max-lines suppression/dead-export problems outside the three-file patch. Targeted typed lint timed out during SDK preparation on its first attempt; one normal retry completed preparation and lint successfully, without changing the wrapper or deadline. The aggregate run is not claimed green; exact-head PR CI remains required.

Measured touched-file wall times: ingestion **17.42s**, canonical backfill **48.97s**. The new backfill regression itself took **423ms**; the complete file also exercises existing SQLite worker, provenance and recovery contracts. CI durations for this new head are not yet available.

The earlier merge-snapshot autoreview's whitespace suggestion does not apply because snippets are normalized and trimmed before the predicate. No filter broadening, timeout increase, assertion weakening, or unrelated cleanup is included.

<details>
<summary>Historical production CLI proof on the original reviewed head</summary>

The original `0e9f75e2aaa9` head was exercised through an isolated real session-backfill CLI. This is historical evidence, not a new CLI run on the October 13 merge.

```text

```

The assistant messages `Need commit PR.` and `Now inspect.` were excluded. The new merge also has fresh canonical-store regression proof as reported above.

</details>

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #145309. Claude CLI transcripts could be looked up under the Gateway's configuration directory instead of the directory selected for the child process, breaking session continuity and imported history.

Main has since landed #175549 (ambient `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for recovery and import) and #164796 (native-login history attestation). This PR builds on both and closes the remaining gap: the root is selected from the **effective child environment** (backend `env`/`clearEnv`, prepared overrides, skill env), retained with the native session binding across restarts, and re-authorized before native history is read or published.

## User Impact

Custom Claude configuration directories keep native session continuity, fallback context, Doctor diagnostics and imported history, including agent-scoped or skill-selected `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` values the Gateway process itself does not carry. Changing or unselecting the effective profile stops access to its old native transcripts while canonical OpenClaw history stays available. A profile change during response preparation prevents publication of a stale native-history result and asks the client to reload.

Existing bindings gain location metadata on subsequent turns. No public configuration option and no SQL schema migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final child environment and canonical cwd select the transcript root. Execution, settlement and recovery retain that location; readers validate it against the currently effective root. Historical cwd locates an authorized transcript; current cwd authorizes relative or empty configuration roots. Paired-node bindings do not trigger Gateway-local native transcript discovery.

One owner per responsibility after the resync with main:

- `claude-cli-project-dir.ts` has a single selector. An explicit `homeDir` without a child environment isolates offline reads (the #175549 contract and its tests are kept); a child `env` uses native nullish/NFC selection and resolves relative roots against the child cwd.
- `child-env.ts` composes on main's `resolveCliChildEnv` (new optional `skillEnv` overlay) instead of duplicating environment composition.
- `chat-history-pages.ts`, `cli-session-history.process-held.ts` and `chat-message-get-handler.ts` carry the authorization guard on main's session-actor read path; semantics match the previously reviewed head.
- `chat-history-handler.ts` was at the 700-line cap, so the short-id/slug `chat.startup` resolution moved unchanged to `chat-startup-handler.ts`.
- Fallback prelude (ClawSweeper P2 on `13b902c522b`): main made `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed` asynchronous, so the authorized root captured before discovery was no longer rechecked after the awaited directory listing and file read. The attempt now derives the authorization once, passes a live `assertNativeHistoryAuthorized` through discovery, the transcript read and formatting, and re-derives the prompt right before the embedded or CLI request; a changed selection throws `NATIVE_HISTORY_AUTHORIZATION_DENIED` inside the reader and the native prelude is dropped (the fallback runs on the canonical prompt only).

## Evidence

Current head `0747101f5b9`: merge of main `ac2f8c2d0e8` (`483d41bb7ba`, 3 conflicted files: `attempt-execution.helpers.ts` lost `charBudget`, `attempt-execution.test.ts`, cli-import test helpers moved to main's `historyRpc`/`historyPayload` fixtures) plus the fallback-authority fix above. Previous head `13b902c522b` merged main `900e6aa3215` into the reviewed head `41a5db29012` (23 conflicted files; production semantics unchanged apart from the single-selector contract above).

Local Windows / Node 24.19.0, this head:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (all shards) pass. `oxlint` on every touched file, `oxfmt --check`, `check:import-cycles`, `check:test-mock-exports`, `check:no-conflict-markers` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Focused suites (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <files>`):

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cli-session-history.claude-config-dir.test.ts` | 22/22 |
| `chat-history-handler.cli-import.claude-config-dir.test.ts` | 5/5 |
| `chat-history-publication.test.ts` | 2/2 |
| `chat-history-handler.cli-import.test.ts` | 17/18 (see below) |
| `cli-session-history.paging.test.ts` | 10/10 |
| `cli-session-history.claude-snapshot.test.ts` | 5/5 |
| `session-history-worker-runtime.test.ts` | 21/29; the PR case passes, 8 pre-existing POSIX-path cases fail on Windows only |
| `claude-cli-project-dir.test.ts` + `.windows.test.ts` | 8/8 + 4/4 |
| `cli-session.test.ts`, `cli-run-settlement.test.ts` | all pass |
| `execute.claude-config-dir.test.ts`, `cli-runner.claude-config-dir.test.ts` | 5/5, 1/1 |
| `attempt-execution.claude-config-dir.test.ts` | 3/3; new boundary case: allowed prelude, revoked during pending discovery (no `access`/`readFile` follows), revoked after the file read (content never formatted) |
| `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts`, `attempt-execution.test.ts` | 89/89, 23/23 on the current head (includes the #175549 configured-root regression and the new production-path trace: `runAgentAttempt` fallback with the profile switched inside the pending native directory listing; the embedded request carries no native content and the old transcript is never accessed or read) |

It times out identically on a pristine `upstream/main` worktree (`900e6aa3215`), so it is inherited, not introduced here. Hosted Linux CI on this head is the authoritative run.

## Maintainer decision still required

Please explicitly accept or narrow the current-root native-history access contract: changing or unselecting the effective Claude profile (or changing cwd for a relative root) makes retained native transcripts from the old root unavailable, while canonical OpenClaw history remains accessible. Passing tests do not constitute owner acceptance. This update requests review and the owner decision; it does not merge or bypass either gate.

prs.title: fix(models): keep generated catalogs credential-free
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated plugin model catalogs still persist provider/model API keys and headers, and refresh can discard a legacy-only credential before recovery. This revision replaces the original broader runtime-auth cutover with the remaining **storage and explicit migration** repair:

- Strip keys/headers from newly planned and published generated catalogs, including direct publisher calls.
- Stop copying a plaintext auth-profile key into a missing root catalog field.
- Preserve unresolved legacy generated rows during ordinary refresh without blocking unrelated providers.
- Have Doctor import and verify recoverable keys, then remove generated copies accounted for by canonical auth or current authored configuration—including already-canonical copies.

## User Impact

Authored root `models.json` bytes and existing SDK/registry authentication behavior are preserved. **No runtime-auth selection change is introduced.** This does not promise universal Gateway root-only auth: an actual root-only Gateway attempt exposed an unchanged embedded-auth prerequisite, documented in the proof.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair retained generated copies. Doctor includes configured agents with generated SQLite catalogs but no root catalog. Unverified fields stay recoverable with warnings. Pending sidecar migration bytes remain intact until retry convergence.

Doctor rereads source/auth after confirmation, checks the current config revision and included files, and validates source state at persistence/cleanup boundaries. Concurrent logout/source changes do not authorize stale recovery or deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#143664](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143664) already blocks generated credentials at request time; [#143647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143647) provides logout cleanup. This PR builds on their existing owners. It adds no dependency, config option, schema migration, or broader credential-precedence policy.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `cae19faf537bb04cbd39301d8a0a82f1b4ca5ac6`. Integrated current main; conflict resolved; final independent AutoReview clean. Exact-head build and added stable-2026.10.5/fresh-publication proofs are in progress. Historical linked receipts below remain attributed to their original heads.

[Immutable evidence bundle](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/README.md) · [file manifest](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/MANIFEST.sha256) · [final runtime boundaries](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-stage-summary.json) · [independent AutoReview](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/review/autoreview-current-cli.md).

- **167/167 focused tests**, 12 files, pass. Includes pre-fix reproductions and repairs for confirmation-time config/include data loss, pending-sidecar recovery, and logout races.
- Targeted lint/core types, formatting, MDX and standard docs routes pass. A hosted test-type error was fixed with a non-null assertion; emitted test JavaScript is identical. Extra anchor auditing found five pre-existing broken anchors in untouched files, disclosed separately.
- AutoReview: **scoped-clean; no actionable P0–P2 findings** on the implementation diff. Final follow-up is test-type-only. The final exact-head build passes; [source/artifact binding](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/0cddae83c7792ccad91a0e43ab7c070f3e8fed3f/runtime/final-source-binding.json) proves all 19 previously bound launchers/changed-owner bundles are byte-identical.
- **Actual published 2026.10.3 → built candidate:** real launcher Doctor migration, canonical/recovered-key Gateway requests, retained conversation and final-head restart/recall pass against an actual CPU local model. Supported logout removes profiles; the protected receiver rejects the subsequent credential-free localhost request, with no revoked-key reuse or upstream inference.
- **Authored compatibility:** built registry/LLM SDK inference with empty canonical auth returns `ROOT-AUTH-OK`, preserving exact authored bytes. The failed root-only Gateway attempt and the invalid initial zero-HTTP-I/O expectation for localhost are retained and explained—not mislabeled passes. Reproduction sources distinguish executed receipts from adapted, unexecuted recipes.

**Current-head CI and final proof refresh are in progress.** Previous-head CI passed; it is not claimed for this integrated commit. Fresh ClawSweeper review will be requested once the new evidence is published. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix(firecrawl): unresolvable baseUrl reported as private-endpoint policy
prs.body:
Closes #135333.
Related: #137783.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a self-hosted Firecrawl `baseUrl` would see a private-endpoint / SSRF policy error when the hostname simply failed DNS (for example `http://raspberrypi:3002` or `http://firecrawl.lan:3002`). The message pointed them at HTTPS or privateness policy when the real cause was resolution failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

`firecrawlEndpointTargetsPrivateNetwork` was swallowing every resolver failure with `catch { return false }`, so DNS misses took the same path as “resolved to a public host.” Resolution failures (empty answers and lookup rejects such as `ENOTFOUND`) now throw a host-specific DNS error; `SsrFBlockedError` still falls through to the existing private-endpoint policy messages. Successful public resolves keep those policy errors. The same classification was previously attempted in #137783 and self-closed over live channel proof this error-path change does not need. The searxng client still has the same swallow-all catch and is left as a follow-up.

## User Impact

Operators and plugin authors who mistype or cannot resolve a Firecrawl `baseUrl` host now see:

`Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: <host>. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.`

instead of the HTTP/HTTPS “must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint” messages. Hosted `api.firecrawl.dev` and correctly resolving private self-hosted endpoints behave as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior (system DNS, no mocked lookupFn)

Same plugin invocation path on current `main` vs this branch. `baseUrl=http://unresolvable.invalid:3002`, keyless `runFirecrawlSearch`, plus `testing.resolveEndpoint`. Host deliberately uses the reserved `.invalid` TLD so resolution fails via real DNS (`ENOTFOUND`).

**Before (origin/main @ cdda5825f8bb):**

```text
=== Before-fix real-DNS Firecrawl proof (current main) ===
ref: origin/main
sha: cdda5825f8bb50e4112f13a9405856cad87bfa79
baseUrl: http://unresolvable.invalid:3002
lookupFn: (none — system DNS)

--- 1) testing.resolveEndpoint ---
error.message: Firecrawl HTTP baseUrl must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint. Use https:// for public hosts.

--- 2) runFirecrawlSearch (keyless) ---
error.message: Firecrawl HTTP baseUrl must target a private or internal self-hosted endpoint. Use https:// for public hosts.
```

**After (fix/firecrawl-unresolvable-baseurl @ c01c38b263a0):**

```text
=== After-fix real-DNS Firecrawl proof ===
branch: fix/firecrawl-unresolvable-baseurl
head: c01c38b263a071d15542606060c6017cac21cdec
baseUrl: http://unresolvable.invalid:3002
lookupFn: (none — system DNS)

--- 1) testing.resolveEndpoint (plugin validation path) ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 2) runFirecrawlSearch (plugin invocation; fails at endpoint validation before HTTP) ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 3) https sibling ---
error.message: Unable to resolve Firecrawl baseUrl host: unresolvable.invalid. Verify the hostname or DNS configuration.

--- 4) DNS sanity (system resolver) ---
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND unresolvable.invalid
```

### Regression tests (mocked DNS)

```text
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts
# 34 passed — including DNS vs privateness classification cases

pnpm test:extension firecrawl
# Test Files  3 passed (3)
# Tests       103 passed (103)
```

prs.title: fix(line): deliver one reply as one billable request
prs.body:
Closes #142734

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a multi-part LINE reply spends one monthly message per part instead of one per request:

- card + caption + image: 3 messages
- location pin + caption: 2 messages
- text containing a Markdown table (rendered as text, card, text): 3 messages

On the free plan (200 messages/month) that decides how long the bot keeps answering; once the allowance runs out, the bot is silent for the rest of the cycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

LINE bills one message per request per recipient, however many message objects the request carries.

- The payload's parts are assembled once, in their existing order, and sent five per request through the batching sender — the shape the quick-reply branch and the inbound reply path already use.
- Media is built before the first request, so a URL LINE refuses no longer takes the text and buttons with it; that failure is reported as a partial delivery.
- The five runtime seams left without a reader are removed. The four `send.ts` helpers they reached (`pushFlexMessage`, `pushLocationMessage`, `pushTemplateMessage`, `pushTextMessageWithQuickReplies`) stay exported from `runtime-api.ts`; deleting that surface is kept out of a bug fix.
- Merged receipts are renumbered, because each request numbers its parts from zero and recovery maps parts back by that number (`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts`). Slack, Matrix, and Telegram do the same after `createMessageReceiptFromOutboundResults`, which merges the receipt here too.
- Quoting (#142092): the quote is resolved once, and `applyLineQuoteToken` places it on the first message that can carry one, across the whole payload before it is cut into requests — so a first request of only cards still quotes the text in the second. `reportLineQuoteCarrierMissing` still fires when nothing can carry it; `sendMedia` is unchanged.

Out of scope: replies core splits before the channel sees them (long text chunks; one media URL per call, with the text as caption) still cost one message per unit. Grouping those is the `sendPayloadGroupsMedia` opt-in (Telegram uses it), whose contract requires cancellation and authority checks before every send — a separate change.

**Maintainer decision.** A part LINE refuses already lost everything queued behind it; batching also loses the up to four parts sharing its request. I accepted that because a reply that stops early looks identical to a finished one, and the failure now carries `visibleReplySent` plus the ids that landed, so nothing is replayed on top. The alternative is the inbound path's text-only retry after a definitive 400 (`canRetryTextOnly` in `extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts`), lifted into a shared owner; another open PR is changing that file. Happy to add it here or as a follow-up.

## User Impact

- A LINE reply the Gateway starts by itself with a card, quick replies, or a location now costs one monthly message per five parts instead of one per part — multiplied by member count in a group.
- Same messages, same order; quick replies still ride the last message.
- An unusable media URL no longer drops the whole reply (before, text + quick replies + bad media delivered nothing).
- The returned receipt names every message of the last request, the delivery observer sees every request, and a failure after an accepted request carries the ids already delivered.
- Every Gateway reply, media included, now goes through a send path that logs LINE's refusal reason.
- Trade-off: a refused message object takes up to four request-mates with it. The troubleshooting docs describe the symptom and how to read the rejected position from the verbose log.

## Evidence

### Live A/B: monthly allowance spent per reply

Against the real LINE Messaging API, driving the plugin's own `sendPayload` rather than a full Gateway turn:

- same payload (a card, its caption, and an image), same account, single recipient;
- `GET /v2/bot/message/quota/consumption` read before and after each run;
- the payload carries `channelData`, which is what makes core hand the whole thing to the channel instead of fanning out itself.

```text
# AFTER (fix) · shape card
platform message ids named by the returned receipt: 3
totalUsage 110 -> 111
monthly messages spent on this one reply: 1

# BEFORE (origin/main outbound) · shape card
platform message ids named by the returned receipt: 1
totalUsage 111 -> 114
monthly messages spent on this one reply: 3
```

Both runs delivered the same three messages to the chat; the id count is what the adapter's return value names, which is the second thing this change fixes. The platform rule behind the numbers, confirmed on the same account: one request carrying five mixed message objects returned five sent-message ids and raised `totalUsage` by 1; the same five sent as five requests raised it by 5.

### Requests per payload shape

Driving the plugin's own `sendPayload` with a recording fetch (no network, no credentials). Every shape here is one core really routes to `sendPayload`:

```text
# BEFORE (origin/main)
one text chunk holding a markdown table: 3 push request(s) => 3 monthly message(s) [text | flex | text]
a card, its caption, and an image:       3 push request(s) => 3 monthly message(s) [flex | text | image]
a location pin with its caption:         2 push request(s) => 2 monthly message(s) [location | text]
a markdown table with quick replies:     3 push request(s) => 3 monthly message(s) [text | flex | text]

# AFTER (fix)
one text chunk holding a markdown table: 1 push request(s) => 1 monthly message(s) [text+flex+text]
a card, its caption, and an image:       1 push request(s) => 1 monthly message(s) [flex+text+image]
a location pin with its caption:         1 push request(s) => 1 monthly message(s) [location+text]
a markdown table with quick replies:     1 push request(s) => 1 monthly message(s) [text+flex+text]
```

### A request is accepted or refused as a unit

Measured with `POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push`, which neither delivers nor spends allowance:

```text
1 valid text alone                        HTTP 200  {}
1 invalid flex alone                      HTTP 400  A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid
valid + invalid + valid in ONE request    HTTP 400  A message (messages[1]) in the request body is invalid
```

The line the troubleshooting docs tell an operator to read, captured from the real API by pushing a valid text followed by an invalid Flex message. LINE refuses the request whole, so nothing was delivered and no allowance was spent:

```text
line: push message failed (400 Bad Request): {"message":"A message (messages[1]) in the request body is invalid","details":[{"message":"`text` or `contents` must be specified","property":"/body/contents/0"},{"message":"invalid text content","property":"/body/contents/0"}]}
```

### Batching cannot build a request LINE refuses for its size

Five Flex bubbles just under the per-bubble cap validate as one 148 KB request, so the five-per-request cap is the only limit in play:

```text
1 bubble(s), request body  29726 bytes  ->  HTTP 200  {}
5 bubble(s), request body 148410 bytes  ->  HTTP 200  {}
```

### Red/green and checks

- Media behavior: with the three production files reverted to `origin/main`, `delivers the text a rejected media URL came with, and still surfaces the rejection` fails; with the change applied it passes.
- Checks: extension-line vitest suite, both `run-tsgo` lanes, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` (this file's grandfathered assertions shrink from 6 to 4), and `config:docs:check`.
- Production diff is net -75 lines against current main, plus 40 lines of docs.

### After merging main

Merged `origin/main` at `1685e53b06f`.

- Conflicts: `outbound.ts` (the quote support above) and the shared test runtime, which now keeps main's real confirm-template fixture.
- The tests #142092 added for the push path asserted one `pushMessageLine` call per part. They now read the same facts off the batched requests: which message carries the token, that only one does, and that a reply answering nothing carries none.
- Two cases were added for what batching makes new; each fails when its guard is taken out, and both pass with the change as committed:

```text
quote applied per request instead of across the payload
  × quotes the first message able to carry it even when an earlier request cannot

missing carrier no longer reported
  × reports a push that answered a message but could carry no quote
```

Local checks on this head, Windows 11: the six outbound and quote test files pass, 113/113, and `oxfmt --check` is clean on every touched file. Type checks, lint and the full suite are left to CI.

prs.title: fix(line): a credential that cannot be read is not enough to run
prs.body:
Closes #142356

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a LINE account whose credential file cannot be read was still treated as able to run:

- the model is offered a send tool on a channel the Gateway has just refused to start;
- `isConfigured`, which core reads as "enough configuration to run", says yes while the Gateway says no;
- a send that names LINE (`openclaw message send --channel line`, a named account) fails with "token missing (set `channels.line.channelAccessToken` …)", sending the operator to a key that was never the problem.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveLineAccount` already tells apart `available`, `configured_unavailable` (the config named a source that could not be read), and `missing`. `hasLineCredentials` only asked "not `missing`?", and every caller used that one answer.
- Those callers ask two different questions:
  - **Can the account run?** `isConfigured` (`resolveChannelAccountConfigured`: *"Resolves whether a channel account has enough configuration to run."*) and the message tool offered to the model. An unreadable credential cannot run, so these now require both credentials to resolve (`hasUsableLineCredentials`).
  - **Is it configured?** `describeAccount`, the status snapshot, and the setup wizard. These keep the account configured, and status marks the unreadable credential unavailable. That is what `docs/plugins/architecture-internals/channel-surfaces.md` asks of read-only surfaces (*"instead of crashing or misreporting the account as not configured"*), what core projects for a blocked account (`configured: true`, `lifecycle: "blocked"` in `src/channels/status/account-state.ts`), and how Telegram already splits the same two questions (`extensions/telegram/src/config-adapter.ts`).
- The message tool follows the account that discovery names. For a channel other than the current one, core passes no account and asks each plugin for its configured-account union (`src/channels/plugins/message-action-discovery.ts`), so LINE offers send while any enabled account has both credentials resolved. An unreadable default does not hide a healthy second account, and a named account still decides alone. A send that names no account still goes to the default account, as on `main`.
- The token resolver every send, rich-menu and quota call shares now tells the two apart too. A `tokenFile` that cannot be used reports the token as configured but unavailable, with the config path and the reason `resolveLineAccount` already recorded (for example `channels.line.accounts.work.tokenFile could not be used (symlink)`), and only a token that was never set asks for `channelAccessToken`. The Gateway does not start this account and the health probe skips it, so neither reports it as missing, and the quota read swallows its error.
- Every core reader of `isConfigured` now treats this account as not configured, as it already does for a Telegram token that cannot be resolved. Going through all of them (`git grep` outside tests), these are the ones an operator will notice; the messages are core's, and the LINE docs now say what each means for this account:
  - channel auto-selection (`src/infra/outbound/channel-selection.ts`): a send that names no channel no longer counts LINE. With LINE as the only channel it reports `Channel is required (no configured channels detected)` instead of picking LINE and failing at the token; with exactly one other channel it goes to that channel, where `main` asked which one to use;
  - cron delivery validation (`src/cron/delivery-channel-validation.ts`): creating a job with `delivery.channel: line`, or moving a job's delivery or failure destination to LINE, is rejected as `not configured` (or `must be one of: …` when other channels exist), where `main` accepted it;
  - `openclaw channels capabilities`, which prints `Status: not configured, enabled` even with `--channel line`;
  - DM pairing through the Gateway (`src/gateway/server-methods/channel-pairing.ts`), which the Control UI's Channels page uses, and which matters because LINE's default `dmPolicy` is `pairing`: the account's pending requests are not listed there, and approving one answers `channel account does not use DM pairing: line:default`, where `main` listed and approved them. `openclaw pairing list line` and `openclaw pairing approve` read the pairing store directly and are unaffected. Requests expire an hour after they were created either way;
  - broadcast (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.ts`): a broadcast that names no channel leaves LINE out;
  - the Gateway conversation list (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`): the account's peers drop out of Control UI and `conversations_list`;
  - `openclaw agents` lists the account as `configured unavailable` (`src/commands/agents.providers.ts`), which is what it is; `main` did not mark it unavailable.

  The remaining readers change nothing an operator sees here: Gateway startup already refuses this account before it asks, `openclaw status` and `openclaw channels status` keep showing it as configured (see the CLI output below), the channel status probe is answered by the Gateway's degraded-account snapshot first, the plugin-trust audit (`src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts`) only looks at channels with native commands or skills, which LINE does not declare, and the per-account channel audit never reaches LINE (see "Not affected" below).
- One case gives something up: with only `secretFile` unusable and the token inline, a send would still have worked, because push needs only the token. The account cannot receive, and the message tool now applies the rule `main` already applies to a missing secret: both credentials, or no send tool.
- No new status reason string: `openclaw channels status` already marks the unreadable credential `(unavailable)`, and with the Gateway running `Degraded secrets` and its startup log name the account and path.
- An earlier revision answered "not configured" everywhere. ClawSweeper's finding (the status warning naming the wrong credential) came from that flipped snapshot, and no longer fires.
- Unchanged: an account with no credentials is unconfigured everywhere, and an account without status fields still falls back to the raw values, a branch that predates this change.

## User Impact

- A LINE account with an unreadable credential file is no longer offered to the model as a send target.
- Status and `describeAccount` keep showing it as configured with the unreadable credential marked unavailable, and the setup wizard shows it as configured and asks for the credential again, instead of telling the operator nothing was configured. That matches `Degraded secrets` and the Gateway's own startup refusal.
- While its `tokenFile` cannot be used, a send that names that account fails with the config path and the reason the file was refused, instead of asking for a token the operator already configured. While only `secretFile` cannot be used, sends that name LINE still go out.
- Until the file is fixed, commands that ask whether LINE is configured leave this account out: a send or broadcast that names no channel does not count LINE, a cron job cannot be pointed at LINE, pending DM pairing requests do not show in the Control UI (the `openclaw pairing` CLI still lists and approves them), its peers are not in the conversation list, and `channels capabilities` shows it as not configured.
- Accounts with working credentials, or with none at all, behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: an unreadable credential file counted as able to run, so the model was offered a send tool on a channel the Gateway refused to start.
Real environment tested: a real Gateway on Windows 11 against a LINE channel whose `tokenFile` pointed at a path that does not exist; on macOS, built from this branch's code: `openclaw channels status` and `openclaw status` against a missing `tokenFile` and a missing `secretFile`, `openclaw message send` against a missing `tokenFile`, a symlinked `tokenFile`, and without `--channel`, `openclaw channels capabilities` against a missing `tokenFile`, and `openclaw security audit` with readable credentials; and the shipped plugin driven directly for each shape.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: see the blocks below.
Observed result after fix: the account cannot run and the message tool is withheld, while `describeAccount`, the status snapshot and `openclaw channels status` still report it as configured with the credential marked unavailable.
What was not tested: file rejections other than a missing path and a symlink (an empty file, a directory, a hardlink, a file over the size limit). They take the same path through `resolveLineAccount` and report their own reason. LINE's credential keys take plain strings only, so there is no SecretRef case. Pairing, cron validation and the conversation list need a running Gateway, and a send with only `secretFile` unusable was not run; those behaviors come from source.
Not affected: the security audit behind `openclaw security audit` (with or without `--deep`), `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw status --all`. All three run in the CLI without loading channel runtimes, so the audit gets each channel's setup plugin (`listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` with setup fallbacks; `--deep` loads only a non-activated metadata snapshot for plugin collectors). No bundled setup plugin carries a security adapter, and `src/security/audit-channel.ts` skips a plugin without one before it asks whether an account is configured. So no LINE account gets the per-account channel audit on `main` or on this branch, readable file or not (config-wide checks such as `security.exposure.*` still read `channels.line.dmPolicy`): with readable credentials, `dmPolicy: "open"` and `allowFrom: ["*"]` on both LINE and Telegram, `openclaw security audit --json` on this branch reports no `channels.*` finding for either. That gap predates this change and belongs in a separate issue.
Proof limitations or environment constraints: the credential file is made unusable by pointing the key at a path that does not exist, which is what a deleted file produces, and, for the send error, at a symlink to a readable file.

### Every surface, asking the shipped plugin

Same config in both columns: `channels.line.tokenFile` points at a path that does not exist, `channelSecret` is inline.

| Surface | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tokenStatus` | `configured_unavailable` | `configured_unavailable` |
| `config.isConfigured` | `true` | `false` |
| message tool actions offered to the model | `["send"]` | `[]` |
| `describeAccount.configured` | `true` | `true` |
| status snapshot `configured` | `true` | `true` |
| status issues | none | none |
| setup `isLineConfigured` | `true` | `true` |
| `sendMessageLine` through the account | `LINE channel access token missing for account "default" (set channels.line.channelAccessToken or LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN).` | `LINE channel access token configured for account "default" is unavailable: channels.line.tokenFile could not be used (not-found). Point it at a readable regular file; symlinks are rejected.` |

Both credentials resolving, and no credentials at all, answer exactly as on `main`. With a healthy second account and discovery naming none, the message tool is still offered, as on `main`.

### Gateway

The Gateway's own refusal is what `isConfigured` now agrees with:

```text
$ node dist/index.js gateway run
[line] channel startup failed: Secret owner account:line:default is configured but
       unavailable (credential file is unavailable).
[gateway] ready
```

### What the CLI shows

Built from this branch's head, no Gateway running. `tokenFile` pointing at a path that does not exist, inline `channelSecret`:

```text
$ openclaw channels status        # no Gateway reachable: config-only
- LINE default: enabled, configured, secret unavailable in this command path, token:*** (unavailable), signing:config

$ openclaw status
│ LINE │ ON │ OK │ configured │
```

Inline `channelAccessToken`, `secretFile` pointing at a path that does not exist:

```text
$ openclaw channels status        # no Gateway reachable: config-only
- LINE default: enabled, configured, secret unavailable in this command path, token:***, signing:file (unavailable)

$ openclaw status
│ LINE │ ON │ OK │ configured │
```

Both describe the account as configured and mark the credential that could not be read.

### Sends, channel selection, capabilities

Same build, no Gateway running, LINE as the only channel:

```text
$ openclaw message send --channel line --target U0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef -m hello   # tokenFile: path that does not exist
❌ LINE channel access token configured for account "default" is unavailable: channels.line.tokenFile could not be used (not-found). Point it at a readable regular file; symlinks are rejected.
[exit=1]

$ openclaw message send --channel line --target U0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef -m hello   # tokenFile: symlink to a readable file
❌ LINE channel access token configured for account "default" is unavailable: channels.line.tokenFile could not be used (symlink). Point it at a readable regular file; symlinks are rejected.
[exit=1]

$ openclaw message send --target U0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef -m hello   # no --channel
Channel is required (no configured channels detected). Run openclaw channels add to configure one, or pass --channel <channel> after enabling a channel. Use openclaw channels list --all to see available channel ids.
[exit=1]

$ openclaw channels capabilities --channel line
Status: not configured, enabled
[exit=0]
```

### Mutation

Each new guard was reverted on its own and the test file rerun; every mutation reddens the case that describes it, and the file is restored with no diff:

```text
message tool union back to the default account only
  × offers the message tool through a healthy account when discovery names none
      Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
isConfigured back to hasLineCredentials
  × cannot run, but stays configured wherever the account is described
      Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
message tool back to "not missing"
  × withholds the message tool the model would otherwise be told it can use
  × offers the message tool through a healthy account when discovery names none
      Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
hasLineCredentials back to "available only" (this PR's earlier revision)
  × cannot run, but stays configured wherever the account is described
      Tests  1 failed | 7 passed (8)
send error back to main's "token missing" (no recorded path and reason)
  × tells a send which token file could not be used instead of asking for a token
  × names the account's own key and why a token file that exists was refused
      Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

### Checks

macOS, one run of each at this branch's head:

```text
tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json                     exit=0
tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json  exit=0
node scripts/check-changed.mjs                       exit=0
oxfmt --check (touched files)                        exit=0
pnpm check:assertion-safety --base origin/main       exit=0
pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base origin/main      exit=0
git diff --check                                     exit=0
vitest (extension-line)                              68 files, 1031 passed
```
