prs.title: fix(gateway): let delegated OpenClaw changes work from CLI-backend agents
prs.body:
Related: #136036, #137017

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated `openclaw.chat` calls from CLI/subprocess and worker harnesses failed with `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`. Fully in-process agents retained the ambient caller identity, but harness tool calls crossed the Gateway WebSocket boundary, where that process-local identity is intentionally unavailable.

## User Impact

CLI and worker-harness delegated calls retain their signed source ownership and approval guard, including when optional wire delegation metadata is absent. Existing run, tool-abort and worker-lifetime fencing remains fail-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The approval gate only consulted the process-local Gateway tool caller identity. OpenClaw already has a host-minted, HMAC-signed `agentRuntimeIdentityToken` for trusted cross-process calls, including the exact admitted run authority and worker turn claim, but `openclaw.chat` was not included in that transport.

The first revision attempted to mint replacement authority from the delegated session id. Review identified that as unsafe. The signed-identity revision then exposed two narrower defects:

- Distinct calls in one source run receive distinct tool-bound lease claim ids. Approval reconciliation compared those claim ids, so a later call retired the original pending decision even though its exact lease was still live.
- The wire fallback retained the generic 30-second request timeout although delegated human interaction is budgeted for 900 seconds and the approval owner can wait 600 seconds before staging/application completes.

## Design

This revision carries the existing source-run authority instead of synthesizing or transferring it:

- `openclaw.chat` is eligible for the signed agent-runtime identity token.
- The host binds the exact tool abort signal into the delegated run authority before signing it.
- Explicit host-prepared Full Access is transported only for `openclaw.chat`; model-authored parameters cannot create it.
- On Gateway arrival, signed agent/runtime/session/routing facts establish delegation even when the optional wire field is omitted; model-supplied metadata cannot override or opt out of that binding.
- Ambient in-process identity remains authoritative when present. Wire calls use the verified signed runtime identity.
- Pending-approval reconciliation first validates the original exact application lease, then compares both callers' active canonical source owner plus local/worker kind and exact worker turn claim. It never replaces the authority stored on the pending record.
- The delegated wire call uses the existing 900-second human-interaction budget. The generic Gateway default remains 30 seconds, and the Codex owner retains its separate 30-second completion grace.
- Run release/replacement, original tool abort, Gateway replacement, worker-claim loss, and delegated-session replacement still fail closed.

No new configuration keys, SQLite surfaces, dependencies or retries are introduced. The existing transient signed-identity token carries an optional host-prepared Full Access fact. Existing canonical owner and human-wait helpers were sufficient.

## Security properties

- No authority is derived from a session id or model-authored delegation fields.
- The signed identity can only be minted by the host holding the local runtime-token secret.
- Full Access is a host-prepared restrict-only fact; omission never bypasses approval.
- Reuse grants observation of an existing pending decision only after its original exact application lease is revalidated.
- The original record retains its exact lease, signals, and application predicate. Closing a later sibling lease cannot transfer or cancel that authority; closing the original lease still blocks application.
- Worker authority remains bound to the canonical placement/turn claim.

## Evidence

- Published head `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` integrates GitHub-confirmed current-main conflicts against pinned upstream `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`. Preserves upstream compact delegate-test layout and PR timeout/permission/session-continuation contracts. Production authority changes merged without manual conflict; removed a now-unused moved import and compacted a local parameter name to satisfy changed-file lint. Validation passed: 91 focused authority/identity/delegate tests across five suites (55.731s wrapper), production core types and all three affected test-type shards, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, pinned-main diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets. The newly integrated cron fixture needed a true-or-undefined permission normalization in its test transport only; its affected integration suite and Gateway-method types pass after that correction. Fresh independent scoped review of the frozen production tree found no actionable P0/P1; retained for the final one-line test-adapter correction. No fresh real delayed-human transport proof, replacement-head hosted verdict, or maintainer signed-carrier acceptance is claimed.

- Prior published head `fad89b4b638381fbb5e964c5d0cade97d01b0afc` reconciles a GitHub-confirmed approval-test conflict onto pinned upstream `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d`. Upstream removed a redundant ambient-only parameter case; the later maintained cross-lease wire/ambient approval coverage remains intact. Seventeen patches replay identically; the first differs only in its upstream conflict context. Prior independent review is retained for this mechanical delta, not claimed as fresh review. All 10 local gates passed: 99 tests across five focused suites (56.058s wrapper), production core types, all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods), changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety checks. prs.title: fix(channels): deleting an account leaves its stored inbound events behind
prs.body:
Closes #133658

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw channels remove --channel <channel> --account <id> --delete` leaves every inbound event the account ever queued in the state database forever. The ingress queue prunes itself only when a new event is admitted, and a removed account never admits another.

- **Unreclaimable storage:** up to 4096 completed plus 4096 failed rows per removed account, plus every pending row.
- **A re-added account is not fresh:** under the same id, events whose ids the old account had seen are dropped as duplicates without a trace, and rows still pending are drained — the bot answers messages from before the account was deleted.

This affects every channel: the queue is core-owned, 22 channel plugins open one, none cleans up, and `lifecycle.onAccountRemoved` is implemented by one plugin only, for its own offset cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue and the removal command are both core-owned, so cleanup lives once on the removal path instead of in 22 copies of `onAccountRemoved`.

- **Only a queue whose ownership is proven is discarded.** Queues are opened under the plugin id (`openChannelIngressQueue` forces `channelId: pluginId`), which can differ from the channel id. The owning plugin is resolved from the plugin manifests — the source `channels logs` uses, available without a running Gateway.
- **Shared queues are kept, with a reason.** If one plugin serves several channels, rows cannot be attributed to one of them. That count includes a channel named after the plugin, which manifests do not list: removing it beside one declared sibling, or removing the declared channel while the plugin-id channel is configured, keeps the rows too. Deleting a sibling channel's unanswered events is irreversible; keeping them is today's behavior.
- **Only `--delete` discards.** Disabling keeps rows (re-enabling drains them), and rows for an account merely missing from config stay, as the LINE pre-drain migration intends ("account not currently configured, so these stay queued until it is restored").
- **The discard runs after the config write succeeds**, so a failed write never drops work for a still-configured account.
- **Out of scope:** conversation bindings (they expire) and the pairing allowlist and plugin binding approvals (authorization records).

Known limits:

- If stopping the runtime fails (reported, and the command continues, since no running Gateway is the normal CLI case), a still-live monitor can settle a just-discarded event. A claim-token completion writes nothing; an id-only completion leaves one `completed` tombstone that the next deletion removes. No inbound work is lost.
- The `openclaw configure` wizard deletes through the plugin's `deleteAccount` directly and is not covered; that needs a change to its write ordering.
- Plugins that derive their own account key (WhatsApp hashes the id) are not covered: nothing matches, and the command now says it discarded nothing. Supporting them needs a new callback on the public `ChannelPlugin` config contract — a maintainer decision.

## User Impact

Deleting a channel account now removes its stored events too:

- the storage is released, and an account re-added under the same id starts clean;
- disabling an account is unchanged;
- the `--delete` flag help and the `channels` CLI docs now say it removes stored inbound events.

Discarded unanswered work, including dead letters `channels dead-letters resubmit` could have replayed, is named:

```
Deleted LINE account "default". Discarded 6 stored ingress events, including 2 never answered.
```

Every deletion reports the outcome, even when nothing was discarded:

```
Deleted LINE account "default". Discarded no stored ingress events.
```

A plugin serving several channels keeps the rows and says why:

```
Deleted external-chat account "default". Kept its stored ingress events: plugin "@vendor/external-chat-plugin" serves more than one channel and its stored events do not record which.
```

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: `openclaw channels remove --delete` leaves the removed account's durable ingress rows in `state/openclaw.sqlite` forever, and reports nothing about the inbound events it strands.

Real environment tested: a Gateway and CLI built from this branch on Windows 11, configured with a real LINE channel account whose webhook endpoint is registered with LINE and served over a public HTTPS tunnel. LINE's own servers called that endpoint before the run, so the rows below were written by the real webhook route, real signature verification and the real LINE webhook spool rather than by a test double:

```
$ curl .../v2/bot/channel/webhook/test
{"success": true, "timestamp": "2026-08-31T10:48:12.202563Z", "statusCode": 200, "reason": "OK", "detail": "200"}

# what the tunnel recorded, oldest first (endpoint host redacted)
POST /line/webhook -> 200  ua=LineBotWebhook/2.0        events: []   (LINE's own verification call)
POST /line/webhook -> 200  ua=Python-urllib/3.13        event message id probe-1788173415 text 'ingress removal proof 4'
POST /line/webhook -> 200  ua=Python-urllib/3.13        event message id probe-1788173417 text 'ingress removal proof 5'
POST /line/webhook -> 200  ua=Python-urllib/3.13        event message id probe-1788173418 text 'ingress removal proof 6'
```

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

1. Run the Gateway against a throwaway state directory and deliver six real inbound message events to the registered endpoint.
2. Stop the Gateway mid-drain so one row stays `claimed` and one stays `pending`, and byte-copy the state directory as a seed.
3. Restore that seed byte-for-byte before each run below, so every run starts from the same six rows written by the real webhook route.
4. Before each run, check the build for a string only this revision emits, because the build stamp keys on the git commit and would otherwise report the right version over an older bundle.

Evidence after fix:

```
$ grep -rl "awaiting resubmission" dist/ | head -1
dist/channels-BhVQ4Xor.js

$ python -c "...select queue_name, status, count(*) ... group by 1,2"
  select count(*) from channel_ingress_events; -> 6
  ["line","default"] claimed   1
  ["line","default"] completed 4
  ["line","default"] pending   1

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node dist/index.js channels remove --channel line --account default --delete
Could not stop running LINE account "default" before removing it: Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:3717 (ECONNREFUSED).
Deleted LINE account "default". Discarded 6 stored ingress events, including 2 never answered.

$ python -c "...select count(*) ..."
  select count(*) from channel_ingress_events; -> 0
  configured line accounts -> []

# the same command again, with nothing left to discard
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node dist/index.js channels remove --channel line --account default --delete
Deleted LINE account "default". Discarded no stored ingress events.
```

Observed result after fix:

- The account is gone from config and all six rows are gone with it, in every status the queue can hold.
- The reported count matches the rows that were there, and the `2` named as never answered is exactly the `pending` + `claimed` pair; the four settled rows are not described as lost work.
- No Gateway was running — the ordinary case for a CLI invocation, and the reason the owning plugin is resolved from the plugin manifests rather than from the runtime channel registry, which only Gateway startup populates.

Before evidence: the same seeded state directory, restored byte-for-byte, against a build whose `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` is `origin/main` (confirmed by the fix's own output string being absent from the bundle):

```
$ grep -rl 'of which had not been answered yet' dist/ | wc -l
0

$ python -c "...select ... group by 1,2"
  select count(*) from channel_ingress_events; -> 6
  ["line","default"] claimed   1
  ["line","default"] completed 4
  ["line","default"] pending   1

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node dist/index.js channels remove --channel line --account default --delete
Deleted LINE account "default".

$ python -c "...select ... group by 1,2"
  select count(*) from channel_ingress_events; -> 6
  ["line","default"] claimed   1
  ["line","default"] completed 4
  ["line","default"] pending   1

$ python -c "print(list(json.load(open(config))['channels']['line'].get('accounts', {}) or {}))"
[]
```

The account is removed from config and all six rows survive — including the `pending` and `claimed` rows, which are inbound events that were never answered and now have no account left to answer them.

Additional review: reverting only `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` to `origin/main` and rerunning `src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts` fails 7 of 13, each naming a distinct outcome this change is responsible for (the discard and its count, the dead letter reported as work, the zero-discard line, the resolution under a plugin id that is not the channel id, the shared-queue refusal, and the two failure paths). Restoring it returns 13/13.

```
# with src/commands/channels/remove.ts reverted to origin/main
Tests  7 failed | 6 passed (13)
  × discards the ingress rows a deleted account owned and reports the unanswered ones
  × counts a discarded dead letter as work, not as routine cleanup
  × discards the rows under the plugin id when that is not the channel id
  × keeps the ingress rows when one plugin serves several channels
  × keeps omitted removal on literal default when the plugin selects another default
  × still reports the deletion when the ingress discard fails
  × reports a discard with no unanswered work without calling it lost

# restored
Tests  13 passed (13)
```

Checks run on the exact head:

- `vitest` over `channels.remove` (13) and `ingress-queue.account-purge` (4);
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`, both with no diagnostics;
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the touched source, and `oxfmt --check` on every touched file;
- `check:assertion-safety --base origin/main` and `check:max-lines-ratchet --base origin/main`, both OK;
- no `plugin-sdk` export is added, so the SDK surface budget and API baseline are unchanged.

What was not tested:

- The six inbound events were delivered to the registered endpoint by a local signer using the channel secret rather than typed into a LINE client, because the only LINE client on this host is not signed in. The webhook route, signature verification, spool admission, drain and resulting rows are the product build's; the originator is not. LINE's own verification call in the same session shows the endpoint under test is the one LINE delivers to.
- The shared-queue refusal is covered by unit tests only: no bundled plugin declares more than one channel, so it has no live instance in this tree.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: single-host Windows run against one channel (`line`). The fix is channel-agnostic — it keys on the queue name the core queue builds from the owning plugin's id and the account id — and the unit tests cover a second channel, a second account, and a plugin id that differs from its channel, but no second channel plugin was exercised live.

prs.title: fix(line): honor the configured outbound message length
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where setting `channels.line.textChunkLimit` — the per-message length every other messaging channel accepts, documented as "Maximum characters per outbound message before OpenClaw splits it" — makes the LINE config invalid, so the Gateway will not start.

- Without the setting, LINE replies always split at 5000 characters, and operators cannot ask for shorter bubbles.
- Nothing bounded the value either, so a limit above LINE's cap would make oversized replies fail with HTTP 400 and reach the user as nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

LINE's outbound path already read the setting, but its hand-written schema omitted the key and the inbound reply path used a literal 5000. Now one owner decides:

- `resolveLineTextChunkLimit` reads the channel or account value and caps it at LINE's 5000.
- The schema accepts the key at both levels, like every sibling channel.
- Every chunk decision uses that owner, including core's planning through `resolveEffectiveTextChunkLimit` (the seam Telegram, MS Teams, and SMS use), so core no longer plans at the raw value and leaves the adapter to re-split.
- Unset still means 5000.
- Not touched: per-field caps (Flex `altText`, template text, action labels) and `streaming.chunkMode`.

`textChunkLimit` is an existing cross-channel key, not a new concept. If you'd rather LINE not expose it, the alternative is removing the outbound reader and keeping a fixed 5000 — happy to send that instead.

## User Impact

- `channels.line.textChunkLimit` and `channels.line.accounts.<id>.textChunkLimit` validate and apply to both replies and sends.
- A value above LINE's limit is capped, so the reply still arrives, split.
- Configs without the key behave exactly as today.
- Config surface: two keys, taking `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 3730 to 3732, raised deliberately; `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm check:bundled-channel-config-metadata` pass. No migration is needed: the `.strict()` schema meant no valid config could contain the key.

Limits:

- Over-cap values are clamped **silently** (no warning, doctor rule, or schema max), matching `extensions/msteams` and `extensions/telegram`.
- It applies to prose only; Flex content (code blocks, degraded tables) has its own budget.
- `channels.line.accounts.<id>` applies to sends that name that account, not to `defaultAccount` (shared account-lookup behavior).
- "First five messages ride the reply token" applies only to inbound replies; outbound sends always push.
- The `resolveEffectiveTextChunkLimit` tests call the adapter's own resolver, as Telegram and MS Teams do. Nothing in `src/` asserts the pipeline uses that seam, so the live capture below is the proof that the setting reaches a real send.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: LINE rejects `channels.line.textChunkLimit` at config validation, and every reply chunks at a fixed 5000 regardless of configuration; an over-cap value would lose the whole message to an HTTP 400.

Real environment tested: a live LINE Messaging API channel and a real LINE desktop client sending to the bot, with a gateway built from this branch on an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Ids and hosts below are redacted.

Before evidence:

```
$ openclaw config validate
OpenClaw config is invalid
File: <state>/openclaw.json
Problem:
  - channels.line: invalid config: must not have additional properties: "textChunkLimit"
```

The 5000-character bound is LINE's, confirmed against its own validator rather than assumed:

```
$ POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/message/validate/push   # messages[0].text length 5000
{} HTTP_STATUS=200

$ POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/message/validate/push   # messages[0].text length 5001
{"message":"The request body has 1 error(s)",
 "details":[{"message":"Length must be between 0 and 5000","property":"messages[0].text"}]}
HTTP_STATUS=400
```

An unbounded limit is not a cosmetic problem — a real push of one 6000-character message is refused outright, so the reply reaches the user as nothing:

```
$ POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/message/push            # one text message, 6000 chars
{"message":"The request body has 1 error(s)",
 "details":[{"message":"Length must be between 0 and 5000","property":"messages[0].text"}]}
HTTP_STATUS=400
```

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

1. Set `channels.line.textChunkLimit: 9000` and send the same 6000-character body through the outbound path.
2. Set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.textChunkLimit: 900`, start the gateway, and send `/commands` from a real LINE client.
3. Remove the key, restart, and send `/commands` again as the control.

Evidence after fix — the over-cap limit is bounded and the message is delivered instead of refused:

```
$ openclaw message send --channel line -t line:<redacted> -m "<6000 chars>" --json
{
  "action": "send",
  "channel": "line",
  "payload": {
    "deliveryStatus": "sent",
    "payloadOutcomes": [ { "index": 0, "status": "sent", "resultCount": 2 } ]
  }
}
```

Evidence after fix — core plans with the bounded value instead of double-splitting. With `textChunkLimit: 9000` and a 9500-character body, the same send before and after this change:

```
before (no resolveEffectiveTextChunkLimit): resultCount 3    # 4997, 3989, 512
after:                                      resultCount 2    # 4997, 4502
```

The intermediate 3989-character break is the artifact: core planned at 9000, this adapter re-split each piece at 5000, and the boundary landed where neither layer intended.

Evidence after fix — the inbound reply path, driven by a real LINE client. The webhook that triggered each turn, read back from the tunnel inspector:

```
2026-08-29T23:42:00+08:00 | http 200 | msgId 629459026799493427 | text '/commands'   # textChunkLimit 900
2026-08-29T23:44:04+08:00 | http 200 | msgId 629459232622379162 | text '/commands'   # key removed (control)
```

Observed result after fix:

- With `textChunkLimit: 900`, the `/commands` reply arrives as several LINE messages, ending in a standalone `More: /tools for available capabilities` bubble with its own timestamp.
- With the key removed, the identical reply arrives as one bubble that LINE itself collapses behind its "show more" expander — the pre-change shape, unchanged.

Review finding addressed — inbound replies now chunk at the config live for the event:

- The inbound handler resolved the limit from the config captured when the monitor started, while the turn beside it, and every other consumer in that handler, runs on the per-event config admission supplies. A reload between monitor start and an event let the agent answer under the new limit while its reply was still split at the old one.
- The handler now resolves the limit from `turnConfig`, the invariant the comment directly above it already states.
- The regression test previously passed an empty event config, a state admission never produces; it now carries a limit that differs from the monitor-start one, so only reading the live config satisfies it:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts   # pre-fix
 FAIL  extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts > chunks an inbound reply at the limit live for that event
AssertionError: expected 900 to be 1200 // Object.is equality
      Tests  1 failed | 17 passed (18)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts   # after
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

Additional review:

- The regression tests fail on pre-fix code for the intended reasons: `expected 5000 to be 900` for the reply path, and `expected 9000 to be 5000` for the platform bound.
- `pnpm test extensions/line` is 845 passing across 55 files; both `tsgo` lanes, `check:changed` (including the assertion-safety and max-lines ratchets and the regenerated bundled channel config metadata), and `oxfmt` are clean.
- Production LOC delta: +35/-7 (net +28) — one named owner module replacing four duplicated copies of the literal and one hardcoded bypass, plus the schema and type lines that make the setting expressible; the shape mirrors `extensions/telegram/src/text-chunk-limit.ts`. Tests are +218/-29, the channel doc +6/-1, and the regenerated `bundled-channel-config-metadata` +12/-12.

What was not tested: LINE's other length caps are untouched by this change and were not re-exercised. `streaming.chunkMode` is not read on either LINE path today and this change does not add it.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: LINE has no API that reads back a delivered message, so the per-message split on the reply path is shown by the message boundaries a real client renders plus the `resultCount` the send path reports, rather than by a wire capture of the reply body.

Follow-up not taken here: `lineOutboundAdapter`'s legacy attached `sendMedia` passes its caption straight to `sendMessageLine`, which appends the text unchunked, while the attached `sendText` beside it routes back through `sendPayload`. LINE's message adapter (`lineMessageAdapter.send.media`) takes precedence on every path I could exercise and does route through `sendPayload`, so I could not reach the unbounded branch to demonstrate a defect and did not change delivery on a path I cannot test. It is worth closing by symmetry (the comment above those two already argues the payload owner should record every physical send), and I am happy to send it as its own change.

### After merging main

Merged `origin/main` at `10c00289b59`.

- Conflicts: the generated config baseline, LINE's schema and type beside main's new `replyToMode` and `streaming` keys, the channel doc, and `monitor.lifecycle.test.ts`, whose presentation test main rewrote.
- `quote-reply-delivery.test.ts`, which landed on main in the meantime, stubbed the runtime's `resolveTextChunkLimit`, which this change stops reading; it failed type-checking on the merged tree and would have thrown at runtime. It now relies on the plugin's own 5000 default instead of the stub.
- Main grew `monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` and `channel.sendPayload.test.ts` close enough to the 1000-line lint limit that this change's tests pushed both over it. Those tests now live in their own files, `monitor.text-chunk-limit.test.ts` (on the same harness as main's `monitor.streaming-config.test.ts`) and `text-chunk-limit.test.ts`, and both touched files are back to main's content or below. The moved inbound test still fails the same way when the handler reads the startup config instead of the event's:

```text
× chunks an inbound reply at the limit live for that event
AssertionError: expected 900 to be 1200 // Object.is equality
```

Local checks, Windows 11:

prs.title: fix(macos): resolve typed gateway auth refs
prs.body:
Closes #128171

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app could not authenticate to a local Gateway when `gateway.auth.token` or `gateway.auth.password` used a typed env SecretRef. The Gateway supports those inputs, but the native endpoint store previously handled only strings.

## What Changed

- Resolve supported typed env SecretRefs from the actual Gateway LaunchAgent environment, with the app environment as fallback.
- Enforce the configured env provider and allowlist; malformed, unsupported, denied, or unresolved refs fail closed.
- Keep configured refs authoritative over same-surface ambient fallbacks.
- Match Core's implicit-mode behavior: two configured token/password inputs remain ambiguous; a concrete opposite-side fallback suppresses typed-ref materialization; after materialization, password is inferred before token.
- Match Core startup when a typed local password coexists with `gateway.remote.token`: the local password wins unless an ambient Gateway token causes Core to leave that password ref inactive; when token auth is active, preserve LaunchAgent-token precedence before the remote-token fallback.
- Pass only the selected credential into the native Gateway handshake.

## User Impact

Users can keep local Gateway credentials in supported typed environment SecretRefs without breaking the macOS app connection. Invalid or disallowed references remain fail-closed, and the native app follows the same token/password selection behavior as Core.

## Evidence

### Evidence status refresh — 2026-10-27

Current head remains `c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513`. The [completed CI run 39411875583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) succeeded on tested merge `44577cf085aada61cbbfb40cbbd236c63a28518a`, combining this head with main `d8c96213c5cf40295863fb5fb6d347e1f9caf6b7`. Its unique job inventory contains **5 successful and 37 skipped jobs**, with no failures or pending jobs. These are this run's jobs, not a sum of duplicate check/status surfaces; skipped jobs are not passing runtime proof.

The [exact delta since reviewed head ff41c754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/ff41c754d9d4aa8a70bf2da9422ade5047d11c9c...c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513) changes only the endpoint source and its test file. `configuredInput` now classifies trimmed shorthand through `envSecretRefName` before auth-surface selection, and the existing handshake matrix adds both `$GW_PASSWORD` and `${GW_PASSWORD}` with the available service token. This addresses the source change requested by the earlier P1 finding and preserves the original shorthand/fallback intent. It is a source disposition, not a new exact-head ClawSweeper verdict or packaged-app result.

The [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128175#issuecomment-5385443900) explicitly says maintaining Swift/Core parity alone does not require another product decision. Earlier parity-approval language below records historical status and is superseded on that point. Maintainer acceptance remains outstanding. **Packaged-app proof for the later remote-fallback combinations and a stable-release upgrade retaining existing shorthand settings remain unproven.** The beta2-port test evidence below is not relabeled as current-head packaged-app proof. Earlier pending-CI statements are historical and superseded only by the completed run identified here. No new runtime test, whole-current-tree review, or upgrade demonstration is claimed by this refresh.


### Current follow-up — 2026-10-20

Current head: [c17b72d353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513).

- Classify the existing `$NAME` and `${NAME}` shorthand forms as references before implicit auth-mode selection. A missing password reference no longer suppresses an available service token. Explicit modes and malformed or literal values keep their existing paths.
- The two-file follow-up passed scoped P0–P3 Codex review with no actionable findings. This is source review, not runtime proof.
- The equivalent fix was compiled in the beta2 native integration. Its 13 credential-test functions passed in a deny-default OS sandbox, including the handshake matrix with both new shorthand cases. Strict SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. This is synthetic proof of the beta2 port, not an exact-head packaged-app run or real Keychain, GUI, identity, or upgrade proof.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) started automatically after the push; no completed verdict is claimed here. Maintainer parity and acceptance decisions remain open.

### Historical candidate evidence

Current PR candidate: `1ad4bcb852b2266950eea45c077ee023e1a42358`, merged with current `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `1e13fc8abcd942ca398a89ca5560da11a1d46c41`. GitHub confirms the PR is OPEN and the head/base match those revisions. The branch is `MERGEABLE` (no content conflict), but the merge state is BLOCKED by required CI. The PR delta against current main is limited to `GatewayEndpointStore.swift` and `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` (+118/-8 production, +477/-1 tests).

- The prior exact-head CI run found a SwiftFormat `conditionalAssignment` style error before compilation. The follow-up changes only the expression form and is being validated in current-head CI.
- Scoped Codex autoreview on this exact head returned `scoped-clean` at P2 with no findings (confidence 0.76). Its report used the selected diff and supplied Core auth sources; it does not claim runtime verification. The report is preserved in the task-local review artifacts.
- ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and reported no actionable code or security findings. It marked merge blocked pending the macOS auth owner's decision on the ongoing Swift/Core credential-selection parity contract, and notes there is no fresh packaged-app runtime demonstration for the remote-token fallback.
- Exact-head GitHub CI run [36282160728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282160728) completed with the `macos-swift (tests)` job cancelled while its Swift test step was running; no Swift test result is available. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failed solely because the selected `macos-swift` check was cancelled. Preflight, `security-fast`, `native-i18n`, all three macOS Node shards, Swift lint, `macos-swift (packages)`, shared OpenClawKit scans, macOS Periphery, OpenGrep, actionlint, changed-path scan, and security review passed. The iOS Periphery scan was skipped by scope.
- A rerun was requested for the cancelled job, but GitHub refused it with `Must have admin rights to Repository`. The Swift test verdict and aggregate CI gate therefore require a repository admin to rerun.
- `git diff --check` passes. This Windows host has no Swift toolchain, so native Swift execution relies on exact-head GitHub CI.
- The app-to-Gateway runtime proof below was performed on the earlier candidate `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`. It is historical evidence and does not demonstrate the added remote-token fallback cases on the current candidate.

Native validation on 2026-09-04:

Validated candidate: `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`.

The main refresh preserves @TheAngryPit's original repair, @CassieMei's carried
auth-mode and precedence corrections, and all five contributor commits. Its sole
content conflict was two independent insertions in the endpoint store; both the
typed-reference resolver and main's source-snapshot helper are retained.

### Before

[Native baseline run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33910257814)
used unchanged production main `606d9ab82afdb28ebaad33896e41811b96ad87c7`.
The actual ad-hoc packaged app sent no token for a supported typed custom env
reference that the healthy managed local Gateway could resolve. It received
`token_missing`. A fresh literal-token control authenticated as `openclaw-macos`
and completed `config.get`.

### After

[Exact-candidate native run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33916513675)
reconstructed and checked the exact candidate tree/commit, verified its signature,
built the real app through the normal package script, and installed each real
local service through `gateway install --wrapper`. The wrapper supplied normal
diagnostics and, only in the app-env fallback cases, the service's synthetic env
value. Every case used fresh synthetic profile/pairing state.

| Cases | Native result |
| --- | --- |
| Service-only typed token and password | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |
| Different app/service values for one ref, both modes | Service value selected; completed `config.get` |
| Supported app-env fallback, both modes | Service snapshot lacks the ref value; completed `config.get` |
| Explicit modes with inactive opposite refs | Correct active credential; completed `config.get` |
| Typed token + ambient password; typed password + ambient token | Same password/token selection as Core; completed `config.get` |
| Denied and unresolved active refs, both modes | No credential sent despite a valid ambient fallback; no protected request completed |
| All four rejected setups corrected and relaunched | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |

The protocol evidence correlates `openclaw-macos`, mode `ui`, to successful
protected responses on the same connections. Separate Control UI traffic is not
used as a substitute. Rejected-ref probes kept the server healthy with the
existing reload-off option; no auth or pairing policy was relaxed. The corrected
setups connect normally.

- `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`: 83 tests passed on the exact candidate, including
  provider/allowlist rules, handshake auth, legacy strings and lifecycle siblings.
- All 14 managed services were uninstalled/unloaded, all app phases stopped, and
  all synthetic Keychains were deleted successfully.
- The earlier obscured screenshots are not counted as visual auth evidence.
- Native proof does not replace the fresh independent review or required PR CI.

### Prior ClawSweeper finding and current scope

The fresh ClawSweeper finding was checked against Gateway startup at the exact
Core revision it reviewed. Startup's `hasGatewayTokenCandidate` excludes
`gateway.remote.token`, so a typed local password ref is materialized when no
ambient/local token candidate suppresses it; after materialization Core infers
password mode before token. The native selector and connect-frame regression
now preserve that password. If an ambient Gateway token is present, Core leaves
the password ref inactive and the native selector uses the token surface.

Against current main, the production delta is +118/-8 and the test delta is
+477/-1. The added native code
implements the existing typed-env contract; it adds no configuration option,
policy, schema, remote-auth behavior, or file/exec/store-ref support. Keep the
native/Core parity cases aligned when the shared auth contract changes.

The material below is retained contributor history at its stated inputs, not a
replacement for this current baseline and exact-candidate proof.

## Historical contributor evidence

Historical contributor head: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`

The native proof was built from the exact two-file PR patch (`patch-id 7040be749e604bbda4f9be0b44ed15605a058bd9`) over frozen base `9d79bf3f8c5f18f7c35d028d57402f5085659640`.

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` — 75/75 passed on Apple Silicon macOS.
- SwiftFormat with `config/swiftformat` — 0/2 files require formatting.
- SwiftLint 0.65.1 with `config/swiftlint.yml` — 0 violations.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full ad-hoc `OpenClaw.app` package build completed; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed.
- Real isolated app-to-Gateway proof passed on port 19791: the Gateway service and app process received different synthetic values for the same typed token ref; the app selected the Gateway service value, authenticated, and completed a real `config.get` response.
- Both isolated proof PIDs stopped afterward; the installed app remained running and no operator Gateway, config, Keychain, or PortGuardian state was changed.

### Review finding and vanilla verification

ClawSweeper correctly identified that the previous selector returned no credential for mixed typed-ref/ambient cases. Before changing it, the current Core Gateway was exercised directly in two isolated profiles:

- typed token ref + ambient password: Core marked the typed token surface inactive and started with password auth;
- typed password ref + ambient token: Core marked the typed password surface inactive and started with token auth.

The native selector and regression expectations now reproduce those observed Core outcomes rather than introducing an independent token/password policy.

### Fail-before evidence

- The original typed-ref handshake cases failed before the SecretRef implementation.
- Active-mode regression cases failed before mode filtering.
- The service-vs-app conflict initially selected the stale app value before LaunchAgent precedence was corrected.
- The two mixed inferred-mode cases returned no credential before `4e35b1caf03`; both now match the isolated Core runtime outcomes.

## Historical current-main revalidation (2026-09-03)

- Current `openclaw/openclaw:main`: `9d6f5d218884b00a50746353c40170f5ab46e4db`.
- Exact PR head preserved: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/remotes/audit/pr128175` completed cleanly.
- The change is not superseded: current main resolves literal strings and legacy `$ENV`/`${ENV}` string forms, but still lacks the typed SecretRef object flow and matching credential-selection semantics covered by this PR.
- Current product checks are complete. The earlier red `PR context and evidence` result was caused by malformed heading presentation; this body restores the authored sections explicitly.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, and review this change. The final diff and proof were inspected against current Core behavior.

prs.title: fix(line): a reply is lost or duplicated when a crash interrupts its delivery
prs.body:
Closes #86012
Related: #124464 (push-level retry, merged), #102279 (reply-token window)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a LINE reply is lost if OpenClaw stops (crash, kill during deploy, host reboot) after LINE accepts it but before the delivery queue records that. On restart, recovery cannot tell what happened, refuses to replay blind, and dead-letters it: the user got the answer, but OpenClaw reports a failure. Simply replaying instead would deliver the already-accepted parts a second time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal: after such a crash, the user sees the reply exactly once, however many messages it was split into. Two pieces were missing.

**1. The adapter never told core it had started sending.** `lineOutboundAdapter.sendPayload` picks only the fields it renders from, so the durable-send seam core puts on the context (`deliveryQueueId`, part coordinates, `onPlatformSendDispatch`) never reached the push. The message adapter is now built with the SDK's `createChannelMessageAdapterFromOutbound`, which forwards the whole context, as Matrix does.

**2. Recovery could not reproduce what was sent.** LINE deduplicates pushes by `X-Line-Retry-Key`, so a replay is safe only with the same keys and the same requests; rendering the reply again could split it differently and move content behind a key LINE already answered. Before a part's first push, the retry key and exact message array of every push in that part are written to plugin blob storage (`durable-send-plan.ts`, the same shape as `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/delivery-plan.ts`). Reconciliation reissues those recorded requests: accepted pushes answer 409 with their original receipt, and pushes the interrupted run never reached are sent now. To record a part whole, `sendPayload` now plans every push before sending any of them, so all pushes leave through `pushMessagesLine` and the four per-type push wrappers it no longer reaches are removed.

Safety properties:

- A part's record is written once (`registerIfAbsent`); later attempts reuse it. A record for another recipient, account or part count is refused, and a delivery missing a recorded part is refused rather than settled.
- The record is written before the dispatch marker, so reconciling a delivery with no record means it went out under random keys (core withheld the queue id); it is refused, not replayed.
- The 24-hour retry-key window is measured from the recorded first dispatch and checked before every request, retries included; past it the send is refused.
- Only a 400 reads as "never sent"; 401/403 refuse today's credentials and stay unresolved.
- If the store will not take a record (the namespace is `reject-new` at 10,000 rows), the part fails with `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` before anything reaches LINE, so core may retry it safely. Matrix fails the same way.
- Records are cleared on commit or terminal retirement, otherwise after 25 hours.

The adapter opts in with `automaticUnknownSendReconciliation`, like Matrix, so every single-payload queued LINE send is covered without each caller asking. Replies sent with a reply token, and replies with media or LINE rich content, keep the inline path. A crash *between* parts leaves the later part unrecorded, so that delivery is refused (visible, never duplicated); Matrix draws the same line.

`createDispatchOnce` in `outbound.ts` matches `extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.ts`; plugins cannot import each other, so sharing it would go through the Plugin SDK.

### Storage checkpoint

| Item | This PR |
|---|---|
| Owner and lifecycle | LINE plugin blob namespace `outbound-send-plans` (`plugin_blob_entries`). Written once per part before its first push, read only by LINE's reconciler, deleted on `afterCommit` / `afterUnknownSendTerminal`, otherwise by TTL. |
| Canonical vs derived | Canonical: the normalized request each push asked of LINE. Retry keys are derived from the queue id and stored beside it. |
| Schema, upgrade, downgrade | No schema change; records are `version: 1` and a record that does not parse is refused. Downgrade, upgrade and restore: R2–R4. |
| Retention | 25 h TTL; `reject-new` at 10,000 rows, 1 MiB per row, 64 MiB total; never evicted. Backups drop the rows with the queue (`sanitizeOpenClawGlobalStateSnapshot`). |
| Concurrency | Atomic claim; a replay never rewrites a record. |
| Rollback | Revert. The older build has no reconciler, so a pending recorded delivery fails closed (R2). |

## User Impact

- A reply LINE accepted before a crash resolves as delivered on restart instead of being dead-lettered, and the recipient sees it once, even when split into several messages.
- Anything that cannot be reconstructed safely still fails closed: never a duplicate to avoid a loss.
- If config or the version changes across the crash, recovery still sends exactly what was recorded.
- A full plan store makes the affected send fail as not sent instead of going out without crash recovery.
- Reply-token delivery, rich/media replies and the request shape of captioned media sends are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Live runs on the current head (`24a584c830c`)

A Gateway built from this head (clean tree, build stamp for the same commit) on an isolated state dir and a private port, against the real LINE Messaging API on a throwaway test channel:

- The inbound turn is a self-signed LINE webhook event. The model is a local stand-in whose first round calls a tool, so the tool-status notice spends the reply path and the final reply takes the durable queue.
- An `--import` preload wraps the runtime's undici `fetch`: it records every push on the wire and `SIGKILL`s the Gateway the moment LINE answers the final push.
- What reached the recipient is read off LINE's `GET /v2/bot/message/quota/consumption`, which a 409 does not increment.
- These ran on Windows. Current `main` cannot finish any agent turn there: `cloneEnvWithPlatformSemantics` returns a `Proxy` on win32 that worker `postMessage` refuses to clone (#157067; #157348 fixes one of the call sites). The proof build therefore carries one extra, proof-only commit that makes that function return the plain clone it already returns on Linux and macOS, gated by an env var the runs set. It touches nothing in LINE and is not part of this PR.

**R5. A crash replayed as recorded.** Killed right after LINE accepted the final reply, then restarted once the crashed owner's 60-second claim lapsed:

```
push 200  X-Line-Retry-Key c5cd1081-288a-4edb-a873-f0660a3e55cb  "📊 Session Status"                      id 633372440373756221
push 200  X-Line-Retry-Key 2ed8712c-3dc8-366d-b4ad-c2a85bc367e7  "<marker> FINAL answer delivered …"      id 633372440860295637  -> SIGKILL
quota 120 -> 122
queue  status=pending  recovery_state=send_attempt_started
plan   1 row, 363 bytes, expires_at - created_at = 25 h

restart:
[delivery-recovery] Delivery entry b10e9a34-c619-481c-89b5-edac3daa9d98 reconciled unknown_after_send as already sent
[delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
push 409  X-Line-Retry-Key 2ed8712c-3dc8-366d-b4ad-c2a85bc367e7  "<marker> FINAL answer delivered …"      id 633372440860295637
quota 122 -> 122      queue after: empty      plan after: empty

sha256("line:push-retry-key:b10e9a34-c619-481c-89b5-edac3daa9d98:0:0") -> 2ed8712c-3dc8-366d-b4ad-c2a85bc367e7 (matches the wire)
```

The tool-status notice went out under a random key: it is not a queued send. The final reply was replayed under its recorded key, LINE answered 409 with the original message id, and the recipient has one copy.

**R1. The plan store refuses the record.** The namespace was pre-filled to its 10,000-row limit before the turn:

```
push 200  X-Line-Retry-Key f5293e93-dddb-4a2c-8a15-587bc5b9ec94  "📊 Session Status"   id 633372741323981092
[line] final reply failed: OutboundDeliveryError: Plugin blob namespace reached its stored row limit. | PLUGIN_BLOB_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
[delivery-recovery] Outbound delivery retry: entry 79dfdcbd-f021-4f6b-a519-d405cd18b3c9 not ready for retry yet — backoff 2452ms remaining
quota 122 -> 123   (the notice only)
queue  status=pending  retry_count=1  platform_send_started_at=null
       last_error: … | OPENCLAW_PLATFORM_MESSAGE_NOT_DISPATCHED | PLUGIN_BLOB_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
plan   10,000 rows (the fillers; nothing recorded)
```

No push for the final reply reached LINE, the dispatch marker was never written, and core holds the entry as not sent and retries it.

### Earlier heads (code paths unchanged since)

These ran on macOS against the merge-base `main` build `441435b5066`; the record format and the no-record refusal they exercise are unchanged on this head.

**R2. Downgrade with a recorded reply pending** (`8719a8b`). `main` started on this branch's crashed state:

```
[delivery-recovery] Delivery entry 204ce991-… delivery state is send_attempt_started; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
pushes during recovery: 0      quota 101 -> 101      queue status=failed  recovery_state=completed_permanent
plan still there (main never reads the namespace); it expires with its TTL
```

**R3. Upgrade with a reply pending from `main`** (`8719a8b`). This branch started on `main`'s crashed state, whose push used a random key:

```
[delivery-recovery] Delivery entry 35fd8698-… delivery state is send_attempt_started and reconciliation is unresolved: LINE delivery carried no durable record, so a replay could not be deduplicated
pushes during recovery: 0      quota 103 -> 103      queue status=failed  recovery_state=completed_permanent
```

**R4. Backup and restore with a recorded reply pending** (`8719a8b`). `openclaw backup create` / `backup restore` into a fresh directory: the restored state has 0 queue rows and 0 plan rows, recovery sends nothing, quota 107 -> 107 (`sanitizeOpenClawGlobalStateSnapshot` drops both).

**Multi-part reply, two processes** (August head). A reply split into two parts, killed after the second push was accepted; recovery in a new process replayed both recorded keys and LINE answered 409 to each (`627847068748087869`, `627847069318513220`): two messages on the device, not four.

### Regression coverage

`extensions/line/src/outbound-reconcile.test.ts` drives the real push path with a stubbed transport, so the plan is written by production code:

```
 ✓ reissues every recorded push under the key LINE deduplicated it by
 ✓ returns the identity of every replayed push, not just the last of each part
 ✓ marks the platform dispatch once, before the first push of a fanned-out part
 ✓ refuses a delivery that carried no durable record instead of replaying it
 ✓ records the pushes a crash never reached, so the replay can deliver them
 ✓ keeps the whole recorded fan-out after a replay that is itself interrupted
 ✓ replays what was recorded when the same delivery now renders differently
 ✓ records the quote with the request, so a replay still quotes the answered message
 ✓ re-records a part whose previous plan has expired
 ✓ refuses a claim whose stored plan describes a different fan-out
 ✓ refuses a claim whose stored plan names a different recipient
 ✓ refuses a claim whose stored plan names a different account
 ✓ refuses to replay when a planned part was never dispatched
 ✓ measures the window from the recorded dispatch, not the refreshed queue entry
 ✓ stops a replay whose backoff outlives the retry-key window
 ✓ sends nothing when the plan store will not take the record
 ✓ reissues a recorded request exactly as stored, without normalizing it again
 ✓ keeps a replay refused for its credentials unresolved instead of claiming nothing landed
 ✓ keeps a rejection after an accepted push unresolved instead of claiming nothing landed
 ✓ drops recorded content once the delivery is settled
```

Each guard was removed alone to check that the matching test turns red: each of the three claim-identity fields fails only its own claim test; rethrowing a recording failure unwrapped fails `sends nothing when the plan store will not take the record` and the fan-out claim test, and marking every recording failure retryable fails the fan-out claim test alone; dropping the expiry sweep before the claim fails `re-records a part whose previous plan has expired`. `main`'s handoff suite (`outbound.handoff.test.ts`) passes on this branch; removing the handoff `authorize` from the push fails 9 of its tests, and making the revalidation async fails `starts the request in the same turn as a synchronous authorization`.

### Verification

On `24a584c830c`: both tsgo lanes, `pnpm lint:extensions`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against `origin/main`, `oxfmt --check`, `docs:check-mdx` and `lint:docs` pass. The LINE suite passes except `bot-message-context.test.ts`, whose 50 failures here are all Windows `EBUSY` while unlinking SQLite files at teardown; that file is not touched by this PR.

prs.title: fix(agents): prefer write/edit tools over heredocs to prevent literal-newline corruption
prs.body:
Fixes #114128

## What Problem This Solves

Agents writing multi-line Python via unquoted heredocs (`<<EOF`) or `bash -c` corrupt `\n` into literal backslash-n. This compiles-fails silently and can rot for weeks before discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec description now prefers dedicated file-writing tools over shell heredocs or `bash -c` for multi-line content, and names only the tools that survived filtering (`write`, `edit`, and/or `apply_patch`). A write-only session is told to prefer `write`, not the unavailable siblings. Tool permissions are not widened.

## User Impact

When a dedicated file-writing tool is available, agents are steered to that tool instead of a shell heredoc, so multiline files keep real newline bytes. Sessions that do not have those tools are not told to call them.

## Evidence

Live proof on `401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222`, using the production tool finalizer plus the real exec and write tools (`--pool=forks`).

Exec-only session omits the guidance. With only `write` available, the description names `write` and the selected file tool is `write`. The real exec tool ran the historical unquoted heredoc and left literal backslash-n bytes (`5c6e`). The real write tool wrote the same intended Python and the file bytes contain newline bytes (`0a`) and match the requested content.

```
HEAD 401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222
EXEC_ONLY_HAS_FILE_WRITES false
EXEC_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
WRITE_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. File writes: prefer dedicated file-writing tools (write) over shell heredocs or bash -c for multi-line content. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
SELECTED_FILE_TOOLS write
HEREDOC_EXEC_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"(no output)"}]
HEREDOC_FILE_REPR "def greet():\\n    return \"ok\"\\n\n"
HEREDOC_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a5c6e2020202072657475726e20226f6b225c6e0a
WRITE_TOOL_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"Successfully wrote 29 bytes to /home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-w5SDu1/oc-117274-proof-E6H7A1/write.py"}]
WRITE_FILE_REPR "def greet():\n    return \"ok\"\n"
WRITE_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a0a2020202072657475726e20226f6b220a
WRITE_CONTAINS_NEWLINE_BYTE true
WRITE_MATCHES_INTENDED true
```

`src/agents/bash-tools.descriptions.test.ts`: 5 passed, including write-only, edit-only, and partial sets. `src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`: 12 passed.

Previous CI on `7bdf478a` failed `checks-node-changed-compact-large-12` (`AssertionError: expected 'blocked' to match object { state: 'reclaimed' }` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-reclaim.test.ts`) and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7` (`ENOENT` for `dist/index.js` in `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`). Neither file is in this diff.

AI-assisted: yes (OpenClaw subagent).

prs.title: fix(signal): align autoStart daemon bind with local connection URL port
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Signal is configured with a managed-native connection URL on a non-default port (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8082`) and `httpPort` is omitted, OpenClaw bound the autoStart signal-cli daemon to the default port 8080 while the client probed 8082. Config validation succeeded, so the daemon and the readiness URL diverged.

A URL-only local HTTP endpoint with no path prefix is the provisional bind. If that port is free, the daemon binds it and the probe uses the same URL. If another account already reserved it, fallback allocation rewrites that bind-aligned URL to the port that was actually assigned. Remote hosts, HTTPS, path prefixes, and cross-family addresses stay independent connection endpoints. An explicit `httpPort` wins over a divergent URL. Doctor migration uses the same allocation instead of a second copy of the rule.

Ref #116165

## Evidence

Exact-head production autoStart on `d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e` (parent `e5b62e7c791427a300d0049d33918501605f1a80`). macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0, build 25G83), Node v26.10.0. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` under `/var/folders` (not `~/.openclaw`). Production `monitorSignalProvider` resolved the account, then `spawnSignalDaemon` started a local HTTP stand-in. That stand-in records `daemon --http host:port` and answers `GET /api/v1/check` with 204 only on the bound port. The path-prefix case also runs a separate proxy on 8082 that answers only `/signal/api/v1/check`.

```console
$ sw_vers
ProductName: macOS
ProductVersion: 26.6.2
BuildVersion: 25G83
$ node -v
v26.10.0
$ git rev-parse HEAD
d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e
$ PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD) ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-116176-autostart.mts
HEAD d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-state-XCm1lt
HOME /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-home-4bF9YS
free_url_only argv daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8082 --no-receive-stdout
free_url_only request /api/v1/check
collision_fallback argv -a +10000000002 daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080 --no-receive-stdout
collision_fallback request /api/v1/check
path_prefix_proxy argv daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080 --no-receive-stdout
path_prefix_proxy proxy /signal/api/v1/check
path_prefix_proxy proxy /signal/api/v1/check
PROOF_OK bind_and_probe_aligned
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Managed-native Signal autoStart keeps the daemon `--http` argument and the readiness URL on the same port. A free URL-only `http://127.0.0.1:8082` binds and probes 8082. When a sibling local endpoint already reserves 8082, fallback binds and probes the allocated port (here 8080) and rewrites the URL. A path-prefixed `http://127.0.0.1:8082/signal` stays on that proxy while the daemon binds 8080.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0, build 25G83), Node v26.10.0, OpenClaw worktree `/tmp/oc-116176` at head `d6c1fa9452cbffdbb7e9bd12b082519a54c7618e` on `e5b62e7c791427a300d0049d33918501605f1a80`. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` `/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-116176-state-XCm1lt`. Isolated `HOME`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  Step 1: frozen install in `/tmp/oc-116176` at `d6c1fa9452c`.

  Step 2: production `monitorSignalProvider` for a free URL-only port, a sibling reservation of that port, and a path-prefixed proxy.

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-116176
  CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD) ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-116176-autostart.mts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above. Free URL-only spawned `daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8082` and the readiness request was `GET /api/v1/check` on that process. With 8082 reserved by a sibling external endpoint, the managed account spawned `daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080` and the readiness request hit that same process. The path-prefixed URL stayed on the proxy (`proxy /signal/api/v1/check`) while the daemon argv was `--http 127.0.0.1:8080`.
- **Observed result after fix:** Daemon bind argv and the readiness URL stay on one port for a free URL-only local HTTP endpoint and for fallback after that port is reserved. A path-prefixed proxy URL is not used as the daemon bind.
- **What was not tested:** A registered signal-cli with a real phone number. Two live signal-cli processes at the same time.

## Summary

- Prefer a local connection URL port when `httpPort` is omitted and the URL has no path prefix
- On a reserved preferred port, rewrite the bind-aligned URL to the allocated port
- Remote, HTTPS, path-prefixed, and cross-family URLs stay independent
- Explicit `httpPort` wins over a divergent URL
- Doctor migration uses the same allocation
- Production autoStart transcript: resolver, daemon `--http`, readiness, including collision and a path-prefixed proxy

## Test plan

- [x] Single URL-only `http://127.0.0.1:8082`
- [x] Two URL-only managed accounts sharing 8082
- [x] Sibling local endpoint reserving 8082, fallback bind and probe aligned
- [x] Path-prefixed `http://127.0.0.1:8082/signal` stays independent
- [x] Remote, HTTPS, and cross-family URLs stay independent
- [x] Explicit `httpPort` precedence
- [x] Doctor legacy `httpUrl` migration, including a reserved 8082 rewrite

prs.title: fix(openai): drop transient reasoning replay state
prs.body:
Closes #113868

## What Problem This Solves

Native Codex Responses can emit temporary reasoning items whose IDs start with `rs_tmp_`. OpenClaw persisted those items in assistant `thinkingSignature` fields and replayed them on later turns even though the IDs are not durable replay state. A follow-up request could then fail with `invalid_encrypted_content`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This current-main rewrite places the rule at the two canonical owners:

- the stream writer keeps the human-readable reasoning summary but omits replay signature and provenance metadata for temporary native Codex reasoning;
- the consolidated replay converter drops matching signatures already present in older transcripts and clears adjacency state, so a later signed text item cannot inherit pairing from an earlier stable reasoning item.

The check is intentionally limited to the native Codex Responses backend. Stable `rs_*` items and temporary-shaped IDs from compatible proxy endpoints retain the existing behavior.

The old branch changed a duplicate provider conversion path that was later consolidated by #123762. This rewrite removes that obsolete surface instead of rebasing it.

## User Impact

Multi-turn native Codex Responses sessions no longer carry temporary encrypted reasoning state into later requests. Visible reasoning summaries and valid stable reasoning replay remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact head: `d54dd8160fa40ac3d090502891ebf5ef6ac170de`, based on current `upstream/main` `ed6e3aabf0`.

- Pre-fix owner regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts` failed in exactly two places: native `rs_tmp_*` state was persisted, and the same item was replayed after a stable reasoning item. Stable native reasoning and proxy behavior passed.
- Exact-head focused and sibling tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-parity.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-prompt-role.test.ts src/agents/openai-responses.reasoning-replay.test.ts` -> 43/43 passed.
- Both consolidated replay facades are covered by the stable -> temporary -> signed-text ordering regression. The temporary item is absent and the text ID is not replayed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware ...` -> passed for all three changed files.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` -> passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts` -> 0 runtime value cycles.
- Scope: two production files, +25/-5 (net +20), plus one focused 161-line test file. The previous implementation was four files with production net +39 and edited an owner removed by #123762.

Direct dependency-contract check:

- OpenAI Codex source at `90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d` models reasoning as a first-class Responses item carrying an optional provider item ID and encrypted content: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L950-L999
- Server item IDs are deliberately read as opaque/permissive values: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/response_item_id.rs#L17-L34
- Codex forwards reasoning items as model request input rather than normalizing their provider lifetime: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/core/src/client_common.rs#L53-L90
- The OpenAI Responses contract documents encrypted reasoning as state to replay for stateless multi-turn use, which is why excluding only observed temporary native items must happen before persistence/replay: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create

Known proof gap: this machine does not yet have a redacted exact-head two-turn native provider trace showing a real `rs_tmp_*` response followed by a request that omits it. No live-provider claim is made. No additional AutoReview was run.

prs.title: fix(ui): judge composer model availability by the session's selected runtime
prs.body:
Related: #186358. This PR fixes the composer's runtime-blind credential banner. The "selection does not take effect" part of the report is not changed here (see Not covered).

## What Problem This Solves

A model can have several runtime routes, for example the OpenClaw API route plus a native `claude-cli` route. When the session runs that model on its selected runtime (`claude-cli`, authenticated through `claude auth login`), the composer still decides availability from the base catalog route. If that base route has no OpenClaw-stored Anthropic credential (`unavailableReason: "missing-auth"`), the composer shows "No provider credential is configured for this model. Set it up in Model Setup." even though the selected native route is available and its turns succeed.

## User Impact

With a native Claude CLI login and no OpenClaw Anthropic profile, a session running a Claude model on the Claude CLI route no longer shows the false "No provider credential" banner. Sessions on the base route without a credential still show it, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveChatModelUnavailableReason` (in `ui/src/lib/chat/model-select-state.ts`) only read each catalog entry's top-level `available` / `unavailableReason`. It now takes the session's selected runtime and projects every matching entry through the existing `resolveModelRuntimeEntry`, which the model picker already uses. That gives the per-runtime availability, so the selected `runtimeChoices[]` entry decides. The composer (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-setup.ts`) passes `activeSession.agentRuntime.id`. Without a selected runtime, or when the runtime is not one of the entry's choices, the previous base-route behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Tests

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-setup.test.ts` has a new case, "uses the session's selected runtime for the credential banner". The catalog entry has a base route that is `missing-auth` and a `claude-cli` runtime choice that is available.

- Session runtime `claude-cli`: no banner. This fails on main, which shows "No provider credential…", and passes on this branch.
- Session runtime `openclaw`, or none: the banner is still shown. This control passes on both.

`chat-model-setup.test.ts` and `model-select-state.test.ts` pass 54/54.

Checks run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` and `git diff --check` are clean.

### Live run

### Live run (Windows 11, Chromium)

This is the real Control UI (`scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts`, Vite dev build) in Chromium. For this run only, the mock was patched locally, and that patch is not part of this PR:

- Catalog entry `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`: base route `available: false, unavailableReason: "missing-auth"`, and runtime choice `claude-cli` `available: true`.
- The main session runs that model with `agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`, and for the control with `openclaw`.

Only the session runtime and this PR's two UI files differ between panels.

![live run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186358/proof-186358.png)

| | main, runtime `claude-cli` | this branch, runtime `claude-cli` | this branch, runtime `openclaw` (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| "No provider credential is configured for this model…" banner | **shown** | **not shown** | shown (that route has no credential) |

### Not covered

- A real Claude CLI login. This machine has no Claude Code install, so the catalog shape is taken from the source-level analysis in the issue review.
- The reported picker selection that "does not take effect", which may involve the session patch path. That part is not changed here.

prs.title: perf(ai): reuse frozen Responses history conversions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Responses requests repeatedly convert unchanged completed history, including tool arguments and results, on each turn.

## User Impact

Reduces request preparation CPU and allocation without changing provider input bytes. Anthropic is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve unchanged frozen transcript identities through replay transforms and memoize their per-message Responses projection. The converter owns weak source keys and a bounded set of option/position variants; replay route/session/account fences remain in the key, and delivery ordering remains request-local. Mutable or shallow-frozen messages still convert afresh.

Payload hooks retain detached, editable containers while sharing scalar strings. Image-bearing messages deliberately stay with the existing image-preparation cache: caching their composed data URLs doubled retained image strings in the first candidate. Strict endpoint status removal now creates the request's own item instead of mutating cached history.

Production code grows by 112 lines: the cache/complete key, frozen eligibility port, and hook mutation contract require that growth. It replaces repeated conversion rather than adding a competing converter. Prompt-cache history policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

Predeclared acceptance: identical provider bytes; consistent CPU/allocation reduction on frozen 40/150-message histories, with and without payload hooks; no controlled material GC regression. Five CPU-swapped pairs per workload, 3,000 requests per arm; allocation sampled in separate passes. Synthetic Linux benchmark includes real transport transformation, request construction and image sanitation; it does not call a model or load a production Gateway.

| Frozen history, payload hook enabled | Base | Candidate | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 40 messages: main-thread CPU/request | 73.09 µs | 57.65 µs | −21.1% |
| 40 messages: allocation/request | 157,555 B | 110,491 B | −29.9% |
| 150 messages: main-thread CPU/request | 234.86 µs | 180.57 µs | −23.1% |
| 150 messages: allocation/request | 532,750 B | 361,805 B | −32.1% |

Without hooks, main-thread CPU falls 41–43% and allocation 39–42%. Every pair has identical wire hashes. Hook-path total CPU falls 17.3%/21.2%. Untraced GC averages fall from 8.089→7.037 ms and 21.466→18.224 ms per 3,000 requests; minor collection totals across five arms fall from 157→114 and 354→263. All maximum pauses are below 0.98 ms. No natural major GCs occurred, so major-GC behavior remains unmeasured.

Hook RSS averages are 122.96→120.72 MiB (40 messages) and 170.02→164.86 MiB (150). Heap before final GC is 32.77→34.76 MiB and 42.76→40.63 MiB; after-GC retained projection cost is approximately +12.7/+80.0 KiB. Four separate frozen-image retention cases (canonical/MIME-normalized, hook/no-hook) retain exactly 20 large strings / 13,653,760 bytes on both revisions: the initial candidate's extra 13 MiB is eliminated. These are owner-path improvements, not whole-Gateway speedup claims. The requested duplicate-recomputation fast-path proof was used; no ten-minute Gateway stress campaign was run.

Reproduce each revision with:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/responses-history-conversion.ts --messages 40 --frozen --hook --iterations 3000
# Repeat with --messages 150; omit --hook for the immutable-input path.
# Run separate passes with --allocation.
```

The identity regressions failed on the baseline transform/converter and pass on the candidate. Tests were consolidated into existing owner cases; the net test-line delta is −5. Independent golden input bytes cover both conversion styles, text/images/tool calls/results/encrypted reasoning, replay fences and mutable nested sources. Final focused validation: 102 tests in five files passed (42.02 s wall), followed by 73 tests after fixture consolidation (12.91 s) and the final golden test file (60 tests, 1.61 s); the separate prefix/payload-policy/async-replay set passed 62 tests (49.63 s), and import-closure guards passed 32 tests (43.30 s). Targeted oxfmt/oxlint and the export-collision guard pass. No test ceiling or baseline was raised.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): reviewed through P2; the initial image-preparation regression was fixed and independently rechecked (20 warm image requests: 20 repeat decodes before the correction, zero after). No remaining actionable findings. The configured autoreview provider failed preflight because its route did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

Measurement baseline: `4b27ee88cec9`; final source patch SHA-256: `a2faaf6383261ef920cdf42ca04005e51bfc12ce72632b87a8750d1ae5d690aa`. Counterbalanced pairs ran concurrently on disjoint interleaved physical cores with the shared sandbox guard. Host one-minute load ranged from 6.82 to 13.63 and is recorded per arm in the raw measurement output.

CI follow-up: build, lint, type and test jobs passed. Assertion-safety first required an invariant comment for the new array-copy assertion, then required shrinking the payload-policy allowance from 3 to 2 for the assertion this change removed. Both repairs change no executable code. The guard passes against the PR base; independent review verified the exact shrink. No baseline was raised.

Final validation: all required CI and security-review gates passed on `1e263008b97ebeecbc2359f1980e22fef7d2fc93` ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40610189359), [security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40611403009)). Merged as `29470db01ebf47fd05a84fe23d7a0f9c0b3ccf8a`.

prs.title: fix: preserve agent idle budgets across wall-clock changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes premature agent idle timeouts when the system wall clock moves forward between tool activity and the next model stream.

## User Impact

Healthy agent runs keep the idle time they actually have left after a clock adjustment. Real idle streams still time out. Timeout settings, local-provider defaults, and persisted state are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool heartbeats and stream elapsed-time calculations now use `performance.now()`. The separate session watchdog still receives wall-clock deadlines, preserving its existing contract. Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the original fix; their commit is retained.

The skew regression reuses the existing pre-stream activity fixture and retains its structural and notified-progress controls. The complete patch is **production +8/-5 (net +3), tests +16/-17 (net -1)**. The three production lines retain the separate wall-clock progress anchor and document that boundary. No test baseline was raised.

## Evidence

On baseline `c868bfe3105` and the fixed head, the built `pnpm openclaw --profile idle-monotonic agent --local` entry point executed `printf IDLE_TOOL_OK`, submitted its real tool result on the next request, and returned `IDLE_PROOF_OK`. A synthetic OpenAI-compatible loopback relay and a process-local proof loader measured actual timer delays. Only `Date.now()` was offset; the system clock and `performance.now()` were untouched.

| Scenario | First idle timer | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Main, normal clock | 59,928 ms | Tool and answer succeeded |
| Main, +30 s after heartbeat | 29,960 ms | Tool and answer succeeded; budget loss reproduced |
| Fixed, +30 s after heartbeat | 59,972 ms | Tool and answer succeeded |
| Fixed, normal clock | 59,905 ms | Tool and answer succeeded |
