prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): keep the cold-start embed deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A healthy `memory_recall` (or automatic prompt recall) can be rejected as a timeout — or an expired embedding request can be dispatched past its budget — when the host wall clock steps during a provider cold start. In `extensions/memory-lancedb/embeddings.ts`, `ProviderAdapterEmbeddings.embed()` seeds its absolute embed deadline with `Date.now()` and, after awaiting the shared provider's cold-start initialization, recomputes the remaining abort budget with `Date.now()` again: a forward step shrinks (or negates) the budget so a healthy query is fenced as `memory-lancedb embedding timed out`, while a rollback inflates it so an already-expired query is dispatched — exactly the "never dispatch that expired query" case the guard exists to stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embed deadline is process-local — never persisted, never compared against a wall-clock epoch by another process — so the monotonic clock is the only correct source, matching the repo's wall-clock-to-monotonic pattern (merged #177155, #183104, #184711 for the sibling recall-deadline path in the same file).

- Seed now uses `performance.now()` instead of `Date.now()`.
- The remaining-budget read is `Math.floor(deadlineAtMs - performance.now())`, keeping the integer contract `setTimeout` requires.
- This is the cold-start path #184711 explicitly scoped out ("cold-start deadline ... out of scope"); the fixes are complementary, not overlapping.
- No signature, config, or persisted-data change; production net +2 lines (an oxfmt line-wrap, not new logic).

## User Impact

A healthy recall whose provider is still cold-starting is no longer rejected because the clock stepped forward mid-initialization, and an expired query can no longer be dispatched past its budget after a rollback. Timeout text, result ordering, and error reporting are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry point: real recall across a clock step

A real `openclaw agent --local` turn (real plugin load, real `RecallService`, real provider adapter, real HTTP embedding dispatch to a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint that logs every request). A `--import` shim steps `Date.now` by +30 s between the adapter's deadline seed and its remaining-budget read — the window a host clock correction lands in. It matches the direct caller frame, so the seed keeps the real clock and only the read is stepped. Every run starts from a fresh state dir, so the provider is always cold-started.

**Pre-fix (`Date.now` seed + read): healthy recall fenced, no embedding request ever sent.**

```console
CLOCK_SEED real=1793116945400 offset=30000 arm=1 seedReturnsReal=1
CLOCK_READ real=1793116945441 stepped=1793116975441 offset=30000
CLOCK_SUMMARY adapterDateNowCalls=2 stepped=true offset=30000
# endpoint log: chat only, zero /v1/embeddings requests
CHAT_REQUEST at=131458ms
[plugins] memory-lancedb: recall failed: MemoryRecallEmbeddingError: memory-lancedb embedding timed out
```

**Post-fix (`performance.now` seed + read): same shim, same step, recall dispatches.**

```console
CLOCK_SUMMARY adapterDateNowCalls=0 stepped=false offset=30000
EMBED_REQUEST at=141768ms model=text-embedding-3-small inputs=1 first="Which editor do you recommend?"
EMBED_RESPONDED at=141773ms
CHAT_REQUEST at=142914ms
# no timeout line anywhere in the run
```

**Control (pre-fix source, shim loaded, offset 0): same path without the step dispatches normally, so the failure above is the clock step, not the harness.**

```console
CLOCK_DISABLED offset=0 mode=control
EMBED_REQUEST at=173117ms model=text-embedding-3-small inputs=1 first="Which editor do you recommend?"
```

The step is injected rather than host-NTP; the measured seed→read window here was 41 ms (1793116945400 → 1793116945441), which is exactly the window an instantaneous clock correction lands in.

### Timeout still enforced after the fix

A 16 s embedding response against the 15 s recall budget is still abandoned at the budget:

```console
EMBED_REQUEST at=151123ms ... delayMs=16000
[plugins] memory-lancedb: auto-recall timed out after 15000ms; skipping memory injection to avoid stalling agent startup
```

### Regression test RED / GREEN

`keeps the cold-start embed deadline on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock step` (`auto-recall.deadline.test.ts`) uses a synthetic cold provider (pending `ready.promise`) and `vi.setSystemTime` to step `Date.now()` by +30 s between seed and read.

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/memory-lancedb/auto-recall.deadline.test.ts   # pre-fix (Date.now)
 ✗ keeps the cold-start embed deadline on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock step
   expect(requests[0]?.aborted).toBe(false)   // requests empty: query fenced pre-dispatch
 Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)

$ npx vitest run extensions/memory-lancedb/auto-recall.deadline.test.ts   # post-fix (performance.now)
 ✓ 3 passed
```

### Full memory-lancedb shard

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb --run` → 18 passed | 1 failed files, 115 passed | 1 failed tests. The single failure is `arrow-null-predicates.test.ts`, which fails identically on clean `main` (`EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed` — apache-arrow's `new Function` predicate compilation blocked in this Node context); pre-existing, unrelated, and recorded as such.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous process-local deadline calculation; no state migration or published contract changes. Blast radius is memory-lancedb cold-start embed deadline handling.


## Independent bundled-enable Gateway Evidence

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186037#issuecomment-6448533591

Enabled the bundled memory-lancedb with the shipped CLI (no plugin install). Fresh built Gateway cold starts, +30s process-only Date.now correction: main twice times out without dispatching embeddings; candidate twice sends one embedding request and completes recall. Both no-step controls complete recall. The same actual clock correction is recorded on both refs. No source edits or pushes were required.

prs.title: fix: include observed usage in inference JSON
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful `infer model run --json` commands drop provider usage, so callers cannot meter one-shot runs from the synchronous result.

Closes #121795. Thanks @aleps001 for the request and @wlassalle724 and @Mirksen for the additional reports and investigation.

## User Impact

Both `--local` and `--gateway` return optional `usage` and `lastCallUsage` fields. Missing observations stay omitted, measured zero stays zero, and explicitly unavailable usage stays unavailable. Existing fields and text output are unchanged; no configuration or data migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI already receives the accounting data but omits it from its output projection. Local execution uses the existing usage normalizer; its one completion supplies both fields. Gateway output preserves the runtime's aggregate-versus-last-call distinction, including authoritative zero/unavailable aggregate cost status. The public envelope type and stable-fields documentation describe the same contract. Cost metadata stays with the existing accounting owner.

## Evidence

- Real `qwen2.5:7b` on macOS, through a recording relay: both transports return `OK` for `--thinking off --prompt 'Reply exactly OK' --json`. Base omits usage despite Ollama terminal prompt/eval counts of 32/2 locally and 48/2 through an isolated Gateway. Fixed JSON preserves those totals in both usage fields. With prefix reuse, the existing normalizer splits local input into 1 uncached + 31 cached, and Gateway input into 1 + 47 cached; totals are 34 and 50 respectively. Fixed wall times: 6.00s local, 3.60s Gateway.
- A deterministic relay exercises both real CLI entry points with 17 input / 3 output tokens. Base omits usage; fixed returns input=17, output=3, total=20 in both fields (6.04s local, 5.01s Gateway).
- Seven regression cases fail on base solely because fields are absent; all 119 existing cases pass. Additional authoritative zero-cost regressions fail on the first candidate and pass with the correction. The two touched files pass 128 tests (92.82s wall, including cold compilation); 12 resource/auth sibling tests also pass. After the test-only lint cleanup, all 25 outcome/usage cases pass again (68.32s wall, including cold compilation).
- Full build passes (4m36.9s). Core and CLI-test TypeScript checks and targeted lint pass. All baseline ratchets pass; affected ratchets pass again after the correction. Test-lines is net -1, with no ceiling increase.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the complete range from `14081a8c8b31b8aa9ef89eb2725710a7b25c4852` to `edde5c3e37f77ffaa12c3711fc7a616404b1040f`. The initial review caught the authoritative zero-cost case; it is fixed, regression-tested, and clean on re-review.

Production: +22/-3 lines (net +19), needed for the optional projections, aggregate status preservation, and shared public types. Tests: net -1, offset by consolidating repeated fixtures/assertions in the same CLI owner without removing coverage. Documentation: +6 lines.

Live validation is macOS/Ollama; PR CI supplies broader checks. No upgrade run was needed for this additive output-only change: persistent state and provider requests are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(telegram): large media sends time out after 30 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #112116 (closed, covered the unhandled rejection after a media upload timeout, not the deadline itself)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a large video or document sent to Telegram fails with `Network request for 'sendVideo' failed!` after 30 seconds when the file needs longer than that to upload.

## User Impact

Media sends get a deadline that grows with the file instead of a flat 30 s. An upload keeps its current guard until its transfer estimate outgrows it (30 MiB for the 30 s methods), and the longest guard is 30 minutes. Operators have no knob for this today: `timeoutSeconds` is in `RETIRED_TUNING_KEYS` (`extensions/telegram/src/doctor-contract.ts:29`), and neither client passes a timeout to `createTelegramClientFetch`.

Tradeoff that needs a maintainer call: the account throttler runs one request at a time per chat, and in a group one at a time across all of its forum topics (`GroupRequestScheduler.drain` in `account-throttler.ts`). A slow upload now holds the requests queued behind it in that chat for as long as its guard, up to 30 minutes, where today they wait at most the 30 s guard (60 s for albums) for it to fail. Other chats are not held.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveTelegramRequestTimeoutMs` gives `sendvideo`, `senddocument`, `sendphoto`, `sendanimation`, `sendaudio` and `sendvoice` a fixed 30_000 ms, and `sendmediagroup` gets the 60_000 ms default. Pinned main `2e7668b2eaad` still uses that table. The Bot API answers an upload with the sent Message, so the response cannot arrive before the file has been uploaded, and a big enough file always loses.

The resolver now takes an optional upload size and returns the larger of the table value and `ceil(bytes / 2 MiB/s)` seconds plus 15 s, capped at 30 minutes. 2 MiB/s is an assumed floor, not a measurement.

The size comes from the InputFile that `prepareTelegramOutboundMedia` builds (recorded in a WeakMap); direct sends, reply media and albums all take their files from it. A grammY transformer installed inside the account throttler, in both `send-context.ts` and `bot-core.ts`, reads the size off the payload (including `sendMediaGroup`'s `media[]`) and hands it to the client fetch through AsyncLocalStorage. I did not take the size from the caller's async context because the throttler runs queued requests from its own drain loop. In a probe on an earlier base, a second request enqueued under its own AsyncLocalStorage value ran under the first request's value, for both a group chat and a private chat.

Two more timers sat under that guard. grammY 1.46.0 races every call against one client timer, `options.timeoutSeconds ?? 500` (`out/core/client.js:77`), with no per-call override, and neither client set it. undici 8.11.2 waits `headersTimeout` for response headers, `300e3` by default (`lib/dispatcher/client.js:317`), and refreshes that timer when a streamed body ends, so it counts from the end of the upload. A self-hosted Bot API server answers only after it has relayed the file to Telegram. Both clients now set grammY's `timeoutSeconds`, and the Telegram dispatchers set `headersTimeout`, to 1860 s (the 30-minute cap plus 60 s), so the per-method guard is the deadline. Every other consumer of the Telegram transport keeps a shorter deadline of its own (getUpdates 45 s, file downloads 120 s to headers, probes through `fetchWithTimeout`).

## Current revision and fixture repair

Head: [`44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737), tree `8abfeb27059dab4f917a1818a34a495c1e303af3`.

This fixture-only commit disables persisted thread bindings in the upload-deadline fixture and registers `bot.stop()` for cleanup. The real bot, send stack and all four upload assertions remain. Upstream #175379 deliberately acquires runtime when thread bindings start; the upload fixture does not initialize that unrelated runtime. Production binding behavior is unchanged.

The preceding head `0afce1f7d17e08adbf2d3818122e9ebb6420cecd` merged main `2e7668b2eaad12171ef4421b68286de6063b7e77`, retaining main's one-argument account-throttler constructor and the upload transformer before the throttler. The sequential transformer/WeakMap/context test requested removed in [the review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151923#issuecomment-5733461410) is removed; the four independent size-boundary cases remain.

[Previous-head CI 40121818105](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121818105) finished with 27 successful jobs, 31 skipped and two failures: the Telegram job failed both polling-bot rows with `Telegram runtime not initialized` before their upload assertions, and the aggregate gate propagated that failure. The four boundary cases, two other send cases and loopback case passed.

## Evidence

### Upgrade from the latest stable release, Telegram settings preserved

Isolated state dir on macOS (Node 24.22.1), everything on loopback. Telegram was a local Bot API stand-in reached through `channels.telegram.apiRoot`, the same override a self-hosted Bot API uses. It records every call; it is not Telegram.

1. Published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (npm `latest`, build `dc2523e5a5c7`) on a fresh state dir: `config validate` exit 0, Gateway polled and consumed update 41, `message send --media <1 MiB zip> --force-document` returned `messageId` 5001, Gateway exit 0. Stored Telegram state: `telegram.update-offsets` `lastUpdateId: 41`, plus sent-message, message-cache and bot-info rows.
2. This head (`44411bc979e3`, tree `8abfeb27059d`) on the same state dir: `config validate` exit 0. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exit 0; its changes are main's database migrations and one derived `groupAllowFrom`, nothing from this PR. All 11 Telegram keys kept their values (`enabled`, `botToken`, `apiRoot`, `dmPolicy`, `allowFrom`, `groupPolicy`, `defaultTo`, `linkPreview`, `silentErrorReplies`, `streaming`, `mediaMaxMb`). The Gateway's first `getUpdates` asked for offset 42, so update 41 was not replayed; it consumed update 42 (`lastUpdateId` 41 -> 42), delivered a 100 MiB document, and exited 0.
3. The same two phases from `2026.10.7` (build `157d8c2bc3ea`, `latest` on 2026-10-26) gave the same result.

Fresh install: this head on an empty state dir with the same config started, polled, and delivered the 100 MiB document below.

### Large upload, main vs this head

Same harness. The stand-in reads uploads at 2 MiB/s, the PR's assumed floor, so a 104,857,720-byte zip takes about 50 s: longer than main's 30 s guard, shorter than this head's guard for that size (66 s by the PR's formula). `mediaMaxMb: 2000` as a self-hosted Bot API operator would set it; at the default 100 MiB cap the file is refused before upload (`file exceeds limit of 104857600 bytes`).

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main `2e7668b2eaad` (merge base) | `sendDocument` aborted at 30.7 s after 64,578,089 bytes; `OutboundDeliveryError: Network request for 'sendDocument' failed!` |
| this head, fresh state | delivered: 104,858,286 bytes in 50.0 s, `message_id` 5001 |
| this head, upgraded from 2026.10.8 | delivered: 104,858,286 bytes in 50.0 s, `message_id` 5001 |

This is the reported failure and its fix through the real CLI, Gateway and Telegram send path. It does not deliver an approximately 893 MiB file to Telegram through a self-hosted Bot API; that run is still open.

### Fixture validation

A separate Linux x64 runner tested the exact published tree using Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependencies, Vitest 5.0.5 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. Lockfile SHA-256: `21592b379203de7ecd8661cfd6e412daf6546f94b203f28c314579db20f76594`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Upload-deadline fixture | Four cases passed; 122.03 s. |
| Independent size boundaries plus loopback transport | Five cases passed; 105.10 s. |
| Restore only the upload fixture from `0afce1f7`, same environment | Exactly the 100 MiB and 1 GiB polling rows failed with the runtime-initialization error; both send rows passed; 125.27 s. |
| Boundary and loopback controls after reversal | All five passed; 129.37 s. |
| Restoration | Exact candidate tree restored; validation processes and allocation drained. |

```sh
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-timeout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-real-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Tested fixture SHA-256: `142a7e49383fc875bed18b2774b39bb862f77c363680890bf953bf54a90ab530`. Validation receipt SHA-256: `181295d70e37bcc0cb488ed9c0728241e315881072b5041d1a6cb6e10663425c`. Independent source review found no actionable issue in this fixture change.

These are fixture results. The loopback case uses a 64 KiB payload tagged with a larger upload size and a fake clock. It proves timer ordering through the local transport; it does not deliver an approximately 893 MiB file to Telegram.

## Historical product regression evidence

At `34a6f9e42fb`, the three upload files and neighboring bot/fetch suites passed 94 cases. Replacing only the four production wiring files with main `4db022470af6` caused all four upload fixture cases and the loopback case to abort at 30,000 ms. Earlier timer probes distinguished grammY's 500-second client deadline and undici's response-header deadline. These remain historical evidence, not a current-head live-platform result.

## Remaining gates

[CI 40138561883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138561883) completed successfully for this head: 29 jobs passed and 31 skipped. Its merge checkout `bd77e2ea717464e780e0a5777fa21633727576ff` has parents main `418aafaae7e8d13792b9095c010a114ca4e058ea` and this head; the upload fixture is byte-identical. All four upload cases, four size-boundary cases and the loopback case passed. The latest dependency, security and aggregate statuses are success ([status publisher 40139326205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139326205)).

The later PR-context check rejected the previous body because its validation heading did not start with `Evidence`. This body restores that required heading. The product and live-proof gates below remain open.

- Maintainer acceptance of the assumed 2 MiB/s budget and up-to-30-minute per-chat wait remains open.
- The approximately 893 MiB send through a self-hosted Bot API must still demonstrate an unpatched timeout and a delivered message on the patched build, with size and elapsed time. No live upload or two-bot proof was performed in this fixture validation.
- The 2 MiB/s floor remains an assumption. Loopback and fake-clock results do not establish real transfer rates.

prs.title: feat(provider): add Databricks Unity Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #155633

## What Problem This Solves

Organizations routing inference through Databricks Unity Gateway currently hand-author workspace routes, credentials, transport and model metadata. This adds provider-specific onboarding and model resolution through an externally distributed plugin.

## User Impact

Operators install `@openclaw/databricks-provider`, supply `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, and run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice databricks-token`. Models use `databricks/<catalog>.<schema>.<model-service>`.

Same-workspace onboarding preserves existing routes, APIs, model entries, aliases and primary selections. Fresh setup uses `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` with `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`. Non-interactive onboarding refuses reuse of a saved profile when `DATABRICKS_HOST` selects a different workspace, and rejects invalid explicit hosts before persistence. Trusted manual provider-config edits remain operator-controlled routing changes; this does not introduce immutable workspace identity in the credential format.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Databricks host validation, auth, onboarding and model resolution stay in `extensions/databricks`.
- Reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible streaming transport and credential store.
- Follows the in-repo-source / external npm and ClawHub package pattern used by official providers such as Cerebras and Radius; excluded from the core npm tarball.
- Adds `DATABRICKS_HOST` to untrusted workspace `.env` filtering, with a regression. Credential environment filtering comes from the manifest.
- No new external runtime dependencies, generic transport, credential owner, schema or migration. The lockfile adds only the workspace importer and existing `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency.

## Current candidate

Merged with current main on October 25, 2026: head `ed3410f89b58993803b30e2cd91d240a3faeb12e`, a merge commit with parents `37b4873865e39e4d9eafd845ce2046df52a46bc7` (the October 21 candidate) and upstream main `e850f7c5419068f4eb598152fd8b0e164f995fcb`. This was a merge, so the branch history was not force pushed.

Merge conflicts were limited to generated docs and the zh-CN glossary. `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` were regenerated through their owning script, and both sides of the zh-CN glossary were kept. Databricks production and transport code are unchanged. The workspace dotenv regression uses main's refactored fixture helper and retains both Databricks host checks. Plugin version, API compatibility and build metadata remain aligned to `2026.10.4`; minimum host remains `>=2026.9.6`.

The installed-package/live/upgrade proof below applies to earlier candidates. It is retained as historical behavior evidence, not claimed as a fresh live run or current-head CI.

## Evidence

### October 25 merge proof

At exact head `ed3410f89b58993803b30e2cd91d240a3faeb12e`:

- `pnpm test extensions/databricks/index.test.ts extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **28 passed** (9 infra + 19 provider/transport).
- The two failures diagnosed on October 21 (planner capacity 80/79 and the Feishu streaming bound) pass on the new main base.
- Package-boundary typecheck through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, lint, `plugins:inventory:check` and `config:docs:check` passed.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40256838088) on this head is still running. At the time of writing, three shards had failed in suites outside this diff: `test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts` (sandbox explain validation JSON), `test/cli-json-stdout.hooks.e2e.test.ts` (remote Gateway hooks error text) and `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/telegram-recovered-artifact.e2e.test.ts`. None of those files or their owners are touched here; their cause is not yet diagnosed and no baseline reproduction is claimed.
- `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/dependency-review` still require maintainer approval of this revision.

### Fresh CI diagnosis — October 21

[Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034) is still running. Two failures observed so far:

- [Planner capacity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034/job/119548250646): `keeps the hybrid hourly plan within the main-tier cap` reports 80 jobs versus cap 79. Reproduced the same planner API/options in separate exact-base `4397e7409d5` and candidate `37b4873865e` checkouts; both fail with the identical 80/79 result. - Normal test entrypoint: `pnpm test extensions/databricks/index.test.ts extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **28/28 passed**, exit 0 on final head `26eea19eb89` (19 provider/transport + 9 workspace dotenv cases). Repeated after incorporating main’s provider-authentication changes. The cold run on preceding head `f22a48bfbb5` also passed (infra 76.99s, extensions 67.96s).

</details>

### Live installed-package proof — October 13

Executed against a real Databricks workspace using the current candidate. The token existed only in the child process environment; onboarding used `--secret-input-mode ref`. Workspace and token are redacted.

| Boundary | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Core runtime build | Completed successfully, 83.3 seconds |
| Release-pipeline plugin pack | `openclaw-databricks-provider-2026.10.2.tgz`, 8 files, 3 runtime JS modules, manifest, package metadata, README and 2 assets; no runtime dependencies |

Using the same packed plugin with bundled discovery and source overlays disabled:

- Started with published latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`), created an existing Databricks Serving route and saved synthetic workspace-A credential through its published SDK, then installed the candidate and ran candidate onboarding. Exit 0; deep comparisons confirmed provider route/API/model metadata, primary selection, aliases/model entries and saved credential including workspace metadata were unchanged.

- Workspace-B selection without a fresh token exited 1 before network access; active configuration hash was unchanged.
- Hostile cwd `.env` supplied an attacker workspace and token. A benign dotenv witness was loaded, proving the actual cwd loader ran, while `DATABRICKS_HOST` stayed absent. Onboarding exited 1 for missing trusted workspace; configuration hash was unchanged.
- A Node preload denied and recorded fetch, HTTP(S) and socket connection attempts. Both negative cases recorded `attempts: []`; it did not modify provider auth/config logic. Synthetic credentials were used for these boundary probes.
- The real-token live run above was separately scanned across 23 isolated state files: zero occurrences of the supplied token.

## October 13 validation (prior head)

- Focused provider, real-transport loopback and workspace `.env` suites: 28 tests passed across 3 files. Combined wall time 80.44 seconds on a heavily loaded macOS arm64 host, Node 26.5. Provider files: 19 tests, 28.32 seconds wall, individual transport scenario 416 ms. No new tests were added in the rebase.
- Extension package-boundary production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and changed-source formatting passed.
- Config baseline, plugin inventory and version-sync checks passed.
- Full docs checks passed: formatting, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples and changelog checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh independent review was completed. Findings were checked against owning paths:

- The proposed interactive SecretRef failure did not reproduce through the registered auth method with source overlays disabled and an explicit plugin load path. The reviewer retracted it.
- The proposed dynamic API override failure is prevented by core's `applyConfiguredProviderOverrides`; the final resolution probe retained `anthropic-messages` and the configured route. No duplicate override was added to the plugin.
- The proposed immutable credential/workspace binding would change the trusted manual-config contract and credential semantics. The implemented guard covers onboarding workspace selection, not arbitrary operator edits; that scope is explicit above.

Prior-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38397087861) completed with 167 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs and 6 failed jobs (5 shards plus the aggregate gate). The Databricks shard, production/test types, lint, package boundaries, docs, source contracts and npm-lock checks passed. The failing shards were OpenAI realtime auth fixtures (missing admitted database worker), Codex dynamic-tool host instructions, node-worker launch wire timeout, Telegram emoji gateway timeout, and QA POSIX SIGTERM lifecycle timeout. These are outside the Databricks diff; only the OpenAI failure was independently reproduced and repaired in separate #171064 (18 unchanged tests pass). Other failures are attributed by hosted logs and unchanged source scope, not claimed baseline reproductions. Dependency approval remains separate from the failed CI gate.

## Limits and maintainer decision

This is Unity Gateway support. Existing workspace Serving configuration is preserved, but broader Serving compatibility belongs to dependent #163202, which still requires its own repair, restack and validation. OAuth token minting/refresh, automatic live model discovery and per-workspace pricing are outside this change; unknown model services use fallback metadata.

The remaining product decision is whether Databricks receives official provider catalog sponsorship and in-repository maintenance. Maintainer edits are enabled. If accepted, the final head requires the existing maintainer dependency-change approval path; publishing/release is a separate action.

prs.title: fix: dashboard handoff stops after one document timeout
prs.body:
Closes #183682

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: first-run onboarding abandons the dashboard when one local document request times out, even though the Gateway is already running.

## User Impact

User impact: a transient two-second dashboard timeout is retried before onboarding gives up. If the dashboard still does not respond, the Gateway stays up and the printed dashboard URL remains the way to open it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared document check treated a thrown request error as final. The reported Windows log showed one fetch timeout after Gateway ready, then "The browser handoff did not finish." Timeout errors now get two more attempts. Other request failures still stop immediately, and a timeout that keeps happening still fails instead of waiting out the asset-build deadline.

## Evidence

- On current main, a `TimeoutError` followed by HTTP 200 `text/html` returned not ready with "request timed out". The same case passes after this change.
- `pnpm test src/commands/control-ui-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed, 14 tests, about 62s wall on this host. Most of that was worker startup; the new cases were a few milliseconds.
- Onboarding, dashboard, and wizard callers of the same check passed: `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-browser-handoff.test.ts src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.test.ts src/commands/dashboard.test.ts src/commands/dashboard/json.test.ts src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (3 shards, about 44s).
- A hanging local server, fetched through the real document probe, threw `TimeoutError` with message "request timed out".
- Changed-file format, lint, and core typecheck passed. `pnpm check:changed` later failed an existing unused-export scan in files this PR does not change.
- Native Windows foreground onboarding was not rerun.

prs.title: fix(subagents): preserve requester source for original singleton completions
prs.body:
Refs #182043
Related: #183712 (lease wake repair, now merged into the tested main)

## What Problem This Solves

A completed original single-child settlement batch can lose the admitted requester needed for its parent's final and fail permanently after a Gateway crash.

## User Impact

Only **new, trusted, complete original singleton batches** enter the retained-requester path. Legacy mixed/unknown batches, original multi-member batches, and larger batches reduced to one remain unresolved and caller-free. This does not close #182043 or authorize a production upgrade.

The fixed main used for this refresh already includes the separate lease wake repair from #183712. The completed-child/pre-send **immediate-restart** scenario now passes on the actual current PR image; this is no longer just the earlier source-only diagnostic that waited for lease expiry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing `retainRequester`/`runWithRequester`, completion custody, Gateway caller and private recovery-claim owners. The source is the tool-preparation-time, host-validated selected requester, never the delegated creator, latest user, route or transcript.

Qualification uses complete unfiltered original accepted-spawn accounting, including canceled/retired members, plus the exact frozen singleton, run/generation/rearm, current custody, physical store and parent incarnation. Recheck currentness after awaited preparation and at actual admission/commit. Default caller-free behavior and an accepted input's independent authority remain. No ended invocation, operational permission or approval grant is restored; original operational-instance accounting is private and process-local.

No principal regrouping, frozen member/input/hash rewrite, legacy migration, schema/config option, receipt compensation or general recovery protocol is added. #164366's sibling/custody policy is not replaced.

### Conflict refresh

Fixed incoming main: `05adffc985175308fef123437d20d1d07599ee75`.
Previous published head: `55e33221f84ef14af8f05c48557bb54562e6240b`.
Current head: `35d777a1f4a36e42931b737803c013207cc1ed0f`.

Ordinary merge preserves published history. Both actual conflicts are resolved: retain upstream #184988's `createOperatorInputRecoverySource` and direct-child target selection alongside requester retention, and keep upstream test consolidation/abort-reason coverage plus this PR's admission checks. A subsequent equivalent two-field destructuring keeps direct delivery within the existing 700-line source limit. No rule, baseline, assertion or test timeout was relaxed.

## Evidence

**Current status:** exact-head official build, scoped autoreview, **303 source tests and six fresh native-entry cases passed**; [inspectable current-head terminal/audit proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183715#issuecomment-6440340912) is public. Core types, all29 configured test typegraphs, format, lint/700-line cap, SQLite worker ratchet and other configured guards passed. The complete local changed-check command remains **FAIL solely on Knip**: fixed main and candidate have identical production8/full-tree7/script0 findings and identical reported source blobs, with no skip/waiver. [Normal CI40492643510](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40492643510) completed **successfully:47 successful jobs;30 selected-out skips are not passes**. CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep and Workflow Sanity also passed. [Current-head ClawSweeper revision5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183715#issuecomment-6400443429) completed successfully in [run40495465168](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/40495465168): proof5/6 sufficient, patch4/6, overall3/6, Findings None. It leaves exactly two maintainer-owned actions and the live status is **waiting on maintainer**; no author-side defect was identified. Review/route completion is confirmed by the command receipt. This bot recommendation does not approve either human decision. The separate current-head security approval gate and singleton policy decision remain outstanding.

Exact tree: `f9ec7cf6ec2b7ce1a427ba13fc9432566e5062e2`.
Official local image ID: `sha256:c8e421fcae7095a890483488904210833449a176914200b27a0f99a17a152ff5`.
Source archive SHA-256: `8c00e5825e9daa5293678399bcd16c8eb45357b5c4a5ee884c99a3eb983dea51`.
The unmodified `git archive` was built using the official Dockerfile `build` target with `GIT_COMMIT=35d777a1f4a36e42931b737803c013207cc1ed0f`; actual `dist/build-info.json` reports that full commit. Runtime: Node v24.22.1, SQLite 3.53.4. The local image is not a published registry reference.

### Current-head source regressions

- Authority/completion/delivery: **240 passed**, 205.108s command wall time.
- Native Gateway input authority/retirement: **25 passed**, 72.743s.
- Requester continuation: **8 passed**, 27.757s.
- Original progress-only sibling: **1 passed** with unchanged assertions, 23.433s; 22 pattern-skips are not passes.
- Upstream direct-child restart integration: **17 passed**, 26.552s.
- Upstream peer-source recovery: **12 passed**, 58.587s.

Total **303 passed**. No tests were added or weakened for conflict resolution. These retain distinct membership, reduced-survivor, missing-source, operator/system, scope/revocation, owner/generation/incarnation, final/expired-wake and accepted-input boundaries.

### Current-head shipped-entry proof

Actual built CLI Gateway, synthetic channel, controlled local model, fresh complete native ext4 state, no external network, no host data binds or published ports. Each crash kills/reaps the full Gateway process tree. Every case uses fresh state and performs a second actual restart.

Recorded audit projection:


Normal, running-child crash and completed-child/pre-send crash settle with one physical send and no pending input/outbound obligation. Active recovery keeps one logical child across two physical run rows. The uncertain-send control deliberately stays owed, preserving its original queue/attempt, with fresh unresolved reconciliation on both restarts and **one actual effect, no replay**. Saved source is never treated as proof of not-sent.

Two additional unchanged native admission fixtures pass **86 independent stopped-state assertions**: A's original operation admits/selects B and accepts exactly one original child. After a full crash, actual personal read/write succeeds only as B; the nearest forbidden A-only target is rejected by the canonical current-role owner. Public B-role revocation after recovery produces the exact correlated role/source refusal before personal I/O; generic abort is excluded. Second restarts add no personal I/O/model attempts. SQLite/transcript/source facts and actual file bytes are independently reopened and compared. All six native archives have verified SHA-256 records.

### Scope and limits of proof

The [original baseline failure, wider native effect controls and stable-created state comparisons](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183715#issuecomment-6404928134) remain explicitly historical evidence at the recorded old baseline/head. They are not relabeled as executed on this refresh. Full old-state upgrade acceptance on this new main, paired-device-specific revocation and pre-start persisted role changes are **NOT_RUN/NOT_COVERED** here. Legacy missing-source recovery remains outside the repair.

The intermediate merge candidate's failed line-cap check is retained; the final head contains the equivalent one-line correction. Initial isolated-check Git ancestry and missing pinned Knip cache were corrected in test preparation, preserving their logs and the original commands. The final static command is complete: all steps except the verified main-identical Knip findings passed. Historical Knip results do not certify this head; the fresh source comparison is linked in the current-head proof. Canonical code reviews cover the full merged patch and then the bounded field-binding follow-up, both P0–P2 scoped-clean; neither is maintainer security approval.

## Maintainer Decisions Before Merge

1. Accept or reject completion-owned selected-requester re-entry for a complete original trusted singleton under these existing authority checks.
2. An authorized maintainer must perform the repository's security review/approval of **this exact current head**.

The required security gate remains enforced. Normal CI, behavior proof, Ready state or a bot recommendation cannot grant those decisions. If there is an additional author-side defect, identify its violated boundary/scenario; approval-only wording remains maintainer work.

Production **HOLD**: no deployment, production Gateway restart or production data/config/credential read. Real QQ/WeChat, online product inference, the OpenClaw Codex provider and business acceptance remain NOT_RUN. No merge or tracking automation.

Withdrawal/rollback: retain branches, native volumes and evidence; withdraw or revert the author's delta against the actual deployment base while preserving persisted obligations. Do not revert incoming main wholesale, delete state or blindly resend uncertain work. No production rollback has been executed or authorized.

prs.title: fix: goals created mid-turn stop after delegated work
prs.body:
Closes #183705

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unfinished Goal stopping after delegated work returns when the agent created the Goal during that same chat turn.

## User Impact

Users can keep pursuing an explicitly requested Goal across a same-process child handoff without sending another message to restart it. There is no schema/configuration migration, restart recovery extension, or new autonomous capability for independent commands or scheduled turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing return owner captured only Goals present before execution. Keep that owner unbound for an admitted built-in chat, then bind the actual `create_goal` result once to the current run/session/agent/store. Retaining the return still requires a committed yield; the existing queue, current Goal, cancellation, budget, and authority checks continue to decide whether another turn may run.

## Evidence

### Repair and Validation Status

Current repaired candidate: `98679a804ab787cb598b8d90979094da8eaf9f2c`, integrating the final bounded snapshot `f39b480c874d8acdae73f3b1c060dbd6cfc7a052`. The preceding `bdefe28105a066bf29a8565972140be3b947c9e4` integrated the observed CI comparison snapshot `23b53fd33fcd0fbaaf62546db23fb032541c9bdc` into `de7fed4b39fdfdd5f0b0c736d914533fbbed5e42`; a subsequent upstream budget edit caused the sole conflict resolved by this final integration. Earlier, `de7fed4` integrated fixed main `a6be2f6aee7fd9782563d54e33e4b60995853008` into `70159c5dc95809b55cb60713a558d871ef08ecad`, retaining both upstream placement coverage and the lifecycle-generation helper at its import conflict. No history was rewritten. All nine original PR files remain byte-identical to `de7fed4`; the only additional changes are the consumer fixture and justified test budget below. The five production-file changes are unchanged.

The focused Goal regression, type, and static gates below passed at the preceding candidate. CI subsequently found a missed consumer fixture and a test-line budget failure; their repair and the retained local failure are reported next. The additional hosted-model exercise did **not** satisfy all requested proof conditions. In particular, a successful shipped-runtime, real-model automatic-continuation demonstration and a real-model restricted-operator final-effect demonstration are still outstanding. These partial/failed exercises are not evidence of a newly identified production defect, and this update does not claim that all review feedback is resolved.

### CI follow-up: real consumer owner and explicit test budget

[CI on `de7fed4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40535982697/job/122302639048) found `Operation has no controller owner` in the existing subagent cohort-conflict regression. Initially Goal-less admitted chat now enters the real Goal return owner, but that consumer fixture supplied an unregistered operation double. The fixture now creates the existing real controller operation with its captured physical store/session target, observes the real failure method through a call-through spy, and completes/joins owner settlement. Every original registry-conflict, visible-error, transcript, and no-model-execution assertion remains. No production owner or authority check was relaxed, and no Goal-wrapper mock was introduced.

The corrected case passed in the original three-file infra group (7.532 s). The command as a whole returned exit 1: **43 passed, one failed**, because the unmodified `refuses held row facts after configured-alias close` case timed out after 120 seconds on Windows. That same case had passed in the original CI job; this does not prove an inherited or platform-only defect. Static investigation found isolated fork workers and no new collection-time controller registration from this fixture, but the stalled await remains unidentified. No timeout was raised, test removed, or green replay substituted. The messaging test type graph, focused lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed. The local run used Node on Windows, not CI's Bun/Linux scheduling.

One bounded diagnostic ran only that failed alias-close case on the final fixed `f39b480` integration inputs; it also timed out after 120 seconds (one failed, 14 explicitly filtered cases). This is a different base from the first local group, not an identical-source replay. It does not establish a preceding-file cause, a Windows-only cause, or a repaired failure. The precise blocked await remains unknown. Both failed local receipts and the wrapper's conservative retained-namespace warnings remain recorded; no further replay or production workaround was added.

The separate [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40535982697/job/122302638696) failed on positive test-line growth. The first fixed CI-snapshot integration measured 6,286,460 total lines and passed its explicit zero-slack budget check. After resolving the subsequent upstream scalar conflict on the final fixed `f39b480` snapshot, the native checker measured **6,286,640** total lines with a **+694** PR delta. The final deliberate ceiling change is exactly 6,285,587 to 6,286,640, with zero slack: 694 retained regression lines plus 359 lines already beyond the ceiling in the comparison tree. That split is arithmetic, not an independent failing run of main. The documented owner permits manual increases with a PR justification. No guard was disabled or required coverage deleted; the native checker passed after the edit.

The new fixture received an independent full-context P0–P3 agent review, and the mechanical integration/budget change received a separate independent assessment. Neither found an actionable issue; neither is a CLI/helper pass. Current-head hosted CI remains separate from the previous failed run and these local receipts.

### Passing Local Evidence

- Historical local Gateway/tool/child-return baseline: a pre-existing Goal continued once and completed; the otherwise matched model-created Goal received no Goal context or nudge and remained active after the child batch committed and Gateway work drained.
- The Gateway regression passes actual `create_goal -> sessions_spawn -> sessions_yield -> committed requester final -> Goal nudge -> complete`, plus a non-yield final control: delegated parent/child requests `6/1`, direct `4/0`, exactly one continuation in each, no provider errors.
- Added actual Gateway authority coverage with identified users and configured roles: a member restricted to `main` receives the real sibling `sessions_create` denial, creates no sibling session, and completes one Goal continuation. After a separate member's role is revoked through `users.setRole`, the held provider socket is actually cancelled; no subsequent provider requests, sibling session, Goal completion, or normal post-revocation assistant chat delta/final content is observed. This is a fixed-provider Gateway regression, not a real-model authority proof.
- At `de7fed4`, Goal owner/tool suites: **73 passed** (`66 + 7`). Both Gateway tests passed. Affected consumers and provider-prefix tests passed across eight files; their combined test total is not asserted because one summary was truncated in the captured output.
- At that preceding candidate, production and affected messaging, agent-tools, and Gateway canonical test type graphs passed. Focused lint, format, and diff checks passed for all nine original PR files. The first lint run found six missing-brace style errors in the new authority test; all were repaired without changing conditions, assertions, or ordering, and the final static checks passed.
- Independent P0–P3 subagent review of the full repaired nine-file candidate against the fixed main snapshot found no actionable findings. The CLI reviewer was unavailable and produced no report. The alternative review was explicitly approved for this PR and is not a CLI pass; the subsequent brace-only delta also received mechanical review.

These Gateway tests use a scripted loopback Responses provider. They are not hosted-model, real-channel, restart, local Codex, or production-scale proof. Hosted CI for the repaired candidate and its CI duration are not established by these local runs.

### Hosted-Model Exercise: Partial Evidence, Both Attempts Failed

Both exercises used an isolated shipped `dist/index.js` Gateway process, the built-in OpenClaw agent runtime, actual public native CLI/WebSocket RPC with the current client version, and Alibaba Bailian `qwen3.8-flash`. All task content was synthetic. This was not a browser/Control UI exercise, and no production service or operator state was used.

The tested source was the tracked-clean preceding candidate `de7fed4b39fdfdd5f0b0c736d914533fbbed5e42`, not the current CI-follow-up head. Native preparation reported `build:false` and `runtime:false`, and the effective build/runtime input fingerprints matched that source. The unchanged producer stamps still record precommit producer HEAD `70159c5dc95809b55cb60713a558d871ef08ecad` with `inputsClean:false`. This is supported source-equivalent artifact reuse for that source, not a claim that the artifacts were freshly built at either repaired commit. No new model call accompanied the CI follow-up.

1. **First model attempt: failed, seven HTTP 200 requests.** The trace records real `create_goal`, `sessions_spawn`, one child request, `sessions_yield`, requester return, and later requests containing the automatic Goal nudge, including `update_goal`. The final harness assertion failed. That original capture omitted the exact assertion phase, last public Goal row, and final receipt, and its isolated state was cleaned. Two response-time ordinal labels also overlap. Consequently, neither completed Goal state nor successful final delivery can be inferred, and this trace is not a passing automatic-continuation proof.
2. **One diagnostic attempt: failed, six HTTP 200 requests.** With a real authorized `sessions.messages.subscribe` observer and named assertion diagnostics, the public Goal was `complete`, its continuation count was **0**, and the final marker was caller-visible. One child request and a real yield occurred, but no automatic Goal nudge occurred. The model instead completed the Goal during the requester child-return, contrary to the synthetic task's instruction to leave an unfinished interim phase. It therefore did not exercise the required automatic-continuation case. This is not attributed to a production defect. The client, Gateway, remote I/O, and accounting writes were joined; only stopped synthetic state was retained privately before normal cleanup.

There were **13 physical hosted-model requests**, all HTTP 200 with usage reported: **96,997 input tokens and 1,164 output tokens**. No further model attempt was made. Private credential configuration and account/budget accounting are not part of this public evidence.

The failed artifacts and accounting are retained locally; no public hosted-model proof artifact is claimed. The unmet proof requirements above remain explicit.

Closes #186365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes terminal diagnostics losing known cancellation and timeout causes, making interrupted runs difficult to explain.

## User Impact

Native embedded runs report the initiating user abort, restart, supersession, external signal, runtime abort, intentional yield or timeout when known. Timeouts retain their owner source and attempt phase. These are optional diagnostic fields; cancellation, retry and terminal-status behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the first accepted interruption before callbacks can reenter, independently of later terminal-status refinement. Forward it through normal cleanup and early exit to `run.completed`, stability records and OpenTelemetry spans. Reuse existing run/session/trace correlation and typed owner facts rather than guessing from provider error messages.

Stability recording, saved-bundle readback, support ZIP export and OpenTelemetry use the same closed-enum normalizer, including for untyped JavaScript events. Unknown values are omitted, raw abort reasons are not copied, and duration metric dimensions are unchanged. Small type/projection extractions keep existing oversized files within the repository's growth limits.

## Evidence

- Eight owner/forwarding regressions failed before cause recording. The real automation-yield reproduction also showed the missing cause before the yield-owner repair. The regression injects a conflicting restart at the accepted session-abort handoff and confirms yield remains the initiating cause.

prs.title: fix: exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory indexing and recall signal
prs.body:
Closes #172547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed dreaming output written into daily memory notes under `openclaw:dreaming` fences is embedded, returned by memory search, and staged into short-term recall, even though it is scratchwork that can never be promoted.

Scope confirmation: this branch implements the scope Peter Steinberger set on #172547 on 2026-10-27: "Managed inline dreaming fences should be excluded from default memory retrieval, before chunking." and "@CloudCorpRecords, please go ahead with your branch on that scope."

## User Impact

User impact: memory search and recall signals no longer surface fenced dreaming scratchwork, while ordinary note content keeps its exact citation line numbers and the note files themselves are never modified. Indexes built by earlier versions rebuild once through the existing chunking generation, so already-indexed fenced chunks are reconciled away, and already-staged fenced candidates stay unpromotable through the existing rehydration owner. No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index preparation now blanks managed fenced ranges (blank lines, never deletions, so line numbers stay exact) before chunking, for memory sources only. The fence policy lives in one new owner, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/dreaming-fences.ts`, exported through the host internals and the `memory-core-host-engine-indexing` plugin SDK surface. Promotion rehydration imports the same helpers and its private copy of the fence regexes and overlap logic is deleted, so indexing and promotion cannot drift on what a fence is. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 so the existing reindex owner rebuilds stored indexes instead of a parallel migration.

## Evidence

- New unit tests for the shared module: 12/12 pass (closed, unclosed, mixed, stray-marker, and CRLF cases).
- Index-preparation tests, including two new fence cases (mixed note excluded with original line numbers; fence-only note produces no chunks): 9/9 pass.
- Differential fuzz of the shared overlap helper against the pre-cutover rehydration implementation, transcribed verbatim: 72,871 cases, 0 mismatches (an earlier run of the same comparison covered 235,839 cases, also 0 mismatches).
- Acceptance scenario from the issue thread, exercised at the preparation and promotion-guard boundaries: a synthetic daily note with ordinary facts before and after a managed fence produces no chunk containing fenced text or markers, chunk texts and start/end lines are identical to a pre-blanked control (the after-fence fact still ends at its original line), the source string is unchanged, and the promotion guard refuses the fenced range and both marker lines while admitting the ordinary lines.
- Red/green check: the pre-change path (strip annotation carriers, then chunk) leaks the fenced text into chunks; the new path does not, and keeps the ordinary facts.
- `tsc --strict` on the new module: clean.

Honest limits: the local runs above used a vitest-shim harness because this sandbox cannot install the repo toolchain (pnpm self-install fails here), so the repo's own test suite, typecheck, and lint are CI's to confirm. The full end-to-end pass from the issue (real memory index, search, and promote paths with isolated state and a real local embedding model) was not run locally because no local embedding model is available in this environment; it is a reviewer or CI step, not something claimed here. The branch was brought current with main by a merge commit; conflicts were resolved by reapplying the branch changes at their current locations, and the resulting diff against main is exactly the 8 intended files.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the conversation when a stopped first Claude CLI turn has no operator authority
prs.body:
Related: #181945
Follow-up to #181966

## What problem this solves

Stopping the first Claude CLI turn still clears its native conversation when the run has no operator model authority. The stopped-first-turn guard from #181966 never runs on that branch, so the next turn starts a new native session even though OpenClaw's host history still retains the original user message.

## Fix and user impact

Always pass the existing composed `assertCurrent` into CLI preparation, including runs with neither operator model execution nor a cron generation. The assertion already checks the caller's abort signal, caller assertion, model authority and cron generation in order. Their composition and authority remain unchanged; the existing guarded publication of a stopped first native binding now runs on the ordinary no-operator path too.

Because the caller's own abort reason can now propagate unchanged, trajectory recording also recognizes identity with that run's `abortSignal.reason`, rather than relying only on a generic `AbortError`. This keeps a caller's `TimeoutError` classified as aborted without treating unrelated errors as cancellation by name.

Users can stop a fresh Claude CLI reply and continue the same native conversation on the documented loopback `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` path. Existing authenticated operator behavior is preserved. No new config, permission, SDK surface, store, schema or credential behavior is introduced.

## Evidence

[Independent real-Claude Gateway, native JSONL, provider-history and regression evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186380#issuecomment-6457381257).

- Main: `591b7795fe8b64aba2b84ee5764534da545b3869`.
- Runtime candidate: `897c0cb639ee5eccf02baf09cf9aae58847b60ba`.
- Final head: `cfc8bb94a9633f5bfa25e6c8904e7b1c83ec8759`; only test consolidation follows the runtime build, so production source is identical.
- Full builds succeeded for both refs inside secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. The **genuine Claude Code 2.1.312 CLI** runs non-root with task-owned native homes, workspaces, Gateway profiles and state. No real Anthropic credentials, personal Claude login, stub CLI, seeded database or fabricated native ID is used.

Public WebSocket `sessions.create` → first `chat.send` with a unique marker → actual native exec tool work (`sleep 3`) and a flushed native assistant checkpoint → hold the following real Messages stream → `chat.abort` → follow-up `chat.send`. The external Messages fixture derives its follow-up answer from the actual received history, not the selected ref or an unconditional marker response.

| Case | Native conversation ID | Original marker in actual follow-up provider history | Public reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main, auth:none, run 1 | changed | absent | `UNKNOWN` |
| Main, auth:none, run 2 | changed | absent | `UNKNOWN` |
| Candidate, auth:none, run 1 | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Candidate, auth:none, run 2 | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Main, authenticated operator control | unchanged | present | original marker |
| Candidate, authenticated operator control | unchanged | present | original marker |

All six public host histories retain the original first user message unchanged. Native IDs are independently matched between Claude's actual JSONL files and the real Messages request metadata. The requests identify their client as `claude-cli/2.1.312 (external, sdk-cli)`.

Focused tests: **19/19 pass** across the stopped-partial-output and trajectory owners. The same no-operator case fails on main with `clearCliSessionBinding:true`; the caller-timeout case fails on main with generic `AbortError` instead of its original `TimeoutError`. Targeted type-aware Oxlint: **0 warnings / 0 errors**. Oxfmt passes on all four changed files.

The no-operator case now shares the existing stopped-first-turn table, preserving flushed/unflushed, refused-write, superseded and resumed controls. Both disabled-trajectory controls remain in a shared table. Whole-PR production delta **+6/-2**; test delta **+50/-55 (net −5)**. No test ceiling change.

### Scope and limits

The real-flow proof covers normal loopback WebSocket chat and authenticated operator controls through the actual Claude runtime against a deterministic local Messages fixture, not Anthropic's real service. Other non-operator ingresses share the runner branch but were not live-tested here. Other native CLI backends were not exercised end to end.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous checkpoint behavior without migrations or stored-data rewrites. Blast radius is shared CLI run checkpoints and CLI trajectory cancellation classification; an incorrect assertion could reject a valid CLI turn or mishandle its stopped binding. Existing caller/authority guards and stopped/resumed/timeout controls remain intact.

## What Problem This Solves

The database-worker ratchet can spend minutes analyzing source without showing which owner phase is active.

## User Impact

The trace reports wall time since main began, excluding module imports and the eager analyzer signature. Native compiler counters are cumulative per API instance: requests, round-trip/server wall time, bytes and AST counts. They are not CPU or peak-memory measurements. prs.title: fix: Muse requests stall or lose approval authority after reuse
prs.body:
Closes #183672
Related: #183282 (independent compaction fallback repair).

## What Problem This Solves

Muse requests can time out behind retained native work, replay an earlier answer into a new reply, or fail with `missing scope: operator.approvals` after reusing a process created by a narrower caller.

## User Impact

Status requests can join native work and receive its current answer. Approval requests use the current admitted caller while preserving genuine System scope limits and revoked-owner checks. Stopping an observation of earlier work detaches that observation; turns started by the current request retain normal cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `ifBusy: "steer"` and the SDK's authoritative started/joined identity. Observe real native tool progress, keep historical items out of the current reply, and fence publication after asynchronous transcript append.

Install approvals before resume traffic and bind each new handler to its prepared attempt context. Pooled stdio callbacks otherwise inherit the process creator's async context. Keep authority checks before host approval and native decisions, cancel pending approval UI when observation ends, and retire a failed SDK projection so a fresh owner can recover the same native session and approval stage.

This keeps approval handling in the harness and transcript/result projection in its existing event owner. No provider, dependency, configuration, permission-policy, or transcript-schema changes.

## Evidence

Validation ran on an isolated macOS arm64 host with Node 24.22.1, task-owned state, and the package-pinned SDK. Tested and committed source files were verified byte for byte.

Current head `da67db5d0bfc054fddaf142d884afd2af5209c13` integrates main `d4ae3a73118767a3f9bf80625a91733d19055393`. Its only conflict was the controlled MSP test helper; the resolution preserves both the native approval-effect controls and upstream helper simplifications. The Muse production harness, event owner, and process pool remain byte-identical to the native-tested parent `15457a3a`. All 60,327 tracked candidate blobs matched the isolated Gronk checkout. The 73 controlled tests, focused source and package-boundary typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and independent conflict-resolution review passed again against the integrated source and frozen current-main lockfile. The maintained lint owner prepared the SDK boundary declarations; no core/app build or additional real-model run was performed.

Parent and integrated-head evidence:

- **73 canonical tests passed:** the four non-live Muse suites (71) plus two real-SDK pooled-context regressions. These cover reply/history isolation, joined abort/timeout, native settlement lifetime, resume-time approval replay, deferred transcript publication, offered refusal safety, and completed-first history.
- The pooled-context regression failed before the fix with the exact missing-scope error. After the fix, one physical peer serves both attempts, approval dispatch carries the current run identity, and exactly one offered approval decision produces the native filesystem effect. The inverse control keeps full admitted authority under a genuinely narrow current System frame and verifies denial with no effect.
- Existing real-SDK controls verify that detached or revoked observations cannot make a native approval decision or effect, and that a fresh owner recovers the same pending stage. Their late-request barrier is causal. Tool-progress fixtures likewise wait for production observation rather than a fixed sleep.
- Package and focused regression typechecks, changed-file typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent P0–P2 source review and structured autoreview found no blocking defects. The final equivalent factory capture location received a focused caller-chain review; review did not substitute for test execution.

Captured controlled-fixture results:

```text
uses the current full approval owner after reusing a pooled native peer: PASS
uses the current narrow approval owner after reusing a pooled native peer: PASS
Tests  2 passed (2)
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  71 passed (71)
```

A matching operator compatibility port also passed a real isolated public Gateway approval-manager flow using SDK 1.4.2 and a controlled MSP peer: narrow warmup → full approval produced a final reply through the same physical host; full warmup → narrow caller remained denied. Its 28 regression controls passed. This is compatibility-port acceptance, not canonical SDK 1.4.10 native-provider/busy-turn qualification.

Real native-provider authority evidence was also captured on exact head `15457a3aebf4124de78ade51d6d478e31ee3e95c`: SDK 1.4.10, official Muse 1.4.13-R6996.1, Meta provider, Node 24.22.1/macOS arm64, and the published declared-compatible OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.3 host. The selected Muse target was built without changing minHost/compatibility metadata; this was not an all-main Gateway build. Native permissions used task-only `:ask-me`, with exact prehashed effects confined to the owned sandbox workspace.

- A genuine narrow warmup followed by a full current owner reused the same physical native host. One public plugin approval and one offered allow decision produced the exact owned effect after resolution.
- A separate native conversation on that same pool was warmed by a full owner, then resumed by a client negotiated with only `operator.read` and `operator.write`. Its real native approval request failed closed: one offered abort decision, zero allow decisions, zero plugin approval events, and no effect after all owned processes ended. The missing-scope Gateway diagnostic was fenced to that admitted run.
- The inverse runner's original **FAIL remains preserved**: `agent.wait` returned `error: "agent run failed"` without the detailed scope string its assertion required. Independent scoped adjudication accepted the authority behavior from the matched wire, run, diagnostic, and filesystem evidence; the runner was not relabeled green.

Captured redacted native result:

```json
{
  "head": "15457a3a",
  "sdk": "1.4.10",
  "samePhysicalPooledHost": true,
  "fullOwnerApprovedEffect": true,
  "narrowOwner": {
    "nativeAbort": 1,
    "nativeAllow": 0,
    "pluginApprovalEvents": 0,
    "effectAbsent": true
  },
  "originalInverseRunnerPassed": false,
  "scopedAuthorityAdjudication": "accepted"
}
```

The real-SDK controlled subprocess tests remain the evidence for busy-turn, cancellation, detached/revoked-owner, and same-stage recovery behavior. Real-native busy-resume, joined Stop, detached/revoked-owner, and same-stage recovery qualification remains outstanding. Maintainer direction on joined-work Stop, timeout, and reset semantics also remains outstanding; the native authority evidence does not resolve those lifecycle or merge-readiness gaps.

Move context-independent Workboard schemas to their defining modules. Each factory still creates execution closures for the current store and caller; the existing finalizer owns detached publication and reuse. This removes repeated TypeBox construction without introducing a memo, invalidation policy, or changes to finalization semantics.

prs.title: fix: default cron retries leave time for model fallback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default same-model retries can consume an entire cron execution budget before a configured fallback gets a turn. A stalled hosted provider behind a local relay can repeatedly hit its 60-second stream watchdog and exhaust a 180-second job.

Related: #183287. Follow-up to the landed watchdog fix #183637; thanks to @tommyjoseph for investigating the relay and exposing this retry-budget interaction.

## User Impact

Bounded runs with an eligible, replay-safe fallback stop admitting default embedded-provider retries once half of the candidate's nominal run budget has elapsed. Explicit retry counts and provider/session request timeouts, native harnesses, final/no-fallback candidates, unlimited runs, and output-limit continuations retain their existing behavior.

An admitted request keeps its timeout. This gives the first fallback an opportunity; it does not guarantee a minimum runtime or divide time across every candidate in a longer fallback chain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing retry window starts at the first failure, excluding the initial stalled request. The retry controller now also checks elapsed run time before waiting for another same-model attempt. It consumes the attempt owner's explicit-timeout fact rather than re-reading configuration. Declaring the existing model request-timeout field also removes an unsafe assertion.

Main is merged through `14081a8c8b31b8aa9ef89eb2725710a7b25c4852`. The watchdog change is already on main; this PR's net diff contains only the retry-budget repair, its callers/tests, and documentation. The earlier skills-policy CI failure was main red introduced by #186306 and fixed by `8828adca7e5877faac3bea151b98c438368a4e3d`, which is included.

## Evidence

- Baseline: isolated Gateway cron, localService-managed relay, `remote: true`, default retries, real Ollama `qwen3:8b` fallback: three primary requests, no fallback, timeout at **180.190s** (CLI 182.761s).
- Fresh merged-head proof: two primary streams stalled for **60.019s** and **60.012s**, then real `qwen3:8b` returned **FALLBACK_OK**. Cron succeeded in **128.186s**, leaving 51.814s in the budget (CLI 133.785s).
- The relay was warmed through a normal Gateway request so the cron endpoint preflight reached a running managed service. An initial cold-endpoint preflight fallback was excluded from retry proof. Primary streams are deterministic HTTP/SSE; fallback is real inference on macOS arm64.
- Earlier explicit-timeout control: a configured 3s provider timeout remained in force; retries continued past half of a 30s job and hit its outer deadline at 30.115s. The retry controller, attempt timeout metadata, result types, and watchdog implementation are byte-identical on the merged head. Main's replay-normalization change is covered by the fresh live run.
- The owner regression failed on the original retry behavior. Merged-head focused proof: **201 tests passed** (173 retry/recovery, 15 DashScope integration, 13 model-progress), 447.92s wall including cold compilation.
- Full build passed (889.48s). Core and all three affected test typecheck lanes, scoped lint, formatting, and all eight ratchets passed. The test-line gate passes under non-growth; no ceiling increase. Fresh independent Codex review: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings.

Production +27/-5 (net +22); tests +83/-92 (net -9); retry docs +2 and a shrinking assertion baseline. Added production code supplies the bounded-admission condition and timeout provenance required to preserve overrides.

Accepted proof limitation: no latest-stable upgrade scenario. This PR changes no configuration schema or persisted state. No changelog or model-facing prompt changes.
