Closes #186333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Microsoft Teams stops applying the allowlists it resolved at startup after any config reload that does not restart the Teams channel (for example `agents.defaults.userTimezone`), until the channel restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: senders listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` or `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>`, and `teams` entries that startup resolved from names to IDs, keep working after unrelated config reloads. Editing `channels.msteams` behaves as before: with the default hot reload it applies right away and restarts the Teams channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

At startup the monitor projects `allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom` and `teams` to stable IDs (provider prefixes stripped, names resolved through Graph, unresolvable lists matching nothing since #184989) and hands that projection to the handler. The handler config reader (`monitor-handler/config.ts`, from #112811) follows the runtime config so allowlist edits apply before a restart, but after any reload it returned the raw configuration for these fields.

The reader now reuses the startup projection while the account's allowlist inputs (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `teams`, `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`) are unchanged. When one of them changes it returns the live configuration exactly as before; with config hot reload in its default `hybrid` mode that edit also restarts the Teams channel (its reload prefix is `channels.msteams`), which resolves the lists again. Accepted edge, not coded around: between an allowlist edit and that restart, the edited values apply as written, as on main today.

This is the reload path #184989 described under "Boundary decisions requested" (2): a name-keyed team beside `"*"` no longer falls through to `"*"` after a reload. With `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`, behavior after a reload now matches startup: names that resolved stay IDs, and display names are not matched again while the four allowlist inputs stay unchanged.

Production change: one file, +30/-2; tests +176. The access-control bullet on startup name resolution now matches the code (user names resolve only with `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`; names that do not resolve are not used for routing) and says when the mapping is refreshed.

## Evidence

- **RED / GREEN at the owning boundary** (`monitor.lifecycle.test.ts`, real monitor startup with Graph resolution mocked): on base `9a0458cf695` the new cases fail at the intended assertions (after the reload the handler gets `user:40a1…`, `msteams:user:50a1…`, the `Product` / `Roadmap` name keys and `"Alice"` instead of the startup IDs): 4 failed / 34 passed. With the fix: 38 passed. The cases cover the default account, a named account and a named account inheriting root lists, and check that an edit to `allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `teams` or the name-matching flag applies before the restart; a mutant that drops any one input from the comparison, compares the raw account entry instead of the merged one, or skips the removed-section guard fails them.
- **Real Gateway, main twice vs this branch twice** (`pnpm openclaw qa msteams`: bundled Teams plugin, loopback Bot Framework connector, mock model). Each scenario sets the allowlist, gets a reply, applies an `agents.defaults.userTimezone` patch, then sends again:

| After the `agents.defaults.userTimezone` hot reload | main `9a0458cf695`, runs 1 / 2 | this branch, runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM sender listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` | no reply / no reply | `QA-MSTEAMS-RELOAD-AFTER-OK` / same |
| Group-chat sender listed as `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>` (`groupPolicy: "allowlist"`) | no reply / no reply | `QA-MSTEAMS-GROUP-RELOAD-AFTER-OK` / same |

On main every run answers the probe before the reload and times out after it (`timed out after 60000ms`). The main Gateway log shows the allowlist patch restarting the Teams channel (`restarting msteams channel`, `starting account (reason: config-reload)`) and the timezone patch applied as `config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.userTimezone)` without a Teams restart. The two scenario files are local QA flows, not part of this PR.

- **Rejections after the reload, and an allowlist edit while a message is pending** (same harness, main twice vs this branch twice; "no dispatch" counts `message dispatch completed` per conversation in each run's Gateway log, "no reply" is a 25 s window with no outbound activity):

| Scenario | main `9a0458cf695`, runs 1 / 2 | this branch, runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM sender not in `allowFrom` (it lists `user:<other-aad-object-id>`); group-chat sender listed as `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>` | unlisted DM: no reply and no dispatch before and after the reload; listed group sender: answered before, no reply after / same | unlisted DM: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed group sender: answered before and after / same |
| Group-chat sender not in `groupAllowFrom` (it lists `msteams:user:<other-aad-object-id>`); DM sender listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` | unlisted group sender: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed DM sender: answered before, no reply after / same | unlisted group sender: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed DM sender: answered before and after / same |
| A listed DM sender's second DM waits in a 15 s inbound debounce; an `allowFrom` edit that keeps the sender lands before it flushes | pending DM answered after the Teams channel restart / same | same / same |
| Same, but the edit removes the sender | pending DM: no reply for 45 s, no model request; a listed group sender is still answered / same | same / same |

The two pending-DM rows are identical on main and this branch: an allowlist edit uses the live configuration exactly as before, and the kept-sender row shows the restart does not drop the pending message, so the removed-sender row is the edit taking effect.

- **Removal during message preparation** (`message-handler.authz.test.ts`, two new cases): the handler is wired like the monitor (raw configuration plus the account-scoped startup projection), an unrelated reload comes first so admission uses the retained startup allowlists, the Graph thread fetch is held, and the team or the channel is removed from `teams` before it resolves. The message is dropped (`dropping message (dispatch-time account authorization changed)`) and nothing is dispatched. The file passes 36/36; a mutant that keeps the startup allowlists after an edit fails exactly these two cases.

- **Upgrade from 2026.10.8, the latest stable release (dist-swap proxy).** 2026.10.8 predates this regression: its handler keeps the allowlists projected at startup for the life of the channel (the reader from #112811 first shipped in 2026.10.10-beta.1). The published `openclaw` package does not bundle Teams (its `files` list excludes `dist/extensions/msteams/**`); Teams runs from the installed `@openclaw/msteams` npm plugin, so a 2026.10.8 install gets this fix through the plugin update that ships with the release. Each run (twice, Linux x86_64): install `openclaw@2026.10.8` and `@openclaw/msteams@2026.10.8`, store Teams settings (`dmPolicy` / `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, `allowFrom: ["user:<aad-object-id>"]`, `groupAllowFrom: ["msteams:user:<aad-object-id>"]`, `teams` with a `19:...@thread.tacv2` team and channel, a name key and `"*"`), validate, start the Gateway, stop it. Then replace the installed plugin package's files with this branch's `@openclaw/msteams` packed by the release tooling (`scripts/lib/plugin-npm-build-and-pack.mts`), keeping its install record, installed dependencies, configuration and state; start this branch's core from its `npm pack` file list (version set to 2026.10.10 locally so it accepts the 2026.10.8 state) on the same state; set `agents.defaults.userTimezone`.

Both runs, copied from the run output (sha256 prefixes; `<id>` redacted):

```text
openclaw.json sha256 after 2026.10.8 / after the plugin swap / after this branch's Gateway start: b1b6a08782092b8e x3 (run 1), 9c0c482331b37ee1 x3 (run 2)
plugins list, this branch's core: msteams origin=global trust=trusted-official status=loaded rootDir=<state>/npm/projects/openclaw-msteams-<id>/node_modules/@openclaw/msteams
Gateway module loads (Node module.registerHooks load hook): 19 msteams files, all from the Gateway's copy of the installed package, 19/19 byte-identical to the packed branch plugin
[msteams] starting provider account default (Gateway route /api/messages)
[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.userTimezone)
msteams channel: running, connected, lastError null; lastStartAt unchanged across the reload
config keys changed since 2026.10.8: agents.defaults.userTimezone, meta.lastTouchedVersion; channels.msteams identical
```

This is a proxy for the plugin update a release ships, not a published release. The upgraded Gateway receives no Teams traffic (the loopback Bot Framework connector exists only inside `pnpm openclaw qa msteams`), so the allow / deny behavior after the reload is the scenarios above.

- **Suites:** `pnpm test extensions/msteams` (16 + 91 files, 156 + 929 tests), `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files pass. The lifecycle file's test time is under 1 s (23.7 s wall, almost all transform; unchanged by this PR). Unit runs: macOS arm64, Node 24.22.1; Gateway legs: Linux x86_64. Test-lines ceiling: main at `b0961419e46` is already 343 lines over its ceiling (6291661 vs 6291318); this PR adds 176 test lines and raises the ceiling to the tree total, 6291837 (the branch merges current main for that line).
- **Not tested end to end:** Graph-resolved team and user names (the QA connector has no Graph); the lifecycle cases cover them with a mocked resolution. Which Teams monitor drops a message pending across an allowlist edit (the stopping one or the restarted one) is not visible in the Gateway log; the handler cases above cover the dispatch-time check.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse ancestor child contributions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Progress events from one subagent repeatedly checked every sibling for every viewer. A parent with 500 children and 20 viewers performed 10,040 membership reads per event, making busy ancestor broadcasts expensive on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

Large subagent trees require less main-thread CPU and allocation to publish session events. Recipient-visible rows, wire fields, authorization and timestamp refresh behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resident projection now updates child activity and disclosure contributions from the owning row, registry and membership changes. Descendant counts retain individual contributions across clock views. The event presenter consumes those prepared facts instead of scanning all siblings again.

Current runtime ownership, scheduler reservations, clock expiry and rewinds still invalidate the relevant facts. Private rows keep frame-scoped preparation, and deletion, archive demotion and disposal release retained parent state. The changed-parent refresh from #185954 remains intact.

This replaces the repeated sibling loops rather than adding a parallel presentation path. Production LOC grows because exact incremental disclosure and activity require reverse dependencies, bounded audience state, clock deadlines and explicit lifecycle invalidation; a parent-only cache would violate those contracts. Final LOC accounting is below with the measurements.

## Evidence

Acceptance was declared before measurement: membership reads per event independent of 50/150/500 children with 20 distinct viewers, lower main-thread CPU and sampled allocation, and identical normalized payload hashes. The owner harness uses the real lifecycle publisher, resident/prepared rows and recipient delivery planner with synthetic sinks. Timing and allocation are separate, serial AB/BA pairs. Generated ancestor revision IDs are normalized; payload fields are otherwise compared byte-for-byte.

Steady-event measurements compare base `61722900dfe21a411f08325f32943a87571760c9` with reviewed candidate `8844bbf6ff5f`. Subsequent repairs moved the unchanged child calculation and its types to acyclic modules and corrected test/benchmark fixtures. Final head is `20f66c7546a78534392f34e7d25009356ba1b4dd`, rebased onto `b0961419e46b72a7b5e0b5f3fd509b58d1bbfbfc`. The supplemental state pass below verifies byte-identical runtime/support/harness files against this final head. Two serial AB/BA pairs, 1,000 events per arm, 20 distinct viewers; separate untraced timing and sampled-allocation passes. All 24 steady-arm payload digests match across revisions. Clock fixed for reproducibility; advancing-clock behavior has a separate regression. CPU uses `process.threadCpuUsage()` on the main thread.

This is deliberately larger than a memo: the new state replaces repeated sibling derivation while preserving live disclosure, subtree runtime ownership, clock-dependent expiry, archive eviction and frame-private rows. No per-tick coalescing is added, because it would change event ordering; unchanged prepared ancestor contributions and recipient rows are reused instead.

The final counter regression fails on current main `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200` at 1,020 / 3,020 / 10,020 reads for prepared parent rows (limit 40). The candidate passes at all three sizes using valid public viewer policy. Canonical prepared invited-filter proof separately covers membership revoke/regrant, exact visible child rows, and stable exclusion keys after equivalent cycles. A separate clock-advance regression caught and now prevents stale `snapshotAt` when one child finishes while another remains active. Reservation-only queued-grandchild changes and repeated equivalent exclusion states are also covered.

Final focused proof: six files / 91 tests passed (registry queries, run liveness, scheduler, event parity, presentation, sharing policy); eager-import and PR-wrapper closure proof passed 32 tests. Earlier focused prepared-read, lineage, projection, archive and retention tests also passed. Scoped format/lint and export-collision checks passed. Core typechecking passed during implementation. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40608058355) passed on `20f66c7546a78534392f34e7d25009356ba1b4dd`, including production/test types, architecture, baseline ratchets, selected test shards and built-artifact checks. Initial CI found import cycles, invalid stored-status and role fixtures, and the added-test-line ratchet. Those are repaired: fixtures use canonical status/policy owners, shared contracts are acyclic, and repeated fixtures/assertions were consolidated without dropping authority cases. The final ratchet passes with zero net test lines despite main exceeding the raw ceiling. A later test-type check caught an over-specific assertion helper input; it now requires only the `runId` field shared by full and prepared records, without a cast or runtime change.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) is clean after addressing its findings. The requested autoreview provider failed the helper's configured-route preflight; no configuration was changed.

The isolated Gateway fixture failed its premeasurement census. Under the explicitly approved fast path, this PR uses owner proof and focused tests plus CI; it does not claim whole-Gateway GC, event-loop or RPC latency results. No production load was started.

Alternates a child’s canonical `done`/`failed` stored state before each publication. Base `50bb32ef09475b3f91e30ad0d9ec78a2c213a8e8`; candidate runtime/support/harness hashes match final head. prs.title: fix: hide pending tool-call text from channel previews
prs.body:
Fixes #186257.

## What Problem This Solves

Channel previews briefly displayed a plain-text bracket/JSON tool call and its arguments before the completed call was removed. Deleting the preview afterward could not undo what participants had already seen.

## User Impact

Pending call syntax stays out of channel previews while preceding prose keeps streaming. Fenced examples, ordinary JSON, final literal text, and raw/ACP event behavior are preserved. Thanks to @obviyus (Ayaan Zaidi) for the report and reproduction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical call grammar now provides a preview mode that holds candidates from their opening marker, including split headers and adjacent calls. Partial delivery reuses that grammar and its existing Markdown checkpoints. It does not reinterpret prose as executable tools or buffer an entire reply.

This is scoped to the reported bracket/JSON path. A separate existing XML parameter-unwrapping issue can remove structural tags before this boundary; direct function/parameter XML is not claimed fixed here.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the original production code. The real subscriber → real Discord draft-stream → recording REST sinks proof passes all 912 required schedules (every two-chunk split plus 1/2/4-character schedules): baseline leaks in 363 cases; the fix leaks in none. All 3,476 required-case REST operations were inspected. Raw text/delta/replace/phase and safe-control streaming sequences match baseline. Another 112 direct-XML controls confirm the separately documented inherited limitation. Latest matrix: 12.402s total, 0.548s after imports, on macOS.

The full 64-file owner suites pass before and after test consolidation: 1,285/1,285 in 178.18s, then 1,291/1,291 in 138.12s. All 11 preview regression cases remain, and 1,273 expanded names are unchanged. The other 12 names map to 18 equivalent table cases: eight API-expanded XML work checks, three reasoning-privacy checks, and one GLM loop exposed as seven independent cases. Every prior behavioral assertion remains covered. Shared Responses/delivery fixtures and existing event helpers remove repeated setup; no production or baseline change was needed for the consolidation.

The built Gateway qa-channel fixture fails before readiness on the existing private `openclaw/plugin-sdk/qa-channel-protocol` import, so channel proof uses the owned mock boundary above. `pnpm build` passes (467.15s). A real CLI → isolated Gateway → Ollama `qwen3:8b` natural-output control passes (55.30s total; one assistant turn, no tools or fallback). Build and live proof ran on production-identical parent `7f615971626`; all later edits are test-only.

Scoped type-aware lint (84.67s), agents-root/state-logging test types (90.79s), formatting, all nine aggregate baseline checks (192.42s), and the separate line-cap ratchet pass. The former test-line CI failure is addressed: the complete PR now adds zero net test lines, without raising the ceiling or removing any behavioral fact.

Independent Codex branch review is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings on head `2a3b07a00a35cea1e746a6a9a55833496a425b25`. Exact-head [CI run 40603130472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40603130472) passes, including the baseline ratchets and `openclaw/ci-gate`. [ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186375#issuecomment-6456029459): no findings and no Before merge items; ready for maintainer review. Its remaining proof-only note is the documented built Gateway-to-channel gap above; the explicitly allowed owned channel boundary proof is used. CI has passed since that review.

Production: +71/-15 lines (net +56). Tests: +372/-372 lines (net 0). The production addition is one projection per preview scope, using the existing parser/checkpoint owner.

prs.title: feature(channels): add channels start|stop|reconnect for existing Gateway RPCs
prs.body:
Implements #183098

## What Problem This Solves

Docs already prescribe `channels.stop` / `channels.start` for non-destructive per-account recovery (keep pairing/credentials; crash-loop safe-mode manual override), but operators must hand-craft `openclaw gateway call` JSON. The channels CLI has list/status/login/logout/dead-letters but no first-class start/stop.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw channels stop|start|reconnect --channel <id> [--account <id>] --json` wraps the existing Gateway RPCs. Blank `--account` fails closed. Unknown channel fails closed. Prefer these over `gateway call`. Distinct from `channels logout` (clears credentials) and `gateway restart` (whole process).

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapters under the **existing** `channels` tree only: forward validated params (including Gateway `--port`/`--url`) to `channels.start` / `channels.stop`, update recovery docs and the crash-loop manual-start hint, and keep Gateway semantics unchanged. No new Gateway methods, schema, or permissions.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/channels/start-stop.ts`, `src/cli/channels-cli.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts` (+ tests), `docs/cli/channels.md`, `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`, `docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
- Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/channels/start-stop.test.ts` — **6 passed**; `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.test.ts` hint cases — **19 passed**
- Packaged CLI e2e below on local Gateway with Telegram accounts

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw channels start|stop|reconnect` that call existing `channels.start` / `channels.stop`; stop/start must return Gateway `stopped` / `started`+`outcome`; blank `--account` and unknown channel must fail closed; status probe remains available after recovery.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw channels stop|start|reconnect` → `channelsStopCommand` / `channelsStartCommand` / `channelsReconnectCommand` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("channels.stop"|"channels.start", …)` → `src/gateway/server-methods/channels.ts`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `addGatewayClientOptions`, `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport`, and `parseAccountSelector`. Does not own channel lifecycle; reuses existing Gateway account start/stop owners (same path login already uses for `channels.start`).

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI after `qaRuntime` build on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run --port 18821` with token auth; Telegram channel enabled with fake BotFather tokens (accounts `default` + `proof`).

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node openclaw.mjs channels stop --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account proof --port 18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels reconnect --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels status --channel telegram --probe --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account "" --json   # blank reject
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel definitely-not-a-channel --url … --json
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# channels --help lists start / stop / reconnect
  start         Start one channel account runtime without re-authenticating (channels.start)
  stop          Stop one channel account runtime without clearing credentials (channels.stop)
  reconnect     Stop then start one channel account (non-destructive reconnect)

# stop (exit 0)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "stopped": true
}

# start --url … (exit 0)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "started": true,
  "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
}

# start --port 18821 … (exit 0) — same started/outcome shape
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "started": true,
  "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
}

# reconnect (exit 0)
{
  "stop": { "channel": "telegram", "accountId": "proof", "stopped": true },
  "start": {
    "channel": "telegram",
    "accountId": "proof",
    "started": true,
    "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
  }
}

# status --probe after recovery (exit 0) — probe present; running reflects lifecycle
# (fake token → probe 401 Unauthorized; recovery path exercised)

# blank --account (exit 1)
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "--account must not be blank" } }

# unknown channel (exit 1)
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "invalid channels.start channel" } }

# unconfigured account (Gateway semantics: exit 0, started:false skipped/unconfigured)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "definitely-missing-acct",
  "started": false,
  "outcome": { "status": "skipped", "reason": "unconfigured" }
}
```

## Notes for reviewers

- Extends existing `channels` CLI tree (not a new top-level namespace).
- Crash-loop recovery hint now points at `openclaw channels start --channel …` instead of `gateway call`.
- AI-assisted. Maintainers can edit.

prs.title: fix: show agent avatars with streamed responses
prs.body:
Fixes #186026.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent avatars appear only after streamed replies finish, although the response text is already visible and the identity is known.

## User Impact

The existing agent avatar appears with the first streamed text. Text continues immediately and uses the same identity and image-loading behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A live run frame starts with no finalized messages. An empty list passed the voice-transcript-only check and suppressed its avatar. Require a nonempty list for that check, preserving genuine voice-only groups.

The change adds one production guard and extends the existing streaming test. There are no new test cases, presentation state, identity requests, or caches.

## Evidence

- All 8 streaming E2E cases and 13 message-group unit cases pass; the streaming regression is red on the base. UI/chat-E2E types, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Exact-head CI [40526123739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40526123739) passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of `43dc38e6..e384668b` is scoped-clean for P0–P2. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; its existing hosted review of this exact head also found no code issues.

## Real Gateway verification

Reproduced with an isolated real Gateway and live model. The frontend baseline is current `main` at `591b7795fe8`; the comparison uses that same tree with only this PR's production guard. The Gateway was unchanged between runs.

The cold case held delivery of the real `agent.identity.get` response until the first streamed text was visible. The warm case reused the delivered identity. Chat frames and identity payloads were forwarded unchanged; no DOM or styling was injected.

| Scenario | Main: avatar visible during streaming | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity response still pending at first text | 0 / 616 sampled frames | 588 / 588, including first text |
| Identity already loaded | 0 / 736 sampled frames | 644 / 644, including first text |

The first text appeared while the identity response was still held. The existing fallback appeared immediately with the fix; text continued normally when identity was released and through completion. These runs verify ordering, not model response speed.

prs.title: fix(imessage): use a PostgreSQL-safe recovery cursor key
prs.body:
Closes #184862

## What Problem This Solves

With the `state` database family on PostgreSQL, the iMessage channel exits on every start: the recovery cursor's plugin-state key is `` `${accountId}\^@${dbIdentity}` ``, and PostgreSQL plugin state rejects NUL in keys (`assertPluginStateKey`, `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT`). The Gateway auto-restarts the channel until it gives up. SQLite stores NUL inside TEXT, so SQLite installs never hit it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `recoveryCursorStoreKey()` now returns `sha256(JSON.stringify([accountId, dbIdentity])).hex.slice(0, 32)`, the same 32-hex shape `state-contract.ts` uses for the catchup-cursor and reply-cache keys. I chose a hash over another separator because it has no character-set or length concerns (`dbIdentity` is a filesystem path or a remote host plus path, and keys are capped at 512 bytes), and because the JSON array encoding keeps distinct `(account, identity)` pairs distinct. A hashed key can match the legacy account-only key only if an account id equals the hash of its own pair.
- The one-time adoption of the legacy account-only key (`consume(accountId)` → `registerIfAbsent`) and the retired catchup-cursor migration are unchanged.
- SQLite installs may already hold a cursor under the old NUL key. On a miss under the new key, the cursor namespace is listed (`entries()`, bounded by `maxEntries: 64`). If the old composite key for this `(account, identity)` is present, it is consumed and re-registered under the new key once, through the same adoption path. The old key is never passed to `lookup`/`consume` unless `entries()` returned it. Nothing on PostgreSQL can return it, so PostgreSQL never sees a NUL key operation, and the plugin does not need to detect the engine or catch the validation error. Swallowing the error would hide real read failures; #175442 deliberately surfaces those.

## User Impact

The iMessage channel starts and stays up on a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway. SQLite users keep their existing high-water mark across the upgrade.

## Evidence

**Discriminating test (real PostgreSQL):** `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts`. It selects PostgreSQL for the `state` family (same harness shape as `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/account-state.postgres.test.ts`), then loads, advances and reloads the cursor through the iMessage plugin runtime. It is registered in `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` and the extension database-workers lane.

Base (`71eacdfe9b5`, source change reverted, test kept):
```
 FAIL  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts > iMessage recovery cursor on PostgreSQL state > loads, advances, and reloads the cursor at channel start (#184862)
AssertionError: promise rejected "PluginStateStoreError: PostgreSQL plugin … { …(3) }" instead of resolving
Caused by: PluginStateStoreError: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
 ❯ assertPluginStateKey src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.kernel.ts:125:11
 ❯ readRecoveryCursor extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.ts:130:29
Serialized Error: { code: 'PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT', operation: 'lookup', ... }
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```
Head:
```
 ✓  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts > iMessage recovery cursor on PostgreSQL state > loads, advances, and reloads the cursor at channel start (#184862)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```
SQLite adoption of the old NUL key is covered by a new case in `recovery-cursor.test-support.ts` (a different database does not inherit the cursor, the active one adopts it once, and the NUL entry is consumed). The existing unit cases now seed the new key.

**Real product: isolated Gateway on PostgreSQL** (`state` and `agent` families on PostgreSQL 17, fresh state after `doctor --fix`, imessage plugin enabled, one account with `cliPath` = Homebrew `imsg` and `dbPath` = a read-only copy of a Messages `chat.db`; `dmPolicy`/`groupPolicy` `disabled`; nothing was sent).

Base build (`71eacdfe9b5`):
```
[gateway] http server listening (3 plugins: anthropic, imessage, memory-core; 2.3s)
[imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
[imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
[imessage] [default] channel exited: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
[imessage] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
...
[imessage] [default] channel exited: PostgreSQL plugin state keys cannot contain NUL characters.
[imessage] [default] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 21s
```
Head build, same config and fresh state, watched for 2 min 40 s:
```
11:42:36 [gateway] http server listening (3 plugins: anthropic, imessage, memory-core; 3.0s)
11:42:37 [imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
11:42:38 [imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
(no "channel exited" / "auto-restart" lines through 11:45:16)

$ openclaw channels status
Gateway reachable.
- iMessage default: enabled, configured, running, connected
```

**Real product: SQLite upgrade from the latest stable release.** The released `openclaw@2026.10.7` (npm, `157d8c2`) builds the same `` `${accountId}\^@${dbIdentity}` `` key. Setup: isolated state on SQLite (no `database` section), the same iMessage account and policies, and `cliPath` pointing at a small wrapper that appends the JSON-RPC requests sent to `imsg` to a log and then execs the real `imsg`. That shows the `since_rowid` each build subscribes from. chat.db `MAX(ROWID)` was 16535 throughout.

1. 2026.10.7 first start, no cursor: `watch.subscribe {"since_rowid":16535}`.
2. Gateway stopped. One cursor row inserted in the format 2026.10.7 writes (key `default` + NUL + `local:<snapshot>/chat.db`, 53 bytes; `{"lastRowid":16530}`). Nothing new had arrived, so 2026.10.7 had no inbound row to advance it. Restarting 2026.10.7 consumed the row as its own cursor:
   ```
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16530}}
   [imessage] suppressed stale inbound backlog account=default ... recovery=true (5 suppressed since start)
   ```
   2026.10.7 then advanced and persisted its NUL-keyed row itself: `plugin_state_entries` → `53 bytes | has NUL | {"lastRowid":16535}`.
3. Upgrade to this PR's build on that same state. 2026.10.7 installs iMessage as a managed npm plugin in the state dir, so I ran `openclaw plugins uninstall imessage --force` (plugin state rows are kept) and put back the identical config, so that the bundled iMessage plugin from this branch loads (`plugins list`: imessage, source = the branch `extensions/imessage`).
   ```
   [imessage] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
   [imessage] [default] starting provider (<imsg wrapper> db=<snapshot>/chat.db)
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16535}}
   plugin_state_entries (imessage.recovery-cursor): 32 bytes | no NUL | 4749f4dc428df92860bc9f5f54542742 | {"lastRowid":16535}
   ```
   The NUL row 2026.10.7 wrote is gone. Its value is now under `sha256(JSON.stringify(["default","local:<snapshot>/chat.db"]))[:32]`.
4. To make the replay position distinguishable from the no-cursor default (the watermark), the cursor was set back to the step-2 value. The Gateway was stopped, and the namespace was replaced with the 53-byte NUL-keyed `{"lastRowid":16530}` row from step 2. Then this PR's build was started:
   ```
   {"method":"watch.subscribe","params":{...,"since_rowid":16530}}
   plugin_state_entries (imessage.recovery-cursor): 32 bytes | no NUL | 4749f4dc...2742 | {"lastRowid":16535}
   ```
   The build subscribes from 16530, the adopted cursor, not 16535. It consumes the NUL row and advances the hashed row after the replay. 2026.10.7 subscribed from 16530 with the same row in step 2. No `channel exited` or `auto-restart` lines in any run.

**Other checks:** `extensions/imessage` tests pass except `monitor.plugin-payload.test.ts > settles rich-link final delivery ... (true)`, which fails the same way on unmodified base on this machine. The red `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` job ([run 40382310876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40382310876/job/121782242862)) is that same case (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once with arguments: [ 'send', ... ]`). It reproduces deterministically on base `71eacdfe9b5` with every change in this PR stashed, so I attribute it to main, not to this change. I could not re-run the job (it needs admin rights). `extension-test-plan`, `database-conformance` and the doctor-contract guard tests pass. Format and the extension typecheck in `pnpm check:changed` pass. Its remaining failures (oxlint in `extensions/copilot`, `extensions/knowledge`, `extensions/qa-lab`, `extensions/workboard`; dead export `PROJECT_CHECKOUT_WAIT_MS`) are in files this PR does not touch.

## Not measured

- No message was admitted during the real-Gateway run (DM and group policy were disabled and nothing was sent), so the Gateway run proves the startup load path, not a live cursor advance on PostgreSQL. The PostgreSQL test covers advance and reload.
- In the SQLite upgrade run, the 16530 cursor was inserted directly into SQLite while 2026.10.7 was stopped, because no new message arrived during the test. 2026.10.7 then consumed it and wrote 16535 itself. I did not test an upgrade where both a NUL-keyed cursor and a pre-database-scoping account-only cursor exist. In that case the NUL-keyed one is adopted, and the account-only one stays as on current main.
- I ran only the new test against PostgreSQL, not the full `test-database-conformance.mjs` suite. Its catalog pre-check needs a role privilege that the local test role lacks.

prs.title: fix: keep dictation settings from changing the chat model
prs.body:
Related: #185817. Thanks @tre1d for the report and clarification.

## What Problem This Solves

When dictation is unavailable, its **Configure** action opens general model setup. Continuing with a discovered local model can replace the agent's default chat model during a dictation settings task.

## User Impact

Dictation **Configure** now opens the existing Talk settings page without entering chat-model activation. Explicit model setup remains available from the chat model controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer wired the dictation action to `model-setup`. Route it to the existing voice settings owner (`talk`), with a regression covering dictation, Talk, and explicit model setup destinations. No new config or activation/rollback behavior is introduced. The existing Talk page remains the voice settings home; this change does not add a dedicated transcription setup wizard.

## Evidence

- Base `d45ff6de6c48`, isolated macOS Gateway + real Control UI: Dictation → Configure → Models → On this Gateway → use the discovered LM Studio fixture changed `agents.entries.main.model.primary` from `ollama/qwen3:8b` to `lmstudio/dictation-fixture-chat`. The captured RPC was `openclaw.setup.activate.start` with `kind: provider-auto:lmstudio` and no dictation scope. Wizard completed; browser flow took 23.447 s.
- Real local-model control: `pnpm openclaw --profile dictation-setup agent --agent main --message 'Reply with the single word OK. Do not use tools.' --thinking off --json` returned `OK` through the Gateway on `ollama/qwen3:8b` (11.553 s model run).
- Regression failed on the base at the dictation destination and passes with the fix. Focused pane + microphone suites: 16 tests passed; new regression 97 ms, total wrapper wall time 82.46 s including cold transforms. The three fixture-consolidation suites also passed (42 tests, 78.57 s wrapper). UI typecheck passed (8.60 s); scoped formatting passed.

- Head on the rebuilt isolated Gateway: Dictation Configure opened `/settings/talk` in 5.809 s, emitted zero setup RPCs, and preserved both global and main-agent primaries at `ollama/qwen3:8b`. A real Qwen control turn again returned `OK` (10.123 s model run; 25.42 s CLI wall time).
- Full production build passed (24m50s); affected lint and UI typecheck passed; formatting, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-exports, config docs, plugin inventory and database ratchets passed. Test-lines passed with a net reduction of 3 lines. Independent Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings through P2.

Before: dictation Configure entered general provider/model setup.

prs.title: fix(auth): tolerate invalid credential symlink targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External JSON credential discovery can abort with ENOTDIR when a credential symlink points beneath a regular file. The shared reader already treats missing targets and cycles as absent; this adds the distinct invalid-directory target case to that same owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep tolerant credential discovery at src/infra/json-file.ts rather than duplicating catches in each consumer. Chained-symlink resolution itself is already supplied by merged #157524; the remaining production change is ENOTDIR handling. Added filesystem regressions retain relative/absolute chains, invalid targets, dangling links and cycles.

## User Impact

An invalid legacy credential target no longer interrupts setup discovery, and readable symbolic links still reach their actual JSON payload. No configuration, default, protocol, schema, dependency, permissions or migration changes. No external authentication success is claimed. Current contribution: 2 files, production +5/-1 (net +4), tests +49/-0. AI-assisted implementation and independent source/proof review.

## Evidence

### Current-head maintenance

- Product head: `a5ed294628460e7b4a6b3d46621a77731ea6c406`; integrated main: `5dce97b1362ff634333c32940aba4f9a1bb477b2`; clean reviewed tree: `d0bd33344e327ff0dc335b467db112b79f94492f`. Original contributor commits are retained; ordinary merge/push, no force-push.
- Repair: Integrated current main while retaining the optional JSON-reader ENOTDIR fix and legal symlink controls. Main’s resolveJsonSaveTarget remains private. The historical CI run failed before creating any jobs/check runs; this integration uses the current workflow but does not invent a failed product test or claim a diagnosed historical workflow root cause.
- Production entry / exact collector command: `node "$HARNESS" "$CHECKOUT" green` (Node 26.12.1, Linux, isolated HOME/config/state; no production service).
- Canonical owner: Real authenticated loopback Gateway openclaw.setup.detect -> existing CLI credential discovery -> optional JSON reader and actual realpath filesystem boundary.
- Recorder/readback boundary: Normally built Gateway and public CLI RPC -> strace filesystem observations -> separately read RPC JSON, symlink target, legal payload and sentinel. Invalid credential targets produce ENOTDIR yet detection completes; legal symlink payload is actually opened; invalid repeat confirms no poisoned cache or file mutation.
- Acceptance-red: retain the original baseline executions and SHAs in the historical evidence below. This maintenance reruns GREEN plus controls and does not claim a new baseline run.
- Validation: 31/31 JSON-owner and CLI-credential tests; changed-file type-aware lint/format and fresh independent complete two-file source/test review PASS. Normal cliStartup build completed on a clean exact-head source. Required hosted CI is tracked after publication.
- Acceptance-green / controls: current-head receipt below. Tests/review are separate from runtime proof.
- Cleanup / limitations: collector children exited and owned listeners closed. Synthetic state is retained with its receipt. Only executable --version discovery uses the supplied synthetic Gemini script. No Gemini runtime, provider login/inference, real external channel, other OS or installed-release upgrade. Main integration used Git’s three-tree merge with the GitHub-verified actual common base because local history was shallow; both authentic parents and all original contributor history remain intact.

prs.title: fix(agents): make skill workflow gates override generic execution bias
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #143155

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a prompt-consistency defect where the built system prompt tells the model to read and obey an applicable skill while generic Execution Bias guidance only permits one generic **blocking** decision as a valid non-final-turn stop and pushes `act now` / "no plan-only finish when tools can act". In an observed 2026.9.3 session the agent read the required multi-stage workflow skills and then skipped their explicit prerequisite/decision gates, proceeding with fork sync, branch deletion, and PR creation. The conflicting clauses are still on `main`: `buildSkillsSection` (now in `src/agents/system-prompt-skills.ts`) still says `Up-front max one. Never invent paths.`, and the Execution Bias section in `src/agents/system-prompt.ts` says `advance with tools, or ask one blocking decision.` (#157447 broadened the ask beyond safety-blocking, but it still never names workflow-required decisions or skill-gate precedence).

- Users relying on ordered, multi-stage skills (e.g. development/debug/Git/PR workflows with mandatory human-decision gates) can see premature repository/external actions even after the required skills are successfully read.
- **Related:** #63940 (earlier, broader skill-discovery PR closed unmerged; it did not cover this narrower workflow-consistency repair). No open fixing PR exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded repair rewrites the two prompt clauses so execution guidance advances through applicable workflow prerequisites and decisions instead of reading as permission to skip them. Targeted initial skill selection, `Never invent paths.`, user authority, safety rules, and tool policy are all preserved; no new config, dependency, hook, or enforcement layer is added.

- **Intended outcome:** the Skills section explicitly allows reading another applicable skill when the active workflow requires it, and Execution Bias (a) treats a workflow-required decision as a valid non-final-turn ask, not only a generic blocking one, and (b) states that an applicable skill's explicit workflow gates override generic Execution Bias, while decisions or authorization the user already supplied, safety rules, and tool policy stay authoritative (a bounded precedence rule per ClawSweeper's review recommendation).
- **Out of scope:** removing targeted initial skill selection, mechanical/security enforcement of skill text, docs, CHANGELOG, and any behavior change for sessions without applicable skills.
- **Highest-risk area:** rewording shared prompt guidance that also applies to non-skill requests.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** the generic act-now / continue-to-done bullets are unchanged; only the decision-ask permission and an explicit precedence statement are added, so non-skill behavior is unaffected; negative regression tests pin the old contradictory wording out.

## User Impact

Multi-skill workflow sessions now receive internally consistent guidance: a workflow's explicit prerequisite steps and required decisions count as valid execution progress, and the agent may load another applicable skill mid-workflow without contradicting up-front selection wording.

- **Success criteria:** rendered prompt (production `buildAgentSystemPrompt`) contains the workflow-consistent wording and no longer contains `Up-front max one. Never invent paths.` or `ask one blocking decision.`; focused prompt tests pass on `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/system-prompt-skills.ts` (`buildSkillsSection`), the Execution Bias section of `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`, and the three new regression cases in `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` guarding the new wording and the old contradictory strings.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** local checkout on branch `feat/issue-143155-bug-system-prompt-execution-bias` at `ef3982d35c1` (rebased on `origin/main`), Node v26.7.0.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # RED: new regression cases against unpatched origin/main source (3 failed)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts -t "workflow"
  # GREEN + full targeted validation (format + lint + same-dir tests + tsgo:core)
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/agents/system-prompt.ts src/agents/system-prompt-skills.ts src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts
  # Real behavior proof: drive the PRODUCTION shipped entry point the Gateway/CLI invokes at every
  # agent turn (buildConfiguredAgentSystemPrompt via attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts), with an
  # applicable installed skill workflow recognized, and capture the delivered prompt.
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <proof>/render-prompt.mts
  # Real Gateway wire proof: boot the real built gateway process (dist/index.js from
  # scripts/build-all.mts), install git-pr-workflow into the workspace skill catalog,
  drive one production agent turn through a local OpenAI-Responses-compatible endpoint,
  and capture the outgoing provider request body on the wire. Run once at PR head
  (PROOF_VARIANT=after) and once with the two prompt files reverted to origin/main
  (PROOF_VARIANT=before, dist rebuilt between runs).
  PROOF_VARIANT=after  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <proof>/gateway-skill-prompt-proof.mts
  PROOF_VARIANT=before node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <proof>/gateway-skill-prompt-proof.mts
  ```
- **Real behavior proof (shipped CLI/Gateway entry point, terminal capture):** the production
  config-aware prompt-assembly entry point renders the delivered prompt with an applicable
  `git-pr-workflow` skill present in `<available_skills>`:
  ```text
  ## Skills
  Scan <available_skills> for a matching workflow.
  ...
  Several: most specific. No relevant skill: read none.
  Up-front max one; read another applicable skill when the active workflow requires it. Never invent paths.
  External writes: batch safely; no tight loops; honor 429/Retry-After.
  <available_skills>
    <skill>
      <name>git-pr-workflow</name>
      <location>/home/user/.openclaw/skills/git-pr-workflow.md</location>
    </skill>
  </available_skills>

  ## Execution Bias
  - Actionable request: act now.
  - Requested action with an available tool: do it. Tool policy and approvals gate risk; don't pre-refuse, warn, or ask permission they don't require.
  - Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one decision the applicable workflow requires (a blocking decision always qualifies).
  - Applicable skill workflow gates (prerequisites, required decisions, ordering) override generic Execution Bias; decisions or authorization the user already supplied, safety rules, and tool policy stay authoritative.
  - Continue to done/real blocker; no plan-only finish when tools can act.
  ...
  ```
  Before/after of the same shipped entry point, same input catalog (origin/main vs PR head):
  ```diff
  ## Skills
  - Up-front max one. Never invent paths.
  + Up-front max one; read another applicable skill when the active workflow requires it. Never invent paths.

  ## Execution Bias
  - Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one blocking decision.
  + Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one decision the applicable workflow requires (a blocking decision always qualifies).
  + Applicable skill workflow gates (prerequisites, required decisions, ordering) override generic Execution Bias; decisions or authorization the user already supplied, safety rules, and tool policy stay authoritative.
  ```
- **Real Gateway wire proof (shipped gateway process, terminal capture):** a real OpenClaw gateway
  process (built `dist/index.js`, the shipped gateway entrypoint; repo e2e instance launcher) was
  booted with the `git-pr-workflow` skill installed in its workspace skill catalog, and ONE
  production agent turn was driven through the gateway (`agent` RPC) with the provider pointing at
  a local OpenAI-Responses-compatible endpoint. The endpoint captured the outgoing provider
  request body on the wire; the system prompt the shipped gateway handed the model is analyzed
  exactly as captured. Same harness, same config, same installed skill catalog for both runs; the
  only difference is the two patched prompt files (`dist` rebuilt between runs). Wire verdicts:
  ```json
  {
    "after": {
      "head": "ef3982d35c1cc14d0b76783e24871bd798bdd2f1",
      "git-pr-workflow_in_available_skills": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasWorkflowConsistentSkillsLine": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasLegacySkillsLine": false,
      "deliveredPromptHasWorkflowRequiredDecisionBiasLine": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasLegacyBlockingDecisionBiasLine": false,
      "deliveredPromptHasBoundedPrecedenceLine": true
    },
    "before": {
      "head": "origin/main",
      "git-pr-workflow_in_available_skills": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasWorkflowConsistentSkillsLine": false,
      "deliveredPromptHasLegacySkillsLine": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasWorkflowRequiredDecisionBiasLine": false,
      "deliveredPromptHasLegacyBlockingDecisionBiasLine": true,
      "deliveredPromptHasBoundedPrecedenceLine": false
    }
  }
  ```
  Delivered prompt diff (real gateway, wire capture, same skill catalog both runs):
  ```diff
   Search by the task goal and distinctive terms. Simple conversation or a self-contained answer does not need a search. Search covers installed skills; it does not install skills.
   Several: most specific. No relevant skill: read none.
  -Up-front max one. Never invent paths.
  +Up-front max one; read another applicable skill when the active workflow requires it. Never invent paths.
   External writes: batch safely; no tight loops; honor 429/Retry-After.
   - Actionable request: act now.
   - Requested action with an available tool: do it. Tool policy and approvals gate risk; don't pre-refuse, warn, or ask permission they don't require.
  -- Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one blocking decision.
  +- Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one decision the applicable workflow requires (a blocking decision always qualifies).
  +- Applicable skill workflow gates (prerequisites, required decisions, ordering) override generic Execution Bias; decisions or authorization the user already supplied, safety rules, and tool policy stay authoritative.
   - Continue to done/real blocker; no plan-only finish when tools can act.
  ```
  In both runs the installed `git-pr-workflow` skill was discovered into `<available_skills>`
  (location `<workspace>/skills/git-pr-workflow/SKILL.md`), so the only behavioral difference on
  the wire is the patched guidance itself.
- **Evidence after fix:** rendered prompt lines (asserted by the regression cases on patched source):
  ```json
  {
    "skills_lines": [
      "Several: most specific. No relevant skill: read none.",
      "Up-front max one; read another applicable skill when the active workflow requires it. Never invent paths.",
      "External writes: batch safely; no tight loops; honor 429/Retry-After."
    ],
    "execution_bias_lines": [
      "- Actionable request: act now.",
      "- Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one decision the applicable workflow requires (a blocking decision always qualifies).",
      "- Applicable skill workflow gates (prerequisites, required decisions, ordering) override generic Execution Bias; decisions or authorization the user already supplied, safety rules, and tool policy stay authoritative.",
      "- Continue to done/real blocker; no plan-only finish when tools can act."
    ]
  }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** `validate.sh` green (format/lint/system-prompt tests + tsgo:core) on rebased head `ef3982d35c1`; the src diff stays at +3/-2 across the two prompt files after the rebase.
- **Before evidence:** unpatched `origin/main` @ d810d753e31 renders the contradictory wording:
  ```json
  {
    "skills_lines": ["Up-front max one. Never invent paths."],
    "execution_bias_lines": ["- Non-final turn: advance with tools, or ask one blocking decision."]
  }
  ```
  RED run against unpatched source: `Tests 3 failed | 48 skipped`.
- **What was not tested:** live model session A/B (the reporter's `opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` runtime is not available here); end-to-end proof that a real model honors workflow gates is outside a prompt-renderer fix. No UI/gateway changes.
- **Proof tier:** L2 — deterministic before/after terminal capture of the delivered prompt from (a) the production config-aware runtime entry point and (b) a real shipped gateway process delivering the prompt to a provider endpoint on the wire, both with an applicable workflow skill recognized; plus regression tests pinning the wording.
- **Proof limitations:** the defect is deterministic prompt text, so delivered-prompt before/after from the shipped entry point is the authoritative proof; model-level compliance remains a follow-up observation and would require a live provider runtime not available in this environment.
- **Review state:** head rebased onto latest `origin/main` as `ef3982d35c1` (fresh CI run started; the src diff is unchanged at +3/-2). The Execution Bias precedence clause implements the **bounded precedence rule** ClawSweeper's review recommended. The review's "Add real behavior proof" item is now addressed with the real Gateway wire capture above (shipped gateway process delivering the revised prompt with the applicable workflow skill installed); after this update ClawSweeper should re-review automatically — if not, `@clawsweeper re-review`. Remaining review gate: the maintainer owner decision on the shared prompt-policy wording (bounded precedence rule).

prs.title: fix(plugins): preserve resultContentSource declared on defineToolPlugin tools
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

<!--
Required PR title: type: user-facing description
-->

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #177275

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where plugin authors using `defineToolPlugin` could not declare `resultContentSource: "network"` on statically defined tools — TypeScript rejected the field, and at runtime the helper silently discarded it before `api.registerTool`, so network-facing tool plugins built on the recommended path never participated in turn-taint propagation or memory provenance that the lower-level `api.registerTool({ resultContentSource: "network", ... })` already supports.
- **Related:** #177275; clawsweeper source-repro review confirmed the complete property-loss path on current main and tagged `fix-shape-clear` / `queueable-fix`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** A static `tool({ resultContentSource: "network", ... })` declaration is retained through the tool-plugin factory and forwarded to the registered `AgentTool`, mirroring how `outputSchema` and `workspaceAccess` already flow through the same adapter. For a network-declared tool, the rest of the turn becomes tainted and derived memory keeps untrusted provenance, identical to the lower-level registration path.
- **Out of scope:** Factory tools keep declaring `resultContentSource` on the concrete `AnyAgentTool` objects they return (`resultContentSource?: never` on the static factory declaration, same pattern as `outputSchema`, because a static copy could drift from the runtime tool); no provenance policy changes, no manifest/catalog metadata surface changes.
- **Highest-risk area:** The union type on `ToolPluginToolDefinition` — narrowing the property to the execute variant keeps factory declarations authoritative.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** TypeScript rejects `resultContentSource` on static factory declarations instead of silently ignoring it, and the regression test pins the execute-path forwarding. Per review feedback, the declaration type is indexed from the public tool boundary (`AnyAgentTool["resultContentSource"]`) instead of importing the private `packages/agent-core/src/types.js` source path, keeping the SDK declaration tied to the exact property `api.registerTool` accepts.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** A tool plugin declared with `resultContentSource: "network"` registers a tool whose `resultContentSource` is `"network"`; tool results taint the rest of the turn and derived memory is classified untrusted, matching documented memory-architecture behavior.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.ts` (type union + factory copy + static register forward) and the regression test "retains a declared resultContentSource on the registered tool" in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; docs example in `docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md` §Network-derived results.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Worktree checkout of current main with the patch applied (`/home/0668000710/code/PR/aispace/worktrees/issue-177275`), zero-mock probe through the real `defineToolPlugin` → `entry.register(api)` → captured `registerTool` path.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Zero-mock probe: register a defineToolPlugin tool declaring resultContentSource: "network",
  # then inspect the object handed to api.registerTool (real SDK factory path, no mocks):
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence-dir>/probe-result-content-source.mts

  # Regression test (RED on origin/main, GREEN with the patch):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts

  # Type checks (local tsrs binary needs GLIBC >= 2.32, EL8 host used the tsgo fallback):
  OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental \
    --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
  OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mts \
    -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugin-sdk.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  AFTER (patched HEAD):
  {
    "registeredToolName": "netprobe_fetch",
    "resultContentSource": "network",
    "forwarded": true
  }
  AFTER EXIT: 0
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The registered tool retains `resultContentSource: "network"`, so tool execution feeds the declaration into `recordLoopOutcome` and the existing turn-taint/memory-provenance path treats subsequent turn content as network-derived. Regression test passes (6/6 in `tool-plugin.test.ts`); `tsgo:core` and the plugin-sdk test-types shard pass clean.
- **Before evidence:** Same probe on unpatched `origin/main` — the declaration was silently dropped before registration:
  ```text
  BEFORE (origin/main):
  {
    "registeredToolName": "netprobe_fetch",
    "resultContentSource": null,
    "forwarded": false
  }
  BEFORE EXIT: 1
  ```
- **End-to-end Gateway behavior proof (redacted, reproduced by reviewer Raven-Gt on an isolated state dir with the PR-equivalent patch; full transcript in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177307#issuecomment-6267713896)):** a plugin installed via `plugins.load.paths` declared `netprobe_fetch` through `defineToolPlugin`'s static `tool({ resultContentSource: "network", ... })` helper; a real Gateway agent turn called the tool against a local loopback endpoint returning marker `PROV-MARK-9Z7Q`. Readback from the agent transcript DB and derived-memory index:
  ```text
  seq=8  role=toolResult  __openclaw={resultContentSource:"network", runId:"[redacted]"}
  seq=10 role=assistant   __openclaw={turnTainted:true, runId:"[redacted]"}

  source=sessions
  origin_class=untrusted
  contains_marker=true
  ```
  This closes the full chain: static `defineToolPlugin` declaration → Gateway execution → network result marker → next assistant turn tainted → derived session memory classified untrusted.
- **What was not tested:** Nothing material remains untested — the previously open gap (a full live Gateway agent turn with a network plugin installed) is now covered by the end-to-end proof above. CI lanes pending on Actions for the rebased head.
- **Proof tier:** L3
- **Proof limitations:** Gateway E2E proof was produced by the reviewer on a PR-equivalent patch with redacted local endpoints/paths; no external endpoint or credential was used.
- **Review state:** Reviewer SDK-boundary suggestion adopted; awaiting re-review

prs.title: fix(plugins): prevent terminal controls in installed plugin reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes installed plugin metadata and discovery diagnostics emitting terminal control sequences during `plugins list` and `plugins inspect`.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect installed plugins without manifest strings changing terminal state. Normal plugin labels, versions, and trusted status colors remain readable. Report JSON retains its raw metadata values; there are no new settings, permissions, protocols, schemas, or migration steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing canonical terminal filter at human list and inspection boundaries, including verbose/all modes and global diagnostic stderr. Filter untrusted table cells before trusted status styling. Plugin discovery, enablement, runtime loading, and structured report data retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### Current-head maintenance

- Product head: `662557a4301c7347ffd185b81b1f7c66982c2fd8`; integrated main: `27e7e5ee87ccbc1cfa11b7e0b79d78bbf503280f`; clean reviewed tree: `8a6cf30d798eb3571014cf39581e06339420c795`. Original contribution and authentic merge parents are retained.
- Repair: Resolved the actual list-renderer merge conflict by preserving terminal sanitization alongside main’s Trust column and verbose trust label. Main’s inline JSON projection remains intact; raw JSON metadata and missing IDs remain unchanged.
- Exact current collector command: `node proof-reports.mjs "$CHECKOUT" green plugins` (Node 26.12.1, isolated synthetic state). Actual command, process excerpts, independent readback and original baseline evidence are inline below; source hashes identify the local collectors.
- Actual runtime readback: Real built plugins list/inspect CLI subprocesses discover a synthetic installed manifest. Tainted and ordinary human reports emit zero unsafe terminal controls; JSON preserves raw tainted metadata. Missing-plugin human errors escape newlines and remove controls, while JSON preserves the original ID. The plugin entrypoint throws if imported, so this is metadata-only discovery.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid oversized raw history in final answers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Isolated post-tool finalization reopened raw session history even when the selected context engine had already excluded that history from the source attempt. A short final answer could therefore send a much larger conversation to the provider.

Fixes #186244. Already-delivered-message admission is tracked separately in #179003 and is outside this repair, as [confirmed by the maintainer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6454269644).

## Why This Change Was Made

The restricted built-in adapter passes the frozen settled model view through a host-private parameter. It uses the explicit OpenClaw transcript capture when present, otherwise the canonical settled `messagesSnapshot`; an explicitly unavailable or foreign-harness projection is refused.

The existing `prepareEmbeddedAttemptHistory` owner selects this view instead of rehydrated raw history and reuses the existing session byte/event window and tool-result omission policy. An empty selected view also replaces the hydrated messages. The original SessionManager retains all transcript writes and receipts.

The finalizer still receives no live context engine. Its bootstrap, maintenance, ingestion, afterTurn hooks, ambient prompt contributors, tools and trajectory capabilities are not restored. Empty-finalizer retries reuse the original settled view. This adds no config/env/schema or public SDK capability and introduces no new current-turn boundary inference.

## User Impact

Excluded old history stays out of the isolated finalization request while the current request, completed tool evidence and selected summary remain available. Durable history is retained. Finalization remains tool-free, and interrupted work cannot be completed by replaying tools during this step.

## Evidence

### Refreshed main integration

Merged main `342da13c92e0af1add7936f9bc479394f01e426c` into the latest contributor head, producing `a8cad32e618122fbe474a5102890fe34e5fc9b57`. The history owner preserves both main's Anthropic turn-scoped system-update clearing and the frozen selected-view snapshot. [Fresh built-Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6456933305) measured one finalizer request per ref: **52,085 bytes on main** (excluded raw canary restored) versus **2,490 bytes on the merged candidate** (summary and current write receipt retained, canary absent). Both turns completed successfully, offered zero finalizer tools, and added no engine lifecycle calls. The 11 finalization tests and 8 upstream bounded-context tests passed again, with focused lint/formatting. Test-line growth remains zero.

### Independent current-main comparison

[Independent built-Gateway evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6456615096) compares current main `4b27ee88cec9a78377a04b2e3a352ba7c503450e` twice with the candidate production code twice, plus normal-finalization controls on both revisions. Isolated finalizer requests measured **52,100 bytes on main in both runs** versus **2,505 bytes on the candidate in both runs**. Main restored the excluded raw canary; the candidate retained the selected summary and current write receipt without the canary. Every isolated finalizer offered zero tools and left context-engine lifecycle counters unchanged. All six measured turns completed successfully. The latest contributor head changes only tests and passed both changed suites (11 tests), focused lint and formatting. Whole-PR test-line delta is zero, without a ceiling change.

### Contributor's earlier proof

Named base: `63ba4974f67c1eba483f8b7121c2bf7416d75ae4`.

Candidate: `a037f29b1bad9717aca3a3db9559b941534e4efd`.

### Real built CLI/Gateway proof on Linux

Both revisions completed frozen dependency installation and full builds. Final candidate full build exited 0 in 3m2.2s; the actual built CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (a037f29)`.

The primary fixture uses a real Gateway, `sessions.create`, two agent CLI turns and an actual committed `write` to a task-owned file. Its HTTP/SSE Responses provider and context-engine plugin are synthetic local fixtures. The empty post-tool answer really enters isolated finalization; the finalizer offers zero tools. A plain read-only continuation is not used as a substitute for that admission.

- Base: ordinary request excluded the old canary, but isolated finalization restored it: 50,786 versus 82,564 reserialized JSON bytes. `ocpr prove --phase pre` recorded command exit 1, with successful tool commit and clean Gateway shutdown.
- Candidate primary: ordinary request 50,793 bytes; finalizer 1,745 bytes. Old canary absent from provider input, current write evidence retained, visible/history answer present, and old raw canary still present in durable history.
- Additional positive scenario: a non-empty engine-selected summary survives ordinary and isolated requests; finalizer 1,880 bytes. Primary lifecycle counts remain `assemble=5`, `commitTurn=2`, `maintain=3`, `bootstrap=1`, with no finalizer engine callbacks.
- Both scenarios confirm an active subsequent turn through real `chat.abort`, omit its cancelled output, preserve the committed write, and close cleanly. The cancelled CLI exits 1 as expected for this cancellation control; each proof driver exits 0 only after the positive cancellation and cleanup assertions.
- Persisted-state compatibility: copy the cleanly closed named-base managed SQLite state, reopen it with candidate built CLI/Doctor/Gateway, and complete a new ordinary turn on that existing session. Old/new answers and the old actual write survive; the original baseline database hashes remain unchanged. This is named-base-to-candidate state compatibility, not a stable-release installer/version upgrade claim.

Exact commands executed by `ocpr`:

```sh
node bin/ocpr prove 186244 --phase pre --sha 63ba4974f67c1eba483f8b7121c2bf7416d75ae4 --cmd "python3 /tmp/oc-186244-runtime-access/formal-entry.py --sha 63ba4974f67c1eba483f8b7121c2bf7416d75ae4 --root /tmp/oc-186244-entry-formal-pre-1 --port 19981"
node bin/ocpr prove 186244 --phase post --sha a037f29b1bad9717aca3a3db9559b941534e4efd --cmd "python3 /tmp/oc-186244-runtime-access/186244-proof-suite.py --sha a037f29b1bad9717aca3a3db9559b941534e4efd --label 2"
```

<details>
<summary>Actual captured post-proof stdout</summary>

The existing detached finalization regression failed on pre-fix code because omitted history reappeared in the finalizer. It now preserves tool receipts and the original transcript manager across empty retries. Earlier oversized-precheck and unclosed-user-turn fixture failures were separately classified and retained; they are not claimed as the product regression.

The implementation candidate passed 84 tests in eight relevant files (77.15s), including screenshot-heavy bounded current-request history, length/incomplete outcomes, unavailable context, delivery, silence, transport, detached custody and empty retries. The final test-only consolidation was rerun on this exact head: 46 tests in both changed suites plus the required runner sibling, three shards, exit 0 (26.05s). The first Ready CI [run 40600657717](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40600657717) exposed a test-line budget failure: the merge tree was already above the ceiling and this PR added 52 test lines. The complete PR now has zero net test-line growth. No baseline, config, ignore or formatter policy was changed. That first CI result remains a failure; the latest head's CI gate now passes.

The complete changed-file command exits 1 only on two global dead-export failures: `extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts: runPrompt` and `ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.test-support.ts: settleActivity`. The same dead-export command was actually run on the exact named base and failed on the identical two exports. Those unrelated files were not changed; the full command is not reported green.

It included the complete bounded selector, limits, snapshot/capture owners, finalization caller and harness lifecycle/selection contracts. Runtime proof above is separate from that review.

Refreshed head `a8cad32e618122fbe474a5102890fe34e5fc9b57` has a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40608440269) and [exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6453523198): overall readiness 5/6, proof confidence 5/6, patch quality 5/6, no actionable findings. No failing jobs remain; one auxiliary auto-response job was cancelled.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the old finalization-context selection without a schema or persisted-format change. Blast radius is the built-in OpenClaw runtime's isolated post-tool final answers; an incorrect selection could omit necessary settled context or restore excluded history. Ordinary finalization, context-engine lifecycle ownership and durable transcript writes remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): escape terminal controls in explain reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sandbox explain` can clear terminal output or insert extra report lines when a configured workspace path contains control characters.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can read effective sandbox paths safely. JSON paths and the effective sandbox/workspace configuration keep their original values.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing terminal sanitizer in the central human-readable value renderer, before styling. JSON returns before this renderer, so consumers retain the original filesystem paths. No config/default, protocol/schema, permission/security-policy, dependency, compatibility, or migration changes.

## Evidence

### Current-head maintenance — October 26, 2026

Node 26.12.1/Linux, isolated HOME/config/state. Build and CLI proof each exited 0; this is not a mocked command action or direct internal-function proof.

Complete collector and helper retained below; collector SHA-256 cd2663f6f7fd0de720e6bddbe30737f1a9996927d4de311c188d233e51e65df8 (only the helper import uses the task-local layout); helper SHA-256 9618fa1e6e0263e7ce22d485b7c1620a8db3cd0dee2ef11727c0d4253bace8cb. The test/type/lint/format results were obtained before the merge commit on the byte-identical tree above; runtime proof and ratchet were run after committing.
- Scope: two files; production +2/-1 and tests +28/-0. Existing-solutions preflight reuses terminal-core sanitization. All central human-rendered path/policy consumers are covered by this owner; JSON returns before rendering. No config/default, protocol/schema, permission/security-policy, dependency, migration or compatibility changes.
- Hosted CI: NOT YET OBSERVED for this new head at package preparation; follow-up comments record actual hosted results.
- Not tested; cleanup and limitations: Linux real-filesystem and subprocess byte-boundary proof only. Docker/Podman/remote runtime launches, sandbox enforcement, rich PTY colors, Windows/macOS terminals and the full CI suite are not exercised. No production sessions, channels, model credentials or service configuration were loaded.
