- Tests: OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/commands/sandbox-explain.test.ts --maxWorkers=1: 10 pass, exit 0; core and canonical commands-test types, explicit type-aware lint, format, ratchet and independent P0-P3 adversarial review pass (measured cost: 103.19 s selected shard; 110.60 s including wrapper; cold preparation reported separately in local task log)
- Not tested: Docker/Podman/remote runtime launches, sandbox enforcement, rich PTY colors, Windows/macOS terminals and full CI suite locally; real filesystem path proof is Linux-only

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the real CLI proof</summary>

Install the pinned dependencies in clean checkouts at the SHAs above, then build normally with `pnpm build qaRuntime` (used on BASE) or `pnpm build cliStartup` (used on HEAD; core CLI only). Save the two files below together outside the checkout. The same collector and scenario run on both versions:

```sh
node proof-sandbox.mjs <base-checkout> red
node proof-sandbox.mjs <head-checkout> green
```

Invocation form: `node proof-sandbox.mjs <checkout> <red|green>`. Only the helper import path is flattened for copying. The collector checks clean Git HEAD against the build stamp and records stdout, stderr, exit status, and readback in its printed temporary receipt directory.

`proof-sandbox.mjs`:

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import {fixture} from './proof-cli-common.mjs';

const f = fixture('sandbox-terminal', process.argv[2], process.argv[3]);
const workspace = path.join(f.root,'café\x1b[2J\x07
FORGED','workspace');
fs.mkdirSync(workspace,{recursive:true});
f.config.agents.entries.main.workspace = workspace;
f.config.agents.defaults.sandbox = {mode:'off'};
f.writeConfig();
const before = fs.readFileSync(f.configPath);
const report = f.run('sandbox-explain',['sandbox','explain']);
assert.equal(report.code,0,report.stderr);
const controls = (report.stdout.match(/[\x00-\x09\x0b-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]/g) ?? []).length;
const forged = (report.stdout.match(/
FORGED/g) ?? []).length;
if (f.phase === 'red') {assert.ok(controls>0);assert.equal(forged,2);}
else {assert.equal(controls,0);assert.equal(forged,0);assert.equal((report.stdout.match(/café\nFORGED/g) ?? []).length,2);}
const json = f.run('raw-path-json-control',['sandbox','explain','--json']);
assert.equal(json.code,0,json.stderr);
const payload = JSON.parse(json.stdout);
assert.equal(payload.sandbox.effectiveHostWorkspaceRoot,workspace);
assert.equal(payload.sandbox.runtimeWorkdir,workspace);
assert.equal(payload.sandbox.sessionIsSandboxed,false);
assert.ok(fs.statSync(payload.sandbox.runtimeWorkdir).isDirectory());
assert.ok(fs.readFileSync(f.configPath).equals(before));
f.config.agents.entries.main.workspace = path.join(f.root,'workspace');
f.writeConfig();
const normal = f.run('normal-workspace-control',['sandbox','explain']);
assert.equal(normal.code,0,normal.stderr);
assert.ok(normal.stdout.includes(`effectiveHostWorkspaceRoot: ${f.config.agents.entries.main.workspace}
`));
assert.ok(normal.stdout.includes('runtime: direct'));
assert.equal((normal.stdout.match(/[\x00-\x09\x0b-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]/g) ?? []).length,0);
f.receipt.observations.push({controls,forged,stdout:report.stdout,jsonPathsUnchanged:true,realDirectoryReadback:true,configBytesUnchanged:true,configHash:f.hash(before),legalWorkspaceControl:true});
f.finish();

```

`proof-cli-common.mjs`:

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';
import {execFileSync, spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';

export function fixture(name, checkoutArg, phase) {
  assert.ok(['red', 'green'].includes(phase));
  const checkout = path.resolve(checkoutArg);
  const root = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), `alix-${name}-`));
  for (const leaf of ['home', 'state', 'workspace', 'tmp']) fs.mkdirSync(path.join(root, leaf));
  const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
  // Read-only containers receive a host Git attestation before the bind mount.
  const head = process.env.PROOF_CHECKED_HEAD ?? execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], {cwd: checkout, encoding: 'utf8'}).trim();
  const status = process.env.PROOF_CHECKED_STATUS ?? execFileSync('git', ['status', '--porcelain'], {cwd: checkout, encoding: 'utf8'}).trim();
  assert.match(head, /^[a-f0-9]{40}$/);
  const stamp = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(checkout, 'dist/.buildstamp')));
  assert.equal(status, ''); assert.equal(stamp.head, head); assert.equal(stamp.inputsClean, true);
  const configPath = path.join(root, 'openclaw.json');
  const config = {agents: {ownership: 'explicit', defaults: {systemAgent: {agentId: 'main'}}, entries: {main: {workspace: path.join(root, 'workspace')}}}, tools: {profile: 'minimal'}, plugins: {allow: [], slots: {memory: 'none'}}, logging: {level: 'warn', consoleLevel: 'warn', file: path.join(root, 'runtime.log')}};
  const receipt = {name, phase, head, time: new Date().toISOString(), root, runs: [], observations: []};
  const save = () => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'receipt.json'), JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2));
  const writeConfig = () => fs.writeFileSync(configPath, JSON.stringify(config), {mode: 0o600});
  writeConfig();
  const env = {PATH: `${path.dirname(process.execPath)}:/usr/bin:/bin`, HOME: path.join(root, 'home'), TMPDIR: path.join(root, 'tmp'), LANG: 'C.UTF-8', TZ: 'UTC', CI: '1', OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH: configPath, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: path.join(root, 'state'), OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN: '1', OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BONJOUR: '1'};
  function run(label, args) {
    const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [path.join(checkout, 'openclaw.mjs'), ...args], {cwd: path.join(root, 'workspace'), env, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 90000, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024});
    const row = {label, args, code: result.status, stdout: result.stdout, stderr: result.stderr};
    receipt.runs.push(row); save();
    console.log(JSON.stringify({label, code: row.code}));
    assert.equal(result.error, undefined, 'Timeout/spawn errors are not product RED');
    assert.equal(result.signal, null);
    return row;
  }
  function finish() {receipt.result = 'PASS'; save(); console.log(JSON.stringify({result: 'PASS', receipt: path.join(root, 'receipt.json')}));}
  return {root, config, configPath, writeConfig, receipt, run, finish, hash, phase};
}

```

prs.title: feature(backup): add backup status CLI for existing backup.status RPC
prs.body:
Implements #182640

## What Problem This Solves

Backup ledger status already exists as Gateway RPC `backup.status` (Control UI Backups + Doctor freshness), but operators must hand-write `openclaw gateway call backup.status`. The CLI has create/list/verify/record/enable/disable/sqlite/git and no `backup status` verb. `openclaw status` only shows a one-line freshness string.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw backup status --json` returns the same `{ targets, schedules, locations }` payload Control UI already uses. Recording an external outcome with `backup record` appears under `targets` on the next status call. Unreachable Gateway fails like sibling Gateway-backed CLI verbs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapter only: register `backup status`, forward empty params to existing `backup.status`, print Gateway JSON, document next to `backup record`, and point the local-state-owner recovery hint at `openclaw backup status`. No new Gateway methods, schema, or permissions.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/backup-status.ts`, `src/cli/program/register.backup.ts`, `src/commands/backup-shared.ts`, colocated test, `docs/cli/backup.md`
- Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/backup-status.test.ts` — **2 passed** (CLI registration + `--port`/`--url` transport targeting; replaces mock call-shape echo)
- Packaged CLI proof below (Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, local Gateway token auth)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw backup status` that calls existing `backup.status` and returns ledger targets + schedules + locations; missing Gateway must fail like sibling RPC verbs.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw backup status` → `backupStatusCommand` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("backup.status", …, {})` → existing Gateway handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/backup.ts`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` and existing `backup.status` owner. No new ledger reader, schema, or permissions.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) after `qaRuntime` build on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run` with token auth.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash

export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"

node openclaw.mjs gateway call backup.status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs backup status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs backup record --status ok --target host-restic --bytes 1 --json
node openclaw.mjs backup status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# negative: backup status --url ws://127.0.0.1:1 --timeout 2000 --json → exit 1
```

### Evidence after fix

```text

# openclaw gateway call backup.status --json  (exit 0)
{ "targets": [], "schedules": [], "locations": [] }

Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (ECONNREFUSED).

{ "targets": [], "schedules": [], "locations": [] }

# after backup record --status ok --target host-restic --bytes 1
```

prs.title: fix: same-requester guidance queues after reconnecting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary guidance from the same signed-in person can become a separate turn after reconnecting with different client capabilities or tool bindings.

## User Impact

User impact: same-requester guidance stays with the active turn in the same channel, account, conversation, and thread, without replacing or expanding its prepared permissions, tools, bindings, or approval destination.

Current caller access and the original execution’s live authority still apply. Questions, approvals, explicit cross-session steering, execution-setting changes, backend compatibility, and cancellation keep their existing checks. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

After validating the authenticated requester and exact conversation, ordinary continuation now retains the active execution’s snapshot instead of comparing an incoming connection’s policy projection with it. Dropping protocol-only `usage-refreshing` metadata therefore no longer moves a correction to a new turn.

This PR contains only the same-requester continuity fix, its regressions, and documentation/help updates. It does not change queue notices, TUI behavior, security presets, or collaborative-steering defaults.

## Evidence

- On original pinned base `c2243320434e1c1ae99105f4b070e1a3a4d24479`, all three authenticated `chat.send` regressions failed with `Compatible requester input was dispatched as a separate turn`: capability removal with collaboration disabled and enabled, and binding drift with collaboration enabled. All three pass with the fix, reaching native steering admission, durable transcript targeting, and subsequent model consumption without changing the incumbent owner, authority fingerprint, bindings, or approval destination.
- **174 focused tests passed again** on conflict-resolved composition `d09a06f6e362141954b9f1f5d888ff32b8647b2d` in 236.54 seconds: 20 Gateway custody cases, 39 continuation joins, 11 handoff joins, plus strict requester/question/cross-session, fallback, and prompt-prefix checks. Independent incoming-authority revocation is rejected while the original authority and outer assertion remain live; other-conversation input retains the compatibility path.
- Core production and applicable test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, docs links (16,094 links; zero broken), config examples, generated config-help checks, and normal `pnpm build` passed on the refreshed composition. Formatting and whitespace checks passed; all nine feature source/test/doc blobs remain byte-identical to the previously reviewed candidate.
- The [hosted review's P2 test-line finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186378#issuecomment-6456175921) is addressed by fixture consolidation and removal of three duplicate owner-table rows already covered at the authenticated Gateway boundary. The repair removed 92 test lines; the complete PR is **−8 test lines** against the refreshed target. The unchanged target ratchet passes; this PR raises no ceiling and weakens no primary regression or authority oracle.
- Independent source review and canonical local AutoReview (Codex-backed, medium reasoning, P0–P3) found no actionable findings on repaired tree `5fc62be924ea399f562acaf4bde711c3591cb1a1`. Those reviews are retained for the nine unchanged feature blobs. The later main integration required only canonical regeneration of the conflicting hash file, qualified separately below. Local ClawSweeper's installed checkout was dirty/ambiguous; hosted review is advisory. Broad exact-head proof is tracked in [PR checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186378/checks).
- **Remaining supplemental E2E gap:** on the earlier qualification head, nine real-Gateway/scripted-provider session-lifecycle cases passed, including requester correction, followup, Stop, cross-session delivery, subagent announcement, and compaction steering. The provenance scenario failed at `gateway.sessions-send-provenance.e2e.test.ts:661`, expecting strict cross-human refusal without selecting strict fallback; its pinned base used personal/quiet queue fallback. The people fixture then stalled, and its three cases remain unqualified after the owned run was stopped and joined (exit 143). These legacy scenarios were not rerun on the original base or after the mechanical conflict refresh. This is **not an aggregate E2E pass**; neither their expectations nor upstream defaults were edited to obtain green results.

<details>
<summary>Authority-chain proof and review follow-through</summary>

Authenticated Gateway dispatch and the real native session loop exercise the changed boundary with fixed external-I/O fixtures. Accepted reconnect inputs assert native acceptance before separate-turn dispatch, unchanged incumbent principal/fingerprint/operator authority, persisted `steerTargetRunId`, and exactly two model-stream invocations after steering is consumed. Different-requester refusal controls assert no native steering and only the original model invocation. This is production-path composition with a scripted model stream, not live external-provider qualification.

The independent caller-revocation case uses different revocation controllers and a fresh incoming authority source. After revoking only that caller, the outer assertion and incumbent authority still succeed, `joined.prepareCurrent()` rejects with `Incoming caller revoked`, no delivery occurs, and frozen-state assertions hold. Gateway commit cases exercise the real backing run's refusal when workspace, session ACL, or lifecycle authority changes at steering commit. Handoff cases retain no-grant-transfer and frozen-fingerprint checks.

Selected terminal results from the reviewed fixture-repair run, all repeated successfully in the refreshed composition (labels shortened):

```text
PASS authenticated chat.send: protocol metadata drift, collaboration false
PASS authenticated chat.send: protocol metadata drift, collaboration true
PASS authenticated chat.send: binding drift, collaboration true
PASS authenticated chat.send: same permissions across different profiles, collaboration false
PASS continuation join: incoming authority revoked independently
PASS continuation join: another conversation with changed policy
PASS real backing-run steering commit: browser custody workspace
PASS real backing-run steering commit: browser custody session ACL
PASS real backing-run steering commit: browser custody lifecycle
174 focused tests passed after conflict refresh; seven Vitest shards completed in 236.54s.
Test-line ratchet against pinned main: net delta -8; target ceiling unchanged; passed.
```

No transport authentication, provider adapter, or final tool-I/O guard is changed by this patch. The hosted review found no concrete authorization bypass; its proof concern is addressed by these admission/effect-boundary assertions and explicit limits, not by treating the supplemental lifecycle suite as reconnect-drift proof.

</details>

<details>
<summary>History-preserving conflict refresh and generated artifact</summary>

GitHub reported a real content conflict after main advanced. A read-only merge preview identified only `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`. Main `845a0636b4e5d160ca71ee16db95a70753c4e71c` was merged without rebasing or rewriting existing commits; all nine feature blobs stayed identical. Only the generated combined/core hashes needed resolution, through `pnpm config:docs:gen` and its check, preserving the newly landed target fields and Josh's help text. Reversing only that help string in each generated JSON recovers the exact pinned-main hash. A later live-main preview was conflict-free, so the tested pin was retained instead of following further main movement.

Delta against the refreshed target remains ten files: production/help +15/−2 lines; tests +95/−103; docs +10/−8; required generated hash +2/−2. No new state, policy owner, wrapper, compatibility layer, config option, or budget is introduced. No visual production changes or external live-model/channel qualification are claimed.

</details>

Requested by @joshavant.

prs.title: fix(compaction): preserve terminal facts from long tool output
prs.body:
Related: #167793. Thanks @KarimVKarmali for reporting the local-model context problem that led to this measured follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction drops terminal facts from ordinary long tool results before the summarizer can read them. In an 18-file local-model workload, all four summary inputs contained none of the result codes; the final answer returned only 12 while claiming 18.

## User Impact

Ordinary long results retain their beginning and end within 2,000 characters, including an explicit elision marker. Short results stay byte-identical. Existing diagnostic projections and their budgets remain intact. Middle content can still be omitted; this remains a lossy projection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing serializer kept only the beginning unless it recognized diagnostic text. Reuse that owner and preserve its established diagnostic rules while retaining ordinary terminal facts too. No new pruning mode, setting, or retention behavior is added; stored tool results remain untouched. The broader pruning request stays separate.

## Evidence

- Final regression captures the actual summarization request: terminal fact absent on pinned main base `caf3034ae08157264c43e8e085a68f892ac5b5cd` (4.50s), present with the fix. Original tool content remains unchanged.
- Focused compaction/branch suites: 57 tests passed, 2.07s wrapper / 1.00s Vitest. Exact 2,000-character short output, Unicode cuts, and diagnostic priority/nonduplication are covered.
- Prompt-prefix stability: 13 tests passed; cold worker compilation dominated its 223.51s duration. Standard prompt snapshots regenerate unchanged (token delta 0).
- Scoped lint, core and targeted test types, and all required baseline ratchets pass. No baseline ceiling raised.
- Independent Codex branch review at P2+ is clean on `48015acc18e0119c91edafa779013545383fc8c8` against the base above. Earlier findings were reproduced and resolved by retaining the original diagnostic path.
- Fresh real Gateway baseline on macOS/Ollama, through an unchanged recording relay: Qwen3 8B read all 18 synthetic 12KB files once, returned 12/18 terminal codes, compacted twice, used 195,897 prompt tokens and reported 143,807 cached tokens; 98.36s CLI wall time. All summary inputs contained zero codes.
- `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed in 6m40s. The fixed run used the same Gateway, recording relay, files, configuration, and model in a fresh session. Its first summary input contains codes 1–6 and the first summary preserves them. A later summary drops those already-provided facts: **Qwen3 final recall remained 12/18.** This fixes the serializer's input omission, not the model's subsequent summary quality.

| Qwen3 8B, fixed 18-file workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Terminal codes in final answer | 12/18 | 12/18 |
| Terminal codes in first summary input | 0 | 6 |
| Completed compactions | 2 | 2 |
| Provider requests / summary requests | 23 / 4 | 23 / 4 |
| Total prompt tokens | 195,897 | 194,997 |
| Reported cached tokens | 143,807 | 143,070 |
| Summary prompt tokens | 11,160 | 11,184 |
| CLI wall time | 98.36s | 110.50s |

These are observed single-run counts, not an isolated speed/cache benchmark. The unchanged standard prompt snapshots have a zero token delta; summary inputs changed by +24 measured tokens across four requests.

The Qwen2.5 7B control also confirms the input fix without proving successful task recall: it acquired all 18 files, attempted nonexistent doc-19 and reread four files, then ended with a progress message containing one code. It completed three compactions in 125.80s, with 36 requests (12 summary requests), 273,204 prompt tokens, and 202,740 reported cached tokens. The original study's unpaired Qwen2.5 run was aborted at 149.90s with no final answer, after three completed compactions, 319,330 prompt tokens, and 237,955 cached tokens. No efficiency or task-quality improvement is claimed from those differing endings.

Production: 9 lines added / 4 removed (net +5); those five lines retain the established diagnostic paths while bounding the ordinary projection. Tests: 31 added / 31 removed (net 0), consolidating overlapping checks while preserving their contracts. Documentation: +2 lines.

The separate measured-pressure handoff is addressed by #186300, merged while this experiment was running. This PR does not change pressure accounting. The controlled before/after comparison keeps the pinned pre-merge pressure behavior identical on both sides. Proof is macOS/Ollama through the real Gateway; it does not cover the reporter's Linux/vLLM 98K window or cron delivery. Shared model traffic can affect cache reuse and latency.

prs.title: fix: subagent turns fail after session metadata changes
prs.body:
Related: #179289

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new subagent turns failing before submission when inherited capability metadata becomes stale after an ordinary session metadata update.

## User Impact

An authorized child follow-up can prepare fresh metadata instead of failing with `Session capability metadata changed`. Existing identity, policy-revocation, and closed-owner checks remain enforced. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Asynchronous capability preparation now refreshes a stale inherited read once per affected lookup and reevaluates current policy. Synchronous retained reads still reject stale authority, and a second invalidation fails rather than retrying indefinitely. The shared capability projection is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Live completed-child follow-up (same head):** [@Marvinthebored’s verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183501#issuecomment-6397556970) on `9f0a7a085e1bd3c3fed1bbd0eb50e7ff50494213` (October 25, 2026, 12:14–12:16 UTC) used an isolated Gateway and real Codex model processes. A child completed and its parent independently recorded the initial Gateway `announce:v1:` completion. After `sessions.patch` changed the completed child’s model, the parent’s `sessions_send` (`mode: followup`) returned `status: ok` and the expected reply. The child’s own history confirmed that final reply under the new model with the same session ID—no replacement child. Follow-up delivery was synchronous (`delivery.status: skipped`), not a second completion announcement. Six native turn completions and successful cleanup were recorded; production was not deployed or restarted.
- **Red → green through final admission:** all three refreshed-child cases fail on the base with `Session capability metadata changed`; all pass with this fix. The tests perform real session writes, inherit a stale read after a model update, prepare the child, register its host-bound run, and inject the follow-up through the production controller and native-input adapter.
- **Final-effect authority harness:** the authorized case reaches native submission exactly once. Policy revocation or session/parent reassignment after entering the native queue fails with `MessageInjectionAuthorityError` before submission. Authority, database reads, and final worker-backed admission are not mocked; only the native transport I/O is a fixture.
- **Bounds and retained guards:** one intervening publication refreshes successfully; a second invalidation stops. A previously retained synchronous guard cannot be renewed after revocation.
- **Checks:** both affected suites rerun: **34 passed**. Messaging test-shard typecheck, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The earlier **79 consumer tests**, core/agents-sessions typechecks, and docs check remain applicable: this follow-up changes only test coverage, not production or documentation.
- **Independent review:** fresh AutoReview on the complete updated candidate returned scoped-clean at its P0 threshold; it did not execute tests or assess lower-priority findings.

**Validation limits:** The live run verifies the patched completed-child follow-up workflow and initial Gateway completion announcement; it is not a base-versus-head reproduction of the stale inherited-read timing and does not establish that the refresh branch executed. The red/green authority harness supplies that narrower causal evidence and the revocation/reassignment negative cases. The exact mutation in the original incident and later `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` retries remain unconfirmed. This PR fixes the reproduced stale-read preparation failure, not the entire broader incident; fallback classification is separate in #179312.

<details>
<summary>Proof path and verification commands</summary>

The refreshed-child regression follows `withPreparedEmbeddedRunToolAuthority → attachActiveEmbeddedRun → queueCurrentReplyRunMessage → createSteeredCliMessageInjection → withMessageInjectionAdmission → native submit`. The negative cases change persisted policy or identity in the native queue, after the initial authority projection but before final admission. They must enter that queue and must not reach its submit callback.

```text
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts -t 'dispatches a refreshed child'
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-capabilities.store.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.worker.test.ts
```

Previously passed and unchanged consumer coverage: requester policy, harness execution, completion lineage, and prompt-prefix stability. Tests use repository wrappers and pinned OpenClaw Bun with the Node 26.12.1 launcher.

Simplification: no new authority owner or parallel recovery path. The existing async preparation owns the bounded retry; retained replay stays fenced. Against the base: production +21/-2, tests +172/-1, documentation +6; test growth is the final-submission security proof rather than new production machinery.

</details>

prs.title: fix: native Codex turns fail with "settlement is closed" when they finish after 6 minutes
prs.body:
Related: #185121

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a native Codex turn that finishes normally after running more than 6 minutes without OpenClaw-visible progress is stopped by the reply watchdog right after it completes. The run then fails with `session placement turn settlement is closed`, and its finished result is discarded.

## User Impact

User impact: long native Codex turns, such as research or scheduled agent runs (and more of them on slower hosts), keep their completed results instead of failing just after they finish. A run that stays stuck after its native turn ends is still stopped, one full stall window (6 minutes) after the release.

Tradeoff: a native runtime that drops liveness without finishing now gets up to one more stall window before the stall stop. Execution deadlines, terminal-cleanup deadlines and explicit Stop are unchanged. Other `runtime_owned` waits (the `agents_wait` collector and sessionless lane executions) keep today's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

While a `runtime_owned` wait is live, the native runtime owns liveness and the watchdog only observes. Other wait owners publish semantic progress when their wait ends. The native turn's wait instead just stops being current, so on the next tick the watchdog measured the stall window from the last progress *before* the turn started, and stopped a run that had just finished.

The native turn's wait is now registered through `beginNativeRuntimeLivenessWait`, which opts in with `releaseStartsSemanticWindow: true`. While such a wait is live, the watchdog records the last time it observed it live, and measures the semantic window from the later of that time and the last semantic progress. Releasing the wait therefore starts a fresh window instead of expiring the protected interval after the fact. No progress event is invented and the stall policy is unchanged.

It is opt-in rather than applied to every `runtime_owned` wait, because `agents-wait-tool.test.ts` ("does not protect a collector after revoked authority / stalled reread") requires the `agents_wait` collector to lose protection immediately, and a blanket change would break that contract.

Tests: the existing `protects explicit live %s waits, not detached flags` case still covers plain `runtime_owned`. A new watchdog case covers the opted-in release. Two `runs.liveness.test.ts` cases encoded the old timing and are updated:

- `reports quiet runtime waits without scheduling abort` now expects the fresh window after release, then the same controller-owned `run_stalled` stop. It releases between diagnostic heartbeats, so the controller timer, not a heartbeat landing on the same instant, reaches the stall first. That tie exists on `main` for any stall deadline that lands on a heartbeat tick.
- `waits in bounded slices, then reclaims host-owned work without a millisecond spin` previously expected a waiting turn to reclaim the run 1 s after the native runtime released liveness. It now reclaims after the fresh window, still with `run_stalled`.

That second case is the main behavior change for review: a waiting turn now waits up to one stall window for a just-finished native turn to finalize, instead of reclaiming it at once. If you would rather keep a faster reclaim, a shorter finalization grace after release (for example the existing 60 s cleanup window) would also fix the reported failures. I kept the full window because that is what other wait owners get when they publish progress on release.

Possible follow-up, not in this diff: when the watchdog stops a run for a real stall, the lane's abort check reports the closed placement before the abort reason, so users see `session placement turn settlement is closed` instead of the watchdog's stop reason. #180212 works on preserving watchdog causes for automation failures.

## Evidence

**Red/green.** Focused tests on unpatched `main` source (new and updated tests kept) fail at the release tick:

```text
 ✓  protects explicit live runtime_owned waits, not detached flags
 ×  starts the semantic horizon when a native runtime-owned wait releases, never retroactively
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
    342|     live = false; // The native turn completed and released liveness.
    343|     await operation.watchdog.tick();
    344|     expect(cancel).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 37 passed (38)
```

(The runner stops after the first failing shard, so the updated `runs.liveness` case was not run red.)

The same tests pass with the fix:

```text
session-controller.watchdog.test.ts
 ✓  protects explicit live runtime_owned waits, not detached flags
 ✓  starts the semantic horizon when a native runtime-owned wait releases, never retroactively
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
runs.liveness.test.ts
 ✓  reports quiet runtime waits without scheduling abort
 ✓  waits in bounded slices, then reclaims host-owned work without a millisecond spin
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

**Related tests with the fix:** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with the fix: `session-controller.watchdog` 38/38, `runs.liveness` 8/8, `agents-wait-tool` 44/44 (including `does not protect a collector after revoked authority` and `... after stalled reread`), `question.recovery` 16/16. `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files. `pnpm tsgo:core` passes. Pre-commit checks, including the line-cap ratchet, pass; the native wait moved into a small exported helper so `runs.ts` shrinks instead of growing.

**Real-world occurrences before the fix.** One Linux host running the native Codex harness (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`), 2026-10-25/26 ET, two scheduled research jobs (A, B). Every failure happened well under the job's configured timeout (1260 s), and each lane ran under one Gateway process (no restarts):

| Error (ET) | Job | Lane time | Agent output written | Watchdog `blocked reason=cleanup_pending` logged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-25 21:04:27.7 | A | 511.6 s | 13.7 s before the error | 21:04:28 |
| 10-26 08:59:56.3 | A | 511.1 s | 4.3 s before | 08:59:57 |
| 10-26 10:41:35.8 | A | 572.4 s | 13.8 s before | 10:41:34 |
| 10-26 11:57:45.1 | B | 408.3 s | (job writes no separate file) | 11:57:44 |
| 10-26 12:22:09 | A | 621.0 s | 13.4 s before | 12:22:07 |
| 10-26 15:34:33.0 | A | 751.3 s | 7.0 s before | not logged |

The watchdog line lands within about 2.5 s of the error each time it is logged. None of these runs logged a `no_semantic_progress` warning first, because the policy only observes while the wait is live. Journal excerpt for the first run (session keys and run ids redacted):

```text
21:04:27.735 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=511596 error="session placement turn settlement is closed" errorName=AbortError taskKind=turn
21:04:27.764 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted candidate=openai/gpt-6.1-sol errorName=AbortError
21:04:28.440 [diagnostic] reply watchdog: sessionKey=<redacted> action=blocked reason=cleanup_pending
```

**Mechanism (line numbers on `main` at d209419bb9):**

- A native Codex turn registers a deadline-free `runtime_owned` wait that stays current while the handle's `ownsLiveness()` is true (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:963-976`). Codex's `ownsLiveness()` turns false once the turn completes (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts:593-597`).
- While a wait is live, the watchdog policy returns `observe` with no warning or stop (`src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog-state.ts:80`). Lane/maintenance waits (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation.ts:190`) and human input (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts:282`) publish semantic progress when they end; the native wait does not.
- On the next 1 s tick (`src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts:397`), the semantic deadline `progressOrigin + abortMs` (`:146`, 6 min from `:111`) is already in the past, so the watchdog returns `stop` / `semantic_stall`.
- The stop runs `expireOwner` (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation.ts:298`) and the execution cleanups (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation-recovery.ts:210-231`), which include the placement's forced-terminal settlement registered at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/lane-controller.ts:457`.
- The lane's normal completion path then re-checks placement in `throwIfAborted` (`lane-controller.ts:291`), which throws `SESSION_PLACEMENT_TURN_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-admission.ts:549`), and the completed result is dropped.

**Live after-fix Gateway proof (2026-10-27 UTC): passed.** A real local Gateway and native Codex turn ran one synthetic native-shell workload for **390,001 ms**. At the exact native terminal receipt, the owning watchdog's last raw semantic progress was **422,336 ms earlier (7m02.336s)**. The turn completed, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, the connected client received the exact final marker, and the same assistant final was persisted in `chat.history`.

```text
last_raw_semantic_progress = 2026-10-27T00:19:58.354Z
native_terminal_receipt    = 2026-10-27T00:27:00.690Z
raw_semantic_quiet_gap_ms  = 422336 (> 360000)
native_status             = completed
native_wait_registered    = true
watchdog_closed/recovery  = false / false
agent.wait                = ok
local_chat_final/history  = exact marker received / exact marker persisted
result_marker             = WATCHDOG_SETTLED_6BA2C4DF45BE0718489A770C
```

The observation used temporary same-process Inspector logpoints that always returned false, bound to the exact synthetic session, run, and watchdog-attempt object. It read the **raw** semantic clock when the native terminal flag became true, rather than the fix's projected semantic horizon. No accepted semantic renewal occurred after that exact native registration. No clocks, policy, waits, or deadlines were changed, and no debugger pause occurred. The target observer disabled and disconnected after recording terminal. This exercised the real native registration, completion, settlement, WebSocket final-delivery, and canonical-history paths while scheduled work continued on the host.

**Build provenance:** reviewed PR head `5374b18239630999118aa5b7d8a9c849d9a67a5c`; installed build `e620ac5f5f927bd29c8ea6c528942893e33822dc`, based on upstream `3d7f8fbf399df62820f8982cab7f7c2de83648b0` plus the operator's existing local patch set and this PR. Both build stamps identified clean inputs at that installed head. All four files changed by this PR exactly matched its reviewed blobs. Seven additional watchdog/native-path files also matched. The notification controller's pre-existing difference only resets suppression telemetry after a confirmed steering input; this one-input run did not steer. The native terminal flag, liveness, and settlement path are identical. This is explicit evidence from the installed variant; the whole repository heads differ.

| Reviewed file | SHA-256 of the matching installed/PR bytes |
|---|---|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts` | `992810824c8c016c706bb3997587399623df0ce393c96ea03cec63cda75cddef` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.liveness.test.ts` | `6fe4754ac016762382b4976b0f96197091914c1ff25accfa709653f09f85990e` |
| `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts` | `cbc74f36bff24217be8cc7879e1b5a1817efc50be283c285f843f4855e8d394c` |
| `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` | `b1b7c7783dfc44a8ce4bce0f059fd86fdfdaf385527cf1efc3842300196fe1f8` |

The existing watchdog and liveness tests continue to verify the `run_stalled` stop once the fresh semantic window expires. A new independent scoped review of the PR head found no actionable P0/P1 defect; the existing exact-head CI remains the broad test evidence.

**Maintainer decision still requested:** confirm acceptance of the full six-minute semantic window after native liveness ends, including unexplained liveness loss. The live proof establishes successful native completion and delivery; it does not substitute for the session-controller owner's product decision.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Goal Resume fails with “requires an idle built-in local session with recoverable history” after an operator stops a run, even after that work has fully settled. Definitive admission refusals also appear as an unconfirmed update.

## User Impact

Operators can resume the same stopped Goal without resetting the conversation or losing its history. Unsupported admission is reported as a rejection instead of leaving an uncertain operation waiting for reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit Resume may follow a settled abort, not just the special running-Goal replacement flow. Apply that distinction to local and supported Codex cloud-worker admission, while retaining live-work exclusion, freshness, placement, session identity, and current-authority checks. Use the existing typed Goal rejection contract so the existing UI can retire the refused request. Ordinary chat and Goal Start eligibility are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the exact reported rejection through the production Goal RPC boundary after a real Stop and settlement. Both regression assertions failed before the fix.
- All 42 Goal admission/continuation tests passed, including Stop → Resume → completion, preserved Goal identity/history, idempotent replay, worker placement, and authority-revocation cases.
- All 30 existing UI Goal recovery owner tests passed, including definitive-rejection retirement.
- Core production and Gateway-server test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent GPT-6.1 Sol Auto Review completed with no P0 findings (P0-scoped review).

Proof uses real admission, queues, and SQLite with simulated model execution and worker transport; live-model and production-session verification are not claimed. This PR does not deploy or change the running Gateway.

<details>
<summary>Scope and validation notes</summary>

No new policy owner, state, scheduler, or retry mechanism. Production delta: +13/−6 lines; test delta: +37/−3 lines. Reused the existing Stop regression and the existing unsupported-admission case rather than adding another harness.

An initial post-fix run failed during compiler setup, before tests, because Rolldown could not allocate its thread pool. Bounding compiler worker threads resolved setup; the complete 42-test run then passed.

</details>

prs.title: feat(codex): explicitly discard unwanted generated image candidates
prs.body:
Related: #184967

## What Problem This Solves

During Codex image iteration, an unwanted earlier candidate can be automatically published after the agent sends its chosen image.

## User Impact

Agents can explicitly discard unwanted candidates before finishing. Intentional batches and other unsent images retain their current delivery behavior. Discard does not delete files, undo messages, or erase generation side-effect tracking. No configuration or migration is required.

**Maintainer decision needed:** this proposes the explicit per-asset discard contract discussed in the issue review; that review is not design approval. Existing native-owned catalogs are preserved, so a saved catalog without this tool needs a fresh thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex plugin exposes `generated_media` (`list` / `discard`) through normal plugin registration, tool policy, discovery, and Code Mode. Listing supplies current-turn IDs and file references; discard validates every ID before changing the existing projection's automatic-delivery set. Sending one candidate does not implicitly discard another.

An existing opaque tool binding connects the tool to that turn's projection and is cleared on disposal. No new core tool, SDK surface, configuration, dependency, global registry, or persistent state.

## Evidence

- **10 production-owner checks passed** on `158b633e` against the actual projection and tool: B-only exact bytes after discarding A; A's artifact and generation provenance retained; untouched batches, destination-scoped receipts, atomic unknown-ID rejection, duplicate events, and expired/closed bindings covered. This source-owner probe is **not** an app-server/model/channel E2E test.
- **Negative control:** restoring unconditional automatic-media seeding in the compiled probe fails the same B-only assertion with A+B. This isolates the delivery invariant, not a claim that the new command exists on the base commit.
- Canonical `autoreview` on `158b633e`: `scoped-clean` through P2. Independent audit caught the missing manifest declaration (fixed); the subsequent test-only relocation was independently reviewed with no P0–P2 findings.
- **CI passed on current head `abf58bbc`:** [completed CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40409199504). All selected test, lint, typecheck, docs, and guard jobs succeeded; nonselected lanes were skipped. This includes the normal `check-lint` lane after replacing the map spread CI caught on the initial head. Local scoped formatting, diff checks, and source typechecks also passed.
- Added projection/bridge, plugin-registration, and attempt/tool-lifecycle regressions. **No local Vitest pass claimed:** compiled-worker preparation and source/watch collection did not reach assertions under the host resource limits. Lint was also stopped during SDK declaration preparation. The selected CI test and static-check lanes subsequently passed on `abf58bbc`, as linked above.

The managed Codex 0.164.0 image result contract was personally inspected at `openai/codex` tag `rust-v0.164.0` (`fe3b29455488c2e189e43ad5526a107900c5e1b7`, `codex-rs/ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs`): Code Mode returns `image_url` and optional `output_hint`, not the native item ID, hence the explicit list operation.

**Real behavior evidence on `abf58bbc`:** [live RUN4/RUN5 failures and successful RUN6 follow-up, actual receipts and downloaded-byte hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185068#issuecomment-6431517948). A fresh native Codex turn discovered the real tool, generated A+B, discarded only A and retained its files. **RUN6 passed the live exactly-one-B criterion:** Discord received one B attachment and a separate text-only final; downloaded B bytes match both retained copies. Earlier RUN4/RUN5 duplicated B because of pre-existing command account bookkeeping; supplying the source account fixes the test context without changing this PR's source. Those failed runs remain documented. This is an isolated programmatic invocation of the candidate's production one-shot command with scoped in-memory SecretRef bootstrap, **not stock CLI or Discord-ingress proof**. Existing Gateways were not changed or restarted. Maintainer contract approval is still outstanding.

prs.title: fix(android): chat metadata failures show the models refresh error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves The Android chat screen shows "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." when `chat.metadata` fails. In that case `models.list` never runs. One `onFailure` handler in `fetchChatMetadata` covers both calls and always posts the models notice. Closes #183031 ## User Impact Users look for a model or provider fault that does not exist. A transient metadata read race, for example the Gateway `UNAVAILABLE` "Session changed while preparing its metadata. Retry the request.", looks like a model catalog outage. After this change, a `chat.metadata` failure shows "Could not refresh chat metadata. Tap Refresh to try again." A `models.list` failure or a `refreshFailed` catalog still shows the models notice. The accepted model choices stay in the picker in both cases. The existing Refresh action clears both notices. ## Why This Change Was Made - `fetchChatMetadata` records when `chat.metadata` succeeds. The failure handler uses that flag to select the metadata notice or the models notice. - `isChatMetadataNotice` treats both notices as one group. `refresh()` keeps either notice, a `refreshFailed` catalog replaces either notice, and a clean refresh clears either notice. - The new string goes through `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`. The change adds no retry policy. ClawSweeper scoped the fix to the diagnostic on the issue. This change redoes the closed #183251 on current main, after #183040 changed `fetchChatMetadata`. ## Evidence Unit tests in `ChatControllerCatalogTest`: | Test | Base `2f534438` | This branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `metadataRejectionNamesMetadataAndKeepsModelChoices` | ❌ expected chat metadata notice, got models notice | ✅ | | `catalogFailuresReplaceRecoveredMetadataNotice` | ❌ expected chat metadata notice, got models notice | ✅ | The first test also asserts that `models.list` does not run after the rejection, and that Refresh clears the notice. The second test covers a `refreshFailed` catalog and a `models.list` exception after metadata recovers. Commands, from `apps/android`: - `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCatalogTest' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerModelSelectionTest' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerSwarmProgressTest'`: 81 tests, 0 failures (Catalog 9.4 s, ModelSelection 6.8 s, SwarmProgress 0.8 s). - `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck :app:lintPlayDebug`: pass. - `pnpm android:i18n:check`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm protocol:check`, `git diff --check`: pass. Live run on an Android emulator (Pixel 8, API 36) against an isolated local Gateway on loopback. The Gateway used a fixture provider with three models and no real keys. A local-only toggle, not part of this PR, made `chat.metadata` or `models.list` return `UNAVAILABLE`. I installed the APK from main first, then the APK from this branch. | Step | Gateway RPC result | Banner | | --- | --- | --- | | Before: metadata fault | `✗ chat.metadata UNAVAILABLE`, no `models.list` | "Could not refresh models" ❌ | | After 1: metadata fault | `✗ chat.metadata UNAVAILABLE`, no `models.list` | "Could not refresh chat metadata" ✅ | | After 2: fault off, Refresh | `✓ chat.metadata`, `✓ models.list` | none ✅ | | After 3: models fault | `✓ chat.metadata`, `✗ models.list UNAVAILABLE` | "Could not refresh models" ✅ | | After 4: fault off, Refresh | `✓ chat.metadata`, `✓ models.list` | none ✅ | The model picker kept all three fixture models, with the default model selected, before and after the fix. Before:
Metadata failsChoices kept
After:
Metadata failsChoices keptRefresh clearsModels failsRefresh clears

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422

## What Problem This Solves

Generated Markdown under an agent workspace's `memory/` tree can enter Memory Search and compete with curated notes, with no supported path exclusion for the default roots.

## User Impact

Users can opt in to workspace-relative `memory.search.excludePaths` globs, for example `memory/dreaming/**` and `memory/.dreams/**`. With no setting, indexing behavior is unchanged. Source files remain intact; changing the scope triggers index rebuilding on the next sync. This PR addresses search indexing and watcher eligibility only, not short-term recall/promotion eligibility or inline generated blocks within otherwise eligible notes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery and local/remote watchers share the same workspace-relative exclusion predicate. It applies to default roots and overlapping extra paths. The configured scope hash changes only for nonempty exclusions, so existing users retain their index identity. The core config baseline increases by four generated entries as an intentional new optional setting.

This is a draft for the open product-scope decision in #101422; it does not claim to resolve the broader coordinated include/exclude request.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: 139/139 passed across config resolution, file discovery, local/remote watch transport, manager indexing/reindexing, and path matching; the final path-boundary regression passed again (3/3).
- Core and extension production typechecks, changed-file lint/format, config baseline check, config example check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- Independent read-only review found two defects (local watcher propagation and a path-segment boundary), both fixed and reverified.
- Extension test typecheck is blocked by an unchanged `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts:675` type error on current main. The broad `check:changed` run was stopped after detecting unrelated current-main UI line-cap/test-root-budget failures; it is not claimed green.
- No production Gateway/config/index migration or live reindex was performed. A deployed release and an operator opt-in are required before existing indexed rows can be removed in a real workspace.

## Follow-up review repair (rebased head `a2008ab09`)

- Fixed the reviewer's P2 shared-watcher finding: the effective `excludePaths` now participates in shared selection identity, so joining/leaving agents with different exclusion policies rebaseline the watcher. A focused regression failed on the prior head and passes with the fix; watcher lifecycle tests passed 36/36 on the rebased head.
- A real fs-safe worker join test passed 2/2: after an excluding agent starts, a non-excluding agent joins on the same worker and receives an edit to a formerly excluded report. The mocked lifecycle test also checks rebaseline on both join and leave.
- Built CLI end-to-end test passed 2/2 in isolated state: a normal config-change index removed the generated report without `--force`, retained a curated note, and indexed its subsequent edit. The new CLI case is not Windows-skipped.
- After rebasing onto upstream main `f8dcd1d7f` (and verifying a clean trial merge with later `2e7bc82ad`), 129 targeted tests passed across source/config/watcher paths, plus 36 watcher-lifecycle tests on the final amended head. Core and memory-core extension typechecks, changed-file lint/format, generated config-doc check, and diff whitespace check passed. Independent read-only review of the full rebased 33-file diff found no actionable P0–P2 defect.
- Latest stable `v2026.10.5` indexed two synthetic files in an isolated upgrade fixture. The new head refused to open that older state until Doctor obtains backed-up client-credential migration custody. No backup/Doctor migration was run, so cross-version upgrade proof remains open; this is not claimed as a feature regression or as a passing migration.
- This branch has not been deployed to the operator's Mac; no live config change or reindex occurred. Maintainer approval of the search-only opt-in contract under #101422 remains required before merge.

prs.title: fix(a2a): complete tasks queued behind an active turn
prs.body:
Related: #144534

## What Problem This Solves

A2A tasks can remain `WORKING` after their model answer finishes when they queue behind an active turn in the same context.

## User Impact

Peers receive the answer and terminal state on the original task instead of waiting indefinitely or receiving a new reverse-direction message. Successful silence, failed execution, and aborted execution settle that same task. Existing peer isolation and terminal-content filtering remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

A2A supplies its task-correlated callback to the existing queue completion owner. The plugin runtime retains that callback's consumer through deferred settlement, while immediate replies keep their consumer until dispatch returns. The optional callback is exposed through the existing `GetReplyOptions` contract. One payload filter serves both immediate and queued replies.

The callback awaits task settlement so it remains compatible with the asynchronous persistence owner in #183490. These are separate fixes; land #183490 first. This branch includes the reviewed #183490 head as a merge parent so its callbacks are checked against the actual asynchronous store; after #183490 lands, only the queued-reply change remains in this PR. This PR does not claim to resolve the entire issue or the separate protocol work in #179380.

Thanks @ensignwesley for the implementation and original real-Gateway proof.

## Evidence

- Main `364c0d4ebcd4`: all four queued inbound cases fail because the callback is missing. The matching-source delivery regression loses its terminal payload to origin routing; the unmatched-source control passes. Cold preparation dominates the 508.57s inbound and 455.85s delivery runs.
- Real isolated Gateway at `0fb88848e7a1`: the first HTTP model response is held, and the second same-context task queues while the request count remains one. After release and the second model response, the original second task still reports `WORKING` with no artifact. Another peer receives `-32001`.

- The repaired candidate passes all 81 focused tests: 56 followup-delivery (390.35s), 10 runtime-channel (121.55s), and 15 A2A inbound (97.60s); cold transforms dominate these times. The runtime build passed in 8m43.7s.
- Real isolated Gateway replay: while the first HTTP response is held, the second same-context task is accepted with only one model request in flight. On release, the original second task `2073fa48-07f6-48e3-9f22-383ba02f685c` becomes `COMPLETED` with the expected `A2A_QUEUE_SECOND` artifact. A different peer receives `-32001`. Both Gateway and fixture stopped cleanly.
- Fixture correction: Activity recaps also call the provider, so responses are scoped by model. Polling uses the isolated config's disabled rate limit; production defaults are unchanged. The earlier rapid-polling attempt hit the default rate limit and is not claimed as passing proof.
- Formatting, core lint, syntax lint, and diff checks pass. Local extension typed lint and typecheck refuse the shared dependency installation; PR CI supplies those checks. Independent Codex P0–P2 review found no actionable issue in the full diff.
- Production +124/-45 (net +79); tests +184/-1 (net +183); docs +18. The necessary production growth retains the existing consumer across deferred settlement; payload filtering is shared. This is two additional production lines compared with the original proposal, for awaited durable settlement and clearer routing.
- Current main `9d27ef2e5ca3` is integrated. It changes none of the A2A, queue-delivery or plugin-runtime owner code touched here. Its existing test budget covers this PR, so no baseline exception remains. The 15 A2A inbound tests pass again after integration (173.37s; cold transforms dominate). The first exact-head run (40581477617) caught two `await-thenable` lint errors because this branch did not yet contain the asynchronous store from #183490. The dependency merge fixes that mismatch without a compatibility wrapper. It also encountered the same five unrelated UI `eslint(curly)` errors as [scheduled main run 40578163761](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40578163761/job/122450734896); the source files and diagnostics match. Final [composed-head CI run 40592767365](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40592767365) is green: all 48 executed jobs passed, with 28 intentional skips.

The HTTP model fixture is local and deterministic. External paid models and real chat platforms are not part of this proof.

The composed head `ce1d4264fc1e0c7904fe937f5a9fc476845a41f7` passes all 15 inbound tests again (121.81s Vitest / 135.45s wrapper), formatting and focused boundary lint. A fresh independent P0–P2 review of the dependency integration found no actionable issue. The only merge conflict was retaining the two independent imports. Live queue/restart proofs above are reused for the unchanged component implementations; no paid-provider proof is claimed. LOC for the queued-reply change relative to #183490 remains production +124/-45, tests +184/-1, docs +18.

Test-line ceiling raised to 6291318: main was already 1312 over (concurrent merges); this PR adds 179 lines of base-red queued-followup completion regressions.

prs.title: fix(mcp): warn when OAuth credentials expire without a refresh token
prs.body:
Related: #160611

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp status` can report `authorized` for an expired OAuth access token that has no refresh token, while `doctor` provides no expiry-specific recovery guidance.

## User Impact

Operators see an expiry warning and the sign-in command needed to restore access directly in status and doctor output. `status --json` exposes the same diagnostic through an optional `oauthWarning`.

This PR addresses the expiry-diagnostic subproblem in #160611.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing CLI OAuth module now supplies one read-only status projection and sign-in recovery message to both status and doctor.

## Summary

```text
native shared OAuth:
  authorized + expired access token + no refresh token
    -> expiry warning + sign-in recovery command
```

## Evidence

Validation head: `b391cd0f636864d9b892c5ad593fded7c3f30f5b`, integrating main `5291a06cc263f0815fa087fd02bbdb29c3839089`.

- **Before:** the CLI integration regression failed because expired credentials without a refresh token produced no expiry warning.
  **After:** the six-scenario regression passes through the real Command/configuration/SQLite boundary in **3.933 seconds**.
- Five focused CLI, OAuth, login-loopback, and import-boundary suites: **53 passed, 1 existing platform-specific test skipped on Windows**. The checks cover manual `--issuer` forwarding and the issuer from the loopback callback.
- Test cost: **758.72 seconds wall time**, including 478.82 seconds preparing compiled workers; the two Vitest shards took 201.08 and 23.23 seconds.
- Production and CLI test typechecks, targeted oxlint, five-file formatting, documentation Markdown lint, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Canonical autoreview against the integrated base: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- Built CLI validation: `status`, `status --json`, and `doctor` all exited **0**, with an expired refresh-token control. Current-head captures are below.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

The core already identifies these notices with isCompactionNotice. Exempt that flag from both Discord progress-block suppression guards instead of treating lifecycle notices as answer deltas. Base returns no notices; cancellation/policy controls pass. Patched: 3/3 pass, including both notice phases and ordinary-block suppression.
- Run: node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.compaction.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (equivalent to pnpm test for the selected file). Final green Vitest duration 5.58s; wrapper wall time 6.84s. Base cold-compile duration 26.56s; wrapper 28.81s. CI seconds not yet available. Existing process fixture imports dominate compile time; the regression needs this composition to cross both suppression points.
- Existing process.draft-final suite: 20/20 pass (6.01s Vitest / 7.33s wrapper). Draft-preview REST fixture suite: 16/16 pass (5.65s / 6.81s).

**Limits:** fixture-backed integration, not live Discord or real-model compaction proof. No external test messages or deployment performed. prs.title: fix(security): pre-auth helper route rule misses non-GET and router registrations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the precise OpenGrep rule for GHSA-92JP-89MQ-4374 (`openclaw-browser-bridge-preauth-helper-route`) does not report a browser bridge helper route registered before the auth middleware when the route uses a verb other than `get`, or a `router`/`server` instance instead of `app`.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. Maintainers get a finding for the pre-auth registration shapes the rule missed (`post`, `all`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options`, `head`, and `router.`/`server.` receivers). Current main has no such registration, so the scan of main stays at 0 findings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rule matched `app.get($ROUTE, ...)` only. A helper route is just as reachable before `installBrowserAuthMiddleware` when it is registered as `app.post(...)`, `app.all(...)` or `router.post(...)`, so those were false negatives.

- The rule now matches `$APP.$M($ROUTE, ...)`, with `$APP` in `app|server|router` and `$M` in `get|post|put|patch|delete|options|head|all`.
- `$APP` and `$M` are bound once per match. The existing exemptions (the middleware installed on the same receiver before the route, or a `hasVerifiedBrowserAuth` guard in the handler) therefore apply only to that same receiver and verb. A route registered after the middleware does not hide an earlier pre-auth registration of the same path under another verb (fixture cases `preAuthPostBeforeMiddleware` and `preAuthGetBeforeMiddleware`).
- The rule's source YAML and a scanner fixture now sit in `security/opengrep/rules/ghsa-92jp-89mq-4374/`, like the other source rules. `precise.yml` is regenerated with `compile-rules.mjs --update-existing`. That changes only this rule's patterns plus the compiler's `advisory-id`/`source-file` metadata (145 rules, 1 updated).
- Tradeoff: the metavariable receiver weakens opengrep's literal prefilter, so this rule parses more files. In a local single-rule full-tree scan it went from 75 s to 112 s. It adds no findings and no new error types: the extra entries are parser `PartialParsing`/`Syntax error` warnings on files the narrower rule never parsed, and the single `Timeout` (a minified asset) is the same in both runs.

## Evidence

opengrep 1.31.0, the CI pin, with the sha256 checked against `opengrep-precise.yml`:

- **Before:** the fixture against the rule as it is on main (the source YAML holding main's exact body): `opengrep test` rc=1, `missing findings lines 23, 30, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 60, 67, 74, 126`. That is 11 of 13 `ruleid` lines; only the two `app.get` cases hit.
- **After:** `opengrep test --config security/opengrep/rules/ghsa-92jp-89mq-4374 security/opengrep/rules/ghsa-92jp-89mq-4374` gives `1/1: ✓ All tests passed`, rc=0.
- **Mutations of the new rule, each rc=1:**
  - `post` dropped from the verb regex: lines 23, 60, 67 and 126 missed.
  - `router` dropped from the receiver regex: line 67 missed.
  - The exemption reverted to a literal `installBrowserAuthMiddleware(app, ...)`: an unexpected finding on line 98, the post-auth router case.
- **Rulepack checks:** `node security/opengrep/check-rule-metadata.mjs` reports ok. `opengrep validate security/opengrep/precise.yml` reports `Configuration is valid … 145 rule(s)`, the same at base and head.
- **Full-tree scan** of `src/ extensions/ apps/ packages/ scripts/` (20,351 paths, `.semgrepignore` applied): 0 findings before and after.
- **Format:** `oxfmt --check` (0.73.0) on the changed files is clean.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Control UI replies stalling when a long response includes a managed `MEDIA:` line.

Fixes #185298

## Why This Change Was Made

The live projector filters completed managed media lines while preserving the canonical display transform for later text. It also keeps whitespace-only lines intact when prose continues after media.

## User Impact

Long Control UI replies with managed media keep streaming, with visible text matching the canonical display transform.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/live-chat-projector.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 tests passed, including canonical whitespace parity.
- `node src/gateway/proof-managed-media-stream.mjs`: runs the focused Gateway proof through the committed runner. The test feeds an assistant delta, a fixture tool result carrying the same relative media URL, then later assistant deltas with that URL marked managed. Production Gateway chat event handlers and the live projector emit the replacement before continued appends, remove the managed directive, preserve the blank line, and retain the absolute unmanaged control. The agent event source is stubbed at the existing Gateway test seam; this proof makes no external model request.

before: `MEDIA:chart.png` appears in the first Gateway delta before the fixture tool result.

after: the full replacement removes the managed directive before subsequent append frames, while canonical blank-line spacing remains.

negative-control: `MEDIA:/tmp/a.png` remains visible because it is an unmanaged absolute reference.

Tested head: `53b30bee1cc13cffc75b800e3114c1cdd9d230c6`.

```text
[gateway-stream-proof] assistantDirective=MEDIA:chart.png toolResultMediaUrl=chart.png toolResultBeforeActivation=true replacementBeforeContinuedDeltas=true frames=[{"state":"delta","deltaText":"Intro\nMEDIA:chart.png\nDone "},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"Intro\nDone again","replace":true},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"\n\nNext"},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"\nMEDIA:/tmp/a.png"}] visible=["Intro\nMEDIA:chart.png\nDone ","Intro\nDone again","Intro\nDone again\n\nNext","Intro\nDone again\n\nNext\nMEDIA:/tmp/a.png"]

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

<summary>Gateway proof script</summary>

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

const result = spawnSync(
  "pnpm",
  [
    "test",
    "src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts",
```

prs.title: fix(devices): approving an expired pairing request reports unknown requestId
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: approving a pairing request that has passed its 5 minute pending TTL answers "unknown requestId" (or "device pairing approval denied" when a paired device approves its own request), so `openclaw devices approve <id>` cannot tell an expired request from a mistyped one.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator who approves a request that timed out now sees "pairing request expired; reconnect the device to request pairing again" instead of an error that reads like a typo or a permissions problem.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expired pending rows are filtered out of reads and out of approval, but they stay stored until the next pending write prunes them, and a refused approval does not prune. The pending read now also returns such a row as `expired` (new `getExpiredDevicePairingRequest`), and `device.pair.approve` uses it:

- admin callers: only after approval returns nothing, so the happy path does no extra read;
- non-admin callers: when the live lookup misses, the expired row goes through the same ownership and role checks a live request gets before it is reported. A device still cannot learn anything about another device's request; that case keeps answering "device pairing approval denied" and now records the same denied security event a live cross-device attempt records.

Accepted edge cases, left as they are:

- once a later pairing write has pruned the row, the answer is "unknown requestId", as today;
- the CLI's local-state fallback (used when the gateway refuses the CLI's own connect) still reports "No pending device request matches";
- a device whose approval connect needs a scope it does not hold still stops at the existing scope-upgrade message before reaching this handler.

## Evidence

Run with the repo's own toolchain (node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) on base 384100f491d7; upstream main has not touched these files since.

- RED, new tests against unchanged production code:
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.test.ts`: 3 failed / 21 passed. A device session and a shared-auth session got "device pairing approval denied", an admin got "unknown requestId", where "pairing request expired; ..." is expected.
  - `src/infra/device-pairing.test.ts`: 1 failed / 30 passed (the new read does not exist yet).
- GREEN at the PR head: `devices.test.ts` 24/24, `device-pairing.test.ts` 31/31.
- Mutation checks: reporting "expired" before the ownership check fails "keeps another device's expired request denied to non-admin device sessions"; returning the row as expired while it is still live fails the infra test.
- Neighbours, all green (135 tests): device-pairing store, worker, churn and prune; `devices.lifecycle`, `device-scope-upgrade`, `devices-cli`, `devices-cli.gateway`.
- `pnpm check:changed` at the PR head: 34 of 35 checks pass, including format, lint, typecheck core and core tests, the line-cap ratchet and the pairing store guards. The dead-export scan fails with the same entries at base 384100f491d7 (`pnpm deadcode:exports`, exit 1): `ReductionCheckpoint`, `rollbackStatelessClawPackages` and `readOriginDeviceTokenReadOnlyForTest`, none in a file this PR touches.

prs.title: fix(agents): personal_instructions fails every turn when a Gateway tool policy lists its actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every agent turn fails with "Gateway tool policy requires personal_instructions to declare a top-level string action field" when `tools.gatewayPolicy` allows `personal_instructions` with a list of actions.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who restrict a Gateway with `tools.gatewayPolicy` can now grant `personal_instructions` with explicit actions (for example only `get`). Before, the only working setting was `actions: []`, which withholds the tool. No change for Gateways without a tool policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway tool policy narrows a tool's actions only when the tool declares `action` as a top-level string field. `personal_instructions` declared it as a union of literals, which TypeBox emits as `anyOf` with no `type`, so the policy refused it on every turn. The tool now uses the shared `stringEnum` helper, like the other action tools, which emits `{ "type": "string", "enum": ["get", "set"] }`. That is also the form providers that reject `anyOf` in tool schemas accept. Execute-time validation is unchanged.

## Evidence

Run on a remote test VM against this head and against `main` (a43a77bf92d):

- A scratch probe (not committed) that builds the real tool and applies a policy of `actions: { personal_instructions: ["get"] }`:
  - on `main`: throws "requires personal_instructions to declare a top-level string action field";
  - on this branch: the schema is `{"type":"string","enum":["get","set"]}`, the narrowed schema accepts `get` and rejects `set`, the policy assertion denies `set`, and `actions: []` still withholds the tool.
- Focused tests: `gateway-tool-policy`, `users-personal-file`, `openclaw-tools.registration`, `tool-catalog` and Gateway `tools-catalog` tests: 5 files, 109 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `oxfmt --check` on the touched file is clean; `check:test-lines-ratchet` net delta 0.

No regression test is added: the change makes this tool match its siblings' declaration, and the test-lines ratchet is at its ceiling.
