prs.title: fix(agents): keep bundle MCP access for turns woken by an exec completion
prs.body:
Closes #183589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a backgrounded host exec exits and `tools.exec.notifyOnExit` (default `true`) wakes the originating session, the woken turn has no bundle MCP tools although the run that started the exec had them (Code Mode telemetry `sources: {openclaw: 51, mcp: 0}`, `tools.effective` notice `mcp-not-yet-connected`), and any child spawned from that woken turn inherits the restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: a turn woken by an exec completion keeps exactly the MCP access of the run that started the exec, and children it spawns do too: an unrestricted run keeps every configured server, a run capped to `fixture__*` wakes a turn that can reach only the `fixture` server, an exact-name policy such as `fixture__read` keeps only that tool. Runs with no `mcp.servers`, or whose cap excludes bundle MCP tools, behave exactly as before, so a woken turn never gains access the producer run did not have. No config, schema, or wire change; `notifyOnExit` no longer has to be disabled to keep MCP in long-lived sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createOpenClawCodingTools` (`src/agents/agent-tools.ts`) builds each tool's Gateway caller with a default `sessionEventSourcePolicy` whose `toolsAllow` lists the finalized coding tools. Bundle MCP tools are materialized afterwards (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`), so no `server__tool` name or `bundle-mcp` marker is ever in that list. The exec tool records the policy as the completion event's `producerPolicy`; `captureSessionEventTarget` intersects the woken turn's `toolsAllow` with it; `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` then finds no bundle name and creates no MCP runtime for the woken turn or its children.

The fix captures the producer's final surface instead of predicting it (revision 5). `createOpenClawCodingTools` now fills a caller-owned array (`sessionEventToolsAllowRef`) with the coding tool names and hands that same array to every Gateway caller as `sessionEventSourcePolicy.toolsAllow`. The embedded attempt (`attempt-bundle-tools.ts`) appends the bundled MCP/LSP tools that survived the attempt's runtime allowlist, `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`, and schema projection, by exact name, in the same place it already captures the cron creator cap and the spawn allowlist. The exec tool reads the policy when it records the completion, so the woken turn gets exactly the tools this run could call:

- sender-scoped denials (`tools.toolsBySender["id:alice"].deny: ["admin__*"]`) already removed `admin__reset` from the producer's final surface, so the senderless woken turn never sees it;
- intersected caps, partial globs (`fixture__read*` ∩ `fixture__*All`), and namespace-reaching globs (`fixture*`) are resolved by the existing runtime matcher on real tools, not approximated;
- a refresh replaces the previously appended bundled names, so a tool quarantined or filtered on refresh drops out;
- no marker or glob is ever added, so the continuation cannot widen past the producer.

The surface stays under the existing 512-name bound the target reader enforces (`SESSION_EVENT_TOOLS_ALLOW_LIMIT`, now exported from `session-event-target.ts`); past it, the attempt logs a warning and the woken turn keeps only the coding tools. Revision 5 deletes `agent-tools.session-event-policy.ts` and its tests (revisions 1–4 projected MCP access from allow patterns, which the review showed cannot preserve denials or every glob shape).

## Evidence

Regression in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts` (`session event tool surface`, 9 cases through `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` with `fixture` and `admin` servers materializing `fixture__read`, `fixture__readAll`, `fixture__write`, `admin__reset`; each captured cap is then run through the woken turn's `intersectSessionEventToolsAllow` → `shouldCreateBundleMcpRuntimeForAttempt` → `applyEmbeddedAttemptToolsAllow`):

- unrestricted producer → all four MCP tools; `["exec", "fixture__*"]` and `["exec", "fixture*"]` → the three fixture tools; `["exec", "fixture__read"]` → `fixture__read`;
- intersected `[["exec", "fixture__read*"], ["exec", "fixture__*All"]]` → `fixture__readAll` (revision 4 returned nothing here);
- `["read", "exec"]` → no MCP tool and no bundle runtime in the woken turn;
- producer final policy drops `admin__reset` (the sender-scoped denial shape) → the woken turn never admits it;
- refresh after a projection drops `fixture__readAll` → the cap shrinks to `["exec", "fixture__read"]`;
- a coding surface at the bound → MCP names are not appended.

Red on `main`: the attempt never appends to the cap, so every case expecting an MCP tool fails, the reported loss.

Suites: `attempt-bundle-tools` 23/23; `bash-tools.exec-notify`, `tools/gateway-caller-context`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `attempt-tool-prepare.web-search`, `session-event-handoff`, `session-event-context`, `session-event-permissions` 115/115. Oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.

### Live Gateway run (revision 3, shipped entry point, real model)

Built dist from this head, isolated state dir, non-interactive onboarding against OpenRouter (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`, custom openai-compatible provider), two loopback streamable-http MCP servers written for the proof (`fixture` on 19882 exposing `echo`, `admin` on 19883 exposing `reset`; each logs every JSON-RPC request), `mcp.servers` for both, `tools.allow: ["read", "exec", "process", "fixture__*"]`, `tools.exec.security: full`, `tools.exec.ask: off`, Gateway started with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19881`.

One turn through the Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs agent --agent main --json --message …`): run `sleep 8; echo done` in the background with exec and end the turn; when woken by the exec completion, call `fixture__echo` with `hi`, then try `admin__reset`, and report both.

```text
13:56:04Z  turn starts
13:56:05Z  fixture initialize / tools/list     admin initialize / tools/list   (bundle discovery of both configured servers; no tool call)
13:56:10Z  assistant: "started"                  agent exit=0 (turn ended, exec still running)
13:56:21Z  woken turn: tool_describe mcp:fixture:fixture__echo
13:56:23Z  woken turn: dispatch_action fixture__echo {"text":"hi"}
13:56:23Z  fixture server log: tools/call echo   CALL echo {"text":"hi"}      → "fixture:echo:ok"
13:56:24Z  woken turn: dispatch_action admin__reset {"text":"hi"}
13:56:24Z  toolResult: {"status":"error","error":"Unknown tool id: admin__reset. Use tool_search to find a tool…"}
13:56:26Z  assistant: fixture__echo returned "fixture:echo:ok". admin rejected: no tool named admin__reset exists in the catalog …
```

The `admin` server log contains no `tools/call` at any time: the `admin__reset` call was refused by the woken turn's tool catalog before any request left the Gateway. The fixture call reached its server and succeeded in the turn woken by the exec exit (the first turn had ended at 13:56:10 with the 8-second command still running). Discovery (`initialize`/`tools/list`) still connects both configured servers during the producer turn, as on `main`; policy filters tools, not discovery.

Not rerun for revision 5. That run proved the ordinary `fixture__*` wake and the `admin__reset` rejection; revision 5 yields the same surface for that config. Not demonstrated live: a sender-scoped denial (needs a channel sender id on the producer turn), a descendant spawned from the woken turn, and revocation between capture and wake. For revocation, the woken turn still runs its own current policy pipeline over the captured names, so a later `tools.deny` removes a tool there; that path is unchanged by this PR.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice requests stall before the backing agent starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Talk voice requests stalling before the backing agent starts when a provider callback runs under a different Gateway scope from the conversation it belongs to.

## User Impact

Voice requests use their existing admission reservation instead of waiting behind a duplicate input. Invalid or stale ownership is rejected before execution. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register each consultation under its captured Gateway and give its runtime the exact registered source. Validate that source before admission and after asynchronous preparation, then consume it only once. This reuses the existing mailbox owner and preserves FIFO, cancellation, and delayed completion custody without introducing another scheduler or global run lookup.

The alternate execution-runtime branch is removed. Production changes are +101/-52 lines; tests and test support are +446/-3, covering the public native handoff, ownership mismatches, one-shot reuse, and concurrent FIFO behavior.

## Evidence

- **129 tests passed across ten focused files after the CI repair**, including all 15 runtime-source cases, the independently constructed native-plugin handoff regression, browser disconnect/close, retained authority, terminal writes, relay adoption, and source ownership. Command wall time: 119 seconds. CI seconds for the revised head are not yet available.
- Production and Gateway-other test typechecks, three-file format/lint checks, mock-export and line-cap ratchets, and diff checks passed after the repair. Checks for unchanged files are reused from the initial five-file validation.
- Fresh bound Auto Review of the final staged candidate completed **scoped-clean with no P0–P3 findings**. The intermediate review's index-only lifecycle finding was resolved before this checkpoint.
- Original head `ae95ef7a24ebbc583c68e1f0fcb2c13706a367e8` failed [two browser lifecycle cases in CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40192516249/job/121166812483) and the [mock-isolation documentation ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40192516249/job/121166812392). The lifecycle failures reproduced locally. The repair keeps transport liveness at admission entry/turn selection while checking the exact source and retained authority before execution; the strengthened tests verify the original registered input is claimed after disconnect/close. The model-isolation reason is now documented in the required form.
- Reused original-discussion evidence: two duplicate-input regressions fail on base `0fc39d235aa26f918844276d0a138de3e3bdf322` by creating two mailbox inputs, rather than merely timing out. The original implementation and initial 95-test run (88.41 seconds) occurred there. This publication session independently applied the patch, passed the original 95-test suite (141 seconds including cold preparation), then made and validated the CI repair above.

The agent's native Talk regression was independently constructed after an external-client symptom report. It exercises public-code registration, source ownership, and admission with synthetic provider/model execution. The agent has not performed an actual Control UI/browser/Talk call. The human-reported native BEFORE evidence below is separate; there is no patched real-call AFTER or live-provider recovery evidence. The controlled regression does **not** establish the original incident's cause. No full-repository build or full test suite was run.

### Human-reported native Control UI BEFORE (not agent-observed)

Related: [#183597](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/183597), reported by @bdjben. The original counter/log report supplies symptom evidence; the later human-published retained-state analysis below supplies stronger structural evidence. This remains Related, not Closes.

@bdjben reports three actual native Control UI calls on clean **2026.10.5**, revision `db207e077b74e95aacca56851957ffd8683cccfa`, using WebRTC/OpenAI/agent-consult on the same pseudonymous **conversation-A**. The browser recognized speech and acknowledged it, but returned no substantive result. Read-only `sessions.describe` reported `hasActiveRun: false`. A `talk.realtime.model` change preceded Call 3; the inspected configuration selected `openai/gpt-live-1-codex`.

<details>
<summary>Human-authorized sanitized timing summary</summary>

All times are milliseconds relative to each call's ready event at +0.

| Call | transcript.done | lifecycle-admission settled/acquired | source-claim waiting/mailbox-selection | Pending inputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | +19,283 | +19,515 | +19,551 | 2 |
| 2 | +8,289 | +8,340 | +8,364 | 4 |
| 3 | Not reported | +29,429 | +29,477 | 6 |

All three waiting observations reported `injectingInputs: 0` and `withdrawalHolds: 0`. Phase records were trace-correlated with `omittedObservations: 0`. The human reports no source/Gateway modification, restart, reset, cancellation, or replay. Raw records remain private; only this sanitized summary is authorized for publication.

</details>

The original counters/logs alone did not establish lookup failure or duplicate-entry causation. As [the preceding qualifications explain](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/183597#issuecomment-6398086378), pending counts include all mailbox entries, withdrawal holds describe the observed input, and the waiting diagnostic precedes selector wakeup. In particular, `hasActiveRun: false` is a visible-active-run projection that excludes hidden Talk registrations; it does not prove that no Talk source is registered.

### Human-reported retained live-state BEFORE evidence

In [@bdjben's published structural report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/183597#issuecomment-6398191857), offline analysis of a single private heap snapshot from the same still-running, unpatched Gateway recovered the following relationships for all three native calls. **These are human-reported findings, not raw-snapshot observations independently inspected by the agent.**

- Each original RPC input remains registered and accepted (`rpcAccepted: true`), has the expected runtime-session identity and a non-aborted signal, and is still `preparing`, with `payload: "unbound"` and no task function.
- A distinct `waiting` input with a task closure follows each original input and lacks `protocolRunId` and `sourceSessionId`. The actual order is **registered-A, waiting-A, registered-B, waiting-B, registered-C, waiting-C** (pseudonyms).
- Each waiting closure retains its corresponding Talk runtime invocation with `source === undefined` and admission `controllerInput === undefined`. Its requested run ID is the **same retained heap string node** as the original registered input's protocol run ID; the retained Talk owner's voice-session/run identity also correlates it to that call.
- All three retained runtimes carry a bound Gateway resolver whose binding chain reaches the captured canonical host resolver, while none of the three original registrations has a Gateway binding slot. The report identifies both the incompatible ownership state and the retained missing lookup result, not just a hypothetical mismatch.
- The taskless `preparing` head has no ready handler; the mailbox has no claim and the controller has no active operation. It does not satisfy the selector's waiting/task-ready requirements, leaving its runnable duplicate behind it.

This published analysis directly supports **source lookup miss → fallback duplicate task input → blocked original reservation** in the reported native calls, materially strengthening the earlier 2/4/6 counters. It establishes retained state at one capture, not every historical binding transition or every possible origin of ambient-scope loss. No live getter/resolver callback was invoked during the offline analysis. Raw memory and identifying records remain private.

The external-client report, human-reported native BEFORE evidence, and independently controlled regression remain distinct. **No patched live Control UI AFTER recovery has been tested.** The related issue remains open; this is not a claim that every similar stall shares this cause.

Additional native-route/final-effect authority coverage is being prepared separately. Its current unrun draft is not validation evidence and is not included in the published change.


<details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep agent names through offline reloads and reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on airplane or spotty-network connections, reloading a cached chat shows “Message Assistant” until the Gateway reconnects, even when the conversation's agent has a custom name.

## User Impact

User impact: cached conversations show the correct agent name and text avatar from their first render and keep them through reconnect, alongside the reconnect indicator. No configuration, migration, or user action is required.

Release-note context: Control UI preserves cached agent names and text avatars during offline reloads and reconnects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The offline shell cannot fetch bootstrap identity, and transport changes reset the pane's displayed name. The existing scoped boot roster already contains the missing display facts. This change reads them through the identity owner before the pane renders and replaces them when live facts arrive, without admitting cached agents into live discovery or adding storage.

The same identity fields serve the composer, chat identity presentation, and working labels. Connection, agent, recovery-account, and retired-access boundaries remain in force. Current discovery replaces cached roster facts so a later disconnect cannot revive an old name or removed agent.

Accepted edge cases: a rename made elsewhere while the browser is completely offline remains unknown until live refresh; a missing, mismatched, or retired cache uses the generic identity rather than borrowing another agent's name. Managed image thumbnails are outside this change; only the cached text avatar is supplied here.

## Evidence

The rig is an isolated local Gateway with synthetic Team-shaped state behind a TCP fault proxy: 700 ms RTT, jitter, ~190 KB/s, silent blackouts / refused connections. The retained offline-reload comparison uses refused connections; the warm scenario uses the slow, jittered connection. Times below are relative to scenario start and are observations, not latency guarantees.

| Scenario | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Offline reload | First composer at 0.332 s says “Message Assistant”; hello at 18.538 s; custom name appears at 19.954 s. | First composer at 0.293 s already says “Message Harbor proof assistant”; unchanged through the outage, hello at 18.969 s, and connected rendering. |
| Warm reload | The campaign observed the same identity gap before live identity arrived. | First composer at 1.185 s has the custom name, before hello at 2.839 s; no name change after reconnect. |

Synthetic offline reload, before:

![Offline reload before: Message Assistant](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/998118a8-29c9-4f2c-a603-9610b6e694a9)

Synthetic offline reload, after:

![Offline reload after: agent name kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63c7ff36-16e3-48ea-aa80-4531b827848c)

Synthetic warm reload, before:

![Warm reload before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/634766a7-0b97-4c1a-a47c-39792a2ed33f)

Synthetic warm reload, after:

![Warm reload after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35fb7a6c-a665-4764-a05b-91106d7a5a26)

The warm-boot regression fails on base with “Message Assistant”. With bootstrap config unavailable and Gateway hello held, it now records only the custom placeholder from first render through matching live identity.

- Passed 164 focused unit cases: warm boot, identity capability, bootstrap identity, pane identity, chat composer, and chat state. Coverage includes different agents, offline agent switching, recovery-account changes, connection revisions, retired scopes, renamed agents, removed agents, and same-client reconnects.
- Passed all 11 warm-boot and offline-session-title E2E cases; rerun after simplification.
- Passed UI typecheck, production UI build, formatting, and diff checks. Independent review is clean through P2.
- Full `pnpm lint` reports inherited repository failures. Changed-file lint reports only bootstrap's inherited line-cap failure: 705 lines on base, reduced to 704, against a 700-line limit. The build reports a non-failing 29-byte CSS gzip overrun. The CI failure comparison below records the follow-up validation.

The simplification pass removed 11 lines of redundant current-placeholder assertions: the retained placeholder-history assertions independently detect both an incorrect first name and any reconnect flip. Every remaining test protects a distinct failure boundary. Production behavior is unchanged by this pass, so the inspected Gateway-rig evidence remains applicable.

Against the merge base after the CI repair: production/docs are +108/−50 lines (net +58); tests/support are +137/−12 lines (net +125). The initial simplification removed 11 redundant test lines; the follow-up centralizes scope selection and reduces production code by another three lines. Necessary growth connects the existing scoped roster to first-render identity and checks ownership; no new persistence, manager, or live-discovery fallback is introduced.

### CI repair and inherited failures

Follow-up head: `df096bfba713`.

The quota failure exposed a stale expectation: the fixture scopes bootstrap “OpenClaw” to Main, then expected that name while Work identity was held. The test now explicitly covers both scoped and unscoped bootstrap. It requires no borrowed Main identity in Work, preserves a genuinely unscoped fallback, rejects delayed Main responses, and requires “Work Agent” after the Work response. Both variants pass.

A separate owner regression proved a real fallback loss on the pushed head: an unscoped bootstrap name disappeared on a foreign-Gateway route (expected “Observatory”, received an empty name). Scope selection now lives in the shared identity projection, preserving an unscoped name while accepting a scoped bootstrap identity only for the matching agent over the same-origin transport. Existing account/recovery retirement still suppresses the entire cache. This adds no fallback store or discovery path.

The same three originally failing specs ran on pushed head `3f11e97d72fa` (5 failures / 19 passes) and detached `origin/main` at `61722900dfe2` (4 failures / 20 passes). Main passes quota and reproduces the other four failures exactly:

| Spec | Matching failure on current main | Source evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat-pasted-text-show-in-text-field.e2e.test.ts` | `sameSize: false` for the attachment cards at both 1280 px and 390 px | #186058 changed fixed 162 px file cards to content-dependent widths. The assertion compares card dimensions, not composer height or placeholder text. |
| `new-session-page.transition.e2e.test.ts` | Desktop/mobile timeout looking for the completion toast's “Open” button | #186028 supplies `actionHref`, rendering the toast action as a link. The old test still looks for a button. |

Those inherited failures are unchanged. The final focused browser invocation includes all three failing specs plus warm boot and offline session title: 32 passes and only the same four inherited failures (36 cases total). The owner/unit set, UI typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, production build, diff checks, and independent review through P2 pass. Full repository lint limitations remain as recorded above.

The post-repair network-fault rig also passes offline reload and warm reload: the custom name is present at 0.271 s before offline-reload hello at 18.212 s, and at 1.228 s before warm-reload hello at 2.964 s. Its placeholder never changes across hello. The inspected synthetic screenshots have the same name/reconnect presentation as the embedded evidence above.

### Mobile palette Escape repair

Follow-up head: `76cf2c13bf016878b96f17da6ee221a64e55ee17`.

The remaining palette-drop failure came from tooltip keyboard ownership. Growing the mobile textarea moves the image remove action under a stationary mouse pointer. Its hover tooltip can reopen after focus has already moved to the textarea, then consume Escape at window capture before the palette receives it. Instrumented failing repetitions recorded the active remove-action tooltip consuming Escape before any document or palette handler ran. The palette and tooltip handling files were identical on the exact CI base and prior PR head; this repair addresses the timing-sensitive interaction at its existing owner.

The tooltip owner now dismisses active or loading tooltips when input occurs outside their owned trigger and content. Both dismissal listeners share the existing cleanup lifecycle. Input inside rich tooltip content and ordinary tooltip Escape behavior remain supported. A visible tooltip without subsequent outside input still owns the first Escape, as before. The identity implementation and existing palette-drop test are unchanged.

The new browser regression fails before repair (Escape never reaches the textarea) and passes afterward. Final wrapper results: all 21 palette-drop, quota-pill, warm-boot, and offline-title E2E cases pass with exit 0; 205 focused unit cases pass with `[test] passed 2 Vitest shards`. All 29 tooltip browser cases pass in both Chromium and WebKit. UI typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, diff checks, and independent review through P2 pass.

The simplification pass kept one owner-level input listener and one distinct browser regression: production delta +25/−9 lines (net +16), tests +24 lines against the prior head. Temporary diagnostics and repeated mobile cases were removed. The previously inspected offline identity rig evidence remains applicable because this follow-up does not change identity, caching, or reconnect behavior. The other failures classified as inherited by the exact CI-base comparison remain untouched.

### Current CI gate repair

Current head: `8fc5062e32f5db5d2e4774f51ddf9bc669b84a87`.

The tooltip browser test now creates an explicitly typed native textarea, avoiding the generic fixture's TS2590 union expansion. The exact failing configuration, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-components.json`, passes locally. The chat and chat-E2E test typecheck configurations also pass.

The repair removes 149 test lines from the prior head and brings this PR's full net test-line delta from +149 to **0**. Identity reconnect checks share the existing connection-replacement table and retain name/avatar assertions through both phases. The five bootstrap scope cases remain, and fixed routes now resolve independently of the fixture's selected agent. Quota assertions check identity and auth together before and after presence and stale Main responses, then require Work's live identity. Stale fork success/error cases share setup while retaining agent-change, reconnect, retained-return, and request-timing boundaries. Bespoke optional recording plumbing and unused canned replies for explicitly held methods are removed; standard screenshots and retained proof files remain. No production code or ceiling changes are included in this follow-up.

Ratchet evidence uses the failed job's actual checkout base, `39e4093b654e907fbf30831ad237dcb5cb79c916`:

| Tree | Test lines | Ceiling | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Candidate branch | 6,285,751 | 6,287,068 | Pass; 1,317 lines of slack |
| Detached main `6b1310042b9fd084de7e6533ab58913767edb136` | 6,289,898 | 6,288,829 | Independently over by **1,069**; inherited |
| That main plus this PR's test diff | 6,289,898 | 6,288,829 | Pass; **net delta 0**, using the existing no-growth rule |

Final focused proof: 24 E2E cases across agent identity reconnect, quota, warm boot, offline session title, and command-palette drops pass with wrapper exit 0. All 204 focused unit cases pass with `[test] passed 2 Vitest shards`. All 29 tooltip browser cases pass in both Chromium and WebKit. The three targeted typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, diff checks, simplification, and independent review through P2 pass. This supersedes the earlier test-growth figures above.

The remaining `new-session-page.prompt-attachments` failure from run `40598818866` was already reproduced on base and is unchanged. The inspected offline identity rig evidence remains applicable because this repair changes only tests. Auto-merge remains absent; landing stays with the lead after CI.

prs.title: perf(gateway): share retained membership participant projections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A local Team-shaped Gateway heap census found that the membership facts store retained a separate participant projection for nearly every session, even when many sessions had exactly the same ordered participant identities. Those copies survive the worker boundary and remain in the main isolate. This is bounded retention, not evidence of an unbounded leak.

## User Impact

Gateways with many sessions retain about 7 MiB less duplicate membership data in the measured synthetic workload, with unchanged membership values and no operator action required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share equal participant projections within each synchronous membership read, keyed by the complete ordered identity sequence. Native worker transport preserves shared references, and the Gateway freezes the received facts. The lookup itself expires when the read returns. Publications still replace changed facts, and a later read constructs fresh projections; there is no persistent cache or new invalidation state. Empty membership/participant values are shared within the same read too.

Production delta: +10 lines. The complete identity key and invocation-local map account for the growth; a partial key would conflate order or remote namespaces. No schema, retention-policy, configuration, authorization, or public response changes.

## Evidence

Local synthetic fixture: 10,800 sessions including archived sessions, 40 requested plugins, 65 resident WebSocket clients, mock-provider turns with tool calls/native subagents, writes, sidebar/list/search/history churn. All raw heap snapshots remain local; this PR contains aggregates only. Team was not accessed.

The same baseline Gateway was warmed for ten minutes, snapshotted, and snapshotted again ten minutes later. Main post-snapshot heap was 471.3 → 500.0 MiB. The membership projection context retained 8.86 MiB at both points. Larger roots included the 32 MiB WASM backing store and Node module caches; these stable runtime owners are unchanged by this patch.

Largest individual retained owner roots at warmup and ten minutes later (nested roots are not additive):

| Owner | Warmed MiB | Later MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| WASM module context / 32 MiB backing store | 32.25 | 32.25 |
| Node ModuleLoader | 19.67 | 19.59 |
| Session row projection `rows` map | 9.51 | 11.07 |
| Membership projection context | 8.86 | 8.86 |
| Plugin metadata cache roots | 7.04 | 7.04 |
| Session row `byKey` index | 6.52 | 6.52 |
| Prometheus store | 4.32 | 7.24 |
| SubagentRunMap | 3.13 | 3.13 |

Owner benchmark: two counterbalanced pairs, 2,000 reads plus worker-wire structured clones per arm (254,321 rows), then a full-cohort retained read. All four value digests match.

| Metric | Base mean | Candidate mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained reply heap | 9.79 MiB | 2.78 MiB |
| Distinct participant projections | 10,807 | 122 |
| Serialized full reply | 3,511,846 B | 1,151,556 B |
| Main-thread CPU per 2,000 reads | 3,890.4 ms | 4,033.7 ms |
| Allocated bytes per 2,000 reads | 3,197,838,804 B | 3,197,373,936 B |

This is a small retention improvement: roughly 7 MiB reclaimed, with allocation essentially unchanged and owner CPU +3.7%. The real Gateway results below establish neutral runtime cost; the microbenchmark alone does not establish end-to-end performance.

Canonical Gateway timing: two counterbalanced pairs, ten measured minutes per arm. All four arms completed 40 turns and 40 matching tool calls/results. Main-isolate exact allocation counters were read at the timing boundaries; snapshots were taken only after telemetry stopped.

| Timing metric (paired mean) | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 7.302% | 7.343% |
| Exact allocation | 21.829 MiB/s | 21.763 MiB/s |
| GC | 0.1507 s/min | 0.1550 s/min |
| Event-loop p99 | 28.918 ms | 28.959 ms |
| Client sessions.list p99 | 50.623 ms | 37.074 ms |
| Main heap at timing stop | 549.85 MiB | 534.75 MiB |
| Main heap after endpoint snapshot | 496.02 MiB | 481.92 MiB |
| Process RSS at timing stop | 2,506.79 MiB | 2,388.70 MiB |

CPU, allocation and GC are effectively neutral. The GC difference is +4.31 ms/min, below the declared material-delta threshold. Client latency differences are context, not evidence of a speedup. RSS includes varying worker heaps and is not wholly attributable to this change. Whole-main-heap differences are observed totals; owner-specific attribution is reported separately.

The retained membership facts map itself was **8.8517 → 1.8822 MiB in both pairs** (−6.9694 MiB, −78.7%). The surrounding membership context was 8.8631 → 1.8937 MiB. This is the directly attributed saving; the larger whole-heap difference is not all credited to this owner.

Separate allocation-sampling arms were 19.445 → 18.201 and 18.880 → 18.070 MiB/s (paired mean 19.163 → 18.135 MiB/s). These instrumented runs are diagnostic. Since the untraced exact counter is essentially flat, this PR claims a retention win, not a confirmed allocation-rate win.

| Untraced arm | Server sessions.list handler mean / p99 bucket upper bound (ms) | Handler samples | Client list samples | Loop samples | Host load, mean [range] |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AB base | 10.192 / ≤50 | 1,173 | 1,202 | 27,987 | 18.77 [12.60–23.13] |
| AB candidate | 10.362 / ≤40 | 1,173 | 1,202 | 28,042 | 17.10 [11.54–25.05] |
| BA candidate | 8.296 / ≤30 | 1,173 | 1,202 | 28,068 | 14.87 [12.27–18.92] |
| BA base | 8.041 / ≤40 | 1,173 | 1,194 | 28,018 | 19.37 [11.11–32.08] |

Server histogram deltas use the first/last scrape inside each window; p99 is a bucket upper bound, not an interpolated exact percentile. No windows or pauses were excluded. Client tails were not used as a rejection gate. No adverse untraced metric met the declared material thresholds, so no A/A rejection control was invoked.

| Untraced arm | Minor: count / total ms / max ms | Major: count / total ms / max ms | Incremental: count / total ms / max ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AB base | 518 / 909.61 / 16.59 | 31 / 748.42 / 50.00 | 31 / 27.20 / 2.35 |
| AB candidate | 495 / 854.89 / 13.07 | 32 / 710.22 / 37.36 | 32 / 27.04 / 1.29 |
| BA candidate | 484 / 807.49 / 9.36 | 30 / 675.85 / 47.60 | 30 / 25.21 / 2.00 |
| BA base | 486 / 767.94 / 8.41 | 27 / 540.72 / 33.12 | 27 / 20.56 / 1.00 |

Major-GC collection tails are context-only because each side has fewer than 50 collections. Minor p95 was 2.665 → 2.617 ms and 2.465 → 2.781 ms; both absolute changes are below 1 ms. No max-pause safeguard tripped.

Measured baseline: `9a0458cf6952f4613efe2ba3fa6e64f8dc6d6102`; candidate: the production patch committed as `6ac1b9cdc162322d5888937f3a95258519611907`, built before that commit. The built membership module hashes are `b1038862ac6954760b2681092957031b9d032a2de5ae1ae856cdfb3a79e5e704` (base) and `93d5fe923041097773e8a4aa41e4a1946734f8647e08ed48c71a56f8faa7ce76` (candidate). Rebased afterward onto `39e4093b654e907fbf30831ad237dcb5cb79c916`; producer, consumer, and regression sources were unchanged upstream. The first preserved-artifact launch failed before measurement because a root launcher file was missing; copying that unchanged launcher fixed setup, and a fresh complete campaign supplied all results.

Reproduction: the new script header documents the owner benchmark. The Gateway comparison uses `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-stress.ts --base <built-base> --candidate <built-candidate> --output <new-directory> --minutes 10 --pairs 2`. Local endpoint captures were added after timing telemetry stopped; raw snapshots are not committed.

## Validation

- Regression fails on baseline at reference sharing while the two existing repair tests pass; candidate passes all 15 tests across membership repair and Gateway projection files. It also checks order, remote namespace, and a subsequent changed membership read.
- Changed-file formatting and lint passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Baseline and candidate runtime builds passed.
- Original production-patch review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable at that time): no accepted/actionable findings. The configured review helper refused to start because its provider did not match the operator configuration; configuration was unchanged. The independent reviewer received only the scoped diff, owner/consumer sources, and brief.
- Prior head `a92a8722dd40`: latest-main rebase passed; changed-file format check and export-name collision guard passed. All 15 focused membership tests and 32 eager-import/PR-wrapper closure tests pass on the rebased head. Exact-head CI has passed the build, lint, Node, source-contract, and evidence checks. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. The baseline-ratchet job failed only `test-lines`; [job evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40599201107/job/122523521741) confirms the same count below.

### Test-line consolidation

Follow-up head: `5a349b35665dda749e91c6eb25431ad6fe7fa2db`.

The test-only follow-up removes 59 lines relative to `a92a8722dd40`, so the complete PR adds **0 net test lines** against merge base `39e4093b654e907fbf30831ad237dcb5cb79c916`. The production implementation and benchmark are unchanged. `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is untouched. The merge-base ratchet passes with 6,289,560 test lines against the unchanged 6,288,829 ceiling: the inherited excess remains 731, and this PR does not increase it.

The sharing regression itself shrinks from 59 to 51 added lines by reusing `f.writeEntry` and a single transactional participant-write helper. All eight assertions remain: equal ordered cohorts share a projection after structured cloning despite different contribution counts/times; reversed order and a different remote plugin namespace do not; a later write produces three participants while the unaffected cohort retains its value and receives a fresh projection.

Each consolidation and its retained covering test:

| Consolidation | Covering test and preserved outcomes |
| --- | --- |
| Reuse owner/category write setup (6 lines saved) | `session-actor-participant-repair.test.ts`: `publishes merged participants to a warm actor after %s canonical repair`, retaining both same-store and cross-store rows, rollback, postimages, durable projection, work/alice → personal/bob metadata, later contribution, and restart checks. |
| Replace five identical capacity samples with one cold/warm table | `session-accessor.sqlite-participants.test.ts`: `measures cold participant capacity and warm contribution reads`; 10 → inserted and 20 → updated each assert zero separate capacity reads, followed by the exact aggregate (count 2, first 10, last 20). |
| Reuse the existing session fixture for schema retry | `reinstalls participant tracking after first-use schema rollback and immediate retry`; preserves rollback, immediate retry, malformed sibling identity, and rejection. |
| Reuse the existing session fixture for sibling publication | `does not hide an untracked sibling change during participant publication: $mutation, $write`; retains all four mutation/write rows and their participant-count, changed-label, or invalid-identity outcomes. |
| Reuse the existing session fixture for merged profiles | `updates a merged profile at the admission bound using resident native aliases (canonical row: %s)`; retains both canonical-row cases, native and worker writers, alias-read behavior, capacity, and aggregate assertions. |
| Reuse session setup and table the two ordered alias transfers | `merges alias contributions with current destination writes and unknown timestamps`; retains both source-key lists in the same transaction, two reads, and the exact count 6 / unknown first / last 40 result. |
| Loop the two identical cross-store copy calls | `preserves over-bound repair histories and does not inflate retried cross-store copies`; still performs both copies and checks 64 records, count 2 after retry, bounded subsequent reads, and overflow rejection. |
| Share child/sibling and participant fixtures; scope SQL-observer cleanup with `using` (9 lines saved) | `session-entry-participant-products.test.ts`: `reuses participant products for %s and observes committed participants`; both cohort and children rows retain zero participant SQL, caller-mutation isolation, and committed first/second identities. |

File deltas for the complete PR are +45 in actor-participant repair, −36 in SQLite participants, and −9 in participant products: **0 total**. No case was moved outside ratchet accounting, and no test-support or production seam was added.

Follow-up validation:

- All 31 tests in the three touched files pass using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <the three files> --maxWorkers=1` (47.38 s Vitest duration; 52.03 s wrapper wall time). The accessor suite exercises 26 real database/lifecycle cases, including full-capacity alias merges; the repair and product suites contain 3 and 2 cases respectively.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` pass (all four root shards).
- Targeted `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json <the three files>`, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check <the three files>`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete test-only working-tree diff against `a92a8722dd40`, P0–P2 coverage: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout had unrelated changes. This review is diff-based; execution evidence is reported separately above.
- The tightened sharing regression was rerun with only `session-membership-facts.ts` replaced by the merge-base production source: it fails at `expect(first[1]![3]).toBe(first[0]![3])`, the intended missing-sharing defect. The production candidate was restored byte-for-byte afterward, and the same focused regression passes again (297 ms test time).
- After fetching main, the requested `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` passes: 6,289,560 lines; ceiling 6,288,829; excess 731; net delta **−1,435** against observed main `4b27ee88cec9a78377a04b2e3a352ba7c503450e`. Main has advanced since the branch diverged; the separate merge-base result of **0** establishes that this PR offsets its own regression without relying on those upstream changes.
- No CI rerun was requested and this PR was not merged. Prior-head CI evidence above is not claimed for the follow-up head.

prs.title: fix: keep conversation prompts stable across continuation turns
prs.body:
Related: #143017

## What Problem This Solves

Local-model conversations lose their reusable prompt prefix when a CLI continuation drops the conversation's presentation instructions, or a scheduled continuation replaces the automations schema with its job-scoped variant.

## User Impact

CLI and scheduled turns keep the conversation's system prompt and tool definitions stable. Current-turn delivery, owner checks, job scope, and automation invocation checks still apply when tools execute. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the canonical session delivery record when an agent request supplies no new route, and carry that existing fact separately for prompt presentation. The actual runtime channel remains the current turn's channel. The same preparation owner builds the saved delivery policy and any current-turn override, so a channel-less CLI continuation of a group can reply automatically. Ordinary conversations keep one automations definition; isolated cron sessions retain their compact surface. Existing scheduled-only actions remain execution-gated.

Thanks to @abacha, @iceteaSA, @VishalJ99, and @duardor968 for the reports and continuation examples. This is a further repair after #183898, #184144, #185887, and #185894; it does not claim every case in the umbrella is resolved.

## Evidence

- Base, real isolated Gateway with a recording compatible relay: a human→CLI continuation changed system JSON from 11,504 to 10,147 bytes (first difference at byte 8,897). The same flip reproduced with real Ollama qwen3:8b and successful replies.
- Base, human→scheduled turn in one conversation: tool JSON changed from 35,984 to 18,788 bytes; names stayed unchanged, but the automations description/schema changed at byte 68.
- Fixed-tree deterministic replay: 11 parent requests across human, internal-event, heartbeat-compatible cron event, scheduled agent turn, spawn/yield/settle and CLI continuation; zero system/tool byte changes. Owner-only `gateway` and out-of-job `automations` calls were refused.
- Real Ollama `qwen3:8b` via the same isolated Gateway and transparent relay: 8 parent requests across human, internal event, cron, spawn/yield/settle and CLI; system JSON stayed 11,504 bytes and tool JSON stayed 37,203 bytes, with identical SHA-256 digests and no differing byte. All requested final replies succeeded. The separate child session has its own expected prompt/tool definition. First-to-last request span: 28.27s; shared-host observation, not a latency benchmark.
- Real main-session replay additionally covered the heartbeat-compatible cron event and all other transitions: 10 parent requests, zero system/tool changes, 44.97s first-to-last request span. This reused synthetic fixture history; it verifies byte continuity and execution, not exact-text model instruction quality.
- Final candidate, saved synthetic Telegram group with group-only message-tool policy: deterministic and real Ollama chat→CLI requests retained the 11,052-byte system prompt and 40,945-byte tool definition; both carried the automatic current-turn override. Real replies were `GROUP_CLI_OK`, with zero tool calls (13.16s first-to-last request). No Telegram account or external send was involved.
- Final candidate, fresh main-session real Ollama replay: 9 parent requests including the heartbeat-compatible event, cron, child/yield/settle and CLI; system 14,361 bytes and tools 40,968 bytes throughout, zero differing bytes (26.18s). This fixture additionally enables the message tool.
- 224 focused tests passed in 257s across 10 files, including the three new owner regressions, non-owner/job-scope refusals, existing computer pinning, and channel-less restart recovery. The regressions fail on their original owners.
- Full `pnpm build` passed initially (6m46s) and on the follow-up (4m15s). Scoped oxlint, core types and five affected test type graphs passed. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, config-docs and plugin-inventory checks passed.
- Independent Codex branch review after the delivery-policy follow-up: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Final-head [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40594896629/job/122513596869) passed on `309fe16c213f8a6484bb0ea4db6c4ef12c193917`. The earlier hosted group-policy finding is fixed and tested; hosted re-review still refers to the earlier head.
- Follow-up: 76 affected prompt tests passed in 258.20s; 20 settled-turn delivery/context tests passed in 105.16s. The saved-group regression fails on the initial candidate and passes with the correction. Final test types pass; the 26-test prompt suite passed again after the assertion type correction in 37.20s.
- Initial-head CI failed only on five pre-existing `eslint(curly)` violations in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx`, plus the aggregate gate. The files and lint config are unchanged from the pinned base; a targeted local lint reproduced all five in 21.38s. The artifact build and other CI jobs passed.

The regenerated ordinary-tool snapshot grows by 1,285 characters (about 322 estimated tokens) to advertise the existing scheduled-only actions consistently. Production +71/−40 lines (net +31), tests +131/−11; generated snapshots and documentation are separate. The added production code carries existing session facts instead of adding a cache or new reads.

Proof platform: macOS and Ollama. The text-only model does not expose a computer tool; computer definition continuity is covered by the existing focused regression, not a physical desktop interaction.

prs.title: fix(memory): session memory search loses earlier transcripts after a session reset
prs.body:
Related: #137265

Replaces my earlier attempt #156256, which changed which transcript block types get exported and does not address this; that one is closed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory search stops finding earlier conversations once a session key rolls over to a new session id (daily or idle `session.reset`), even though the transcript is still stored.

## User Impact

User impact: with `memory.search.sources` including `sessions`, what was said before a reset stays searchable after it. `memory status --index` keeps counting the earlier transcripts and `memory index --force` no longer drops them. Installs that already lost those index rows get them back on the next index pass, which costs one extra transcript read per rolled-over session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session corpus used by the search index only listed the current transcript behind each session key, so after a reset the earlier transcript looked stale and its chunks were removed, while `docs/cli/memory.md` says retained and reset transcripts stay eligible. Retained SQLite transcripts were only requested by dreaming ingestion.

The sync now requests retained transcripts as well and keeps the ones a live session rolled over from, following the recorded `previousSessionId` chain. Transcripts of deleted sessions that are still awaiting cleanup are not in that chain, so they keep dropping out of the index as before. Corpus entries now carry `previousSessionId` from the session window for this. Because a rolled-over transcript shares its session key with the current one, and the sync pipeline addresses SQLite transcripts by that key, each retained transcript gets its own address inside the sync. Targeted cleanup after a transcript update now protects every SQLite-backed transcript path, not only the current session's, so an update queued before the rollover cannot remove the restored history; and archive copies of a rolled-over session no longer erase its recorded predecessor link.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `manager-session-rollover.test.ts`, each red before its repair and green after:
  - rollover: seeds a transcript under `agent:main:main`, indexes, rolls the key to a new session id that records the previous one, indexes again. Failed on the base with `files: 1, chunks: 1` (the earlier transcript gone).
  - targeted sync after the rollover addressing the previous session id: the earlier transcript stayed indexed only once targeted cleanup protects retained SQLite paths (review finding 1).
  - three-generation lineage where the middle session also has a `.jsonl.reset.*` archive: the first transcript stayed searchable only once archive duplicates stop erasing the recorded predecessor link (review finding 2).
- Existing guard `index.test.ts` "prunes removed sessions without re-embedding unchanged survivors" still passes, which is what keeps deleted sessions out of the index.
- Real entry point, built from this branch, local mock model/embedding server, `session.reset: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 1 }`:
  - base behavior (same on 2026.8.2 and 2026.10.5): after the rollover `memory status --index` reported `sessions · 1/1 files`, `memory search <marker>` returned nothing, `memory index --force` did not bring it back.
  - this branch, after the same rollover (`session_windows.previous_session_id` set, Gateway stopped, CLI offline):

    ```
    $ openclaw memory status --index --agent main
    Indexed: 3/3 files · 12 chunks
    Dirty: no
      sessions · 2/2 files · 2 chunks · 24.1 KiB text + embeddings
    $ openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
    -> sessions/main/6ea00220-….jsonl  "User: La parola di controllo memoria è ZAFFIRO927. ..."
    $ openclaw memory index --force --agent main && openclaw memory search ZAFFIRO927 --agent main --json
    -> same hit; the current session (sessions/main/fab0013e-….jsonl) stays indexed and searchable too
    ```
- Focused suites run locally with `--maxWorkers=1`: memory-core `manager-session-*`, `manager-reads`, `manager-targeted-sync`, startup catch-up, sync control, `index.test.ts`, `tools.real-manager`, `memory-mutation-authority`, `session-backfill`, `dreaming-phases`, and `session-transcript-corpus` in memory-host-sdk; `check-changed` on the touched files.
- CI on c2d01282ae0: one shard failed in `index.test.ts` › "prunes removed sessions without re-embedding unchanged survivors" with SQLite `database is locked` at the test's own direct agent-DB write right after the manager closed (Bun shard). The failure report classifies it as unknown (no matching job on main); the file passes locally 5/5 under Node, this PR does not touch that test, and the same error class is tracked as intermittent in #170107. Not re-running CI just to get green.

prs.title: chore(release): close out 2026.10.8 on main
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw 2026.10.8 is published to npm `latest` from `release/2026.10.8`. The signed tag `v2026.10.8` points to `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`. Core npm came from run 40491275202, under Release Publish parent 40486387421. That parent failed after core npm verified, on a transient `fetch failed` / `write EPIPE`. Resumed parent 40496801542 succeeded and published Docker, the GitHub release and the Linux request.

`main` still says 2026.10.7. It is missing:
- the shipped notes
- the 2026.10.8 update-compat entry
- the 2026.10.8 shipped Plugin SDK surface
- refreshed release shard timings

## Solution

This is the stable main closeout, following `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/references/stable-main-closeout.md`.

- **Version:** the root version is now `2026.10.8`, along with the `pnpm release:prep` generated outputs (plugin and package versions, the official channel catalog, and matrix plugin changelog alignment). I corrected the macOS `Info.plist` base version (`2026.10.8` / `2026100800`) by hand, as release preflight requires.
- **Update-compat inventory** (`scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json`, in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked separately):
  - It records `openclaw@2026.10.8`: 53 chunks, commit `dc2523e5a5c7`, `sha512-fWOIOOyd…xZOrQ==`.
  - I regenerated it with `update-compat-inventory.mts --release <dir>=<integrity>` from npm tarballs of all 19 recorded releases. Each tarball's SHA-512 was checked against its published `dist.integrity` before extraction.
  - All 18 existing entries are byte-identical, and the diff is additive only (+1338/-0).
- **Changelog:**
  - `CHANGELOG/2026.10.8.md` and `CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.8.md` match the tag byte for byte. I read them through `scripts/release-changelog.mjs read --version 2026.10.8 --ref v2026.10.8`, with and without `--record`. Their blob IDs `951706d6a606` and `d52b78b51f7c` equal the tag's.
  - The root `CHANGELOG.md` index was refreshed by `release-changelog.mjs split` (one added line). Other release entries are unchanged.
  - There is no appcast change, because the macOS build is not published yet.
- **Shipped Plugin SDK surface** (`scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json`): regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:shipped-surface:gen -- --release v2026.10.8`. It records 151 typed subpaths and 3645 named exports. Only `commit` and `release` change, so the shipped surface is identical to v2026.10.7.
- **CI timings** (`config/ci-test-timings.json`):
  - Refreshed by `scripts/ci-shard-timings-refresh.mts --run 40454704623`. That run is the normalCi child, attempt 4, of Full Release Validation 40454025021, which passed (stable/all with soak, attempt 2) on `dc2523e5a5c7`.
  - It covers 131 hosted shard costs, and I committed the generated output unedited.
  - As in the 2026.10.7 closeout, GitHub returned HTTP 502 for the `jobs?per_page=100` page on repeated tries. I ran the generator once with a temporary, uncommitted `per_page=50` page size; it is otherwise unchanged.

## Release-branch audit

`git cherry origin/main v2026.10.8 v2026.10.7` lists 177 unmatched commits. After matching cherry-pick trailers and PR numbers to main, 26 commits remain without a main origin. Of the 162 PRs in the 2026.10.8 contribution record, 161 are on main. The exception is #181465, a `release/2026.10.7` backport PR.

What remains falls into three groups:

- **Release-only, intentionally not forward-ported:**
  - `chore(release): prepare 2026.10.8` (`a8a5fed3555d`)
  - the 2026.10.7 update-compat entry `84070ac42682` (already on main through the 2026.10.7 closeout)
  - the notes commit `dc2523e5a5c`
- **Release-line adaptations of main work:**
  - `c36086f8827` syncs native locale artifacts with strings that came from main.
  - `d99892dab47b` (session follow-up staging outside the legacy writer reservation) is a stable-only adaptation. Main replaced that reservation with the session input actor FIFO in #168607.
  - `5c40b473bb66` completes the stable adaptation of #164843.
  - `884f3a2661df` (#172959) is on main as `eb2255b5d9bd`.
  - `35bdf391ecda` carries #180834, a `release/2026.10.6` PR. Main retired `heartbeat_respond` in #182154, so it doesn't apply there.
- **Test, refactor and line-cap adaptations of backported tests:** the remaining `test(release)`, `refactor(release)` and `chore(release)` commits.

No release-only product fix missing from main was found, so nothing is forward-ported here.

## Known gaps (tracked elsewhere)

- **ClawHub:** `@openclaw/acpx`, `@openclaw/cloudflare`, `@openclaw/diffs` and `@openclaw/feishu` 2026.10.8 are not on ClawHub. ClawHub's family-contract change (openclaw/clawhub#4031) now rejects legacy `bundle-plugin` rows that have no bundle manifest. This is tracked in openclaw/clawhub#4086. npm has all of them.
- **macOS and appcast:** release-ops preflight and validation were still running when this PR opened. The appcast lands separately once the macOS publish completes.

## Evidence

- `pnpm deps:npm-lock:check`: pass (109 packages).
- `node scripts/release-changelog.mjs check`: 135 releases, 27 records.
- `node scripts/update-compat-inventory.mts --check --release …` (all 19 verified tarballs): pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: "shipped Plugin SDK v2026.10.8: no unauthorized removals". The surface *budget* half fails: public entrypoints 160 > 158, public exports 3839 > 3822, callable exports 2224 > 2214. That failure is pre-existing on main: the same check on a clean `origin/main` checkout (`443530a55b7`) prints identical numbers, and this PR touches no `src/plugin-sdk` file.
- `pnpm release:generated:check`: the only drift reported is that same pre-existing SDK surface budget.
- `git diff --check`: clean. The branch merges cleanly into current `main`.
- Per operator policy for release work, checks ran locally rather than on Testbox.

prs.title: feat(agents): env overrides for claude-cli stream-json per-turn output limits
prs.body:
## Problem

Long tool-heavy claude-cli turns fail with:

```
CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.
```

The 8 MiB raw-chars and 20,000-line per-turn budgets in `src/agents/cli-output-stream-limits.ts` are frozen constants. There is no config key or environment variable, so the only way to raise them is a rebuild.

## Change

- Add `OPENCLAW_CLI_STREAM_JSON_MAX_TURN_CHARS` and `OPENCLAW_CLI_STREAM_JSON_MAX_TURN_LINES`, parsed with `parseStrictInteger`. Non-integer values keep the defaults.
- Clamp to 64 KiB to 1 GiB chars and 100 to 10,000,000 lines so a typo cannot fail every turn or retain unbounded output.
- Defaults are unchanged (8 MiB / 20,000 lines).
- Limits are resolved per parser instance, so values applied by Gateway config `env.vars` are honored.
- The single-line cap follows the chars budget, as before.
- Docs: `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`, "Inputs and outputs".

## Tests

- New `src/agents/cli-output-stream-limits.test.ts`: defaults, override, non-integer and clamp cases.
- Existing parser tests unchanged and green: `cli-output-framing`, `cli-output-partial-messages`, `cli-output-subagent-budget`, `cli-runner/execute.output-limit` (43 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix(teams-meetings): accept newer Microsoft work meeting links
prs.body:
Closes #146824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes rejection of Microsoft's newer short work-meeting invitations by the Teams meetings plugin.

## User Impact

Users can supply the complete short work invitation to the existing native meeting workflow without recreating the meeting or converting it to a legacy link. Different opaque passcodes remain separate session identities.

**Actual meeting admission and live audio remain unverified.** Existing tenant, permission, ownership, and plugin-trust requirements still apply. Unrecognized browser launch routes deliberately fail closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Microsoft documents the newer work-link format in its [shorter meeting URL announcement (roadmap 381953)](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/publicsectorblog/march-2025---microsoft-365-us-public-sector-roadmap-newsletter/4394967).

This change adds the format to the existing parser and uses that same parser for browser identity checks. It preserves the opaque join query, compares meeting ID and passcode, and excludes unrelated tracking from identity. It does not reconstruct legacy links or interpret the token as the displayed meeting passcode.

Rejected URLs cannot fall back to an old meeting marker. Only the known same-origin application route remains eligible for existing owned-session retention. Legacy work and consumer formats remain covered. No trust/provenance bypass, new permissions, dependency changes, or configuration migration is included.

## Review Follow-up

The revision addresses the two actionable findings in [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146828#issuecomment-5651874677):

- Microsoft sign-in redirects retain `teams-login-required` guidance **after** the shared status guard denies ownership and cleans up the request-owned resources. Login pages do not gain join, microphone, camera, caption, audio, or leave authority. New tests cover short work, legacy work, and consumer invitations.
- The caption-rerender fixture now uses a consistent work origin and asserts that the caption observer is actually installed before detaching its control.

The revision also removes the added lint suppressions while preserving control-character rejection, and replaces potentially undefined split-array elements with definite strings in the negative URL fixtures. These address the two PR-caused CI failures in the suppression guard and test typing.

The earlier workflow-guard fixture error about missing `scripts/tsx.mjs` is not the failure reported by the revised CI run. The focused guard test passes on the local source base; neither that fixture nor CI configuration is changed in this PR. The remaining CI failures are classified below; this is not a claim that all CI is green.

## Evidence

- **245 Teams plugin tests passed across 17 files**, including the new login-diagnostic and denied-audio cases, existing parser/browser identity parity, session reuse/recovery, captions, and safe leave.
- **Two targeted tooling guard tests passed**: production suppression inventory and the previously failing workflow-routing guard. Other tooling tests were not selected for that focused run.
- Focused Teams test typing passed using the repository's inherited extension-test compiler settings and normal guarded compiler, with the include set limited to Teams tests plus the original declaration roots. **The broad all-extension local typecheck timed out and failed cleanup verification; it is not claimed as passing.** The retained ownership evidence was preserved and associated processes were verified stopped before recovery.
- Formatting passed. Guarded type-aware lint passed on the four revision files after correcting a test-only missing-braces style error.
- Repository autoreview of the substantive revision: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**. A subsequent change only added the required braces around an existing test assertion loop.
- Earlier SDK declaration generation, native runtime build, pack-only checks, and minified/packed parser assertions passed for the initial patch. **Those package-build results predate this revision and are not fresh package or live-deployment proof.**

**No live E2E or audio proof:** offline tests do not establish actual Teams redirects, admission, two-way speech, live captions, or completed departure. Full-repository and target-host installation qualification remain outstanding. Maintainer edits are enabled; no workflow files are changed.

## CI on the Revised Head

At **2026-09-13 09:10 UTC**, head `80fcf67331a709530490c06de5d69a308e2d018b` had **177 completed check runs: 129 successful, 44 skipped, 4 failed; none pending**. These counts include separate repository-automation runs on the same head, not 177 distinct tests.

- The original patch-caused failures are cleared: [test typing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939656) and [tooling guards](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939704) pass. [Production typing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939598) and [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939637) also pass.
- [The remaining test-shard failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939783) is `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.executable-invocation.test.ts:77`, **runs a verified plugin CLI script through its resolved interpreter**: `CLI produced no output for 1s and was terminated` (`cli_no_output_timeout`). Its shard reports 1 failed / 3,196 passed / 12 skipped tests. The failing fixture, its test helper, and the three CLI execution/error/timeout owners were verified byte-identical between this head and inspected upstream `0f23fae715b83f0ca9d7db09cef68f81d6ff1159`; none is changed by this seven-file Teams PR. This is an unrelated core CLI fixture timeout, not evidence of a Teams regression. The underlying runner timing cause was not reproduced or claimed fixed.
- [The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103701848409) is correctly red because the selected core-test shard failed; it is not an additional test defect.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): preserve session resume and fresh admin authority after reconnect
prs.body:
Related: #167867.

A fresh administrator message after a browser reconnect can be classified as recovered input, hiding automations from other sessions. Simply dropping the reconnect marker restores authority but rolls over an expired conversation. This change preserves the displayed conversation while distinguishing a current foreground submission from offline, restored, or retried delivery.

The UI captures submission ownership and checks it at delivery. A matching fresh reconnect uses the private `"fresh"` marker; the Gateway normalizes lifecycle resume separately from recovered-input classification. Existing scope, source-lifetime, and revocation checks still apply. Durable recovery stores only the boolean resume marker, so it cannot replay freshness. Restored and retried messages retain their restricted classification, including after a document reload.

Current candidate: `436ef3edba92532ebd95114bbcc0a5a0fa1f5aa5`.
Integrated base: `c868bfe31058fcb50c24b4d41f57f6121f7ab01d`.

Validation:
- [Red reproduction](https://github.com/lucafucci/openclaw/actions/runs/40601091127), candidate `7c4fbc2b18c4754032490608a3fb1b9e1f386d17`: the real browser/Gateway test fails because a daily-expired conversation changes lifecycleRevision and sessionStartedAt after fresh reconnect.
- [Current candidate proof](https://github.com/lucafucci/openclaw/actions/runs/40603338261): 214 UI tests, 67 Gateway tests, 39 browser E2E tests, and 14 ownership tests pass. Gateway coverage includes durable recovery and existing native resume/rollover behavior.
- The compiled Gateway and real browser pass the expired-session, fresh, offline, reload, and visible Retry flow (33.812 seconds). Session ID, lifecycle revision, and start time remain unchanged for the expired reconnect.
- Eight separate compiled-Gateway protocol checks pass with the fresh marker: authenticated RPC, remote pairing/effective scopes, administrator read and persisted update, write-only read/write denials, and revocation before disclosure or persistence.
- Build, formatting, focused lint, max-lines, and the unchanged-base comparison pass. Four regressions fail on the base while the connection-change control passes.
- Integrated upstream fixes for Activity rendering, attachment previews, toast links, participant palettes, and curly lint. The selected scenarios behind the previous six broad-CI failures now pass.
- Independent Codex P0-P2 static reviews of the production repair and complete proof helpers found no actionable issues.

The current proof workflow is **not fully green**: its sole failing step is the global test-line limit. Candidate total is **6,289,906**, ceiling **6,288,829**. The exact base already contains **6,289,398** (+569); this PR adds **508**, producing an overage of **1,077**. No ceiling increase, test deletion, or bypass was applied.

Inference and fixture data are synthetic; browser, compiled Gateway, authenticated RPC, pairing, tool execution, and storage are real. This does not claim physical-device coverage or completion of broad upstream CI. Product/security-owner acceptance of fresh-input classification, renewed review, and normal integration gates remain outstanding. Android #182848 is separate.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The October backport's advisory failure cancels useful CI. Running the remaining checks also exposes stale prompt snapshots, an incomplete provider fixture, an oversized UI startup bundle, static import cycles, unregistered E2E entrypoints, stale SDK surface counts, and a detached-completion test with a still-registered foreground parent.

## User Impact

Restores CI coverage without upgrading dependencies or runtime pins. Following upstream, ordinary CI skips advisory scanning and release/pre-commit scans warn; the separate Dependency Audit remains strict. Its daily schedule targets the default branch, not an automatic backport audit. Runtime permission and recovery behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backport [Peter Steinberger's audit policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a3d541f21265d5c0cd4e9e1d55af808e858972e0) and [Shakker's Devices locale lazy loading](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8bae5df5b28cf736e9a860f6ac0f10200b0eeb05). Synchronize cron snapshots with the merged description, repair the provider fixture, and make one internal-only helper private.

Remove five static dependency cycles by importing existing leaf definitions and relocating unchanged helpers/types. Register three real recovery E2E executable entrypoints rather than ignoring their source. Account precisely for the already-backported `resolveSilentReplySettings` API (#177809): public exports 3644→3645 and callable exports 2109→2110, with explicit approval. Repair the detached-completion fixture by unregistering its foreground parent before releasing the ordinary client lease, matching production cleanup and preserving every retention/delivery/close assertion. No new API, dependency/lockfile change, relaxed UI budget, or weakened runtime assertion.

## Evidence

- Base: `3021ed52edcb0b25e8a4363112b1131be9ebe360`.
- Initial focused validation: 189 tests passed. Follow-up validation: 34 core compaction/session tests and 422 Codex recovery/authority, Slack silence, configuration and SDK surface tests passed; the Linux-only process-lifetime case also passed in remote CI. The final direct-import cleanup also passed its 263 targeted tests.
- Full architecture chain passed; final static import scan reports zero cycles. Native changed-check types, guards and lint passed for the first candidate; incremental types, lint, line-cap and dead-export checks passed. Full `pnpm build` passed, including all declaration groups and SDK exports.
- Production UI startup gzip is 372,703 B against the unchanged 373,454 B ceiling; all 912 compressed sidecars verified. Devices catalog preserves all 246 text leaves.
- Actual warning audit exits 0; unchanged strict audit exits 1 with the existing 18 advisories. Key/workflow scanners remain enforced. Source SDK report matches the exact approved counts.
- Independent source reviews found no actionable P0/P1/P2 issues; moved function bodies are identical. CLI autoreview was unavailable, so a separate independent reviewer performed the review.
- The [second CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40602820232) cleared all three original downstream failures, including the complete dependency/unused-file gate. It exposed one existing detached-completion fixture failure; the same 13-file shard reproduced it locally (1 failed, 390 passed). The fixture lacked parent unregister, so the implementation correctly deferred detached delivery. After the repair, the original shard and completion-delivery/close siblings passed. Final-head CI completed successfully.

- Final head `3eb9d7e4f29d33fd48fca4bb91986b103cc03679`: [CI run 40604327136](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40604327136) passed. PR checks: 98 successful, 40 conditionally skipped, no failures or pending checks at verification. All 408 fixture/adjacent tests and native changed checks passed locally. [ClawSweeper exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186371#issuecomment-6455887869) completed with zero findings. Merge awaits the maintainer’s explicit confirmation.

prs.title: feat(ui): show paused child sessions in the handoff wait line
prs.body:
Related: #185585 #185918

## What Problem This Solves

When a parent hands off with `sessions_yield` and a child pauses on its own `sessions_yield`, the Control UI shows that child as **Done**. If a paused child is the only one left, the waiting line disappears entirely, even though the child still owes its task.

## User Impact

- A paused child reads **Paused** in the handoff list, sorted after **Needs your input**. The header counts it, as in **Waiting on 3 sessions · 1 needs your input · 1 paused · 10m**. With a single child, the line reads **Waiting on** _name_ **· Paused**.
- A paused child keeps the waiting line open even when nothing else is running. Paused children are not counted as running, and the parent is never shown as working.
- While every remaining child is paused, the waiting line shows no elapsed time. If any child is still running, the time stays. This follows the children's execution state, not the labels shown on the rows, so a running child that has asked for your input still keeps the time.
- After the parent resumes, if the only children left are paused, the reply ends with a quiet note instead of a waiting line: **CI action pins is paused** (with the name linked), or **2 sessions are paused**. The **Resumed** list shows the paused child with its **Paused** chip.
- A paused child that has its own work still running (`hasActiveSubagentRun`) or a newer active run reads **Running**, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185918 added `subagentRunState: "paused"` to session rows, so the UI can now tell a yielded child from a finished one. The change stays in the existing owner, `projectSubagentStatus`/`listHandoffSessions`: a single `isPausedChild` check feeds the status, the wait condition, the `pausedOnly` clock fact, the resumed note, and the resumed-row memo key. As #185585 requires, the UI names and links children only after the pane's own child query has completed. The new strings go through the normal i18n flow, and no CSS was added; the existing status chip and muted working-line styles are reused.

Accepted edge case: if the handoff is outside the loaded history, the UI can't tell whether the parent has resumed, so a wait with only paused children shows the note.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI e2e, light theme, 1280×900, synthetic content.

**Three children, one paused** (before = current `main`, after = this PR)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: three-session wait on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/516d3670-964f-41e4-ab21-a807b1706d89) | ![After: three-session wait with Paused chip and count](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2de4803-9212-4fda-aa5b-b68851deea99) |

**Parent resumed, only a paused child left**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: resumed on main, paused child shown as Done](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/621952f3-6438-411e-9e5c-9553c10cb40a) | ![After: resumed with quiet paused note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df72bf6d-0845-46c8-a9f0-c5c3d51ecdde) |

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-subagent-wait.test.ts`: the paused status, the wait staying open while uncounted, hydration gating, the resumed note, and the clock following execution facts even when attention changes a row's label. These assertions fail on `main` and pass here.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-run-activity.test.ts`: a settled **Resumed** rule repaints to **Paused** after a roster update that changes only the paused state. This fails without the memo-key change.
- e2e `chat-yield-acknowledgment` (3/3) and `chat-subagent-waiting` (2/2) pass. The resumed scenario asserts the note, its link, and that no waiting line appears.
- 14 related chat UI test files pass (155 tests).
- `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, stylelint, `ui:i18n:verify`, and `git diff --check` pass. Local autoreview (P1) is clean.
- Test-lines ratchet: net 0 against `main`; `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is unchanged.

Design decisions by josh (@jalehman).

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ceec074b-9ab4-49d4-9b0d-a70f82be6a12)
