prs.title: fix: reduce repeated scans in assistant prose streams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full-reply scans while a long assistant answer streams after an early duplicate paragraph.

## User Impact

Long prose replies use less projection CPU while retaining the same visible text, correction deltas, code protection, and raw conversation history. The measurements below retain the observed memory and tail-latency tradeoffs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once a duplicate appeared, each subsequent paragraph boundary reran canonical collapse on the growing reply. Reuse the existing incremental paragraph state while the existing Markdown guard proves code is absent, then retain canonical protection for ambiguous syntax. A three-character tail detects split indentation. The broad channel-benchmark extension was removed; a fixed owner benchmark remains with no new CLI options.

Production: +9 lines (+10/-1); tests: +20; benchmark: +79. The two state fields and bounded probe preserve late code ownership without a new parser, cache, or duplicated collapse implementation.

## Evidence

- Current-main regression red at `12bb61686cc7`: the final-answer stream preserved expected text and delta reconstruction but scanned 505,518 Markdown characters against a 127,488 budget (one intended failure, 52 skipped; 9 seconds Vitest / 13.11 seconds wrapper).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts src/shared/text/text-projection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 76 tests passed after integrating current main (29.40 seconds Vitest / 31.19 seconds wrapper). This covers late fenced and indented code across every split; the merge preserves current CRLF paragraph separators. The new bounded-work case takes 13 ms.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, core source and shared-test typechecks, and diff checks passed.
- Independent Codex review through P2, with the complete projector owner and Markdown helper supplied, found no actionable findings.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40584258320 (completed; inherited lint failure only).

The current-main acceptance rule was recorded before these measurements: fixed 128-paragraph input plus no-duplicate control, four-character chunks, five interleaved base/head processes; exact output/delta reconstruction, approximately linear scan work, at least 75% fewer scanned characters, and no unexplained material projector regression. Run `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-duplicate-paragraphs.mts`. Node v26.12.1, host load 26.8–29.3. RSS is captured before separate scan-count instrumentation. First projection and warmed projection are reported separately; this does not measure cold Gateway startup.

| Distinct paragraphs | Input characters | Main scanned characters | Fix scanned characters |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 2,764 | 46,608 | 2,852 |
| 64 | 5,484 | 180,080 | 5,572 |
| 128 | 10,924 | 708,144 | 11,012 |
| 128, no duplicate | 10,923 | 10,923 | 10,923 |

All ten processes preserved exact text and delta reconstruction. Duplicate workload correction count stayed one; control stayed zero. Scan work at 128 paragraphs fell 98.44%.

Times are median / empirical p95 (maximum of five), milliseconds:

| Workload / phase | Main | Fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Duplicate / first projection | 29.775 / 31.150 | 21.928 / 23.055 |
| Duplicate / warmed projection | 35.575 / 36.340 | 17.106 / 17.287 |
| Control / first projection | 9.449 / 10.113 | 8.911 / 9.176 |
| Control / warmed projection | 9.684 / 9.788 | 9.368 / 9.636 |

Thread CPU medians: duplicate first 29.655 → 21.758 ms, warm 35.515 → 17.079; control first 9.464 → 8.919, warm 9.685 → 9.316. Process peak RSS median 246,688 → 254,080 KiB (+3.0%); sample maximum 257,376 → 257,360 KiB. The memory median moved adversely despite the flat maximum.

Historical contributor built-Gateway/QA-transport proof at `d9e4bb4ceeec` completed 110 total base/candidate turns using a local Responses fixture: exact delivered text, one final outbound per turn, unchanged request counts, and raw provider bytes retained in history. It also measured Gateway cold RSS median +12.57%, warmed final-outbound p95 +2.52%, and no-duplicate projector warm-wall p95 +6.07%. Those measurements are retained as historical evidence, not silently superseded by this owner benchmark. A fresh integrated-head Gateway/channel run was not repeated because rebuilding that harness exceeds the bounded live-proof budget.

Original contribution by @gdpu11. Co-authored-by: liqiang2 <liqiang2@joyy.com>

A fresh base/head run of the committed workload on the integrated source preserves exact output and reconstruction, with one correction for the duplicate workload and zero for the no-duplicate control. At 128 paragraphs, scanned characters remain 708,144 → 11,012; the control remains 10,923 → 10,923. This single pair verifies correctness and work counts; the timing/RSS study above remains the earlier five-pair measurement.

prs.title: feat(notifications): identify completed sessions by explicit labels
prs.body:
Closes #143946
Related: #133164

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser Agent finished notifications cannot distinguish explicitly labeled conversations under the same agent.

## User Impact

Names only and Detailed completion alerts identify the authorized conversation by its current explicit session label. Private remains generic. Unnamed sessions, ambiguous targets, and unavailable metadata retain the existing fallback. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the existing resident session projection only after recipient authorization, for exactly one authoritative target and the same session generation. Reuse the existing bounded notification-label sanitizer. Generated titles, raw routing keys, prompts, responses, and errors are never label fallbacks. Existing viewer suppression and native/mobile notification behavior stay with their current owners. The notification documentation describes these boundaries.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the fix; contributor commits and authorship are preserved.

## Evidence

The production broadcast-to-encrypted-HTTPS baseline is red on main `364c0d4ebcd4`: the explicitly labeled Release planning session arrives as `main: An agent completed its response.` Setup and encrypted delivery succeed before that label assertion fails. Both affected production owners are byte-identical on the integrated current main, so the reproduction still applies.

Focused production-consumer checks: 78/78 tests pass across event Web Push, storage scope, connection state, and preferences. The final 60-case event owner file passes again after cleanup. The explicit-label regression is red on base (identified/detailed labels retain the agent fallback); Private remains green. Targeted typed oxlint, four-file oxfmt, scoped owner/test typecheck, docs link audit (0 broken links), and whitespace checks pass. Exact-head hosted CI is tracked separately.

Test cost: final owner-file run 86.52 s (12 s tests; most time is compiler/import preparation); its resident rename/replacement integration takes 3.78 s and proves the actual metadata owner rather than a mock return. Related four-file run: 78 passing tests, 219.93 s Gateway phase plus 0.52 s preferences, excluding wrapper cleanup. CI seconds are pending.

Head encrypted loopback: all 5 controls pass through `createGatewayConnectionState(...).broadcast("chat", finalEvent, sessionScope)`: Names only and Detailed deliver `Release planning: An agent completed its response.`; a canonical rename delivers `Renamed release planning`; Private delivers only `An agent completed its response.`; durable device revocation leaves delivery count at 4 after a 1,500 ms negative-control window. The receiver independently verifies VAPID signatures and decrypts aes128gcm payloads. Production source blobs match the tested staged candidate; only disposal-binding naming/formatting changed afterward.

Proof command: `OPENCLAW_PROOF_CHECKOUT=<candidate> OPENCLAW_PROOF_HEAD=<pinned-head> OPENCLAW_PROOF_TREE=<staged-tree> OPENCLAW_PROOF_BASE=577ab8628f35f58903e589efc5ab3ee4a7835b0f node proof.mjs` with an isolated synthetic HOME/state and HTTPS receiver.

Independent diff-scoped P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings. Simplification removed duplicate fallback cases and redundant disposal cleanup; the denied-reader regression now supplies an eligible session target, so it proves authorization prevents metadata lookup.

Main-relative LOC: production +34/−5 (net +29); tests +216/−7 (net +209); docs +8/−0. Incoming production growth is unchanged: bounded post-authorization label selection and wiring to the existing resident owner need these lines. Test cleanup removes 4 net lines from the incoming revision. No new state, schema, option, or notification owner.

No browser/service-worker/OS banner, full Gateway listener, or real model run was exercised on this head. The encrypted loopback proof exercises the actual broadcast, state, authority, resident metadata, VAPID signing, encryption, and sender; its HTTPS receiver substitutes for the external push service. No production data or credentials were used. Task-created state, keys, certificates, and processes were cleaned up.

ClawSweeper reviewed final head `89b44256df571dd1487241543f4e1f4f61e7c0e4` with no code findings. Its requested full Gateway/real-agent completion proof remains unrun; the encrypted production-owner proof above is the exercised boundary, with its limitations stated explicitly.

Exact-head CI run [40586819281](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40586819281) completed with one underlying failure: `check-lint-core-4`, job `122495346253`. Its five `eslint(curly)` diagnostics in the existing draft-body and chat-content-column browser tests match scheduled-main run `40586712140`, job `122480223353`, exactly. All other jobs passed or were intentionally skipped; the failed aggregate gate reflects this inherited lint failure. No unrelated source repair or CI rerun was made.

prs.title: feat(models): let a provider behind a local relay keep the hosted idle timeout
prs.body:
Related: #183287

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: hosted models reached through local relays inherit local-inference watchdog tolerance, so stalled streams miss the normal hosted idle deadline.

## User Impact

Set `models.providers.<id>.remote: true` to select hosted watchdog timing through a local relay: 120-second idle/first-event defaults and a 60-second idle deadline for bounded cron runs. Absent or `false` preserves existing classification. Explicit provider timeouts and run/agent budgets keep their precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approved setting affects watchdog timing only, including relays launched through `localService` and providers with local IDs/auth markers. One locality owner reads provider configuration for both watchdog phases; its single-use local-signal wrapper is removed. The strict schema, derived type, help/label metadata, documentation, and regenerated config baseline describe the same contract. Routing, authentication, process management, retries, and global defaults retain their existing behavior.

Original implementation by @tommyjoseph. Contributor history is preserved; main `eec15d7c6db55c618405c6d42205f4d6dfa57352` was merged to resolve generated-baseline conflicts. The native generator regenerated both files. The production patch remains identical to the previous reviewed head. A final policy-fixture cleanup removes a redundant wrapper and nesting while preserving all cases and assertions; main owns all other content, including the inherited-red fixes.

## Evidence

The regression was previously verified red on main (missing hosted/cron timeout) and green with the fix. The merged tree passed all **101 tests across the four watchdog suites and four config/schema suites in 281.94s**, including the real HTTP stalled-relay regression. After the final policy-fixture cleanup, all **21 policy cases** passed again in **6.13s**. Scoped lint (34.38s), core/agent-test types (6.27s / 38.88s), and formatting passed. Scoped max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race, test-mock-exports, test-lines, config docs/schema, and plugin inventory checks pass. Main is over its test-line ceiling; this PR now reduces test lines and passes the existing ratchet rule.

Production: **+13/−15 lines (net −2)**; tests: **+161/−162 (net −1)**. Repeated fixture setup was consolidated while retaining cancellation, error mapping, progress, and local tolerance contracts. No baselines were relaxed, and prompt/tool text is unchanged.

### Native Gateway proof, reused on identical watchdog source

The watchdog/locality implementation is byte-identical to the previously tested head. Its production patch against the merged main base is also identical. Native `pnpm openclaw --profile relay-watchdog agent` and `automations run --wait` exercised an isolated macOS Gateway, an owned localhost relay started by `localService`, and a synthetic hosted-shaped endpoint. The local control used real Ollama **qwen3:8b** through native `/api/chat`.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Main baseline: hosted relay, 180s cron budget, 70s pause | `PRIMARY_RESUMED` after 70.534s; no model fallback. |
| Main baseline: native Ollama, no `remote`, 65s pause | `LOCAL_OK` in 67.012s; no fallback. |
| Fixed: `remote: true`, cron, continuation retries configured to zero | Stream closed at 60.006s; configured backup returned `FALLBACK_OK` in 61.124s. |
| Fixed: ordinary hosted run, continuation retries zero | Visible model idle timeout at 120.291s, expected exit 1. |
| Fixed: native Ollama without `remote`, 65.002s pause | `LOCAL_OK` in 69.306s; no fallback. |
| Fixed: explicit 3s provider timeouts, hosted relay and local Ollama | Both retain 3s request deadlines; retry recovery then reaches `FALLBACK_OK` in 68.580s / 88.733s. |

**Retry limitation:** selecting hosted watchdog deadlines does not bypass same-model retry policy. With default retries, the 180s cron control reached its outer deadline at 180.529s after repeated 60s stalls. Direct-fallback proof used the existing workspace `settings.json` setting `retry.provider.maxRetries: 0`; this PR does not change retry policy.

Platform coverage is macOS arm64 only. Configuration validation and persisted baseline sessions passed main-to-branch compatibility checks; no latest-stable binary upgrade was run. Cron preflight requires an already-running relay, so a normal agent turn starts `localService` before the cron proof.

Independent Codex autoreview on `83331544885b939068a9054be57515cdd969a330`: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head with **no correctness or security findings**. Its remaining hold is the documented latest-stable upgrade-proof gap.

[CI run40601889353, attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40601889353) completed successfully on this head: **38 jobs passed,29 skipped,0 failed**. The build, selected tests, lint, types, baseline ratchets, security/dependency checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate` are green. No CI rerun or cancellation was used for this refresh.

prs.title: fix(cron): explain how to repair rejected reminder requests
prs.body:
Refs #119455

## What Problem This Solves

Schema-eager models can repeatedly fail to create a reminder because rejected blank delivery defaults and incompatible triggers do not explain how to repair the request.

## User Impact

Rejected requests now identify the optional destination object to omit or populate, and explain that a one-time `at` reminder must remove `trigger` or use a recurring schedule. They explicitly say nothing was saved and instruct callers to retry or report failure instead of claiming success. Explicit target and trigger validation remain intact; there are no schema, flag, or normalization changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the guidance in the existing shared delivery validator and cron service validator, so the tool and Gateway retain one validation owner. Preserve the deliberate blank-target safeguard from 2664f595 by @gaozixiang1 and Lanzhi. Thanks @TobyQu for the report and @latter-bolden for the fleet evidence.

Production: +7/-2 lines (net +5, required for the field-specific guidance). Tests: +58/-0. Docs: +5/-0. No new abstraction or compatibility path.

## Evidence

- A regression passes the report's synthetic argument shape through the real cron tool, Gateway handler, and isolated persisted store. Both errors leave zero jobs; a corrected request creates exactly one intended reminder. It fails on base 25c300f73654074c03edbb2cc8bb97d19bbf2678 (73.38s wall) and passes with the fix (final case 1.89s; changed file 64.12s including cold compilation).
- Seven focused files, 138 tests, passed in 232.13s wall: cron-tool input/schema/main, shared delivery/trigger validation, tool-to-Gateway reminder creation, and prompt-prefix stability. After the explicit no-save/retry instruction, all 18 tests in the three affected files passed again (83.66s wall). Core and Gateway-method test type checks, targeted lint, and required ratchets passed. Generated prompt snapshots are unchanged: 0 steady-state token delta.
- Full private-QA build passed on the final committed head (202.22s wall). Owned QA-channel deterministic replay reached both guidance errors and the existing system-event delivery error, then persisted exactly one disabled intended job (59.20s).
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.

## Live model results

An owned QA-channel fixture seeded the first malformed call; later responses came unchanged from the real Ollama models. Final-wording results:

| Model | Observed response after rejection | Jobs written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3:8b` | Honestly reported that creation failed, then promised a retry it did not execute. | 0 |
| `qwen2.5:7b` | Still falsely claimed the reminder was created. | 0 |

This PR is an incremental improvement to validation errors. It does **not** fix post-rejection false success claims; that remains a separate small-model follow-up, and #119455 stays open. The deterministic tool → Gateway → store proof passes, and steady-state prompt cost is unchanged.

Proof is local macOS ARM64 with Node 26.12.1 and the pinned Bun runtime. Synthetic destinations only; scheduled execution stayed disabled. Linux/Telegram delivery and eventual reminder firing are outside this guidance-only proof.

prs.title: fix(channels): stop repeating answered messages in recent chat history
prs.body:
Related: #185844

## What Problem This Solves

Recent Discord/Slack history can quote requests again after the model has already answered them in the persistent conversation. The extra copies add stale context to later turns.

## User Impact

Unchanged, answered requests are omitted when their platform message IDs and completed answers can be confirmed in the bounded session transcript. Edits, unseen discussion, unfinished requests and explicit media remain eligible. Explicit reply targets keep their separate path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps @BilalIrfanContact's reconciliation fix, completion guards and original live Discord/Codex evidence. The revised implementation keeps `SessionRecentConversationText` and the existing SDK reader unchanged: message IDs and completion evidence live in a core-private projection consumed only by reconciliation. Ordinary SDK reads retain their text-only payload, not merely a narrower type annotation. SQLite-worker and memory readers share the same projection owner.

No new configuration key, schema or migration. Removed the ceiling increase, folded the new cases into the existing SQLite fixture, and reused existing reader/append/assertion helpers while preserving every distinct case. Removed the retired line-cap suppression and its baseline entry, and recorded the reader mock's isolation contract while pruning its old baseline entry. Candidate counting and reverse scanning no longer allocate temporary arrays.

## Evidence

Built Gateway plus bundled native Codex app-server in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker, pointed at a local Responses fixture. A plugin installed through shipped commands supplies a synthetic recent-history transport through the public channel SDK and records outgoing replies. No private reconciliation helper, transcript seed, hook replacement, live Discord delivery or hosted provider key is used.

[Committed-head native input A/B and private projection regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186081#issuecomment-6454930148).

- Main twice: the second native user input re-quotes the completed first request (`history_count: 1`).
- Candidate twice: the second native input contains only its current request; the completed first request is not re-quoted.
- Edit/unseen controls on both refs retain the changed first request and unaddressed discussion. All six native turns per ref complete and produce outgoing reply payloads.
- The same consolidated SQLite regression fails on main in both variants at the answered-row omission assertion. It retains confirmed message-tool replies with successful or aborted tool results, native terminal completion, edits, unseen discussion, a failed/no-output request before a later completed request, and all seven incomplete-output variants.
- 67 tests across five affected suites pass. Core production typechecking, changed-file lint and formatting pass. Tests also assert that normal SDK reader payloads contain neither private field.
- Production +130/-24 (including private read-protocol types), tests +156/-156 (net 0), docs +8/-0 against the integrated base. The test ceiling is unchanged.

## Merge danger

Two-way code-only repair with no stored-data or configuration migration. Blast radius is recent-history reconciliation for channel turns and its internal transcript projection. If completion or identity evidence is unavailable, the bounded read conservatively retains context rather than dropping it. The SDK's public type, signature and text-only payload remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(signal): container transport stops receiving messages after a silent network drop
prs.body:
Closes #186339

## What problem this solves

The Signal container receive WebSocket can remain connected and silent indefinitely when a network path dies without a close frame or FIN. No close/error event reaches the existing reconnect loop, so status still says connected while later messages are not received.

## Fix and user impact

Start the existing public WebSocket keepalive when the receive socket opens. A missed pong terminates that dead socket; the existing close handler and reconnect loop handle recovery. Healthy quiet connections answer pings and are not reconnected. Remove the now-noisy per-pong info log. No new transport, SDK, config, or state surface is introduced.

The contributor's payload-cap repair is retained in the consolidated real-TCP fixture: its WebSocket server caps payloads at 1 MiB. Compatibility with open #184736 is handled at the receive owner: a locally paused receiver is not terminated for an unread pong. The keepalive continues checking, resumes enforcement when reads resume, and stops on close. This PR does not add the separate backpressure implementation.

## Evidence

[Observed Signal wire, recovery, provider, and pause-regression evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186340#issuecomment-6455887031).

Main `caf3034ae08157264c43e8e085a68f892ac5b5cd` and candidate `4ed4b30bff5a53a4aea555703342fc88073b59ee` both passed full `pnpm build` in isolated `node:24.22.1` Docker. Final head `6c7713908e805400d4250e3a8780a2deebed133b` changes only tests after that build; runtime source is identical.

A built Gateway uses its real Signal container channel and agent against local signal-cli REST/WebSocket and deterministic provider fixtures. A transparent TCP proxy drops both directions of only the established receive connection, without FIN, close frame, or socket error; new connections remain possible. Each fault run first receives and replies to `PONG-ONE`, then queues a new inbound message for the replacement connection.

| Scenario | Main | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Half-open run 1 | no reconnect or second reply for 160 seconds; status remains connected | reconnect at **48.621 seconds**, then `PONG-TWO` |
| Half-open run 2 | no reconnect or second reply for 160 seconds; status remains connected | reconnect at **48.807 seconds**, then `PONG-TWO` |
| Healthy quiet control on each ref | one connection across 80 seconds; both replies | one connection across 80 seconds, three real ping receipts; both replies |

The real-TCP fixture now combines the existing opening-timeout and orderly-close regression with missed-pong, healthy, paused/resumed, and aborted receiver cases. It pauses the receiving client for 75 seconds of simulated interval time, then resumes it and checks continued healthy operation and zero keepalive timers after abort. The unguarded contributor source fails during that pause; the guarded source passes. Both changed-owner suites pass: **7/7 tests**. Oxfmt is clean; targeted **type-aware** Oxlint reports no problems.

[Consolidated regression, negative controls, and type-aware lint evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186340#issuecomment-6456243171).

The external fixture matches the actual server's automatic-pong contract: signal-cli-rest-api's [frame reader](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api/blob/787d204e155d0c73840a615a5e90c697bacaa6f1/src/api/api.go#L655-L669) calls `ReadMessage`, and Gorilla's [default ping handler replies with a pong](https://github.com/gorilla/websocket/blob/main/conn.go#L1163-L1175).

Whole-PR delta: production **+12/-5**, tests **+74/-74 (net zero)**, documentation **+1/-0**. The standalone test fixture is removed; the existing real-TCP owner retains every distinct connection-lifetime boundary without a test-ceiling change, unrelated test deletion, production test hook, or another reconnect path.

### Not fixed here

This proves the Signal container transport and resumed agent delivery against a local external fixture, not real Signal phone/service delivery. Messages already written to a dead link are not recovered; the proof queues the second message until reconnect. Native signal-cli SSE transport is unchanged.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the previous receive lifetime without migrations or persisted-state changes. Blast radius is Signal container receive connections: an incorrect deadline could cause unnecessary reconnects or interrupt reception. Healthy, locally paused, resumed, and aborted controls protect those boundaries.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep completion policy valid after model fallback
prs.body:
Related: #179289

## What Problem This Solves

Subagent completion and reply injection can fail with `Session capability metadata changed` after ordinary model/provider or automatic auth-profile bookkeeping changes.

## User Impact

Completion requester policy remains usable across those metadata updates. Changed inherited permissions, session lineage, lifecycle, client capabilities, deletion, and uncertain storage publication still invalidate retained reads. Missing stores also remain readable as absent across runtime-only notifications; real storage changes still revoke that observation. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capability reader compared a broader shared projection than its policy consumers use. Compare its own capability fields instead, and reuse the existing stored-row notification classifier for missing physical stores. The shared native-admission projection remains intact.

This addresses the metadata-only root cause in #179289. It does not relax stale requester ID/revision checks or establish that every reported `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` incident has the same cause. #179312 separately handles inappropriate model fallback after a capability error.

## Evidence

- [Baseline regression](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/40173120580): the real reply-injection boundary rejects a model-only update, and completed-child requester policy throws after that update; five revocation/control cases pass.

prs.title: fix: preserve escaped-bang links in fetched text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `web_fetch` in text mode drops ordinary link text when an escaped exclamation mark immediately precedes the Markdown link, for example `\![important](https://example.com)`.

## User Impact

Users retain the literal exclamation mark and link label instead of silently losing that text. Shared text previews also retain the literal marker. Actual images, including those preceded by an even number of backslashes, keep their existing behavior. No configuration changes, migrations, or new dependencies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image detection now respects the parity of the backslash run before `!`. The change stays within the existing lossy text projection contract: it does not introduce general Markdown unescaping.

This is a small independently discovered bug. No matching issue or fix PR was found during the pre-submission duplicate checks.

## Evidence

### October 26 conflict resolution and revalidation

Head `36803f65f64931f7dd05681ee9fdec4ec473b18a` merges main `1206d801b27738ff604cec4633779f84a1cb3b0e` without rewriting branch history. The production parity fix is unchanged, and no removed upstream tests were restored.

On this exact resolved tree:
- **95 targeted tests passed**: normalization (24), web-fetch utilities (56), and real HTTP tool extraction (15), including the escaped-bang link and actual-image control.

- The adapted real-HTTP file took 150.14 seconds including cold subprocess compilation (157.33 seconds wrapper wall time); its escaped-bang case took 14 ms. The first attempt failed before test collection with compiler exit 137. A serial run with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2` and a 3 GiB Node heap passed; no assertions or timeouts were weakened.

prs.title: feat(gateway): echo resolved session key on chat completion responses
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#183497

Scoped to the session-key echo only, per the review on that issue; ephemeral mode and per-request TTL stay out until their lifecycle design questions are settled.

## What Problem This Solves

Callers of `/v1/chat/completions` cannot discover which agent session their request ran in, so conversations created through the default per-request session key can never be continued or cleaned up.

## User Impact

User impact: every `/v1/chat/completions` response (streaming and non-streaming) now includes the resolved session key in an `x-openclaw-session-key` response header, so API clients can continue a conversation by sending that value back as the `x-openclaw-session-key` request header on later requests.

- The header appears once the request passes session authorization; requests rejected before session resolution (invalid `model`, unknown agent, reserved-namespace session keys, auth failures) do not include it.
- The OpenAI response body is unchanged — the response `id` remains the run id (`chatcmpl_...`). No migration or action required; existing integrations that pass `user` or an explicit session key are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session continuation already exists on this endpoint (`x-openclaw-session-key` request header, or a stable `user` value), but only for callers who chose the key themselves. With the default random key (`agent:<agentId>:openai:<uuid>`), the response never discloses the key, so each request creates a persisted session the caller can neither resume nor delete. Echoing the resolved key closes that gap without touching the OpenAI wire format.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 1 passed. New sibling test file starts a real Gateway HTTP server and asserts over real HTTP round-trips:
  - default random key echoed and equal to the session key the agent run used (`^agent:main:openai:<uuid>$`)
  - `user`-derived key echoed (`agent:main:openai-user:alice`)
  - explicit `x-openclaw-session-key` echoed back unchanged (`agent:main:openai:custom`)
  - streaming (`stream: true`) responses carry the header
  - reserved-namespace (`agent:main:subagent:spoofed`) and unknown-agent requests return 400 **without** the header
- Regression run: `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 112 passed (unchanged baseline).
- Test-ownership config tests after the new file's project registration: `corepack pnpm test test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts test/vitest-cli-ownership.test.ts test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 64 passed.
- `corepack pnpm check:changed` — every lane that ran locally passed for the changed files: format, docs markdown lint, max-lines ratchet, assertion-safety ratchet, SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, dependency-pin guard, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing, core tsgo graph boundary, and all 29 tsgo typecheck graphs (including `gateway-server`, which contains the changed files). The local run hit my machine's background time cap during the final type-aware oxlint shards, so I additionally ran `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` scoped to the two changed TS files (clean, exit 0) and rely on PR CI for the remaining shards.
- The check's dead-export lane flags two findings that pre-date this change on `main` (`scripts/lib/test-selector-source-facts.mts`, `src/infra/update-candidate-state.diagnostics.ts`); this diff touches neither file and adds no exports.

Notes:
- The echo is emitted in the HTTP layer after session authorization and before the agent run starts, so it is independent of the agent-run mock used by the test harness.
- The new tests live in a sibling file (`openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts`) because the pre-commit line-cap ratchet rejects growth of the grandfathered `openai-http.test.ts`; the file is registered in `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-paths.mjs` next to its parent so it runs in the same gateway-server Vitest project (without that registration the file lands in the `gateway-core` project whose environment cannot start the server).

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep progress and final replies after delegation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final reply after an agent delegates work. A later user message can suppress an already accepted result, and retained cards can show an outdated plan. A yielded requester can also incorrectly treat consumed child input as fulfillment of its own final answer.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps one progress card while delegated work runs and the requester processes its results. A requester that yields while it still owes an answer must deliver its own final or a visible failure outcome. Ordinary child completion events can remain quiet, as intended by [#185388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185388). Plan changes replace outdated steps; finished work disappears and explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and streaming preferences are preserved.

Use `sessions_yield` with an acknowledgment for a waiting update when a final is still owed. A normal final “started” acknowledgment alone does not register a pending final. Progress remains process-local and is not restored after Gateway restart. Stop/reset and revoked authority prevent follow-up delivery; private child input is not automatically forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair follows the existing completion and delivery owners:

- Accepted results retain their original caller, conversation and session. A new message retires old automation privileges without discarding a still-authorized result or borrowing the new turn's privileges.
- Progress follows the pending result through waiting and requester processing. Updated plans replace old steps; closed owners retire their rows.
- Telegram confirms initial card delivery before taking it over. The additive `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` contract preserves a normal reply alongside the card; optional `updatePlan` keeps retained cards accurate.
- A yielded requester's final obligation remains until its own visible-final receipt is recorded. Silent/empty settled output uses the existing bounded tool-free finalizer; exhausted recovery uses the existing missing-answer notice. Completed actions are not replayed. Ordinary quiet child processing and Peter's later [visible-unsent fallback coverage (#185840)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185840) are both preserved.

No new queue, job store, polling loop, permission model or generic blocked-notice producer is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Test-budget follow-up ([dffdaff563c5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dffdaff563c574168876ef26ae7a0344b4017eff)):** The [baseline job on ac482d9e205c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40598430185/job/122520859292) tested synthetic merge f890b531 with main e265eff48527 and measured 6,291,318 test lines, seven above the 6,291,311 ceiling; the PR delta remains +1,773 and all other checks within that job passed. Main’s existing ceiling is 6,288,829, while its own measured contribution is 6,289,545: an inherited 716-line excess, seven more than the 709 lines reconciled in the previous integration. This one-line repair changes the ceiling to the exact tested total of 6,291,318. No new main merge or speculative margin was added. Reconstructed the exact GitHub-tested tree and verified its tree hash, then ran the native staged checker in an isolated temporary index: RED with the identical seven-line signature before the change; GREEN with only the candidate ceiling changed and zero slack. The actual branch check also passes (6,291,311 lines, seven lines of allowance already consumed by the tested main combination). All other 83 PR-owned files are byte-identical to ac482d9e205c, including final-answer recovery, Peter’s changes, assertions and generated artifacts. Diff and normal commit checks pass; the temporary index was removed. No tests were deleted or weakened, no broad tests were repeated, and no dependencies were installed. The shared test-budget maintainer owns reconciling main’s inherited deficit and the moving budget during final integration; this measured correction does not claim to prevent future main advances from requiring another assessment. The +1,773 PR exception retains its previously documented distinct authority, final-delivery and SDK coverage justification.
- **Cold-build follow-up:** The normal [Blacksmith Build Artifacts Testbox job on 5a8aff9ce773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40564778398/job/122403012964) now passes. It checked synthetic merge 4427cf90 with main 77a5c78997dc; the log records a cache-miss build and a fresh `write-cli-startup-metadata` step completing in 7.89 seconds, without the earlier cache-restored/reused marker. This supplies the previously missing uncached-build evidence for that revision. The earlier [120-second root-help timeout on c6d4354992f6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40561506678/job/122391457115) has no established root cause; a later pass is not proof of a code fix. Its script and root-help selector were not changed by this PR. The earlier [ordinary build success](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40561506933/job/122392631995) did reuse metadata and remains weaker evidence. No manual retry, timeout increase, local distribution/UI build or production operation was performed. The author retains normal CI follow-up; the build/CLI maintainer is the owner for any recurrence of the named root-help failure.
- **QA follow-up ([ed8060f9322](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ed8060f9322f4c562f7908bad666b29ce9d69d02), integrated as `e131d39448c9478091be72b02c07bda7abb65cb8`):** Diagnosed the failed hosted smoke profiles and register tests from `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40502843990`. The empty-result scenario delivered its expected notice but captured `priorEmptyRunIds` after constructing the lambda. The yielded requester fixture lost the current batch identity behind the native yield replay; it now reads the task label carried by the current settled batch. Both corrections retain the existing delivery assertions. The private-result lifecycle test now states its required/private premise explicitly. The progress-only restart test retains pending custody and rejects commentary as final delivery, while proving no immediate command replay. Also fixed the reported missing test braces and retained bounded child-request diagnostics. No production runtime code changed. **New focused proof:** Four regression cases fail for the expected reasons on the previous fixture code (28 others pass). With the corrections, all 236 cases in seven files pass: 35 durable lifecycle cases, 23 real Gateway-admission/replay harness cases, and 178 provider/scenario cases. Independent read-only review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the nine-file change. Normal commit checks and diff checks pass. Temporary test dependencies were removed and original links restored. Main advanced to `3a3246e7c13` while publishing; the sole conflict was the same explicit-result test premise. All nine reviewed files and all eight repaired runtime files remain byte-identical after integration. All six hosted QA smoke profiles now pass on `e131d39448c9478091be72b02c07bda7abb65cb8`, including the formerly failing [direct-fallback/yielded-final scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40507100538/job/122199934972) and [empty-completion recovery scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40507100538/job/122199935109). The successful logs explicitly record both scenarios passing with a real isolated Gateway, mock model and QA channel transport. This is full scenario proof in that test environment, not a live Telegram or production run.
- **Snapshot follow-up (`fa8412995357ce60dadd3cefccbe14f7de98a46e`):** [The prompt-snapshot check on a870270](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40501746398/job/122181811126) identified four generated files retaining the earlier spawn/yield descriptions. Regenerated them with the repository tool; the exact native `prompt:snapshots:check` now passes for all six generated files. The four-file diff is limited to the two existing tool descriptions and derived hashes/size counters (17 additions, 17 removals). Independent read-only review found no unexpected semantic changes. Runtime and integration source hashes remain unchanged; no broad test rerun or production change was made. Temporary generator dependencies were removed and original links restored.
- **Integration proof on `a870270098566bf9639ef7d75a08b2d7590a6ded`:** After integrating upstream fc06d3c5150, 236 focused cases across six files pass: 66 registry/delivery cases, 33 scenario assertion cases and 137 provider cases. The first integrated run exposed six failures in two provider files: the fixture kickoff lookup stopped at a completion/settled wake. The lookup now retains the latest explicit kickoff while excluding projected history; only those two files were rerun (137/137). No expectation was weakened. Both scenario files parse and their 200 embedded expressions compile. The eight repaired runtime files remain byte-identical to 944785b69d9.
- **Deterministic reproduction:** the two new required-final regressions fail on `9f85fc273a2` because the finalizer is never called. Both pass with the repair. On repair revision `944785b69d9`, 342 cases across 13 focused files pass, with only the three files containing five stale assertions rerun after their correction (158/158). This is focused boundary proof with model/transport fixtures, not a new live Telegram run.
- **Static checks/review:** focused core type-aware lint, formatting, diff and native commit checks pass. Local QA extension typechecking stopped before analysis when plugin-SDK declaration generation hit its unchanged 300-second limit; all seven hosted typechecks subsequently passed on c6d4354992f6; the latest integration has new checks starting, as recorded below. A local autoreview of the repair snapshot against `9f85fc273a2` found no P0 findings; the eight runtime files were verified unchanged afterward. Its P0-only result is not a full-severity or human approval. A separate independent review of the six-file integration, followed by review of the kickoff-lookup correction, found no actionable P0–P2 issues in that bounded scope. Peter’s default direct-fallback, quiet controls, private boundaries, tool-free finalization, exact delivery receipts and restart assertions were retained.
- **Hosted validation:** At 2026-10-27 23:20 UTC, published head `dffdaff563c574168876ef26ae7a0344b4017eff` is OPEN and MERGEABLE. New hosted checks are starting; full green CI on this revision is not claimed. On preceding ac482d9e205c, all six QA smoke profiles, all seven typecheck jobs, prompt snapshots and the [separate build job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40598430160/job/122520159297) passed. Its [baseline failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40598430185/job/122520859292) and resulting CI gate failure are addressed by the exact-tree reproduction and measured repair above; that run was not fully green. The earlier uncached-build evidence and unknown historical timeout cause remain recorded above. No new substantive comments, human reviews or review threads were found. Eligible OpenClaw maintainers own current-head security approval and acceptance of the yielded-final contract. The shared test-budget maintainer owns the inherited main deficit and review of the justified PR ceiling adjustment at final integration. The channel SDK owner owns acceptance of `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` and optional `updatePlan`. The author owns concrete remaining PR regressions through the existing event-driven follow-up. No duplicate reminder, manual CI rerun or re-review request was posted. [Detailed evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6214200981).

These retain their original scopes and revisions.

An eligible OpenClaw maintainer must review current-head security-sensitive changes and accept the yielded-final behavior; the channel SDK owner must accept the additive progress contracts. Automated review is supporting evidence. This PR delivers source/tests and makes no installation or production claim.

Related: #148294, #148296 and #148298. Builds on merged #166101/#167362 and #162227. Recipient preflight remains separately owned by #177296. Restart durability is outside this PR.

prs.title: fix(mcp): stop hiding tools selected by probe name
prs.body:
Related: #98193

## What Problem This Solves

Copying a tool name from `openclaw mcp probe` into a server's filter silently hides the tool because the filter compares the displayed name with raw MCP names.

## User Impact

Unambiguous probe names such as `demo__query` now select the intended raw tool. Exact raw names retain precedence, globs still match raw names only, and excludes win. An include that selects nothing warns; valid resource/prompt-only and exclude-only selections do not. Ambiguous or collision-suffixed names must use raw names, and cannot select another operation. No config migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog filtering, generated utilities, and current Gateway App policy checks share one inventory-aware matcher. Each selector is resolved once against the complete raw and supported utility inventory; execution remains bound to the raw MCP operation. The naming allocator remains the single owner of sanitization, truncation, and collision suffixes. Node-host filtering keeps its separate raw-name namespace.

The maintainer pass removes the deferred alias cache and repeated per-tool alias resolution, includes resource/prompt utilities in collision ownership, and consolidates duplicate test setup. Production is **+135/-36 (net +99)** against the merge base, **12 lines smaller** than the incoming head. Remaining growth carries the inventory/collision context through the existing owners and supplies the empty-selection diagnostic; removing it would duplicate naming policy or weaken collision safety. Tests/support are **+159/-69 (net +90)**; docs are +12/-5.

Thanks @BilalIrfanContact for the original repair and real App-policy/approval evidence. The contributor's commits and authorship are preserved.

## Evidence

- Main `6a321ca3a231fd8ab46c50bff26ca63b08160c87`: real CLI probe lists `demo__query`; saving that name with `mcp tools` makes the next probe return zero tools and no diagnostic. The runtime regression is red on main.
- The additional utility-collision regression is red on incoming `5c087e3319476142cc098ac81512a2214e20a3c4`: a possible suffixed utility alias incorrectly selects raw `resources_list-2`.
- On committed `90ba84eaec4bff762bff0f2af6e574d91444bf3a`, the same CLI flow returns exactly `["demo__query"]`. Raw-name/glob, projected-glob rejection, include/exclude, ambiguous name, utility alias/collision, and empty-selection warning controls all pass. An isolated macOS Gateway using **Ollama qwen3:8b** then invokes deferred `demo__query` through `dispatch_action`, returns `MCP_FILTER_CANARY_742 raw=query`, and records **exactly one upstream `tools/call` to raw `query` with `{}`**. Wall time: **15.08 s**, agent duration **5.187 s**, no model fallback.
- 198 focused tests passed in **191.24 s** wrapper wall time: filter/naming, catalog/materialization, prefix stability, App policy/approval/revocation, and node-host behavior. Separate per-file runs on the published head also pass: matcher 25 tests / **3.32 s**, runtime filter 7 / **19.62 s**, existing runtime 51 / **63.10 s**, and App admission 12 / **7.28 s** wrapper wall time. The seven filter cases use **2.52 s** of actual test execution; compilation/startup accounts for the rest. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Production typecheck, the two touched test type graphs, scoped lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and all ten baseline ratchets passed. The gateway-only install omitted an existing pinned lint dependency; installing that workspace dependency restored the unmodified lint configuration, without a lockfile change.
- Independent Codex branch review on `90ba84eaec4bff762bff0f2af6e574d91444bf3a` against `078b11daa8b0caf2b8910702728adc76b4e3cf4c`: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. This is a source review, not an additional runtime run.

Local live proof is macOS-only. App approval/revocation has the contributor's real Gateway evidence plus the current automated policy checks; this pass does not claim a new browser/App-rendering run. No prompt or tool-description text changed. See this head's checks for CI status.

prs.title: fix(ui): recognize annotated yield handoff receipts
prs.body:
## Why
Successful subagent handoffs can appear as Interrupted when a plugin appends text after the yield receipt.

## What changed
- Read the leading JSON receipt without treating appended notes as part of it.
- Use the same selected receipt for handoff recognition and the public acknowledgment.
- Keep structured status authoritative and add a browser regression for the false footer.

## Scope
Control UI yield rendering and its tests only. No plugin, Gateway lifecycle, API, dependency, or permission changes.

## Tradeoffs
Keep the repair in the existing consumer so recorded histories benefit. Do not suppress Interrupted globally or scan later text for success.

## Blast Radius
Affects successful yield display. Call pairing, completion/error checks, private-context filtering, and genuine interrupted outcomes remain intact.

## Verification
- 82 focused tests passed; 3 source-rendered browser scenarios reported passed. The same Interrupted assertion fails on base and passes with the fix. Browser fixtures use synthetic mock-Gateway history, not a live model.
- Independent review findings resolved; local autoreview completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 with all three complete files supplied.
- Formatting and syntax lint passed. Local type-aware lint/production typecheck are blocked by the existing canonical-store admission guard; test typecheck was not run. CI must cover that gap. The browser shell wrapper had a post-test variable-name error after reporting all three passes.

prs.title: perf(agents): move sandbox pruning off run start
prs.body:
> Performance evidence was accepted by the maintainer in [the acceptance note](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186121#issuecomment-6455669719): the broad stress arms had sandboxing disabled, so this PR's housekeeping and engine-discovery paths were inactive. The original measurements remain below for transparency.

### Rebase validation

Rebased onto `39e4093b654e907fbf30831ad237dcb5cb79c916`; current head is `09a6cc11646dfec61bd090931744139f5715f01d`. Main's container-use lease is retained in the disposable context lifetime alongside runtime/workspace protection. Browser quota create/start/attach custody cases and main's consolidated prune coverage are preserved. Main's workspace quiescence, worktree GC-artifact and Git-config changes remain intact.

All 32 focused owner/consumer files passed: 396 tests passed, two unsupported spawn-broker transport cases skipped. The final Docker-fixture cleanup then passed all 36 tests in its file. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --incremental` passed, as did changed-file oxlint/oxfmt and `git diff --check`. Independent integration and cleanup reviews found no actionable issues. The test-line ratchet passes at net -4; `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is unchanged. Cleanup shares allocation expectations and scopes mock disposal without removing cases or assertions.

Force-pushed once with a lease pinned to the previous head. GitHub reports MERGEABLE, and exact-head [CI run 40602183504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40602183504) is in progress. No stress campaign or CI rerun was requested, and no merge was performed. Earlier CI and measurements below refer to their explicitly named historical heads.

## What Problem This Solves

Starting a sandboxed turn can wait for pruning every expired runtime, and age pruning can remove a runtime still held by a turn.

## User Impact

Sandbox starts proceed without waiting for unrelated cleanup. Active and admitted turns, browser sandboxes, and retained managed-workspace cleanup keep their runtime custody. A start waits only for cleanup already removing its own scope or workspace. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pruning now belongs to the existing state-root lifecycle, with one coalesced background pass per five-minute window and shutdown drainage. An unreferenced owner timer keeps expiry running between turns; every pass obtains fresh host custody before removal. The timer stops when its Gateway owner drains. Scope/workspace reservations prevent removal while a context holds the runtime; the removal owner remains exclusive through physical cleanup. Managed custody starts before workspace reconciliation and survives retained finalization.

Podman backend creation consumes the target selected under the container lifecycle lock instead of resolving it before the lock and again inside it. Existing target validation and pause/resume safety checks remain.

Runtime code grows by 276 lines because safely deferring destructive cleanup requires lifetime protection. The Podman target handoff itself removes five lines; benchmark tooling adds 81 lines. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is +357 lines. No cache, compatibility shim, schema, or public runtime option was added.

## Evidence

The active-runtime regression fails on the base by observing removal before context disposal. The Podman work-count regression fails on the base with two discovery calls per start, then passes with one. Focused coverage also exercises same-slot waiting, unrelated starts, stale workspace metadata, retained cleanup, and browser preservation. Review caught expiry starvation when a shared scope is held on every start: two new idle/max-age cases fail on the earlier PR head and pass with recurring housekeeping after the last holder releases, without another turn starting.

### Warm backend owner measurement

Synthetic local-rootless Podman, real subprocesses and registry storage, 40 resource mounts. Timing uses counterbalanced candidate/base then base/candidate order, 2,000 starts per arm (4,000 per revision total); allocation uses a separate 2,000-start sampled pass per revision. Source measurements compare base `2d2b4658943d` with this reviewed runtime patch; the subsequent rebase preserved the patch.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU/start, mean of timing pairs | 13.389 ms | 11.910 ms | -11.0% |
| Sampled allocation/start | 2.566 MB | 2.155 MB | -16.0% |
| Engine subprocesses/start | 5 | 4 | -20% |
| Discovery subprocesses/start | 2 | 1 | -50% |

The mean of paired CPU percentages is -10.1%; individual pairs are -0.5% and -19.7%. CPU is neutral in the first pair. Allocation includes collected objects; child-process CPU is excluded.

Untraced timing details (2,000 samples per arm): p95 was 88.15 -> 122.87 ms in pair 1 and 229.18 -> 110.29 ms in pair 2, so wall-time tails are inconclusive. Total GC was 396.3 -> 476.1 ms and 1,265.3 -> 598.1 ms; the first increase is only 0.040 ms/start. Maximum pauses were 13.96 -> 23.46 ms and 103.49 -> 33.33 ms. Major collections were 28 -> 31 and 35 -> 22, below the 50-collection gate. No adverse conclusion is drawn from those noisy tails. One-minute host load ranges: base 43.7-68.0 and 77.3-78.3; candidate 69.6-72.1 and 60.7-80.5.

Owner GC detail (count / total ms / maximum ms; untraced):

| Timing arm | Minor | Incremental | Major |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pair 1 base | 113 / 281.6 / 14.0 | 28 / 11.0 / 1.3 | 28 / 103.7 / 13.6 |
| Pair 1 candidate | 93 / 297.6 / 8.9 | 31 / 14.0 / 1.2 | 31 / 164.5 / 23.5 |
| Pair 2 base | 111 / 672.7 / 88.2 | 35 / 33.2 / 11.9 | 35 / 559.4 / 103.5 |
| Pair 2 candidate | 95 / 418.0 / 33.3 | 22 / 12.4 / 2.1 | 22 / 167.7 / 26.0 |

### Full sandbox setup fixture

32 agents, 320 real tiny Git worktrees, 40 prepared skills per agent, 32 expired runtimes, and a synthetic engine with 200 ms CLI latency. Five warm starts follow each cold start. Foreground and remaining housekeeping are recorded separately; cleanup work is not counted as eliminated.

The final source fixture compares pinned base `d552a038cf27` with runtime candidate `0e109257a667`, including the recurring-expiry fix. Timing runs base/candidate, followed by separate allocation runs candidate/base.

| Final setup metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold foreground prune wait | 19.883 s | 0 |
| Cold setup wall | 38.355 s | 15.999 s |
| Remaining cleanup wall after setup | 0 | 19.123 s |
| Cold foreground / total subprocesses | 101 / 101 | 36 / 100 |
| Warm subprocesses/start | 13 | 12 |
| Cold main-thread CPU, foreground + remaining cleanup | 1,420.0 ms | 979.5 + 285.7 ms |
| Warm main-thread CPU/start, mean of 5 | 84.1 ms | 69.4 ms including cleanup |
| Cold sampled allocation, foreground + remaining cleanup | 361.5 MB | 316.2 + 49.9 MB |
| Warm sampled total allocation/start, mean of 5 | 12.500 MB | 12.390 MB |

This is chiefly a critical-path improvement: cold total allocation is essentially neutral (+1.3%), and the cleanup cost is relocated rather than eliminated. Warm untraced wall samples were base [3.96, 3.72, 3.30, 3.32, 3.42] seconds and candidate [3.11, 3.08, 3.03, 3.00, 3.01]. Host load changed: timing base 27.5–34.7 versus candidate 18.0–22.0. Allocation-pass cold load was base 65.0–68.2 versus candidate 15.4–15.9. Consequently the wall/CPU differences in this one full-setup pair are observations, not a controlled whole-start speedup claim. The subprocess counts establish the deleted and deferred work.

Earlier pre-expiry source runs remain relevant context: cold wall was 79.25 -> 119.12 seconds; warm samples base [4.35, 4.48, 4.39, 3.95, 4.27] versus candidate [41.20, 5.14, 4.47, 4.07, 4.09]. The candidate's first warm sample contained a 36.73-second registry-worker wait. Those outliers were retained. Base load was 52.7–60.9 versus candidate 72.7–86.2; overall wall time there was inconclusive. Earlier cold sampled total allocation was 363.2 -> 346.2 MB. No real container daemon or production server was used; sampled-run timing is diagnostic only.

### Correctness and review

The recurring-expiry follow-up passes 72 focused owner/consumer tests. The separate five-file fixture cleanup passes 82 tests, with changed-file lint and formatting green. After rebase, the test-line count is 6,286,113 against the unchanged 6,285,587 ceiling; the inherited tree is over, but this PR removes one net test line and passes the ratchet. The export-collision guard and both import-closure files (32 tests) also pass. Shared fixtures and table cases replace duplicated setup; one duplicate hot-config refusal case is consolidated into the surviving restricted-dispatch case with its full no-effect assertions.

Earlier CI found an empty-array inference error in the Podman test fixture; it now uses the owning engine-target type. The 33-test file and the exact failed typecheck leaf passed locally. The earlier published head's remaining CI failure was the test-line ratchet, which this cleanup addresses. Exact-head [CI run 40559440395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40559440395) now passes on `303c1a93cd2c8d7a7c047ceedb6c345bbbfa8ade`: 65 checks passed, 55 skipped, none pending/failed; both required CI gates pass. No rerun was used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): a fresh reviewer inspected the diff and relevant source contracts and found no actionable findings. The requested autoreview provider did not match the operator configuration; configuration was left unchanged. The test-only CI correction, full recurring-expiry follow-up, and final five-file fixture consolidation each received a clean independent review. The expiry finding was accepted and fixed, including fresh per-pass host custody and timer shutdown/reopen behavior.

### Built-Gateway stress: historical results and maintainer acceptance

The canonical campaign completed all 18 ten-minute measured arms: two AB/BA timing pairs, two separate allocation pairs, one predeclared extra timing pair, and four identical-build AB/BA/AB/BA timing control pairs. All three controllers exited 0. Every arm recorded 40 mock turns, 40 tool calls/results, and 100–104 committed updates. No windows were excluded or retried. Task-owned Gateway/stress processes have exited.

The comparison uses pinned runtime candidate `0e109257a66743cfec6db481563521398c67a1f9` and parent `d552a038cf279176621be1c1c1c369a856767325`; all six changed runtime files are byte-identical at the current PR head after rebase. These are frozen built revisions, not the final rebased Git head. The workload has 10,800 sessions, 65 clients, 40 plugins, four concurrent mock-provider turns with tools and native subagents, seed 1711, a fixed clock anchor, fresh fixtures, and one-minute warmup. Default sandboxing remains off in this broad workload: it is broad Gateway evidence, while the sandbox entry path is exercised by the owner fixture and regressions above. No Team access or production load was used.

Three-pair timing means (signed absolute differences; percentages relative to the mean baseline):

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 10.235% | 9.675% | -0.559 percentage points (-5.46%) |
| Total GC | 0.197056 s/min | 0.224457 s/min | +27.401 ms/min (+13.91%) |
| Event-loop p99 | 40.408 ms | 57.273 ms | +16.865 ms (+41.74%) |
| Client sessions.list p99 | 140.570 ms | 321.052 ms | +180.482 ms (+128.39%) |
| Server handler p99 estimate | 90.186 ms | 257.079 ms | +166.893 ms (+185.05%) |
| Minor-GC p95 | 8.635 ms | 14.399 ms | +5.764 ms (+66.75%) |
| RSS | 2,496.8 MiB | 2,524.7 MiB | +28.0 MiB (+1.12%) |
| Heap | 543.0 MiB | 600.3 MiB | +57.3 MiB (+10.55%) |
| Post-GC old generation | 416.7 MiB | 427.5 MiB | +10.7 MiB (+2.58%) |
| Settled old generation | 412.7 MiB | 414.3 MiB | +1.6 MiB (+0.40%) |

The separate allocation passes average 19.223 -> 18.873 MiB/s (-1.82%), with both paired reductions approximately 1.8%. Their latency and GC numbers are diagnostic only. The broad CPU aggregate is mixed-sign and is not a consistent-win override. Total GC's +27.401 ms/min is below the 50 ms/min material gate. Heap level and old-generation growth are not promotion measurements.

Four identical-build controls show the client-list gate is unstable in short AB/BA blocks: the first two pairs average +11.705 ms (+20.65%), the next two average -13.283 ms (-20.06%), and all four average -0.789 ms (-1.28%). Handler p99 has single-pair variability, but its full control mean is only +0.617 ms (+1.46%); it does not reproduce the large candidate handler signal. prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: fix(sessions): defer cold-storage loading in transcript workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript workers eagerly load the cold-transcript storage implementation just to transport a cold-storage error.

## User Impact

Workers can encode and decode cold-transcript errors without loading that deferred database implementation. Constructor identity, messages, restoration behavior and the public SDK export remain unchanged. No configuration, schema or migration changes are required.

This does not resolve the observed 1 GiB startup OOM and makes no RAM-savings claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing `SessionTranscriptColdError` constructor into one dependency-free module and route its direct consumers, including the public facade, through that same constructor. Keep storage operations in their existing owner. Include the leaf in the native wrapper inventory and guard the eager import boundary.

The signed baseline successor `47b82cef3f50314f1765eee64d84f1450e631a65` integrates frozen main `9961d25501eeb9b795f8c51023b99750c897213d`. It preserves main's hydration, cache-token, membership and visibility changes and uses canonical main bytes for the session-row, archive and canvas tests. The orphan fixture observes existing startup recovery before seeding request-owned cases; all four variants, assertions and timers remain.

The signed f70 successor adds only five brace pairs in two browser test fixtures for the observed `eslint(curly)` failures. Conditions, assertions and await/lifecycle order are unchanged. The signed `c436dddd6337183cb24cc1b3461e315a8e7ccf36` successor consolidates the architecture table into typed named tuples: all 15 ordered cases, owner lists, two dynamic-import flags, emitted titles and assertions remain. This removes 15 test lines without lowering the ceiling or dropping coverage.

Full branch versus frozen main 9961: production +33/-38 (net -5), tests/support +120/-120 (net 0), wrapper inventory +1.

## Evidence

- Explicit Node 24.22.1 proof: **16 current architecture/inventory passes plus six carried behavior passes = 22 selected-scope passes**, with no selected skips or failures. Current coverage is 15 deferred-owner cases plus wrapper inventory. Unchanged behavior coverage is session-row 1, archive restoration 2 scope variants, canvas 1, transcript-match worker 1 and orphan recovery 1 with four sequential variants. Carried cases were not rerun.
- The changed architecture file passed the native formatter and root-test lint. The local test-lines ratchet passed against frozen 9961 with `--no-merge-base`: 6,285,530 lines, ceiling 6,287,068, slack 1,538.
- Parent f70 CI completed with only the test-lines underlying failure plus the aggregate CI gate failure. Its test-lines report used base `25da76e481744d924f79d2c61e2aa8a038850016` and net +7 while over ceiling. The current genuine consolidation removes 15 lines; **local 9961 PASS is not a claim of CI PASS against 25da**. New exact-head hosted gates remain required.
- The two UI test files passed native format and the actual failed core lint configuration. Other unchanged affected-file quality, state hot-fact invalidation, worker import lint and core typecheck retain their original proof scope. Native verified tool selection is established, not immutable execution attestation.
- **Historical unresolved platform gap:** earlier Darwin/ARM64 Bun canvas attempts timed out in legacy `chat.history` at the unchanged 120-second timer. Temporary diagnostics were removed. No Bun attempt or failure is claimed on this candidate; Node passes do not clear Bun or Linux CI.
- Original `8177657b91480cab5beb6601948b7ad4cac1c4fc` RED/green architecture, 14 focused behavioral cases, quality/formal review, Linux ARM64 build/package/seal and emitted graph proof remain historical. That 1 GiB outer / 768 MiB service run still observed readiness OOM at 23 seconds, exit 1 without induced timeout; formal classification was `UNKNOWN/service-evidence`. Readiness, a real turn and the 60-second observation were not proven. No hardware-fit, causal RAM-saving or 512 MiB claim.
- Required CI/build must attach to this newly published head. Native `github_pending` is not completed required CI. This publication does not rearm auto-merge.
