prs.title: fix(codex): preserve protected scheduled continuations
prs.body:
## Problem

A same-session scheduled or internal continuation can arrive while its retained Codex thread is still protected by native/background work. If the current dynamic-tool surface or producer-owned turn context differs, warm reuse can fall through to cold replacement and fail with:

```
Codex thread ... is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

## What changed

- Recover the accepted native tool catalog only for a verified local protected binding.
- Rebuild executors from the current turn and bind only definitions whose names, schemas, and descriptions exactly match the accepted contract, so current authority remains decisive at tool I/O.
- Mark producer-owned conversation context as turn-local and relay it outside immutable thread identity.
- Annotate the direct cron delivery prompt path that was missing from #174900.
- Keep compaction/plan restoration distinct from transient developer handoff context.
- Pass the exact admitted session workspace to existing media-root validation; sibling/shared workspace access remains excluded.

## Safety boundaries

- Genuine immutable policy, provider, runtime, MCP, and plugin changes still rotate or reject.
- Genuine simultaneous claimed ownership is still rejected; this is not a concurrent claim-takeover mechanism.
- Direct/no-relay connections remain fail-closed: handoffs supplement creation policy, and changed protected context without a safe relay still refuses.
- Accepted catalogs restore declarations only. Executors and execution-policy checks are rebuilt from the current admitted turn.
- This intentionally avoids the broader persisted-catalog and completion-ownership architecture in #174900.

## ClawSweeper remediation evidence

| Concern | Evidence added |
|---|---|
| Allowed current owner | Retained declarations execute through freshly prepared current executors. |
| Identityless/private completion | Owner-only effects remain unavailable without current admitted authority. |
| Authority revoked before tool I/O | Revocation is asserted before executor invocation; no second executor call occurs. |
| Scheduled context delivery | Producer-to-harness and direct cron delivery paths are covered. |
| Post-compaction context | Current transient context is restored separately from compacted native history. |
| Existing stored data | A concrete v2026.10.6 stored binding is decoded and recovered without schema migration. |
| No-relay behavior | Documented and tested as fail-closed for changed protected context. |
| Consumer regressions | History, skill, attribution, subscription, and context-budget assertions now distinguish the exact conversation handoff while preserving their original semantics. |
| Provider mocks and protected hook | Real runtime exports are preserved and native metadata is seeded from the actual accepted declaration. |
| Media isolation | Production steering with `workspaceOnly:false` delivers the exact session-workspace image and withholds sibling-session and shared-workspace images before native dispatch or transcript persistence. |

## Relationship to existing work

- Supersedes #176177 while retaining its verified native-catalog/current-executor repair and Stronggenetics attribution.
- Selectively incorporates the safe transient-context portion of #174900, with Ricardo Almeida and Paul Bohm attribution preserved.

## Validation

- Merged current `main` at `364c0d4ebcd`; GitHub reports the branch mergeable.
- Native app-server steering-media proof: **3/3 boundary cases passed** through the packaged `codex-cli 0.164.0` app-server, and **15/15 tests passed** in the complete steering-media suite.
- Red-on-without-fix: removing only the session-workspace argument from the production media-root call produced **2 failures / 1 pass**:
  - exact admitted session image: expected accepted, observed rejected;
  - sibling-session image: remained rejected;
  - shared-workspace image: expected rejected, observed accepted.
- Fixed-head changed-file `oxlint`: 0 warnings/errors.
- Fixed-head changed-file `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent P0-P2 review found no actionable findings. The normal autoreview helper could not launch because this host has no `codex` executable; the permitted separate reviewer assessed the supplied exact diff and production control flow without helper-owned frozen-input guarantees.

### Native app-server proof (redacted)

The proof ran in an isolated temporary OpenClaw namespace; artifacts contain no credentials, personal identifiers, public IPs, or non-public endpoints.

- **Shipped native transport:** each case starts the repository-pinned `codex-cli 0.164.0 app-server`, verifies its reported version, creates a real native turn, and sends steering through the real client. A deterministic loopback Responses endpoint keeps provider output credential-free.
- **Steering authorization boundary, `workspaceOnly:false`:**
  - exact admitted session workspace → accepted;
  - sibling session workspace → rejected;
  - shared workspace → rejected.
- **Final native effect:** the accepted case receives a successful native `turn/steer` acknowledgment whose input contains the expected synthetic PNG bytes as a data URI.
- **Forbidden final effects:** both rejected cases emit zero `turn/steer` requests, make zero `persistApproved` calls, and create zero visible transcript entries.
- **Red/base behavior:** without the production fix, the same proof withholds the admitted session image and exposes the shared-workspace image. The sibling remains withheld.
- **Production path exercised:** `runCodexAppServerAttempt` → packaged native app-server process → active turn → production steering queue → `detectAndLoadAgentHarnessPromptImages` → production media-root resolver → native `turn/steer` acknowledgment. The rejection occurs before `beforeSubmit`, so forbidden media cannot be persisted or dispatched.

The deterministic provider endpoint proves native app-server delivery and acknowledgment, not downstream model interpretation of the image. No live credentials were copied or migrated.

Additional previously supplied evidence covers scheduled context, immediate post-compaction inference, lifecycle revocation before provider/native I/O, and automation final-effect authorization.

## Remediation revision

The current proof revision is `7f8792a8855fe18420bffda5dc35555f59b4f1a6`. It preserves the exact RomneyDa coauthor trailer and the existing human attribution.


## CI ratchet justification

The native packaged-app-server proof adds a distinct transport and lifecycle regression matrix that cannot be represented by the protocol fixture. Hosted CI measured 6,286,693 test lines on the current merged tree, exactly matching the updated ceiling; revision `7f8792a8855fe18420bffda5dc35555f59b4f1a6` raises `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` to that exact observed total. The ratchet passes locally against current `origin/main`, and an independent P0-P2 review found no findings.

prs.title: fix(ui): speed up large Board tab switches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Boards still allocate offscreen report chrome and body renderers, and native report cells subscribe to foreign-frame work they do not use. Visiting and returning to tabs republishes that work across hundreds of retained cells.

## User Impact

Large Boards open and switch tabs faster while preserving card geometry, keyboard focus, report identity, current hidden updates, and foreign-widget teardown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing report-entry latch for fixed-report chrome, and admit its body once. Retain admitted bodies across hidden height-mode changes and MCP retirement. Move the existing content-visibility rule to the fixed card while retaining strict body containment. Native cells avoid foreign-frame reactive inputs and the HTML-only exact-height calculation; loading-covered native readiness remains observed.

The Board data/live-update owner is unchanged. One memo is added; no new observer, cache, dependency, or eager import. Cell LOC is 717 → 725; stylesheet 893 → 895. Signals 6 → 6, effects 2 → 2, cleanup registrations 2 → 2, memos 6 → 7. Tests add zero net lines across the PR.

## Evidence

The Board source is byte-identical to the reviewed and measured candidate after integrating main. The sole conflict was resolved to main's Activity test bytes exactly; both former test repairs are now absent from this PR. Current head is `a6e5ae69253499482ddd116b98b4f1966f945666`, with **9 files, 5,533 → 5,579 LOC (+46)**. The 200 ms at 4× goal remains open.

Full CI [40600568936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40600568936) completed with **42 passing jobs, 24 skipped, and one failed E2E job plus its aggregate**. All UI units, both real-Gateway shards and the strict performance check passed. CI remains failed; the documented native inherited-failure route is used with exact-case evidence.

prs.title: perf(process): avoid decoding child memory samples
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Polling Linux host command memory decodes each procfs file into a UTF-8 string and creates regex matches or PID tokens on every sample, including unchanged process trees.

## User Impact

Lower allocation while monitoring command memory, with the same RSS-plus-swap limit, descendant coverage, and one-/five-second sampling cadence. No configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse the bytes returned by the existing callback-based `readFile` owner. This keeps Node's native batched file reading and eliminates whole-file decoding and regex/token arrays. Every thread is still inspected on every sample, so new worker-thread children remain visible immediately at the existing cadence.

Runtime code grows by 24 lines because direct numeric parsing replaces string/regex parsing while preserving RSS/swap and PID handling. Benchmark tooling adds 27 lines; the requested non-test diff is +51 lines overall. Test code decreases by five lines after consolidating the regression cases. There is no cache, shared reader state, new exported API, or alternate enforcement path. Benchmark usage stays in the existing script header.

## Evidence

- Base: `d7acde6ae97e3e95c3ce4b07fb86cd6eb92db7fb` (includes the earlier child-memory polling and empty-tokenization optimizations).
- Regression: the consolidated worker/grandchild and missing-process cases request 6,115 decoded fixture bytes on base and zero on candidate. Both base cases fail the decoding assertion while their memory-limit result remains correct; candidate passes. The separate real ten-process allocation-budget regression is detailed below.
- Focused owner/supervisor validation: 45 tests passed; 7.32 seconds wall time, 3.14 seconds Vitest duration. Includes worker-thread descendants, grandchildren, swap, long status files, ENOENT/ESRCH races, cancellation, and memory-limit SIGKILL ownership.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. Broad checks are delegated to PR CI; no Testbox was allocated. The first CI run passed behavioral/type/lint checks but rejected the initial +27 test-line delta against an already-over-ceiling tree. The test-only follow-up consolidates coverage to net −5 test lines; no baseline or ceiling file changed. [Final CI run 40601101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40601101773) passed on `2e6c1429e8b09d8f9027db746e59ec14a2cf6945`, including the ratchet.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): final diff reviewed at P0–P2, no actionable findings. The configured autoreview provider preflight refused the selected route; no operator configuration changed. Hosted Codex review also completed on the final head with no findings.

Five paired, concurrent 30-second real-procfs runs after warmup on Linux/Node 26.12.1: one unchanged ten-process tree, nine descendants spawned by nonleader worker threads; interleaved CPU sets swapped each pair. Sampling timers alone were accelerated to 1 ms. Base/candidate completed 73,826 / 73,555 samples. The predeclared win is less allocation/sample without a material paired CPU regression; CPU differences are interpreted against identical-source controls.

| Paired mean | Base | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V8 allocated bytes/sample | 179,312 | 147,256 | −17.9% (−32,056 B) |
| Main-thread CPU µs/sample | 468.27 | 486.57 | +3.9% (+18.30 µs) |
| Total CPU µs/sample | 1,051.43 | 1,070.25 | +1.8% (+18.83 µs) |
| GC µs/sample | 3.587 | 3.353 | −6.5% |
| GC ms/min | 104.89 | 98.91 | −5.97 ms/min |
| End-of-run RSS MiB | 96.77 | 88.47 | −8.31 MiB |
| End-of-run heap used MiB | 14.33 | 11.40 | −2.92 MiB |

This is an allocation improvement, not a demonstrated CPU speedup. Allocation improved in every pair (17.1–19.1%); CPU changed signs and identical-source controls showed substantial spread. RSS/heap are contextual end-of-run readings, not forced-GC retained-memory claims. Loop p99 was 20.972–21.004 ms on both sides at 20 ms monitor resolution, with 1,496–1,497 samples per arm. No RPC/session-list latency claim is made. Host one-minute load ranged 3.34–18.22; all sandbox guards passed.

Four matched identical-source A/A controls also used synchronized warm starts, swapped interleaved CPUs, and alternating launch order. Main-thread CPU deltas were −28.02%, −2.26%, −2.32%, +2.51%; total CPU deltas −32.18%, +0.59%, +1.19%, +0.61%. Their absolute-mean CPU displacement was −39.45 µs main-thread / −89.06 µs total, larger than this candidate's +18.30 / +18.83 µs. CPU is inconclusive in this protocol; allocation controls stayed close (mean +0.395%, individual −0.51% to +1.74%). Control host load was 7.4–18.5; guards passed.

A separate fixed 170,000 B/sample regression threshold, chosen before seeing the simple candidate result, fails base at 180,208 B/sample (4,141 samples; exit 1) and passes candidate at 154,140 B/sample (4,156 samples; exit 0).

Real unaccelerated worker-spawned runaway proof: both revisions SIGKILL the tree after a burst immediately following a quiet five-second sample, at 5,016 ms / 5,029 ms respectively. The fixture crossed its cap after 101 ms on both sides. Unit tests separately preserve the one-second near-limit cadence.

<details>
<summary>Per-pair results and reproduction</summary>

| Pair | Samples base/candidate | B/sample base/candidate | Main CPU µs/sample base/candidate | Max GC pause ms base/candidate | Host load before → after (both arms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15,793 / 13,029 | 178398 / 147805 | 387.7 / 585.9 | 0.110 / 0.752 | 3.34 → 3.81 |
| 2 | 13,556 / 13,653 | 179413 / 146890 | 517.7 / 539.9 | 0.189 / 0.561 | 4.64 → 18.22 |
| 3 | 14,111 / 17,399 | 181499 / 146839 | 536.3 / 343.2 | 0.365 / 0.169 | 10.88 → 9.50 |
| 4 | 13,133 / 12,795 | 178813 / 147908 | 550.1 / 599.3 | 0.148 / 0.703 | 10.74 → 11.00 |
| 5 | 17,233 / 16,679 | 178437 / 146836 | 349.4 / 364.5 | 0.169 / 0.149 | 10.63 → 9.68 |

V8 allocation median/range across pairs: base 178,813 B (178,398–181,499), candidate 146,890 B (146,836–147,908). Main-thread CPU median/range: base 517.7 µs (349.4–550.1), candidate 539.9 µs (343.2–599.3). Across the five 30-second capture windows per arm: Minor GC total: 262.215 → 244.676 ms; Major GC total: 0.000 → 2.016 ms; Incremental GC total: 0.000 → 0.594 ms. Minor GC counts were 3,559 / 3,258; major and incremental counts were 0 / 3 each, so major-GC tails are context only. Every maximum pause remained below 1 ms.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/child-memory-measure.ts   --owner <revision>/src/process/child-memory.ts   --trees 1 --descendants 9 --sample-delay-ms 1 --seconds 30   --output .local/child-memory.json
# Separate negative/positive allocation regression:
# add --max-allocation-bytes-per-sample 170000
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/child-memory-adaptive-runaway.ts   --owner <revision>/src/process/child-memory.ts --output .local/runaway.json
```

Validation covers the process-memory owner and real descendant enforcement. No full Gateway stress campaign or production load was started.

</details>

prs.title: fix: long streamed HTML/JSX replies no longer re-project the whole reply at every partial tag
prs.body:
Fixes #185289
Related: #180765, #181397

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated whole-reply comparisons, searches, and copies when streamed HTML, JSX, or XML ends a chunk on a possible tool-call tag prefix.

## User Impact

Ordinary partial tags take incremental work while preserving the visible reply and existing tool-call filtering. This removes unnecessary work from the Gateway text path; a stable end-to-end Gateway latency improvement is not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter previously returned a sliced prefix for each held tag. Its caller then compared that prefix with the previous reply, and the scanner searched the accumulated source again. The filter now carries pending bytes and scans the append, resynchronizing once for replacements or earlier transformations.

The implementation is by @JasonBuildAI. The maintainer follow-up consolidates duplicate resynchronization, adds full-delivery parity coverage, and fixes an independently reviewed empty-update defect: reusing cached transformed text must preserve synchronization state. Canonical filtering policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

The complete production-chain sweep covers 318 adversarial documents at every two-chunk split and one-/four-character chunking, including empty appends at every boundary. All 44,516 schedules and 209,934 prefixes match the complete batch filter stack, including its final code-preserving trim. Both projected snapshots and replayed deltas match byte-for-byte; the merged-tree repeat passed in 16.041 seconds.

For the same 65,520-character HTML source and four-character appends, the complete production projector records:

| Operation input characters | Main `d45ff6d` | Final production `0872dd26` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefix comparisons | 165,637,836 | 514,584 |
| `<` searches | 941,100,552 | 133,810 |
| Large prefix slices | 90,791,348 | 0 |

Both runs reconstruct the canonical HTML exactly. These full-chain counters include downstream stages and therefore differ from the earlier XML-only counters. No Gateway instrumentation was added; Gateway output parity is checked separately from production-projector work counts.

Earlier validation for `18e6306336d986b16298a3135a69ac8bb0b46d0b` after merging main `a189175a` (the only manual conflict resolution preserves main's compact test fixtures):

- Merged-tree owner suites: 170 tests passed in 25.23 seconds; the prior production/test head passed the same suites in 61.93 seconds. All corpus, empty-update, replacement, and three work-bound assertions remain; total PR test change is +11 lines against the merged main. Neighbor suites also passed in the earlier four-file run (221 tests, 121.16 seconds).
- All three consolidated work bounds fail with main's XML implementation; the repaired owner passes them. The empty-update regression was also red before its fix in XML and full-delivery profiles.
- Core/shared-test types, scoped type-aware lint/format, and eight baseline ratchets passed. No ceiling increase.
- Full `pnpm build` passed on the built production/test head `ce6a392a` in 6m 13.2s (production blob `0872dd26c21224ac3acac26883831bb478469396`), including all 160 public SDK subpaths and UI budgets. The earlier production build also passed in 20m 4.7s. The XML production blob is unchanged by the mechanical main merge; the inspected visible-text behavior and live proof are reused.
- Independent Codex production review `54b40694..9442bedd`, test-consolidation review `9442bedd..ce6a392a`, and final complete branch review `a189175a..18e63063`: all scoped-clean through P2.
- Main and built production-head (`ce6a392a`) Gateways delivered the exact canonical 65,519-character HTML response through `/v1/responses`, each with one provider request and a completed response. Their raw delta grouping differed (12,552 versus 16,380 events), while concatenated bytes matched. Response phases were 46.929s and 6.627s on this shared host; these observations are not a stable latency claim.

It returned the requested HTML marker in a code fence with extra prose; this proves the real transport/text path, not exact instruction compliance. prs.title: fix(lmstudio): send binary on/off reasoning efforts to binary-thinking models
prs.body:
Closes #181888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: the native LM Studio route sends graded `reasoning_effort` values (`medium`, `xhigh`, ...) to models that only support binary on/off reasoning, so LM Studio warns and silently falls back to its own default instead of honoring the requested thinking level.

## User Impact
Selecting any thinking level on a binary-thinking LM Studio model (for example Gemma 4 12B) now delivers the intended semantics: every enabled level sends `on`, and turning thinking off sends `off`. No more "Reasoning setting 'medium' is not supported" warnings with a fallback the user never chose. Graded-native models are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Discovery normalized binary `on/off` capability metadata into the graded OpenAI-compat ladder for the catalog, but the compat effort map still carried graded target values, and the shared completions transport passes the requested graded level through for non-OpenAI providers — so the wire carried a value the endpoint rejects. Binary-capability models now keep the graded ladder for the catalog while their compat map carries on/off wire tokens, and the LM Studio stream wrapper rewrites outgoing `reasoning_effort` through that map (graded-native models stream through unpatched).

## Evidence
- `models.test.ts`: discovery of a model reporting `allowed_options: ["off","on"]` now yields the graded supported ladder plus the binary wire map (`minimal..xhigh → on`, `off/none → off`); red on base, which produced graded map values. Graded-native and off-only discovery cases unchanged.
- `stream.test.ts` (real wrapper pipeline with payload capture): thinking `medium` on a binary-map model sends `reasoning_effort: "on"` (red on base: sent `medium`), thinking `off` sends `"off"`, and a graded-native model still sends `medium` untouched.
- Suites: lmstudio stream + models + setup, 99/99 (node 24.19, direct vitest against the `extension-providers` shard config).
- Not run locally: a live LM Studio server (none available); CI covers typecheck and lint lanes.

prs.title: fix: honor LM Studio thinking modes in chat
prs.body:
Fixes #181888
Related: #182151

## What Problem This Solves

LM Studio's Chat Completions endpoint rejects literal `on/off` reasoning effort and warns before substituting its own mode for graded values on binary-thinking models.

## User Impact

Ordinary LM Studio chat uses its documented `/v1/messages` endpoint with native enabled/disabled thinking, including existing saved configurations. Requests requiring structured output keep Chat Completions, selected before sending because Messages does not enforce response schemas. Embeddings and explicit API choices other than Chat Completions/Messages retain their transport.

Saved reasoning maps remain authoritative. On the structured-output path, only the temporary request model translates binary aliases to accepted `none/high` wire values. Explicit inverted maps and adaptive intent are preserved. Enabled structured-output requests can still produce LM Studio's graded-effort warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

LM Studio's [Messages endpoint](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/anthropic-compat/messages) supports client tools and history that its native REST chat endpoint does not. The plugin reuses OpenClaw's existing Anthropic request, stream, tool-call, usage, cancellation, and replay owners. Provider `createStreamFn` selects the transport; the existing wrapper owns preload, instance selection, usage compatibility, and unsupported schema cleanup.

This retains #182987's shared reasoning policy on the Completions exception. It removes obsolete global map normalization and a redundant off-wrapper that could override an explicit user map. No core provider special case, parser, dependency, config option, or persisted-map rewrite is added.

## Evidence

Final tested head: `869d90be6426cfda4509a2829936a1bf6ba141f6`.

Real local proof used LM Studio **0.4.26+4**, `google/gemma-4-e4b`, the **4-bit MLX** build, and an isolated Gateway on macOS ARM64. A transparent local relay captured real upstream traffic; it did not generate model responses.

| Live cell | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published stable 2026.10.8: plain answer, actual tool, tool-result replay | 3 turns / 4 Completions requests | 14.84s |
| Same state on this head after supported Doctor migration | 8 turns / 10 Messages requests | 10.85s |
| Replay the actual stable-created tool session on this head | Passed; no additional tool call | 0.77s |
| Fresh discovery, preload enabled | 8 turns / 10 Messages requests; existing loaded instance reused | 22.05s |
| Saved binary map, structured output, off / enabled | Enforced JSON schema; wire `none` / `high` | 8.09s / 3.05s |
| Invalid native token limit | Real HTTP 400 surfaced as Gateway terminal error | 2.42s |

The Messages cells verified streamed answers, native thinking off/on, a real plugin tool with an authored `pattern` constraint removed on the wire, emitted parallel calls and their results, multi-turn replay, usage, cancellation after a visible delta, upstream closure, and a successful next request in the same session. A direct Completions calibration reproduced the original warning; the subsequent Messages window contained **zero** such warnings. Provider settings, default model, custom header, preload setting, saved models, and model parameters remained equal through the stable-to-head migration (Doctor: 66.64s).

- Genuine failing regressions preceded repairs: original route 7 failures plus a passing control; saved-map failure plus canonical control; payload/configured-intent 3 failures plus override control; saved binary wire mapping 4 failures; adaptive schema requests 2 failures plus 2 passing controls.
- Focused transport/auth/preload/index suite: 57/57 (450.06s); typed fixture follow-up: 18/18 (405.08s); tool-prefix stability: 13/13 (370.27s). Final Messages suite: **26/26** (36.13s). Cold compiler preparation dominates the earlier runs.
- Final changed-file type-aware lint and scoped types passed (57.78s / 60.06s). Formatting, affected size/safety/test ratchets, config docs, plugin inventory, and plugin boundaries passed.
- Final-head build passed: **3m 9.6s** active time. Independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings** on this head.
- Production **+197/-74 (net +123)**; tests **+663/-176 (net +487)**; docs **+37/-32**. Growth is transport dispatch, request translation, and safe cross-API replay; parsing and lifecycle remain shared.

Limitations: proof is macOS/MLX, not Windows/WSL/GGUF. The upgrade cell reuses published-stable state with the built candidate and Doctor; it is not an installer/update-distribution test. Backend inference-slot release is not asserted. Gemma showed formatting/arithmetic variation and once continued the canceled task; the successful recovery probe explicitly replaced that task. LM Studio accepts an unknown Messages model name as an alias, so the error proof uses an invalid token limit. Historical endpoint probes cover images; the new Gateway matrix focuses on chat/tools/replay.

The temporary model directory was removed after proof; the original symlink, unchanged settings, and service launch state were verified restored. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head with no findings and no Before merge items.

CI completed with 30 successful jobs. The [core-lint failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40589132072/job/122489956708) is inherited: five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` (31–32) and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx` (288–289, 364). Both files are byte-identical in the actual CI merge checkout and its main base `2e628e80c294d67e4fd903cbe2334fcc0aa28758`. The repository lint wrapper reproduced all five errors against those exact base blobs locally (30.38s with CI's pinned oxlint 1.88.0), with matching lint config and dependency versions. The aggregate CI gate remains red; this PR does not modify those UI files. No CI rerun or unrelated code change was made.

Thanks to @mushuiyu886, whose #182151 surfaced the transport mismatch, and @mze2 for reporting #181888. Human contributor credit is preserved in the commit history.

prs.title: fix: keep session lists usable during provider reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.list` can invoke a retained thinking-policy callback after its provider has been retired during reload, returning `UNAVAILABLE` / `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`. This targets the session-list symptom reported in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165970; it does not claim to resolve that issue's broader publication or subagent failures.

## Behavior

Prepare the current provider catalog at the existing asynchronous selection boundary, then recheck readiness across selection awaits. Reuse the existing replacement promise, loader, and cancellation owners; propagate failures without substituting an ambient provider policy. Completed facts remain available for ordinary background enrichment.

A disconnected WebSocket reader now passes its existing connection signal to that catalog wait, combined with any existing async-work signal. This ends that reader's wait without canceling provider replacement, catalog refresh, or another reader. Shared-response ownership remains unchanged.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169375 explicitly accepted temporary retained-callback rejection until refresh/retry. This PR intentionally proposes a narrow change to that tradeoff: **adopt cancellable waiting for session lists**, instead of returning the retired-provider error during a known replacement. The real session-list failure and local before/after proof motivate the proposal. Maintainer approval of that choice is requested before merge; no owner approval is claimed here.

## Evidence

[Redacted standalone base/head terminal transcript, including request cancellation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182783#issuecomment-6388992800).

The standalone capture launches the supported `pnpm dev gateway run` entrypoint in a separate process, with isolated state, authenticated WebSocket clients, and a synthetic provider plugin. A loopback HTTP fixture holds the old provider's real service shutdown after quiescence. A read-only subscription to the existing `openclaw.gateway.rpc` diagnostics channel observes server dispatch completion; core runtime code is not patched or mocked for this capture.

- Clean pre-fix base `f2fccfab05f36f400a671026d95263db790affd2`: `sessions.list` fails with the exact retired-plugin exception.
- Repaired head `3cdd3f7fa592105d3f7327a2d26b4cb4a5b4f4e6`: a disconnected reader's server request finishes while replacement is still held and another reader is still pending. After release, the surviving reader and a subsequent list use the successor's `high` thinking default and retain the created session.
- The committed real-Gateway regression deterministically observes current-catalog preparation, asserts the disconnected wait rejects with `AbortError` before release, and verifies a concurrently waiting reader survives. That cancellation assertion failed on the previous PR head with a retired-generation `Error`; it passes with the signal repair.
- **27 targeted tests passed**: real WebSocket reload/cancellation, plugin/projection catalog contracts, and shared-response behavior. Gateway regression: **13.68 s test time; 18.46 s suite wall time** with prepared runtime artifacts.
- Production core and Gateway-root test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in the cancellation repair.
- Exact-head CI passed: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40128326221), including `openclaw/ci-gate`, and the [aggregate CI/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40128860939) are green on `3cdd3f7fa592105d3f7327a2d26b4cb4a5b4f4e6`.

Reproduce the committed regression:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/gateway.sessions-list-provider-reload.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Proof Limits

The provider/model configuration is synthetic. This proves the running Gateway's reload, session-list policy, cancellation, and cleanup behavior; it does not claim external-provider inference, installed-package acceptance, or migration acceptance. Local validation is the targeted scope above, rather than a claim that every sibling suite was run locally.

prs.title: docs(security): add ATR threat detection rule mapping for OpenClaw security threats
prs.body:
## Update (April 2026)

ATR has grown significantly since this PR was first submitted:

- **108 detection rules** across 9 threat categories (v1.1.1 on npm)
- **Adopted by Cisco AI Defense** — 34 rules merged into official skill-scanner
- **Threat Cloud live** — 14,979 skill threats processed
- **Benchmarks**: 96.9% recall / 100% precision on SKILL.md, 99.7% precision on MCP
- We're also working on an ATR security scanning skill for OpenClaw (separate PR coming)

---

## Summary

- **Problem**: OpenClaw's security documentation describes threats and hardening measures, but lacks mappings to executable detection rules that practitioners can deploy immediately
- **Solution**: Adds a comprehensive mapping of [ATR (Agent Threat Rules)](https://github.com/Agent-Threat-Rule/agent-threat-rules) — 71 open-source detection rules — to 9 OpenClaw threat categories documented in the security docs
- **Scope**: Documentation only — one new file in `docs/gateway/security/`, no code changes
- **Value**: Gives OpenClaw operators a path from "understand the threat" to "detect it in production" using free, open-source rules

## Change Classification

- [x] Documentation

## Scope Mapping

- [x] Security

## What This Mapping Covers

| OpenClaw Threat Category | ATR Rules | Coverage |
|--------------------------|-----------|----------|
| Prompt Injection & Goal Hijacking | 18 rules | STRONG |
| Tool Interaction Manipulation | 9 rules | STRONG |
| Credential & Secret Exposure | 8 rules | STRONG |
| Skill Supply Chain Attacks | 13 rules | STRONG |
| Cross-Agent & Multi-Agent Exploitation | 6 rules | STRONG |
| Privilege Escalation & Authorization Bypass | 6 rules | STRONG |
| Resource Exhaustion & Runaway Loops | 4 rules | MODERATE |
| Data Exfiltration & Privacy Leakage | 5 rules | MODERATE |
| Session & Memory Manipulation | 4 rules | MODERATE |

Each rule includes: rule ID, title, severity level, and specific relevance to OpenClaw's architecture (e.g., how it applies to DM access model, shared Slack agents, tool delegation).

## Why ATR

- 71 open-source detection rules (MIT licensed), YAML-based, engine-agnostic
- 61.4% recall / 99.6% precision on [PINT benchmark](https://github.com/lakeraai/pint-benchmark) (850 adversarial samples)
- OWASP Agentic AI Top 10: full 10/10 coverage ([mapping merged](https://github.com/precize/Agentic-AI-Top10-Vulnerability/pull/14))
- Scanned 36,394 ClawHub skills in production — found 182 CRITICAL, 1,124 HIGH severity threats
- Complements VirusTotal (which doesn't detect prompt injection) and `openclaw security audit` (which doesn't scan skill content)

## Root Cause Analysis

N/A — documentation addition, not a bug fix.

## Regression Testing

N/A — documentation only, no code changes.

## Security Checklist

- [x] No new permissions required
- [x] No secrets handling
- [x] No network calls
- [x] No command execution
- [x] No data access changes
- [x] Documentation only — zero runtime impact

## Human Verification

- [x] Verified all 71 ATR rule IDs match the published rule set at [agent-threat-rules v0.4.0](https://github.com/Agent-Threat-Rule/agent-threat-rules)
- [x] Verified mapping categories align with OpenClaw's security documentation at `docs/gateway/security/index.md`
- [x] Verified all referenced CVEs and threat descriptions match OpenClaw's documented threat model
- [x] Cross-referenced with [OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 mapping](https://github.com/precize/Agentic-AI-Top10-Vulnerability/blob/main/ATR-DETECTION-MAPPING.md) (merged PR #14)

## Evidence

- ATR PINT benchmark results: [pint-eval-report.json](https://github.com/Agent-Threat-Rule/agent-threat-rules/tree/main/data/pint-benchmark)
- OWASP mapping PR (merged): https://github.com/precize/Agentic-AI-Top10-Vulnerability/pull/14
- ClawHub ecosystem scan data: 36,394 skills scanned, 182 CRITICAL findings
- Academic paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19178002

prs.title: fix: keep session lists usable during provider reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session lists failing while a provider plugin is being replaced.

Related: #165970.

Includes the original contribution from #182783; this branch carries the reviewed update because the fork could not accept a maintainer push. Contributor commits and authorship are preserved.

## User Impact

Session lists wait for the replacement provider policy and then return current results. Disconnecting one reader cancels its wait without cancelling other readers or the reload. Retired plugin callbacks remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection retained completed catalog facts during replacement, but session-list defaults could still call a retired provider's thinking policy. The existing catalog owner now gates those reads on replacement and refresh, with request and projection cancellation. Background metadata reads retain their existing behavior.

Original contribution by @ceckert (Chris Eckert <christopher.k.eckert@gmail.com>), preserved in the branch history.

## Evidence

- Baseline: all three focused session-list replacement cases fail; the publication case returns `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`, and cancelled/disposed readers settle before the replacement. With this fix, all three pass.
- Focused session-list, catalog lifecycle, and shared-read suites: 25 tests passed, including a repeat after integrating current main (`9d27ef2e5ca3`). The shared-read coverage preserves independent reader cancellation and authority checks.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, core and Gateway test typechecks, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex P0–P2 review, repeated on the integrated candidate, found no actionable issues.
- Production +60/-9 (net +51), tests +491, docs +2. Submitted-head production was +52; removing duplicate disposal state and an unused static-catalog check keeps the cancellable wait with one lifecycle owner. The remaining growth implements cancellable observation of the existing replacement and refresh owners.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40580684599 (completed; inherited lint failure only).

The isolated real-Gateway test timed out during startup on the local host before exercising the reload. No external provider or channel round-trip was run.

Co-authored-by: Chris Eckert <christopher.k.eckert@gmail.com>

CI note: run [40580684599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40580684599) has an inherited `check-lint-core-2` failure: five `eslint(curly)` errors in `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-body.browser.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx`. All five diagnostics exactly match scheduled main run [40578163761, check-lint-core-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40578163761/job/122450734896); both files are byte-identical at the PR and main heads. The classifier initially calls this new because it compares stripe names; the same work is packed into different stripes. No unrelated UI edits or CI rerun were made.

prs.title: fix(database): split punctuation-joined tokens in PostgreSQL keyword search like SQLite FTS5
prs.body:
Closes #183439

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing PostgreSQL memory and transcript matches when a query word appears inside a date, path, filename, or slash-separated pair such as `2026-08-18`, `/v1/models`, `server.py`, or `input/output`.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL keyword search finds the words SQLite FTS5 already finds. Long transcript snippets show the matching passage and retain its punctuation. Ranking policy and canonical memory/transcript content are unchanged; Unicode normalization and engine-local scores can still differ.

Agent schema 38 reparses existing PostgreSQL text indexes once, including persisted memory search extensions. SQLite advances schema metadata only. Operators should retain the matching pre-upgrade backup for rollback; the first PostgreSQL migration includes a one-time index backfill.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared PostgreSQL search owner applies the same punctuation split to indexed text and query terms. A trigger maintains the stored vector because PostgreSQL 16 cannot replace a generated expression in place, and dropping/re-adding the column would break the sealed catalog's column positions. The migration preserves those positions and GIN indexes, while historical definitions remain available for old-store backup and restore. Snippets locate the passage in position-preserving normalized text and return the corresponding original text.

Integrated main at `dc960f50ad6e`; main still uses agent schema 37, so this migration remains 38. Production delta is +204/-24 lines (net +180) for version propagation, the migration, and historical backup/port compatibility. Shared test-fixture cleanup keeps the test/support delta to +460/-453 (net +7), without raising the test-line ceiling. Docs are +37/-7; metadata/tooling +2/-1.

Thanks to @lonexreb for the implementation and @etzelm for the report and [independent real-index validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183547#issuecomment-6405295918). Contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

Current integration proof used a disposable local PostgreSQL 17/pgvector container, synthetic data, and the production store/search owners. No operator state or database was used.

- **Current-base red → integrated-head green:** the punctuation regression failed on `364c0d4ebcd4` at `08 18: expected [] to deeply equal [{id: 'deploy'}]` (8.68s Vitest, 70.49s total). On the integrated head, 21/21 tests in five files passed (45.07s Vitest, 108.04s total): the same regression, populated 37→38 migration and reopen, schema-35 memory-path upgrade through current, historical backup descriptors, and the real session-search owner returning the late punctuation-preserving snippet.
- **Current checks:** targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, canonical PostgreSQL generator verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings on the complete integrated diff.

The following broader CLI, Gateway, stable-upgrade and hybrid proof was previously recorded on the unchanged implementation before this main integration; it was not rerun during this pass:

- **Red before the fix:** built main CLI found `server` on SQLite, then returned no results after a real `database port --family agent --to postgres`. The regression also failed on exact initial CI base `7c4bc0162dc` at `08 18: expected [] to deeply equal [{id:'deploy'}]` (34.80s Vitest; 252.11s including cold setup).
- **Existing-store repair:** Doctor upgraded PostgreSQL 37→38 in 123.31s. Before any search/rebuild, stored vectors already contained separate `08`, `18`, `server`, `py`, `models`, `input`, and `output` tokens. All four search-column positions were preserved. Six independent CLI searches (`08 18`, `server`, `models`, `input output`, `server.py`, `Release`) passed in 130.70s; reopen retained the schema version and catalog seal.
- **Snippet and restoration:** the shipped Gateway `sessions.search` returned the late `fix to server.py landed` passage with punctuation (13.62s). A verified schema-37 archive restored in 7.52s, upgraded in 43.44s, and passed search plus an independent reopen with an unchanged admitted extension set and seal.
- **Published-stable upgrade and current port:** the real npm `2026.10.8` SQLite seed upgraded agent 25→38/state 20→35 in 49.77s. Both integrity checks passed, both memory chunks remained, and two opens retained identical schema metadata and recovery-file inventories. Stable predates PostgreSQL port support; the upgraded store then passed the current CLI port to PostgreSQL (19.26s) and keyword search.
- **Live hybrid control:** Ollama `nomic-embed-text` rebuilt 768-dimensional vectors and returned `server.py` with text score 0.97348 and vector score 0.63478. Final rebuild/query took 44.74s/73.52s, with the same model digest before, between, and after. An earlier attempt encountered a shared Ollama outage (connection reset/refused and transient provider-identity mismatch); no service restart, model unload, suppression, or metadata edit was used.
- **Checks:** final-head full build passed (455.93s); core and focused test types, targeted lint, formatting, Kysely guardrails, PostgreSQL generator verification, and applicable baseline ratchets passed. Independent Codex branch review is clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Tests:** 14 PostgreSQL files cover 114 tests. Initially 112 passed; two unchanged `DROP DATABASE` cleanup statements timed out during a 243s container checkpoint. Only those cases were replayed after checkpoint completion, with unchanged limits: 2/2 passed (5.62s test file, 104.13s with setup). The nine-file unit/tooling batch passed 240/240 in 570.02s. The original PostgreSQL batch took 1300.47s, including the 20-case historical rollback matrix (497.27s).

Initial [CI run 40448958449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40448958449) was investigated against its exact base. Four failures have independent main repairs now included: QA ACK #185840, Google Chat authority #185972, Copilot ordering #185612, and iMessage lookup #185409. The Feishu lifecycle failure did not reproduce on the exact base (8/8); its unchanged shared-state/KV path does not use this agent PostgreSQL search migration. This is an intermittent/unresolved initial failure, not a claimed fix. Final exact-head CI is recorded below.

Limitations: this integration used PostgreSQL 17; the earlier CLI proof used 17.11; PostgreSQL 16 compatibility is supported by the `DROP EXPRESSION` contract and the contributor's earlier PG16 run, rather than a fresh PG16 run here. The published stable's indexing command needed bounded cleanup interruption while seeding; cold integrity checks passed before upgrade.

Fresh CLI/Gateway/live-model proof was not repeated for this integration: the production-boundary PostgreSQL regression, upgrade, reopen and snippet tests were rerun, while the broader prior-head evidence above is retained explicitly.

An earlier integrated-head CI run, [40589855961](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40589855961), exposed eight inherited memory fixture failures in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-24` / `-27`. All eight reproduced on unchanged main `25c300f73654`. Upstream repair `b954f6cef456` makes embedding-failure fixtures change their input instead of expecting unchanged chunks to be embedded again; it is included by the final main integration. The PostgreSQL production owners and migration are unchanged from the earlier successful database proof. Fresh independent P0–P2 review after this integration is clean.

After the final main integration, all 16 tests across the three affected memory suites passed (163.09s total). The eight previously failing cases are green. The earlier 21-test real-PostgreSQL proof remains applicable because the integration does not change those production owners.

Final exact-head validation: [CI run 40593236753](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593236753) passed on `26a81af6cb1dcfab3875a5df36ec45795080e08d`: 159 jobs passed, 24 skipped, no failures or cancellations. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards, all three repaired memory-test bundles, and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. [ClawSweeper's review of the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183547#issuecomment-6397098386) is complete with no findings or Before merge items.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer optional transcript renderers at chat boot
prs.body:
> **Current-head proof pending; auto-merge is not armed.** Current head `d66b560771a85f71299a05aad885ceffad1215b9` integrates main `c2243320434e1c1ae99105f4b070e1a3a4d24479`. Integrated Activity 35/35, forwarded-attribution 23/23, admission 5/5 and UI typecheck pass. Production Knip/build and fresh performance proof are in progress. The earlier RTT layout result remains held; the repair is not causal exoneration. Fresh paired coverage/readiness/CPU proof will replace the historical measurements below before merge. All older measurements below belong only to their named prior heads and must not be attributed to the current head.

## What Problem This Solves

Cold Chat evaluates renderer implementations for transcript row kinds that are absent from the first screen.

## User Impact

Chat preserves its existing appearance, row identity, and scroll position while downloading less code and evaluating fewer optional renderers at boot. Failed renderer loads offer a visible retry. This is an incremental reduction; it does not meet the lane’s approximately 950 KB unused-raw target.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit a row batch only when its required renderers are available, retaining accepted rows and geometry while loading. Prepare cached transcript renderers before publication. Common renderer chunks preload with the route so downloads stay parallel; uncommon question, conflict, realtime, and forwarded/session-activity presentations load on demand. The message/frame/stream path stays eager. Host tags, row keys, CSS classes, and the sanitizer boundary are unchanged.

Performance status: **pending / needs work; do not merge**. The fixed 30-triplet RTT result retains a layout CPU p95 increase of **12.71% versus base and 16.95% versus A/A**. No further extension is planned.

## Evidence

Base `161c376d51b886186e1a6527775350d4a07f86ab`; measured head `48977be7fda5587d3816b3d5883e9555467b79db`. Same machine, isolated Chromium, production bundles, and one frozen canonical cold-load harness (source b6253b3, separately pinned from both UI builds). Synthetic 240-message desktop Chat (390-session roster, 1719×1179 viewport). Localhost and 100 ms RTT / 10,000 kbps measured separately. Coverage diagnostics, untraced timing, and traced compiler diagnostics are separate cohorts. No samples excluded.

Acceptance: fewer unused raw bytes, no extra Chat request, and readiness median within 5% with no worse p95 (20 localhost and 30 RTT counterbalanced base/base/head triplets, with one fresh browser process per sample). A/A and renderer CPU measurements qualify wall-time noise on the loaded shared host. Sub-1% p95 movement is noise unless repeated pairs confirm it.

This final integration comparison uses new builds of the exact main baseline and integrated head. Canonical build/copy and metadata preparation made all eight plugin declarations and 21 packaged UI assets identical. The frozen b625 harness and synthetic fixture are shared by both variants, separately pinned from their UI source revisions. Each timing and coverage sample starts a fresh browser process; roles are counterbalanced within each timing triplet. The earlier reused-renderer cohort and its CPU-tail regression remain retained separately. Opening/closing censuses verify the bundles, generated plugin inputs, frozen harness, external dependencies and Chromium.

The canonical workload is `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts`, compiled once from the separately pinned b625 source using the repository tsdown configuration, then shared unchanged by both bundles. The runner invokes one fresh output directory per sample:

```sh
node <frozen>/bench-cold-load.js --bundle-dir <base-or-head>/dist/control-ui \
  --gateway-http --first-load --cold-http-cache --face chat --boot-route chat \
  --viewport desktop --fixture-now-ms 1800000000000 --capture-ms 0 \
  --thread-cpu-time --runs 1 --untraced --network-latency-ms 0 --download-kbps 0 \
  --output <fresh-output>
```

For RTT, use `--network-latency-ms 100 --download-kbps 10000`. Coverage adds `--coverage`; the eight separate compiler diagnostics omit `--untraced`. Timing initially rotates base/control/head, head/base/control, control/head/base over 20 triplets per profile; the preregistered RTT-only extension continues the same rotation for ten more triplets, retaining all 30 RTT triplets. Control is an independent fresh-process run of the exact base bundle. Both `pnpm ui:build` and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --json` ran on each source; the head strict check additionally used `--base-dist <base>/dist/control-ui`.

| Asset measure | Base | Head |
|---|---:|---:|

| Startup gzip JS | 90,069 | 90,073 |
| Startup Brotli JS | 81,703 | 81,764 |
| Startup JS requests | 3 | 3 |

| New Session JS requests | 15 | 15 |
| New Session CSS requests | 3 | 3 |

The strict checker passes on both bundles. No UI asset budget changed. Startup is unchanged in raw bytes (+4 B gzip; +61 B Brotli), and Chat CSS is unchanged in raw bytes (+60 B gzip; +5 B Brotli). New Session grows by 6 raw B, 337 gzip B and 433 Brotli B. It remains below its 797,395 B gzip cap, but this is disclosed growth, not a New Session win.

### New Session compressed-byte attribution

Both strict checks pass with zero violations. Base New Session is 769,200 B gzip and head is 769,537 B; the current cap is 797,395 B (28,195 B base headroom; 27,858 B head headroom). Base is below its cap, so the already-over-budget 64 B exception does not apply. No cap or baseline changed. This is disclosed compressed growth, not a New Session win.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| app-sidebar-online.js | +0 | +4 | +13 |

Every changed chunk has identical source-map module membership and source-content hashes before/after. The emitted import references/minified chunk glue changed; the largest compressed change is the shared boot chunk (+307 B gzip with identical raw length). These are deterministic differences in the two emitted artifacts, not a claim that another build would remove them. Detailed filenames, hashes and per-chunk source comparisons are in `new-session-attribution.json`.

| Coverage / HTTP measure | Local base | Local head | RTT base | RTT head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

V8 execution coverage is not a network ledger or complete compilation measurement. HTTP counts include inert preloads. Unused raw reduction is 21,954 B locally and 22,649 B with RTT; avoided HTTP transfer is 8,640 raw B. This incremental step remains far below the lane’s approximately 950 KB unused-raw target; deltas across moving bases are not added together.

The HTTP encoded increase is in compressed response bodies, not header accounting. All 62 script requests reconcile to emitted Brotli sidecars or identity bodies. Brotli bodies total 1,203,708 → 1,203,862 B (+154); identity bodies remain 43,125 B. Resource Timing header accounting remains 18,600 B. Raw HTTP scripts decrease by 8,640 B. prs.title: perf(ui): load session and account copy with its consumers
prs.body:
> **Current-head proof pending; auto-merge is not armed.** Current head `2d988d90d0c775eba1d607ea05e32ee98dbd48f4` integrates main `c2243320434e1c1ae99105f4b070e1a3a4d24479`. Current strict comparison: startup 281,415 → 280,862 raw B / 90,333 → 90,230 gzip B; Chat 4,017,365 → 4,009,720 raw B / 1,255,017 → 1,252,459 gzip B. Request counts unchanged. Production Knip and UI typecheck pass. Fresh paired coverage/readiness/CPU proof will replace the historical measurements below before merge. All older measurements below belong only to their named prior heads and must not be attributed to the current head.

## What Problem This Solves

Cold Chat loads the full English session-management and account-settings catalogs when its resident controls need only a small set of labels.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Chat downloads 19,336 fewer raw JavaScript bytes (5,109 fewer encoded bytes) in the measured cold load, with the same 62 JavaScript requests. Translation text, active locale, and existing UI behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The personal-session list and Chat account control now register small catalogs containing their required labels. Full session-management and account-settings copy remains with the existing lazy consumers. The full catalogs reuse the same string definitions in their existing property order, and registration still updates the existing namespace objects in place.

The slim catalogs stay in the measured shared boot chunk; the full catalogs have separate deferred chunks. This avoids adding a request to first-screen rendering. No new loader, state owner, dependency, or feature boundary is introduced.

prs.title: fix(codex): saved user turn is reported as a failed write when prompt annotation is refused
prs.body:
Closes #179892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved user turn is reported as a failed write, and its persisted-message notification is skipped, when Codex native prompt annotation is refused.

## User Impact

User impact: a refused prompt annotation no longer raises a false persistence error for a turn that was saved, and persistence listeners are still told the admitted turn was persisted. A refused annotation with no host admission still writes nothing, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Annotation only adds provenance to an admission that is already durable. The fix catches and logs annotation failures inside the mirror promise instead of letting them reject the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. Keeping the catch inside that promise preserves the existing ordering: persistence waiters still wait for annotation to settle. When annotation fails and there is no host admission, the function returns as it did before rather than falling back to the generic mirror writer.

## Evidence

- New admission test where `annotateCurrentUserTurn` rejects: no `onPersistenceError`, exactly one persisted-message notification, the admitted message unchanged, and no extra transcript writes. It fails on `main` without this change (`onPersistenceError` is called).
- The existing `transcript-mirror*.test.ts` suites pass (44 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.



## Real behavior proof (production Gateway, before and after)

These are redacted logs from a production Gateway running 2026.10.5 (source build). This change was deployed there on 2026-10-21. Run and session IDs are replaced with labels; timestamps are UTC.

**Before the fix (2026-10-20).** Annotation was refused at turn start. When the run settled, the Gateway reported a failed user-turn write:

```
18:00:08.001 [agent/embedded] failed to mirror codex app-server prompt at turn start error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-A> sessionId=<session-A>
18:03:46.522 [gateway] agent user transcript persistence failed: Error: native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence
```

The user turn had been saved anyway. In the agent's session database, `<session-A>` holds the admitted user message at seq 1 (created 18:00:05). The session's last event is at 18:03:46, the same moment the false error was logged.

**After the fix (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-22).** The same refusal happened on five Codex turns. Each one logged only the new warning, with no persistence error:

```
2026-10-21 19:51:25.581 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-B> sessionId=<session-B>
2026-10-22 02:35:56.558 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-C> sessionId=<session-C>
2026-10-22 13:25:39.513 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-D> sessionId=<session-D>
2026-10-22 13:27:28.648 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-E> sessionId=<session-E>
2026-10-22 13:30:47.032 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-F> sessionId=<session-F>
```

From 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-27, the Gateway journal has 1 `agent user transcript persistence failed` line. It is the pre-fix one above. In each of the five post-fix sessions, seq 1 is the saved `role: "user"` message, with no provenance annotation written.

**A caveat about current `main`.** The refusal seen in production, "would restore redacted evidence", was removed from `main` in #169063. The bug itself is still there. In `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts` (`main` at 1b1c96578f6), `annotateCurrentUserTurn` is still awaited without a catch inside the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. The annotation binder still throws on its remaining guards: "cannot replace an edited admission", "conflicts with recorded provenance", "does not match admitted content" and "no longer available for native annotation". Any of these produces the same false persistence error and skipped notification. I haven't observed those remaining refusals in production.

I re-ran the added admission test against `main` at 2868c5448f7 today. Without this change, it fails at `expect(onPersistenceError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. With this change applied, the file passes (5/5).

prs.title: improve: verify plugin reload across independent projects
prs.body:
Related: #182024. Follow-up coverage for #185315 and #185544; the remaining overlap design is tracked in #184243.

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin reload coverage needs to show what happens to an independent running project and to new work submitted while reload is in progress.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The tests distinguish admission during an ongoing turn from full isolation: a long unrelated tool call still delays reload and new work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing Gateway handover fixture with two agents using separate workspaces. The running agent only calls an unchanged plugin; reload replaces another plugin, and the second agent requests that replacement after public status reports `reloading`.

Three cases cover the serialized control, opted-in handover, and handover during a six-second unrelated tool call. For handover, the fixture holds the original turn's final model response until the new turn reaches the model server, proving concurrent admission without racing final deliveries. Assertions check seven actual tool effects with distinct call IDs, one final reply per turn, expected end hooks, the unchanged plugin's original generation, and the replacement's new generation. The five upstream cases, including bundled Knowledge from #186267, mixed opt-in and context-engine disposal/commit checks, remain. Bundled Knowledge keeps its upstream observations; synthetic effect-log and generation assertions remain required for every synthetic-plugin case. Plugin allow lists and authenticated Gateway requests remain in use; production authority and lifecycle code are untouched.

## Evidence

- **Current integration head `7d15266c4d55127cb5d36d966768b7fbdb2d6109`:** merged pinned main `709b1a1ca3fe8179409004502b0491b853580d5e` to reconcile the shared test-line ceiling after its CI failure. The handover test file is byte-identical to the previous integration (Git blob `32890236fbc32269c6571d4c5de11920e896935d`). Because main also changed agent execution and plugin loading, the complete **8/8** scenario file was rerun on the committed tree and passed in **254.69 s**. The canonical test-line ratchet fails before the scalar correction and passes afterward at **6,290,097 lines / 6,290,097 ceiling, zero slack**; `git diff --check` passes. Hosted CI is checked separately after push.
- **Test-line allowance:** this PR adds **199 net test lines** for the three distinct cross-project scenarios and exact-effect/reply/generation checks. The integrated main already exceeds its recorded 6,288,829 ceiling by **1,069 lines**, so the exact measured increase is **1,268**. The shared fixture is retained; no assertions or scenarios are removed, and no ratchet is disabled. [Original failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40597845718/job/122518714359) used an earlier synthetic merge and reported 881 over (682 inherited + 199 from this PR); that one failure accounts for the three red statuses. No blind workflow rerun.
- **Previous integration `56315b453038a2cbd8cf8e98311589c5dd27fdd4`:** resolved the shared-fixture conflict with #186267 on main `d7acde6ae97e3e95c3ce4b07fb86cd6eb92db7fb`. All **8/8** passed in **452.00 s**, as did changed-file formatting, source-backed root-test lint, the E2E TypeScript project and `git diff --check`. Local Codex autoreview was `scoped-clean` at its **P0-only** scope. Those static/review results remain evidence for that earlier tree, not a new-head human approval.
- **Historical separate CLI execution on `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f`:** two disposable Linux Gateway runs use `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`, the public SDK client and distinct workspaces. Both recorded seven unique effects, one final reply per project, four end hooks and the expected plugin generations. The long call still delays reload. [Captured output, timing, cleanup and exact reproduction source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185793#issuecomment-6443348584).
- Red/green control: disabling only the fixture's handover declaration caused the new-admission gate to fail: no new model request arrived while the original turn stayed active. Restoring the declaration made the test pass. This validates the test against the existing feature; it is not a new runtime fix.
- On the pre-integration head `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f`, the complete file passed **7/7**, followed by **10/10** focused runs for five serial A/B pairs on identical test bytes.
- The long-call case observed reload completion after **6.45 s** and a new-work wait of **6.24 s**. The held call completed **6.06 s** after the reload request; both reload completion and admission followed it. All seven effects and both replies completed without duplication.
- Historical validation on that same pre-integration head: changed-file formatting/lint, the E2E TypeScript project, and `git diff --check` passed. [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40488465663) passed on `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f`; the CI gate and security checks are successful.
- An earlier campaign passed 9/10 and exposed a fixture assumption about final-reply order. The final fixture synchronizes on admission instead; the failed campaign is excluded from the table below, and the complete five-pair series was repeated after that correction.

<details>
<summary>Measurements and reproduction</summary>

Historical measurements from `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f`, before integrating main. Base: `863839d032939ec1ef582ce3b991df77e35e7aaf`. Same production source and six-step tool workload in both arms, with handover disabled (A) or enabled (B). macOS, Node 26.12.1, 10 logical CPUs, 16 GiB RAM; cached compiler outputs and a fresh process/Gateway for every sample. Results are median (minimum–maximum), seconds unless marked otherwise.

| Observation | A: serialized | B: handover |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Reload completion | 7.13 (6.85–8.00) | 3.64 (1.79–9.52) |
| New-work wait until its first model request | 7.60 (6.14–11.29) | 3.14 (1.78–10.01) |
| Complete workload including reply/end-hook checks | 20.72 (18.84–33.14) | 16.17 (15.40–42.87) |
| Test-process user + system CPU during workload | 14.03 (13.70–20.15) | 13.29 (12.28–24.66) |
| RSS before workload, MiB | 1505.15 (1494.51–1555.12) | 1497.43 (1477.48–1527.61) |
| RSS after workload, MiB | 1974.64 (1947.53–2002.67) | 1965.42 (1928.32–1992.67) |
| OS-reported process peak RSS, MiB | 1020.06 (751.69–1132.75) | 954.06 (778.80–1085.05) |

The host had substantial unrelated background load, and A always preceded B. These are descriptive local observations, not an isolated performance benchmark or a CPU/memory improvement claim. Process CPU excludes child processes; RSS snapshots and the OS-native peak counter are separate measurements, and the peak includes startup. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is simply the maximum, not a stable tail estimate. Every measured case produced seven effects, two final replies and four end-hook effects. New work started while the original turn was active in all five handover samples and none of the five controls. One handover sample waited longer than its paired control; the median is not a general speedup guarantee.

```sh
OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-plugin-turn-handover.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For paired samples, run the same command five times per arm in fresh processes, alternating `-t ': unrelated project without handover$'` and `-t ': unrelated project$'`. Set `OPENCLAW_E2E_PROOF_OUT` to a separate file for each invocation to retain its JSON proof. The six-second case is separate from these paired short-call samples.

This adds coverage for successful handover and its current tool-call boundary. It does not qualify generation overlap, cancellation, credential revocation, repeated/failed reloads, or all production plugins. Those broader safety and ownership requirements remain part of the existing upstream work.

</details>

### Separate Gateway execution

The separate entry-point proof on pre-integration head `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f`, requested in [review revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185793#issuecomment-6439897681) was completed before the main integration. It has not been rerun on the combined base; current integration proof is the eight-case source test above. [Full captured results and exact standalone scripts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185793#issuecomment-6443348584) run the pinned source build through the normal CLI in a separate Gateway process, with public SDK requests and a local synthetic model HTTP server. No Gateway test-helper imports are used.

Environment: disposable Hetzner CX33, Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB nominal RAM, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0. One `qaRuntime` build of `d64c011329c9da43ad9d57952a70fde01808f77f` passed in 6:07.16 with GNU time maximum RSS 4,390.82 MiB. The CLI printed `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (d64c011)`; the full SHA identifies the tested candidate source.

| Observation | Short tools | Six-second unrelated call |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Effects / unique call IDs | 7 / 7 | 7 / 7 |
| Final replies, original / new project | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| End hooks | 4 | 4 |
| Unchanged / replacement plugin generation | 1 / 2 | 1 / 2 |
| Reload completion | 4.813 s | 6.922 s |
| New-work wait until first model request | 4.385 s | 5.985 s |
| New work admitted before original final | yes | yes |

The long call finished 6.238 seconds after the reload request; reload and new-project admission both followed it. The original final model response is held until new-project admission, so this proves admission while the original turn remains active, without assuming final-reply order. These are single-sample execution observations, separate from the paired measurements above.

Normal token/device authentication, loopback binding, explicit plugin allowlists, public local-install capability/trust consent and configuration validation remained in use. The provider was synthetic; live provider integration, production installation, failed/repeated reloads, cancellation and credential revocation are not qualified by these runs. There is still no full generation-overlap claim.

The workload and Crabbox client both exited 0. The one VM lease was released; independent exact GETs for its server, SSH key and primary IP returned 404 and exhausted resource lists were empty. Total supervised launch through absence verification was 842.869 seconds. No production files or services were changed.

Closes #183371

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem:** The Chat guide explains mobile Return and Side chat input, but leaves desktop users to infer the main composer's send/newline shortcuts and IME confirmation behavior.

## User Impact

Windows, macOS, and Linux users can find the Send shortcut setting and distinguish confirming composed text from submitting a message. This documents existing behavior; it does not change runtime behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause:** The guide has a Mobile message input section but no equivalent main-composer desktop section.

**Fix:** Add a short shortcut table and a Chinese Pinyin example, and link the existing queue/steer explanation rather than duplicate it. The change is limited to 22 documentation lines; no production code, dependencies, or tests are added.

## Evidence

**Reproduction:** At base `6a628215b3607629cbc68885d7e307259eff6a5a`, read Mobile message input, Side chat, and Stop and abort, then look for the main desktop composer's send/newline and IME instructions.

**Expected / Actual:** A desktop reader should find that guidance together; previously it was absent or had to be inferred from other surfaces. The new section supplies it next to the mobile instructions.

**Verification:**
- Cross-checked `chat-composer-keydown.ts`, `ime.ts`, the appearance preference owner, and the existing mobile/follow-up documentation.
- `oxfmt@0.73.0 --check docs/web/control-ui/chat.md`: passed.
- Repository Markdown lint configuration: 32 available Markdown files checked, zero findings.

- Synthetic calls to the existing IME helper cover active composition, keyCode 229, post-composition Enter, and deliberate Enter after clearing the guard. This is helper-level evidence only.

**Limitations:** Documentation-only validation on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with Node 26.8.2. No native Chinese/Japanese/Korean IME, Windows browser, live Gateway, full UI test suite, or deployed documentation preview was exercised. No new runtime defect or end-to-end fix is claimed. Checks used standalone tools with the repository configuration because this sparse checkout has no full workspace dependency installation.

AI-assisted investigation, drafting, and checks. I take responsibility for the submitted evidence and its stated limitations. This is a small Control UI Focus Week documentation contribution relevant to desktop keyboard use in the upcoming Windows/Mac week.

Review tooling limitation: the required autoreview was attempted with Codex, but API/model connectivity errors ended in a 180-second timeout. The permitted Claude fallback was not logged in. Neither attempt produced a completed review verdict; they are not counted as passing checks.

A separate read-only source review of the final 22-line diff found no actionable issues in the shortcut, IME, follow-up, or mobile scope statements. That review did not execute browser tests and is reported separately from the unavailable CLI autoreview.


### Current-main maintainer verification

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183380#issuecomment-6456053681 documents a claim-by-claim audit at main `eec15d7c6db55c618405c6d42205f4d6dfa57352`, six passing production-built Chromium application-flow cases, and exact-head docs checks. Composition events were synthetic; physical IMEs remain unverified. The repository-wide anchor audit has six identical unrelated failures on the actual parent and candidate; the new link resolves. No source or documentation repair was needed.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: this adds guidance only; reverting fully removes it without state, schema, or runtime changes. Blast radius is readers of the desktop Chat guide if keyboard guidance is misunderstood.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve Daybreak toggle activation during streamed updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Daybreak switch occasionally ignoring a click while streamed session snapshots refresh otherwise unchanged access preferences.

## User Impact

Turning Daybreak off sends the Standard preference, and turning it on selects the available remembered/default program. Native device settings continue to reconcile with their owner's returned snapshots.

## Why This Change Was Made

An unchanged access snapshot could dirty the shared switch's grouped input bindings between native checkbox activation and its change event. That restored the old checked value before the callback read it. Memoize the Daybreak enabled/disabled projections at the access-control boundary so equal streamed values do not rerun those bindings. The shared switch and native settings contracts remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Scheduled main run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40569017511. Failing case: `ui/src/e2e/chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` — `Daybreak through a real built Gateway > persists visible selections and refreshes queued requests on desktop`.

The new native-click regression fails on the base by requesting Daybreak again instead of Standard during an unchanged snapshot refresh, and passes with the fix. All 43 focused model-controls, shared-settings, and native-device tests pass. The native-device cases caught regressions in the initial shared-control approach; the final change is confined to Daybreak's projection and restores those contracts without editing their tests. The final diff adds two primitive memos and folds the regression into existing model-controls coverage. Consolidating fixture duplication preserves every original assertion and reduces total test lines by three. No sleeps, timeout changes, baseline changes, or assertion weakening are included.

The original built-Gateway scenario remains unverified locally: it was absent from the first PR CI selection, and a Testbox allocation queued without running a payload and was cancelled. No live-proof success is claimed.

Default chat-test tsrs, typed UI lint, formatting, size ratchets, and the Control UI controller guard pass. Independent P0–P2 review is clean. A separate local browser attempt failed during production-build setup before tests ran; it provides no behavioral verdict. No dependency, lint-baseline, or timeout changes were made.

The prior PR CI revision passed all UI and typecheck jobs but exceeded the repository-wide test-line ceiling: main was already 251 lines over, and the separate regression added 43. The final version adds no net test lines and preserves the regression at the full model-controls boundary.
