prs.title: fix(gateway): explain Tailscale ingress loss in recovery logs
prs.body:
Related: #183482

## What Problem This Solves

Operators lose the cause of a managed Tailscale route claim ending after readiness: the Gateway logs recovery without the worker or CLI exit details.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish a CLI failure from an abruptly terminated route-owner worker using exit codes, signals, lifetime, and captured-output byte counts. Raw CLI stdout/stderr are excluded from this diagnostic record.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve typed exit facts through the existing claim promise and append them to the existing recovery warning. Worker termination and the optional final CLI report remain separate, so a missing CLI report is not guessed from the worker status.

Current upstream already reclaims managed Serve/Funnel routes with backoff. This patch preserves that behavior, ownership checks, and cleanup; it does not implement configurable reconnection policy requested in #183482. No configuration migration or user action is required.


## Evidence

Current candidate: `00165ba1a489337ff51046a389daad8c8842a466`, merging main `32276e16fb7807083d4452f2a9ec50084f6c95ae` into the original PR. The one test conflict preserves main’s intentional consolidation; both production files and both new diagnostic regressions remain byte-identical to the reviewed PR. Independent review found no actionable integration defect.

- Native `qaRuntime` build passed on Linux arm64 with Node 24.22.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0 dependencies.
- Three affected files passed **76 tests** through the repository runner. Main’s consolidation accounts for the changed count from the earlier 79-test run. An initial compiled-test preparation was kernel-killed at 4 GiB; the unchanged checks passed with the qualified 6500 MiB limit. No assertions were relaxed.
- Original regressions were red on production base `6e0e4e03c5a0b3f5ebcd08b8853c64a1c05100ee` because the recovery warning lacked exit facts.
- Formatting passed for all five changed files. Scoped type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors using the supported oxlint fallback and `--tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`. Pinned Bun parity was not rerun for this head. `git diff --check` passed and tracked source stayed clean.
- Current-head [CI completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40353327532). [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183518#issuecomment-6396617996) accepted the running-Gateway proof, found no actionable defects, and marked this revision ready for maintainer review. Canonical local autoreview remains unavailable after the earlier network/export approval rejection; no such report or bypass is claimed. This integration also received independent manual review.

## Running-Gateway process proof

Both captures used the shipped entry point:

```text
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --port <isolated-port> --auth token --tailscale serve
```

Each scenario first required the actual “serve enabled” log and a successful loopback health response. The Gateway, route-owner worker, fork/IPC and CLI child process were real and unmodified. Only the external Tailscale executable was a disclosed deterministic CLI fixture; no internal owner, fork or logger was mocked.

**Post-ready CLI process failure:** the fixture emitted synthetic stderr and exited 42. Actual Gateway recovery warning, with only its timestamp/logger prefix omitted:

```text
serve route claim exited; recovering managed Tailscale ingress; exit={"workerCode":1,"workerSignal":null,"ageMs":236,"stopping":false,"phase":"active","cli":{"code":42,"signal":null,"stdoutBytes":22,"stderrBytes":20}}
```

**Abrupt route-owner termination:** SIGKILL targeted only the exact worker after checking its start time, executable, owner argument and ancestry from this Gateway. Actual warning:

```text
serve route claim exited; recovering managed Tailscale ingress; exit={"workerCode":null,"workerSignal":"SIGKILL","ageMs":169,"stopping":false,"phase":"active"}
```

The second record correctly omits unavailable CLI facts. Both captures verified raw stdout/stderr markers were excluded from the recovery warnings, configuration bytes stayed unchanged, and all task Gateway/helper/worker cleanup joined. The two-scenario capture completed in 11.54 seconds.

Isolation: separate task VM; Docker private PID namespace, `--init`, `--network none`, no published ports, no host HOME/state/socket/SSH-agent mounts, read-only public source and fresh synthetic state. No live Gateway or Tailscale daemon was interrupted.

This proves the shipped Gateway → real worker/process → IPC → recovery-log composition. It does **not** prove actual Tailscale daemon connectivity, tailnet policy, ingress reachability or successful real-route recovery. The source change still leaves the existing reconnection/backoff policy unchanged.

prs.title: fix(matrix): adopt upstream AIFC audio duration fix
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves Matrix's reliance on a local workaround for incorrect AIFC/IMA4 audio durations by adopting the upstream fix in [music-metadata 12.3.1](https://github.com/Borewit/music-metadata/releases/tag/v12.3.1).

Related: https://github.com/Borewit/music-metadata/pull/2869

## User Impact

Matrix audio and voice messages retain their existing durations, including 640 ms IMA4 clips whose headers store packet counts. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workaround was introduced in [openclaw/openclaw#116890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/116890), commit [9922ea02e96](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9922ea02e962f288db2ab35bd1718ca2e89f21f3), on July 31, 2026, to correct IMA4 packet-count interpretation locally. The upstream fix now makes that duplicate parsing unnecessary.

Upgrade Matrix's music-metadata dependency from 12.2.1 to 12.3.1 and use its reported duration directly, removing the duplicate AIFC parser. Keep the existing duration hints, optional-error handling, and nonnegative millisecond rounding. Add version-specific release-age exceptions for music-metadata and its required strtok3 update.

## Evidence

With the workaround removed, the production `sendMessageMatrix` path uploads a playable 640 ms IMA4 fixture through the real Matrix SDK and HTTP transport to an isolated loopback homeserver fixture. The receiver verifies the uploaded bytes and captures the outgoing event:

```json
{"msgtype":"m.audio","url":"mxc://fixture.test/audio","info":{"mimetype":"audio/aiff","duration":640,"size":15098}}
```

This is a subset of the received event checked by the test, using only synthetic identifiers. The new case uses the installed music-metadata 12.3.1 parser directly. As a negative control, temporarily selecting 12.2.1 with the workaround still removed makes the same HTTP assertion fail: the emitted duration is 10 ms instead of 640 ms. Restoring 12.3.1 passes.

Reproduce the outbound HTTP proof and unchanged duration contracts with:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/send/media.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Result: 40 Matrix send tests and eight media tests pass (48 total, 21.26 seconds wrapper wall time; send-file test execution approximately 1.7 seconds). The six existing duration regressions still return 640 ms for mono/stereo IMA4 packet counts and decoded frames, and 10 ms for A-law, mu-law and malformed IMA4 packets. Scoped lint and extension-test typecheck pass. The fixture is a 44.1 kHz mono sine wave encoded by FFmpeg as Apple IMA4: 441 packets, 64 decoded frames per packet, and 28,224 decoded frames.

The test controls file loading and the local homeserver responses; it does not mock the duration parser, the Matrix client, upload, send, or HTTP transport. This proves the outgoing protocol payload locally; it is not a live homeserver or recipient-delivery demonstration. The review's live-Matrix proof request and current-head maintainer dependency approval remain outstanding. No re-review has been requested.

[music-metadata v12.3.1](https://github.com/Borewit/music-metadata/releases/tag/v12.3.1) includes [Borewit/music-metadata#2869](https://github.com/Borewit/music-metadata/pull/2869), which supplies the correction previously handled by the local workaround.

prs.title: fix(a2a): keep finished tasks available after Gateway restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Finished A2A task results disappear when the Gateway restarts, even while they are still inside the retention window.

## User Impact

Authenticated peers can retrieve their completed and other terminal tasks after a restart, with the same result, ownership, and message-ID deduplication. Retention remains bounded to 24 hours from completion and 500 terminal tasks per account. Active inference is not resumed, and results already lost by an older Gateway cannot be recovered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing task owner persists terminal results through the worker-owned plugin-state store before publishing them and restores them before registering HTTP routes. Shutdown joins accepted writes. Definite storage refusals produce an explicit non-durable failure while retaining any completed artifact; an uncertain acknowledgement cannot overwrite a possibly committed answer. There is no new schema, configuration option, or background service.

This change covers restart durability. The separate queued-follow-up completion fix is tracked in #183803.

Thanks @ensignwesley for the implementation and original restart, storage-refusal, and stable-upgrade proof.

## Evidence

- Current-main restart regression at `364c0d4ebcd4`: reconstructing the task store loses the completed answer (expected terminal result, received `undefined`). The actual isolated Gateway also completed a synthetic HTTP task and then returned `-32001 Task not found` after a clean restart.
- Tested persistence candidate `0fb88848e7a1a21c88bf72955b553bb3dcc1cb13`: the built isolated Gateway completed a synthetic authenticated HTTP task. After a clean stop and a new Gateway process on the same state, `GetTask` returned the byte-identical terminal task (including artifact ID and answer); the other peer received `-32001`. The runtime build passed in 9m28.5s.
- **68 focused tests pass** across the A2A task-store, persistence, lifecycle, HTTP, and inbound suites. They cover recovery, peer isolation, replay deduplication, retention, commit-before-publication, shutdown, and definite versus uncertain storage failures. The real storage regression uses the existing database-worker lane (645 ms test time; 134.53 s cold worker preparation/run). The other four suites passed in 175.87 s for inbound and 60.10 s for the extension shard; CI timing remains pending. After integrating main `9d27ef2e5ca3`, the 12 inbound/real-storage tests pass again (147.68s Vitest; 164.65s wrapper). The A2A production and test diff is unchanged by that integration.
- Formatting, syntax lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Local type-aware lint/typecheck refuse the shared dependency installation under the repository's checkout guard; PR CI supplies those checks.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the persistence candidate against `364c0d4ebcd4`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The subsequent one-line test-routing repair restores the host-broker environment required by the existing real-storage test.
- Production: +152/-34 lines (net +118); tests and test routing: +275/-27 (net +248); docs: +3/-1. This is three fewer production lines than the original proposal. Remaining growth implements durable commit/recovery through the existing owner.

Live paid-provider testing is not included; the Gateway replay uses the repository's deterministic local HTTP model fixture and isolated synthetic state.

The earlier CI run [40572011560](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40572011560), job `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, exceeded the repository test-line ceiling by 207 lines. Integrating current main incorporates its test consolidation and budget update; the real ratchet now passes with 6,285,781 lines under the 6,287,068 ceiling. This PR does not add a baseline exception. The distinct restart, isolation, retention, shutdown, and storage-failure coverage is retained. Final [exact-head CI run 40581071430](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40581071430) completed: every selected product/test/type/package-boundary check passed. The only failing work job is [check-lint-core-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40581071430/job/122485113230), followed by its aggregate gate: five `eslint(curly)` errors in two unchanged UI browser tests. prs.title: fix(matrix): password accounts stay offline forever after the homeserver revokes the cached token
prs.body:
Closes #186011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Matrix account with password auth stays offline permanently (every request `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`, E2EE never initializes) after its device is deleted or logged out on the homeserver, because the plugin keeps reusing the revoked cached token and never logs in again.

## User Impact

User impact: password-configured Matrix accounts now recover on the next start by logging in again with a fresh device, instead of requiring operators to hand-edit `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Accounts without a configured password, and transient homeserver/network failures, behave exactly as before.

Note for operators: recovery creates a new Matrix device, so the account needs the usual E2EE verification/bootstrap for that device afterwards (same as any new device).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMatrixAuth` returned matching cached credentials before ever reaching the password login, and nothing cleared them when the homeserver rejected the token (`clearMatrixCredentials` had no runtime caller). Now, when a cached token is about to be used and a password is configured, the token is checked once with `whoami`. Only a definitive revocation (`isMatrixAccessTokenInvalidatedError`) clears the cached credential and falls through to the existing password login; any other failure keeps the cached token. A successful check is remembered per process, so repeated auth resolves (probe, directory, shared client) do not add round-trips.

Tradeoff: one extra `GET /account/whoami` per cached token per process, only for accounts that have a password configured.

## Evidence

- New tests in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts`:
  - revoked cached token → credential cleared, password login, fresh token/device saved (fails on `main` without this change, passes with it)
  - non-revocation whoami failure (HTTP 500) → cached token kept, nothing cleared or saved
  - live cached token → verified once, second resolve skips whoami
- `pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts`: 24/24 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes ok (typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint changed files, format, plugin boundaries, import cycles, …) except the dead-export scan, which reports `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts: SessionColdOversized` — an unrelated file this PR does not touch.
- Live reproduction against a throwaway Synapse 1.163.0 in Docker (bot with password auth + `encryption: true`), steps from #186011:
  - before (OpenClaw 2026.10.7): after deleting the bot's devices via the admin API and restarting, 0 login attempts, 8× `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`, cached credential unchanged, no device on the server.
  - after (this branch, built with `pnpm build`, gateway via `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`): starting from the same state (cached credential for device `IGBSDYPYCO`, no devices on the server), the gateway logged in again on startup — the server now lists a new device `VTHIDYRSLN`, the cached credential was replaced with it, and the log shows 0 `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` errors.
  - Not covered here: the new device then hits the existing secret-storage/cross-signing state of the account (`Initial cross-signing bootstrap failed and automatic reset is disabled`) and needs `openclaw matrix verify bootstrap` like any new device. That is pre-existing behavior and out of scope for this PR.

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `openclaw/ci-gate`) is red because `main` is already over the test-line ceiling on its own; this PR adds +61 test lines in `client.test.ts` and leaves `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched (details in the PR conversation).
- Secret scanning: synthetic token fixtures in the new tests carry `// pragma: allowlist secret`, and the pre-existing `https://user:pass@matrix.example.org` fixture (the embedded-credentials rejection test) now carries `// trufflehog:ignore`; TruffleHog 3.99.4 flagged that line as a URI credential and blocked the automated review. A local TruffleHog 3.99.4 scan of the changed files, diff and PR text is clean.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the conversation when the first Claude CLI chat turn is stopped
prs.body:
Fixes #181945 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a Claude CLI chat loses its whole conversation when the user stops the very first turn; every following turn starts a new native session until one turn finishes normally. ## User Impact User impact: stopping the first turn of a Claude CLI chat (Control UI Stop, `chat.abort`) keeps the native session, so the next turn resumes it and the model still knows what was said. Affected today: every native-login Claude CLI chat whose first turn is stopped (for example a long first research turn); later turns see no history, because history reseeding across the auth boundary is refused (`auth-unknown`). Turns that already had a binding were not affected and behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made A stopped turn returns its partial output, but `executeCliAttempt` then calls `assertCurrent()` (`src/agents/cli-runner.ts`) and rethrows the abort before settlement. For a resumed turn that is fine: the existing binding stays. For a first turn nothing was bound yet, so the new native session id is dropped even though its transcript is on disk. The runner now catches only that case at the same boundary, hands the new session to a store write owned by the turn's placement settlement, and rethrows the unchanged abort. Nothing else changes for the stopped run: no settlement, no transcript or hook writes, no replay, no fallback. The write is deliberately narrow: - only a direct user stop (`isAgentRunDirectAbortReason`); superseded, restart and generation aborts bind nothing; - only a first turn: no reusable session and no resume id, so resumed turns, fork successors and fresh-session retries are untouched; - only Claude CLI with session binding enabled, and only after `isCliBindingFlushed` finds the native transcript on disk (also for live sessions); - only into an empty binding, under the turn's `assertSettlementCurrent` and the exact local session id, lifecycle revision and active writer (`patchCliSessionBindingInStore`), so a reset, released or replaced session is never written; - not for room events or provenance that preserves user-facing session state; - a refused write is logged and the abort still propagates. On https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147139 ("New claims … retain their abort guards"): that PR protects an established binding from being replaced by an unfinished claim. This change keeps all of those guards. It does not settle a cancelled run or let a new claim replace anything; it only fills a binding that is still empty, for the one session the stopped first turn created. The caller-abort check of the normal publication path (`assertCliSessionBindingResultCommitAllowed`) is unchanged. The binding uses the same facts as normal settlement (auth profile/epoch, prompt and tool hashes, cwd, MCP hashes, reseed receipt), now built by shared helpers `buildCliSessionBinding` and `buildCliReseedReceipt` in `cli-run-settlement.ts`. Not covered: the command path (`src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts`) and scheduled runs keep their current behavior; the reported case and the reproduction go through the chat reply path. ## Evidence Live, isolated test Gateway (own state dir, port 19893, Claude CLI native login). Script: turn 1 in a fresh chat contains a password, writes text, sends a `message` progress update and runs `exec sleep 90`; `chat.abort` after 30 s; turn 2 asks for the password "only from this conversation". | Run | Build | Turn 2 native session | Answer | |---|---|---|---| | before | 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) | new `e42d27dc…` (turn 1 was `6b96039d…`, 220 KB JSONL on disk) | "Aus diesem Gespräch weiß ich das nicht." | | before | main `da34185e6d5` + settlement-only change | new session (same picture) | does not know the password | | after | this PR (`c4f97d3`) | same `43097dc1…` as turn 1 (one JSONL, 4 user entries) | "Das Kennwort ist **MANGO-58** … **RECHERCHE-31**" | In the second "before" run, instrumentation of the built `dist` showed `executeCliAttempt` receiving the returned interruption (`terminalInterruption: aborted`, new session id) and then throwing at `assertCurrent` (`OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT`), so settlement never ran.
Gateway log, after (UTC; chat.abort sent 21:53:21.455Z, returned aborted: true) ```text 21:53:01.126Z cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown 21:53:01.314Z cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 activeSessions=1 21:53:23.492Z claude init ws=main session_id=43097dc1-bec4-4878-8cfb-4402bce57c2e 21:53:23.493Z cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 durationMs=22200 outBytes=29 21:53:33.942Z cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 activeSessions=1 21:53:37.785Z claude init ws=main session_id=43097dc1-bec4-4878-8cfb-4402bce57c2e 21:53:37.786Z cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 durationMs=3853 outBytes=328 ``` Before (2026.10.5): turn 1 `session_id=6b96039d-38da-46ed-909e-74287a396ae2`, turn 2 `session_id=e42d27dc-0f8c-4a6d-8ed8-b08bb425b967`.
Tests (VPS, `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`): - `src/agents/cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output.test.ts`: 7/7 with the fix (87 s wall time incl. shard setup). Without the runner change the two new binding cases fail (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called …`), the guard cases (superseded abort, resumed turn, unflushed transcript) pass both ways. - `src/agents/cli-session-store.test.ts`: 30/30 (40 s), new cases: fills an empty binding; keeps a binding bound meanwhile; skips a reset session; skips a released writer; refuses after the turn owner closed. - Neighbor suites on macOS (Mac mini, arm64): 92 test files that cover `cli-runner*`, `cli-runner/`, `cli-session*`, `attempt-execution*`, `run-entry-cli` and every test importing the CLI candidate or settlement: 1232/1232 passed, 9 Vitest shards, 704 s (`--maxWorkers=2`). - `tsgo` core and the changed test files, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` on changed files, `git diff --check`: clean. Observed, not changed here: after resuming a session whose last native entry is an unanswered tool result, Claude CLI adds its own `No response requested.` assistant entry, which shows up in the imported history before the real answer. ### Maintainer validation **Verdict: LAND-AS-IS** at `c4f97d36ea5805243bcc164eb3c37721d27de8ab`. The contributor implementation and commit remain unchanged. Main `968fca6072c8028043eaa31cf0e8c9c207ede005` still drops the returned first native session at `src/agents/cli-runner.ts:361`; the changed production files and inspected settlement guards have no intervening drift that requires a main merge. The repair uses the existing session-store owner to fill only an empty binding while preserving the original direct abort. The current session, lifecycle, writer, and settlement-owner checks remain at publication. Shared binding construction preserves the native conversation's original auth, prompt, tool, workspace, MCP, and reseed facts for next-turn compatibility checks. No rewrite was warranted. Targeted static validation passed: oxlint checked all 8 changed files against 258 rules with zero diagnostics (`--no-ignore` was needed for the local cache-path checkout), oxfmt checked all 8 files, and `git diff --check` passed. The prescribed isolated Codex autoreview returned `scoped-clean` with no actionable P0–P2 findings. ClawSweeper also reported no findings on this exact head. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40031744382) passed; the check set has 60 passes, 55 skips/neutral results, and no failures. Runtime tests and live Gateway/channel e2e were not rerun locally per maintainer policy; PR CI is the broad gate. The contributor's live observations and regression results above remain attributed evidence. The stopped-first-turn runner regression would fail on the base because the post-execution abort throws before the persistence callback is reached. Numstat against merge base `da34185e6d5cc789da09adc376a177a9cbc3de21`: production **+190/-47** (net +143), tests **+146/-2** (net +144), docs **+0/-0**. The production growth adds the narrow stopped-turn publication operation and shares binding construction without weakening normal cancellation settlement; reaching a nonpositive delta would require unrelated cleanup. The PR is left open and ready for the separate landing step.

prs.title: feat(ui): identify guests in the people list and hovercards
prs.body:
Fixes #186013.

## What Problem This Solves

The People list and person activity hovercard do not distinguish guests from other users on a shared Gateway.

## User Impact

Known guests now have a small, neutral Guest label after their name in the People list and a Guest badge in the hovercard. Names can truncate independently while the Guest label and menu remain visible. Unknown identities remain unlabeled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing restricted-session guest rule for both the signed-in user and Gateway-resolved profile policy. Carry one optional presentation flag through the existing presence and user-directory responses, without changing read scopes, role assignments, membership, or persistent identity data. Presence uses the policy already resolved during connection admission, preserving identities without a resident profile and avoiding roster-time profile lookups.

## Evidence

- Reproduced missing indicators in the real Control UI renderer with synthetic Gateway fixtures; verified the fix in light and dark themes, including live removal of both indicators and no guest labels on regular or unknown users.
- After the producer repair, 61 affected tests passed across 8 suites, including every previously failing authentication and presence-audience case (76.18 seconds wall time). The nonresident-presence regression failed before the repair and passed afterward. Existing real Gateway coverage also verifies the guest flag and unchanged restricted roster access.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, protocol generation, and English catalog validation passed.
- Fresh local autoreview covered the full change through P2. Its sole finding was the resident-profile lookup; the reviewed working-tree repair removes it, with no additional actionable findings.
- Simplified to one shared presentation predicate and existing response/render owners: production +121/−32 lines; tests +67/−9 lines. One new nonresident-presence regression; existing directory, live Gateway, and grouping cases extended. No visual snapshots or styling assertions added.

- The presentation follow-up passed 43 existing UI tests, UI typechecking, targeted lint, stylesheet lint, and formatting. A fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable issues in that delta. No new permanent tests were added for styling.
- The three-dot menu now aligns with the avatar, name, and Guest badge. The light, dark, and narrow layouts retain the existing spacing, label, and long-name truncation. Focused rendering, formatting, and stylesheet checks passed.

## Visual evidence

Captured from the real Control UI renderer with a mock Gateway and synthetic identities. The first reference shows the earlier leading icon; the alignment reference shows the menu before this adjustment. Current captures place Guest after the name and align the menu with the row. prs.title: perf(auth): reduce allocations from unrelated file watcher events
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Auth-file observation allocates a temporary database-key array and predicate for every unrelated directory rename, including SQLite sidecars that it immediately ignores. This is residual work after #183348, #183818, and #184250; all three were ancestors of the profiled build.

## User Impact

Lower allocation during directory event churn, with no change to watched paths, notification timing, credential identity checks, or configuration. Native filesystem event counts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Iterate the existing identity map directly and return at the first exact basename match. Undefined names and legacy auth names retain their refresh path. No cache, invalidation policy, exclusion list, or public API is added. Production delta is +3 lines: the explicit loop removes the temporary snapshot and per-event predicate while preserving matching and early return. Test-line delta is zero.

## Evidence

Five interleaved base/candidate pairs, each replaying 256,000 unrelated rename events through 64 real auth owners and the directory-observer callback composition, with one retained database per directory. Native handles are mocked; allocation sampling and untraced CPU/GC runs are separate. Base: `d7acde6ae97e3e95c3ce4b07fb86cd6eb92db7fb`.

| Owner workload metric | Base mean | Candidate mean | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled owner bytes/event | 249.85 | 64.42 | −74.2% |
| Total sampled bytes/event | 273.32 | 85.93 | −68.6% |
| Untraced CPU / 256k events | 104.09 ms | 84.80 ms | −18.5% |
| Untraced GC / 256k events | 0.526 ms | 0 ms | −0.526 ms |
| Auth publications for irrelevant events | 0 | 0 | unchanged |

The benchmark's `--allocations --max-owner-bytes-per-event 100` regression assertion fails on all five base runs and passes on all five candidate runs. Candidate owner samples span 57.38–72.23 B/event; base spans 242.73–256.56. The semantic test also passes on base; the allocation assertion is the red/green proof. A four-identity sensitivity run before mocking native handle setup measured 383.78→161.75 owner B/event.

CPU host one-minute load was 25.9–31.1 (base) and 25.9–30.2 (candidate); a build was concurrently active. The paired CPU deltas were −11.52, −69.45, −7.91, +0.19, and −7.75 ms. Only two minor collections occurred per baseline run; no candidate or major collections occurred in these short windows. Baseline max GC pauses were 0.222/0.360/0.272/0.284/0.271 ms; candidate had none. Loop tails have only 112–386 samples/run and are context only. RSS/heap at the end of these short, non-normalized GC windows averaged 263.0/54.5 MiB base versus 276.1/59.4 MiB candidate; this is not retained-heap proof.

Reproduce the owner workload with:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/auth-file-watch-events-measure.ts --state-dir <new-dir> --allocations --max-owner-bytes-per-event 100
# Use --owner <frozen-file-state.ts> for baseline, retaining its relative imports.
# Omit --allocations and the threshold for CPU/GC runs; --identities 4 tests multiple databases.
```

Focused proof: auth file-state, worker, and owned-directory observation tests (27 passed); the final zero-growth test consolidation also passed (14 tests). Build passed (5m16s); changed-file lint/format passed. Export collision guard and both source-closure test files passed (32 tests). Test-line ceiling is inherited over budget; no baseline was changed and this diff adds zero test lines.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh context, complete diff and relevant owners, P2+ scoped clean. Autoreview itself refused the provider route because it did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed. The test-only consolidation preserves the reviewed branches.

The explicitly requested fast-path proof is used for this semantics-preserving owner allocation deletion. A bounded isolated Gateway watcher census is recorded below; no ten-minute A/B whole-Gateway performance claim is made. Native onchange allocation remains outside this fix.

The candidate-only, two-minute canonical-harness census used the built Gateway, 10,800 sessions, 40 plugins, 65 clients, mock turns/tools/native subagents and worktree churn. A synthetic 5,000-write/delete burst of an unrelated `watcher-probe.sqlite-journal` file in the observed agent directory delivered 235 rename notifications over the 15.007-second counter interval (940 events/min). These were the only watcher events during that interval; no recursive workspace watcher was implicated. Native event delivery rate is unchanged by this patch and was not measured in a separate base Gateway. The much higher production event incidence was not reproduced on macOS; the owner callback cost is established by the replay above.

Candidate census context (not an A/B performance gate): main-thread CPU 10.79%, GC 0.227 s/min, event-loop p99 32.70 ms (5,604 samples), client sessions.list p99 106.26 ms and server handler p99 48.64 ms (265 samples each; below the p99 gating threshold), RSS 2,114 MiB, main heap 526.8 MiB. Eight mock turns completed with eight tool calls/results and twenty committed writes. Allocation rate was not sampled in this timing-only census.

The census ended at host load averages 15.02/20.60/19.67 (1/5/15 minutes). Measurements used the pre-rebase build; the final branch was rebased onto `caf3034ae081` with the authored patch unchanged.

prs.title: improve(android): shorten store release source checkout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Store Release spent 22:55 checking out source in [run 40552056685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40552056685), importing 3,873 branches and 543 tags. Checking out the source files themselves took about four seconds.

## User Impact

Store and Internal testing releases fetch only the selected source's complete ancestry while preserving the exact release commit, release-note history, version allocation, and public phone/Wear baseline lookups. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A depth-one exact-SHA checkout followed by a targeted unshallow fetch removes unrelated branch/tag history. The selected main commit remains cached at `origin/main` so the release owner can negotiate common ancestry when fetching live main. A shallow-only checkout would truncate release-note history. The existing release owner still fetches current main and immutable public baseline refs itself. iOS and the separate Android GitHub publication workflow retain their existing contracts.

## Evidence

### Hosted source preparation

[Five-sample nonpublishing measurement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780), with five serial fresh `ubuntu-24.04` runners at the original release source `0d838ac431b57bbce984636ce4e395b4e2108e7b`. All five samples passed.

| Sample | Checkout + complete source history | Fetch current main | Total source preparation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780/job/122464844746) | 7:29 | 3s | 7:38 |
| [2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780/job/122464844581) | 11:03 | 2s | 11:11 |
| [3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780/job/122464844517) | 10:05 | 3s | 10:15 |
| [4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780/job/122464844254) | 10:55 | 3s | 11:05 |
| [5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582365780/job/122464844681) | 8:32 | 4s | 8:42 |

Median checkout/history: **10:05** (range 7:29–11:03; nearest-rank p95 11:03). Median total source preparation: **10:15** (range 7:38–11:11; nearest-rank p95 11:11). Even the slowest total was below half the original 22:55 checkout; the median total was 55% shorter.

Acceptance was recorded before measurement: preserve all 121,122 selected-source commits; initially import only the selected source at `origin/main`, without tags or unrelated refs; pass live-main ancestry and the authentic saved public baseline lookup; match full-checkout endpoint-diff and first-parent-history SHA-256 fingerprints; and improve on the observed 1,375-second checkout. All five samples passed these checks. Total preparation also includes baseline lookup/fetch and clean detached staging.

The historical baseline is one production sample, not a controlled timing distribution; no fixed speedup is guaranteed. The temporary diagnostic job lives on a separate branch and is absent from this PR. No mobile build, signing, upload, or store promotion is part of this validation.

### Checks and review

- Focused mobile release CI suite: 22 tests pass, 17.29s wrapper wall time (16.08s Vitest; new Git fixture 0.87s). The real shallow-remote fixture covers main advancing, divergent phone/Wear baselines, detached staging, identical release-note inventory/history, and exclusion of unrelated history.
- Workflow validation, targeted tooling typecheck/lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent local autoreview of the complete final candidate, committed as `a6768d3246421a47163c51ee4dd36cb65ea989e0`: scoped-clean at P0/P1. Hosted ClawSweeper found no actionable findings on the earlier `e2d6754` head. Local ClawSweeper failed output-schema validation and is not counted as a clean review.
- [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582361761) has settled. Android screenshots, phone/Wear tests, ktlint, native checks, workflow sanity, CodeQL, security review, and API-diff reporting passed. The following failures are inherited:

| Failed job | Signature and attribution |
|---|---|
| [Fast release lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582361761/job/122465605277) | Five `eslint(curly)` errors in `draft-body.browser.test.tsx:31,32` and `chat-content-column.browser.test.tsx:288,289,362`. The actual merge tree `3156d85c` differs from its live-main base `12bb6168` only in this PR's three files; both offending UI blobs also match original base `63ba4974`. |
| [Core lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582361761/job/122465605931) | The same five errors on exact head `a6768d32`, in unchanged source. The automatic classifier calls this new because a newer scheduled main job passed; source and diagnostic comparison establish it was not introduced here. |
| [Dependencies](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40582361761/job/122465605979) | Unused `runPrompt`, unused `settleActivity`, and 18 unused `scripts/perf/*` files. Affected files, Knip configuration, check scripts, and dependencies are unchanged from the original base. |

The aggregate CI gate is red because of these failures. Automatic hybrid CI and OpenGrep were canceled to honor the no-Blacksmith requirement; the supported hosted exact-head CI dispatch supplied broad validation. OpenGrep has no hosted dispatch route and remains unrun.

prs.title: fix(agents): retain skill guidance for reader-enabled routines
prs.body:
Closes #186285.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: scheduled agents lose eligible skill guidance when their explicit tool limits still permit reading instructions. Also prevents readerless Code Mode runs from advertising skill instructions they cannot read.

## User Impact

Reader-enabled routines retain their skill catalog. Excluded or unavailable readers, write-only Code Mode, and explicit `toolsAllow: []` still receive no catalog. This adds no tools, filesystem access, permissions, configuration, or persistence changes. A model still decides whether to follow the instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep Gio Della-Libera's original native-reader fix and remove the blanket finite-cap catalog suppression. The canonical skills renderer owns capability guidance: Code Mode now requires both its `exec` control and the admitted `skills_read` capability. Permission refresh uses the same final capability set. Runtime caps and minimal prompt mode remain enforced.

Thanks @giodl73-repo for the original fix and request-level regression coverage; the original commit is preserved. Redundant prompt fixtures and equivalent cases were consolidated so the new regressions add no net test lines.

## Evidence

- Red/green serialized-provider regressions: native `read` and `skills_read` positives fail on main; write-only Code Mode and reader-removal refresh fail on the original PR renderer. The final consolidated regression still produces exactly those two Code Mode failures with seven controls passing. Excluded/unavailable readers and explicit empty caps remain omitted.
- Final focused run: **146 tests pass across six files**, including prefix stability, in **129.84s** wrapper wall time. Shard times including transforms: 19.17s, 37.24s, 27.33s. All 34 executed jobs in [exact-head CI, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40591701355) passed (27 unrelated jobs skipped). Both its `openclaw/ci-gate` and the separate aggregate gate passed. The six changed-test jobs took 141s, 289s, 373s, 476s, 198s, and 220s wall time including setup.
- Clean-main cron reproduction uses one disabled, no-delivery synthetic job and a recording Ollama relay: native `read` is offered but the canary catalog is absent. Real Qwen3 8B receives the same omission and guesses an incorrect token without reading the skill.
- On the final head, the same fixture run offers native `read` plus the canary catalog, obtains successful skill-file and canary-file receipts, and returns the exact token. Real **Qwen3 8B** repeats those two reads and the exact answer in **4.457s**; delivery remains `not-requested`. The token is absent from the initial request. Raw synthetic runtime captures are retained locally and are not attached to this PR.
- Scoped production and final test TypeScript pass (3.13s and 2.63s); targeted lint passes (12.48s); formatting, whitespace, and applicable ratchets pass. No baseline was raised.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview of the final committed head: **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. [ClawSweeper reviewed the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186306#issuecomment-6453715391): no findings or before-merge items.
- Prompt snapshots regenerated with no committed changes: **0 snapshot token delta**. The initial Qwen wire request increases from 1,903 to 2,107 prompt tokens (+204; per-run session/runtime facts differ). Local validation is macOS only; no hosted deployment or other-platform proof is claimed.

Production **+5/-7** (net -2), tests **+254/-254** (net 0), documentation **+5/-0** against the merge base. No compatibility path or new owner was added.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep pending follow-ups in the chat queue
prs.body:
Fixes #186021

## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up sent during an active conversation could move from Queue into the transcript before its placement was known, then return to Queue when delayed Gateway custody arrived. Finishing the previous run during that interval could also release the provisional message. Local Discard could appear after transmission even though it could not cancel the received request.

## User Impact

Pending follow-ups stay in Queue until their placement is known, without an intermediate transcript bubble. Rejected sends keep their recovery controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-ups retain their chosen placement with the existing outbox item. An acknowledgment without a transcript receipt reconciles through the history owner. Provisional admission keeps the local source in Queue until placement or consumption is confirmed. The shared handoff retains complete message and attachment bytes for both durable and memory-only sends, including steering chronology and late receipts. Already-admitted sources do not re-enter the send drain. Outbox lookups use their canonical captured scope.

Idle sends and explicit interrupts keep their existing fast path. Rejected sends retain inline errors and Retry; local Discard is available before transmission or after rejection. Accepted queued inputs still cancel by their exact run ID.

## Evidence

- 366 focused tests pass across 12 outbox, send, custody, history and recovery files. Existing regression cases fail on the prior behavior; the repair preserves retry identity, attachment custody, nonqueued steering order and consumed-before-transcript handling.
- Production browser scenarios hold ACK and custody independently, with the previous run either active or completed. The follow-up stays in Queue throughout.
- An isolated real Gateway with synthetic local inference preserves an admitted follow-up in Queue and reloads without another send or model request.
- Control UI build, UI/chat/E2E typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, line ratchets, documentation checks and independent P0–P2 review pass.

Risk and coverage: the additional authoritative read applies to active follow-ups whose ACK lacks transcript placement. Their existing outbox source remains recoverable if that read fails or its scope retires. No visual delay timer, second queue, new configuration or storage format version is introduced.

## Visual Evidence

The same real renderer with deterministic Gateway responses. In the earlier PR revision, a started ACK promoted the follow-up before queued custody moved it back. With the repair it remains in Queue. The fixture delays expose protocol ordering; the captures do not measure production network or model latency.

prs.title: fix(update): restore managed Gateway after updater process death
prs.body:
Refs #164800. Supersedes #186328; this draft combines the helper and repair lanes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a managed Gateway remaining stopped when its updater is killed before, during, or after package publication, including when the updater itself stopped the service.

## User Impact

The live helper settles the interrupted update and restores a verified Gateway. If the helper also dies, `openclaw update repair` can recover promptly and restart the Gateway the update left stopped. Operator stops, lost ownership, named data risk, and unverifiable runtime identity still prevent automatic restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The live Linux reproduction exposed two related ownership gaps. The helper only armed restoration when it parked the service through the foreground protocol; the normal native updater stops systemd itself (`update-command-service-maintenance.ts:618`). Its SIGKILL therefore reached the old “no verified recovery result” branch. Standalone repair also only recognized the helper's `service-stop` step. Dead handoff owners could additionally retain the 45-minute recovery grace.

Both recovery paths now consume `findUpdateGatewayStop` in `src/infra/update-run-gateway-stop.ts`. It recognizes the helper's stop, or a managed handoff followed by activation with the service currently stopped. The existing completed `managed-service update handoff` receipt is written by both Gateway `update.run` (`src/gateway/server-methods/update.ts:546`) and automatic updates (`src/infra/update-startup-auto-run.ts:379`), so it remains usable after target selection changes `installationMethod` to `npm-global`. The initial `update.run` running snapshot is not a restart receipt. Later incoming running observations after activation persist the existing `service-running` receipt; those receipts, replacement boot/settled verification, completed managed restarts, and newer settled runs retire the stop. These receipts survive ledger compaction. No new stop protocol, ledger schema, or updater-side stop receipt is needed.

The helper uses its staged runtime to retain bookkeeping while the installed tree is missing. It cancels untouched publication preparation; once displacement begins it completes publication forward through the sealed publication owner, runs the installed post-core finalizer as this run's continuation, then uses `gateway restart --preserve-definition --json` and verifies readiness/version/build identity. Updater-stopped recovery does not require the helper-only parked systemd generation. History records rollback, success with recovery, or failure with repair/deep-status guidance.

Repair reclaims promptly only when the recorded owners are proven dead; live/unknown owners and descendant/runtime-holder fences remain. After finalization, it uses the same stop evidence to start and verify an update-stopped service while preserving later operator stops.

Rejected alternatives: treating a signal as an unrecoverable result; inferring restart permission solely from an inactive unit; requiring a new native-stop receipt from an older installed driver; importing bookkeeping from the package while it is being swapped; and adding a second helper/repair stop policy. The combined change retains one publication owner and one stop-evidence reader.

LOC against base `4daeb9252ce`: production +800/−235; tests/support +764/−73; docs +76/−12; total +1640/−320 across 39 files. The required growth covers sealed crash recovery, standalone service restoration, and their boundary proof. Simplification removed the repair-only stop inference and reuses existing durable handoff evidence.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** 364 tests across 16 files passed, including all nine SIGKILL/publication cases, native-stop group-death repair, operator-stop negatives, data-risk refusals, systemd/launchd recovery, lifecycle/terminal outcomes, and ledger receipt/interruption coverage. The full run initially found seven stale termination-harness source lookups; removing the duplicate lookup and rerunning that file passed all seven. Production was unchanged for that rerun.
- **Red/green:** with production temporarily reverted to pre-follow-up merge `cc34e4ae6ea`, five helper regressions, two repair regressions, and two compaction regressions failed. Native-stop fixtures include the real entry point's initial `serviceRunning: true` snapshot. The base reproduced the old no-verified-result branch and the missing installed-runtime failure during publication. Production was restored with SHA-256 verification; all corresponding tests pass on this change. A separate interim run also proved that the initial running snapshot suppressed recovery before its fix (three helper and two repair failures).
- **Build/checks:** packaged runtime build passed (2m22s), including CLI bootstrap and Doctor closure checks. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- **Typecheck limitation:** the requested `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` stops before source checking with `Declaration input escapes checkout` for `tsrs` in the prescribed external pnpm virtual store. The checkout containment guard was preserved; this is not a passing typecheck.
- **Autoreview:** Codex local review of the complete combined diff against `4daeb9252ce` finished `scoped-clean` (P0–P2), with no accepted/actionable findings. A fresh final pass included the termination-harness fix.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-service.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-ledger.compaction.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize-refusal.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-systemd.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-launchd.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-triage.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-terminal-result.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-termination.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-ledger.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-capture-receipts.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-interruption.worker.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

The termination file was rerun with the same runner after fixing its stale lookup. The existing manager/lifecycle suites exercise process startup, publication, cancellation, and lease custody and take longer than unit-only tests.

</details>

The helper boundary uses real SIGKILL children, package publication journals, ledger writes, and native lease custody, with synthetic native-manager/readiness/finalizer I/O. The repair boundary runs the registered CLI with real ledger and dead-handoff reclamation. This is not a fresh live Linux/systemd upgrade result; the AWS reproduction still needs to be rerun against this head.

prs.title: fix(telegram): table replies stall the Gateway on a long zero-width cell
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram reply that contains a table stalls the Gateway for seconds to minutes when one cell is a long run of zero-width characters ending in a printable combining character.

## User Impact

User impact: table replies to Telegram render in normal time whatever the cell text is. The rendered grid and the measured widths stay exactly the same.

The monospace grid is used for tables wider than 20 columns when `channels.telegram.richMessages` is enabled, and for HTML `<table>` content in HTML-mode sends. Default Markdown replies take a different table path and are unaffected. On the affected paths the cell text comes from model output, so a sender who can get the model to repeat a string into a wide table (directly, or through fetched content it summarizes) can block the Gateway event loop for every channel and session it serves.

## Why This Change Was Made

`telegramMonospaceGraphemeWidth` decides whether a grapheme is non-printing with

```js
/^(?:\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}|\p{Control}|\p{Format}|\p{Mark})+$/u
```

The branches overlap. U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER is both `Format` and `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point`, so for a grapheme of N such characters the engine has 2^N ways to match the run. Graphemes have no length limit: U+200C has Grapheme_Cluster_Break=Extend, and so does U+FF9E HALFWIDTH KATAKANA VOICED SOUND MARK, which is printable (`Lm`) and matches none of the branches. `"‌".repeat(N) + "ﾞ"` is therefore one grapheme on which the match fails only after every split is tried. The earlier width checks in the same function (keycap, emoji presentation, wide ranges) all miss this grapheme, so it reaches the regex.

Every branch matches exactly one code point, so the alternation becomes one character class:

```js
/^[\p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}\p{Control}\p{Format}\p{Mark}]+$/u
```

It accepts the same strings and runs in linear time. A comment records why the class must stay a class.

The pattern came in with #117890. All three grid paths share it: HTML `<table>` fallback in `renderTelegramHtmlText`, the over-wide table fallback in `markdownToTelegramRichBlocks`, and the rich-HTML map.

## Evidence

**Real Telegram Test Server and built Gateway:** [native delivery, Gateway health probes, and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183217#issuecomment-6455681768).

Fresh `pnpm build:runtime` artifacts: main `caf3034ae08157264c43e8e085a68f892ac5b5cd` and unchanged candidate `4b3754c613b2e936ff58348a7811f87cae3ad666`, in isolated `node:24.22.1` containers. The checked-ref Telegram userbot skill used one leased Test Server bot and an independently authenticated QA user, sequentially across both refs. Real agent turns used deterministic local Responses output; the Bot API and native TDLib delivery were real, not fixtures.

Each reply was a 21-column Markdown table with rich messages enabled, forcing the affected monospace fallback. After a normal-table warm-up, two turns used a first cell of exactly 24 ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINERs (U+200C) followed by printable Extend character U+FF9E. A normal-table control followed. Independent processes probed Gateway health and the separate provider fixture.

| Turn | Main max Gateway health latency | Candidate max Gateway health latency | Main / candidate native delivery after send |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pathological 1 | **829.11 ms** | **6.01 ms** | 1966 / 1795 ms |
| Pathological 2 | **959.60 ms** | **3.72 ms** | 1779 / 1634 ms |
| Normal-table control | 3.42 ms | 6.29 ms | 1657 / 1694 ms |

Main queued 3 and 6 health responses over 100 ms, respectively, then released each burst within 4 ms and 2 ms. The candidate queued none over 100 ms. The independent provider stayed responsive (maximum 6.09 ms during the pathological main turns), demonstrating a Gateway stall rather than merely delayed Telegram delivery. These bounded 24-character runs produced sub-second stalls on this machine; no multi-second stall or large end-to-end delivery speedup is claimed from these measurements.

All eight replies, including warm-ups and controls, arrived as complete native `messageRichMessage` objects containing `pageBlockPreformatted`. Every full grid, header separator and padded cell matched an independently constructed expected string. Both pathological replies per ref retained all 24 U+200C characters and the U+FF9E terminator. Both recordings and every send completed. Credential scratch was removed, the lease released, and both task containers stopped.

**Earlier supporting checks (contributor):** the local fake-Bot-API Gateway fixture showed 9.31 s versus 0.36 s model-to-send and 5971 ms versus 95 ms maximum health latency on its recorded baseline; a separate real HTTP-client fixture showed identical HTML send content with the stall removed. The character-class replacement agreed with the original over all Unicode code points and 200,000 random strings. The contributor reported 164 passing tests across six Telegram width/format/rich-block files, including an exact-grid timing regression that fails on main. Those are supporting fixture/unit results, not the new live Test Server proof above.

No source or test changes, push, or CI rerun was needed for the live proof. Latest contributor head was fetched and preserved. No live OpenAI response or Telegram client screenshot is claimed; native content and Gateway responsiveness are the observed signals.

## Impact and merge danger

Production delta: +4/-1 (one equivalent regex replacement and its rationale); tests +18/-0. The overlapping alternatives are removed without another owner, parser, input limit, configuration option, or fallback. Existing grid behavior is retained.

Thanks @LeizhenZhang for finding the issue, the minimal fix, and the discriminating regression.

Two-way door: reverting restores the old regex and its stall. No persistence, schema, configuration defaults, permissions, or public API changes. The formatter blast radius is Telegram monospace grids in wide rich Markdown tables and HTML table paths; the original stall could affect every session sharing that Gateway.

prs.title: fix(memory): rebuild remote workspace indexes through the Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes remote workspace memory maintenance that cannot rebuild the Gateway index through the standalone memory CLI. That CLI process does not own the running Gateway's registered remote file access, so it can inspect local files instead of the Harness workspace.

## User Impact

Operators can run `openclaw gateway call memory.index --params '{"agentId":"main"}' --timeout 180000` to rebuild with the current Gateway configuration and remote workspace binding. Workspace files stay on the Harness; the derived index stays on the Gateway. The method requires `operator.admin` and may call the configured embedding provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory-core plugin already owns indexing and remote file discovery. This adds an administrative Gateway entry point that reuses those owners. It carries the caller's live authority through asynchronous preparation, embedding dispatch/retry boundaries, and the existing database publication guard. Disconnection, revocation, or configuration replacement prevents later host-issued embedding calls and index publication. The result uses the native asynchronous status helper, so built-in database reads run in their worker and PostgreSQL returns aggregate counts. Status and repair guidance direct remote workspace maintenance to the Gateway.

This is a general split-storage maintenance gap exposed by the OCE + Strands Box integration. It is not a Box syscall defect and does not require a Box-specific memory implementation. No schema, storage format, embedding default, or network policy changes are included.

The existing manager and publication worker still own indexing, writes, and cleanup. The admitted request/connection cancellation signal is composed with the inline embedding operation's existing timeout signal. An existing retry backoff may finish before authority is rejected, but no later host dispatch is admitted. Already accepted provider work cannot be retracted; provider-owned asynchronous batches retain their existing API, which does not expose a cancellation signal.

## Evidence

The PostgreSQL path now discards a cancelled or revoked operation's private TEMP stage even when another borrower keeps the same database connection alive. Only `database.stage.discard` bypasses the expired request-maintenance assertion. The live database, captured Agent owner, caller guard and worker connection still authorize cleanup; publication remains refused.

- Real PostgreSQL regression: both disconnect and revocation leave a TEMP table on the original implementation, and both pass with this change. The test retains a co-borrower, verifies the same backend PID, unchanged published source rows, zero remaining TEMP stages, caller-owner rejection and preservation of the original failure. The baseline leak run preceded an additional caller-refusal assertion; these are not byte-identical test snapshots.
- All 95 directly changed cases pass: 63 embedding-policy, 2 PostgreSQL cleanup, 15 workspace-file, 3 paused-deadline and 12 Gateway SDK cases. An additional 33 conformance-runner / native-worker registry cases and the concrete shared-fixture cold-status consumer pass (129 distinct cases total). Native formatting, scoped typed lint and the memory-core production, extension-test and tooling typecheck lanes pass with the locked dependency graph. No hooks or package checks were disabled.
- Fresh independent source review traced the cleanup permission to the connection-owned stage map and found no remaining actionable authority issue. This was a separate read-only subagent review; the previously unavailable local autoreview helper did not produce a validated machine report.
- Test setup now initializes only its owned database before plugin registration; the workspace-file suite initializes its own per-case state. The shared cold-state fixture remains cold for other consumers. The initial broader fixture proposal was rejected after its status-only consumer failed, and the final narrower change passed that regression. This is test initialization, not a production database-admission change. All 41 consumers of the shared fixture were enumerated, but only the directly affected suites and the identified cold-status risk were rerun.
- The installed OCE qualification uses the existing approved older OpenClaw runtime plus its compatibility backports; those results do not substitute for current-main PostgreSQL proof. No OpenClaw version pin is changed here.

Draft only. The independent-helper merge hold remains; no merge or readiness promotion is requested. Fresh installed OCE + Strands Box acceptance is in progress on a new image and will be reported separately.

prs.title: fix(update): Android/Termux foreground Gateways cannot verify their identity for updates
prs.body:
Related: #165296

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway updates on Android/Termux (Control UI or chat `update.run` against a foreground Gateway) refuse with `managed-service-handoff-unavailable`, or fail because the foreground Gateway owner cannot be verified.

## User Impact

User impact: a foreground Gateway running under Termux can now prove its own process and boot identity the same way a Linux Gateway does, so the verified foreground update handoff from #152466 can admit it instead of refusing up front.

Unattended auto-update still needs a managed service (by design). On Termux it keeps reporting `managed-service-handoff-unavailable` and printing the shell command. Gateways already on 2026.9.4 run the old updater for the first hop, so they need one manual update to reach a release that contains this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node on Termux reports `process.platform === "android"`, but the kernel is Linux and exposes the same procfs. The identity owners gated their procfs reads on `linux` alone. As a result, on Android:

- `getProcessStartTime` / `getFileLockProcessStartTime` returned `null`, so the foreground owner lease recorded `startedAt: null` and `update.run` could not build a verified `foregroundOrigin`.
- The handoff boot reader threw `OS boot identity unavailable`.
- The gateway-lock and state-lease PID-namespace identities were missing, so ownership checks stayed `unknown`.

The procfs readers now treat Android as Linux. The boot reader records Android's boot under the kernel platform `linux`, so the persisted handoff, lock and lease schemas stay unchanged and no older reader sees a new platform value. The state-lease namespace capture now keys off the recorded boot platform rather than `process.platform`, and the gateway-lock namespace cache keys on `process.platform`.

Rejected alternative: adding `android` as a new persisted boot platform. That would grow three strict schemas for a kernel fact Linux already describes.

Production LOC: +17/-12 (mostly the shared procfs predicate and its comment).

## Evidence

Focused tests, which fail on `origin/main` and pass with the fix:
- `src/shared/pid-alive.test.ts`: Android parses `/proc/<pid>/stat` start times, including through `getFileLockProcessStartTime`.
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-identity.test.ts`: Android reads `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` and records platform `linux`.
- `src/infra/gateway-lock.namespace.test.ts`: Android produces the Linux gateway-lock namespace through the real boot reader.

On base, 3 of these fail. With the fix, 94/94 pass both locally on macOS and on Linux.

For the real-kernel proof, Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m5zbbjp358wa19nsa3pe7dwm` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40564139750)) ran Linux 6.6 with Node reporting `process.platform = "android"` and called the real readers with no mocks:
- Base `origin/main`: `selfStartTime: null`, the boot reader throws, the gateway-lock namespace is `null`, and the state-lease owner has `startedAt: null`, namespace `null`, status `unknown`.
- Fix: the self and child start times are read from procfs, the boot is `{platform: "linux", identity: <boot_id>}`, the gateway-lock namespace carries `pidNsInode`, and the state-lease self status is `live`.
- Without the shim, real Linux output is unchanged.

Gap: there was no real Android device. Android SELinux or `hidepid` could still deny `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` or `/proc/self/ns/pid` to a Termux app. In that case the readers fail closed exactly as before (the update refuses, and lock and lease custody stays `unknown`), so this cannot regress, but it is unverified on hardware.

The Android cases were folded into the existing Linux procfs tests, so this PR's net test-line delta is -2. Main is already over the test-lines ceiling.

Review: `$autoreview` (Codex) returned scoped-clean on the fix commit and on the test-compaction commit (head `5a927524371`).

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(macos): chat accent updates after Control UI changes
prs.body:
Related: #128922

## What Problem This Solves

The Mac chat window does not refresh the Gateway-wide saved accent (`ui.prefs.accent`) when only chat is open. The existing per-profile accent path already updates separately; Gateway-wide changes can leave chat on its old color.

## Why This Change Was Made

The long-lived Mac control connection reads Gateway config on connection and `config.changed`, resolving the saved Gateway preference before `ui.seamColor`. The Talk Mode config reader uses the same precedence so it cannot overwrite the chat color. Profile appearance retains separate inherit, theme, and color states, so an explicit theme choice cannot fall through to a Gateway color. The shared hex decoder used by iOS remains available with its prior result. Superseded reads and replaced Gateway leases remain fenced.

## User Impact

Chat can pick up a Gateway-wide saved accent without opening Mac Settings or Talk Mode, while a personal profile accent continues to win. Normal shared-token Control UI connections receive an owner profile and save Appearance changes through `users.prefs.set`; this PR does not claim that those edits exercise the Gateway-wide path.

## Evidence

- Current head `b34033c907786da68f99e5006d0feb2bf8793b7f` restores the shared `decodeProfileAccentHex` entry point still used by iOS. [Hosted Mac native run 40560680084](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40560680084) checked out this exact head and passed 48 control-connection, 8 Talk Mode, and 9 shared preference tests, including the restored iOS hex projection; [complete logs artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40560680084/artifacts/12762489056). Independent Claude review found no actionable issue in the compatibility patch.

Package typecheck still fails on the previously recorded `control-ui.ts:25` side-effect CSS import (`TS2882`); that file and package typecheck configuration are byte-identical to the earlier failing baseline. prs.title: perf(ui): preserve unchanged dashboard report content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updating one saved dashboard report makes unchanged reports repeat content work because the full snapshot gives them fresh objects.

## User Impact

Unchanged reports retain their prepared content while the changed report and all layout or metadata changes still appear. No user action or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway Board provider preserves an unticketed native report when its name, instance, revision and envelope are unchanged. Changed envelopes still publish every incoming field while retaining the unchanged content reference. Explicit refreshes, replacements, missing identities, and ticketed or framed reports retain their existing refresh behavior. Key enumeration avoids creating a pair array for every compared field.

The Gateway remains authoritative. Content puts advance the report revision; layout operations do not. The provider still reads and scans the full snapshot in O(N); this is not a delta-only update path. The base already contains fixed-report viewport activation and CSS containment; this change addresses the remaining snapshot identity work rather than introducing another rendering or caching owner.

The benchmark keeps distinct labels for the supported 48-report workload, a staged 1,000-report stress workload, and the legacy 1,000-report workload. Staged cases install the synthetic reply before timing, then measure event delivery, the full board.get request/response, reconciliation, visible metric 2 and settling. The legacy case retains fixture installation inside its original interval. None is a live-Gateway or actual-network measurement, and the 1,000-report fixture exceeds the current 48-widget new-write cap.

prs.body:
Related: #173839. Thanks @lyrakat for the English-token pressure measurements.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes prematurely reduced output budgets during tool continuations when an OpenAI-compatible provider returns tool-call IDs that require normalization.

## User Impact

Matching same-turn continuations retain their measured prompt budget. Fresh user turns, missing usage, and changed prefixes keep the existing conservative fallback. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

#181343 already passes measured prompt pressure to the transport, but strict tool-ID normalization could replace the exact request context after that measurement was bound. The transport then missed it and fell back to the larger character estimate. Move the existing normalization into provider prompt projection before observation; remove the former inner wrapper. The estimator and its validity checks are unchanged.

Production: +32/-19 lines (net +13), tests: +16/-0, docs: +2/-0. Growth is the typed callback plumbing needed to keep normalization policy with its existing owner while running it before measurement. No additional estimator, state, or compatibility path.

## Evidence

- Regression failed on the base with serialized output caps `[8192,5957]`; fixed full request-admission suite passes 20/20 and preserves `[8192,8192]` plus normalized wire ID `readreport`. Red: 335.11s; green: 433.60s, mostly cold compilation.
- Real isolated Gateway, Qwen3 8B via llama.cpp and a recording relay, 256K configured context and about 170K server-reported prompt tokens. The relay changes only returned tool IDs to include punctuation; real model output and usage are retained. Results below.
- Summary audit: `summary-tail,suffix-head` discloses bounded compaction-artifact trimming, separately from transport budgeting; existing safeguard/degraded-fallback suites pass 46/46 (274.64s). No summary policy change.
- Isolated Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P2; no actionable findings.

| Request | Transport estimate | Server prompt tokens | Output cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base, fresh user turn | 220180 | 169881 | 35819 |
| Base, punctuated-ID continuation | 220260 | 169953 | 35739 |
| Fixed, fresh user turn | 220439 | 170124 | 35560 |
| Fixed, punctuated-ID continuation | 170238 | 170196 | 85761 |

The same long English session gains one user turn between base and fixed runs; it is not an identical-payload benchmark. Fixed CLI wall time: 23.09s; both real provider calls completed in 6.60s total.

Other validation: transport params 52/52 (17.44s), prompt submission/projections 61/61, prefix stability 13/13, execution phase 19/19. The combined affected run took 780.98s and also exposed one inherited cache-warning expectation failure; it reproduces on the exact base (193.47s) and is already corrected on main by #186233. Targeted replay with that upstream fixture correction passes 2/2 (130.49s). No duplicate fixture change is included here.

Core typecheck passed (656.81s, including artifact-lock wait); runtime build passed (652.23s); all baseline ratchets passed (497.43s), separate line-cap check passed (4.11s), formatting and docs link checks passed (0 broken links, 37.59s). The model executed the requested read but miscopied a marker in its final answer. The reporter's release predates #181343; their prose does not identify whether the capped request was a same-turn continuation or a fresh user turn.
