prs.title: perf: share delegated update authority snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Delegated update authority checks open separate rollback-reader snapshots for parent and receiver leases during every Doctor assertion. Validate both roles in one synchronous lease-store operation and one existing snapshot. Preserve all authoritative row queries, full-handle equality, role-specific process identity and liveness checks, revocation checks, and the complete six-statement rollback-reader envelope. Deduplicate only within an assertion; retain no validity cache across assertions or awaited work.

The accepted visibility edge is that a peer revocation committed between the former parent and receiver snapshots is observed by the next assertion. There is no await or external effect within the combined snapshot. Initial delegation admission, effect boundaries, heartbeat checks, and crash/stale-claim recovery remain intact.

## Acceptance rule (registered before runs)

Flow: native `openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart --json`, synthetic isolated state, real local QA Gateway, both full Doctor passes. Frozen v3.1.5 SQL observer and unchanged Doctor workload. The same installed current-main driver runs baseline and candidate target revisions; the changed executor runs in target finalize workers. One matched count-only pair (n=1 per arm), with cold and warm and first/second Doctor cells reported separately. No latency, CPU, median or p95 claim.

First confirm the baseline still reproduces the duplicate rollback-reader pattern. Owner regression must fail on base and pass on candidate: one assertion uses one envelope instead of two, with the same five row queries for a simple lineage (17 to 11 SQL). Existing revocation, identity, recovery and refusal-to-false tests must pass. Full Doctor SQL must decrease consistently with removed envelopes, requests must not increase due to this change, and Gateway MAIN must not increase. Any adverse count cell of at least 20% stops acceptance. Report all full-Doctor SQL, requests, process-main and Gateway MAIN counts independently; do not combine process-main with Gateway MAIN.

## Follow-up

The number of authority assertions (roughly 2,000–2,800 per full Doctor pass in retained synthetic evidence) comes from layered maintenance admission (`assertDatabaseAccess`, `assertAdmission`, `run`, `assertReadAdmission`). A later owner cutover may reduce those calls; this change preserves their count and checks.

## Evidence

Reviewed implementation at c4e619404c85f96ed9eb95d3124b93bd0d103243. Integrated current main at a06d918ae27f6dc848dc4479a0831a3d06d16f91 to include the UI lint fix; all five changed file blobs remain identical to the reviewed implementation. The native owner regression fails on base because it observes two envelopes; the candidate observes one with the same five SELECTs. Final reader and settlement suites: 43/43 pass. Earlier candidate identity/recovery suites: 58/58 pass; native executor suite: 6/6 pass. Final-head CI supplies broad confirmation after the owner placement change. A retained-service requester-refusal case initially hit its unchanged 15-second child deadline. A focused base comparison passes, and the final head then passes the same case with the existing exit/refusal/unchanged-config/parent-authority assertions. No timeout or production change was made.

Two isolated Codex reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings and verified unchanged input. Net production delta +31 lines: the existing mutation reader owns combined row and process checks, replacing executor-side memoizers and duplicate orchestration. Net test delta -1 line; all cases retained, duplicate setup/echo/fixture assertions removed.

Exact integrated-head CI [40593509503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593509503) passed: 45 successful jobs, including all selected tests, production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, baseline ratchets, and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. The PG logs confirm actual test execution in all three shards. The earlier unrelated UI lint failure is resolved by the main integration. Local check:changed passed its executed non-type guards, lint and format; the required internal dependency layout blocked three declaration checks before compilation, now covered by the passed CI type jobs. The local Knip scan reported no new findings; its two inherited exports are attributed in the retained proof.

Open-PR overlap: #149882 at `aca8f05544e2`; final base-only and prospective-candidate `git merge-tree` against current main `e265eff48527` each have the same 89 existing conflict paths, with no new paths or increased conflict markers. The indexed peer head is unchanged.

No full-pass saving or timing claim is made yet. The unchanged baseline and prepared candidate will complete once that operation releases the lock. Results will report full Doctor SQL, requests, process-main and Gateway MAIN separately; any Gateway MAIN increase or adverse count cell of at least 20% will be reported immediately for a revert decision. Exact-head database/identity semantic approval is complete.

prs.title: fix(cli): report interrupted commands before cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #185902. Related: #136311.

## What Problem This Solves

Non-interactive commands such as `openclaw memory index --force` could exit with status 143 after SIGTERM without telling the operator that a signal interrupted the command.

## User Impact

The CLI now prints `Command interrupted by SIGTERM. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` before its existing shutdown drain. SIGINT similarly names the signal and retains status 130. Specialized signal owners keep their own output and lifecycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accepted-signal owner already knows when it owns shutdown, so the fix is one stderr write there. Current main already waits for memory shadow cleanup; this does not add another cleanup or cancellation path. Admitted work may finish and publish a complete index during shutdown. An incomplete or failed rebuild preserves the published index. The memory CLI docs now make that distinction explicit.

Thanks to @NovaLux12 for the detailed release reproduction and follow-up evidence. The older orphan reports in #136311 informed the explicit current-main shadow check; no new orphan-reaping policy is introduced.

Production: +1/-0 line; tests: +8/-1; docs: +4/-0. No obsolete code in the signal owner justified unrelated deletion to offset the single diagnostic line.

## Evidence

- Regression is red on base `451ec41c26c67cca7d8a61b7da6b0188cf52249e`: exactly the SIGINT/SIGTERM notice assertions fail (8 other tests pass; 5.11s Vitest, 9.47s wrapper).

- Fixed signal-owner and command-cleanup suites: 27 passed (142.24s Vitest including compiled graph preparation; 176.29s wrapper). The existing fallback signal cases themselves take 110/102ms. They assert notice-before-cleanup ordering, exit 130/143, natural exit, and silence when a custom owner handles the signal.
- Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, test-mock-exports, test-lines, config-docs and plugin-inventory checks passed. Isolated Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Real non-TTY `pnpm openclaw --profile sigterm-index memory index --agent main --force`, with synthetic isolated state and an owned embedding relay. Baseline healthy-request control: signal only the CLI after shadow creation; status 143, no signal notice, all shadow/WAL/SHM files removed, admitted work finishes publication.
- Real Ollama `nomic-embed-text` control (768-dimensional embeddings): seed and search an original index, hold a replacement embedding request, signal only the CLI, then fault-inject rejection of the held response. Baseline: status 143 without a signal notice, no shadow-family leftovers, stored memory/index/vector table snapshot unchanged, and successful search after reopening. The 20-second signal-to-exit interval includes the deliberately held provider response.
- Final full `pnpm build` passed in 21m18.9s. Both rebuilt CLI cases passed: the notice was visible before releasing the held response; exit 143 and shadow-family cleanup were preserved. Healthy fixture work completed publication and the replacement was searchable. The real `nomic-embed-text` rejection case preserved the original stored index snapshot and reopened search returned the original memory. The deliberate hold dominates signal-to-exit time (20.57s for the fixture; 20.35s for the real-model rejection).

prs.title: fix(signal): container receive memory grows with every queued frame while an inbound message is being stored
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/127383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Signal container receive client keeps reading and holding every valid frame of a burst in memory when one inbound message is slow to be stored, so memory grows with the size of the burst.

## User Impact

User impact: a Signal account that receives a large burst while message storage is slow no longer grows Gateway memory with the burst. Such a burst comes, for example, from signal-cli reconnecting to Signal and pulling its backlog, or from a busy group. Gateway memory stays bounded at about one socket read, and messages still arrive in order.

The container ([signal-cli-rest-api](https://github.com/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api) in json-rpc mode) does not queue messages for a slow reader. Once the socket buffers between it and OpenClaw are full, its blocking write stalls, and messages beyond its 64-message receive channel are dropped inside the container, the same way it drops them when no client is connected. So a stall long enough to fill the socket buffers moves the loss from unbounded Gateway memory into the container. Shorter stalls lose nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each container frame is parsed and appended to a promise chain that stores messages one at a time, but the socket was never paused, so the chain could hold any number of accepted-but-unstored frames. The receive handler now pauses the WebSocket when it accepts a frame and resumes it once that frame is the last one stored. `ws` still emits the frames it already decoded from the current socket read, so at most about one read stays in memory. The rest waits in the socket buffers, and beyond them the container blocks or drops as described above. Order, the shutdown drain, and failure propagation are unchanged. When storage fails, the client resumes before closing so it reads the peer's close frame. Without that, a paused socket only closes after `ws`'s 30 s close timeout.

Accepted edge case: the container never times out a missing pong, so a paused client keeps its connection. But the container's keepalive pings and message writes share one lock across every `/v1/receive` WebSocket it serves. While OpenClaw is paused and the container's write to it is blocked, the container sends no messages or pings to any of its receive sockets (other accounts or clients on the same container) until OpenClaw resumes. Storage stalls are short, and an admission that never settles is already a broken state.

## Evidence

Tested at `2aa4292c0762` (base `upstream/main` `3ac21799e844`).

The plugin's real `streamContainerEvents` client (real `ws` over loopback TCP, Node 24, Linux x64) ran against a local `ws` server in its own worker thread. The server stands in for the signal-cli container's `/v1/receive` endpoint and sends 50,000 valid frames of about 1 KB each. The receive handler holds its first event for 2 s, standing in for slow durable storage. The harness instruments the `ws` client's `emit` to count decoded `message` events. It also measures retained frames, client heap growth after `gc()`, and the server's `bufferedAmount`, then releases the hold and checks delivery order. The client under test is not stubbed. There is no Signal account or real container.

Before (base `3ac21799e844`):

```text
frames sent by server:            50000
delivered to onEvent while held:  1
decoded by client while held:     50000
retained, accepted not delivered: 49999
client heap growth while held:    67.7 MiB
peer bufferedAmount while held:   0.0 MiB
delivered after release:          50000 (ordered: true)
```

After (this PR):

```text
frames sent by server:            50000
delivered to onEvent while held:  1
decoded by client while held:     5
retained, accepted not delivered: 4
client heap growth while held:    -0.0 MiB
peer bufferedAmount while held:   43.9 MiB
delivered after release:          50000 (ordered: true)
```

Observed result: on base, retention grows with the burst. 20,000 frames held 27.2 MiB, 50,000 held 67.7 MiB, and 100,000 held 135.2 MiB. Five alternating base and fix samples at 50,000 were taken at `2aa4292c0762`. Every base sample retained 49,999 frames (+67.7 MiB). The fix samples retained 4 to 8 frames with no heap growth. The rest stayed in the server's send buffer, and all frames arrived in order.

Unstalled throughput at `2aa4292c0762`, 50,000 frames, alternating base and fix runs, 5 samples each (median):

| Receive handler                     | base   | fix    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ | ------ |
| async, one `setImmediate` per event | 228 ms | 218 ms |
| resolves synchronously              | 229 ms | 222 ms |

Regression tests: in `client-container.backpressure.loopback.test.ts`, "stops reading while admission is held…" sends 512 frames (about 16 MB, more than loopback socket buffers hold) and holds the first. After 100 ms it asserts three things:
- the server still has unsent frames (`bufferedAmount > 0`);
- the client decoded fewer than 512 frames;
- the socket is paused.

On base it fails at the first assertion (`expected 0 to be greater than 0`, because the client has already read the whole burst). With the fix it passes. "closes the paused socket when a receive handler fails" guards the failure path: with the `resume()` before `close()` removed, it times out because the peer waits for `ws`'s close timeout. The existing fake socket in `client-container.websocket.test.ts` gained no-op `pause()`/`resume()`.

Checks:
- The touched tests pass (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`).
- `pnpm check:changed`, scoped to these files, passes format, ratchets and the guard lanes locally.
- Its typecheck and lint lanes are red here only because of a sparse local install: a module used by `qa-lab` and `eslint-plugin-solid` are missing. With the solid overrides removed, oxlint is clean on the three files. The unused-export scan flags only files outside this diff. This PR's CI is the proof for those lanes.

| Test file                                                            | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `extensions/signal/src/client-container.backpressure.loopback.test.ts` | 6.1 s (tests 197 ms)  |
| `extensions/signal/src/client-container.websocket.test.ts`           | 6.0 s                 |

Simplify pass: the failure path resumes directly instead of sharing the success path's "last in chain" check, because every frame after a failure skips the rejected chain anyway. Production `client-container.ts` +21/−6, tests +116 against the merge base.

Not covered:
- A real signal-cli container.
- The full Gateway receive path: storage is a held promise.
- Real-container buffering. The stand-in server buffers unsent frames without bound in user space (the 43.9 MiB above). The real container instead blocks its write and drops later messages, as described under User Impact.
- The keepalive edge case above is not exercised.

prs.title: improve: finish deferred model retirement with a shorter second Doctor pass
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A native `openclaw update` can repeat all 70 Doctor contributions even when unchanged plugins have converged and deferred model retirement is its only remaining obligation.

## User Impact

That second Doctor now finishes through six existing contributions, while keeping complete startup, custody, schema admission and config preparation. The measured second pass used **8,478 fewer SQL statements cold and 8,885 fewer warm**, with worker requests falling from **231 to 137** and **234 to 137**.

**Rollout:** the benefit starts once the installed updater includes this change—one update after release. Older installed updaters continue requesting the full Doctor. Standalone Doctor repair remains full.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater negotiates the candidate Doctor's existing private child capability and sends an optional stdin selection hint. The config owner independently proves eligibility from its prepared migration plan, applied changes and retirement receipt; the hint grants no authority. The retained contributions run in existing order: initial config persistence, auth/catalog migration, complete session-transcript repair (including post-session plugin detectors/handlers), session-route repair, final config/cron work, and strict final validation.

Warnings, findings, deferrals, unrelated work, plugin changes, incomplete discovery, constrained selections or an unbound migration plan select the full list. A late discovery uses that existing full list in the same admitted context; retained inspections may repeat on this exceptional path. Durable-write receipts avoid duplicate writes, and a later config commit invalidates prior post-write completion. Current refusals stay terminal. Durable config still precedes retirement-ledger completion and cron effects; final validation and real readiness remain mandatory.

No public flag, new cache, generation, manager, schema or SQL syntax is added. Production growth is +219 LOC (+299/−80), carrying owner facts through the existing transport and selection flow. The full implementations remain necessary for standalone Doctor and fallback.

## Evidence

Frozen synthetic native-update workload: `scripts/perf/doctor-retirement-measure.mts`, Node 26.12.1 on macOS arm64, private-QA profile, identical 179-plugin inventories, symlinked `.artifacts`, isolated real Gateway and qa-channel. Matched baseline installed X → target Y versus candidate X+patch → Y+patch, with one identical complete patch on both candidate versions. All four native updates reached the exact target and passed both Doctors, authoritative retirement skipped → completed, lint and real QA readiness. Both candidate second Doctors received the hint and ran exactly six contributions.

| Second Doctor | Cold baseline | Cold candidate | Warm baseline | Warm candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Contributions | 70 | 6 | 70 | 6 |
| SQL statements | 38,327 | 29,849 | 38,744 | 29,859 |
| Worker requests | 231 | 137 | 234 | 137 |
| Process-main SQL | 37,643 | 29,541 | 38,038 | 29,551 |
| Worker-thread SQL | 684 | 308 | 706 | 308 |
| Second-Doctor process CPU (s) | 41.889 | 23.690 | 42.389 | 32.778 |

SQL savings are 22.1% cold and 22.9% warm. Request operations: task 210 → 121 cold / 213 → 121 warm; execute 17 → 12 in both; open/close unchanged at 2/2. Whole-update SQL fell 110,751 → 102,344 cold and 98,162 → 86,334 warm.

Acceptance was recorded before capture: frozen v3.1.5 observation, one baseline cold+warm arm then one candidate cold+warm arm, at least 1,000 fewer second-pass SQL statements or a clear CPU reduction, with adverse metrics stopping for review. The approved loaded-host disposition is **one count/CPU pair**, not a wall-time benchmark. Cold/warm are separate n=1 cells: no latency, median or p95 claim. Process CPU includes that Doctor's threads, not the complete subprocess tree; missing exit counters prevent a total-tree CPU claim. Warm main-thread CPU rose 18.896 → 19.486 s (+3.12%). Complete per-contribution SQL/request attribution and shared/unknown buckets were retained for every Doctor pass before raw capture cleanup.

### Accepted one-time startup MAIN difference

Warm final Gateway root SQL rose 75 → 76, with aggregate `PRAGMA busy_timeout = ?` 12 → 13. This is a one-time post-update startup effect of the state left by the narrower Doctor; the exact differing root call is unresolved at n=1. Total warm Gateway SQL fell **589 → 578**, requests **151 → 148**; cold final Gateway root SQL fell **89 → 82**; canaries were unchanged. No ≥20% adverse count cell occurred.

The maintainer explicitly accepted this startup-only difference after a changed-hunk audit: shared `plugin-model-catalog-repair.ts` additions only track/return an in-memory boolean from already-parsed data; they add no SQL, file/database I/O, connection, lease, worker request or awaited store work. `refreshStartupPluginQuarantine` and all following helpers are byte-identical (SHA-256 `017df0b30d2d50e086e5fd7ed49ecbe57c1be643ba86889b8532311691d260ba`); the changed convergence return belongs to Doctor. `update-doctor-result.ts` changes only an erased type. Thus changed Gateway-executed code cannot issue the extra connection-open PRAGMA. This waiver does not permit a steady-state or per-turn MAIN increase.

### Correctness and checks

Owner/config-flow tests passed 108 + 34 cases; cancellation 13, convergence 9, prompt-prefix stability 13. They cover plugin changes, pending migrations, incomplete discovery, constrained selections, credentials, refusal, restart/resume authority, durable-write/cron ordering, session warnings/deferment and late fallback. T1/dialect ratchets, Madge, line limits and formatting passed. Local `check:changed` preparation hit the external declaration-custody boundary before type analysis; no local type pass is claimed.

Earlier CI exposed two script/test typing errors and test-line growth; those were corrected without changing production or the measured behavior. Prior-head CI [40594216587](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40594216587) passed, including all three PostgreSQL shards. One initial readiness deadline reproduced on the original baseline and candidate; the deadline and assertion were retained. All final-head checks are recorded below.

Two isolated production-head Codex reviews completed at P0–P2 with no actionable findings after disposition. Script/test corrections received isolated delta reviews. Production remains +219 LOC. The final separate test-only consolidation removes 271 lines across seven owner suites: config model validation, CLI dispatch, Doctor contributions, restart coordination, input extraction, media parsing and plugin uninstall. It retains every distinct fixture and assertion, including authority, security, ordering and rejection cases. The complete PR's test delta is −2 against its merge base; the test-line ceiling and check are unchanged. This follows the ratchet's existing over-ceiling rule for changes that do not add test lines.

Final cleanup commit `d3aecc3e9400011d3b5496703db593ddb4bc4c7f` passed normal hooks, targeted formatting/lint and an isolated Codex P0–P2 review with final source verification. The exact reviewed tree is `928a2d7d13c6a013d7dbd37222fed9fc6f3b226a`. Fresh prospective merge with main `c868bfe31058` is clean and confirms test delta −2. Final exact-head CI is pending.

The cold baseline's fixed installed updater passed the database-backup step with symlinked `.artifacts` (snapshot exit 0; activation exit 0). All four successful native updates reaffirm #185680, #185789 and #185977, including retained warm agent state.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction pins, PostgreSQL checklist and overlap</summary>

Baseline driver X `22f1ebdbc2bac08e3dc5164a4f7fbdf82f6ad594`; baseline target Y `455a9d678baadc72410a3a532400ea3a63e1bc7b`. Candidate driver `d816fbbe83968ec2f365044dd3162f22865aa16f`; candidate target `ec6cdc38d526c5d2de4876a1fc56782bbb6fdce8`. Identical patch ID `a3d704f8740c5fae8efaa05343e574184ddfbc0e`. Measured workload SHA-256 `ea75f2c1294cde77051c0e1b5e6eac66d8c44ab44d677b1772e1b1bd19ae2ed1`; the script-only typed-local correction produces `afdf0178636bf8cd4404d5a62d4a00fc7a3fbe2a0a36e03ce5500adb4eb70bad`, with unchanged workload behavior; capture probe `5536f9fbb72e35519147d75e5109b51c38c7261610eca0fdd4a8b09def23e41c`. All 37 frozen observer files verified; approved capture instrumentation preserves native gates and fixtures.

PostgreSQL reach is **yes**, through Doctor's existing dialect-neutral config/session/cron owners. No SQL text changes:

1. Existing statement shapes, transaction/advisory-lock envelopes and cross-store commit ordering are unchanged when retained owners run. Full-only contributions are omitted only after eligibility; durable config remains before ledger/cron.
2. No expanded query, buffered result, iterator or payload bounds; no work moved to a different query/thread.
3. Eligibility carries existing owner facts; no cache, revision, generation, freshness probe or external-writer assumption added. Hint is not authority; late discovery falls back under existing custody.
4. No schema, PRAGMA, identity, permission, admission or recovery change. Full startup/custody/schema/config flow and the bound-plan guard remain.
5. All statement/request counts above include process-main and workers. The only Gateway MAIN increase is the explicitly accepted startup cell, with no I/O added to Gateway-executable hunks.
6. PostgreSQL semantic review is approved for `ec6cdc38d526c5d2de4876a1fc56782bbb6fdce8` and explicitly carried across the subsequent script/test-only corrections; the Doctorfast production delta is unchanged. Integration also contains main's independent released-upgrade cron fix #185723. All three PG conformance shards executed and passed in CI run 40589353443 (jobs 122490122890, 122490122998 and 122490122970); the new test-only head still requires its own three-shard run. SQLite native proof passed; no PostgreSQL timing claim.

Open-PR paired merge-tree comparison covers 90 peers. The final test cleanup received four fresh paired comparisons; 86 unchanged-head proofs carry after path-disjoint verification against the shared PR index. All comparisons pass. Refreshed heads are checked against base-only and base+candidate; no unapproved conflict growth. Previously accepted exact exceptions remain #158723 (one added preflight hunk on an already-conflicting path) and #143781 (credential-result capture, unchanged call arguments/security behavior). Current main merges cleanly with this head.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep two-line sidebar titles readable with touch controls
prs.body:
Related: #181583

## What Problem This Solves

Two-line sidebar session titles disappear during hover or keyboard focus when the primary pointer is coarse and supports hover. The hover/focus padding outranks the coarse-pointer reset, reserving action space twice. Replacing `:is` with zero-specificity `:where` lets the existing reset reserve that space once. Touch targets are unchanged.

## Evidence

[Real-Gateway before/after proof and inspected screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181631#issuecomment-6452738056).

Built main `63113761e0c5f03a498b6046655d3a098192917f` and contributor head `e70d47853e1c9f3a27c9b100606148c7520131a8`, each served by a real isolated built Gateway. Sessions and previews came through Gateway APIs. Native Chromium capabilities were hover=true, primary coarse=true/fine=false, both available pointer types. No CSS/DOM rewriting, matchMedia override, or Gateway mock was used for this proof.

Main twice and candidate twice: hover and keyboard focus collapse main's title from 119px to 0px, while the candidate retains 119px. The line-box height stays 18px: the defect is horizontal collapse, not loss of line height. Fine-pointer controls agree on both builds (255px at rest, 203px on hover/focus). Physical hybrid hardware remains unverified.

## Regression coverage

The built-UI browser regression uses native hybrid capabilities plus fine-pointer and ordinary-touch controls. Existing overlapping touch-centering and fine-hover assertions are consolidated into the pointer matrix: title width and action gap, unread-badge stability, title origin, fine-pointer reservation, touch button centering, and enlarged-text nonoverlap remain covered. Optional screenshot-output scaffolding was removed; screenshots above come from the independent real-Gateway harness. The suite exports its existing named contract rather than deriving it from a concrete function.

Main was merged to repair the stale test-line ratchet baseline; the ceiling was not raised by this PR. Relative to the original integration base, test growth is reduced from 117 to 27 lines. Production net LOC remains zero. Hosted CI and exact-head review remain authoritative for the submitted head.

Container validation after integration: production Gateway and UI builds pass; both affected neighboring E2E files pass (10 tests), and the corrected mobile pointer/menu suite passes all 7 tests. Formatting passes for all four modified test/support files. An initial consolidation run exposed an incorrect unread-dot selector in the new assertion; it was corrected to the existing rendered selector before the passing run.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous CSS and test structure, with no persisted-state or protocol changes. Blast radius is sidebar title/action layout in the Control UI, especially hybrid coarse-pointer devices.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): dream diary writes fail when the gateway user doesn't own the workspace
prs.body:
Closes #184867 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the dream diary (`DREAMS.md`) is never updated when the gateway runs as a user that can write the agent workspace but doesn't own it, such as a workspace shared through group or ACL permissions. ## User Impact User impact: dreaming writes its diary and Deep Sleep summary to a workspace the gateway user can write but doesn't own, and writing `DREAMS.md` no longer tightens an existing workspace directory to 0700. ## Why This Change Was Made The `DREAMS.md` writer was the only memory-core writer that didn't pass `dirMode` to `replaceFileAtomic`, so fs-safe applied its 0700 default to the existing workspace directory. Only a directory's owner can chmod it, so a non-owner failed with EPERM before anything was written. The writer now keeps an existing workspace's mode, as `dreaming-markdown.ts` and `short-term-promotion-memory-write.ts` already do; fs-safe skips the chmod when the mode already matches. A directory the writer has to create still gets 0700, the same split #171869 made for the state root. The remote memory worker calls the same writer, so it is covered too. Files the gateway user creates, a new `DREAMS.md` and the nightly dreaming reports, are still written as 0600, so in a shared workspace only that user can read them. An existing `DREAMS.md` keeps its mode. Changing the mode of new files is a separate decision. ## Evidence - Regression test `keeps the workspace directory policy (new=false)`: fails on `main` (`expected 448 to be 504`, the workspace came back 0700 instead of 0770) and passes with the fix. - Guard test `keeps the workspace directory policy (new=true)`: passes on `main` and with the fix, and fails if the writer reuses the mode of a directory it just created (`expected 493 to be 448`, 0755 under umask 022). - `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-dreams-file.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30 tests pass in 35 s wall, mostly transform. The two new tests take 6 ms each here, and 21 ms and 10 ms in CI (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`). - Two-user reproduction on Linux through the CLI: `openclaw memory rem-backfill --path `, which writes `DREAMS.md`. The workspace is owned by uid 1000, mode 0770, with ACL `user:1001:rwx` (plus the default ACL); state is isolated with `OPENCLAW_HOME`. | Run | `main` | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | As uid 1001 (write access through the ACL) | `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod`, no `DREAMS.md` | Diary entry written; workspace still 0770, ACL mask `rwx` | | As the owner | Diary written, but the workspace becomes 0700 with ACL mask `---`, locking uid 1001 out | Diary written; workspace still 0770, ACL mask `rwx` |
Captured output: CLI reproduction on main (797f83a1) and this PR (cc76b1c3) ```text $ run.sh other # memory rem-backfill, build 797f83a1 == before: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx { "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod" } } EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod == exit: 1 == after: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx (no DREAMS.md) ``` ```text $ run.sh owner # memory rem-backfill, build 797f83a1 == before: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx { "workspaceDir": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws", "sourcePath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md", "sourceFiles": [ "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md" ], "groundedFiles": 1, "writtenEntries": 1, "replacedEntries": 0, "dreamsPath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws/DREAMS.md" } == exit: 0 == after: 700 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx #effective:--- mask::--- -rw-------+ 1 1000 1000 332 Oct 26 21:21 DREAMS.md ``` ```text $ run.sh other # memory rem-backfill, build cc76b1c3 == before: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx { "workspaceDir": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws", "sourcePath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md", "sourceFiles": [ "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md" ], "groundedFiles": 1, "writtenEntries": 1, "replacedEntries": 0, "dreamsPath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws/DREAMS.md" } == exit: 0 == after: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx -rw-------+ 1 1001 1001 332 Oct 26 21:23 DREAMS.md ``` ```text $ run.sh owner # memory rem-backfill, build cc76b1c3 == before: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx { "workspaceDir": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws", "sourcePath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md", "sourceFiles": [ "/tmp/oc-e2e/notes/2026-10-20.md" ], "groundedFiles": 1, "writtenEntries": 1, "replacedEntries": 0, "dreamsPath": "/tmp/oc-e2e/ws/DREAMS.md" } == exit: 0 == after: 770 1000:1000 user:1001:rwx mask::rwx -rw-------+ 1 1000 1000 332 Oct 26 21:23 DREAMS.md ```
- The nightly dreaming run end to end, in the same two-user setup: the gateway runs as uid 1001 in a container without network access, with dreaming on and `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` as the model, configured with `applyMockOpenAiModelConfig`. The managed dreaming job is forced with `openclaw cron run --wait`, over two daily notes in `memory/`. Promotion thresholds are 0 so that one sweep also promotes. | | `main` | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Sweep | `dreaming promotion failed for workspace …: EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod`, then `failed=1` | `failed=0` | | `DREAMS.md` | Not created: the narrative fails with the same EPERM, and so does its fallback entry | The model's text as the diary entry, plus the Deep Sleep summary | | Deep report in `memory/dreaming/deep/` | Not written | Written | Both runs write the light and REM reports and promote six entries into `MEMORY.md`, and the workspace stays 0770 with ACL mask `rwx`. With an owner's existing `DREAMS.md` of mode 0670, this PR's rewrite keeps 0670.

prs.title: perf(gateway): carry prepared stores into group mutations
prs.body:
**Parked draft:** waiting for contributor PR #167717 by @Marvinthebored. That change uses membership results to skip category writes. If it lands, this optimization must preserve that behavior while folding its needed membership facts into preparation; if it closes, this draft can resume its existing validation. No runtime saving is claimed yet.

## What Problem This Solves

Session-group rename and deletion scan every member twice even though the first scan's membership result is discarded.

## User Impact

Group changes preserve session identity, timestamps, ordering and access checks while avoiding a redundant worker request and membership scan. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the same logical store targets from the existing catalog prepare command, after its write transaction commits. Category writers consume those prepared targets. Remove the standalone membership request, wrapper and handler together. The authoritative membership rescan before retiring the source group remains, as do current target/category authorization checks and partial-change recovery. Shared stores retain logical agent identities rather than substituting their physical owner. No schema, cache, generation, transaction span or cross-store commit ordering changes.

## Acceptance rule

Registered before the first runtime benchmark. Extend the existing committed `scripts/perf/session-group-registration-measure.ts` real WebSocket/isolated Gateway workload. Run separate rename and delete processes with one first mutation and five warm mutations, thirteen synthetic members, exact category/key/timestamp/catalog/sidebar readback after every mutation. First means first mutation after setup, not cold process or cold database handles. Retain the registration default.

Compare three alternating same-platform baseline/candidate pairs using identical committed workload bytes and frozen v3.1.5 observer hashes. Report SQL statements, worker requests and MAIN per mutation index and owner as median/p95/[min–max], with first and warm phases separate; also report boot/setup/readback/shutdown and whole-process totals. Requests and statement work must disappear, not move to another thread or phase. Expected target: one standalone membership request removed per mutation; actual SQL reduction is measured, not inferred. Runtime MAIN may not increase. Any comparable count increase requires attribution; a 20% adverse cell stops the performance claim for disposition. Shared exact-entry/actor-hydration/snapshot/row-fact/watermark counts must hold or have a demonstrated unrelated cause.

Use ordinary campaign proof slots, load below64 and internal free at least12GiB for count runs. Profile all observable Gateway threads and spawned helpers on both heads separately for ownership attribution; record missing profiles. These are count/profile runs, with no latency or CPU-speed claim. Timing claims would require a separate acceptance update, timing lock, load below24 and at least five samples per arm.

## Evidence

Production base: `6b3cf0c1f95ef1dd974ff029fb1c68af76af1a9e`; common-workload measurement baseline: `2fd774ae6ace2926b4c5b1e2f542e63de794000f`; candidate: `c09313c5ae9cba76d82adafcb79beef5312b2684`. Both measured revisions contain identical workload SHA-256 `686e70046eb134e19efd64af4a7ce7b7d29c8e2abb3b9ef731979a05cf7707f0`.

The shared logical/retired physical-owner fixture passed on base and candidate. The completed-request regression failed on unchanged production because deletion issued one standalone state-read request; candidate passes with zero such reads and two catalog-writer requests. Five owner suites passed 62 tests, including late members, changed authority, source defaults, partial recovery, and shared-store rename/deletion. The RPC mock consumer passed another nine tests; its generated-input verification completed. Two isolated Codex P0–P2 production reviews completed scoped-clean, plus a separate clean workload/proof review. Changed-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass.

Production delta: +44/−45 lines (net −1); obsolete request, handler and forwarding wrapper removed together. Preparation errors conservatively retain the existing partial-change/retry guidance, including errors before a write. Discovery runs after the existing write transaction, so filesystem discovery does not extend write-lock duration. Security checks removed: none; current catalog admission, per-target category authority and retirement membership/source/destination checks survive.

Before parking, local T1 (170→170), T1-compat (15→15), dialect, line-cap, assertion and timeout ratchets passed. Remaining local checks and canonical Knip scans were intentionally stopped; they have no completed verdict. No count or profile arms were launched. Automatic CI run 40173018000 did not select PostgreSQL conformance; skipped jobs are not passing evidence. PostgreSQL review and remaining validation are deferred until this draft resumes.

The seven-peer overlap audit found a new group-mutation conflict with #167717 and an expanded existing import conflict with #136476 after removing the unused config type. Peers #183285, #180610, #157427, #155808 and #153907 have no new conflict blocks against the pinned comparison base. Parking avoids landing over the active contributor work; these comparisons must be refreshed before resuming. No runtime savings or speed claim yet. No update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle change; the published-driver update cell is not applicable.

prs.title: feat(ui): render inline widgets during generation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI previously waited for a complete `show_widget` call before displaying content. ToolSearch-wrapped calls and a preceding hidden skill receipt also prevented partial widgets from appearing.

## User Impact

The Control UI can display useful HTML/SVG while `show_widget` arguments are still being generated, including calls routed through ToolSearch. Partial content is inert: generated scripts, navigation, network resources and host APIs remain unavailable until the completed, authenticated Canvas document loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing tool stream, catalog lookup, inert Canvas renderer and session layout cache provide the required ownership boundaries.

The preview stays at zero height when it contains only styles or an empty JavaScript-generated container. It preserves authored `hidden` content, attaches after ordinary assistant content rather than a hidden skill call, and carries its measured height through direct and nested tool results. The existing layout owner handles the final size adjustment.

Routine Show Widget disclosures remain hidden in presentation; transcript events, errors and permission handling are retained.

## Risk and coverage

- Reduced real-agent checks used an isolated Gateway and synthetic data. KPI with ToolSearch ON showed content 4.32 seconds before tool execution; the direct-tool control showed content 9.70 seconds before execution. To-do showed content 10.72 seconds early and its completed counter changed from 3/12 to 2/12 on a real checkbox click.
- After the final `hidden` fix, the rich SaaS dashboard showed useful content 25.82 seconds before execution. Its completed SVG chart rendered and account search changed visible rows 6 → 0 → 6.
- JavaScript-only content correctly showed no useful partial preview and reserved zero pixels before execution; the completed widget rendered normally. These timings describe individual runs, not a benchmark or latency guarantee.
- Tests reuse existing harnesses and cover stream identity, cancellation, inert rendering, hidden content, owner lifecycle, handoff and final interaction. The hidden-content regression failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Fresh independent review of the complete PR candidate completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. After integrating current main, focused stream-projection/producer/wrapper tests, 64 UI tests, five autosizing E2E cases and three activity tests pass. Canonical UI typechecking, scoped lint and `git diff --check` also pass. The real-agent results above precede this integration and are reused alongside these focused integration checks.
- Live checks ran on the isolated rebased runtime with the same fixes; focused tests ran on this PR checkout. The capture, transport, layout and document owners remain separate; no draft persistence or new execution authority was added.
- A pre-existing duplicate Canvas can appear briefly when the assistant streams a matching `[embed]` shortcode before `chat.final`. It was observed for about 1.16 seconds, then returned to one final widget. Its builder/incremental reconciliation fix is being handled in a separate PR; this PR does not claim to fix it.

## Evidence

The images below are inspected crops of real Control UI runs with synthetic data. Cropping removes account/model controls; it does not restyle the UI. The before/after runs use the same KPI task, with separately generated content.

| Before: no visible partial widget | After: useful content during generation |

| ![Before, widget content absent while generation continues](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b337cd4-420f-402e-8b5e-52f812c2b972) | ![After, KPI content visible before the tool executes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fd028a5-0354-441c-ab00-0c805d07da9f) |

Completed KPI widget:

![Completed KPI widget](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb552f7b-80b8-4a5b-88a2-b5ef710d00ba)

Rich dashboard during generation; authored hidden fallback remains hidden:

![SaaS dashboard preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b0e0636-62be-4a47-9898-501facdc48b1)

Completed SVG chart and working to-do result:

![Completed SVG chart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8221562-9766-45dc-90a6-b7796c8c471f)

![To-do after the checkbox changed the counter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae593afe-84fd-47c6-bcc2-0aa717e7bdcf)

prs.title: feat(agent): read piped messages in ordinary agent turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary `openclaw agent` turns treat `--message-file -` as a filename, so scripts cannot pipe prompts into the command. Closes #167076.

## User Impact

Scripts can pipe multiline UTF-8 prompts into Gateway-backed or embedded agent turns. Exact `-` reads stdin; use `./-` or an absolute path for a file named `-`. File and stdin input retain the 4 MiB limit, strict UTF-8, BOM removal, and blank-prompt rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bounded input reader now handles stdin alongside the descriptor-based file path. File handling still preserves symlinks, FIFOs, and procfs descriptors. The reader owns file/stdin validation, while the command validates inline messages. Extracting this responsibility keeps the oversized command from growing; command-boundary tests replace helper-only coverage. The owning CLI and agent-send docs explain the pipe convention and literal-dash escape.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the original implementation and investigation. Contributor commits and authorship are retained.

## Evidence

- Base regression: four stdin cases fail with `Message file not found: -` through `agentCliCommand`; the original CLI pipe fails the same way before dispatch. The current-main reader has the same determining code.
- Candidate: 65 command tests pass (one Linux-only procfs control skipped on macOS), including chunked BOM/Unicode, blank/malformed/oversized stdin, literal dash files, blank files, and the existing file/dispatch controls. Final combined command run: 47.61 s Vitest / 62.36 s wrapper, mostly compilation; the six input tests take under one second. CLI registration: 26 tests pass, 80.38 s cold run.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, diff checks, and line-cap checks pass. The changed-file check caught an intermediate inline implementation growing an oversized file; the final reader extraction passes both base and pre-commit growth checks.
- Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings. The cleanup pass retains one input owner, removes a duplicated file-open error handler, and avoids growing the existing command or its large test suite.
- LOC against integrated main: production +77/-57 (net +20), tests +109/-0, docs +13/-7; assertion baseline -1. Production growth is the bounded stdin branch and explicit input validation; no new flag, config, dependency, or public helper API is added. The earlier proposal was production net +11 / tests +55; the extra coverage now proves dispatch and rejection at the command boundary.

- Built head `31cdc3afb58a462c87b0acca390bb10b60cba8c9` and exercised `openclaw agent --agent main --message-file - --thinking off --json` with real stdin, an isolated Gateway/state directory, and the repository HTTP model fixture. Piped BOM/multiline Unicode, the ordinary file, and `./-` each completed with `STDIN_PROOF_OK`; the provider received the Unicode/multiline prompt. Blank, malformed UTF-8, and oversized stdin returned exit 1 with no additional primary-model requests (three successful requests total). All proof processes stopped cleanly. Build: 3m 16.5s.
- No paid-provider or external-channel round-trip was run; this proof uses the real CLI/Gateway/agent path with a deterministic local HTTP model.
- Local typechecks refused the shared dependency layout. The broad changed-file run also reported seven unused exports in unchanged files outside this PR; its earlier line-cap findings were repaired. Exact-head PR CI supplies the broad proof.

CI: [run 40584738935](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40584738935) caught a test-fixture TS2554 error: the shared success-reply helper requires response text. Commit `e48505117451df695a22f0f919b621b94dcffb2a` supplies it; production code is unchanged. All six focused input tests pass again (98.61s Vitest / 127.06s wrapper), targeted lint/format pass, and fresh independent P0–P2 review is clean. The earlier 65-test and live proofs remain applicable. Final [exact-head CI run 40593867339](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593867339) is green: all 35 executed jobs passed, with 30 intentional skips.

The earlier run also has the same five unrelated UI `eslint(curly)` errors as [scheduled main run 40578163761](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40578163761/job/122450734896); the file/line/rule/message diagnostics and both source blobs match. No unrelated UI repair or rerun is included.

Release-note context: ordinary `agent --message-file -` reads stdin; explicitly address a literal dash file as `./-` or an absolute path.

prs.title: improve(doctor): stop copying bundled plugin operation code on every Doctor contract load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` spends about 8 CPU-seconds per run copying bundled plugin code it never runs, even when there is nothing to repair. Deployments and CI that run Doctor before every Gateway start pay this each time.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` uses 11-16% less CPU and finishes 6-7 s sooner on a 4-CPU container. What Doctor checks, migrates and prints is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor loads each plugin's doctor contract through a setup module loader. For a bundled plugin that ships state-operation modules (today memory-core's `recall-operation-api`), binding that loader also captures the operation closure into a private plugin generation, which copies the files and links their dependencies. Doctor loads the contracts four times per run: three times on the main thread and once in the database engine inspection worker. Each capture costs about 1.7 s of main-thread time.

Doctor never uses that capture. Its migration contexts open plugin state stores without an operation source (`state-migrations.plugin-doctor-context.ts`), and `createPluginStateOperation` refuses a store that has no operation source. So nothing reached through a Doctor contract loader can run a plugin state operation.

The setup loader now takes `{ stateOperations: false }`, and only Doctor contract loading passes it. Those loaders skip `captureBundledPluginStateOperationModules`; the cache key includes the flag, so a setup instance that does need operations is never handed a loader without them. Gateway runtime, setup entries and other setup loaders are unchanged, and external plugins still capture their full package as before.

## Evidence

**Workload and acceptance rule (written before the runs):** `node /app/openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive` on images built from upstream's own Dockerfile (`OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS="slack codex"`), base `59498872202` against this branch. Each run used a fresh container on a 4-CPU cpuset with no network and a read-only external config. CPU is the container cgroup's `usage_usec` across all Doctor processes. There were four cases. **fresh**: an empty state dir. **fresh-again**: the same state, already migrated, so there is nothing to do. **released**: state from an older release that needs migration. **released-again**: that state after migration. Each arm had 5 samples, interleaved base/candidate (ABAB). Acceptance rule: the median CPU drops in every case, the ranges do not overlap, and no metric gets worse.

| Case | CPU-s base, median [range] | CPU-s this PR | Δ CPU | Wall s base → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh | 49.6 [48.3-51.1] | 41.8 [41.3-42.5] | −7.8 (−16%) | 34.1 → 28.0 |
| fresh-again (nothing to do) | 55.4 [55.0-56.1] | 47.6 [47.1-48.8] | −7.8 (−14%) | 43.7 → 37.3 |
| released (migration) | 64.1 [62.0-64.9] | 55.0 [54.7-59.4] | −9.1 (−14%) | 47.2 → 40.2 |
| released-again | 64.4 [63.2-65.4] | 57.2 [55.5-60.2] | −7.1 (−11%) | 51.5 → 45.3 |

- **Profile (base, fresh-again, `--cpu-prof` on every thread):** `loadPluginDoctorContractEntry` → `captureBundledPluginStateOperationModules` → `capturePluginGenerationArtifact` took 5.1 s on the main thread and 1.75 s in `doctor-database-engine-inspection.worker`. It was called from `detectLegacyStateMigrations`, the plugin state-migration run, and `preparePluginDoctorMigrationBackupResources`. An env-gated experiment that skipped this capture saved the same ~8-10 CPU-s before I wrote the scoped change.
- **Doctor output is unchanged.** For each of the 12 base/PR pairs, I normalized timestamps, ids and numbers and sorted the lines. The outputs are identical, apart from Doctor's own "(Ns elapsed)" slow-step progress lines, which the faster run prints less often. Every run exited 0. The released cases cover an upgrade from older-release state.
- **Upgrade from latest stable (`ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.10.8`, digest `sha256:82b6ce63…`).** I ran two arms, one for base `59498872202` and one for this PR (`84901b53dd8`). Each arm used a fresh volume and the same config, and ran these steps in order:
  1. The 2026.10.8 Gateway started and reached `/readyz`.
  2. 2026.10.8 `doctor --fix` ran.
  3. The target build's `doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran.
  4. The target build's Gateway started on the upgraded state.

  Both Doctor runs exited 0 in both arms, and both target Gateways reached `/readyz`. After each step I copied every SQLite database and read its schema version and per-table row counts. The two arms match exactly at every step: 102 tables after stable, then 106 after the target Doctor across `state/openclaw.sqlite` (schema 20 → 35), `client/credentials.sqlite` and `control/services.sqlite`, then 109 after the target Gateway. Stable's data carries over identically in both arms, including the device identity, user profile, cron jobs and config health. The arms differ only in the hash of `openclaw.json` and the migration-run file names. Both already differ right after the stable steps, before any target code runs, because they hold run timestamps and UUIDs.
- **Regression test:** a test loaded a bundled plugin's doctor contract next to a `state-operation-api.mjs` and asserted that the setup instance has no captured operation source. It failed on base (`expected { resolve: [Function resolve] } to be undefined`) and passed with the change. I removed it in the second commit because the tree is over the test-lines ceiling, and the openclaw-performance skill keeps perf proof in the PR. The test is in this branch's first commit (`5de1c38d01e`) if a maintainer wants it back.
- **Neighbouring tests pass:** 15 files, 208 tests. These are the doctor-contract-registry suites, `plugin-state-operation-source`, the `setup-registry` suites, `loader.async-preparation`, `plugin-module-generation.disposal`, `state-migrations.caller-mode.plugin-execution` and `provider-discovery.runtime`.
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, and `oxfmt` is clean on the touched files.

prs.title: feat: make busy-session messages automatic with coherent security presets
prs.body:
Related: #184846, #185381

## What Problem This Solves

Busy-session messages can be refused or require a manual `/followup` resend, while execution and steering defaults express inconsistent trust assumptions.

## User Impact

Default-personal messages steer when compatible and otherwise queue quietly for a requester-owned turn, without automatic queue-status spam or a resend requirement. Explicit strict rejection remains available.

`security.preset: "personal" | "corporate"` supplies coherent defaults across sandboxing, approvals, managed files, steering, conversation reach, and DM routing. Personal is the default trusted-operator/full-access posture; corporate selects session sandboxes and stricter steering/reach defaults. Explicit source and agent/session settings retain precedence; mandatory host, role, access, and approval floors are never granted or bypassed.

**Tradeoffs:** collaboration retains incumbent execution authority—not a permission intersection or causal tool attribution. Shared history remains shared. Corporate is configurable, not compliance certification or hostile-tenant isolation; sandbox networking does not cover every host tool/plugin/browser request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing requester-owned queue instead of dropping input. Expand presets only at runtime configuration materialization, removing the competing persisted steering-default writer from Doctor and fresh configuration paths.

Existing explicit steering booleans, including older Doctor-persisted values, remain unchanged; unset an override to follow the preset. Runtime expansions are not persisted as authored settings. Corporate changes future DM routing keys without deleting or moving prior history. No live configuration, identity grants, public shares, authentication, or deployment is changed.

The documentation compares primary sources for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, distinguishing approval UX, isolation, and managed policy floors.

Credit: @obviyus identified the dropped-message workflow and proposed automatic queue fallback in #184846. This work adds quiet handling, explicit strict refusal, and the broader defaults requested by @steipete. It retains @jalehman’s landed attempt-scoped preparation/adoption owner from #185381 rather than maintaining our competing identity-only exception; the distinct before-first-call regression remains.

prs.title: fix(agents): recover deferred tool calls through native correction
prs.body:
Fixes #183085.

## What Problem This Solves

A model that prints a call to an available deferred tool can finish with an empty, incomplete turn because terminal detection considers only the tools directly offered to the model.

## User Impact

The runner recognizes the deferred call and requests its existing bounded native correction. The model must then invoke the native tool interface; recognizing text does not authorize executing a deferred tool from that text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal detector now recognizes both live and available deferred names. Structured text promotion retains its live-only allowlist. The existing parser already recognizes the wrapped call, so this fix adds no XML grammar or parallel recovery path. Documentation describes the correction and repeated-call failure behavior.

Thanks to @Linux2010 for the report and original fix. The maintainer follow-up adds a bounded streaming parity table and consolidates existing test setup without removing the alias, prefix, or terminal-result assertions.

## Evidence

- Real CLI reproduction with a deterministic local provider: main made two requests, never requested native correction, and ended with `incomplete_turn`. The repaired head makes three requests: native correction, a native dispatch with a real skill result, and `BRIEFING-LOADED` (27.956 seconds).
- Production promotion plus visible projection: 72 adversarial documents, 5,569 schedules, 17,570 prefix checks; zero mismatches. Includes every two-chunk split, one-/four-character chunking, wrapped calls, partial syntax, ordinary prose, inline/fenced/indented examples, and CRLF. The committed 14-row table also verifies no deferred execution and exact streamed/done/result source preservation.
- Full canonical projector: 311 documents, 42,922 schedules, 202,314 prefix checks including empty appends; zero mismatches. Temporary composition with #184529 and #185293 additionally passed 3,096 delivered-message schedules with no hidden-call leaks or lost visible bytes, while preserving the XML optimization's work counts.
- The detector regression fails on the main implementation when the deferred name is available (one failure, one pass). Final head passes all 103 tests across five focused files, including the runner and prompt-prefix checks (537.89 seconds including cold compilation and cleanup).
- Local native Ollama `qwen2.5:7b` answered through `pnpm openclaw agent exec` on both main and the repaired head. The final basic control disables tools and returns the exact requested marker in 36.574 seconds; the scripted fixture separately proves native tool recovery. A full-catalog control completed but pursued an unrelated portal instead of the marker, so it is not claimed as an instruction-compliance pass.
- Scoped lint/test types and baseline ratchets pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2 with no findings on this head. Full exact-head build passed (1,016.44 seconds including declarations and artifact checks). Exact-head CI completed with the inherited lint failure recorded below.

Production: +4/-1 lines (net +3); tests: +129/-123 (net +6); documentation: +7. No prompt/tool definition change. Validation is local macOS; the scripted provider proof and real local-model control are separate evidence.


CI note: exact-head run [40581447707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40581447707) is complete. prs.title: fix(ui): prevent hidden-run read floods after reconnecting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: returning from airplane mode or a spotty connection can flood the Gateway with read acknowledgements when the open chat has many hidden subagent runs, delaying other session changes and messages.

## User Impact

User impact: opening or marking a parent chat read acknowledges its hidden runs in batches of at most 100, with one request in flight, and reconnecting again does not repeat successful acknowledgements. New manual unread reminders survive acknowledgement of an older snapshot. No user action or migration is required.

Release-note context: Control UI avoids bursts of hidden subagent read requests after reconnecting on unreliable networks.

Accepted edge cases: serial batches take additional round trips on slow connections. Failed implicit reads remain silent and may be retried on a later read or reconnect; explicit actions report their failures together. Failed runs, active attention requests, manual unread reminders, and runs the viewer cannot modify remain unread. Missing or incomplete row events still use the existing paced roster-refresh owner; this change does not add a list read after each successful batch or a global limit across separate clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat pane launched an unawaited patch for every unread hidden run; the organizer used the same fan-out through `Promise.all`. Both now use one sessions capability operation that serializes protocol-sized batches, preserves each target's session identity and conditional unread-marker guard, and retains the chat pane's revision deduplication. Successful acknowledgements settle through the existing optimistic owner and admitted Gateway row events. The server validates the conditional guard against each complete target patch, and its existing slow-patch diagnostic adds only bounded target counts and sorted mutation names.

The simplification pass removed mandatory post-acknowledgement roster reads and synthetic refresh failures. The read owner is 125 lines versus 150 in the first version; the complete handwritten production delta is +159 lines versus +165 before that reduction. This final pass shares repeated reconnect request filtering (239 → 233 E2E lines), preserves every assertion, and names the pending-read deduplication regression explicitly. Remaining growth provides the shared serial owner, per-target wire guard, and bounded diagnostic.

## Evidence

The bundled-browser/mock-Gateway regression was red on base. With 150 unread hidden runs, parent viewing, reconnect admission, and organizer mark-read each changed from **150 individual patches / 0 batches / peak 150 in flight** to **0 individual patches / 2 batches (100 + 50) / peak 1**. A second real disconnect/reconnect cycle adds **zero** acknowledgements. Admitted row events settle all 150 reads without an additional implicit-read roster request.

Live context: the burst was observed on a production Gateway, where one Control UI connection sent ~136 individual `sessions.patch` requests within ~100 ms about 35 s after reconnecting while its session list reloaded; some failed with worker-capacity errors and the rest queued behind the agent-database writer for up to ~24 s, slowing other users' patches and sends. The server-side guard is proven through the real `sessions.patchMany` handler tests below; the fan-out is proven at the bundled-browser boundary above. The new slow-patch diagnostic (`targets=<n> fields=<sorted names>`, no keys or values) makes any future burst attributable from Gateway logs after deploy.

Focused checks passed before this final test-only cleanup: 120 related UI unit tests, 12 browser E2E tests, 19 diagnostic/handler tests, and 30 protocol-schema/server guard tests. They cover concurrent callers, stale access, optimistic rollback, partial failures, manual markers before and after acknowledgement, server-side conditional no-ops, invalid target combinations, and diagnostic bounds. Protocol generation/determinism checks, targeted UI/Gateway typechecks, scoped lint/format, and diff checks passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Final cleanup validation passed: the pane deduplication regression (1 test), all three parent-view/reconnect/organizer browser cases (59.90 seconds), targeted UI chat/E2E test typechecks, scoped lint/format, and diff checks. Production behavior is unchanged by this cleanup, so existing rig evidence can be reused once supplied. There is no visual layout change.

prs.title: fix(update): name the next step when update repair leaves the Gateway stopped
prs.body:
Related: #153094

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` reports success while the managed Gateway stays stopped after a failed update that refused rollback over migrated state.

## User Impact

User impact: when repair finishes and leaves a stopped managed Gateway stopped, the run records and prints a warning naming `openclaw gateway start` (and `openclaw gateway status --deep`), so the install no longer stays down behind a green "OpenClaw updated" line. Repair still never starts a Gateway that an earlier run or the operator stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

A failed update whose Doctor ran migrations refuses code-only rollback (`state-migrated-no-rollback`, or a refused database rollback), stops the Gateway, and points at `openclaw update repair`. Repair's Doctor maintenance intentionally restores only its own stop, so the already-stopped Gateway stayed down with no outcome reported. The decision for a Gateway Doctor did not stop now lives in the restoration owner (`resolveUnstoppedGatewayRestoration`, same conditions as before) and, only for a public repair run (`lifecycle.ownsUpdateRepairRun`), returns the warning. Legacy update parents that restart their own stop are unchanged and get no warning.

Rejected alternative: having repair start the Gateway. The repair docs make operator stops and data-risk refusals stay stopped; changing that is a product decision, so this PR only makes the outcome visible.

Production LOC: +72 / -28 (the extraction moves the existing 28-line branch into the restoration module; net growth is the new warning, its gate, and the lifecycle getter). Tests: +21 / -7.

## Evidence

Published-driver × candidate cells on a Linux Crabbox (AWS c7a.8xlarge, systemd user Gateway, Node 24.22.1), with the candidate's live post-install Doctor forced to exit 71 after it finished migrating (rehearsal Doctors untouched):

- 2026.9.9 driver → main `161c376d51b8` candidate: update fails with `Database rollback could not finish; keep the Gateway stopped` (state schema 19 → 35), Gateway inactive. Unpatched main `openclaw update repair`: exit 0 in 79 s, "OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.7", Gateway still inactive, no mention of it.
- Same cell with this patch: repair exit 0 in 73 s, `warning:finalize:doctor:5` = "Gateway service is stopped and remains stopped; … Start it with `openclaw gateway start` …", also listed by `openclaw update status`; running that command brought `/readyz` to ready/coreReady. (The box built the first revision of this patch; the follow-up only moved the unchanged decision into the restoration module and is covered by the tests below.)

Local: new `doctor-maintenance.settlement` case is red on main (`expected [] to deeply equal [StringMatching]`) and green here; 8 maintenance/finalize suites, 149 passed / 1 skipped; `tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt clean. Codex autoreview (local, base `161c376d51b8`): scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.97)".

Closes #185044. Thanks @travellingsoldier85 for the report.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes premature compaction after tool rounds renew temporary Anthropic runtime context, even when the effective model context remains below the configured byte guard.

## User Impact

Long tool-driven turns keep their useful history without unnecessary compaction. Stored transcripts remain append-only, and raw storage and history-read bounds stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The byte-pressure owner now discounts only runtime-context body bytes proven expired by the current direct Anthropic API-key route. It retains envelope bytes and all history outside the bounded read. Preflight, manual compaction, the retry latch, and fallback-window selection use the same accounting semantics. OAuth, proxy routes, persistent updates, and ordinary history retain their existing byte charge.

## Evidence

Reproduced through an isolated macOS Gateway using a deterministic Anthropic-compatible SSE relay: a 30-KB ingress envelope and ten real `read` tool rounds. The stored carriers and serialized wire payload remain intact.

| Measurement | Base | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Raw active bytes | 399,239 | 399,144 |
| Bytes used by compaction guard | 399,239 | 92,354 |
| Configured guard | 204,800 | 204,800 |
| Summarizer requests / saved compaction boundaries | 4 / 1 | 0 / 0 |

The fixed ten-tool turn completed in 5.027s. Its request carried 341,828 serialized message bytes and 34,168 effective bytes after `clear_at`. A 0.139s follow-up retained all ten tool results; all 49 prior transcript rows were byte-identical. Real Ollama `qwen3:8b` inference also passed through the Gateway before and after the fix (one read, expected terminal reply; 11.900s / 4.125s). These timings are observations, not a performance comparison.

Focused tests: 88 passed across eight files/five shards (862.96s, including cold compilation); the final fixture cleanup also passes the six-case regression rerun (115.68s). The new preflight regression fails on the original code and passes with the fix; controls cover non-clearing API routes, OAuth, proxies, persistent updates, and genuine user history. Production and touched-test types, lint, formatting, docs links, and all seven affected ratchets pass. Full build passes (15m42s). Isolated Codex review is clean at P0–P2.

Production LOC: +215/-26 (net +189); tests: +206/-1 (net +205). The added bounded reader shares current-route classification and conservative accounting across the pressure consumers; the same expiration classifier serves fallback sizing. Storage retains its existing raw counters.

Limitations: macOS local proof only; no live Anthropic API call. Rows outside the bounded accounting read remain conservatively charged. Wire bandwidth and disk footprint are unchanged.


Hosted reviews completed on `49a326c`: GitHub Codex and [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186304#issuecomment-6453643299) reported no findings; ClawSweeper lists no before-merge items and rates the supplied proof sufficient.

CI at handoff (2026-10-27 21:33 UTC): [run 40581738226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40581738226) has 20 successful checks and 28 queued jobs, with no failed checks. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` remains pending. Landing awaits that gate.

prs.title: perf: avoid redundant update Doctor close probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Update Doctor repeats database-generation and custody checks when each migrated SQLite handle closes, even though its session already publishes the final state of every captured database it opened. A later companion migration can also reject that session's own changes.

## User Impact

Updates perform fewer database probes. First-open validation, untouched-database refusal, migration exclusion, credential authority checks, and automatic rollback receipts remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the migration-specific native-close observer and use the existing opened-path fact for companion admission, matching the session settlement introduced in #185789. Keep per-operation publication and credential provenance, native locks, created-file checks, and the separate handoff/lease store unchanged.

The accepted edge remains the one documented in #177831: raw outside writes to databases opened during the Doctor session may be included in its settled postimage. Captured databases the session never opened must still match.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before native measurement: one matched synthetic native-update count pair on macOS, using the same current-main installed driver for both arms and distinct baseline/candidate descendants. Each arm runs a cold update and a subsequent warm update through both finalization Doctor passes, exact target activation, and real loopback Gateway readiness. Report each full Doctor pass's SQL/requests and canary/final Gateway MAIN separately. Win requires zero close-triggered generation/authority work, fewer full-pass SQL statements, valid final receipts, and no added worker-request work or runtime Gateway MAIN. Any adverse count cell of 20% or more stops the change. This is n=1 count evidence; no latency or timing claim.

Maintainer-approved landing condition: land on the baseline-red/candidate-green owner work-count regression and green exact-head CI. The matched native count pair is a required post-merge follow-up, currently waiting on a shared package-store operation. Report full-pass SQL, requests and Gateway MAIN when it completes; immediately escalate any Gateway MAIN increase or adverse count cell of 20% or more for a revert decision. No native savings claim is made before that result.

The owner regression is red on the baseline: native close performs an unwanted generation read, and a companion already opened by the session is rejected. The consolidated candidate cases pass: no close-triggered generation/authority work, valid final receipt, changed opened-companion admission, and changed untouched-companion refusal. All 18 non-retirement cases pass across the focused runs. The existing native-parent retirement/credential case passed; the worker-parent case hit the unchanged 120-second limit on both the candidate and exact base (reported 139/144 seconds versus 165 seconds). No timeout or retry changes are included. Prior-head CI [job 122440037186](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40575058637/job/122440037186) passed all 20 attribution-owner cases, including native and worker retirement, both no-close-probe modes, untouched-companion refusal, created-family and credential coverage. The containing group passed 2 files / 38 tests with exit 0; this resolves the local worker-parent proof gap without changing its deadline. Two isolated production reviews were clean; a further isolated review of the final test-only consolidation was also clean. All three completed source verification with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Production: +2/−39 lines (net −37); tests: +168/−168 (net 0). All original boundary cases remain; consolidation removes redundant setup and combines the new assertions into existing custody cases. Formatting and whitespace checks pass. Production Knip has the exact same single unused-export finding on base and candidate (`extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts: runPrompt`); the reviewed-head all-exports scan also exactly matches base, with only `ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.test-support.ts: settleActivity` reported. Neither scan adds a finding. Local type-aware lint cannot admit declarations from the required external virtual store (`Declaration input escapes checkout`); the exact-head CI lint/type/declaration jobs cover that environment gap.

Native counts remain pending. Exact-head CI [run 40593068545](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593068545) passed for `516f07d006b6f40ecf20d296e479711f0d405e43`: 43 checks passed, 26 skipped, zero failed/pending. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards actually executed and passed ([1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593068545/job/122503257346), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593068545/job/122503257975), [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593068545/job/122503257506)). The [owner job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40593068545/job/122503257811) again passed all 20 attribution cases (combined 2 files / 38 tests). Lint, production/test types, source contracts and architecture checks passed; Madge reports zero cycles, SQLite T1 is 168→168, compatibility 15→15, and the dialect ratchet has no growth. Earlier corrected-head [run 40590282500](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40590282500) passed all three PostgreSQL shards and the test-cleanup lint correction; its only lint errors were five inherited UI diagnostics. Main's fix for those diagnostics was then merged cleanly. The integration changes neither file in this PR; no inherited-failure waiver is currently requested.

The matched native proof uses common installed driver `364c0d4ebcd400ee4285eb989ed60d2a8b000b93`, identical-tree baseline descendant `5145cd649ba992e59e7b22caf24072548d36d5a2`, and candidate target `b6193a123a6676fc9f7a418061851de5e1412270`. The changed production file is byte-identical at the reviewed, measured and integrated heads. Main integration also brought unrelated Doctor heartbeat and port-memory changes, so the measured target is reported separately; whole-tree equivalence to the integrated head is not claimed.

The test-only promise cleanup correction uses explicit nested `try/finally`, passes four focused regression cases, and has a clean isolated delta review. Open-PR overlap index currently finds no other PR touching either changed file.
