prs.title: fix(config): persist memory search provider/fallback in canonical casing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory.search.provider` and `memory.search.fallback` are persisted with whatever casing the author typed (for example `"None"` or `"NoNe"`), so the value written to `openclaw.json` does not match the value the runtime actually resolves, and the same setting can mean different things depending on how it was typed.

## User Impact

User impact: a `memory.search.provider` value written through the config write path is now stored in the same canonical lowercase form the config schema resolves at runtime, so the file on disk and the effective setting can no longer disagree. This is a persisted-file change: the first write that sets these fields normalizes their casing on disk. Providers, adapters, and validation rules are untouched, and the case-insensitive sentinel `"none"` keeps resolving exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config schema already canonicalizes `memory.search.provider` / `memory.search.fallback` with `normalizeOptionalLowercaseString` when it parses a config, so the runtime always sees a lowercase value. The write path, however, persisted the authored projection without applying the same rule, which left a disk/runtime disagreement: the file could say `"None"` while the runtime resolved `"none"`.

The change adds a small seam at the config persistence point that applies the **existing** normalization rule to just the two fields, and only to the slots the write actually authored. It deliberately does not introduce a second casing rule, does not rewrite the rest of the config, and does not tighten startup or runtime validation.

### Persisted-config casing compatibility

This is the compatibility-relevant part of the change, so it is spelled out explicitly:

- **Only two slots are ever touched**: root `memory.search.provider` / `memory.search.fallback`, and the same pair on a single agent entry under `agents.entries.<id>`. Nothing else in the file is rewritten.
- **Only values this write authored are canonicalized.** The seam is anchored to the write's explicit value source, not to the file. A legacy value that the write did not set keeps its exact original bytes.
- **Whole-roster writes are refused.** A write that replaces `agents`, `agents.entries`, or `agents.list` as a whole does not canonicalize any provider inside it, so replacing a roster cannot silently rewrite members the author never set.
- **Sentinel and `auto` values are unaffected semantically.** `"none"`, `"auto"`, and the `fallback` slot are already case-insensitive at resolution time; they are now stored in the same lowercase form rather than in the author's casing.
- **Blank values are left alone.** A whitespace-only value is stored as authored and continues to resolve as unset; removing the key is the unset path's job, not a casing rule's.
- **Env-var templates are never re-cased.** A value containing an env reference (for example `${MEM_PROVIDER}`) is skipped entirely, so the referenced variable name is never altered.
- **The runtime-facing lookup is unchanged.** Adapter lookup stays a case-sensitive exact match; the change only aligns what is written to disk with what the config schema already resolves. A third-party adapter that registers a non-lowercase id behaves exactly as it did before this change.

## Evidence

An independent QA pass (single round, post-freeze) reviewed the exact committed bytes and returned **PASS-WITH-NOTES, 0 blockers**. The reviewer reproduced the base-commit baseline independently, confirmed the new regression test is sensitive to the fix (it fails when the seam is reverted, so it is not tautological), and confirmed the seam's rule is byte-for-byte the schema's rule.

**Targeted verification**

- New persistence regression test — 2 passed (root case, per-agent case). Reverting only the config-write file makes both fail (`expected 'None' to be 'none'`, `expected 'NoNe' to be 'none'`); restoring it returns 2/2.
- 5 config-write suites — 5 files passed, 171 tests passed.
- Typecheck — clean, no diagnostics.

**Full `src/config` shard, candidate vs base commit**

| | Test files | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate | `2 failed, 499 passed, 2 skipped` (503) | `2 failed, 5493 passed, 9 skipped` (5504) |
| Base | `2 failed, 497 passed, 2 skipped` (501) | `2 failed, 5480 passed, 9 skipped` (5491) |

The **same two files fail on both sides, with identical assertions and error signatures**, and neither is in this diff:

1. `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-excluded-rows.test.ts` — a UTF-8 vs UTF-16 row-filter expectation. The reviewer reproduced it independently at the base commit with all candidate files reverted (`1 failed | 13 passed`), and with the candidate (`1 failed | 14 passed`).
2. `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-memory.test.ts` — `PluginStateStoreError: ... OpenClaw state database lifecycle is retired`. It passes in isolation with the candidate and fails only inside the full shard, on base and candidate alike.

The `+2` file delta is exactly the two new test files, and the skipped count is identical on both sides. **No candidate-caused test failure exists in the shard.**

### Open review notes (6, all non-blocking)

These are disclosed in full so reviewers can judge them rather than discover them.

1. **Ancestor explicit paths also canonicalize.** An ancestor write (for example `agents.entries.<id>` or `memory.search` as a subtree) canonicalizes a provider value carried inside that subtree, even when that value was carried over from the previous file rather than authored in this write. It is bounded to the two authorized slots, never a whole-config rewrite, and semantically inert because the runtime already lowercases the same field. Same mechanism that makes an explicitly-set root provider canonical.
2. **Unresolved env templates still differ in memory.** The config schema lowercases an *unresolved* template (`${MEM_PROVIDER}` → `${mem_provider}`) in the parsed config, so file and runtime still disagree for unresolved templates. This seam correctly leaves the file alone; resolved templates are unaffected (`MEM_PROVIDER=NoNe` loads as `none`). The schema file predates this change.
3. **Blank values stay as authored.** A whitespace-only provider stays on disk as authored while the runtime resolves it as unset. Deliberate: this seam's job is canonical casing, and removing a key belongs to the unset path.
4. **Strict validation rejects an unknown provider id even on unrelated writes.** A write that does not touch the provider field can still fail if the config contains a provider id that is not registered. This was confirmed **not** to be caused by this change: with the seam call removed, the same write still fails with the same message. Realistic ids (`voyage`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`, `none`, `auto`, `gemini`) all write successfully. The validation rule itself predates this change.
5. **The new test file covers 2 of the behaviors in this diff.** There is no case for the `fallback` slot, for env-template preservation, for whole-roster refusal, or for a root-scope byte-identity assertion. The reviewer verified each of those behaviors directly, so this is a suite-completeness gap rather than a behavior gap.
6. **Mixed-case third-party adapter ids are lowercased.** The seam lowercases any explicitly-set provider string. This matches what the config schema already resolves at runtime, so it removes a file/runtime disagreement rather than creating one; the case-sensitive exact-match adapter lookup is unchanged, and all in-tree adapter ids are already lowercase.

### Scope of this diff

This branch carries 11 files: the persistence seam (`src/config/io.write-memory-search-provider.ts` + its call site in `src/config/io.write.ts`), the new regression test, and the config-schema and plugin-registry changes that define the canonical provider/fallback shape the seam reuses.

One note for reviewers: the branch is based on the `v2026.10.7` release line, where all touched files are byte-identical to the base commit, so the diff applies without conflict and introduces no unrelated churn.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.10-beta.4

### Highlights

### Changes

### Fixes

- Automations: preserve authenticated operator authority for explicit same-conversation scheduled follow-ups, including one-shot `next_check` rearming, while retaining role, session, cancellation, target, and tool-policy revocation boundaries. (#176422) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Gateway security: keep an environment-referenced `hooks.token` out of agent host-exec and CLI child environments at startup and across config reloads, while preserving explicit per-command overrides. (#179199) Thanks @VACInc and @RomneyDa.
- Memory Wiki: preserve human-authored Notes when OKF concept pages are re-imported or removed from the producer bundle, including changed producer content and legacy pages without a marked Notes slot. (#175707, #179657; related #175700) Thanks @YangManBOBO and @RomneyDa.
- Claude CLI: keep the native Claude session and its context when subagent completions or channel turns run in a Control UI-started session, instead of reseeding from saved history each time. (#178955; fixes #178953) Thanks @Marvinthebored and @RomneyDa.
- Model catalogs: honor a configured primary account pin when deciding model readiness, so native Claude CLI models no longer appear as missing auth when the selected token profile is ready. (#178522; related #178502) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @RomneyDa, and @eduardonunesfreire-rgb.
- Backup and restore: preserve supported legacy exec-approval allowlists when sanitizing snapshots instead of replacing them with deny-all; malformed policies remain fail-closed. (#164297) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666, @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @dor-sr, @cristianoc, and @brucemccurdy.
- Linux companion: persist each saved Gateway dashboard's private browser identity across restarts, while removing storage for deleted Gateways so re-added endpoints pair as fresh devices. (#158908) Thanks @dor-sr, @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @wangmiao0668000666, and @brucemccurdy.
- Agent database lifecycle: keep peer readers and borrowers alive when maintenance or PostgreSQL opening is refused, preserve the original refusal and clean-restart seal, and retain pre-dispatch recovery behavior when a worker generation disappears. (#175987, #163258, #179320) Thanks @RomneyDa, @shanselman, @dor-sr, @wangmiao0668000666, @brucemccurdy, @goutamadwant, and @hawkit.
- macOS bundled Gateway: show the actual installed Gateway version, keep failed or incomplete recovery actionable, and prevent stale or pending update receipts from blocking a valid repair. (#181389) Thanks @shanselman, @RomneyDa, @dor-sr, @wangmiao0668000666, and @brucemccurdy.
- Model refresh: let explicit catalog refreshes use their existing extended discovery budget through HTTP acquisition while ordinary preparation remains bounded. (#177313) Thanks @jlapenna and @RomneyDa.
- Webhooks and scheduled scripts: classify trusted immediate producers as events, retain each webhook's own automation scope, and refresh disposed script hooks before execution without replaying completed effects. (#172775, #177825, #178904) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jlapenna, and @jalehman.
- Runtime security: backport patched embedded runtimes to the 2026.10.10 line. (#181074) Thanks @RomneyDa and @joshavant.
- Update finalization: keep a verified healthy target successful when a recognized late restart-health or legacy-wrapper maintenance step fails, while authority, data-at-risk, deferred-admission, and unknown failures remain fatal. (#181166; fixes #181020) Thanks @najef1979-code.
- Package update recovery: automatically settle verified interrupted publications or retire untouched preparations, preserve the installed candidate and original Gateway recovery evidence, and keep live update ownership and restart authority fenced. (#181307; fixes #181235) Thanks @agroman1993.
- CLI config writes and setup with a running Gateway: `openclaw config set`, `config unset`, and `openclaw setup` now send their change through the running Gateway as one `config.patch` instead of refusing, with the same result as an offline write, no restart while reload is off, and a success acknowledgement when the Gateway accepts a restart, so Windows companion setup completes again. (#182951, #184194, #184392, #184532, #185109) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Codex native subagents: unblock parent replies after native children finish, are interrupted, or complete follow-ups; stop resurrecting undeliverable child completions; replay completed grandchildren correctly after Gateway restarts; keep native tool declarations across completion turns; and let Stop succeed after parent thread reuse. releases.name: openclaw 2026.10.8
releases.body:
## 2026.10.8

### Highlights

- **Updates that finish and recover:** an ordinary post-update Doctor failure restarts the Gateway instead of leaving it stopped, an orphaned maintenance worker no longer blocks every CLI command and Gateway start, and updates no longer abort on ACL filesystems, Windows pnpm optional-dependency links, pnpm 10 global installs, debug console logging, or a missing legacy OAuth directory. (#180668, #181695, #181141, #181596, #181456, #182850, #180174) Thanks @hannesrudolph, @SMF12138, @rayluo88, @PonySlayer28, and @VN77-77VN.
- **Gateway service installs on every desktop:** macOS recovers a loaded launchd registration whose plist was deleted, Linux installs under the Ubuntu default umask create a private state directory instead of being refused, and the macOS updater waits for the serving Gateway to release its databases before Doctor runs. (#180390, #179538, #182055) Thanks @avnishkirnalli and @XiaoPengYouCode.
- **Conversations keep accepting messages:** killed runs release their restart-recovery fence, interrupted and just-accepted child sessions recover after a Gateway restart, inbound messages stop retrying forever when the reply runtime cannot publish, and the Control UI forgotten-send retry delivers the reply instead of an authoring error. (#181992, #178888, #181871, #181300, #182219) Thanks @najef1979-code, @handcraftrc-pixel, @sukhdeepjohar, and @teddashh.
- **Startup and database resilience:** startup work no longer inherits a closed SQLite reader scope, so models, chat metadata and channel replies stay available; transient lock contention during agent database startup is retried; and model catalogs stay available during skill runs. (#182615, #182446, #182385)
- **Security hardening:** exec allowlist mode requires approval for `test -v` operand expansion, generic node invoke refuses browser proxy commands, sandboxed spawned children cannot run host CLI backends, the secret egress proxy rejects distrusted eMudhra chains, Fish Audio and Gradium errors no longer expose API keys, and deeply nested Tlon content can no longer stall the channel. (#180880, #179880, #178742, #179249, #178877, #177536) Thanks @eleqtrizit and @joshavant.
- **Windows exec and plugins:** agent exec works under S4U scheduled tasks while Store PowerShell is installed, native plugins load on machines with Endpoint DLP, and Doctor recovers dangling dependency junctions and plugins on another filesystem. (#182898, #179949, #179549, #179445) Fixes #182652 Thanks @RomneyDa, @tre1d, @coaiMax, @paulcam206, @JIRBOY, and @ceckert.
- **Provider and model continuity:** Codex turns keep their budget with older runtime plugins instead of silently falling back, Codex native child inference works after startup, OpenAI OAuth works with stale catalogs, Anthropic PDF analysis works with setup-token OAuth, a timed-out MCP session close no longer fails the next turn, and CLI history owner changes stop instead of silently replaying on another provider. (#182995, #176311, #181356, #178420, #182189, #180075) Fixes #181619 Thanks @RomneyDa, @kip-claw, @enki, @sasan1200, @sunlit-deng, @khensthoth, @aniketkrs, @goslingmanagment, @wr-web, and @teddashh.

### Changes

- **Fresh OpenAI setup:** first-run model metadata no longer restricts the model picker to one model. (#175945) Thanks @matthematics1137 and @jb-dev1.

### Fixes

- **Channel accounts:** default Slack, Google Chat, X, Nextcloud Talk and Zalo accounts keep starting and keep their secrets after a named account is added. (#176267, #180450, #182608) Thanks @555aaditya, @progerjkd, and @masatohoshino.
- **Slack:** an isolated `invalid_auth` is retried before a socket-mode channel is disabled, and silent relay network drops reconnect. (#181056, #182368) Thanks @mushuiyu886 and @marns.
- **Matrix, Twitch, Zalo, iMessage and Feishu delivery:** ordinary Matrix messages are no longer treated as text commands, Twitch sends normalize channel targets, Zalo DMs with URLs are handled, iMessage recovers after the Messages bridge dies, and Feishu quick-action cards send again. (#179506, #178480, #178938, #180900, #79832) Thanks @xiaopan-xydt, @doomy, @HeZ2z, @Takhoffman, @zzrs-xxxr, @namchamvinhcuu, and @xiabee.
- **Agent runs and providers:** heartbeat loops stop when background commands finish, temporary Codex probe workers no longer accumulate, Codex native turns stay alive during host work, Claude CLI turns no longer stall 15 minutes when stream output hits its limit, provider stream errors surface immediately, and session admission races no longer trigger model fallback. (#179060, #167390, #181839, #159931, #117397, #179347) Fixes #178937, #181805, and #178000 Thanks @maxdjohnson, @sunlit-deng, @Terwox, @AINCHORS, @robertmsale, and @davidcittadini.
- **Voice and meetings:** Discord realtime voice consults initialize their runtime, voice calls use the configured agent model, and long meeting talk-back replies keep their audio. (#179462, #181451, #178254) Thanks @shoaibulhaque, @yagizkus, @potoior, @BeyonceBot, and @sukhdeepjohar.
- **Remote access and history:** Tailscale Serve and Funnel recover after tailscaled restarts, and cron history stays readable after provider changes. (#180081, #181311) Thanks @enki, @saariuslystoned, and @xtimor.
- **Doctor repairs:** retained transcripts verify after heading repairs, and repair keeps the Codex host compaction model. (#179089, #179914) Thanks @mrsavingsblogspot-rgb and @LiuwqGit.
- **Plugins and nodes:** older plugin debounce callbacks keep working, computer use accepts input results from older Mac nodes, and Memory Wiki keeps user Notes when OKF concepts disappear. (#118011, #137755, #179657)
- **Secrets and hooks:** the 1Password secret provider accepts group-writable OpenClaw files, and concurrent session-memory captures no longer overwrite each other. (#181127, #181081) Thanks @jalehman, @jason-allen-oneal, and @yetval.
- **Doctor recovery messages:** when Doctor cannot restore a Gateway it stopped, it prints the failure and how to start the Gateway. (#181941)
- **Codex native children and replies:** completed or undeliverable child completions no longer replay or wedge parents, replies unblock after native children finish, are interrupted, or complete follow-ups, final answers survive transient retries, settled turns without a mirrored prompt finalize, native tool declarations stay stable, queued chats recover after plugin reloads, submitted steering commits before terminal release, and Codex accepts managed loopback proxy defaults. (#173018, #175246, #177577, #179099, #179050, #183286, #181779, #183077, #182104, #184062, #183232) Thanks @quqi1599, @Stronggenetics, @linancn, @wtfichigo, @mmartoccia, @Marvinthebored, @sukhdeepjohar, @jjjhenriksen, @aatreya, @ermaxinc, and @RomneyDa.
- **Claude CLI sessions:** unrelated native tasks no longer hold the final answer, parent replies finish after nested background agents, a stopped first turn keeps its conversation, room events no longer reset sessions, operators can keep native Agent and Workflow tools, resumed sessions see conversation updates, and Claude CLI models stay available with saved subscriptions. (#170322, #182267, #181966, #182273, #183765, #183059, #179203) Thanks @cassthebandit, @VACInc, @goslingmanagment, @holgergruenhagen, @xiaopan-xydt, @Marvinthebored, @scarabone, @atomsmasher81, @josh-cornelius, and @teddashh.
- **Subagents and agent turns:** model fallback stops after local runtime faults, recovered child results deliver after session reuse, private completion receipts reconcile after a restart, parents keep waiting for active collectors, batched tool calls settle before `sessions_yield`, delayed `sessions_send` replies are no longer cut at 4,096 characters, turns finish after tool-result recovery, messages sent during transcript rebuilds are recovered, and completed attempt callbacks are released. (#180042, #184069, #184041, #172959, #184021, #178271, #175685, #182666, #164843, #183884) Thanks @sunlit-deng, @danielsiemers, @johan-eilertsen, @jailbirt, @rjdotdev, @wr-web, @seriouslysean, @MSNexploder, and @PollyBot13.
- **Gateway stability and streaming:** long HTML and JSX answers, crafted Teams HTML, and replies that look like tool calls no longer stall the Gateway; reasoning tags are withheld before streaming; silent turns no longer send rich payloads; channel restarts survive exited-run cancellation; the Gateway closes after forced plugin retirement; plugin service schedules outlive the scope that created them; and cold tool inventories no longer grow memory. (#175472, #183438, #183252, #182454, #129244, #182433, #181270, #182207, #178596) Thanks @JasonBuildAI, @LeizhenZhang, @zax0rz, @JOY, @0xtc23, @bguliano, @obviyus, and @wuqxuan.
- **Updates, installs and Doctor:** Windows managed updates no longer lock themselves on TEMP aliases, the Windows installer runs through `iex`, updates complete during channel outages and keep accepted policy pins, stopped database backups allow readers, Doctor restores the Gateway after SIGHUP, keeps valid reseeded configs and inherited logins, repairs unsupported Node runtimes, recovers agents after deletion journal loss, restores plugin host links, handles very large retained histories, and uses less memory on large fleets. (#183622, #183145, #179471, #180505, #180827, #182901, #183703, #179726, #181618, #181804, #181140, #180414, #180792, #181465) Thanks @ryandle, @duyufansh2008, @waynegault, @csabatatrai, @samueltardieu, @4140leal-cw, @rybing7, @RomneyDa, @LiuwqGit, @sukhdeepjohar, and @teddashh.
- **Sessions and storage:** relative session stores resolve against the state directory, sessions archive through symlinked state paths, stale restart-recovery sources no longer wedge sessions, cron cleanup keeps live child sessions, archived Discord slash-command sessions restore in place, background plugin work keeps its SQLite reader, and session deletes reuse warm archive workers. (#182444, #181554, #180853, #179057, #168596, #179031, #171156, #175091, #183410) Thanks @erickj92, @Cloud-Ocean, @Oldrich333, and @PollyBot13.
- **Auth and providers:** rate-limited profiles cool down only as long as the provider asks, shared OAuth refreshes past deleted peers, concurrent agents keep MCP tool access while an OAuth credential is leased, utility models no longer return thinking-only replies, custom GLM providers generate session titles, Kimi K3.1 Pro gets the K3 thinking and video controls, Bedrock Mantle GPT models route through Responses, Google streams recover, and native conversations survive a compaction fallback model. (#180280, #179205, #179997, #169920, #172580, #181923, #182437, #117194, #183282) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev, @WG-Mojo, @maliv2, @danielsiemers, @jacobtomlinson, @TommyLei666, @obviyus, @rayvader, and @pstarkgit.
- **Channels:** Telegram and Mattermost default accounts keep their tokens after a named account is added, X accounts with capitalized keys can be managed and synced, iMessage stops answering its own self-chat replies, Feishu keeps streamed text across tool calls, Google Chat delivers remote attachments as links, Synology Chat stops reporting false delivery failures, Tlon recovers after network drops, and channel images a turn could not read are retried. (#183618, #182706, #183263, #183461, #183383, #182438, #182416, #177654, #178358, #183390) Thanks @555aaditya, @rodricksz4h5, @wangmiao0668000666, @nxmxbbd, @sukhdeepjohar, @felirami, @kentuscn, @jailbirt, @HootRock, @masatohoshino, @yetval, and @teddashh.
- **Voice, apps and browser:** realtime Talk survives early output and brief Gateway stalls, GPT-Live Talk and Bun realtime voice use the managed proxy, oversized macOS recordings error instead of disconnecting the node, Android chat binds to an allowed agent, the Tauri app no longer crashes before the dashboard is ready, FaceTime accepts new calls after a disconnect, the Control UI detects dead Gateway links, and browser control no longer rewrites trusted-proxy Gateway auth or holds profile leases after timeouts. (#182919, #180572, #175886, #176567, #182593, #182767, #183841, #154230, #179101, #181620, #154246) Thanks @anmol0b, @StatsR4Losers, @kybrcore, @MertBasar0, @jalehman, @CheatosBu, @xiaopan-xydt, @dawidkulpa, @Solvely-Colin, @fuller-stack-dev, and @LLagoon3.
- **Config, cron and workspaces:** Control UI saves accept fully masked SecretRefs, short session URLs with navigation hints load, cron jobs keep running after sending to their own target and after a hook plugin is replaced, provisioned workspaces work without templates, Windows workspace sync no longer fails before lease acquisition, trusted-proxy readiness probes succeed without forwarded headers, and restart-recovery notices no longer claim a Gateway restart. (#183571, #183148, #177518, #177825, #120943, #183064, #182823, #172843) Thanks @lonexreb, @Valkster70, @xiaopan-xydt, @2991495215, @masatohoshino, @jlapenna, @shakkernerd, @ericcaiwx-star, @treez-admin, and @obviyus.

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.7..fdd5997b8fa1c0b69159adcadd1d6ca191416e09 history: 162 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 162 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

I used the nanobot web UI to start a process, asked a few questions, and then left the window idle. The next day, I ran out of memory; when I checked the Windows Task Manager, I saw that the Python process was using over 5 GB of memory.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. nanobot webui
2. ask some qa
3. wait 1day
4. check mem

### Expected Behavior

Memory usage isn't that high

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Here is an analysis of myself using Nanobot
A valuable clue: I ran a 4-minute sample and found that the nanobot webui process (PID 6104) consistently increased its private memory by ~2.6 MB/min (≈3.7 GB/day) even when completely idle. I continued to narrow it down to a specific line of code.

The analysis is complete. The root cause has been identified and verified through testing; it is not located at the agent or session level, but rather in the nanobot’s Windows process identity query function.

nanobot/process_runtime.py::_windows_process_identity() redefines a ctypes.Structure subclass, four ctypes.POINTER(FileTime) types, and one ctypes.WinDLL(“kernel32”) on every call. ctypes maintains a module-level _pointer_type_cache that permanently holds type objects as keys, resulting in a permanent memory leak of ~6.5 KB per call that the garbage collector cannot reclaim. This function is located within two hot loops running at 0.5 s and 1 s intervals:

nanobot webui launcher: _attach_to_background_gateway() calls runtime.status() every 0.5 s (with approximately 6 `identity` calls per invocation)
Gateway: `monitor_gateway_clients()` calls `_live_state()` every 1 s (twice per client)

+++ b/nanobot/process_runtime.py
@@ -676,41 +676,57 @@
     return process_group, started_at_seconds, started_at_microseconds
 
 
-def _windows_process_identity(pid: int) -> str | None:
-    if os.name != "nt":
-        return None

-    class FileTime(ctypes.Structure):
-        _fields_ = [("low", ctypes.c_uint32), ("high", ctypes.c_uint32)]
-
-        @property
-        def value(self) -> int:
-            return (int(self.high) << 32) | int(self.low)
-
-    process_query_limited_information = 0x1000
+class _FileTime(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [("low", ctypes.c_uint32), ("high", ctypes.c_uint32)]
+
+    @property
+    def value(self) -> int:
+        return (int(self.high) << 32) | int(self.low)
+
+
+_FILE_TIME_PTR = ctypes.POINTER(_FileTime)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _windows_kernel32() -> Any:
+    """Bind kernel32 process-identity entry points exactly once.
+
+    Defining a fresh ``ctypes.Structure`` subclass and a fresh ``WinDLL`` on
+    every call permanently grows ``ctypes._pointer_type_cache`` (~6.5 KB per
+    call that ``gc`` cannot reclaim), so the WebUI launcher and the gateway
+    both leaked while polling process identity every 0.5-1 s.
+    """
     kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
     kernel32.OpenProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.BOOL, wintypes.DWORD]
     kernel32.OpenProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
     kernel32.GetProcessTimes.argtypes = [
         wintypes.HANDLE,
-        ctypes.POINTER(FileTime),
-        ctypes.POINTER(FileTime),
-        ctypes.POINTER(FileTime),
-        ctypes.POINTER(FileTime),
+        _FILE_TIME_PTR,
+        _FILE_TIME_PTR,
+        _FILE_TIME_PTR,
+        _FILE_TIME_PTR,
     ]
     kernel32.GetProcessTimes.restype = wintypes.BOOL
     kernel32.GetExitCodeProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.DWORD)]
     kernel32.GetExitCodeProcess.restype = wintypes.BOOL

-    handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(process_query_limited_information, False, pid)
+    return kernel32
```

issues.title: WebUI: allow changing an existing chat's project directory (picker is unreachable after the first message)
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

In the WebUI a chat's project (working directory) can only be chosen while the chat is still empty. Once the chat has one user message, the directory control disappears from the composer, so moving an existing topic to another folder is impossible from the UI — the only workaround is to start a new chat and lose its title and history.

I keep ~15 topics grouped by project in the sidebar. Re-organizing them, or fixing a topic that was created before I picked the right folder, currently has no path at all.

### What I checked on `main` @ b07b3ea (2026-10-27)

1. **Front-end gate.** `projectPickerAvailable` in `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadComposer.tsx:1199` is now `!workspaceProjectLocked && ...` (before #6256 it was `isHero`, i.e. new-chat only). The picker is rendered in exactly one place, the composer (`ThreadComposer.tsx:2435`), so an existing thread falls back to showing only the permission menu.
2. **Lock source.** `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx:796` computes

   ```ts
   const projectLocked = session?.projectLocked === true
     || (session?.projectLocked === undefined && displayMessages.some((message) => message.role === "user" && ...));
   ```

   `webui/src/lib/api.ts:209,231` reads `project_locked` from `GET /api/sessions`, but no gateway code ever emits that field (grep `project_locked` under `nanobot/` → 0 hits). The fallback therefore keeps **every existing chat locked**.
3. **The gateway already accepts the change.** `set_workspace_scope` (`nanobot/webui/inbound_commands.py:428`) → `WebUIWorkspaceController.scope_for_set_request` (`nanobot/webui/workspaces.py:412`) only refuses while the chat is running (`chat_running`, 409). There is already a test for the set-request path: `tests/utils/test_webui_workspaces.py::test_remote_existing_chat_can_reduce_its_workspace_access`.

So the gap looks like a missing marker in the sessions payload plus a missing affordance, not a missing capability.

### Proposed Solution

- Emit `project_locked` in the `/api/sessions` payload — for example `false` for an idle, non-temporary session and `true` for temporary chats — or simply show the picker for existing chats and let `set_workspace_scope` stay the authority.
- Keep the existing guards: 409 while a turn is running, temporary chats stay locked, and the next turn must re-derive runtime context / system prompt from the new scope.
- Optional: a sidebar affordance (topic context menu → "Change directory", like the existing "New chat in project") so re-organizing many topics does not require opening each chat.

### Alternatives Considered

- Create a new chat in the target folder and restate the task. That is today's workaround, and it drops the topic title and history.
- Hand-editing session metadata under `~/.nanobot/`. Undocumented and error-prone.
- Dragging the topic into another sidebar project group. Drag-and-drop in `webui/src/components/ChatList.tsx` only moves tabs/panes; it does not change project membership.

### Related Component

Other (WebUI)

### Additional Context

- Environment: nanobot 0.3.5 installed from `main` @ d617b72, Windows 11, Edge, WebUI served at `127.0.0.1:8765`.
- #6256 states "The existing project-lock behavior is not redesigned here" and lists the directory lock as a known limitation, so I am filing this as a follow-up rather than a regression. If locking a topic's folder after its first message is intentional (to keep memory/context bound to one project), a documented way to relocate a topic would also solve the problem — happy to adjust this request to whatever direction fits the design.
- Unrelated to #1302 (per-session isolation for non-WebUI channels).

issues.title: atomic_write_text doubles CR in CRLF text on Windows
issues.body:
On Windows, `atomic_write_text` does not preserve the exact UTF-8 text promised by its docstring. Default newline translation changes LF to CRLF and existing CRLF to CRCRLF. This helper is used for cron/trigger persistence and automation run records.

Reproduced on native Windows with Python 3.13.9 against main `3230013`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from nanobot.utils.atomic_file import atomic_write_text

path = Path("record.txt")
content = "first\r\nsecond\r\n"
atomic_write_text(path, content)
print(repr(path.read_bytes()))
```

Actual: `b'first\r\r\nsecond\r\r\n'`
Expected: `b'first\r\nsecond\r\n'`

Opening the temporary stream with `newline=""` preserves the supplied text. The existing exact-content test uses one line and `read_text`, masking this conversion. Extending that test to compare bytes for LF, CRLF and CR produces **2 failed, 1 passed** on unmodified main (LF/CRLF fail; CR passes).

AI assistance: investigated and reproduced with Codex. No model calls or external services were used.

prs.title: fix(runtime): stop Windows identity polling memory leak
prs.body:
## Why

On Windows with Python versions before 3.14, each process identity query created a new `FileTime` structure and pointer type retained by ctypes' global pointer cache. Idle WebUI launcher and gateway client polling repeatedly called this path, causing unbounded memory growth. Reuse the native types and bindings rather than reducing polling or caching process identities.

Fixes #6506
Resolves NAN-378

## What changed

- Share the `FileTime` structure and pointer type, and cache the kernel32 function bindings.
- Keep each PID identity query live, preserving HANDLE signatures, exit-state checks, and `CloseHandle` cleanup.
- Add one native Windows regression that checks a stable process identity without creating new pointer types after warmup. It detects the original allocation pattern even on Python 3.14, whose ctypes cache no longer retains these types globally.

## Scope

This fixes the shared Windows process identity helper used by WebUI launcher status and gateway client monitoring. It does not change polling intervals, process lifetime policy, or non-Windows identity behavior.

## Verification

- Native Windows regression on Python 3.13.7: **failed before the fix, passed after the fix** (`tests/gateway/test_runtime.py::test_windows_identity_polling_reuses_pointer_types`).
- Earlier isolated Windows/Python 3.12.10 diagnosis: 10,000 real identity queries followed by GC grew Private Working Set by 58.3 MiB and Private Bytes by 58.8 MiB, retaining 10,000 extra pointer-cache entries. The reporter's proposed shared-type/cached-binding correction eliminated that growth in the controlled comparison.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The complete test suite is delegated to GitHub Actions; it was not run locally. An overnight WebUI run was not performed.

## Credit

Thanks to @snailak for the report, diagnosis, and suggested patch in #6506. The fix commit includes their `Co-authored-by` trailer; please retain it when merging.

prs.title: fix(agent): isolate inline command failures
prs.body:
## Problem

  `/status` runs inline in `AgentLoop.run()`, outside the session worker's exception handling. If session loading or runtime resolution raises an unhandled
  exception, it escapes the command handler and terminates the consumer.

  The loop then calls `aclose()`, cancelling active tasks in other sessions and closing shared resources. Under the standard gateway startup path, the runtime task
  failure also triggers gateway cleanup.

  ## Changes

  - Catch ordinary handler exceptions at the inline command execution boundary.
  - Log the failure while respecting the session's logging policy.
  - Reuse `TurnDelivery.fail()` to send a safe error response with the request's routing metadata.
  - Avoid publishing completion or idle events for an already active session.
  - Preserve existing session queue/conflict exception handling and `CancelledError` propagation.

  Successful command dispatch and response publication remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(discord): send step updates without notification pings
prs.body:
## Problem

With `streaming` enabled, one turn can push many intermediate messages into a Discord
channel — progress text and tool hints — and each sends a notification.
A normal question triggers 3-6 pings and the actual answer one more,
so the message that matters is buried under the ones that don't.

## Change

Intermediate updates are sent with Discord's Suppress Notifications (`@silent`) flag
(`channel.send(..., silent=True)`): they still land in the channel, they just stop
pushing to phones and issuing notficiations. Final replies are untouched.

The gate is one `isinstance(msg.event, ProgressEvent)` check computed in
`DiscordBotClient.send_outbound` threaded into the text and attachment
paths.

## Configuration

`channels.discord.silentProgress` (bool, default `true`) is the config. Documented in `docs/chat-apps.md` alongside
`streaming` and `replyToMessage`, with a matching setup-form field and label copy in all
ten locales.

The key is optional and `DiscordConfig` ignores unknown keys, so a config that already
sets it still loads on an older build, where it simply does nothing.

## Not a client/host contract change

Normalize fontkit's legacy ASCII PostScript-name records without accepting a different face. The packaged native probe now exercises Chinese C4 labels and generated Latin punctuation; no glyph or font guard is skipped.

Windows/Linux x64 uncompressed TUI binaries are 128.18/122.88 MiB, below the 135 MiB budget; other targets are below 150 MiB. The growth is measured, not assumed unchanged. No intermediate universal wheel, test environment, private configuration or database is in the upload set.

prs.title: refactor(webui): unify code and diff highlighting
prs.body:
## Why

Replace the WebUI's separate Prism code/preview/diff paths with shared highlighting while preserving the existing reading and file-change workflows. This also restores the earlier single-conversation preview layout: messages and Composer stay together in the left column, with the file preview filling the right column.

## What changed

- Replace `react-syntax-highlighter`/Prism with shared Highlights tokens and CSS-variable colors. Load Shiki only for grammars absent from Highlights; render source through React text/spans and preserve complete preview text, native find/selection, copy, ANSI, streaming settlement, wrapping, line numbers, themes and reading sizes.
- Render each complete read-only file diff through one Pierre instance, with bounded metadata/AST caches and a render window read from the existing chat scroller. Preserve file summaries, line limits, expansion/collapse, hunk gaps, truncation notices and local previews.
- Keep the single-conversation Composer inside its conversation column. Actual multi-pane tabs retain the shared footer, including compact rendering. Update both lockfiles, lazy-chunk guards, dependency notices and behavioral tests.

## Scope

WebUI only. No backend, TUI, provider, protocol or persistence-format changes; no patch editing/applying, new scroller ownership or bottom-mask removal. Uses pinned `@pierre/diffs` 1.6.1, `@pierre/highlights` 0.2.0 and Shiki 4.5.0.

## Tracking

Related: [NAN-343 — 统一 WebUI 代码与只读 diff 高亮，保留源码操作及侧栏布局](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-343).

## Tradeoffs

**Draft: large-diff scrolling and first-use transfer tradeoffs have not been remeasured after the fixes below.** This is not presented as a blanket performance improvement.

Five interleaved original-Prism/new-renderer trials on equivalent synthetic production fixtures, taken **before the final preview-layout follow-up**, found:

| Workload | Prism → replacement |
| --- | --- |
| 600-line code block, warm topic return | 316.6 → 190.0 ms |
| 600-row diff, warm expanded viewport | 189.5 → 30.7 ms |
| Code-block browser Private Working Set increment | 203.6 → 120.0 MiB |
| Diff browser Private Working Set increment | 217.8 → 171.6 MiB |
| Large-diff scroll p99, normal / Chromium 4× CPU throttle | 16.8 → 33.4 ms / 33.4 → 183.4 ms |
| Whole JS/CSS/WASM first-use transfer, code / diff | 708.8 → 797.1 KiB / 706.9 → 887.8 KiB |

Memory subtracts each independent browser's blank-host baseline; private commit was measured separately. Transfer is actual negotiated response-body bytes, not decoded size. Diff viewport readiness is separate from a complete source-coordinate traversal. The 600-row diff is a stress fixture above the ordinary default 500-row native output cap; 4× throttling is not a real low-end device. These figures are retained evidence for that earlier snapshot, **not a performance claim for this repaired head**.

## Blast Radius

Shared Markdown/code rendering, source-file previews, read-only file activity and single/multiple-pane Composer placement. Main review risks are grammar-loading failures and resource ownership, source/line-ending integrity, virtual-diff geometry and scrolling tails, and draft/attachment retention when changing pane ownership.

## Verification

The repaired source/build passed locally: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` (**3297 tests**), `bun run test:browser` (**246 cases**), `bun run build --outDir <isolated-output>` and `git diff --check`. The source inventory, normalized staged blobs/Git tree and frozen production assets were checked against the repair commit; no source change intervened after those checks.

A new isolated production gateway passed **32 normal black-box cases** on desktop/light and narrow/dark: code blocks including INI, PowerShell, C#, Docker and literal unknown-language HTML; exact clipboard content; themes; full previews/native find and selection; long-line plain-text budgets; six kinds of diff including the INI Worker path; complete retained coordinates, line limits, expansion, truncation and close/reopen. No browser or HTTP errors occurred in these normal cases. Preview open/close retained the same Composer DOM instance and its draft.

The targeted production regression checks also passed: a real failed INI grammar request in the direct source-file preview retained complete plain source, the same Composer and draft, working theme/close controls, and local diagnostics. The normal → blocked → normal controls each used a fresh browser context in the same Service-Worker-blocked interception mode; this is not a claim of automatic same-page module retry. Ordinary black-box cases used the normal Service Worker path. A real mouse drag plus native wheel across the original virtual-window boundary retained the exact selection; further scrolling kept both the selected rows and current viewport, native Copy matched the selection, and clearing it released the pinned rows without changing total scroll height.

The full browser suite additionally covers forward/backward selection and multi-hunk missing-context coordinates, native clipboard content and 26px localized gaps. Earlier built-gateway single → multiple → single pane checks with text and browser-File drafts remain recorded against the initial review commit; pane/Composer ownership source was unchanged by this repair, and the full current unit/browser checks were rerun.

## Review results

The initial review of `48e7177e9669f86f2f50ae462871ad296a19abd1` independently confirmed two P2 defects in the production UI. Both are repaired in [`d4469e316`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/d4469e316ce26a9169d911d7ebd33ff765d51049):

1. **Contain grammar/highlighter failure in CodeBlock.** Optional syntax enhancement can fail without clearing the source-file preview or the app. Keep the full plain source and Copy control outside the failed child; discard failed cached resources after the fallback commits, while retaining diagnostics.
2. **Preserve native diff selection during window movement.** Replace the function-valued hunk separator that disabled Pierre 1.6.1 partial rendering with built-in separators and local shadow-root label updates. Convert composed/shadow selection coordinates to rendered rows, retain only the active selection's minimal continuous envelope with the current viewport, and return to the normal bounded window when selection clears. Chromium's retargeted document `Selection.isCollapsed` is not used to reject a real shadow selection.

A focused independent read-only review of the repair implementation and installed library APIs found no new confirmed actionable finding. The exact parent failure triggers now pass through the new production build, as detailed above. This was not a formal GitHub approval.

Keep Draft pending performance reassessment: earlier scrolling/transfer measurements remain tied to the older pre-layout snapshot, not this incremental-render repair. Non-Chromium native shadow-selection fallbacks are statically checked but not browser-accepted. CI for the pushed head is reported separately from local tests and these synthetic-fixture UI checks.

prs.title: fix(webui): retain history touch gestures across message replacement
prs.body:
## Why

A history pull can lose its remaining touch events when React replaces the message node under the finger, such as when a lazy Markdown renderer replaces its fallback. The viewport then never receives the move, release, or cancellation: a short pull can remain at 22.6775px, or a longer pull can fail to reach the loading threshold.

## What changed

- Keep the originating touch target observed for the lifetime of the viewport-owned gesture. Forward events to the existing handlers only when their DOM path no longer reaches the viewport, so connected events are not processed twice.
- Release the target listeners on touch end/cancel, effect cleanup, and conversation changes; cancel an active pull when another finger is added.
- Add real Chromium touch regressions that gate the actual Markdown renderer and replace the target before movement, release, or cancellation, plus multi-touch and conversation-switch checks.

## Scope

Only the WebUI history touch lifecycle and its browser tests. Existing spring physics, pull thresholds, wheel/keyboard scrolling, request ownership, backend, persistence, worker counts, retries, and timeouts are unchanged. No diagnostic instrumentation is included.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the controlled browser regressions reproduced both observed values: long-pull displacement 0 instead of at least 56px, and short-release displacement 22.6775px instead of 0. They pass with the fix, including cancellation followed by a new pull.
- The full history-boundary spec passed all 25 cases; history-spring unit tests passed all 7 cases.
- Lockfile/import checks, lint, full WebUI and browser TypeScript checks, build, and the full unit/coverage suite passed (3,490 tests).
- **Full browser verification is not green, so this PR remains Draft.** The first candidate run had 395 passed / 1 failed: a blank chat-failure fixture. A fixed, isolated full baseline/candidate diagnostic pair then had 390 passed / 1 failed on the baseline (Dock touch reopening) and 394 passed / 2 failed on the candidate (the same Dock assertion and a blank compaction-reasons fixture). The page-blank failures have not been causally attributed; the original chat-failure blank was not reproduced. No assertions or timings were relaxed and these failures are not counted as fixed.
- The controlled target-replacement path is confirmed. The exact event interleavings in the earlier CI failures were not captured, and physical-device acceptance has not been performed.

Contributes to NAN-374

prs.title: fix(websocket): abort disconnected HTTP handshakes before sending
prs.body:
## Why

A browser or HTTP client can disconnect while a WebUI HTTP route is awaiting work. With websockets 15/16, the handshake then tries to send the stale response and hits `assert not self.eof_sent`, producing repeated internal-error logs. Allowing 17.x alone leaves Feishu installations on the affected 15.x resolution.

## What changed

* Register one synchronous `process_response` hook on TCP and Unix listeners. Immediately before sending, terminate only an already-disconnected connection's handshake task. The request callback has already finished; callback failures remain visible in the existing server logs.
* Keep `websockets>=15.0,<17.0` and Feishu SDK requirements unchanged. This replaces the earlier dependency-ceiling approach.
* Cover full-close and TCP half-close through the real channel and binary HTTP bridge, followed by normal HTTP and WebSocket traffic. Cover connected and disconnected callback failures separately.
* Run focused transport regressions before optional channel installation in CI, then exercise Feishu's older compatible resolution in the all-channel suite. These regressions do not skip on websockets 15/16.
* Isolate Settings and HTTP-route tests from the user's configuration.

## Scope and tradeoffs

The production change remains 18 added lines in the WebSocket channel. There is no SDK fork, global monkeypatch, handshake-method copy, new log filter, transport replacement or dependency upgrade. The response hook must stay synchronous so it cannot yield between checking connection state and sending. Request callbacks are allowed to finish; their effects are not rolled back.

Rebased onto main `219c8bb2`. Conflicting ripgrep and attachment-boundary test fixes, plus duplicate account-fixture patches, were resolved by keeping main's existing implementations. The final PR delta is five files; the three-commit sequence and author metadata are retained.

## Verification

Rebased head `1f08c9a4`, Windows / Python 3.14.6, isolated worktree and private non-input desktop:

* Default websockets **16.1.1** transport selection: **12 passed / 4 Unix-only skips**.
* Actual channel installation selected **lark-oapi 1.7.5 / websockets 15.0.1**; affected listener, HTTP, Settings, Feishu and retained Windows fixture regressions: **549 passed / 8 skipped**. Dependency consistency passed.
* Current Windows CI main group with two local workers: **10,783 passed / 148 skipped**; serial CLI group **244 passed / 9 skipped**; serial native-process group **59 passed**; coordination selection **20 passed / 5 skipped**. Heavy installer and isolated-update matrices are left to their existing remote CI jobs. These counts are separate selections, not an aggregate full-suite claim.
* Full Ruff, strict BasedPyright and Python import boundaries passed.
* Full WebUI import checks, lint, typecheck, coverage tests and production build passed. A fresh real headless-Chrome `/help` exchange and refresh passed; its disposable gateway was stopped and ports released.
* The real Feishu SDK established a loopback WebSocket connection, sent its binary ping and stopped. Bootstrap/identity calls were stubbed; no real account or external platform was used.

A pre-rebase full run recorded one SQLite `disk I/O error`; its cause remains unconfirmed. Original/candidate targeted probes, the subsequent pre-rebase private-desktop full run and the rebased CI main group passed. No SQLite workaround, retry, delay, assertion weakening or new skip was added; the earlier failure is not claimed fixed.

Current-head remote verification is running in [Test Suite](<https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40484147705>). Linux/Python 3.11, Unix-socket and remaining installer/update acceptance belong to remote CI. The daily instance was unchanged.

Contributes to NAN-362

prs.title: fix(webui): keep Dock taps working after touch drags
prs.body:
## Why

A fast touch drag can leave Chromium with an internal fling even though the subtask Dock handle uses `touch-action: none`. The next tap stops that fling instead of producing a DOM click, leaving the closed Dock unable to reopen.

## What changed

- Cancel native handle touch movement only after the existing tap slop is crossed, using a nonpassive listener. Normal taps keep their native click, while the task list keeps its independent scrolling.
- Attach and clean up the listener with the visible handle, including when completion feedback disappears and later work restores the Dock.
- Add a controlled fast-release regression that verifies one-tap reopening and native click delivery, while retaining the existing drag, cancellation, mouse, keyboard and list-scroll coverage.

## Scope

Only Dock handle touch ownership changes. This does not change history gestures or add waits, retries, extra taps, or synthetic click fallbacks.

## Verification

- The new regression failed on the unchanged Dock at the reopening tap (0 tasks instead of 23), then passed with the fix. The unchanged touch-drag/list-scroll scenario also passed.
- A Chromium input trace of the fixed regression recorded no native fling starts or tap suppression; the next native tap generated a trusted click and reopened all 23 tasks.
- Windows, Bun 1.3.13: lockfile validation, import boundaries/checker tests, lint, full application/unit and browser TypeScript checks, production build, and full unit/coverage suite passed (3,490 tests).
- Full browser suite passed: 393 tests, two workers, zero retries. The tracked source snapshot remained unchanged throughout verification.

Touch verification used Playwright/CDP with Chromium 156 on Windows; physical touchscreen hardware was not exercised.

prs.title: feat(web): add google-browser-scraper as a web_search provider
prs.body:
## What

Adds [google-browser-scraper](https://github.com/nodemaven/google-browser-scraper) as a `web_search` provider. Its `serve` command runs Google searches in a real browser through the user's own proxy and answers SerpApi-style JSON on a local address, so it works like the SearXNG provider: a self-hosted base URL, no paid API.

- `google_browser_scraper` in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` with `credential: base_url`; `GBS_BASE_URL` as the env fallback, falling back to DuckDuckGo when neither is set, like SearXNG.
- `GET {baseUrl}/search.json?q=...`, maps `organic_results` (`title`, `link`, `snippet`). An optional key goes out as `Authorization: Bearer` from `apiKey` or `GBS_API_KEY`.
- A blocked page (captcha, refused exit) comes back as HTTP 200 with `search_metadata.status = "Error"`; it is returned as a tool error, not as "No results".
- `exclusive` like DuckDuckGo: the server runs one browser search at a time, so parallel calls would only queue there.

## Why built in rather than MCP

It needs no key and no new dependency, and as a `web_search` backend it keeps nanobot's own result format, DuckDuckGo fallback and serialized calls. The scraper also has an MCP mode for people who prefer that.

## Testing

`tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`: success (endpoint, params, Bearer header, unresolved links skipped, count), env base URL without a key, blocked page, HTTP 401, no base URL -> DuckDuckGo, exclusive. 97 passed; the new tests fail without the change. Also checked against google-browser-scraper's own `serve` HTTP handler with the browser stubbed out.

## Docs

Provider table row, a config example in `docs/configuration.md`, and `google_browser_scraper` in the `tools.web.search` provider list.

prs.title: refactor(channels): move tool hint rendering out of core
prs.body:
## Why

Tool activity should describe what happened, not decide how every chat platform must display it. The runner currently generates both structured events and a universal shortened hint; this change moves that presentation decision to each channel while preserving existing delivery behavior.

## What changed

- Core hooks publish tool start/end/error facts with call IDs, arguments and results, without generating hint text; remove the presentation-length plumbing from the agent loop and hook assembly.
- Add channel-owned `prepare_tool_events()` before queueing. Plain-text channels reuse the shared formatter, while WebSocket, Linear and Weixin's native progress path consume structured events directly. Project once so retries retain the same envelope and multipart delivery cursor.
- Migrate both classic CLI paths and document the channel/callback contract. WebUI and TUI keep their existing grouping and rendering.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Core: structured tool facts] --> B[Target channel]
    B --> C[Native activity / WebSocket events]
    B --> D[Optional shared text formatter]
    C --> E[Platform-specific presentation]
    D --> E
```

## Scope

Preserves the current wire/storage formats, per-channel visibility defaults and overrides, tool start versus terminal visibility policy, hint-length setting, thread metadata and FIFO/retry handling. No execution, model-context, WebUI layout or file-list UX redesign.

## Tradeoffs

Reuse `ProgressEvent` rather than adding a second tool-event protocol. Third-party channels inheriting the default text projection retain readable starts; native consumers opt out of that projection. Direct `on_progress` consumers must accept `tool_events` to display tool activity instead of relying on core-generated text.

## Blast Radius

The change touches tool progress for local and provider-hosted calls, channel adapters, and classic CLI output. Regression coverage retains Telegram quotes, Feishu cards, Slack text, Linear actions, Weixin native/legacy delivery, Email suppression, and same-envelope WhatsApp multipart retries.

## Verification

- Python Ruff, import-boundary checks and full BasedPyright: passed.
- Serial CLI suite: 246 passed, 9 skipped. Core/channel regression checks were also run during development; the final full Python suite remains unverified.
- TUI full suite: 309 passed. An earlier binding-test timeout also reproduced in the frozen baseline; the isolated baseline binding checks and sequential candidate run passed without changing tests or timeouts.
- WebUI full typecheck, lint, production build and 212 focused unit tests: passed. An isolated production gateway with a local SSE model stub verified empty-text tool start/end frames, two-file activity grouping, refresh/history replay, and unchanged tool results in the model continuation.
- **Draft / verification outstanding:** both local full-Python attempts were interrupted because nested Windows integration processes opened visible terminal windows. An outer private desktop did not contain every nested process. No further local retry is planned; full verification is deferred to remote CI. No live third-party IM credential tests were performed.

## Why

A model stream can deliver an apparently complete reply and then fail before its terminal event arrives. The browser keeps the text, but the runner previously persisted only an error placeholder, so subsequent requests could not see the reply the user had already read. Fixes [NAN-373](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-373).

## What changed

- Retain observed assistant text at the shared runner boundary when the final model result fails, with an interruption marker. Keep diagnostics and reasoning separate, preserve tool results, and include the retained text in ordinary follow-ups and native continuation.
- Keep failure and explicit recovery intact. Project the committed saved-reply fact through live and attached recovery state; show a short saved-reply notice only when that fact is present. Review and update all ten supported locales.
- Cover interrupted streams, retry/fallback segments, mid-turn input, and actual Responses request-body construction. Settle real lazy imports and asynchronous save admission in affected full-suite tests without changing assertions or timeouts.

## Scope

No historical backfill, changes to real conversations or shared instances, automatic tool replay, or retry-policy changes. A reply that looks complete does not turn a failed request into a successful one.

## Blast Radius

The shared streaming runner serves all channels. The principal risks are accidentally retaining diagnostic/reasoning text, duplicating retry prefixes, and omitting retained output from provider-native state. Focused regressions cover these boundaries; the optional recovery field carries only the committed preservation fact.

## Verification

- Red before the fix: both complete-looking and unfinished replies were replaced by the error placeholder.
- Python: 272 focused tests passed; full Ruff, strict BasedPyright, dependency consistency, and import boundaries passed. An additional core-focused set passed 366 tests.
- WebUI: all 3,490 tests in the complete coverage suite passed with a two-worker local resource budget; full typecheck, lint, import checks and production build passed. Earlier default-worker local executions failed on asynchronous test races/timeouts; their results are retained. Those UI repairs preserve the existing timeouts, assertions and coverage.
- The first remote Windows run failed before a token-estimation test reached its estimator (10,787 passed, 1 failed, 135 skipped). A controlled scheduling comparison reproduced the faulty startup deadline. The test now synchronizes on estimator entry or turn completion, retains its five-second blocked-worker gate, and calls the real estimation chain; all four deliberately-inline mutation cases still fail. The complete responsiveness module passes 17 tests locally.
- Copy review: all ten languages checked against `.agent/copywriting.md`; the live-state omission found during review was fixed and covered by live/attached tests.
- Final remote [CI run 40464240680](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40464240680) passed all 12 selected checks; the installer and native-package jobs were path-skipped. The Windows full compatibility step passed 10,788 tests, followed by 244 serial CLI tests.
- After CI passed, isolated production-gateway/headless-Chrome black-box checks passed at 1440px and 390px using a local Responses fault service: complete-looking and partial replies followed by stream termination, reload, ordinary follow-up, explicit Continue with native state, and a later no-output error. Captured network request bodies contained the retained reply and completed tool output exactly once; the real tool ran once. No browser page errors occurred. Screenshots are attached to the Linear verification record; raw requests are retained in the task's local verification artifacts. No commercial-model credentials or real conversation data were used.

prs.body:
## Summary

Recent WebUI CI failures have several distinct causes. One is a real interaction bug: a closed Dock `HoverHint` can remain mounted during its pending entry animation, leaving a Radix dismissable layer that consumes Escape before the Dock can close or cancel a drag. Mount the hint content only while it is enabled and open, and cover both cases while preserving Escape priority for an open tooltip and a task detail dialog.

Stabilize the affected test setup without changing worker counts, retries, or timeouts:

- Establish the history boundary before opening offscreen archived tasks so the setup cannot prefetch the history being measured.
- Capture the actual background-color transition at the theme commit before sampling its midpoint.
- Freeze the task clock and distinguish the row elapsed time from the detail's independent activity clock.
- Await the real lazy Markdown and automation-detail modules where the tests need their rendered content, and use complete paste interactions for longer proxy values while preserving draft/cancel/save assertions.
- Keep the native-link event and destination assertions while preventing Happy DOM from making a real external network request.

## Verification

- Windows: full WebUI unit/coverage suite (3,486 passed), full Playwright browser suite (391 passed), lint, full WebUI and browser TypeScript checks, import checks, lockfile check, and build.
- Linux: [diagnostic WebUI CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40465218498) passed 3,486 unit tests and 391 browser tests. Its WebUI patch matches this candidate; its test branch additionally changes the CI selector and diagnostic artifact upload, which are not part of this PR.
- Controlled browser checks reproduced the closed-tooltip Escape failures with an extended pending-animation window and verified that genuinely open tooltips and detail dialogs retain Escape priority.

Two earlier touch-history failures were not reproduced in the targeted diagnostic samples; this PR does not claim to resolve their cause.

prs.body:
Fixes #6474

`atomic_write_text` promises exact UTF-8 text, but its default text-stream newline translation changes LF to CRLF on Windows and turns existing CRLF into CRCRLF. Extend the existing exact-content test to compare bytes for LF, CRLF and CR, including non-ASCII text. Previously it wrote a single line and used `read_text`, which could not detect newline conversion.

The first CI run passed Linux 3.11/3.14 tests, lint/type checks, Docker and native acceptance, but the Windows isolated-update job timed out in `test_stale_first_supervisor_cannot_take_new_confirmation`. Its status already reported `succeeded` while the supervisor had not exited within 40 seconds. Production timeouts are unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(webui): centralize outbound delivery (NAN-365)
prs.body:
## Why

Adding a WebUI event or changing history behavior still requires editing the WebSocket channel's business-specific send paths. Centralize outbound presentation, stream state, durability policy and delivery-turn completion so those changes no longer spread into connection transport code.

Tracks [NAN-365](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-365), which contains the **before/after Mermaid architecture diagrams**, ownership changes and acceptance boundaries. This follows the completed [NAN-102](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-102) wire-encoding extraction rather than reopening it.

## What changed

- Replace the old projector with one `WebUIOutboundDelivery` owner for ordinary messages, text/reasoning streams, file-edit events and the existing hydration/discard/session-refresh hooks.
- Reduce its transport contract to recipient snapshots and raw-frame enqueue. Move feature-specific payload construction, transcript policy, stream buffers, pairing projection and WebUI delivery completion out of the socket channel; retain the existing connection queues and drain behavior.
- Complete public payload types, tighten import boundaries and migrate tests to emitted frames/durable history, including a subscriber joining while history persistence is awaiting.

## Scope

Preserve public wire fields, history schemas, BaseChannel streaming entry points, temporary-chat/restart-control policy, offline persistence, incomplete recovery, audience isolation and late-owner handling. `SessionState` remains the persistent authority; the moved completion logic is the WebUI delivery projection, not Agent execution ownership.

No frontend, AgentLoop/runner, database migration, WS-to-HTTP mutation redesign, admission-receipt change, new event bus or deployment is included. Existing command-router changes only reconnect its outbound hooks to their owner.

## Tradeoffs

Evolve the existing projector into a single delivery owner instead of adding a coordinator/effect-plan layer. Keep read-only connection identity snapshots at this adapter edge rather than introducing opaque-recipient wrappers; the owner never performs socket I/O. Each send captures its recipients before the persistence await, while subsequent broadcasts take their own snapshots.

## Blast Radius

WebUI and TUI outbound delivery share this path. The principal regression risks are stream ordering/merging, history failures clearing a turn too early, audience selection and slow-client isolation. The channel retains ready ordering, writer budgets, timeouts, retirement and in-flight drain accounting.

## Verification

All verification below is bound to `8acf73a1975e689a467a6d9c4c50bcff8544513d`; no product or test source changed during this readiness pass.

- **Fresh white-box regression: 1694 passed**, 0 failed/errors/skipped, in 73.38s: all colocated WebSocket tests and WebUI Python tests, selected session history/recovery, bus, channel-manager streaming/reasoning/compaction/concurrency, turn helpers, response-source and architecture tests.
- Strict BasedPyright **1.39.0** for all `nanobot/webui` and `nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py`: **0 errors, warnings or notes**. Ruff on all 11 changed Python files, import boundaries (13 rules / 217 files), production imports and diff whitespace: passed.
- **Public black-box acceptance passed** against a real isolated CLI gateway and a local deterministic OpenAI-compatible model fixture: authentication rejection/acceptance; ordinary command and literal-shell delivery/replay; all-connection session refresh; text/reasoning streaming; a second client attaching to a live turn; actual file-edit tool activity and durable replay; all clients disconnecting before completion; and process restart restoring the completed result without replaying the model.
- **Built WebUI browser acceptance passed** without route mocks: real access-secret login, normal composer send, streamed fixture-model answer, terminal event, durable refresh and narrow-viewport reachability. Bun **1.3.6**, Playwright **1.64.1**, Chromium **156.0.8078.4**; no page errors or unexpected HTTP failures. The existing empty-draft 404-to-null behavior is preserved, not counted as a product failure.
- Owned gateways, local model server and browser were closed; all three temporary listening ports were checked closed and temporary runtime state removed. Daily/handed-off services and real user sessions/configuration were not used or changed.
- [Exact-head CI, run 40358925261, attempt 1](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40358925261): **15/15 jobs successful**, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows, installer/process compatibility, WebUI checks/browser, TUI on both platforms, native package acceptance, Docker and required gates.

Test selection:

```bash
python -m pytest -q nanobot/channels/websocket/tests tests/webui tests/session/test_display_history.py tests/session/test_recovery.py tests/bus tests/channels/test_websocket_application_boundary.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_delta_coalescing.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_reasoning.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_compaction_notices.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_concurrency.py tests/utils/test_webui_turn_helpers.py tests/agent/test_response_source.py tests/architecture/test_import_boundaries.py
basedpyright --pythonpath <test-environment-python> nanobot/webui nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py
python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries
```

Local white-box environment: Linux, Python **3.12.10**, websockets **16.0**, pytest **9.1.1**. Packaging fixtures used hatchling **1.32.4** only through an isolated test dependency directory; shared runtime dependencies were not changed. An initial long temporary path exceeded the existing SSH control-socket limit; the full same suite passed after correcting the harness path. Browser harness assumptions about intentionally hidden `/model` responses and topic-dependent composer labels were corrected before the final complete pass. Failed-attempt inputs/results were retained; no tests were skipped or product source patched to make verification pass.

Black-box verification used fresh isolated state and a local model fixture, not a commercial/real-account model; external tokenizer download was blocked and the gateway used its existing UTF-8 byte estimates. This is affected-contract verification rather than a claim of universal compatibility or absence of risk. The PR is Ready for review; formal review/approval is still required. No merge or deployment was performed.

## Why

Users expect selecting a subtask's visible content to open that task's details. The handler was attached only to its title button, leaving running tool-call rows, error text and completed-result Markdown unresponsive. #6478 addressed an offscreen title instead; the user explicitly corrected that interpretation.

## What changed

- Make the task item own content activation: clicking tool activity, error text, result headings, prose or code opens the owning task through the existing detail owner and canonical title button. Remove the sticky-header workaround from #6478.
- Leave nested buttons, links, form/disclosure/editable controls and React-owned portals to their existing actions. Selecting text does not activate the card, and closing details preserves the scrolled result's position.
- Exercise tool/error/result activation and task identity in unit tests; use real desktop/narrow pointer and simulated-touch browser interactions for result access, native selection, links, copying, images and focus/reading-position restoration. Keep the existing title button as the native keyboard entry.

## Scope

Only the WebUI task item's click boundary and its tests. No new task/detail state, backend, protocol, persistence, drawer gesture, cancellation or shared-instance changes. No timers or delayed click arbitration.

## Verification

- Before the production change, both new tool-activity and result-body unit regressions failed because no detail dialog opened.
- Focused unit tests: 51 passed across subtask UI and archives.
- Full task-drawer browser file: 27 passed, including actual tool/result taps, scrolled result clicks, drag selection, native new-tab links, code copying, image portals, scrolling, stopping and keyboard focus.
- Application/browser TypeScript, ESLint, import boundaries, 42 import-checker tests and production build passed. Existing large-chunk advisory remains.
- Full `bun run test:coverage`: **3468 passed / 3 failed**. The failures are in literal-output Markdown rendering (`message-bubble`), automation detail loading (`session-info-popover`) and Provider proxy setup (`shared-proxy-setup`). All three also fail on the unchanged parent `23c4acc21609c006aea77e694e0e4c63fa97f3ea`, whose full run had **3464 passed / 6 failed**. The command remains FAIL; no coverage-total pass is claimed.
- Full `bun run test:browser`: **392 passed / 4 failed**. All four are existing desktop/narrow, light/dark literal-output clipboard assertions in `inline-references.spec.ts`. Running those four cases on the unchanged parent reproduces **0 passed / 4 failed** at the same assertion.

Publishing as Draft because full-project checks remain red. No timeout, retry setting or unrelated assertion was weakened, and the separate failures were not mixed into this interaction fix.
