prs.title: feat(webapp): copy agent+desktop packages' desktop halves on the serving host
prs.body:
## Stack

Webapp desktop plugins, merged bottom-up. Each PR adds its commits on top of the one below it; the whole stack is rebased on current `main`.

| # | PR | Change | Issue | Live check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #145072 | Load desktop plugins in a browser tab | Closes #145073 | ✅ works in a real browser |
| 2 | #145539 | Hot-reload an edited `plugin.js` | review follow-up | ✅ works in a real browser |
| 3 | 👉 **#145549** (this PR) | Copy agent+desktop packages' desktop halves on the serving host | Closes #145540 | ✅ works in a real browser |

Tracking: #144648 · Review that started the follow-ups: [@BearHuddleston on #145072](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145072#pullrequestreview-5667771348) · CSP note for WA-11: #144705

## What does this PR do?

The change here is the last commit, `84be2b5ee7`; the rest is #145072 and #145539. Rebased on current `main`; I'll rebase again as they merge.

The desktop half of an agent+desktop package (`<home>/plugins/<name>/desktop/plugin.js`) only reached `<root>/desktop-plugins/<name>/` when native Desktop copied it there (`reconcileUnifiedDesktopHalves` in `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-plugins-root.ts`). A host that native Desktop only reaches over SSH never runs that copy. The Webapp serves that host's folder, so those halves never appeared. See #145540, raised by @BearHuddleston in the [#145072 review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145072#pullrequestreview-5667771348).

The serving host now makes the copy itself, at the same two points Electron does:

```text
Electron (native Desktop, unchanged)          Webapp (this PR)
desktopPluginsRoot()  -> reconcile, then root  GET  /api/desktop-plugins/root       -> reconcile_desktop_halves(), then root
reconcileDesktopPlugins() after an install     POST /api/desktop-plugins/reconcile  <- bridge's reconcileDesktopPlugins()
                                                                                       (plugin-install-run.ts, plugins-tab.tsx, linked resync)
```

`hermes_cli/desktop_plugin_halves.py` keeps Electron's on-disk contract exactly, because both writers share the folder on a host that also runs native Desktop:

- Same `.hermes-package.json` fields (`package`, `source`, `sourceMtimeMs`, `linked`, `repo`/`sha`/`catalogName`), so the loader pairs the half with its agent row and keeps it off until enabled (GHSA-mcfc-hp25-cjv7).
- The default home wins over a profile for the same name. A package root follows symlinks; the app root does not.
- A marker-less folder whose `plugin.js` matches byte for byte is adopted. Anything else is the user's own plugin and is never touched (#112450).
- An installed package re-copies when its source is newer; a linked dev checkout compares bytes.
- Copies are staged and renamed into place, so a failure never leaves a partial, marker-less folder.
- A copy is pruned only when its source `plugin.js` is really gone (ENOENT), never when it just can't be read.
- Server threads share one lock, as Electron serializes writers in its main process.

### Design call: where the copy runs

Bear suggested moving the copy into the Python install/update/enable path so both surfaces share one implementation. I put it where the loader looks instead (root resolution, plus the on-demand route the renderer already calls after an install). That point covers what an install hook would miss: packages linked in by hand (`ln -s`), installs from before this change, and a removal through any path. With the Webapp's 5 s scan, an install shows up within seconds without a separate hook.

Electron keeps its own TypeScript copy in this PR. Retiring it means native Desktop has to call into its local Python on every scan, which is a bigger change to Desktop's boot path. I'd rather do that as its own PR once this behaviour has run on the Webapp. Until then the Python tests pin the contract above, and the two implementations write the same marker. If you'd rather unify first, I'll rework it.

## Related Issue

Closes #145540
Refs #144648

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/desktop_plugin_halves.py` (new): `reconcile_desktop_halves`, `materialize_desktop_half`.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/desktop_plugins.py`: the root route reconciles first; new `POST /api/desktop-plugins/reconcile`. Same `SurfacePolicy.desktop_plugins` gate.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-desktop-plugins.ts`: `reconcileDesktopPlugins` calls the new route.
- `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: the half now appears on a headless host too.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_desktop_plugin_halves.py` (new), end to end through the real routes against a temp Hermes root.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_desktop_plugin_halves.py tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_desktop_plugins.py`
2. Live: on a host with no native Desktop, install an agent+desktop package (`hermes plugins install ...`), open the Webapp, and check that the desktop half shows up in Capabilities → Plugins, off until enabled.

Before and after:

```text
test_webapp_desktop_plugin_halves.py (each reads the folder the way the browser's loader does: /root, /list, /read)
                                                                   without this change    with it
a_package_installed_on_a_headless_host_brings_its_desktop_half     KeyError: 'radar'      passed (marker: package, source)
the_copy_follows_its_package_until_it_is_uninstalled               KeyError: 'radar'      passed (v2 re-copied; gone after uninstall)
a_users_own_plugin_is_never_overwritten_and_the_default_home_wins  KeyError: 'radar'      passed
a_copy_made_before_markers_existed_is_adopted_in_place             TypeError (no marker)  passed
```

Also passing: `test_webapp_desktop_plugins.py` (7), `runtime-loader.test.ts` + `browser-desktop-plugins*` (35), `tsc --noEmit`, `python scripts/check`.

Live run (Windows 11; isolated `HERMES_HOME`; gateway from this checkout serving the Webapp on 127.0.0.1:9391; bundle built from `feat/webapp-desktop-halves` (`be01a0a8d0`, before the conflict-free rebase onto `main`), which carries this PR; real Chromium tab signed in with a one-use link):

```text
host has plugins/radar/{plugin.yaml, desktop/plugin.js}, no native Desktop, desktop-plugins/ holds only livecheck
open the tab                           server copies desktop-plugins/radar/ + marker {package: radar, source: <home>/plugins/radar/desktop}
Capabilities -> Plugins                Radar listed as a User package, switch off; no RADAR chip (opt-in, as native)
turn Radar on                          chip "RADAR HALF" renders from the copied half
remove plugins/radar on the host       copy pruned, chip gone ~3 s later; the standalone livecheck plugin untouched
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Reverting stops the server's copies. Folders it already wrote have a marker in the same format Electron writes, so native Desktop keeps managing them, and its prune removes them once their package is gone.

**Blast radius:** Webapp surface only; the routes 404 elsewhere, and native Desktop is unchanged. This is the first write behind these routes: on the serving host, `<root>/desktop-plugins/<name>/` folders appear for installed agent+desktop packages and go away when the package is uninstalled. Folders without a marker (the user's own plugins) are never written or removed. On a host that also runs native Desktop, both write the same folders with the same rules. A race between the two processes fails that copy, and the next pass (5 s later) redoes it.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [ ] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) (stacked: also carries #145072 and #145539 until they merge)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (ran the affected files through `scripts/run_tests.sh`, not the full suite)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (tests and a live run in a real browser, see above)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

## What does this PR do?

Credential previews stop showing any character of the stored secret. Every preview (dashboard `/api/env`, messaging channel creds, desktop Keys settings, `hermes config` / `status` / `dump`, proxy tokens, MCP config, the gateway session credential hint) and every log / model-context token mask becomes a keyed fingerprint: `***#a3f91c`.

**The exploit.** `agent/redact.py` `mask_secret()` showed first-4/last-4 of any value of 12 or more characters. A short password pasted 2-3× gets past that length floor and is shown in full:

```
mask_secret('PasswordPassword')      -> Pass...word        # the whole password
_mask_token('PasswordPassword12')    -> Passwo...rd12      # log / model-context path, 6+4
Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)> -> Basic <first 6 b64 chars>...   # base64 head decodes to the username
```

A 9-11 character password pasted twice leaked 8 of its characters the same way. The web dashboard and desktop app also rebuilt the same `xxxx...xxxx` preview client-side right after a save.

**Fix.** `mask_secret()` returns `***#` + the first 6 hex characters of `HMAC-SHA256(install_key, b"hermes-secret-fingerprint-v1\0" + value)`. If the key can't be read or created it returns `***`. It never falls back to showing characters. `_mask_token()` uses the same fingerprint for tokens of 18+ characters and still returns `***` below that.

**Why HMAC and not a plain hash.** A plain SHA-256 of a weak password can be brute-forced offline from a screenshot or a shared `hermes dump`. Without this install's key the fingerprint tells an outsider nothing. The input is domain-separated so the key can't be confused with any other use.

**Why a per-install key at the install root and not per profile.** The point of a fingerprint is to confirm a rotation took and to see when two places hold the same key. The key lives at `<install root>/secret_fingerprint.key`, resolved from the active home with `get_default_hermes_root(home=get_hermes_home())`, so it follows a routed-profile override. That means every profile on a machine fingerprints the same secret the same way. A bare `HERMES_HOME=/x` (Docker, tests) is its own root. The key is random, 32 bytes, stored hex-encoded and mode `0600`. It is created symlink-safe with `tools/spill_safety.write_text_exclusive` (`O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`). A symlinked, non-regular, group/world-readable or malformed key file is refused and the preview falls back to `***`. It is deliberately **not** `install_id`, which is shared with hosted-room peers. `hermes backup` excludes it, because a restore on another machine should mint its own key.

**Value-only fingerprint (deliberate trade-off).** The HMAC covers the value only, not the variable name. Two variables holding the same secret show the same fingerprint, which is the reuse/rotation signal. The cost is that a reader can see two vars share a value, which is the intent.

**Why the write guard moved to `save_env_value`.** `is_redacted_credential_preview()` only ran in `PUT /api/env` (and a couple of router pre-checks). `hermes config set`, setup wizards, `web_routers/messaging.py`, MCP config, `credential_lifecycle.save_provider_env_credential` and the agent's own tools all reach `hermes_cli/config.py` `save_env_value()` with no check, so a copied preview could be persisted as the secret (the #35519 bug class).
- The shape predicate and `REDACTED_CREDENTIAL_WRITE_DETAIL` now live in `agent/redact.py`, next to the producers, and can be imported without a cycle.
- `save_env_value()` raises `ValueError` before touching `.env`. Existing routes already map that to 400.
- `web_routers/_common.py` keeps a thin wrapper as a pre-mutation check.
- The guard learns the `***#xxxxxx` shape. It also checks the ASCII-only form `save_env_value` would store, so a zero-width/NBSP-padded preview can't slip past and then be "sanitised" into one.
- Related: #42748 covers `config set` placeholders only.

**Alternatives considered.** Plain `***` for every set value, with no key file, is simpler. But you can no longer confirm a rotation took or tell whether two profiles share a key. The fingerprint costs one 32-byte file. Keeping known public vendor prefixes (`sk-`, `ghp_`) in log masks was left out. The prefix list would need its own care, and `_mask_token_nonreusable` already shows the label where it matters (`file_read`).

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Display/redaction-mask bypasses are listed in SECURITY.md §3.2 as out of the private channel, so this is a regular PR. Related: #35519, #42748.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (§3.1 scope). Not applicable: §3.2 redaction bypass.

## Changes Made

**Affected surfaces:**
- `hermes config` / `config get` / `status` via `redact_key`
- `config_show`
- `hermes dump`
- `proxy_cli` token listing
- `web_server_mcp`
- `web_routers/ops.py`
- `web_routers/_common.redacted_credential_preview`, used by `/api/env` and by **`web_routers/messaging.py` channel credentials** (`ChannelsPage.tsx`)
- `gateway/session_local.py` credential hint
- `RedactingFormatter` logs, model-context and egress redaction via `_mask_token`

**Changes, one commit each:**
- `fix(redact): show keyed fingerprints instead of secret characters`. Changes `agent/redact.py` (`mask_secret`, key handling, preview predicate, `refuse_credential_preview`), `hermes_cli/config.py` (`save_env_value` guard), `hermes_cli/web_routers/_common.py` (thin wrapper) and `hermes_cli/backup.py` (exclude the key file). Tests updated or added.
- `fix(dashboard): stop deriving credential previews from the secret`. Adds `web/src/lib/env-state.ts` `credentialPreview`. `EnvPage.tsx` stores `«redacted-secret»` after a save and renders through `credentialPreview`. `ChannelsPage.tsx` renders through `credentialPreview`.
- `fix(desktop): stop deriving credential previews from the secret`. Removes `redactedValue` from `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/helpers.ts`. `env-credentials.tsx` stores `«redacted-secret»`, and the fingerprint arrives on the next env refetch.
- `fix(redact): fingerprint log/display tokens too (Basic-auth username leak)`. `_mask_token` uses the fingerprint. Old vendor-prefix / `...` assertions move to the new contract.
- `fix(redact): keep the closing quote after a masked API-key header`. This one is optional and can be dropped on its own. `_SECRET_HEADER_RE` used `(\S+)` and swallowed the closing quote in `curl -H 'X-Api-Key: …'`. It now uses the quote-excluding class `_AUTH_HEADER_RE` already uses.

**Known limits:**
- Old desktop builds and open browser tabs still compute `xxxx...xxxx` locally until they update. The server keeps refusing that shape as a write, so there's no integrity risk.
- Fingerprints differ across machines by design.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_redact.py -q`. Covers fingerprints for 1-16 char passwords × 1-4 repeats, the key file 0600 at the install root, profiles sharing the root key, a home override resolving its own root, symlinked / world-readable / truncated keys falling back to `***`, `_mask_token`, Basic auth, JWT and header quotes.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_secret_previews.py tests/hermes_cli/test_config_preview_write_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_backup_fingerprint_key.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py tests/hermes_cli/test_set_config_value.py tests/gateway/test_local_session_info_fields.py -q`. Checks that `/api/env` returns `«redacted:***#xxxxxx»`, a bare fingerprint PUT returns 400, and the `save_env_value` guard leaves `.env` untouched for `***`, `***#abcdef`, `«redacted:***#abcdef»`, `«redacted-secret»`, `abcd...efgh` and zero-width variants.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh $(grep -rlE "redact_sensitive_text|redact_for_egress|RedactingFormatter|redact_terminal_output|_mask_token|redact_cdp_url" tests --include=*.py) -q`
4. `cd web && npm test && npm run typecheck`, then `cd apps/desktop && npm test -- src/app/settings && npm run typecheck`.
5. Manual, under a scratch `HERMES_HOME`: `save_env_value("EXA_API_KEY", "PasswordPassword")`. `hermes config` then shows `Exa ***#67baf9` with no `Pass`. `secret_fingerprint.key` is `-rw-------` at the install root, and a `profiles/p1` home under that root prints the same fingerprint.
6. `python scripts/check`

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (related, not duplicate: #42748, #125428)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. The targeted suites above pass. In `tests/agent tests/hermes_cli tests/gateway`, the remaining failures also fail on unmodified `upstream/main` in this environment (missing `keyring`, update/source-build/gui/fs-workspace tests).
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 7.0)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docstrings updated. No user docs mention the old preview shape. Otherwise N/A.
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A (no config keys)
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A

prs.title: Add muse-harness plugin catalog entry
prs.body:
## What this plugin does

`muse-harness` starts a local `muse serve` process and speaks Muse Session Protocol (newline JSON-RPC) so a Hermes tool can run one turn inside Muse Code. Wonder Full stays inside the official harness. The tool can attach session MCP servers, which is how that turn calls something like Unreal mid-run.

It does not mint a Muse Code subscription key, does not read Muse credential files, and does not call `api.meta.ai` itself.

## Surfaces

- One tool: `muse_turn` (`ctx.register_tool`)
- No hooks, middleware, desktop UI, or env secrets

## Disclosure (catalog rule 13)

- Spawns the user-installed `muse` binary and talks to it on stdin/stdout. That process calls Meta through Muse's own login.
- Removes `META_API_KEY`, `MODEL_API_KEY`, `META_MODEL_API_KEY`, and `MUSE_CODE_SUB_TOKEN` from the child environment so a pay-as-you-go key cannot replace the CLI login. It does not read those values.
- Default approval mode is `denyUnmatched`. `allowAll` is only used when the tool call sets it. No `--yolo`, no sandbox disable.
- Unattended runs hit `timeout_s` (default 600, max 1200) instead of waiting on a browser login.
- No telemetry. No self-updater. No bundled binaries.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` passed on `23d53b8654a0939340db5bb6e80e5e98789c959b` (manifest, capability probe, security scan safe, no core override).

Pinned repo: https://github.com/SnoobieJunes/hermes-muse-harness

prs.body:
## What

SHA bump for the existing `kiwi` community entry: the pinned buyer runtime moves from `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5` to `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7`.

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-catalog/kiwi.yaml` → `sha` | `5d23517308bf9e5d75b62dcda63a19dd03ab0491` | `6703b4f6187f9a2ec0826959f0c87ccc2d0f14fe` |
| `version` | `"1.2.2"` | `"1.2.3"` |
| `mcp.json` runtime pin | `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5` | `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7` |

- Plugin repo: <https://github.com/harrylabsj/hermes-plugin-kiwi> (public) — commit `6703b4f`, tag `v1.2.3`, release note: *pin the buyer runtime to @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7*.
- Engine: `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7` on the public npm registry (`dist-tags.latest = "0.12.7"`), published from the open-source A2A commerce runtime <https://github.com/harrylabsj/kiwi> (Apache-2.0).
- tier: `community` · category: `tools` · `capabilities`: all four keys empty — this is a portable manifest-only package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`), there is no host `__init__.py`/`register()` to probe. The tool surface is disclosed in `description`.
- Entry diff is exactly three lines (`sha`, `version`, the pin version inside `description`); `repo`, `maintainer`, `docs_url`, `platforms`, `capabilities` unchanged.

## What changed upstream (0.12.5 → 0.12.7)

Release notes: <https://github.com/harrylabsj/kiwi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md> (v0.12.7 section). Buyer-facing, enforcement-side changes:

- **Delegation limits are now actually enforced on accept** (`max_total_price` / `max_unit_price` / `max_quantity` / `allowed_merchants` / `allowed_currencies`), with fail-closed rejection when a price cannot be parsed as a structured amount. Previously these limits were declared but not applied on the accept path.
- **ASK approvals are bound to `task_id` + candidate digest and are single-use** (consumed once accept/handoff lands).
- `GetExtendedAgentCard` now requires an authenticated identity (anonymous calls are rejected with `authentication_required`); `message/send` anonymous T0 inquiries are unchanged.
- Optional buyer-side A2A request signing (`a2aSigningKeyDir`, Ed25519 / RFC 9421) — unset keeps the previous anonymous-T0 behaviour.
- Merchant listings may now carry a platform product page (JD / Taobao / Tmall) surfaced to buyers as an `external_checkout_url` handoff destination; Kiwi still neither orders nor pays.
- Buyer HTTP surface (`kiwi buyer-api serve`) now fails closed without a bearer token; loopback is not exempt.

No buyer tool was added, removed or re-parameterised — the MCP tool surface is unchanged (see evidence below), so the bundled `kiwi-buyer` skill text needs no behavioural edit for this bump.

## Verification (run locally for this revision)

1. **Consumer path, neutral directory** (no `package.json` in cwd, `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`): `npx -y @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7 mcp serve` with JSON-RPC `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list` → **13 tools**, `serverInfo: kiwi-buyer-mcp 0.1.0`, every description ASCII/English.
2. **Tool surface unchanged**: full `tools/list` JSON dumped for `0.12.5` and `0.12.7` and compared — **byte-identical** (same 13 tool names, schemas and descriptions), so no bundled-skill drift.
3. **Pinned-source segment**: `git clone https://github.com/harrylabsj/hermes-plugin-kiwi` → `git checkout --detach 6703b4f6187f9a2ec0826959f0c87ccc2d0f14fe` → `hermes plugins validate .` → `Validation passed.` The only message is a pre-existing warning (`skill:kiwi-buyer: metadata must map string keys to string values`) that also shows up on the currently catalogued `5d23517` commit; it is not introduced by this bump.
4. **Structural segment**: `uv run --with ruamel.yaml==0.18.17 python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog` at upstream `main` (`dc39239`) with this change applied → `OK: 861 file(s) valid`, exit 0.
5. **No self-update logic** in the pinned tree (grep for update-fetch / self-replace patterns: no hits). Updating the runtime pin is exactly this SHA-bump PR.

## Checklist

- [x] `sha` is a 40-character commit that is pushed and publicly reachable in the plugin repo
- [x] `version` matches the plugin repo's release tag (`v1.2.3`)
- [x] No self-update / fetch-and-replace logic in the package
- [x] Bundled `SKILL.md` is English-first (`SKILL.zh-CN.md` ships as the translation)
- [x] `capabilities` left empty (portable package, no host code to probe)
- [x] `platforms` unchanged (`[]` — pure npx/Node, no OS-specific dependency)

prs.title: fix(skills): duckduckgo-search: -o saves a file, it does not print JSON
prs.body:
**Problem:** The duckduckgo-search skill lists `ddgs text ... -o json` as "JSON output for parsing". In the ddgs CLI, `-o` saves results to an automatically named file in the current directory and prints nothing, so an agent following the skill gets empty output and leaves a stray file wherever it happens to be.
**Fix:** Describe `-o` as a save-to-file flag with an explicit path, drop it from the search-then-extract example, and show JSON on stdout through the Python API (`json.dumps`). The generated docs page is regenerated to match.

## Details
- Repro (ddgs 9.16.0, Linux), in an empty directory:
  ```
  $ ddgs text -q "python programming" -m 2 -o json > stdout.txt; ls
  stdout.txt  text_python_programming_20261025_075443.json
  $ wc -c stdout.txt
  0 stdout.txt
  ```
  `ddgs text --help`: `-o, --output TEXT  csv, json or filename.csv|json (save the results to a csv or json file)`. `-o out/results.json` writes exactly that file.
- Checked: the new Python snippet prints a JSON array; `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py` changes only this skill's page; `python scripts/check` passes.
- Docs-only change, so no tests added. Not a duplicate as far as I can find (searched issues and PRs for ddgs/duckduckgo with -o/json/output/file). #136867 edits only this skill's description, so it doesn't overlap.
- Prepared by an AI agent (Hermes); reviewed and submitted by @GeekKingCloud, who is accountable for it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): an auto-started gateway exits when its home's state.db is deleted under it
prs.body:
**Problem:** If a client deletes its throwaway `HERMES_HOME` while the `--idle-exit` gateway it started is still running, that gateway never exits. It still holds the deleted `state.db` WAL, so the deleted-WAL guard refuses every new `SessionDB` for that home. The heartbeat/loop/handoff gates fail closed on that refusal, and idle exit reports `active heartbeat in <home>` forever. Each leftover process holds 150-230 MB.
**Fix:** In `busy_reason`, skip homes whose authority store was deleted or replaced. Nothing there can be written or served by this process any more, and the next client starts a fresh gateway.

## Details
- Repro on current `main`: start the watcher, unlink the home's `state.db-wal`/`-shm`, and `busy_reason` returns `active heartbeat in …` on every tick. With work already queued in that store it reports `admissions pending`, though those rows can never run either.
- Detection uses the store's own `_raise_if_db_replaced()` (`StateDbReplacedError`, which includes `DeletedWalGenerationError`). Every other probe still fails closed.
- Test: one case in `tests/gateway/test_unmanaged_idle_exit.py` with the real store gates (fails on `main`, passes here). `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the idle-exit tests (10 files, 70 passed) and `python scripts/check` pass.
- No existing issue or PR found (searched idle exit + deleted home / active heartbeat / `DeletedWalGenerationError` / never exits). #140509 and #143089 are different causes.
- Prepared by an AI assistant (Hermes); reviewed and submitted by @GeekKingCloud, who is accountable for it.

prs.title: fix(browser): forward the sandbox CDP port before a vault fill attaches
prs.body:
**Problem:** When the browser runs inside the terminal sandbox (Bot Screen placed in a Docker or SSH backend), `browser_vault_fill` attaches its supervisor to the CDP URL the sandbox reports, such as `ws://127.0.0.1:9223/...`. That is the sandbox's loopback, not the host's, so the fill fails with `supervisor_required`. If something on the host happens to listen on that port, the vault attaches to the wrong browser.
**Fix:** `_ensure_supervisor` now goes through the existing `_reach_sandbox_cdp` forward, the same one `browser_use_cli` uses. If the forward fails, the vault refuses to attach instead of falling back to the raw loopback URL.

This PR was prepared by an AI coding agent (Hermes). Ian, who opens this PR, reviewed it and is the accountable human.

## Details

- Cause: `_ensure_supervisor` (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py`) calls `get cdp-url` and attaches to the result directly. `_reach_sandbox_cdp` (`tools/browser_use_cli.py`) already handles this case, and its docstring names the vault supervisor, but the vault path never calls it.
- Repro: put the browser in the sandbox (`placement: terminal`, Docker backend), save a login, then call `browser_vault_fill` on its login page. The supervisor is pointed at the sandbox's loopback port on the host. I confirmed this against `main` with the offline tests below (fake forward and supervisor). I haven't run it end to end against a live Docker sandbox.
- Edge case: if the forward happens to get the same local port number as the sandbox port, the URL is unchanged and the fill refuses. That is rare, and it fails closed.
- Related: #136660 (re-attach after a configured browser restarts) and #128694 (attach to the effective session key) change the same function for different bugs. Neither forwards the sandbox port, and whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- Tests: `tests/tools/test_browser_vault_sandbox_cdp.py` has two offline tests. One checks that the supervisor attaches to the forwarded port; the other checks that a failed forward never attaches. Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix.

## What does this PR do?

Covered above.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Found while running sandboxed Bot Screen together with vault fill. I searched issues and PRs in all states and found no duplicate.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/browser_vault_tool.py`: `_ensure_supervisor` forwards the sandbox CDP port before attaching, and refuses an unforwarded sandbox loopback URL.
- `tests/tools/test_browser_vault_sandbox_cdp.py`: two regression tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_vault_sandbox_cdp.py`. Both tests fail on `main` and pass on this branch.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py tests/tools/test_bot_desktop_placement.py`. Existing vault and placement tests still pass.
3. Manual check: Docker backend with `placement: terminal`, then run `browser_vault_fill` on a saved login.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run the affected test files with `scripts/run_tests.sh` and they pass (the full suite was not run)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Arch Linux (Omarchy), Python 3.14.7

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docs, `cli-config.yaml.example`, CONTRIBUTING/AGENTS, tool schemas: N/A (no behaviour or config surface change)

prs.title: Optional deep-researcher skill: evidence-ledger research that batches searches in code
prs.body:
Adds `deep-researcher` as an official optional skill (`hermes skills install official/research/deep-researcher`) for long, multi-source research with a claim/evidence ledger. Searches, extraction and ledger writes are batched inside `execute_code`.

## Maintainer salvage (rebased onto current main, @BrentWilkins's commit kept as-is)

The contributed skill landed as `3ff9e37` with its authorship intact. Three commits on top:

- **`c79582a` Search-as-code.** The skill banned inline Python and capped discovery at 4/8/12 single `web_search` calls, so every query cost a model turn and left its raw snippets in context. New `references/search-as-code.md` covers four steps, each run as ONE `execute_code` call through the native `hermes_tools.web_search`/`web_extract`:
  - **Discovery round:** fan out every query, dedupe canonical URLs in Python, keep a persisted seen-set, print a ranked shortlist.
  - **Extraction round:** select passages in code and cache pages with line locators.
  - **Recording round:** write the whole batch through the ledger CLI.
  - **Deep mode:** independent sub-questions go to parallel `delegate_task` children, and the parent stays the single ledger writer.

  SKILL.md also lists the CLI signatures and the report format the audit expects, because live runs spent 6–10 calls on `--help` and reading script source. `evidence_ledger.py --question` now accepts the leading ID (`Q1`) and refuses an unknown question when the record is written (before this, only `check` caught it).
- **`74d6762` Tests trimmed to two invariants:** hostnames never count as independent origins, and `archive --prune` keeps every registered artifact restorable byte-for-byte while leaving unregistered files alone.
- **`32be5fa` Code-health ratchet:** `check_url`'s catch-all is narrowed to what `urlopen` raises. CC is waived on the two vendored validators (`# health: allow CC -- vendored upstream`).

### Why: comparison with Perplexity Computer's Deep Research

Perplexity Computer made Deep Research a built-in skill inside its agent harness ([help center, Oct 26 2026](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/2026102603-deep-research-and-model-council-in-computer); [launch post](https://x.com/perplexity_ai/status/2065124948793028691)). In their words, it runs on "Search as Code": *"the model writes code that assembles search itself, running thousands of retrieval steps in parallel."*

| | Contributed skill | This PR | Perplexity Computer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Query fan-out | 1 `web_search` per turn, ≤12 total | all of a round's queries in one `execute_code` call | generated search code |
| What reaches context | every raw snippet | deduped, ranked shortlist + selected passages | not documented |
| Sub-questions | serial | parallel `delegate_task` in deep mode | sub-agents |
| Evidence bookkeeping | one `terminal` call per record | one batched CLI call per round | not documented |

### Live A/B: real `hermes chat -q`, same prompt, same model

Setup: `google/gemini-3.8-flash` on OpenRouter, Firecrawl web backend, scratch `HERMES_HOME`, standard mode, one question (did 2025 European heat pump sales recover, which countries drove it, what are the barriers). Numbers below are read back from each run's own `state.db` and run dir; N=1 per leg.

| | base (contributed skill) | head (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Model API calls | 44 | **34** |
| Tool calls | 48 | 33 |
| `--help` calls | 6 | **0** |
| Distinct queries issued | 10 | **24** |
| Canonical URLs considered | (not tracked) | 136 |
| Ledger: sources / claims | 10 / 12 | 12 / 11 |
| Tool-result chars entering context | 214k | **151k** |
| Estimated cost | $0.514 | $0.488 |
| Wall clock | 339 s | 745 s (one 29 s reasoning step + more extraction) |
| `audit_report.py --no-live` | PASS | PASS |

A first head iteration without the recording recipe and signature list cost 54 API calls: the model wrote `evidence.json` by hand and ran `--help` 7 times. Those two additions are what brought it down to 34.

**Not covered:** the deep-mode `delegate_task` fan-out was not exercised live (the A/B ran standard mode). Single-model, single-question, N=1. The live link check (`audit_report.py` without `--no-live`) was run once on the head report: 1 expected 403 warning.

**Tests:** `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_deep_researcher_skill.py tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py tests/website` gives 1530 passed. `scripts/check --only health` is clean, and the skills guard verdict is `safe`.

## Contributor follow-up: upstream validation refactor

Merged back into [research-skills #1](https://github.com/BrentWilkins/research-skills/pull/1), preserving the selected maintainer fixes and the broader upstream test suite. The matching Hermes refactor is now in `54b9571738`: the ledger validator and report audit are split into focused stages and both vendored-upstream CC waivers are removed. With the pinned Ruff 0.15.22, their complexity drops from 37 to 2 and 29 to 3; extracted helpers are at most 12. Diagnostics and exit status are unchanged across 1,000 ledger and 108 report comparison fixtures.

Validation: all 13 `scripts/check` checks pass; `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_deep_researcher_skill.py tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py -q` passes 1,482 tests in a fresh PM-built locked environment. The upstream suite passes all 25 tests. This follow-up does not change the maintainer's research budgets or batching recipes in Hermes. Local-model wall-time/token comparisons are separate work and are not a performance claim for this refactor.

## Infographic

![deep-researcher search-as-code](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0236d/Fnt6gQy8KzXvfnhhddqtT_GBAVZa2w.png)

---

## Original description (@BrentWilkins)

## What does this PR do?

Adds `deep-researcher` as an official optional research skill, with a catalog entry and generated documentation page. It guides substantial multi-source investigations using native Hermes retrieval tools, a persistent claim/evidence ledger, explicit collection budgets, and resumable research runs.

The skill is maintained at https://github.com/BrentWilkins/research-skills. This contribution includes only the core skill and its standard-library helpers. The separately installable research-access plugin is not included or required. No core tools, model configuration, dependency manifests, or user settings change.

## Why a separate optional skill?

`grounded-citations` already covers source registration, citation rendering, and evidence-backed answers. This skill is for the larger research lifecycle: question-specific atomic claims and counter-sources, explicitly assessed shared-origin groups, source coverage limitations, bounded gap discovery, progress checkpoints, and verified archive/restore. It points simple lookups and single-claim checks toward a smaller workflow. It does not replace `grounded-citations` or claim to verify semantic truth automatically.

The existing researcher-now proposal (#47932) integrates a hosted research service; this skill uses Hermes's configured native retrieval tools and local bookkeeping, with no additional research service or model calls introduced by its helpers.

## Type of Change

- [x] New skill (official optional)

## Changes Made

- `optional-skills/research/deep-researcher/`: instructions, dossier template, synthetic worked example, run-management reference, and ledger/audit/archive helpers.
- `tests/skills/test_deep_researcher_skill.py`: behavioral tests for evidence links, shared origins, brief truncation, report auditing, checkpoints, storage warnings, safe paths, codec fallbacks, and byte-exact archive/prune/restore.
- Optional-skills catalog, generated skill page, and sidebar entry.

Archives retain the readable report and recovery manifest. Pruning is opt-in and limited to registered files after verification. Compression falls back from LZMA to deflate to uncompressed ZIP without installing dependencies. The storage budget is a warning, not a hard quota.

## How to Test

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_deep_researcher_skill.py tests/website/test_generate_skill_docs.py -q
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py -k deep-researcher -q
python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff origin/main
```

On Linux / Python 3.11: 14 research tests, 7 documentation-generator tests, and 6 skill-specific authoring checks pass. Hermes's skill scanner reports `safe` with no findings. The staged Windows-footgun check and `git diff --check` pass. Tests use temporary synthetic artifacts and no live network calls. The symlink test is Linux-marked; portable path checks remain cross-platform.

For a manual skill exercise, use the synthetic example in `references/worked-example.md`, then audit a report, mark the run complete, archive/prune, restore into a fresh directory, and resume. After merge, install with `hermes skills install official/research/deep-researcher`.

## Validation limits

The full Hermes suite, full Docusaurus build, and a new live-model research session were not run for this PR. macOS and Windows execution are not yet verified. Script checks establish structural invariants, not source truth, semantic independence, or research-quality equivalence.

prs.body:
## What & Why

`hermes doctor` reports npm vulnerabilities in the root (agent-browser), `web`, and `ui-tui` workspaces. These come from the committed `package-lock.json` (reified by `npm ci` on every `hermes update`), so a local `npm audit fix` never persists — the durable fix is a lockfile bump, per the doctor's own guidance (#116774).

This PR bumps the existing `overrides` in `package.json` to the patched releases:

| Package | From | To | Advisory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brace-expansion` | 5.0.9 | 5.0.12 | GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7, GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p |
| `js-yaml` | 4.3.1 | 4.3.2 | GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh |
| `undici` | 6.28.0 | 6.29.0 | GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v, GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5 |
| `yaml` | 2.8.1 | 2.9.1 | GHSA-48c2-rrv3-qjmp |

`undici@6.29.0` is under the 14-day `min-release-age` gate, so a temporary `min-release-age-exclude[]=undici` entry was added to `.npmrc` (the repo's established pattern for vuln-fix packages — remove once it's > 2 weeks old).

## How to test

```bash
npm audit --workspaces=false        # root / agent-browser
npm audit --workspace web
npm audit --workspace ui-tui
```

All three now report **0 vulnerabilities** (previously 2 high / 1 high+1 moderate / 1 high+1 moderate).

## Verification

- `web` typecheck passes (`tsc -p . --noEmit`).
- `ui-tui` typecheck unchanged vs. clean `main` (only pre-existing `vitest` module-resolution errors in test files, unrelated to this change).
- Remaining `npm audit` findings (dompurify, ip-address, mermaid, socks, streamdown) are in the `apps/desktop` workspace, which `hermes doctor` does not audit — left as a follow-up.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Node v26.7.0, npm 12.1.0.

prs.title: fix(providers): require the /api/ps fingerprint before treating a loopback server as Ollama
prs.body:
## Problem

`detect_local_server_type()` labels any loopback server that answers `/api/tags` with a body containing `"models"` as **Ollama**. That verdict drives `query_ollama_num_ctx()`, which injects Ollama's proprietary `options: {num_ctx: N}` into every chat-completions request.

**magpie** (yetone/magpie, a popular local model-router gateway on `127.0.0.1:3425`) deliberately emulates part of the Ollama surface — its docs list `/api/version`, `/api/tags` and `/api/show` as served "for a client that takes only an Ollama endpoint". So when Hermes is configured with a `custom` provider pointing at magpie:

1. `detect_local_server_type()` → `"ollama"` (magpie answers `/api/tags` with a models list),
2. `/api/show` reports `magpie.context_length: 1000000` → `query_ollama_num_ctx()` returns 1000000,
3. every request now carries `options: {num_ctx: 1000000}`,
4. magpie's routing groups forward to upstreams that speak strict OpenAI wire — **NVIDIA NIM rejects it with `400 Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): options`** — and the whole agent run dies after 3 retries.

In production this killed a scheduled cron job for 6 consecutive runs (`RuntimeError: NVIDIA NIM: Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): 'options'`), because the router only lands on the strict upstream for a subset of requests — a plain curl against the router looks healthy, so the failure is hard to diagnose.

## Fix

`/api/ps` separates a real Ollama from an emulator: real Ollama answers it with `200 {"models": [...]}`; magpie 404s it (its `/api/ps` returns an error body noting it only serves the OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini gateway paths). `_is_ollama_server()` now additionally requires this fingerprint before the `ollama` verdict gates `options`/`num_ctx` injection. The fingerprint is cached (300s TTL) — this runs at agent init, not per turn.

- Real Ollama: fingerprint passes, `num_ctx` detection and injection unchanged (verified live against Ollama 0.40.11: `num_ctx=262144` still detected).
- Emulator/router: `options` never injected; requests go out on the plain OpenAI wire.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_ollama_num_ctx.py`:
- existing `detect_local_server_type` mocks now also stub the fingerprint (Level 1 & 3 suites);
- new `TestOllamaEmulatorIsNotTreatedAsOllama`: an `ollama`-waterfall verdict without the `/api/ps` fingerprint yields no `num_ctx`, and the fingerprint requires `200` + `"models"` body.

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_ollama_num_ctx.py tests/plugins/model_providers/test_custom_profile.py tests/agent/test_unsupported_parameter_retry.py` → **50 passed, 0 failed**.

prs.title: fix(cli): a session paused on a lost turn refuses the prompt and /discard resumes it
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

If the gateway restarts in the middle of a turn, the owner marks that turn `unknown` and pauses the session FIFO. Until the lost turn is acknowledged, nothing queued behind it runs. The classic CLI (`hermes chat`, gateway-backed) still submitted new prompts into that paused FIFO and then waited for a `message.complete` that would never arrive. On screen this looks like `Initializing agent...` that never ends, and the classic CLI had no way to recover from inside the chat: the session's own `/discard` command was not wired into it, and the only way out was `hermes sessions discard <id>` in a separate terminal.

This PR covers the classic-CLI and messaging-gateway side of #139532. #139541 covers the ACP editor side and does not touch these paths.

## Related Issue

Refs #139532 (CLI + gateway paths; ACP is #139541)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: `run_conversation` now refuses the prompt before submitting when the session has an `unknown` admission. It returns `failure_reason="unknown_execution"` and copy that names `/discard`. If the fence lands after submit (the owner restarted while the prompt was being submitted), `_pump` sees the prompt still `queued` behind the lost turn, withdraws it with `prompt.cancel`, and returns the same refusal instead of waiting forever. When the prompt is queued behind another admission that is still running (for example an automation turn that the restarted owner drains first), the CLI says so once rather than staying silent. That silence is what made users resend the same message into the queue.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: `SessionState` now tracks `pending` from the resume snapshot and from every `session.info` frame. A redial resubscribes, so the state reflects what the restarted owner fenced.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_cli_commands.py`, `hermes_cli/commands.py`, `cli.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py`, `locales/*.yaml`: `/discard [admission_id]` wired into the classic CLI, the in-chat form of `hermes sessions discard` (the registry entry itself is the gateway's; this extends it with the CLI route and its copy). It goes through the same fenced `prompt.resolve_unknown` call with the generation the owner stamped. The lost turn is acknowledged and not replayed. A bare `/discard` covers every lost turn in the session, so it lists them and asks `Proceed? [y/N]` first, as `hermes sessions discard` does; naming admission ids is the explicit form that does not ask. Without a gateway session the command reports that there is nothing to discard.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`, `agent/error_surface.py`: `unknown_execution` is now a site failure code on the gateway layer. The CLI shows the copy as written and does not classify it as a provider failure.
- `gateway/session_authority.py`: the `Session … paused: unknown_execution` warning used to say "ask the operator". It now names the exact operator command, including `-p <profile>` for non-default profiles. (The messaging pause notice itself is upstream's in-chat `/discard` advice; this PR keeps that wording.)
- Regenerated `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-command-parity.md` and `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-slash-registry.json`.

Fail-closed is preserved: nothing is replayed, and no turn is discarded without an explicit `/discard`.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_cli_lost_turn.py`: 4 passed. On base, all 4 fail on the 20 s per-test timeout, because each one waits forever.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_native_pause_notice.py -k one_notice_per_episode`: passes. Fails on base, since the paused messaging waiter never returns and no notice names a way out.
- Affected files: `test_gateway_agent.py`, `test_gateway_cli_commands.py`, `test_gateway_command_parity.py`, `test_desktop_slash_registry.py`, `test_failed_turn_site_codes.py`, `test_failed_turn_chat_copy.py`, `test_i18n.py`, `test_commands.py`: all pass.
- `python scripts/check`: ok.

Note: `test_crash_mid_turn_then_platform_message_gets_one_pause_notice_and_reset_unpauses` (the live-daemon e2e) fails in my environment on unpatched base too. Its fixture daemon never reaches `ready` because the launcher runs a source-update dependency step first. It is unrelated to this change.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this is not a duplicate.
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix.
- [x] I've run relevant tests locally.
- [x] I've added regression coverage.
- [x] Documentation update: generated parity table and desktop registry regenerated.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; protocol-level Python behavior.

prs.title: fix(mcp): drain list_* pagination in the server capability probe
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The `hermes mcp` **Test server** probe reported prompt/resource **counts** from a single `list_prompts()` / `list_resources()` call. The MCP spec lets servers paginate `prompts/list` and `resources/list` via an opaque `nextCursor`, and the Python SDK's `ClientSession.list_*` returns exactly one page per call — so on a paginated server the probe stopped at page 1 and understated the server's real capabilities.

This is the same nextCursor-draining invariant already applied to the tools / resources / prompts **discovery** sites in `tools/mcp_tool.py` (the `_paginate_full_list()` sweep). The capability probe was a remaining `list_*` site that still fetched only page 1. The gap was visible *within a single probe*: the tool count in the same result already comes from the paginated discovery (`server._tools`), while the prompt/resource counts did not follow the cursor — so a paginated server rendered as, say, "42 tools, 2 prompts" when it actually exposes many more.

The fix reuses the existing `_paginate_full_list()` helper (opaque-string cursor validation + 50-page runaway cap) under the server's `_rpc_lock`, exactly matching the discovery handlers. The probes stay best-effort: a server that doesn't advertise/allow the capability still just yields `0`, and the existing capability-gating (`tools.prompts` / `tools.resources` config + advertised-capability check) is untouched.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py` — in `_probe_single_server`, drain `list_prompts` / `list_resources` through `_paginate_full_list()` (held under `server._rpc_lock`) instead of reading a single page, and import the helper. Counts now reflect every page.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_config.py` — add `test_probe_counts_drain_pagination` (a mocked server paginating prompts 2+1 and resources 1+2 reports 3 and 3); give the capability-gating test doubles an `_rpc_lock` so they exercise the drained path.

## How to Test

1. Configure an MCP server that paginates `prompts/list` / `resources/list` (returns a `nextCursor`), e.g. one exposing >1 page of prompts.
2. Run the `hermes mcp` **Test server** action (or the web dashboard test endpoint) against it.
3. Before this change the reported prompt/resource counts stop at the first page; after it they reflect the full catalog — matching the tool count, which was already paginated.

Automated:

```
pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_config.py tests/tools/test_mcp_list_pagination.py tests/tools/test_mcp_probe.py -q
# 74 passed
```

The new test fails without the source change (`assert 2 == 3`) and passes with it.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(scope):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run the relevant test suites and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings/comments) — or N/A
- [x] cli-config.yaml.example — N/A (no config keys changed)
- [x] CONTRIBUTING.md / AGENTS.md — N/A (no architecture/workflow change)
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — N/A (pure async/list logic, no platform-specific code)

prs.title: feat(kanban): show generic handoff attention in web and desktop
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Kanban's Review column does not distinguish ordinary agent review from a question or testing request waiting for a person. Web and Desktop now show one current attention badge: **Needs your answer** in amber, **Awaiting your testing** in blue, or **Run failed** in red. The drawer shows the concrete request/error.

A producer can replace the current testing badge with short plain text and a fixed semantic tone (`success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`). For example, an integration can supply a green acceptance label without adding project-specific client logic. Clients continue to use the underlying native wait state; the label does not change ordering, dispatch, permissions or CI/merge decisions.

## Changes Made

- Reuse the dashboard's existing bulk task/run/event reads to project `current_attention`. Event/run identity, not timestamps or prose, identifies the current ended handoff; a new claim or lifecycle transition clears stale attention.
- Keep the projection in one topical native sibling shared by the dashboard API and the optional annotation setter. `set_review_attention(..., expected_handoff_event_id=..., badge=...)` accepts only the current unclaimed `awaiting-test` handoff; `None` clears, identical writes are no-ops, and invalid/stale writes return false. Annotations use the existing event log, with no schema or new task state.
- Render one escaped badge in both existing Web plugin and Desktop card/drawer components. The server supplies custom text and one of four semantic tones; clients own the fixed palette. There is no repository-specific condition, extra border, generic plugin framework or new build pipeline. Existing default labels remain localized; the Web plugin follows its existing translation/fallback convention.
- Include existing event IDs in native `kanban show --json`, so integrations can identify handoffs through the supported CLI response. The REST detail response already exposes event IDs.

## Validation

On macOS arm64:

- Canonical native runner: **76 passed** across the attention, real CLI serialization and dashboard REST tests.
- Desktop component tests: **35 passed** across attention, actual board cards and drawer behavior.
- Web tests: **3 passed**, including loading the actual registered Kanban IIFE and checking card/detail rendering, one badge, default/custom tones, stale suppression and escaped text. The test uses Web's declared React/ReactDOM packages, not Desktop-only test dependencies.
- Full Desktop and Web typechecks, focused ESLint, and **all 13 canonical repository checks** against the PR base pass.
- The CLI regression fails against the prior missing-ID response; the Web regression fails against the prior renderer without badges. Independent read-only review found no blocking correctness or scope issues.

The full repository Python suite and manual visual acceptance have not been performed. Remote CI is reported by GitHub separately. This contribution does not include any runtime fork's DNS, recurrence, dependency, restart or consumer-specific policies.

## How to Test

1. Use the existing `kanban_request_review` tool with a concrete summary and `metadata={"wait_reason":"awaiting-answer"}` or `awaiting-test`. On a human-review board, inspect the Web/Desktop card and drawer.
2. For the current unclaimed testing handoff, call the native annotation setter with its exact handoff event ID and `badge={"label":"Ready for acceptance","tone":"success"}`. It should replace the blue label with one green label. Repeat to verify idempotency, then pass `badge=None` to restore the default.
3. Reopen, resolve or claim the task: old attention must disappear. A harmless comment or priority edit must preserve a current question. Ordinary review must not infer human attention from historical metadata or summary wording.
4. Inspect a current failed run: its red badge shows the recorded failure; resolution clears the badge without deleting history.

Desktop and runtime ship independently: an existing official Desktop without this renderer will not display new producer badges solely because a server was updated. Official support requires this client change to be accepted and released. Older clients/backends retain their existing presentation.

## Checklist

- [x] Feature stays within existing native handoff, event-log and UI surfaces.
- [x] No schema, configuration, scheduler or dispatch-policy change.
- [x] Regression tests and user guide updated.
- [x] Both client typechecks and canonical checks pass.

prs.title: feat(cli): run hermes chat -q in-process and load a per-run MCP overlay
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A process that spawns `hermes chat -q` once per task can now run that turn in the child process and attach MCP servers that are not in `config.yaml`.

`HERMES_INPROCESS_CHAT` set to a truthy value, together with a non-empty `-q` query, calls the existing one-shot path and does not enter the shared gateway. Interactive chat, the TUI, and `hermes chat` without `-q` stay on the gateway.

`HERMES_MCP_OVERLAY` is a path to a JSON file, `{ "<name>": { "url": "https://…", "headers": { … } } }`. The file is read for that process only. Only `http` and `https` URLs are kept, header values must be strings, and the suspicious-server filter still applies. Each server is exposed as toolset `mcp-<name>`. When the enabled-toolset list is a concrete list, those toolsets are appended. `None` still means all toolsets. After the reply, the process prints `session_id: <id>` when a session id exists.

These are process inputs from the spawning program. They are not written into the user's Hermes con

## Related Issue

No existing issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/main.py`: `cmd_chat` routes a non-empty `-q` query to the one-shot path when `HERMES_INPROCESS_CHAT` is set. `provider=auto` is passed as no explicit provider.
- `hermes_cli/oneshot.py`: append `mcp-<name>` toolsets for overlay servers, and print `session_id:` after the reply when `HERMES_INPCESS_CHAT` is set.
- `tools/mcp_tool_config.py`: load `HERMES_MCP_OVERLAY` after portable servers. Overlay entries win on a name clash. The file is read with `utf-8-sig`.
- `hermes_cli/mcp_startup.py`: a non-empty overlay is enough to start MCP discovery when `config.yaml` has no `mcp_servers`.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_inprocess_chat_overlay.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_startup.py`, and `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_overlay.py`.

## How to Test

1. From the checkout, run `source ./activate` in bash, or in zsh run `unsetopt NOMATCH` first.
2. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_inprocess_chat_overlay.py tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_startup.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_overlay.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py -q`.
3. Run `python scripts/check`.
4. Manual check: write an overlay JSON file with one `https` URL, then run `HERMES_INPROCESS_CHAT=1 HERMES_MCP_OVERLAY=/path/to/overlay.json hermes chat -q "list your MCP tools"`. The process should answer in that process and print a `session_id:` line. A chat with no query should still open the normal gateway session.

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore reasoning display after gateway reconnect
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Restore the classic CLI's reasoning display preference when its existing connection reconnects to the gateway.

The gateway's `live.show_reasoning` flag is intentionally session-scoped and in-memory. `GatewayAgent.reasoning_callback` sends it and caches the last `(session_id, enabled)` pair. After a gateway restart the CLI keeps that cache, but the new owner has no flag. `GatewayConnection._resubscribe` restores the subscription without restoring the preference. Replies still stream, but live reasoning no longer does; the CLI can subsequently render `last_reasoning` in its end-of-turn fallback box, below the streamed reply. Restarting the CLI masks the problem by sending the flag again.

Keep the preference in this viewer's per-session state and replay it after a successful resume, before the reconnected socket becomes ready. Use the asynchronous client already on that loop, not the blocking `connection.call`. Preserve explicit hidden preferences too; sessions without a preference are untouched. A restore failure follows the existing reconnect failure path, so no prompt is silently admitted before restoration. No prompt replay, persistent config write, transcript mutation, or new protocol/config field is introduced.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (classic CLI reconnect regression).
Related: #139470 restores the same live flag on ACP reattachment. This PR changes the classic CLI only; it does not duplicate ACP, Desktop, reasoning-effort persistence, or commentary routing work.

Searched open and closed/merged issues and PRs for the symptom, `show_reasoning`, reconnect/restart, and the cache symbol; checked the tracker body and comments. No existing classic CLI fix for this path was found.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`: remember the callback-derived preference on the session's shared viewer state.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_connection.py`: restore that preference after resuming each retained session, before readiness/new requests. A refused resume is still skipped, with no config write for that session.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py`: exercise shown/hidden preferences, first-turn ordering, same-connection write deduplication, and independent preferences for multiple sessions. Update the existing lost-turn test for the added restore request.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py`: use a real disposable gateway daemon and a loopback fake model, restart the daemon, and verify the same CLI connection/agent receives reasoning before answer deltas on its next turn.

## How to Test

Interactive reproduction:
1. Start a classic CLI session with streaming and `/reasoning show`.
2. Finish a turn, then restart its gateway while keeping the CLI open.
3. Ask another question in the same CLI. Expected: live reasoning still arrives before the reply, without restarting the CLI. On the base, the owner loses its flag and reasoning falls back to the end-of-turn box.

Automated validation on Linux, Python 3.14.7:
- Base: `0f3eac0b8f7ccef9c469c9e9469c5b08e538d8f4`.
- New regression cases on the unchanged base: **3 failed**, at missing reasoning callbacks / missing restore writes (not collection failures).
- The real-daemon restart test also fails on a clean archive of the base: the second turn returns the answer but receives no reasoning (`'' != 'REASONING-BEFORE-THE-ANSWER'`). With the fix it passes, retaining the same connection/agent and receiving all reasoning before the first answer delta. No production gateway or external model is used.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_agent.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_session_store.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_disconnect_outcome.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_tools.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_chat_blocking_controls.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_reasoning_reconnect_live.py --file-retries 0 -j 2`: **126 passed, 0 failed** (7 files, no retries).
- `python scripts/check --base origin/main`: **12 checks passed**.

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs for duplicates.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep OpenCode Go keys on a per-model upstream 429
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

OpenCode Go returns HTTP 429 for two unrelated conditions:

| Body | Meaning | Correct recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"GoUsageLimitError",...},"metadata":{"limitName":"weekly"}}` | the key's plan window (5-hour / weekly / monthly) | bench the key, rotate (already classified `billing` on main) |
| `{"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later."}}` | one model's upstream throttle | keep the key, defer to fallback |

On main both bench the key for the 429 hour. Repro with a two-key `opencode-go` pool where the primary has hit its weekly window: the main agent's model gets the per-model upstream 429, the pool logs `marking <backup> exhausted (status=429)`, and then every auxiliary task pinned to a *different* model on the same provider (approval, vision, compression) fails with `credential pool: no available entries`, although a direct call with the backup key on that other model returns 200.

## Changes

- `plugins/model-providers/opencode-zen/__init__.py`: the `opencode-go` profile sets `classify_api_error` (the existing provider-profile seam) and maps a 429 whose message contains `upstream request failed` to `upstream_rate_limit`. Every other error declines (`None`), so `GoUsageLimitError` keeps its built-in `billing` verdict.
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_recover_provider_pool`: the main path (`recover_with_credential_pool`) already skips rotation for `upstream_rate_limit`, but the auxiliary path only used substring predicates and benched anyway. It now consults `classify_api_error` and skips the bench for an `upstream_rate_limit` verdict. That also covers OpenRouter-wrapped upstream 429s on the aux path, which had the same gap.

## How to test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_rate_limit_scope.py`: red on main (2 failures: upstream body classified `rate_limit` and benched on the aux path), green with the fix.
- Directly affected suites: `test_opencode_go_profile.py`, `test_auxiliary_error_classification.py`, `test_provider_profile_recovery_seam.py`, `test_auxiliary_client_cache_eviction.py`, `test_error_classifier.py`: 239 passed.
- Main-path E2E against a temp `HERMES_HOME`: a real `CredentialPool` with two mock entries fed through `recover_with_credential_pool`. Upstream body → no rotation, both entries `ok`. Plan-wall body → primary `exhausted`, rotated to the second entry.
- `scripts/check`: ok.

Platform: Linux (Debian 13).

prs.title: fix(cli): a send on a dead gateway socket no longer kills the spinner thread
prs.body:
## What

A classic CLI attached to the gateway lost its spinner and live-work dock for the rest of the session after one gateway disconnect. Instead, it printed this to the terminal:

```
Exception in thread Thread-4 (_tui_spinner_loop):
  File "hermes_cli/cli_tui_mixin.py", line 412, in _tui_spinner_loop
    monitor.tick()
  File "hermes_cli/cli_subagent_monitor.py", line 127, in tick
  File "hermes_cli/gateway_tools.py", line 154, in subagent_rows
    result = self.connection.call("subagent.list", ...)
  File "hermes_cli/gateway_client.py", line 218, in rpc
    await self.websocket.send(json.dumps(...))
websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError: sent 1011 (internal error) keepalive ping timeout; no close frame received
```

## Why (exact lines)

- `hermes_cli/gateway_client.py` `GatewayClient.rpc`: `_read()` already turns a lost answer into `GatewayClientError("… turn outcome is unknown …")`. `websocket.send()` is not wrapped the same way. If the socket is already closed (here, after a keepalive ping timeout), the raw `websockets.ConnectionClosedError` escapes. That class derives from `Exception`, not from `ValueError` or `RuntimeError`.
- `GatewayConnection.call_tagged` only translates `TimeoutError`. So the raw error reaches `gateway_tools.subagent_rows`, which catches `(GatewayClientError, RuntimeError)`, and `subagent_tail`, which does the same.
- `cli_tui_mixin._tui_spinner_loop` calls `monitor.tick()` in a bare `while` loop. One raise ends the thread, and that thread drives both the spinner and the dock poll.

## Fix

1. `rpc()` reports a failed send (`ConnectionClosed`, `OSError`) as the same unknown-outcome `GatewayClientError` that a lost answer gets. It is not reported as `NOT_SENT`, because the frame may already have left before the socket died. `gateway_queue` retries `NOT_SENT`, so using it here could duplicate work. Every existing `except GatewayClientError` caller now sees the disconnect it already handles.
2. `SubagentMonitor.tick` skips one beat when a poll fails, logging at debug level with `exc_info`. Previously a failed poll ended the spinner thread. The guard lives in the monitor, not in the over-cap `cli_tui_mixin.py`.

## Tests (red on `main`, green with the fix)

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_client_rpc.py::test_send_on_a_dead_socket_is_a_client_error_not_a_raw_websockets_one`
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_subagent_monitor_gateway.py::test_a_failing_tick_keeps_the_spinner_thread_alive`

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_client_rpc.py tests/hermes_cli/test_subagent_monitor_gateway.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_subagent_monitor.py tests/hermes_cli/test_subagent_monitor_ui.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_client_backlog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_client_recovery_backlog.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_reconnect.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_connection_command_socket.py
scripts/check   # 12 checks, ok
```

Tested on Linux (Debian 13, Python 3.14, websockets 15.0.1).

Duplicate search: no open or closed PR or issue covers `ConnectionClosedError` from `subagent.list`, `_tui_spinner_loop`, or `rpc` send failures. #140163 and #140158 only demote 1011 log noise.
