prs.title: fix(security): harden dashboard secret reveal (opt-out, no-store, per-principal limit, 30s auto-hide)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Hardens secret revelation across the dashboard backend, web dashboard frontend, and native desktop app.

The reveal endpoint (`POST /api/env/reveal`) returns the plaintext value of a configured environment variable or credential so operators can view keys when necessary. Previously, plaintext secrets remained indefinitely in React component state once revealed until manually toggled back, and the backend lacked an opt-out switch, rate limiting, no-store caching directives, and principal audit logging.

This PR provides end-to-end hardening:
1. **Opt-out switch**: `security.dashboard_reveal_secrets` in `config.yaml` (default: `true`). When set to `false`, `/api/env/reveal` returns `403 Forbidden`. The default remains `true` for single-tenant local developer ergonomics, while remote or gated deployments should set `security.dashboard_reveal_secrets: false` to restrict operators to blind write/delete operations.
2. **`Cache-Control: no-store`**: Added to the `POST /api/env/reveal` response to guarantee that intermediate HTTP proxies and browser caches never persist sensitive secret payloads.
3. **Per-principal rate limiting**: Keyed on authenticated `Session.user_id` or client host IP address to throttle rapid extraction attempts.
4. **Audited access**: Emits a structured log line recording the target profile and accessing principal (user ID or client host), strictly omitting the secret value itself.
5. **Frontend ephemeral auto-hide (Web & Desktop)**: auto-hide after 30 s; clear on window blur; clear on hidden tab (visibilitychange); clear on route/profile change; clear on unmount

## Related Issue

Companion to PR #145787 ("fix(security): never reveal secret characters in credential previews"). While #145787 replaces character-revealing credential previews with keyed secret fingerprints so secrets are never displayed at rest, this PR hardens explicit on-demand revelation with opt-out enforcement, no-store headers, per-principal rate limits, audit logging, and 30s ephemeral auto-hide.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update

- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)

prs.title: fix(delegation): honour key_env pointers and refuse cross-endpoint key inheritance
prs.body:
## What this fixes

A delegation or auxiliary route that sets `base_url` and no credential resolves `api_key=None`,
which `_build_child_agent` reads as "inherit the parent session's key". If the route points at a
different endpoint than the parent, the child sends the parent's credential to that host and the
provider rejects it.

Live repro (config shape only): `auxiliary.review` = `provider: cliproxy` + `base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1`,
no key, launched by `/review` from a session on `api.anthropic.com` →
`401 {"error":"Invalid API key"}` on the local proxy, one failed subagent, zero diagnostics.

## Changes

- `tools/delegate_tool_config.py`
  - `_route_credential_pointer` — resolve `key_env` / `api_key_env` on a delegation or auxiliary
    block through `hermes_cli.config.get_env_value_prefer_dotenv` (the same reader the rest of the
    credential surface uses). Inline `api_key` still wins; a pointer that resolves empty leaves
    `api_key=None`, so inherit semantics are unchanged.
  - `_refuse_unkeyed_foreign_endpoint` — after the direct-endpoint branch, raise `ValueError` when
    no credential resolved **and** the route's endpoint is provably different from the parent's
    live endpoint. Same-endpoint routes and unprovable parents keep the documented behaviour.
- `agent/review_engine.py` — `_load_review_credentials_cfg` carries `key_env` through, otherwise
    the pointer is stripped before it reaches the resolver.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_delegate_key_env_pointer.py` — 5 cases (pointer, alias, inline wins,
  empty pointer, base_url untouched).
- `tests/tools/test_delegate_foreign_endpoint_refusal.py` — 6 cases (refusal + message contents,
  inline key, pointer key, same-endpoint inherit preserved, unknown parent, `/review` surface).

Related: #122052 (same `key_env` reader for the delegation block; this PR adds the refusal and the
`auxiliary.review` passthrough), #108951, #82610, #91308.

prs.title: fix(tools): reuse supervisor session for browser_cdp target_id (salvage #32950)
prs.body:
Fixes #32685. Salvage of #32950 (credit @LeonSGP43 — that branch has been conflicting since May with the review feedback unaddressed; all three review asks are applied here). Triage marked this `best fix — fixes` for the #32685 family.

## Summary

- **Symptom:** `browser_cdp` opens a fresh CDP WebSocket per call. On Browserless-style backends that spawn a private browser per connection, a target id returned by one call is invalid by the next — the documented `Target.getTargets` → `target_id` workflow always fails, and even a discovery call enumerates a *different* browser than the one a follow-up call executes in.
- **Change:** when the task has a live `CDPSupervisor`, `browser_cdp` rides its persistent WebSocket: `target_id` calls reuse the supervisor session already attached to that target (top-level page, OOPIF frame, or auto-attached child — `CDPSupervisor.resolve_target_session`), and browser-level calls (no `target_id`, e.g. `Target.getTargets`) go out on the same connection (`_browser_cdp_target_via_supervisor`; payloads carry `"connection": "supervisor"`). The supervisor records its page's target id wherever the page session is set (initial attach, reconnect, and `focus_page`, i.e. the vault login/checkout re-point), so a target id only ever resolves to its own page's session. No supervisor, or a target the supervisor doesn't track → the legacy stateless attach, unchanged.
- **Behavior:** a discovery → `target_id` chain observes ONE browser on per-connection backends; plain Chrome (targets shared across connections) behaves as before. The route runs *after* the shared `_browser_cdp_private_guard` (can't become the sibling bypass fixed for `frame_id` in 47764f19) and the supervisor payload goes through the same `_redact_cdp_output` boundary as the stateless one. `website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md` no longer claims every non-`frame_id` call is stateless.
- **Since 2026-10-27:** rebased past `68500d9ff9`, which removed the built-in browser tools and with them `browser_snapshot`. This PR therefore no longer adds a public `SupervisorSnapshot.page_target_id` for `browser_snapshot` to show: agents find target ids with `Target.getTargets`, which now rides the supervisor's connection too.

## Evidence

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_tool.py                                   # 51 passed (first commit alone: 49)
HERMES_E2E_BROWSER=1 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_supervisor.py -m integration   # 8 passed (first commit alone: 7; real Chromium)
```

Unit: private-page guard blocks the target route; fallback to stateless without a supervisor; supervisor route redacts a secret result; discovery without `target_id` rides the supervisor; discovery without a supervisor falls back; after a `focus_page` re-point, the supervisor's page target id names the focused tab and the old page's id never resolves to its session. Integration (real Chrome): a target found with `Target.getTargets` routes via the supervisor; discovery → evaluate rides one connection. New tests fail before the fix (against `main`'s `tools/`: 4 unit and 2 integration failures, from the missing route and `resolve_target_session`).

Production verification: self-hosted Browserless v2, Fedora 43, rootless podman — chains that previously landed in a fresh empty browser now resolve against the supervisor session (details in the #32685 / #32950 threads). The supervisor↔daemon split for the *dialog* half is tracked separately in #74216 (its snapshot half went with `browser_snapshot` in `68500d9ff9`).

## Overlap with in-flight PRs

Re-checked 2026-10-27 against current heads: #123723 `dcc5205c34`, #123794 `73ff15284d`, #126556 `af50b70278`.

- **#123723** and **#123794** no longer merge cleanly into `main` on their own (both predate `68500d9ff9`), so their pairwise notes need redoing once they're rebased. From the 10-08 check: #123723's `focus_page` assignment was byte-identical to this PR's, and #123794 has a one-line conflict in `_attach_initial_page` (both set `self._page_target_id`; keep #123794's `self._web_page_seen = self._driver_bind_failed = False` beside it).
- **#126556** (the open PR for #126523, which this PR deliberately leaves alone) merges cleanly into `main` and still has one conflicting hunk with this branch in `browser_cdp`: it hoists the `safe_timeout` clamp into `_clamp_cdp_timeout()` above the `frame_id` branch, and this PR's supervisor-routing block sits right after the old inline clamp. Resolution unchanged: take the hoisted clamp, drop the old clamp lines, keep the routing block (it uses the same `safe_timeout`). The other clamp PR, #126559, was closed unmerged by its author on 2026-10-08.

## Branch state

On current `main` (`74885f997b`, 2026-10-27), past upstream's browser-tools removal (`68500d9ff9`, 2026-10-22) and the 10-08 lint sweep (`d76cce4f11`) — re-homed onto the #102117 module split on 2026-09-04 (both files survived the split; upstream dropped `_child_sessions`, so `resolve_target_session` checks the page target then `_frames`, whose OOPIF frame ids equal their target ids). **Happy for this to be cherry-picked / salvaged**, or grafted onto #32950 if maintainers prefer the earliest-open PR — either is fine. Commit 1 carries all of the source and is green on its own (49 unit + 7 real-Chrome tests); commit 2 adds the browser-level discovery tests. The new routing function's two exception handlers follow upstream's code-health ratchet: the supervisor import catches only `ImportError`, and a failed supervisor-routed call is logged with its traceback at debug level before it becomes a tool error.

## Platforms tested

Linux (Fedora 43), Python 3.14.9 (the house runner's managed environment); Chrome for Testing 148 headless (integration) + in-process mock CDP server (unit). `python scripts/check --commit HEAD --base upstream/main` (code-health ratchet, Windows footguns, ruff, …): 13 checks ok on both commits.

prs.title: fix(liveness): tolerate ±2s cross-process probe drift in pid liveness fingerprints
prs.body:
## Problem

Processes on one host read the same pid's start time with ~1s disagreement (observed +1.00 s exactly: 178978036115 recorded vs 03:12:40.15 kernel). Bit-exact start-time compares in liveness predicates then declared live owners dead/recycled:

- `cron/executions.py` `_owner_is_live` reclaimed 9 running executions (reclaim-job falsely swept live jobs).
- Sibling predicates had the same bit-exact class: `gateway/status.py` (`_pid_marker_names_self`, `_scoped_lock_owner_state`, `_validated_scoped_lock_gateway_owner`), `gateway/delivery_ledger.py` (`_owner_alive`), `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py` (`_pid_recycled`) — drift made a live scoped-lock owner read "exited" (lock stolen while held) and a live worker read "recycled" (termination refused for the wrong pid).

## Fix

- New helper `gateway.status.start_times_match(current, recorded, *, tolerance=200)`: ±2 native units (centiseconds: psutil `create_time()*100` on macOS, /proc field 22 at USER_HZ=100 on Linux — same scale on both), False on junk, documented int() coercion.
- All five liveness predicates route through it. Probe-None → live in liveness contexts (unprobeable ≠ dead).
- Kill-permission gates (`_start_times_agree` force-kill, `pid_is_hermes`) deliberately stay bit-exact: a refused kill is fail-safe, a wrongly permitted one is not.
- String fingerprints (kanban dispatch) keep the epoch part exact — cross-boot reuse still detected; only the start-time component widens.

## Tests (18 new, all green; drift polarity empirically verified to fail on pre-fix sources)

- `tests/cron/test_owner_liveness_fingerprint.py` — drifted live owner stays live; far/recycled still detected; probe-None stays live; boundary ±200 inclusive.
- `tests/gateway/test_liveness_fingerprint_tolerance.py` — same polarities for all five sibling predicates + `_validated_scoped_lock_gateway_owner` corroboration compare.

Independent reviewer verdict: APPROVE (two-pass).

prs.title: fix(desktop): respect chat text scale in Bot Mode group rooms
prs.body:
## Summary

Bot Mode group-room messages ignored Appearance → Chat text size because their message bodies were outside the conversation typography scope. At 150%, the shared Markdown renderer still displayed 13px text.

Apply the existing `--chat-text-scale` contract to message bodies in both canonical rooms and the legacy room view. Canonical messages now expose the same content slot as legacy messages, and both use the conversation font-size token in place of fixed `text-xs`.

Extend the same typography scope to the canonical composer, the shared legacy/inline-reply editor, and canonical notices. Editor line height follows the conversation tokens. Room labels, timestamps, buttons, and editor width retain their sizing, and changing text size preserves the unsent draft.

Fixes NousResearch/hermes-agent#144095.

## Contribution credit

Thanks to **Kevin Rose (@kropdx)** for the complementary [composer/notice scaling fix and Electron regression](https://github.com/kropdx/hermes-agent/commit/661369b57d75d53f227308e182e1f53c21094840), [offered in this discussion](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/144510#issuecomment-6428684816). His contribution retains its original author attribution. The commits have been rebased onto current upstream `main`; the canonical composer now receives the scaling through upstream’s shared mention-aware editor. The Electron fixture was updated for that editor’s SDK imports.

## Validation

- Regression coverage for user and member messages in canonical and legacy rooms at default 110% and changed 150% scales.
- 52 related Vitest tests across 9 files passed after rebasing onto upstream `main`.
- Contributor's Electron regression passes on the rebased head as well as the original `661369b57d`; the same test failed with the production files restored to the original PR head, specifically for notice/composer font sizes and composer line height.
- Electron checks cover canonical Markdown, notices, composer font size and line height at 100%, 175%, 90%, and 110%, plus unchanged control fonts/editor width and draft preservation. The shared legacy editor has passing existing behavior tests, without a separate legacy browser scenario.
- Desktop `npm run typecheck` passed.
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files: no errors; two pre-existing effect-cleanup warnings in `canonical-group-workspace.tsx`.
- `python scripts/check --base upstream/main`: all 13 checks passed after rebasing.
- Initial message-body Chromium verification: before = 13px at both 100% and 150%; after = 13px at 100% and 19.5px at 150%. With the follow-up, canonical messages, notices, and composer measure 13px at 100% and 22.75px at 175%.

## Before / after screenshots

The screenshots below document the initial message-body fix at `3090519`; the composer/notice follow-up is demonstrated in [@kropdx’s before/after GIFs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/144510#issuecomment-6428684816).

Captured at matching 100% and 150% **chat text-size** settings, with a fixed 1200 × 900 viewport. This is a seeded rendering fixture using the production canonical group history, shared Markdown renderer, stylesheet, and chat text-size store; it does not require a live model or gateway. The surrounding fixture header shows the selected setting.

| 100% | ![Before at 100%](https://github.com/cryptictech/hermes-agent/releases/download/t3-evidence-144095/before-100.png) | ![After at 100%](https://github.com/cryptictech/hermes-agent/releases/download/t3-evidence-144095/after-100.png) |

prs.title: Web Access: a failed restart names its cause, page icons load without sign-in, an empty own URL shows no LAN address
prs.body:
Three small Web Access issues @dokterdok found live on a real Mac (thanks!, [report](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/144648)). A failed gateway restart now says why instead of a generic 90-second timeout. The page icon loads without sign-in, like the favicon. The "My own URL" address row no longer shows the LAN address while the URL field is empty.

Refs #144648

From the report:
> after 90 s the pane showed "Couldn't change web access: The gateway didn't serve the web app within 90 seconds." … It doesn't name the cause, which appears only in `logs/gateway-restart.log`.
> `/apple-touch-icon.png`, which the page also uses as its icon, requires sign-in, while `/favicon.ico` doesn't … That likely explains the `login_start` (`auto_sso`) entries with no matching success after each page load.
> under "My own URL", while the field is still empty, the address row keeps showing the LAN address.

## What changes (live, main `74885f997be` vs head)

| Case | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| Restart gateway; the restart child exits at once with `run \`hermes pm repair\`` | Pane keeps showing "Starting". After 90 s: "The gateway didn't serve the web app within 90 seconds." | About 1.5 s later: "The gateway couldn't restart: error: Hermes's dependency environment is missing; run \`hermes pm repair\`". The pill goes back to "Restart needed". |
| `curl /apple-touch-icon.png`, no cookie, gated Webapp | `302 → /login?next=%2Fapple-touch-icon.png` | `200 image/png` (same bytes as the bundle's icon) |
| `curl /favicon.ico`, no cookie (control) | `200 image/x-icon` | `200 image/x-icon` |
| `curl /hermes.png` and `/`, no cookie (other files stay gated) | `302 → /login` | `302 → /login` |
| My own URL selected, field empty | Address row shows `http://<LAN IP>:9120` | No address: the row reads "Web access" |
| My own URL, `https://hermes.example.test` typed | (row shows the LAN address) | Row shows `https://hermes.example.test` |

Screenshots (native Desktop, Electron under Xvnc, attached to a real `gateway run --force` on a scratch HOME; each md5 matches its run's capture):

- **Restart failure, main** (shot 120 s after the click): ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e3e2091b3d160d864fc5f50882eb16bc/raw/base-restart.png)
- **Restart failure, head** (shot 5 s after the click): ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e3e2091b3d160d864fc5f50882eb16bc/raw/head-restart.png)
- **My own URL with an empty field, main:** ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e3e2091b3d160d864fc5f50882eb16bc/raw/base-ownurl.png)
- **My own URL with an empty field, head:** ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e3e2091b3d160d864fc5f50882eb16bc/raw/head-ownurl.png)
- **My own URL with a URL typed, head:** ![](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/e3e2091b3d160d864fc5f50882eb16bc/raw/head-ownurl-typed.png)

## Changes

- **A failed restart names its cause.** `GET /api/webapp-access/status` now returns `restart_failure: {pid, exit_code, reason}` when the newest restart of that gateway exited nonzero (`hermes_cli/web_server_gateway.py::gateway_restart_failure`). `reason` is the last line the child wrote in its own section of `logs/gateway-restart.log`, or `exit code N` when it wrote nothing. The section is found by the pid and byte offset recorded when that child spawned, so a later retry that fails to spawn can't lend it its text. The pane compares `pid` with the `restart_pid` that its Start/Stop/Restart got back, so a failure from an older restart is ignored. The pane checks for a matching failure before it accepts the status, so a Stop of a web app the gateway couldn't serve also names the failed restart.
- **Page icons skip the sign-in gate.** `/apple-touch-icon.png` (the Webapp's `rel=icon`, `apple-touch-icon` and `shortcut icon`) is added to `/favicon.ico`'s unauthenticated list in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py`, as an exact match. That is the only icon the bundle ships, and there is no manifest. Its prefix siblings (`/apple-touch-icon.png.map`, `…pngx`) stay gated, and so does every other public file.
- **Empty own URL, empty row.** Until Web Access starts, the address row shows the address being picked: the typed URL under My own URL (empty while the field is empty), or the LAN address under This network. Once Web Access runs, the row shows the saved config as before.
- New string `restartFailedBecause` in all 9 locales, and `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.

## Design calls

- **Where the failure travels:** the restart route still answers at once (`restart_started: true`). Making it wait on the child would hold the request for as long as a slow, successful restart takes. The status route the pane already polls reports the outcome, keyed by the pid the restart returned. The data comes from the record `_spawn_gateway_restart` already keeps (`_LAST_GATEWAY_RESTART`), filtered to this gateway's own `gateway restart` argv. No new state and no new writer.
- **Boundaries:** the status route is still native-Desktop-only (`owner_on_this_machine`). The only route that gets wider is one exact static icon path. It never falls back to the SPA's `index.html`: a missing file answers the static-asset 404.
- **Native Desktop:** only the Web Access pane changes. The Webapp renderer is untouched.
- **Not covered:** if the restart child kills the old gateway and the new one never comes up, nothing is left to answer `/status`, so that case still ends in the 90-second timeout. The report's case (the child exits while the old gateway keeps serving) is the one fixed here.

## Tests (each red on main, green on head)

Greptile's two P2 threads were fixed in cf5cafdc70e and answered inline.


- `tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_access_restart_failure.py`: the real restart route and the real `_spawn_hermes_action` (log header included), with the child swapped for a stand-in that exits 1 with the report's line, exits 0, exits 3 with no output, or is followed by a retry that fails to spawn. No gateway lifecycle code runs.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_page_icons.py`: on a gated Webapp, `/apple-touch-icon.png` and `/favicon.ico` answer 200 with no session. `/hermes.png` and the icon's prefix siblings still redirect to sign-in.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/web-access-settings.test.tsx`: the pane names the cause of the matching restart, including after a Stop while the web app was unavailable, and ignores an older restart's failure. The address row shows no LAN address under an empty own URL.
- Ran clean: `test_webapp_access.py`, `test_dashboard_auth_middleware.py`, `test_dashboard_auth_body_limit.py`, the pane's vitest file, the i18n tests and `scripts/check`.

## How it was run live

- **Restart failure:** a `sitecustomize` swapped the restart child's argv for a stand-in that prints the report's `run \`hermes pm repair\`` line and exits 1. The real `hermes gateway restart` never runs. Both legs' `logs/gateway-restart.log` ended with that line.
- **Icons:** a real `gateway run` serving the Webapp on `0.0.0.0` with the basic-auth provider, which needs no Portal account. `HERMES_WEBAPP_DIST` pointed at a small bundle holding the real `apple-touch-icon.png`, `favicon.ico` and `hermes.png`.
- **Not run live:** the Nous auto-SSO path. Basic auth sends unauthenticated loads to `/login`, not auto-SSO, so the removed orphan `login_start` entries were not observed directly. The gate check that skips them is the same one.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab01bc1/z2lCP7jsf-Q66pej13Zlo_74bLBdaF.png)

prs.title: fix(kanban): the active_pr respawn guard respects PR state, card lane, and an explicit unguard
prs.body:
# Dispatcher: stop the `active_pr` respawn guard from stranding merged/report cards

Two cards sat in `ready` for hours today with `!!! [critical] stranded_in_ready` and zero workers
spawned; the gateway logged `kanban dispatcher stuck: … Last tick held back: active_pr=1`. The guard
in `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py::check_respawn_guard` treated *any* GitHub PR URL in a comment
inside a hardcoded 24 h window as "a duplicate PR is about to be opened":

1. a card whose comment **reported an already-merged PR** stayed guarded — its own conclusion locked
   it out of running;
2. a `local-only` report card that merely **mentioned** a PR in a coordination comment was frozen for
   24 h, and could never escape because it can never be handed to a different profile;
3. single-owner cards had no CLI lever at all (the workaround was `assign <other>` then `assign <back>`).

## What changed

- **PR-state awareness.** Every distinct PR URL in the window is resolved with one bounded
  `gh api repos/O/R/pulls/N` call (10 s timeout, no shell, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `check=False`), cached per
  process for 300 s — **failures are cached too**, so a host without `gh` or auth does not fork a
  subprocess per card per tick. `MERGED`/`CLOSED` on every distinct URL lifts the guard; `OPEN` or an
  unresolved lookup still guards (fail closed, unchanged).
- **Lane awareness, from `completion_contract`.** `local-only` is a card's own declaration that it
  produces no PR, so the guard does not apply at all and costs **zero** `gh` lookups — unless one of
  the card's runs recorded `published_pr`, which makes it implementer work whatever it declared. Any
  other contract (repo slug, PR URL) is PR-bearing, and so is an unset one (legacy rows, fail closed).
- **Config knob.** `kanban.respawn_guard_pr_window_seconds` (default `86400`, `0` disables the step),
  overridable per process with `HERMES_KANBAN_RESPAWN_GUARD_PR_WINDOW_SECONDS`; negative/non-integer
  falls back to the default. Read inside the resolver (like `_resolve_rate_limit_cooldown_seconds`),
  not threaded through `DispatchContext`.
- **Operator escape hatch.** `hermes kanban unguard <id>` records an `unguarded` event, which lifts
  the guard exactly like a handoff. It is denied to `delegate_task` children so a worker cannot lift
  its own guard. Same-profile `assigned` semantics are untouched: a no-op re-assign still does **not**
  lift the guard for the implementer who opened the PR (`#111910`); `unguard` is the sanctioned lever
  for a single-owner or report card.

## Layout note (code-health ratchet)

`kanban_db_dispatch.py`, `kanban_db.py` and `config_defaults.py` are all over the 2000-line target, so
they may not grow. The behaviour went into topical siblings instead:

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_pr_guard.py` — the `gh` lookup + cache, `_task_publishes_pr`, `_is_handoff_event`,
  `_pr_guard_reason` (the `active_pr` step, taking the dispatcher's `_resolve_pr_state` so tests keep one
  monkeypatch seam) and `unguard_task`;
- `kanban_db.py` re-exports `unguard_task` from the tail import block (facade publishes, sibling owns);
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults_kanban.py` holds the `kanban` defaults block, embedded into `DEFAULT_CONFIG`
  as-is — `DEFAULT_CONFIG["kanban"]` is identical to `main`, verified by comparison.

`hermes_cli/kanban_diagnostics.py` is untouched: `_rule_stranded_in_ready` is deliberately age-based and
not guard-aware. The acceptance for the diagnostics item is that the card **spawns** (test 1) and
therefore leaves `ready`, not a rule change.

## Reviewer attention: the lane heuristic and `create_task`

`create_task` normalises an omitted `completion_contract` to `local-only` (`validate_contract`), so a
card created without an explicit contract lands in the report lane and is not guarded unless a run
recorded `published_pr`. That follows the card's rule (only an *explicit* `local-only` is the
exemption; unset rows stay PR-bearing) but narrows the duplicate-PR protection for contract-less
cards. The pre-existing `active_pr` tests now declare an explicit repo contract, so their intent —
an open PR still guards — is unchanged; `test_active_pr_guard_holds_through_same_profile_reassign_and_unassign`
is untouched in behaviour.

## Verification (all run in the worktree, `origin/main` @ `fde4219745` merged in)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_lifecycle.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_lifecycle_complete.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py` → **70 passed, 0 failed**.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli -q -k kanban` → **545 passed, 47 failed, 1 collection error**;
  the same run on unmodified `origin/main` gives **533 passed, 47 failed, 1 collection error** with the
  identical failing-file list (the extra 12 passes are this branch's new tests). Every failure is
  environmental — `home_io_guard` ("file I/O against the REAL hermes home", this worktree lives under
  `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`), `ModuleNotFoundError: keyring`, and the pre-existing
  `test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`.
- `python scripts/check --only health` → **0 blocking** (3 before the offset commit).
- `python scripts/check --only ruff` → ok. `python -m scripts.ci.check_docs_drift` → ok (124 config keys).
- No test shells out to `gh`: the file-level autouse fixture pins `_resolve_pr_state` to `None` and
  clears the cache on both sides; the report-lane test asserts a call counter stays at zero.

## Tests added

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_lifecycle.py`: merged PR spawns (also the diagnostics acceptance),
closed PR spawns, open PR still guards, unknown state fails closed, lookup cache (success and failure),
`local-only` report card exempt with zero lookups, `local-only` + `published_pr` still guards, window
knob (`0` disables; a short window with a backdated comment), `unguarded` lifts the guard + unknown id
returns `False`. `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py`: `hermes kanban unguard <id>` returns 0, writes
the event, is in `_DELEGATED_CHILD_DENIED_ACTIONS`, and reports `no such task` for an unknown id.

## Risks / rollback

- Cost: at most one `gh` subprocess per distinct PR URL per 300 s per process; report-lane cards and
  `0`-window installs cost none. A `gh` failure is cached, so no fork storm.
- Behaviour change is one-directional: a card can now spawn where it previously held; the only new
  "hold" is none (an unresolved lookup keeps today's behaviour).
- Rollback: revert the two commits; the config key is additive and the `unguarded` event kind is inert
  without the guard change.

prs.title: fix(desktop): branch mid-turn boundary + branch-at-message row cut
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two desktop session-branching defects. Two logical commits, defect 2 first (smaller and independent), defect 1 second.

### Operator-visible behavior

Two symptoms, both on the message-row path. The session-menu path is unaffected:

- **Session-menu branch works correctly.** Right-click a conversation in the left session menu and branch from it: it branches properly, with no restriction even while a turn is running.
- **Message-row symptom 1 — wrong cut.** Clicking "branch from message" on a specific message does NOT branch from that message — the child transcript ends at a PREVIOUS message.
- **Message-row symptom 2 — refused mid-turn.** Branching from a specific message is refused while a turn is going on — a restriction that does NOT exist on the session-menu path.

That the menu path is unaffected is the key diagnostic evidence: the defect is in the client's message-row path (the local-projection→row-count mapping and the blanket client-side busy gate with no backend guard), not in the shared branch backend — which is why the session-menu branch behaved correctly all along.

Repro evidence (measured on real sessions): the "install openwebui" parent `20261019_100605_7dd727` = 26 authoritative spine messages. "install openwebui #2" (branched at the last message) cut correctly. "install openwebui #3" (branched 27 s later at the same last message) cut 10 messages early, through row 43564 ("The env file is root-owned (0600)").

**Defect 2 — "branch at the bottom of a message cuts at an EARLIER message."**
Clicking the branch option at the bottom of a message branched the child from an earlier message. Root cause: the client sent the visible-message `count` it derived from its LOCAL message list, and the backend did `history[:count]`. When the renderer's local list is a COMPACTED model projection it is shorter than the authoritative display projection, so the count prefix landed on an earlier message. Measured from real sessions: a parent whose local projection had compacted, and a child branched 27 s after its sibling from the same last message, kept only the first 16 of the 26 authoritative spine messages — cut 10 early.

Fix: the durable row boundary is now the source of truth. The legacy dial keeps the canonical `through_message_id` (it no longer strips it), the backend cuts by the row boundary (which **wins** over `count`) so the child keeps exactly the prefix through the clicked bubble's last durable row, and `count` is a legacy fallback only. A pre-v9 backend that refuses the new key (4000 "out of sync", `extra="forbid"`) is handled by `forkBranch`'s catch — it retries the same branch count-only, which is exactly the pre-v9 behaviour.

**Defect 1 — the "Session busy" blanket gate blocked all branching mid-turn.**
The desktop refused all branching while a turn was busy, because an unguarded mid-turn branch would copy the in-flight prompt row (persisted at submit), queued prompt rows, and mid-turn pivot markers into the child as settled messages.

Fix: the backend now cuts the branch source at the TURN-START boundary and the client relaxes the gate only for a genuine in-flight turn.
- **Backend (contract 9):** `_lock_in_submit_turn` records `branch_turn_boundary` (the settled display length) under the history lock; `_branch_live` truncates the branch source to it while the turn runs, so the child keeps exactly the settled transcript. The half-streamed assistant text never enters the source (it lives in `inflight_turn`). Cleared in `_clear_inflight_turn` when the turn settles. The branch response carries `mid_turn`. The backend does NOT refuse mid-turn branches (TUI/other clients unaffected; an old client on the new backend is already safe).
- **Client:** `session.info` reports `turn_in_progress` (`inflight_turn is not None`). A manual-compaction hold is `running=true` with NO inflight turn and re-anchors the session key mid-flight, so the gate relaxes ONLY when `turnInFlight` AND this session's own backend reported `desktop_contract >= 9`. A compaction hold, a pre-v9 backend, or an unreported contract keeps the historic "Session busy" refusal. New honest copy (branchSettledTitle/Body) in all 8 locales.

## Related Issue

Upstream product work. Spec direction: cut at the turn-start boundary, relax the gate only for a genuine in-flight turn.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill

## Changes Made

**Commit 1 — defect 2 (row boundary):**
- `tui_gateway/methods_session_branch.py`: `_branch_live` cuts by `through_message_id` (`_row_id <= through`) winning over `count`.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py`: `SessionBranchParams.through_message_id`.
- `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`: legacy dial keeps `through_message_id` (removed from `LEGACY_STRIP`).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/gateway-rpc.ts`: `isOutOfSyncRpcParams` matches the 4000 refusal (`forkBranch` falls back count-only).
- `apps/desktop/src/api/canonical-protocol-wire.test.ts`: wire test — legacy dial keeps the boundary; a pre-v9 4000 reads as out-of-sync.
- Regenerated gateway contract (`through_message_id` on `session.branch`).

**Commit 2 — defect 1 (mid-turn boundary + gate):**
- `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py`: record `branch_turn_boundary` under the history lock in `_lock_in_submit_turn`.
- `tui_gateway/session_history.py`: clear it in `_clear_inflight_turn`.
- `tui_gateway/methods_session_branch.py`: `_branch_source_history` truncates to the boundary while running; response carries `mid_turn`.
- `tui_gateway/contracts/common.py` (`SessionLiveInfo.turn_in_progress`), `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` (`mid_turn`), `tui_gateway/server.py` (`DESKTOP_BACKEND_CONTRACT` 8→9, `turn_in_progress` in `_session_info`).
- `apps/desktop/...`: per-session `turnInFlight` + `backendContract` state; relaxed gate in `branchLoadedSession`; new copy in 8 locales; contract regen; CC extracted into `applyBackendContract` + `sessionInfoNoChange` helpers; `FILE_LINES` waivers on the over-cap files that gained a few lines.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_branch_mid_turn.py`: backend unit tests for both defects (mid-turn boundary cut, count+boundary, settled full, idempotent retry, row-boundary-wins-over-stale-count, inclusive boundary, hidden-rows-between-settled regression).

## How to Test

1. **Defect 2:** open a long session that has compacted; click branch at the bottom of the LAST message. The child now ends at that message (previously at an earlier one). Regression: `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_branch_mid_turn.py::test_row_boundary_lands_between_hidden_rows` (tool rows between settled spine messages, compacted local projection shorter than the authoritative display).
2. **Defect 1:** send a prompt, and while it streams, branch the chat. The child holds the settled transcript without the in-flight prompt; the toast says "Branch from the last settled message." A manual-compaction hold, a v8 backend, or an unreported contract still shows "Session busy." Regression: `use-session-actions.test.tsx` "branchLoadedSession mid-turn gate (contract 9)" (5 cases) + the backend boundary tests.
3. Backend: `venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server_branch_mid_turn.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py -q` (9 pass). Client: `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx src/api/canonical-protocol-wire.test.ts --project ui` (157 pass).
4. Contract regen is verified by `tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py` (generated files current).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run the branch suites: `tests/tui_gateway` (branch tests 9/9; the rest of the directory passes on this head, and its remaining reds reproduce identically on clean main), and the full desktop `ui` vitest project (11996/11996)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs — 12 checks ok)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings) — N/A otherwise
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — N/A (no platform-specific code)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Verified: `python scripts/check` (12 checks) ok; branch backend tests 9/9; client suites green (`use-session-actions.test.tsx` + `canonical-protocol-wire.test.ts` 157/157, full `ui` project 11996/11996); desktop typecheck clean. Defect 2 delta measured from real state.db sessions (a compacted parent + two children branched from the same last message).

prs.title: feat(delegation): Desktop route presets with next-session isolation
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds saved delegation-route presets to the existing **Settings → Model → Subagents** editor and makes saved route changes genuinely next-session-only unless the user explicitly applies them now.

Closes #145841.

Companion plugin PR: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/218 (closes NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#217).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature
- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Desktop selector restores a whole preset on selection; save-current, rename and delete use the plugin-owned authenticated API. Names/active marker only cross that API, not credential snapshots.
- Explicit, confirmed apply-now dispatches the existing slash command only to the focused runtime session on the same connection/profile. Delayed responses and old success messages cannot leak into another chat's status.
- Preserve plugin-owned preset metadata when the existing route editor replaces options/default.
- Capture one immutable delegation configuration for **both** schema construction and runtime routes; publish the matched tools/backend/settings together under the existing tool snapshot lock.
- Persist selected runtime settings with the session tool pin, including worker-store transfer and resume. An unchanged schema with new model values still refreshes on `--now`.
- Pending rebuild requests are profile-scoped. Sessions without `delegate_task` do not persist a delegation configuration.
- Optional `DelegationProvider.snapshot_settings()` projects runtime-only settings; the companion plugin excludes inactive preset libraries. Old providers retain their existing settings contract.

## Verification

- Focused core regression gate: **115 passed across 11 files**, covering config/schema race probes, startup/refresh, session restore, profile routes, plugin host, HTTP routing, and ACP.
- Desktop routing suites: **23 passed across 4 files**.
- Renderer TypeScript and scoped ESLint: passed.
- `python scripts/check --base aad60e1ac670268aa39b364b16b16dbf06de85df`: **13 checks passed**, including code health with zero blocking/advisory findings.
- Dark-mode browser fixture using the actual component: dropdown/save/rename/delete passed with synthetic transport and no live backend; apply-now disabled without an eligible chat. This is not a live Electron/chat end-to-end claim.
- Broader `tests/tools/test_delegate.py`: **70 passed, 1 failed** on both the feature snapshot and exact base commit. The failure compares `/private/var/tmp/...` and `/var/tmp/...` as raw strings on macOS; no unrelated test or production change is included.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Behavioral regressions reproduced before repair: same-name model changes affecting an existing session; concurrent config edits creating schema/routing disagreement; stale apply results after switching focused chats.

## Compatibility and release notes

- Pair this with official-plugins PR #218 for the full feature. Missing/older/disabled preset APIs leave the route editor available and show an upgrade/unavailable message.
- The plugin catalog pin is a separate release step after the plugin commit is merged.
- Legacy sessions with only a backend-name pin capture current settings on first restore; historical settings cannot be reconstructed.
- Literal inline credentials in **active** runtime routes remain in the session snapshot to preserve explicit routing semantics. Prefer provider credential references. Inactive saved preset libraries are excluded by the plugin projection; no delegation config is pinned when the tool is absent.
- Explicit snapshot builds bypass the global schema memo to avoid mixing configuration revisions; no performance benchmark is claimed.
- No live user installation/configuration changes or real model calls were required for validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Read contribution guidance and checked for duplicate work.
- [x] Conventional commit and task-scoped changes only.
- [x] Added behavioral tests and documented the provider hook.
- [x] Ran targeted tests, renderer checks and repository lint locally on macOS.
- [ ] Entire repository test suite (not claimed).
- [ ] Hosted CI green (check actual PR checks).

prs.title: fix(webapp): send a Content-Security-Policy for the Webapp page
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

WA-11 on #144648: the Webapp page sends no Content-Security-Policy, though the sign-in handoff pages do. #144721 tried one and reverted it. `::preview` widgets and HTML artifacts render in `srcdoc` frames that inherit the embedding page's policy, so their CDN libraries were blocked. This PR takes the next step the revert named: previews get their own route and policy, then the page gets a strict one.

**1. Preview documents get their own route** (first commit)
- **`/assets/webapp-preview.html`** is a fixed, credential-free shell. It's sandboxed (`allow-scripts`, no `allow-same-origin`, so its origin is opaque) and has its own policy.
- **How content arrives:** the renderer sends the HTML over `postMessage`, and the shell accepts it only from its parent on the gateway origin. It renders the HTML in an inner frame that keeps the caller's script permission, so file previews stay inert.
- **What's allowed there:** previews keep the reach they have on `main` today: any `http(s)` library, image, fetch, worker or embed, inline scripts, and string evaluation (D3's CSV parser compiles with `new Function`). Their isolation is the opaque sandbox with no credentials, not a source list.
- **"Open in browser":** loads the same shell from its owned `blob:` wrapper through a fixed same-origin loader. That avoids policy inheritance and Chromium's URL-length limit, and keeps the `about:srcdoc` base so anchors still work.
- **Native Desktop:** keeps its direct `srcdoc` frames.

**2. The page policy** (second commit)

| Directive | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `script-src` | `'self' blob: 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` plus SHA-256 hashes | The bundle and lazy chunks; plugin blob modules; Shiki's WASM; the built inline scripts and the server bootstrap |
| `script-src-attr`, `object-src`, `base-uri`, `form-action`, `frame-ancestors` | `'none'` | No inline handlers, plugins, base changes, form posts or framing |
| `style-src`, `font-src` | `'self'`, inline styles, Google Fonts, `data:` fonts | React and theme styles; the shipped font choices |
| `connect-src`, `media-src` | `* data: blob:`, with `ws: wss:` listed explicitly in `connect-src` for older WebKit | Left open on purpose: provider-direct voice, the capabilities catalog, Radio, update notes, local `http:` servers and proxied sockets all reach outside the gateway |
| `img-src`, `frame-src` | `'self' data: blob: https: http:` | Images, embeds, site previews and SDK `data:` frames keep working |

This locks down what can *execute*, not where the app may connect. Every spelling of the entry document gets the policy, including `%2e%2f` segments and `INDEX.HTML` on a case-insensitive disk.

## Related Issue

Refs #144648 (WA-11)
Refs #144705

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/webapp_previews.py`: the preview shell, its policy and the export loader. Webapp surface only.
- `hermes_cli/webapp_page_policy.py`: the page policy and hashes of the trusted inline scripts.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_dashboard.py`: serves the policy on `/`, `/index.html`, SPA routes and every alias of the entry file.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/ui/preview-document-frame.tsx` (new): the browser path for widgets, artifacts and file previews. `inline-preview-directive.tsx`, `preview-artifact.tsx` and `preview-pane.tsx` use it.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-uploads.ts`: "Open in browser" goes through the shell.
- Tests for the policy per route, the preview assets, the entry-file aliases and the frame component.

## How to Test

**Real browser:**
- **Setup:** Google Chrome 155 in a fresh Playwright profile, against a real gateway in a temporary home. A local fake model replies with a `::preview` widget and an HTML artifact. The widget loads D3 and KaTeX from jsDelivr, calls `d3.csvParse`, and tries to read the parent page, its cookies and its storage.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| App, chat, Settings and its lazy chunks (Shiki WASM included) | render, 0 CSP violations, no console errors |
| `::preview` widget | runs in the preview shell; D3 loads, `csvParse` works; parent page, cookies and storage are blocked |
| HTML artifact pane | same as the widget |
| "Open in browser" | `blob:` wrapper with `opener` null; D3 loads; the `#target` anchor scrolls |
| `/%2e%2findex.html` | served with the policy |
| **WebKit** (Playwright build, Safari 27.2's engine), the same checks | all pass; WebKit reports the sandboxed cookie as empty rather than throwing |
| **HTTPS reverse proxy** (Caddy, `https://hermes.localtest.me:8443/hermes`, `X-Forwarded-Prefix`, password sign-in), Chrome and WebKit | sign-in, then the app under `/hermes` with the policy; the socket connects to `wss://…/hermes/api/ws`; the preview page loads under the prefix and the widget passes the same checks; 0 violations |
| "Open in browser" with 2.29 MiB of HTML (the bridge path the artifact button uses), Chrome and WebKit | opens with `opener` null; the full page renders; D3, `csvParse` and the `#target` anchor work; probes blocked; console clean |
| A workspace image in a reply (gateway file route), Chrome and WebKit | loads under the policy |
| **Safari 27.2** (the app itself, through `safaridriver`) | the app loads with the policy; the widget, workspace image, artifact pane and "Open in browser" (`opener` null) pass the same checks; 0 violations on the app page |
| A second profile on a multiplexed gateway (switched with ⌘⇧]), Chrome and WebKit | the chat is stored in `profiles/second/state.db`; its workspace image and widget load and pass the same checks; 0 violations |

On `main`, the same fixture renders the same widget content, unprotected by any policy.

**Unit:** `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_page_csp.py tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_preview_documents.py tests/hermes_cli/test_webapp_page_previews.py` and `npx vitest run --project ui src/components/ui/preview-document-frame.test.tsx src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge.test.ts`. Each new test fails on `main` without its product change. The final head passes the CSP Python suites, 1,132 renderer tests in the touched areas, `tsc`, and all 13 `scripts/check` checks. The browser table above was run on the final policy.

**Limits:**
- **Plugins (#145072):** a `SandboxedFrame` `data:` document renders, but a *scripted* `data:` document inherits the page policy. A plugin that needs script there should use an `https:` page or the preview route. #145072 merges cleanly with this branch.
- **Code editor:** Pug syntax highlighting compiles with `Function`, so in the browser its attribute highlighting degrades.

**How this was checked:** two independent review passes (security, then functionality and regressions), a slimming pass, and an adversarial review of the final diff. Each finding was fixed with a red/green proof, and the browser checks above were run.

prs.title: feat(compression): warm handoff, the summary on the main model's cached prompt (compression.warm_handoff: off|on|auto)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

It adds an opt-in **warm handoff** to the built-in compressor: `compression.warm_handoff: off | on | auto`.

Today the compaction summary is a separate auxiliary request: a new prompt with a cut-down transcript. The server cannot reuse the prompt cache of the conversation, and the summarizer sees only parts of long messages.

With the warm handoff, a compaction first sends the **last main-model request of the session once more**, with the history rows that came after it and one appended instruction. The system prompt, tools, and request settings stay the same, so a server with prefix caching (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, LM Studio, hosted prompt caches) reads only the new rows. The main model writes a five-heading Markdown handoff (Goal, User instructions, Current state, Key facts, Next step), and that text becomes the summary. Tail selection, the summary carrier, and the commit path do not change.

This works for manual `/compress` and for automatic compaction (before a turn and inside a turn after tool rows).

| Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `off` (default) | No change: always the auxiliary summary call. |
| `on` | Always try the warm request first. |
| `auto` | Try it only when `auxiliary.compression` resolves to the main model on the main endpoint, the server reported cached prompt tokens for the last main request, **and** that request completed less than 5 minutes ago. |

Any refusal or failure falls back to the normal auxiliary summary call **in the same attempt**: no capture yet (for example right after a resume), a history row that a hook or middleware rewrote (the stored text must be inside the sent text, and tool arguments must match), an API mode other than `chat_completions`, request settings that cannot be replayed (request-local headers other than Relay's `traceparent`, `extra_query`, `n > 1`, a forced `tool_choice`, `response_format`, audio), a history that does not start with the captured request, a request that would not fit the window (checked with the server-reported prompt count of the captured request plus an estimate of the new rows), a provider error, the 120 s timeout, or a reply without the five headings. A session whose summarized turns have no user turn keeps the auxiliary summary (the summary check needs its no-user section).

**Same post-processing as the normal summary.** The accepted handoff text goes through the existing `_generate_summary` path: think-block stripping, `_redact_compaction_text` secret redaction, `[SKILL_PRUNED]` re-injection, task-snapshot grounding, lean-mode sections, and the user-provenance check. The request itself goes through `llm_execution` middleware and the Relay intercept chain like a main request, so audit and policy plugins see it; a middleware that blocks it makes the attempt use the auxiliary summary. Memory-provider context enters the instruction as the same sanitized, data-framed block as in the normal summary prompt.

**Why `auto` checks the route:** Hermes lets users send compression to a different (often smaller) model. That model cannot reuse the main model's cache, so the speedup only exists when the summary would go to the main model anyway.

**Why `auto` checks the reported cache.** The warm request is a plain OpenAI-compatible call, so it runs on any `chat_completions` server and falls back on any failure. It is only faster when the server reuses its prefix cache. Hermes cannot query that ahead of time, so `auto` uses the last main response as evidence: `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens > 0`, recorded less than 5 minutes ago. Where it is used, by server (from their documentation and issue trackers; tested here only on DGX and LM Studio):

| Server | Prefix cache | Reports `cached_tokens` | `auto` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted APIs with prompt caching | yes | yes | used |
| vLLM | yes (default) | only with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` | used with that flag |
| SGLang | yes, radix cache (default) | only with `--enable-cache-report` | used with that flag |
| TensorRT-LLM `trtllm-serve` | yes, KV block reuse | yes | used |
| llama.cpp `llama-server` | yes, per slot | yes | used |
| MLX `mlx_lm.server` | yes | yes | used when the cache holds |
| Ollama (`/v1`) | yes | no | skipped |
| LM Studio | yes | no | skipped |

Users of a server that caches but does not report it can set `on`. A later change could read Ollama's native `prompt_eval_cached_count`.

### Results

Synthetic sessions of 100K+ prompt tokens on unpatched Hermes `45871e10`, one session at a time, same logic running as a standalone plugin ([Elevatormusic/hermes-warm-compaction](https://github.com/Elevatormusic/hermes-warm-compaction), metadata-only evidence in its `evidence/` folder):

| Engine, mode | Compaction, median (warm / built-in) | Compaction + next reply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DGX Spark, GLM 5.3 flash (OpenAI-compatible, reports cached tokens), manual | 10.2 s / 32.7 s | 12.5 s / 36.9 s |
| DGX Spark, GLM 5.3 flash automatic | 10.1 s / 39.9 s | 11.5 s / 42.9 s |
| LM Studio, Qwen3.5 4B, manual | 20.9 s / 34.4 s | 25.2 s / 64.5 s |
| LM Studio, Qwen3.5 4B, automatic | 21.1 s / 41.8 s | 25.7 s / 54.9 s |

On DGX each warm request read about 108K prompt tokens and the server reported ≥ 99.9 % of them as cached. A second run (DGX, automatic, 10 sessions of ~105K tokens) also compared against hermes-lcm 0.21.0-rc2: compaction median 16.8 s (warm) / 43.5 s (lcm) / 78.5 s (built-in); compacted facts kept 59/60, 43/60, 50/60; a fact in the middle of a long message 10/10, 0/10, 0/10.

**Cost on a paid API.** The auxiliary summary is also a new, uncached request, but a small one: `_serialize_records_for_summary` cuts each message to 4,000 + 1,500 characters and caps the block at 160,000 characters (6.7K–8K prompt tokens in the runs above, 800–2,600 output tokens). The warm request reads the whole conversation, almost all of it cached, and writes a shorter reply (370–780 output tokens). With a valid cache the cost is about the same. The real risk is an expired provider cache, which would make the warm request a full-price read of the whole conversation; `auto` therefore skips it when the last main request is older than 5 minutes.

Limits: one synthetic task family, one model per engine, the author's hardware. The default here is `off`; I propose `auto` as the default once maintainers are comfortable with it.

## Related Issue

Fixes #89515 (opt-in via `compression.warm_handoff`; default `off`, `auto` proposed as the default later).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/prefix_request.py` (new): captures the final body of each main Chat Completions call (only when the engine asks for it via `wants_prefix_request`), binds it to the response that body produced, and builds the one-shot same-prefix request (`PrefixRequest`, `build_prefix_request`). Not streamed, no tools dispatched, nothing persisted, one call per attempt, cancellable through the commit fence.
- `agent/context_compressor_warm.py` (new): `WarmHandoffMixin`: the instruction, the reply gate, the `off|on|auto` gate (`_summary_route_is_main` + reported cache), and `compress()` which sets up the attempt and runs the existing body (`_compress_messages`).
- `agent/context_compressor.py`: mixes in `WarmHandoffMixin`; `_call_summary_llm` asks the warm path first.
- `agent/turn_api_call.py`, `agent/turn_api_request.py`, `agent/prefix_request_capture.py`, and the streaming driver: capture hooks at the final post-Relay provider boundary, with one token per physical request (no-ops unless enabled).
- Warm dispatch checks final identity and capacity after middleware and Relay. It revokes saved callbacks when the attempt exits, and permits one physical dispatch. Relay's current trace header stays outside the captured JSON body.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: passes the prefix request to engines whose `compress()` accepts it (older plugin signatures are unaffected).
- `agent/agent_init.py`, `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`, `cli-config.yaml.example`: `compression.warm_handoff` (default `"off"`).
- Desktop: **Settings → Memory & Context → Context & compression → Warm Handoff** with Auto / On / Off and a description (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/constants.ts`, translations for all bundled locales).
- Docs: `website/docs/developer-guide/context-compression-and-caching.md` (new "Warm handoff" section), `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`.
- Code-health offsets (no behavior change), so every touched file stays at or below its size on main: summary refusal detectors → `agent/context_compressor_refusal.py` (re-exported); `_aux` → `hermes_cli/config_defaults_aux.py`; `aux_inherits_main_route` → `hermes_cli/route_identity.py` (now shared with the `auto` check); Context & compression field copy of de/es/fr/ja/ru/zh → `<locale>_compression.ts`, as in 68420e19.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_prefix_request.py tests/agent/test_prefix_request_wiring.py tests/agent/test_warm_handoff_mode.py tests/e2e/core/compaction/test_compaction_warm_handoff.py tests/agent/test_compression_attempt_ownership.py tests/agent/test_prefix_request_relay.py -q`
   - The e2e file drives a real `AIAgent` + `SessionDB` against the recording fake provider: manual `/compress`, automatic compaction over seeded sessions with tool rounds, `auto` with and without a reported cache, fallbacks, and every C4 invariant after compaction.
2. Manually: set `compression.warm_handoff: on` (or `auto` on a server that reports `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`), run a long session, then `/compress`. `agent.log` shows `Compression warm handoff accepted: elapsed_s=… prompt_tokens=… cache_read_tokens=…`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (plus the code-health offsets listed above)
- [ ] Full repository suite on the current head (not run).

Earlier local runs: the 76 warm-handoff tests passed; after merging the latest main, 434 warm-handoff and context-compressor tests pass. In the 64 test files that touch the summary call, 1,257 pass and 5 fail the same way on unmodified main on this machine (provider resolution and vision routing). A wider run of every compression, compaction, agent-init, and config test file (1,730 tests) had 25 failures on this Windows machine: 21 fail the same way on unmodified `main`, and the other 4 (config loader / LKG backup) pass when run alone, so they depend on test order.

Current validation on `e6372fcd37d49f36718638ffa67055adde52b483`: the six-file warm, ownership, and Relay suite passed 183 tests, including all 15 controlled compaction E2E cases. Adjacent Relay and streaming files passed 147 tests with four expected skips; the SDK request-transform file passed five tests. All 11 exact-commit source checks passed against PR merge base `fe7710900a3064958cfa57741a7920dc07e7b056`, with zero code-health findings. The final moved stream seam was checked again with its affected tests. These runs used the canonical runner on Windows with isolated Hermes state and controlled providers. File retries were disabled. They do not measure live provider cache savings.

The added cases cover final capacity after execution middleware, saved callbacks after attempt exit, a valid worker wrapper, real Relay parameter rewrites, streaming capture and response pairing, fresh trace headers, refusal of non-trace headers, and one physical warm dispatch. The original three defects were proved before their fixes. The attempt-ownership repair keeps kvnloo's two original commits and author credit.

- [x] `python scripts/check` passes on the current head against the PR merge base: 11 checks ok
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (unit + e2e tests), live runs on DGX and LM Studio with the plugin form

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example`
- [ ] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` — N/A

Additional validation on the same head, `e6372fcd37d49f36718638ffa67055adde52b483`, on 2026-10-07:

- Linux: all 183 tests in the six-file warm/ownership/Relay suite passed, including all 15 controlled compaction E2E cases and `test_auto_mode_uses_the_warm_handoff_when_the_server_reports_a_cache`. Zero failures, errors, or skips. Ubuntu 24.04.4 x86_64 in a disposable Docker container, PM-pinned Python 3.14.7 and pytest 9.1.1. The canonical runner used one worker, retries disabled, isolated Hermes state, and synthetic providers; external container networking was disconnected for the tests.
- Desktop on Windows x64: the full `apps/desktop` typecheck passed (renderer, Electron, E2E helper types, and builder JavaScript). Eight focused settings/locale UI files passed all 87 tests. ESLint passed for all 15 changed desktop TypeScript files. Toolchain: supported Node 24.16.0, PM-locked npm 12.0.2, TypeScript 6.0.3, Vitest 4.1.10. The isolated install used `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; this does not validate native install scripts. CI pins Node 26.7.0, which was not used for this local desktop run.
- Source and lockfile were unchanged. The full repository suite, full desktop UI/E2E suite, native install checks, and new live model/cache benchmarks were not run.

Upstream CI still reports `action_required` and needs maintainer action. These local results do not replace the required `All required checks pass (v2)` result. prs.title: fix(gateway): spawn the updater in its own systemd transient unit
prs.body:
## Problem

The `/update` command spawns the updater with `setsid`, which detaches the **session** but leaves the process **inside the gateway's systemd cgroup**. A gateway restart — which the update itself triggers at the end, and which external watchers (e.g. a code-skew heal timer) may also issue mid-run — SIGKILLs the entire cgroup (`KillMode=mixed`), destroying the updater and its bash wrapper mid-build. The update is stranded with no exit code, a stale lock, and a 30-minute spurious timeout.

## Fix

When a systemd user manager is reachable, spawn the updater as a **transient systemd user unit** (`systemd-run --user --collect --unit=hermes-update-<pid>-<ts> bash -c …`) so it runs in **its own cgroup** and survives gateway restarts.

- Probe the user manager first with a bounded `systemd-run … true` call (5s timeout) so we never silently fail to start the update.
- Fall back to the existing `setsid` spawn, then to `start_new_session=True`, when `systemd-run` is missing or no user session is reachable (the original reason `setsid` was chosen — e.g. the gateway running as a root system service without a user bus).
- Windows path untouched.

## Why this approach

- This is the **structural** fix: the updater can no longer be killed by a gateway restart at all, instead of only being detected afterwards.
- Conservative fallback chain: on any systemd failure, behavior is identical to today.
- `--collect` garbage-collects the transient unit after exit; the unit name is unique per spawn.

## Validation

- New unit tests in `tests/gateway/test_update_command.py`:
  - `systemd-run` available + probe OK → Popen called with `systemd-run --user --collect` and the update command
  - probe fails → falls back to the `setsid` spawn (no silent failure)
- Existing spawn tests unchanged and passing (`test_spawns_with_gateway_flag`, `test_writes_pending_marker`, `test_fallback_when_no_setsid`, …) — 17 passed in `tests/gateway/test_update_command.py`.

fix(gateway): refuse inbound turns on stale code instead of ImportError crash

A long-lived gateway/serve process holds `sys.modules` from boot. When
`hermes update` (or a manual `git pull`) replaces the checkout underneath
it but the unit is not restarted — e.g. root-gated systemd restart of
`hermes-serve` is skipped and left to the operator — the first inbound
message on a new code path lazily imports a freshly-pulled consumer module
against the stale boot-time module graph and crashes with a cryptic
`cannot import name ...` (observed in production:

    cannot import name 'fill_empty_non_final_wire_payload'
    from 'agent.agent_runtime_helpers'

on a serve process kept alive across an update). The desktop shows a
"Gateway error" banner and the user's message is lost.

The codebase already guards the two highest-risk import sites with the
shared detector in `gateway/code_skew.py`:
- model switching (`_model_switch_skew_guard`, slash_commands.py, #97046)
- the dashboard model picker (`_dashboard_code_skew_guard`,
  web_server.py, #86207)

The plain-message turn path — the first lazy-import site a stale process
actually hits — was still unguarded ("we don't guard every import site,
only this one"). This adds the mirror guard for turns:

- `GatewayRunner._turn_code_skew_guard()` returns a deployment-agnostic
  "restart the backend" notice when `detect_code_skew()` reports drift
  (never a false positive: no boot fingerprint -> no refusal).
- `_handle_message_with_agent` checks it before any session/agent work and
  refuses with the notice delivered via `_deliver_platform_notice`
  (platform privacy rules respected) instead of crashing. The user's
  message is not silently lost; they are told to restart and resend.

Why not restart automatically: the serve unit restart is often root-gated
(polkit/sudo), which is exactly the case that leaves the stale process
running; the update already surfaces "restart manually" guidance. The
guard makes the failure mode a clear instruction instead of a crash.

Tests: three additions to tests/test_code_skew.py — guard returns None
without skew, message names both revisions and the restart action without
hardcoding a systemd unit, and a behavioral test proving a skewed handler
delivers the notice and never spawns the agent.

Validation: tests/test_code_skew.py (15 passed) and
tests/test_stale_utils_module_import.py (3 passed) with the project venv;
ruff clean.

issues.title: Add Android API 19 support for x86_32 and x86_64 architectures
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

Expand PicoClaw's Android compatibility to cover legacy devices and emulators running **Android 4.4 (API 19)** on **x86_32 (32-bit)** and **x86_64 (64-bit)** architectures. 

Many older TV boxes, tablets, and single-board computers (SBCs) still in use today rely on x86-based Android builds (e.g., Intel Atom or AMD APUs) with API 19. Furthermore, x86 Android emulators are widely used for testing and development. Providing pre-built binaries or APKs for these targets would fulfill the project's goal of being a truly lightweight AI assistant that runs on almost any hardware. 

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Provide dedicated release artifacts (standalone binaries or APK builds) for the following targets:
- `android/386` (x86_32)
- `android/amd64` (x86_64)

These builds should be compiled with a minimum API level of 19.

## 🔧 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- **Go Cross-Compilation**: Since PicoClaw is written in Go, adding these targets to the build matrix (e.g., in `.goreleaser.yaml` or the Makefile) is straightforward:
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=386 GOARM=` (for x86_32)
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=amd64 GOARM=` (for x86_64)
- **CGO/NDK**: Ensure any C dependencies (if present) are compiled using the Android NDK with `APP_PLATFORM=android-19`.
- **Binary Size**: The current build is already very small (~10MB); x86 builds should remain similarly lightweight.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment

- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

**Justification**: While modern Android devices are predominantly ARM64, the x86 Android ecosystem (especially for old TV boxes and emulators) is still active. This feature would significantly expand the user base and align with the project's "runs anywhere" philosophy. 

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Running via Termux**: The current Termux guide only supports ARM64 devices. Termux on old x86 Android builds is often unstable and not officially supported.
- **Using the current APK**: The current APK requires a minimum of Android 7 (API 24) and is built for ARM64, making it incompatible with API 19 x86 devices.

## 💬 Additional Context

- **Existing 32-bit limitation**: A related issue (#2954) already reports that 32-bit Android is not supported. This request extends that to the x86 architecture.
- **Low resource footprint**: PicoClaw is known for using less than 10MB of RAM. It is an ideal candidate for reviving extremely old x86 Android hardware (e.g., first-generation Intel TV sticks).
- **Testing**: I am willing to test the binaries on an x86_32 Android 4.4 emulator and an old x86_64 TV box if the builds are provided.

prs.title: fix(discord): bump discordgo fork past the gateway handshake deadlock
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

The Discord channel can go permanently deaf: the bot stays "connected", but nothing comes in or goes out, no heartbeat is sent, and nothing is logged. The cause is a deadlock in the pinned `discordgo` fork commit (`yeongaori/discordgo-fork@e8e546f`, 2026-03-19). The fork fixed it a week later. This PR moves the pin forward and adds a regression test.

**The deadlock.** `Session.Open` holds `s.Lock()` (deferred unlock) for the whole handshake. If Discord's first packet after IDENTIFY/RESUME is Op 9 (Invalid Session) or Op 7 (Reconnect), `onEvent` handles it by calling `CloseWithCode`, which calls `s.Lock()` again. `sync.RWMutex` isn't reentrant, so `Open` never returns. The heartbeat goroutine waits behind it, and the reconnect loop never runs. Op 9 is Discord's normal reply to a failed resume, so a network blip followed by a resume is enough to trigger it.

Goroutine dumps from two real wedges on one bot, same stack both times (`wsapi.go:186 → 631 → 931`):

```
sync.(*RWMutex).Lock
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).CloseWithCode(0xc0002d4708, 0x3f4)   // 1012, wsapi.go:931
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).onEvent(...)                           // Op 9 branch, wsapi.go:631
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).Open(...)                              // holds s.Lock(), wsapi.go:186
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).reconnect(...)
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).heartbeat(...)   // second dump: (*Session).listen
```

**The fix** was upstreamed to the fork as `16ef341` ("Fix deadlock (#5)", 2026-03-26). `onEvent` now returns `errReconnect` for Op 7 and Op 9, and the caller reconnects once `Open` has released the lock. This PR moves the `replace` to the fork's current head, `a10ba9c`, which also includes the fork's later fixes for the gateway resume loop (`6f7dfa3`) and silent gateway stalls (`a10ba9c`). The only change on our side is `go.mod`/`go.sum` plus a test.

**Regression test.** `pkg/channels/discord/discord_gateway_test.go` runs a fake gateway that answers IDENTIFY with Op 9 or Op 7, and checks that `Open` returns and the session lock is released afterwards. It uses its own `websocket.Dialer`, because the default dialer's `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` caches the environment on first use and would break `TestApplyDiscordProxy_*`.

| pin | result |
|---|---|
| `e8e546f` (current `main`) | both cases FAIL: `session.Open() never returned: deadlocked on the session lock` |
| `a10ba9c` (this PR) | both cases PASS in under 1 ms |

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [ ] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

Written with Claude Code. The analysis comes from the goroutine dumps above, and the fix and test were verified red then green and on a real bot (below). Opened as a draft so a human reviews it first.

## 🔗 Related Issue

None filed. The description above covers it. I can open an issue if you'd like to track it separately.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://github.com/yeongaori/discordgo-fork/commit/16ef34198ced6c051880166ecbcda6fc9cc7f011 (fork fix), https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/gateway#resuming (Op 9 after a failed resume). The same deadlock is still open in upstream `bwmarrin/discordgo`: https://github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo/pull/1694 (unreviewed since 2026-02-09), so dropping the fork for upstream wouldn't fix this either.
- **Reasoning:** The bug and its fix are in the dependency, and picoclaw already pins that fork with a `replace`, so moving the pin is the smallest correct change. The test guards that pin from regressing, because a future fork bump could bring the deadlock back without anyone noticing. Release branches may want this cherry-picked: `v0.3.1` has the bug.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (Intel Xeon W-3265, x86_64)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, picoclaw in a rootless Podman container (v0.3.1 + this pin)
- **Model/Provider:** N/A (gateway-level change)
- **Channels:** Discord (also running Slack, unaffected)

Checks, run in `golang:1.25` to mirror `.github/workflows/pr.yml`:
- `go test -tags goolm,stdjson ./...`: pass as a non-root user. As root, `pkg/evolution`'s `TestRuntime_RunColdPathOnce_DraftSaveFailureRollsBackAppliedSkill` fails, because it needs an unwritable path. That's the same on `main` and unrelated.
- `golangci-lint run --build-tags=goolm,stdjson` (v2.10.1): 0 issues.
- `golangci-lint fmt --diff`: no diff in changed files. It flags `pkg/providers/bedrock/provider_bedrock.go`, which is already on `main`.
- `govulncheck`: results identical to `main`'s.
- `go vet`, `go mod verify`, `scripts/lint-docs.sh`, `web/backend` tests: pass.

## 📸 Evidence (Optional)
<details>
<summary>Real bot: gateway outage, failed resume answered with Op 9, clean recovery</summary>

Outbound 443 was blocked in the container's network namespace for 150 s, then restored. On reconnect, Discord rejected the resume with Op 9, the sequence that wedged the old pin. The new pin re-identified and recovered without a restart:

```
22:17:39 [test] blocked 443
22:18:02 WRN error reading from gateway wss://gateway.discord.gg/ websocket, websocket: close 1000 (normal)
22:18:03 INF calling reconnect() now
22:18:48 ERR error connecting to gateway wss://gateway.discord.gg/, dial tcp 162.159.130.234:443: i/o timeout
22:19:34 ERR error connecting to gateway , dial tcp 162.159.136.234:443: i/o timeout
22:20:09 [test] unblocked
22:20:10 INF Op 10 Hello Packet received from Discord
22:20:10 INF sending resume packet to gateway
22:20:10 INF Received Op 9 (Invalid Session) from gateway
22:20:10 INF Gateway session is not resumable, discarding its information
22:20:10 ERR error reconnecting to gateway, reconnect required by gateway
22:20:14 INF trying to reconnect to gateway
22:20:15 INF Op 10 Hello Packet received from Discord
22:20:15 INF We are now connected to Discord, emitting connect event
22:20:15 INF successfully reconnected to gateway
[test] container restarts: 0
```
</details>

## ☑️ Checklist
- [x] My code/docs follow the style of this project.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own changes.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. (No docs change needed.)
