prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, the barrel import, and five exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal` and no Proton DMARC verdict at all. Either way, the `From:` must be a single plain dot-atom address. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command, so duplicate labels can't shadow each other. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed (a terminal edit), or no longer holds a row for, refuses later replies, giving core's reason when it gave one ("that request has closed: ⏱️ Timed out — no response"). Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused (delivery fails) rather than pushing one out.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`) — core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received". If that acknowledgement fails to send, the answer still stands.
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required (it was opportunistic: a listener without STARTTLS received the bridge password in clear); certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter rather than falling back.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until a fixed 30 s after `setup()`, whatever the poll interval, so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing at startup. The inbound message id is chosen by the adapter (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID, which stays in `content` for threading. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts (a new agent's name, a rejection reason) get just the answer. A mail whose handling fails *inside the adapter* (fetch, parse, card lookup, sending a refusal notice) is retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`. **Routing failures inside the host are not retried**: `onInbound` hands the mail over and the host catches its own routing errors, so the mail is already marked read. Messages are fetched one at a time; mail over 40 MB is skipped.
- **Limits**: HTML-only mail uses mailparser's own text conversion. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300, and Message-ID and References are bounded. Attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. State lives under `STORE_DIR`; `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. Loops are stopped by the own-address check, by the inbound filter for bounces and auto-replies, and by a limit of 20 mails an hour from any one sender; beyond it mail is left unread. That limit is what stops two agents answering each other.
- **Message kinds**: the body comes before the subject, so a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743 — a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them, and Proton's clients offer none. Bridge takes `From` from Proton's sender record. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values, and if Proton stopped sending the header, internal mail would go back to being refused.
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, five deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` on this branch → clean
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/` → 746 passed, 19 skipped (68 files), run locally: CI does not run on PRs into `channels`. This includes:
  - `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC and `X-Pm-Origin`), plain-address check, card matching and distinct commands, framing, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip rules.
  - `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against fake IMAP/SMTP and real mailparser:
    - sender identity: forged sender refused; Proton-internal mail delivered; forged `internal` beside `external` refused; own address dropped; quoted local part refused;
    - approval cards: a late `/approve` answers its own card; cards survive a restart; a closed or missing card refuses replies; a failed acknowledgement keeps the answer; unanswered cards survive pruning; the gateway confirmation;
    - delivery: no mail read before the startup delay, even with a one-hour poll; adapter-chosen inbound ids; bare-body replies; the 20-an-hour sender limit; the card ceiling refusing new cards; capped attachment-name lists; retries on fetch and notice-send failures, and giving up; attachments held until approval; subject and Message-ID caps;
    - also slash commands, `send_card`, edits, and STARTTLS with pinning.
- `eslint` 0 errors, `prettier --check` clean on the new files
- Header probes against live Bridge 3.27.0 (26 Oct): our Message-ID survives Bridge; Proton strips forged `X-Pm-*` and `mail.protonmail.ch` headers from external mail; Proton-to-Proton mail carries `X-Pm-Origin: internal` and no Authentication-Results. See the second details block above.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 run as uid 10001 with no capabilities — IMAP connects with the pinned certificate over required STARTTLS; SMTP STARTTLS + AUTH verified against the pin; inbound mail ingested. The 26 Oct review fixes are covered by the tests and probes above; they are not yet live on that install.
- Demonstrated before the fix, against #3726's code: a squatter on 127.0.0.1 without STARTTLS received the (fake) bridge password; a late `/approve` to card A approved card B

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass, and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other. This covers ordinary chat and `/` admin commands as well as cards: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. An owner who writes from a Proton address is identified by mailbox, not by domain (below). For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, which means Proton authenticated the sending account; anyone with a free Proton account is therefore verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card. Approvals additionally need the per-card token, so only someone who can read the approver's mailbox can answer.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, so a stranger cannot park large events in `pending_channel_approvals`.
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Attachment filenames pass `isSafeAttachmentName`; bodies are capped at 50k characters; bounces, auto-replies, mailing lists and mail from the Bridge account's own address are dropped before the router.
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Code for the `/add-proton-mail` skill in #3726, which copies the four `src/channels/proton-mail*` files from this branch and appends the barrel line.

issues.title: [申诉] LobsterAI 账号被误封，未恶意使用却被封禁（******2020 / *****0160）
issues.body:
## 账号信息
- 账号 1：18***2020
- 账号 2：13***0160
- GitHub 账号（申诉人）：https://github.com/7597qqme

## 问题现象
两个 LobsterAI（有道龙虾）账号近期无法登录/使用，系统提示账号已被封禁或异常。
本人声明：**两个账号均未进行过恶意使用、未刷接口、未批量调用**，封禁认定疑似误判。

## 补充说明（可能的误判来源）
我曾在本地第三方 DSH 插件（dsh-comprehensive-platform / our-free-model）中配置过 LobsterAI 账号凭据，用于调用有道模型服务。
该插件存在自动化流量：
1. 每日自动签到（每天 1 次，模拟正常 App 行为）；
2. 之前版本的模型目录自动刷新间隔为 5 分钟，会带真实账号凭据轮询 `GET /api/models/available`，每渠道每天产生约 288 次带凭据请求。

我已意识到这可能被上游风控系统判定为“异常活动（unusual activity）”，导致账号被封。**现已从本地彻底移除相关 LobsterAI 凭据，且修复了刷新间隔（已改为默认 6 小时 + 抖动 + 无已登录账号时零请求），不会再产生自动化流量。**

## 诉求
1. 查明封禁原因，并告知两个账号的封禁时长；
2. 若确认为误判，请解除封禁，恢复正常使用；

issues.body:
## 环境信息

- 操作系统：Windows 11
- 应用版本：v2026.3.24
- 网络连接方式：有线网络

---

## 严重等级

🟡 Minor

---

## 复现步骤

1. 打开 LobsterAI，在输入框中输入一个需要长回复的问题（如"写一篇3000字的文章"），点击发送
2. 在 AI 开始流式回复后，立即拔掉网线，断开网络
3. 等待几秒后，重新插上网线，恢复网络
4. 在输入框中输入"继续"，点击发送按钮或按回车发送

---

## 预期结果

AI 开始回复后，输入框中的发送按钮变为停止按钮，用户可以点击停止按钮中断 AI 的回复。回复结束后，停止按钮变回发送按钮。

---

## 实际结果

AI 开始回复，但回复过程中：
- ❌ 输入框中的按钮**保持发送按钮样式**，未变为停止按钮
- ❌ 发送按钮**不可点击**
- ❌ 用户**无法中断 AI 的回复**，只能等待回复自然结束

回复结束后，按钮恢复正常可用状态。

---

prs.title: fix(computer-use): reuse approvals for Windows process paths
prs.body:
## Summary

Reuse a Windows Computer Use session approval when the same executable is passed as a path for launch and as `process:<path>` for a subsequent window operation.

## Related Issue

Refs #2895 (the executable-path variant of the same-session repeated prompt).

## Changes Made

- Normalize absolute Windows executable paths in approval keys, including the `process:` prefix, separator and case variants.
- Keep display names and application IDs separate; do not infer executable identity from a basename.
- Exercise the Windows client elicitation path through the existing stdio MCP bridge harness.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- Baseline: the new launch-to-window regression fails on unchanged `main` because two approval prompts are recorded instead of one.
- `npm test -- src/main/computerUse/computerUseMcpBridge.test.ts src/main/computerUse/computerUseMcpServer.test.ts`: 21 passed, 8 skipped. The skipped cases require a platform/helper setup; this is not a live Windows helper/UI end-to-end run.
- Changed-file ESLint with zero warnings: passed.
- `npm run compile:electron`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Local checks reused an existing dependency installation. The missing declared `fast-xml-parser@5.11.1` dependency was supplied before the successful compiler run. No manifest or lockfile changes.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

No UI changes.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective
- [x] Relevant unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)

## Additional Notes

Sensitive-app and self-app checks remain ahead of the approval cache lookup. Tests cover distinct executable paths with the same basename and continued denial of sensitive/self apps after an unrelated grant.

This deliberately does not add persistent grants, a new approval UI, or arbitrary display-name / AppsFolder identity resolution. Those broader parts of #2895 remain open.

issues.title: [Bug]: Automatic Memory Search 开启后同一轮重复调用 memory_search，拦截后无法正常回复

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

`python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('qwenpaw'))"` → `2.2.2`

## Description

开启 **Automatic Memory Search（自动记忆搜索）** 后，同一个用户回合内，模型会以相同或几乎相同的 query 反复调用 `memory_search`。

达到第 4 次重复调用后被重复搜索保护拦截，但**拦截之后的正常回复仍然无法生成**：收尾（finalize）与一次受控恢复（recovery）产出的内容被判定为 `tool_block` 或 `raw_tool_markup`，最终向用户返回固定兜底文案，而不是基于已有记忆结果的正常回答。

关键对照：

- **关闭 Automatic Memory Search 后，同一段对话可以正常继续。**
- 更换模型（本地 35B 与云端 Qwen3.8-Flash 等）后**仍可复现**。

因此这不是单一模型的工具调用能力问题，更像是自动记忆注入内容与工具调用循环之间的交互问题。

预期：自动搜索在同一用户回合最多执行一次，结果作为参考上下文提供；即使模型仍重复搜索，也应拦截工具调用并**基于已有结果生成正常回答**，而不是返回兜底。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Windows 10 (AMD64)
- **Install method:** 本地 venv 安装（`pip install qwenpaw`，启动脚本 `启动QwenPaw-2.2.2.bat`）
- **Python version:** 3.11.9
- **Memory backend:** ReMeLight
- **Automatic Memory Search:** enabled
- **Relevant config:** `auto_memory_search_config.enabled = true`
- **Channel:** WeChat / Console

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 在记忆设置中开启 Automatic Memory Search，并确保该 agent 已有可检索的历史记忆。
2. 在一个已有较长上下文的会话中正常提问，使自动记忆搜索被触发。
3. 观察同一用户回合内模型的工具调用：会以相同或等价 query 再次调用 `memory_search`。
4. 重复到第 4 次时被重复搜索保护拦截，停止继续执行工具。
5. 观察最终回复：收尾与恢复生成的内容被判定为 `tool_block` / `raw_tool_markup`。
6. 最终用户收到固定兜底文案（"本轮检测到重复搜索……请重发一次"），而不是正常回答。
7. 对照组：关闭 Automatic Memory Search，同一会话可正常回复。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**
  - 同一用户回合内 `memory_search` 被重复调用多次，参数相同或高度相似；
  - 第 4 次被拦截后，收尾/恢复的输出被判定为包含结构化工具块或原始工具标签，判为无效；
  - 用户最终只收到固定兜底文案；
  - 该行为跨模型复现；关闭自动搜索后不再出现。

- **Expected:**
  - 同一真实用户回合只自动搜索一次；
  - 自动搜索结果作为明确的"系统提供的参考上下文"进入模型，不表现为模型刚刚发起的一次工具调用；
  - 若模型仍然重复搜索，拦截工具执行，但允许基于已有结果生成纯文本回答；
  - 已存在可用记忆结果时，不应返回"请重发一次"这类兜底。

## Logs / Screenshots

日志中可观察到的关键序列（示意，已去除会话内容）：

```text
MemoryMiddleware: memory_search repeated (same query, same params)
MemoryMiddleware: repeated memory_search blocked (4th call)
MemoryMiddleware: memory_search finalization — answering without tools
MemoryMiddleware: finalization rejected (reason=tool_block)
MemoryMiddleware: attempting one recovery answer
MemoryMiddleware: recovery rejected (reason=raw_tool_markup)
MemoryMiddleware: returning fallback reply
```

另一模型复现时出现的预算分支：

```text
MemoryMiddleware: recovery skipped (reason=budget_unknown, no output limit)
```

说明：被拒绝的具体模型原文未落盘，因此无法提供逐字内容；但拒绝原因码与"返回兜底"的结果可稳定复现。

## Relation to PR #6120

PR #6120（`fix(memory): restrict automatic memory to external user queries`）解决的是**另一层**问题：只有带 `external_user_query` 标记的真实外部用户消息才能触发自动搜索，内部注入的 `loop_continuation` 等 `user` 角色消息不再被误认为新用户问题。

该修复在 2.2.2 中已存在且生效：本地实测中，加入一条 `loop_continuation` 警告后，自动搜索次数仍为 1，且搜索使用的是原真实用户消息。

因此本 issue **不是 #6120 的回归**，而是剩余的一层：

- 自动搜索**结果本身**在上下文中仍以「assistant 文本 + thinking + `memory_search` tool_call + tool_result」的形态呈现；
- 该结构可能被模型当作"自己刚发起的、可继续重复的工具交互"来模仿；
- 重复调用被拦截后，收尾/恢复阶段仍可能产出工具块或原始工具标签，导致最终没有可用正文。

## Suggested Fix (compromise, keeps the feature)

保留 Automatic Memory Search 与完整检索结果，只改变"结果的呈现方式"，并给收尾阶段一个明确的成功出口：

1. **区分自动证据与真实工具调用**
   为自动注入结果增加内部标记（例如 `auto_memory_evidence`），并在构造时不再复用 assistant 工具调用形态；以系统参考上下文的身份呈现，保留完整结果正文与来源信息。

2. **保持注入去重与回合隔离**
   同一真实用户回合只搜索一次；多次 model call 复用同一份证据，不重复叠加；跨回合不串用；关闭自动搜索时完全不注入。

3. **不要让它冒充真实用户消息**
   证据消息不得携带 `external_user_query` 标记，避免影响用户问题识别与自动记忆批次边界。

4. **拦截后必须能给出正文**
   重复搜索被拦截时，使用已有证据生成纯文本回答；若首次收尾被判定无效，允许一次恢复，且恢复请求不得重新注入可被模仿的工具调用示范。

5. **失败要可诊断**
   在拒绝时记录原因码与被拒绝内容的类型（是否为结构化工具块、命中哪类标签、是否 final 帧），便于区分"模型真调用工具"与"校验误杀"。

## Additional Notes

- 临时规避：关闭 Automatic Memory Search 后问题消失（已实测）；agent 仍可在需要时显式调用 `memory_search`。
- 相关历史 issue：#6113（一直卡在搜索记忆）、#6241（`memory_search` 死循环）。两者均已关闭，本 issue 描述的是**#6120 之后仍然存在的剩余部分**：重复搜索被拦截后无法产出正常回复。
- 本 issue 不涉及安全或凭据问题。

## Summary

Allow browser level/OS level message push for pending approvals.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI

- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation
When executing long term task with guards enabled for better safety protocol, user may leave the web UI tab in the background, thus missing the approval messages that only available to user when explicitly brought to fore ground. When the approval times out, agents got rejected and the agent SOP derails. 

## Proposed Solution

For approvals that needs user attention, allow notification messages to be delivered by browser, which allows messages to be pushed at OS level when appropriately delegated.

[Any other approaches or workarounds you thought about.]

We are running QwenPaw in containers and accessing UI through browser.

issues.title: [Bug] LLM `Request timed out` 后永不自动恢复，必须手动重启 QwenPaw 进程才能恢复（2.2.1）

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# [Bug] LLM `Request timed out` 后永不自动恢复，必须手动重启 QwenPaw 进程才能恢复（2.2.1）

## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1（`pip show qwenpaw` → Version: 2.2.1；`qwenpaw --version` → QwenPaw, version 2.2.1）

## Description

一旦 LLM 调用开始以 `openai.APITimeoutError: Request timed out.` 失败，**QwenPaw 进程就再也无法自行恢复**：所有后续请求继续以同样的超时失败，持续数小时，直到**手动重启 QwenPaw 进程**才立刻恢复。期望是：网络/上游 gateway 的短暂抖动不应该让整个 agent 永久瘫痪，更不应该必须重启进程。

关键点：**这不是"网络一直坏"**。同一个进程重启后，**同一个 provider、同一个模型、同一个网络环境**下，第一次请求就成功（9/21 14:04:19 重启 → 14:11:29 同 session 同 provider `opencode/deepseek-flash` 成功返回，prompt_tokens 高达 4,938,175）。也就是说，失败状态是**进程内残留的本地状态**，只能靠重启清除。

**两天内 4 次复发，每一次都终止于手动重启，没有一次在进程存活期间自行恢复：**

| # | 失败窗口（本地时间） | 规模 | 结束方式 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9/21 上午（至 11:3x，约 80 分钟） | 235 条 `LLM call failed`/`Request timed out` 日志、35 个失败 turn | 手动重启 |
| 2 | 9/21 12:03 – 14:03:57 | 200 条超时/重试日志、33 个失败 turn | **手动重启 14:04:19 → 14:11:29 立刻成功** |
| 3 | 9/21 ~14:3x | 超时爆发 | **手动重启 14:34:37 → 恢复** |
| 4 | 9/22 09:43:50 – 15:01:26（5h18m） | **778 条超时/重试日志、125 个失败 turn、185 次 agent 重建**、全部集中在单一会话 | **手动重启 16:56:30 → 恢复** |

重启后仍然会偶发**同样的**连接超时（9/22 17:03:01 `LLM call failed (attempt 1/4): Request timed out.`），但此时重试即可成功 —— 说明"偶发连接超时"本身不致命，**致命的是它留下的、只能重启清除的进程状态**。

**Related PR(s):** 无（reporter 未找到相关 PR）

**Security considerations:** 无。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI) —— 仅"错误呈现"部分：前端 30s 提前中断并显示 `Request timeout after 30000ms`，掩盖真实原因
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1（pip 安装，`site-packages` 安装态，无 git 提交信息）
- **OS:** Linux (WSL2), kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, Ubuntu userland; host timezone Asia/Shanghai
- **Install method:** pip（venv `/home/pavino/.qwenvenv`）
- **Python version:** 3.12
- **Provider:** 自定义 OpenAI-compatible provider（`id=opencode`，`chat_model: OpenAIChatModel`），`base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`，`model=deepseek-flash`
- **相关配置（reporter 侧）:** `llm_max_retries=3`、`llm_backoff_base=1.0`、`llm_backoff_cap=10.0`、`llm_max_concurrent=10`、`llm_acquire_timeout=300`；`fallback_policy.enabled=true` 但 `fallback_models=[]`（空）

## Steps to Reproduce

### A. 观测复现（reporter 实际经历，可回查日志）

1. 使用上述 provider，在 console 会话中正常对话；网络到 `opencode.ai` 出现短暂建连困难（reporter 实测该域名建连耗时波动 0.19s – 10.29s，其中一次 DNS 7.56s / TLS 8.11s）。
2. 某次请求开始失败：`openai.APITimeoutError: Request timed out.`，每次尝试固定 ~16–19 秒后放弃，固定重试 3 次（`attempt 1/4 → 2/4 → 3/4`，退避 1/2/4s），整轮约 60s 后 `runtime: unhandled error` + console `process/reply failed`。
3. **保持进程不重启**，等网络恢复后继续发送请求 → 仍然 100% 以相同超时失败，误差特征完全不变（不递增退避、不切换模型、不报"provider 不可用"），可持续 5 小时以上。
4. **重启 QwenPaw 进程** → 立即恢复；同一个 provider/模型/网络下首个请求即成功。

### B. 建议的确定性复现（reporter 未执行，仅提议）

1. 把 provider 的 `base_url` 指向一个会 **blackhole TCP** 的目标（例如对本机出向增加 `iptables -A OUTPUT -d <provider_ip> -j DROP`，或指向不可路由地址），使 `connect()` 悬停而不是被拒绝。
2. 在 console 发一条消息 → 观察到 `LLM call failed (attempt 1/4..3/4): Request timed out`，以及 `/tmp/qwenpaw_query_error_*.json` 现场转储。
3. **不重启 QwenPaw**，撤销第 1 步的 DROP 规则 / 恢复真实 `base_url`，等 TCP 连通性正常。
4. 再发一条消息：
   - 若**仍然失败**（或长时间无响应）→ 复现了本 bug；
   - 连不上的模型实例/连接池状态应由进程自行重建，而不需要重启。
5. 重启 QwenPaw 后重复第 4 步 → 立即成功（对照组）。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:**
  - 一次上游连接抖动后，**进程进入永久性失败状态**：所有后续 LLM 调用持续以 `APITimeoutError: Request timed out.` 失败，**永不自愈**（9/22 连续 5 小时 18 分，125 个失败 turn，185 次 agent 重建）。
  - 失败策略完全僵化：固定 3 次重试 + 固定 1/2/4s 退避，**无熔断、无递进退避、无 provider 健康判定、无 fallback 切换**；`providers/retry_chat_model.py:466 _ensure_provider_available()` 只检查"上一个 stream 的清理任务是否还在跑"，并非健康检查。
  - 真实原因对上下游全部不可见：前端 30s 提前中断只显示 `Request timeout after 30000ms`；通过 API 调用的上游只能拿到 `unknown error`。
  - 只有**手动重启进程**能恢复。
- **Expected:**
  - 连接类失败应能被识别并**自动恢复**：重建 HTTP client / 连接池、递增退避、provider 级熔断（暂停 + 定期健康探测）、必要时切到 `fallback_models`；进程不应需要人工重启。
  - 即使无法自动恢复，也应**明确告知**："provider X 连续 N 次不可达，已暂停投递 / 请检查网络"，而不是把 `Request timed out` 抛给前端和 API 调用方。

## Logs / Screenshots

**（1）9/21 决定性对照：重启前全部连接超时 → 重启 → 同一个 provider 立刻成功**

```
# 重启前，同一会话持续失败（每轮 3 次尝试，固定 ~19s 间隔）
2026-09-21 14:03:17 | WARNING | qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py:900 | LLM call failed (attempt 1/4): Request timed out.
2026-09-21 14:03:35 | WARNING | qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py:900 | LLM call failed (attempt 2/4): Request timed out.

```

**（5）故障期间全系统没有一次 LLM 调用成功（09:43–16:56），且失败全部集中在一个会话**

```
$ awk '/09:40:/,/15:02:/' qwenpaw.log | grep -cE "LLM call failed|Request timed out"   # → 778

$ grep -c "Usage for session" (09:43–16:56 窗口内的真实模型调用)                       # → 0
$ ls /tmp/qwenpaw_query_error_*.json | grep "Sep 22" | wc -l                          # → 125 个失败 turn 现场
```

**（6）reporter 侧网络实测（同一台机器，排查时）**

```
DNS(resolve opencode.ai) : 0.010s – 7.56s   (多次采样，抖动极大)
TLS  handshake            : 0.19s – 8.11s
单次 HTTPS 请求           : 0.86s / 0.88s / 10.29s
```

## Additional Notes

**reporter 的推断（供 maintainer 参考，未获 maintainer 确认）——为什么"只有重启能解决"：**

失败状态是**进程级、跨 turn 存活、只能由重启清除**的本地状态。2.2.1 中可疑的候选点：

1. `providers/retry_chat_model.py` 模块级全局：
   - `_pending_stream_cleanup_tasks` / `_pending_provider_cleanup_tasks_by_model`，配合 `_STREAM_CLEANUP_TIMEOUT = 1.0`；
   - `_ensure_provider_available()`（第 466 行）在该模型仍有 pending cleanup 时抛 `StreamCleanupPendingError`（"LLM stream cleanup for {model_key} is still in progress"）。若某个 stream 清理任务因底层连接 blackhole 而永久悬挂，则该模型被**永久隔离**，且没有任何看门狗会解除——只有重启。
2. `providers/rate_limiter.py` 的全局 `LLMRateLimiter` 单例（并发额度 / 全局 pause）；额度或 pause 一旦泄漏，所有 LLM 调用全局受影响，且只有重启能重置。
3. 若 provider / model 实例（含 `AsyncOpenAI` 与其 httpx 连接池、DNS 缓存）在进程内被复用，则被"毒化"的连接池状态会跨越所有后续 turn 持续存在 —— 与"重启后第一发即成功"的现象吻合。
4. 缺失的防护（建议一并补上）：
   - **provider 级熔断**：连续 N 次 connect timeout → 暂停该 provider + 递增退避 + 主动健康探测（参考代码里 MCP 客户端 `drivers/handlers/mcp_stateful_client.py` 已有的熔断状态机，LLM 路径目前没有）；
   - **连接层自愈**：超时后丢弃并重建 HTTP client / 连接池；
   - **fallback 生效**：本例 `fallback_policy.enabled=true` 但 `fallback_models=[]`，等于没有降级；
   - **真实错误透出**：前端不要用 30s 提前中断掩盖 `provider unreachable / retrying`；API 调用方不应只拿到 `unknown error`；
   - **进程内自检**：可考虑暴露"provider 健康/最近 N 分钟失败率"并在 UI 提示"可能需要重启"，至少让用户不必靠猜。

**Workaround（当前唯一有效手段）：** 手动重启 QwenPaw 进程；症状出现后不要依赖等待（reporter 实测等待 5 小时以上未恢复）。

**影响（真实场景）：** 该进程承担盘中自动化投递（每 ~4 分钟一批的行情分析请求）。9/22 一次故障窗口 **09:43–15:01 覆盖几乎整个 A 股交易时段**，期间所有投递 100% 失败、`/compact` 失败、两条告警投递被上游放弃，整体不可用 5 小时 18 分，且必须人工介入重启。

**Related:** reporter 侧另有独立的观测——同一窗口内，上游投递方各自也有 3 次重试，导致单条请求被放大约 3 倍；这与本 issue 无关，但会放大故障面（仅作背景说明）。

issues.title: [Bug]: Tool_call structure lost during context compaction, causing 400 errors / message count mismatch

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

v1.1.12.post2

## Description

During context compaction, `LightContextManager.pre_reasoning()` passes all messages
(including `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks) to `format_msgs_to_str`, which converts
them to plain text for LLM summarization. The structured tool_call data is permanently
lost after compaction. On the next request, the model receives orphaned `tool_result`
messages with no matching `tool_use`, causing 400 errors or `message count mismatch`.

**Expected:** Recent tool_use/tool_result message pairs should survive compaction
with their structured data intact.

**Actual:** All tool call history is flattened into a plain-text summary. The model
can no longer see the structured tool call context, leading to broken tool call
sequences and API errors.

**Related PR(s):** #(optional)

**Security considerations:** N/A

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** v1.1.12.post2
- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.x

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an agent with `context_manager_backend: light` and tool-calling enabled.
2. Have a long conversation that includes multiple tool calls (e.g. `get_current_time`).
3. Allow context to grow until compaction is triggered (`compact_threshold_ratio` exceeded).
4. After compaction, ask the agent to call a tool again.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** Post-compaction requests result in 400 errors (`Invalid 'content'`) or
  `Assistant message count mismatch after formatting`, because `tool_result` messages
  have no matching `tool_use` in the compacted context.
- **Expected:** The most recent tool call pairs should be preserved with full structure
  after compaction.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
Assistant message count mismatch after formatting (N expected survivors, got M)
Invalid 'content': 'content' objects must have a 'type' field that is either
'text' or 'image_url'
```

## Additional Notes

Root cause: `pre_reasoning()` in `light_context_manager.py` calls
`format_msgs_to_str()` on all messages including tool call messages, converting
structured `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks to plain text before passing to the
compaction LLM. The summary retains only narrative content (goals/progress/decisions),
permanently discarding tool call structure.

Suggested fix: Before compaction, extract the N most recent `tool_use`/`tool_result`
message pairs from `messages_to_compact` and move them to `messages_to_keep`, so they
are never passed through `format_msgs_to_str`.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
Title:
[Bug] CoPaw Desktop UI: Agent response disappears after brief display (console channel print failure on Windows)
Body:
markdown
￼
￼
## Bug Description

When using CoPaw Desktop UI (Windows), agent responses appear briefly then disappear, leaving a blank interface. The response content is lost.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start CoPaw Desktop on Windows (`copaw desktop`
)
2. Select any agent (e.g., `quant_team_coordinator`
)
3.
 Send a message to the agent
4.
 Observe: response flashes briefly, then disappears

## Expected Behavior

Agent responses should remain visible in the chat interface.

## Actual Behavior

Response appears briefly (~1 second) then disappears. The interface becomes blank.

## Environment

-
 OS: Windows 10
-
 CoPaw Version: 1.0.2
-
 Channel: console
-
 Model: MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed

## Root Cause Analysis

From `copaw.log`:
Print failed with OSError [Errno 22], attempting fallback encoding Failed to print even with fallback: [Errno 22] Invalid argument console stream done: event_count=419 has_response=True
The issue is in `copaw/app/channels/console/channel.py`:
- The `_safe_print` method fails to print Chinese/UTF-8 content on Windows
- Even the fallback encoding fails with OSError [Errno 22]
- When printing fails, the response content is lost from the frontend

## Relevant Code

File: `copaw/app/channels/console/channel.py`

```python
def _safe_print(self, text: str) -> None:
    try:
        print(text)
    except OSError as e:
        if e.errno == 22:
            try:
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(
                    text.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
                )
            except Exception as fallback_err:
                logger.error("Failed to print even with fallback: %s", fallback_err)
                # BUG: Response content is lost here, not recovered
Additional Notes
• CLI command works fine: copaw agents chat --from-agent default --to-agent quant_team_coordinator --text "hello"
• The issue affects ALL agents when using CoPaw Desktop UI on Windows
• This is a regression or design flaw in the console channel implementation

issues.title: [Bug]: Plugin hot-install aborts when importlib.invalidate_caches() raises on distro-patched Python 3.11（我的插件被这个卡了））

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

## Description

The plugin loader calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` unconditionally at three
sites (`loader.py:201`, `loader.py:465`, `loader.py:1094`). On Python builds where
this stdlib function itself raises (a real-world distro backport bug, see
Additional Notes), the exception propagates and aborts the entire plugin
install / hot-update.

Cache invalidation is best-effort by design — a failure here should not be fatal.

**Related PR(s):** N/A
**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Linux x86_64 (Lifsea 8 container, kernel 5.10.134-18.0.12.lifsea8)
- **Install method:** pip (venv)
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11.15 (`libpython3.11-minimal 3.11.2-6+deb12u9`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On an affected Python build, verify the environment bug directly:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "import importlib; importlib.invalidate_caches()"
   ```

   → `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`

2. With QwenPaw running, install any plugin whose `requirements.txt` contains a
   not-yet-satisfied dependency (Console upload or `qwenpaw plugin install`).
3. The install aborts with the TypeError above; the plugin directory is copied
   into `plugins/` but the plugin never loads.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The entire plugin install fails with `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`.
- **Expected:** A cache-invalidation failure degrades to a warning and the install proceeds.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
File ".../qwenpaw/app/routers/plugins.py", line 847, in upload_plugin
  record = await _load_plugin_with_optional_force_reinstall(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1179, in load_plugin_from_path
  record = await self._load_plugin_from_path_unlocked(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 1316, in _load_plugin_from_path_unlocked
  await asyncio.to_thread(...)
File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py", line 465, in _install_requirements_locked
  importlib.invalidate_caches()
File "/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/__init__.py", line 70, in invalidate_caches
  finder.invalidate_caches()
File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap_external>", line 1409, in invalidate_caches
TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## Additional Notes

Root cause has two layers:

1. **Environment (not QwenPaw's fault):** this distro build backported the
   CPython 3.12 change "PathFinder.invalidate_caches also clears
   importlib.metadata caches" into 3.11's frozen bootstrap, but the backported
   `/usr/lib/python3.11/importlib/metadata/__init__.py` (line 918) lost its
   `@classmethod` decorator:

   ```python
   def invalidate_caches(cls):      # ← @classmethod missing in backport
       FastPath.__new__.cache_clear()
   ```

   So **every** `importlib.invalidate_caches()` call raises. Reproduced with a
   bare interpreter, including under `python3 -S`. The same environment bug
   also breaks `pip`, `pytest`, etc., so QwenPaw cannot rely on the
   environment being fixed — it should tolerate the failure.

2. **QwenPaw side:** `loader.py:201` / `:465` / `:1094` call it unguarded.

**Suggested fix** — wrap all three sites:

```python
try:
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
except Exception:
    logger.warning("importlib.invalidate_caches() failed; continuing", exc_info=True)
```

**Workaround for plugin authors:** ship the plugin without `requirements.txt`
when all deps are already QwenPaw host dependencies — `loader.py:392` returns
early when the file is absent, bypassing the failing path entirely. (Verified:
`pyyaml>=6.0` is already a direct `Requires-Dist` of the `qwenpaw` package.)

issues.title: [Bug]: Atomic file writes reject valid long filenames
issues.body:
### What happened?

`write_file` / `edit_file` fail for long filenames that the underlying filesystem accepts. The shared atomic writer derives its temporary basename as `.{target.name}.{16 random hex characters}.tmp`, adding 22 bytes to the destination name. A valid 243-byte filename therefore becomes an invalid 265-byte temporary name on a filesystem with a 255-byte component limit.

Reproduced on Linux, Python 3.11, current main `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`. Both `"a" * 240 + ".md"` and `"报告" * 40 + ".md"` can be created with normal filesystem writes, but QwenPaw's atomic writer raises `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`. The public file tool returns an error instead of writing the file.

### Reproduction

Run from a QwenPaw development environment:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from qwenpaw.utils.io_utils import write_text_atomic

with TemporaryDirectory(dir=".") as directory:
    target = Path(directory) / ("报告" * 40 + ".md")
    target.write_text("old", encoding="utf-8")  # succeeds
    write_text_atomic(target, "new")           # Errno 36
```

Expected: valid destination filenames work for atomic writes, including new files and replacements, with no leftover temporary files.

Actual: the temporary file allocation fails before the replacement. Existing destination contents are preserved, but the requested write/edit cannot complete.

### Evidence and proposed scope

- Existing utilities/configuration/backup/file-tool selection: **853 passed**.
- Six added real-filesystem regressions on unmodified production code: **6 failed**, covering ASCII/UTF-8 names, new/existing destinations, and the public write tool. No filesystem mocks.
- A small fix can use a bounded temporary basename in the same directory while retaining exclusive creation, permissions, fsync, atomic replace, collision retries and cleanup.
- Searched issues and open PRs for long filenames, `ENAMETOOLONG`, atomic filenames and `_open_atomic_temp`; no same-fault open fix found. #6528 touches atomic writes for validation/retry behavior, not temporary basename length.

I am preparing the focused fix and regression tests. AI assistance: discovered and reproduced with Codex; the counts above are from actual local runs, not upstream CI.

issues.title: Session permanently wedged by media blocks: "At most 0 video(s) may be provided in one prompt" and "[unsupported_request] Message content supports text content only" miss both media classifiers
issues.body:
### Summary

Same wedge family as #8171 (audio, still open) and #7015 / #7024, but with two rejection shapes that **neither** the media-capability classifier **nor** the media-payload classifier matches. Because the wordings contain no `does not support` / `is not supported` / `unsupported modality` / `vision is not enabled` phrasing, the strip → retry → learn recovery never triggers: nothing is stripped, nothing is retried, no capability is learned, and **every later turn in the session fails identically**.

The same session also hit the second half of the wedge: it accumulated ~61 MB of inline base64 media, **all of it under the per-file cap and ~0 tokens**, and every turn was then rejected with 413 — exactly the gap that open PR #8034 targets.

### Environment

- QwenPaw **2.2.2** (latest release, 2026-10-15), Python 3.12, Windows 11
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible aggregator gateway (`opencode`), model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Channel: console
- Start of the incident: first 413 in this session on 2026-10-11; video shape on 2026-10-16; both shapes again on 2026-10-17

### Rejection shape A — video block replayed from history (permanent 400)

```
Streaming response failed: [400] At most 0 video(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=video)
```

A `video/mp4` DataBlock ended up in the persisted session history (agent had delivered/loaded media earlier in the session). `agent_state.state.context` held **2 × `video/mp4`** blocks. Every subsequent model call in the session returned this 400 — the video sibling of #8171's audio case.

### Rejection shape B — endpoint media disabled while the model is declared multimodal (permanent 400)

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'type': 'server_error', 'message': 'Upstream request failed: [unsupported_request] Message content supports text content only. Images, audio and files are not enabled.'}}
```

The endpoint actually serving the deployment has media disabled, but the client still formats the stored media blocks into the request. No capability check happens before the send, and the wording matches none of `_GLOBAL_MEDIA_CAPABILITY_PATTERNS` / `_EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS`.

### Rejection shape C — request-body byte explosion from accumulated inline media (permanent 413)

```
Error code: 413 - {'error': {'type': 'server_error', 'message': 'Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.'}}
```

Measured on the failing request itself:

- serialized `agent_state`: **61.0 MB**
- of which inline media: **61.1 MB** — 38 × `image/png` (1.4–2.3 MB each), 1 × `image/jpeg`, 2 × `video/mp4`
- **every individual file was below `MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (2 MB)** — i.e. all in-spec media, cumulatively unbounded
- media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction never fired
- the request bodies that failed were 62–66 MB (the error dumps written to `%TEMP%\qwenpaw_query_error_*.json` are themselves 62–66 MB)

This is the identical situation described in the open PR #8034 (a design-review session accumulating ~20 MB of inline screenshots, every one under the per-file cap).

### Verification with the runtime's own classifiers

Run against QwenPaw 2.2.2's shipped code:

```python
from qwenpaw.agents.react_agent import QwenPawAgent as A
A._is_explicit_media_capability_error(Exception(msg))   # media-capability retry
A._is_media_payload_rejection_error(Exception(msg))     # media-free retry
A._is_global_media_capability_error(Exception(msg))     # learn rejects_media
```

| real error string | capability retry | payload retry | learns `rejects_media` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[400] At most 0 video(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=video)` | no | no | no |
| `[400] [unsupported_request] Message content supports text content only. Images, audio and files are not enabled.` | no | no | no |
| `[413] Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.` | no | no | no |
| `[422] unknown variant video_url, expected one of text, image_url, file` | no | no | no |
| `[413] {'code': 'EntryTooBig', 'type': 'Request Entity Too Large'}` | no | no | no |
| **control:** `This model does not support media input.` | **yes** | no | **yes** |

**5/5 real shapes miss, the control matches** — the classifier mechanism is sound, the signal tables simply do not cover these wordings. Notably `_is_media_payload_rejection_error()` does see the media nouns in shape B ("Images, audio and files") but rejects it because `are not enabled` is not in `_MEDIA_PAYLOAD_REJECTION_SIGNALS`.

### Actual result

Every user message in the affected session returns the same error; from the user's side the channel simply stops sending messages. Nothing in the product recovers it. The only recovery we found is manual history surgery, or the built-in `/compact` if it happens to evict the offending message — measured: **61 MB → 1.47 MB after `/compact`, session usable again immediately**.

### Suggested fix

1. **Broaden the classifier** — or classify generically: a 400 on a request that *did* carry media (`_last_wire_request_had_media()`), whose message names image/audio/video/media, should at least justify a **media-free retry** for that request. Keeping the model-wide `rejects_media` learning conservative is fine; failing to retry at all is what wedges the session.
2. **Cover the 413 body-size case with the same media-free retry.** The media *is* the bulk of the body, so dropping it for the retry would very likely succeed — instead the size signals are explicitly excluded from the capability patterns (see the `size_signals` early-return in `_is_explicit_media_capability_error`).
3. **Land #8034** (cumulative inline-media budget per request, `max_total_bytes`, default 8 MB). The 61 MB case here is exactly its repro, and a compact placeholder would also keep the evidence readable.
4. **Resolve media capability against the endpoint that actually serves the request**, not only against the declared model, before formatting.

Happy to test a patch against this repro; I can also attach the sanitized error dumps (62–66 MB each) if useful.

### Related

- #8171 (open) — `send_file_to_user` audio file permanently wedges the session (same mechanism, audio shape)
- #8034 (open) — bound inline media per request, not just per file
- #8100, #8070, #8066, #7973, #7966 (open) — media capability resolution / history media handling
- #7015 / #7024 — earlier DashScope-shaped wedge

issues.title: [Bug]: Out-of-workspace write hard-block is blind to kimi-code's Write tool — `_paths` extraction does not recognize kimi toolCall path fields

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
**Environment**: QwenPaw 2.2.0 (desktop, macOS arm64); kimi-code runner via ACP.

**Observed (live negative probe, 2026-09-12)**:

1. A delegated kimi-code ACP session was asked to write a probe file at `/tmp/kimi_oob_probe.txt` — outside the agent's workspace.
2. The write succeeded without triggering QwenPaw's out-of-bounds hard block and without a path-related permission prompt. (The file was verified to exist on disk afterwards.)
3. Inspection of the toolCall payload shows kimi-code's Write calls do not expose the target path in any of the fields QwenPaw's `_paths` extraction recognizes (`locations` / `diff` / `rawInput.path`). The path boundary check therefore sees an empty path set and has nothing to deny.

**Why this matters**: operators configuring ACP runners reasonably assume the workspace-boundary hard block applies uniformly to all runners' file-writing tools. For kimi-code it silently does not — the effective guard reduces to the catastrophic-shell-command regex plus whatever the runner itself enforces. This is a silent security-posture gap, not a usability issue.

**Suggested fix**:
1. Extend `_paths` extraction to also parse kimi-code's toolCall shapes — the path is available in `rawInput` (under tool-specific keys) and/or the human-readable `title` field; and/or
2. Fail-closed option: when a toolCall is known to be a file-write operation (by tool name/kind) but `_paths` extraction yields nothing, treat it as out-of-bounds or force an interactive confirmation rather than silently allowing.

**Minimal repro**:
1. Configure a kimi-code ACP runner (default policy, workspace boundary enabled).
2. Via `delegate_external_agent`, instruct the runner to create a file at an absolute path outside the workspace (e.g. `/tmp/probe.txt`) using its Write tool.
3. Expected: hard block (or at minimum an explicit out-of-bounds prompt). Actual: file is written with no boundary intervention.

issues.title: [Bug]: `server/discover` HTTP 422 with plain-text body (DBX MCP) is not treated as legacy-protocol evidence — streamable_http driver never activates (status=inactive, Console 503)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`, QwenPaw Hub deployment, Linux container runtime)

## Description

An MCP card of type `streamable_http` pointing at **DBX** (local database tool, server version 0.4.102) fails Driver construction with `Failed to build Driver 'dbx': MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 422`. The client card stays `status=inactive` forever and the Console reports `503: MCP client 'dbx' is saved but not active yet`.

Root cause — same negotiation gap as #7728 / #7827 but a different status code and body shape:

- The server rejects the unknown `server/discover` probe with **HTTP 422** and a plain-text body `Unexpected message, expect initialize request` (it mandates `initialize` as the first message and answers unknown/misordered requests with 422, no JSON-RPC error envelope).
- In `_unwrap_jsonrpc_result`, the 422 body is not a JSON-RPC envelope → raises `httpx.HTTPStatusError`.
- In `_negotiate`, the `except httpx.HTTPStatusError` branch only classifies bare **400/404/405** as legacy-protocol evidence (`_is_legacy_protocol_evidence` → `status_code in {400, 404, 405}`) → 422 propagates → the whole Driver build fails.

Control group: the same server completes a classic `initialize` handshake (HTTP 200, protocol 2025-03-26) and answers `tools/list` with 25 tools — it works perfectly via the legacy `HttpStatefulClient` path once the fallback triggers.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** macOS host + Docker Linux runtime (QwenPaw Hub, one container per user)
- **Install method:** Docker
- **MCP server:** DBX 0.4.102, `streamable_http` at `http://host:5225/mcp` (Bearer auth)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an MCP card (`streamable_http`) pointing at a DBX MCP server.
2. Let QwenPaw build the Driver (startup or card hot-reload).
3. Driver build fails, card stays inactive, Console tool queries return 503.

Minimal probe against the same server (from any HTTP client):

```text
POST /mcp  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"protocolVersion":"2026-07-28"}}}
→ HTTP 422  "Unexpected message, expect initialize request"

POST /mcp  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26",...}}
→ HTTP 200  (SSE, serverInfo dbx 0.4.102, capabilities tools+resources)
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `Failed to build Driver 'dbx': MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 422`; legacy fallback never triggers because 422 is not in the legacy-evidence status set.
- **Expected:** the 422 response is recognized as "server does not support `server/discover`" and negotiation falls back to the legacy handshake, which connects successfully.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
WARNING | drivers/manager.py:159 | Failed to build Driver 'dbx': MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 422
WARNING | app/mcp/config_service.py:141 | Failed to list tools for MCP client 'dbx': 503: MCP client 'dbx' is saved but not active yet (status=inactive)
```

## Additional Notes

Suggested fix (any one suffices; the first is one line and verified locally):

1. Add `422` to the status set in `_is_legacy_protocol_evidence` (`{400, 404, 405}` → `{400, 404, 405, 422}`); or more generally treat *any* 4xx discover response whose body is not a standard JSON-RPC envelope as legacy evidence.
2. Same direction as the pending PR #7729 (Java `jsonRpcError` envelope, HTTP 500). It would be great to unify the three known shapes — bare 400/404/405 (#current), non-standard 5xx envelopes (#7728), bare 500 empty body (#7827), and 422 non-JSON-RPC (this issue) — into one "discover probe failed with a non-modern answer → let the legacy handshake arbitrate" rule.

Local workaround (deployed and verified): patched image with the one-line change from suggestion 1. Log then shows the expected path and full tool list:

```text
INFO | mcp_streamable_http.py:969 | MCP client 'dbx' falling back to legacy: MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 422
INFO | mcp_stateful_client.py:251 | MCP client connected: dbx
(list_tools → 25 tools)
```

Related: #7728 (500 + jsonRpcError envelope), #7827 (bare 500 empty body), PR #7729.

issues.body: ## Summary Add an optional PowerContext-backed long-term memory backend for QwenPaw through the existing BaseMemoryManager and memory_registry extension points. ## Motivation The default local memory backend is suitable for single-machine use, but deployments may need a shared, persistent, explicitly scoped memory service. PowerContext provides cross-session continuity, scope isolation, citation-aware retrieval, and a remote HTTP boundary without coupling QwenPaw to a database driver. ## Proposed scope - Add PowerContextMemoryManager as a selectable peer of ReMeLightMemoryManager. - Support automatic pre-turn retrieval and non-blocking post-turn task_state persistence. - Expose memory_search and memory_remember only when PowerContext is selected. - Preserve PowerContext citation metadata in search results. - Add optional Console configuration for URL, token, scope, timeout, and auto-search settings. - Register dynamic tools with the unified governance registry. - Keep the default backend and Agent main flow unchanged. ## Non-goals This proposal does not add Handoff, Experience, Skill, Candidate, Artifact, or database-driver integration to QwenPaw. PowerContext remains an external HTTP service. ## Validation The prototype has 181 QwenPaw unit tests passing, Console TypeScript and locale checks passing, and has been exercised against a local PowerContext service for remember/search, citation preservation, cross-session recall, and scope isolation. A PR with the implementation will reference this issue.

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, so it is charged
  to the budget as well: the enforcing pass has to walk the same sequence of
  sizes the measuring pass measured.

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
64 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failures below are pre-existing in this
environment (missing optional dependencies: `acp`, `playwright`, `reme`, …)
and are identical on the unmodified head commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        148 failed, 4224 passed
# unmodified head:    148 failed, 4219 passed   (+5 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or `max_total_bytes` on the model) to match
their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- `model_factory`'s tool-result video path (`_video_oversize_placeholder`)
  applies its own per-file cap and is untouched — it does not go through
  these formatters, so it is not covered by the cumulative budget. Worth a
  follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: fix(desktop): handle Windows installer preparation failures
prs.body:
## Description

Fix two locally reproduced causes of Windows installer preparation failure and make preparation errors visible:

- Prefer `$SYSDIR\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` when it exists, falling back to the original `powershell.exe` search when it is absent. Share this selection across preparation, launcher restoration, and CLI PATH updates. This removes the PATH dependency on standard installations while preserving the original lookup when the system executable is missing.
- Check for empty native-host launcher/backup contents before calling `Contains()` or `ToLowerInvariant()`. `Get-Content -Raw` returns no content for empty files, causing preparation or restoration to throw.
- Replace the blanket file-contention message with a preparation-failure message, showing the return result and existing script output. Explicitly identify failures to start Windows PowerShell. Update the six existing installer translations.

Existing process selection, launcher restoration, and cancellation behavior are preserved.

**Related Issue:** User-reported Windows desktop installation failure; the exact trigger on the reporter's machine remains unconfirmed.

prs.body:
## Description

Remove the SDK-specific dependency audit and route SDK plugins through the existing plugin dependency installer. This prevents the additional SDK conflict checks from rejecting installations before the framework’s normal dependency handling runs.

Also simplify plugin tests and improve reliability:

- Remove redundant tests, ineffective assertions, and unnecessary CDN-dependent smoke tests.
- Consolidate repeated scenarios while retaining installation, rollback, ownership, and cleanup coverage.
- Fix leaked test threads and child-process lifetime assumptions that caused slow or misleading failures.
- Replace fragile timing assumptions and shorten controlled timeout tests.

prs.title: fix(memory): inject automatic recall as reference context
prs.body:
## Description

Automatic memory recall was represented as an assistant-authored thinking/tool-call/tool-result sequence. Models could imitate that synthetic trajectory and call `memory_search` again in the same turn.

This change represents automatic recall as transient, untrusted system reference context instead. When a request already has a system message, the evidence is merged into a copy of that leading message so provider message-order requirements remain valid. Explicit model-initiated `memory_search` calls are unchanged.

The original user query is not copied into the system evidence, avoiding both duplicated context and elevation of untrusted user instructions.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8361

**Security Considerations:** Retrieved memory is explicitly labeled as untrusted reference data. The wrapper tells the model not to follow instructions found in the retrieved content, and raw user query text is never promoted into the system evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

With Automatic Memory Search enabled, the injected context looked like a tool call the assistant had just made. Some models continued that synthetic trajectory by repeatedly calling `memory_search`; after the duplicate-call guard stopped the loop, they could still fail to produce a usable text response. The model now receives the retrieved content without a tool-call example to imitate.

- Add provider-configurable Realtime Voice chats with speech input, playback, interruption, and model selection in the existing Chat UI.
- Hand admitted speech to the ordinary Chat execution path so history, tools, long-running work, queueing, persistence, and rendering remain shared.
- Keep running Voice UI and canonical history aligned through semantic reply groups, including replay, refresh, multi-input answers, and tool-result attribution.
- Add provider-neutral realtime contracts plus a DashScope adapter with recoverable idle-close handling and automatic reconnect.
- Persist Voice capability in the existing Chat metadata while keeping `source="chat"`, including migration of early development records for downgrade safety.

## Module Layout

Two-layer split — provider-neutral vendor layer vs. application orchestration:

- `providers/realtime_voice/` — vendor-neutral contracts (`RealtimeProviderSession`, `ProviderEvent`, `RealtimeSessionConfig`) plus the DashScope adapter. No application dependencies.
- `app/realtime_voice/` — orchestration: `VoiceCoordinator`, `VoiceTaskBridge`, `SpokenTurnCommitter`, `PresentationQueue`. Pure prompt building lives in `prompts.py`; user-facing text and ordinals in `labels.py`.
- `app/routers/realtime_voice.py` — HTTP/WS boundary only, no business logic.

Input vs. reply source of truth: `runtime/input_context.py` (`ChatInputContext`) owns committed input identity/order and admission status; `runtime/reply_cycle.py` (`ReplyCycleContext`) owns run and reply identity. `InputStateEvent` flows one-way from the reply cycle into the input context as a read-only projection.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** Provider credentials remain server-side. The Console uses the authenticated application relay and does not receive provider API keys.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] **Contract test** exists in `tests/contract/channels/test_<channel>_contract.py` (REQUIRED)
- [ ] Contract test implements `create_instance()` with proper channel initialization
- [ ] All 19 contract verification points pass (see `tests/contract/channels/__init__.py`)
- [ ] **Optional**: Unit tests in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` for complex internal logic

## Testing

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH='src;packages/qwenpawmail-mcp/src'
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest `
  tests/unit/app/realtime_voice `
  tests/unit/app/routers/test_realtime_voice.py `
  tests/unit/providers/realtime_voice/test_dashscope.py `
  tests/unit/app/chats/test_models.py `
  tests/unit/app/chats/test_repo.py `
  tests/unit/app/chats/test_run_coordinator.py `
  tests/unit/app/chats/test_manager.py -q

Set-Location console
npm run test:run -- `
  src/features/realtime-voice/useRealtimeVoice.test.ts `
  src/pages/Chat/runtimeTimelineProjection.test.ts `
  src/pages/Chat/tests/testLargeSession.test.ts `
  src/pages/Chat/ChatPage.coverage.test.tsx

$env:NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192'
npm run build:test

Set-Location ..
$files = @(git diff --name-only upstream/main -- '*.py')
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m flake8 --extend-ignore=E203 $files
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

## Evidence

```text
Backend affected-area tests: 256 passed
Frontend Voice/Chat tests: 4 files, 147 passed
TypeScript + Vite production build: passed (19,373 modules, 3m 28s)
Changed Python files: Flake8 passed
Patch hygiene: git diff --check passed
```

Synthetic-microphone E2E used local WAV input through the real browser capture, WebSocket relay, DashScope Realtime, ordinary Chat agent/tool execution, and AudioContext playback path:

- Ten independently admitted long-running spoken tasks completed without duplicate execution, dropped tasks, or `Conversation already has an active response`.
- Running cards, tool results, final answers, refresh, and reconnect retained semantic input/output ownership without `missing_final_answer`.
- Two DashScope idle closes normalized to recoverable session closure and reconnected across generations 1, 2, and 3 with no product error; the next spoken turn completed and played normally.
- Raw local E2E logs and audio are intentionally excluded from the PR.

## Additional Notes

- This remains a draft while physical-microphone listening and providers other than DashScope remain outside the completed acceptance matrix.
- The default local Node heap reached its 4 GB limit while Vite rendered chunks after the upstream rebase; the unchanged build passed with an 8 GB heap. Existing chunk-size and mixed dynamic/static import warnings remain.

## Follow-up: durable speech evidence and cold restart recovery (2026-10-20)

Commit: `fcc00651a` (`fix(voice): persist speech evidence and restore chat ownership`).

### Changes

- Persist the independent ASR snapshot/final evidence against its existing execution input ID through the Chat timeline journal. Evidence remains model-only context and does not create another visible user turn or permission to repeat work.
- Save available speech evidence before admitting execution; retain late final transcripts, deduplicate repeated events, and wait for in-flight history writes when Voice closes.
- Merge pending timeline evidence into the loaded Agent context, including legacy sessions, so a stale Agent save or restart does not hide a committed final transcript. Keep pending records until safe reconciliation.
- Restore Chat ownership from public Agent replies at Voice startup. Process-local bridge records can be empty after a restart even when complete persisted history exists; subsequent live speech now retains the existing fallback if the native voice model omits its handoff call.

### Verification

Focused coordinator/handoff/history tests: **67 passed**.

```sh
python -m pytest tests/unit/app/realtime_voice/test_coordinator.py tests/unit/app/realtime_voice/test_handoff.py tests/unit/app/chats/test_conversation_view.py -q --tb=short
```

The local run used the configured Python environment and AgentScope 2.0.10 SDK overlay. Coverage includes restored ownership, final-transcript ordering/replay, exactly-once admission, native-handoff deduplication, no history-triggered execution, and preserving direct replies for voice-only conversation history. `git diff --check` also passed.

Persistence E2E verified final ASR arriving after handoff, duplicate final delivery, disconnect during a five-second delayed commit, and recovery of committed-but-unreconciled evidence after terminating the test backend. The restored real model request contained the provisional and final evidence once each, with no task replay or extra visible user messages.

Built-in-browser E2E against the real DashScope speech model and ordinary Chat Agent/tools used the same synthesized WAV in three runs, with **two actual backend process restarts**:

| Scenario | Native handoff | Application fallback | New Python executions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial voice request | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Restart, reload the same chat, repeat the WAV; no fault injection | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| Restart again; deliberately omit native handoff tool definitions for this test connection | 0 | 1 | 1 |

- Both restored sessions had zero in-memory bridge records, complete persisted history (`omitted=false`), and Chat ownership restored before new speech.
- All three requests had distinct input/tool-call IDs, ran `python3 -c "print(211 * 37)"` once, and returned the actual tool output `7807`.
- The controlled missed-handoff run produced a real native response with `had_tool_call=false`; the application suppressed that unexecuted direct answer, admitted the new request once, and completed real tool execution.
- Startup history did not replay old work. Final public history contained exactly three user inputs. Provider error events: zero.
- The E2E verifier passed, and all nine changed source/test files matched their pre-E2E hashes. Test instrumentation stayed outside the repository and was disabled/closed afterward.

### Boundaries

Playback was muted and input was synthesized, so this is not a physical-microphone acceptance result. The third run deliberately disabled the native model's handoff tool definitions; it demonstrates the fallback under a missed handoff, not spontaneous reproduction or a measured model failure rate. Brand-new conversations with no prior Chat execution evidence still rely on the native model to initiate the first handoff. Raw local logs/audio/session data remain excluded from the PR.

prs.title: fix(providers): route content inspection errors to fallback
prs.body:
## Description

Ali-compatible gateways can return `data_inspection_failed` or `inappropriate content` when a request is rejected by content inspection. QwenPaw currently classifies both messages as `bad_request`, so `FallbackChatModel` stops instead of trying the next configured model. This change classifies those provider markers as `content_safety` and allows fallback while keeping same-model retry disabled.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8092

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, network policy, or user content handling changed. The change only affects provider error classification and fallback eligibility.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change

- [x] I ran focused tests locally and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (not needed for an internal provider classification fix)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

```text
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit/providers/test_model_error_policy.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_fallback_chat_model.py
57 passed in 1.32s after Black formatting
```

The baseline probe classified both Ali markers as `bad_request` with `fallback_eligible=false`; the fixed probe classifies them as `content_safety` with `fallback_eligible=true` and leaves `retryable=false`.

All pre-commit hooks pass on the three files changed by this PR. The full-repository run reports pylint E1120 for `ctypes.c_ulong()` in the unchanged sandbox file above; that file has the same Git blob before and after this PR. Black's two formatting changes are included.

The default full pytest command encounters duplicate `test_backup` module names during collection. After setting `PYTHONPATH=src:tests/integration` and `--import-mode=importlib`, the complete suite ran with four workers: **19,356 passed, 30 skipped, 3 xpassed, 3 failed in 24m44s** (exit 1). A runner-only `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook sorted nodeids to handle the existing set-derived parameter order; serial and all four workers collected the same 19,387 unique nodeids, with no added or removed tests.

All three failures also reproduced on the unmodified baseline `f3895346` using the same test environment (3 failed in 121.24s): `test_plugins_get_nonexistent` and `test_providers_get_nonexistent` receive HTTP 405 instead of their expected 404/400, and `test_matrix_bot_own_message_ignored` times out waiting for its probe response. No full-suite pass is claimed. These are existing upstream tests; no new mocks or test exclusions were introduced.

## Evidence

- Added regression coverage for the existing content-safety marker, `data_inspection_failed`, and `inappropriate content`.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- OCR pre-PR review completed with the fallback provider: 1 changed source file reviewed, 0 findings, complete coverage.

prs.title: fix(tools): preserve line endings and encoding in edit_file (#8414, #8415)
prs.body:
Fixes #8414, #8415.

## What Problem This Solves

`edit_file` rewrote the whole file through a text-mode writer (`newline='\n'`, UTF-8). Two user-visible bugs followed:

- **CRLF files were converted to LF on every edit** (#8414, #8415) — a one-line change rewrote every line ending in the file, which shows up as a whole-file diff in git and can break files that require CRLF (Windows batch scripts, some configs).
- **Non-UTF-8 files were destroyed** — an ISO-8859-1 file with bytes outside ASCII was re-encoded (or failed) even when the edit itself touched nothing near them.

The fix writes the snapshot back byte for byte: `edit_file` now reads the raw bytes, decodes with the encoding the file actually uses (BOM detection first), applies the replacement, re-encodes, and hands the result to a new `_write_bytes_atomic` that writes a sibling temp file in binary and `os.replace()`s it into place. Line endings are normalised for *matching* only, then the file's own ending is re-applied to inserted text.

## Evidence

Unit tests in `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py` (all new, per file-ending/encoding case):

- `test_crlf_endings_survive_a_one_line_edit` — a CRLF file edited in the middle keeps CRLF everywhere; byte-comparing the whole file passes
- `test_lf_file_is_unchanged_in_shape` — an LF file is not rewritten into CRLF
- `test_iso_8859_1_bytes_are_not_destroyed` — a Latin-1 file with non-ASCII bytes around the edit point round-trips
- `test_utf8_bom_is_preserved` — the BOM is still there after editing
- `test_new_lines_in_new_text_follow_the_file_ending` — inserted text uses the file's ending, not a hardcoded `\n`

The atomic writer also keeps the target's mode: `shutil.copymode(target, temp)` when the file exists (which additionally preserves setuid/setgid bits that a `st_mode & 0o777` mask dropped), and the constant `0o644` for a brand-new file.

CI on this revision: pre-commit (black 23.3.0, flake8, mypy, pylint) clean, CodeQL clean, unit tests passing.
