prs.title: fix(channels): re-apply the system prompt cap after per-turn skill refreshes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The channel-turn system prompt is modified after the initial `max_system_prompt_chars` finalization (skills refresh splice on fresh sessions or mode changes, per-message signal block, peer-map append, thinking prefix prepend), so the operator's cap silently stopped applying exactly when the prompt was largest.
  - Re-apply `finalize_system_prompt` with the agent's cap as the last step before the system message enters history (message-processing path), and at the provider-switch retry path (`refresh_channel_history_skills`) and after the startup builder's own post-finalize additions (tool instructions, deferred section, receipts addendum), so the cached prompt starts in-cap too.
  - `finalize_system_prompt` now strips existing `TIMESTAMP_ORIENTATION` occurrences before head-retention truncation, making re-finalization idempotent (a re-finalized cached channel prompt previously always gained a duplicate orientation, since the base orientation survives into the retained head).
- **Scope boundary:** no new settings, no canonical-source duplication; the no-op path of `finalize_system_prompt` (prompt within cap) is untouched; compaction/history trimming behavior unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** channel system-prompt assembly only. Agents whose prompts already fit the cap see no change (finalization is a no-op for them). Agents with large skill sets on fresh sessions now get a capped prompt; the previously possible over-cap prompt instead reached the context-floor budget refusal (`context_floor_exceeds_budget`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12044 (deferred bootstrap sections), Related #12056 (identity-head truncation, whose zone-aware finalize this reuses).

### What this does, simply

`max_system_prompt_chars` is the operator's ceiling for what the system prompt may occupy. It was enforced only when the prompt was first built at startup. Later, on the first message of a new conversation (or after a skills-mode change), the runtime replaces the skills section with a freshly rendered one — in Full injection mode that is every skill's full instructions — and appends per-message extras. None of those steps re-checked the ceiling, so a fresh conversation could dispatch a system prompt several times larger than the configured cap. In production this surfaced as a hard refusal for brand-new conversations (`system prompt and tool definitions (148706 tokens) exceed context budget (100000)`) while long-lived conversations kept using the older, capped cached prompt and worked fine. This PR applies the existing cap, with the existing identity-aware truncation, after all of those modifications — and makes re-applying it safe by de-duplicating the runtime-owned timestamp orientation block first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — behavior is fully covered by new regression tests that reproduce the incident shape (skill refresh exceeding the cap before the fix, capped after), and the pre/post delta is asserted in-test.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (telegram path in the repro test, mechanism is channel-generic)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

- New `process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh` (zeroclaw-channels): builds a real startup prompt under a 4000-char cap, drops a ~26KB-body skill on disk in Full mode, and asserts (1) the refresh splice really exceeds the cap (incident reproduction), (2) the refreshed history prompt is ≤ cap with exactly one timestamp orientation, (3) end-to-end, the provider receives a system prompt ≤ cap with one orientation.
- New `refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation` (zeroclaw-runtime): re-finalizing an already-finalized prompt does not duplicate the orientation.
- Before the fix the e2e assertion fails (~26K chars vs cap 4000 reaching the provider); after, green.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib process_channel_message_reapplies_prompt_cap_after_skill_refresh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib refinalizing_an_over-cap_prompt_keeps_a_single_timestamp_orientation
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI on this PR (build/test/clippy across feature matrix) — the change touches the channel orchestrator and system-prompt finalization used by all channels.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** local run covered lib targets of the two touched crates; full-workspace integration binaries were not built locally (CI covers them).
- **Commands run and tail output:** both new tests and neighbors (`final_prompt_budget*`, `timestamp_orientation_respects_budgets`, full `agent::system_prompt` module — 35 tests, `process_channel_message_refreshes_available_skills_after_new_session`) pass; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` exits 0 with no new warnings in the changed lines.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Idempotence of the added finalization on under-cap prompts (no-op path) via the orientation-count assertions; not verified: full workspace integration binaries and non-Linux platform runs.

prs.title: fix(runtime): enforce the system prompt size budget (fail closed)
prs.body:
Fixes #11908.

## What

The `max_system_prompt_chars` runtime-profile limit was advisory only. This makes it a hard gate and removes the unlimited default:

- **Fail closed in the turn gate** (`turn/mod.rs`): when the assembled system-prompt floor reaches/exceeds the context budget, the turn returns a typed `SystemPromptFloorExceedsBudget` error **before dispatch** — the over-budget request no longer reaches the provider. The historical WARN keeps its `error_key: context_floor_exceeds_budget` so existing trace dashboards still match.
- **Finite safe default** (`schema.rs`): `default_max_system_prompt_chars()` 0 → 50000. An explicit `= 0` in a profile keeps opt-in unlimited.
- **Workspace bootstrap respects the cap** for `compact_context = false` sessions (oversized-bootstrap regression test: 5×200K files under a 50000 cap).

## What this is NOT

The budget is resolved atomically with the rest of the profile from one generation-stamped config snapshot (`resolved_agent_config`), and the new gate measures the provider-bound request — the suspected snapshot-race and history-vs-request divergence paths were inspected and do not reproduce as independent defects; the gate now rejects any such bypass regardless.

## Tests

New regression tests (prefix `prompt_budget_cap_`): gate trip conditions, typed+localized refusal, capped workspace bootstrap with `compact_context = false`, finite schema default.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior change: a turn that would previously dispatch with a flooded system prompt now fails with a clear, localized error. Operators see the remediation text instead of a silent confabulated reply.
- `turn/mod.rs`/`outcome.rs` touched — happy to add the ADR-016 exception row if required (per #11578/#11625 precedent).

prs.title: fix(mcp): replay a tool call rejected for a stale HTTP session
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A Streamable HTTP MCP server that has terminated a session (idle eviction, restart) must answer every request carrying that `Mcp-Session-Id` with HTTP 404, and the client must start a new session ([spec, Session Management](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#session-management)). The HTTP transport already maps this to `McpTransportError::StaleSession`, but the request stays marked outcome-unknown, so `dispatch_rpc` recovers the session in the background and fails the call with `outcome unknown and request was not replayed`.
  - The 404 is a definitive answer: the server rejected the request at session lookup and never executed it. This PR marks such a request as rejected-unexecuted (back to the pre-write phase, same epoch) before returning `StaleSession`, so the existing bounded pre-write path resets the transport, re-runs the handshake and replays the call on the new session.
  - In practice every first tool call after the server dropped the session failed. With a server that evicts idle sessions after 30 minutes, that is the first call of almost every conversation with a low-traffic agent.
  - This restores, for Streamable HTTP only, the replay that #7351 added (`call_tool_reconnects_on_stale_session`) and #9418 removed together with the other post-write replays. The test #9418 rewrote into no-replay is rewritten back.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the Streamable HTTP transport's 404/410-with-session branch. Timeouts, dropped streams and other post-write failures keep the no-replay rule from #9418. The legacy SSE transport is unchanged: its 404 stays outcome-unknown (`sse_post_404_is_not_replayed_to_derived_endpoint` untouched). A sessionless 404 is still a plain error (`call_tool_does_not_retry_sessionless_404` untouched).
- **Blast radius:** HTTP MCP servers only: a call that got a stale-session 404/410 is now replayed after the reconnect instead of failing. `MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` (2) bounds it: a server that keeps answering 404 after fresh handshakes gets three attempts in total, then the error surfaces (new test `call_tool_stale_session_replays_are_bounded`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9418, Related #7351

### What this does, simply

When an MCP server forgets a session, for example after the session sat idle for half an hour, it answers the next request with "404, no such session". ZeroClaw already understood that answer and reconnected, but it threw away the request that got the 404, so the user's tool call failed even though the server had done nothing with it. Now ZeroClaw reconnects and sends that same call again; if the server keeps rejecting it, ZeroClaw gives up after two retries. Calls whose fate really is unknown (a timeout, a connection that dropped mid-request) are still never repeated.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the wiremock tests reproduce the server's 404 deterministically; a manual run needs an MCP server with a short idle-session TTL.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `zeroclaw-tools` unit tests cover the transport phase change and the client replay path.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)
$ cargo test -q -p zeroclaw-tools --locked --lib mcp_
test result: ok. 245 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1120 filtered out; finished in 1.20s
$ cargo clippy -q -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
(no output)

# same tests with the mcp_transport.rs change reverted (master behaviour):
thread 'mcp_client::tests::call_tool_replays_once_after_stale_session' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/mcp_client.rs:3096:14
thread 'mcp_client::tests::call_tool_stale_session_replays_are_bounded' panicked at .../wiremock-0.6.5/src/mock_server/exposed_server.rs:367:17
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed
```

prs.title: fix(providers): retry Codex streams as streams on the default endpoint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - After a streaming decode failure, `send_responses_request` retried once with `stream: false` (#6668). The default ChatGPT Codex endpoint accepts only streaming requests and rejects that retry with `400 {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, so on the subscription route the recovery could never succeed. A truncated stream became a non-retryable "provider rejected the request" error.
  - On the default endpoint (`!custom_endpoint`), the one retry is now a streaming retry. Custom endpoints (`provider_api_url`) keep #6668's non-streaming recovery unchanged.
  - The final error and log attributes name the retry kind (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`).
- **Scope boundary:** one retry, as before. No change to which failures are retried: API error events and non-success HTTP statuses still are not retried. No config keys, no change to the request shape, `reliable.rs` classification, or other providers.
- **Known limit:** the retry kind follows `custom_endpoint`, which is derived from the configured URL. A custom `provider_api_url` that proxies the ChatGPT Codex backend still gets the non-streaming retry, as on master.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI Codex provider on the default endpoint (OAuth / ChatGPT subscription) when a stream fails to decode. Custom-endpoint deployments are unaffected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12072. Related #6668.

### What this does, simply

Sometimes the ChatGPT Codex backend ends a response stream before sending any output. ZeroClaw tried to recover by asking again without streaming, but that backend refuses non-streaming requests outright, so the recovery always failed and the user saw a misleading "request rejected" error. Now ZeroClaw asks again the way the backend accepts, once, and if that also fails the error says what actually happened.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: covered by deterministic mock-server tests. Live reproduction depends on the backend truncating a stream, which is intermittent.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `provider` = `openai-codex`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `Test` job runs the `zeroclaw-providers` lib tests, including the new and existing `openai_codex` retry tests; `cargo clippy` CI covers lint.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live ChatGPT Codex call.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# at eaec11f46, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, aarch64 Linux
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- openai_codex::
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_reports_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_retries_streaming_after_empty_stream ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_streaming_retry_http_error_is_not_retried_again ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_failed_http_status ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_stream_api_error_events ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_contains_malformed_frame_after_text ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_decode_fails ... ok
# test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1932 filtered out

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0, no diagnostics

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai_codex.rs
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check origin/master
# both exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - RED/GREEN: the test module from this branch was run against the production code of unpatched master `99bd353c7`. The three default-endpoint tests fail there with the exact production error, `OpenAI Codex API error (400 Bad Request): {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, because the stream-only mock rejects the `stream: false` retry the way the real backend does. All pass with the fix.
  - The default-endpoint tests give the mock provider an OAuth profile and `custom_endpoint = false`; their mock server rejects `stream: false` with that 400 without consuming a queued reply. The custom-endpoint path is pinned by the existing `codex_retries_non_streaming_*` tests and by `codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure` (passes before and after: behaviour preserved).
  - The fallback block is identical on master and on the build where the failure was observed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally (Raspberry Pi host); the change is confined to one function in `zeroclaw-providers`, covered by the focused run above and by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (same single retry, now with `stream: true` on the default endpoint)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Log text changed: the warning "retrying without streaming" is now "retrying once" with a `retry` attribute (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`), and the final error says "stream decode and retry both failed". Log matches on the old strings need updating.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

prs.title: fix(providers/openai-codex): do not retry the default endpoint without streaming
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** when a Codex responses stream fails to decode, the provider retried the same request with `stream = false`. The ChatGPT Codex backend requires streaming and rejects that body with `400 {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, so the retry cannot succeed there. Worse, the 400 replaces the original error: a transient, retryable decode failure is reported to the caller as a non-retryable provider error, and the reliability layer then refuses to retry it, ending the turn.
- The fallback is preserved for custom endpoints, which commonly accept both modes. It is skipped only for the default endpoint, keyed on the `custom_endpoint` flag the provider already computes from `is_default_responses_url`. The original decode error is surfaced instead, so the failure the caller sees is the failure that happened.
- **Scope boundary:** one branch in `chat()`'s decode-failure path. No change to request construction, streaming behavior, or the custom-endpoint fallback.
- **Blast radius:** `openai_codex` provider error handling.
- **Linked issue(s):** none filed; found in production, evidence below.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `provider`, `provider:openai`, `risk:low`, `size:XS`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `No` — the failure needs a real stream decode error against the live Codex endpoint, which is not reproducible on demand.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required gate builds and tests `zeroclaw-providers`, which owns the changed file.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real decode failure against the default endpoint; `mock_codex_provider` binds a local port and is therefore a custom endpoint by construction, so the mock-backed tests exercise the retained fallback rather than the skipped one. The added test pins the flag both paths branch on.

The symptom is absent and the change is deployed, but the skipped branch has not itself been observed firing in production.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The human-readable `gateway get-paircode` path printed a fetch failure then returned `Ok(())`, so the process exited 0.

- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11972. Related #11975.

### What this does, simply

If you ask the CLI for a pairing code and the gateway cannot be reached (or the admin token is missing), ZeroClaw already printed a clear error, but it still exited successfully. Scripts that check `$?` thought everything was fine. This change keeps the same message and exits with code 1 instead.

prs.title: fix(config): fall back when absolute shell canonicalize hits EPERM
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - On Android, `Path::canonicalize("/system/bin/sh")` fails with `PermissionDenied` (SELinux denies `open(O_PATH)` used by bionic `realpath`) while `execve` still works, so every native `shell` tool call fails since #10381.
  - When `canonicalize` fails that way for an **absolute** path, canonicalize the parent directory and join the file name; reject unresolved symlinks via `symlink_metadata`.
  - Relative / bare-name resolution and successful `canonicalize` paths are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change Android’s pinned shell constant, does not skip validation of relative or bare names, and does not change Docker path canonicalization.
- **Blast radius:** Only `zeroclaw-config` Unix executable resolution (`resolve_executable` / `validate_and_canonicalize`). Affects native runtime shell and any other absolute launcher resolved through this helper.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12075

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw’s native runtime on Android always uses `/system/bin/sh`. After a security fix that canonicalizes launchers before changing the workspace directory, that path can no longer be “canonicalized” on some Android SELinux policies, even though the shell can still be executed. This PR keeps the absolute, cwd-independent path requirement, but when the kernel refuses to open the file for realpath, it canonicalizes the parent directory (which works) and keeps the same file name—still absolute and still checked as a regular executable file.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — needs an Android/`untrusted_app` device where `canonicalize(/system/bin/sh)` returns EPERM; not available in CI.

### How I tested

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No physical Android EPERM reproduction in this environment.


- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Logic matches the issue’s Option 1 and the reported `realpath(/system/bin)` OK / `realpath(/system/bin/sh)` EPERM split. Did **not** run on a physical Android device.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed

### What this does, simply

The translated docs come from a separate repository. Before v0.8.7 shipped, every new or changed translation was read against its English page. The read found 125 strings that were wrong, used a different term from the rest of the page, or needed polish, mostly on pages new in v0.8.7. This PR points master at the corrected catalogues.

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for a gitlink-only change.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

prs.title: feat(web): add opt-in focused workspaces
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Keep Classic as the default browser layout: Dashboard, full navigation rail/mobile drawer, chat tabs, and SOP collection/view/editor routes.
  - Offer Focused explicitly during Quickstart and in Appearance, with Home, Agent, Code, SOP, and Admin workspaces. The browser preference is independent of themes and falls back to Classic when missing, invalid, or unreadable.
  - Keep conversations, approvals, configuration drafts, SOP drafts, and opened helpers mounted across navigation and layout changes. Both presentations use the existing runtime and configuration owners.
  - Add the authenticated, allowlisted Code WebSocket bridge, workspace availability, shared settings search/editor, and SOP source/helper/run tools. Integrate current master while retaining its principal isolation and history paging.
- **Scope boundary:** No plugin-aware settings redesign, per-widget customization, server layout configuration, or change to runtime authorization policy. Classic can still reach the new Code and Admin tools.
- **Blast radius:** Browser navigation and presentation; gateway Code bridge and generated API; ACP session summary and RPC activity reporting.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11546, #11547, #11548, #11549, #11550, #11551. These follow-up backend contracts remain outside this PR; it does not close them.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `web`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `topic:operator-ux`.

### What this does, simply

Existing installations open the familiar Dashboard and navigation. Operators who want the focused workspace experience can choose it in Appearance or during setup, and switch back at any time. Changing presentation keeps ongoing work alive. In Classic, a SOP's view shows the saved definition; Edit returns to its retained draft. Setup is still triggered by server-reported installation state, never by a missing browser preference.

Code connects to the daemon through a paired-token bridge restricted to code-session methods. Settings edits still use the existing schema, validation, drafts, and explicit save operations. Opening a SOP helper does not send a model prompt; applying its proposal changes the draft and saving remains explicit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; Code uses the daemon RPC transport and `zerocode_code` interaction surface.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A paired local daemon with an enabled agent; use synthetic data and a harmless tool approval. For deterministic browser tests, serve the built bundle (including its /_app/ asset prefix) and use the HTTP/WebSocket fixtures in `web/scripts/workspace-smoke.cjs` and `web/scripts/sop-workspace-smoke.cjs` with Playwright and Chrome available.
- **Steps to run:** Open the dashboard with no `zeroclaw-layout` preference. Inspect desktop navigation and the mobile drawer. Open Quickstart or Appearance, choose Focused, reload, and choose Classic again. Open a conversation and leave an unsent message or pending approval while switching layout. In SOPs, open a saved SOP, Edit, change a field, switch layouts and return; create and explicitly save a new SOP.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Classic initially; the explicit choice survives reload independently of color themes. The same conversation, pending approval, and unsaved SOP/helper draft remain available after switching. Existing configuration and SOP URLs work.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Classic navigation and SOP workflows are available, but there is no Focused choice, Code workspace, shared workspace settings search, or SOP coding helper.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local checks below; published-head CI must be evaluated separately.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Browser layout/continuity is checked by synthetic browser scripts, including actual rendering and interaction. No paid model or production external-service calls were used.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Final generated-theme synchronization: `cargo generate installers --check` passed; generator tests 5/5 and Zerocode theme tests 7/7 passed; formatting and diff checks passed. All 41 existing generated palettes and defaults are unchanged; Calm entries match the canonical registry. The following UI/runtime checks ran on the unchanged-source prior revision `f04318bdc922bdce6ece9b637bcad187690bb711`:  Fresh merged-source checks passed: `cargo web check`; `npm test` (including secret-map tests); `npm run test:permissions`; `npm run test:contexts`; `npm run build`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; relevant docs quality/link gates; both production browser smoke scripts. ACP session store: 85 passed. Gateway Code bridge: 5 passed. Fresh runtime executable: 22 targeted tests passed, covering scoped principals, history paging, projected counts, session state, final prompt authorization and bound-owner approvals. Master-relative diff check passed; source-relative whitespace findings are confined to unchanged upstream vendored crossterm documentation.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected actual Chrome screenshots for Classic desktop/mobile navigation, loaded SOP graph and fields, Focused workspace/mobile editor, and layout selectors. The scripts exercise storage fallback, first-run routing, setup/Appearance selection, reload/reversal, theme independence, chat/Code approval and socket continuity, SOP creation/view/edit, source validation, helper drafts, and run approvals. External provider execution and cross-process disconnect recovery are not claimed by these UI tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `a31c8ad8f8af42f9fbd5cdcbc5953f20d754dba9` only regenerates the Zerocode theme table from the unchanged canonical web registry. The browser/API/runtime checks below were run on `f04318bdc922bdce6ece9b637bcad187690bb711`; those sources and tracked screenshots are unchanged. Production browser suites include SOP rename continuity and grouped secret-map search focus.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Production-renderer captures of unchanged presentation, synthetic fixtures; pinned to this candidate.

![Default Classic dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/a31c8ad8f8af42f9fbd5cdcbc5953f20d754dba9/docs/book/src/developing/assets/workspace-classic.png)

![Appearance opts into Focused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/a31c8ad8f8af42f9fbd5cdcbc5953f20d754dba9/docs/book/src/developing/assets/workspace-layout-appearance.png)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Mode switches preserve socket counts, visible approval outcomes, unsent chat/helper text, and SOP drafts; Classic create/save returns to the saved view, while explicit Focused choice persists across reload.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace test/Clippy runs and credentialed live-model tests are not claimed; focused changed-boundary checks and fresh API generation cover this update locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** The new browser Code bridge exposes selected existing RPC code-session capabilities. It requires a paired token even when ordinary gateway pairing is disabled, rejects methods outside its allowlist, and leaves workspace resolution and tool approval policy to the runtime.
- New external network calls? **No** new third-party service is required; browser calls use the paired gateway and its local daemon RPC.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** The Code WebSocket validates the gateway bearer token before upgrading. Browser frames cannot select arbitrary local RPC endpoints or forward shell environment/configuration methods.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Added fixtures and screenshots use synthetic data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** The SOP helper can receive an explicitly submitted workflow definition; inserting context is visible and requires the operator to send it. Proposed source is validated into the draft, with a separate explicit save. Existing tool approval boundaries remain in force.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Browser access to code sessions is a trust boundary requiring security review; method/envelope/auth checks and real gateway bridge tests accompany it. Layout selection itself creates no runtime authority or configuration.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Classic remains the default, existing routes remain reachable, and both layouts share runtime state owners.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.** Layout is a browser preference only.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No** relative to current master.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Choose Classic in Appearance to stop using the Focused presentation. To remove the PR's backend/browser additions after merge, revert the merged PR commit and rebuild/redeploy the prior bundle and daemon together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Browser-only `zeroclaw-layout` (`classic` or `focused`); absent/invalid/unreadable values select Classic. This is not a runtime permission flag.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing navigation, lost composer/draft state, reopened chat/Code sockets during layout changes, inaccessible pending approvals, failed `/ws/code` authentication, or TypeScript/API mismatch. Existing session/configuration stores need no layout migration.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A; no PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): refresh the context budget after a trim
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The displayed context fill only moved on a usage sample. A history trim is emitted after that sample, and a terminal trim has no later sample in the same turn, so the bar kept the pre-trim count until the next turn.
  - Zerocode now adopts the trim's `tokens_after` and governing `token_budget` when a `history_trimmed` update arrives. A calibrated count renders with `~`, because it is not a provider measurement.
  - The web meter applies the same snapshot on the trim frame, and the gateway usage fold updates the displayed fill so the terminal `done` frame cannot restore the pre-trim count.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change trim selection, billing totals, or model-capacity resolution. Message-limit trims still leave the displayed snapshot alone because they carry no token accounting.
- **Blast radius:** Zerocode status bar, the web agent chat context meter, and the gateway websocket `done` frame's displayed fill (`last_input_tokens` / trim budget). Provider-measured billing totals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

The context bar shows how full the current session is. After older turns were trimmed, that bar kept showing the size from before the trim until the next model call reported new usage. This updates the bar from the trim event itself, using the post-trim count and the budget that governed the trim. A trim that only drops messages to satisfy a turn-count limit still leaves the bar alone, because that event has no token count to display.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui` (Zerocode status bar) and `surface=web` (agent chat context meter). The gateway websocket `done` frame is the web meter's terminal source.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A session whose history exceeds the configured context budget, so a turn emits `history_trimmed` with `tokens_after` and `token_budget`.
- **Steps to run:** Start a turn that trims history. Watch the context bar at the moment the trim notice appears, before the next model call.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The bar's used count drops to the trim's post-trim count, and the trim-budget marker follows the budget on the trim event. A calibrated count is marked approximate.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The bar keeps the pre-trim usage sample until a later turn's usage event arrives.

### How I tested

Focused tests cover the changed display boundary. Full workspace `cargo test` / `cargo clippy --all-targets` were not run locally; required CI on this head covers that broader surface.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Pending on this head. `CI` / `Lint` cover the Rust gateway and Zerocode changes; the web unit test is local evidence because it is outside that Rust job.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The web context-limits unit test is not part of the Rust CI job, so it was run locally. No screenshot of the live TUI or browser bar was captured.

```text
test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1542 filtered out
```

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make versioned, append-only session events the canonical conversation and execution history, so replay rebuilds state without repeating external effects.
  - Separate the kernel coordinator, storage implementations and host composition into explicit ownership boundaries. CLI, RPC, ACP, gateway and channel adapters use the same Session model and authorized history queries.
  - Capture provider attempts, reasoning and multimodal output, tool progress and outcomes, approvals, model/policy observations, context compression and linked child execution. Preserve provider item identities and supplemental fields without copying normalized bodies.
  - Provide SQLite and JSONL persistence, crash recovery, idempotent receipts, branches, search and auditable payload erasure. Interrupted external effects retain diagnostics and an unknown outcome when completion cannot be proved.
  - Upgrade legacy SQLite, JSONL and ACP history into the configured native format with resumable imports, writer fencing and renamed source backups. No per-session locator or independent ACP history database remains after upgrade.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not replace the file/blob, memory, cost, task or live-config authorities; their historical references remain session evidence. No additional at-rest encryption, dashboard redesign or complete runtime/plugin extraction.
- **Blast radius:** Session startup, persistence and recovery; provider and tool dispatch; approvals; child agents; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway history; session cleanup, alias lifecycle and existing storage configuration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### What this does, simply

A saved transcript currently cannot fully explain how a session reached its final answer. This change saves the observed execution as ordered events: what the user supplied, which model ran, what the model returned, which tools and approvals were involved, and what happened when execution failed or stopped. Conversation views and retained context are rebuilt from those facts.

All entrances use the same session storage. Existing histories are imported automatically and the original files become backups. Historical permissions explain past execution; they never grant permission to a resumed session. Unknown completion remains unknown, and reading or replaying history never reruns a tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, using a disposable configuration/data directory on each branch.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, plus the ACP protocol entrance and messaging-channel adapters covered by automated tests.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and tool policy in a disposable copy of an existing installation. Stop other processes using that directory. Use separate copies for `master` and this branch. Select `channels.session_backend` as `sqlite` or `jsonl` and repeat for both.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /var/tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange a message, request a harmless permitted tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Inspect the installation's `sessions` directory and the imported source backups. Repeat with a copy containing legacy ACP history, then open/resume it through ACP.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A native event history and installation manifest are created; user/provider/tool/approval observations and retained context survive reopening. Legacy sources are renamed after successful import. ACP uses the standard session store. An interrupted effect without a proven outcome is not silently rerun.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Mutable transcripts and separate persistence paths retain conversation messages but do not provide the common execution-event history or installation-wide migration described above.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None claimed before PR creation. Local checks below provide the current evidence; PR CI remains to run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace/all-features, cross-platform/MSRV builds, million-event performance and VM power-loss scenarios were not rerun in the final validation round. Summary/catalog queries still scan event history; this is not a constant-time performance claim.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies, `TMPDIR=/var/tmp`. Tested production source matches commit `61d3eb2d24`; the only subsequent test change replaced a prohibited error macro with an equivalent constructor and its regression was rerun.

```sh
cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# kernel:       137 passed; 0 failed
# providers:   2017 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
# session-host:  10 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# runtime:  5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
# channels: 2025 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
# gateway:   674 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib provider_content_metadata_survives_complete_and_interrupted_capture   -- --test-threads=4
# providers: 1 passed; 0 failed (SQLite/JSONL, complete/interrupted)

cargo +1.99.0 clippy --locked   -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-kernel   -p zeroclaw-session-host -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 58s

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

git diff --cached --check
# exit 0

DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md   bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Linting: 1 file(s); Summary: 0 error(s)

python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
# Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
```

Earlier validation of the session-unification stage also passed API 346, infra 357 and tools 1,368 library tests, plus three standalone ACP CLI component tests. The infra round skipped the expensive commit-byte-boundary test after its separate passing run; these earlier checks are not represented as a final full-workspace rerun. The final all-targets Clippy compiles the updated test and entrance call sites.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed migration publication and source-backup ordering, canonical field ownership, live read/effect authorization, partial/error/unknown distinctions and payload-reference reuse. Automated boundary tests exercise both stores, reopening, concurrent metadata observations, queued input recovery, owner isolation, reasoning access, erasure and child policy. No live-provider or production-data manual smoke is claimed. The staged secret scan flagged two synthetic redaction fixtures, including one moved existing fixture; both were inspected and contain no real credentials.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes execution and storage behavior, not interface layout or styling.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `61d3eb2d24`; library/integration boundaries and ACP wire tests listed above. Public storage and recovery contract: `docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for presentation; relevant automated output tails are included above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Complete and interrupted provider captures retain supplemental fields in both backends; queued inputs retain the admitted workspace; ACP wire resume uses the shared store; current authorization remains effective after reopening and policy changes.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The complete feature/platform/MSRV and VM power-loss matrices require separate environments and were not repeated in the final round. Focused checks and the ten-crate all-targets lint cover the implemented boundaries without claiming those matrices.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Introduces session command/query capabilities and native history files within the existing configured data directory. They default to current owner/policy checks; history and reasoning access are separately authorized, and stored policy evidence cannot mint live grants.
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing provider, tool and delivery transports remain the effect owners.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** No history-content credential filtering or new encryption system is added in this PR. Ordinary messages, reasoning, media, and execution history remain plaintext under the existing local authorization model. Existing configuration credentials retain their current handling.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use synthetic values; private audit documents and local reports are excluded.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Context is restored from event-backed projections. Provider metadata and unknown fields remain classified evidence, cannot confer authority, and are not blindly injected into model-visible text; replay does not execute external effects.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): add /load-session to resume a saved session by name or id
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds a ZeroCode-local `/load-session [name|id]` slash command to the Code (ACP) and Chat panes. Before this, the only way to resume an earlier session inside ZeroCode was scrolling the `Ctrl+S` list, and a session id copied from logs or another terminal couldn't be pasted.
  - A new pure resolver (`apps/zerocode/src/chat/session_lookup.rs`) checks tiers in order: exact session id → exact name → name ignoring case (Unicode lowercase) → id prefix ignoring case. The first tier with any hit wins. One hit loads the session through the existing `switch_to_session_entry` path. Several hits open the session picker filtered to those sessions. With no argument, the command opens the same picker as `Ctrl+S`.
  - When nothing matches, the session list can't be fetched, or the target is already focused, the command shows a localized notice. It never sends `session/new` for an unmatched query and never closes the previously focused session, which stays live in the background, as with `Ctrl+S`.
  - Refactor with no behavior change: `Ctrl+S` and `/load-session` now share one source for "which sessions this pane may load" (`Chat::list_pane_sessions`) and one picker opener. Commands whose completion fills `"<cmd> "` instead of submitting (`/model`, `/model-provider`, `/load-session`) now go through a single `command_takes_argument` helper instead of two duplicated string checks.
  - Adds four English-only Fluent keys (other locales follow the `cargo fluent` workflow), a help line in both panes, and a paragraph in `docs/book/src/zerocode/running.md`.
- **Scope boundary:** No daemon or RPC changes. Each pane searches only its own store: `session/list-acp` for Code, and `session/list` with channel-backed sessions excluded for Chat. There's no cross-store loading. Not included: session naming or renaming (#10285), argument tab-completion, fuzzy or substring matching, and a `--session` startup flag. Owner visibility filtering stays with the daemon.
- **Blast radius:** Limited to `apps/zerocode`:
  - The `Ctrl+S` picker now lists sessions through the extracted helper (same RPCs, same empty picker on error, same first-row selection).
  - `/model` and `/model-provider` completion now go through the shared helper (unchanged behavior; existing tests cover it).
  - The pane help gains one line.
  - Slash-command completion gains `/load-session`, so `/lo…` now has a candidate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12069. Related #10285 (Code-pane name lookup starts working once ACP sessions carry names; id and id-prefix lookup work today).

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode can keep many saved sessions, but until now getting back to a specific one meant opening the session list with Ctrl+S and scrolling to it. This PR adds a typed shortcut: `/load-session` followed by the session's id, the start of its id, or its name jumps straight to that session. If the text matches more than one session, you get the usual list showing only those. If it matches nothing, you get a short message and nothing else changes. Typing `/load-session` on its own simply opens the list. The command only looks at sessions belonging to the pane you're in, so Chat sessions and Code sessions stay separate, as they already are in the Ctrl+S list. Code sessions can't be named yet (that's #10285), so in the Code pane you load sessions by id for now.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui` (ZeroCode Code and Chat panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A running local daemon with at least two saved Code sessions for an agent, and a Chat session with a name (for example, one renamed through the web dashboard). Note one Code session's id from the `Ctrl+S` list.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In a Code pane, type `/load-session <full id>` and press Enter.
  2. Type `/load-session <first 6 characters of another id>` and press Enter.
  3. Type `/load-session nope` and press Enter.
  4. Type `/load-session` on its own and press Enter.
  5. In a Chat pane, type `/load-session <session name in a different case>` and press Enter.
  6. Open help (`/help`).
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Steps 1 and 2 load the session with its transcript, and the previous session stays in the sidebar.
  - Step 3 shows `No saved session matches "nope".` and nothing changes.
  - Step 4 opens the same list as `Ctrl+S`.
  - Step 5 loads the named Chat session.
  - Step 6 lists `/load-session [name|id] — resume a saved session`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `/load-session …` isn't a command, so it's sent to the agent as an ordinary prompt. The only way to resume is the `Ctrl+S` list.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required Rust lint, test and docs jobs cover `apps/zerocode` and `docs/book`. Locally, I ran the `zerocode` package's tests and clippy plus the docs gates (below). The change is confined to that package and one docs page.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known. I ran clippy locally only for `-p zerocode`, not workspace-wide. CI's `--all-targets` run covers the rest, and nothing outside `apps/zerocode` changed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run at `f72bf4a593`, which has the same code as head; `b2968024f7` changes docs only.

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(exit 0, no output)

$ cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Checking zerocode v0.8.7 (apps/zerocode)
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4.10s

$ cargo test -p zerocode
test result: ok. 52 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 1574 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
(plus single-test subprocess binaries, all ok)

$ cargo fluent check --catalog zerocode
ok  apps/zerocode/locales/{en,es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/zerocode.ftl

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
Linting docs files: docs/book/src/zerocode/running.md
Summary: 0 error(s)

$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

  New tests:
  - **`session_lookup` (12):** each tier, tier precedence (including a name beating a hex-looking id prefix), ambiguity within a tier, empty list or query, and unnamed sessions.
  - **`input_bar`:** parsing with no argument, whitespace only, a single token, and a query with internal spaces. Completion fills `"/load-session "`, a second Enter opens the picker, and there's no argument completion.
  - **`chat`:**
    - The store is chosen per pane, and channel sessions are hidden in Chat.
    - The listing error comes through to the user.
    - Attach by id (Code) and by name (Chat).
    - A background session is focused without a second `session/new`.
    - The already-focused notice is shown with no RPC beyond the listing.
    - An ambiguous query gives a filtered picker.
    - The not-found and listing-error notices are shown.
    - The per-pane cap is enforced.
    - A key-dispatch test sends Enter through `Chat::handle_key` while a turn is running, confirming the command runs immediately like `Ctrl+S`.

  Failure-path tests check that no `session/new` is sent. All `/load-session` tests hold the env lock and use a temporary `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing beyond the automated tests. I haven't yet run the A/B steps above against a live daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot` is required: the change adds a help-overlay line and info-bar notices in the TUI. It isn't attached yet.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Automated tests at `f72bf4a593` (same code as head). TUI screenshots still to come.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Not attached yet.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the expected results above. Automated tests assert each notice's exact localized text and the picker's contents and selection.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I ran clippy only on the changed package instead of workspace-wide. CI covers the workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`. The command uses the existing `session/list`, `session/list-acp` and `session/new` daemon RPCs.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`. Fixtures use placeholder ids such as `sess-target`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`. The query is matched on the client and never reaches the model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The command can only load sessions the daemon already returns to this client through its existing owner-visibility filtering. Authorization for `session/new` and attach is unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`. This adds a TUI slash command, with no config, env, or CLI flags.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-to-medium risk and client-only. Rollback is `git revert` of the squash commit.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `/load-session` loads the wrong session.
  - The `Ctrl+S` list is empty when sessions exist. That would point to a regression in the shared `list_pane_sessions` helper.
  - `/model` completion submits instead of filling.

prs.title: fix(security): stop treating a bare semicolon or pipe as command injection
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** The prompt guard's command-injection rule treated any bare `;` or `|` as a shell construct, so ordinary sentences, tables, signatures and tool output came back `Suspicious`, or `Blocked` under a block threshold below 0.6. This drops the two single-character tokens, and with them the `| head` / `| tail` / `| grep` exemption that only existed for `|`. The multi-character constructs stay: backtick, `$(`, `&&` (with its short-text exemption), `||`, `>/dev/` and `2>&1`. On the public sets in #12066, this removes every false flag in the clean emails (57 of 78 to 0) and clean tool results (162 of 1,054 to 0), with no lost detection.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Only `check_command_injection` changes. The other five categories, the scores, and the block comparison stay as they are.
  - The meaning of the guard's sensitivity setting is a separate issue (#12067) and isn't touched here.
- **Blast radius:** `PromptGuard::scan`, whose only production caller is the untrusted SOP trigger screening in `ContentSafety::screen_event`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12066. Related #12067.

### What this does, simply

Before an outside message can start an automated procedure, a safety check looks for signs of an attack. One of its rules treated every semicolon and every `|` character as a sign of a hidden shell command, so most normal emails and tables looked suspicious. The rule now looks only for the shell patterns that ordinary text doesn't use.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** No. The new unit tests cover both directions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` for `zeroclaw-runtime`, which holds the guard and its only caller, and clippy.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::
test result: ok. 380 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5493 filtered out; finished in 1.08s
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 48s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `prose_punctuation_is_not_command_injection`: a sentence with a semicolon, a pipe table and a pipe-separated signature all stay `Safe` under `Block` at 0.1.
  - `shell_constructs_still_flag_command_injection`: `$(…)`, `2>&1`, `>/dev/tcp/…` and a backtick each still flag, with exactly one pattern.
  - The measurement in #12066 uses the public BIPIA and InjecAgent sets only.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The test strings are made up and use `example.com` and a documentation IP range.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, the screening of untrusted SOP input gets narrower. The two dropped tokens caught none of the attack samples measured in #12066, and every construct that did catch one is kept. Shell safety for tool arguments stays with the shell tool's command policy, which this guard doesn't replace.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Content with a bare `;` or `|` and no other match is now `Safe` instead of `Suspicious` or `Blocked`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. `[sop] untrusted_input_guard = "warn"` (the default) only logs.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a shell-shaped payload that relied on `;` or `|` alone is no longer logged as `command_separator` or `pipe_operator`.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep allowlisted Discord bots from answering approvals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A plaintext Discord approval reply (`<token> yes|no|always`) whose author is a bot is now `Rejected` even when that bot is allowlisted. `listen_to_bots` plus `external_peers` exist so the agent can converse with another bot; they shouldn't also make that bot an approver of the agent's tool calls.
  - The gateway now computes the payload author's `bot` flag once (the value the `listen_to_bots` gate already read) and passes it to `resolve_approval_reply`, which treats a bot responder as not allowed. Rejection reuses the existing `Rejected` path from #9574: the pending approval is kept and the message is not forwarded to the agent.
  - Component (button) approvals are unchanged; only a human can click a Discord component.
- **Scope boundary:** Discord plaintext approvals only. No config keys, no change to `listen_to_bots`, message admission, peer resolution, destination binding, component approvals or other channels. Slack's `allow_bots` text-approval path looks similar and is left for a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** Discord deployments with `listen_to_bots = true` where a bot is allowlisted and answered approval prompts in text. Human responders are unaffected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12064. Related #9574.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can ask in Discord for permission before running a sensitive tool, and someone replies with the approval token to allow or deny it. Since #9574 that someone must be on the allowlist and reply in the same channel. When two agents share a channel (`listen_to_bots = true`), the operator allowlists the other bot so the agents can talk. Until now that also let the other bot answer approval prompts, so one agent's model output could approve the other agent's tool calls. After this change only humans can approve; a bot's approval reply is refused, and the prompt stays open for a human.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the change is covered by deterministic unit tests at the resolver and a source-scan test for the gateway wiring; a live repro needs two Discord bot accounts.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `Test` job (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace`) builds `zeroclaw-channels` with default features, which include `channel-discord`, and runs both tests below; `cargo clippy` CI covers lint.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live Discord gateway run.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# at bd646bac4, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, aarch64 Linux
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord:: approval
# test result: ok. 369 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1649 filtered out; finished in 3.13s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- plaintext_approval_requires_authorized_responder_and_destination gateway_plaintext_approval_passes_payload_bot_flag
# test discord::tests::plaintext_approval_requires_authorized_responder_and_destination ... ok
# test discord::tests::gateway_plaintext_approval_passes_payload_bot_flag ... ok
# test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0, no diagnostics

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check origin/master
# both exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A/B on unpatched master 99bd353c7: a throwaway test (not committed) with an allowlisted `peer-bot`, `listen_to_bots = true` and a pending approval for `c1` got `Resolved` from `resolve_approval_reply("tok123 yes", "peer-bot", "c1")`, and the receiver got `Approve`. On this branch the same reply with `responder_is_bot = true` returns `Rejected` and the pending approval remains, while the allowlisted human still resolves it. Not verified: a live Discord gateway with two bot accounts.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally (Raspberry Pi host); the changed surface is one function in `zeroclaw-channels`, covered by the focused runs above and by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (narrows who can resolve approvals)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change removes a path where another agent's model output could act as the human approval for this agent's tool calls.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No, intentionally: an allowlisted bot can no longer resolve Discord approvals by text.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No`: a setup that relied on a bot relaying approvals must have a human answer the prompt (text or buttons) instead.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data or config migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A human allowlisted responder cannot resolve a Discord text approval in the prompt's channel (the pending approval times out instead).

### What this does, simply

This proposal establishes typed rules and storage contracts for a future Goal feature. It gives the runtime a common representation for task ownership, session identity, budgets, and guarded lifecycle transitions, without claiming that a user can run a Goal through a production transport today.

Budget admission distinguishes absent values from explicit zero. For a start without command budget flags, at least one positive configured default is a budget; two explicitly configured zeros select unlimited operation. One zero plus one unset value, or both unset, is unconfigured and returns the typed `GoalResponse::BudgetRequired` response before task creation. That response is a non-admission outcome, not a config-validation error. Invalid current Goal configuration is validated first and keeps its error precedence. Explicit command budgets remain independent of absent defaults.

Dashboard/gateway PATCH, per-field PUT/DELETE and section initialization now reject a save that leaves the edited Goal inputs invalid, before disk or live-config publication. Enabling Goal without a valid verifier is rejected; selecting a valid verifier and enabling Goal in the same save works. An unrelated save can still preserve an existing Goal error with a warning. Edits to Goal settings or, while enabled, to the verifier's provider profile must leave Goal valid; those profile edits are not unrelated saves. Disabling Goal clears the enabled-verifier requirement, not other numeric/model validation. An existing Goal error no longer hides an invalid unrelated edit; an edit touching Goal inputs may still report the Goal error first. This repair changes save behavior and whole-config first-error ordering, not the wire schema or error codes; it adds `Config::goal_validation_input_paths` for shared validation-input ownership.

The follow-up also closes two edge cases: trusted ingress rejects malformed session keys even when a caller constructs the public key variant directly, while preserving canonical IDs; and status lookup rechecks the task after reading its Goal details, returning the existing stale response if its ID, status or execution epoch changed. It does not make the two reads atomic or enable a production Goal transport.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes — typed capability contracts, not new grants.** Principal/session binding and current-config checks apply here; durable storage transitions use epoch guards. Task/epoch/command validation at launch/acquisition remains the later executor's obligation, not a production guarantee of this prefix. No production adapter or broader permission is enabled.
- New external network calls? **No.** No production client or provider route is added. The webhook change is test-fixture-only.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** Credential storage, transport, and configuration are unchanged.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use neutral values.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes — typed Goal inputs remain untrusted data.** Objective/history text is not an authorization fact; this slice does not assemble a new production model prompt or add an egress path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Future adapters must keep user-controlled Goal text separate from trusted principal/session facts. This slice's typed boundary makes that distinction explicit but does not enable a live adapter.
- The follow-up adds no permission, external call, credential handling or data field: it rejects noncanonical direct session-key variants at the existing trusted-ingress boundary and uses the existing stale response when the current task changed during status lookup.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for Rust consumers of the changed public interfaces**, including removed-method callers, custom trait implementers, struct literals and exhaustive matches. Relative to integrated `master`, `TaskKind::Goal` already existed in the runtime registry; `TaskKind`, `TaskStatus`, and `TaskRecord` move to canonical `zeroclaw-api` definitions and remain re-exported at the existing runtime paths. `TaskRecord` adds `session_id: Option<String>` and `execution_epoch: i64` (Serde defaults `None` and `0`), so Rust struct literals must supply them; ordinary task records use those default values, while Goal creation goes through the guarded registry.
  The existing public `GoalTaskRegistry` and `GoalTaskRecord` move to `zeroclaw-goal::task`, retaining runtime re-exports but not full source compatibility. Removed trait methods are `create_goal`, `update_goal_objective`, `pause_goal_task` and `resume_goal_task`. Implementers must provide ten new required methods: `current_goal_for_session`, `terminal_reason_for_session_goal`, `create_or_replace_session_goal`, `pause_session_goal`, `resume_session_goal`, `finish_session_goal`, `admit_pending_operation`, `settle_pending_operation`, `update_session_goal_limits` and `delete_session_goal`. Session mutations require exact task/session/epoch predicates; handle `GoalTransitionResult::Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing` explicitly and reload authoritative state before deciding what to do after stale/missing outcomes. Objectives are immutable rather than updated in place.
  `GoalTaskRecord` adds public `pending_call_id: Option<String>`, `pending_call_epoch: Option<i64>` and `accounting_state: GoalAccountingState` fields; update literals or use its default. Serde defaults retain old-record readability; they do not preserve Rust literal compatibility. `GoalAccountingState` and `GoalTransitionResult` are new public types. Generic `TaskRegistry::create` rejects `TaskKind::Goal`, and generic mutators reject session-bound Goals: migrate those callers to the controller or guarded session-Goal registry APIs instead of bypassing lifecycle guards.
  Relative to earlier published proposal revisions, `GoalResponse` gains `BudgetRequired`, which may require downstream exhaustive matches to be updated, and `GoalHostSettings::from_config(&Config, owner_pid, owner_boot_id) -> Result<_>` replaces the earlier `new`/`PartialEq` settings API. Construct fresh settings from the current canonical config per operation. These host-settings/response APIs, unlike the existing Goal store interfaces above, are new relative to integrated `master`. The `zeroclaw-goal` crate now reports version 0.8.7 with the workspace; upstream's own compatibility changes follow upstream release notes.
  Compared with integrated `master`, `Config` gains a public `goal` field: Rust struct-literal consumers must provide it or use `Config::default()` and modify needed fields. The unused public command variants `BuiltinCommandId::Goal` and `CommandExecution::GoalAdmission` are removed; Rust callers must remove those matches or use the transport-neutral parser/controller contracts. No working Goal command handler or native transport is removed. The config-save repair itself adds the public `Config::goal_validation_input_paths` method without changing the wire schema or error codes.
  These two follow-up commits add no public enum variant, trait method, field, signature, serialized field, schema migration, or durable-ID format. They intentionally correct edge behavior: trusted ingress now rejects noncanonical session-key values even when callers construct the public enum variants directly, and status lookup returns the existing typed stale result if the task ID, status or execution epoch changed during the read. Valid canonical keys retain their exact prior values and durable IDs. This does not promise an atomic snapshot across task and Goal storage.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes — new Goal contracts/configuration compared with integrated `master`; no user-facing Goal command is wired.** Relative to earlier proposal revisions, missing budget defaults no longer count as unlimited consent: both defaults explicitly zero select unlimited, while absent defaults or one zero paired with an unset dimension produce `BudgetRequired`. Explicit command limits remain separately supported. No new environment key or runnable user command syntax is enabled by this slice. The removed channel-only `/goal` catalogue entry was present but unwired on integrated `master`; no production channel renderer consumed it and no Fluent key existed. Rendered help is unchanged; the public catalogue/API removals are the source-compatibility changes described above.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No declared floor change.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: The inherited task-store migration advances control-plane schema version 10 to 13 when the store is opened; it is not a manual migration requested here, and no live migration/deployment was performed. Keep a recoverable store backup. Rust consumers should update struct literals and exhaustive matches as above, use `GoalHostSettings::from_config` with the current config for each operation, and retain existing runtime type re-export paths or import the canonical API types. No automatic database downgrade is claimed; review data compatibility before reverting to an older binary.

**Legacy Goal data on upgrade:** On first store open, running or paused Goals created through the old session-less API are retained but marked failed, normally with `legacy_goal_missing_session` (an existing error is preserved), and receive a completion timestamp. They cannot be resumed as sessionless Goals; review the retained objective/state and recreate them as session-bound Goals through guarded admission. The same reconciliation fails active rows with a missing objective (`legacy_goal_missing_objective`); malformed legacy execution epochs have a separate `goal_invalid_execution_epoch` safety path. Completed Goal statuses and non-Goal data are preserved by this reconciliation. Old-record deserialization does not imply active-Goal resumability. Back up the store before opening it with the new version.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** To revert only this follow-up in a separately reviewed rollback change, first revert `afadb4058eb1c7395e63046c8bfa19b2e04f3e69`, which only adds the async test-fixture lifetime annotation; then revert `c716dd73af99c9565ae065c2323767d5001fefcd`, which contains the behavior change and regression tests. Reverting `c716dd73af99c9565ae065c2323767d5001fefcd` restores the prior invalid-direct-key admission and unfenced status-projection behavior. These commits add no persistent data or schema change. To undo only the config-save repair in a rollback PR, `git revert fa7136de529eb55076e04c162c43b1bb4b6ddc1b` restores the former save-with-warning behavior, including its defect; that is a separate reviewed decision. Before merging to master, undo the upstream integration with `git revert -m 1 d8f7fd7eea1b46e76e8f51ee7653fcdc596e7f11` through the same gates; later re-integration requires reverting that revert. To revert the entire slice, use `git revert <PR squash commit>` after reverting dependent Goal slices in reverse dependency order. Preserve the task database and usage ledger; do not delete them. This is not an automatic schema downgrade. Reverting the whole stack prefix or running an older binary against migrated data requires a separate reviewed data-compatibility decision. No live rollback was performed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[goal].enabled` remains default-off. Do not enable it as a completed user-facing feature before production adapter, execution, accounting, and placement gates are met.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** After this follow-up, a malformed direct session-key variant is rejected at trusted ingress, and a status request whose task changed during the read returns the existing stale response. Those are intentional outcomes, not new error codes or evidence of a production transport rollout. Configuration admission errors include `Goal configuration does not admit execution`; a legacy active Goal may instead be retained as failed with `legacy_goal_missing_session` or `legacy_goal_missing_objective` after upgrade. Opening newer-schema data emits `control-plane DB was created by a newer schema version` with `db_version` and `known_version`; that warning is not a safe-downgrade guarantee. Inspect the durable task/session/epoch state for persistence/recovery errors. No live deployment or rollback was exercised.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — this PR does not claim to supersede another PR.
