prs.title: chore(docs): pin translations to v0.8.7
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (the v0.8.7 release candidate, `5d4b18d335`)
- **What changed and why:** This moves the `docs/book/po` gitlink from `7b8879371c` (the v0.8.6 catalogues) to `152d650552`, the v0.8.7 catalogues in `zeroclaw-docs-translations` (tag `v0.8.7`). That is five commits on the v0.8.6 pin: `2aabad2919` refreshes the catalogues, `05acf49bd5` replaces the fill errors found in review, `8a4c39fe49` removes a space the French catalogue had put before the colon in the custom provider's `Authorization` header example, `3d9951b8da` translates strings that still opened in English (such as "MQTT connections utilisent…") and replaces "redact" rendered as drafting or editing (such as Spanish "redactado"), and `152d650552` applies the corrections from an independent second read of those changes, including table cells and headings that had broken across two lines and crate names that had been translated. The v0.8.7 docs build from the tagged commit's pin, so this pin is what brings the French, Japanese, Spanish and Simplified Chinese docs up to v0.8.7.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the gitlink changes. No source, docs text or workflow changes.
- **Blast radius:** The translated docs site, for the release and for master.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

The translated docs come from a separate repository. This PR points ZeroClaw at the catalogues refreshed for v0.8.7, so the docs in other languages aren't stale.

**New strings:** each language gains 192 new strings and drops 46 that no longer exist. Most of the new ones come from:
- the plugin release acceptance runbook (78);
- the Discord channel page (44);
- the sandboxing page (17).

**Code samples fixed:** the catalogue commit also repairs code samples that earlier translation runs had broken. String literals inside code blocks had been translated or had lost their quotes, so the translated pages showed invalid examples. For example, the logging page's JSON showed `"severity_text": INFO,`. Those literals now read exactly as in English:
- fr 314, ja 346, es 222, zh-CN 237 entries;
- only msgstr lines change;
- comments and prose in code blocks stay translated.

**Fill errors replaced:** the fill was checked for refusals, leaked notes and half translations, and every confirmed entry was rewritten one at a time and checked against its msgid, not refilled with the tool. That is 858 entries: fr 187, ja 286, es 203, zh-CN 182. Of these, 66 are new strings from this release and 792 were inherited from earlier fills. They include:
- model replies in place of a translation ("I can't post to the tracking issue…", "Please paste the English text…");
- translator notes left in the text ("Wait, I should translate…", "Translation:");
- half-translated strings ("The jeton…", "A recarga…");
- text in the wrong script (Devanagari inside Spanish, a Korean paragraph in the Japanese catalogue, mojibake);
- dropped text;
- record names, error messages and config values inside code spans that had been translated, such as `channel inbound message`;
- code samples broken by translation: YAML keys and shell words translated inside samples (a docker-compose sample read `サービス:` / `画像:`), single-quoted shell arguments and grep patterns changed, and code blocks that had lost their fences. These now read exactly as in English.

Only msgstr lines change.

**Config reference defaults:** the six default paths in the generated config reference now match what the docs build generates, so those rows no longer fall back to English.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. This only moves a gitlink; Validate Translations Pin checks the pinned catalogues.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Validate Translations Pin checks three things: the pinned commit has catalogues, each one passes `msgfmt --check-format`, and all catalogues carry the same msgids.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At the release candidate `5d4b18d335` with these catalogues, on macOS:

  ```text
  $ cargo mdbook check
  All .po files OK.
  ```

  The same check fails, as expected, when a local file path is planted in one French string.

  On Linux, at the same release candidate with the catalogues at `8a4c39fe49`. `3d9951b8da` and `152d650552` change msgstr text only, so the msgids this checks are unchanged:

  ```text
  $ cargo mdbook sync
  ==> fr: up to date, skipping AI step
  ==> ja: up to date, skipping AI step
  ==> es: up to date, skipping AI step
  ==> zh-CN: up to date, skipping AI step
  ```

  I also ran the Validate Translations Pin steps locally on the same catalogues: `msgfmt --check-format` passed, and msgid parity held across catalogues (21222 msgids). A check for the fill-error classes above reports 0 entries in every catalogue; 18 entries it flags were reviewed and are correct (translations, or crate names kept as identifiers). A second check, for strings that open in English, "redact" rendered as drafting or editing, and stray or garbled characters, reports 0 entries apart from 96 reviewed ones that are correct as they are (product names, UI labels, identifiers such as crate names, glossary terms). Code-sample literals (double- and single-quoted strings, code tokens, fenced blocks) report 0 broken.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for a gitlink-only change.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `152d650552` is signed, tagged `v0.8.7` in `zeroclaw-docs-translations`, and is five signed commits on top of the v0.8.6 catalogues.
  - An entry-level comparison against `2aabad2919` shows that only msgstr text changed (21222 entries per locale) and that no entry was emptied.
  - A check of every code-sample literal finds 0 broken entries in each locale.
  - The logging page's JSON example now reads exactly as in English in all four languages.
  - Not verified here: a full build of the translated site. The docs deploy builds it after merge.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. Catalogue text only; no layout or styling change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `5d4b18d335` with the catalogues at `152d650552`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo mdbook sync` was not repeated on `152d650552`: its msgids are identical to `8a4c39fe49`, where it reported every locale up to date.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: reverting this commit puts the pin back on the v0.8.6 catalogues.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded agent owned-state retirement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the agent owned-state retirement and knowledge-graph scoping in #9745 (which fixes #9647). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #9745 (`src/agent_owned_state.rs:741-745`, 2026-10-25), which found that the knowledge export-and-purge flow has no covering exception.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #9745 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `123b8396f3`, eighteen files: `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local,types,wss}.rs`, `src/tools/{mod,delegate}.rs`, `src/control_plane/task_store_sqlite.rs`, `src/i18n.rs`, `locales/en/{cli,tools}.ftl` and `locales/{es,fr,ja,zh-CN}/cli.ftl`. Most of it is continued work on a subsystem the crate already holds. On `master`, `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` carries `live_acp_session_count`, `archive_agent_workspace`, `OwnedStateReport`, `cascade_owned_state`, `RenameStateReport` and `cascade_rename_agent`, and the gateway reaches them through a three-line `pub use` shim; #9745 moves them into the new `src/agent_owned_state.rs`, re-exports the four functions from `agent_lifecycle` for compatibility, deletes the gateway shim, and extends them. The additions the row names are: the `PathPresence` classifier `inspect_lifecycle_path`, which re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe so an uninspectable path is residue on Windows as on Unix; the committed delete and rename residue contracts `committed_delete_residue_exists` and `committed_rename_residue_exists`, which probe the workspace, cron, control-plane (through the new read-only `SqliteTaskStore::count_existing_by_agent`), ACP, memory, knowledge and session stores; the shared resolvers that both contracts and both cascades use to reopen the configured memory or session backend when the live handle is absent, or for memory is the `none` placeholder, while config still expects persistence, so a delete or rename cleans or re-points that store instead of skipping it (on `master` the RPC delete substituted `NoneMemory` and warned, and the cascades returned zero for an absent backend); `AgentDeletionArchive`, which replaces `WorkspaceArchiveReport`, with an exclusively created leaf, `create_new` artifact writes and directory syncs up to the data directory, so a successful export gates the memory, knowledge, cron and ACP purges and a failure is reported in `warnings`; `prepare_knowledge_retirement` and `cascade_owned_state_with_retirement`, which export the agent's knowledge rows before the config commit, archive them as `knowledge.json` and purge through `KnowledgeGraph::purge_archived_owner` only while the store still matches the archived snapshot, plus the knowledge rename follower and the knowledge counts on both reports and the manifest; `plan_agent_delete_recovery_with_acp_count`, the recovery-mode preflight for a committed delete; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `run_agent_delete` behind `agents/delete` and `config/map-key-delete` (alias-grammar validation before any probe, so a reserved or malformed alias is now an `INVALID_PARAMS` error on `agents/delete` where `master` returned a `deleted: false` result; config-write authority for `agents.<alias>`, which `agents/delete` did not require before, and for every scrubbed path rechecked inside the commit, which neither method required before; a committed-delete retry that resumes the cascade without a config publication; and, on the map-key adapter only, refusing an agent with active RPC sessions as rename already does and answering `deleted: false` rather than an error for an unblocked alias with neither a config entry nor residue), the rename adapter validating both aliases and probing the old workspace through the classifier, `alias_create_refusal_message` for `config/set`, `config/set-many` and `config/map-key-create` when the alias they would create still owns knowledge or its store cannot be inspected, and the optional `owned_state` field on `ConfigMapKeyDeleteResult`; in `src/tools/mod.rs`, `knowledge_scope_for_agent` and the knowledge tool registration that binds a `KnowledgeScope` from the trusted agent alias, resolved per graph operation through the existing read-only live config handle (it registers no live-config consumer and acknowledges nothing) or from the configured `read_knowledge_from`, assigns unattributed legacy rows to `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` or the sole enabled agent, and withholds the tool when ownership is ambiguous; in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `knowledge_tool_for_target`, rebinding the knowledge tool to the delegation target as the memory tools already are; the seven Fluent keys (five in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, two in `locales/en/tools.ftl`), of which `cli-alias-create-knowledge-{retained,uninspectable}` and `delegate-knowledge-init-failed` are translated in `es`, `fr`, `ja` and `zh-CN` with every-locale tests in `src/i18n.rs`; and the tests, including the test-only `pause_knowledge_archive_under` and negative-probe hooks and the `memory` parameter on the test-only `RpcContext::for_persistence_tests` with its call sites in `src/rpc/{dispatch,local,wss}.rs`. The row leaves out, as an implementation detail, the boxed `handle_config_map_key_delete` future that keeps `process_line` inside its stack budget. Everything else #9745 does lives in its owning crate and needs no runtime permission: `KnowledgeScope`, grant resolution, legacy assignment, `export_existing_owner`, the generation-checked `purge_archived_owner` and `rename_owner` in `zeroclaw-memory`; the scoped `KnowledgeTool` and the `model_routing_config` retirement check in `zeroclaw-tools`; the alias admission rule (`create_map_key_checked`, `ensure_knowledge_owner_retired`, `Config::ensure_map_key_for_path`) and the `read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` settings in `zeroclaw-config`; the HTTP adapters in `zeroclaw-gateway`; and the CLI paths in the `zeroclaw` binary. The row excludes per-principal ownership, the unwired Postgres graph (`knowledge_graph_pg.rs` is untouched), any new RPC method (the `Method` enum gains no variant), grant source, config key, store or persisted schema in the runtime (the existing archive bundle gains the `knowledge.json` artifact and its manifest counts), the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` (which still removes an agent without the cascade), the environment-override creation path (applied at config load without the retirement check), and any non-English locale beyond the three keys named. The `remove_agent` and environment-override items are pre-existing gaps #9745's body lists as out of scope. The row also says that it does not ratify the cascade's own landing in the crate (see below).
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9647 and #9745 (head `123b8396f3`). Precedent: #11701, #11963, #12058 and #12062, the four row proposals open at the same table position.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #9745 gives every knowledge-graph row an owning agent and makes an agent's delete and rename carry that ownership with the alias: deletion exports the agent's knowledge, archives it next to the memory, cron and ACP exports the cascade already wrote, and purges it only when the archive is durable and still matches the store; rename moves ownership to the new alias; a committed delete or rename whose cleanup failed, or whose stores cannot be inspected, stays retryable on the RPC and gateway surfaces instead of reading as finished (the CLI's committed-rename retry is #10373); and no explicit config write can recreate an alias while its knowledge remains (an environment override that names a new agent is still applied at load, a pre-existing gap #9745 documents). The runtime half of that is the cascade itself, the RPC adapters that run it, and the knowledge tool's binding to the calling agent. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

### Why a row rather than relocation

Every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. The owned-state cascade sits in `src/agent_lifecycle.rs` on `master`, next to the delete preflight, and the RPC delete and rename adapters in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` already call it; the gateway and CLI call the same functions. It landed there on 2026-09-30 through #10621, after this table existed, and has no row of its own; this row covers #9745's changes to it and says so, and does not ratify that landing, which is a separate Core decision if one is wanted. The cascade reaches the cron store (`crate::cron`), the control-plane task store (`crate::control_plane`) and the runtime's Fluent catalogue (`crate::i18n`), all of which the holding crate still contains, so a crate of its own today would either pull those along or invert the dependency the kernel extraction is meant to settle. ADR-016 describes that case: extraction would establish a crate boundary the roadmap does not intend. #11701's proposed row (open, approved) names the agent-lifecycle owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction as this subsystem's destination, and this row uses the same destination. The knowledge-specific logic that can live elsewhere already does: scope, grants, export and purge are in `zeroclaw-memory`, the tool in `zeroclaw-tools`, the admission rule in `zeroclaw-config`. What remains in the runtime is the lifecycle wiring between them.

### Coverage analysis

No row on `master` covers this work. All 47 active rows were read for the paths #9745 touches:

- `src/agent_lifecycle.rs`: no row names it. #11701 (open, approved) is the first row to touch the file, for #11301's rename recovery, and its scope cell excludes exactly this work: "No delete recovery, knowledge-graph follower, new follower store, new lifecycle operation, or non-English locale".
- `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: named by the #10905, #10407, #11466/#11506, #10911, #11181, #10513/#10522, #11607, #9872/#10391, #11692, #11622, #11513, #11698, #11730, #11221, #11463 and #11286 rows. Each is limited to its own pull request and behavior (compaction, session prompts, config receipts, live-config publication, steering provenance, `sops.run`, the refresh pre-filter, the delegation ceiling call, budget warnings, message times, the profile projection, personality reload, delegate activity, tool selection, diff capture, one WSS regression). None covers the agent delete or rename adapters, alias admission, or the map-key delete response's `owned_state` field and `deleted: false` answer (the #11466/#11506 row covers only that response's `revision` receipt).
- `src/tools/mod.rs` and `src/tools/delegate.rs`: the #9872/#10391 bounded-delegation row covers rebuilding "a bounded delegate's context-sensitive tools for the target workspace", but is limited to #9872/#10391 and the caller ceiling; the #11221 row covers built-in tool selection and name reservation; the #11462 row covers delegate operator approvals; the #11465, #11473, #10331/#11450, #11292, #11730, #11456, #9579, #9447, #11698, #10911 and #10407 rows cover cancellation context, schema deferral, worker-loss recovery, progress, activity forwarding, resident-memory supervision, the docs skill, terminal handling, personality reload, live-config publication and session prompts. None covers binding the knowledge tool to a `KnowledgeScope` or rebinding it for a delegate. The #10911 row excludes a "new live consumer" of the live-config authority; the knowledge scope only reads the existing read-only handle per graph operation and registers nothing, which the row states.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(memory): add per-agent attribution and scoping to the knowledge graph
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds mandatory agent ownership to the shared SQLite knowledge graph. `KnowledgeScope` is bound from trusted registration; writes keep caller ownership and directional `read_knowledge_from` grants widen reads only.
  - Makes legacy attribution explicit and fail-closed, with a sole-agent automatic path or configured `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` for ambiguous multi-agent upgrades.
  - Makes agent delete/rename recovery lifecycle-specific: delete probes exported memory while rename detects even an empty agent identity row; filesystem inspection errors retain residue; workspace/knowledge archives surface failures; cron and ACP rows are purged only after durable export.
  - Makes the fail-toward-residue rule uniform across surfaces. The gateway workspace mover and committed-rename probe no longer collapse a metadata error into absence, and the CLI deletion path archives through the shared helper instead of a hand-rolled copy that swallowed its errors.
  - Makes that fail-toward-residue rule platform-independent. A workspace whose parent is a file surfaces as an error on Unix and as an ordinary "not found" on Windows, so every surface now classifies a path through one shared `inspect_lifecycle_path` helper that re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe. An uninspectable workspace is residue on every supported platform, and the regressions assert that classification instead of the platform's error shape.
  - Gives every deletion archive an exclusively created leaf, so a duplicate delete inside the same clock second cannot adopt another attempt's directory, and writes the archive artifacts with `create_new` so a shared leaf could not replace a durable export even if one were reached.
  - Prevents shared inbound edges from suppressing the caller's own relation and requires a scope-visible anchor for every direct graph-neighbor query after grant revocation.
  - Validates lifecycle aliases before any recovery probe or filesystem path derivation, keeps unreadable RPC rename workspaces retryable, and serializes the global node cap across per-agent SQLite connections.
  - Boxes the RPC map-key delete future, which the master merge showed is needed to keep `process_line` inside the two-megabyte stack budget `master` now pins.
  - Resolves grants from live policy for each graph operation after acquiring the database connection. Purge verifies the archived snapshot in an immediate transaction, using durable edge generation identities to distinguish recreated relations.
  - Refuses to recreate an agent over a retired agent's knowledge on every config creation path. Explicit creation and property writes that would create the agent (`zeroclaw config set` and `config patch`, gateway PUT and PATCH, RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many`) share one admission rule: never the reserved `default` agent, and never an absent alias whose knowledge remains or whose store cannot be inspected without waiting. The refusal is a 400 `validation_failed` on HTTP (explicit creation previously reported it as 404) and a localized message on RPC and the CLI. The `model_routing_config` tool's `upsert_agent`, which inserts agents directly, runs the same retirement check against the store the runtime opens; an agent defined by environment overrides is live and is not probed. The probe re-walks the ancestors of a store reported as missing, so a store under a regular-file parent is refused on Windows as on Unix.
  - Merges current `master` (`5d4b18d335`) and ports the knowledge-ownership paths onto its atomic live-config publication: the live knowledge scope reads a `LiveConfigHandle`, and agent delete and its committed-delete retry admit a `ConfigCommit` and publish only when config changes.
- **Scope boundary:** Knowledge ownership is per agent alias, not per authenticated principal; different principals using the same agent share its knowledge. The unwired Postgres graph is unchanged. Knowledge tool schema/shape is unchanged, but row visibility is intentionally narrowed by `KnowledgeScope`. Gateway and RPC can retry committed rename residue; CLI cannot yet, and #10373 owns that shared recovery follow-up. Lifecycle requests now enforce the canonical alias grammar before touching recovery state. #10149 owns durable recovery for a failed custom workspace archive. Not changed here, and predating this PR: an environment override that names a new agent is applied at config load without the retirement check (documented as an operator caveat), and the `model_routing_config` tool's `remove_agent` removes an agent without the owned-state cascade.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-memory`, tools/runtime registration, config, gateway/RPC/CLI alias lifecycle, SQLite knowledge/session/memory stores, cron and ACP cleanup, workspaces, and documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9647. Related #9646. Related #10149. Related #10373.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `config`, `gateway`, `memory`, `runtime`, `tool`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `priority:p1`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `topic:identity-access`, `release:v0.9.0`

Agent aliases remain the canonical ownership key already used by configuration, workspaces, grants, and lifecycle operations. The storage API requires scope so foreign rows behave as absent even if a caller knows an ID. Disabled configured siblings remain valid explicit read sources; they do not become writers.

### What this does, simply

Agents previously shared the same knowledge graph. This change gives each row an owning agent and limits an agent to its own knowledge unless an operator grants read access to another agent's rows. Deletion archives owned knowledge before removing it, and rename moves its ownership. The latest repair makes revoked sharing take effect for retained tools and stops cleanup from purging rows that differ from its archive. If cleanup fails, creating that agent again through any config surface is refused until a retried delete removes the old knowledge, so a new agent with the same name never inherits it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` through the registered `knowledge` tool and alias lifecycle RPC/CLI paths.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Enable knowledge and configure neutral agents `agent_a` and `agent_b`.
- **Steps to run:** Capture a unique node as `agent_b`; search, inspect statistics, traverse, and relate by ID as `agent_a`; then add `read_knowledge_from = ["agent_b"]`, restart, and repeat. Exercise rename/delete once with a temporarily unavailable configured memory/workspace path, restore it, and retry. For the archive path, issue the same `agents delete` twice inside one second and inspect `<data_dir>/agents/_deleted`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign rows are absent before the grant; reads become visible after the directional grant while writes remain caller-owned. Failed lifecycle cleanup retains retryable residue. Creating the alias again, explicitly or through a property write such as `zeroclaw config set agents.<alias>.enabled true`, is refused while its knowledge remains or the store cannot be inspected, and is admitted once a retried delete converges. The duplicate delete lands in its own archive leaf and the first attempt's export is untouched.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Agents shared one unscoped graph, and several committed lifecycle failures could be mistaken for completed cleanup.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `e248cfe531`. `959cb698a3` merges `master` at `5d4b18d335`, and `e248cfe531` is the alias-recreation fix. Results below are from macOS arm64 at that head unless noted. Hosted CI was still running on this head when this was written.

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> clean
  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> no warnings
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 5951 tests run: 5951 passed, 9 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 727 tests run: 727 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component
    -> 263 tests run: 263 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 526 run: 525 passed; filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled
       timed out under full-suite load and passes alone
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 2531 run: 2530 passed; policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception
       fails identically on master on macOS (open PR #11646)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools -E 'test(/model_routing_config|knowledge/)'
    -> 56 tests run: 56 passed
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> no prose em-dashes; 0 errors
  ```

- **Not run as scripted here:** this machine's `rg` cannot load `libpcre2`, so `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` and the provider-dispatch step of `rust_quality_gate.sh` abort, and nine `content_search` tool tests fail for the same reason. The comment hygiene checker passed when given the same file set through `git ls-files`, and the fix adds no `ModelProvider` method calls. Hosted CI runs both gates.
- **Regression coverage for the blocker:** a failed knowledge purge followed by recreation is refused at each boundary: config unit (`auto_create_refuses_retained_knowledge_and_uninspectable_store`), gateway PUT, PATCH and explicit create (`property_writes_cannot_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), RPC `config/set` and `config/set-many` after a real committed delete with a blocked store, then admitted after the retried delete converges (`config_set_cannot_recreate_agent_until_retired_knowledge_converges`), the CLI binary (`config_patch_refuses_to_recreate_agent_with_retained_knowledge`), and the `model_routing_config` tool (`upsert_agent_refuses_alias_with_retained_knowledge`, `upsert_agent_admits_env_defined_agent_that_owns_knowledge`). Busy and uninspectable stores fail closed; the Windows-shaped not-found branch is driven directly (`missing_store_under_a_file_ancestor_is_uninspectable`).
- **Mutation checks:** restoring the old auto-create path (retirement check skipped, reserved check kept) makes the config, gateway, RPC, and CLI regression tests fail; probing the tool's env-free file config or skipping its probe fails the tool test; disabling the env-defined-agent check fails its test.
- **Known gap:** no Windows execution here; the gateway and RPC uninspectable fixtures rely on the new ancestor walk on Windows and are untested there until the advisory Windows job runs.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Previously reviewed head:** `be62e0b5160f65f3ddc937c427691395d968eb75`. The required [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36767407780/job/110069381765) passed. That re-review inspected source and regression assertions; it did not run local Cargo.
- **Historical validation below:** Commands, counts, and Windows results below were reported for `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`; they are not current-head execution claims.

- **Historical head under test:** `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, which merges `origin/master` (`46479bdca7`) into the branch and adds the two portability repairs described below.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `CI Required Gate` rollup plus the advisory Windows nextest job. This head exists to repair a Windows-only behavior, so the advisory Windows job is the one that actually exercises what changed; the required gate covers everything else.
- Hosted CI on this head (`4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34554821248.
- **Advisory Windows disclosure:** On historical head `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, [Windows job 103129316312](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34554821248/job/103129316312) ran the repaired unreadable-workspace, path-classifier, duplicate-archive, existing-export protection, and refused-move tests successfully. The job remains failed: its initial batch reported 13,163 tests run, 13,160 passed, 3 failed, and 20 skipped. The remaining failures are the architecture publish-contract test and two runtime PowerShell tests; none is one of the repaired lifecycle regressions. Subsequent scoped batches passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No Windows execution is available locally, so the Windows result for that historical head comes from the runner; what is proven here is that the shared classifier returns `Uninspectable` for the `Ok(false)` shape Windows reports and that every lifecycle surface routes through it. No live two-agent daemon A/B, and no live multi-process duplicate delete. The duplicate-archive regression drives two cascades of the same alias inside one clock second in-process, which is the interleaving the finding described, but it is not a two-daemon race. CLI committed-rename retry remains #10373.
- **Commands run and tail output (historical head `4291450ec`):**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean (exit 0)

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    -> No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
       (one pre-existing MD038 on an unchanged line of agents/internals.md, reported non-blocking)

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> 1 link collected, 0 errors

  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    -> fmt clean; workspace clippy --all-targets --features ci-all -D warnings clean;
       provider dispatch gate clean (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 4305 tests run: 4305 passed, 5 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 521 tests run: 521 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 383 tests run: 383 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 532 tests run: 532 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
    -> 15654 tests run: 15653 passed (2 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
    -> the single failure is zeroclaw-providers
       grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant,
       a known macOS-local timing flake unrelated to this change
  ```

  Both repairs were proven to fail before and pass after, on this machine.

  The Windows-shape defect was reproduced by reverting the new classifier to the
  pre-fix rule (`Ok(false)` means absent), which is exactly the path Windows
  takes:

  ```text
  # classifier temporarily reverted to `Ok(false) => Absent`
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --test-threads=1 --no-fail-fast \
    -E 'test(a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes) + ...'
    -> FAIL a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes
       panicked: a negative probe over a non-directory ancestor is not absence

    -> 5 tests run: 5 passed, 4270 skipped
  ```

  The cross-device failure was reproduced literally, by putting `TMPDIR` on a
  separate mount from the install root the pre-fix fixture reached into:

  ```text
  # pre-fix, TMPDIR on a separate filesystem
    -> FAIL duplicate_delete_cascades_cannot_share_an_archive_or_truncate_the_first_export
       ["workspace archive failed (<install-root>/agents/agent_a/workspace ->
         <tmpdir>/data/agents/_deleted/agent_a-<ts>-2/workspace): Cross-device link (os error 18)"]

  # after pinning config_path under the test's TempDir, same split-mount run

       and the install root was left empty, which is the property that was missing
  ```

- **Historical evidence (previous head `64d8944a4275a31aa39ce4094c5d655dce205ecf`):** the exact-head hosted rollup [run 34188562577](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34188562577) completed with 37 successful checks, 1 failure, and 3 skipped. The required `CI Required Gate` passed; the single failure was the advisory Windows nextest job described above. Local focused suites at that head passed, which is the asymmetry this head removes: the assertions they made were Unix-only. That head also needed one master-driven repair, kept here as history: `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` landed on `master` after the branch's previous head and aborted on the merged tree because the agent-delete branch of `handle_config_map_key_delete` left the owned-state cascade's future inline in the caller; it passed on `origin/master` alone, aborted on the merged head, and passed again after the delete future was boxed.

- **Historical evidence (earlier head `ab20806838a56a5ed9027e34c2517d4ee8af950e`):** the exact-head hosted rollup completed 38/38 successful check runs, including the required aggregate gate, strict lint, tests, Landlock, security, platform checks, MSRV, and the parallel runtime gate. Focused suites at that head were `zeroclaw-memory` knowledge_graph 30 passed, `zeroclaw-tools` knowledge 18 passed, `zeroclaw-config` knowledge 5 passed, `zeroclaw-runtime` `config_map_key_` 10 passed, and the gateway `agent_delete_`/`agent_rename_` suites 7 and 4 passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read the exact-head Windows job log rather than inferring the failures from the summary, and confirmed that five of its six failures are this PR's own `try_exists().is_err()` assertions and the sixth is the inherited packaging assertion. I re-audited every filesystem probe on the lifecycle surfaces so that all of them, including the deletion archive and the knowledge-database probe inside the residue predicate, now route through the one classifier. I mounted a separate filesystem locally to reproduce the reviewer's cross-device failure instead of taking it on faith, and confirmed after the fix that the test leaves the install root untouched. Earlier rounds established the master baseline for the stack regression in a separate worktree. I did not run a live daemon interaction, I did not exercise the duplicate delete across two operating-system processes, and I cannot execute Windows here.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no visual presentation changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo deny check` was not re-run locally; it is unchanged by this head and the hosted security job covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**; `read_knowledge_from` is an explicit directional read grant. It defaults empty, validates aliases, and never widens writes.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; output shape is unchanged and storage authorization reduces visible rows.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Trusted config is the only grant source; mandatory storage-layer predicates, foreign-as-absent results, and caller-owned writes constrain it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for ambiguous multi-agent legacy knowledge; it remains hidden until assigned. Single-agent upgrades are automatic.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**; adds `agents.<alias>.workspace.read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent`; alias lifecycle commands now cascade owned state and reject noncanonical/reserved aliases before recovery I/O. Explicit creation, rename, and property writes that would create an agent refuse retained knowledge or an uninspectable knowledge store, and the explicit HTTP create reports that refusal as 400 `validation_failed` instead of 404.
- Storage schema: Adds durable `edges.generation` identities and an insert trigger for archived-snapshot comparison.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Multi-agent operators with legacy knowledge set `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent = "<enabled-alias>"`, restart, verify ownership, then remove the migration setting. Add read grants only when deliberate.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable knowledge, back up its SQLite file, then revert the eventual PR landing commit. An old binary does not enforce ownership and may create unattributed rows, so rollback is containment only. The `edges.generation` column and insert trigger remain in the SQLite database across a binary downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[knowledge].enabled = false`; remove `read_knowledge_from` entries to revoke sharing.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `still owns knowledge` or `cannot inspect retired knowledge` refusals when recreating an agent (WARN `config.retired_agent_vivify_refused` for property writes), legacy-ownership ambiguity warnings, owned-state cascade warnings, retained cron/ACP rows after archive failure, `workspace inspection failed` warnings on a delete or rename result, or repeated delete/rename results reporting configured-but-unavailable residue.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(onboarding): use native Claude Code accounts with supervised plugin apply
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `codex/native-onboard-foundation-20261007` (parent #11602; eventual target `master`).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add the typed `claude_code_native` provider so ZeroClaw can use an installed, unmodified Claude Code client and its selected native account for inference.
  - Keep conversation, tools, approvals, and risk policy in ZeroClaw. Native inference runs one fresh safe-mode turn with native tools and MCP servers disabled and native session persistence off.
  - Extend `native-onboard --client claude-code` to verify the selected native account and explicit billing source, commit the canonical agent configuration, and use the shared bounded readiness proof.
  - Add plugin apply supervision so users can review explicit onboarding choices, observe progress, cancel, and retain owned state after a failed or interrupted attempt.
- **Scope boundary:** Native Code owns login, refresh, managed policy, and final billing/auth decisions. The existing `claude-code` Anthropic HTTP alias keeps its meaning. Native vision, token streaming, model discovery, exact replay, native Windows execution, and detached-descendant containment are not claimed.
- **Blast radius:** Provider config/factory/attribution, native subprocess boundaries, the shared onboarding command, and the Claude plugin's plan/apply flow.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9009. Related #10684. Depends on #11602. This updates existing #11596 and preserves its review history. The foundation depends on #11597; the ChatGPT client skill package remains a separate sibling above #11602.

### What this does, simply

Claude Code being signed in does not currently give ZeroClaw a native Claude inference path. This change lets ZeroClaw ask the installed client for a model completion while ZeroClaw continues to decide which tools may run and which actions need approval. It references the native account directory rather than importing credentials.

The onboarding command and plugin create a separate ZeroClaw instance with explicit model, agent, risk, and billing choices. A plan or an auth-status result is not readiness: the shared command must complete one normal agent request and recheck the saved configuration. Native account settings and entitlement can change between the probe and generation; the native client remains the final authority.

The corrected native default-account namespace has been verified in the complete flow: plugin MCP apply used the native subscription account, reached the canonical YOLO `ready` state, and the resulting ZeroClaw agent successfully wrote and read a file through its own tools. The request completed with the expected marker, exit status 0, and no stderr. The final combined-source gates passed. Sanitized exact-output evidence appears below; current-head required CI passed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Native client/account selection and the plugin's apply/cancel experience need user-boundary checks.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; Claude Code plugin slash-command/MCP interface. No web or TUI interface claim.
- **Setup / preconditions:** macOS or Linux/WSL, an unmodified Claude Code 2.1.289+ installation, Python 3.9+ for the plugin helper, a native account with the selected billing source, and a build containing the foundation and this provider. Use an absent absolute destination with an existing parent. Verify the selected account using the native client's `auth status --json` and `/status`; for an explicit directory, use `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/existing-native-account claude auth status --json`.
- **Steps to run:** Run the same commands on `master` and this branch:

  ```sh
  zeroclaw native-onboard --help
  zeroclaw --config-dir /path/to/new-native-instance native-onboard \
    --client claude-code \
    --provider-alias native --agent-alias assistant \
    --model '<native-account-visible-model>' \
    --risk-preset balanced --expected-billing subscription \
    --native-config-dir /path/to/existing-native-account
  ```

  In a separate fresh destination, omit `--native-config-dir` to check the native default account. Try an unauthenticated account and an intentionally mismatched billing choice; neither should claim readiness. Interrupt a run and rerun the identical accepted choices.

  ```sh
  claude plugin validate --strict integrations/claude-plugin
  claude --plugin-dir ./integrations/claude-plugin
  ```

  Invoke `/zeroclaw:onboard`, review its plan, and use the offered apply action only after accepting the model, account, billing source, risk preset, and fresh destination. Exercise cancellation from the presented apply flow. YOLO also requires `--accept-yolo`; API billing also requires `--accept-api-billing`. `cloud_or_gateway` is the explicit cloud/gateway billing choice.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The native provider uses the selected native account, refuses ambiguous/mismatched billing, and returns a structured completion to ZeroClaw's normal tool loop. Onboarding commits only accepted canonical configuration and reports `ready` only after the shared proof. Plugin apply reports bounded progress and preserves owned state on cancellation/failure. The live default-account subscription flow and subsequent ZeroClaw file tools succeeded; sanitized exact-output and final combined-source gates are recorded below.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The typed native provider and this onboarding command are unavailable. The legacy `claude-code` alias uses Anthropic HTTP rather than the installed native client's account. The same fresh-instance command cannot complete this flow.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37681249874) passed, including Lint, Test and CI Required Gate, for `a6c6e24b5c8fa2eed49e87fac1a1697ad5cc71c1`. Parent #11597 passed its required gate. Shared onboarding #11602 has its own current-head CI. Results are recorded separately from live account proof.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Live validation covers the native default subscription account and canonical YOLO flow. An alternate account directory and API/cloud billing were not separately exercised live. POSIX cleanup was checked; native Windows and descendants creating another session are outside the supported boundary.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```sh
  RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -j2 -- --test-threads=1
  RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw native_onboard::tests -j2 -- --test-threads=1
  RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw --test native_onboard_cli -j2 -- --test-threads=1
  RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw --all-targets --no-deps -j2 -- -D warnings
  RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets --no-deps -j2 -- -D warnings
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  python3 -I -B -m unittest discover -s integrations/claude-plugin/tests -v
  claude plugin validate --strict integrations/claude-plugin
  ```

  ```text
  provider library: 2024 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
  native onboarding: 21 passed; 0 failed
  actual CLI: 14 passed; 0 failed
  Claude plugin: Ran 84 tests ... OK
  supervisor: 22 passed
  Rust 1.98 strict Clippy and formatting: passed
  strict native plugin validation: passed
  final extracted MCP discovery: bootstrap.status, bootstrap.plan, bootstrap.apply
  exact CI Fluent coverage regression: 1 passed; 0 failed
  ```

  Native provider qualification includes 18 focused tests and 36 guard mutations. CLI/default-selector qualification adds 13 mutations; supervisor qualification adds 26. Each mutation failed its intended behavioral assertion, then source bytes were restored. Independent re-review cleared executable admission, receipt freshness, and normal-session cleanup blockers. The final shared CI fix removes three test-only diagnostics; its coverage regression failed before the fix and passed afterward without changing the scanner or baseline. Local proof used isolated warm targets with matching source bytes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The unmodified native client completed subscription inference. A safe-mode isolation check showed native tools/MCP servers empty, a hostile unmanaged SessionStart hook not firing, and hostile local instructions ignored. Actual plugin MCP apply then reached canonical YOLO `ready` using the native default subscription account. The resulting ZeroClaw agent executed real `file_write` and `file_read` successfully. Native client account, quota, managed policy and billing remain authoritative.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text CLI/MCP output and tool trace below. Synthetic supervisor checks cover progress/cancellation through timeout, MCP cancellation, EOF and SIGTERM. No desktop screenshot or broader visual-layout claim.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Final head `a6c6e24b5c8fa2eed49e87fac1a1697ad5cc71c1`; `surface=cli`, English plain text and JSON MCP. Sources: `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/claude_code_native.rs`, `tests/native_onboard_cli.rs`, and `integrations/claude-plugin/tests`. Native provider SHA-256 `5a9777e44c78e287cf4f29899be6b191873d81b75acc58fe9b43eabe88dfb523`; supervisor SHA-256 `3fd250a71eaaf5f70eec39d798250ff79b1733efbd24c0d2782e7596328f11db`; final standalone ZIP SHA-256 `31f5f1ea7aa0c09c50405267f9d04a93fc9993da213fd0d4c307f833382ab729`. No terminal-width or desktop-layout claim.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Sanitized completed-flow fields; account identity, absolute root and timestamps omitted:

  ```json
  {"status":"ready","configuration_owner":"zeroclaw native-onboard","provider_reference":"claude_code_native.subscriber","inference_verified":true}
  {"trace_tools_observed":["file_read","file_write"],"matching_tool_trace_events":6,"exit_code":0,"stderr_present":false,"credential_copy":false,"selected_native_default":true}
  ```

  Exact final agent output: `NATIVE_TOOL_ROUNDTRIP_OK`. The trace records successful completion of both ZeroClaw tools in the canonical instance workspace.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Fixtures verify config/factory admission, literal stdin/argv, native auth/billing checks, one-turn isolation, structured success/error/usage, deadlines and cleanup. Actual MCP apply created the accepted separate instance, proved canonical YOLO readiness, and its agent subsequently completed the file-tool round trip.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live alternate account, API/cloud billing, native Windows, detached-session, streaming, vision, model-listing or exact-replay proof is claimed. Python 3.9 syntax/API compatibility was checked; execution used Python 3.14.6. English docs follow the normal localization workflow.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Adds a native inference subprocess and explicit plugin apply. Native tools/MCP are disabled for inference; ZeroClaw retains tool approval and the selected canonical risk policy. Apply is restricted to the accepted fresh-instance request; YOLO requires explicit acceptance.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** The installed native client can contact its configured provider under the selected native billing source. Ambiguous status and contradictory auth selectors are refused; the native client remains final billing authority.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** The adapter selects the native account namespace and probes sanitized status; native Code owns credential access and refresh. The adapter does not read or copy credential files, accept generic provider keys/endpoints, or expose raw native stderr. The corrected default namespace was verified through live subscription inference and ZeroClaw tools.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Examples and fixtures use synthetic data; attached live evidence is sanitized.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Native model output returns to ZeroClaw's existing tool loop. Safe mode, disabled native tools/MCP, fresh sessions, explicit policy, and bounded subprocess input/output limit the native execution boundary; the installed client itself is trusted.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Native Code can apply managed policy and choose opaque model fallbacks, so exact model replay and pricing are not asserted. Auth/settings can change between status and inference. POSIX cleanup covers the created process group, not descendants that detach; time and output bounds reject incomplete or malformed results. Reverting the code does not log out or revoke the native account.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** The legacy `claude-code` HTTP alias retains its meaning; native inference uses a distinct typed family.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Adds `providers.models.claude_code_native.<alias>` with native binary/account-directory references and required expected billing, enables the Claude client in `native-onboard`, and adds the plugin apply flow.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** No Rust floor change is included. Native Code 2.1.289+ and Python 3.9+ are external prerequisites for the relevant surfaces.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Install the foundation/provider build and plugin, use the native client's own login/setup, review its billing source, then run the fresh-instance command above or accept the equivalent plugin plan. Omit `--native-config-dir` to retain the native default-account namespace; use an existing absolute directory when deliberately selecting an override. Select `subscription`, `api`, or `cloud_or_gateway` explicitly; API requires `--accept-api-billing`, and YOLO requires `--accept-yolo`. No native credential migration is performed.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Cancel active plugin apply, stop using the native provider/new plugin apply flow, and restore the previous compatible binary/plugin version or revert this layer newest-first: `git revert a6c6e24b5c8fa2eed49e87fac1a1697ad5cc71c1 c7be285e7804df9c9f4516579fe5c0229a7cd3b6 679b3b1a0bd67abffef2a5d1407f1e05cc1ac142`. Retain created instance files; native account logout/revocation remains a separate native-client action.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Select a different existing model-provider alias to stop native inference, and disable/uninstall the Claude plugin to stop its apply surface. Native inference requires its typed provider and explicit billing selection.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Native version/auth/billing refusal, malformed or oversized output, subprocess deadline/cancellation errors, nonzero plugin apply outcome, or a shared onboarding receipt that never advances to `ready`. Inspect fixed sanitized errors rather than raw account output.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: N/A; no PR is superseded.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? **No.**
- If `No`, why: No superseding relationship or incorporated contributor attribution is introduced. Existing #11596 and #11597 retain their numbers and review history.

---

Labels are managed in the GitHub label UI under the repository labeler rules.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.

prs.title: feat(tools): add Firecrawl web search provider
prs.body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds Firecrawl as a `web_search_tool` provider (`search_provider = "firecrawl"`, aliases `firecrawl-search` / `firecrawl_search`). It calls `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` with the key as a Bearer token and asks for web results only (`sources: ["web"]`), so each result is a title, URL and short description like the other providers. Full pages stay with `web_fetch`.
  - The key is a new optional secret, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key` (`#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret`, same as the other keyed providers). It is resolved and decrypted from `config.toml` on every call, so adding, rotating or removing it needs no restart. When the loader applies `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`, the runtime factory passes that effective value to the tool; a blank override means "not configured" and never falls back to the stored key.
  - Responses go through the shared helpers: non-2xx statuses use `http_search_failure` (so a 429 is `search_status=unavailable`), the body is read through the bounded reader (1 MiB), a `success: false` answer on a 2xx is a failure, a missing `data.web` means no results, and titles, URLs and descriptions are whitespace-collapsed, results without a URL are skipped, and titles and descriptions go through `cap_result_content`. The query is cut to the 500 characters the API accepts, and redirects are disabled on the Firecrawl client.
  - The default provider is unchanged (`duckduckgo`).
- **Scope boundary:** No changes to the other providers, the default provider, `web_fetch` (including its existing Firecrawl fallback), plugins, or approvals. New user-facing errors use Fluent keys in both en tool catalogs. No new dependency or feature flag. The key resolver follows the existing per-provider resolvers instead of refactoring them into a shared helper, to keep this PR to one concern; happy to do that as a follow-up if you want it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-tools` (routing and tool), `zeroclaw-config` (one new optional secret field, defaults to `None`, existing configs parse unchanged), `zeroclaw-runtime` (passes the effective env override into the tool), and the tools overview page.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

`web_search_tool` can already use several search backends, chosen with `[web_search] search_provider`. This adds Firecrawl to that list. Someone who sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"` and a `firecrawl_api_key` gets web results from Firecrawl instead of the default DuckDuckGo scrape. Nothing changes for anyone who does not opt in.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It needs a Firecrawl API key, created at <https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys>.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (any surface that runs `web_search_tool`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[web_search] search_provider = "firecrawl"` and `firecrawl_api_key = "..."` in `config.toml`, or `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key` in the environment.
- **Steps to run:** ask the agent to search the web for anything, or call `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)` followed by numbered results, each with a URL and a description of at most about 500 characters.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `search_provider = "firecrawl"` is unknown, logs `Unknown web search model_provider 'firecrawl'; falling back to 'duckduckgo'`, and scrapes DuckDuckGo.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Test job runs the `zeroclaw-tools`, `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` suites, which hold every new test (aliases, key resolution and rotation, env override, secret-safe parse errors, request shape on a mock server, bounded body reads, redirect rejection, 429 handling, render caps). Docs Style covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the live endpoint is not exercised in CI, same as the other providers; request shape is pinned by wiremock tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (rustc 1.99.0, at `27fdddf`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                         clean
cargo deny check                                     advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --features tools-external --lib web_search   183 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                       1818 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features tools-external --lib api_key_override   1 passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A real search through `WebSearchTool::execute` against `api.firecrawl.dev` with the key supplied as `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`: 5 results in about 0.8 s, output labelled `(via Firecrawl)`, every result a title, URL and usually a description, and the key does not appear anywhere in the output. Descriptions can come back as long multi-line excerpts (one was over 10,000 characters before the cap), which is why the text is whitespace-collapsed and capped. Not verified live: a real 429 (covered by a wiremock test).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`. The only user-visible change is the `web_search_tool` plain-text result block, which is deterministic and unstyled.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `27fdddf`, `cli` (`web_search_tool` output as returned to the model). Locale and terminal width do not shape the output.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
Search results for: what is the rust programming language (via Firecrawl)
...
2. Rust Programming Language
   https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US
   Rust's rich type system and ownership model guarantee memory-safety and thread-safety, enabling you to eliminate many classes of bugs at compile-time.
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** set `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, called `web_search_tool` with `{"query": "what is the rust programming language"}`, and got the Firecrawl-labelled result block instead of the DuckDuckGo fallback log line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace `cargo nextest` run was not done locally; the hosted run covers it. Clippy with `-D warnings` and the newer local toolchain stops on an existing deprecation in untouched code (`fetch_update` in web_search_tool.rs), so lint is left to the hosted job.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (reuses the existing web-search tool surface and config read path).
- New external network calls? Yes. `POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search`, made only when the operator sets `search_provider = "firecrawl"`, through the same proxy-aware client builder (`apply_runtime_proxy_to_builder`) as the other providers. The request carries the query, the result limit, `sources: ["web"]` and a fixed `origin` value of `zeroclaw` that names the caller.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. One new optional secret field, `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key`, on the existing `#[secret]` / `encrypted_secret` path. The key is sent only as a Bearer header, never in the URL, body or logs. Redirects are disabled, success bodies are limited to 1 MiB before decoding, and malformed-TOML errors expose only a stable code and a derived line number.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test fixtures use placeholder keys and neutral queries.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Firecrawl result titles, URLs and descriptions are provider-controlled text returned to the model and must be treated as untrusted. Provider opt-in and the per-result and total output caps limit exposure and volume, but do not sanitize prompt injection.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: opt-in egress to one provider-scoped host; the key is handled by the established encrypted-secret path; output is bounded.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. New optional `[web_search] firecrawl_api_key` (default `None`), a new accepted value for `search_provider`, and the schema-mirror override `ZEROCLAW_web_search__firecrawl_api_key`. Existing configs parse unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the squash commit. The provider is opt-in; configs that never set `search_provider = "firecrawl"` are unaffected. If the provider misbehaves, tool errors read `firecrawl search failed (search_status=..., http=...)` in the tool log.

Updates `tokio` from 1.53.3 to 1.54.1
Release notes

Sourced from tokio's releases.

Tokio v1.54.1

1.54.1 (October 21st, 2026)

Fixed

  • time: revert "remove the runtime handle from timers" (#8692)

#8692: tokio-rs/tokio#8692

Tokio v1.54.0

1.54.0 (October 19th, 2026)

The 1.54.0 release includes all changes up to 1.53.3.

The MSRV is increased to 1.85. (#8514)

Added

  • fs: add File::set_times, File::set_modified, and fs::FileTimes (#8504)
  • net: implement Default for named_pipe::{ClientOptions, ServerOptions} (#8378)
  • runtime: add Builder::max_io_events_per_busy_tick (#8410)
  • runtime: stabilize tokio::runtime::worker_index() (#8431)
  • sync: add SemaphorePermit::semaphore() (#8482)
  • sync: add blocking_acquire methods to Semaphore (#8269)
  • sync: add watch::Receiver::is_closed (#8481)
  • wasm: support JSPI for Emscripten target (#8285, #8627)
  • wasm: support the wasm32-unknown-emscripten target (#8281, #8422, #8528, #8628)

Changed

  • fs: reject zero in File::set_max_buf_size (#8449)
  • io: make copy_buf cooperative (#8459)
  • io: panic when BufReader or BufStream is created with zero capacity (#8494)
  • io: panic when in-memory pipe is created with zero capacity (#8397)
  • io: reject zero buffer size in copy_bidirectional_with_sizes (#8454)
  • io: support vectored writes in Sink (#8663)
  • net: start UnixStream::pair and UnixDatagram::pair sockets as writable (#8444)
  • net: start accepted sockets as readable and writable (#8435)
  • net: support UCred on Fuchsia (#8257)
  • process: use mio::unix::pipe for Unix child stdio (#8603)
  • runtime: cache-pad the shared injection queue and idle state (#8622)
  • runtime: decide auto-boxing of spawned futures at monomorphization time (#8414)
  • runtime: make enable_io available whenever rt is enabled (#8387)
  • runtime: move block_in_place setup into a non-generic function (#8315)
  • runtime: move the multi-thread inject queue to its own mutex (#8382)
  • runtime: panic when max_io_events_per_tick is zero (#8476)
  • runtime: suggest .await in nested block_on panic message (#8501)
  • sync: avoid atomic reader count in broadcast slots (#8357)
  • sync: use acquire/release orderings in Notify (#8325)
  • time: remove the runtime handle from timers (#8458)

Updates `libc` from 0.2.189 to 0.2.191
Release notes

Sourced from libc's releases.

0.2.191

Support

  • Emscripten: Support v4.0.12 to v6.0.11 (#5610)

Added

  • Apple: Add F_SETNOSIGPIPE and F_GETNOSIGPIPE (#5609)
  • Apple: add ifaliasreq and in6_aliasreq (#5557)

  • Haiku: Add AI_* and NI_* constants from netdb.h (#5585)
  • Hurd: Add POSIX_SPAWN_* flags (#5578)
  • NuttX: Add AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (#5614)
  • OpenBSD: Add sensordev (#5534)
  • QuRT: Add isatty (#5618)
  • WASI: Add pthread_condattr_{get,set}clock (#5626)

Fixed

  • FreeBSD-aarch64: Fix gpregs and fpregs (#5603)

Changed

  • AIX: Restore 'c_ulong' as the type of 'statvfs.f_fsid'. (#5616)
  • Android: Make prop_info an extern type (#5561)
  • Apple: Mach API is now available on non-MacOS targets again. This should resolve some issues building ecosystem crates. (#5612), (#5636)
  • FreeBSD: Add back NOTE_PCTRLMASK with a deprecation warning (#5600)

0.2.190

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.
  • 32-bit Windows-GNU
  • ESP-IDF (all targets with this environment are 32-bit)

Most other 32-bit platforms are either already using 64-bit time_t, or are considered legacy and will not be gaining support from their upstream maintainers.

You can enable this using RUSTFLAGS:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

Note that there may still be some changes to features gated by this config option, hence "unstable"
