prs.title: feat(providers): honor runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models or unverified API/tool combinations retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates use their own profiles; bounded delegates inherit their caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Explicit raw-body overrides retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: automated mock HTTP regressions exercise the real CLI/channel/Agent/delegate paths and assert outgoing efforts; judging model answers manually would not verify the wire setting. The real CLI regression is reproducible with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `45e47dcded9400d035d612ee9c4eab6855b03491`, [Quality Gate run 40482915746](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40482915746) completed successfully, including `CI Required Gate`, `Test`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, lint, build, platform/MSRV and docs checks. Conditional skips are not executed coverage. The earlier `d9ffb9e04d631ed25074d6e412b0310446c20537` run had three checkout cancellations and a failed gate; the successful current-head run supersedes that CI result. Local validation covers all five owning crates, real turn/delegate/channel mock HTTP boundaries, schema persistence and export, strict workspace Clippy, Rustdoc, documentation and both comment gates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local host is macOS. CI pins Rust 1.98.0; strict local validation used installed 1.98.1, while local tests and nextest ran on Rust 1.99.0. Live provider availability, account entitlements and paid API behavior were not tested. Broad and parallel local runs expose baseline platform/timing failures, detailed below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
bash scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 6m 05s
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate (no direct ModelProvider method calls outside ProviderDispatch)
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib native_ -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 172 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 1830 filtered out; finished in 27.45s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib native_ -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 91 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5796 filtered out; finished in 3.20s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib thinking -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 57 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5830 filtered out; finished in 1.77s

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh
58 passed, 0 failed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

At the initial published revision `d9ffb9e04d631ed25074d6e412b0310446c20537`, the `native_` filters across API, config, providers, runtime and channels passed 307 tests; the broader `thinking` filters passed 160 tests. The separate real CLI regression passed on that revision with the exact test name:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint -- --exact
running 1 test
test agent::loop_::tests::native_thinking_cli_profiles_override_global_effort_on_the_shared_endpoint ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5886 filtered out; finished in 1.26s
```

Schema checks cover all six serialized levels and configuration save/reload; generated-field documentation and API Rustdoc checks passed.

The earlier workspace nextest run on `3cda22a0741704f2dc73ca4a8f63bb41cc29f004` completed 19,423 passing tests, 28 failures and 42 skips (two passing tests were reported leaky). One failure was an obsolete generated-description assertion introduced with the documentation change; it was corrected and its focused test passes. Twenty-four failures pass with isolated configuration/environment or a controlled rerun. The remaining Telegram 100 ms deadline, ZeroCode 40 ms polling assertion and macOS `nul`/`NUL` fixture collision reproduce against unchanged `master` product code at `5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9`.

All six planned 16-thread crate rounds completed. Runtime rounds reported 5,877 passed/one failure, 5,876 passed/two failures, and 5,878 passed/no failures, with nine ignored each; the failing cases were the webhook-audit two-second timeout and queued-RPC transaction timing assertion. All three channel rounds passed 2,017 tests with two ignored each. Three full unchanged-master concurrency rounds reproduce those same failures, alongside other timing failures. These failures are retained as validation limitations; this PR does not change those tests or production paths.

A separate concurrency run timed out in the existing five-second background-result waiter while the new delegate regression still reported `Running`, before its effort assertions. The regression passed its focused run, all three earlier 16-thread runtime rounds and two later runs outside the outer sandbox; a different pre-existing background test also hit that waiter. This remains a load-sensitive fixture limitation and is reported separately from unchanged-baseline failures.

Independent validation on that initial published revision repeated the strict gate, the corrected 307-test `native_` batch, the 160-test `thinking` batch and the relevant generated-configuration test successfully. Its three workspace partitions ran the same 19,451 tests: 19,414 passed and 37 failed. The local failures are retained as configuration-environment conflicts, nested macOS sandbox denials, case-sensitive-fixture assumptions and timing/loopback limitations; the OpenAI effort assertions passed. All three independent runtime rounds are reported: the first, under the outer coding sandbox, had 5,852 passed, 26 failed and nine ignored; a nested single-test subprocess also failed within that run. The second, outside the outer sandbox, had 5,878 passed/no failures; the third had 5,873 passed/five timing or loopback failures, with nine ignored each. These runs are not uniformly green. All three independent channel rounds passed 2,017 tests with two ignored each.

Both comment gates, feature and exception docs/local-link gates, API Rustdoc and the API doctest passed. Config/runtime had no doctests; the provider doctest is declared ignored. The governance, compatibility and validation limits in this body remain explicit. Future model additions require updates to the verified capability tables; unknown IDs continue to use existing global/default behavior.

The follow-up commit `45e47dcded9400d035d612ee9c4eab6855b03491` gives the supported legacy `openai-codex`, `openai_codex` and `codex` factories the same subscription capability mapping as typed OpenAI aliases. Its outgoing-payload regression failed before the fix (`high` sent instead of requested `low`) and passes afterward for all three spellings, including streaming, one-shot calls, opt-out/global controls and unknown models. Fresh affected checks on this commit used Rust 1.99.0 for tests and Rust 1.98.1 for strict lint:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib native_ -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 173 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 1830 filtered out; finished in 13.68s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib thinking -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1923 filtered out; finished in 1.12s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib codex -- --test-threads=4
test result: ok. 58 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1946 filtered out; finished in 4.48s

bash scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 4m 28s
==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean

cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh
58 passed, 0 failed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

The earlier broad workspace, runtime/channel concurrency, schema, documentation and CLI evidence above is retained with its original revision and limitations; those checks were not all rerun for this isolated factory correction.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced every changed request constructor/rebuilder, factory selection and fallback boundary. Mock tests assert actual Responses/Chat/Codex bodies, tool and streaming requests, model remapping, concurrent-profile/session-reset isolation, Agent cache bypass and delegate inheritance. Verified model capabilities against official model documentation and the list-visible Codex catalog. No live-provider smoke test or paid API call was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface or presentation behavior changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `45e47dcded9400d035d612ee9c4eab6855b03491` for the fresh provider payload tests, strict workspace lint, formatting and both comment gates. The initial published revision `d9ffb9e04d631ed25074d6e412b0310446c20537` and earlier parent runs supply the separately identified broad/CLI/schema/documentation evidence above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Relevant literal validation output appears above. Wire assertions are in `openai_reasoning_tests.rs`, channel orchestrator tests, and runtime Agent/loop/delegate/turn tests.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Different opted-in profiles on the same endpoint produce their own efforts; fallback attempts remap against the serving model; opting out retains the old global/default path; explicit overrides bypass response-cache reuse.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Desktop/UI and live-provider tests are outside this change. Optional external link validation was skipped because `lychee` is not installed; local target checks and link-collector fixtures passed. No network/API capability probing or toolchain installation was performed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: bypassing response-cache reuse for an explicit native-thinking override can issue an existing model request where a cached result was previously returned. Requests use the same configured endpoints and authentication; tests use local mock servers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No: existing thinking-prompt selection is preserved.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Explicit overrides can increase model calls, latency and token cost. The existing `native_thinking` opt-in and rollback path control this behavior. Diagnostics include requested/effective effort, provider alias, model and mapping outcome; they exclude credentials, prompts, endpoint URLs and response bodies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust source constructing or exhaustively destructuring affected public structs. Existing TOML values, schema enum values, provider defaults and serialized configuration remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new key, environment variable or CLI option. Existing opted-in profile levels now affect supported OpenAI native requests.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: No configuration migration. Downstream `ChatRequest` literals must initialize `thinking_level` (`None` for unrelated requests); rebuilders copy the original level, and exhaustive patterns add the field or `..`. `ThinkingLevel` remains available from its old configuration paths through a re-export. Callers of `default_budget_tokens()` through that path must import `zeroclaw_config::scattered_types::ThinkingLevelBudget`. Public runtime `ThinkingParams` literals need `native_level`; use the existing resolution helper where applicable. Recreate/reconnect Agent/RPC sessions after changing their profile defaults.

A successfully mapped non-`none` public OpenAI reasoning request omits optional `temperature`, as the verified models require. Existing runtime prompt/temperature policy, unmapped/global requests and other providers retain their behavior. Effort changes may affect latency and token usage; subscription model access still depends on the account's existing entitlements. Public API capabilities were checked against [official OpenAI model pages](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; subscription sets come from list-visible entries in the [Codex catalog at commit `126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/126a0ee92ed2c5e73cd8a8f7e37563e8527552d7/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json). Client delegation modes such as `ultra` are excluded and never sent as wire efforts.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `native_thinking = false` on affected runtime profiles and apply it through the existing runtime reload or restart lifecycle, including recreating/reconnecting Agent/RPC sessions, to return OpenAI requests to the existing global/default effort path. For a full rollback, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if merged as separate commits, revert the complete feature commit range, including its API, config, provider and runtime changes together.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Existing `native_thinking` only. Disabling it on a mixed-provider profile also disables its existing native token budgets; revert the complete feature when those budgets must stay enabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Upstream request rejection, unexpected latency/token use, an unmapped-level diagnostic, or an effort substitution inconsistent with the serving model. Inspect `requested_level`, `effective_effort`, provider/model and mapping outcome diagnostics without logging request bodies or credentials.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Propose a bounded runtime holding-crate exception for the existing native-thinking setting in feature request #12054.
  - Name the permitted adapters, their extraction destination and review condition, while keeping approval explicitly pending.
- **Scope boundary:** One table row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. This PR adds no runtime behavior and does not grant itself an exception. Canonical types, budget policy and OpenAI model/wire mapping remain with their API, config and provider owners.
- **Blast radius:** Governance for the twelve named runtime files. Core Team approval and a durable approval reference must be recorded before the implementation can merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12054. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
- **Implementation PR:** #12059 depends on this exception request. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12059

### What this does, simply

The OpenAI profile-thinking fix needs to carry an existing setting through the runtime's current request paths. The runtime is a transitional holding crate, so those additions need a recorded Core Team exception under ADR-016. This PR proposes the narrow scope for that decision. Publishing or merging a row that still says "Pending Core Team approval" does not supply the missing approval. Before this PR merges, the pending approval cell needs the actual Core Team approver and review link.

The permitted slice covers existing CLI, Agent/RPC, delegate, tool-round, summary, recovery and streaming adapters; the response-cache bypass; required request-constructor updates; explicit core-turn future `Send` contracts; and focused regressions. `cost.rs` and `vision_route.rs` have test-only constructor changes, while `skills/creator.rs` initializes the new request field to `None`.

The intended destination is the agent-loop and delegation owners in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction; auxiliary skills construction follows its existing owner. Review the exception at the agent-loop or delegation extraction design review, whichever comes first, or before widening supported turn surfaces, retained state, mapping ownership or native thinking beyond OpenAI.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this changes only the governance table; inspect the row's scope, destination, pending authority and review condition.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The added-link collection policy includes this changed `.md` file. Its docs-style Markdown-lint/em-dash step auto-selects only `docs/book/src/**`, so it skips this `AGENTS.md`. The explicit-file local run below supplies that style coverage. The exact-head run for `0b860428e6d16b1735fc6a119e22dcf28b7cd148` is terminal and not green: five jobs exceeded their five-minute limit while fetching repository history inside checkout, before their check scripts ran. `CI Required Gate` failed and dependent jobs, including `Docs Style`, were skipped. No CI workflow was changed by this one-row proposal; a maintainer rerun is needed. These results do not establish Core Team approval. [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40468285791).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The checkout cancellations left required CI coverage incomplete. The five cancelled jobs were `Common Ancestor`, `Detect changed paths`, `Detect crates.io version bump`, `Detect Windows Clippy changes` and `Detect parallel runtime test changes`. Separately, the default Markdown-lint/em-dash selection skips `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`; local validation ran with `DOCS_FILES` set to that exact file. Core Team approval remains a separate human gate.
- **Commands run and tail output:** With `BASE_SHA` set to the common base and `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`:

```text
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Linting docs files: crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md
Summary: 0 error(s)

bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Ran 6 tests in 1.636s
OK
Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row remains inside the existing Active Exceptions table, names all twelve affected runtime paths, and explicitly grants nothing until Core Team approval is recorded. The implementation is on a separate branch and is not included here.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no runtime interface state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `0b860428e6d16b1735fc6a119e22dcf28b7cd148`; Markdown governance row and local docs-gate output quoted above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Relevant docs-gate output is quoted above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Added one proposed row with pending authority; no executable behavior changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Rust builds/tests are unnecessary for this Markdown-only proposal. No live-provider calls were made.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. This is a proposed development exception, not a runtime permission grant.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before merge, withdraw the proposal. After merge, revert this PR's merge/squash commit; if it is merged unchanged as a single commit, `git revert 0b860428e6d16b1735fc6a119e22dcf28b7cd148` removes the proposed row.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A row without an actual Core Team approval reference remains an unsatisfied implementation merge gate. Any runtime additions outside the listed scope need a separate decision.

Bumps the actions-all group with 9 updates in the / directory: | Package | From | To | | --- | --- | --- | | [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) | `4.38.0` | `4.39.1` | | [Swatinem/rust-cache](https://github.com/swatinem/rust-cache) | `2.9.2` | `2.9.3` | | [actions/setup-node](https://github.com/actions/setup-node) | `7.0.0` | `7.1.0` | | [actions/upload-artifact](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact) | `7.0.1` | `7.0.2` | | [github/codeql-action/init](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) | `4.38.0` | `4.39.1` | | [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) | `4.38.0` | `4.39.1` | | [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) | `8.0.1` | `8.0.2` | | [docker/setup-buildx-action](https://github.com/docker/setup-buildx-action) | `4.3.0` | `4.4.1` | | [anchore/sbom-action](https://github.com/anchore/sbom-action) | `0.24.2` | `0.24.3` | Updates `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` from 4.38.0 to 4.39.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

v4.38.1

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded RPC denial reason exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the stable RPC denial reasons and reason-keyed denial records in #11289 (which closes #11005). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #11289 (`src/rpc/auth.rs:97`, 2026-10-12), which found that no recorded exception covers RPC denial reporting.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11289 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `5740f15a35` (three files: `src/rpc/auth.rs`, `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`): the `RpcDenialReason` identifier type with `as_str`, its private `code` and `message_key` mappings and `From<DenyReason>`; on the existing `AuthDenied`, the private `reason` field and `reason()` accessor, the private `new`, `with_message` and `with_values` builders, the `quoted` helper, the 21 named `pub(crate)` constructors that replace `auth_required` and `forbidden` (with `from_deny_reason` rebuilt on the private `with_message` and the five other `auth.rs` functions named in the row building their denials through them), and `audit_attrs`, which gives the existing `RPC authorization denied` record its `method`, `reason`, `denial_message`, `code`, `principal_id` and `auth_provider` attributes; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `audit_denial` emitting those attributes, `RpcDispatcher::refuse`, the `authorize` gate and the 21 other refusal functions named in the row building their denials through the constructors or refusing through `refuse`, the gate attributing a denial after a failed revalidation to the principal whose binding it drops, the `steering_admission` closure's record changes (its ownership and remote local-capability refusals recorded under their own reasons, the latter with that reason's `-32003` on the record while the steer is still answered `-32012`; the refusals its binding checks record themselves recorded once rather than twice, so a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved leaves no denial record), the selectors' refusals of an uninitialized connection now recorded, the retired `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL` literal, the fourteen `rpc-auth-*` keys and their translator comment (thirteen replacing an inline literal, `rpc-auth-session-local-capabilities` feeding only the record), and focused tests. `RpcDenialReason`, `as_str` and `reason()` are `pub`; no other crate consumes them. `DenyReason`, the JSON-RPC error codes and the grants stay in `zeroclaw-api`, and the record sink in `zeroclaw-log`, so they need no runtime permission; the root `AGENTS.md` bullet and the `docs/book` section that #11289 adds are outside the holding crate. It excludes any identifier in a client response, recording a refused `initialize` handshake or the other refusals answered without an `AuthDenied`, and any new RPC method, grant source, config key, record kind, record sink, retained runtime state or non-English locale.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The row is not active until a Core Team member other than the author approves it; the `Approved by` cell is filled with that review's permalink before merge, so merging this pull request is what records the vote.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11005 and #11289 (head `5740f15a35`). #11289 lands after #11326, whose global-stream wording the row's key note reflects. Precedent: #11701, #12058, #11963, and the #11286 row already in the table, which covers `src/rpc/auth.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl` but is limited to roster-bound pairing tokens.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #11289 gives every RPC authorization refusal built through `AuthDenied` a stable identifier such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, writes that identifier into the denial record the daemon already emits (the refusal text moves to its own `denial_message` attribute), moves the refusals' inline English literals into the Fluent catalogue (the gate's grant refusal and the global-stream, SOP, session-environment and upload-ownership refusals as well as the selectors'), and keeps the principal and provider on the record when a policy change drops a connection's binding. Clients receive the same codes and English text as before (the global-stream refusal takes the wording #11326 gives it), and never the identifier. The set of recorded refusals changes slightly: the selectors' refusals of a connection that never initialized are now recorded, a steer refused by its agent, workspace or environment check is recorded once rather than twice, and a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved is no longer recorded. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the RPC authorization-gate and inbound-authentication owners in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

Why placement is right: every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. On master, `AuthDenied`, with its `auth_required`, `forbidden` and `from_deny_reason` constructors, sits in `src/rpc/auth.rs` next to `RpcInboundAuth`, `AcceptedAuthState` and `AuthorityLease`; `RpcDispatcher::authorize`, `audit_denial` (which already writes the `RPC authorization denied` record, with the message as its `reason`), `current_authority`, the selectors and `still_authorized` sit in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`; and the handshake denials already resolve `rpc-auth-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The reason is set by the code that decides to refuse, so it lives where that decision is made, and it reaches only the log record: `rpc_err(denied.code, denied.message)` still sends the client the code and text alone, so the identifier is not part of the wire contract `zeroclaw-api` owns, and `zeroclaw-log` records whatever attributes the gate hands it. Moving the vocabulary out on its own would split the gate from its refusals ahead of the kernel extraction that owns the RPC boundary, which is the case the exception policy describes. #11005 names `src/rpc/{auth,dispatch}.rs` and the catalogue among the work's likely files.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; documentation-only change to a Markdown table. Please review the row's scope against the #11289 head (`5740f15a35`): `git diff --stat 5d4b18d335 5740f15a35 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` lists the three files it names.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the docs-links and comment-hygiene gates. `Docs Style` lints only `docs/book/src`, so it does not cover this file; markdownlint was run by hand below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no CI markdown lint for `crates/*/AGENTS.md` (run by hand below). No check can confirm that a row matches the code it covers or that a Core decision exists; that is this review.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
git diff --check                                              passed
BASE_SHA=5d4b18d335 scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh             No added links detected in changed docs lines.
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-runtime    Comment hygiene gate passed.
python3 -I scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
                                                              Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
python3 -I scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py --root crates/zeroclaw-runtime
                                                              Checked authored Markdown links in 11 file(s); no broken local targets.
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md
                                                              Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row names every runtime path #11289 changes at `5740f15a35` (`git diff --stat` against master `5d4b18d335`: three files under `crates/zeroclaw-runtime`) and nothing else; every type, function, constructor, Fluent key, record attribute and test it names exists at that head (28 `RpcDenialReason` variants, 21 constructors, 32 constructor call sites in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, 14 added `rpc-auth-*` keys, and no surviving `AuthDenied::auth_required`, `AuthDenied::forbidden` or `AuthDenied { .. }` literal anywhere under `crates/`); the table still has four cells per row, the new row is the last row directly under the previous one, and the file has no em-dash. No Rust was built: no code changes.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`; no user-visible interface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `N/A`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Rust gates do not apply to a Markdown-only change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`; once approved, the row permits only the named additions in the holding crate and grants no execution or data-access authority.
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk, documentation only: `git revert <sha>`. Before approval, withdrawing the row grants nothing; after approval, narrowing or revoking it is a reviewed docs change and does not remove code that already landed.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(rpc): stable denial reason identifiers and localized selector denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every RPC authorization denial now carries an `RpcDenialReason`, a stable identifier set by the typed constructor that builds it. The constructor also derives the JSON-RPC code from the reason and renders the message from the reason's Fluent key. `AuthDenied`'s `reason` field is private, so a denial cannot be built without one; the free-text `auth_required(message)` and `forbidden(message)` constructors are gone.
  - The denial audit record (`RPC authorization denied`) emits the identifier as `reason` and the localized text as a separate `denial_message` attribute, so operators can group and alert on refusals without depending on wording or the daemon's locale. The attribute is not named `message` because log exporters copy attributes out flat and log backends reserve that name.
  - The coarse grant denial and every selector refusal (config path, agent, cron, session workspace, `fs/list_dir`, attachment source, session environment, global streams, SOP) resolve through 12 new `rpc-auth-*` Fluent keys with arguments instead of inline English literals. Request values are quoted and escaped exactly as the old `{:?}` literals quoted them, so the English text is byte-identical. The one exception is the global-stream refusal, whose key carries the wording #11326 gives it, naming the persisted log.
  - A denial after failed revalidation now records the principal id and auth provider of the binding it drops. Before, the dispatcher cleared the binding first and the record carried nulls. The same change removes a production `expect()`.
  - The branch merges current master, so the denial sites #11171 added (the authority lease, the expiry helper, and the chunked-upload recheck) use the typed constructors too. The upload recheck's session-ownership refusal gets its own `session_not_owned` reason. The later merge converts #11132's sites the same way: `require_additional_grant` refuses with `grant_missing`, and steering admission records its ownership refusal as `session_not_owned` and its remote local-capability refusal as a new `session_local_capabilities` reason instead of rebuilding denials from message text, while the binding checks it calls record their own refusals once rather than twice.
- **Scope boundary:** The JSON-RPC wire shape is unchanged: codes and English message bytes are identical (apart from the global-stream refusal's #11326 wording), and the identifier is not sent to clients. Gateway HTTP denial bodies, handshake (`initialize`) auditing, the refusals that bypass `AuthDenied` (session ownership outside chunked uploads, shared memory plane, SOP decision authorization, TUI signature, remote-WSS SOP methods), and translated catalogues are unchanged. The cron refusal's client text ("Cron job not found: ...") stays an inline English literal on purpose: it must match the genuinely-missing-job answer, which comes from the cron store, so the refusal does not confirm that a job exists.
- **Blast radius:** The audit record's `reason` attribute changes from prose to an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`. The record merged in #10259 on 2026-09-24 and is in no release tag, so no released consumer depends on the prose. Open PRs that build denials with `AuthDenied::auth_required`/`forbidden` or struct literals will stop compiling at rebase; the fix is a variant, a key, and a typed constructor per new site.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11005. Depends on #11326: the denial-records docs and the global-stream refusal describe `logs/query` and `logs/get` as limited to administrators and the shared operator, which that PR implements, so this lands after it. Related #8289, #10259.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `runtime`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

When the daemon refuses an RPC request because the caller lacks permission, it writes a warning to its log. Until now the "reason" in that warning was the English sentence the client saw, so it changed whenever the wording changed and would change with the daemon's language, which makes it a poor thing to alert on. It is now a short fixed code such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, and the sentence moves to its own field. Several refusal sentences were written directly in the code instead of in the translation catalogue; they now live in the catalogue like the rest. Finally, one kind of refusal, when a policy change invalidates an existing connection, forgot who the connection belonged to before logging; it now records that. Clients see the same error codes and English messages as before, apart from the refusal for daemon-wide logs, which now also names the persisted log.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the changed output is a structured log record, and the new tests drive real refused requests through the dispatcher and assert the record each one writes.

### How I tested

**Current validation — `5740f15a35` (2026-10-26).** Clean additive merge of master `5d4b18d335`; the five-file feature diff is unchanged. Depends on #11326, which remains unmerged and must land first. This refresh validates the current branch; it does not test a combined merge with #11326.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037/job/121894004645) passed on `5740f15a35`. [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037/job/121886707052) and [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037/job/121886924048) cover the runtime and RPC regressions; [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037/job/121886707245) covers Rust; [Docs Style](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037/job/121886923960) covers the changed documentation. The full [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412570037) and [Code Analysis run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40412569786) passed. The exact-head check rollup has 45 passing checks, 11 conditional skips, and no failures or pending checks.
- **Commands run and tail output:** macOS arm64, rustc/cargo 1.97.1; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, with a dedicated target directory. Tests used default harness concurrency and the inherited macOS temporary directory, without `RUSTFLAGS` or a `TMPDIR` override.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no output.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0, no diagnostics.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib denial`: `18 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::`: `865 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5879 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib principal_gate`: `20 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin fluent -- check`: all catalogues parsed successfully.
  - `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin fluent -- scan`: exit 0, 2,275 English keys scanned; no `rpc-auth-*` key flagged. This informational inventory also reports 111 stale keys and 66 missing tool keys outside this PR's denial keys.
  - `BASE_SHA=5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9 bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`: markdownlint 0 errors for the changed authentication documentation.
  - `BASE_SHA=5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9 bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: 6 collector tests passed; 0 added links across the two changed Markdown files.
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- **Warnings investigated:** The runtime test build emits macOS ld's `__eh_frame` size warning about compact-unwind encoding. The same warning was reproduced on pinned master `5d4b18d335` with the same compact build settings during the preceding validation. It was not suppressed. The earlier runtime failures and strict-Clippy findings recorded below did not recur on this revision.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the clean merge and unchanged feature diff. Automated denied-dispatch tests use synthetic principals and inspect audit records for stable identifiers and retained principal/provider attribution; gateway tests cover the shared authority boundary. No new mutation experiments or credentialed live-service tests were run in this refresh.
- **Known CI coverage gap / intentional skips:** No live daemon under a translated locale or local Windows execution was performed. Hosted Windows compilation passed. No separate local full-workspace test run was added; the exact-head hosted Test job supplies that broader coverage. Optional combined #11326 validation was not run; its landing dependency remains explicit.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for this master refresh: no presentation change. The feature's audit-record behavior is covered by denied-dispatch assertions.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `5740f15a3597e8c01f995dbc11d5dd40a8ade057`; RPC authorization/audit records and gateway principal gating; exact-head job links above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No screenshot was needed for the merge-only refresh; actual test-result tails are listed above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Denied RPC requests retain stable audit reason identifiers and prior known attribution after failed revalidation. All focused checks and the full runtime suite passed on the refreshed branch.

<details>
<summary>Historical validation from earlier revisions (retained)</summary>

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` and `Parallel Runtime Test` run the new unit and dispatcher tests; `Lint` covers the Rust changes; `Docs Style` and the links gate cover the documentation section.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Head 0a386d6cce** (merges master 6c0b1f9eea, which includes #11132 and #11330): `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16` gives `5721 passed; 2 failed`. `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget` is the known parallel-load flake on master (#11350). `rpc::dispatch::tests::new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which #11132 added, fails on macOS only: the default temp dir lives under `/var`, a symlink to `/private/var`, so the live session's workspace spelling differs from its resolved path and steering refuses it as an alias; it passes with `TMPDIR` set to a canonical path, and on Linux CI. `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, clippy (no findings in changed files), the comment hygiene gate and the docs quality gate pass. The earlier merge (da62caf7e1) dropped c94abbf93e's configure-race synchronization in favor of #11330's fence, so this PR does not touch `session/configure`.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1, head 2e3f2e5101, which merges master a0f70b7925, unless noted):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`: `5455 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored`. The two failures are `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `tools::send_message_to_peer::tests::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`. Master a0f70b7925 itself fails the same way under the same command (the configure test in 2 of 2 runs, the cost test in 1 of 2), each passes alone 3 of 3 times on this branch, and neither touches code this PR changes. Before merging master (2d96dfa52d, on 2443af29ea) the same command passed clean: `5313 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: `637 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `ws::tests::websocket_handler_projects_anthropic_empty_terminal_stream_as_user_error` hitting its response deadline under load; it passes alone 3 of 3 times, and `ws.rs` changes only in master's commits.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets`: no findings in changed files. Under `-D warnings` it stops on four findings in files this PR does not touch, byte-identical to master: `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, macOS test builds) and three `clippy::drop_non_drop` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, which appear only when `-p zeroclaw-gateway` builds channels without `channel-telegram`.
  - `cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps`: 0 warnings.
  - `cargo fluent check`: all FTL files ok. `cargo fluent scan`: no `rpc-auth-*` key reported stale.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint 0 errors), `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`: pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each restored afterwards:
  - Emitting the message text as `reason` again fails all six dispatcher capture tests.
  - Auditing after the binding is cleared (the old order) fails `denial_after_failed_revalidation_keeps_the_principal_it_dropped` with a null principal.
  - Renaming one identifier fails the identifier-pinning test and the matching dispatcher test.
  - Deleting one new key from `cli.ftl` fails three tests that render the `{rpc-auth-agent-not-entitled}` missing-key marker.
  - Not verified: a live daemon under a translated locale; Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the changed output is a log record whose attributes the tests assert.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No `--no-default-features` check: nothing in `rpc/` is feature-gated, so no constructor can lose its only caller in that build.

</details>

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The record carries the principal id and provider label it already carried, never bearer material; the attribution fix stops dropping data the dispatcher already held.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Test principals are synthetic roster names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Request values that appear in denial messages (agent aliases, paths, job ids, procedure names) are quoted and escaped, so control characters cannot break a message or its log line.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for clients: codes and English messages are unchanged, apart from the global-stream refusal's wording. The audit record's `reason` attribute now holds an identifier and the text moves to `denial_message`; the record has not shipped in a release.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records whose `reason` is not one of the identifiers documented in `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md`, or a `denial_message` or client error message that is a `{rpc-auth-...}` missing-key marker.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Refusal cost:** argumented Fluent lookups parse the catalogue on each call. On an Apple Silicon Mac that measured about 180 µs per refusal for an English daemon and about 530 µs for a translated locale that lacks the new keys (every translated locale until a translation pass). This affects only refused requests. Caching parsed bundles would remove it, but it changes every argumented call site, so it is left for a separate PR. The same cost makes a cron refusal for another agent's job slightly slower than one for a missing job; the answers themselves are identical.
- **Unbound selectors:** the five selector helpers that refused an unbound dispatcher with a bare literal now use the existing first-call key and write a record. They are unreachable once the gate has run.
- **`code` stays a public field** derived once from the reason at construction, so the gateway's readers are untouched.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Expose `reason` on the wire and in gateway HTTP denial bodies.
- Audit handshake denials and the refusals listed as unrecorded in the new docs section.
- Translation fill for the `rpc-auth-*` keys, and parse each Fluent catalogue once.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(providers): support multiple models per provider profile
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; includes upstream master `ee2f5f58f7` (fetched again on October 21, 2026).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add optional `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>.models.<model_alias>]` entries so models share one connection profile while retaining their own model ID, sampling, capacity and capability settings. Canonical selection handles explicit nested references, `models.default`, a sole nested entry and legacy profile-level fields, including profile aliases containing dots.
  - Make provider construction own raw, reliable and routed assembly. Encapsulated `BuiltModel` bindings keep provider, selected identity and route resolver consistent. `zeroclaw-api` stays independent of configuration; explicit `CallSampling` preserves candidate defaults across routes/retries without changing the scalar `None = omit` contract.
  - Use named Agent/delegate/run contexts at production consumers, resolve model-dependent tools from the admitted generation, and install prepared provider updates atomically with their configuration generation. Refresh includes nested selections, active in-turn switches, fallback dependencies and shared construction options.
  - Preserve upstream effort-routing restrictions, per-call native single-tool-round policy, steering, supervised delegation, tool execution context and config application acknowledgements across the merge. Effort permissions resolve connection profiles canonically while construction retains the full selected model reference.
  - Reduce runner stack ownership through `Arc<Config>` and heap boundaries before composing large async scopes. The earlier 16 MiB setting was test-process headroom, not a provider/API limit; focused default-stack verification and its limits are recorded below.
- **Dotted TOML key follow-up (`9c0244f8a1`):** Preserve complete configured profile/model keys in model-alias cascade paths, alias pickers, routing edits, delegate compatibility construction and web catalog dropdowns. Profile boundaries use configured keys; property paths are not parsed as TOML text. Regression coverage includes quoted TOML keys, save/reparse, overlapping short/long profiles and aliases containing `.models.`. Existing restrictions on newly created alias names are unchanged. Only formatting/diff checks ran locally; tests and builds are delegated to CI.
- **CI follow-up (`9d24e5b826`):** Fixed the PR-introduced Clippy diagnostic in dotted profile cascade parsing and relaxed a narrow-terminal picker regression assertion to validate the complete option state while retaining RPC and post-selection rendering checks. Existing parallel cost-ledger timing and dependency-security failures are unchanged baseline issues.
- **Latest CI / Greptile follow-up (`f58163e7bf`):** Model-provider picker options now come exclusively from typed configured maps, preventing nonexistent truncated dotted profiles; exact-list regressions cover `openrouter."glm-5.2"` and overlapping profiles/models. Fixed the new delegate regression test initializer flagged by Clippy. The unused-render-capture finding was already resolved in `a1323b736c`, with loaded-section initialization and full rendering assertions restored. Previous-head main Test, Parallel Runtime Test and Format passed. This head has local formatting and diff checks only; fresh CI is pending.
- **Latest CI follow-up (`7a19fbc7d0`):** Main Test on `32193d51c3` still failed after the ledger wait reached 30 seconds, disproving the earlier scheduling-only diagnosis. The detached-delegate fixture allowed the parent's final $0.015 response to raise ancestor spend from $0.030 to $0.045 before the child's first budget check, correctly refusing the child before any ledger entry. The parent's final response now reports explicit zero usage so completion order cannot consume the child's budget; the test awaits the durable child task outcome, then checks its one priced request, the parent's $0.030 spend, and the ancestor-budget refusal. The common ledger polling helper is restored. Local fmt/diff checks passed. On `7a19fbc7d0`, hosted CI run `40483322530` passed main Test (including the formerly failing detached-delegate case), opt-in tools, Parallel Runtime Test, Greptile Review, Format, Lint, Common Ancestor and Zerocode RPC Boundary; remaining platform/backend legs were still running at the last check. Greptile, opt-in tools, Parallel Runtime Test, all build/check/lint/security jobs passed on `32193d51c3`; Common Ancestor and Zerocode RPC Boundary were canceled during GitHub checkout, before their checks ran.
- **Greptile localization follow-up (`d74fab746c`):** Rollback messages use Fluent keys in the canonical English tool catalogue and its embedded mirror. No dependency versions were changed.
- **Latest CI / Greptile follow-up (`c5a4152d3e`):** Unified model probe outcomes so skipped probes are not reported as verified, moved provider construction into the blocking-safe adapter, reused factory auth readiness for keyless/local/OAuth providers, preserved complete nested model references through channel switches, fixed ZeroCode dotted-profile model lookup, and kept full aliases in event/migration attribution. CI compilation, Clippy and provider/tool test coverage passed on this revision; the detached-delegate timing failure is handled in the follow-up above.
- **Latest review follow-up:** Addressed the three October 21 Greptile findings in `d83a007511`: provider cascade planning resolves the longest configured profile before renaming/deleting keys; doctor derives model selectors from the resolved profile prefix; both web configuration links resolve actual configured aliases through the map-keys API. Regression cases cover overlapping `gw`/`gw.v2` profiles, dotted doctor targets and web links including `openrouter.glm-5.2`; web link coverage is wired into navigation CI. Local fmt/diff checks passed; tests/build remain delegated to hosted CI. Previous head `082c83c483` passed parallel runtime and opt-in tests; the main Test job encountered an inherited cost-ledger timing failure, and dependency-security findings remain outside this PR.
- **Scope boundary:** Retry/fallback order and pricing remain owned by existing profile-level policy. No new model-level fallback/pricing schema, permission grant, background service or global configuration cache. Existing scalar provider calls remain compatible.
- **Blast radius:** Provider API/wrappers, config resolution and alias mutation, Agent/CLI/RPC/ACP/channel construction and refresh, delegation/model tools, SOP, doctor, memory/consolidation, gateway, config/model picker consumers and xtask.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8310, Related #8754, Related #9573, Related #9938.

### What this does, simply

A single endpoint can serve several models with different settings. A configured `custom.gateway.fast` selection now follows the same model, credentials, temperature and context-window rules when it starts through CLI, a live session, a channel, a delegated task or a model switch. Editing a live model profile prepares a complete replacement before publication; an already running call keeps its admitted configuration, and the next admitted call receives the updated binding. Construction failures remain errors instead of silently reusing stale settings.

The optional model tables are additive. This branch keeps the current schema version **3** and does not migrate legacy `model` values or introduce the V4/V5 migration previously described in this PR.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; RPC consumers used by `surface=web` and channel runtimes are covered by focused mock-boundary regressions. Live hosted-provider and browser interaction verification remain separate gaps.
- **Setup / preconditions:** In a disposable config, configure `custom.gateway` with a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint and a fixture-only key. Add `models.fast` (`id="fast-model"`, `temperature=0.2`) and `models.big` (`id="big-model"`, `temperature=0.8`), then set the agent's `model_provider` to `custom.gateway.fast`. Capture POST bodies at the mock endpoint.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a <alias> --message hi`; repeat with `--model-provider custom.gateway.big`. In a live session, update the selected nested entry's temperature through `config/set` and issue the next prompt. Also switch between the two entries using `model_switch`, then edit the active entry or a referenced fallback profile and prompt again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first two requests carry `fast-model`/0.2 and `big-model`/0.8 with the shared profile connection. The next admitted request after an acknowledged edit uses the updated options. A switch between entries with the same wire model ID still changes entry-specific tuning/capacity. Fallback candidates retain their own defaults; explicit invocation overrides remain explicit. Effort routing refuses attempts or switches outside its allowed connection profiles.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Nested model selections are unavailable; each model needs a separate profile repeating its connection. The nested-reference recipe cannot dispatch the named model. Existing profile-level behavior provides the comparison baseline for retries, explicit overrides and effort restrictions.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local checks below provide merge-integration evidence. The pushed head is awaiting a fresh hosted CI run; no pending CI result is represented as passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full-workspace/platform matrix, live hosted-provider/OAuth flows, browser screenshots and manual Web/ZeroCode CRUD are not verified by these focused Rust regressions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
Current source: 7a19fbc7d0 (October 27, 2026); latest local verification: formatting and diff checks only. Earlier results below apply to the revisions at which they were run.

CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime \
  -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw --all-targets
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] ... in 2m 39s
  (Inherited Rust 1.99 atomic deprecation warnings.)

cargo test --offline -p zeroclaw-api --no-default-features --lib -- --quiet
  test result: ok. 316 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --offline --no-default-features -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- \
  model:: temperature:: model_pin:: reliable:: router:: vision_override:: \
  dispatch:: qwen implicit_nested_routes tests::routed_ \
  single_tool_round native_tool_round --test-threads=4 --quiet
  test result: ok. 380 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy --offline -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-providers \
  -p zeroclaw-memory --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] ... in 5m 44s

Merged-head runtime focused tests were attempted with `RUST_MIN_STACK` unset. The fresh lib-test compilation reached the runtime crate but the rustc process was terminated with SIGKILL while concurrent workspace builds were consuming the shared build resources; no runtime test result is claimed from that attempt. Earlier premerge evidence recorded 328 runtime regressions with the same source stack fixes, and two default-stack reflection/shared-options tests passed, but those are not substituted for a merged-head full runtime result. A clean rerun should use an idle runner and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
  Passed

git diff --check
  Passed

The remaining runtime, workspace test, Clippy, parallel-stack and security checks are intentionally delegated to hosted CI because local build load was high. The pre-existing RustSec findings from transitive dependencies were not upgraded in this PR.
git diff --check
  Passed
BASE_SHA=ee2f5f58f7 bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
  (One inherited duplicate heading outside changed lines.)
BASE_SHA=ee2f5f58f7 bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Ran 6 tests ... OK; local target checked.
  Optional HTTP links skipped: lychee is unavailable.
Canonical tools_ftl::render_file mirror check
  Passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Compared construction/update consumers, upstream conflict blocks and call signatures against the merged master. Verified the provider/API dependency direction, complete binding installation, generation fences, explicit sampling forwarding, effort permission checks and inherited worker context at their real call boundaries. HTTP fixtures use local endpoints and synthetic credentials.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Missing for the pre-existing model/config picker changes carried by this PR; browser screenshots are still required before visual sign-off. The backend merge checks below do not substitute for rendered-interface evidence.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Merge-integration checks are recorded for the final source tree below. Local command logs are summarized here; historical premerge CLI smoke output is not presented as final-head evidence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** No final-head browser screenshots attached.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Mock-boundary tests inspect the selected model/options, retry/fallback requests, allowed provider attempts and acknowledged generation updates. See the command results above for completed coverage.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace/release builds and optional HTTP documentation link checking were not run; the latter requires `lychee`. Full release-mode `cargo generate installers --check` was replaced by checking the English tools mirror with its canonical renderer.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing provider/catalog/probe calls retain their purpose; construction and credential refresh move through the blocking-safe adapter where needed.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Connection and credential selection now derive from the canonical selected profile, including dotted aliases, fallback profiles and endpoint overrides. Fixtures use synthetic keys; cache identity hashes configuration instead of storing plaintext credentials.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** The model-switch result retains upstream guidance to continue the current task within the same turn. This tool result grants no authority; normal tool permissions, approval, effort limits and cancellation still apply.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Wrong selection could route a call with another profile's connection or stale policy. Central construction, sealed identity, admitted configuration and wire-level tests cover that boundary. Per-turn effort checks remain in the classifier, vision, reliability and switch paths.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for some Rust consumer APIs; yes for existing configuration and scalar provider-call semantics.** Newly introduced binding fields are encapsulated. SOP's provider adapter accepts a configuration resolver; configured `LlmTaskTool` consumers use a resolver. Doctor structured calls return `Result`, and reflection takes explicit sampling.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Add optional nested model tables and nested provider references; model pickers/config consumers expose those entries. Existing profile-level configuration remains valid. Schema version stays **3**; there is no automatic rewrite to V5.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Existing users need no config migration. To opt in, add nested `models` entries and select `<family>.<profile>.<model_alias>`. Out-of-tree Rust callers should use `build_model`/raw/reliable constructors with `ProviderOverrides`, named Agent contexts and the resolver-based tool/SOP constructors; handle fallible doctor results explicitly. Scalar calls retain `None` as omission, while configured per-candidate defaults require explicit sampling.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual squash commit. For this development branch, restore the pre-PR implementation through normal reviewed revert commits; do not revert the upstream-master merge wholesale. Before running an older binary, replace nested references with legacy profile-level `model` entries (separate profiles when necessary). No database or schema-version rollback is required.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Nested model tables are opt-in.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unresolved model selections, provider construction errors, unexpected wire model/temperature, stale capacity after an acknowledged config update, rejected effort-route attempts, or a different requested/served route in provider attribution.

prs.title: ci(rust): bump routine toolchains to 1.99.1
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Upgrade routine GitHub Actions, release, platform, audit, and local CI toolchains to Rust 1.99.0.
  - Move generated Rust container builders to the 1.99 image tags and refresh registry digests from the canonical manifest, including Node and unchanged-tag Debian, distroless, and Alpine runtime base images.
  - Fix Rust 1.99 Clippy compatibility findings while preserving the declared workspace MSRV.
- **Scope boundary:** `Cargo.toml` remains unchanged at Rust 1.96.0. Historical changelog/audit entries and fixed-version release test fixtures remain historical or synthetic data rather than routine toolchain policy.
- **Blast radius:** CI, release builders, local CI containers, demo/relay image builds, and Windows test scope contracts use the newer routine compiler. No runtime behavior, configuration, API, permission, or security policy changes are intended.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9527

### What this does, simply

This keeps ZeroClaw's routine builds and checks on Rust 1.99.0, including pinned container builders that compile release images. The source compatibility floor remains Rust 1.96.0, so existing users are not required to upgrade their supported compiler. New compiler diagnostics are handled with behavior-preserving assertion changes and the `Atomic*::try_update` API, which has been stable since Rust 1.95; no new lint or deprecation allowances are added.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - this is CI/toolchain configuration and compiler-lint maintenance with no user-facing workflow to exercise manually.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No pending check is claimed as evidence. The local commands below cover the Rust 1.99 lint surface, the declared Rust 1.96 MSRV, affected atomic behavior, plugin egress behavior, architecture, Windows scope, and generated-installer surfaces.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation did not execute native macOS or Windows tests. Current-head platform and required CI runs provide that target-specific evidence once complete.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  # Tested revision ba4856008b
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  pass

  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile ... in 3m 29s

  cargo +1.96.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
  Finished `dev` profile ... in 19m 56s

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::upload
  test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib checkpoint
  test result: ok. 72 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib acp_prompt_two_observed_trims_survive_abort_and_reopen
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib scrape_entropy_varies_between_calls
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw diff_is_empty_when_declaration_matches_grant_in_any_order
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed

  git diff --check
  pass

  # Earlier synchronized head ef71dd2d76
  ```
